heroTitle: Hiring an IB tutor in India, decided properly
heroSubtitle: IB Gram is an independent platform that matches families with verified tutors for home tuition, online lessons or a hybrid of the two. You tell us the programme, the subject, the level and your locality; we shortlist tutors who fit. A demo session can be arranged before you commit to anything.
introSummary: IB tutors in India work across three separate programmes and two marking cultures at once, which is why this search is harder than it looks, and why most families start by asking for home tuition from someone who has actually taught the syllabus rather than a general Maths teacher with a new label. This page is the decision guide for the whole set. It covers what an International Baccalaureate (IB) tutor does that a CBSE or ICSE tutor usually cannot, what the Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) and Diploma Programme (DP) each demand, how to shortlist and trial in five steps, and how the three lesson modes compare in Indian cities. Fees, coaching and exam preparation get a paragraph each.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist IB tutors in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, we ask what the student is actually studying, and a shortlist comes back of tutors whose profiles have been verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. If the fit turns out wrong after two or three lessons, you ask for a different match. That is the whole mechanism, and it is deliberately unglamorous.

The questions matter more than the turnaround. Board and programme first, because an MYP 4 student and a DP1 student need different people even in the same subject. Then the level: Higher Level (HL) carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level (SL), and a tutor who is comfortable with SL Economics can be out of depth on the HL extension. Then the school calendar, because a family whose mocks land in January is planning backwards from a different date than one whose school runs them in November. Then location, down to the locality rather than the city. Powai is not Bandra for a weekday evening visit, and Gachibowli is not Secunderabad. Then the slots that are genuinely free once school timings, Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments and travel have been counted.

Only after all of that does a name appear. Availability stays conditional on level, subject and schedule. For a thinly taught Higher Level subject the honest answer is sometimes that the right person teaches online rather than at your door, and we would rather say so than send someone weaker who happens to live close by.

Bring evidence to the first call. A report card with criterion comments, a marked script, a returned Internal Assessment (IA) draft with the supervisor's notes. Ten minutes spent reading those tells us more about which tutor to send than an hour of description does. Parents often apologise for the marked script being unflattering. It is the single most useful document you own.
items: 1. Send a query naming board, programme, subject and Higher or Standard Level
2. Answer the calendar questions: term dates, mock weeks, exam session
3. Give your locality and the two evening slots that are genuinely free
4. Read the shortlisted profiles and ask each tutor one syllabus-specific question
5. Take a demo session, then decide, or ask for a different match

contentBlocks.heading: What IB home tutoring looks like at PYP, MYP and DP level in India
contentBlocks.body:
Three programmes, three completely different jobs. Treating them as one service is the commonest mistake families and providers both make, and it is why a tutor who was excellent for an older sibling in DP2 can be wrong for a child in MYP 3.

The Primary Years Programme runs from ages three to twelve. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, which the IB names as Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet. Children work through units of inquiry against the ten attributes of the learner profile, and finish with the PYP exhibition in the final year. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades. So a PYP home tutor is not preparing anyone for anything. The useful work is reading fluency, number sense, and helping a child who has gone quiet in class find something to say in an inquiry.

The Middle Years Programme runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8. The total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Community Project falls in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so ask your coordinator before assuming your child sits an on-screen examination at all. MYP home classes usually start because one criterion is stuck while the others are fine.

The Diploma Programme is two years, DP1 and DP2: six subjects from six groups, three or four at HL. Every subject is graded 1 to 7, Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 points, 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. This is where most paid tutoring in India actually happens.
items: PYP: no external exams, no published grades; tutoring is habit and confidence work
MYP: four criteria per subject, each out of 8, totalling 32
MYP 5 eAssessment is optional; confirm with your school before planning for it
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL, each graded 1 to 7
TOK and EE together add up to three points towards the maximum of 45
Twenty-four points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects do students in India need most help with?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics first, and by a distance. The split between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (AI) catches families out because the names sound interchangeable and the choice is made at fourteen or fifteen, often on the advice of a relative who did engineering. A student who is capable but slow at algebraic manipulation can spend two years fighting AA Higher Level when AI would have suited both the way they think and the courses they actually want to apply for. A tutor cannot undo that choice mid-course. A tutor can tell you, honestly, in week three of DP1, whether the choice is survivable.

The sciences come next. IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology all carry a scientific investigation as internal assessment, and Indian students arriving from CBSE or ICSE are usually strong on content and weak on the parts that carry marks here: designing something that can actually be measured, handling uncertainty honestly, and writing an evaluation that criticises their own method. That last one is genuinely counter-cultural for a student trained to present a clean result.

IB Economics surprises people. It reads like a subject you can revise the night before and it is not. The internal assessment portfolio asks for commentaries built on real articles, which means reading news properly for two years rather than cramming definitions.

IB English A is the subject families underestimate most, and the one where a home tutor pays off quietly over a long period rather than dramatically in a month. Then there is TOK, which almost nobody feels equipped to help with at home: the exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 prompts, up to 950 words, internally assessed and worth a third of the grade, while the essay answers one of six prescribed titles released each session, up to 1,600 words and externally assessed.
items: Mathematics AA against AI: the choice is made early and rarely revisited
Sciences: the scientific investigation rewards honest evaluation, not a clean result
Economics: commentaries need two years of real reading, not revision notes
English A: slow gains over terms, not a four-week rescue
TOK exhibition, 950 words, three objects, one of 35 prompts
TOK essay, 1,600 words, one of six prescribed titles for the session

contentBlocks.heading: IB tutor coverage across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
IB tutors in India are not spread evenly, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's month. IB teaching capacity clusters where IB schools cluster, and thins fast outside those pockets. Here is the honest map.

In Delhi NCR the pool is deep and the geography is the problem. An IB home tutor in Delhi covering South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri can hold three evening slots a week without much strain. Cross into Gurugram along Golf Course Road, or out to Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad, Dwarka or Ghaziabad, and evening traffic on a weekday can stretch what looks like a short trip on a map into something no tutor will do twice a week for long. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the same pattern repeats vertically: an IB home tutor in Mumbai serving Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel or Malabar Hill is workable, while Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are effectively separate markets. Bengaluru is the clearest case of all. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala and Indiranagar have real depth; Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road often depend on someone crossing the city at exactly the wrong hour.

An IB tutor in Hyderabad usually works the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet belt, with Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills close behind and Secunderabad a genuine trek. An IB tutor in Chennai covers Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam comfortably, with Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar depending on the hour. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar sit close together, while Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi form their own cluster.

Beyond the six metro clusters the arithmetic changes. In Gujarat, Ahmedabad's Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway areas plus Gandhinagar carry some supply, with Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot much thinner. Across Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore have a little, and Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna very little. The same holds for northern India beyond Delhi NCR, where Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur are mostly online markets; for southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, meaning Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai; and for central and western India, where Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa families should plan on online lessons for anything at Higher Level.
items: Delhi NCR: deep pool, but Gurugram and Noida evening runs limit weekly frequency
Mumbai: Powai, Thane and Navi Mumbai behave as separate markets from the island city
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are dense; Yelahanka and Electronic City are not
Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune each have one dense belt and one long commute
Ahmedabad, Kolkata, Chandigarh, Kochi and Indore: online is often the better match
Never accept a travel-time promise; ask the tutor which evenings they already hold nearby

contentBlocks.heading: How the school year in India shapes when tutoring starts
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools appear here only as context for the calendar most international-school families in India are living inside.

The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session rather than November. Results are released in early July. Those two facts drive almost every sensible decision families make about IB tutors in India. A DP1 student starting in April has two full years; a DP2 student ringing in December has a few months, most of which are already committed to internal assessment deadlines and mock cycles.

So the year has a shape. April to July is the quiet window and the cheapest time, in effort rather than money, to fix something structural: a weak algebra base before HL Mathematics gets serious, or the reading habit an English A student never built. August to October is when IA drafts start landing and the first real criterion feedback arrives. November through January is mock season in most schools, and it is also when families panic, which is precisely the worst moment to start something new. February and March belong to the student, the school and revision. A tutor who joins then should be doing past-paper work and nothing else.

Parents at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore tend to describe similar pressures: a heavy coursework load that arrives in clusters, a CAS commitment that cannot be dropped, and a school that communicates in criterion language parents were never taught to read. None of that is a reason to hire someone in a hurry. It is a reason to hire early, when there is still room to be wrong once.
items: Indian academic year runs roughly April to March; May is the dominant exam session
May results are released in early July, which sets the retake conversation
April to July: the quiet window for structural repair work
August to October: IA drafts and the first real criterion feedback
November to January: mocks, and the worst moment to start a new tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which mode actually suits your family
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor is better when the problem is behavioural rather than academic. A student who does not start work unless someone is sitting there, a child who hides a blank page, a DP2 candidate who has quietly stopped opening one subject: presence solves those in a way a screen does not. The tutor sees the desk, the phone, the notebook nobody has written in since August, and the parent gets an unfiltered read on what the week actually looks like.

Online is better when the problem is scarcity. If a student takes a Higher Level subject that two people in the city teach well, distance stops being the deciding factor. Online also survives the things home tuition does not: monsoon week, a tutor's own travel, an exam period when lessons need to move at short notice. And it makes a specialist in one city available to a family in another, which is the whole argument for families outside the metros.

Hybrid is the arrangement most DP families drift into by month three without anyone planning it. One home session a week for the long working sitting, where the tutor watches the student produce answers under something like exam conditions, plus one or two shorter online sessions for doubt-solving, past-paper marking and checking a draft. It costs the family less travel and costs the tutor less dead time, so slots are easier to hold across a full year.

The trade-off, stated plainly: a home tutor gives you presence and accountability but limits you to whoever will travel to your locality at that hour; an online tutor gives you the whole country's supply but needs a student who will sit down without being watched; hybrid gives you most of both and asks the family to actually run a schedule. Families hiring IB tutors in India should pick on the failure they can least afford.
items: Home tuition wins on accountability, study-space visibility and reluctant starters
Online wins on scarce Higher Level subjects and on schedule resilience
Hybrid: one home session for long writing, online sessions for marking and doubts
Monsoon, exam weeks and tutor travel all break home schedules first
Younger children generally need presence; DP2 students often do not

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before hiring an IB tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
Check the syllabus knowledge yourself, in one question, before anything else. Ask the tutor to explain how a mark is actually awarded in the subject your child takes: which criterion, what the descriptor says, what separates the top band from the one below. A tutor who has taught the course answers in the IB's own vocabulary without effort. A general subject tutor answers in terms of right and wrong answers. That single question sorts most shortlists in ninety seconds.

On our side, a profile is verified before it goes live: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the specific programmes and levels the tutor says they teach. What that verification does not do, and no platform's can, is predict chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old. That is what the demo session exists for, and why asking for a different match is a normal request rather than a complaint.

There are claims worth treating with real caution. Be wary of anyone advertising a guaranteed grade, a promised points jump or a published success rate. No tutor can guarantee a grade. Be equally wary of a provider implying a relationship with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson that does not exist; these organisations authorise schools, not tutoring services.

Then check the practical things a family only discovers in week four. Will the same person teach every session, or does a name rotate. What happens to a missed lesson. Whether the tutor will put a short written note to you after each session, which matters more than it sounds because criterion feedback is hard to read second-hand. And, for home visits, whether the tutor is genuinely able to reach your locality on a weekday evening every week, or only on the first enthusiastic fortnight.
items: Ask how a mark is awarded in your child's subject; listen for criterion language
Identity, qualifications and the programmes claimed are verified before a profile goes live
No verification predicts rapport; that is what the demo session is for
Be wary of guaranteed grades, promised points jumps and published success rates
Confirm who teaches every week, and what happens to a missed session

contentBlocks.heading: What an IB tutor does that a CBSE or ICSE tutor usually cannot
contentBlocks.body:
Students move into the IB from CBSE, ICSE and state boards, and back out again, and the differences they meet are consistent enough to list. Marking is criterion-referenced and driven by command terms rather than a fixed answer key. Coursework and internal assessment carry real weight towards the final grade. Wider reading and independent research are assumed. There is less emphasis on memorised derivations. A tutor who has only taught board syllabuses can be excellent at the physics and still leave marks on the table, because the marks are not where they expect them to be.

Take command terms. Describe, explain, evaluate and discuss are not synonyms in the IB; each one names a different thing the answer must do, and an examiner marking an evaluate question finds nothing to credit in a flawless description. An IB tutor's first job with a transferring student is usually to sit with a script the student is proud of and show them where it earned nothing.

Internal assessment is the second gap. A board tutor's instinct is to help a student produce a good piece of work. That instinct, followed too far, becomes an academic integrity problem, because the IB requires the work to be the student's own and the school to authenticate it. A tutor working properly discusses the criteria, asks questions about the student's own draft and points at what the descriptor asks for. A tutor working improperly writes sentences. Families should know the difference before they hire, not after a school raises it.

The third is TOK, which has no board equivalent at all and which most families cannot help with from the kitchen table. And the fourth is quieter: equivalence for Indian university admission is issued by the Association of Indian Universities, requirements differ by university and by course, and anyone telling you a single blanket rule is guessing. Confirm with the institution.
items: Criterion-referenced marking and command terms replace a fixed answer key
Internal assessment carries real weight and must be the student's own work
Independent research and wider reading are assumed rather than taught
TOK has no board equivalent; most parents cannot coach it at home
Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence; confirm rules with each university

contentBlocks.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks?
contentBlocks.body:
Not a grade. Four weeks is far too short for a 1 to 7 grade to move, and any provider pointing at a grade jump after a month is either lucky or describing a mock that was easier. What should have changed in four weeks is smaller and much more reliable.

The student should be able to tell you what the criterion they were weak on actually asks for, in their own words. They should have produced at least one piece of work that was marked against the descriptor in front of them rather than handed back with a number. They should be starting work on that subject without an argument, which sounds like a low bar and is the single best early indicator there is. And you should have heard something specific from the tutor: not that your child is doing well, but that their evaluation sections are still descriptive and here is the plan for that.

By eight to twelve weeks you should see it in school feedback, and that is the right moment to review honestly rather than renew automatically. Ask the tutor what they would stop doing. A good one always has an answer.

There are cases where the right advice is to stop. If a student is being tutored in four subjects at once, the tutoring itself has become the workload problem. If the difficulty is sleep, anxiety or a school relationship that has broken down, a subject tutor is the wrong tool and an honest one will say so. If a child in PYP is being tutored because a parent is anxious rather than because a teacher raised something, stopping is usually the better decision. And if a family started three weeks before the May session hoping for a rescue, the useful conversation is about triage across papers, not about coverage.

Tutoring should have an end. Plan for it at the start.
items: Four weeks: the student can explain the criterion in their own words
One piece of work marked against the descriptor with the student watching
Work on that subject starts without an argument at home
Eight to twelve weeks: the change should show in school feedback
Stop if the tutoring load has become the problem, or the issue is not academic

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition: what to prepare before the first lesson
contentBlocks.body:
Prepare four things and the first session stops being a get-to-know-you hour. The most recent report with its criterion comments. One marked script the student did badly on. The school's assessment calendar for the term, including mock weeks and IA deadlines. And a single sentence from you about what you actually want, written down, because families frequently discover they disagree about it while saying it aloud.

Set up the space before the tutor arrives. A table the student can spread a past paper across, a chair that is not a bed, a light that works after dark, and a door. Home classes fail more often over a bad study corner than over a bad tutor. If lessons are online or hybrid, the equivalent preparation is a charged laptop with the camera working, a headset, and a second screen or a printed paper so the student is not toggling between the tutor's face and the question.

The first session itself should be diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend most of it watching the student attempt work rather than explaining. Expect uncomfortable questions about what the student does not understand from six months ago. Expect a short written plan afterwards naming what will be worked on, in what order, and roughly when it should show.

A parent being somewhere in the house during a home session is good practice, particularly for younger students, and it is not the same as sitting in the room. Younger children in PYP and early MYP generally do better with an adult nearby. A DP2 student almost always does worse.

As for money: fees vary with level, subject scarcity, experience and whether the tutor travels, and we will tell you the structure before any lesson is booked rather than after. Nothing is charged for the consultation or for asking.
items: Bring the latest report, a badly marked script and the term's assessment calendar
Write one sentence saying what you actually want from the tutoring
Set up a real table, working light and a door before the first home lesson
For online or hybrid, add a headset and a printed paper or second screen
Expect a diagnostic first session and a short written plan afterwards

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost in India?
faqs.answer: There is no single figure, and any page quoting one is guessing. Fees move with the programme, the level, how scarce the subject is, the tutor's experience, and whether they travel to your locality. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level because the preparation is heavier. Home visits cost more than the same tutor online, since travel time is real time. A DP subject specialist in Mumbai and an MYP generalist in Coimbatore are not comparable at all. We will tell you the structure that applies to your match before any lesson is booked.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor come to our locality, and how often?
faqs.answer: Usually yes in the six metro clusters, and the frequency depends on where you are rather than whether the tutor is willing. A tutor living within a short run of your area can realistically hold two or three weekday evenings a week. One crossing Bengaluru from Whitefield to Kanakapura Road, or Delhi to Greater Noida, can rarely hold more than one, and may not hold that past the first month. Ask any prospective home tutor which other evenings they already teach nearby. It is the most honest availability test there is.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and the nearest IB school is not close. Can our child still get an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online is almost certainly the right mode. Outside the metros, local supply for IB subjects thins quickly, and the same is true across Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Guwahati and Bhubaneswar. Going online means the pool stops being whoever lives nearby and becomes whoever teaches that subject anywhere in the country. For Higher Level subjects and for TOK, that difference is usually larger than anything presence would have given you. A hybrid arrangement works too if one of the family travels occasionally.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring really as good as a tutor at home?
faqs.answer: For a motivated DP student, yes, and sometimes better because the tutor is a stronger subject match. For a student who does not start work unless someone is present, no. That is the real dividing line, not the technology. Online lessons handle marking, past papers and draft discussion very well, since everything is on a shared screen anyway. What they cannot do is notice that the student has not opened the textbook in three weeks. Younger children in PYP and early MYP generally need home classes or a hybrid pattern.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at the same time?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two only when there is a clear reason. A DP student already carries six subjects, the core and CAS commitments. Adding three tutors adds three sets of homework on top of school homework, and the usual result is that everything gets done badly. Start with the subject where the gap costs the most points, run it for six to eight weeks, and review. If the second subject still looks weak after that, add it then. Tutoring that becomes its own workload has stopped helping.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor take a late weekday evening slot in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth thinking about what a late slot actually costs the student. After school, travel and an activity, a session starting at eight in the evening is being taught to a tired teenager, and the last half hour is rarely productive. In Gurugram, Noida and Thane particularly, a tutor arriving late because of evening traffic then compresses the lesson. Two shorter weekday sessions, or one weekend morning session paired with a shorter online slot midweek, usually produces more than one long tired evening.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and ask for a different match. That is a normal request and it does not need justifying at length. Before you do, try to name the problem precisely, because it changes who we send next: a tutor who knows the subject but cannot hold the student's attention is a different replacement from one the student likes but who is vague about criteria. Three weeks is enough to judge fit and communication. It is not enough to judge results, so separate the two before deciding.

faqs.question: Does a child in the Primary Years Programme need a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and we would rather say that than sell you something. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, so there is nothing to prepare for. The situations where help genuinely pays are narrow: a real reading gap, number sense that never formed, a child who has switched boards mid-primary, or a learning difference the school has flagged. If a teacher has raised nothing and the worry is yours alone, wait a term. Anxiety at the parent's end is a poor reason to add an hour to a nine-year-old's week.

faqs.question: How is hiring a tutor different from joining IB coaching classes?
faqs.answer: The short version is that a tutor starts from your child's own work and a coaching batch starts from a syllabus plan. Batches are built around the commonest subject combinations and a fixed timetable, which suits a disciplined student who likes peers and pace. A tutor diagnoses first, which suits a student whose problem is specific and personal. Cost per hour usually favours the batch and attention favours the tutor. Neither is the better product in general; they are answers to different questions.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the rules, and the boundary matters. A tutor can teach the criteria, ask questions about the student's own draft, point out that a section described where it should have evaluated, and help plan a realistic schedule against the school's deadlines. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or supply text, because the work must be the student's own and the school authenticates it. If anyone offers to draft an IA or an Extended Essay for your child, that is the moment to walk away. The school's supervisor remains the primary guide throughout.

faqs.question: Our daughter is moving from CBSE into DP1. How much catching up is involved?
faqs.answer: Less content than families expect and more method than they expect. Students switching boards usually arrive strong on content and unprepared for criterion-referenced marking, command terms, coursework that counts, and the amount of independent reading assumed. The first term is where that shows, often as a capable student getting mediocre grades and nobody understanding why. Six to ten weeks of work on how answers are marked, starting in April rather than in October, fixes most of it. Confirm any university equivalence questions with the institution rather than relying on general advice.

faqs.question: How long before the May session should we start?
faqs.answer: For structural work, a full year, and ideally from April at the start of DP1. For targeted repair of one weak subject, a term is enough. Starting in January of DP2 is late but not useless, provided everyone accepts the goal has changed from coverage to triage: which papers can still move, which topics are worth abandoning, and how to protect the marks already within reach. Results arrive in early July, so leaving it until after mocks compresses everything into the busiest weeks of the two years.

Outside the metros, local supply for IB subjects thins quickly, and the same is true across Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Guwahati and Bhubaneswar. Going online means the pool stops being whoever lives nearby and becomes whoever teaches that subject anywhere in the country. For Higher Level subjects and for TOK, that difference is usually larger than anything presence would have given you. A hybrid arrangement works too if one of the family travels occasionally.

mainEntity.name: Is online IB tutoring really as good as a tutor at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a motivated DP student, yes, and sometimes better because the tutor is a stronger subject match. For a student who does not start work unless someone is present, no. That is the real dividing line, not the technology. Online lessons handle marking, past papers and draft discussion very well, since everything is on a shared screen anyway. What they cannot do is notice that the student has not opened the textbook in three weeks. Younger children in PYP and early MYP generally need home classes or a hybrid pattern.

mainEntity.name: How many subjects should we tutor at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: One, in most cases, and two only when there is a clear reason. A DP student already carries six subjects, the core and CAS commitments. Adding three tutors adds three sets of homework on top of school homework, and the usual result is that everything gets done badly. Start with the subject where the gap costs the most points, run it for six to eight weeks, and review. If the second subject still looks weak after that, add it then. Tutoring that becomes its own workload has stopped helping.

mainEntity.name: Can a home tutor take a late weekday evening slot in Gurugram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, and it is worth thinking about what a late slot actually costs the student. After school, travel and an activity, a session starting at eight in the evening is being taught to a tired teenager, and the last half hour is rarely productive. In Gurugram, Noida and Thane particularly, a tutor arriving late because of evening traffic then compresses the lesson. Two shorter weekday sessions, or one weekend morning session paired with a shorter online slot midweek, usually produces more than one long tired evening.

mainEntity.name: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What should we do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us, and ask for a different match. That is a normal request and it does not need justifying at length. Before you do, try to name the problem precisely, because it changes who we send next: a tutor who knows the subject but cannot hold the student's attention is a different replacement from one the student likes but who is vague about criteria. Three weeks is enough to judge fit and communication. It is not enough to judge results, so separate the two before deciding.

mainEntity.name: Does a child in the Primary Years Programme need a tutor at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not, and we would rather say that than sell you something. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, so there is nothing to prepare for. The situations where help genuinely pays are narrow: a real reading gap, number sense that never formed, a child who has switched boards mid-primary, or a learning difference the school has flagged. If a teacher has raised nothing and the worry is yours alone, wait a term. Anxiety at the parent's end is a poor reason to add an hour to a nine-year-old's week.

mainEntity.name: How is hiring a tutor different from joining IB coaching classes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The short version is that a tutor starts from your child's own work and a coaching batch starts from a syllabus plan. Batches are built around the commonest subject combinations and a fixed timetable, which suits a disciplined student who likes peers and pace. A tutor diagnoses first, which suits a student whose problem is specific and personal. Cost per hour usually favours the batch and attention favours the tutor. Neither is the better product in general; they are answers to different questions.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the rules, and the boundary matters. A tutor can teach the criteria, ask questions about the student's own draft, point out that a section described where it should have evaluated, and help plan a realistic schedule against the school's deadlines. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or supply text, because the work must be the student's own and the school authenticates it. If anyone offers to draft an IA or an Extended Essay for your child, that is the moment to walk away. The school's supervisor remains the primary guide throughout.

mainEntity.name: Our daughter is moving from CBSE into DP1. How much catching up is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Less content than families expect and more method than they expect. Students switching boards usually arrive strong on content and unprepared for criterion-referenced marking, command terms, coursework that counts, and the amount of independent reading assumed. The first term is where that shows, often as a capable student getting mediocre grades and nobody understanding why. Six to ten weeks of work on how answers are marked, starting in April rather than in October, fixes most of it. Confirm any university equivalence questions with the institution rather than relying on general advice.

mainEntity.name: How long before the May session should we start?

acceptedAnswer.text: For structural work, a full year, and ideally from April at the start of DP1. For targeted repair of one weak subject, a term is enough. Starting in January of DP2 is late but not useless, provided everyone accepts the goal has changed from coverage to triage: which papers can still move, which topics are worth abandoning, and how to protect the marks already within reach. Results arrive in early July, so leaving it until after mocks compresses everything into the busiest weeks of the two years.

We come back with a shortlist of verified tutors who match, arrange a demo session before you commit, and change the match if the fit is wrong. Nothing is charged for asking, and the same process applies to IB tutors in India whether you want them at home or on a screen.

An online tutor suits a family chasing a scarce Higher Level specialist. A centre batch suits a disciplined student who works better with peers and a fixed timetable. A recorded course suits revision and nothing else. The trade-off that usually decides it is whether the student will start work unsupervised.

heroTitle: An IB Home Tutor at Your Address in India
heroSubtitle: IB Gram matches families with verified IB home tutors who travel to the flat or house you actually live in, from Powai to Whitefield to Sector 128 Noida. Weekday evening slots, society gate entry sorted in advance, and an honest word when online would serve you better.
introSummary: IB home tutors in India are tutors who travel to your address and teach at your dining table, in your study, or wherever the household can hold ninety quiet minutes. That is the whole service on this page: the visit itself. What a tutor can reach in weekday traffic, how they get past a society gate, which room works, what they carry in a bag, what you need to set up, and the evenings when a home visit is simply the wrong call. IB Gram is a matching platform, so the practical questions below are the ones parents ask on almost every call, and the answers are the same ones we give families in Gurugram, Thane and Gachibowli.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match an IB home tutor in India to your address?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, we ask where you live and when the student is free, and we shortlist verified tutors whose profiles fit the board, subject, level and travel. A demo session can be arranged before you commit to anything. Matching starts with geography, because a home visit nobody can sustain is worth nothing.

So the first questions are dull and practical. Which building, which sector or layout, which gate. Is there parking or an auto stand close by. Does the lift run reliably in the evening. Then the academic side: Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) or Diploma Programme (DP), the subjects, Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), and what the last report actually said. A DP1 student who needs Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) HL twice a week is a completely different search from a nine-year-old who needs an hour of reading support on Saturday mornings.

Next we look at the calendar you keep rather than the one you would like to keep. School finishes at one time, the bus reaches the gate at another, and football or Carnatic music classes swallow two evenings. Tutors who cannot hold that slot week after week are left off the shortlist, however strong their subject background, because a home tutor who reschedules constantly costs a family more than they add.

Availability stays conditional throughout. IB home tutors in India cluster around the places where IB schools already sit, so in a locality with none within easy reach, the honest answer may be that the right subject specialist sits thirty minutes away on a good evening and out of reach on a wet one. We would rather say that plainly than send someone who quietly drops out in week five.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with your locality and school timings
2. We ask about board, programme, subject, level, term calendar and your exact area
3. You get a shortlist of verified tutors who can hold that weekly slot
4. Arrange a demo or trial session at home before committing to anything longer
5. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong after the first sessions

contentBlocks.heading: What a home visit looks like in PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
A visiting tutor's job changes completely with the programme, and so does the shape of the evening.

The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages three to twelve. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, and learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet, with the ten attributes of the IB learner profile running through them and the PYP exhibition in the final year. Home classes at this stage are short. The tutor builds reading fluency and number sense, then leaves the parent something small to hold on the four evenings when nobody is visiting.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to 5, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0-8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. This is where a tutor sitting at the table earns their fee. A parent reading a report line that says criterion C sits at 4 has no idea what to do on Tuesday evening; a tutor who has taught that criterion does. The Personal Project arrives in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and there the boundary is firm: question and teach, never write. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so ask yours before planning around it.

Diploma Programme (DP) visits are the longest and the most tightly booked. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) contributing up to 3 further points towards a maximum of 45.
items: PYP: forty to sixty minutes is usually the ceiling for a young child
MYP: work from the criterion strands, not the rounded 1-7 grade
MYP 5 Personal Project: the tutor questions and teaches, the student writes every word
DP: Higher Level carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level
DP2 households often want two visits a week, subject to tutor availability

contentBlocks.heading: Subject work that goes better with a tutor beside the desk
contentBlocks.body:
Some subject problems are visible on a screen and some are only visible on paper, at the table, as they happen. That difference decides whether a visit is worth the travel.

Mathematics is the clearest case. In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation (AI), at both Higher Level and Standard Level, marks are lost in the middle of a solution rather than at the end. A student who skips a line of algebra, writes the substitution nowhere, or rounds early will often reach a defensible answer and still drop method marks. A tutor sitting to the student's right sees the pencil stop, sees the line that was never written, and interrupts at the moment it matters. Over a screen the same error surfaces ten minutes later, if at all.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology bring the practical write-up and the diagram. Uncertainties, axes, units on a table header, a labelled apparatus sketch: these are all things a student produces badly at speed and defends confidently afterwards. Home sessions let the tutor watch the graph being drawn rather than receive the photograph of it. Internal Assessment (IA) work in the sciences also benefits from the tutor being able to look at the actual lab notebook, the messy one, instead of a tidied summary.

Economics and English A are more about drafting. Here the visit works differently: the student writes for fifteen minutes with the tutor quietly present, which is a discipline most teenagers cannot impose on themselves, and then the two of them read it back line by line. For English A commentary work and for Economics evaluation paragraphs, that read-aloud step catches more than any amount of written feedback emailed at midnight.
items: Mathematics AA and AI: method marks are lost mid-solution, where a tutor can see it
Physics, Chemistry and Biology: uncertainties, axes, units and labelled diagrams under time pressure
Sciences: the tutor reads the real lab notebook, not a tidied-up summary
English A: fifteen silent minutes of drafting, then a line-by-line read-back
Economics: evaluation paragraphs improve faster when written and challenged in the room

contentBlocks.heading: Travel radius in India: what a home tutor can realistically reach
contentBlocks.body:
Ask how far they travel and experienced IB home tutors in India answer in minutes, not kilometres. That is the right way to think about it.

In Delhi NCR the radius is narrow on a weekday evening and wide on a Sunday morning. An IB home tutor in Delhi who lives in South Delhi will hold a slot in Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri comfortably and hesitate over Dwarka. Gurugram (Gurgaon) largely works within itself, with Golf Course Road and the sectors around it forming one pool. Noida, Sector 128 Noida and Greater Noida form another, and Faridabad and Ghaziabad a third. Crossing between those pools in evening traffic is the single most common reason a promising match falls apart by the second month.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is a set of corridors rather than a circle. An IB home tutor in Mumbai working in Bandra, Juhu or Andheri stays on that arm; Powai has its own pool; Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill form a southern cluster that is hard to reach from the suburbs after six. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are better served from within, and families there often do better asking for a tutor who already lives across the creek.

Bengaluru is the city where distance lies most convincingly. An IB home tutor in Bangalore based near Whitefield or Sarjapur Road will cover Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout on the right evening, while Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each need someone local. Pune splits similarly: Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar on one side, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Aundh and Wakad on the other. In Hyderabad, an IB home tutor in Hyderabad working around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet rarely wants Secunderabad on the same evening, though Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills sit conveniently between. Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad follow the same rule, and an IB home tutor in Chennai or an IB home tutor in Kolkata will quote you an evening window rather than a distance.
items: Delhi NCR splits into South Delhi, Gurugram, Noida and Faridabad-Ghaziabad evening pools
Mumbai runs along corridors: the western arm, Powai, the south, and Navi Mumbai
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road rarely pair with Yelahanka or Electronic City
Pune divides across the river into the Koregaon Park side and the Baner side
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kokapet form one pool, Secunderabad another
In Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad, ask for an evening window, never a distance

contentBlocks.heading: The school year in India that home visits must bend around
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and international schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session rather than November. May results are released in early July. Those three facts shape every home tuition timetable in the country, and a tutor who plans without them will be booking sessions in the weeks when nothing can be absorbed.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Nothing here describes what any particular school teaches or where it sits.

What we can describe is the pressure families report. The first term after the summer break is the quiet window, and it is the term most parents waste. Home classes started in July or August do the unglamorous work: closing gaps from the previous year, fixing note-taking, building the habit of a weekly session before anything is urgent. By the time the winter mock cycle arrives, that student is revising rather than learning the topic for the first time.

Then the calendar tightens. Internal Assessment deadlines in the Diploma Programme tend to stack in DP1's final term and DP2's first, often across three or four subjects within a few weeks. The Personal Project runs alongside ordinary coursework in MYP 5. Meanwhile school events, sports days and the long Diwali break interrupt whatever rhythm existed. A good home tutor front-loads content before the break and uses the weeks after it for past questions rather than new material.

One more calendar detail worth planning for: after May results arrive in early July, a family considering a retake route or an enquiry upon results has a short window to decide, and that decision is better made with the school's coordinator than with a tutor.
items: The Indian school year runs roughly April to March; most candidates sit the May session
Exam sessions run in May and November; May results are released in early July
July to September is the quiet term most families waste and should be using
Diploma Programme Internal Assessment deadlines stack across subjects within a few weeks
Front-load new content before Diwali; use the weeks afterwards for past questions

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which one suits your week in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition suits a student who needs supervision and a room that becomes serious for ninety minutes. Online suits a family chasing a specialist who is not in their city, or a week too fragmented for a fixed visit. Hybrid, meaning some sessions at home and some on screen, suits most DP households once the travel cost of a weekday evening becomes obvious. That is the honest ranking, and it depends far more on your address and your week than on the student.

There are evenings when a home visit is simply the wrong call. If the student's slot is 8.30 pm on a Wednesday and the tutor must cross from Andheri to Powai to get there, the lesson starts late, the tutor is tired and the family feels guilty about both. If your subject is one where the local pool is thin, insisting on a home tutor means choosing a weaker teacher over a stronger one for the sake of physical presence. And during heavy monsoon weeks in Mumbai or a long spell of Bengaluru evening traffic, online keeps continuity that a visit cannot.

Most IB home tutors in India will discuss a hybrid pattern openly, because they lose evenings to weather and traffic too. Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. A common pattern is one home visit at the weekend, unhurried, for the work that needs paper and a long stretch, and one shorter online session midweek for doubt-solving and checking that the homework was actually done. The tutor keeps the relationship built in person, and the family stops losing a session every time it rains.

The trade-off stated plainly: home gives you attention, supervision and a tutor who sees the written working; online gives you choice of tutor and reliability; hybrid keeps most of both, at the cost of two different routines the student has to get used to.
items: Home tuition: best for supervision, handwritten working and younger students
Online: best when the subject specialist you need lives in another city
Hybrid: a weekend home visit plus a short midweek online check-in
Switch to online during monsoon weeks rather than cancelling the session
A late weekday slot across a metro is usually a hybrid week waiting to happen

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a tutor enters your home?
contentBlocks.body:
Check identity at the door, check subject experience in the demo, and check that the person who arrives is the person whose profile you were shown. Those three take ten minutes and settle almost everything that goes wrong later. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified, but a platform check and a parent's own judgement are different things and you should use both.

Profile verification covers who the tutor says they are and what they say they have taught: identity documents, the qualifications claimed, the programmes and levels they have handled, and the subjects they are willing to be matched for. A tutor who says they teach Diploma Programme Chemistry is matched for Diploma Programme Chemistry, not for anything in the sciences that happens to be asked about.

What the platform cannot do is sit in your living room, so ask the same questions of every one of the IB home tutors in India you shortlist. So on the first visit, ask to see an identity document and note the name at the society gate register yourself. Ask which syllabus version the student is on and listen for whether the answer is specific. Ask how they would approach the topic the student is currently stuck on, and listen for a method rather than reassurance. A strong tutor will say what they do not teach.

For a younger child there is a further layer. The lesson should happen in a room with an open door and ordinary household traffic passing, not behind a closed bedroom door, and a parent or another adult should be at home. This is not a comment on any individual; it is simply the arrangement that protects everyone, including the tutor, and any professional will expect it.

Finally, be sceptical of anyone who promises an outcome. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a person who offers one at the door has told you something useful about their judgement.
items: Ask for an identity document on the first visit and log the name at the gate
Verified profiles cover identity, claimed qualifications, programmes and subjects taught
Ask how they would teach the exact topic the student is stuck on now
Keep young learners' home classes in an open-door room with an adult at home
Treat any promise of a specific grade as a warning sign, not a selling point

contentBlocks.heading: Inside a ninety-minute home session with an IB home tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
A home visit is a small logistical operation repeated every week, and the households where it works are the ones that set it up once and then stop thinking about it.

Start with the gate. Most gated societies and apartment complexes in India require a visitor entry, and the friction is real: a tutor standing at the boom barrier at 6.05 pm while the guard calls the flat is five minutes of the lesson gone, every single week. Register the tutor as a regular visitor if your society allows it, add them to the app your complex uses, and tell the guard the day and time. In older buildings without an app, a written note at the desk does the same job. Where parking is scarce, say so before the first visit rather than after.

Then the room. A dining table beats a bedroom desk in almost every Indian flat, because two people can sit side by side and spread papers out. Keep the television off and the younger sibling elsewhere, put the phone in another room rather than face down on the table, and make sure there is a plug point within reach for a laptop. Light matters more than families expect; a tutor reading a student's pencil working under a dim ceiling light will miss things.

A workable ninety minutes usually runs like this:
1. Ten minutes on last week's homework, marked in front of the student rather than collected.
2. Fifty minutes of new teaching or past questions, with the student writing and the tutor watching the writing.
3. Thirty minutes of independent work in the room, where the tutor only speaks when asked.

The tutor brings their own past questions, mark schemes and a spare pen. You provide the table, the light, the plug point and the water. Nobody needs to provide snacks, though most Indian households will anyway.
items: Register the tutor as a regular visitor so gate entry never eats lesson time
The dining table usually beats a bedroom desk: two people, papers spread out
Phone in another room, television off, younger siblings occupied elsewhere
A plug point within reach and good light over the page, not behind it
The tutor brings questions and mark schemes; you provide the space and water

contentBlocks.heading: What progress looks like, and what a home tutor cannot fix
contentBlocks.body:
Give any new arrangement four to six sessions before judging it, and judge it on specifics rather than mood. The first visit or two will look unimpressive because a competent tutor spends them finding out what the student actually knows, which is rarely what the report said.

By the third or fourth session you should be able to see concrete things. The student attempts questions they used to skip. Homework comes back with working shown rather than answers alone. In the Middle Years Programme, feedback starts referring to a criterion strand by name instead of a general grumble. In the Diploma Programme, a past question that used to take forty minutes takes twenty-five. None of these is a grade, and none of them should be. Grades move slowly and they move after the habits do.

Now the limits, honestly. A home tutor cannot fix attendance, sleep or a student who has decided the subject is not for them. They cannot compress two years of missed foundations into the weeks before a mock, though they can choose what to sacrifice and make that choice deliberate. They cannot write Internal Assessment or Extended Essay content, and a tutor who offers to is putting the student's diploma at risk rather than helping. And no tutor can guarantee a grade, whatever their examining background.

There is also a case for stopping. If the school's subject teacher has not been asked to help yet, ask them first; it is free and they know the class. If a student is being tutored in four subjects and still sleeping five hours, the answer is fewer tutors, not more. Families who start late, in the final term of DP2, should hear plainly that the plan is to protect what is reachable and give up on what is not.
items: Judge after four to six sessions, on working shown rather than on marks
Early signs: fewer skipped questions, faster past questions, criterion-specific feedback
A tutor cannot recover two years of gaps in the weeks before a mock
Internal Assessment and Extended Essay text must be the student's own work
Four subjects of tuition and five hours of sleep is a timetable problem, not a tutoring one

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in India: what to prepare this week
contentBlocks.body:
Getting a good match is mostly about what you send in the first message, and most parents send too little. Ten minutes of preparation saves a fortnight of back and forth.

Write down the student's grade and programme, the exact subjects and levels, and the two or three things that are actually going wrong. Not the grade. The behaviour behind the grade: leaves Paper questions half done, cannot start an essay, guesses at algebra, panics under time. Add the school's term dates and mock weeks if you have them, and the exam session the student is entered for. Then add the timetable constraints that are not negotiable, including the tuition-free evenings you want to keep.

Send the address area, not just the city. Sector 128 Noida, Kharadi, HSR Layout, Kokapet: a locality lets us search the right pool immediately instead of asking twice. Mention parking and gate rules now rather than on the evening of the first visit. If the family is open to hybrid, say so, because that opens the shortlist considerably.

For the first session, have last term's report, the most recent marked script or assessment, and the current textbook or unit plan on the table. A tutor who can read a marked script in the first ten minutes will plan a better term than one who works from a description of it.

After that, the sequence is simple. A shortlist, a demo or trial session at home, and a decision. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match; that is a normal request and not a difficult conversation. IB home tutors in India are booked earliest in the term, and availability depends on level, subject and the evening you need, so asking sooner gives you a better shortlist.
items: List subjects, levels and the behaviours going wrong, not just the grade
Send the locality, parking situation and society gate rules with the first query
Keep last term's report and one recent marked script ready for session one
Name the evenings that are not negotiable, including the ones kept free
Say if hybrid is acceptable; it widens the shortlist immediately
Ask early in the term, since availability depends on subject, level and slot

faqs.question: Will an IB home tutor travel to my part of the city on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the honest answer depends on the route rather than the distance. Tutors hold weekday evening slots well inside their own pool and badly across a metro, so a tutor living in Gurugram will cover Golf Course Road easily and think twice about Ghaziabad at 7 pm. Tell us your locality and the exact slot you need at the start. If nothing in that pool fits the subject, we will say so and suggest a hybrid week rather than a match that collapses in a month.

faqs.question: How far will a home tutor realistically travel in Bengaluru or Delhi NCR traffic?
faqs.answer: Think in evening minutes, not kilometres, because the same route behaves differently at 4 pm and 7 pm. In Bengaluru, a tutor based around Whitefield or Sarjapur Road will usually cover Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, while Yelahanka, Hebbal and Electronic City need someone local. In Delhi NCR, South Delhi, Gurugram, Noida and Faridabad behave as separate pools on a weekday. We never quote a travel time, because nobody can promise one. We do ask the tutor what they can hold every week without fail.

faqs.question: Where in the house should home classes actually happen?
faqs.answer: The dining table is the best room in most Indian flats, and it beats a bedroom desk for a simple reason: two people can sit side by side with papers spread between them. Keep the television off, move the phone to another room, and check that there is a plug point within reach and decent light falling on the page. For a younger child, an open-door room with ordinary household traffic passing is the right arrangement. A cramped corner desk will quietly limit what the tutor can do with working and diagrams.

faqs.question: How do we handle society gate entry and visitor passes?
faqs.answer: Set it up once, before the first session, and it stops costing you lesson time. Most gated societies in Mumbai, Gurugram, Hyderabad and Pune now use a visitor app or a gate register, so add the tutor as a regular visitor for a fixed day and time and tell the guard. In older buildings a standing note at the desk does the same job. Mention parking rules and any lift restrictions in your first message. Five minutes at the boom barrier every week adds up to a lost session over a term.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For a young child, yes, an adult should be at home, and for teenagers it is good practice rather than a requirement. Being at home is not the same as sitting in. Most sessions go better when the parent is somewhere in the flat, available, and not in the room correcting the student. A quick word at the door afterwards gives you more than hovering for ninety minutes. If nobody can be home for a particular week, move that session online instead of leaving the student alone with a visitor.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor bring, and what should the family provide?
faqs.answer: The tutor brings teaching material: past questions, mark schemes, their own notes, a spare pen, and usually a laptop or tablet. You provide the table, the chairs, the light, a plug point and drinking water. Keep the student's own textbook, notebook and the most recent marked script on the table before the tutor arrives, because ten minutes spent hunting for a script is ten minutes of teaching lost. Printing is worth sorting out early; some families print at home, others agree that the tutor brings printed papers.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor cannot reach us because of rain or traffic?
faqs.answer: The session should move online rather than disappear, and that expectation is worth agreeing in the first week. Mumbai monsoon evenings and long Bengaluru traffic spells will break a home visit sooner or later, and families who have already agreed a fallback lose nothing. Ask the tutor to message early rather than at the scheduled hour. For a missed session with proper notice, a reschedule within the same week is the normal arrangement, subject to what the tutor's other slots allow.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in India cost?
faqs.answer: Fees are set by level, subject, city and how far the tutor travels, and a home visit sits above an online session because travel time is part of the hour you are paying for. Higher Level Diploma Programme subjects cost more than Middle Years Programme support, and a scarce subject costs more than a common one. We will not publish a figure here, because any number would be wrong for most readers. Ask for the fee in writing before the trial, including what happens with missed sessions.

faqs.question: We live in Navi Mumbai, far from any IB school. Is a home visit still practical?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided you look for a tutor who already lives on your side rather than one who commutes to you. Families in Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar, Greater Noida and outer Pune often assume they must pull someone from the central pool, and that arrangement is the one most likely to fail by month two. The local pool may be smaller and shallower in rare subjects. Where it genuinely has nobody for your subject, an online specialist plus an occasional weekend home visit is the better plan.

faqs.question: Can we switch between home visits and online sessions during the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Diploma Programme families end up doing exactly that. A common pattern is a longer home visit at the weekend for work that needs paper and a steady stretch, and a shorter online session midweek for doubt-solving. Exam terms often shift the balance further towards online, because nobody wants to lose a revision slot to weather. Agree the pattern with the tutor rather than switching week by week, since an unpredictable format is harder on the student than either mode alone.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, and do it without feeling awkward about it. Say what specifically is not working: the student is not attempting homework, explanations go over their head, the slot keeps moving. That detail makes the next match better. Sometimes the fix is not a new tutor at all but a changed slot, a shorter session for a younger child, or fewer subjects. If the problem is that grades have not moved in four weeks, be aware that habits change first and marks follow later.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two children in the same home visit?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends far more on the gap between them than on the subject. Two Diploma Programme students taking the same subject and level can share a session productively. A Middle Years Programme child and a Diploma Programme sibling cannot, and attempting it shortchanges both. Back-to-back sessions in one visit work well, save the tutor a second trip, and are easier to staff than a shared slot. Tell us both children's programmes, subjects and levels at the start so the shortlist reflects the real request.
