h1: IB Home Tuition in India: How the Weekly Arrangement Works
heroTitle: The Weekly Shape of IB Home Tuition in India
heroSubtitle: Most families here do not need to be sold on tuition. They need to know what a week actually looks like: how many sessions, what happens between them, who keeps the plan, and when somebody tells you honestly that it is working or not. That is what this page sets out.
introSummary: IB home tuition in India usually runs as a fixed weekly arrangement: a verified tutor comes to your flat or house on agreed days, teaches one or two subjects, sets work for the gap between sessions, and reports back to you every few weeks against a written term plan. The number of sessions depends far more on the programme than on the subject. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child and a second-year Diploma Programme (DP) candidate are running on different clocks. Everything below is about that rhythm: what the plan should contain before the first session, how work between sessions is checked, what each review conversation should cover, and the point at which a parent's involvement starts to slow the student down.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a request for IB home tuition in India become a weekly timetable?
contentBlocks.body:
Four steps, and the tutor's name is the last of them. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, the programme, the subjects and levels, the school's calendar, your locality and the two or three slots your family can genuinely protect each week. A shortlist of verified profiles follows from those answers. That sequence is what makes IB home tuition in India a plan rather than an introduction.

Those questions are not a formality. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student who is home by half past three and a second-year DP candidate who gets back after a long bus ride are available at different hours, and the hour decides which tutors are reachable at all. Locality works the same way. A tutor living in Koramangala can hold a six o'clock slot in HSR Layout most weeks and will struggle to hold that same slot in Yelahanka. So the timetable is fixed first, and the shortlist is drawn to fit the timetable rather than the other way round.

Then the demo. A trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and the thing worth watching is not how warm the tutor is. It is how much the student talks. A tutor who lectures for forty minutes in a demo will lecture for forty minutes in June, when the student needs to be the one working.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match and say why in one line: too slow on the harder questions, too much talking, nothing set for the week. One specific line changes the next shortlist far more than a long complaint does. Availability at any particular hour depends on level, subject and schedule, so a Sunday morning slot in a dense pocket of South Delhi may take longer to fill than a Wednesday evening one in Dwarka.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation; give the programme, year and subjects
2. Answer the matching questions: board, level, school calendar, locality, workable slots
3. Read the shortlisted verified profiles and pick one or two to meet
4. Take a trial session and watch how much of it the student speaks
5. Agree the term plan, then fix the weekly slots in writing before session one

contentBlocks.heading: How many sessions a week does each IB programme need?
contentBlocks.body:
One short session a week is usually enough in the Primary Years Programme, one a week per subject through most of the Middle Years Programme, and two a week for a Higher Level subject once the second Diploma year starts. The stage sets the load, because the International Baccalaureate (IB) asks for very different amounts of work at each one.

Start with the Diploma Programme (DP). It runs two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL) and the rest at Standard Level (SL). The IB recommends 240 teaching hours for an HL subject and 150 for an SL subject. That gap is the whole argument for where tuition should go: a student taking HL Physics and SL Economics almost never needs equal support in both. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to three further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well, and it eats evenings that families forget to count.

The MYP is a different shape. Five years, eight subject groups, every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, with the total out of 32 converted to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A weekly session here is often aimed at one weak criterion rather than at the subject as a whole. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and both create short bursts where an extra session helps and a permanent extra session does not.

At PYP there are no examinations at all, and most children do not need a tutor. Where one helps, keep it short and keep it about reading, number sense or a language the child has fallen behind in.
items: PYP: one or two sessions a week, thirty to forty minutes, reading or number work
MYP 1 to 3: one session a week per subject, extra only around a project deadline
MYP 4 and 5: two a week in a subject where one criterion keeps scoring low
DP1: one a week per subject, rising as the first internal assessment drafts fall due
DP2: two a week for a Higher Level subject from the mock season to study leave
Any stage: cut the load in the last fortnight before papers, never raise it

contentBlocks.heading: What a term plan covers, subject by subject
contentBlocks.body:
A term plan is a one-page document the tutor writes before the first session and revises every few weeks. It should name the units the school is teaching this term, the dates of the school's own assessments, the criteria or papers being targeted, the command terms the student keeps getting wrong, and the point in the term when past papers replace teaching. If a tutor cannot write that page after reading the student's last report and one marked script, they have not read either properly.

Subjects differ in what belongs on the page. For IB Mathematics, the first line should say Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at which level, because the two courses reward different work: one rewards algebraic fluency and proof, the other rewards modelling and the interpretation of real data. For IB Physics and IB Chemistry, the plan should carry practical work and the internal assessment (IA) separately from the taught units, since those run on school deadlines rather than the tutor's. For IB Biology the risk is volume, so the plan should schedule revisiting, not only covering. For IB Economics, the commentaries need dates written in rather than a vague slot late in the term. For IB English A, the plan should name the texts and tasks the school has chosen, because no two schools pick the same set.

Command terms belong on every plan. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each demand a different depth of answer, and a student who writes a description where the paper asked for an evaluation loses marks on content they clearly knew. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and the subject reports are the most under-read document in the house: they say in plain language what examiners actually saw go wrong.
items: The units the school is covering this term, in the school's own order
School assessment and mock dates, written in before anything else
The two or three command terms the student keeps misreading
Internal assessment milestones with draft dates, not only the final deadline
The week teaching stops and timed past-paper work begins

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition timings across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Geography decides whether a weekly slot survives past October. In Delhi NCR a tutor can hold South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri in one evening run, but Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad each sit far enough out that a tutor usually commits to one of them per evening. Families looking for IB home tuition in Delhi from Gurugram (Gurgaon) often do better with someone already teaching along Golf Course Road, and a request from Sector 128 Noida is easier to fill on a weekday than on a Saturday, when the same tutor is booked across the river.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the constraint is the corridor rather than the distance. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are close on a map and expensive in evening traffic, so IB home tuition in Mumbai works best when a tutor teaches two families in one pocket on the same night. Powai is its own case and usually served from inside. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are the same story, and a tutor who lives in Thane is worth more to a Thane family than a better-known name in town who can only offer Sunday.

Bengaluru splits into belts. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City form one; Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar another; Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road sit apart again. IB home tuition in Bangalore fails most often when a family books across two belts and then wonders why the tutor is late from January onwards.

IB home tuition in Chennai is kinder. Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are workable in one run, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery are best served by somebody already on that side, and Anna Nagar is a separate trip. In Gujarat, IB home tuition in Ahmedabad concentrates around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar reachable at fixed hours only; Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot have thinner local supply, so online or hybrid is often the honest answer. The same holds for IB home tuition in Pune outside Koregaon Park, for IB home tuition in Hyderabad beyond Gachibowli, and for IB home tuition in Kolkata beyond the Salt Lake side.
items: Delhi NCR: one corridor per evening; Dwarka and Ghaziabad rarely share a tutor
Mumbai: two families in one pocket on the same night keeps a slot alive
Bengaluru: book inside your belt, not across Whitefield and Jayanagar
Chennai: OMR, Perungudi and Velachery are best served from that side
Gujarat: Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar work at fixed hours; Surat and Rajkot lean online

contentBlocks.heading: How the school year in India shapes a term plan
contentBlocks.body:
The school year in India runs roughly April to March, and IB schools here almost all enter candidates for the May examination session. November exists, but it is used by a small minority of schools and by retake candidates. Those two sentences set nearly every date on a term plan. May results are released in early July, which is why an enquiry that starts in July is a completely different conversation from one that starts in August.

Work backwards from May and the year takes a clear shape. DP1 should end with internal assessment work genuinely started rather than merely discussed. The first term of DP2 is the last comfortable period for teaching new content. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, and those mocks are the real deadline most families plan around, because predicted grades and university conversations follow from them. A home tutor who does not know your school's mock window is planning blind, so give them the date in week one.

Schools also run their own calendar of unit tests, project weeks, sports weeks and long holidays, and these rarely line up between two schools in the same city. Two students living in the same building in Powai can be six weeks apart in the same subject. Ask the tutor to copy the school's assessment calendar into the term plan at the start rather than reconstructing it in October from memory.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School and Stonehill International School come up in enquiries simply because families write in from them, and nothing about a tutor's suitability follows from a school's name.
items: April to March school year; May is the session almost every IB school here uses
November is used by a small minority of schools and by retake candidates
Mock dates are set by each school, usually several months before May
May results come out in early July, which reshapes the July enquiry
Copy the school's own assessment calendar into the plan in week one

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which rhythm holds through the year?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition wins on consistency and loses on flexibility. Online tuition is the reverse. Hybrid, meaning the same tutor teaching at your house on one fixed day and online on the other, holds up best across a full year in a large Indian city, because the home session protects the relationship and the online session survives rain, traffic and the tutor's own travel. Most families who ask about IB home tuition in India are really choosing between these three modes, not two.

Here is the trade-off stated plainly. A tutor at your house sees the desk, the phone, the sibling and the actual state of the student's file, and a session cannot quietly shrink into a half session. But that tutor is limited by how far they can travel on a weekday evening, which narrows your choice to whoever is nearby and free at your hour. Online removes the travel constraint completely, so a family in Rajkot or Greater Noida can work with a specialist sitting in another city, and it costs something real: attention is harder to police through a screen, and younger students in particular drift.

Hybrid is not a compromise for its own sake. It is a way of keeping a good tutor whose commute would otherwise end the arrangement by the monsoon, and of adding a short second session in a heavy week without asking anyone to cross a city twice. A lot of DP2 families end up here by February without ever having planned it.

One rule saves arguments later: decide the mode for each session before the term starts and write it into the plan. Switching to online whenever the evening looks difficult turns into online by default, and a home arrangement stops being one without anybody deciding that it should.
items: Home: fixed desk, visible files, no half sessions; limited by evening travel
Online: the widest choice of subject specialists; needs a quiet room and a charged device
Hybrid: one home day, one online day, written into the plan in advance
Younger students drift sooner on screen, so keep remote sessions with them short
Switching mode on the night, week after week, ends a home arrangement by accident

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor enters your home
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile reaches your shortlist, IB Gram verifies identity and the qualifications and teaching experience the tutor claims, then matches what they say they can teach against the board, programme, subject and level in your enquiry. Profiles that do not match are not sent to you. That is the platform's half of the work.

Your half starts at the trial session, and it matters more for home tuition than for any other format, because this person will be in your flat for months. Ask three questions. Which papers or criteria have they actually prepared students for, in this subject, at this level? What will the first four weeks cover, and how will you know at the end of them whether it worked? What do they expect the student to do between sessions? A tutor who answers the third question with whatever homework the school happens to give has not planned a term.

Then check the small things nobody thinks to check. Agree the arrival time and what counts as late. Agree who informs whom if a session has to move, and by when. Agree society or building gate entry once, at the start, so that it is not renegotiated weekly with a guard. Decide where the session will happen and hold that decision; the dining table with the television visible is not a study space, and no tutor will fix that for you.

Finally, be sceptical of anything that sounds like a promise. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and claims about scores or rankings deserve caution rather than trust. What a good tutor can offer is a plan, a record of what was taught, and an honest answer when you ask whether the student is closer than they were in August.
items: Identity, claimed qualifications and teaching experience are verified before a profile is shared
Profiles are matched to board, programme, subject and level before they reach you
Ask which papers or criteria the tutor has actually prepared students for
Agree arrival time, rescheduling rules and building gate entry in the first week
Fix one study space in the house and keep every session there

contentBlocks.heading: The weekly rhythm of IB home tuition in India
contentBlocks.body:
A good weekly session has a shape, and it is not revise chapter four. The first ten minutes belong to the work set last week, marked in front of the student rather than collected silently. The middle is new teaching or a hard question type, with the student writing and the tutor watching them write. The last ten minutes set the next piece of work and add one line to the record of what was covered. That last ten minutes is the part that gets cut when a session starts late, and it is the part that makes the following session work.

Spacing matters more than duration. Two hours on a Tuesday and a Friday do more than one long Sunday sitting, because the gap between them is where retrieval happens. If only one slot is possible, put it mid-week and let the work set between sessions carry the weekend.

That work should be small, specific and checkable: four questions of a named type, one past-paper question under timed conditions, a paragraph rewritten to an actual command term. Read the chapter cannot be checked and will not be done. Checking is the tutor's job rather than yours, and it should happen at the start of the next session in front of the student, so that skipping it carries a visible cost.

Which brings us to the parent's role, and to where it should stop. You set the conditions: a quiet space, a protected hour, a charged laptop, and no rescheduling for anything short of illness. You ask for the record every few weeks. You do not sit in the room from week three onwards, you do not answer for the student, and you do not ask the tutor to re-teach the school's lesson because the school's teacher is unpopular at home. Parents who stay in the room past the first fortnight almost always get a quieter student and a slower one. It is the commonest way a working arrangement in IB home tuition in India quietly goes wrong.
items: Ten minutes on last week's work, marked in front of the student
The middle of the session: the student writing, the tutor watching them write
Ten minutes at the end to set the next task and record what was covered
Two spaced hours beat one long Sunday sitting in almost every subject
Work set must be checkable: four questions, one timed answer, one rewritten paragraph
The parent sets the conditions, then leaves the room after the first fortnight

contentBlocks.heading: What should progress look like after six weeks?
contentBlocks.body:
After six weeks you should see a change in behaviour, not yet a change in grade. The student attempts the question type they used to skip. Work set is done without a reminder. The tutor can tell you, without looking anything up, which criterion or paper is still weak and what is being done about it. Grades move later, usually after the next school assessment. Six weeks is simply the first honest checkpoint in IB home tuition in India.

Be realistic about timescales. A student who has misunderstood a foundational topic for two years will not repair it in a month, and a tutor who says otherwise is selling. A DP2 student starting in January has a real but narrower set of options than one starting in April of DP1, and the right plan in January is triage: the paper sections carrying the most marks, the internal assessment that can still be improved, and the two or three topics that appear most often. Starting late is not hopeless. It is a different plan, and it should be described as one from the first conversation.

Review every four to six weeks, in a short call rather than a long meeting. A useful review has three voices in it and takes about fifteen minutes. If the only answer to what has changed is that he seems more confident, ask for the evidence: a marked question, a mock section, a criterion score that moved.

And know when to stop. Some students need fewer subjects tutored rather than more. Some need sleep and a calendar. If a tutor tells you your child does not need two sessions a week in a subject they are already managing, that is a tutor worth keeping.
items: 1. The student reports first: what felt easier this month and what still does not
2. The tutor reports next: criteria targeted, evidence of movement, what remains unfixed
3. The parent reports third: sessions actually held, work done at home, timing problems
4. Agree one change for the next cycle, put it in writing, and change nothing else

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in India: the first fortnight
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first session, put four things on the table: the last school report with the subject teacher's comments, any marked scripts from last term, the school's assessment calendar for this term, and the unit outlines or subject guides the school has shared. A tutor who sees marked work in week one writes a far better term plan than one who is told only that he is weak in Maths. The first fortnight of IB home tuition in India decides how the rest of the year runs.

Then set up the shelf. Home classes work better when the materials stop travelling. Keep one ring binder per subject with the unit outline at the front, past papers and markschemes printed rather than left on a phone, a squared notebook for working, and the internal assessment draft in a labelled folder that never goes into the school bag. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels; ask the tutor which two or three to print first instead of printing a decade of them.

The first session itself should not be teaching. It should be a diagnostic: a short set of questions across the topics covered so far, watched rather than marked later, so that the tutor can see where the student hesitates and how they set out their working. Expect to be told something you did not want to hear.

By the end of the second week you should have the term plan in writing, the weekly slots fixed, the study space agreed, and a first piece of work set and checked. If any of those four is still vague, raise it now. It does not get clearer in November.
items: Last report, marked scripts, the term's assessment calendar and the school's unit outlines
One ring binder per subject, kept at home, never carried in the school bag
Past papers and markschemes printed; ask the tutor which to print first
The first session is a diagnostic, not a teaching session
By day fourteen: plan written, slots fixed, space agreed, first work checked

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is normal for IB home tuition in India?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the common starting point, and two only where the evidence supports it. At PYP, one or two short sessions cover everything most children need. Through MYP 1 to 3 a single weekly hour per subject is usually enough, rising in MYP 4 and 5 if one criterion keeps scoring low. In DP1, one a week per subject works until internal assessment drafts arrive. In DP2, Higher Level subjects often move to two from the mock season. More than two a week in a single subject usually means the plan is wrong, not that the student needs more hours.

faqs.question: What should be in the term plan before the first home session?
faqs.answer: The plan should exist before session one and should fit on a single page. It names the units the school is covering this term, the school's own assessment and mock dates, the criteria or papers being targeted, the command terms the student misreads, the internal assessment milestones with draft dates, and the week when teaching stops and timed past-paper work begins. It should also say what work will be set between sessions and how it will be checked. If a tutor wants two sessions to get to know the student first, that is fair; if the page still does not exist in week three, ask why.

faqs.question: How is the work set between sessions actually checked?
faqs.answer: At the start of the next session, in front of the student, by the tutor. That is the only method that reliably changes behaviour. Work should be small enough to check properly: four questions of a named type, one timed past-paper answer, a paragraph rewritten to a command term. The tutor marks it there, says where the marks were lost, and sets the next piece from what they have just seen. Collecting a notebook and returning it a week later teaches almost nothing. Checking is not the parent's job; your job is to make sure an hour existed in which the work could be done.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor reach Powai or Whitefield on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes if the tutor already teaches in that belt, and usually no if they are crossing the city for a single student. Evening traffic between distant parts of Mumbai or Bengaluru can stretch a short trip badly, so a tutor who lives or already teaches near Powai, Whitefield or Sarjapur Road will hold a six or seven o'clock slot far more dependably through the year. Ask at the trial session where their other weekday sessions are. A slot that depends on an empty road will not survive the monsoon or the exam season.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to sit in during home tuition?
faqs.answer: For the first session or two, yes; after that it usually does more harm than good. Sitting in early lets you see how the tutor teaches and whether the student speaks at all. Beyond the first fortnight, a parent in the room tends to produce a quieter student who checks your face before answering, and a tutor who teaches towards you rather than towards the child. Stay within earshot if the student is young. Ask for the written record and the review call instead, because those tell you far more than an hour of watching does.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in week one, before it happens. A workable arrangement usually says that a session cancelled with a day's notice is rescheduled within the same week if a slot exists, and one cancelled an hour before is not. Illness on either side is the obvious exception. Put the reschedule window into the term plan, because the weeks when sessions get missed are exam weeks, project weeks and festival weeks, which are exactly the weeks a student can least afford to lose. Repeated cancellation from either side is a reason to review the match.

faqs.question: What actually moves IB home tuition fees up or down?
faqs.answer: Level, subject scarcity, travel and session length, in roughly that order. A Higher Level subject takes more preparation than a Standard Level one, so it costs more to teach. Scarce subjects cost more than common ones. A tutor crossing a city on a weekday evening is pricing that travel in, which is why an equally good tutor in your own locality often works out lower. Longer or twice-weekly sessions change the total rather than the rate. No amounts are published here; ask for the structure in writing before starting, and ask what would change it mid-year.

faqs.question: We are in Ahmedabad and cannot find a subject tutor locally. What then?
faqs.answer: Take the online tutor for the scarce subject and keep the home slot for the one where local supply is good. This is the normal answer across Gujarat. Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway have reasonable coverage for mainstream subjects, while Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and much of Gandhinagar do not, particularly at Higher Level. A hybrid arrangement is often the practical shape: one subject taught at home by somebody nearby, another taught online by a specialist in another city. Waiting several months for a local specialist who may not exist costs the student more than the screen does.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence before changing anything. A month is short, and behaviour shifts before grades do, so the first question is whether the work set is being done and checked. Ask the tutor which criterion or paper section was targeted, what the student produced, and what is still wrong. If the answer is vague, or if the sessions have quietly become homework supervision, that is a planning problem and one conversation can fix it. If the answer is clear and nothing has moved in eight to ten weeks, ask for a different match and say precisely what did not work.

faqs.question: Is searching for IB home tuition near me the right way to start?
faqs.answer: It is the right instinct for a weekly home arrangement and the wrong filter for a scarce subject. Nearby matters, because a tutor who travels ten minutes holds the slot and one who travels an hour eventually does not. But at Higher Level, and in subjects few people teach, the nearest tutor may not teach your actual course. Start with the course and the level, then sort by distance, and use online for the subject where both cannot be satisfied at once. In Delhi NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the local answer is usually available; elsewhere it often is not.

faqs.question: How should past papers and materials be kept at home?
faqs.answer: One binder per subject, kept at home, is enough. Put the unit outline at the front, printed past papers and markschemes behind it, and keep a separate labelled folder for internal assessment drafts so they never travel in the school bag. Printed papers get annotated; papers on a phone get scrolled past. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, so ask the tutor which two or three to print first rather than printing everything available. The subject reports are worth reading yourself at least once a year.

comparison.heading: Which format holds a weekly IB rhythm best across India?
comparison.intro: Four formats, one question: which of them still runs in the same slot in February? Use this as a checklist rather than a verdict. A batch is genuinely cheaper per hour and suits a confident student who only needs pace. A small online group gives peer discussion that one-to-one cannot. One-to-one at home buys attention and visibility. One-to-one online buys reach and reliability.

h1: IB Private Tutors in India for One-to-One Subject Teaching
heroTitle: One Student, One Plan, Across India
heroSubtitle: A tutor teaching one student cannot hide behind a batch average. The first fortnight is diagnosis: which topics are genuinely missing, which are known but unusable under exam conditions, and which are simply unpractised. Everything after that is a plan built for a single learner, at home or online.
introSummary: IB private tutors in India teach one student at a time, usually as home tuition in the family's own flat or house, and the real value of that is diagnosis before instruction. A batch has to move at the speed of its syllabus. A private tutor has to move at the speed of one learner, which means the first two sessions are spent finding out what is actually wrong rather than starting at Chapter 1. Sometimes the answer is a content gap. More often it is a student who knows the physics but cannot structure a Paper 2 extended response, or who has never been shown how a criterion is marked. This page explains what one-to-one buys, how to test whether you are getting it, and when a group class is the better spend.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Find IB Private Tutors in India Who Actually Fit?
contentBlocks.body:
You describe the student rather than the subject, and you keep the first commitment small. IB Gram asks which board and programme the student is on, the level in each subject, what the school calendar looks like this term, where you live and which evenings are genuinely free. Matching profiles are shortlisted, a demo or trial session comes before you commit, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match.

The part families skip is the calendar. A Diploma Programme (DP) student in October of DP1 is in a completely different position from one in October of DP2, and a tutor who never asks will teach the same sequence to both. So say when the mocks fall. Say when the Internal Assessment (IA) draft is due with the subject teacher. Say whether the school enters candidates for the May session, as schools in India overwhelmingly do, or for November.

Location matters more than parents expect for one-to-one at home. A tutor twenty minutes away will hold a weekday evening slot for two years. A tutor from the other side of the city will start cancelling once the rains set in, and those cancellations tend to land in exactly the weeks you needed the sessions most. The shortlist is therefore built from people who can realistically arrive on a Tuesday at half past six. Where nobody nearby teaches the subject at the level you need, the honest answer is an online tutor rather than a weaker local one.

Availability stays conditional throughout. It depends on the subject, the level, the slot and the season, and the fortnight after May results are released in early July is the hardest window of the year in which to secure anyone good. Ask earlier than feels necessary. If the student is entering DP1 in a few months, the conversation belongs in the spring, not in September when the first unit test has already gone badly.
items: 1. Send your query: board, programme, subject, level and your locality.
2. A short call covers report comments, mock dates and target areas.
3. You receive a shortlist of verified profiles matched to those needs.
4. Book a demo session and watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures.
5. Confirm slots, or ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: One-to-One Teaching Across PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
One-to-one means something different in each of the three International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes, and a tutor who treats them the same is worth avoiding. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) there is no external examination to aim at, so a private teacher is working on reading fluency, number sense and the confidence to ask a question out loud. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) the target is criterion performance. In the Diploma Programme the target is points.

The MYP runs five years, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8, and the total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. That structure is what makes one-to-one useful here. A student can be strong on knowing and understanding and weak on investigating, and a batch report will never separate the two. A private tutor can look at four criterion scores, see which one is dragging the conversion down, and spend six weeks on that alone. The Community Project arrives in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, with on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so there is no single national MYP examination in India.

The DP is two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four sit at Higher Level (HL), with 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level (SL), with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. A personal IB tutor in India working with a DP student is usually working inside that arithmetic rather than outside it.
items: PYP: no external exam, so progress is read from work and confidence, not marks
MYP: four criteria per subject, each 0-8, totalling 32 before boundaries apply
MYP 3 or 4 carries the Community Project; MYP 5 carries the Personal Project
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL with 240 recommended hours each
DP core: TOK and the EE add up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45
An IB private tutor for HL work should say which of the extra hours they cover

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth a Single Student Can Reach in One Hour
contentBlocks.body:
The argument for one-to-one is strongest in subjects where the marks are lost in a specific, identifiable place. Take the DP sciences under the structure first assessed in 2025. Paper 1 has two parts: 1A is multiple choice and 1B is data-based. Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. A batch teaching Physics will cover the content of both papers. It will rarely stop for forty minutes on one student's habit of writing a correct physical explanation in the wrong order, which is where the marks actually go.

The scientific investigation is the sharper case. It is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, with a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. A one-to-one IB tutor can read a draft against those four criteria and say, plainly, that the data analysis is fine and the evaluation is doing nothing at all. In a room of fifteen, nobody's individual evaluation gets that hour. HL and SL share the assessment structure, with HL adding Additional Higher Level (AHL) content on top.

Mathematics splits the same way. Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) reward different instincts, and a student steered into AA HL because it sounded safer will show it within the first term. Private teaching can test that quickly, because the tutor can simply hand over questions from both routes and watch. In Economics and English A the bottleneck is usually writing under time pressure rather than understanding. The only reliable fix is a tutor marking this student's own script in front of them, line by line, then asking for the same question again a week later to see whether anything held.
items: Physics, Chemistry and Biology: Paper 1A multiple choice, 1B data-based, Paper 2 extended
Scientific investigation: 20 per cent, four criteria of 6 marks, 3,000 words maximum
Group work of up to three is allowed, but every report is written individually
Mathematics AA against AI: test the fit early rather than after the first term
Economics and English A: timed writing marked against the actual criteria, then repeated

contentBlocks.heading: Where Private Home Tuition Is Practical Across India
contentBlocks.body:
IB private tutors in India are matched by IB Gram across five regions in detail, and the practical answer differs in each. In Delhi NCR, a family in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri usually has depth of supply within a short radius, while Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad thin out quickly for HL specialists. Gurugram along Golf Course Road and Noida around Sector 128 sit in between. An IB private tutor in Delhi will often take the metro rather than drive, which changes which evening slots are realistic for home classes.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the constraint is the geography itself. A tutor living in Andheri or Juhu can reach Bandra, Worli or Lower Parel on a good evening and cannot reliably reach Thane or Kharghar on any evening. Powai and Malabar Hill are their own islands in practice. Navi Mumbai and Vashi are best served by a tutor who already lives there, and where one is not available at the right level, an IB private tutor in Mumbai teaching online is a better outcome than a long cross-city commute that collapses by October.

Bengaluru is the clearest case for hybrid. An IB private tutor in Bangalore living near Indiranagar or Koramangala can hold HSR Layout and Jayanagar comfortably, but Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road each behave like separate cities on a weekday. Hyderabad is easier: Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District and Kokapet cluster tightly, though Secunderabad sits apart from that cluster. Pune runs along two axes, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar on one side, Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi on the other, and crossing between them in the evening is what breaks schedules. An IB private tutor in Chennai, in Kolkata or in Ahmedabad is found the same way, with online filling the gaps local supply leaves. Never accept an estimate of travel time from anyone. Ask instead which evening slots the tutor has actually kept for a year.
items: Delhi NCR: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri are dense; Ghaziabad is not
Mumbai: Bandra, Juhu, Worli and Powai are reachable; Thane and Kharghar rarely are
Bengaluru: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City behave as separate cities
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills and Kokapet cluster within a short radius
Pune: crossing between Kharadi and Hinjewadi on a weekday evening breaks schedules
Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad: online fills what local one-to-one supply cannot

contentBlocks.heading: The International School Year in India and Where One-to-One Lands
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore are named only because families searching for private tuition are often at schools of this kind.

The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and schools here overwhelmingly enter DP candidates for the May examination session, with results released in early July. That single fact shapes the whole tuition calendar. The stretch families underestimate runs from late October to February of DP2: mock examinations, IA final submissions and Extended Essay deadlines arrive close together, and a student who is behind in one subject in November will be behind in three by January, because everything competes for the same weekday evenings.

Expectations at international schools in India add their own pressure. Coursework is continuous rather than concentrated at the end, so there is no quiet term in which to catch up. Parents' evenings produce criterion comments rather than percentages, and those comments are far more useful than they look. A private tutor should read them before the first session. A comment saying a student describes rather than analyses is a teaching instruction, not a pleasantry.

One warning about integrity, because it comes up every year. Schools are clear that the IA, the EE and MYP projects must be the student's own work, and a tutor who offers to write, redraft or substantially rewrite them is putting the student's candidature at risk. What a tutor may legitimately do is teach the skill, discuss the criteria, ask hard questions about a draft the student has already written, and stop there. Any tutor who is vague about that boundary should be declined, however impressive the subject knowledge sounds.
items: Indian academic year roughly April to March; May session, results in early July
Late October to February in DP2 stacks mocks, IA submissions and EE deadlines
Criterion comments on a report are teaching instructions, not polite remarks
Continuous coursework means there is no quiet term in which to catch up
A tutor who offers to write an IA or EE should be declined immediately

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: Which Carries One-to-One Best?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition carries one-to-one best when the problem is attention, habit or a young student, and online carries it best when the problem is finding someone who genuinely knows the subject at the level required. Hybrid, which usually means home sessions at the weekend and online sessions midweek, is what most DP families in the metros settle into after a term of trying one or the other.

Home classes have advantages that are easy to underestimate. The tutor sees the desk, the light, the phone lying face up, the younger sibling in the next room. They can pick up the student's own notebook and read the handwriting, which is how you find out that the working is missing rather than wrong. A student who talks freely at a dining table often says nothing on a video call. Against that, a home tutor is limited to whoever lives within reach, and for HL Chemistry or HL Economics in a smaller city that pool may be close to empty.

Online removes the geography entirely. A student in Kochi, Indore or Guwahati can work with a specialist based in Bengaluru or Mumbai, and a shared screen with a past paper open and annotated live is genuinely good teaching once the student is old enough to hold attention for an hour. It is weaker for younger learners, weaker when the house is noisy, and dependent on a connection that is stable at seven in the evening rather than at eleven in the morning.

Hybrid is the honest compromise, and it is how a good many IB private tutors in India now work. The tutor visits for the session that needs presence, usually the long weekend one where written work is marked together, and runs the shorter midweek check online. Families in Bengaluru and Pune reach this arrangement quickly, because the weekday crossing is the problem rather than the teaching. Decide it on evidence: try home classes for three weeks, try online for three, and keep whichever produced work you can actually see.
items: Home tuition: the tutor reads the notebook, the desk and the distractions directly
Online: reaches HL and rarer subject specialists who do not live in your city
Hybrid: a weekend home session for marking, a short midweek online check
Younger students usually need home classes; DP2 students often prefer online
Test both for three weeks each rather than deciding from the first impression

contentBlocks.heading: What Is Checked Before a Private Tutor Reaches Your Home?
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile is shortlisted, IB Gram verifies identity and the qualifications and teaching experience the tutor claims, and confirms which programmes, subjects and levels they have actually taught. That is the platform's side of the work. Your side matters just as much, because the checks that protect a family during a home visit are the ones the family makes itself in the first fortnight.

Start with the claims a profile makes. There is a real difference between a person who has taught the DP inside a school, a person who has attended IB professional development workshops, and a person who has tutored DP students privately for years. All three can be excellent. They are not the same thing, and a profile should be readable enough for you to tell which one you are looking at. If a tutor says they have marked or examined, ask which component and in which years, and listen for whether the answer is specific or hedged.

Then watch the demo with a checklist rather than a feeling. Does the tutor ask to see the student's last marked script before teaching anything? Do they name the criterion or the paper they are working towards? Do they stop and make the student attempt something in front of them, or do they talk for fifty minutes? A tutor who lectures well in a demo will lecture well for the whole year, and a lecture is precisely the thing you are paying not to receive.

For home visits, set the ordinary rules and do not apologise for them. Lessons happen in a common area rather than a bedroom, with the door open. Someone is at home. Gate entry and society access are arranged in advance so that a tutor is not stuck at the boundary for fifteen minutes of a sixty-minute session, which happens constantly in gated developments in Gurugram, Noida and Kharadi. Cancellations are communicated by a fixed time. None of this implies distrust. It is what any working arrangement inside a family's own house requires.
items: Identity, claimed qualifications and teaching experience are verified before shortlisting
Ask which component a tutor has marked, and in which examination years
In the demo, watch whether the tutor asks for the last marked script first
Home classes happen in a common area, door open, with an adult in the house
Agree gate and society entry in advance so access does not eat the session

contentBlocks.heading: What One-to-One Actually Buys, Measured Against a Batch
contentBlocks.body:
One-to-one buys diagnosis, and everything else follows from it. That is the single thing IB private tutors in India are hired for, whatever the subject on the invoice. A batch tutor has to teach the topic the schedule says is due this week. A private tutor can spend the first two sessions doing almost no teaching at all, working out which of four very different problems the student actually has: missing content, content known but not retrievable under time pressure, technique that was never taught, or a student who understands the subject perfectly well and is losing marks to how the answer is written.

Here is a worked case. A DP1 student is scoring in the low fours in Chemistry. The school report says she needs to revise more. A batch would re-teach the unit. In session one a private tutor asks her to attempt two past questions cold and sees that the multiple-choice work in the style of Paper 1A is fine, that the data-based questions in 1B are mostly right, and that the extended responses in Paper 2 lose marks by answering roughly three-quarters of what was asked. In session two the tutor checks whether this is a reading problem or a structure problem by giving her the same questions with the command terms underlined. The score jumps. So the plan is not more revision. The plan is eight weeks of command-term work, ten minutes at the start of every session, with one timed Paper 2 question every fortnight.

That is what a one-student plan looks like, and it is visibly different from a batch syllabus, which must cover the whole course because fifteen students need fifteen different things. The other difference is pace. In a batch, pace is set by the median student. One-to-one, pace is set by the learner, which sometimes means moving much faster through a unit the student already holds and spending a month on the one that is broken.

So how do you tell real personalisation from a tutor who is simply going slower? Ask what the next six weeks contain and why. A personalising tutor names a specific weakness, a specific measure and a date. A slow tutor describes the syllabus.
items: Session one: attempt work cold, untaught, so the diagnosis is honest
Session two: test one hypothesis about the weakness and discard it if wrong
A real plan names a weakness, a measure of improvement and a review date
Going slower is not personalisation; skipping what is already secure is
Ask monthly what the tutor has stopped doing, not only what they have added

contentBlocks.heading: When Is One-to-One the Wrong Spend for a Family in India?
contentBlocks.body:
One-to-one is the wrong spend more often than a tutoring platform is supposed to admit. If a student understands the subject, attends school regularly and simply has not practised enough past papers, a private tutor is an expensive way to enforce a habit that a parent, a study timetable and a quiet room can enforce for nothing. A small revision batch in the weeks before mocks does that job well and adds peer comparison, which is genuinely motivating for some students and worth paying for on its own.

It is also the wrong spend when the problem is spread across five subjects. That is rarely five subject problems. It is usually sleep, organisation, or something happening outside school, and adding five one-to-one slots to an already full week makes it worse rather than better. Speak to the school coordinator before hiring anyone. One honest conversation there has saved families a great deal of unnecessary tuition, and it costs nothing.

What should progress look like when tuition is the right call? Within two to three weeks you should be able to see the tutor's diagnosis written down. Within six weeks, a measurable change in the thing that was named, which might be a mark on a timed question rather than a subject grade. Subject grades move slowly and should not be expected to move in a month. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim about a specific score or a percentage improvement deserves real scepticism.

Some honest limits. Starting in February of DP2 narrows what is possible to exam technique and triage across a small number of topics, which is worth doing but is not the same as fixing two years. A student who does not want tuition will absorb very little of it, however good the teaching is. And a tutor who is excellent for one child may be wrong for their sibling. If the fit is wrong after a fair trial, ask for a different match early rather than waiting out the term.
items: Practice, not teaching, is missing: a revision batch may do the job for less
Problems in five subjects at once usually point outside the subjects themselves
Speak to the school coordinator before hiring anyone; it is free and often decisive
Expect a written diagnosis in three weeks and a measurable change in six
Subject grades move slowly; a mark on a timed question moves first
If the fit is wrong after a fair trial, request a different tutor early

contentBlocks.heading: Starting With an IB Private Tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first session, gather four things: the most recent school report with its criterion comments, the last two marked scripts or tests in the subject, the school calendar showing mock dates and IA deadlines, and an honest note of which evenings are free once school transport and activities are accounted for. That packet turns a vague first meeting into a working one, and a good tutor will ask for all four anyway.

The first session should feel uncomfortable in a productive way. The student will be asked to attempt things without being taught them first, because a tutor cannot diagnose from a conversation. Expect roughly two-thirds of the hour to be the student working and being questioned, and one-third to be teaching. If it runs the other way round, say so after the session rather than after the term.

By the end of the first fortnight you should have, in writing, what the tutor believes the problem is, what they intend to do about it, how they will know whether it worked and when you will review it together. Ask for it plainly. A tutor who can produce that in five sentences is doing one-to-one properly. A tutor who cannot is teaching a batch of one.

Send a query or book a free consultation to begin the search for IB private tutors in India. IB Gram will ask about board, programme, subject, level, your locality and your schedule, then shortlist verified profiles that fit those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything, lessons can run at home, online or hybrid, and a different match can be requested at any point if the fit is wrong. Slots depend on the subject, the level and the time of year, so the earlier in the term you ask, the more choice you will have.
items: Bring the last report, two marked scripts, the calendar and your free evenings
Expect the first session to be mostly the student working, not the tutor talking
Ask for a written diagnosis and review date by the end of the first fortnight
Choose home, online or hybrid after trying both, not before
Book a demo before committing; ask for a different match if the fit is wrong

faqs.question: What does a private IB tutor actually do in the first two sessions?
faqs.answer: Mostly diagnosis, not teaching. The tutor asks the student to attempt work cold, without input, so that the weakness is visible rather than reported. They read the last marked scripts and the criterion comments on the school report, then test one hypothesis: is this a content gap, a retrieval problem under time pressure, a technique that was never taught, or an answer-writing problem? By the end of session two you should be told which of those it is, in a sentence you could repeat to the school coordinator without translating it.

faqs.question: How is a one-to-one plan different from what a coaching batch teaches?
faqs.answer: A batch has to cover the whole syllabus because fifteen students need fifteen different things, so its plan is the course itself. A one-student plan starts from a named weakness and deliberately leaves out what the student already holds. If a DP student is secure on mechanics and losing marks on extended response structure, the plan is eight weeks of structure work with timed questions, not a march through the textbook. Ask any tutor what they intend to skip. The answer tells you whether the plan is real.

faqs.question: Will a private tutor come to our home in the evening on weekdays?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, subject to tutor availability and to where you live. Weekday evening slots between roughly six and eight are the most requested hours of the week in every Indian metro, so they are booked first and held by tutors who live close by. A tutor crossing Bengaluru from Indiranagar to Whitefield, or Pune from Kharadi to Hinjewadi, may manage it in September and struggle by July. Ask any home tutor how long they have held their current weekday slots.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home while home classes are running?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth being straightforward about it. Home tuition should run in a common area such as a dining or living room with the door open, and an adult should be in the house. This is standard practice rather than a comment on any individual tutor. It also helps the teaching, because a parent nearby hears what is being worked on and can see whether the session is the student working or the tutor talking. Arrange society and gate entry in advance too.

faqs.question: How much do IB private tutors in India charge?
faqs.answer: Fees are not published here because they vary with programme, level, subject scarcity, city and whether the tutor travels to you. What you can control is the structure of the arrangement. One-to-one at home is the most expensive format per hour, because a tutor's whole evening is committed to one student. Online one-to-one is usually lower, since nobody is paying for travel time. A small group is shared between families. Ask for the fee structure in writing before the trial, including cancellations.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one worth it if my child is already scoring reasonably?
faqs.answer: Often not, and that is worth hearing from a tutoring platform. A student who understands the material and simply needs more past-paper practice does not need a private tutor to supervise that. A revision batch in the weeks before mocks, or a structured timetable at home, does the same job for less. One-to-one earns its cost when there is something specific and identifiable to fix, or when a Higher Level subject has genuinely outpaced the student and nobody at home can help.

faqs.question: How do I tell real personalisation from a tutor simply going slower?
faqs.answer: Ask what the next six weeks contain and why. A personalising tutor names a weakness, a measure and a date: extended response structure, one timed question a fortnight, reviewed in mid-November. A tutor going slower describes the syllabus and says they will cover it thoroughly. Another test is what they skip. Personalisation always involves leaving out material the student already holds. If nothing is ever skipped, you are paying one-to-one rates for a batch delivered to one person.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor help with the Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: They can teach the skills and discuss a draft the student has written, and they must not write or substantially rewrite any of it. That boundary is not negotiable, because the IA and the Extended Essay have to be the student's own work. A legitimate session looks like reading the student's draft against the published criteria, asking why a conclusion follows from the data, and pointing at the evaluation criterion that is scoring nothing. If a tutor offers to do more than that, decline the match.

faqs.question: We live in Navi Mumbai and nobody local teaches HL Economics. What now?
faqs.answer: Take the online specialist over the weaker local match. This is common in Vashi, Kharghar and Thane, and equally common in Greater Noida, Electronic City and parts of Secunderabad, where general tutors are available and Higher Level subject specialists are not. A student working with someone who genuinely knows the assessment will progress faster on screen than with a nearby tutor learning the course alongside them. Hybrid is the middle path: one session a week at home and one online with the specialist.

faqs.question: What if there is no progress after a month of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Raise it immediately rather than waiting for the term to end. First check what was actually promised: subject grades rarely move in four weeks, but the specific measure the tutor named should have moved. If the tutor never named one, that is itself the problem. Ask for the written diagnosis and the plan, and if neither exists, request a different match. IB Gram can arrange another tutor, and a second demo costs you an evening rather than a whole term.

faqs.question: Is online one-to-one as good as a tutor sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: For a DP or upper MYP student, usually yes, and sometimes better, because the choice of tutor is far wider. A past paper shared on screen and annotated live is genuinely strong teaching. For younger students, and for anyone who drifts the moment nobody is watching, home classes work better. The deciding factors are age, self-regulation and how quiet the house is at seven in the evening. Try three weeks of each before settling, and keep the format that produced visible written work.

comparison.heading: How Does One-to-One Compare With Group Formats in India?
comparison.intro: One-to-one at home suits a student whose problem is specific and whose attention wanders in a room of fifteen. One-to-one online suits a family that needs a subject specialist their own city cannot supply. A small online group suits a student who works better with someone to argue against. A large batch suits disciplined revision at the lowest cost per hour. The trade-off is attention against price and peer pressure.
