h1: IB Private Tuition in India Across a Full Academic Year
heroTitle: Private IB Tuition Held Steady Across India
heroSubtitle: Most families do not need one lesson. They need a tutor who is still there in February, who remembers what went wrong in August, and who plans around mocks and the long summer break. This page is about holding that arrangement together across an Indian school year.
introSummary: IB private tuition in India works best as a year-long arrangement rather than a string of separate lessons, and for most families that means one verified home tutor holding a fixed weekly slot from the start of the school year to the final papers. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) is a two-year course, so a DP1 student who starts tuition in July is signing up for something closer to twenty months than twenty hours. That changes what you should ask for: a written scope, a term-by-term review, a plan for the long summer and Diwali breaks, and an agreed way to change tutor without losing the thread. This page covers all of it, including when to stop.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram set up a year-long home tuition arrangement in India?
contentBlocks.body:
IB private tuition in India begins with a query or a free consultation, and the first conversation is about the year rather than the week. IB Gram asks which board and programme the student is in, which subjects and levels, when the school's mocks fall, where you live, and which evenings are actually free. A shortlist of verified profiles follows, then a demo or trial session before anything longer is agreed.

That order matters for a long arrangement. A tutor who suits a two-week crisis is not always the home tutor you want in December, when the same person has to remember that a Paper 2 essay structure was fixed in September and has quietly slipped again. So the matching conversation asks about the calendar first. A DP1 student beginning in July has two years ahead of them. A student switching boards in the middle of a term has something quite different to solve, and the shortlist should look different too.

Location shapes availability more than families expect. A weekday evening slot in Powai is a different proposition from the same slot in Dwarka, and a tutor crossing a large city twice a week in the rain will eventually ask to move the time. Say where you are, say which evenings are already taken by football or music class, and let the shortlist be built around the schedule you can hold in February as well as in July.

If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match. That is not a failure of the process. It is the reason a trial exists, and for a family committing to most of an academic year it is the single most useful thing a matching platform offers.
items: 1. Send a query with board, subjects, levels and the school's exam calendar
2. Talk through locality, weekday evenings and the year's fixed commitments
3. Review a shortlist of verified profiles matched to that schedule
4. Run a demo or trial session before agreeing anything longer
5. Agree scope, review dates and notice in writing, then start the weekly slot

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: what a year of private tuition covers at each stage
contentBlocks.body:
Private tuition looks different in each programme, and the year is shaped by different pressures. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) there are no external examinations at all, so a year of tuition is measured in reading fluency, number sense and the habit of sitting down to work without being asked twice. Progress reviews here are conversations, not marks, and a tutor who talks about syllabus coverage for a PYP child has misunderstood the programme.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. A parent used to percentage marks will misread this the first time, and often the second. A year of tuition in MYP 4 is usually aimed at one or two weak criteria rather than at the whole subject. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and both eat into the same terms. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, which combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it, so ask yours before planning a year around it.

The DP is the reason most families here sign a long arrangement. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level (SL) with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points, the maximum is 45, and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed alongside all of it.

So a DP arrangement is planned backwards from May, and a PYP one is planned in terms of habits. Do not let anyone sell you the same plan for both.
items: PYP: no external exams, so review reading, number sense and work habits instead
MYP: four criteria per subject, each 0 to 8, a total of 32 converted to 1 to 7
The MYP 5 Personal Project and MYP 3 or 4 Community Project compete for the same terms
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL with 240 hours, the rest SL at 150 hours
TOK and the EE add up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45, with 24 the diploma minimum

contentBlocks.heading: How many subjects can one IB student sustain at once?
contentBlocks.body:
Two is usually the honest answer, and three is the practical ceiling for most students. Past that point tuition starts eating the evenings a student needs for their own work, and the extra hour buys less than sleep would. Families who arrive asking for five subjects are almost always describing a workload problem rather than a subject problem, and adding tutors makes a workload problem worse.

Work out where the marks actually sit before choosing. In Mathematics, the Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) routes reward different things, and a student struggling with AA HL algebra needs different weekly work from one who cannot get an exploration started. In IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology the internal assessment (IA) is one piece of work that runs hard for several weeks and then stops, so tuition around it should be intense and short rather than permanent. IB Economics students routinely underprepare the commentary portfolio and then panic in DP2. IB English A rarely needs weekly tuition across two years; it needs concentrated work before Paper 1 and around the Individual Oral.

That is the argument for staggering rather than stacking. Take Mathematics weekly through DP1 because it compounds and nothing else does quite the same way. Add Chemistry for the eight weeks around the scientific investigation. Bring English A in for a block before mocks and let it go again afterwards. A family running that pattern uses fewer total hours across the year than one that books three subjects every week from July and never revisits the decision.

One more test, and it is a good one. If your child cannot say what they want out of a session before the tutor arrives, that subject is probably not the one to add. Ask them directly. The answer is usually blunt and usually right.
items: Two subjects weekly is sustainable for most students; three is the practical ceiling
Stagger by need: Mathematics AA or AI weekly, sciences in blocks around the IA
Economics commentaries and English A papers reward short concentrated blocks
Count the student's own study hours before adding a subject, not afterwards
Review the subject list every term and drop whatever has done its work

contentBlocks.heading: Holding a weekly slot across India: NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, the north and the east
contentBlocks.body:
A year-long slot survives or fails on geography. In Delhi NCR a tutor living in South Delhi can hold a Tuesday evening in Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri without much trouble, and will think twice about the same slot in Greater Noida or Faridabad once the December fog starts. Families searching for IB private tuition in Delhi usually widen to Dwarka, Sector 128 Noida and Ghaziabad, and find the choice improves sharply once they do.

Mumbai splits by corridor rather than by distance. IB private tuition in Mumbai clusters around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, while Powai holds a pool of its own. Across the creek, families in Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar generally do better with a tutor from their own side than with a stronger one from the island city, because a monsoon evening cancels the second and not the first.

Bengaluru is the clearest case for a hybrid week. IB private tuition in Bangalore is straightforward to arrange in Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar, and harder in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City, Hebbal, Yelahanka and along Kanakapura Road, where evening traffic between the tech corridors and the older suburbs can stretch a short trip into an unusable one. One home session a week and the rest online is the pattern many Bengaluru families settle into by term two.

Elsewhere the pool thins and the year needs planning further ahead. In Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, one good local tutor may be the only local tutor, so agree cover early. Kolkata families in Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, and families in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna, often run one subject at home and everything else online. IB private tuition in Kolkata, IB private tuition in Hyderabad around Gachibowli, IB private tuition in Chennai, IB private tuition in Pune and IB private tuition in Ahmedabad all follow the same rule: choose for the twelfth month, not the first.
items: Delhi NCR: a South Delhi tutor holds Vasant Kunj easily, Greater Noida far less so
Mumbai: Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar usually need a tutor from that side
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road families often settle on one home session a week
Smaller cities: agree cover before the year starts, because the local pool is thin
Searching IB private tuition near me is a starting point, not the finished shortlist

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar that shapes tuition across India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and an IB family's tuition calendar is pinned to it. Term one, from April to the summer break, is where new content lands and where a tutor should be building the foundations nobody will have time for later. Many international schools in India break for several weeks over the summer, return in late June or July, then run to a Diwali break that moves each year with the festival. Term two carries the heaviest coursework load of the course. Term three is mocks, revision and the May session, and May results are released in early July.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School and Oakridge International School meet the same calendar pressures whatever their programme, and those pressures repeat year after year in almost the same weeks.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. Nobody outside the school can tell you when yours fall, so get the date in writing from the coordinator during term one and hand it to the tutor. That single date reorganises everything else: when past papers start, when internal assessment work has to be finished, when a second subject can safely be added, and when tuition should be cut back so the student can revise alone.

Schools also set internal deadlines that run earlier than the IB's. Parents tend to discover this in October, at speed. Ask for the school's own deadline calendar at the start of the year and treat that, rather than the official one, as the real timetable.
items: Term one, April to the summer break, is when foundations are cheapest to build
Get the DP2 mock dates in writing from the coordinator during term one
Internal school deadlines run earlier than the IB's; ask for the school calendar
Diwali moves each year, so the second break never falls in the same week
Plan the final revision block tutor-light, with the student working alone

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid over a full year in India
contentBlocks.body:
Over a full year of IB private tuition in India, home tuition, online tuition and a hybrid week each fail in a different way, and it is worth knowing which failure you can live with. Home tuition gives the tutor the student's real conditions: the desk, the noise from the next room, the phone face down or not. It also leaves the fewest excuses. Its failure mode is attrition, because travelling across a large city twice a week is the thing a tutor quietly starts to resent by November.

Online tuition never cancels for traffic and opens the whole country's supply, which matters for a rarer HL subject. Its failure mode is drift. A student can attend thirty online sessions and be genuinely present for twenty of them. Written work also moves more slowly: a scanned script is not the same as a tutor turning a page and seeing the working that was crossed out and rewritten.

Hybrid is where most Indian families land by term two, and for a year-long arrangement it is usually the right answer. One home session a week holds the relationship and catches what a screen hides. The others run online and survive rain, exam weeks and the tutor's own travel. When the student is in Thane or Whitefield and the right tutor is not, hybrid is the only version of the arrangement that lasts twelve months.

Here is the trade-off stated plainly. Home classes cost the tutor travel time, which shows up in your fee structure and in their willingness to keep the slot in month eight. Online costs you supervision and some feedback quality on handwritten work. Hybrid costs a little of both and keeps the arrangement alive. Pick the failure you can manage, then write the pattern into the agreement so nobody reopens it in January.
items: Home tuition: the best evidence of real study conditions, the worst resilience to traffic
Online tuition: national supply and no travel, but attention and script feedback suffer
Hybrid: one home session weekly plus online sessions, where most long arrangements end
Write the mode pattern into the agreement so it is not reopened mid-year
Move online for the weeks around mocks rather than cancelling the slot outright

contentBlocks.heading: How are tutors verified for a long arrangement in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they go live: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the subjects and levels a tutor says they teach. For an arrangement that runs most of an academic year, treat that as the floor rather than the ceiling, because the checks that matter most are the ones you make yourself in the first month and repeat in the sixth.

Ask a tutor to be specific about levels rather than subjects. Someone who teaches Mathematics AI SL well may be genuinely out of their depth in AA HL, and the honest ones say so at the first meeting rather than the fourth. Ask what they do when a student's IA draft arrives. Listen for where they draw the line. A tutor who offers to improve the draft is describing something the school's academic integrity rules do not allow, and that single answer tells you more than any certificate will.

For home lessons there is a second layer. You are giving someone regular access to your flat in Bandra or your floor in Salt Lake, so agree who is at home during sessions, whether the society gate has the tutor's details on file, and what happens in a week when both parents are travelling. None of this is awkward if you raise it before the first session. It becomes awkward in month four.

A platform cannot see everything, and any platform that says otherwise is overselling. It cannot see whether a tutor is patient at eight in the evening after a long day, whether they mark work between sessions, or whether they will still be in the same city in March. Those things you learn by watching, which is why the review points matter. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anyone who offers one is telling you about their honesty rather than their teaching.
items: Identity, qualifications and the levels claimed are checked before a profile goes live
Ask about levels, not subjects: AA HL and AI SL are genuinely different jobs
Ask where the line sits on an IA draft, and listen to the whole answer
Agree gate entry, who is at home, and travel weeks before the first session
Re-check the arrangement at six months, not only at the start of the year

contentBlocks.heading: IB private tuition in India as a year-long arrangement
contentBlocks.body:
A year-long arrangement is not simply a longer version of a short one. It has a shape: a build phase, a heavy middle, a taper before examinations, and two long gaps that most families handle badly. The gaps are the summer break, which can run for several weeks, and the Diwali break, which moves each year and always seems to arrive just as term two work is accelerating.

Over the summer, stopping entirely is usually wrong for a DP1 student and usually right for an MYP 3 one. The DP1 student is about to walk into the heaviest term of the course, and a single light weekly session keeps the material warm and the habit intact. A younger student needs the break more than the content. The middle position, which suits many families, is a short block of three or four sessions in the last fortnight of the holiday, aimed squarely at whatever term two opens with. Agree which of the three you want in April, in writing, so the tutor does not give the slot to another family.

Changing tutor mid-year is the part nobody plans for and a fair number of families end up doing. Something real is lost in the change: the accumulated knowledge of which topics failed in July, the error log, the shorthand a student and tutor build up over months. What can be saved is the record. Ask any tutor from the first session to keep a running note of topics covered, marks on practice work and current weaknesses, and to share it with you monthly. That note is your handover document. Without it a new tutor spends three sessions rediscovering what the old one already knew, in the middle of the year, when three sessions are expensive in time rather than money.

Ending well matters as much as starting well. Almost every arrangement should end at some point. The good ones end on purpose, at a sensible moment, with the student holding the plan.
items: 1. Say why it is ending: exams over, gap closed, fit wrong, or the load too heavy
2. Give notice at a term boundary, or an agreed number of sessions ahead
3. Ask for the running note: topics covered, practice marks, current weaknesses
4. Run one closing session that hands the plan to the student, not to the parent
5. Confirm in writing whether this is a pause with a restart date or a proper end

contentBlocks.heading: What should change by the end of each term?
contentBlocks.body:
By the end of the first term you should see a change in how the student works, not yet a change in the grade. That is the honest sequence, and it is worth saying out loud because IB private tuition in India is often sold in the opposite order. Marks move last, after the habits and the technique that produce them.

In term one, watch the small things. Does your child now start a question by reading the command term and deciding what depth it asks for? Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent all demand different answers, and students lose more marks here than on missing content. Is there an error log, or at least a list of the mistakes that keep returning? Has practice work started being marked against the actual criteria rather than being ticked and handed back?

Term two is where marks should begin to move, and where a flat result calls for a conversation rather than more hours. Ask the tutor directly what they think is blocking progress and whether it is something tuition can fix at all. Sometimes the answer is that the student is doing too much, and the right recommendation is to drop a subject from the tuition list. A tutor willing to say that out loud is worth keeping for the rest of the year.

Term three is the taper. In the weeks before mocks and before the May session, sessions should get shorter or fewer, because the student needs long stretches to work alone under timed conditions. If your tuition load is rising in April of DP2, something went wrong the previous July.

And if nothing has shifted after three months of steady attendance, change something. Usually the subject. Sometimes the mode. Occasionally the tutor.
items: Term one: technique and habits shift; command terms get read before answering
Term two: marks start moving, or the plan needs changing rather than extending
Term three: fewer sessions, more timed practice the student does alone
A running error log the student maintains is the clearest sign of real work
No change after three months of steady attendance means change the plan

contentBlocks.heading: What to agree in writing before the first session
contentBlocks.body:
Write it down. Not a contract with clauses, just a shared note both sides have read, because nine months is long enough for two reasonable people to remember an arrangement differently. The note should settle six things: the subjects and levels, the number of sessions a week and their length, where they happen and in which mode, what the tutor does between sessions, how often you get an update, and how either side ends it.

Session length deserves a sentence of its own. Ninety minutes suits a DP subject with past-paper work in it. Sixty is plenty for an MYP student and more than enough for a younger child. Two shorter sessions usually beat one long one for anyone below the DP, and a tutor who insists on two hours for a twelve-year-old is planning around their own travel rather than around the student.

Set the review points at the same time. Put a date in term one, one shortly after the school's mock results arrive, and one before the final run-in. A review is twenty minutes with the tutor about what has changed and what has not. Families who schedule these in April actually hold them. Families who intend to hold them as and when needed almost never do.

Availability is always subject to the tutor's schedule and to the level you need, so book the slot you want early in the year rather than in August, when every DP1 parent in the country has had the same thought. Then prepare for the first session properly: the last report, a marked piece of work, the school's deadline calendar, and the mock dates if you already have them. A tutor who sees those documents in session one will plan a better year than one who sees them in November.
items: Agree subjects, levels, session count, length, mode and venue in one written note
Fix three review dates in advance: term one, after mocks, before the final run-in
Bring the last report, a marked script and the school deadline calendar to session one
Availability is subject to the tutor's schedule and the level you need
State in the note how either side pauses or ends the arrangement

faqs.question: How long should we commit to IB private tuition at the start?
faqs.answer: Start with one term and review it, rather than with a year. A term is long enough to see whether the tutor and the student work well together, and short enough that leaving costs nothing awkward. Put the review date in the written note before the first session. If the fit holds through that first review, then plan the rest of the year properly, including the summer block and the taper before mocks, and book the slot while it is still free.

faqs.question: Should home tuition continue through the long summer break?
faqs.answer: For a DP1 student, usually yes, at a reduced rate of one session a week. The summer break runs for several weeks and term two opens with the heaviest content of the course, so a light slot keeps the material warm and the working habit intact. For an MYP or PYP child, stopping is generally the better call. A middle option that works well is three or four home sessions in the last fortnight before school reopens, aimed at whatever term two starts with.

faqs.question: How do we change tutor in the middle of the year without losing ground?
faqs.answer: Ask for the handover note first, then overlap the two tutors if the schedule allows. The running record of topics covered, practice marks and current weaknesses is what makes a new tutor useful in week one instead of week four. Tell the outgoing tutor honestly why the change is happening. Keeping the old slot running for a fortnight while the new tutor starts means nothing gets dropped, and asking for a different match is faster than beginning the whole search again.

faqs.question: What exactly should be agreed in writing before the first session?
faqs.answer: Six things: subjects and levels, sessions per week and their length, mode and venue, what the tutor does between sessions, how often you get an update, and how either side ends the arrangement. None of that needs a lawyer or a formal contract. A shared note that both sides have read is enough, and it prevents the common argument in January about whether the tutor was meant to be marking past papers or only teaching new content.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we realistically tutor at once?
faqs.answer: Two weekly, three at the absolute maximum, and probably fewer than you are imagining. Every tuition hour comes out of the student's own study time, which is where most of the actual learning happens. A better pattern is to keep one compounding subject such as Mathematics running all year, then bring others in for short blocks around an internal assessment deadline or a set of mocks, and drop them again once that work is done.

faqs.question: Will the tutor still come home during Diwali and the mock weeks?
faqs.answer: That depends on what you agreed in April, which is exactly why it should be written down. Diwali moves each year with the festival and most tutors take at least part of that break. Mock weeks are a different question: many families want extra sessions then, and the honest advice is usually fewer, because the student needs uninterrupted hours to sit full papers alone. Agree both in advance and the question never becomes a disagreement.

faqs.question: We are in Thane and the best tutor is in Bandra. Will a weekday home slot survive the year?
faqs.answer: Probably not as a twice-weekly home visit, and it is much better to know that in June than in October. A tutor crossing the Mumbai Metropolitan Region on a weekday evening, in the monsoon, will eventually ask to move or drop the slot. The arrangement that lasts is hybrid: one home session at a time that suits the travel, and the rest online. Families in Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar generally reach the same conclusion by term two.

faqs.question: What happens to the arrangement if we move city in the middle of the year?
faqs.answer: The tutor usually continues online, which is the strongest argument for choosing someone who teaches well on a screen even when you start at home. Transfers between cities are common in Indian corporate families, and a move from Bengaluru to Salt Lake in the middle of DP1 does far less damage if the same tutor stays. Tell them early. Rebuilding a working relationship in a new city during term two costs weeks you do not have.

faqs.question: Can we pause tuition for a month rather than stopping altogether?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a pause is often the right answer during a heavy coursework month or a family event. Say clearly that it is a pause, give a restart date, and accept that the tutor may not be able to hold the exact slot, since availability depends on their other commitments and on the level you need. A pause with a date on it usually restarts. A vague pause usually turns into an ending nobody actually decided.

faqs.question: How do we know after three months whether it is working?
faqs.answer: Look at how the student works before you look at the marks. By month three you should see command terms being read properly, an error log or at least a list of recurring mistakes, and practice work marked against the real criteria rather than ticked. Marks tend to follow a term later. If nothing at all has changed after three months of steady attendance, the plan needs changing, and sometimes that means fewer subjects rather than a different tutor.

faqs.question: Is private tuition from a school teacher a better long-term option?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it can also create an awkwardness worth thinking through first. A teacher who knows the school's internal deadlines and marking habits brings real context that an outsider lacks. The complication is that the same person may be assessing the student's work, which some schools restrict outright and some parents find uncomfortable. Ask the school's policy before arranging anything. Where the policy allows it, agree scope, reviews and an exit in writing exactly as you would with anyone else.

Say clearly that it is a pause, give a restart date, and accept that the tutor may not be able to hold the exact slot, since availability depends on their other commitments and on the level you need. A pause with a date on it usually restarts. A vague pause usually turns into an ending nobody actually decided.

mainEntity.name: How do we know after three months whether it is working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at how the student works before you look at the marks. By month three you should see command terms being read properly, an error log or at least a list of recurring mistakes, and practice work marked against the real criteria rather than ticked. Marks tend to follow a term later. If nothing at all has changed after three months of steady attendance, the plan needs changing, and sometimes that means fewer subjects rather than a different tutor.

mainEntity.name: Is private tuition from a school teacher a better long-term option?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, and it can also create an awkwardness worth thinking through first. A teacher who knows the school's internal deadlines and marking habits brings real context that an outsider lacks. The complication is that the same person may be assessing the student's work, which some schools restrict outright and some parents find uncomfortable. Ask the school's policy before arranging anything. Where the policy allows it, agree scope, reviews and an exit in writing exactly as you would with anyone else.

IB Gram asks about the board, the school calendar and your locality, then shares a shortlist of verified profiles. A demo session can be arranged before you commit to anything longer, and if the match turns out to be wrong you can ask for a different tutor.

h1: IB Online Tutors in India for Students in Any City
heroTitle: Reaching an IB Subject Specialist Anywhere in India
heroSubtitle: Some Higher Level subjects have almost no local teacher outside a handful of cities, and that single fact is why most families start looking at IB online tutors in India. This page covers choosing one, testing them in a trial, the equipment that genuinely matters, and the students online does not suit.
introSummary: IB online tutors in India teach one student at a time over a video call, with a shared screen, an annotated past paper and a digital whiteboard doing the work that a dining table and a notebook do at home. Families rarely choose this for convenience. They choose it for supply. A Higher Level subject that only a few teachers in your city can handle properly is a subject you will probably have to look outside the city for, and online removes the travel while widening the pool to every metro at once. It also removes the tutor from the room, which suits some students and defeats others. Both halves of that are on this page, along with trial questions, verification, and the home tuition and hybrid options if a screen turns out to be the wrong answer.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match an online tutor across India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks what you are actually trying to solve, and a shortlist of verified profiles comes back against the subject, the level and the hours you can realistically keep. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. That is the whole mechanism. Everything below is about making it produce a good match rather than a fast one.

The opening questions are deliberately narrow. Which programme: Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) or Diploma Programme (DP)? Which subject, and at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL)? Which year of the two-year DP, because DP1 in September and DP2 in January are not the same job at all. What does the school calendar look like, particularly the mock examination dates, which every school sets for itself. And what does the week already contain, since a student with Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments on two evenings has fewer usable slots than a parent tends to assume.

Location matters less for an online match than for a home visit, but it does not disappear. A family in Kochi and a tutor keeping evening hours out of Pune still have to agree a time that leaves the student able to think rather than able to nod. So the schedule question is settled before the tutor question.

Matching is not instant, and it should not be. A rare HL subject takes longer to fill than Mathematics. Availability depends on the level, the subject and the hours you need. If the first match is wrong after two or three sessions, say so early and ask for a different one. That request is ordinary, and it costs a fortnight rather than a term.
items: 1. Send the query: subject, programme, level, year group, city and workable slots.
2. A short call establishes the real problem, not only the subject name.
3. Verified profiles are shortlisted against that brief, subject to tutor availability.
4. A trial or demo session runs with the student present and talking.
5. Lessons start online, at home or hybrid, and the match can change.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB programmes and levels work well online in India?
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme is where most online tutoring actually happens, and the structure explains why. The DP runs across two years, DP1 and DP2. A student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) contribute up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service has to be completed alongside all of that.

Those extra Higher Level hours are why HL students run short first. Ninety more recommended hours of content per subject is a great deal of material, and a school that timetables HL and SL groups together does not always find them. An online tutor is normally hired for one or two HL subjects, not for six.

The Middle Years Programme sits differently. MYP students are younger, assessment is criterion-based rather than a set of terminal papers, and holding attention through a screen is harder at thirteen than at seventeen. Online still works for MYP 4 and MYP 5, particularly in mathematics and in language subjects, provided the sessions are shorter and each one is built around something the student has to produce.

The Primary Years Programme is the honest exception. Most primary children learn badly through a screen, and a parent ends up sitting in to keep the lesson moving, which defeats the purpose. For a PYP child, home tuition is almost always the better arrangement, and any platform that tells you otherwise is selling.

Exam sessions run in May and November. Indian schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March, and May results are released in early July. Plan backwards from that date.
items: DP1 and DP2 need different tutoring: building content, then sitting timed papers.
Higher Level carries 240 recommended hours against 150 at Standard Level.
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points towards 45.
MYP 4 and 5 online works in shorter sessions with a product.
PYP online rarely works; a tutor at home suits young learners better.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is the subject most families can fill locally. The scarcity lies elsewhere. The genuinely hard searches are Higher Level sciences taught by someone who has worked at that level rather than one grade below it, IB Economics at HL, and English A for a student who needs literary analysis rather than language support. Less commonly taken languages and Group 6 subjects are harder again, and outside the metros they are frequently unavailable locally at any price.

Online handles some of this better than a table does. Take the mathematics exploration, the internal assessment (IA) that is the same task for Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) at both levels. It carries 20% of the final grade, runs to 12 to 20 pages, and is marked out of 20 on five criteria: A Presentation (4 marks), B Mathematical communication (4), C Personal engagement (3), D Reflection (3) and E Use of mathematics (6), with HL work judged against a higher standard on criterion E. A tutor sharing the draft on screen can put the criterion and the paragraph side by side and show the student exactly where reflection has been asserted instead of demonstrated. The school teacher may comment on one draft, and the work must be the student's own. Any tutor offering more than discussion is a risk, not a discovery.

Command terms reward the same treatment. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each demand a different depth of answer, and the quickest way to teach that difference is a past paper question and its markscheme open together on a shared screen, with the student rewriting one answer in real time. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels. Ask a prospective tutor which of those they work from, and what they do with a subject report, before you book anything.
items: HL sciences and HL Economics thin out fastest outside the larger cities.
English A needs a literature tutor, not a language-support tutor.
The mathematics exploration is 20% of the grade across five criteria.
Command terms set answer depth: describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent.
Ask which past papers, markschemes and subject reports the tutor works from.

contentBlocks.heading: IB online tutors in India: coverage well beyond the metros
contentBlocks.body:
An IB online tutor in Mumbai keeps the same evening hours whether the student is in Bandra or across the harbour in Vashi, and the same tutor can teach a student in Kochi on the following slot. That arithmetic is what changes for families outside the six metro clusters.

In southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai usually have one international school within reach and very little tutoring supply that grew up around it. Online IB classes are often the only route to an HL specialist there. The same is true across central and western India, where Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad sit a long way from the tutor pools of the big cities.

Kolkata and eastern India splits in two. Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat carry enough local supply for common subjects, so an IB online tutor in Kolkata is a choice rather than a necessity; Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna are a different situation entirely.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR behaves much the same way. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula have reasonable reach between them, while Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur thin out quickly once you name a subject and a level. In Gujarat, an IB online tutor in Ahmedabad may be searching from Satellite, Bodakdev or somewhere off SG Highway, and families in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot look beyond their own city from the start.

Inside the metros the argument shifts from supply to traffic. An IB online tutor in Bengaluru, still Bangalore to most parents, saves a Whitefield or Sarjapur Road family a weekday evening crawl. An IB online tutor in Hyderabad reaches Gachibowli and Kondapur without anyone crossing town, an IB online tutor in Pune does the same between Hinjewadi and Koregaon Park, an IB online tutor in Chennai covers Adyar and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), and an IB online tutor in Delhi serves Dwarka, Noida and Gurugram (Gurgaon) on one timetable.
items: Southern India: Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam and Madurai rely heavily on online.
Central and western India: Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Goa and Nashik.
Eastern India: strong supply in Salt Lake, thin in Guwahati, Ranchi, Patna.
Northern India: Chandigarh and Mohali reach further than Dehradun or Kanpur.
Gujarat: Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot look outward by default.
Metro families choose online to avoid the weekday evening crossing, not for supply.

contentBlocks.heading: How the school calendar shapes an online tuition plan
contentBlocks.body:
The calendar belongs to the school, not to the tutor, and an online arrangement that ignores it wastes a term. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools of the kind families here attend, among them Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School and Pathways World School, set their own internal deadlines, and those deadlines are what a tutor has to plan around.

The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, so DP1 begins in the middle of a calendar year and DP2 ends with the May session. Each school fixes its own DP2 mock examinations, usually several months ahead of May. Mocks are the single most useful date in the year for a tutoring plan, because they produce the first realistic evidence of where a student stands under timed conditions. Book the tutor before the mocks, not after them.

Internal assessment deadlines stack. A student can face a science IA, the mathematics exploration, a TOK submission and Extended Essay drafts inside the same crowded window, usually with CAS still running. Online tutoring copes with that stacking better than a fixed home visit does, since a half-hour draft discussion can be slotted into a weekday morning before school.

Festivals bend the schedule too, in ways a national page ought to admit. Pujo empties Kolkata, Ganesh Chaturthi reshapes a fortnight in Pune and Mumbai, Onam takes a week in Kochi, and Diwali interrupts almost everywhere. Agree in advance what happens during those weeks rather than cancelling three sessions and losing the rhythm entirely.

Ask your school's DP coordinator for the internal deadline sheet, and give it to the tutor in the first week. It is the cheapest thing you can do to make the arrangement work.
items: Get the school's internal deadline sheet to the tutor in week one.
DP2 mock dates are set by each school, usually months before May.
IA, TOK and Extended Essay deadlines stack inside one crowded window.
Agree festival weeks in advance: Pujo, Onam, Ganesh Chaturthi, Diwali.
May results arrive in early July, which sets the retake conversation.

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid: which mode suits your student in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in plain terms. A home tutor sits beside the student and sees the page, the hesitation and the crossed-out line, which is worth a great deal for a younger student or for anyone who stops working the moment nobody is watching. An online tutor gives you a far larger pool of subject specialists and no travel, which is worth more once the student is self-directed and the subject is scarce. Hybrid runs both: a home session each week for the sit-down work, an online session for review, marking and quick draft discussion.

The trade-off is presence against reach, and it is a real trade-off rather than a marketing one. For a DP2 student working on Higher Level Chemistry in Visakhapatnam, reach wins easily, because the alternative is not a better local tutor but no specialist at all. For an MYP 3 student in Thane who has drifted in mathematics for a year, presence usually wins, because the problem is attention and habit rather than content.

Hybrid deserves more attention than it gets in India. Many families settle into it without ever planning it: a tutor visits on Saturday morning and takes a shorter online slot midweek. That pattern survives traffic, examination weeks and the tutor's own travel, and it keeps the in-person relationship that makes a student answer honestly when asked whether they actually understood.

There is a scheduling argument as well. Home classes need a fixed slot that includes travel at both ends, so a family in Noida or on Malabar Hill effectively blocks longer than the lesson itself. Online lessons can be shorter and more frequent, which fits revision better than one long weekend visit does. Try the mode you think is wrong for a single session before deciding. Families are often surprised, in both directions.
items: Home tutoring: presence, the page in front of them, strongest for younger students.
Online: reach across India, no travel, best for scarce Higher Level subjects.
Hybrid: one home session weekly plus a shorter online review midweek.
Online suits frequent short sessions; home classes suit one longer sitting.
Test the mode you assume is wrong for a single session first.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you verify a tutor you will never meet in person?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification of IB online tutors in India rests on two halves, and both have to happen: what the platform checks before a profile goes live, and what you check in the first two sessions. IB Gram verifies profiles before shortlisting them, covering identity, the qualifications a tutor claims and their stated teaching experience. No verification process can see how a person teaches your particular child, which is precisely what the trial is for.

Start with identity, which sounds obvious and is routinely skipped online. The person on the call at session one should be the person on the profile and the person from the trial. If a substitute appears, stop and ask. For a minor, the ordinary safeguarding rules do not soften because the lesson is on a screen: keep sessions in a shared family space rather than a closed bedroom, keep communication on the channel the platform provides rather than a personal number, and expect a tutor to be comfortable with a parent walking through the room at any moment.

Then test the teaching claims against something specific. A tutor who says they teach Higher Level Physics should be able to say what a subject report is for, describe how they mark an answer against a markscheme, and tell you what they would do differently for an SL student. Vague answers here are the most reliable warning sign in the whole process.

Recording is worth agreeing in writing at the start. Some families want sessions recorded for revision, some tutors decline, and both positions are reasonable. What is not reasonable is discovering the position in week six.

Finally, check that reporting exists. You should know after each session what was covered and what was set. A tutor who cannot summarise a lesson in three lines is not tracking it closely enough.
items: Identity checked before the profile is shortlisted; confirm the same face appears.
Qualifications and stated experience verified; teaching fit is tested at the trial.
Keep online lessons in a shared room, not a closed bedroom.
Agree the recording policy in writing before the first paid session.
Expect a three-line summary after each session: covered, set, next.
Vague answers about markschemes and subject reports are the clearest warning sign.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging an online tutor in a single trial lesson
contentBlocks.body:
A trial is not a sales call, and you should not let it turn into one. Send the tutor something real beforehand: a marked script, a returned IA draft, a report comment, or the three questions your child got wrong last week. What you are testing is whether this person can find the actual problem in forty minutes, through a screen, with a student who is slightly nervous.

Watch for diagnosis first. A good trial opens with the tutor asking the student to attempt something, then asking why they did what they did. A weak trial opens with the tutor explaining a topic beautifully for twenty-five minutes. Beautiful explanation is easy to buy and is rarely the thing that was missing.

Watch the screen craft next, because it is specific to online teaching and it is learnable, so its absence tells you the tutor has not done much of this. Can they annotate a past paper live rather than reading it aloud? Do they use a shared document the student can write in too? Does the student's own work appear on screen, or only the tutor's slides? Is the tutor's face visible while the student works, or have they vanished behind a whiteboard?

Then listen to who is talking. If the student has spoken for less than a third of the trial, the ratio is wrong for one-to-one teaching.

Ask two closing questions of your own. What would you work on for the first month, and why in that order? And what would tell us in four weeks that this is not working? A tutor who answers the second question honestly is worth more than one who cannot imagine failing. End by asking the student, privately, whether they understood more than usual. That answer decides it.
items: Send real evidence before the trial: a marked script or returned draft.
A good trial starts with diagnosis, not with a polished explanation.
Check live annotation of a past paper and a shared editable document.
The student should be talking for at least a third of the session.
Ask what would show, in four weeks, that this is not working.
Ask the student privately whether the session made anything clearer.

contentBlocks.heading: What progress looks like, and who online does not suit
contentBlocks.body:
Set the expectation properly and you will avoid the common mistake of judging IB online tutors in India after three weeks. In the first two or three sessions the tutor is diagnosing, and what you should see is the problem described more precisely than the school report described it. By four to six weeks you should see a change in how the student works: attempting a question before asking for help, showing steps, using the command term in the answer. Marks move later, usually at the next set of timed papers, and they move unevenly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim otherwise deserves real scepticism.

Now the honest half. Online does not suit every student, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's money.

A student who needs someone physically present to start working will not start working because a laptop is open. A student who has drifted for two terms with no study routine needs a person in the room first, and home tuition for a few months before any screen. Very young learners are usually poorly served online. So are students with significant attention difficulties, unless sessions are short and a parent is an active partner in the arrangement. A student who will not turn the camera on, and whose family will not insist, is effectively listening to a podcast.

There are also households where the connection genuinely will not hold through a ninety-minute evening session. A shorter, more frequent pattern often works better than fighting that, or hybrid, or a local home tutor for the bulk of the teaching with online reserved for the specialist subject. Say the constraint out loud at the matching stage. It changes what a sensible match looks like.
items: Weeks one to three: diagnosis, and a sharper description of the real problem.
Weeks four to six: changed working habits, steps shown, command terms used.
Marks usually move at the next timed papers, not before.
Online fails students who need a person present to begin working at all.
A camera left off for weeks means the arrangement is not working.
Weak connection at home? Shorter sessions, hybrid, or a local tutor instead.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started with IB online tutors in India
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first lesson, spend twenty minutes on the setup. Most of what goes wrong online in the first month is equipment and desk rather than teaching, and it is the cheapest problem on this entire page to solve.

1. A laptop or desktop with a real keyboard, not a phone, and ideally a second screen or a tablet so the student can write while the shared document stays visible.

2. A wired headset with a microphone. Room audio through laptop speakers is the most common reason a student mishears a definition and then repeats it wrongly for a month.

3. A camera the tutor can actually see the student's face in, positioned so written work can be held up to it.

4. Paper, a pen and a scientific or graphic display calculator on the desk, because the student still has to write by hand in the examination.

5. A stable connection, tested at the time of day the lesson will run, not at eleven in the morning when the building is empty.

What does not matter is worth saying as well: an expensive graphics tablet, a dedicated study studio, a premium subscription to a whiteboard tool. A tutor who insists on those is solving their own problem, not your child's.

Then send your query or book a free consultation. Say the board, the programme, the subject and level, the year group, your city and the two or three slots you can genuinely keep each week. IB Gram asks about the school calendar and the schedule, shortlists verified profiles that fit, and arranges a trial so the student can judge the tutor before you commit to anything.
items: Laptop with keyboard, headset with microphone, camera on, paper and calculator ready.
Test the connection at the hour the lesson will actually run.
Skip the graphics tablet and premium whiteboard tools; they solve nothing.
Send board, programme, subject, level, city and two workable weekly slots.
Ask for the trial before committing, and involve the student in the decision.

faqs.question: Is an online IB tutor really as effective as one who comes home?
faqs.answer: For a self-directed Diploma Programme student in a scarce subject, yes, and often better, because the local alternative is a weaker subject match. The screen costs you something real: the tutor cannot see the crossed-out line, the sideways glance or the page the student is quietly hiding. It gains you a national pool of specialists and no travel at either end. The honest rule is that presence matters most where attention is the problem, and reach matters most where subject expertise is the problem.

faqs.question: What internet speed and equipment does my child actually need?
faqs.answer: A stable connection matters far more than a fast one, and the only test that counts is running a video call at the hour the lesson will actually happen. Beyond that: a laptop with a keyboard rather than a phone, a wired headset with a microphone, a camera the tutor can see the student's face in, and paper and a calculator on the desk. Skip the graphics tablet and the premium whiteboard subscription. Neither has ever rescued a lesson.

faqs.question: How do I judge a tutor in a single trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Judge the diagnosis, not the explanation. Send a marked script or a returned draft in advance, then watch whether the tutor asks the student to attempt something and follows up by asking why they did it that way. Check that the student talks for at least a third of the session, that a past paper can be annotated live on screen, and that the tutor answers honestly when you ask what would show, in four weeks, that this is not working.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi. Can we really reach a Higher Level specialist?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and this is exactly the situation online was built for. Families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore or Guwahati often have one international school nearby and almost no tutoring supply around it, so a local search for an HL subject ends quickly. Looking nationally changes that, subject to availability in the subject and at the hours you need. Expect a rarer HL subject to take longer to match than Mathematics or English.

faqs.question: How is a tutor verified if we never meet them in person?
faqs.answer: Profiles are verified before they are shortlisted, covering identity, claimed qualifications and stated teaching experience, and the trial session then tests everything verification cannot see. Your own checks matter just as much. Confirm the person on the call is the person on the profile, keep lessons in a shared room rather than a closed bedroom, keep communication on the platform channel, and agree the recording policy in writing before the first paid session.

faqs.question: My child gets distracted the moment a laptop is open. Will this work?
faqs.answer: Probably not yet, and that is worth saying plainly before you spend anything. A student who needs a person present to begin working will not begin because a video call has started. In that situation a home tutor for a few months usually does far more good, and online becomes viable later, once a working routine exists. If you want to try anyway, use shorter sessions, make the camera a condition rather than a request, and sit within earshot.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the rules, and the screen is genuinely useful here. The exploration carries 20% of the final grade, runs to 12 to 20 pages and is marked on five criteria, so a tutor can put the criterion and the student's paragraph side by side and ask where the reflection actually appears. What a tutor must not do is write, restructure or supply the work. The school teacher comments on one draft, and the exploration has to be the student's own.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed, or the power goes during a lesson?
faqs.answer: Agree the policy before you start, because power cuts and connection drops are a normal part of the year in most Indian cities. A sensible arrangement covers how much notice a cancellation needs on both sides, what happens to a session cut short by an outage, and whether a shorter make-up slot can be found that week. Settle it in writing at the matching stage rather than negotiating in the middle of a bad evening.

faqs.question: Can we start online and move to home tuition later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and plenty of families in Delhi NCR, Pune and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region end up hybrid without ever planning it. The usual pattern is a home session at the weekend for sit-down work and a shorter online slot midweek for marking and draft review. Switching entirely to home classes depends on finding a verified tutor who can travel to your locality, so it is easier in a metro than in Ranchi or Jabalpur. Ask early.

faqs.question: How many online sessions a week does a DP student need?
faqs.answer: One subject usually needs one or two sessions a week, and the honest answer is that more is often worse. A student already carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service has very few free evenings. Two heavily tutored subjects is a realistic ceiling for most DP students. If a student appears to need tutoring in four subjects at once, the problem is usually workload or subject selection rather than teaching, and that conversation belongs with the school.

faqs.question: Do lessons work across city timings, say a tutor in Chandigarh and a student in Chennai?

A student in Chennai who finishes school late and a tutor in Chandigarh who only keeps early evening hours is a genuine clash, and it is much better found at the matching stage than in week three. mainEntity.name: Is an online IB tutor really as effective as one who comes home?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a self-directed Diploma Programme student in a scarce subject, yes, and often better, because the local alternative is a weaker subject match. The screen costs you something real: the tutor cannot see the crossed-out line, the sideways glance or the page the student is quietly hiding. It gains you a national pool of specialists and no travel at either end. The honest rule is that presence matters most where attention is the problem, and reach matters most where subject expertise is the problem.

mainEntity.name: What internet speed and equipment does my child actually need?

acceptedAnswer.text: A stable connection matters far more than a fast one, and the only test that counts is running a video call at the hour the lesson will actually happen. Beyond that: a laptop with a keyboard rather than a phone, a wired headset with a microphone, a camera the tutor can see the student's face in, and paper and a calculator on the desk. Skip the graphics tablet and the premium whiteboard subscription. Neither has ever rescued a lesson.

mainEntity.name: How do I judge a tutor in a single trial lesson?

acceptedAnswer.text: Judge the diagnosis, not the explanation. Send a marked script or a returned draft in advance, then watch whether the tutor asks the student to attempt something and follows up by asking why they did it that way. Check that the student talks for at least a third of the session, that a past paper can be annotated live on screen, and that the tutor answers honestly when you ask what would show, in four weeks, that this is not working.

mainEntity.name: We live in Kochi. Can we really reach a Higher Level specialist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually yes, and this is exactly the situation online was built for. Families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore or Guwahati often have one international school nearby and almost no tutoring supply around it, so a local search for an HL subject ends quickly. Looking nationally changes that, subject to availability in the subject and at the hours you need. Expect a rarer HL subject to take longer to match than Mathematics or English.

mainEntity.name: How is a tutor verified if we never meet them in person?

acceptedAnswer.text: Profiles are verified before they are shortlisted, covering identity, claimed qualifications and stated teaching experience, and the trial session then tests everything verification cannot see. Your own checks matter just as much. Confirm the person on the call is the person on the profile, keep lessons in a shared room rather than a closed bedroom, keep communication on the platform channel, and agree the recording policy in writing before the first paid session.

mainEntity.name: My child gets distracted the moment a laptop is open. Will this work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Probably not yet, and that is worth saying plainly before you spend anything. A student who needs a person present to begin working will not begin because a video call has started. In that situation a home tutor for a few months usually does far more good, and online becomes viable later, once a working routine exists. If you want to try anyway, use shorter sessions, make the camera a condition rather than a request, and sit within earshot.

mainEntity.name: Can an online tutor help with the mathematics exploration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the rules, and the screen is genuinely useful here. The exploration carries 20% of the final grade, runs to 12 to 20 pages and is marked on five criteria, so a tutor can put the criterion and the student's paragraph side by side and ask where the reflection actually appears. What a tutor must not do is write, restructure or supply the work. The school teacher comments on one draft, and the exploration has to be the student's own.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a session is missed, or the power goes during a lesson?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree the policy before you start, because power cuts and connection drops are a normal part of the year in most Indian cities. A sensible arrangement covers how much notice a cancellation needs on both sides, what happens to a session cut short by an outage, and whether a shorter make-up slot can be found that week. Settle it in writing at the matching stage rather than negotiating in the middle of a bad evening.

mainEntity.name: Can we start online and move to home tuition later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and plenty of families in Delhi NCR, Pune and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region end up hybrid without ever planning it. The usual pattern is a home session at the weekend for sit-down work and a shorter online slot midweek for marking and draft review. Switching entirely to home classes depends on finding a verified tutor who can travel to your locality, so it is easier in a metro than in Ranchi or Jabalpur. Ask early.

mainEntity.name: How many online sessions a week does a DP student need?

acceptedAnswer.text: One subject usually needs one or two sessions a week, and the honest answer is that more is often worse. A student already carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service has very few free evenings. Two heavily tutored subjects is a realistic ceiling for most DP students. If a student appears to need tutoring in four subjects at once, the problem is usually workload or subject selection rather than teaching, and that conversation belongs with the school.

h1: IB Online Tuition in India: What a Good Session Looks Like
heroTitle: Inside an Online IB Lesson in India
heroSubtitle: A screen is not the problem. A badly run session is. This page describes what happens minute by minute in a strong online IB lesson: the past paper opened live, the tutor's pen moving over the student's own working, and the point where attention starts to slide.
introSummary: IB online tuition in India works when the lesson is built for a screen rather than transplanted onto one: a past paper annotated live, the student's handwritten script photographed and marked in front of them, and a running order that assumes a teenager's attention will dip around the fortieth minute. That is the whole difference. A tutor who talks at a camera for ninety minutes is running a worse version of a classroom. A tutor who makes the student write, then marks that writing on screen while they watch, is doing something a crowded classroom rarely manages. This page covers the mechanics of the session itself: the tools, the running order, what gets recorded, the failure modes and their fixes, and how online sits beside home tuition and a hybrid week.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram set up an online IB session in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks what the student is taking and how the week actually looks, and a shortlist of tutors whose profiles are verified comes back. A demo or trial session follows if you want one. Nothing is paid before that. The setup differs from home tutoring in one respect worth saying plainly: the first conversation includes a technical check, because a session that loses its first ten minutes to a microphone problem has lost the part of the lesson where the student is freshest.

What gets asked about is specific. Which programme: Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) or Diploma Programme (DP). Which subjects, and at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL). Which examination session the school enters candidates for, which in India is overwhelmingly May. Whether the student writes on paper or on a tablet, because that decides how a script reaches the tutor's screen. And what the evenings really contain, since a DP2 student in Gachibowli with Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments on two weekdays has fewer usable slots than the calendar suggests.

The demo is where you learn most. Watch whether the tutor shares a real past paper or a slide deck. A slide deck is a lecture. A shared paper with a pen hovering over question three is a lesson.

Matching is subject to tutor availability, and availability for this kind of work depends on level and schedule far more than on your address. A family in Bhubaneswar and a family in Indiranagar are choosing from a similar pool. That is the honest advantage of the format, and it is the reason IB online tuition in India reaches households that no local pool would serve.

If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, ask for a different match, and say why. A vague complaint produces a vague replacement.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation describing subjects, level and school timings
2. Answer the matching questions: programme, syllabus, examination session, device and usable evening slots
3. Sit in on a demo session and watch which tools the tutor actually opens
4. Agree a weekly slot, a recording policy and how written work will be shared
5. Review the fit after three or four sessions and ask for a change if needed

contentBlocks.heading: What changes online between PYP, MYP and DP lessons in India?
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme is where online tuition is most common, and the structure explains why. A DP student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to three further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. CAS runs alongside all of it. A DP2 student in the middle of the year has mock preparation, an internal assessment deadline and CAS commitments live at once, and the session that survives that week is the one that requires nobody to travel.

Middle Years Programme sessions run shorter and need more structure on screen. A thirteen-year-old will not hold a ninety-minute video call, and a tutor who tries is wasting your money. Sixty minutes, with the student writing for at least half of it, works better. The camera stays on. The work goes up on the shared screen every ten or fifteen minutes, so there is nowhere to drift to.

PYP is the honest exception. Online tuition for a seven-year-old is hard, and for some children it does not work at all. Where it does work, sessions are short, an adult sits within earshot for the first few weeks, and the tutor points a document camera at real objects rather than opening slides. Many PYP families are better served by home classes, and a platform that will not say so is not being straight with you.

So the programme decides the format before anything else does. Ask a prospective tutor how long their MYP sessions run, and why. A tutor who gives the same answer for a DP2 Physics student and an eleven-year-old has not thought about it.
items: PYP: short sessions, an adult nearby, a document camera instead of slides
MYP: sixty minutes, with the student writing for at least half of it
DP1: subject teaching plus the first internal assessment drafts
DP2: past papers, timed writing and marked scripts returned quickly
HL subjects usually need more frequent sessions, not longer single sittings

contentBlocks.heading: Annotating a science paper on screen, question by question
contentBlocks.body:
Take a Diploma Programme science paper, because it shows the mechanics best. Under the structure first assessed in 2025, Paper 1 comes in two parts: 1A is multiple choice and 1B is data-based questions. Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. HL and SL share that structure, and HL adds Additional Higher Level (AHL) content on top. Online, the tutor opens a 1B question on the shared screen, keeps the markscheme closed, and makes the student talk through the axes and the units before writing anything. Then the pen comes out on a graphics tablet and the working appears in a second colour over the printed question, one line at a time.

The internal assessment is where a shared screen earns its keep. The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, inside a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. A tutor can hold the criteria in one window and the student's draft in another and ask, criterion by criterion, where the evidence for six marks actually sits. The tutor writes none of it.

TOK behaves the same way. The exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 internal assessment prompts, up to 950 words, internally assessed, and it carries one third of the grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for each examination session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed, two thirds of the grade. Reading a draft aloud on a call with the prescribed title pinned at the top of the screen catches drift faster than any written comment.

Mathematics AA and AI need the graphics tablet most. Economics and English A need it least. Physics, Chemistry and Biology sit between the two, and the diagram is usually the argument.
items: Paper 1B data questions read aloud before the student writes anything
Markschemes opened only after the student has committed to an answer
Internal assessment criteria and the student's draft open side by side
TOK prescribed title pinned on screen while the draft is read aloud
Mathematics AA and AI worked freehand on a graphics tablet, line by line

contentBlocks.heading: IB online tuition in India, from Whitefield to Salt Lake
contentBlocks.body:
Online removes the travel problem, which is a different thing from removing geography. Where you live still decides which tutors you can realistically reach, what time a session can begin, and whether home tuition is a sensible alternative at all.

In Bengaluru, families in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Indiranagar, Koramangala, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Electronic City often start with a home tutor and move online in DP2, because evening traffic between the east of the city and anywhere else can stretch a short trip into an unusable one. IB online tuition in Bangalore is frequently a decision about the clock rather than about teaching. Hyderabad splits similarly. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District have reasonable local supply, while families in Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Secunderabad and Kokapet often find the specialist they want sits on the other side of the city, so IB online tuition in Hyderabad wins on scheduling.

Beyond those two, the argument changes from convenience to access. Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai may have no HL specialist for a given subject within reach at all. The same holds through central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa. For these households online is not the second choice. It is the only version of the choice, which is what people are really searching for when they type IB online tuition near me.

In Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore carry more local depth than Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi or Patna, and IB online tuition in Kolkata often runs as a hybrid week. Delhi NCR, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Chennai and Pune have enough supply that the question is which tutor, not whether one exists. IB online tuition in Mumbai, in Delhi, in Chennai, in Pune and in Ahmedabad is usually chosen for the calendar rather than for scarcity.
