Hyderabad: Gachibowli supply is good, cross-city evening travel is not
Kochi, Coimbatore and Visakhapatnam: online is access, not convenience
Indore, Nagpur, Bhopal and Goa: HL specialists are rarely available locally
Salt Lake and New Town families commonly run a hybrid week instead

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars that decide when online lessons run in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, IB schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session rather than November, and May results are released in early July. Those three facts set the shape of every tutoring year. They matter more online than at home, because an online slot is easy to keep and therefore easy to keep badly, long after it has stopped being the right hour.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore appear only as context for the kind of calendar that families at international schools in India work around.

That calendar has predictable pressure points. Internal assessment drafts and the Extended Essay stack up through DP1 and early DP2. Schools run their own mock examinations on dates each school sets for itself, and those weeks swallow ordinary revision whole. CAS commitments fall on fixed weekday evenings and rarely move. A family that books an online session for eight in the evening on a Tuesday in July, without checking what Tuesdays look like in December, will lose that slot exactly when it matters.

So plan the year backwards from May rather than forwards from today. Ask the school's Diploma Programme coordinator for the mock dates as soon as they exist, and tell the tutor in the first week rather than the week before. Expect the shape of the sessions to change as the examination session approaches: less new content, more timed writing, and marked scripts returned within a day or two instead of a week.
items: Plan the tutoring year backwards from the May session, not forwards from today
Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for mock dates as early as they exist
CAS evenings are fixed, so book the weekly slot around them
Expect sessions to shift towards timed writing before the examinations
Results arrive in early July, which is when retake questions begin

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid: which suits an IB student in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in one paragraph. A home tutor sitting beside the student catches what a camera misses: the pen stopping, the wrong constant copied from the data booklet, the page turned too fast. Online tuition gives you a far wider choice of tutors and a slot that does not move because of traffic, and it leaves a saved, marked copy of everything by default. A hybrid week takes both: one home session at the weekend for the hard teaching, one or two online sessions midweek for past papers and doubt-solving. The trade-off is plain. Presence buys attention to the student, and IB online tuition in India buys choice of tutor and reliability of time.

Which one wins depends on the student more than on the subject. A fourteen-year-old who drifts the moment nobody is watching usually needs home classes, at least to begin with. A DP2 student working on an HL subject with a scarce specialist should take the specialist online and stop arguing with the map.

Hybrid deserves more attention than it gets. It solves the common Indian case of a good tutor who lives too far away to come three times a week but can come once. Plenty of families in Pune and Delhi NCR run exactly that pattern through DP1 and then move fully online in the months before May, when nobody wants to lose an hour to a road.

There is one combination worth avoiding. Do not run home tuition and online tuition with two different tutors in the same subject unless the two of them actually speak to each other. The student ends up holding two methods for the same question and trusts neither. If you want both formats, keep one tutor across both, and let the format change while the person stays the same.
items: Home: the tutor sees the pen stop, which a camera often misses
Online: the widest choice of HL specialists and a slot traffic cannot move
Hybrid: one home session at the weekend, past papers online midweek
Keep one tutor across both formats rather than two who never speak
Younger and easily distracted students usually start better with home classes

contentBlocks.heading: How is an online IB tutor verified before you pay?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification answers a narrow question: is this person who they say they are, and have the claims on the profile been looked at? IB Gram checks identity and the qualifications a tutor lists before a profile goes live, and shortlists only profiles that have been through that. What verification cannot tell you is whether this particular tutor will teach your particular child well. Only the demo tells you that, and it takes about four minutes to find out.

Online makes your own checking easier rather than harder, because everything happens on a screen you can watch. Ask the tutor to share a past paper during the demo and annotate one question live. Look for three things. Whether they open the markscheme after the student has answered rather than before. Whether they ask the student to explain the command term in their own words. And whether they write on the student's work or only on their own.

Ask direct questions and expect specific answers. Which components of the paper do you teach most often? How exactly do you handle an internal assessment draft? What do you do when a student has not done the work you set? A tutor who answers in generalities has told you something useful anyway.

There is a safeguarding side that exists only online, and it deserves a plain conversation at the start rather than an awkward one later. Agree who may join the call, whether the session is recorded, and where any recording is stored. For a younger student, keep the sessions in a shared room of the house rather than a bedroom, with the door open. This is ordinary practice, and no reasonable tutor will object to any of it.
items: Identity and listed qualifications checked before a profile becomes visible
Ask the tutor to annotate one past-paper question live during the demo
Watch whether the markscheme appears before or after the student answers
Agree recording, storage and who else may join the call
Keep a younger student's sessions in a shared room with the door open

contentBlocks.heading: What a strong ninety-minute online IB lesson contains
contentBlocks.body:
A good session has a shape, and you can hear it from the next room. It opens with two or three minutes of admin and nothing more: what was set last week, what got done, what did not. Then twenty minutes of the student working with a pen while the tutor mostly keeps quiet, usually a past-paper question under something close to examination conditions. The photograph of that working goes up on the shared screen, and the next stretch is the heart of the lesson. The tutor annotates the student's own handwriting in a second colour, saying out loud where a marker would stop giving credit and why.

Around the fortieth minute attention will dip. Plan for that instead of pretending otherwise. The strongest tutors change the mode at exactly that point: the student takes the pen, or explains a step back to the tutor, or marks an anonymised answer against the criteria. Passive listening past forty minutes is where IB online tuition in India quietly fails, and it fails without anybody complaining.

The last long stretch teaches whatever the marked work exposed as missing, and the final five minutes set the week's work in writing, on the screen, where both of you can see it.

Tools matter less than people think, but three earn their place. A graphics tablet, so the tutor writes freehand rather than typing. A document camera, or simply a phone on a stand, so a printed page or a real piece of apparatus can be shown. And a shared folder where the marked scripts pile up in date order, which by March is the best record of the year anyone has.

Recordings are a real decision, not a default. A recorded lesson is useful for revision and useless if nobody rewatches it. Agree at the start whether sessions are recorded, who may see them, and how long they are kept. For a student under eighteen, the parent settles that, not the tutor and not the student.
items: Two or three minutes of admin, then the student starts writing
Twenty minutes of past-paper work under near-examination conditions
The student's own script photographed and annotated in a second colour
A deliberate change of mode around the fortieth minute
Five closing minutes setting the week's work in writing on screen

contentBlocks.heading: Progress, honestly: what should change, and by when
contentBlocks.body:
Nothing visible changes in the first fortnight, and a tutor who suggests otherwise is selling rather than teaching. What changes first is not the grade but the behaviour around the work. The student starts attempting the hard question instead of leaving a gap, and starts saying why an answer is wrong before being told. That usually shows by the third or fourth session, and it is the signal worth watching.

By six to eight weeks you should be able to see something in the marked scripts themselves: fewer marks lost to method, better handling of command terms, working laid out so a marker can follow it without guessing. Ask the tutor to keep the scripts in date order precisely so that you can look. Grades on school assessments move later than any of this, and they move unevenly, because the difficulty of what is being tested keeps changing underneath.

Now the limits, stated flatly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anyone who does has told you something about themselves. Starting in the final term before May narrows what is possible to examination technique and triage, which is genuinely worth having but is not the same as teaching a subject. A student who will not do work between sessions will not improve much, online or at home, and buying more sessions is the wrong answer to that particular problem.

The format has its own failure modes, and they are easy to spot once named. Camera off for weeks. One-word answers. Sessions rescheduled so often that the arrangement has stopped being weekly. Written work never photographed and never sent. Two of those at once means the arrangement is drifting, and a conversation this week is cheaper than three more months of it.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match and describe precisely what went wrong. Naming the problem is what makes the second match better than the first.
items: Weeks one to three: behaviour around hard questions changes first
Weeks six to eight: fewer marks lost to method in marked scripts
School grades move later and unevenly, so do not read them weekly
Camera off and one-word answers are the early warning signs
No tutor can promise a grade, so treat anyone who does carefully

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB online tuition in India: what to have ready
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send a query, spend ten minutes gathering four things. The most recent marked script, not the report card. The subject and level list, with HL and SL written against each subject. The mock and internal assessment dates, if the school has published them. And an honest map of the week, including CAS evenings and anything that already fills a Saturday morning.

The first session is not a teaching session and should not pretend to be. A good tutor spends it reading the marked script with the student, asking where the marks actually went, and setting one piece of work. By the end you should have a rough plan for the term. If you do not, ask for one before the second session is booked.

What happens after the query is simple enough to state in full. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule. It shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything. Lessons then run online, at home or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. If the match turns out wrong, you can ask for a different one.

One last practical point, and it is the one families skip. Test the setup the day before the first session rather than five minutes before it: microphone, camera, the shared document, and the student's ability to photograph a page and send it without help from you. Ten minutes spent on that saves the first lesson, and the first lesson is what decides whether a teenager takes the whole arrangement seriously.
items: Bring the most recent marked script rather than the report card
List every subject with HL or SL written against it
Note mock dates, internal assessment deadlines and CAS evenings
Test microphone, camera and file sharing the day before
Ask for the term plan at the end of the first session

faqs.question: Does online IB tuition actually work, or is it a compromise?
faqs.answer: IB online tuition in India works for most students from about age thirteen upwards, and it is a compromise for younger children. The thing that decides it is not the technology but the running order. A session where the student writes, has the writing marked on screen, and changes activity around the fortieth minute holds attention as well as a lesson at the dining table. A session that is ninety minutes of someone talking over slides does not, and would not work in a classroom either.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark my child's handwritten script in an online session?
faqs.answer: The student photographs the page and sends it, and the tutor annotates the image on screen while the student watches. That is the whole mechanism. Most tutors use a graphics tablet so the comments are handwritten rather than typed, which makes the corrections easier to follow on a diagram or a line of algebra. The marked copy is then saved to a shared folder. Over a year that folder becomes a record of exactly which errors kept repeating.

faqs.question: How long should an online session be, and how many a week?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for a Middle Years Programme student and ninety for a Diploma Programme student is the usual shape, with one or two sessions a week per subject. More than two sessions a week in one subject rarely helps unless the student is recovering ground after an illness or a school change. Frequency beats length for Higher Level subjects. Two ninety-minute sessions spread across the week do more than one three-hour block on a Sunday.

faqs.question: Should online sessions be recorded?
faqs.answer: Record them only if someone will genuinely rewatch them, and decide it at the start rather than halfway through the term. Recordings help most for a technical derivation or a worked past-paper question that the student will need again before mocks. They help least for discussion-heavy subjects. Agree in writing who may see a recording and how long it is kept. Where the student is under eighteen, that decision belongs to you rather than to the tutor.

faqs.question: My son stops paying attention after half an hour on a call. What can be fixed?
faqs.answer: Change what he is doing rather than shortening the lesson, at least to begin with. Attention usually fails because the student has been listening passively, not because the session is long. Ask the tutor to hand over the pen every fifteen minutes: the student works a question, explains a step aloud, or marks an anonymised answer against the criteria. If that does not help within three or four sessions, move to sixty-minute sessions twice a week, or try home classes instead.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and there is no IB tutor nearby. Is online the only option?
faqs.answer: For a Higher Level subject, very often yes, and that is a reasonable outcome rather than a sad one. Cities such as Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore and Guwahati have far thinner local supply for specific Diploma Programme subjects than Bengaluru or Delhi NCR. Online closes that gap directly. Where a subject does have local teachers, a hybrid week is often better: one home session for the difficult teaching, online sessions midweek for past papers.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and these are two of the parts of the diploma that online support suits best. TOK in particular works well on a shared screen, because the prescribed title can be pinned at the top while the draft is read line by line underneath it. The supervisor at school remains the person who signs off the Extended Essay and manages the reflection sessions. A tutor works around that role rather than replacing any part of it.

faqs.question: Can internal assessment work be discussed online without crossing academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor discusses the student's own draft against the published criteria and writes nothing. The boundary is the same online as at home. For the scientific investigation, that means talking through research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation while the student holds the keyboard. A shared screen actually makes the boundary easier to hold, because there is a visible record of who typed what. Your school's coordinator is the final word on its own policy.

faqs.question: The connection drops in our building in Powai during the monsoon. What then?
faqs.answer: Agree the fallback before it happens, because it will happen at least once. The usual arrangement is a phone hotspot as a backup, an agreed rule about how long to wait before both sides reconnect, and a made-up slot if more than fifteen minutes are lost. Ask about this in the first conversation. A tutor who has taught through a Mumbai or Kolkata monsoon will have a ready answer, and a tutor who has not will improvise badly.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than online for a Diploma Programme student?
faqs.answer: Better for discipline, worse for choice, and that is the real trade-off. A home tutor sees the pen stop and the page turned too quickly, which a camera can miss. Online gives you a far wider pool of Higher Level specialists and a slot that traffic in Bengaluru or Delhi NCR cannot move. Many families in Pune and Chennai run both: home tuition at the weekend for the heavy teaching, online midweek for past-paper practice.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram and ask for a different match, and be specific about what went wrong. Pace too fast, no written work set, sessions that drift into conversation, a personality clash with a teenager who has stopped speaking: each of those leads to a different replacement. A vague complaint produces a vague second match. Availability for the new tutor depends on level and schedule, so expect the replacement slot to sit at a slightly different hour.

comparison.heading: How does an online IB lesson in India compare with a home tutor or a batch?
comparison.intro: One-to-one at home suits a student who needs someone physically present to stay honest with the work. One-to-one online suits a student who needs a specific specialist, or a slot that traffic cannot move. A small online group adds peer discussion at a lower cost per student, and a large batch is the cheapest hour of teaching available. Presence or choice: that is usually the decision.

h1: IB Tuition in India: Does Your Child Actually Need It?
heroTitle: When IB Tuition in India Actually Helps
heroSubtitle: Most parents reach this page after a report card, not after research. So begin with the diagnosis rather than the tutor. What follows is how to read criterion comments honestly, what the school should be asked to fix first, and the situations where a home tutor is simply the wrong answer.
introSummary: IB tuition in India is worth starting only once you can name the problem it is meant to solve, and for most families a home tutor is the format that makes that diagnosis possible in the first place. A slide from a 6 to a 4 in one reporting cycle is not, on its own, evidence of anything. It may be a harder unit, a new teacher, a fortnight of illness, or a study habit that quietly stopped working when the workload grew. This page is about telling those apart. It covers reading criterion feedback properly, the questions to put to the subject teacher and the programme coordinator first, a numbered decision sequence to run before you hire anybody, the signs that a student is already over-tutored, and how long to give it before judging whether it worked.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Turns a Diagnosis Into a Shortlist in India
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every enquiry opens with a grade. A 4 in Chemistry. A comment about inconsistent analysis. Our first reply asks for the layer underneath: the criterion breakdown, the returned script, the teacher's written comment in full rather than the sentence you remember. Without that, a match is guesswork dressed up as service.

The free consultation is a conversation, not a sales call. You are asked which programme and year the student is in, which subject and level, what the school has already tried, when the next report or mock falls, where you live, and which evenings are genuinely free after school, activities and travel. Families in Powai or Whitefield often discover the honest constraint is not money but the sixty minutes between a school bus arriving and dinner. That constraint shapes the shortlist more than anything else.

Only then do we look at tutors. Profiles are verified before they go live, and the shortlist is built from the ones whose subject, level and availability fit the weakness you described, subject to who is free in your area. You see a small set rather than a directory. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything, and we suggest you use it on the exact weakness rather than on a general introduction.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. That is a normal request and not a complaint. What IB Gram does not do is tell you that your child needs tuition. Plenty of consultations end with a suggestion to speak to the coordinator first and come back in a month, because the evidence points to a timetable problem or a rough term rather than a subject gap. A platform that never says that is not diagnosing anything.
items: 1. Send the report comments and criterion breakdown, not only the final grade.
2. Name the paper, criterion or unit where marks are actually being lost.
3. Ask the subject teacher what the school is already doing about it.
4. Book a free consultation and describe your locality, evenings and school calendar.
5. Use the demo session on that one weakness, not a general introduction.
6. Review after four to six weeks against the same evidence you began with.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: Which Stage Actually Warrants Tuition?
contentBlocks.body:
The stage changes the answer more than the subject does. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP), which runs from ages 3 to 12 through six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, there are no external examinations and no published grades. There is nothing to rescue a score from. Paid support at this stage is justified by a specific, observable gap in reading fluency or number sense, or by a child who has moved school systems mid-year. It is not justified by a parent's anxiety about Grade 6.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) is where diagnosis becomes possible. Five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, eight subject groups, and every subject assessed against four criteria (A to D), each scored 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. That structure is a gift to a parent who reads it: a student sitting at 6 on knowing and understanding but 3 on communicating does not have a Science problem, they have a writing problem inside Science. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and a dip in that year is often a time problem wearing a subject's name.

The Diploma Programme (DP) raises the stakes and narrows the room. Two years, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level (SL), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. Here the calendar, not the parent, sets the deadline.
items: PYP: no external exams, no published grades, so no score to rescue
MYP: four criteria per subject, each 0-8, totalling 32 before conversion
MYP 5 Personal Project and MYP 3 or 4 Community Project squeeze the year
DP: six subjects, HL 240 hours against SL 150, graded 1 to 7
TOK and the EE contribute up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45
A dip in one criterion is diagnostic; a dip in all four rarely is

contentBlocks.heading: Reading Subject Feedback Before You Book Anything
contentBlocks.body:
Take the actual words the teacher wrote and translate them into a mark. In IB Mathematics, the split between Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) matters for what a comment means: a student losing marks for unjustified steps in AA is being marked on reasoning, while the same student may be fine on the modelling that AI leans on. Book a tutor for the reasoning, not for Mathematics in general.

In Physics, Chemistry and Biology the recurring comment is that answers are right but thin. That is a command term problem. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a depth, and a student who answers every one of them at the level of describe will be capped no matter how well they understand the content. This is learnable in weeks, and a decent tutor will demonstrate it in the demo by taking one of your child's own answers and showing where the marks stopped.

Economics and English A produce the opposite pattern: fluent writing that does not answer the question asked. Look for comments about structure, about evidence, about relevance. Those are not subject gaps either.

Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show exactly how marks are awarded. Ask the subject teacher for one marked script rather than a summary. Twenty minutes with a real script tells you more than any diagnostic test a provider will offer you for free, because the script carries the marker's reasoning. If the school will not release one, that is itself worth raising with the coordinator before you spend anything on tuition for IB students.
items: AA marks reasoning and justification; AI leans harder on modelling and context
Command terms set depth: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent
Answers that are correct but thin usually signal a command term gap
Ask for one marked script, not a summary of several
Past papers, markschemes and subject reports reach families through the school

contentBlocks.heading: What Starting IB Tuition Looks Like City by City Across India
contentBlocks.body:
Where you live changes the shape of the first month, not the diagnosis. In Delhi NCR the distances are the problem. A family in Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri or South Delhi has a reasonable local pool, while Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad thin out quickly, and a weekday evening trip from Gurugram's Golf Course Road to Sector 128 Noida in peak traffic can stretch well past what any tutor will hold twice a week. Families searching for IB tuition in Delhi usually end up hybrid.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is dense but slow. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are close together on a map and much further apart on a Tuesday evening. Powai sits awkwardly for tutors coming from the western suburbs, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are effectively separate markets. IB tuition in Mumbai works best when the tutor lives inside the same cluster as the student.

Bengaluru splits along the same lines. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City behave as their own towns, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road each hold their own supply. Parents looking for IB tuition in Bangalore should ask where the tutor actually starts their evening from.

Chennai concentrates around Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar, with Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery pulling south. Pune spreads between Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Aundh and Viman Nagar on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Wakad, Hinjewadi and Kharadi on the other, and the crossing between them at seven in the evening is what decides whether home sessions survive past a month. In Hyderabad the same logic applies between Gachibowli, Jubilee Hills and Secunderabad. Families asking about IB tuition in Chennai, IB tuition in Pune, IB tuition in Hyderabad, IB tuition in Kolkata or IB tuition in Ahmedabad get the same answer: map the evening before you map the tutor.
items: Delhi NCR: strong supply in South Delhi and Gurugram, thinner towards Ghaziabad
Mumbai: Bandra, Juhu and Worli are one cluster; Thane and Kharghar another
Bengaluru: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City behave as separate towns
Chennai and Pune: the evening crossing decides whether home sessions survive
Outside the metros, a searched phrase like IB tuition near me rarely returns a specialist
Ask where a tutor begins their evening, not only where they live

contentBlocks.heading: The School Calendar That Decides When to Start in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and IB schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session, with November used by a small minority and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. Every timing decision a parent makes sits inside that frame.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School and Mahindra International School describe the same rhythm, whatever city they are in.

The first report of the year is the one worth acting on, and it is also the one parents most often wait out. A weakness identified in the first term can be worked on across months at one session a week. The same weakness identified after DP2 mocks has to be fixed in weeks, at a higher intensity, while the student is also finishing internal assessment work. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, and those mocks are the single most useful piece of evidence you will get all year. They are also the moment when many families panic and over-buy.

So plan backwards. If the mocks are the checkpoint, the useful window opens well before them, not after. Ask the coordinator at the start of the year when reports, parent meetings and mocks fall, write the dates down, and decide in advance what evidence would make you act. A parent who has already decided what a bad mock means is far less likely to sign up for four subjects in a week of alarm. And a student carrying CAS commitments and stacked deadlines usually needs fewer hours, better placed, rather than more.
items: Indian academic year runs roughly April to March; the May session dominates here
May results are released in early July; November suits retakes and a small minority
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually months before May
Act on the first report of the year, not the one before the mocks
Write the reporting and mock dates down in April and decide your triggers early

contentBlocks.heading: Should the First Sessions Be at Home, Online or Hybrid?
contentBlocks.body:
For a diagnosis, home tuition has a real advantage and it is not comfort. A tutor sitting beside the student sees the working that never reaches the page: the step skipped in their head, the diagram redrawn three times, the pause before a question is attempted. Those are the observations that separate a content gap from a confidence gap. A screen hides them unless the tutor insists on a camera pointed at the paper, which many do not.

Home classes also fail in predictable ways. If the only workable slot is nine at night because the tutor is crossing the city, the sessions will be poor and then they will stop. If the flat has one table and a younger sibling, the lesson competes with the household. Be honest about both before you book.

Online tutoring wins on reach and on stubborn timetables. A specialist in a rarer subject may simply not exist within travelling distance of Kochi, Coimbatore or Jaipur, and an online tutor removes the travel that makes weekday evenings impossible in Mumbai or Delhi NCR. Sessions can be shorter and more frequent, which suits revision better than one long weekly block. The trade-off is that the tutor sees less, so the first two sessions must be designed to make the student's thinking visible on screen.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. A fortnightly home visit anchors the relationship and catches the habits, while the weeks in between run online and stay flexible around mocks and school events. If you are choosing for a diagnosis specifically, start with two home sessions, then decide. The information you get in the room during those first two hours is usually worth the travel, even if you never buy a home session again.
items: Home tuition shows the working and the habits a screen usually hides
A late slot forced by travel produces poor sessions that quietly stop
Online tutoring reaches specialists who do not live within travelling distance
Hybrid pairs a fortnightly home visit with flexible online weeks
For a first diagnosis, two home sessions usually repay the travel

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a Tutor Before a Diagnosis Becomes a Commitment
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on a platform and verification by a parent are two different jobs, and only one of them can judge teaching. Profiles on IB Gram are checked before they go live: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the subjects and levels a tutor says they teach. That stops the obvious problems. It cannot tell you whether this person will be good with your thirteen-year-old on a Wednesday evening.

So do the second job yourself, and do it in the trial. Hand the tutor one of your child's marked answers and ask them to mark it again in front of you both, naming the criterion or the command term where the marks stopped. A tutor who works at the level of the actual assessment will do this comfortably. A tutor who talks about concepts and confidence instead, and never touches the script, is telling you something.

Ask two more questions. What would you do differently in the first month if the problem turns out to be study habits rather than the subject? And what evidence will you show me in six weeks? Vague answers to either are a reason to keep looking. Availability is always conditional on level and schedule, so confirm that the slot discussed in the trial is the slot actually on offer for the term.

Check the ordinary things too, because families forget them in the relief of finding someone. Who is in the flat during a home visit. What happens to a session missed because of school events or illness. Whether the tutor will speak to you directly or only through a coordinator. None of this is distrust. It is the same due diligence you would apply to anyone who spends two hours a week alone with your child and shapes how they study.
items: Profiles are checked for identity, qualifications claimed, and subjects and levels taught
In the trial, ask the tutor to mark your child's own answer aloud
Ask what changes if the real problem turns out to be study habits
Agree in advance what evidence you will see after six weeks
Confirm slot, missed-session handling and who is home during a visit

contentBlocks.heading: Is IB Tuition in India Worth It for Your Child?
contentBlocks.body:
Families searching for IB tuition in India are usually answering a symptom, and there are three things a poor grade can mean. They need three different responses. The first is a genuine subject gap: the student did not understand a topic when it was taught, the topic is foundational, and everything built on it since has wobbled. This is the case tuition is actually for. You can usually spot it because the weakness is specific and it persists across different kinds of task.

The second is a study-skills problem. The student understands the material in the room and cannot reproduce it under conditions: no notes worth revising from, no error log, revision that consists of rereading, work started the night before a deadline. A subject tutor hired for this will teach the subject and the problem will remain, because the problem is not the subject. A tutor can still help, but only if you name the goal as habits and agree that the first month looks like planning and note-taking rather than content.

The third is a rough term, and it is more common than either. A new teacher, an illness, a house move, a friendship that fell apart, a Personal Project that ate two months. One bad reporting cycle with no pattern behind it is usually this. The right response is to wait for the next data point.

Which brings up the case nobody sells you: the over-tutored student. Watch for a child with three or four external classes, who has stopped attempting anything without being shown first, who does homework twice, and who has no unscheduled evening in the week. Adding a fifth class to that will lower the grades, not raise them. Sometimes the honest recommendation is to cancel two of the existing arrangements and see what happens over a term. Fewer hours, better aimed, is a real answer.
items: Subject gap: specific, persistent, and visible across different task types
Study-skills problem: understands in the room, cannot reproduce under conditions
Rough term: one cycle, no pattern, usually resolves without paid help
Over-tutored: several classes, no free evenings, nothing attempted unaided
Name which of the three you are buying for before you book anything
Two arrangements cancelled can raise a grade more than a third one added

contentBlocks.heading: How Long to Give Home Tuition Before You Judge It
contentBlocks.body:
Nobody selling IB tuition in India enjoys this section, because it sets a date on which you are allowed to stop. Six weeks is the shortest honest review point, and even that is early. In the first two sessions a good tutor is still gathering evidence, so the visible output is often a list of gaps rather than progress. By week three you should be able to see a change in what the student produces without help: a structured answer where there was a paragraph, working shown where there was a bare result, a plan for a piece of coursework that did not exist before.

What you should not expect to see in six weeks is the grade. Reporting cycles are slower than that, and criterion grades in the MYP move in whole steps that can hide months of real improvement. Judge the work, not the number, until a report arrives that covers the period the tutor has actually taught.

Set the review up properly at the start. Agree which criterion or paper you are targeting, keep the marked script you began with, and compare like with like at the end. A tutor who cannot show you what changed in the student's own writing is asking you to take improvement on faith.

Be willing to stop. If after two months the student is no more independent than at the start, either the diagnosis was wrong or the match is. Ask for a different tutor before you conclude that tuition does not work. And accept the limits honestly: no tutor can guarantee a grade, a student who will not do work between sessions will not improve at any frequency, and starting three weeks before a mock buys damage control rather than understanding. Saying that plainly at the outset saves a family a term of disappointment.
items: Weeks one and two are diagnostic; expect a gap list, not progress
By week three, look for changes in unaided work rather than in grades
Keep the original marked script and compare like with like at review
Criterion grades move in whole steps and lag real improvement
If nothing has changed in two months, change the tutor or the diagnosis
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and no schedule fixes work never done

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB Tuition in India Without Over-Committing
contentBlocks.body:
Starting IB tuition in India goes badly when a family buys a timetable before it has a brief. Come to the first conversation with four things and it will take twenty minutes instead of three exchanges. The latest report with the criterion or grade breakdown. One marked script or returned assignment. The school's reporting and mock dates for the year. And two evening slots that are genuinely free once school, travel and activities are accounted for. Families who bring these get a shortlist that fits; families who bring a grade get a longer conversation.

Book one subject, not three. If two subjects look weak, the odds are good that one cause sits underneath both, and a single tutor working on that cause for six weeks will tell you more than two tutors working in parallel. It also costs less and takes less of the student's week, which matters more than parents expect.

The first session should not be a lesson. It should be an assessment of what the student can do unaided: attempting a past paper question cold, talking through their own marked answer, showing how they revise. Ask the tutor to send you three sentences afterwards saying what they found and what they will work on. If those three sentences match what the school told you, you have a real diagnosis. If they contradict it, that is worth a conversation with the coordinator before the second session.

From there it is simple. Sessions run at home, online or hybrid depending on your evenings and your city. A demo or trial can be arranged first, subject to tutor availability. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. And if the honest answer after four weeks is that your child did not need a tutor, stopping is not a failure. It is the outcome the diagnosis was for.
items: Bring the report, one marked script, the school dates and two free evenings
Start with one subject; a shared cause often sits under two weak grades
Ask for a written three-sentence summary after the first session
Compare the tutor's finding with the school's before booking a term
Sessions run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability

faqs.question: Do IB students need tuition?
faqs.answer: Most do not, and the ones who benefit usually need it for one subject at one stage rather than across the board. The students for whom tuition genuinely changes something have a specific, persistent weakness that the school has already identified and cannot resolve in class time. If you cannot name the criterion, paper or topic where marks are being lost, you are not ready to hire anybody. Ask the subject teacher first, and give the next reporting cycle a chance to confirm the pattern.

faqs.question: How do I tell a real subject problem from a rough term?
faqs.answer: Look for a pattern across different kinds of task rather than a single low grade. A genuine subject gap shows up in class tests, in homework and in the mock, and it stays attached to the same topics each time. A rough term produces a scattered drop across several subjects at once, usually with an explanation behind it: illness, a new teacher, a house move, or a Personal Project that consumed two months. One bad cycle with no pattern is almost always the second thing, and the right response is to wait for the next data point.

faqs.question: What should I ask the subject teacher before hiring a tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions and write the answers down. Which criterion or paper is the student losing marks on, specifically? Is this a content gap, a technique gap or a working-under-conditions problem? What is the school already doing about it, and by when should we expect to see a change? And can I see one marked script rather than a summary? A teacher who can answer all four has given you a brief. A teacher who cannot is a reason to speak to the programme coordinator next.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition in India cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate for IB tuition in India, and fees vary with the level taught, the subject, the tutor's experience and whether sessions run at home or online, so any single figure quoted to you before those are known is a guess. Home sessions carry the tutor's travel, Higher Level and examination-year teaching usually sit above Middle Years Programme work, and scarcer subjects cost more than common ones. Ask for the structure rather than a number: what a session length is, how the term is billed, what happens to a missed session, and whether a demo is charged.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come on weekday evenings in Mumbai or Bengaluru?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the slot depends entirely on where the tutor starts their evening from, and it is the first thing to settle. Within a single cluster, such as Bandra to Juhu or Indiranagar to Koramangala, weekday evening home classes are usually workable twice a week. Across a city, from Thane to Worli or Whitefield to Jayanagar in peak traffic, a tutor will rarely hold that slot past a month. Availability is subject to who is free in your area, so ask for locality before you ask for a timetable.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in the room during home tuition?
faqs.answer: For a first session, staying nearby is sensible; for every session, it usually backfires. A student who is being watched will perform confidence rather than show confusion, and confusion is exactly what the tutor needs to see in the diagnostic weeks. Sit in for the opening ten minutes if the child is young or the tutor is new, then work within earshot in the next room. Ask for a two-minute summary at the door instead, which gives you more than an hour of listening would.

faqs.question: How long before I know whether tuition is working?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is the earliest honest review, and what you judge at that point is the work, not the grade. By week three the student's unaided answers should look different: structure where there was none, working shown, a plan for coursework that previously did not exist. Grades lag because reporting cycles are slow and criterion levels move in whole steps. Keep the marked script you started with, compare like with like, and if nothing in the writing has shifted in two months, change the tutor or revisit the diagnosis.

faqs.question: My child already has several classes. Should we add another?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and this is the situation where an honest answer costs a platform a booking. A student with three or four external classes, no unscheduled evening, and a habit of waiting to be shown before attempting anything is over-tutored already. Adding a fifth arrangement reduces the thinking time that produces improvement. Cancel the two that were added most recently, keep the one attached to a named weakness, and look again after a term. Fewer hours aimed at one problem beat more hours spread thin.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work as well for working out what is wrong?
faqs.answer: It can, but only if the setup is designed for it, and many are not. The tutor must be able to see the student's paper as they write, either through a second camera, a document camera or a graphics tablet, and must ask the student to think aloud rather than answer quickly. Where that discipline exists, an online diagnosis is close to a home one. Where the student simply reads answers off a screen, the tutor is guessing. Ask how the trial will make the student's working visible.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, and do it early rather than after a term of hoping. Fit problems show up quickly: the student goes quiet, sessions drift into being watched rather than working, or the tutor teaches at a level that does not match the student's. This is a normal request and not a complaint about the tutor's competence, since the same person may suit a different student very well. Describe what did not work, because that description improves the next shortlist more than a general dissatisfaction does.

faqs.question: We live outside the big metros. Is IB tuition near me realistic?
faqs.answer: For common subjects, often yes; for scarce ones, plan on online from the start. Cities such as Kochi, Coimbatore, Jaipur, Lucknow and Chandigarh have some local capacity in Mathematics and the sciences, but a specialist in a rarer subject or a Higher Level option may not live within travelling distance at all. Rather than settling for a general tutor who has never taught the programme, use a local tutor where one genuinely fits and an online specialist where none does. A hybrid split across two subjects is common outside the metros.

faqs.question: Should we start in the MYP or wait until the DP begins?
faqs.answer: If the evidence is there, earlier is cheaper and calmer. A criterion weakness identified in MYP 4 can be worked on across terms at one session a week, while the same weakness reaching DP1 has to be fixed alongside Higher Level content and internal assessment deadlines. But waiting is right when the dip has no pattern behind it or the student is already carrying the Personal Project. Use the first report of the year as your checkpoint, not the mock, and decide in advance what would make you act.
