h1: IB Tuition Classes in India: Which Format Suits Your Child
heroTitle: Choosing an IB Class Format Across India
heroSubtitle: Four formats do most of the work in India: one-to-one at home, one-to-one online, a small online group of three or four, and a large classroom batch. This page compares what each does to attention, marking turnaround and your child's weeknight timetable, then says which student each one genuinely suits.
introSummary: IB tuition classes in India usually take one of four shapes: one-to-one home tuition, one-to-one online, a small online group of three or four students, or a large classroom batch. The format matters more than most families expect. It decides how quickly written work comes back marked, how much of a ninety-minute session your child actually speaks in, and whether the class survives a week of mocks. A Diploma Programme student rebuilding his written answers needs something quite different from a Middle Years Programme student who has misread one criterion. Below, each format is set against a real Indian school week, from Bandra to Gachibowli, with the timetable it demands, the trade-off it carries and the student it suits.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a family to the right class format in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, and the first conversation is about structure rather than about tutors. IB Gram asks which programme and year the student is in, which subjects and levels are in trouble, when the school's mock examinations fall, where you live, and which evenings are actually free. Format follows from those answers, and only then does a name go on a shortlist.

That sounds obvious. It is not how most enquiries start. Parents usually open with a subject and a request for the strongest available teacher, and the format then gets decided by accident, by whatever that teacher happens to run. So the conversation is deliberately turned around. A DP2 student in Powai with four subjects wobbling and mocks eight weeks away cannot be served by four separate weekly one-to-one slots; the week simply will not hold them. A Grade 9 student in Kondapur with one weak criterion in Individuals and Societies does not need a crash course. He needs an hour a week and somebody who reads his writing.

Once the shape is agreed, shortlisting begins. IB Gram puts forward tutors whose profiles are verified and who already teach that programme, subject and level in the format you have chosen, subject to availability in your locality and in your time slot. You see how each one structures a class of that type: what happens in the first fifteen minutes, how written work is returned, what the student is expected to do between sessions. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything, and if the fit turns out to be wrong you can ask for a different match.

Format is not permanent either. Many families run weekly one-to-one home tuition through the year, add a subject revision class in the weeks before mocks, then drop back to the weekly rhythm. Say that out loud at the start, so the tutor plans the year around it rather than being surprised in February.
items: 1. Tell us the programme, year, subjects and levels that are actually struggling.
2. Give the school's mock dates and the evenings your child is genuinely free.
3. Agree a format: one-to-one, a small group, a revision class or a holiday intensive.
4. Meet a shortlist of verified tutors who already run that format at that level.
5. Run a trial session, then confirm, change the match, or change the format itself.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP in India: which class format each stage can carry
contentBlocks.body:
Format has to match the stage, not only the subject. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) a class longer than about forty minutes stops being a class and becomes supervision, so a short one-to-one home session is usually the only format worth paying for at all. Group formats rarely hold a young child, and an online group almost never does.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, and every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. Those four scores add to a total out of 32, which the school converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A student is therefore never weak at Science in general. He is weak at one criterion, and that is a small enough target for a small group to hit. Three students working the same criterion task learn a great deal from hearing how the other two answered it.

MYP 5 brings the Personal Project and MYP 3 or 4 brings the Community Project. Both are the student's own work, so no class format should be built around completing them. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it; there is no single national MYP examination in India. Ask your coordinator before buying anything sold as MYP exam preparation.

The Diploma Programme (DP) changes the arithmetic. DP is two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four taken at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. An HL subject built on 240 hours cannot be rescued by a weekend batch. An SL revision block often can do real work.
items: PYP: short one-to-one home classes; group formats rarely hold a young child's attention
MYP: four criteria scored 0-8, a total out of 32, converted to a 1-7 grade
MYP 5 Personal Project and the MYP 3 or 4 Community Project stay the student's own work
DP: six subjects, three or four at Higher Level (240 hours), the rest Standard Level (150)
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points; 45 is the maximum, 24 the diploma minimum

contentBlocks.heading: Does batch size change what an IB subject class can do?
contentBlocks.body:
Yes, and the change is almost entirely about how much of your child's own writing gets read. Command terms decide IB marks: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent. Each one sets the depth an answer needs. A student who answers an evaluate question with a describe answer loses marks while feeling he knew the content perfectly well.

Catching that requires someone reading his sentences, not his final answers. In a one-to-one class the tutor reads two or three written responses inside the session and rewrites one of them with him, out loud, changing the verbs. In a group of three or four, one response per student is realistic in ninety minutes. In a batch of thirty, nobody's writing is read live, and work handed in comes back days later, often ticked rather than marked against the criterion it was set for.

That matters unevenly across subjects. IB Mathematics AA and AI carry long method-heavy questions where a batch can still teach a technique well, because the technique is the same for everyone in the room and repetition is what fixes it. IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology split down the middle: numerical work survives a batch comfortably, extended written explanation does not. IB Economics and IB English A are almost entirely writing, and a large batch teaches the content while leaving the actual assessed skill untouched.

So the honest rule is to pick the format by what is failing, not by the subject name on the invoice. If your child cannot do the question type at all, a batch or even a recorded course may be enough, and it will cost less per hour. If he can do the question type but keeps losing marks in how he writes the answer, only a format where his own script is read will move anything. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels and show exactly how marks were awarded. Ask any tutor to work from those rather than from their own notes.
items: Command terms set answer depth: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent
One-to-one: two or three written answers read and reworked inside the same session
Small group: roughly one written answer per student in a ninety-minute class
Large batch: technique taught well, individual scripts almost never read live
Ask the tutor to mark against official markschemes and subject reports from the school

contentBlocks.heading: IB tuition classes in India: what each region changes about the timetable
contentBlocks.body:
Geography decides how IB tuition classes in India are timetabled far more often than pedagogy does. In Delhi NCR the first question is whether a tutor can cross the city on a weekday evening at all. A family in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri usually has local supply. A family in Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad frequently does not, and evening traffic between Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Dwarka can stretch a short trip badly. Golf Course Road families often settle this with home classes on two weeknights and an online class on the third.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region splits along the same line. An IB tuition class in Mumbai booked for Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel or Malabar Hill is usually viable as a home visit, because the distances are short even when they are slow. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are a different calculation: a tutor living on the island city will not hold a seven o'clock slot in Kharghar through a monsoon week, and a small online group class is the format that actually survives July.

Hyderabad is the easiest metro for home formats. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Kokapet and the Financial District sit close enough together that an IB tuition class in Hyderabad can often be scheduled back to back for two children in one evening. Secunderabad is further out and usually needs an earlier start. In Chennai, an IB tuition class in Chennai for Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet or Nungambakkam behaves like a neighbourhood arrangement, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery families should assume the tutor arrives late at least once a month and should plan a hybrid week around it. Anna Nagar sits somewhere in between.

Gujarat runs on shorter distances and earlier evenings. Families in Satellite, Bodakdev or along SG Highway in Ahmedabad, and families in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, usually find local one-to-one supply for Mathematics and the sciences and go online for everything else. An IB tuition class in Ahmedabad often starts by six, which is an hour ahead of most Mumbai bookings. Bengaluru adds its own difficulty: an IB tuition class in Bangalore run from Whitefield or Sarjapur into the centre is rarely worth the travel either way, so online becomes the default. An IB tuition class in Pune around Koregaon Park and an IB tuition class in Kolkata around Salt Lake both sit in thinner markets, where a parent searching for IB classes near me may find nobody at all teaching the level required.
items: Delhi NCR: Greater Noida and Ghaziabad families usually need a hybrid week, not daily visits
Mumbai: Bandra and Worli suit home classes; Kharghar and Thane suit online groups better
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Kondapur and Jubilee Hills allow back-to-back home classes for siblings
Chennai: OMR and Perungudi bookings should assume monsoon disruption and hold a spare slot
Gujarat: Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat and Vadodara classes usually start earlier in the evening
Thinner markets: an online group often exists where no local tutor teaches that level

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars in India and where each class format fits
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and IB schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May examination session; November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. Every format you buy should be planned backwards from those two dates.

Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore all work to similar pressure points, even though each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

The pressure is not spread evenly through the year. Internal deadlines cluster, mocks arrive, and a class booked in a quiet week quietly disappears in a busy one. A plan that survives contact with a real school calendar looks like this:

1. Twelve to sixteen weeks before the May session, fix the weekly one-to-one or small group slots and stop moving them.
2. Six to ten weeks out, once mock results are back, convert one weekly slot into a subject revision class aimed only at the question types the mock exposed.
3. Two to four weeks out, switch to short, frequent past-paper sessions under timed conditions and cut everything that is not examined.

Holiday intensives sit outside that line. The long summer break and the Diwali break are the two windows where an intensive course can add ground rather than simply add hours, because the school is not also setting work at the same time. Book intensives into the breaks. Keep term time for the weekly rhythm, and keep one evening a week with no class on it at all.
items: The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March; schools mostly enter the May session
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before the May session
May results are released in early July, which frames any retake conversation
Book intensive courses into the summer and Diwali breaks rather than into term weeks
Keep weekly slots fixed through the mock period and change the content instead

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online classes or a hybrid week?
contentBlocks.body:
Take the same class and change only where it happens. A home class puts the tutor in the room: he sees the student's actual working on paper, the phone face-down or not, the noise from the next room, and the way a question gets abandoned halfway through. That visibility is the whole argument for home classes, and it is worth more for younger students and for anyone whose real problem is habits rather than content.

An online class trades that visibility for reach and reliability. Nobody travels, so a Tuesday slot at seven stays a Tuesday slot at seven, in Kharghar as much as in Bandra. A specialist who teaches an uncommon Higher Level subject may live in another city entirely, and online is the only way your child ever meets her. The cost is supervision. A student who drifts online drifts quietly, and a parent ends up doing some of the work the tutor would otherwise do simply by being present in the room.

Hybrid is the arrangement most families settle into once they stop treating it as a compromise. One home session a week, usually the longer one, for written work done under the tutor's eye, and one or two shorter online sessions for doubt-solving, past-paper walkthroughs and marking feedback. It keeps the in-person diagnosis and removes three trips across a metro from the week.

The trade-off stated plainly: home classes give the best information about how your child actually works, online classes give the best access to the right teacher and the most dependable timetable, and a hybrid week gives you most of both at the price of slightly more coordination. Pick home tuition if the problem is behaviour or basics. Pick online if the problem is finding anyone who teaches the subject at that level. Pick hybrid if the problem is the calendar, which in most Indian metros it is.
items: Home classes: the tutor sees paper working, distractions and abandoned questions directly
Online classes: no travel, so the weeknight slot holds through monsoon and exam weeks
Online reaches a specialist for an uncommon Higher Level subject in another city
Hybrid: one longer home session for written work, shorter online sessions for doubts
Online needs more parental supervision, especially below Middle Years Programme 4

contentBlocks.heading: How is a tutor checked before an IB class begins?
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile goes live on IB Gram, identity and claimed teaching experience are checked, and the programme, subjects and levels a tutor says he teaches are recorded against what he can actually show. A profile claiming Higher Level Physics and Standard Level Mathematics AI has to be consistent with the qualifications and the teaching history behind it. That is what verification means here, and it is worth saying plainly what it does not mean.

It does not mean anyone has watched every lesson. It does not mean a tutor is right for your particular child. And no platform can see in advance whether a tutor will hold a Thursday evening slot in Velachery through an exam week in June. Those are things a family discovers, which is exactly why a trial session exists.

For a class format specifically, there are checks worth doing yourself in the first conversation. Ask how many students are in the group and whether that number is capped in writing. Ask who teaches it every week, because in some batch arrangements the teacher rotates between terms without anyone telling the parents. Ask how written work is collected, marked and returned, and how long that takes; a group class that returns marked scripts within a few days is doing something a batch of thirty structurally cannot. Ask what happens when your child misses a class, and whether the content is repeated, recorded or simply lost.

Then watch the trial for one thing above everything else. Does the tutor read your child's own writing, or does he only present his own? A class in any format that never touches the student's script is a lecture. Lectures are useful, cheaper per hour and available in recorded form, but they are not what most families believe they are buying when they book tuition.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed teaching experience are checked before a profile goes live
Verification is not observation, so treat the trial session as your own check
Ask whether group size is capped in writing and whether the same teacher takes every class
Ask how written work is collected, marked and returned, and how long that takes
Ask what happens to the content when your child misses a session

contentBlocks.heading: One-to-one, small batch, revision class and intensive, compared plainly
contentBlocks.body:
IB tuition classes in India are sold under four names, and the names are not standardised, so ask what is actually being described before you compare two arrangements.

One-to-one is a class of one, usually sixty to ninety minutes, where the order of work is set by the student's gaps rather than by a course plan. It is the only format in which the first two or three sessions can be spent diagnosing rather than teaching. It suits a student who is failing for a reason nobody has yet identified, a Higher Level student who needs depth rather than coverage, and any student whose difficulty is in how he writes answers. It is the wrong purchase for a student who has simply not practised enough. That student needs questions, not conversation.

A small batch of three or four is a genuinely different product, not a discounted one-to-one. Three students at similar levels, working the same question, get something one-to-one cannot give them: they hear a wrong answer explained. The format collapses if the three are at different stages, if the group grows past five, or if the tutor cannot see all three scripts inside the session. It suits confident students who need pace and comparison, and it suits two families who want to share a slot.

A subject revision class is time-boxed and question-led. It should not reteach the course. It should work through the question types the student has already got wrong, using past papers and markschemes, and it should end when the mock ends. Run it for six to ten weeks, not all year.

An intensive course compresses a term of revision into a holiday block: several hours a day for one or two weeks, usually across two or three subjects. Intensives work when the student already knows the material and needs volume and timing practice. They fail when used as a rescue for content never learned, because three hours a day for ten days cannot replace 150 hours of Standard Level teaching, let alone 240.
items: One-to-one: pace set by the student, and the only format that can properly diagnose first
Small batch of three or four: peer comparison and pace, if the levels genuinely match
Revision class: six to ten weeks, question-led, built from past papers and markschemes
Intensive course: a holiday block for volume and timing, not for learning content afresh
Ask what a provider means by each name before comparing two quoted arrangements

contentBlocks.heading: What progress should look like across a term in India
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the IB does not arrive as a jump in a percentage, because there is no percentage. In the Middle Years Programme you are watching criterion scores out of 8 move, one criterion at a time, and a student who goes from 4 to 6 on the criterion he was weakest at has had a good term even if the overall 1 to 7 grade has not shifted yet. In the Diploma Programme the visible signal is a mock script that loses marks in fewer places, not a whole grade appearing.

A reasonable timeline runs like this. After two or three classes you should be able to say what the tutor thinks is wrong, in one sentence, and it should either match what the school said or explain why it does not. After a month there should be evidence, meaning marked work with a pattern in it. After a term, a measurable change in the specific thing that was identified. If after a month nobody can tell you what is being fixed, the arrangement is the problem, not your child.

Be realistic about what a change of format can move. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any arrangement sold on that basis should be treated with real scepticism. Starting an intensive four weeks before the May session in a subject that was never properly learned narrows what is possible to exam technique and partial credit. That is still worth having. It is not the same as two years of teaching, and an honest tutor will say so in the first conversation rather than the last.

Some families do not need IB tuition classes in India at all. If the report says the student is coasting rather than struggling, the fix is usually work volume and a conversation with the subject teacher. A good tutor will tell you that in the trial, and lose the booking.
items: MYP: watch one criterion score out of 8 move before the overall 1-7 grade does
DP: watch a mock script lose marks in fewer places, not a whole grade jump
After three classes the tutor should name the problem in a single sentence
After a month there should be marked work showing a pattern, not just attendance
A late intensive can improve technique; it cannot replace 240 hours of Higher Level teaching

contentBlocks.heading: Preparing for the first IB home tuition class
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first class, collect four things: the most recent report with its criterion or subject comments, two pieces of marked written work, the school calendar with mock dates marked on it, and a list of the evenings your child is genuinely free after school activities. Most families bring the first and forget the other three, and the first class then goes on questions the paperwork would have answered in a minute.

For a home class, decide where in the house it happens before the tutor arrives. A dining table with the television off beats a bedroom desk in most flats, because a parent passing through is a mild and useful form of supervision. Tell your building or society gate about a regular visitor so that the first fifteen minutes are not spent at reception on a weekday evening. Keep one folder at home for the tutor's worked examples so they do not vanish into a school bag by Thursday.

The first class itself should not be a lesson. Expect the tutor to look at the marked work, ask your child to attempt one question cold, watch how he starts it, and ask him to explain his reasoning out loud. Expect to be told something slightly uncomfortable at the end of it. Expect a plan for the next three or four sessions with the format stated explicitly: weekly one-to-one home classes, a small online group, or a revision block that ends at the mocks.

And if your child is in DP2 with mocks close, say so in the first message rather than in the first class. The plan is different when the calendar is short, and a good tutor will tell you which of the four formats is now realistic and which one is not.
items: Bring the latest report, two marked scripts and the school calendar with mock dates
List the evenings your child is genuinely free after school activities and travel
Agree a fixed study space at home and tell the society gate about a regular visitor
Expect the first class to diagnose rather than teach, and to end with a written plan
Say early if mocks are close, because the realistic format changes with the calendar

faqs.question: Which IB class format suits a DP2 student eight weeks before mocks?
faqs.answer: Usually a weekly one-to-one class plus a short subject revision block, not a new course. Eight weeks is enough to change technique and not enough to relearn a syllabus, so the work should start from the question types the last set of marked papers exposed. Keep the weekly slot fixed through the mock period. Add a second, shorter session in the two subjects that are actually costing points, and drop anything that is not examined. If three or more subjects are failing at once, fix the weakest two first, because spreading eight weeks across four subjects usually moves none of them.

faqs.question: How many students should an IB batch class have?
faqs.answer: Small enough that every student's written work is read during the class, which in practice means three or four. Past five, the tutor stops reading scripts live and starts lecturing, and the format quietly becomes a cheaper version of the classroom your child already sits in all day. Ask whether the cap is written down or merely aspirational, and ask what happens when a sixth family wants to join mid-term. A group of three at the same level and the same option is a good class. A group of six at mixed levels wastes everyone's weeknight.

faqs.question: Do IB revision classes before mocks cover anything new?
faqs.answer: They should not, and that is the point of them. A revision class is question-led: it works through the question types the student has already got wrong, using past papers, markschemes and subject reports that come through the school or the IB's official channels. If a revision class is introducing fresh content four weeks before a mock, either the school is behind or the class has been mis-sold. Ask for the list of topics it will cover before you book, and check that list against your child's own marked work rather than against the full syllabus.

faqs.question: Is an IB crash course before the May session worth booking?
faqs.answer: It is worth booking for a student who knows the material and needs volume, and it is a poor use of money for one who does not. An intensive compresses several hours a day across one or two weeks, usually in the holiday before the session, and what it genuinely adds is timed practice, pacing and exposure to unfamiliar question wording. It cannot substitute for the 150 hours behind a Standard Level subject or the 240 behind a Higher Level one. Before booking, ask what the daily schedule looks like and how much of it is the student writing rather than the tutor talking.

faqs.question: Can a home class be scheduled after school activities on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families it is the only slot that exists, but be honest about what is left of the child by then. A class starting at eight after sport and travel will be shorter in real attention than the clock suggests, so a sixty-minute home class often beats a ninety-minute one on a weekday. Many families keep one longer weekend home class for written work and one shorter weeknight session online for doubt-solving. Tell the tutor the true finishing time of school activities rather than the timetabled one, or the first month will be spent adjusting.

faqs.question: What if a home class is missed because the tutor is stuck in Mumbai traffic?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because at some point it will. The workable arrangement is that a tutor who cannot reach Powai, Thane or Kharghar in time converts that session into an online class from wherever he is, and a session cancelled with notice is rescheduled rather than lost. What you should not accept is a pattern. One delayed evening in a monsoon month is weather. Three in a term means the travel distance was never realistic, and the arrangement should move to a hybrid week or to a tutor who lives closer.

faqs.question: Nobody near Greater Noida teaches Higher Level Economics. What format works?
faqs.answer: An online one-to-one class, almost certainly, with a tutor who may live in another city entirely. Supply for Higher Level options thins quickly outside the central pockets of Delhi NCR, and a family in Greater Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad can spend months waiting for a local match that never appears. Online removes the travel constraint on both sides and widens the pool to anyone teaching that option anywhere in India, subject to availability. If your child also needs supervision, run a hybrid week: online for Economics, and a local home class for whichever subject does have local supply.

faqs.question: Does an online group class work for a Middle Years Programme student?
faqs.answer: It can, from roughly MYP 4 upwards, and it is considerably harder below that. MYP work is assessed against four criteria, each scored 0 to 8, and criterion work suits a small group because students learn a great deal from seeing how somebody else answered the same task. The limit is attention. A thirteen-year-old in a group of four online needs a tutor who calls on each student every few minutes and a parent within earshot. Below MYP 4, a short home class usually achieves more in less time and with less negotiation.

faqs.question: Can one class format cover two children in the same house?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends far more on the gap between them than on the subject. Two students in the same year taking the same option can share a small group class at home, and in Hyderabad or Ahmedabad, where distances are short, families often book two back-to-back one-to-one home classes on the same evening instead. What rarely works is a single class split between a Grade 9 student and a DP1 sibling. The content diverges immediately, and both children end up with half a session each.

faqs.question: How do we tell after a month that the format is wrong rather than the tutor?
faqs.answer: Look at what the sessions are being consumed by. If the tutor explains well but spends the class talking because four other students are waiting, the format is wrong and one-to-one will fix it. If the tutor explains well and your child still cannot start a question alone, the format may be right and the missing piece is practice volume between sessions. A tutor who cannot tell you what is being fixed, in one sentence, after four sessions is a tutor problem, and you can ask for a different match.

faqs.question: Should we drop classes entirely during the Diwali break?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but the shape should change. Term-time weekly classes exist to keep pace with school, and a break is the one window where an intensive or a holiday block can add ground, because no new school work is landing at the same time. For a DP1 student the Diwali break is a sensible place to recover a subject that slipped in the first term. For a younger student, stopping completely for a fortnight is usually right, and a tutor who insists otherwise is selling hours.

faqs.question: Can a class help with the Personal Project or an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Only within the limits your school and the IB set, and those limits are stricter than most families assume. A tutor may teach the skills behind the work, discuss a plan, ask questions about a draft and explain the criteria being applied. A tutor may not write, edit or contribute content to a submission. The Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 are the student's own work, and any class sold as project completion support should be refused. Confirm the boundary with your coordinator before booking anything.

comparison.heading: How do the four IB class formats compare across India?
comparison.intro: Each of these four formats wins something real. One-to-one at home buys attention and information about how your child actually works. One-to-one online buys the right specialist and a slot that holds. A small online group buys peer comparison at a lower cost per family. A large batch buys structured coverage cheaply. The trade-off that usually decides the choice is how much of your child's own written work needs reading every week.

rows.label: Attention per student
cells: The whole session on one student, with paper working and hesitation visible to the tutor
The whole session on one student, though a screen hides some of how he works
Split three or four ways, so each student gets a share of live feedback
Little individual attention, because questions are answered for the whole room

rows.label: Syllabus fit (HL, SL, AA, AI, MYP criteria)
cells: Plan built around one student's Higher Level or Standard Level gaps and weak criteria
Same personalisation, plus easier access to a tutor who teaches that exact option
Works only if the group shares the level and option, such as three AA SL students
Fixed course plan, so AI or Standard Level students often sit through the wrong material

rows.label: Travel and time in Indian cities
cells: The tutor travels, so a Powai or Greater Noida booking can lose a slot to traffic
Nobody travels, so the weeknight slot holds through monsoon weeks and exam weeks
Nobody travels, and one start time can be agreed for the whole small group
The student travels to a centre, losing study hours on Chennai and Delhi NCR evenings

rows.label: Marking turnaround on written work
cells: Scripts read inside the session and rewritten with the student the same evening
Scripts shared on screen or photographed, then annotated live during the class
Usually one script per student per class, with the rest returned within a few days
Slowest of the four, and work often returns ticked rather than marked to a criterion

rows.label: Cost structure
cells: Highest per hour, with the tutor's travel time built into the arrangement
Lower per hour than a home visit, because no travel time is being paid for
Shared between three or four families, so noticeably lower for each of them
Lowest per hour of any format, which is its strongest and most honest argument

rows.label: Trial before committing
cells: A demo session at home can be arranged before the family commits to anything
A trial is easy to schedule and easy to repeat with a second tutor
A trial depends on the group having a free place at your child's level
Usually a sample class rather than a trial matched to your own child

rows.label: Continuity across a school year
cells: One tutor holds the whole history, including which topics failed in DP1
The same continuity, and the tutor remains reachable if the family relocates
Continuity depends on the other students staying in the group all year
Teachers may rotate between terms, so ask who takes the class each week

rows.label: Who it suits best
cells: Younger students, habit problems, and anyone whose written answers need watching
Higher Level and uncommon subjects, and families outside the main metro clusters
Confident students who need pace, comparison and a shared weeknight slot
Students who already know the content and need structured volume before mocks

h1: IB Coaching in India and Why the Coaching Model Needs Changing
heroTitle: IB Coaching in India, Honestly Assessed
heroSubtitle: Most families searching for IB coaching want what coaching gave them for board and entrance exams: a batch, a timetable, a syllabus drilled hard. The Diploma Programme does not reward that method evenly. This page explains where the model fits, where it fails, and what to check before enrolling.
introSummary: IB coaching in India usually means a centre with batches and a fixed timetable, and for a criterion-marked, coursework-heavy programme that model fits some subjects well and others badly, which is why many families end up combining it with home tuition. Coaching grew out of entrance-exam preparation, where one correct answer key and heavy repetition win marks. The International Baccalaureate (IB) marks against criteria and command terms, and a large share of the grade comes from work the student produces individually. So the question is not whether coaching is good or bad. It is which parts of your child's problem a batch can solve, which parts need one-to-one attention at home or online, and what you should ask any centre before you pay for a term.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram build a shortlist instead of a batch in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks what the student is actually stuck on, and it shortlists verified tutor profiles that match the board, subject, level, school calendar, locality and schedule you describe. No batch is formed around your child. The match is built around one student's evidence, and a demo session can be arranged before you commit to anything.

The questions asked at that first stage are deliberately narrow. Which programme: Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) or Diploma Programme (DP)? Which subjects, and at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL)? What did the last report say, criterion by criterion? Is the problem content the student never understood, or a way of answering that loses marks on material they do understand? A coaching centre rarely asks the second question, because its timetable was fixed before your child walked in.

Location comes next, and it changes the answer more than parents expect. A family in Gachibowli or Kondapur has a different set of realistic options from a family in Indore or Dehradun. Where a verified tutor can reach the house at a workable hour, home tuition is usually the better first choice. Where the subject is thinly taught locally, online is not a compromise, it is the only way to reach someone who has taught that syllabus.

Then it is your turn to check. Ask for the tutor's subject and level, ask how they would handle a piece of internal assessment (IA) without crossing the IB's academic integrity line, and watch the demo for whether the student talks or only listens. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. That is a normal request, not a complaint, and it is far easier than withdrawing mid-term from a batch you have already paid for.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, in writing if you prefer.
2. Answer questions on board, subject, level, school calendar, locality and weekly schedule.
3. Receive a shortlist of verified tutor profiles matched to that description.
4. Sit through a demo or trial session before committing to anything.
5. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, subject to tutor availability.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: what a coaching batch can and cannot carry
contentBlocks.body:
The IB is not one qualification. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) has no external examinations, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years and is assessed against criteria, and the Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year course most centres actually mean when they advertise. Batch teaching behaves very differently in each, and IB coaching in India rarely says which one it means.

In the DP a student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. A batch can march a room through HL content. It cannot march a room through an EE research question, because every student has a different one.

The MYP resists batching harder. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8; the total out of 32 converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A student losing marks on criterion C in a science and a student losing them on criterion A are not in the same lesson, even when they share a desk. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and both are individual work. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so ask yours before assuming any examination exists.

PYP is the clearest case. With no external examination to prepare for, a batch for a primary child is often solving a problem the family does not have. Reading, number sense and confidence respond to a patient adult at home, not to a timetable.
items: DP: six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level
HL carries 240 recommended teaching hours, SL 150, each graded 1 to 7
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45
MYP: four criteria per subject, each scored 0 to 8, totalling 32
Personal Project in MYP 5, Community Project in MYP 3 or 4
PYP has no external examination, so ask what a batch would even cover

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects respond to drilling, and which resist it?
contentBlocks.body:
Drill works where the marks come from technique repeated accurately, and it works badly where the marks come from judgement. So Mathematics and parts of Physics and Chemistry take reasonably well to batch practice, while English A, Economics coursework and every internal assessment need one student's work read closely by one teacher.

Take IB Mathematics. Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) are different courses, not easier and harder versions of one course, and at Higher Level each makes demands the other does not. A batch can run past-paper practice in AA HL effectively, provided every student in the room is on AA HL. Sit an AI SL student in that batch and the hours are wasted politely.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology split down the middle. Definitions, standard derivations and calculation routines drill well. The data question, the extended written answer and the practical write-up do not, because they are marked on reasoning a batch teacher cannot inspect twenty times over in one sitting. Economics is the sharpest example: the internal assessment asks the student to analyse material they selected themselves, and nobody else can choose it or write it for them.

English A is where batch teaching most often disappoints families who switched from CBSE or ICSE. There is no answer key. A student who has learned to reproduce a model answer will hit a ceiling fast, and the way out is a tutor reading their paragraphs, asking what the command term demanded, and sending them back to rewrite the weakest one. That is slow work, and it is one-to-one work, at home or online. It is also the work that moves a 4 to a 5 in a subject where content revision has stopped paying.
items: Mathematics AA and AI are separate courses, not easy and hard versions
Calculation routines and definitions drill well in a batch setting
Data questions and extended answers need one marker reading one script
Economics internal assessment uses material the student selected themselves
English A has no answer key, so memorised model answers hit a ceiling

contentBlocks.heading: IB coaching in India: what the search looks like region by region
contentBlocks.body:
IB coaching in India is not one market. Searches for IB coaching in Mumbai, IB coaching in Delhi, IB coaching in Bangalore and IB coaching in Hyderabad all return centres, but what those centres can offer depends almost entirely on how far your family sits from them on a weekday evening.

In Delhi NCR the question is the crossing. A student in South Delhi or Vasant Kunj can often reach a centre in the same part of the city, but a family in Dwarka, Faridabad, Ghaziabad or Greater Noida is looking at a trip in each direction on top of school and CAS commitments. Evening traffic between Noida and central Delhi can stretch a short trip badly. This is where a home tutor coming to the flat, or an online session with no travel at all, beats the batch on hours alone. Chanakyapuri, Golf Course Road and Sector 128 Noida families ask the same question in different words.

In Hyderabad the IB families cluster around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad a different drive again. Searches for IB coaching in Hyderabad often end in home tuition once a parent adds up the return trip. The same holds in Powai, Bandra and Thane, in Whitefield, Indiranagar and Sarjapur Road, in Koregaon Park and Baner, and in Adyar and along Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) in Chennai. IB coaching in Pune and IB coaching in Chennai are supply questions as much as distance questions.

Outside the metros the picture changes. In Gujarat, families in Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev, along SG Highway, and in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot find general tuition easily and IB-specific teaching much less easily; IB coaching in Ahmedabad is a real search with thin local supply behind it. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar and Kanpur, and across central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Nashik and Goa, a batch for one HL subject may not exist at all. Typing IB coaching near me there returns entrance-exam centres. Online tutoring is the honest answer, and a hybrid arrangement, with a local tutor at home for routine work and a specialist online for the hardest paper, is often better still. IB coaching in Kolkata sits between the two pictures.
items: Delhi NCR: a Dwarka or Ghaziabad family loses the evening to the trip
Hyderabad: Gachibowli and Kondapur cluster tightly, Secunderabad does not
Mumbai and Pune: Powai, Thane, Koregaon Park and Baner face the same arithmetic
Gujarat: Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat and Vadodara have thin IB-specific supply
Indore, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Dehradun: online or hybrid is usually the only route

contentBlocks.heading: How the school calendar in India collides with coaching timetables
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session rather than November. May results are released in early July. Those two dates set everything, and most coaching timetables are built around a different calendar entirely. IB coaching in India is sold on a term basis that rarely maps onto a school's own deadlines.

Work backwards from May. DP1 ends with a long break that families routinely waste, and it is the last real stretch of time before internal assessment deadlines start landing on top of each other in DP2. Schools set their own internal deadlines well ahead of the IB's, so the pressure point arrives earlier than parents expect. By the time a batch starts its revision programme in the new calendar year, the coursework that carries a real share of the grade has usually been submitted already.

Add the rest of the school's expectations. CAS has to be completed, the Extended Essay has a supervisor and a set of school checkpoints, and mock examinations sit in the middle of all of it. Families at international schools in India also deal with school-set predicted grades, which matter for university applications long before the May papers. A centre that cannot tell you when your child's school submits coursework cannot plan around it, and a tutor who does not ask is not planning either.

One thing to be clear about. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. School names come up in these conversations because parents raise them, and a tutor who has taught students from a particular school knows its rhythm, but no platform speaks for a school. Confirm every deadline and every requirement with your child's coordinator.
items: The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March
Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session
May results are released in early July
School coursework deadlines usually fall well before the IB's own
Predicted grades matter for applications long before the papers

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which format fits after a coaching batch?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition suits a student who needs presence and routine, online suits a student who needs a specialist their city does not have, and hybrid suits most families in between. The batch is a fourth option that trades attention for cost. That is the whole comparison, and everything else is detail about your own week.

Home classes have a physical advantage that is easy to underrate. The tutor sees the desk, the phone, the notes, the half-finished problem set. A student who performs attentiveness in a classroom cannot perform it across a table. For MYP students and younger DP students that presence often matters more than the tutor's subject depth. The cost is travel: the tutor's time in transit is time you are effectively paying for, and in most Indian cities it narrows the slots available on a weekday evening.

Online removes travel and widens supply to the whole country. For a thinly taught HL subject, or for TOK and the Extended Essay, it is often the only route to someone who has actually taught it. The screen costs something in return. A tired student at nine in the evening is easier to lose online than across a table, and a shared document with an annotated past paper needs a tutor who is fluent with the tools rather than fighting them.

Hybrid is underused. A tutor at home once a week for the subject the student is failing, plus an online specialist for the one paper nobody local teaches, covers both problems without doubling the travel. Families in Nagpur, Raipur and Bhopal end up here often, and so do families in Thane and Greater Noida who simply lose too much of the evening to the road. Run it for a month, then look at the student's own marked work and decide what to keep.
items: Home tuition: presence, routine and a tutor who sees the actual desk
Online: reach a specialist for a subject nobody teaches in your city
Hybrid: a home tutor weekly plus an online specialist for one paper
Batch: lower cost per hour, far less attention per student
Travel time in Indian cities decides how many evening slots exist

contentBlocks.heading: What should you verify before enrolling anywhere in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Verify three things before any money changes hands: who exactly will teach, what they have taught before on this programme and at this level, and what happens if it does not work. A brochure answers none of the three. The same three questions apply to IB coaching in India whether the provider is a centre, an agency or one person working alone.

On IB Gram, tutor profiles are verified before they go live, and a family can ask for a demo or trial session before committing. Verification means checking identity and claimed teaching background. It does not mean the platform has watched every lesson, and no honest platform will tell you otherwise. What verification buys you is a shorter list of plausible people. What the demo buys you is evidence.

At a centre the questions are different, because the person teaching can change. Ask who teaches the Friday batch in February, not only who is teaching the trial in August. Ask whether the person taking HL Chemistry has taught the current syllabus, or a different one some years ago. Ask what the centre does if your child is the only AI SL student in a room of AA HL students. Ask for the refund and transfer terms in writing before you pay for a term, and read what happens if you leave halfway.

Then check yourself, over the first month. Is the student producing work between sessions, or only during them? Can they explain what a command term is asking them to do? Has anyone shown you a piece of their marked work with the criterion written beside it? If the answers are no, the arrangement is not working yet, whatever it cost, and you should say so early rather than at the end of the term.
items: Ask for the individual teacher's name, subject and level, in writing
Ask whether they have taught the current syllabus, not an older one
Ask for refund and transfer terms before paying for a term
Use the demo to watch who does most of the talking
Check after a month: is the student working between sessions?

contentBlocks.heading: Where coaching in India came from, and what it was built to do
contentBlocks.body:
Coaching, as the word is used in India, is a specific invention. It was built for competitive entrance examinations: a fixed syllabus, a single correct answer, a very large number of candidates and a ranking at the end. In that setting the model is genuinely efficient. One strong teacher, a hall full of students, a tested sequence of problems, relentless timed practice. Marks respond.

Families carried that model into every other examination because it worked, and because it is legible. You can see the timetable. You can see the test scores going up week by week. Parents who cleared their own examinations that way trust it, and a centre advertising IB coaching classes is trading on that trust rather than on anything specific to the programme.

The IB was designed against almost every assumption in that model. There is no single answer key, because most marks are awarded against criteria and command terms. A large share of the grade comes from work each student produces individually: internal assessments, the Extended Essay, the Personal Project in MYP 5. The IB's academic integrity rules are explicit that the work is the student's own, that a teacher may give feedback on one draft, and that nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit a submission. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone.

So the mismatch is structural rather than a matter of effort. A batch cannot give criterion-level feedback on twenty different pieces of individual work in one evening. It can teach content, run timed practice and hold a student to a schedule. Families searching for IB coaching in India are often looking for that third thing, discipline, and calling it the first. Worth naming, because discipline can be bought more cheaply and far more precisely than a term of batch classes.
items: Coaching was built for ranked entrance examinations with one answer key
The IB marks against criteria and command terms instead
Internal assessment is individual work the school submits and checks
A teacher may give feedback on one draft, and no more
Nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit a submission
A batch can hold a schedule; it cannot mark twenty different projects

contentBlocks.heading: What real progress looks like, and when home tuition is the wrong answer
contentBlocks.body:
Give any arrangement about six weeks before judging it, and judge it on the student's own marked work rather than on how the sessions feel. Early progress in the IB rarely looks like a grade moving. It looks like a student who can say what a question is asking before they start answering it.

In weeks two to four the change should show up in process: notes organised by criterion rather than by date, a draft started earlier than last time, fewer blank starts on a problem set. By week six you should be able to see a marked piece where the teacher's comment matches what the tutor said would improve. If nothing in the student's folder has changed by then, the problem is the match, the format or the diagnosis, and adding more hours will not fix any of the three.

Now the honest limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anyone implying otherwise is selling something. Starting in the second half of DP2 narrows what is possible, because the coursework has largely gone in and only examination technique is left. A student who is not doing the work between sessions will not improve regardless of who teaches them, and more sessions can make that worse by creating the comfortable feeling that the work is being handled by somebody else.

And sometimes home tuition is the wrong answer. A student who is coping but anxious may need less scheduled input, not more. A student whose difficulty is one unit in one subject may need three sessions, not a term. A student carrying six subjects, CAS and an Extended Essay who is already drowning does not need a seventh commitment; they need someone to help them plan the term. Say that out loud when you enquire, and treat a provider who agrees with you as a better sign than one who agrees with your wallet.
items: Weeks two to four: better notes, earlier drafts, fewer blank starts
Week six: a marked piece that matches what the tutor predicted
No tutor can guarantee a grade, whatever the format
Starting late in DP2 narrows what tutoring can still change
Sometimes the answer is fewer commitments, not another one

contentBlocks.heading: Starting out in India: what to prepare before the first home session
contentBlocks.body:
Before you enquire anywhere, put four things in one place: the last school report with the criterion comments intact, a recent marked piece of work, the school's deadline calendar for the term, and an honest note of which two evenings a week are genuinely free. That packet answers most of the questions a good match depends on, and it saves a fortnight of guessing.

When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, level, the school calendar, your locality and your schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who fit, subject to availability. You will be asked where sessions should run: at home, online, or a mix of the two. Say if a weekday evening slot is the only realistic one, because that single constraint decides the shortlist in most Indian cities.

The first home session should not be a lecture. A good tutor spends much of it diagnosing: watching the student attempt a question, asking why they chose that method, reading one piece of their marked work against the criterion, and asking what the school has already said about it. You should come away with a plan for the next four sessions and one specific thing the student will do before the next one.

If the fit is wrong after the trial, say so and ask for a different match. Nobody is offended by that, and a platform that treats it as a complaint has told you something useful. Getting this right in the first month is worth more than months of persistence with an arrangement that was never going to work.
items: Bring the last report with criterion comments, not only the grades
Bring one recent marked piece of the student's own work
Know the school's coursework deadlines for this term
Decide which two evenings a week are genuinely free
Ask for a demo or trial before committing, subject to availability

faqs.question: Is IB coaching the same thing as IB tuition?
faqs.answer: No, though the two words are used interchangeably in India. Coaching normally means a batch at a centre with a fixed timetable and a shared sequence of material, while tuition usually means one-to-one teaching at your home or online, built around one student's gaps. The distinction matters because the Diploma Programme puts a large share of the grade into individual coursework that a batch cannot mark twenty times over. Ask any provider which of the two they actually run before you enrol.

faqs.question: Does a coaching batch work for Higher Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: It can, provided every student in the room is on the same course and the same level. Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) are different courses, and an AI Standard Level student sitting through AA Higher Level practice gains very little from the hour. Batches suit repeated technique: algebraic manipulation, standard methods, timed practice under pressure. They suit an unresolved conceptual gap far less well, because the teacher cannot stop the whole room to rebuild one student's foundation.

faqs.question: What should I ask a coaching centre before paying for a term?
faqs.answer: Ask who will teach, not what the centre claims about itself. Get the individual teacher's name, the subjects and levels they have taught, and whether they have taught the current syllabus. Ask how many students sit in the batch and how mixed it is by level. Ask exactly what help is given with internal assessment, and listen for whether the answer respects the IB's rules. Then ask for refund and transfer terms in writing. A centre that will not put those in writing has already answered you.

faqs.question: Can a coaching centre or a tutor help with internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only within strict limits. The work must be the student's own. A teacher may give feedback on one draft; nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit the submission. A good tutor teaches the underlying skill, questions the reasoning, points at a criterion and asks the student to reread their own paragraph against it. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB. Anyone offering to fix a draft for your child is risking the diploma.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor come to our locality on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Usually yes in the larger metros, subject to tutor availability and the traffic between the tutor and your area. Weekday evening slots are the most requested and the first to go, so a family in Dwarka, Thane or Whitefield that can offer a fixed weekly time will fill it more easily than one asking for a different slot each week. If your locality sits far from where tutors for that subject live, a hybrid pattern, home classes for one subject and online for another, works better than waiting for the perfect match.

faqs.question: There is no IB coaching centre anywhere near us. What now?
faqs.answer: Go online, and stop treating it as the second-best option. Outside the metros, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jaipur, Dehradun, Rajkot or Vadodara, the centres that exist are almost always built for entrance examinations rather than for criterion-marked coursework. A local general tutor can still help with foundations and routine at home, while an online specialist handles the actual IB subject and its assessment. That combination reaches further than anything within driving distance of most Indian towns.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in during home classes?
faqs.answer: For a young child sometimes, for a Diploma Programme student rarely. Presence in the room changes how a teenager answers a question, and the tutor needs to hear the wrong answer to find the gap behind it. Stay in the house, keep the door open, and stay out of the lesson itself. For a Primary Years Programme child, sitting nearby for the first session or two is reasonable, then step back. Ask instead for a short written note after each session; that tells you more than listening would.

faqs.question: My child has been in a batch for a month with no change. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Look at the marked work before changing anything. Ask for a recent script and check whether the losses are content the student never learned or a way of answering that costs marks on material they know. A content gap can justify staying, if the batch is genuinely covering it. Everything else points to one-to-one, because the fix requires somebody reading this student's own writing. Raise it with the centre first, in writing, and ask what they propose. Then decide, rather than stacking a second commitment on the first.

faqs.question: Is online coaching really as effective as sitting in a classroom?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma Programme subjects a well-run online session beats a poorly matched local classroom, and loses to a good home tutor for younger students. What online buys is the right teacher, which matters most for thinly taught subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. What it costs is attention late in the evening, and the informal signals a tutor picks up sitting in the room. Judge it on the same evidence as anything else: the student's own marked work after six weeks.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we take outside school?
faqs.answer: Start with one, and rarely go beyond two at a time. A Diploma Programme student already carries six subjects, Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and every added session removes time from independent work, which is where much of the grade is actually earned. If three subjects look weak, treat the weakest first and reassess after six weeks. Families who book everything at once usually cancel most of it by the second term anyway.

faqs.question: Do coaching centres plan around the May examination session?
faqs.answer: The good ones do, and it is a fair test of whether a centre understands the programme at all. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, results come out in early July, and a school's own coursework deadlines fall well before the IB's. A centre planning revision on a generic calendar, without asking when your child's school submits coursework, is running a timetable rather than a plan. Ask them to show you how their term maps onto your school's deadlines.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss a scheduled home session?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because at some point it will. Ask whether a session cancelled with notice is rescheduled or forfeited, how much notice counts as notice, and what happens when the tutor cancels instead. For home tuition the answer is often a rescheduled weekend slot or a shorter online session in its place, which is one practical reason to keep a hybrid arrangement available. School trips, mock examinations and festivals all collide with tuition calendars in India, so plan for them in advance.

Stay in the house, keep the door open, and stay out of the lesson itself. For a Primary Years Programme child, sitting nearby for the first session or two is reasonable, then step back. Ask instead for a short written note after each session; that tells you more than listening would.

mainEntity.name: My child has been in a batch for a month with no change. What should we do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at the marked work before changing anything. Ask for a recent script and check whether the losses are content the student never learned or a way of answering that costs marks on material they know. A content gap can justify staying, if the batch is genuinely covering it. Everything else points to one-to-one, because the fix requires somebody reading this student's own writing. Raise it with the centre first, in writing, and ask what they propose. Then decide, rather than stacking a second commitment on the first.

mainEntity.name: Is online coaching really as effective as sitting in a classroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most Diploma Programme subjects a well-run online session beats a poorly matched local classroom, and loses to a good home tutor for younger students. What online buys is the right teacher, which matters most for thinly taught subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. What it costs is attention late in the evening, and the informal signals a tutor picks up sitting in the room. Judge it on the same evidence as anything else: the student's own marked work after six weeks.

mainEntity.name: How many subjects should we take outside school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with one, and rarely go beyond two at a time. A Diploma Programme student already carries six subjects, Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and every added session removes time from independent work, which is where much of the grade is actually earned. If three subjects look weak, treat the weakest first and reassess after six weeks. Families who book everything at once usually cancel most of it by the second term anyway.

mainEntity.name: Do coaching centres plan around the May examination session?

acceptedAnswer.text: The good ones do, and it is a fair test of whether a centre understands the programme at all. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, results come out in early July, and a school's own coursework deadlines fall well before the IB's. A centre planning revision on a generic calendar, without asking when your child's school submits coursework, is running a timetable rather than a plan. Ask them to show you how their term maps onto your school's deadlines.

mainEntity.name: What happens if we miss a scheduled home session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree the rule before it happens, because at some point it will. Ask whether a session cancelled with notice is rescheduled or forfeited, how much notice counts as notice, and what happens when the tutor cancels instead. For home tuition the answer is often a rescheduled weekend slot or a shorter online session in its place, which is one practical reason to keep a hybrid arrangement available. School trips, mock examinations and festivals all collide with tuition calendars in India, so plan for them in advance.

finalCta: Send a query or book a free consultation, and say plainly what is going wrong: the subject, the level, the school's next deadline and the evenings you can actually keep. IB Gram will ask about board, programme, location and schedule, then shortlist verified tutors who fit, subject to availability. Arrange a demo, watch who does the talking, and ask for a different match if it is not right.

comparison.heading: How does a coaching batch compare with one-to-one tuition in India?
comparison.intro: No format wins every row. A batch buys structure and a lower cost per hour; one-to-one buys diagnosis and criterion-level feedback; a recorded course buys availability at midnight before a test. The trade-off that usually decides it is this: how much of your child's lost marks come from material never learned, and how much from a way of answering that only an individual reader can correct.
