h1: IB Tutoring in India: What Actually Happens in a Good Session
heroTitle: What a good IB tutoring session in India contains
heroSubtitle: This page is about method rather than booking. What a tutor should do in the first ten minutes, how a command term is taught, what marking a student's own answer in front of them looks like, and how an error log gets reviewed. Home, online and hybrid lessons all run on the same method.
introSummary: IB tutoring in India should look almost nothing like a second school lesson, and the difference is visible within ten minutes: in good home tuition the student is writing and the tutor is reading, not the other way round. This page sets out the method. It covers how command terms are actually taught, what it means to mark one of the student's own answers against a criterion while they watch, how an error log is built and reviewed, the questioning that surfaces a misconception instead of papering over it, and the running order a single session should follow from opening to close. Judge any tutor you meet against it.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a home tutor's method to a student in India?
contentBlocks.body:
IB tutoring in India is matched on the failure, not on the subject. Two DP1 students can both be scoring 4 in Chemistry for entirely different reasons, and they need different tutors. One has content gaps and needs reteaching. The other understands the chemistry perfectly and writes answers that never do what the command term asked, which is a marking problem and takes a different kind of person to fix.

So the consultation asks for evidence rather than adjectives. A marked script beats any description a parent can give, because the pattern of lost marks is right there: whole questions left blank means timing, correct working with no final statement means method, long correct paragraphs scoring nothing means the student answered describe when the paper said evaluate. From that we can say which of four broadly different teaching styles the student needs, and shortlist tutors whose verified profiles show they work that way.

Then the practical layer. Programme and level, since Higher Level and Standard Level differ in hours and depth. Your locality, because a home tutor who is genuinely nearby holds a weekday evening slot far more reliably than one crossing the city. The school's mock dates, because method work has to happen before the pressure arrives, not during it. Availability remains conditional on level, subject and schedule.

A demo session follows, and it is worth watching how the tutor spends it. If they lecture for forty minutes, the method is wrong for tutoring regardless of how good the explanation was. If they ask the student to attempt something within the first ten minutes and then work from what came out, that is the right instinct. Ask for a different match if what you see is not that.
items: Send the marked script, not a summary: the pattern of lost marks drives the match
Say which programme and level, since HL and SL need different depth
Give the school's mock dates so method work lands before the pressure
Watch the demo for who is writing and who is talking
Ask for a different match if the tutor lectured the whole hour

contentBlocks.heading: Method by stage: inquiry at PYP, criteria at MYP, command terms at DP
contentBlocks.body:
The method has to change with the programme, and a tutor who runs the same session for a nine-year-old and a seventeen-year-old is running the wrong one for at least one of them.

In the Primary Years Programme, which covers ages three to twelve, there are no external examinations and no published grades. Learning sits inside six transdisciplinary themes, which the IB names as Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet, and children finish with the PYP exhibition in the final year. The method is short cycles, physical materials, and a great deal of asking the child to explain their own thinking aloud. Nothing here is exam technique, because there is no exam.

In the Middle Years Programme, MYP 1 to MYP 5, every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8, with the total out of 32 converting to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. That structure dictates the method. A tutor should be working on one criterion at a time, and should be able to show the student the descriptor for the band above the one they are hitting. The Community Project arrives in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional, and each school chooses, so nobody should be drilling on-screen practice until you have checked.

In the Diploma Programme the method is dominated by command terms and by internal assessment. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, each graded 1 to 7, with TOK and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Home classes at DP level should be roughly half writing.
items: PYP: short cycles, materials, and the child explaining their own reasoning aloud
MYP: one criterion at a time, descriptor visible, band above named explicitly
MYP criteria are scored out of 8 each, totalling 32 before conversion
DP: command terms and internal assessment drive almost every session
DP home classes should be close to half student writing time
Check whether your school offers MYP 5 eAssessment before practising for it

contentBlocks.heading: A worked example: marking one DP science answer with the student watching
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the method made concrete, in a subject most Indian DP families care about. The DP sciences first assessed in 2025 use a Paper 1 in two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, and a Paper 2 of short-answer and extended-response questions. So a student who is fine in class and weak in the exam is usually failing at one of those three things specifically, and a tutor should find out which before teaching anything.

Take a Paper 2 extended-response question the student has already attempted and scored poorly on. The tutor does not explain it. The tutor puts the markscheme beside the student's own script and reads it with them, line by line, asking where each mark was meant to be earned. Almost always the student discovers something uncomfortable: they knew the content and wrote around it. The answer said discuss, and they described. That is a five-minute discovery which a term of explanation would not have produced.

Then the internal assessment, which in the sciences is the scientific investigation: worth 20% of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of six marks each, being Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, within a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. The criterion Indian students lose most on is Evaluation, because it asks them to attack their own method, and school training rewards presenting a clean result. A tutor cannot write any of it. A tutor can hand back a draft with the descriptor beside it and ask which sentence does what the descriptor asks for.

The same method transfers. In Mathematics, whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, it is reading the marks for method against the marks for the answer. In Economics, it is the commentary against its criteria. In English A, it is the difference between retelling and analysing.
items: Paper 1A multiple choice, 1B data-based, Paper 2 short and extended response
The scientific investigation is worth 20% of the subject grade
Four criteria of six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion, Evaluation
Maximum 3,000 words; group work allowed up to three, reports written individually
HL and SL share the structure; HL adds Additional Higher Level content
Evaluation is where Indian students most often lose marks, and it is teachable

contentBlocks.heading: Where method meets traffic: IB tutoring in India, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
Method survives a screen. It does not survive a tutor who arrives half an hour late and has forty minutes left, which is why geography belongs in a page about pedagogy at all. A session that gets compressed always loses the same part first: the marking. The tutor keeps the explanation, because explaining feels productive, and drops the twenty minutes where the student writes and the work gets marked in front of them. That is the wrong half to lose.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, IB tutoring in Mumbai runs smoothly across Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, where a tutor can hold two evenings in the same area. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are different markets rather than suburbs of the same one, and a family there should expect either a local tutor or a screen. Bengaluru is where compression bites hardest. IB tutoring in Bangalore concentrates around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala and Indiranagar; a tutor coming from there to Yelahanka, Hebbal, Electronic City, Jayanagar or Kanakapura Road on a weekday evening is arriving tired, and the marking is what gets cut.

Pune is more forgiving because its clusters are tight. IB tutoring in Pune across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar, or across Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi, keeps sessions intact. IB tutoring in Chennai works well in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam, with Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar depending entirely on the hour. Delhi NCR and Hyderabad show the same split, between South Delhi or Gachibowli on one side and Greater Noida or Secunderabad on the other.

Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, which is to say Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, the method argument settles the mode question by itself. A screen with a shared document and a markscheme open on it delivers the marking part of the method better than a tired tutor who drove a long way. Pick the mode that protects the marking.
items: A compressed session always loses the marking first, and that is the valuable half
Mumbai: island-city areas hold two evenings; Thane and Navi Mumbai rarely do
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are dense, Yelahanka and Hebbal are a stretch
Pune and Chennai clusters are tight enough to keep sessions intact
Kochi, Coimbatore and Visakhapatnam: a screen protects the method better than travel

contentBlocks.heading: Why school feedback in India reads the way it does
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools appear here only because a tutor's method has to start from what the school has already told you, and parents in India are routinely handed feedback they were never taught to read.

A report that says your child needs to develop analysis in criterion C is not vague by accident. It is criterion language, and it points at a descriptor. The tutor's first job is to find that descriptor, put it in front of the student, and translate it into something doable this week. Develop analysis usually means the student is stating what happened and stopping. The next step might be as small as a sentence starter used five times.

The calendar shapes the method too. Schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May session; November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, and results are released in early July. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they are the documents that show how marks are awarded. A tutor who has never opened a subject report for the course they teach is working from memory.

Parents at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore describe the same thing: plenty of feedback, very little translation. Ask the tutor to bring the descriptor to the first session. If they cannot find it, that answers a question about method before anyone has taught anything.
items: Criterion comments point at a descriptor; ask the tutor to bring it
Develop analysis usually means the student states and stops
May session dominates in India; November is for a minority and retakes
Schools set their own DP2 mock dates, usually months before May
Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB

contentBlocks.heading: Does the method change in home, online and hybrid lessons?
contentBlocks.body:
The method behind IB tutoring in India does not change with the mode. What changes is which part of it is easy to run and which needs deliberate effort, and knowing that is how a family picks the mode without guessing.

In a home session the marking is natural. Tutor and student sit over the same script, the tutor can see the working being crossed out and can stop the student mid-sentence, and the error log is a physical notebook that lives on the desk. What is harder at home is resources. A tutor arriving by scooter carries less than a tutor with a screen and a folder of papers. And accountability cuts the other way: home tuition is where a tutor notices the untouched textbook, the phone face-up, the study corner that is really a dining table between meals.

Online makes the document work easier and the attention work harder. Annotating a markscheme beside a student's answer on a shared screen is genuinely better than passing paper back and forth, and the whole session can be saved so the error log builds itself. What online lessons cannot do is tell whether the student is actually attempting the problem or waiting it out. So a good online tutor compensates deliberately: cameras on, work photographed and shared, silence enforced while the student writes rather than filled with talk.

Hybrid suits the method best for most DP students. One home session a week for long timed writing, where presence stops the student stopping, plus a shorter online session for marking, doubt-solving and reviewing the error log. It also survives the Indian calendar: monsoon weeks, exam periods and a tutor's own travel break home visits before they break screens.

The trade-off in one line: home tuition protects attention, online protects the documents and the schedule, hybrid protects both and asks the family to actually run a timetable.
items: Home: marking and accountability come free, resources and continuity do not
Online: shared annotation is better, attention has to be engineered deliberately
Hybrid: home session for timed writing, online session for marking and review
Online sessions can be saved, which makes the error log almost automatic
Monsoon, mocks and tutor travel break home schedules before they break online ones

contentBlocks.heading: How can you tell whether a tutor's method is any good?
contentBlocks.body:
Watch one session of IB tutoring in India and count who is talking. If the tutor speaks for most of an hour, you are paying for a lecture, and your child already attends those at school. In a session that works, the student writes for a meaningful stretch, the tutor reads it, and then there is a conversation about a specific sentence. Talking time is the crudest possible diagnostic and it is still the most reliable one available to a parent standing in the next room.

Ask to see the error log after three weeks. A working tutor has one: a running record of the mistakes this student keeps making, sorted by type rather than by date, with the ones that have stopped recurring struck out. If it exists and it is being reviewed at the start of sessions, the method is real. If the answer is that everything is in the tutor's head, it is not.

Then listen to how the tutor questions. A weak tutor asks whether the student understood, and a fifteen-year-old says yes. A strong one asks the student to explain it back, or gives a slightly altered version of the same problem and watches what happens. Misconceptions do not announce themselves. They have to be hunted, and the hunting looks like patience with silence.

On our side, identity, qualifications and the programmes and levels a tutor claims to teach are verified before a profile goes live. That establishes who someone is, not how they teach. No verification can do the second part, which is why the demo exists and why asking for a different match is routine. Be wary of anyone promising a guaranteed grade or a points jump from a method. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a method that claims to is selling certainty nobody owns.
items: Count talking time: a lecture for an hour is not tutoring
Ask to see the error log after three weeks and check it is reviewed
Listen for explain it back rather than did you understand
Identity, qualifications and claimed programmes are verified before a profile goes live
Be wary of a method advertised with a guaranteed grade attached

contentBlocks.heading: The running order of a single IB tutoring session in India
contentBlocks.body:
A session has a shape, and the shape is what separates tutoring from paid revision company. Here is the running order a competent tutor follows, roughly, for a sixty to ninety minute lesson with a secondary student.

It opens with the error log, not with new content. Three or four minutes on what went wrong last time, and whether it has stopped going wrong. That single habit converts a series of disconnected hours into something cumulative, and it is the thing most home tutoring in India skips. Then a short attempt: a question of the type the student is weak on, done cold, in silence, while the tutor watches how they start. How a student begins a question tells you more than how they finish it.

The middle of the session is marking and teaching together. The tutor reads what the student produced, names the command term the question used, and shows what depth that term demanded. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent are not interchangeable, and each one sets the depth the answer needs. A student who genuinely internalises that distinction gains marks across every subject at once, which is why it is worth spending real time on.

Then reteaching only where reteaching is needed, which is often less than a parent expects. Then a second attempt at the same type of question, because the point is the student doing it differently, not the tutor having said it differently. The session closes with two things written down: the new entries in the error log, and one piece of work due before next time, small enough to actually get done.

What it should never be is a second school lesson. Your child has already sat through the explanation once. Paying for it again is the commonest waste in Indian home tuition.
items: 1. Open with the error log: what went wrong last time, and has it stopped
2. Cold attempt at a weak question type, in silence, while the tutor watches
3. Mark that attempt together, naming the command term and the depth it wanted
4. Reteach only the specific gap the marking exposed, and no more
5. Second attempt at the same question type, done differently by the student
6. Close by writing new error-log entries and one small task before next time

contentBlocks.heading: What should change first, and what takes a term?
contentBlocks.body:
The first thing IB tutoring in India should change is the student's language about their own work. Within two or three sessions they should stop saying they are bad at the subject and start saying something specific: that they lose marks when the question says evaluate, or that they never finish Paper 2. That shift is not cosmetic. A student who can name the failure can work on it, and one who cannot is just anxious.

The second thing is timing behaviour. Method work shows up early in how a student starts a question, because that is where the habit was. By week three or four they should be annotating the command term before writing, or sketching the structure of an extended response, without being reminded. Small, visible, and quick.

What takes a term is the grade. A 1 to 7 grade is a coarse instrument and it moves slowly, particularly at the top of the scale where the difference between a 6 and a 7 is consistency across a whole paper rather than one fixed weakness. Anyone describing a rapid jump after a month is talking about a mock that was easier, not a method that worked. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a method is not a promise.

There are honest limits. Method work cannot replace content a student never learned, so a Higher Level student who missed a term of teaching needs reteaching first and technique second. It cannot fix a subject choice that was wrong at fourteen. It cannot help much in the final fortnight before a session, when the only sensible work is past papers under time. And if a student is being tutored in several subjects at once, the tutoring has become the workload. Stopping one is often the intervention that helps most.
items: Two to three sessions: the student names the failure instead of the subject
Three to four weeks: command terms get annotated before writing, unprompted
A term: the 1 to 7 grade, and only with consistency across whole papers
Method cannot replace missed content; reteach first, then technique
In the last fortnight, timed past papers beat any new method

contentBlocks.heading: Setting up home classes so the method actually works
contentBlocks.body:
Three things make the difference between a method that runs and one that quietly collapses into conversation, and all three are the family's job rather than the tutor's.

First, a surface. The student needs to spread a past paper, a markscheme and their own answer side by side, which means a table rather than a bed and a light that works after dark. Home classes fail over the study corner far more often than over the tutor. If lessons are online or hybrid, the equivalent is a printed paper or a second screen, so the student is not switching windows between the question and the tutor's face.

Second, the documents. Bring the last two marked scripts, the school's criterion feedback, and the term calendar with mock weeks and internal assessment deadlines on it. A tutor who has those can plan a term. A tutor who has only a parent's account of the problem spends the first three sessions finding out what the script would have said in ten minutes.

Third, a rule about the room. A parent nearby is useful, especially for younger students in PYP and early MYP, and it is different from sitting in. For a DP2 student, presence in the room usually makes the silence that the method depends on impossible.

When you are ready, send a query or book a free consultation. We ask about programme, subject, level, school calendar, locality and schedule, shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified against those needs, and arrange a demo session before you commit. Watch that demo for the running order described above. Fees depend on level, subject and whether the tutor travels, and we set out the structure before any lesson is booked.
items: A real table, good light and room for three documents side by side
Bring two marked scripts, the criterion feedback and the term calendar
Online or hybrid: print the paper or use a second screen
Parent nearby for younger students, out of the room for DP2
Watch the demo session against the running order before committing

faqs.question: What should happen in the first ten minutes of a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: The error log, then an attempt. A good tutor opens by reviewing what went wrong last time and whether it has stopped going wrong, which takes three or four minutes, and then puts a question in front of the student to attempt cold while they watch. What they are watching is how the student starts, because that is where the habit lives. If the first ten minutes are the tutor explaining something new, the session has begun as a second school lesson and the hour is already compromised.

faqs.question: What exactly is an error log, and how is it reviewed?
faqs.answer: It is a running record of the mistakes one student keeps making, organised by type rather than by date. Entries look like forgets units in the final answer, or writes description when the command term says evaluate, or runs out of time on the last extended response. The tutor reviews it at the start of each session, strikes out patterns that have stopped recurring, and adds new ones at the close. Ask to see it after three weeks. A tutor who keeps everything in their head is not running a method.

faqs.question: How does a tutor teach command terms without it becoming a vocabulary lesson?
faqs.answer: By marking the student's own failed answer against the term the question used. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a student learns the difference far faster from seeing a paragraph they were proud of earn nothing than from a list of definitions. The tutor names the term, shows what the markscheme expected, and then asks for a second attempt at the same question type. That second attempt is the part that makes it stick.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor use this method with a younger MYP student?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the criteria in place of command terms. In the Middle Years Programme each subject is assessed against four criteria scored out of 8, so home tuition at this stage works on one criterion at a time with the descriptor for the next band up visible on the table. Sessions should be shorter than a DP lesson and should contain more talking out loud. The error log still applies, though for an MYP student it is usually shorter and more about process than content.

faqs.question: My son says the tutor explains well but his marks have not moved. Why?
faqs.answer: Because explanation and marks are only loosely connected in the IB. A student can follow every explanation and still lose marks on structure, command terms, timing or the internal assessment criteria, none of which improve by listening. Ask what proportion of the session your son spends writing. If the honest answer is very little, that is the problem, and it is fixable without changing tutors: ask for half the session to be the student attempting work and the tutor marking it in front of him.

faqs.question: Does the method work the same way in online lessons?
faqs.answer: The method is identical, but two parts need deliberate handling. Marking is actually easier online, because a markscheme and the student's answer sit side by side on a shared screen and the session can be saved, which makes the error log almost automatic. Attention is harder, because nobody can see whether the student is attempting the problem or waiting. Good online tutors insist on cameras, have work photographed and shared, and keep silence while the student writes rather than filling it with talk.

faqs.question: We are in Kochi and there is no local IB subject tutor. Does that limit the method?
faqs.answer: No, and in southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai it usually improves the match. Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru and Visakhapatnam have thin local supply for IB subjects, so insisting on a tutor who can travel to your door often means accepting a weaker subject specialist. Online lessons remove that constraint entirely. Given that the marking half of the method runs at least as well on a shared screen, the trade-off almost always favours the better tutor over the closer one.

faqs.question: How much should the student be writing in a session?
faqs.answer: Roughly half the time at Diploma Programme level, less at MYP, and much less at PYP. That is a rule of thumb rather than a measurement, and it exists because writing is where the marks are earned and where the tutor gets something to read. A session that is ninety per cent explanation gives the tutor nothing to diagnose from. If your child comes out of every lesson with a full notebook of the tutor's working and none of their own, something has gone wrong.

faqs.question: Should a session ever be used for the Internal Assessment instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary has to be clear. A tutor can read the student's draft with the criteria beside it, ask which sentence does what the descriptor asks for, point out that a conclusion has not engaged with the data, and help plan realistically against school deadlines. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or supply text, because the work must be the student's own and the school authenticates it. Your school's supervisor remains the primary guide. Anyone offering to draft the work is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: How do we keep home classes from turning into a chat with the student?
faqs.answer: Structure and a surface. Insist that each home session opens with the error log and contains a timed attempt, and ask the tutor to leave one written task at the end. Set up a table where a past paper, a markscheme and an answer can sit side by side, because a lesson held on a sofa becomes a conversation almost automatically. If a parent is in the house but not in the room, most students settle within two sessions. For a DP2 student, presence in the room usually makes it worse.

faqs.question: Is this method different for Higher Level and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The structure is the same and the depth is not. Higher Level carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and in the sciences HL adds Additional Higher Level content on top of a shared assessment structure. So an HL session spends more time on extended response and on the harder end of data analysis, and less on basic recall. The error log tends to be longer too, because there is more surface area for a habit to go wrong on.

faqs.question: How long before mocks should method work start?
faqs.answer: A term, ideally, and never during mock week itself. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before the May session, and method changes need time to become habit before they are tested under pressure. Starting eight to ten weeks out is workable. Starting the week before means the student is being asked to change how they write while also revising, which reliably produces a worse mock than leaving them alone would have. After mocks is a good moment, because the evidence is fresh.

mainEntity.name: What should happen in the first ten minutes of a tutoring session?

acceptedAnswer.text: The error log, then an attempt. A good tutor opens by reviewing what went wrong last time and whether it has stopped going wrong, which takes three or four minutes, and then puts a question in front of the student to attempt cold while they watch. What they are watching is how the student starts, because that is where the habit lives. If the first ten minutes are the tutor explaining something new, the session has begun as a second school lesson and the hour is already compromised.

mainEntity.name: What exactly is an error log, and how is it reviewed?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a running record of the mistakes one student keeps making, organised by type rather than by date. Entries look like forgets units in the final answer, or writes description when the command term says evaluate, or runs out of time on the last extended response. The tutor reviews it at the start of each session, strikes out patterns that have stopped recurring, and adds new ones at the close. Ask to see it after three weeks. A tutor who keeps everything in their head is not running a method.

mainEntity.name: How does a tutor teach command terms without it becoming a vocabulary lesson?

acceptedAnswer.text: By marking the student's own failed answer against the term the question used. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a student learns the difference far faster from seeing a paragraph they were proud of earn nothing than from a list of definitions. The tutor names the term, shows what the markscheme expected, and then asks for a second attempt at the same question type. That second attempt is the part that makes it stick.

mainEntity.name: Can a home tutor use this method with a younger MYP student?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with the criteria in place of command terms. In the Middle Years Programme each subject is assessed against four criteria scored out of 8, so home tuition at this stage works on one criterion at a time with the descriptor for the next band up visible on the table. Sessions should be shorter than a DP lesson and should contain more talking out loud. The error log still applies, though for an MYP student it is usually shorter and more about process than content.

mainEntity.name: My son says the tutor explains well but his marks have not moved. Why?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because explanation and marks are only loosely connected in the IB. A student can follow every explanation and still lose marks on structure, command terms, timing or the internal assessment criteria, none of which improve by listening. Ask what proportion of the session your son spends writing. If the honest answer is very little, that is the problem, and it is fixable without changing tutors: ask for half the session to be the student attempting work and the tutor marking it in front of him.

mainEntity.name: Does the method work the same way in online lessons?

acceptedAnswer.text: The method is identical, but two parts need deliberate handling. Marking is actually easier online, because a markscheme and the student's answer sit side by side on a shared screen and the session can be saved, which makes the error log almost automatic. Attention is harder, because nobody can see whether the student is attempting the problem or waiting. Good online tutors insist on cameras, have work photographed and shared, and keep silence while the student writes rather than filling it with talk.

mainEntity.name: We are in Kochi and there is no local IB subject tutor. Does that limit the method?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and in southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai it usually improves the match. Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru and Visakhapatnam have thin local supply for IB subjects, so insisting on a tutor who can travel to your door often means accepting a weaker subject specialist. comparison.heading: How does one-to-one method compare with school, a batch and self-study in India?
comparison.intro: These four are not competitors so much as different jobs. The school teacher owns the curriculum and the authentication of coursework. A one-to-one tutor owns diagnosis and the marking of the student's own work. A batch owns pace and peers. Self-study with past papers owns volume. The question that decides your mix is simple: does this student know why they are losing marks?

rows.label: Diagnosing why marks are lost

h1: IB Tutoring Services in India: Everything a Family Can Ask For
heroTitle: The Full List of IB Tutoring Services in India
heroSubtitle: Subject tuition, Internal Assessment and Extended Essay support inside the integrity rules, Theory of Knowledge help, mock preparation, board-switch bridging and subject-selection guidance. Each one described with what it does not include, because the limits matter more than the list.
introSummary: IB tutoring services in India cover six requests a family can reasonably make: subject tuition delivered as home tuition or online, coursework support that stays inside the academic integrity rules, Theory of Knowledge help, mock preparation, bridging for a student arriving from another board, and guidance on subject selection. This page is the catalogue, and it is written the way a catalogue should be: every service paired with what it excludes. A service list that only says yes is useless to a parent trying to work out what to buy. Families in Gurugram, Powai, Whitefield and Salt Lake ask for the same six things, and the difference between a good outcome and a wasted term is usually scoping, not effort.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you scope which IB tutoring services in India you actually need?
contentBlocks.body:
IB tutoring services in India are usually bought the wrong way round, from the menu rather than from the evidence. One marked script, one report and one honest conversation with the student will tell you which service to buy, and it will usually be narrower than the one you had in mind when you opened this page.

The common mistake is buying breadth. A parent worried about Diploma Programme results asks for four subjects, twice a week each, from March. What the evidence often shows is one subject with a genuine content gap, one with an exam-technique problem that three past questions a week would solve, and two that are fine. Scoping down is the single most valuable thing a service can do for a family, and it is also the thing a service loses money by doing.

Scoping also decides delivery. A student who needs supervision gets home tuition; a student who needs a rare Higher Level specialist gets online; a household with two exam calendars usually ends up hybrid. The service is the same, the delivery is not, and mixing that up is why some families conclude that tutoring does not work for them.

Once the scope is clear, the rest is mechanical. IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against that scope. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match. Nothing beyond that is promised, and you should be wary of any service that promises more.
items: 1. Collect one recent marked script, the latest report and the school's term calendar
2. Name the problem as a behaviour: skips questions, cannot start, mismanages time
3. Decide the narrowest service that addresses it, then stop adding subjects
4. Choose delivery: home tuition, online, or a hybrid week that survives traffic
5. Run a trial session, then review the scope again after four sessions

contentBlocks.heading: Which services does a PYP, MYP or DP student actually use?
contentBlocks.body:
The catalogue is the same at every stage. What changes is which items are worth buying, and at two of the three stages the honest answer is fewer than parents expect.

In the Primary Years Programme there are no external examinations and no published grades, so anything sold as exam preparation at this age is selling you nothing. Learning runs through six transdisciplinary themes, among them Who we are, How the world works and How we organize ourselves, and the final year brings the PYP exhibition. The useful services here are narrow: reading fluency, number sense, and support for a child who has joined from another system mid-year. Everything else can wait.

The Middle Years Programme changes the picture. Five years, eight subject groups, and every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0-8, with the criterion total out of 32 converted to a 1-7 grade through IB boundaries. Criterion-specific support is a real service and a useful one, because a student who scores 3 on criterion D in Sciences has a definable problem. The Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 are supervised school tasks, not tutoring products; a tutor may teach research and planning skills around them and nothing more. Some schools offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 and some do not, so confirm before buying preparation for it.

The Diploma Programme is where the full catalogue applies. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay for up to 3 further points towards a maximum of 45, and 24 points as the minimum for the diploma. Subject tuition, coursework skills, mock preparation and subject-selection advice all earn their place here.
items: PYP: reading, number sense and settling in after a mid-year move, nothing exam-shaped
MYP: criterion-specific support, judged against the four criteria scored 0-8 each
MYP projects are supervised school tasks; a tutor teaches skills around them only
DP: the full catalogue applies, including mock preparation and subject-selection advice
Confirm whether your school runs MYP eAssessment before paying to prepare for it

contentBlocks.heading: Subject tuition in India: what the core service includes and excludes
contentBlocks.body:
Subject tuition is the service most families mean when they ask about IB tutoring services in India, and it is the easiest one to define precisely. A tutor teaches the syllabus content the student has not grasped, practises questions with them, and builds exam technique in that subject at that level. It does not include doing the student's school homework for them, chasing the school, or covering a second subject informally because the tutor happens to know it.

The subject decides what the service looks like. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation, at both levels, are taught through worked questions and method; the mathematics exploration is a separate piece of work and should be scoped separately. Physics, Chemistry and Biology split between content teaching and practical write-up skills. Economics splits between diagram accuracy and evaluation writing. English A is largely drafting, reading closely and structuring commentary. A tutor who says they can take all six at Higher Level should be asked, politely, which ones they have taught most recently.

Bridging is a distinct service and worth naming separately. A student arriving from CBSE, ICSE or a state board into MYP 5 or DP1 is not behind in content so much as unfamiliar with how the work is assessed: criteria rather than chapter tests, open-ended questions, marks for method and communication rather than for the final answer, and coursework that must be their own. Bridging covers that translation over a defined number of weeks and then ends. It is not indefinite subject tuition under another name, and a service that lets it drift into one is not doing the family a favour.
items: Includes: syllabus content, question practice and exam technique in one named subject
Excludes: doing school homework, chasing teachers, or informally adding a second subject
Mathematics exploration work is scoped separately from ordinary subject tuition
Bridging from CBSE, ICSE or a state board teaches assessment style, not fresh content
Bridging should run for a fixed number of weeks and then stop by design
Ask any tutor which of the six subjects they have taught most recently, and at which level

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB tutoring services in India are delivered, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Every service on this page exists everywhere in the country, but not in the same form, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's time.

In Delhi NCR the subject pool is deep enough that most requests can be met in person. South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri form one pool, Gurugram (Gurgaon) with Golf Course Road another, Noida, Sector 128 Noida and Greater Noida a third, with Faridabad and Ghaziabad served better from within than across. An IB tutoring service in Delhi will usually offer coursework skills and mock preparation face to face. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves as corridors: Bandra, Juhu and Andheri along one arm, Powai on its own, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill to the south, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar better matched locally. An IB tutoring service in Mumbai often delivers subject tuition in person and Theory of Knowledge support online, simply because TOK specialists are scarcer than mathematics teachers.

Bengaluru and Hyderabad are the cities where delivery splits most visibly by service. An IB tutoring service in Bangalore can staff subject tuition around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, while Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road often work better online for anything specialised. An IB tutoring service in Hyderabad draws on Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District, Kokapet, Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills, with Secunderabad usually its own pool. Pune and Chennai follow the same pattern.

Kolkata and eastern India is where the catalogue narrows most, and families there should know it going in. Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat can support subject tuition in the common subjects. In Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna, an IB tutoring service in Kolkata or an online specialist is frequently the realistic route, and mock preparation in a rarer Higher Level subject will almost always be delivered on screen.
items: Delhi NCR: four evening pools, deep enough for most services to run in person
Mumbai: subject tuition locally, TOK and rarer options usually online
Bengaluru: the Whitefield and Sarjapur Road belt differs from Yelahanka and Jayanagar
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kokapet as one pool, Secunderabad as another
Kolkata: Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge and Rajarhat cover the common subjects
Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna: online delivery for anything specialised

contentBlocks.heading: School deadlines in India that decide which service you need this term
contentBlocks.body:
Buy the service the term calls for, not the one that sounded reassuring in August. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session, and May results are released in early July. Work backwards from those three anchors and the sequence writes itself.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Nothing here describes any particular school's programmes or policies, and your own coordinator's deadlines always override anything you read online.

The first term after the summer break is for content and habits. This is when subject tuition and bridging earn the most, and when coursework skills should be taught in the abstract before any actual draft exists. By the middle of the year, internal assessment deadlines begin landing across subjects within a few weeks of each other, Extended Essay reflection sessions are being scheduled, and the useful service shifts from teaching content to protecting time.

The final term changes the catalogue entirely. Mock preparation replaces ordinary tuition, and it is a different job: timed papers under real conditions, marking against the published criteria, and a deliberate decision about what to leave out. A student who is weak in four topics and has five weeks cannot fix four. A good service names the two that carry the most marks for the effort, protects them, and says plainly that the others are being sacrificed.

After results arrive in early July, the questions change again, and most of them belong with the school's coordinator rather than a tutor.
items: The school year runs roughly April to March; most candidates sit the May session
Term one: subject tuition, bridging and coursework skills taught before drafts exist
Mid-year: internal assessment deadlines stack, so the service shifts to protecting time
Final term: timed papers, criterion marking, and a deliberate list of what to drop
May results arrive in early July; the questions after that belong with the coordinator

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: the same service, three deliveries
contentBlocks.body:
Every service in this catalogue can be delivered three ways, and the right choice depends on the service rather than on a general preference.

Home tuition is the strongest delivery for anything where written work has to be watched as it is produced: early mathematics method, science diagrams, and any student who needs the room to become serious for ninety minutes. A tutor at the table also sees the messy notebook rather than the tidy photograph of it. The cost is travel, and in a metro that cost is paid every single week, which is why late weekday slots across a city tend to erode.

Online is the stronger delivery for scarce services. Theory of Knowledge support, a rare Higher Level option, mock preparation in a subject nobody local teaches: in each case the choice is between a well-matched specialist on a screen and a general tutor in your drawing room, and the specialist usually wins. Online is also more reliable through the monsoon and through exam terms when nobody can afford to lose a slot.

Hybrid is the arrangement most Diploma Programme families reach eventually. One home visit for the long, paper-heavy work and one shorter online session midweek for doubt-solving and accountability. It keeps the relationship that in-person teaching builds and the reliability that online delivery has, at the cost of the student getting used to two routines.

Stated plainly: choose home classes when the work must be watched, online when the expertise is scarce, and hybrid when both are true. And if a service insists on one delivery for every request regardless of what you are buying, that is a staffing constraint being sold to you as a philosophy.
items: Home tuition: written method, science diagrams, younger students, supervision
Online: scarce specialisms, Theory of Knowledge, rare Higher Level options
Hybrid: one home visit for long paper work, one online session for accountability
Exam terms usually shift the balance towards online so no slot is lost to weather
A service that offers only one delivery is describing its staffing, not your need

contentBlocks.heading: What should you ask a service to prove before you book?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask three things: who the tutor is, what they have actually taught, and what the service will refuse to do. The third question is the one that separates a professional operation from a sales conversation, and it takes about a minute.

IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified: identity, the qualifications claimed, the programmes and levels handled, and the subjects they are matched for. Verification is about accuracy of the claim, not a prediction of results, and anyone who presents it as the latter is overselling. A profile that says Diploma Programme Chemistry means that tutor is matched for Diploma Programme Chemistry, not for whatever science question turns up mid-term.

What you should check yourself is easier than it sounds. In the trial session, name the exact topic the student is stuck on and listen for a method rather than encouragement. Ask which syllabus version the student is following and see whether the answer is specific. Ask how the tutor handles a coursework question, and listen for the boundary being drawn without you having to raise it. A tutor who volunteers the integrity limit before you ask has told you a great deal.

Then listen for what is refused. An honest service will not promise a points total, will not write or edit coursework, will not claim affiliation with the IB or any examination board, and will not quote a grade improvement. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the willingness to say so out loud is worth more than any credential on a profile page.
items: Ask who the tutor is, what they last taught, and what the service refuses to do
Verified profiles confirm identity, claimed qualifications, programmes, levels and subjects
In the trial, name the stuck topic and listen for a method, not encouragement
A tutor who states the coursework boundary unprompted is showing you their standards
Refusals to expect: no promised points, no written coursework, no claimed board affiliation

contentBlocks.heading: Internal assessment, Extended Essay and TOK support: exactly where a tutor stops
contentBlocks.body:
This is the part of the catalogue where families get into trouble, so it is worth stating precisely. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft. It does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit the submission. The school submits the work, runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than by the school alone.

So what can be bought? A tutor may teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. Take the mathematics exploration, which is the same task for Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels: 20% of the final subject grade, 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 across five criteria, A Presentation worth 4, B Mathematical communication 4, C Personal engagement 3, D Reflection 3, and E Use of mathematics 6, with Higher Level work judged against a higher standard on criterion E. A tutor can teach what reflection means and why a page of restated theory scores nothing on personal engagement. A tutor cannot supply the topic, the writing or the corrections.

The Extended Essay works the same way. Up to 4,000 words, roughly 40 hours of work, supervised by a teacher at the student's own school with reflection sessions recorded along the way, graded A to E and combined with Theory of Knowledge for up to 3 points. The guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so no honest tutor will quote criterion mark allocations to you; follow the version your coordinator issues.

TOK support has two halves. The exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 prompts, up to 950 words, internally assessed and worth one third of the grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for that session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed, two thirds of the grade. A tutor can teach the areas of knowledge and challenge a weak justification. The objects, the claims and the sentences must be the student's.
items: Every internal assessment is the student's own work; a teacher may comment on one draft
A tutor may teach the skill, question reasoning and point at a criterion
Mathematics exploration: 20% of the grade, 12-20 pages, five criteria marked out of 20
Extended Essay: up to 4,000 words, about 40 hours, supervised at the student's own school
TOK exhibition: three objects, one of 35 prompts, up to 950 words, one third of the grade
TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles, up to 1,600 words, two thirds of the grade

contentBlocks.heading: What each service can change, and what it cannot
contentBlocks.body:
Judge IB tutoring services in India the way you would judge any other paid work: say in advance what should change, then check later whether it did. Vague hopes are not a specification, and they are how families end up paying for a year of sessions that nobody can evaluate.

Subject tuition should change what the student attempts. Within four to six sessions, questions that used to be left blank get a genuine try, working appears on the page, and the student can explain a method rather than reproduce it. Coursework skills support should change the drafting habit: a plan before the writing, a reread against the criteria, an earlier start. Mock preparation should change timing before it changes accuracy, because a student who finishes the paper and then improves is on a better path than one who is accurate and unfinished. Bridging should end. If a bridging arrangement is still running eight months later, it was never bridging.

Now the limits. No service can make a student attend school, sleep properly or care about a subject they have written off. None can replace a school's teaching over two years in six weeks, though a good one can choose what to salvage and say so out loud. None can touch coursework text, and any that offers to is risking the diploma, not helping it. And no tutor can guarantee a grade or a points total, whatever their examining background.

There is also the case for buying nothing. If the school's subject teacher has not yet been asked what is going wrong, ask them first. If a student is already in four tuitions and sleeping badly, the right service is subtraction. Services that never recommend less are not advising you; they are selling.
items: Specify in advance what the service should change, then review it after four sessions
Subject tuition changes attempts and working before it changes marks
Mock preparation changes timing first, accuracy second
Bridging that is still running eight months later was never bridging
Nothing in the catalogue includes writing or editing a student's coursework
Sometimes the right advice is fewer services, or none, and a word with the school

contentBlocks.heading: Booking home tuition or online support in India: what to send first
contentBlocks.body:
A precise first message gets a precise shortlist, and most enquiries about IB tutoring services in India arrive far too vague to answer well. Send four things and you will skip a week of back and forth.

First, the student's programme, year and exact subjects with levels. Higher Level Physics and Standard Level Physics are different requests, and Analysis and Approaches is a different request from Applications and Interpretation. Second, the service you think you need, in your own words, and the evidence behind it: the marked script, the report line, the comment from the class teacher. Third, the school's term dates, mock weeks and any coursework deadlines the coordinator has issued. Fourth, the practical constraints, which means your locality, the evenings that work, and whether home tuition, online or a hybrid week suits the household.

If you are unsure which service applies, say that instead of guessing. Scoping is part of the consultation, and a family that arrives saying they are not sure whether the problem is content or technique usually gets a better outcome than one that arrives with a confident but wrong diagnosis.

What happens next is short. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shares a shortlist of verified tutors matched to that scope. You can arrange a demo or trial session before committing, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on the subject, the level and the slot you need, and rarer Higher Level requests take longer to staff in some cities than in others.
items: Send programme, year, exact subjects and levels, not just the subject names
Say which service you think you need and attach the evidence behind it
Include term dates, mock weeks and any coordinator-issued coursework deadlines
State your locality and whether home classes, online or hybrid suits the week
If you cannot tell content problems from technique problems, say so and ask
Expect rarer Higher Level requests to take longer to staff in some cities

faqs.question: What exactly is included in subject tuition, and what is not?
faqs.answer: Subject tuition covers syllabus content, question practice and exam technique in one named subject at one named level. It does not include completing the student's school homework, negotiating with the school on your behalf, or quietly absorbing a second subject because the tutor knows it. If a second subject is genuinely needed, it should be scoped, priced and reviewed as its own service. Keeping the boundary clear protects the quality of the first subject, which is the one you actually came for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary: the tutor can teach the skill and question the reasoning, but every internal assessment must be the student's own work. The integrity policy allows a teacher to comment on one draft, and no tutor or parent may write, rewrite or edit the submission. In practice that means a tutor can explain what a criterion is asking, ask the student to reread a paragraph against it, and refuse to suggest sentences. The school submits the work and runs similarity checking, so the risk of crossing that line falls on the student.

faqs.question: What does Extended Essay support actually look like?
faqs.answer: It looks like research and writing coaching, not essay production. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of work, and it is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school with reflection sessions recorded along the way. A tutor can help the student narrow a research question, plan a structure, read critically and manage the schedule around other deadlines. Because the guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, be sceptical of anyone quoting criterion marks at you; ask your coordinator which version applies to your session.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge tutoring worth buying?
faqs.answer: It is, for students who write vaguely, and less so for students who are simply behind on other subjects. TOK has two assessments: the exhibition, which uses three objects linked to one of 35 prompts, runs to 950 words and is internally assessed for a third of the grade; and the essay, which answers one of six prescribed titles for that session, runs to 1,600 words and is externally assessed for two thirds. A tutor can teach the areas of knowledge and attack a weak justification. The objects and the argument must be the student's own.

faqs.question: How is mock preparation different from ordinary tuition?
faqs.answer: It is a different job with a different clock. Ordinary tuition teaches content; mock preparation runs timed papers under real conditions, marks them against published criteria, and forces a decision about what to leave out. With five weeks and four weak topics, a student cannot fix four, and a good tutor will name the two worth protecting and say the rest are being sacrificed. Expect the first sessions to feel worse than usual, because timing improves before accuracy does and an honest timed score is often a shock.

faqs.question: My child is moving from CBSE or ICSE into DP1. What service is that?
faqs.answer: That is bridging, and it should be bought as its own short service rather than as open-ended tuition. The gap is rarely content. It is the shift to criterion-based assessment, marks awarded for method and communication, open-ended questions with no single expected answer, and coursework that must be genuinely the student's own. Bridging teaches that translation over a defined number of weeks and then ends. Families in Pune, Noida and Chennai ask for this every June and July, and the ones who set an end date get better value from it.

faqs.question: Can we get home tuition for one service and online for another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many households that is the sensible arrangement. A common split is home tuition for mathematics, where written method needs watching, and online for Theory of Knowledge or a rare Higher Level option where the specialist is in another city. Two tutors means two relationships to manage, so keep the scopes separate and written down. Families in Bengaluru often run exactly this pattern, with a local tutor around Whitefield or HSR Layout and a specialist reached on screen.

faqs.question: Do you offer help with subject selection?
faqs.answer: Guidance, yes; the decision, no. A tutor can explain what Higher Level commitment looks like in practice, how Analysis and Approaches differs from Applications and Interpretation in daily work, and what a six-subject load feels like alongside Creativity, Activity, Service. What a tutor cannot do is know your school's option blocks, your child's teachers or the entry requirements of the courses being considered. Those belong with the Diploma Programme coordinator and the university counsellor, and a service that claims otherwise is overreaching.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor or an online specialist better for a rare Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For a rare option, the online specialist is usually the better call, and this is the trade-off worth being unsentimental about. Home tuition gives supervision and a tutor who sees the written working, which matters greatly in mathematics and the sciences. But choosing a nearby generalist over a distant specialist for an unusual Higher Level subject buys convenience at the cost of expertise. In Kolkata and eastern India, including Bhubaneswar, Guwahati and Patna, this comes up regularly and online is frequently the honest answer.

faqs.question: How many services should one student have at the same time?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with, and almost never more than two subjects plus one skills-based service. A Diploma Programme student already carries six subjects, coursework across several of them, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Adding four tuitions to that produces a timetable nobody can sustain and sleep that nobody should accept. If the honest answer is that everything needs work, the problem is bigger than tutoring and belongs in a conversation with the school first.

faqs.question: What will a service refuse to promise?
faqs.answer: Any honest service refuses to promise a grade, a points total or a percentage improvement, because no tutor can guarantee a grade. It will also refuse to write or edit coursework, refuse to claim affiliation with the IB or any examination board, and refuse to name a figure for results it has not seen. Availability is conditional too: whether a particular subject and level can be staffed in your locality depends on the term, the slot and the specialism. A confident promise early in a sales call is a warning sign.

faqs.question: How quickly can a service actually start?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the level, the delivery and the time of year, and the honest range is wide. Common subjects in a deep metro pool move quickly. A rare Higher Level option, a Theory of Knowledge specialist, or a home visit in a locality with few IB families nearby takes longer, and the weeks just before mocks are the hardest time to staff anything. If you know you will need support in the final term, ask early, because the same request is far easier to fill in August than in February.
