h1: IB Tutor Agency in India: How Agencies Work and What to Ask
heroTitle: What an IB Tutor Agency in India Actually Does
heroSubtitle: Agencies, marketplaces and freelancers all end up sending a tutor to your door, and they behave very differently when something breaks. This page is about the business model behind the booking: who screens the tutor, who holds the relationship, who answers the phone in November, and what the paperwork should say.
introSummary: An IB tutor agency in India is a business that keeps a pool of tutors, screens them, and assigns one to your family for home tuition or online sessions, taking responsibility for the match rather than simply listing profiles. That is the difference worth understanding before you pay anybody. A marketplace shows you tutors and then steps back. A freelance tutor found through a parents' group answers to you alone. An agency sits between the two, and its worth depends entirely on what it screens, who you call when something goes wrong, and how honestly it describes what it cannot do. What follows is the model, the questions and the warning signs.

contentBlocks.heading: How does an IB tutor agency in India actually assign a tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
An agency works from a requirement, not from a catalogue. Someone takes your enquiry, writes down the board, the programme, the subject, the level and the days you can hold, searches its own pool against that record, and puts forward a small number of profiles it believes can teach that exact course. The assignment is the product. Everything else is admin around it.

That is also where agencies differ from each other. A serious one asks what your child scored in the last school assessment and what the teacher wrote, because a request for Higher Level Chemistry help means three different things depending on whether the problem is calculations, practical write-ups or reading the question. A weaker one asks only for your locality and budget, then sends whoever is free on Tuesday. You can usually tell which you are dealing with inside the first phone call, and the tell is how many questions come back at you.

Assignment is not the end of the process either. Ask what happens in week four. A good agency expects a short review, keeps a record of what has been taught, and treats a mismatch as ordinary rather than as a complaint. IB Gram works this way: you send a query or book a free consultation, questions follow about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, verified profiles that match are shortlisted, a demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match.

What nobody should promise is a specific outcome. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and an assignment process that skips the diagnosis in order to start on Monday is selling speed rather than teaching.
items: 1. Intake: board, programme, subject, level, school calendar, locality and workable days
2. Diagnosis: last report, marked script, and what the subject teacher actually wrote
3. Search: the agency matches its own screened pool against that written requirement
4. Shortlist and demo: meet one or two, before any commitment is made
5. Review in week four, with the option to ask for a different match

contentBlocks.heading: Which programmes an agency can genuinely staff in India
contentBlocks.body:
Staffing gets harder as the programme gets older, and an honest agency will say so. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), and demand from Indian families is concentrated almost entirely at the last of those.

The DP is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects from six groups, three or four taken at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7; Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) contribute up to three further points towards a maximum of 45, with 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) also has to be completed. An agency's real capacity shows at HL. Plenty of pools can cover SL Mathematics in every city they operate in and thin out badly at HL Physics or HL Chemistry, especially in the evening slots every family wants.

MYP staffing has a different failure mode. The programme runs five years across eight subject groups, and every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, with the total out of 32 converted to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A tutor who has taught only national-board syllabuses can teach the content and still miss the criteria entirely. Ask the agency directly whether the tutor has marked against criteria before.

PYP is the honest gap. There are no examinations, most children do not need tuition at all, and an agency that enthusiastically sells PYP packages is worth a second look.
items: DP: deepest demand, thinnest supply at Higher Level in evening slots
MYP: ask whether the tutor has marked against criteria A to D before
PYP: little genuine need; treat an eager sales pitch here with caution
TOK and the Extended Essay are staffed separately from subject teaching
A pool that covers every programme everywhere is a claim worth testing

contentBlocks.heading: Subject cover, and where an agency pool runs thin
contentBlocks.body:
Subject cover is the question that separates a real pool from a long list of names. Ask for it subject by subject rather than as a total, because the total tells you nothing about the one course your child is actually taking.

IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at two levels, so it is four courses rather than one. An agency that cannot tell you which of the four a tutor has taught is guessing. IB Physics and IB Chemistry are usually available at SL across the larger cities and scarcer at HL, and scarcer still where the request includes internal assessment (IA) support close to a school deadline. IB Biology is generally the easiest of the three to staff. IB Economics is well covered in the metros and thin elsewhere. IB English A is the one families most often assume is easy to fill and most often is not, because the texts and tasks are chosen by the school and a tutor has to work with that choice rather than a fixed list.

Then there is the core. TOK and the EE are taught by fewer people than any subject, and an agency will often quietly offer a subject tutor for EE supervision instead. That can work if the essay sits in that tutor's subject and the school's supervisor stays in charge, and it does not work as a substitute for the supervisor.

Command terms are the practical test of subject knowledge. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each demand a different depth of answer. Ask a prospective tutor how they would teach the difference between describe and evaluate in your child's subject. The answer separates a teacher from a graduate with good marks.
items: Ask about cover course by course, not as a headcount across the pool
Mathematics is four courses: AA and AI, each at Higher and Standard Level
Higher Level sciences and IB English A are the usual gaps in a pool
TOK and Extended Essay support is staffed separately and is always scarcer
Test subject depth by asking how they teach describe against evaluate

contentBlocks.heading: Agency reach across India: who really comes to your home
contentBlocks.body:
Reach is claimed nationally and delivered locally, so ask where the tutor for your subject actually lives. In Delhi NCR an agency may hold a genuinely deep pool for South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Golf Course Road, and much less for Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad, where a weekday evening visit means one family per night. Families asking about an IB tutor agency in Delhi from Sector 128 Noida should ask specifically whether the named tutor already teaches in Noida or would be travelling in.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves as several markets. An IB tutor agency in Mumbai can usually staff Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill from within the island and western suburbs, while Powai, Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are better served by tutors who live there. In Bengaluru the belts matter: an IB tutor agency in Bangalore will have different depth in Whitefield and Sarjapur Road than in Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar or Kanakapura Road, with Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Electronic City each behaving as their own pocket.

Gujarat is a supply story. An IB tutor agency in Ahmedabad typically covers Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway well, reaches Gandhinagar at fixed hours, and has far less to offer in Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, where online is often the only honest route.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR is the clearest test of a national claim. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula have a small pool between them; Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have fewer IB tutors still, and an agency promising a home visit there for an HL science should be asked for the tutor's locality before anything is paid. The same question applies to an IB tutor agency in Hyderabad, an IB tutor agency in Chennai, an IB tutor agency in Pune and an IB tutor agency in Kolkata: reach is a person with a scooter, not a map on a website.
items: Ask which locality the named tutor lives in, not which cities the agency lists
Delhi NCR: deep in South Delhi and Golf Course Road, thinner in Ghaziabad and Faridabad
Mumbai: island and western suburbs staffed separately from Thane and Navi Mumbai
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are a different pool from Yelahanka
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun: small pools, so verify before paying

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars an agency has to plan around in India
contentBlocks.body:
An agency that does not ask which school your child attends is not planning anything. The school year in India runs roughly April to March, and IB schools here almost all enter candidates for the May examination session, with November used by a small minority and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. Those dates decide when a pool is stretched and when it is idle, which is why the agency you call in December will sound busier than the one you call in June.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, and mocks drive predicted grades. An agency worth its fee knows that its DP2 assignments have a hard ceiling in January and February, and staffs accordingly instead of taking every enquiry and thinning its existing families' slots.

Households often run two calendars at once. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually across Grades 9 and 10, with Cambridge series in February/March, May/June and October/November and Edexcel series in January and May/June. A family with one child in DP2 and another in Grade 10 is asking an agency to staff two peaks that do not coincide, and that is a reasonable thing to say out loud at the first call.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. School names such as Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School or Oakridge International School appear in enquiries because families write in from them, and no tutor's suitability follows from a school's name.
items: April to March school year, with May the session almost every IB school here uses
Mock dates are set by each school, usually several months before May
Agency capacity tightens from December and loosens after results in early July
Cambridge series run February/March, May/June and October/November
Two children on different boards means two peaks the agency must staff

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits, online or hybrid: what does the agency arrange?
contentBlocks.body:
All three, and the mode you pick changes who carries the risk. A home visit puts the cost of traffic on the tutor and the agency, which is why the radius quietly shrinks over a year. An online assignment removes that cost entirely and widens the pool to the whole country. Hybrid, meaning one home visit and one online session each week with the same tutor, is the arrangement that most often survives a full academic year in a big Indian city.

Ask the agency what it commits to in each mode. For home tutoring, ask about the arrival window, who informs you if the tutor is delayed, and what happens if the tutor moves house in October. For online, ask whether sessions are recorded, whether the tutor can annotate a past paper on screen, and what the fallback is when a link fails. For hybrid, ask which day is which and get it written down, because an unwritten hybrid drifts into an all-online arrangement within a term.

There is a fairness point worth stating. Agencies price home visits higher for a real reason: an evening spent crossing Bengaluru or Delhi is an evening the tutor cannot sell to anyone else. If your subject is scarce and your locality is far from the pool, the honest recommendation is online with a specialist rather than a nearby generalist teaching at home.

And for a younger child, the reverse holds. Attention is harder to hold through a screen, so a home teacher or a short home session usually beats a longer online one at MYP level and below.
items: Home visits: ask about the arrival window and who calls you when a tutor is delayed
Online: ask about screen annotation of past papers and the fallback for a dropped link
Hybrid: fix which day is at home and which is online, in writing
Scarce subject plus distant locality usually means online with a specialist
Younger students hold attention better in home sessions than on screen

contentBlocks.heading: How are tutors sourced and screened before assignment?
contentBlocks.body:
Sourcing and screening are two separate jobs, and an IB tutor agency in India will usually be far more forthcoming about the first. Tutors come from referrals by existing tutors, from applications through the agency's own site, from teacher networks, and from graduates of the programmes themselves. That mix is normal. Screening is what you should ask about, because it is the part that costs the agency money.

A reasonable screen covers identity, the qualifications and teaching experience the tutor claims, and a match between what they say they can teach and the board, programme, subject and level requested. IB Gram verifies profiles on that basis and shortlists only tutors whose verified profile matches your requirement. Beyond that, ask what the agency has actually seen: a subject test, a sample lesson, a recorded demo, feedback from previous assignments. There is a real difference between an agency that has watched a tutor teach and one that has read a curriculum vitae.

You can verify a few things yourself in twenty minutes. Ask which papers or criteria the tutor has prepared students for in this subject at this level, and listen for specifics rather than years. Ask them to talk you through one question from a past paper your child got wrong. Ask what they would set for the first week and how they would check it.

One caution about documents. Marksheets and degree certificates confirm what somebody studied, not what they can teach, and a strong result in a subject at university says very little about teaching a criterion-marked MYP task. Weigh a demo above a document. Then weigh the fourth week above the demo, because that is when you find out whether the planning was real.
items: Identity, claimed qualifications and teaching experience are checked before a profile is shared
Ask whether the agency has ever watched this tutor teach, not just read a CV
Ask which papers or criteria they have prepared students for at this level
A degree certificate proves study, not the ability to teach a criterion-marked task
Judge the demo, then judge week four, which is where planning shows

contentBlocks.heading: Agency, marketplace or direct hire in India: three models compared
contentBlocks.body:
The three models differ on one axis: who is accountable when the arrangement stops working. In an agency model the agency is, because it chose the tutor and it holds the relationship. In a marketplace model you are, because the platform introduced you and the contract sits between you and the tutor. In a direct freelance hire there is nobody in between at all, which is either the cheapest arrangement available or the loneliest, depending on the week.

Read the paperwork with that axis in mind. Ask in writing who your agreement is with, the agency or the individual tutor. Ask what the notice period is on either side, what happens to unused sessions, and whether a replacement is offered at the same rate if the tutor withdraws mid-term. Ask whether the tutor can be engaged directly later, and what the policy says about that, because an unwritten answer becomes an argument in February. None of these questions is rude. Any organisation that treats them as rude has answered them.

The direct hire deserves a fair hearing. A freelance tutor recommended by a parent whose child you know is a genuinely good bet: no intermediary, direct communication, and often a lower rate because there is no business to fund. What you lose is cover. If that tutor moves to another city in September, you restart the entire search in the middle of DP1.

A marketplace gives you choice and speed and asks you to do the screening. An agency does the screening and asks you to accept a narrower field. Choosing between an IB tutor agency in India and the other two models is really a choice about which job you want to keep for yourself.
items: Agency: it chooses, it screens, it replaces; you accept a narrower field
Marketplace: wide choice and fast, with the screening left to you
Direct freelance hire: cheapest and most personal, with no cover if they leave
Get in writing who the agreement is with and what happens to unused sessions
Ask about the replacement policy before you need it, not after

contentBlocks.heading: What warning signs should you look for in an agency's claims?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with anything numeric on the front page. A headline count of tutors on the books cannot be checked by you and rarely means what it appears to mean, since a pool includes everyone who ever registered. Success percentages, score improvements and named results without context are worse, because they describe a selected handful of students and imply the same for yours. And a claim to be first in the country is marketing, not evidence. Treat all of it as noise and go back to asking about the one tutor who will actually sit with your child.

The second category is paperwork. Be wary of a refusal to name the tutor before payment, of a full term demanded in advance with no written cancellation terms, of a scope that never says how many sessions or how long each one is, and of anything described verbally as standard practice without being written anywhere. Ask for the terms by email. An agency that will not put its own policy in an email has told you something.

The third category is language. Promises of a specific grade should end the conversation; no tutor can guarantee a grade, and an agency that says otherwise is either inexperienced or dishonest. Vague reassurance about the best tutors in the city, with no answer about which course the tutor has taught, is the same problem with better manners.

A fair note in the other direction. An agency that tells you your child may not need tuition, or needs one subject rather than three, or should wait until after the next school assessment, is behaving well even though it costs them. That answer is rarer than it should be, and it is a better signal than any badge on a website.
items: Headline counts of tutors and success percentages cannot be verified by you
A refusal to name the tutor before payment is a real warning sign
Insist on written scope: number of sessions, session length, cancellation terms
Any promise of a specific grade should end the conversation
An agency that says your child needs less tuition is worth trusting more

contentBlocks.heading: Questions to ask before you commit to home tuition
contentBlocks.body:
Print this list and take it into the first call, because these questions get harder to ask once money has moved. They apply to an IB tutor agency in India, to a marketplace and to a freelance tutor, with only the wording changing.

Most of them can be answered in five minutes by somebody who knows their own pool, and the hesitations tell you as much as the answers. If the person on the phone has to check whether the tutor has taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, that is fine; if they cannot find out, that is not. Ask everything before the first session rather than after the first invoice.

What happens next at IB Gram is deliberately short to describe. You send a query or book a free consultation. You are asked about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule. Verified profiles that match those needs are shortlisted for you. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid of the two. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match. Availability depends on subject, level and schedule, and nothing beyond that is promised.

One closing thought for parents who have been through a bad arrangement before. The failure is almost never that the tutor was unqualified. It is that nobody wrote down what the tuition was for, so there was no way to tell in week six whether it was working. Fix that at the start and the choice of model matters far less than it seems to now.
items: 1. Which exact course and level has this tutor taught, and for how long?
2. Who is my agreement with, the agency or the tutor, in writing?
3. What is the replacement policy if the tutor withdraws mid-term?
4. What is set between sessions, and how is it checked?
5. What happens to unused sessions, and what notice applies on either side?
6. Can I have a trial session before committing to a term?

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor agency in India do that a marketplace does not?
faqs.answer: It chooses for you and stays accountable for the choice. A marketplace publishes profiles, lets you filter, and leaves the screening, the negotiation and the follow-up to you. An agency takes a written requirement, searches its own screened pool, proposes a small number of tutors, and expects to be called if the arrangement stops working. That accountability is the whole product, so the right test of an agency is not how many tutors it lists but what it does in week four. If the answer is nothing, you are paying agency rates for a marketplace.

faqs.question: Who is my contract actually with, the agency or the tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer by email before paying. Both arrangements exist in India: some agencies contract with you directly and pay the tutor themselves, while others introduce the tutor and step back, leaving the agreement between you and that individual. The difference matters when a session is missed, when a refund is discussed, or when you want to continue with the same tutor next year. Also ask what the policy says about engaging the tutor directly later, because an unwritten understanding on that point turns into a dispute at exactly the wrong time of year.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor leaves in the middle of DP1?
faqs.answer: A reasonable agency offers a replacement at the same terms and passes on the record of what has been taught. That record is the part families forget to ask about. Without it, the new tutor spends three sessions rediscovering what the last one already knew, which is why you should ask for written session notes from the first week, not the first crisis. Ask specifically whether the replacement is offered at the same rate, how quickly, and whether unused sessions carry over. If the answers are vague now, they will be vague in September.

faqs.question: Can an agency arrange home tuition in Gurugram or Thane on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if a tutor for that subject already lives or teaches in that pocket. A home visit on a weekday evening depends on the tutor's other bookings far more than on the agency's coverage map. Along Golf Course Road or in Thane, a tutor who already teaches two families nearby can add a third slot easily; one travelling in from across Delhi NCR or from south Mumbai often cannot hold it past January. So ask where the named tutor lives and what else they teach that evening, before agreeing the day.

faqs.question: Is a school teacher's private tuition better than an agency tutor?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it carries a complication worth naming. A teacher who teaches that course every day knows the school's scheme, the internal deadlines and the assessment style better than anyone an agency can send. But if they also teach your child at school, feedback becomes harder to question and the relationship gets uncomfortable if progress stalls. Many schools also have their own policies on staff tutoring their own students. Check that first. A teacher from a different school often gives you the syllabus knowledge without the conflict.

faqs.question: How should I read an agency's claims about its tutors?
faqs.answer: Treat unverifiable numbers as decoration and ask about the one tutor instead. Counts of tutors on the books, success percentages and results quoted without context describe a selected group, not your child, and none of it can be checked from outside. Replace every claim with a question: which course has this tutor taught, at which level, for how long, and what would they do in the first four weeks. A good agency answers those in a few minutes. A weak one returns to the brochure, which is the answer you needed.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a full term in advance?
faqs.answer: Not without written cancellation terms, and rarely before a trial session. Paying a term up front is common enough and it is not automatically a warning sign, but it should buy you something in return: a fixed number of sessions of a stated length, a named tutor, a clear notice period and a stated position on unused sessions. Ask what happens if the student falls ill for a fortnight, or if the tutor withdraws in week six. A few sessions paid at a time is a fair first arrangement while everyone works out whether the match holds.

faqs.question: We live in Jaipur and cannot find an IB tutor locally. What can an agency do?
faqs.answer: Honestly, it can offer you an online specialist, and that is usually the right answer. Outside Delhi NCR, the pool thins quickly in Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Chandigarh, Ludhiana and Kanpur, particularly at Higher Level and in the Diploma core. An agency that promises a home visit in those cities for a scarce subject should be asked for the tutor's locality before any payment. A hybrid arrangement sometimes works: a local tutor at home for a mainstream subject and an online specialist for the one nobody nearby teaches.

faqs.question: Do agencies help with Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Within limits, and the limits matter more here than anywhere else. A tutor can teach the skills an investigation needs, discuss the shape of a research question, explain a criterion, and give feedback on the student's own draft. The writing and the analysis have to be the student's, and the school's supervisor remains in charge of the Extended Essay. Any agency offering to produce, heavily rewrite or supply an Internal Assessment is offering academic misconduct with a different name, whatever it is called on the invoice.

faqs.question: How quickly should an agency come back with a tutor?
faqs.answer: A first shortlist within a few days is reasonable; a tutor named within an hour usually means no matching was done. Speed depends on the subject and the slot rather than on the agency's efficiency, so an SL Economics request for a Saturday morning fills faster than an HL Chemistry request for six o'clock on a Tuesday in an outlying suburb. Ask for an honest estimate at the first call and ask what will be sent if the ideal match is not available. Availability always depends on subject, level and schedule.

faqs.question: What should the agency ask me before proposing a home tutor?
faqs.answer: The board, the programme, the year, the exact subjects and levels, your school's calendar including mock dates, your locality, and the days you can genuinely hold. Then something about evidence: the last report, a marked script, what the subject teacher wrote. If nobody asks for evidence, the match is being made on your description of the problem rather than on the problem. Parents are usually right that something is wrong and often wrong about what it is, which is exactly what a diagnostic first session is for.

h1: IB Tutor Service in India: What You Should Expect After You Book
heroTitle: The Part of Tutoring India Rarely Explains
heroSubtitle: Booking a tutor is easy. Keeping the arrangement working through a mock week, a monsoon evening, a transfer to another city and a tutor who resigns in January is the part nobody writes down. This page writes it down: replacements, reschedules, reporting and escalation.
introSummary: An IB tutor service in India is judged after the booking rather than before it: how quickly your query is answered, whether the home tutor arrives when promised, and what actually happens in the week the fit turns out to be wrong. Marketing pages stop at the shortlist. Families live with everything that comes afterwards, which is rescheduling around mocks, a tutor who leaves in January, a session lost to rain in Mumbai, and the question of how much a parent is told and how often. This page sets out the operational side plainly: what to expect between the query and the first session, how a replacement is arranged, how missed sessions are handled, the escalation path when something goes wrong, and the promises no honest service will make.

contentBlocks.heading: What Happens Between Your Query and the First Session in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Four things, in order: a conversation about requirements, a shortlist of verified profiles, a demo session, then confirmed slots. Any IB tutor service in India that skips one of those four is selling you a contact rather than an arrangement. IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, level, the school calendar, your locality and your schedule before any name is put forward, because a shortlist assembled without those details is just a list of people who teach the subject.

The requirements call is the step families rush and later regret. It should establish more than the subject. It should establish the level in each subject, whether the difficulty is content or technique, what the last report said, when the school's internal deadlines fall, whether anyone is at home during the proposed hours, and how firm the timing really is once school transport and activities are counted. A family that says any evening works will discover in week three that no evening works.

The demo is a genuine decision point, not a formality. Treat it as an interview run in both directions. The tutor is testing whether they can help this student; you are testing whether they ask before they explain. After the demo, confirm slots in writing, and confirm what happens if either side cannot make one.

How long all of this takes is honestly variable. A widely taught Standard Level subject in a dense part of Delhi NCR or Chennai moves faster than a Higher Level subject in a smaller city. The slowest window of the year is the fortnight after May results are released in early July, when every family reorganises at once. So ask for a realistic timeline at the start, written down, rather than assuming the first session will happen this week. And ask what the service does if the shortlist produces nobody suitable, because that answer separates a service from a directory.
items: 1. Send the query with board, programme, subject, level, locality and timing.
2. Take the requirements call; bring the last report and the school calendar.
3. Receive a shortlist of verified profiles matched to those stated needs.
4. Run a demo or trial session before any commitment is made.
5. Confirm slots, reporting frequency and cancellation terms in writing.

contentBlocks.heading: Service Levels Differ Across PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
The operational load of a tutoring arrangement changes completely with the programme, and a service that runs one process for all three will fail the Diploma Programme families first. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) the arrangement is stable. Sessions are short, deadlines are few, and a missed session can usually be made up the following week without consequence.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) introduces the first real scheduling pressure. It runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, scored 0 to 8, and the total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Community Project lands in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5, and both create weeks where a student needs more contact than the weekly slot allows. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, with on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, is optional and decided school by school, so there is no single national MYP examination in India to plan a service calendar around. That is precisely why reporting matters here: without an external date, drift is invisible.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is where service quality is genuinely tested. Two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), all graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45, with 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) to be completed alongside. Examination sessions run in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May. A tutor lost in DP2 is a different emergency from a tutor lost in MYP 2, and the replacement process has to reflect that.
items: PYP arrangements are stable; a missed week is rarely consequential
MYP projects in Years 3 to 5 create short bursts of extra contact
MYP has no single national examination in India, so reporting replaces deadlines
DP1 to DP2 is a two-year commitment across six subjects and the core
Losing a DP2 tutor in January is the hardest replacement of the whole cycle
Ask how the service handles CAS and TOK weeks that compress subject time

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Cover, Substitutes and What No Service Can Stock
contentBlocks.body:
A service can cover some subjects at short notice and simply cannot cover others, and the honest ones say which is which at the point of booking rather than at the point of crisis. Mathematics at both Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A are taught widely enough across Indian metros that a substitute can usually be found inside a week. That is not true everywhere and it is not true at every level.

Higher Level is the constraint. A student taking HL Economics or HL Chemistry needs a tutor who has taught at that level, and the pool is smaller than the pool for the same subject at Standard Level. Language subjects, and any subject taken by a handful of students in a given city, are harder still. So the question to ask before booking is not whether the service teaches your subject. It is whether the service could find a second person for that subject and level within two weeks if it had to, and in which delivery mode.

The answer changes what you should agree upfront. Where cover is thin, ask for the replacement clause to allow online delivery, because insisting on a home tutor for a rare Higher Level subject in Nagpur or Raipur means waiting rather than switching. Ask also whether a substitute can take two or three sessions while a permanent replacement is arranged, because continuity through a mock week is worth more than a perfect long-term fit arranged slowly.

One more subject-level detail worth settling early. If the student is taking a subject the tutor does not teach, say Biology when the tutor teaches Chemistry, agree explicitly that the tutor will not stray into it. Families drift into this because the tutor is already sitting at the table, and the result is usually an hour of confident, unhelpful teaching.
items: Widely taught subjects can usually be re-covered within a week in a metro
Higher Level pools are smaller than Standard Level pools in every city
Ask at booking whether a second tutor exists for that subject and level
For rare subjects, allow online delivery in the replacement clause
Agree that a tutor will not teach outside the subject they were booked for

contentBlocks.heading: Response Times and Home Visit Coverage Across India
contentBlocks.body:
Coverage is not the same as a map with pins on it, and the difference shows up in how fast a service can respond when something breaks. In Delhi NCR, South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri hold deep supply, so a replacement home tutor can usually be arranged quickly. Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are slower. Gurugram along Golf Course Road and Noida around Sector 128 sit in between, with the practical obstacle being society and gate entry rather than distance; a tutor who is not pre-registered at the gate loses part of every session.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is the hardest place in the country to promise speed. A tutor in Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Powai or Malabar Hill covers a small radius well. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar need someone who already lives there. During the monsoon, a service worth using tells you in advance what its wet-weather rule is: whether a home visit converts to an online session automatically, and who decides.

Chennai behaves differently again. Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are compact, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar stretch the evening commute in ways that decide whether a 7 pm slot survives. Pune splits along two axes, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi on the other. Across central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, local supply for IB subjects thins sharply, and an IB tutor service in India that is honest will say so and lead with online rather than promise a home visit it cannot staff. Bengaluru and Hyderabad sit between the two extremes. Never accept a stated travel time from anyone; ask instead how long the tutor has held their current evening slots.
items: Delhi NCR: pre-register the tutor at the society gate or lose session time
Mumbai: agree a monsoon rule before June, not during the first washout
Chennai: OMR, Perungudi and Velachery commutes decide whether a 7 pm slot holds
Pune: crossing between Kharadi and Hinjewadi midweek is the usual failure point
Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Goa and Nashik: expect online to lead
Ask how long a tutor has held their current slots, never how far away they live

contentBlocks.heading: School Calendars in India That a Tutor Service Must Track
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore are named only as examples of the kind of school whose families use a service like this.

The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and schools here overwhelmingly enter DP candidates for the May session, with results released in early July. An IB tutor service in India that does not hold those dates against every active arrangement will schedule badly. There are four predictable pressure points in a year, and all four generate rescheduling rather than teaching problems: the settling weeks after the year starts, the mock period, the internal deadline cluster, and the study leave that empties the timetable and then floods it.

The cluster is the one that hurts. In DP2, mock examinations, final internal assessment submissions and the Extended Essay deadline tend to fall within a few weeks of each other. Every family wants extra sessions in the same fortnight, and every tutor is already teaching in the evening. So a service should be asking in advance which weeks you will want more contact, and should be candid that extra slots in those weeks depend on availability rather than being something that can simply be arranged on request.

The quieter failure is the opposite one. During study leave and long breaks, families often pause tuition to save money and then find that the slot has gone to another student. Whether a slot is held during a pause, and on what terms, is a question to settle in writing at the beginning, not by message in December.
items: Academic year roughly April to March; May session, results in early July
Four predictable pressure points a year, all of them scheduling problems
In DP2, mocks, IA submissions and the EE deadline collide within weeks
Extra sessions in peak weeks depend on availability and cannot be assumed
Settle in writing whether a slot is held during study leave or a break

contentBlocks.heading: Can You Switch Between Home, Online and Hybrid Mid-Term?
contentBlocks.body:
You should be able to, and the ability to switch without renegotiating everything is one of the clearest tests of a service. Families change modes for ordinary reasons: a relocation from Pune to Hyderabad, an illness, a month of heavy rain, a tutor moving house, or a DP2 student who simply stops wanting anyone in the room while revising.

Home tuition is the default for most families here, and its failure modes are logistical rather than educational. Travel collapses in bad weather, gate entry eats time, a parent is not at home, the dining table is needed for something else. Each of those has a workable answer, and a service should have agreed the answers with you before they are needed. The most useful one is an automatic conversion: if the tutor cannot reach you, the session runs online at the same time rather than being cancelled and chased.

Online is the resilient mode, and it is often the only realistic mode for a Higher Level subject outside the large metros. It also makes short, frequent contact practical. A twenty-minute check on a Thursday before a Friday test is possible on a screen and absurd as a home visit. Against that, it asks more of the student's self-regulation, and it hides the things a tutor notices in a room.

Hybrid, in service terms, means a single arrangement with two delivery modes and one price structure, not two bookings. The common shape is a longer home session at the weekend, where written work is marked together, and a shorter online session midweek. Get the switching rule in writing: who can trigger a switch, by when, and whether it changes the fee. A service that treats a mode change as a new booking will be slow every time you need it.
items: Agree an automatic conversion rule: unreachable tutor means an online session, not a cancellation
Home classes fail on logistics, not teaching; each failure has a pre-agreed answer
Online makes short midweek checks practical in a way home visits never are
Hybrid should be one arrangement with two modes, not two separate bookings
Put the switching rule in writing: who triggers it, by when, and at what fee

contentBlocks.heading: What Is Checked Before Booking, and What Is Rechecked Later?
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile is shortlisted, IB Gram verifies identity and confirms the qualifications and teaching experience a tutor claims, including which programmes, subjects and levels they have actually taught. Verification at the point of booking is the easy half. The harder half is what happens to that check three terms later, when the arrangement has become routine and nobody is watching it.

Ask the service two questions about the ongoing half. First, what triggers a review of an active arrangement: a complaint, a schedule of check-ins, a report cycle, or nothing at all. Second, who at the service actually knows your case. If every message goes to a general number and is answered by a different person each time, the arrangement is being administered rather than managed, and you will re-explain the whole history every time something goes wrong.

There is also a verification job that belongs to you and cannot be delegated. You are the only person who sees the session. Watch for the signals that matter: does the tutor arrive with a plan or ask what the student wants to do today, does the student's own written work increase over a month, does the tutor reference the school's feedback, and can they tell you without notice what the current weakness is. A tutor who answers that last question in one specific sentence is running the arrangement properly.

For home visits, the practical rules stay in force for as long as the arrangement does. Sessions happen in a common area with the door open and an adult in the house, gate and society entry is arranged in advance, and cancellations are communicated by an agreed time rather than at the doorstep. These are not signs of suspicion. They are the ordinary terms of someone working inside your house every week for two years.
items: Identity, qualifications and taught levels are verified before a profile is shortlisted
Ask what triggers a review of an arrangement that has been running for months
Ask who at the service knows your case, and whether that person changes
Test the tutor without notice: what is the current weakness, in one sentence
Home visit rules hold for the whole arrangement, not only the first month

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Replace an IB Home Tutor Without Losing the Term?
contentBlocks.body:
You raise it early, you keep the existing sessions running while the replacement is arranged, and you hand over in writing rather than starting again from nothing. It sounds obvious, and it is the single thing families most often get wrong with an IB tutor service in India. Most families do the opposite. They wait a month hoping it will improve, then stop abruptly, then lose three weeks finding someone new, and the student ends up worse off than if nothing had changed.

Start by separating two very different problems, because they have different remedies. A fit problem means the teaching is competent and the pairing is not working: the student does not speak, the pace is wrong, the personalities grate. A quality problem means the teaching itself is weak: no plan, no reference to criteria, sessions that are conversation rather than work. A fit problem is often solved by a different tutor. A quality problem is a matter for the service, and it should want to hear about it.

The handover is the part that saves the term. Whatever the reason for the change, the incoming tutor should receive the diagnosis, what has been covered, what was deliberately skipped, the marked work and the dates that matter. Without it, the new tutor spends two sessions rediscovering what the last one already knew, in the middle of a year that has no spare fortnight.

One caution about timing. Changing tutors in the weeks immediately before mock examinations is usually a mistake even when the current tutor is mediocre, because a new person cannot build a working relationship and produce results inside three weeks. Better to hold the arrangement through the mocks, use the results as evidence, and change during the break that follows. The exception is a serious concern about conduct or reliability, which is not a scheduling question at all and should be raised the same day.
items: Separate a fit problem from a quality problem before asking for anything
Keep existing sessions running until the replacement is confirmed
Insist on a written handover: diagnosis, coverage, skipped topics, marked work
Avoid switching in the three weeks before mocks unless conduct is the issue
Raise conduct or reliability concerns the same day, not at the term's end

contentBlocks.heading: The Promises an Honest IB Tutor Service in India Will Refuse
contentBlocks.body:
A service that refuses to promise certain things is telling you something useful about the things it does promise. No tutor and no platform can guarantee a grade, a point total or a percentage improvement, because the examination is external, the student's own work carries it, and nobody controls what happens in the room on the day. Any service willing to put a number on the outcome is either careless with language or hoping you will not remember the conversation.

The same applies to a few quieter claims. No service can promise that the same tutor will be available for two full years, because tutors relocate, change jobs and have lives. No service can promise a home visit in every locality, because supply is uneven across India and pretending otherwise leads to a family waiting in Raipur for someone who is never going to come. No service can promise a slot at the most requested hour of the week during the busiest fortnight of the year. Availability is always conditional on level, subject, schedule and season.

What can reasonably be committed to is process. A named point of contact. An agreed response window for messages, written down. A defined path for requesting a different tutor. A stated rule for missed and rescheduled sessions. A reporting rhythm you can hold the service to. Those are promises about behaviour rather than about outcomes, and behaviour is the only thing a service actually controls.

Progress itself should be described carefully. Expect a written diagnosis within the first two or three weeks, and a visible change in the specific thing the tutor named within about six. Subject grades move more slowly than that, and a service that tells you otherwise in October is setting up a disappointment in March. Ask for evidence in the student's own work rather than in reassurance.
items: 1. Write down the problem, with dates and specifics, before contacting anyone.
2. Raise it with the tutor directly first; most issues end here.
3. If unresolved in a week, escalate to your named contact at the service.
4. Ask explicitly for a different match, with the handover in writing.
5. Keep sessions running until the new tutor starts, unless conduct is the issue.

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an IB Tutor Service in India, Step by Step
contentBlocks.body:
Before you book anything, write down five things you want the service to confirm: who your point of contact is, how quickly messages are answered, what happens to a missed session, how a different tutor is requested, and how often you will be told what is happening. A service that answers all five in writing without hesitation is one you can hold to account later. A service that answers in adjectives is not.

Prepare the same small packet for the first session that any good tutor will ask for: the latest school report with its criterion comments, two recent marked pieces of work, the school calendar with mock dates and internal deadlines, and an honest statement of which evenings are genuinely free. It takes twenty minutes to assemble and removes the first two weeks of guessing.

Then keep one habit going for the whole arrangement. Once a month, ask the tutor two questions: what has changed since last month, and what are you doing differently as a result. The answers accumulate into a record of whether the arrangement is working, and they are far more reliable than the impression you form on any single evening.

To begin with an IB tutor service in India, send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, level, your locality and your schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles have been verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, lessons can run at home, online or hybrid, and you can ask for a different match at any point if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on the subject, the level and the time of year, so the earlier you ask, the more choice there is.
items: Get five answers in writing: contact, response window, missed sessions, replacement, reporting
Bring the report, two marked pieces, the calendar and your real free evenings
Ask monthly what changed and what the tutor is doing differently
Choose home, online or hybrid after a trial rather than at the enquiry stage
Request a different match as soon as the fit looks wrong, not at term's end

faqs.question: How quickly should an IB tutor service in India answer my first query?
faqs.answer: Fast enough to tell you the realistic timeline, which matters more than the speed of the first reply. What you want within a day or two is a human conversation about requirements, not an automated message. The shortlist itself takes longer and should: matching a Higher Level subject in a smaller city genuinely takes time. Ask at the outset for a stated response window for ordinary messages and put it in writing, then judge the service against its own number rather than against your expectations.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tutor misses a session without notice?
faqs.answer: Raise it once, politely, and then watch whether it repeats. A single missed session with a late message is ordinary life in Indian cities, particularly during the monsoon in Mumbai or on a bad evening in Bengaluru. A pattern is a service issue and should go to your named contact rather than being absorbed. The arrangement should already specify a notice deadline, whether the session is made up or credited, and whether an unreachable tutor converts the session to online at the same time.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a different tutor, and how awkward is it?
faqs.answer: You can, and it is much less awkward when it goes through the service rather than directly to the tutor. Say what is not working in specific terms: the pace, the lack of a plan, the student not speaking, the absence of marked work. IB Gram can shortlist a different match, and the request itself is treated as ordinary rather than as a complaint. Ask for the handover to be written, so the incoming tutor does not spend two sessions rediscovering the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Do I pay for a session the student misses?
faqs.answer: That depends on the terms you agreed, which is why it belongs in writing before the first session rather than in a message afterwards. The common and reasonable arrangement is a notice period, often the previous evening, after which the session is chargeable, with genuine emergencies handled by discussion. Illness, an unexpected school event and a family obligation are different from forgetting. Settle also what happens during examination study leave and long breaks, because that is where most disputes actually arise.

faqs.question: How often should the service tell me what is happening?
faqs.answer: Monthly at minimum, and immediately when something changes. A useful update names what the student worked on, what improved, what has not moved, and what the next month targets. It should take three sentences, not a template. You should also be told without being asked if sessions are being cut short, if homework is not being done, or if the tutor thinks the arrangement should end. Agree the rhythm at booking and treat silence as information in itself.

faqs.question: Our society does not allow visitors easily. Does that affect home tuition?
faqs.answer: It affects it every single week if it is not handled once at the start. Gated developments in Gurugram, Noida, Kharadi and Thane commonly require pre-registration, an entry pass or a resident's approval per visit, and a tutor stuck at the gate for fifteen minutes loses a quarter of an hour of teaching. Register the tutor as a regular visitor with your society office, share the schedule at the gate, and tell the service so that substitutes are registered too.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but my child still is not progressing?
faqs.answer: Check what was actually measured before concluding anything. Subject grades move slowly, so a month is too short a window; the specific weakness the tutor named should have moved, and if no weakness was ever named, that is the real fault. Ask for the written diagnosis and the plan. If the plan exists and the measure has not shifted in six weeks, the approach needs changing rather than the effort increasing. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and more hours is rarely the correct answer.

faqs.question: We are relocating from Pune to Chennai mid-year. What happens to the arrangement?
faqs.answer: Tell the service before the move rather than after it, because the useful options depend on timing. The simplest continuity is to keep the same tutor online, which removes the handover entirely and matters most in DP2. If you want a home tutor in the new city, the service can shortlist in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam or along Old Mahabalipuram Road, subject to availability, and a short hybrid overlap lets the incoming tutor learn the history before the outgoing one stops.

faqs.question: Is there an escalation path if the service itself is unresponsive?
faqs.answer: There should be, and you should ask what it is before you need it. A reasonable path is a named contact first, a defined response window second, and a route to someone more senior if that window passes. Keep your own record: dates of sessions, dates of messages, what was promised. That record makes an escalation short and factual. If a service cannot tell you at booking who handles an unresolved complaint, treat the answer as a result in itself.

faqs.question: Can we pause tuition during study leave and keep the same slot?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on what was agreed. A weekday evening slot is the scarcest thing a tutor has, and a tutor who holds an empty slot for six weeks is turning away other families. Some arrangements hold the slot at a reduced retainer, some hold it informally, and some release it. None of that is unreasonable; being surprised by it in January is. Ask the question in writing before the first pause rather than at the point of resuming.

faqs.question: Does using an online tutor change the service commitments?
faqs.answer: The educational side changes more than the operational side. Response windows, replacement paths, reporting and escalation should all work identically whichever mode you use. What changes is that travel disruption disappears, short midweek sessions become practical, and the pool of available replacements widens considerably, which matters in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Goa or Nashik where a Higher Level subject may have no local tutor at all. Ask whether the fee structure differs between home, online and hybrid before booking.
