h1: IB Tutor Finder: How to Search, Shortlist and Trial in India
heroTitle: Finding an IB Tutor in India, Step by Step
heroSubtitle: A good shortlist has three names on it, not thirty. This page is the method: where to look, which parts of a profile are noise, the questions that separate an IB subject tutor from a capable general one, and how to run a trial lesson that produces evidence rather than a nice feeling.
introSummary: An IB tutor finder in India is only as useful as the brief you give it, so start by writing down what you actually need: the programme, the subject, the level, and whether you want a home tutor in your own locality or the strongest person available anywhere online. From there the work is narrowing. Most families begin with a list of names from school parents, a search engine and two or three platforms, then stall because every profile reads the same. The method below cuts that list to three, tests each one in a single lesson, and gives you a way to compare the two you liked without guessing. It ends with what to do when none of them is right.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a shortlist actually get built in India?
contentBlocks.body:
An IB tutor finder in India works from a brief, not from a browse. You send a query or book a free consultation and answer six questions: which board and programme, which subject, which level, where you live, which evenings are free, and what has already been tried. IB Gram then shortlists verified profiles that match those answers, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything.

The reason to give a tight brief is that it changes the shortlist more than anything else you do. A request for a Mathematics tutor produces a long list of people who can all teach Mathematics. A request for an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level tutor for a DP1 student in Gachibowli, on Thursday evenings, who has supervised the exploration, produces a short list of people who can actually do that job. Short lists are far easier to judge.

Do exactly the same thing when you search on your own. Write the brief once and send identical text to every source: the school parents group, the platform, the tuition centre two streets away. Identical briefs give comparable replies, and comparable replies are the only reliable way to tell real availability from vague enthusiasm.

Three names is the target. Two is too few to compare properly and five is more trials than any family will actually sit through. If the first round produces one name, widen the mode before you lower the standard. An online tutor in another city is usually a better compromise than a nearby generalist who has never opened an IB paper.
items: Write one brief: board, programme, subject, level, locality, free evenings, what was tried
Send identical text to every source so the replies can be compared honestly
Aim for three names, not thirty, before booking a single trial
Widen the mode before lowering the standard if only one name comes back
Ask for a different match when the shortlist plainly misses the brief

contentBlocks.heading: Which stage are you hiring for: PYP, MYP or DP?
contentBlocks.body:
The stage changes what you are looking for more than the subject does. For a Primary Years Programme (PYP) child there are no external examinations at all, so a candidate's examination record tells you nothing useful. Ask instead how they would spend forty minutes with a seven-year-old who reads slowly, and listen for whether the answer involves the child doing something rather than the tutor explaining something.

In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) a tutor who does not understand criterion marking will teach the wrong thing with great confidence. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, and the total out of 32 converts to a grade of 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. A candidate who cannot tell you which criterion your child is weakest on after reading the report is not an MYP tutor. Ask about the Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and check that they know the limits on what an outsider may do with either.

For the Diploma Programme (DP) the level question decides everything. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level (SL) with 150 hours, each graded 1 to 7. A tutor comfortable at SL may not be comfortable at HL, and that gap surfaces in month two rather than week one. If the diploma core is the problem, that is a separate search: Theory of Knowledge (TOK) has an exhibition of three objects tied to one of 35 prompts, up to 950 words and a third of the grade, and an essay on one of six prescribed titles at up to 1,600 words for the other two thirds. Few subject tutors teach TOK well, and the honest ones volunteer that.

So write the stage and the level into the brief. Never the subject alone.
items: PYP: ask how a candidate would use forty minutes with a slow reader
MYP: a real MYP tutor names the weak criterion from the report, not the topic
DP: SL and HL are different hires, so say which one you need
TOK needs its own search: a 950-word exhibition and a 1,600-word essay
Check the candidate knows the limits on Personal Project and Community Project help

contentBlocks.heading: The three questions that identify a real IB subject tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Three questions, asked on the phone before any trial is booked, will separate an IB subject tutor from a capable general tutor in about four minutes.

The first. Which command terms does this subject's marking hang on, and how would you teach the difference between explain and evaluate? An IB tutor answers immediately, with examples from the subject in front of them. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a student who ignores them loses marks already earned on content. A general tutor will talk about understanding the concept instead, which sounds fine and answers a different question.

The second. What does the internal assessment look like in this subject, and what may you not do with a draft? In IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology the scientific investigation is assessed against published criteria. In IB Economics it is a portfolio of commentaries drawing on different units and key concepts. In IB Mathematics AA and AI it is an exploration. Different work, different rules, different risks. A candidate who answers generally about coursework has not taught the subject at this level. A candidate who volunteers what they will refuse to touch in a draft has just told you something worth more than a certificate.

The third. Here is a past paper question; tell me where students lose marks on it. This one cannot be bluffed. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and a tutor who has read subject reports talks about specific repeated errors rather than about careless mistakes.

Ask all three. Then ask what the first month would look like, and notice whether the answer begins with a diagnosis or with a syllabus.
items: Question one: how would you teach the difference between explain and evaluate?
Question two: what is the IA here, and what may you not do with a draft?
Question three: where do students lose marks on this past paper question?
Listen for subject detail: an exploration is not a scientific investigation
Then ask what the first month targets, and expect a diagnosis before a syllabus

contentBlocks.heading: Searching across India: NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and the south
contentBlocks.body:
Supply is not spread evenly, so the same search behaves differently depending on where you live. In Delhi NCR the pool is large but split. An IB tutor finder in Delhi surfaces people in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri quickly, while families in Dwarka, Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad usually get better results by asking for online candidates first and treating a home visit as the bonus rather than the requirement.

Mumbai has real depth and a geography problem at the same time. An IB tutor finder in Mumbai returns names around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Malabar Hill and Powai, but the creek matters. A candidate in the island city and a student in Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane or Kharghar are describing two quite different weekday evenings. Ask every shortlisted candidate the same travel question and note carefully who hesitates.

Bengaluru and Hyderabad reward a wider search. An IB tutor finder in Bangalore picks up Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar easily and thins towards Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road, where evening traffic between the tech corridors and the older suburbs can stretch a short trip into an unusable one. An IB tutor finder in Hyderabad covers Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Secunderabad and Kokapet, and the same rule holds: the tutor's commute, not their enthusiasm, decides whether the slot survives to March.

Further south the arithmetic changes completely. In Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, the honest question is not how to find an IB tutor nearby but whether one exists for that subject at that level at all. An IB tutor finder in Chennai or an IB tutor finder in Pune still returns a genuine local list. An IB tutor search in India run from a smaller city usually ends with a specialist online, and that is a good outcome rather than a consolation prize. An IB tutor finder in Kolkata and an IB tutor finder in Ahmedabad sit somewhere between the two extremes.
items: Delhi NCR: ask Noida and Faridabad candidates the travel question before the trial
Mumbai: the creek splits the shortlist, so Thane and Vashi families should ask first
Bengaluru and Hyderabad: Whitefield and Gachibowli commutes decide slot survival
Kochi, Coimbatore or Visakhapatnam: check the subject exists locally before searching harder
Typing IB tutor finder near me is where a list starts, never where it ends

contentBlocks.heading: Reading a profile against the school calendar in India
contentBlocks.body:
A profile tells you what a tutor wants you to know. The calendar tells you what they will actually be able to do in December. Read the two together before booking anything at all.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore are each working to their own school's internal deadlines, and those deadlines are what any candidate has to fit around.

Schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May session. November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and May results are released in early July. A tutor who tells you in September that any evening is free may be entirely honest and may simply not yet have the DP2 families who will book them in November. So ask directly. How many students are you carrying into mock season, and which evenings are already committed for the rest of the year?

The useful parts of a profile are narrow. Which syllabuses and which levels, taught for how long, in which mode, and what the tutor will not teach. The rest is noise: photographed certificates, lists of every board in existence, and results nobody outside the family can check. A profile claiming six boards and twelve subjects is describing a catalogue rather than one person's week.
items: Ask how many students the candidate is carrying into mock season
Useful profile fields: syllabuses, levels, years taught, mode, what they refuse
Noise: photographed certificates, twelve subjects, results you cannot verify
Indian schools mostly enter the May session, so December availability is the real test
Match free evenings against your own school's internal deadline calendar

contentBlocks.heading: Should the shortlist include home tutors, online tutors or both?
contentBlocks.body:
Both, in almost every case, and the reason is arithmetic rather than principle. Restricting the search to home tutors in one locality can cut the candidate pool to a handful for a common subject and to nobody at all for a rarer HL one. Restricting it to online candidates throws away the one thing a screen cannot give you.

Home tuition earns its travel time when the problem is how the student works. A tutor at the same table sees the page, the crossed-out line, the exact point where attention goes. For a younger MYP student, and for anyone whose difficulty is written working rather than understanding, home classes are the better first choice and the trial will show you why within twenty minutes.

Online earns its place when the problem is the subject. If your child needs AA HL or a thinly taught Group 3 option, the right person is probably not in your locality, and a weekly video lesson with someone who teaches that level daily beats a nearby generalist learning it alongside them. Online also survives the monsoon, which matters more in Mumbai and Kochi than most shortlists allow for.

Hybrid settles the argument for most families: one home session a week, the rest online. Whatever you choose, run the trial in the mode you intend to book. A candidate who is excellent in your living room can be flat on a screen, and the reverse happens just as often, so testing the wrong mode tells you almost nothing useful. If you are genuinely torn after the first trial, book a second with the same tutor in the other mode and the same material. An hour spent there settles a year.
items: Keep home and online candidates on the same shortlist, then compare like with like
Home classes win when the problem is working, attention or handwriting
Online wins when the problem is the level, especially HL and thin options
Run every trial in the mode you actually intend to book
Hybrid means one home session a week with the rest online, and it suits most families

contentBlocks.heading: What a verified profile in India proves, and what it does not
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram means identity, the qualifications claimed, and the subjects and levels listed have all been checked before the profile goes live. Any honest IB tutor finder in India will describe that as a filter rather than an answer. It removes the worst outcomes of a classifieds search. It does not tell you the person is right for your child.

What a check cannot establish: teaching quality, patience at nine in the evening, whether the tutor marks work between sessions, and whether they will still be available in March. You find those out in the trial and in the first month. Treat verification as the reason it is safe to spend an hour on a trial, not as the conclusion of the search.

Some claims deserve a polite follow-up. Examiner experience is genuinely useful and is often described loosely, so ask which component and in which recent sessions. Professional development workshops come in categories, and attending one does not by itself make somebody an experienced teacher of the subject. Years in an IB classroom correlates best with usefulness and is also the easiest claim to state precisely, so a vague answer there is informative in itself.

Run your own checks too, particularly before home visits. Confirm the name against the identification the person actually carries. Give the society gate in Powai or Gachibowli the correct details in advance, so the first session does not begin with a long argument at the barrier. Agree who will be at home during lessons. And ask the question most families skip: what happens when you are unwell or travelling, and does anybody cover? A candidate who has already thought about that has run tuition before.
items: Verification covers identity, claimed qualifications and the levels listed
It cannot show patience, marking habits or availability next March
Ask which component and which recent sessions behind any examiner claim
Give the society gate the tutor's details before the first home visit
Ask who covers when the tutor is unwell or travelling for work

contentBlocks.heading: Running a trial lesson that tells you something new
contentBlocks.body:
A trial that simply goes well tells you nothing. A trial designed to produce evidence tells you a great deal, and the difference lies almost entirely in what you send beforehand.

Send material. A marked piece of work, ideally one the student did badly on, plus the report comments and the topic the class is doing this week. Say plainly that you want the tutor to work on that marked piece rather than deliver an introduction to themselves. A candidate who arrives without having read it has already answered your most important question, and you have saved a month.

Then watch four things during the hour. How much of the talking the student does, which should rise as the lesson goes on. Whether the tutor finds the real misconception or treats the symptom, which you can hear in the questions they ask rather than in the explanations they give. Whether anything gets marked against actual criteria in front of the student. And what the last five minutes contain, because a session that ends with one specific piece of work set is a session with a next step attached.

Afterwards ask two questions. Ask the student what they understand now that they did not understand this morning; a vague answer is a result, not a failure of the question. Ask the tutor what they think the underlying problem is and what the first month would target. When those two answers point the same way, you have a match worth booking.

Run both trials in the same week, on the same material. Memory fades quickly, and a fortnight's gap turns a comparison into a preference.
items: 1. Send a marked script, the report comments and this week's class topic in advance
2. Ask for work on that script, not an introduction to the subject
3. Watch who is talking, and whether the student talks more by the end
4. Check whether anything is marked against real criteria during the hour
5. Afterwards ask the student what changed and the tutor what month one targets

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing two shortlisted tutors without guessing
contentBlocks.body:
Two good trials leave most families stuck, because both tutors were pleasant and the student said both were fine. Comparison needs something firmer than an impression, and the point of an IB tutor finder in India is to make the comparison possible rather than to make it for you.

Score the two candidates on four things you actually observed, and write the scores down before discussing them with anyone. Diagnosis: did the tutor identify a specific problem in the student's own work and name it? Evidence of marking: did they show the student where a mark was lost against a criterion or a markscheme? Plan: can they say what the first month covers and why in that order? Fit with the week: does the slot they offered survive traffic, activities and the student's energy on that particular day?

Diagnosis usually decides it. A tutor who correctly works out that the student understands the physics and cannot structure an extended answer will be more useful than a warmer candidate who plans to reteach the topic from the beginning. Where both diagnoses agree, take the better slot, because the arrangement you can keep beats the one you admire.

When nobody on the shortlist is right, stop and change one variable rather than booking the least bad option. Change the mode. Change the level of specialism you are asking for. Widen the city. Sometimes the correct conclusion is that the student does not need a tutor this term and needs a frank conversation with the subject teacher instead, and that conclusion saves more time than any amount of searching.

No tutor can guarantee a grade. What a good one can do is tell you, after a single hour, something about your child's work that you did not already know.
items: Score diagnosis, marking evidence, the first-month plan and the slot's realism
Write the scores down before discussing them with anyone else
Diagnosis beats warmth: the sharper diagnosis usually makes the better tutor
Equal diagnoses means take the slot that survives an ordinary week
If nobody fits, change one variable rather than booking the least bad option

contentBlocks.heading: Starting the search: what to send, and a home tutor brief that works
contentBlocks.body:
The brief is the whole search compressed into one message, so it is worth ten minutes of your evening. Include seven things: board and programme, subject, level, the student's grade or year, your locality, the evenings that are genuinely free, and one sentence on what has already been tried. That last line alone saves everybody a week.

Add the awkward details rather than hiding them. If the student has refused tuition before, say so. If two earlier tutors did not last, say why they did not. A home tutor brief that mentions a strict gate policy, a small flat with a sibling on an online class in the next room, or a parent who travels every week will produce a shorter shortlist and a considerably better one.

Say what you want from the first month too. Wanting the IA finished, wanting Paper 1 technique fixed, and wanting a child who stops dreading Mathematics are three different requests, and they suit three different people.

Then send it. An IB tutor finder in India should ask about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule before it shows you anybody, which is what IB Gram does before shortlisting verified profiles. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, availability depends on level and schedule, and if the match is wrong you can ask for a different one. Nothing in the first month has to be permanent, which is exactly why the search is worth doing properly rather than quickly.
items: Send seven things: board, subject, level, year, locality, free evenings, what was tried
Include the awkward details, because they shorten the shortlist and improve it
State in one sentence what the first month should achieve
Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability
Ask for a different match if the first shortlist misses the brief

faqs.question: Where do Indian families actually find IB tutors?
faqs.answer: Four places, and each one fails differently. School parent groups give trusted names but a tiny pool and no verification. A search engine gives volume and no filter. Tuition centres are easy to visit and rarely one-to-one. Platforms check profiles before listing them and can arrange a trial. Most families use an IB tutor finder in India alongside word of mouth, then judge every name from both sources by the same trial lesson rather than by where it came from.

faqs.question: How many tutors should be on a shortlist?
faqs.answer: Three names, trialled down to two, then one. Fewer than three gives you nothing to compare against, and more than three means you will never actually run the trials, because each one costs an evening and a certain amount of household negotiation. If your first round produces only one name, that is a signal to widen the mode or the city rather than to settle immediately for whoever replied first.

faqs.question: What should I send a tutor before a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: A marked piece of work the student did badly on, the latest report comments, and the topic the class is covering this week. Add one line saying what you want from the hour. This costs you five minutes and changes the trial completely: instead of a polite introduction you get to watch somebody diagnose a real problem, which is the only thing you are actually trying to assess.

faqs.question: How do I check a home tutor is who they say they are?
faqs.answer: Confirm the name on the profile against identification the person carries, and do it at the first home visit rather than the fourth. On a verified platform, identity and claimed qualifications are checked before a profile goes live, which is a real filter but not a substitute for your own look. Register the tutor's details with the society gate in advance, agree who will be at home during sessions, and keep the study area within earshot of the rest of the flat.

faqs.question: Nobody near us teaches the subject at the level we need. What now?
faqs.answer: Widen the mode before you widen your standards. A specialist teaching that exact level online every week is a better hire than a local generalist who will learn the syllabus alongside your child. Ask the school coordinator whether other families are in the same position, since a shared online group sometimes forms that way. And check whether the gap is really the subject or the school's own teaching, because those need different responses.

faqs.question: Is a nearby home tutor better than a stronger tutor online?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is going wrong. If the student's difficulty is careless working, handwriting under time pressure or simply not starting, somebody in the room wins clearly. If the difficulty is depth at Higher Level, the stronger online tutor wins just as clearly. When you cannot tell which it is, run one trial of each in the same week on the same marked script, and the answer usually becomes obvious within the hour.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutors when both trial lessons went well?
faqs.answer: Score them on four observable things rather than on how the hour felt. Did each one name a specific problem in the student's own work? Did they show where a mark was lost against a criterion? Can they describe what the first month covers and in what order? Does their slot survive a normal week? Diagnosis is usually the tie-breaker. Where diagnoses match, take the tutor whose timing you can actually keep.

faqs.question: We are in Whitefield in Bengaluru and every candidate lives across the city. What should we ask?
faqs.answer: Ask what their current commute to a student looks like on a Wednesday evening, not whether they are willing to travel. Willingness is free in September and expensive in January. Ask whether they already teach anyone in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road or Electronic City, because a tutor with one student nearby will hold a second slot far more reliably. Then propose a hybrid pattern before they do.

faqs.question: Should the trial lesson be free?
faqs.answer: A demo or trial session can be arranged before a family commits, and many tutors treat the first meeting as a diagnostic rather than a paid lesson. Do not make it the deciding factor. A tutor who charges for a genuinely useful diagnostic hour is a better buy than one who gives away a pleasant hour that teaches you nothing. Ask what the hour will contain, and judge the answer rather than the price.

faqs.question: What are the warning signs in a tutor profile?
faqs.answer: Breadth without depth is the main one. Twelve subjects across six boards describes a catalogue rather than a person. Also watch for results you cannot verify, vague examiner claims with no component named, reluctance to say which levels they teach, and any language about assured outcomes. A profile that states two subjects, two levels and what the tutor does not teach is far more credible than one promising everything.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and found nobody locally. Does an online specialist really work?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most subjects, and families across Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam and Madurai do this routinely. The trade-offs are real: written working is harder to follow, the student needs a quiet corner and a stable connection, and attention has to be actively managed. Test it properly with a trial in that exact mode. If handwriting and method marks are the problem, pair the online specialist with occasional home sessions from a local generalist.

comparison.heading: Which kind of IB tutor should a family in India shortlist?
comparison.intro: These four options are not ranked, and the right one changes with the problem you are solving. A student whose written working is a mess needs somebody in the room. A student who needs a rarer Higher Level subject needs the person who teaches it daily, wherever they live. Read each row against your own case rather than looking for an overall winner.

An online tutor anywhere in India
A tuition centre in your neighbourhood
A specialist in another city, online

h1: IB Tutor Platform in India: Profiles, Verification and Matching
heroTitle: What an IB Tutor Platform Does in India
heroSubtitle: A platform is not a directory with better design. It checks who a tutor is before you ever see the profile, holds a record of the arrangement, and keeps a route open when the match is wrong. Here is what that covers for home tuition and online lessons, and what it cannot cover.
introSummary: An IB tutor platform in India is a place where tutor profiles are verified before a family sees them, matched against one specific request, and booked for home tuition, online lessons or a hybrid of the two. That is a different thing from a classifieds listing, where anyone can post, and from a WhatsApp parents group, where the recommendation is real but the checking is somebody's memory. This page sets out the mechanism: what verification actually covers before a profile goes live, what a good profile shows field by field, how matching runs end to end, what safeguarding looks like when a stranger teaches your child at your dining table or through a screen, and the checks that stay yours no matter which platform you use.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a tutor platform in India turn a query into a shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Matching is a sequence, not a search box. You send a query or book a free consultation, a short conversation establishes what is actually wrong, verified profiles are shortlisted against that brief, a trial or demo session is arranged, and lessons begin at home, online or hybrid. If the fit is poor, you ask for a different match. Each of those steps exists because the step before it produces something the next one needs.

The brief is the part families underestimate. A request that says Physics tutor, Grade 11, Powai is not yet a brief. A request that says Higher Level Physics, DP1, struggling with the written explanation questions rather than the calculations, school mocks in January, two free evenings after seven, prefers a tutor at home is a brief, and it produces a very different shortlist. The consultation exists to turn the first into the second.

Shortlisting weighs four things against each other: subject and level, availability at the hours you named, travel radius if you want home classes, and teaching style against the student's temperament. Those four pull in different directions. A tutor who is right on subject may be an hour of evening traffic away from Koregaon Park. Something gets traded, and it is better to choose the trade deliberately than to discover it in week three.

Then comes the part no platform can do for you. Sit in on some of the trial. Ask the student afterwards. A shortlist is a filtered set of plausible people, and the filtering is real, but the judgement about your own child stays with you.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, with subject, level and city.
2. A short call turns a vague request into a specific teaching brief.
3. Verified profiles are shortlisted against subject, level, hours and travel radius.
4. A demo or trial session is arranged before any commitment is made.
5. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, on the agreed weekly slots.
6. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong; it is expected.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB programmes a profile should name, and how precisely
contentBlocks.body:
A profile that says IB tutor tells you almost nothing. The International Baccalaureate runs three programmes that ask different things of a teacher, so the useful profile names the programme, the year and the level.

For the Diploma Programme (DP), precision matters most. The DP is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, with Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) completed alongside. A profile should therefore say HL or SL, not merely the subject, and should say whether the tutor has taught DP2 through to the May session or only DP1 content.

The Middle Years Programme is a different craft. MYP assessment is criterion-based rather than examination-driven, and a tutor who has only taught DP will often mark MYP work as though it were a shorter DP answer. Look for a profile that mentions criteria and the kind of tasks the student is actually set.

The Primary Years Programme asks for something different again: a teacher comfortable with young children, inquiry-led units, and a parent in the next room. For PYP, home tutoring is nearly always the right mode, so travel radius on the profile matters more than anything else.

One warning. A tutor who lists every programme and every subject group is either extraordinary or imprecise, and imprecise is far more common. Narrow profiles are usually the more honest ones.
items: A DP profile should state HL or SL, not just the subject name.
Ask whether the tutor has taught DP2 through to a May session.
MYP needs criterion-based marking experience, which DP-only tutors often lack.
PYP profiles: travel radius and patience with young children matter most.
A profile claiming every programme and subject group deserves harder questions.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you read the subject claims on a tutor profile?
contentBlocks.body:
Read every subject line as a claim that has to be testable, because that is exactly what it is. A profile is marketing until the trial turns it into evidence, and the questions that turn it are subject-specific.

In Mathematics, the claim to test is the exploration. The mathematics internal assessment (IA) is the same task for Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) at both levels: 20% of the final grade, 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 on five criteria, which are A Presentation (4 marks), B Mathematical communication (4), C Personal engagement (3), D Reflection (3) and E Use of mathematics (6), with HL judged against a higher standard on criterion E. A tutor who genuinely supervises explorations can say which criterion Indian students usually lose marks on and why. A tutor who cannot will talk about topics instead.

In the sciences, ask how they handle an extended response against the command term. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a science tutor who treats all six as a request for information is teaching the wrong thing. In English A, ask whether they work on literary analysis or on language support, because those are two jobs and profiles blur them constantly.

Across every subject, ask which past papers, markschemes and subject reports the tutor works from. Those come through the school or the IB's official channels and show how marks are actually awarded. A tutor who never mentions them is teaching content and hoping.

Write the answers down during the trial. Two weeks later, all four tutors sound the same in memory.
items: Mathematics: ask which exploration criterion students most often lose marks on.
Sciences: ask how they teach the difference between explain and evaluate.
English A: literary analysis and language support are two different jobs.
Every subject: ask which past papers, markschemes and subject reports they use.
Write down trial answers; tutors blur together within a fortnight.

contentBlocks.heading: IB tutor platform in India: how coverage differs by city
contentBlocks.body:
An IB tutor platform in India covers the country unevenly, and one that pretends otherwise is not being straight with you. What changes between cities is not the mechanism but the size of the local pool and the travel maths inside it.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, supply is deep but the geography is unforgiving. A tutor in Bandra or Juhu will rarely take a weekday evening home visit in Thane or Kharghar, and a family in Navi Mumbai or Vashi is often better served by pooling the search across the whole region online while keeping home classes for one subject. Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit close enough to several tutor pools that a same-locality match is realistic.

Bengaluru divides along its own commute lines. An IB tutor platform in Bangalore, as most parents still say, is really matching within corridors: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road on one side, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout in the middle, Hebbal and Yelahanka north, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road south. Evening traffic between those corridors can stretch a short trip badly, which is why so many Bengaluru families end up hybrid.

An IB tutor platform in Hyderabad concentrates around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Kokapet and Secunderabad drawing from a smaller set. An IB tutor platform in Pune works similarly across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad.

Kolkata and eastern India is the clearest case for pooling. Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat carry a workable local pool, so an IB tutor platform in Kolkata can usually match a home tutor for common subjects. Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna cannot, and there an online IB tutor platform is the realistic answer. The same logic applies to an IB tutor platform in Delhi across Dwarka, Noida and Gurugram, to Chennai, and to an IB tutor platform in Ahmedabad.
items: Mumbai: deep supply, but harbour and suburban distance decide home visits.
Bengaluru: matching happens inside commute corridors, not across the whole city.
Hyderabad: the western corridor holds most supply; Secunderabad draws from less.
Pune: Hinjewadi to Koregaon Park on a weekday evening is a real obstacle.
Kolkata has a workable pool; Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna need online matching.
Ask a platform directly what it can and cannot cover in your locality.

contentBlocks.heading: What a platform knows about your school calendar in India
contentBlocks.body:
Very little, until you tell it. This is the most common gap between what families expect from a platform and what any platform can actually hold. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, so it has no access to internal school documents. Schools of the kind families here attend, among them Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Indus International School and Mahindra International School, each set their own internal deadlines and mock examination dates, and those live inside the school.

So the platform asks you. The matching conversation includes the school calendar for a practical reason: a tutoring plan built without mock dates is a plan built blind. Each school fixes its own DP2 mocks, usually several months before the May session. Indian schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for May rather than November, the academic year runs roughly April to March, and May results are released in early July. Those four facts frame every tutoring timetable in the country.

What you can usefully hand over in the first week is short: the internal deadline sheet for internal assessments, the mock examination window, the reporting dates when criterion feedback or predicted grades appear, and the school holiday list. A tutor holding those can plan a term instead of reacting to it.

There is a boundary to respect here too. A tutor works alongside the school, not against it. When a tutor and a subject teacher disagree about an approach to an IA, the coordinator's guidance governs, and any platform that encourages a family to work around the school is doing something reckless.

Ask your coordinator for the deadline sheet. It takes one email and it changes the whole arrangement.
items: Platforms hold no school documents; the calendar comes from you.
Hand over the internal deadline sheet and mock window in week one.
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates ahead of the May session.
Reporting dates matter: criterion feedback and predicted grades shape the plan.
Where a tutor and the school disagree, the coordinator's guidance governs.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: what the platform actually arranges
contentBlocks.body:
All three are bookable, and the platform's job is to make the differences explicit before you choose rather than after. A home tutor travels to your address and teaches at your table. An online tutor teaches over a video call from anywhere in the country. Hybrid mixes the two on a fixed pattern, most often a longer home session at the weekend and a shorter online slot midweek.

The trade-off is simple to state and hard to feel until you have tried both. Home classes buy presence: the tutor sees the working, the hesitation and the page the student would rather not show, and a student who does not start work without someone in the room will start. Online buys reach: the pool is national, so a scarce Higher Level subject becomes findable, and nobody spends an hour in traffic. Hybrid buys a bit of each and asks you to hold two habits instead of one.

The practical differences that families notice are administrative. A home visit needs a confirmed address, gate and society access, and a slot long enough to absorb travel at both ends. An online lesson needs a device, a headset and a tested connection. A hybrid arrangement needs both, plus an agreement about which work happens where, or the midweek session quietly becomes a chat.

Mode also interacts with age. For a PYP or early MYP child, home tutoring is usually the only arrangement that holds. For a DP2 student revising Higher Level content, online is frequently better, because the specialist is more important than the proximity.

Change the mode if it is not working. Switching from online to home lessons, or the other way, is an ordinary request and should not need a new tutor.
items: Home tuition: your address, your table, travel time built into the slot.
Online: a national pool, which matters most for scarce HL subjects.
Hybrid: a longer home session weekly plus a shorter online review midweek.
Home visits need gate and society access agreed before the first lesson.
Younger students need home classes; DP2 revision often works better online.
Changing mode should not require changing tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: What does verification cover before a profile goes live?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on an IB tutor platform in India should mean something specific. On IB Gram it covers identity, the qualifications a tutor claims, and their stated teaching experience, checked before a profile is shortlisted to any family. That sentence is the whole promise, and the useful part of this section is what sits outside it.

Verification cannot tell you how a tutor teaches. It cannot predict whether a quiet fifteen-year-old will talk to this particular adult, whether the tutor will stay patient in week nine when the same misconception returns, or whether they will actually mark the work they set. Those are behaviours, and behaviours are observed, not documented. That is why the trial session exists and why nobody should skip it.

Verification also cannot see into a school. A platform does not know your child's predicted grades, the internal deadlines, or what the subject teacher has already tried. You supply that.

Set against the alternatives, though, the difference is substantial. On a classifieds site, the only filter is whoever paid to post, and a qualification is a line of text nobody has looked at. In a parents WhatsApp group the recommendation is genuine, which is its strength, but it is one family's experience with one child in one subject, and nobody has checked a document.

What a platform adds beyond checking is a record and a route. There is a record of what was agreed, and a route to raise a problem that is not an awkward conversation at your own front door. Families underrate that second point until the week they need it.

Ask any platform, including this one, two questions: what exactly do you verify, and what do you not verify? An answer that is specific on both halves is the one to trust.
items: Verified before shortlisting: identity, claimed qualifications, stated teaching experience.
Not verifiable: patience, marking discipline, and fit with your child.
A platform holds no school data; predicted grades and deadlines come from you.
Classifieds filter by who paid to post, not by who was checked.
A platform adds a record of the arrangement and a route to raise problems.
Ask what is verified and, just as directly, what is not.

contentBlocks.heading: Platform, classifieds site or a WhatsApp group: what changes?
contentBlocks.body:
Three routes, three different risk profiles. Most Indian families use all three at once without noticing, so it helps to separate them.

A classifieds site is an open noticeboard. Anyone can list, listings rank by payment or recency rather than quality, and the same tutor often appears under three different names and rates. The contact happens off the site, so nothing about the arrangement is recorded anywhere. What you gain is volume and speed. What you lose is every check, and the loss is invisible until something goes wrong.

A parents WhatsApp group is the opposite. The information is trustworthy because it comes from someone with no incentive to mislead you, and it carries detail no profile ever will, such as the fact that the tutor is excellent with a hard-working student and hopeless with a distracted one. Its weaknesses are coverage and bias. The group knows the tutors the group has used, which skews towards one locality and a few common subjects, and nobody in the group has verified a certificate. A good tutor recommended by a neighbour in Alipore is still worth pursuing. Just run the same checks you would run on a stranger.

A platform sits between the two. It holds a verified profile before you see it, matches against a stated brief rather than proximity alone, arranges a trial, keeps a record of what was agreed, and gives you somewhere to go when the match is wrong. It costs more than a classifieds listing, because checking and matching are work that somebody does.

Use the group for reputation, the platform for verification and continuity, and treat classifieds as a last resort. And never use any of them as a substitute for sitting in on the first session.
items: Classifieds: open listing, no checks, nothing recorded, ranked by payment.
WhatsApp group: honest and detailed, but narrow coverage and nothing verified.
Platform: verified profile, brief-based matching, trial, record, and a replacement route.
A neighbour's recommendation is a starting point, not a completed check.
Whichever route you use, sit in on part of the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: Safeguarding basics for home lessons and online lessons in India
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor is an adult alone with your child, at your table or on a screen, and the sensible arrangements are dull and worth making anyway. None of this implies suspicion of a particular person. It is the same logic as a seatbelt.

For home sessions, teach in a shared space rather than a bedroom, with the door open. Keep an adult at home during the lesson, especially for a younger student. Establish who at the gate is expected and on which days, so the society register and the guard are not improvising. Fix the slot and the duration rather than letting sessions drift late. And be present at the end of the session often enough that a short conversation with the tutor is normal rather than an event.

For online sessions, the same principles translate. The lesson happens in a shared room with the screen visible, not behind a closed bedroom door. Communication stays on the platform channel rather than a personal number or a social media account. Agree the recording policy in writing at the start, whichever way you decide. Confirm that the person on the call is the person on the profile, at the first session and again if anyone unfamiliar appears.

For both modes, payment belongs through the agreed channel, not in cash that leaves no record of what was booked.

And tell your child, plainly, that they can say if anything feels off, including something small like a tutor who is consistently sarcastic. Students often assume that a complaint means losing the tutor and disappointing a parent, so they say nothing for months. Say the opposite out loud, early.

If something does go wrong, raise it with the platform rather than handling it at your own doorstep. That is one of the things a platform is for.
items: Home lessons in a shared room with the door open, an adult at home.
Agree gate and society access in advance so entry is never improvised.
Online lessons in a shared room; communication stays on the platform channel.
Agree the recording policy in writing before the first paid session.
Pay through the agreed channel, so what was booked stays on record.
Tell your child early that raising a concern will not cost them anything.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting on an IB tutor platform in India: what to send
contentBlocks.body:
The quality of the first message to an IB tutor platform in India decides how good the shortlist is, so spend ten minutes on it rather than two.

Send the programme and year: PYP, MYP or DP, and which year of the two-year Diploma Programme if that applies. Send the subject and the level, HL or SL, because those produce different tutors. Send the evidence you already hold: the last report, a marked script, a returned IA draft, or the comment a teacher made at the parent meeting. Evidence turns a guess into a diagnosis.

Then send the logistics, which decide as much as the academics. Your city and locality, so travel radius can be assessed for home classes. The two or three weekly slots you can genuinely keep, not the ones you wish you could. Your preferred mode, and whether you are open to hybrid. The school's mock window and internal deadline sheet, if you have it.

One more thing is worth writing down: what you want to be different in two months. Not a grade. A behaviour, such as the student attempting a question before asking for help, or showing working instead of jumping to an answer. That sentence gives the tutor something to aim at and gives you something to measure against.

After that, the process is the one described above. A consultation, a shortlist of verified profiles, a trial session, then lessons at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability at the level and hours you need. If the match is wrong, say so in the first month and ask for another. That is how the mechanism is meant to be used, and using it that way is not a complaint.
items: Send programme, year, subject and level: HL and SL need different tutors.
Attach real evidence: a report, a marked script or a returned draft.
Give locality and realistic weekly slots, not aspirational ones.
Say your preferred mode and whether hybrid is acceptable.
Name one behaviour you want changed in two months, not a grade.

faqs.question: What exactly does IB Gram verify before a tutor appears in my shortlist?
faqs.answer: Identity, the qualifications a tutor claims, and their stated teaching experience, all checked before the profile is shortlisted to a family. What verification does not cover is how the person teaches your particular child, whether they mark what they set, or how they behave in week nine when the same mistake reappears. Those are only visible in practice, which is why a trial session is arranged before you commit and why sitting in on part of it is worth your time.

faqs.question: How is a platform different from a tutor listing site?
faqs.answer: A listing site is an open noticeboard where anyone can post and ranking usually follows payment rather than quality. Contact moves off the site immediately, so nothing about the arrangement is recorded and no document has been checked by anyone. A platform verifies the profile before you see it, matches against a written brief rather than proximity alone, arranges a trial, keeps a record of what was agreed, and gives you a route to change the match. You pay for that work.

faqs.question: A parent in our building recommended someone. Do I still need a platform?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and a recommendation from someone who has watched the tutor work is genuinely valuable. Just remember what it is and is not. It covers one child, in one subject, at one level, and nobody in that group has seen a certificate. Run the same checks you would run on a stranger: qualifications, level taught, how they mark, and a trial with your own child. Reputation and verification answer different questions, and you want both.

faqs.question: What should a good tutor profile show, field by field?
faqs.answer: Programme and level, stated separately: DP with HL or SL named, MYP with criterion experience, PYP with age range. Subjects listed narrowly rather than exhaustively. Teaching experience with years and the kind of setting. Availability by day and time, and travel radius if home tuition is offered. Modes offered: home, online or hybrid. A short description of how they run a session. A profile listing twenty subjects across three programmes is telling you something, and it is not what it intends.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a home tutor in my own locality specifically?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should say it at the query stage rather than later, because travel radius is one of the four things shortlisting weighs. Being specific helps: naming Whitefield, Kondapur, Alipore or Baner produces a better shortlist than naming the city. Understand the trade-off though. Insisting on the same locality narrows the pool, and for a scarce Higher Level subject it may narrow it to nobody, at which point online or hybrid is the realistic answer.

faqs.question: Who should be at home while a tutor teaches my child?
faqs.answer: An adult, in the house, for the whole session, particularly for a younger student. The lesson belongs in a shared space with the door open rather than in a bedroom, and it helps if you are visible at the end often enough that a brief conversation with the tutor feels ordinary. This is not about suspecting anyone. It is a standing arrangement that removes ambiguity for everybody, including the tutor, and it also means you hear how the session actually went.

faqs.question: How does the platform handle a tutor who stops turning up on time?
faqs.answer: Raise it early and through the platform rather than at your own front door. Punctuality problems almost never fix themselves, and they are easier to resolve as a recorded issue than as an awkward personal conversation. The practical route is a note of what happened and on which dates, a clear statement of the slot you agreed, and a request to either fix it or change the match. Families wait far too long before doing this.

faqs.question: Does a platform know my child's predicted grades or school deadlines?
faqs.answer: No, and no platform in India does. Schools hold that information internally, and IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any school, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. The matching conversation asks you for the calendar because of this gap: mock examination dates, internal assessment deadlines and reporting dates change what a sensible tutoring plan looks like. Sending the deadline sheet in the first week makes the whole arrangement more useful.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach at home one week and online the next?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and hybrid is a normal arrangement rather than an exception. Many families in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Pune fall into it because of traffic: a longer home session at the weekend and a shorter online slot midweek for marking or a draft discussion. Agree the pattern rather than improvising it, and agree what work belongs to each mode, otherwise the online session drifts into a conversation and the home session absorbs everything.

faqs.question: How quickly does a shortlist come back?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the level and the hours you have named, and a common Standard Level subject fills faster than a rare Higher Level one. A request that is open to online, or open on timing, is matched sooner than one that insists on a home visit in a specific locality at a specific hour. Rather than pushing for speed, push for a better brief. A fast shortlist against a vague request wastes more time than it saves.

faqs.question: What are the checks that stay mine no matter which platform I use?
faqs.answer: Four of them. Sit in on part of the first session and listen to who is talking. Ask the student privately whether anything became clearer. Check after three or four weeks that work set is actually being marked and returned. And look at whether the tutor can describe your child's specific weakness in a sentence, rather than describing the syllabus. No verification process can do any of these, and they catch most mismatches inside a month.

faqs.question: Is a platform worth the cost compared with finding a tutor directly?
faqs.answer: An IB tutor platform in India is worth paying for when checking, matching and continuity are the things you lack. If you already have a trusted name, the time to check their claims, and a plan for what happens if it fails, direct is cheaper and perfectly sensible. If you are searching a scarce subject, or you are new to a city, or you want the arrangement recorded and replaceable, the checking and matching are the thing you are actually buying. Families usually discover the value of the replacement route rather than the search.

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually yes, and hybrid is a normal arrangement rather than an exception. Many families in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Pune fall into it because of traffic: a longer home session at the weekend and a shorter online slot midweek for marking or a draft discussion. Agree the pattern rather than improvising it, and agree what work belongs to each mode, otherwise the online session drifts into a conversation and the home session absorbs everything.

mainEntity.name: How quickly does a shortlist come back?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the subject, the level and the hours you have named, and a common Standard Level subject fills faster than a rare Higher Level one. A request that is open to online, or open on timing, is matched sooner than one that insists on a home visit in a specific locality at a specific hour. Rather than pushing for speed, push for a better brief. A fast shortlist against a vague request wastes more time than it saves.

mainEntity.name: What are the checks that stay mine no matter which platform I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four of them. Sit in on part of the first session and listen to who is talking. Ask the student privately whether anything became clearer. Check after three or four weeks that work set is actually being marked and returned. And look at whether the tutor can describe your child's specific weakness in a sentence, rather than describing the syllabus. No verification process can do any of these, and they catch most mismatches inside a month.

mainEntity.name: Is a platform worth the cost compared with finding a tutor directly?

acceptedAnswer.text: An IB tutor platform in India is worth paying for when checking, matching and continuity are the things you lack. If you already have a trusted name, the time to check their claims, and a plan for what happens if it fails, direct is cheaper and perfectly sensible. If you are searching a scarce subject, or you are new to a city, or you want the arrangement recorded and replaceable, the checking and matching are the thing you are actually buying. Families usually discover the value of the replacement route rather than the search.

finalCta: Send a query or book a free consultation with the programme, subject and level, your locality, and the weekly slots you can realistically keep. IB Gram asks about the school calendar and schedule, shortlists verified profiles against that brief, and arranges a trial session before anything is committed. Lessons then run at home, online or hybrid, and if the match is wrong you can ask for a different tutor.

A school teacher knows the internal deadlines better than anyone outside the building. A platform adds checking, brief-based matching and somewhere to go when the arrangement stops working. Decide by which of those you are short of.
