h1: IB Teachers in India: What Qualifications and Training Mean
heroTitle: Reading an IB Teacher's Credentials in India
heroSubtitle: Workshop certificates, examiner experience, a master's degree, fifteen years in a classroom. Four claims, four different meanings, and only one of them tells you how your child's Thursday evening home tuition will actually go. This page explains what each claim covers and what it quietly leaves out.
introSummary: IB teachers in India and IB tutors are not doing the same job, and the difference decides who you should hire for home tuition. A teacher plans and delivers a course to a class across a year, handles internal assessment administration, and answers to a coordinator. A tutor works with one student and starts from that student's errors. The overlap is real but partial, which is why a credential that looks impressive on a school website can mean very little at your dining table. What follows is a plain reading of the usual claims: International Baccalaureate (IB) professional development workshops, examiner or moderator experience, years in an IB classroom, and a subject degree. Also how to check any of them politely, and when a serving school teacher is the wrong choice for your child.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a family in India with the right person?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, and the questions come before the shortlist. Which board and syllabus, which programme, which subjects and at which level, what the school calendar looks like this term, where you live, and which evenings are genuinely free. From that, IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles have been verified against what they claim, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything. Lessons then run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability.

The part worth paying attention to is what you say about credentials, because most families ask for the wrong thing. Asking for an examiner produces a shortlist of examiners, some of whom have never taught a fourteen-year-old one to one. Asking instead for somebody who has taken students through Higher Level (HL) Chemistry more than once, and who can show you how they mark a Paper 2 extended response, produces a better list and a shorter one.

Be specific about the student too. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student stuck on criterion C is a different brief from a Diploma Programme (DP) student who understands everything and writes badly under time pressure. The first needs a teacher who can rebuild a skill. The second needs somebody who will sit through timed writing and mark it hard.

If the first match does not work, ask for a different one and name the reason. Credentials rarely cause a bad fit. Pace, manner and the willingness to set written work cause most of them, and none of those appear on a certificate.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with subjects, levels and school timings
2. Describe the problem in the student's own work, not the credential you imagine fixing it
3. Review shortlisted profiles and ask each candidate two subject-specific questions
4. Take a demo session and watch how the person marks written work
5. Confirm the weekly slot, then review the fit after three or four sessions

contentBlocks.heading: What a PYP, MYP or DP specialist in India is actually trained for
contentBlocks.body:
Training is programme-specific, and that is the first filter most families skip. The Diploma Programme is a two-year course of six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to three more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. Somebody trained to deliver that has spent years inside a marking culture that an excellent CBSE physics teacher has simply never worked in.

The Middle Years Programme is a different animal again. It runs five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups, and every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project falls in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so there is no single national MYP examination in India. A teacher who cannot discuss criteria in those terms has not taught the programme.

Primary Years Programme experience is the hardest to read from a certificate and the easiest to test in conversation. Ask how they would handle a child who reads fluently but cannot explain what she read.

So match the training to the year your child is in, not to the most senior-sounding line on the profile. A DP2 specialist is not automatically the right person for an MYP 3 student, and sometimes is exactly the wrong one.
items: DP: six subjects from six groups, HL at 240 hours and SL at 150
MYP: four criteria per subject, each scored 0 to 8, total out of 32
Personal Project in MYP 5, Community Project in MYP 3 or 4
MYP eAssessment is optional and decided by each school individually
PYP claims are best tested by a question, not read off a certificate

contentBlocks.heading: A subject degree against teaching skill: a worked example
contentBlocks.body:
Put a doctorate in chemistry beside a DP Chemistry paper and the gap shows within one question. Under the structure first assessed in 2025, Paper 1 comes in two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, while Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. A research chemist will answer every one of them correctly. That is not the skill being hired. The skill is knowing that a student who writes a chemically correct paragraph can still score two marks out of four because the command term said evaluate and the answer only described.

Command terms are the clearest test of teaching skill in this system. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent: each sets the depth an answer needs, and markschemes reward that depth rather than general knowledge. Ask a candidate what changes in an answer when discuss becomes to what extent. Somebody who has taught the subject will answer in about fifteen seconds and reach for an example. Somebody who only knows the content will talk about the topic.

The internal assessment shows it again. The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade and is marked on four criteria of six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, within a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may work in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. A subject expert will improve the science. A trained teacher will notice that the Evaluation section describes limitations without ever weighing them, which is where the marks were lost.

Both kinds of knowledge are useful. For Mathematics AA and AI at HL, or for a student aiming at the top of the scale, deep subject command matters more than usual. For everybody else, hire the person who can read a markscheme aloud and make it make sense.
items: Ask what changes in an answer when discuss becomes to what extent
A correct paragraph can still lose marks against the wrong command term
Internal assessment criteria reward weighing limitations, not listing them
Deep subject command matters most at HL and at the top of the scale
Test teaching skill with a markscheme, not with a hard content question

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB teachers in India are, and where they are not
contentBlocks.body:
IB teachers in India cluster where the international schools are, and the gaps between those clusters are wide. In Delhi NCR the density sits around South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128 Noida, and Greater Noida, while families in Dwarka, Faridabad and Ghaziabad often find the same names travelling further and charging for the travel time in hours rather than money. An IB teacher in Delhi who already teaches a full school day will usually offer you one weekday evening and a Saturday, and not much else.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves similarly but with harder geography. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill hold most of the experienced people, and a Powai family can often find somebody locally. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are a different conversation, because the crossing at the wrong hour can consume the evening. An IB teacher in Mumbai who says yes to Thane on a Wednesday has usually not thought it through.

Bengaluru spreads the supply more evenly. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road all have some depth, though an IB teacher in Bangalore who lives in the east rarely takes work in the south. Chennai concentrates around Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Alwarpet, Velachery and Perungudi.

Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, the position is different in kind rather than degree. There may be one or two genuinely experienced people in the whole city for a given HL subject, and they are already teaching. Hyderabad and Pune sit between the metros and that thinner picture. This is where online reaches a teacher your city does not contain, and where a hybrid week keeps the good local person you do have.
items: Delhi NCR: depth in South Delhi, Gurugram and Noida, thinner in Ghaziabad
Mumbai: Bandra to Worli is well served; Thane and Kharghar are a travel problem
Bengaluru: supply spreads across Whitefield, Indiranagar, HSR Layout and Jayanagar
Chennai: clustered around Adyar, OMR, Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun: often one or two people per HL subject

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars, and why a serving teacher's diary is already full
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore appear only as context for the kind of calendar families at international schools in India live with.

That calendar explains most of what you will experience when you try to book a serving teacher. IB schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May session; November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. So a serving teacher's heaviest marking load lands precisely in the months when your child most needs weekly attention, and the sessions that get cancelled are the private ones, not the school's.

There is a second issue, and it is the one families find uncomfortable. A teacher from your child's own school may be marking work that counts. Even where a school permits private tuition, the conversation about a predicted grade becomes awkward for everyone, and the student learns to perform rather than to ask. A teacher from another school, or a full-time tutor, avoids the whole problem.

When is a serving teacher the right call? When the subject is thinly taught in your city, when the arrangement runs at a fixed weekend hour, and when the teacher is not connected to your child's school. Otherwise, hire somebody whose diary is built around home tuition rather than around a timetable that will always win.
items: May is the dominant session; November serves a small minority and retakes
Schools set their own DP2 mock dates, usually months before May
A serving teacher's cancellations land in the term you need most
Avoid a teacher who marks your own child's work at school
Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through official channels

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which format suits a qualified teacher?
contentBlocks.body:
State the comparison plainly. A home tutor sees the student's page, the posture and the moment the pen stops, and that is worth more than any credential for a student who avoids difficulty quietly. Online widens the pool enormously, which matters precisely when the credential you want is rare in your city: the HL specialist, the TOK teacher, the person who has actually supervised Extended Essays. A hybrid week takes both, usually one home session at the weekend for teaching and one online midweek for marked practice. Presence buys honesty about effort; a screen buys access to expertise.

Experienced teachers often prefer online for a practical reason nobody advertises. Travel costs them an hour each way in Bengaluru or Delhi NCR, and that hour has to be paid for by somebody. A teacher who will not travel to your locality may still take your child online at the same standard, and refusing that on principle is how families end up with a less experienced person who happens to live nearby.

There are cases where home classes win outright. A younger student. A student who has stopped opening the textbook. A household where nobody is checking whether the work was done. In each of those, physical presence is the intervention, and the credential matters less than the discipline.

One warning about hybrid arrangements. Keep the same person across both formats. Two people teaching the same subject in two formats will contradict each other on method within a month, and the student will quietly stop trusting both. Change the format as the year demands, but keep the teacher.
items: Home lessons suit a student who avoids difficulty when nobody is watching
Online reaches the rare HL, TOK or Extended Essay specialist your city lacks
Hybrid: home classes at the weekend, marked practice online midweek
A teacher who will not travel may still be excellent on a screen
Keep one person across both formats rather than splitting the subject

contentBlocks.heading: How do you verify a teaching credential politely?
contentBlocks.body:
You ask, in order, and you ask in a tone that assumes the answer is fine. Most claims are true. The purpose of checking is to find the small number that are stretched, and to learn what the true ones actually cover. Do it in this sequence: 1. ask which programme and which subject the training was for; 2. ask which workshop or category it was, in which year, and who delivered it; 3. ask what examining or moderating they have done and for which component; 4. ask how many full cohorts they have taken from the start of the course to the examination; 5. ask them to mark one question from your child's last script and talk you through the marks. The fifth answer is worth more than the first four together.

IB professional development workshops are described in categories, and a certificate records attendance at professional training for a programme or role. It is not a licence to tutor privately, and no workshop certifies that somebody teaches your child well. Ask to see the certificate. Most IB teachers in India will produce one without any fuss at all.

Examining is genuinely useful and routinely oversold. An examiner marks one component of one subject for a session, so the insight is narrow and real: they know how marks are actually awarded on that paper. They may not have taught the full course, and examining work is confidential, so nobody can show you scripts or predict what will appear. Treat any suggestion otherwise as a warning sign.

On IB Gram's side, identity and listed qualifications are checked before a profile goes live. That narrows the field. It does not replace your own five questions, and it is not meant to.
items: Ask which programme and subject the training covered, not just that it exists
Ask for the workshop year, category and provider, then ask to see the certificate
Ask which component they examined, and accept that the insight is narrow
Ask how many full cohorts they have taken through to the examination
Ask them to mark one question from your child's script and explain each mark

contentBlocks.heading: Teacher or tutor: what the difference means for home tuition in India
contentBlocks.body:
A teacher owns a course. Over a year they plan a sequence, teach thirty students at once, administer internal assessment, write reports, sit in meetings about grade boundaries and answer to a coordinator. A tutor owns a student. There is no syllabus to get through unless the school has left one unfinished, no class to manage, and nothing to plan beyond what last week's marked work revealed. Both are skilled. They are not the same skill, and the better one for your family depends entirely on what has gone wrong.

When a teacher is what you need: the school has not covered a unit properly, or has changed staff mid-year, or the student has missed weeks. Rebuilding a topic in sequence is teaching work, and a person who has delivered the full course knows what order it has to come in.

When a tutor is what you need: the student understands the content and still loses marks. That is diagnosis work. It starts with a marked script, finds the pattern across several of them, and fixes one habit at a time. A brilliant classroom teacher who has never worked one to one sometimes handles this badly, because their instinct is to explain, and explaining is not what a student who already understands requires.

The best home tuition usually comes from one of the IB teachers in India who has done both jobs, and you can hear it in how they talk about a student. Listen for whether they describe a child or a topic in the demo.

One more distinction. A teacher's authority comes from the room. A tutor's comes from being useful to one teenager who did not ask for your help. In the home, the second kind is what survives the first difficult month, and it has nothing to do with the certificate on the wall.
items: A teacher owns a course and a class; a tutor owns one student's errors
Missed weeks or a staff change is teaching work, done in sequence
Marks lost despite understanding is diagnosis work, done from scripts
Ask a candidate to describe a past student, not a favourite topic
Explaining more is the wrong reflex for a student who already understands

contentBlocks.heading: What good teaching looks like after a month of home classes
contentBlocks.body:
In the first two or three sessions almost nothing measurable changes, and that is normal. What you should see is a change in the questions the student asks. They move from asking for the answer to asking whether the method was right, and from silence to naming which part of the question they did not understand. That shift is the whole basis of everything that comes later, and it is visible from the next room.

By four to six weeks the marked scripts should look different. Working set out so somebody else can follow it. Answers that actually match the command term. Fewer marks lost to careless transcription. Ask the tutor to keep the scripts, in date order, and look at them yourself once a month. You do not need subject knowledge to see whether the same comment is being written four times.

Now the honest limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, whatever they have examined or however long they have taught. Among IB teachers in India, a credential predicts very little about one relationship with one teenager. Starting in the last term before May narrows the work to examination technique, which is genuinely useful and is not the same as teaching the subject. And a student who does no work between sessions will not improve, no matter who is sitting across the table.

There is one failure mode particular to hiring on credentials. A very senior teacher can pitch consistently above the student's head and mistake the resulting silence for understanding. If your child has stopped asking questions after a month, that is the problem, not shyness. Say so, and if it does not change within two sessions, ask for a different match.
items: Weeks one to three: better questions, not better marks
Weeks four to six: cleaner working and answers that match the command term
Keep marked scripts in date order and read them yourself monthly
A student who has stopped asking questions is being pitched to too high
No credential predicts the fit between one teacher and one teenager

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an IB teacher in India for home or online lessons
contentBlocks.body:
Gather three things before you send the query, and the whole process gets shorter. The student's most recent marked script, with the marks visible. The subject list with Higher Level and Standard Level written against each. And the school dates you already know: mocks, internal assessment deadlines, and any week when the school itself runs revision.

Then say what you want in terms of the problem rather than the credential. The difference between asking for an examiner and asking for somebody who can show you how a Paper 2 extended response earns its marks is the difference between a long shortlist and a useful one.

The process itself is simple. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match.

Use the demo for one purpose above all others. Hand over a marked script and watch the candidate work through it with your child. Do not ask them to teach a topic; anybody can teach a topic for twenty minutes. Ask them to explain where six marks became four. How they answer that is the credential you are actually buying, and unlike a certificate it cannot be produced in advance.
items: Bring the most recent marked script with the marks still visible
Write HL or SL against every subject before you send the query
Describe the problem, not the credential you think will fix it
In the demo, ask the candidate to explain where marks were lost
Confirm the weekly home or online slot only after that conversation

faqs.question: What is the difference between an IB teacher and an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: A teacher delivers a course to a class over a year; a tutor works from one student's errors. The teacher plans a sequence, administers internal assessment and reports to a coordinator. The tutor has no syllabus to finish and starts from last week's marked script. Both skills are real. For a student who has missed content, hire the first. For a student who understands the material and still loses marks, hire the second.

faqs.question: Does an IB workshop certificate mean the tutor is officially qualified to tutor?
faqs.answer: No. A workshop certificate records attendance at professional training for a programme or role, and it is not a licence to teach privately. It tells you the person has been trained in a particular programme and subject, which is genuinely useful information. It tells you nothing about whether they can hold the attention of your fourteen-year-old on a Tuesday evening. Ask to see the certificate, then judge the teaching separately, in a demo.

faqs.question: Is an examiner automatically a better tutor?
faqs.answer: No, though examining does give one narrow and real advantage. An examiner marks a specific component of a specific subject for a session, so they know precisely how marks are awarded on that paper and where candidates routinely lose them. What examining does not supply is experience of teaching the whole course, or of working one to one. Examining is also confidential, so anyone hinting at advance knowledge of papers should be ruled out immediately.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor without IB experience teach my child if they have a strong subject degree?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for content gaps, and rarely for anything else. A strong subject degree fixes a misunderstood topic well. It does not help with command terms, criterion marking or internal assessment structure, which is where most marks are actually lost. If you do hire on subject strength, pair it with your own attention to the markscheme, and expect to change the arrangement before the mock examinations rather than after them.

faqs.question: Should I hire a teacher from my child's own school for home tuition?
faqs.answer: Usually not, even where the school permits it. If the teacher marks work that counts towards an internal assessment or a predicted grade, the private relationship distorts the school one, and the student starts performing instead of admitting confusion. Scheduling is the second problem: their cancellations arrive in mock season. A teacher from another school, or a full-time tutor, removes both issues without losing any real expertise.

faqs.question: How many years of experience should I look for?
faqs.answer: Ask how many full cohorts they have taken from the start of the course to the examination, which is a better question than years. Two complete cycles teaches somebody far more than six years of covering odd classes. For Diploma Programme work, somebody who has seen students through both DP1 and DP2 knows where the year goes wrong. For Middle Years Programme work, ask instead how often they have marked against all four criteria.

faqs.question: We are in Lucknow and cannot find an experienced teacher locally. What now?
faqs.answer: Take the experienced person online, because IB teachers in India are concentrated in a handful of metros. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Chandigarh, Dehradun and Kanpur often hold one or two genuinely experienced people for a given Higher Level subject, and they are usually already teaching full time. Online reaches the rest of the country. Where a capable local teacher does exist for the basics, run a hybrid week and keep the specialist for the harder sessions.

faqs.question: How do I check a credential without sounding rude?
faqs.answer: Assume it is true and ask for detail, which is how professionals talk to each other anyway. Which programme and subject was the training for, which year, who delivered it, and could you send a copy of the certificate. Nobody legitimate objects to that. If a candidate deflects, changes the subject or becomes irritated, you have learned something more valuable than the answer would have been.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundary that they discuss and never write. The supervisor at school signs off the Extended Essay and runs the reflection sessions, and that role cannot be delegated to a tutor. What a tutor adds is time: reading a draft against the assessment criteria, arguing with a weak research question, pushing back on an essay that answers a title the student invented rather than the one prescribed.

faqs.question: My child's home classes feel too advanced. Is the teacher too senior?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is a common failure when families hire on credentials alone. A very experienced teacher can pitch above a student's head and read the resulting silence as comprehension. The test is simple: has your child stopped asking questions since the sessions began? Raise it directly with the tutor and ask them to work only from the student's own script for two sessions. If nothing changes, ask for a different match.

faqs.question: Are verified profiles on a platform enough on their own?
faqs.answer: They narrow the field and they do not finish the job. Verification confirms identity and checks the qualifications a tutor lists, which removes the most obvious problems before you ever see a profile. It cannot predict the chemistry between one adult and one teenager, or whether this person sets written work and chases it. That is what the demo is for, and it is why a trial session exists before any commitment.

mainEntity.name: Does an IB workshop certificate mean the tutor is officially qualified to tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A workshop certificate records attendance at professional training for a programme or role, and it is not a licence to teach privately. It tells you the person has been trained in a particular programme and subject, which is genuinely useful information. It tells you nothing about whether they can hold the attention of your fourteen-year-old on a Tuesday evening. Ask to see the certificate, then judge the teaching separately, in a demo.

mainEntity.name: Is an examiner automatically a better tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, though examining does give one narrow and real advantage. An examiner marks a specific component of a specific subject for a session, so they know precisely how marks are awarded on that paper and where candidates routinely lose them. What examining does not supply is experience of teaching the whole course, or of working one to one. Examining is also confidential, so anyone hinting at advance knowledge of papers should be ruled out immediately.

mainEntity.name: Can a home tutor without IB experience teach my child if they have a strong subject degree?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, for content gaps, and rarely for anything else. A strong subject degree fixes a misunderstood topic well. It does not help with command terms, criterion marking or internal assessment structure, which is where most marks are actually lost. If you do hire on subject strength, pair it with your own attention to the markscheme, and expect to change the arrangement before the mock examinations rather than after them.

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a teacher from my child's own school for home tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not, even where the school permits it. If the teacher marks work that counts towards an internal assessment or a predicted grade, the private relationship distorts the school one, and the student starts performing instead of admitting confusion. Scheduling is the second problem: their cancellations arrive in mock season. A teacher from another school, or a full-time tutor, removes both issues without losing any real expertise.

mainEntity.name: How many years of experience should I look for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask how many full cohorts they have taken from the start of the course to the examination, which is a better question than years. Two complete cycles teaches somebody far more than six years of covering odd classes. For Diploma Programme work, somebody who has seen students through both DP1 and DP2 knows where the year goes wrong. For Middle Years Programme work, ask instead how often they have marked against all four criteria.

mainEntity.name: We are in Lucknow and cannot find an experienced teacher locally. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take the experienced person online, because IB teachers in India are concentrated in a handful of metros. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Chandigarh, Dehradun and Kanpur often hold one or two genuinely experienced people for a given Higher Level subject, and they are usually already teaching full time. Online reaches the rest of the country. Where a capable local teacher does exist for the basics, run a hybrid week and keep the specialist for the harder sessions.

mainEntity.name: How do I check a credential without sounding rude?

acceptedAnswer.text: Assume it is true and ask for detail, which is how professionals talk to each other anyway. Which programme and subject was the training for, which year, who delivered it, and could you send a copy of the certificate. Nobody legitimate objects to that. If a candidate deflects, changes the subject or becomes irritated, you have learned something more valuable than the answer would have been.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the boundary that they discuss and never write. The supervisor at school signs off the Extended Essay and runs the reflection sessions, and that role cannot be delegated to a tutor. What a tutor adds is time: reading a draft against the assessment criteria, arguing with a weak research question, pushing back on an essay that answers a title the student invented rather than the one prescribed.

mainEntity.name: My child's home classes feel too advanced. Is the teacher too senior?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly, and it is a common failure when families hire on credentials alone. A very experienced teacher can pitch above a student's head and read the resulting silence as comprehension. The test is simple: has your child stopped asking questions since the sessions began? Raise it directly with the tutor and ask them to work only from the student's own script for two sessions. If nothing changes, ask for a different match.

mainEntity.name: Are verified profiles on a platform enough on their own?

acceptedAnswer.text: They narrow the field and they do not finish the job. Verification confirms identity and checks the qualifications a tutor lists, which removes the most obvious problems before you ever see a profile. It cannot predict the chemistry between one adult and one teenager, or whether this person sets written work and chases it. That is what the demo is for, and it is why a trial session exists before any commitment.

finalCta: Send a query or book a free consultation, and describe the problem in your child's marked work rather than the credential you have in mind. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against that. A demo can be arranged first, and lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability.

h1: IB Home Teachers in India for Younger PYP and MYP Learners
heroTitle: IB Home Teachers in India for Younger Learners
heroSubtitle: Teaching a nine-year-old at the kitchen table is a different craft from preparing an examination candidate. Shorter sessions. Habits before content. A parent close enough to hear and far enough not to rescue. This page is about that job, and about the families who do not need it.
introSummary: IB home teachers in India who work with Primary Years Programme and early Middle Years children are doing something other than syllabus coverage: home teaching at this age builds the routines that make later study possible. A seven-year-old cannot concentrate for ninety minutes, and nobody should ask them to. A twelve-year-old meeting criterion feedback for the first time needs to learn what the words mean before anyone drills content at them. So the session looks different, the room matters, and the measures of progress are behaviour rather than marks. This page covers session length by age, the habits worth building, inquiry work that does not turn the kitchen into a classroom, where a parent should be while the lesson runs, and the safeguarding basics every family should insist on.

contentBlocks.heading: Finding an IB Home Teacher in India for a Younger Child
contentBlocks.body:
Tell us the age first. Everything else follows from it, and most enquiries about IB home teachers in India arrive with the subject named and the age left out. A request that begins with the subject leads to a shortlist built for the subject, and for a child of eight or eleven that is usually the wrong shortlist. What matters more is whether the teacher has taught children at this stage, can hold attention without raising their voice, and is comfortable ending a session early when a child has run out of road.

The free consultation asks about the programme year, what the class teacher has said, how the child behaves around work at home, and what your evenings actually look like once school transport and activities are counted. Parents in Baner or Yelahanka often have a narrower real window than they think: a child who reaches home late and has eaten at seven is not available at eight for anything useful. We would rather find a Saturday morning that works than sell you a weekday slot that will collapse.

Shortlists are small. Profiles are verified before they go live, and we match on stage and temperament as much as on subject, subject to who is free in your locality. You will be asked whether you want the same person across two subjects, which for younger children is usually better than two specialists, because one adult holding the whole picture can spot that the Mathematics problem is a reading problem.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Watch it for one thing: does the child talk during the lesson, or only listen. And if the honest conclusion after the trial is that the child needs more unstructured time rather than a teacher, we will say so. Families come back a year later far more often than they think they will.

Say what the class teacher has observed, in their words if possible

contentBlocks.heading: What PYP and Early MYP Actually Ask of a Child
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12 and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet. Children work through units of inquiry rather than chapters, alongside the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, and they complete the PYP exhibition in the final year. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades.

Read that last sentence again before hiring anybody. There is no score to raise. A home teacher working in the PYP is building capability that will be measured years later, which means the honest goals are things like reading a page and being able to say what happened, holding a number line in the head, finishing what was started, and asking a question about a topic without being prompted.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) changes the vocabulary sharply. Five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, eight subject groups, and each subject assessed against four criteria (A to D) scored 0 to 8, with the total out of 32 converting to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. For an eleven-year-old arriving from the PYP, the shock is not difficulty but language: criterion B asks for investigating patterns, criterion C for communicating, and a child who has never been marked on how they explain their working suddenly is.

The Community Project comes in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5, both of them independent work that rewards planning habits built years earlier. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so do not assume it applies to your child. Early MYP home teaching is mostly translation work: turning criterion language into things a twelve-year-old can actually practise.
items: PYP spans ages 3 to 12 with six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry

contentBlocks.heading: Reading, Number Sense and the Habits Underneath Them
contentBlocks.body:
For a younger child, almost every presenting problem is one of two problems. Reading that is accurate but not fluent, so comprehension collapses when the passage gets long. Or procedures learnt without number sense, so the child can do long division and cannot estimate whether the answer is sensible.

Fluency is built by reading aloud, daily, at a level slightly below what the child can technically manage. A good home teacher will spend ten minutes of a session on this and will not apologise for it, because it is the intervention with the longest reach: comprehension, spelling, writing rhythm and confidence all move with it. Ask the teacher what they are having the child read and why that book.

Number sense is rebuilt by taking the pencil away. Estimate first, then calculate. Ask what a reasonable answer would look like. Use the fruit on the table, the cricket scores, the price list at the shop. A child who says that 6 times 48 is about 300 before working it out has something that cannot be drilled into them later, and a child who writes 288 with no idea whether it is plausible will struggle in MYP Mathematics however many worksheets they complete.

Writing sits on top of both. In the early MYP the marks move when a child learns to plan for two minutes before writing, and to reread one sentence back. Science at this stage is mostly about explaining, not about knowing. If your child's teacher reports that answers are right but short, that is an explaining problem, and it is best treated at nine or twelve rather than at sixteen, when it has hardened into a habit and the deadlines have arrived.
items: Ten minutes of daily reading aloud, slightly below the child's ceiling
Estimate before calculating so the child can judge a plausible answer
Number sense uses shop prices and cricket scores, not extra worksheets
Two minutes of planning before writing moves early MYP marks
Right-but-short answers are an explaining problem, best fixed early

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB Home Teachers Work Across India, City by City
contentBlocks.body:
Supply for younger children behaves differently from supply for examination years. Fewer specialists, but more capable generalists, and a shorter acceptable travel distance because nobody will cross a city for a forty-five minute lesson.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region that means clusters. An IB home teacher in Mumbai working in Bandra, Juhu or Andheri will rarely take a booking in Thane or Kharghar for a young child, and the reverse is equally true. Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill each hold their own small pool, and Navi Mumbai and Vashi are best treated as a separate market with their own teachers rather than as suburbs.

Bengaluru is the easiest of the big cities for this age group because the residential clusters are self-contained. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala, Indiranagar, Jayanagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road each support local teaching, and an IB home teacher in Bangalore who lives inside the same cluster will hold an early evening slot reliably. Pune works the same way across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Aundh, Baner, Balewadi, Wakad, Kharadi and Hinjewadi, though the crossing between the eastern and western halves at seven in the evening is what breaks arrangements.

Gujarat has real depth in Ahmedabad, particularly around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close enough to share teachers, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot are thinner and often better served online. The same is true across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai: Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai have local teachers for primary work but few who know the programme itself. Delhi NCR, Hyderabad and Chennai families face a different version of the same question, which is whether the nearest good teacher is near enough to come twice a week.

contentBlocks.heading: How the School Year Shapes Home Teaching in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and for a primary child the rhythm that matters is the unit of inquiry rather than any examination. Units change through the year, and a home teacher who asks the school which unit is running can connect the reading and the writing practice to what the child is already curious about. That single question separates a teacher who fits into the child's week from one who runs a parallel syllabus at home.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Ecole Mondiale World School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School and The International School Bangalore describe the same pressures whichever city they are in.

The pressures are real and they are mostly about time. Parent-teacher conferences and student-led conferences arrive with specific feedback, and that feedback is the best brief a home teacher will ever get, far better than a parent's summary. Ask for it in writing. The PYP exhibition in the final year absorbs a term of the child's attention, and a family adding two new subjects during that term is working against their own child.

There is also a quieter pressure, which is comparison. In many cities the conversation among parents at pick-up is about how many classes each child attends. A child of nine with four scheduled activities and a home teacher twice a week has no time left to be bored, and boredom is where a lot of primary learning actually happens. If the school is not worried, and the child reads for pleasure, the honest answer may be that nothing needs buying at all this year.
items: Ask the school which unit of inquiry is running and teach alongside it
Written feedback from conferences beats a parent's summary as a brief
The PYP exhibition absorbs a term; do not add subjects during it
The academic year runs roughly April to March, so plan in terms

contentBlocks.heading: Does Online Teaching Work for a Seven-Year-Old?
contentBlocks.body:
Mostly, no. Below about nine, a screen asks a child to do two hard things at once: attend to an adult who is not in the room, and manage their own materials without help. Some children manage it and most do not, and the failure is quiet. The child appears to be listening, the parent hears a pleasant lesson from the next room, and nothing transfers. This is the honest reason the lead option on this page is a teacher who comes to the house.

Around ages nine to eleven that changes. A child who can open their own book, hold a pencil while looking at a screen and say when they are lost can work online for thirty or forty minutes productively, particularly for reading discussion or for talking through a piece of writing. By early MYP, online teaching is a genuine option rather than a compromise.

Home classes have their own failure modes and you should plan around them. The television in the same room. A younger sibling who wants attention. A dining table cleared for the lesson and re-laid for dinner halfway through. And the teacher who arrives late twice and then becomes unreliable, which happens most often when the travel distance was always too far.

Hybrid suits this age better than most people expect. One home visit a week for the work that needs paper, pencil and a watching adult, and one short online session midweek for reading aloud or for going over a piece of writing, keeps continuity without adding travel. For families in Surat, Mysuru or Vijayawada, where a teacher who knows the programme may not live nearby at all, hybrid is often the only arrangement that gives a child both a local adult in the room and a specialist voice.
items: Below about nine, online lessons usually fail quietly rather than obviously
From nine to eleven, thirty to forty online minutes can work well
Plan around the television, a younger sibling and the dinner table
A teacher travelling too far becomes an unreliable teacher within a month
Hybrid: one home visit for paper work, one short online reading session

contentBlocks.heading: Safeguarding When a Teacher Visits a Young Child at Home
contentBlocks.body:
This is the part of the conversation Indian families are often too polite to have, and it should be had plainly. A home teacher spends hours alone with a child in your house. Every reasonable teacher expects to be checked and will not be offended.

What the platform does: profiles are verified before they go live, covering identity and the qualifications and teaching experience claimed. What you should do sits alongside that, and it is not a substitute. Meet the teacher yourself before the first session rather than sending a member of staff to open the door. Keep lessons in a room with an open door or in a shared space such as the dining area, never behind a closed bedroom door. Make sure someone responsible is at home for the whole session, every session, not just the first few.

Set the communication rule early. Messages about scheduling come to you, not to the child, and a teacher who starts messaging a ten-year-old directly should be asked to stop. Photographs of the child's work are fine when you have agreed to it; photographs of the child are not. Ask how a missed or late session will be communicated, and to whom.

Then watch the child, because they will tell you things they cannot say. A child who is reluctant on the day, who goes quiet afterwards, or who has stopped mentioning the teacher when they used to, is worth asking about gently. Most of the time it is boredom or a clash of pace and a different match will fix it. Ask for a different teacher if the fit is wrong; there is no obligation to persist with an arrangement your child is unhappy in, and no good teacher wants you to.
items: Identity, qualifications claimed and teaching experience are checked before a profile goes live
Meet the teacher yourself before the first session at your home
Lessons stay in a shared space with an open door, never a closed bedroom
Scheduling messages come to the parent, never directly to a young child
A responsible adult is at home for every session, not only the first

contentBlocks.heading: What Does an IB Home Teacher Do That a DP Tutor Does Not?
contentBlocks.body:
Parents comparing IB home teachers in India with a Diploma Programme tutor are comparing two jobs that share a word and little else. Length is the first difference. A Diploma Programme session runs ninety minutes or two hours because the content demands it. With a child of seven or eight, thirty to forty minutes of real work is the ceiling, and forty-five including settling and a break is a full session. At ten or eleven, forty-five to sixty minutes works. In early MYP, an hour. A teacher who proposes ninety minutes for an eight-year-old has either never taught one or is pricing the slot rather than planning it.

The second difference is the object. An examination tutor covers a syllabus against a deadline. A home teacher for a younger child builds habits that have no deadline: sitting down without an argument, starting before understanding everything, checking work once, saying when they are stuck. These sound small and they are the whole game. A child who will attempt something unaided at nine is a very different student at fifteen.

The third is that the work should not look like more school. Inquiry at home means the child's own question taken seriously: measuring the balcony plants each week and drawing the results, working out how much water the household actually uses, writing four sentences about why the lift is faster than the stairs. Attached to the unit of inquiry where possible, and never as a second worksheet set.

The fourth difference is who the teacher reports to. With a DP student, the tutor mostly talks to the student. With a young child, the teacher is coaching you as much as the child: showing you how to hear reading without correcting every word, how to ask what the question is asking rather than supplying the answer, and how to stop helping. That last one is the hardest and the most valuable.
items: Ages seven to eight: thirty to forty minutes of work is the real ceiling
Ages ten to eleven: forty-five to sixty minutes; early MYP: about an hour
Habits, not coverage: starting unaided, checking once, saying when stuck

contentBlocks.heading: Should You Sit in the Room During the Lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
This is the question families put to IB home teachers in India more than any other, and the answer changes after week one. For the first session, yes, and quietly. You are judging whether the teacher can hold your child's attention and whether they let the child struggle for a few seconds before stepping in. After that, presence becomes interference more often than support, because a child performing for a parent will not show the confusion the teacher needs to see.

The workable middle is to be within earshot and out of sight. The next room with the door open. Close enough that a young child feels safe and the safeguarding basics hold, far enough that they forget you are listening. Younger than six or seven, or in the first fortnight with a new teacher, stay closer. And if your child has a habit of appealing to you when work gets hard, leaving the room is itself the intervention.

Progress at this age is behaviour before it is attainment, and that makes it easy to miss. Look for a child who opens the book before being asked, who rereads a sentence without prompting, who says I do not understand instead of going silent, who finishes something. Those changes show up in four to six weeks. Reading fluency takes a term. Writing quality takes longer, and number sense rebuilt properly is a year's work rather than a month's.

Be willing to stop, too. Some children need less, not more: a nine-year-old with four activities and two home teachers is unlikely to gain from a third adult. No teacher can guarantee a grade or a reading age by a date, and anyone who offers one is selling. If after two months your child is no more willing to start work alone than before, the match or the plan is wrong, and it is worth saying so before another term is booked.
items: Sit in for the first session, then move within earshot and out of sight
A watched child performs confidence instead of showing confusion
Behaviour changes in four to six weeks; reading fluency takes a term
Look for rereading unprompted and saying I do not understand
Number sense rebuilt properly is a year's work, not a month's
Some children need one fewer commitment rather than one more

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a First Home Session in India Without Overloading a Child
contentBlocks.body:
Good IB home teachers in India will ask you for the same three things before the first visit, so prepare them and the session will be useful rather than polite. The most recent written feedback from school. A book the child is currently reading, at whatever level that actually is. And a clear answer to what you want different in three months, stated as behaviour: starts homework without being asked, reads a chapter and can retell it, attempts a word problem before asking.

The first session should be assessment disguised as work. The teacher should hear the child read, watch them attempt something slightly too hard, ask what they already know about the current unit of inquiry, and notice what happens when the child gets stuck. No new content. At the end, ask for three sentences about what they found, in writing, and compare it with what the school told you.

Start with one session a week. Two is right for a specific gap with a deadline behind it, such as a child entering MYP 1 with shaky arithmetic, and rarely otherwise. Sessions run at home, online or hybrid depending on the child's age and your city, and availability depends on level, locality and schedule. A demo or trial can be arranged before you commit to a term, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is not right.

Then protect the rest of the week. A younger child needs unstructured time the way an examination student needs past papers, and a calendar with nothing free in it is a poor investment however good the teaching is.
items: 1. Settle and review the last session's one habit, about five minutes.
2. Read aloud together for ten minutes at a comfortable level.
3. Work on the target skill for fifteen minutes, hardest part first.
4. Let the child attempt something unaided for ten minutes while the teacher watches.
5. Close with what was learnt, said aloud by the child, in five minutes.
6. Send the parent three sentences: what was found, what comes next.

faqs.question: How long should a home session be for a PYP child?
faqs.answer: Thirty to forty minutes of real work for a child of seven or eight, and forty-five to sixty for a ten or eleven-year-old, including settling time and a short break. Attention, not content, sets the limit. A teacher proposing ninety minutes for a young child is planning around a fee rather than around the learner, and the last half hour of such a session is usually copying rather than thinking. Two short sessions in a week beat one long one at every age below twelve.

faqs.question: My child has no grades to improve. What would a home teacher even do?
faqs.answer: Build the things that get measured later. The Primary Years Programme has no external examinations and no published grades, so the goals are capability rather than scores: reading fluently enough to follow a long passage, estimating before calculating, planning two minutes before writing, and starting work without an argument. Ask the teacher to state their three-month goals as behaviour you can observe at home. If they can only describe topics they will cover, they are teaching a syllabus that does not exist at this stage.

faqs.question: Should a parent be in the room during home classes?
faqs.answer: Be present for the first session, then move within earshot and out of sight. Children perform for a watching parent and hide the confusion the teacher needs to see, which slows everything down. The next room with the door open keeps the safeguarding basics intact and lets the child forget you are listening. Stay closer for a child under six or seven, or for the first fortnight with a new teacher, and ask for a short summary at the door instead of listening in.

faqs.question: What safeguarding should I insist on for home teaching?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them are rude to ask for. Meet the teacher yourself before the first session. Keep lessons in a shared space with the door open, never in a bedroom. Have a responsible adult at home for every session rather than only the first few. And require that all scheduling messages come to you and not to the child. Profiles on the platform are verified for identity and claimed qualifications before they go live, but that check sits alongside your own arrangements rather than replacing them.

faqs.question: Is an IB home teacher in Pune or Ahmedabad easy to find for primary years?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided you stay inside your own cluster. Pune supports local teaching around Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Aundh on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Wakad and Kharadi on the other, and crossing between them on a weekday evening is what breaks arrangements. Ahmedabad has real depth around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close enough to share teachers. Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot are thinner, and hybrid often works better there.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for a young child?
faqs.answer: Below about nine it usually does not, and the failure is hard to spot. The child looks attentive, the lesson sounds pleasant from the next room, and very little transfers, because attending to an adult on a screen while managing your own materials is two demanding tasks at once. From nine to eleven, thirty to forty minutes can work well for reading discussion or talking through writing. By early Middle Years Programme, online is a real choice rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: What is inquiry-led work at home, in practice?
faqs.answer: It is the child's own question, taken seriously, with a small piece of recorded work at the end. Measuring the balcony plants weekly and drawing the change. Counting how many buckets of water the household uses in a day. Writing four sentences on why the lift is quicker than the stairs. Connected to the unit of inquiry running at school where possible, which is why a good teacher asks the school what that unit is. What it is not is a second set of worksheets after a full school day.

faqs.question: How is early MYP teaching different from PYP teaching?
faqs.answer: The language changes before the difficulty does. In the Middle Years Programme every subject is assessed against four criteria, each scored 0 to 8, with the total out of 32 converting to a 1 to 7 grade, and an eleven-year-old is suddenly marked on how they investigate and how they communicate rather than only on whether they are right. Early MYP home teaching is mostly translation: turning criterion wording into something a child can practise, such as showing a pattern before stating a rule.

faqs.question: How soon will I see a change?
faqs.answer: Behaviour shifts first, within four to six weeks: opening the book unprompted, rereading a sentence, saying that something is not understood rather than going quiet. Reading fluency moves across a term of daily practice. Writing quality takes longer than that, and number sense rebuilt from the foundations is realistically a year's work. No teacher can promise a reading age or a grade by a date. Judge the change in what your child does unaided, and keep a piece of their work from week one to compare against.

faqs.question: What if my child does not take to the teacher?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, early. Fit at this age is mostly about pace and warmth rather than subject knowledge, and a teacher who suits a quiet ten-year-old may be wrong for a restless eight-year-old. Watch for reluctance on the day, silence afterwards, or a child who has stopped mentioning the teacher. Describe what did not work rather than simply asking for someone else, because the description makes the next shortlist better. There is no obligation to persist with an arrangement a child is unhappy in.

faqs.question: Can one teacher handle two children of different ages?
faqs.answer: Back-to-back sessions with the same teacher often work well and save a family an entire evening of coordination. Teaching them together rarely does, unless the children are close in age and at a similar stage, because a shared session tends to be pitched to the older one while the younger copies. If the ages are three or more years apart, book two shorter consecutive sessions instead. Availability for consecutive slots depends on the teacher's schedule and your locality.

faqs.question: Does my child actually need a home teacher at all?
faqs.answer: Often not, and it is worth asking before you book. If the school is not raising concerns, the child reads for pleasure, and homework happens without a nightly argument, there may be nothing to buy this year. A child of nine with four activities and no free evenings usually needs fewer commitments rather than another adult. The cases that genuinely justify paid help are a specific gap the class teacher has named, a mid-year move between school systems, or a child who has stopped attempting anything alone.

mainEntity.name: How long should a home session be for a PYP child?

acceptedAnswer.text: Thirty to forty minutes of real work for a child of seven or eight, and forty-five to sixty for a ten or eleven-year-old, including settling time and a short break. Attention, not content, sets the limit. A teacher proposing ninety minutes for a young child is planning around a fee rather than around the learner, and the last half hour of such a session is usually copying rather than thinking. Two short sessions in a week beat one long one at every age below twelve.

mainEntity.name: My child has no grades to improve. What would a home teacher even do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build the things that get measured later. The Primary Years Programme has no external examinations and no published grades, so the goals are capability rather than scores: reading fluently enough to follow a long passage, estimating before calculating, planning two minutes before writing, and starting work without an argument. Ask the teacher to state their three-month goals as behaviour you can observe at home. If they can only describe topics they will cover, they are teaching a syllabus that does not exist at this stage.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent be in the room during home classes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Be present for the first session, then move within earshot and out of sight. Children perform for a watching parent and hide the confusion the teacher needs to see, which slows everything down. The next room with the door open keeps the safeguarding basics intact and lets the child forget you are listening. Stay closer for a child under six or seven, or for the first fortnight with a new teacher, and ask for a short summary at the door instead of listening in.

mainEntity.name: What safeguarding should I insist on for home teaching?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four things, and none of them are rude to ask for. Meet the teacher yourself before the first session. Keep lessons in a shared space with the door open, never in a bedroom. Have a responsible adult at home for every session rather than only the first few. And require that all scheduling messages come to you and not to the child. Profiles on the platform are verified for identity and claimed qualifications before they go live, but that check sits alongside your own arrangements rather than replacing them.
