h1: IB Private Teachers in India for Long-Term Academic Mentoring
heroTitle: Long-Term IB Mentoring Across India
heroSubtitle: A private teacher kept for years is a different hire from a subject tutor booked for a term. This page covers what that person actually does with study skills, note-taking and planning, how the arrangement should be reviewed each term, and the point at which hours ought to come down rather than up.
introSummary: IB private teachers in India are usually hired for a longer job than a single subject: one teacher, most often coming to the family for home tuition, who stays with one student across several school years. The subject is the visible part. The work underneath it is how the student takes notes, plans a fortnight, reads criterion feedback and decides what to revise first. A good mentoring arrangement changes shape as the student matures, and it should shrink before it ends. This page sets out what such a teacher covers, how one person follows a student from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma Programme, how to run a termly review, and how to recognise dependence early enough to reverse it.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a student with a long-term private teacher in India?
contentBlocks.body:
A multi-year arrangement is matched differently from a single-subject booking, because you are choosing somebody your child will still be working with in two years. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the programme and year, the subjects and levels involved, the school calendar, your locality and the schedule you can genuinely hold. Then comes the question a short booking never needs: what should this look like at the end?

Parents answer that in two broad ways. Some want one subject fixed and nothing further, which is a perfectly good reason to hire somebody and a poor reason to hire a mentor. Others describe a student who works hard and disorganised, who revises the wrong things the night before, who leaves the Extended Essay (EE) until the supervisor chases him twice. That second description points at mentoring, and mentoring changes the shortlist completely. Somebody superb at Higher Level Chemistry for one term may not be the right person to hold a student for three years.

Shortlisting then filters on range and staying power as much as on subject. IB Gram puts forward verified profiles covering both the stage the student is in and the stage he is moving into, so a family starting in MYP 4 meets teachers who also work with Diploma Programme students. Availability stays conditional on locality and on the slot you need. A demo or trial session can be arranged before anything is agreed, and if the fit is wrong at any point you can ask for a different match rather than persist out of politeness.

The first conversation should also produce an ending. Agree the notice period, the review dates and a rough sense of when hours ought to fall. Arrangements with no agreed end keep running for reasons that stop having much to do with the student, which is the quiet failure mode of long private teaching.
items: 1. Describe the student rather than the subject: habits, organisation, and what worries you.
2. Share the school calendar, present levels, and the stage your child enters next.
3. Meet verified teachers who cover both the current stage and the following one.
4. Run a trial, then agree the weekly shape, the review dates and a notice period.
5. Review every term, and cut hours deliberately once the student can work alone.

contentBlocks.heading: From MYP into the Diploma Programme: one teacher across the transition
contentBlocks.body:
The strongest argument for keeping one teacher is the handover that never has to happen. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, with every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A teacher who has watched a student score consistently well on knowing and understanding and consistently badly on communicating already knows something no report summary transmits.

MYP 5 brings the Personal Project, and MYP 3 or 4 brings the Community Project. Both belong entirely to the student, and a mentor's job there is to ask questions and to protect the timeline, never to contribute content. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional and each school decides whether to offer it; there is no single national MYP examination in India, so ask your coordinator what your school actually does before planning anything around it.

Then the Diploma Programme (DP) arrives and the scale changes. Two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay combine for up to 3 further points, making 45 the maximum and 24 the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed alongside all of it.

A mentor who was already in place through MYP 4 and 5 spends the first DP1 term on load management rather than on introductions. He knows which subject the student chose for the wrong reason, which habit will break under six subjects, and which criterion weakness is about to reappear in a different costume.
items: MYP: four criteria per subject, each 0-8, a total out of 32, converted to a 1-7 grade
The Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 stay the student's own
MYP eAssessment is optional and each school decides; confirm with your coordinator
DP: six subjects, three or four at Higher Level (240 hours), the rest Standard Level (150)
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points; 45 maximum, 24 the diploma minimum

contentBlocks.heading: Does one private teacher cover several IB subjects well?
contentBlocks.body:
Within one group, often yes. Across the whole diploma, almost never, and a teacher who claims otherwise is telling you something about his marketing rather than his teaching. IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology overlap enough in method and in written explanation that one science teacher can hold two of them credibly. IB Mathematics AA and AI are a separate specialism, and IB English A is a different discipline altogether.

The realistic pattern for a mentor is one taught subject plus oversight of everything else. He teaches Mathematics weekly, and for the other five subjects he reads the returned work, asks what the criterion feedback meant, checks that deadlines are recorded somewhere other than the student's memory, and flags a subject that is slipping while it is still a slip. That oversight role is worth more than a second taught subject in most households, because a student being taught four subjects privately has no time left to practise any of them.

Theory of Knowledge is the exception worth naming, because schools support it unevenly and students underestimate it consistently. TOK has two assessments. The exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 internal assessment prompts, up to 950 words, internally assessed, and it carries one third of the TOK grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for each examination session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed, and carries the remaining two thirds. The course runs on the core theme of knowledge and the knower, two of five optional themes, and five areas of knowledge: history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts.

A long-standing mentor is well placed to keep TOK moving, because he sees the student every week anyway and can push the exhibition forward in twenty minutes at the end of a session. TOK and EE grades run A to E, and an E in either is a failing condition, so nobody should be discovering the essay in DP2.
items: One science teacher can credibly hold two of Physics, Chemistry and Biology
Mathematics AA or AI and English A are separate specialisms, not add-ons
Most useful pattern: one taught subject plus weekly oversight of the other five
TOK exhibition: three objects, one of 35 prompts, up to 950 words, one third of the grade
TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles, up to 1,600 words, the remaining two thirds
TOK and EE grades run A to E, and an E in either is a failing condition

contentBlocks.heading: IB private teachers in India: where a multi-year arrangement holds
contentBlocks.body:
A three-year arrangement survives or fails on the practicality of one weekly journey, so locality matters more here than for a short booking. IB private teachers in India who commit to weekly home tuition are agreeing to that journey in July and in January alike. In Delhi NCR, a teacher living within South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri will hold a Tuesday slot in those pockets for years. The same person taking on a family in Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad is agreeing to a commute he may resent by the second monsoon, and evening traffic between Golf Course Road, Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Dwarka does not improve with familiarity. An IB private teacher in Delhi is best hired from inside the radius he already travels.

Mumbai behaves the same way with shorter distances. An IB private teacher in Mumbai working across Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel or Malabar Hill can sustain several households in a week. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar sit far enough out that the honest arrangement is usually one home visit a fortnight with online sessions between, rather than a weekly visit that quietly becomes irregular.

Hyderabad and Chennai are kinder to long arrangements. An IB private teacher in Hyderabad covering Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Kokapet and the Financial District moves between them without much loss, though Secunderabad adds a real leg. An IB private teacher in Chennai based near Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet or Nungambakkam holds those slots easily, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar families should build a hybrid week from the start rather than discover the need for one in November.

Central and western India is where mentoring changes character. Families in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur and Jabalpur, and in Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, frequently cannot find anyone locally who teaches the level required, and a parent searching for an IB private teacher near me finds general tutors instead. Online mentoring is the realistic answer there, and it works well for a relationship measured in years, because the weekly habit matters more than the room. An IB private teacher in Bangalore, an IB private teacher in Pune, an IB private teacher in Kolkata and an IB private teacher in Ahmedabad all sit between those two situations: supply exists, but rarely in the specific locality you live in.
items: Delhi NCR: hire inside the radius the teacher already travels, not across it
Mumbai: a fortnightly home visit plus online sessions beats a weekly visit that lapses
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Kondapur and Jubilee Hills sit close enough for a stable weekly slot
Chennai: OMR, Perungudi and Velachery families should plan a hybrid week from day one
Central and western India: Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Goa and Nashik usually mentor online
A personal IB teacher who resents the commute will not last three years, however good

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars in India and the mentor's role each year
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May examination session, with November used by a small minority and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. A mentor's year is built around those dates and around the school's own internal deadlines, which cluster far more than any annual calendar suggests.

Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore encounter the same rhythm even where the details differ. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

The role a mentor plays is not constant across the year, and a family paying the same weekly fee in August and in April should expect the content to differ sharply. Early in the year the work is systems: a planner that is actually used, a note format that survives a term, a folder structure per subject, and a rule about when homework is started rather than finished. Mid-year the work is diagnostic, reading returned assessments and identifying the pattern in them. Late in the year it becomes narrow and technical, aimed at whatever the mocks exposed.

One warning about school teachers. Where a school permits its own staff to take private tuition, a family sometimes hires the student's own subject teacher, and the arrangement can be excellent. It also removes independence: the person coaching the work is the person assessing it, and a student then has nobody to complain to about either. Ask the school what its policy is before making that choice, and consider keeping the mentor separate from the classroom even where it is allowed.
items: The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March; most schools enter the May session
May results are released in early July, which sets the retake and appeal timeline
Early-year mentoring is systems work: planner, note format, folders, start times
Mid-year mentoring is diagnostic: read returned assessments and name the pattern
Check the school's policy before hiring your child's own subject teacher privately

contentBlocks.heading: Home mentoring, online sessions or a hybrid year?
contentBlocks.body:
For a relationship measured in years, the mode matters less than the consistency, but each one buys something different and it is worth choosing deliberately.

Home tuition gives the mentor the evidence nobody else can gather. He sees the desk, the folder, the planner that was supposed to be filled in, the phone, the younger sibling, the hour at which the student actually starts work. A mentor whose job includes study skills needs that evidence, because study habits are physical and local. He can pick up the note file, look at last week's handwriting and say the thing a screen cannot support him in saying. For a student in MYP 2 or MYP 3, home classes are usually the only version of this that works at all.

Online sessions buy reach, which matters most where supply is thin, and they buy resilience. A weekly slot that never depends on traffic is a weekly slot that is still running in year three. Screen sharing suits the review parts of mentoring well: reading a returned assessment together, building a revision plan, working through a TOK exhibition draft. It suits the observational parts badly.

A hybrid year is the arrangement that fits mentoring best, and most long-running families end up there whether or not they planned it. One home session a fortnight, or weekly where distance allows, for the observational work, and shorter online sessions in the intervening weeks for review and planning. The trade-off stated plainly: home tuition gives the best information and the worst reliability, online gives the best reliability and the least information, and hybrid buys most of both in exchange for a schedule that has to be written down rather than remembered.
items: Home sessions let a mentor see the desk, the planner and the real start time
Younger MYP students usually need home classes; online mentoring suits older students
Online sessions never lose an evening to traffic, which protects a multi-year habit
Hybrid: fortnightly home visits for observation, online weeks for review and planning
Write a hybrid schedule down; remembered schedules decay within about a term

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a private teacher you plan to keep for years
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram covers identity, qualifications and claimed teaching experience, recorded against the programmes, subjects and levels a teacher says he teaches, before the profile goes live. For a long arrangement that is a starting point and not a conclusion, because the checks that matter most for mentoring are ones no platform can run on your behalf.

Ask how long the teacher's current arrangements have lasted. Somebody who has held students for two and three years works differently from somebody whose bookings all end after a term, and the answer is easy to give honestly. Ask what he does in a session when the student has done no work since the last one, because that situation will arise and the answer reveals a great deal. Ask how he records what was covered, and ask to see the format. A mentor without written records is relying on memory for a job that runs longer than memory does.

Then ask the awkward one. Ask what he would say if he thought the student no longer needed him. A teacher who cannot imagine that conversation is a teacher whose hours will only ever go up.

There are also safeguarding basics for any regular visitor to your house. Somebody should be at home during sessions with a younger child. Lessons happen in a shared room rather than behind a closed bedroom door. Communication about schedules and progress goes to a parent, not only to the student. None of this implies suspicion of anybody; it is simply the arrangement that makes a multi-year relationship comfortable for everyone, including the teacher, who has an interest in clear boundaries too.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed experience are checked before a profile goes live
Ask how long his current arrangements have run, and why the ones that ended did
Ask what a session looks like when the student has done nothing since last week
Ask to see how he records coverage; memory does not survive a three-year arrangement
Keep sessions in a shared room, with an adult at home for younger students

contentBlocks.heading: What an IB private teacher in India does beyond one subject
contentBlocks.body:
The subject hour is the part families price. The rest is the part that changes outcomes, and it is worth describing concretely rather than calling it mentoring and leaving it there.

Note-taking comes first, because most students in an IB school have never been taught it and are improvising. A mentor looks at a fortnight of actual notes and usually finds one of three problems: transcription, where everything the teacher said is written and nothing is organised; absence, where notes exist only for the subjects the student enjoys; or decoration, where the file is beautiful and unusable. The fix is specific to the problem and takes weeks, not one conversation. He sets a format per subject, checks it for a month, and then stops checking.

Planning is second. Not a colour-coded timetable that lasts nine days, but the smaller skill of turning a task into a start time. A student who writes down that the Internal Assessment draft is due on the twelfth has not planned anything. A student who writes down that he will do the method section on Saturday morning has. A mentor sits with the school's deadline list and converts it, out loud, in front of the student, until the student can do it unaided.

Third is reading feedback. Criterion comments and subject feedback are written in language that means something precise, and most students read them as praise or blame. Teaching a fifteen-year-old to extract an instruction from a comment is slow and genuinely transferable work.

And fourth is the conversation nobody else has time for: which subjects are worth the extra hour this month, when to stop revising something, what to tell the coordinator when a deadline is going to be missed. IB private teachers in India who take that role seriously spend perhaps two thirds of a session on the subject and the remainder on all of this, and the remainder is what families remember two years later.
items: Note-taking diagnosed properly: transcription, absence or decoration, each fixed differently
Planning taught as turning a deadline into a start time, not into a colour-coded chart
Reading criterion feedback as an instruction rather than as praise or blame
Deciding which subject deserves the extra hour this month, and which does not
Roughly two thirds of a session on the subject, the rest on how the student works

contentBlocks.heading: When should home tuition hours be deliberately cut back?
contentBlocks.body:
When the student can produce the same quality of work without the session, which is a moment that arrives quietly and is easy to miss because nobody is looking for it. Dependence is the specific risk of long private teaching, and it does not announce itself as failure. It looks like a comfortable arrangement where everyone is happy.

The signs are recognisable. The student stops attempting anything difficult between sessions and saves it for the teacher. He asks the teacher rather than the school when he does not understand something, which is a slow disaster because the school marks the work. His written answers improve in the presence of the teacher and not on a timed paper. Or he simply cannot say, when asked, what he would do differently if the sessions stopped next month.

The remedy is planned reduction rather than a sudden stop. Move from weekly to fortnightly and use the intervening week as a deliberate test. Change the session format so the student presents work he has already completed instead of working through new material live. Move one subject to independent study while keeping the mentor's oversight. Most students take a term to adjust and then hold the new level, which is exactly the point.

Be realistic about what mentoring can and cannot achieve. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a teacher who describes a specific outcome should be questioned rather than admired. A mentor who has been with a student since MYP 4 has a genuine advantage in DP2, but the advantage is knowledge of the student, not control of the result. And some students never need this arrangement at all. A student who is organised, who reads feedback and who asks his teachers questions needs subject help when a subject goes wrong, and nothing else.
items: Dependence looks like comfort, not failure, so review it on a date rather than a feeling
Warning sign: difficult work is saved for the session instead of attempted alone
Warning sign: the student asks the private teacher instead of the school subject teacher
Reduce by moving weekly to fortnightly and treating the gap week as a test
Change the format so the student presents finished work rather than working live

contentBlocks.heading: The termly review, and how to run it in India
contentBlocks.body:
Every long arrangement needs a fixed review, held three times a year, written down, and attended by the parent as well as the student. Twenty minutes is enough. Without a date in the calendar the review never happens, because there is always a deadline that makes this week the wrong week.

Run it in this order:

1. The student speaks first, for five minutes, on what has improved and what has not, with no interruption from either adult.
2. The teacher presents evidence: marked work from the term, the note file, and the pattern he sees across subjects rather than in one.
3. The parent raises anything not visible in the work, including hours, cost, fatigue and whether the household schedule is still holding.
4. The three of you agree one change for the coming term, and one thing to stop doing.
5. Decide the hours for next term explicitly, including whether they should fall.

The fifth step is the one families skip, and it is the reason arrangements drift. Deciding to keep the hours the same is a decision. Failing to discuss them is not.

To begin, send a query or book a free consultation and describe the student rather than the subject. IB Gram asks about programme, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists verified teachers who work at both the present stage and the next one, subject to availability. Arrange a trial before committing. And ask, in that first conversation, what the teacher expects the arrangement to look like in two years.
items: Fix three review dates a year in the calendar before the term starts
Student speaks first for five minutes, with neither adult interrupting
The teacher brings marked work, the note file and a cross-subject pattern
Agree one change and one thing to stop, then set next term's hours explicitly
Deciding to keep hours unchanged is a decision; not discussing them is drift

faqs.question: What is the difference between a private teacher and a subject tutor?
faqs.answer: A subject tutor is hired to fix a subject, and a private teacher in the mentoring sense is hired to stay with the student. In practice that means the tutor's session is planned around content and the mentor's session is planned around the student's week. The mentor teaches a subject too, usually one, but he also looks at notes, deadlines, planning and criterion feedback across all six. Hire a tutor if one subject is failing. Hire a mentor if the problem repeats across subjects.

faqs.question: How long should a private teaching arrangement last?
faqs.answer: As long as it is producing something the student cannot yet produce alone, and no longer than that. Many families run three years, from MYP 4 through to the end of DP1, and then reduce sharply. Others run one intense year. What matters is that the length is decided at reviews rather than by default. Set three review dates a year, decide the hours explicitly at each one, and treat an arrangement that has never reduced in two years as a question rather than a success.

faqs.question: Can a private teacher help with the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Within the boundaries the school and the IB set, yes, and those boundaries are stricter for the core than for ordinary subject work. A mentor may explain the assessment, discuss a research question, ask questions about a draft and hold the student to a timeline. He may not write, edit or contribute content. The Extended Essay has a school supervisor whose role cannot be substituted. For TOK, keeping the exhibition moving week by week is legitimate and useful; drafting it for the student is not.

faqs.question: Should a home tuition arrangement continue through DP2 mocks?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but the content should change completely. Before mocks, a mentor's planning and oversight work is more valuable than another taught hour, because a DP2 student's problem in that period is allocation rather than knowledge. Keep the slot, and spend it deciding what to revise, reviewing marked papers and protecting sleep. After mock results arrive, narrow the sessions to the two subjects the results actually implicate and reduce everything else. Adding hours across all six subjects in that window helps nobody.

faqs.question: Our home in Powai is small and my son shares a room. Does that rule out home teaching?
faqs.answer: No, though it changes where and when sessions happen. A dining table with the television off works better than most bedroom desks, and many families in Powai, Thane and Kharghar run sessions at a time when the flat is quietest rather than at the time that suits the calendar. If the space genuinely cannot be protected, a hybrid week helps: one home session for written work and observation, and online sessions from whichever corner is free in the intervening weeks.

faqs.question: Is a personal IB teacher worth it for a student who is already doing well?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the honest answer depends on what doing well is costing him. A student scoring highly while working until midnight has a study-skills problem disguised as success, and that is exactly the case mentoring addresses. A student scoring highly, sleeping properly and managing his own deadlines does not need a private teacher, and should not have one. Ask what would change. If nobody can answer in a sentence, the arrangement is being bought out of anxiety rather than need.

faqs.question: We live in Indore and cannot find anyone locally. Does online mentoring really work?
faqs.answer: For mentoring, it works better than most families expect, because the core of the job is conversation about work rather than observation of it. Families in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur and Jabalpur routinely run multi-year online arrangements with a teacher in another city, and the weekly habit survives well precisely because nothing depends on travel. The part you lose is the physical evidence: the desk, the note file, the real start time. A parent can supply some of that by photographing the week's work before each session.

faqs.question: How do we change teacher mid-year without losing everything he knew?
faqs.answer: Ask for a written handover before the last session, and make it a condition of the arrangement from the beginning. The handover should list what has been covered, the current weak criteria or topics, the note and planning systems in use, and what the outgoing teacher would do next. It takes him half an hour. Without it, a new teacher spends three or four sessions rediscovering things, and the student repeats a diagnosis he has already sat through once, which damages confidence more than the change itself does.

faqs.question: How many hours a week is reasonable for a long arrangement?
faqs.answer: Less than most families start with. One session a week of sixty to ninety minutes is enough for a mentoring arrangement in the MYP years, and two is usually the ceiling during the Diploma Programme, including the taught subject. Beyond that the student has no time left to work independently, and independent work is where learning actually happens. If the hours keep rising, something in the arrangement is being used to manage parental anxiety rather than the student's workload.

faqs.question: What should we do if our son will not speak during sessions?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly with the teacher, and expect him to change the session rather than wait for the student to change. Silence in a one-to-one session usually means the student is being talked at, or that the level is pitched wrongly, or that he is embarrassed about how little he did that week. A good mentor restructures around the student producing something: writing an answer, presenting a plan, marking his own work. If silence persists over a month across different approaches, ask for a different match.

faqs.question: Does a private teacher speak to the school directly?
faqs.answer: No, and it is better that he does not. The relationship with the coordinator and the subject teachers belongs to the family and to the student, and a private teacher contacting the school on his own initiative can create real awkwardness. What a mentor should do is prepare the student for those conversations: what to ask, when to ask it, and how to describe a difficulty precisely. Teaching a sixteen-year-old to email his coordinator about a missed deadline is more useful than doing it for him.

faqs.question: How do we end the arrangement well?
faqs.answer: Give notice at a review rather than by message, and plan a final phase instead of stopping abruptly. A sensible ending runs over a term: weekly becomes fortnightly, then monthly check-ins, then nothing. Ask for the handover notes even if no new teacher is coming, because the student may want them later. Say plainly that the arrangement has done its job. A teacher who has mentored a student for years has earned that conversation, and most will have seen it coming before you did.

comparison.heading: Four ways to hire a long-term private teacher in India
comparison.intro: These four routes differ less in teaching quality than in what happens when something goes wrong two years in. A freelance teacher you found yourself may be excellent and is entirely your own risk to manage. A centre gives you an institution and less choice of person. A school teacher knows the classroom and cannot be independent of it. Continuity, replacement and accountability are what actually separate them.

h1: IB Online Teachers in India for Cities Without Local Specialists
heroTitle: Online IB Teaching Across India, Honestly Costed
heroSubtitle: If your city has no IB teacher for the subject your child needs, the shortage is real and it is geographic. Online teaching does not fix everything, but it changes who is reachable on a Tuesday evening. This page is about that trade, and what you pay for it.
introSummary: IB online teachers in India exist mainly to solve a supply problem: outside Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune, the number of people who have actually taught a given Higher Level subject drops sharply, and in plenty of cities it reaches zero. A family in Kochi or Raipur is rarely choosing between a good local teacher and a remote one. They are choosing between a specialist on a screen and nobody. That changes how the option should be judged. What matters is which subjects are genuinely scarce where you live, what a screen costs a fourteen-year-old on a school night, where a home tutor still wins, and how a weekly schedule survives a teacher sitting in another time zone.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match an online teacher to a student in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks which board, programme, subject and level the student is on, what the school calendar looks like and where you are, then shortlists verified tutor profiles that fit. For a remote request, your location works differently: it fixes the hours that are possible, not the radius. A demo session can be arranged before the family commits to anything.

The second question decides the match. Not which subject, but which part of it. A DP1 student in Nashik who cannot see how to begin a Mathematics Applications and Interpretation (AI) modelling task needs a different teacher from a DP2 student in Guwahati whose Economics answers never quite reach the command term. Bring a recent marked script to the consultation and the shortlist gets shorter and sharper in the same move.

Time is the third question, and remotely it is the hard one. Say plainly which evenings survive school, travel and sleep, and say which ones only look free. If the one person who has taught your child's exact course works from a different time zone, you will be offered slots that sit early in the morning or late at night for somebody, and one of the two households absorbs that cost every week. Better to see it before the first session than in the fourth.

Then you test the match. Watch the demo for whether the teacher makes the student work or simply performs at them. Ask them to open a past paper and mark one answer aloud, with the criterion visible on screen. Ask what they would do with an internal assessment draft, and listen for whether the answer contains any limits at all. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match, subject to availability.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, naming the subject and level.
2. Share a recent marked script so the gap is diagnosed, not guessed at.
3. State which evenings genuinely survive school, travel and sleep.
4. Take a demo and watch who is doing the thinking on screen.
5. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, subject to availability.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: what each stage can take from a screen
contentBlocks.body:
The younger the student, the less a screen carries on its own. That is the honest ordering, and it should shape what you buy. A Diploma Programme (DP) student can work productively with a teacher they will never meet in person. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child usually cannot, and a Middle Years Programme (MYP) student sits between the two, depending on the subject and on the child rather than on the technology.

The DP is where remote teaching earns its place. A student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. Those are specialised hours. The person who has taught them before is often not in your city.

In the MYP the calculation shifts. Language Acquisition runs in phases 1 to 6, and a student in phase 2 who needs steady spoken practice can do a great deal of it on a call, because talking is the whole task. A student who needs somebody to notice that they stopped writing four minutes ago is harder to serve that way.

For PYP children, keep expectations small and sessions short. A young child works better with an adult in the room, and where that is possible a home tutor is the better first choice. Where it is not, keep remote sessions brief, frequent and built around reading aloud and talking rather than worksheets.
items: DP: six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level
HL is 240 recommended teaching hours, SL 150, each graded 1 to 7
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points, with 45 the maximum
MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases 1 to 6
Younger children need shorter, more frequent remote sessions
For PYP, an adult in the room beats a bigger screen every time

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects have almost no local teachers outside the metros?
contentBlocks.body:
Scarcity is not spread evenly. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) at Higher Level, Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level, Economics, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision are the hardest to staff locally once you leave the six big clusters. English B is the quiet one nobody expects to be scarce, and often is.

Start with Mathematics, because the confusion there costs families the most. DP Mathematics is two different subjects, each offered at both levels. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology used throughout. A capable local mathematics teacher who has taught Class 12 boards for years can usually help an AA student through calculus, and will often be genuinely lost on an AI modelling task, because the technology use and the statistical framing are not part of what they have taught. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often steered towards AA, though the right choice depends on the degree and the student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement.

Then the languages. A student whose first language is not English takes Language Acquisition: English B at SL or HL, or English ab initio at SL for genuine beginners. English B is built around five themes, Identities, Experiences, Human ingenuity, Social organization and Sharing the planet, and it is assessed through Paper 1, a writing task, Paper 2, listening and reading, and the individual oral, with two literary works added at HL. There is no IB subject called ESL, whatever a search result says. Parents who type that usually mean this, and the teacher they need has taught the individual oral before.
items: Mathematics AA is algebraic and proof-heavy at both levels
Mathematics AI is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology throughout
HL Physics, HL Chemistry and Economics are thinly staffed outside the metros
English B: Paper 1 writing, Paper 2 listening and reading, individual oral
English ab initio is SL only, for genuine beginners
The IB has no subject called ESL, though parents search for it

contentBlocks.heading: IB online teachers in India: the map of who has local options
contentBlocks.body:
Draw the map honestly and the case makes itself. IB online teachers in India are hired for two quite different reasons, and geography decides which reason applies to you. Families searching for an IB online teacher in Mumbai, an IB online teacher in Delhi or an IB online teacher in Bangalore usually do have local choices and are going remote for the specific subject or the specific hour. Everybody else is going remote because the alternative is nothing.

Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, there are strong general tutors in every neighbourhood and very few people who have taught an IB Higher Level course. The same is true across central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa. A parent in Jabalpur is not being difficult when they say there is nobody; there is genuinely nobody for that subject, and a search for a remote IB teacher is the rational next step.

In Kolkata and eastern India the picture is mixed. Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore have some depth, and an IB online teacher in Kolkata is often chosen for a single scarce subject rather than for everything. Move out to Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi or Patna and depth disappears quickly. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula hold a little supply between them, while Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur mostly do not.

Gujarat deserves its own paragraph because the searches are heavy and the supply is thin. Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev and the corridor along SG Highway generate steady demand, as do Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, and an IB online teacher in Ahmedabad will frequently be teaching a student whose school has one section of the programme. Compare that with an IB online teacher in Hyderabad, in Chennai or in Pune, where a family can usually find somebody in Gachibowli, in Adyar or in Koregaon Park, and where online is chosen for convenience rather than survival. Powai parents often want both: a tutor at home for routine work and an online IB faculty member for the hardest paper.
items: Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Madurai: strong general tutors, almost no IB specialists
Indore, Bhopal, Jabalpur, Raipur: remote teaching is usually the only route
Kolkata holds some depth; Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna do not
Chandigarh and Mohali have a little supply, Jaipur and Kanpur have less
Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot: heavy demand, thin local staffing
In Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune, remote is a convenience rather than a necessity

contentBlocks.heading: School deadlines in India when the teacher sits in another time zone
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, examination sessions fall in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May. Results are released in early July. A remote teacher who does not have those dates in front of them will plan against the wrong year, and a teacher living abroad will plan against their own school calendar unless you correct them in the first week.

Give the teacher your child's internal deadlines, not the IB's. Schools set their own coursework dates well ahead of the board, and they set mock examinations, predicted grade decisions and Extended Essay checkpoints on a calendar the teacher has no way of guessing from another country. Send the school diary. Ask for the term plan to be written against those dates rather than against a generic sequence of topics.

Time zones then decide what the week can actually hold. A teacher whose working day begins several hours after yours will be offered your child's late evening, which is the worst hour for a tired MYP student and only just workable for a DP2 student in February. A teacher ahead of India can take an early morning slot before school, which suits some students remarkably well and ruins the day for others. Try both for a fortnight before fixing the timetable, and protect one evening a week with no session at all.

A note on schools themselves. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Teachers may have taught students from schools you recognise, which tells you something about the rhythm they are used to and nothing about any relationship. Confirm every date with your child's coordinator.
items: Exam sessions run in May and November; Indian schools mostly enter May
May results are released in early July
The school's own coursework deadlines fall before the IB's
Send the school diary to the teacher in week one
Trial an early morning and a late evening slot before fixing either

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid: which one is right for your city?
contentBlocks.body:
If a qualified specialist lives near you, home tuition is usually the better buy. If one does not, remote teaching is not a compromise, it is the only version of the thing that exists. Hybrid, which most families arrive at eventually, puts a local tutor at the desk for routine work and a specialist on the screen for the part nobody nearby can teach. For most families beyond the metros, IB online teachers in India are the reach half of that plan rather than the whole of it.

Home classes carry information a screen loses. The tutor sees the desk, the phone face down beside it, the unopened textbook, the three pages of notes that were supposed to be six. They also see a student go quiet in a way that does not register on a video call. For MYP students and for any student whose real problem is organisation rather than content, that visibility is worth more than subject depth, and a good local home tutor beats a distant specialist comfortably.

Remote teaching wins on reach and on the calendar. A session can run the evening before a deadline without anyone crossing a city. Annotated past papers, shared documents and recorded explanations are genuinely better than the paper equivalents, provided the teacher is fluent with the tools rather than fighting them. What it cannot do is notice the room.

Hybrid is the quiet answer for most families outside the metros. One home tutor, weekly, for the subject the student is behind in and for the habit of sitting down at the same hour. One online specialist, weekly or fortnightly, for HL Physics or for Extended Essay supervision. A family in Vijayawada or Ranchi can build that in a week. Run it for a month, look at the student's own marked work, then drop whichever half is not earning its hour.
items: Home tuition wins when the problem is habit, organisation or attention
Remote teaching wins when the problem is a scarce subject or a tight week
Hybrid: a home tutor for routine work, a specialist online for the hard paper
A screen loses the room; it does not lose the mark scheme
Review after a month and drop the half that is not earning its hour

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a teacher you will never meet in person?
contentBlocks.body:
Check three things: that the person is who the profile says, that they have taught this exact course rather than something adjacent, and that somebody answers when things go wrong. Distance makes all three more important, not less, because you will never run into this teacher at the gate.

On IB Gram, profiles are verified before they go live, which means identity and claimed teaching background are checked. It does not mean anyone has sat through every lesson, and no honest platform will claim otherwise. Verification narrows the list to plausible people. The demo is where you get evidence, and the first month is where you get proof.

The subject questions are specific, and they are the ones a general tutor cannot answer smoothly. Which level have you taught, and for how many cohorts? Have you taught Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, or both? For English B, walk me through how you prepare a student for the individual oral. For an Extended Essay, what do you do when a student's research question is too broad? A teacher who has done the work answers in specifics and examples. A teacher who has not answers in adjectives.

Then the operational questions, which families skip and regret. Who do you contact if the teacher stops replying? What happens to a paid session when the power goes out at your end, or the teacher's connection fails at theirs? Is the session recorded, and who keeps the recording? Will you get a short written note after each session, and does anybody read it? Settle these in writing during the first week, while everybody is still enthusiastic.
items: Ask which course and level they have taught, and for how many cohorts
Ask a syllabus-specific question and listen for specifics, not adjectives
Agree what happens when a connection or the power fails mid-session
Ask whether sessions are recorded and who keeps the recording
Ask for a short written note after each session, and actually read it

contentBlocks.heading: What families outside the metros did before online teaching reached India
contentBlocks.body:
Before a specialist could be reached on a screen, families in smaller cities had four options and all of them were bad. They travelled. A parent in Nagpur or Vadodara put a child on a train or a flight to a metro every second weekend for a run of sessions, which cost the weekend, the money and most of the student's independent study time. Or they leaned on the school, asking a teacher to take extra hours after class, which works when the teacher has the hours and fails when the school has one section and one teacher for the subject.

Or they made do. An engineering graduate in the family took the mathematics, a retired professor took the physics, and nobody in the house had seen an IB mark scheme. The content was often taught well. The assessment was taught not at all, and the student lost marks on command terms and criteria while getting the science right.

The fourth option was the quietest and the most expensive. Families changed the child's subjects to whatever the school could staff properly, or moved the child to a hostel in another city, or left the programme. Subject choice was being set by local labour supply rather than by what the student wanted to study.

What changes when a specialist elsewhere becomes reachable is narrow but real: the constraint moves from geography to timetable. A student in Dehradun can keep Higher Level Chemistry because somebody who has taught it is available at eight on a Wednesday. The teacher competes on evidence rather than on proximity, so the shortlist gets better as it gets longer. And a family stops paying for travel and starts paying for teaching, which is the only part that was ever worth buying. IB online teachers in India did not make the teaching better. They made it reachable, which for a student in Jabalpur or Madurai is the difference that counts.
items: Weekend travel to a metro cost the weekend and the independent study
School teachers taking extra hours works only where the hours exist
A family member teaching content rarely teaches the mark scheme
Subject choice used to be set by local staffing, not by the student
Reach moves the constraint from geography to the weekly timetable

contentBlocks.heading: What remote teaching cannot fix, and what the reach costs you
contentBlocks.body:
Reach is bought with attention, and that is the trade nobody advertises. A student who is tired at nine in the evening is easier to lose on a call than across a table, and the teacher has fewer ways to notice. Judge the arrangement on the student's own marked work after about six weeks, not on how the sessions feel while they are running.

There are practical costs before that. A session needs a quiet room, a device better than a phone, a stable connection and somewhere to write that is not the same surface as the screen. Power cuts and patchy connectivity are real in a lot of Indian towns, so agree the rule for a dropped session before it happens. A student who has to take sessions in a shared living room with the television on will not concentrate, whoever is teaching.

Then the things distance cannot repair. No teacher can guarantee a grade, and a remote one has less leverage over the work done between sessions, which is where most of the improvement actually happens. Accountability has to be built deliberately: a specific task each week, sent before the next session, checked at the start of it. If a student is not doing that work, more hours on the screen will not help and may make things worse by creating the impression that somebody else is handling it.

And some students simply need a person in the room. A young child, a student with attention difficulties, a student in real distress about school. For them a home tutor two evenings a week is better than the best specialist in the country on a screen, and it is worth saying so plainly rather than selling the reach.
items: Judge on marked work after about six weeks, not on how sessions feel
A quiet room, a real device and a stable connection are the minimum
Agree in advance what happens when the power or the connection fails
No teacher can guarantee a grade, and distance weakens accountability
Some students need a person in the room, and should have one

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with an IB online teacher in India: the first month
contentBlocks.body:
Before you enquire, gather four things: the last school report with its criterion comments, one recent marked script, the school's deadline calendar for the term, and an honest list of the evenings that are genuinely free rather than theoretically free. Those four make the difference between a shortlist and a guess.

When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, level, the school calendar, your location and your schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who match, subject to availability. Say at that point whether you would also consider a home tutor locally for routine work, because a hybrid plan is often cheaper in hours and better in outcome than a single remote teacher carrying everything. Most families who end up with IB online teachers in India arrive by that route rather than by choosing a screen on principle.

The first session should be diagnosis, not a lecture. A good teacher shares a past paper, asks the student to attempt one question live, and then asks why they chose that method. They read one marked answer against the criterion with the student watching. They finish by naming one task for the coming week and the point of it. You should be able to read the session note afterwards and know exactly what happened.

By week four you want three things in place: a fixed slot that survives school and sleep, a task cycle the student actually completes, and one piece of work where the school's comment and the teacher's prediction agree. If any of the three is missing, say so and ask for a different match. Doing that in week four is straightforward. Doing it in February of DP2 is not.
items: Gather the last report, one marked script and the school deadline calendar
List the evenings that are genuinely free, not theoretically free
Ask about a hybrid plan with a local tutor for routine work
Expect diagnosis in session one, not a lecture on the topic
By week four: a fixed slot, a task cycle and one piece of agreeing evidence

faqs.question: Is an online IB teacher really as effective as one in the room?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma Programme student, usually yes, and for a young child, usually no. The variable is not the technology but how much of the problem is content and how much is habit. A DP2 student who needs somebody to pull apart their Economics answers loses almost nothing on a screen. A Grade 6 student who needs an adult to notice they have stopped working loses a great deal. Match the format to the problem rather than to the convenience.

faqs.question: Which subjects should we look for online rather than locally?
faqs.answer: Start with the ones your city is least likely to staff: Higher Level Mathematics in either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level Physics and Chemistry, Economics, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision. English B is the surprise on the list, because families assume any English teacher can cover it and the individual oral catches them out. For foundational work in younger years, a good local tutor is usually easier and better.

faqs.question: Our teacher would be in another time zone. Does that actually work?
faqs.answer: It works when the slot is chosen honestly and reviewed after a fortnight. A teacher whose day starts later than yours will offer your child a late evening, which is survivable for a DP student in short bursts and poor for anyone younger. A teacher ahead of India can take a slot before school, which suits some students and wrecks the school day for others. Trial both, keep one evening free of sessions, and do not let a good teacher in a bad slot run for a full term.

faqs.question: We live in Coimbatore and there is no IB teacher we can hire. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start by separating the subject problem from the study problem. Hire locally for the second: a general tutor who can sit at the desk two evenings a week and hold the routine. Hire remotely for the first: somebody who has taught that exact course and level. This is the pattern that works across Kochi, Vijayawada, Madurai and Visakhapatnam, and it usually costs less than sending a student to a metro for weekend classes.

faqs.question: What does a remote session actually need at our end?
faqs.answer: A quiet room with a door, a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, a stable connection, and a writing surface that is not the screen itself. A cheap graphics tablet helps enormously in Mathematics and the sciences, because the student can show working rather than describing it. Agree beforehand what happens if the power goes out in Bhopal or the connection drops in Guwahati, since that conversation is much easier before the first missed session than after it.

faqs.question: Would a home tutor still help if we already have an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Very often, yes, and this hybrid pattern is underused. The online specialist handles the subject content and the assessment technique. The home tutor holds the routine: a fixed hour at the desk, homework actually started, notes organised before the week runs away. Families in Ranchi, Nashik and Rajkot frequently find that the local tutor makes the remote sessions worth more, because the student arrives at them having done the work.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and drifts during online lessons. What should change?
faqs.answer: Shorten the sessions and change what happens in them before you change the teacher. Forty minutes of active work beats ninety minutes of watching, and a middle-years student should be writing, talking or solving something for most of the call. Ask the teacher to use shared annotation so the student is holding the pen. Move the slot earlier if you can. If none of that helps within a month, the format is wrong for this child and a home tutor is the better answer.

faqs.question: Can an online teacher supervise the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and this distinction matters. The school appoints the supervisor, and the school submits the work. An online teacher can help the student narrow a research question, plan a reading schedule, discuss method and ask hard questions about the argument. They cannot write, rewrite or edit any part of it. If anybody offers to tidy up the draft, stop there; the work has to be the student's own and the school runs it through similarity checking.

faqs.question: How do we verify a remote teacher we will never meet?
faqs.answer: Verify the person, the course experience and the fallback plan. Platform verification covers identity and claimed teaching background, and is a filter rather than a promise. Ask course-specific questions and listen for whether the answers contain real detail. Then ask the operational ones: who you contact if the teacher disappears, what a dropped session costs, whether sessions are recorded. A teacher who has done this before will have ready answers to all of it.

faqs.question: Is remote teaching suitable for a primary-age child?
faqs.answer: Rarely as the main arrangement, though it can work in small doses. Young children need an adult present, short sessions and a lot of talking, and most of what helps them at that age is reading together, number confidence and routine rather than subject expertise. If you are in a city with no IB specialist, that is fine, because a primary child does not need one. A patient local home tutor, or a parent with twenty minutes each evening, does more.

faqs.question: What happens if the internet fails in the middle of a session?
faqs.answer: Whatever you agreed in writing during the first week, which is why the agreement matters. The common arrangements are a rescheduled remainder, a credited part-session, or a short extension to the next one. Decide also who calls whom, so five minutes are not lost to both sides waiting. Power cuts and connection drops are a normal part of the year in many Indian towns, and a teacher who has taught here before will not be surprised by the question.

faqs.question: How soon should we expect to see a difference?
faqs.answer: Look for process changes in weeks two to four and evidence in the marked work by about week six. Early signs are a student who can say what a question is asking before answering it, drafts started earlier, and notes organised by criterion rather than by date. If the folder looks the same after six weeks, the problem is the match, the diagnosis or the slot, and adding hours will not fix any of the three. Ask for a different match instead.

comparison.heading: Remote, at home or in a batch: what each format buys a family in India
comparison.intro: Four formats, and the right one depends mostly on what your city can actually supply. A home tutor buys presence, a remote specialist buys reach, a batch buys structure at a lower cost per hour, and a recorded course buys availability at any hour. The question that settles it is whether the problem is the subject, which travels well across a screen, or the student's working habits, which do not.

h1: IB Tutor Near Me: Finding One Wherever You Live in India
heroTitle: What near actually means for an IB tutor in India
heroSubtitle: Near is not a distance. It is whether someone who teaches your child's exact subject and level will reliably reach your door on a weekday evening, week after week. This page works out how wide your search has to be, and when widening it is the right decision rather than a compromise.
introSummary: Typing IB tutor near me in India returns a list, and the list is the wrong shape for the problem, because the real constraint is not distance but whether anyone within reach teaches that subject at that level. Home tuition works beautifully when supply is dense and badly when it is thin, and supply for International Baccalaureate (IB) subjects in India is very unevenly spread. This page treats the near-me search as a geography problem. How far a tutor will genuinely travel, how local supply differs between a metro suburb and a smaller city, how to judge a close tutor against a stronger distant one, and the order in which to widen the search.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram find an IB tutor near me in India?
contentBlocks.body:
A request for an IB tutor near me in India is answered by searching outward in rings, and by saying plainly when a ring runs out. The first ring is your own locality, the second is the cluster of localities a tutor will cross on a weekday evening without the journey eating the lesson, the third is the city, and the fourth is the country by screen. Most families get a match in the first two rings for Mathematics or English A at Standard Level, and reach the fourth for a Higher Level subject that few people teach.

What we need from you is precise. Not the city but the locality, because Kondapur and Secunderabad are not the same search even though both say Hyderabad. Not the subject but the subject and level, since Higher Level carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level and a tutor comfortable with one may not teach the other. And the actual evenings that are free after school timings, travel and Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, because a slot that exists only in theory produces a home tutor who cancels by week four.

Then we come back honestly. Sometimes the answer is that three tutors nearby fit. Sometimes it is that the nearest person who genuinely teaches Higher Level Chemistry is across the city and the sensible arrangement is online, or a hybrid of one home visit and one screen session. Availability is always conditional on level, subject and schedule.

A demo session can be arranged before the family commits, and with a near-me search there is one extra thing to test in it. Ask the tutor how they got there and how long the return trip usually takes at that hour. A tutor who is quietly overreaching will tell you, and it is far better to hear it in week one than in week five when the cancellations start.
items: Give the locality, not the city: Kondapur and Secunderabad are different searches
Give subject and level together; HL and SL are not the same vacancy
Name the evenings that genuinely survive school, travel and CAS
We say when a ring is empty rather than stretching someone to fill it
In the demo, ask how the tutor travelled and how long the return takes

contentBlocks.heading: Does near matter more at PYP, MYP or DP?
contentBlocks.body:
It matters most for the youngest children and least for the oldest, which is the opposite of what most families assume when they start searching.

For the Primary Years Programme, covering ages three to twelve, near matters enormously. A seven-year-old cannot hold attention on a screen for long, and the useful work happens with physical materials and an adult sitting beside them. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, so there is no exam-technique argument for accepting a distant specialist. Learning runs through six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, ending with the PYP exhibition in the final year, and none of that requires a rare expert. Take the good tutor nearby.

For the Middle Years Programme, MYP 1 to MYP 5, near still matters but the balance shifts. Each subject is assessed against four criteria scored out of 8, totalling 32 before conversion to a 1 to 7 grade, and by MYP 4 and 5 the criterion work is specific enough that a tutor who genuinely knows the programme is worth travelling for. A capable generalist nearby usually beats a specialist far away until roughly MYP 4, and after that the calculation flips subject by subject.

For the Diploma Programme, near matters least. A DP student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions. At that level the gap between a subject specialist and a general tutor is wide, visible within two sessions, and worth more than proximity. A seventeen-year-old also works perfectly well on a screen.
items: PYP: take the good local tutor; no exam argues for a distant specialist
PYP has no external examinations and no published grades at all
MYP 1 to 3: a capable nearby generalist usually beats a distant expert
MYP 4 and 5: criterion work gets specific enough to justify widening
DP: the specialist gap is wide and proximity matters least of all
Higher Level runs 240 recommended hours against 150 at Standard Level

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects run out of local tutors first?
contentBlocks.body:
Theory of Knowledge, before anything else. It has no equivalent in CBSE, ICSE or state boards, which means the pool of people in any Indian locality who can teach it is drawn almost entirely from current and former IB school staff. In most neighbourhoods that pool is empty. Families searching for TOK help nearby are usually searching for something that does not exist within reach, and the sooner that is accepted the sooner the student gets help.

Higher Level sciences come next. IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology at Higher Level each need someone who has taught the internal assessment as well as the content, and the internal assessment is where the local pool thins fastest. Plenty of excellent board-trained science tutors live near you. Far fewer have marked a scientific investigation against IB criteria.

Mathematics is the interesting case, because it looks abundant and is not. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are distinct courses, and a tutor who teaches one well may be unfamiliar with the other. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, in particular, has a thin supply almost everywhere outside the largest metros. IB Economics is similar: the subject looks like something any commerce graduate can cover, and the internal assessment portfolio quickly proves otherwise.

The subjects where near-me searches usually succeed are IB English A, Standard Level Mathematics, and the sciences at Standard Level up to about MYP 5, plus general PYP and early MYP support. So a reasonable rule emerges. Search locally first for those. For TOK, the Extended Essay and anything at Higher Level, assume from the start that the search will need to widen, and treat a nearby match as a pleasant surprise rather than the plan.
items: TOK has no board equivalent, so the local pool is usually empty
HL sciences need someone who has marked the scientific investigation, not just taught content
Mathematics AA and AI are separate courses with separate tutor pools
HL Applications and Interpretation is thin outside the largest metros
English A and SL subjects are where near-me searches usually succeed
For TOK, the Extended Essay and HL, plan to widen from the start

contentBlocks.heading: What near means in each part of India
contentBlocks.body:
Everyone who types IB tutor near me in India means something slightly different by near, because the word stretches differently in every city. Here is what a realistic radius looks like around the country.

In Delhi NCR, near is a corridor rather than a circle. A tutor in South Delhi treats Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri as local and Dwarka as a trip. Gurugram along Golf Course Road forms its own market, as do Noida and Sector 128 Noida, while Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad each sit slightly outside everyone else's radius. Evening traffic on a weekday can stretch what looks adjacent on a map into something nobody repeats twice a week. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the same logic runs north to south: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill exchange tutors readily, while Powai sits on its own, and Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are separate markets that mostly supply themselves.

Bengaluru has the sharpest edges in the country. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala and Indiranagar form one dense east and south belt. Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road each sit beyond it, and a tutor crossing between them on a weekday evening is making a decision they will reconsider. In Hyderabad, the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet belt is effectively one neighbourhood for tutoring purposes, with Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills adjacent and Secunderabad genuinely far. Chennai splits between Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam on one side and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar on the other. Pune is kinder: Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar sit close, as do Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi.

Outside the metros near means something else entirely, because the limit is supply rather than travel. In Gujarat a tutor may happily cross Ahmedabad between Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and Gandhinagar, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families find very little locally. The same holds across Kolkata and eastern India, where Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore carry a little supply and Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna carry almost none; across northern India beyond Delhi NCR in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur; across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai; and across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa. In those places a nearby IB tutor is a lucky accident, not a search result.

Mumbai: the island belt trades tutors freely; Thane and Navi Mumbai supply themselves
Bengaluru has the sharpest edges between its east, south and north belts
Hyderabad's Gachibowli to Kokapet belt behaves as one neighbourhood; Secunderabad does not
Outside the metros the limit is supply, not travel time
