faqs.question: Should the tutor come to our home or should we go to theirs?
faqs.answer: Your home is better for the student and their home is cheaper in effort for the tutor, so it usually comes down to who absorbs the travel. A tutor at your house sees the study conditions and cannot quietly shorten the session. Going to them removes your control of the environment and adds a school-night trip for a student who has already travelled once that day. If the tutor's rate for visiting is the obstacle, consider one home visit and one online session each week instead.

faqs.question: Is a neighbourhood tuition centre worth considering for one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and read the offer carefully first. Many centres describe individual attention while teaching a small batch, which is a different product and often a perfectly good one for a confident student who only needs pace. Ask how many students are in the room, who teaches the Higher Level sessions, and whether the same teacher stays with the group all year. Centres win on cost and on structure. They rarely win on matching a specific course, and almost never on following an individual investigation.

faqs.question: How long should we wait for a local match before going online?
faqs.answer: A couple of weeks in a metro, and less than that anywhere else. If a verified local match for the exact course has not appeared in that time, the pool is telling you something. Waiting through a term for a nearby specialist costs the student more than starting online immediately, particularly in DP2, where the mock season arrives several months before the May session. Start online, keep the local request open, and switch later if a good nearby tutor becomes free. Availability always depends on subject, level and schedule.

mainEntity.name: How far away is too far for a home tutor on a weekday evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Judge it by what the tutor already does at that hour rather than by kilometres. A home tutor who teaches another family in your pocket at five and yours at seven will hold the slot for a year. A tutor with nothing else nearby is making a dedicated trip, and dedicated trips are the ones that get cancelled from January onwards. Evening traffic between distant parts of Delhi NCR, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region or Pune can stretch a short journey badly, so ask where their other weekday sessions are before agreeing the day.

mainEntity.name: Is a nearby average tutor better than a distant excellent one?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a young child, usually yes; for a Higher Level Diploma subject, usually no. Presence does most of the teaching at primary and early middle-years level, where attention and habit are the real work. By DP1 and DP2 the constraint is knowing one specific course deeply, and no amount of proximity substitutes for that. The middle cases are genuinely close, and the deciding question is how independently the student works. A student who drifts the moment nobody is beside them needs the nearby tutor, whatever the subject.

mainEntity.name: Can we use a local tutor for one subject and an online one for another?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is often the best available arrangement rather than a compromise. Put the subject that needs watching, usually Mathematics or an investigation write-up, with the tutor who comes to your house. Put the scarce Higher Level course with an online specialist who teaches it every week. The one thing to manage is the student's total load: two tutors means two sets of work between sessions, so ask each to keep their tasks small and specific rather than each setting a full week of practice.

mainEntity.name: What does a tutor sitting in the room actually notice?

acceptedAnswer.text: The things students never report. Working crammed into a margin so that a sign gets lost. An answer started before the question is read. A phone face-up on the table. A file with three months of loose sheets in no order. A student who nods at every explanation and cannot reproduce any of it ten minutes later. Some of this shows on a shared screen if the tutor asks the right questions, and most of it does not. It is the single strongest argument for hiring locally.

mainEntity.name: We are in Vadodara and searching for an IB private tutor near me in India. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Widen the search to online and stop waiting for a local match. Outside Ahmedabad, coverage in Gujarat thins quickly, and in Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot a Higher Level science or a Diploma core subject often has no local teacher at all. The practical route is an online specialist for that subject, and a local tutor at home only where somebody genuinely capable is nearby. A personal tutor near me search will keep returning general tuition rather than the exact course, which is the trap in smaller cities.

mainEntity.name: How do we compare a local and an online tutor fairly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give both the same material and ask both the same questions. Hand each of them the same marked script and the same topic, book the same number of sessions over four weeks, and at the end ask what was targeted, what the student produced and what is still wrong. Most comparisons fail because the two tutors were given different subjects or different amounts of time. Four weeks will not show a grade change, and it will show whether work was set and checked, which is what you actually need to decide.

mainEntity.name: Does a local tutor cost more than an online one?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, because travel time is real working time and gets priced in. A tutor crossing a city on a weekday evening gives up an hour that cannot be sold to anyone else, so home visits sit above online sessions for the same person. A tutor already in your locality prices that travel lower, which is one practical reason to look close before looking far. h1: IB Tuition Near Me: Every Local Option, Compared by Locality
heroTitle: Every Nearby Option, Compared Across India
heroSubtitle: Near is a question about places, not about providers. Your dining table, the tutor's flat, a centre two localities away, a library corner, or a screen. Each costs something different in travel, supervision and study time, and the cheapest-looking option is often the most expensive one.
introSummary: Parents searching IB tuition near me in India are really asking a venue question rather than a provider question. Should home tuition happen at your own dining table, should the student travel to a tutor's house or a neighbourhood centre, or should the lesson simply run online? The honest answer changes by locality, by the student's age and by the hour of the evening. A short walk within Alwarpet is not the same decision as a crossing from Whitefield to Koramangala at seven in the evening. This page compares each venue on four things parents rarely add up: travel time taken out of study time, supervision, safety, and what the family actually gives up. It also says when the nearest option is the wrong one.

contentBlocks.heading: How Does a Near Me Search Become a Real Shortlist in India?
contentBlocks.body:
By turning the word near into two numbers you can actually use: how many minutes of the student's evening you are prepared to spend travelling, and how many evenings a week. Everything else follows from those. IB Gram asks for the programme, subject, level, your locality and your realistic evening window, then shortlists verified tutor profiles that can work inside it, whether that means a home visit or a screen.

The mistake almost everyone makes with IB tuition near me in India is starting from a map. A search for tuition sorted by distance gives you the people closest to your flat, which correlates with nothing you care about. Sort instead by whether the person teaches your subject at your level, then apply distance as a filter rather than as a ranking. In most Indian localities that reverses the result entirely, and in Kokapet, Rajarhat or Balewadi it is the difference between a suitable tutor and a nearby one.

The second thing to establish is who is travelling. If the tutor travels, distance costs you reliability, because their commute is what breaks first in bad weather. If the student travels, distance costs you study time and supervision. Those are different currencies and families often pay the wrong one without noticing.

Then run a demo before you commit, in the venue you actually intend to use. A demo at your dining table tells you nothing about whether the student will concentrate at a centre on a Thursday after school, and a demo on a screen at eleven on a Sunday morning tells you nothing about a session at eight on a weeknight. Test the real conditions. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match rather than persisting because the location is convenient.
items: 1. Fix your evening travel budget in minutes, and the number of evenings.
2. Filter by subject and level first, then apply distance as a limit.
3. Decide who travels: the tutor, the student, or nobody.
4. Run the demo in the venue and at the hour you will actually use.
5. Re-check the arrangement after the first month of real traffic.

contentBlocks.heading: Venue Matters Differently in PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
The right venue changes as the student gets older, and families often keep the arrangement that suited a ten-year-old long after it has stopped suiting a sixteen-year-old. For a Primary Years Programme (PYP) child, the venue is almost decided for you. Home classes work, travel does not, and a young child sent out for tuition after a full school day arrives tired and learns little. Keep it at home and keep it short.

In the Middle Years Programme (MYP), which runs five years from MYP 1 to MYP 5 across eight subject groups, the balance shifts. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, with the total out of 32 converting to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. That means much of the work is written, marked against criteria and returned, so the session needs a table, the student's own folder and enough quiet to read feedback properly. A cafe fails that test. The Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5 add stretches where the student needs space to spread out and a supervising adult nearby.

By the Diploma Programme the venue decision becomes a time decision. The DP runs two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A DP2 student has almost no spare evenings. Every hour spent travelling to a centre is an hour not spent on an internal assessment draft. That is the arithmetic behind most families moving to home tuition or online in the final year, and it is usually the right move.
items: PYP: keep it at home and keep sessions short; travel after school rarely works
MYP: criterion-marked written work needs a table, a folder and quiet
MYP 3 to 5 projects need space to spread out and an adult within reach
DP1: a centre can still work if the commute is genuinely short
DP2: travel competes directly with internal assessment and Extended Essay time
Review the venue at each programme change rather than keeping the old habit

contentBlocks.heading: Which Subjects Are Worth Travelling For in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Very few, and the test is whether the subject needs something the venue supplies that your home does not. Mathematics at both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, Economics and English A need a table, a pen and an undistracted hour. There is nothing a centre adds to that, so travelling for them is paying in study time for no return.

The sciences are the argument people reach for, and it is weaker than it sounds. Physics, Chemistry and Biology tuition is overwhelmingly about working through questions, reading mark schemes and writing answers that match the command term, and a tutor cannot run a proper laboratory at a tuition centre anyway. What the sciences genuinely need is a specialist who has taught the subject at Higher Level, and that person is more likely to be found by widening the search than by shortening the journey.

Command terms are worth dwelling on here, because they are where most marks are quietly lost, and they are venue-neutral. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth of answer. A student who explains when the paper said evaluate has written a good answer to the wrong question. Fixing that habit takes a tutor, a past paper, a mark scheme and repetition, all of which fit on a dining table or a screen equally well.

There is one honest case for travel. Where a student works far better away from home, because the house is crowded, because a younger sibling interrupts, or because home has become the place where nothing gets done, a neutral venue changes behaviour. That is a real reason. It is just not a subject reason, and it should be recognised for what it is.
items: Mathematics, Economics and English A need a table and quiet, nothing more
Sciences need a Higher Level specialist, which is a search problem, not a venue one
Command terms decide answer depth and can be taught anywhere
Past papers and mark schemes come through the school or official IB channels
Travel is justified by a bad study environment at home, not by the subject

contentBlocks.heading: What Near Actually Means, Locality by Locality Across India
contentBlocks.body:
Near is elastic in India, and the same number of kilometres behaves completely differently depending on where you stand. In Delhi NCR, South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri are genuinely walkable to a neighbouring locality, while Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are not, and the crossing from Gurugram on Golf Course Road to Noida near Sector 128 is an evening lost either way. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, near means the same rail corridor or the same road: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri and Powai connect in some directions and not others, while Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill form their own cluster, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are separate worlds from the island city.

Bengaluru is the sharpest example. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road each behave as independent towns after five in the evening, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar are mutually reachable on a good day. Hyderabad is kinder: Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District and Kokapet sit close together, with Secunderabad apart. In Chennai, Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are compact, and Old Mahabalipuram Road, Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar stretch the same trip into something else. Pune divides between Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi on the other.

Beyond the largest metros, near stops being about traffic and starts being about supply. In Gujarat, families in Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev, along SG Highway, in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot often find general tutors close by and no Higher Level specialist at all. The same holds in Kolkata and eastern India across Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore, Rajarhat, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna; in northern India beyond Delhi NCR in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur; in southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai; and across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad. Searching IB tuition near me in India from any of those places usually returns the wrong answer, because what is near is not what is needed.
items: Delhi NCR: Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri are walkable; Ghaziabad and Dwarka are not
Mumbai: near follows the rail corridor, so Thane and Kharghar sit outside it
Bengaluru: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City are separate towns by evening
Hyderabad and Chennai: tight central clusters, with Secunderabad and OMR as outliers
Gujarat, Kolkata, Jaipur, Kochi and Indore: supply, not traffic, is the real limit
Ask which evenings a tutor has actually held, never how many kilometres away they live

contentBlocks.heading: School Timings and the Shared Evening Window Families in India Face
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore appear only as examples of the kind of school whose families face this problem.

Here is why venue is harder than it looks. International schools in India tend to finish in the middle of the afternoon, and many students then spend a long stretch on school transport before reaching home. Add an activity or a sport two evenings a week and the usable window for tuition narrows to a couple of hours that every other family in the locality is also trying to book. That is why the slots between roughly six and eight in the evening disappear first, and why a venue requiring travel effectively removes one of those hours.

The calendar tightens the same window at predictable points. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and schools here almost all enter DP candidates for the May session, with results in early July; November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May. In the weeks around mocks and internal deadlines, families want more sessions in the same narrow evening window, and a venue that costs travel time becomes untenable.

One practical consequence. If you intend to use a centre or the tutor's home, test it in the worst month rather than the easiest one. An arrangement that works in a dry week in September may not survive a mock week in January with rain. Families who plan for the bad weeks keep their arrangements; families who plan for the good ones renegotiate in the middle of the year.
items: School transport eats the first part of the evening before tuition can start
Six to eight in the evening is the contested window in every locality
Academic year roughly April to March; May session, results in early July
November suits a small minority of candidates and retakes, not the norm
Test a travel-based venue in a mock week, not in an easy September week

contentBlocks.heading: Home, a Centre or Online: Which Venue Suits Your Evening?
contentBlocks.body:
Among the venues covered by IB tuition near me in India, home tuition wins on time and supervision, a centre wins on discipline and cost, and online wins on choice of teacher. Which of those three matters most is a family decision rather than an educational one, and it should be made deliberately instead of by default.

Home classes cost the student nothing in travel, and that is the largest single advantage in any Indian metro. A parent is present, the student's own books and folder are within reach, and a session can run late by ten minutes without anyone missing a bus. The costs are real too: the house has to be quiet, someone has to be home, and you are limited to tutors who can reach your locality on a weekday evening.

A neighbourhood centre buys a routine. Some students work better when they leave the house, sit in a room where everyone else is working and cannot reach the television. It is usually cheaper per hour, because the teaching is shared. The trade-offs are travel in both directions, less individual attention, and a fixed timetable that does not bend around a school deadline. For a younger student the supervision question also matters: you should know who is in the room and who is at the front desk.

Online and hybrid arrangements have become the default answer in much of India because they solve the supply problem rather than the convenience problem. A student in Ranchi, Madurai or Jabalpur can work with a specialist in Bengaluru or Delhi. Hybrid keeps one home session a week for marking written work face to face and runs the rest on screen, which suits DP students with crowded evenings. So the sequence is simple: decide what you are short of. Short of time, stay at home. Short of discipline, try a centre. Short of a suitable teacher, go online.
items: 1. List what you are short of: time, discipline, supervision or a suitable teacher.
2. Short of time means home tuition; travel is the first thing to cut.
3. Short of discipline means a centre, where leaving the house changes behaviour.
4. Short of a subject specialist means online, whatever the local options look like.
5. Re-run this list at the start of DP2, when evenings disappear.

contentBlocks.heading: Sending a Teenager to a Tutor's Home: What to Check First
contentBlocks.body:
Visit once before the arrangement starts, and go with the student. That single visit answers more than any amount of messaging: who else lives there, which room the tuition happens in, whether other students are taught at the same time, and whether the place is quiet enough to work. If a tutor is reluctant to have you see the room, that is the answer.

IB Gram verifies identity and confirms the qualifications and teaching experience a tutor claims, along with the programmes, subjects and levels they have actually taught. That covers who the person is. It does not cover the physical arrangement at their house, which is why the visit matters and why a few plain questions are reasonable. Ask who else will be at home during sessions. Ask whether the student will be taught alone or alongside others, because a tutor advertising one-to-one and teaching three is a different arrangement at a different price. Ask about the entrance: a separate study or a front room is a different proposition from a bedroom.

Then fix the logistics that go wrong later. Agree how the student gets there and back, and who confirms arrival and departure. For a younger teenager, an adult should handle both legs, and a return trip after dark in an unfamiliar locality is worth avoiding whatever the convenience. Agree what happens if the tutor cancels after the student has already left. Share a phone number that is answered during the session, not only between sessions.

If any of that feels excessive, compare it with the alternative. When the tutor comes to you, home visits happen in a common area with the door open and an adult in the house, and none of these questions arise. That difference is a genuine part of the venue decision and deserves to be weighed rather than assumed away.
items: Visit the tutor's house once, with the student, before agreeing anything
Ask who else is home and whether other students share the session
Confirm the teaching room: a study or front room, not a bedroom
Agree both legs of the journey and who confirms arrival and departure
Keep a number that is answered during the session, not only afterwards

contentBlocks.heading: How Much Study Time Does the Commute Actually Cost in India?
contentBlocks.body:
More than families count, because the cost is not only the journey. Take a typical DP1 evening. The student reaches home from school, changes, eats something, leaves again for a centre, sits a session, travels back, and then tries to start homework. The journey itself is the visible cost. The invisible costs are the settling time before leaving, the impossibility of doing anything useful in the half hour beforehand, and the flatness afterwards when the student is back at a desk but no longer sharp.

Run the comparison honestly for your own locality rather than in the abstract. Ask the student to note, for one week, when they actually started studying on tuition evenings and on free evenings. The gap is the real price of the venue. In families who do this, the result is often that two travel evenings a week cost roughly one full evening of work, and that is before any traffic surprise or a monsoon washout.

The same arithmetic explains why online sessions can be shorter and more frequent. A twenty-minute check the evening before a test is worth having and is impossible if it requires a journey. Home tuition sits in between: no travel for the student, but the tutor's own commute limits how many short sessions are practical, so the arrangement tends to settle into one or two longer visits.

None of this makes a centre wrong. It makes the comparison fair. A centre that is genuinely close, that the student can reach without an adult and without crossing a major road, costs very little time and may buy a routine worth more than the minutes. A centre that requires a car and a driver two evenings a week costs a great deal, and the cost is paid by the student in the one currency the Diploma Programme leaves them short of.
items: Count settling time before and flatness afterwards, not only the journey
Log actual study start times for one week, on tuition and non-tuition evenings
Two travel evenings a week often cost about one working evening
Short, frequent sessions only work where nobody has to travel
A walkable centre costs little; a driven one costs the most scarce hours

contentBlocks.heading: When No Local Venue Works and Online Is Simply Better
contentBlocks.body:
There is a point at which the nearest option should be refused, and recognising it early saves a term. IB tuition near me in India is a useful search only until it starts returning the wrong sort of tutor. The clearest case is a scarce subject. If nobody within reach teaches Higher Level Chemistry or Higher Level Economics, the local tutor who teaches the subject at Standard Level is not a smaller version of what you need. They are teaching something else. A student is better served by a specialist on a screen than by a nearby generalist learning the course in parallel.

The second case is timing. If the only local slot is at a time the student is exhausted, the venue has already decided the outcome. A session at half past eight after a long journey produces very little, however good the teacher.

The third is repeated disruption. If a home tutor cancels through the monsoon, or the student misses a third of the sessions at a centre because of traffic, the arrangement has failed as a schedule regardless of the teaching quality. Count the sessions actually held over two months rather than the sessions booked.

What should progress look like once the venue is right? Within two or three weeks you should have the tutor's diagnosis in writing, and within about six a visible change in the specific thing they named, usually in the student's own written work rather than in a school grade. Subject grades move slowly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim attaching a number to the outcome should be treated with scepticism. If the arrangement is not working after a fair trial, change the tutor or change the venue, but change one at a time so you learn which was the problem.

A slot at an hour the student is exhausted has already decided the outcome

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Where IB Tuition Happens Near You in India
contentBlocks.body:
Decide the venue before you decide the person, because the venue eliminates most of the shortlist for you. That is the whole practical answer to IB tuition near me in India. Write down three things: the evening window you genuinely have, how much of it you are willing to spend on travel, and who is at home during those hours. Most families find that the answer narrows to home tuition or online within five minutes of writing it down.

Then prepare the same short packet any good tutor will want at the first session: the latest school report with its criterion comments, two recent marked pieces of work, the school calendar with mock dates and internal deadlines, and the list of evenings that are actually free. Bring it whether the session happens at your table, at a centre or on a screen.

One habit is worth keeping for the whole arrangement. At the end of each month, ask what has changed and what the tutor is doing differently as a result. If the answer is vague twice in a row, the problem is the teaching rather than the location, and moving venue will not fix it.

To start, send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, level, your locality and your schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles have been verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, lessons can run at home, online or hybrid, and you can ask for a different match at any time if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on subject, level and season, so the nearer you get to a mock period the fewer the options.

faqs.question: How far is too far for weekly IB tuition?
faqs.answer: Judge it in minutes of the student's evening rather than in distance, and set the limit before you start looking. A useful rule is that travel should never cost more than a third of the session length in each direction, and less than that in DP2. What counts as near differs hugely: a locality crossing in Alwarpet or Jubilee Hills is nothing, while the same distance between Sarjapur Road and Hebbal is an evening. Measure the trip at the hour you would actually make it.

faqs.question: Is home tuition always better than sending my child to a centre?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth saying so plainly. Home tuition protects study time and supervision, but it depends on the house being quiet and someone being present. A student who does nothing at home, who is interrupted by younger siblings, or who works better when everyone around them is working, often does more in a centre. The honest question is not which is better in general, but which fixes the specific problem your child has. Try one term of each if you can.

faqs.question: What should I check before my child studies at a tutor's home?
faqs.answer: Visit once, with the student, before anything is agreed. Look at the room where teaching happens and confirm it is a study or front room rather than a bedroom. Ask who else is at home during sessions and whether other students are taught at the same time, because one-to-one advertised and three taught together is a different arrangement. Then settle both legs of the journey, who confirms arrival and departure, and a phone number answered during the session.

faqs.question: Why does a search for IB tuition near me in India show so few results outside metros?
faqs.answer: Because supply follows schools, and IB schools cluster. In Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Bhubaneswar, Ranchi, Jaipur, Dehradun, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam and Nagpur you will usually find capable general tutors and very few who have taught a specific Higher Level subject. A near me search ranks by distance, so it returns the closest people rather than the right ones. Widen the search to online before concluding that nothing exists, because the specialist almost always exists somewhere in the country.

faqs.question: Can we do part of the week at home and part online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement many DP families in the metros end up with. The usual shape is one longer home session at the weekend, where written work is marked together and the tutor can read the student's own handwriting, and a shorter online session midweek for questions and checking. Agree the fee structure for both modes at the start, and agree who can switch a session to online and by when, so bad weather does not turn into a cancellation.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition near me cost compared with online?
faqs.answer: Fees are not published here, but the structure is predictable. A tutor travelling to your home is the most expensive way to buy an hour, because the commute is part of what is being paid for. The same tutor online is usually less. A neighbourhood centre is cheaper per hour again, since teaching is shared across a batch. A scarce Higher Level specialist costs more in any mode. Ask for the structure in writing, including cancellation terms, before a trial.

faqs.question: My child is in DP2 and has no free evenings. What is the realistic option?
faqs.answer: Cut travel first and keep the teaching. In the final year, mocks, internal assessment deadlines and the Extended Essay compete for the same hours, so an evening spent travelling to a centre is an evening not spent on submitted work. Most families in this position move to home tuition or online, shorten sessions and increase their frequency slightly. Also cut subjects rather than hours: tutoring three subjects badly helps less than tutoring one properly until it is fixed.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre near us teach the IB properly?
faqs.answer: Some do and some teach a syllabus that resembles it, so ask specific questions rather than reading the signage. Ask which programme and level is taught, how many students share the batch, whether past papers and mark schemes are used in sessions, and how the tutor handles command terms such as evaluate and to what extent. Ask what happens with internal assessment work, and be cautious of any centre offering to write or heavily redraft it, which puts a candidature at risk.

faqs.question: We live in Thane and the good tutors are all in south Mumbai. What now?
faqs.answer: Do not import a tutor across that distance for a weekly evening slot; it fails by the second monsoon. The workable options are a local tutor for subjects taught widely, an online specialist for anything at Higher Level, or a hybrid split with a weekend home visit from someone in Thane and midweek online sessions with the specialist. The same pattern applies to Kharghar, Greater Noida, Electronic City and Rajarhat, where local supply is thin and long commutes look tempting.

faqs.question: Will the tutor still come for home classes during the monsoon?
faqs.answer: Usually, but plan for the evenings when they cannot. Agree before June that an unreachable tutor means the session runs online at the same time rather than being cancelled and chased later, and agree who decides and by when. This matters most in Mumbai, Kochi, Guwahati and coastal Gujarat, where a fortnight of heavy rain can otherwise cost four sessions. Families who set this rule in advance lose almost nothing; families who negotiate it during the first washout lose weeks.

faqs.question: Is a library or a cafe a reasonable place for IB tuition?
faqs.answer: A quiet library corner can work for an older student doing written practice; a cafe rarely does. The session needs a table large enough for a past paper, a mark scheme and the student's own folder, low enough noise to hear an explanation, and enough privacy for the student to be told their answer is wrong without an audience. There is also no supervision and no place to leave things. For a teenager, home tuition or a proper room at a centre is almost always better.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in India for Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
heroTitle: IGCSE Tutors Across India for Two Exam Boards
heroSubtitle: Two boards, two grading scales, three exam series and a tiering decision most parents are never formally asked about. Before you hire anybody, find out which syllabus code your child is entered for. Everything else on this page follows from that one answer, including what a tutor is worth.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in India work to one of two boards, and the first job of any home tutor you hire is to teach the syllabus your child is actually entered for rather than a general version of the subject. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grade differently, tier differently and run different exam series. Cambridge also offers a February/March series that exists only for India, which pulls the whole two-year plan forward for the schools that use it. This page covers the board comparison, Core and Extended tiering, the syllabus codes worth knowing, what tuition should do in Grade 9 against Grade 10, and how to choose and trial a tutor. None of it replaces the school's own confirmation of the series and tier your child is entered for.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you choose and trial an IGCSE tutor in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the syllabus code, never with the subject. Any competent IGCSE tutor in India can tell you before you book which code they teach and which tier they teach it at, because Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended is a different job from 0580 Core, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) Higher is different again. IB Gram asks for that detail at the start rather than at the trial.

The query itself is short. You give the board, the syllabus codes if you have them, the tier if it has been decided, the grade the student is in, your locality and the evenings that are genuinely free. Or you book a free consultation and work it out in conversation. IB Gram then shortlists verified profiles against those answers, a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything, and if the match turns out wrong you can ask for a different one.

The trial is where the decision is really made. Send a marked past paper question in advance and ask the tutor to work through that with the student instead of introducing themselves. Watch three things: whether they read the mark scheme aloud, whether they talk about method marks rather than right answers, and whether the student is writing by the second half of the hour. A tutor who lectures for fifty minutes has shown you the next six months.

One practical note about timing. Grade 10 families across India tend to start looking in September, which is exactly when the workable weekday evening slots disappear. Availability always depends on the level and the schedule, so if the tier and the code are settled in July, start in July.
items: 1. Confirm the board, syllabus code and tier with the school before searching
2. Send the query with codes, grade, locality and genuinely free evenings
3. Review the shortlist of verified profiles and read past the marketing
4. Run a trial on a marked past paper question, not an introduction
5. Agree sessions, mode and a review date before series planning begins

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: which IGCSE is your child actually taking?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means one of two things, and parents routinely do not know which. Cambridge IGCSE comes from Cambridge International Education. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is a separate qualification from a separate board. Both usually run as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and both commonly lead into the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11.

The differences are practical. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9-1 versions under different codes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1 throughout. Cambridge exam series run in February/March, which is offered only in India, May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The school decides which series a student is entered for, and a student cannot choose a series independently of the school, so this is a conversation with the coordinator rather than a family decision.

Tiering is where the two boards diverge most visibly. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher instead. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered altogether, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

One more thing worth checking early rather than in Class 11. The Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and requirements change, so confirm current expectations with the university or board concerned rather than relying on what another parent was told two years ago. A tutor is not the right source for that answer either.
items: Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1
Cambridge series: February/March in India, May/June and October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June
Cambridge Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*
The school decides the series entry, not the family and not the tutor

contentBlocks.heading: The syllabus codes every IGCSE parent should be able to name
contentBlocks.body:
Learn six numbers and most tutoring conversations become straightforward. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580. Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610. Economics is 0455 and First Language English is 0500. A parent who opens with the code rather than the subject name gets a noticeably more honest answer about what a tutor has actually taught.

The paper structure follows the code. In 0580 from the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1, which is non-calculator, and Paper 3 with a calculator. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4 with a calculator. The non-calculator papers changed how Grade 10 revision has to be built, and a tutor still setting only calculator practice has not read the current syllabus.

The Cambridge sciences examined from 2023 share a shape. Paper 1 is multiple choice for Core candidates and Paper 2 for Extended. Paper 3 is theory for Core and Paper 4 for Extended. Practical work is assessed either through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school chooses which. The weighting is multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%. That last figure explains why families who ignore the practical paper until March lose marks they could have banked in December.

A Cambridge IGCSE tutor and an Edexcel IGCSE tutor are not interchangeable, even in the same subject. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each science, and practical skills appear inside the written papers instead of a separate component. Ask which of these two structures the candidate has taught most recently, and in which series.

Cambridge sciences weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%
The school chooses Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical
Edexcel sciences are untiered, with practical skills inside the written papers

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE home tuition across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tutors in India cluster where the international schools cluster, so the same search behaves very differently from one city to the next. In Delhi NCR an IGCSE tutor in Delhi is reachable across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka, with a thinner but real pool through Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. Home tuition works well inside a corridor and badly across one. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, an IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is easiest to find around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Malabar Hill and Powai, while Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar families should ask about monsoon arrangements before agreeing a weekday slot.

The southern metros behave differently from each other. An IGCSE tutor in Bangalore is straightforward in Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar, harder in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City, Hebbal, Yelahanka and along Kanakapura Road, where evening traffic can stretch a short trip badly. An IGCSE tutor in Hyderabad covers Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Secunderabad and Kokapet. An IGCSE tutor in Chennai works across Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Alwarpet and Perungudi, where the OMR corridor is its own scheduling problem. An IGCSE tutor in Pune ranges over Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad.

Gujarat has a genuine pool now. An IGCSE tutor in Ahmedabad covers Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway stretch, with Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families often running hybrid weeks. In the east, an IGCSE tutor in Kolkata serves Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna families usually start online and add home sessions later.

Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, one subject specialist may serve a whole city. Southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, meaning Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, is similar. Central and western India, including Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, is the thinnest of all for named syllabus codes. Searching IGCSE tutors near me from any of these places is a reasonable start and rarely the finish.

Chennai's OMR stretch and Bengaluru's Whitefield side both favour a hybrid week
Gujarat, from Ahmedabad and Bodakdev to Surat and Rajkot, has a workable pool
Salt Lake and Rajarhat have local supply; Guwahati and Ranchi usually start online
Indore, Nagpur, Kochi and Chandigarh: expect one specialist per city, if that

contentBlocks.heading: How the February/March series reshapes the two-year plan in India
contentBlocks.body:
The February/March Cambridge series exists specifically for India, and it changes everything about pacing. It lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for entry to the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels in the same academic year. For a family, the practical effect is that the final revision block lands in the winter rather than in the spring, and the last teaching term is shorter than anyone expects.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School all plan against their own school's chosen series and internal deadlines, which is the calendar a tutor has to work to.

Ask the coordinator two questions in Grade 9, not Grade 10. Which series is this cohort entered for? And when are the school mocks? If the answer is February/March, past papers need to start earlier, coursework deadlines bite sooner, and the Diwali break sits uncomfortably close to the run-in. If the answer is May/June, the shape is gentler and the summer break becomes the natural consolidation point.

One caution that costs families every year. Schools decide the series, and a student cannot enter a different one independently. So a tutor who proposes a plan without knowing the series is guessing, and a plan built on the wrong series wastes a term.

Ask the coordinator in Grade 9 which series the cohort will be entered for
A February/March plan starts past papers earlier and squeezes the Diwali break
May/June entry makes the summer break the natural consolidation point

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a batch: which suits a Grade 10 student?
contentBlocks.body:
For IGCSE specifically, the mode question turns on paper rather than preference. A great deal of what goes wrong at this level is visible only in handwriting: working that skips a line and loses method marks, a diagram drawn too small to label, an answer that runs out of time three questions from the end. A home tutor sitting beside the student catches all of that in week one. On a screen, the same problems can hide for a month.

Online tuition answers a different problem, which is supply. If your child takes a syllabus almost nobody near you teaches, an online teacher who works on that code every week is a better hire than a local generalist reading ahead. Online also holds its slot through rain, exam weeks and a parent's travel, and for families in smaller cities it is frequently the only route to a specialist at all.

A batch at a coaching or tuition centre has genuine strengths that one-to-one does not. Peer discussion helps in Economics 0455 and in English 0500, where hearing four other answers to the same question teaches more than being told what a good answer looks like. Batches also impose a rhythm, and some students need the rhythm more than the attention.

Hybrid is the arrangement most Grade 10 families in India end up with, and it is not a compromise so much as a design. One home session a week for written work and marking, one or two online sessions for content and past papers. Write the pattern down at the start. The temptation in January is to add hours in every mode at once, which usually produces a tired student rather than a better script.
items: A home tutor catches lost method marks, cramped diagrams and timing problems
Online teaching solves supply, not handwriting, and holds its slot through the monsoon
A centre batch gives peer discussion that helps in Economics 0455 and English 0500
Hybrid: one home session weekly for written work, the rest online for content
Agree the mode pattern in writing before the January urge to add hours

contentBlocks.heading: Checking an IGCSE tutor's claims before the first lesson
contentBlocks.body:
Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they go live: identity, the qualifications claimed and the syllabuses and levels the tutor lists. Most IGCSE tutors in India will pass that stage, so treat it as the baseline rather than the verdict. The checks that separate a good hire from a poor one are the ones you make in a ten-minute phone call, and they are all specific.

Ask which syllabus codes the candidate has taught in the last two series, and for which board. A tutor who says Maths and Science without naming 0580, 0625, 0620 or 4MA1 has answered a different question. Ask which tier they usually teach, because Core and Extended candidates sit different papers and a tutor whose recent work is all Core will pace an Extended student wrongly. Ask what they do about the practical component, since the school chooses between Paper 5 and Paper 6 and the preparation differs completely.

Examiner experience deserves a follow-up rather than admiration. Ask which component and which recent sessions. Cambridge professional development also comes in categories, and attending a course is not the same as years of teaching a named syllabus. The claim that predicts usefulness best is the dullest one: how many cohorts have you taken through this exact code.

For a home visit, add the domestic checks. Confirm identification at the first session, register the tutor with the society gate in advance, agree who is at home during lessons, and settle what happens when a session is missed. Parents searching for the best IGCSE tutor India can offer often skip these entirely, then discover in November that nobody agreed how a cancelled Tuesday gets replaced. Best, in practice, is the tutor who is still teaching well in the last month before the series.
items: Ask which codes and which board the candidate taught in the last two series
Ask which tier they usually teach: Core and Extended need different pacing
Ask how they prepare for Paper 5 or Paper 6, whichever the school has chosen
Behind an examiner claim, ask for the component and the recent sessions
Settle identification, gate entry and missed sessions before the first home visit

contentBlocks.heading: What IGCSE tuition should look like in Grade 9 and Grade 10
contentBlocks.body:
The two years are not the same job, and a tutor who runs them identically is wasting one of them. Grade 9 is a building year. The student is meeting mark schemes for the first time, learning that a command word changes what an answer must contain, and forming the note-taking habits that will either survive Grade 10 or collapse in it. Tuition here should be light, at most one session a week per subject, and heavily weighted towards how to work rather than towards coverage.

Grade 10 tightens quickly. Content finishes, coursework deadlines land, and past papers become the main material rather than the finishing touch. A reasonable rhythm is content until the school's mock period, then timed practice against real papers with the mark scheme read alongside. The single most useful thing a tutor does in Grade 10 is mark the student's own script in front of them and show exactly where each mark went. That is worth more than an hour of explanation.

A few families arrive in Grade 10 with a genuine crisis, and the plan is different again: diagnose from marked papers, pick the two or three topics carrying the most marks, and accept that some ground will not be recovered. Honest triage beats optimistic coverage.

IGCSE tutors in India are asked to do many adjacent things as well, and each is its own decision rather than an add-on. Tiering evidence, which is gathered from marked papers over a term. Coursework support, which stops at the boundary the syllabus sets. Bridging work for a student arriving from CBSE or ICSE, which is mostly about writing and command words rather than content. Subject choice advice for Grade 9, which belongs to the school first. Ask for one of them at a time.
items: Grade 9: one light session a week, aimed at method, notes and mark schemes
Grade 10: content to the mocks, then timed papers with the mark scheme alongside
The highest-value Grade 10 hour is a script marked in front of the student
A late start means triage: the two or three topics carrying the most marks
Bridging from CBSE or ICSE is mostly writing and command words, not content

contentBlocks.heading: Core or Extended: who decides, and when should it be revisited?
contentBlocks.body:
The school decides, using evidence, and the family should be part of the conversation well before the entry deadline. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the decision has consequences for Class 11 and beyond. It is also reversible for longer than most parents realise, which is why it should be revisited rather than settled once in Grade 9 and never mentioned again.

The evidence that matters is marked work under timed conditions, not classwork and not a feeling. A student scoring consistently across Extended past papers over a term belongs at Extended. A student who is comfortable on routine questions and collapses on the harder final section may be better served by a confident C than by a stressful two years and a poor Extended grade. Neither answer is shameful, and a tutor who pushes Extended in every case is not giving advice.

When school and family disagree, ask to see the evidence behind the school's view: which papers, which marks, over what period. Then gather the same evidence independently through a tutor, under the same conditions, and compare. Disagreements usually dissolve once both sides are looking at scripts rather than impressions.

Progress, meanwhile, should be visible on the same timescale. Within a term you should see method marks being recovered, working set out properly and timing improving. Marks on full papers move later. If nothing has changed after a term of steady sessions, change the plan rather than adding hours. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim about a specific outcome at a specific tier should be treated with real scepticism.
items: Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*, and the school enters the student
Decide on timed past paper evidence gathered over a term, not on classwork
Revisit the tier at least once rather than fixing it in Grade 9 forever
If school and family disagree, compare scripts rather than opinions
Within a term expect recovered method marks and better timing, not new grades

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started with IGCSE tutors in India
contentBlocks.body:
Gather four things before you approach any of the IGCSE tutors in India you have shortlisted, and the whole process shortens. The board and the syllabus codes, which the school can confirm in an email. The tier, if it has been set. The most recent marked paper, ideally one that went badly. And your real weekly availability, meaning the evenings that survive football practice and a parent's commute rather than the ones that look free on a calendar.

Then send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs, and can arrange a demo or trial session before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid. Availability is subject to the tutor's schedule and the level required, and the family can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.

The first session is worth planning. Bring the marked paper, the school's deadline calendar and the mock dates. A tutor who spends session one diagnosing from evidence will build a better two-year plan than one who starts at chapter one of the textbook because that is where textbooks start.

And set a review date now, in the same conversation. Six weeks is enough to know whether the working method is changing. Write it down, keep it, and be willing to change the subject, the mode or the tutor at that review. The families who do this end up with fewer total hours of tuition across Grades 9 and 10, which is the outcome everybody actually wants.
items: Gather the board, the codes, the tier and one marked paper before contacting anybody
Send a query or book a free consultation with your real weekly availability
Bring the marked paper, deadline calendar and mock dates to the first session
Set a six-week review date in the same conversation and keep it
Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability

faqs.question: How do I find out which board and syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the coordinator and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject in writing. Schools answer this readily and parents rarely ask. The code matters because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grade and tier differently, and because a tutor who has taught 0625 for years may never have taught the Edexcel equivalent. Keep the reply, and give it to every tutor you speak to.

faqs.question: Does the February/March series really change how we plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. The February/March Cambridge series is offered only in India, so Grade 10 results arrive in time for Class 11 admissions and for IB Diploma or A Level entry the same year. Practically, the final revision block falls in winter rather than spring, past papers have to start earlier, and the last teaching term is shorter than families expect. Confirm the series with the school before agreeing any two-year tuition plan.

faqs.question: Should we book home tuition or online lessons for Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Book home tuition if the marks are being lost on paper, and online if they are being lost on content. A tutor beside the student sees skipped working, cramped diagrams and the moment timing goes wrong. An online specialist teaching your exact code weekly is the better answer when nobody locally teaches it. Most Grade 10 families in India end up hybrid: one home session a week for written work, the rest online.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we take tuition in?
faqs.answer: Two, or three at the outside, even though IGCSE students sit far more than that. Tuition hours come out of independent study time, which is where most improvement actually happens at this level. Choose by where the marks are, not by which subject feels most alarming. A better pattern is to keep one subject running all year and bring others in for short blocks around coursework deadlines and the mock period.

faqs.question: Who decides Core or Extended, and can it change?
faqs.answer: The school decides and enters the student, using evidence from marked work. It can usually be revisited during the course, which is why it should be reviewed rather than fixed once in Grade 9. Gather timed past paper evidence over a term before arguing either way. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the decision matters, but a confident Core grade sometimes serves a student better than a stressful Extended one.

faqs.question: We are in Thane and most tutors are in Bandra. What is realistic for a home slot?
faqs.answer: One home session a week is realistic, two is not, and the monsoon will test even the one. Families across Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar reach the same conclusion by the second term. Either find a tutor on your side of the creek and accept a slightly smaller pool, or take a stronger tutor online and add a local person for written work. Agree the arrangement before June rather than during it.

faqs.question: Is a coaching centre batch ever better than one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, in specific cases. Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 both improve when a student hears several answers to the same question, and some students need the imposed rhythm of a fixed weekly class more than they need individual attention. Batches also tend to cost less per teaching hour. Check batch size, who teaches it, whether that person changes mid-course, and how quickly written work comes back marked.

faqs.question: What should the first month of IGCSE tuition actually produce?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis you can read, and a visible change in how the student writes answers. By week four you should see command words being addressed, working set out so method marks survive, and at least one script marked against a real mark scheme with the student watching. Grades usually move a term later than habits do. If none of that has happened in a month, the plan needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: Our school teaches Edexcel but every tutor near us advertises Cambridge. Does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more in some subjects than others. The underlying content overlaps heavily, but paper structure, tiering and mark schemes do not. Edexcel sciences are untiered with practical skills inside the written papers, while Cambridge uses Paper 5 or Paper 6 separately. A strong Cambridge tutor can teach Edexcel content well and still misjudge the paper. Ask directly whether they have taught 4MA1 or 4CP0 and in which recent series.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skills, discuss the task, question the student's thinking and explain how the criteria are applied. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit the submitted work. The line is the school's to enforce and it is stricter than many families assume. Ask any candidate how they handle a draft before you hire them, and treat an offer to improve the writing as a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: We live in Indore and cannot find a tutor for our science code. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Widen to online and search by code rather than by subject. Central and western India, including Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Nashik, has the thinnest local supply for named IGCSE syllabuses, and families there routinely work with teachers in other cities. Ask the school whether other parents share the problem, since small online groups often form that way. Keep a local tutor for written work if handwriting and timing are the weakness.

comparison.heading: How do IGCSE tutoring formats compare for families in India?

A recorded course buys availability at two in the morning before a mock. Read the rows against the specific problem you are trying to solve, because the honest answer for many families is a combination rather than one of them.
