h1: IGCSE Home Tutors in India Who Teach at Your Address
heroTitle: IGCSE Tutors Who Teach at Your Table in India
heroSubtitle: Grade 9 and Grade 10 are written subjects. Marks are won and lost in the working, the diagram and the handwriting under time, and those are the things a tutor sitting beside the student can see. This page covers what that presence buys, what it costs in travel, and when a screen is the better answer.
introSummary: IGCSE home tutors in India come to your address and teach at your table, which matters more at Grade 9 and Grade 10 than at almost any other stage, because this is where the marks live in the working rather than the answer. A tutor beside the student watches the pen. They see the step that was skipped, the rearrangement done in the head, the diagram drawn too small to label, the question abandoned after four minutes. None of that is visible on a screen, and a student will rarely report it. This page covers what home tuition catches, how travel radius and society gate entry actually work in Indian cities, how evening slots fit a Grade 10 timetable, and the subjects where online is honestly the better choice.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you get an IGCSE home tutor in India matched to your address?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks which board, which syllabus codes, which tier and which locality, then shortlists verified profiles who can actually reach you at the hours you named. A trial session is arranged before you commit. The address is part of the brief from the first message, because for home classes it decides as much as the subject does.

The board question comes first and families often answer it wrongly. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. They are different qualifications with different papers and different grading, and a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. If you are unsure, the syllabus code on the student's own materials settles it: Cambridge subjects carry codes such as 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0455 and 0500, while Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1.

The tier question comes next. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, where Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, and Edexcel Mathematics A is tiered Foundation or Higher. A tutor needs to know which one the school has entered your child for, and whether that entry is settled or still under discussion.

Then the logistics. Your locality, the days, the earliest the student is home from school, and whether a weekend morning is realistic. Travel radius is a hard constraint rather than a preference, so naming the locality rather than the city produces a better shortlist. Availability depends on subject, tier and the hours you need.
items: 1. Send board, syllabus codes, tier, grade and your locality, not just the city.
2. A short call confirms what the student is actually losing marks on.
3. Verified profiles within reach of your address are shortlisted, subject to availability.
4. A trial session runs at home, with the student's own marked work.
5. Weekly slots and gate access are fixed before the first paid lesson.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: which tier is your child actually on?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and in India it is followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. That destination should shape the tutoring from the start, because a student heading towards Higher Level Diploma sciences needs different habits from one heading to ISC Commerce.

The exam series differ by board and they matter for planning. Cambridge series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, in May and June, and in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. A Grade 10 student sitting the February and March series has a compressed run-in compared with one sitting May and June, and a tutoring plan that ignores that difference wastes the autumn.

Grading differs too. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. So a parent comparing a sibling's old grades against a current report may be comparing two different scales.

Tiering is the decision that a home tutor is best placed to inform, because it depends on evidence rather than ambition. Many Cambridge subjects offer Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1) is Foundation or Higher. A tutor watching a student work through past paper questions week after week builds the honest picture of which tier is right, and that picture belongs in the conversation with the school rather than in an argument at home.
items: Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November.
Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June.
Core is capped at grade C; Extended reaches A*. Confirm the entry.
Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher.
Where the student goes in Class 11 should shape Grade 9 habits.

contentBlocks.heading: Where the marks are lost on paper: 0580, 0625, 0620 and 0610
contentBlocks.body:
Method marks are the reason this page exists. In a multi-step Mathematics question, a student who writes only a final answer has staked everything on the arithmetic. The same student who writes the rearranged formula, the substitution and then the answer keeps credit for the method even when the last line slips. Every experienced tutor in India has watched a strong student lose marks they had genuinely earned, silently, because the working stayed in their head.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 makes this concrete from the 2025 examinations. Core candidates sit Paper 1, which is non-calculator, and Paper 3 with a calculator. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4 with a calculator. The non-calculator paper is where habits show. A student who has done two years of work with a calculator in hand writes almost nothing down, and a tutor sitting beside them can stop that within a fortnight by simply refusing to accept an unwritten step.

The sciences carry a different risk. For Cambridge syllabuses examined from 2023, the structure is Paper 1 multiple choice for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, Paper 3 theory for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, and practical assessment through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. The weighting is multiple choice 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. That means half the marks in Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 come from written explanation, which is precisely where handwriting, structure and the abandoned half-answer cost marks. Pearson Edexcel sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

In Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 the issue is planning rather than arithmetic. A tutor at the table can see an essay being started without a plan, which no amount of online explanation catches.
items: 0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 with a calculator.
0580 Core: Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 with a calculator.
Cambridge sciences: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%.
Practical is assessed by Paper 5 or Paper 6, whichever the school chose.
0455 and 0500: watch for essays begun without any plan on the page.
Edexcel sciences are untiered, with practical skills inside the written papers.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE home tutors in India: travel radius, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
Travel decides which IGCSE home tutors in India are genuinely available to you, so it is worth being blunt about geography. An IGCSE home tutor in Delhi working across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri is in a different practical situation from one covering Dwarka, Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. Evening traffic across Delhi NCR can stretch a short trip into an ordeal, and the tutor who agrees to it in week one is the tutor who starts cancelling in week six. A match within the same sector or the adjoining one holds far better, which is also why Golf Course Road and Gurugram families usually match inside Gurugram.

An IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai faces the sharpest version of this. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit within a workable radius of each other; Powai is its own pocket; and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar realistically need a tutor from the same side of the region. Crossing the harbour for a weekday evening lesson is not a plan, it is a hope.

Bengaluru divides by corridor. An IGCSE home tutor in Bangalore, as parents still say it, will typically hold Whitefield and Sarjapur Road together, or Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, or Hebbal and Yelahanka, or Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road. Matching across two corridors on a weekday works only for a late slot.

An IGCSE home tutor in Hyderabad usually covers Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet as one zone, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad as another. An IGCSE home tutor in Pune matches across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Kharadi, or Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi, and the two halves rarely meet on a Tuesday evening. In Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad the same rule applies: name the locality, not the city.
items: Delhi NCR: match inside your own sector or the adjoining one, not across NCR.
Mumbai: harbour crossings and Thane runs do not survive weekday evening traffic.
Bengaluru: tutors hold one corridor; a second corridor means a late slot.
Hyderabad: the western zone and the Jubilee Hills side are separate pools.
Pune: east and west of the city rarely share a weekday evening tutor.
Name your locality in the query; city-level requests produce weaker shortlists.

contentBlocks.heading: The Grade 10 timetable in India that shapes every evening slot
contentBlocks.body:
A Grade 10 week is fuller than parents remember it being, and the tutoring slot has to survive it. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools of this kind, among them Oberoi International School, Pathways World School, Oakridge International School and Good Shepherd International School, deal with the same pattern: school until late afternoon, travel home in the worst hour of city traffic, an activity or two in the week, and homework that arrives in clusters.

Work backwards from that. A student who reaches home at five is not ready to think at five fifteen. A session at six thirty or seven usually runs better than one squeezed in immediately, even though the earlier slot looks tidier on paper. Two shorter sessions a week beat one long Sunday marathon for nearly every Grade 10 student, because retention improves and because a single weekend session is the first thing a family cancels.

Mock examinations are the pivot. Schools set their own mocks and they usually land a few months before the series the student is entered for, so a February and March Cambridge candidate faces mocks much earlier in the year than a May and June candidate. Book tutoring before the mocks. The mock script is the single most useful document a home tutor can read, and arriving after it has been returned wastes a term of evidence.

Festivals and the monsoon both interrupt. Diwali empties a week almost everywhere, Pujo does the same in Kolkata, Ganesh Chaturthi reshapes Pune and Mumbai, and a heavy monsoon evening in Mumbai or Chennai can cancel a home visit outright. Agree in advance that a washed-out session moves online rather than disappearing.
items: Grade 10 students think better at six thirty than at five fifteen.
Two shorter weekly sessions beat one long weekend sitting for retention.
Book before the school mocks; the mock script is the best evidence available.
February and March candidates face mocks earlier than May and June candidates.
Agree that a monsoon evening or festival week moves online, not away.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid for IGCSE across India
contentBlocks.body:
Stated plainly: IGCSE home tutors in India see the paper, an online tutor reaches further, and hybrid gives you some of both at the cost of holding two routines. For IGCSE specifically, the balance tilts towards home more than it does for older students, because Grade 9 and Grade 10 problems are so often habits rather than knowledge.

Home tuition wins where the issue is process. Unshown working, a diagram drawn too small, a question left half-finished, handwriting that a marker would struggle with under time, a student who stops the moment they are stuck and waits to be rescued. All of those are visible from the next chair and nearly invisible on a call, because the student sends a photograph of the finished answer rather than the four minutes of hesitation before it.

Online wins on supply and on specific content. If your child takes a syllabus almost nobody near you teaches, the choice is not between a local tutor and a distant one, it is between a distant one and nobody. Online also suits short, frequent work: a twenty-minute review of a returned paper midweek is practical on a call and absurd as a home visit.

Hybrid is what a lot of families in Pune, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR end up with once traffic has had its say. A home session at the weekend for sit-down practice, a shorter online slot midweek for marking and corrections. It also keeps the arrangement alive through exam weeks and travel.

One caution about hybrid. It works when the two sessions have different jobs and fails when they are the same lesson delivered twice. Write down what belongs to each one before you start.
items: Home classes: the pen, the page and the hesitation are all visible.
Online: the answer to scarce syllabuses and to short midweek reviews.
Hybrid: weekend home session for practice, midweek online slot for corrections.
Process problems need presence; content scarcity needs reach.
Give each hybrid session a different job or the midweek one drifts.

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a tutor comes into your home?
contentBlocks.body:
Two sets of checks matter, and they do different work. IB Gram verifies profiles before shortlisting, covering identity, claimed qualifications and stated teaching experience. The second set is yours, and for a tutor entering your house it is not optional.

Start at the gate, because in most Indian apartment societies this is a real administrative step rather than a formality. Register the tutor with the society office or the guard for a standing weekly entry, so nobody is improvising at seven on a Tuesday. Agree which entrance, which days and which duration. For an independent house, the same logic applies to whoever opens the door.

Inside, the arrangement is simple and worth fixing on day one. Lessons happen in a shared room, at a table, with the door open, not in a bedroom. An adult stays at home for the session, particularly for a Grade 9 student. Payments go through the agreed channel rather than cash with no record. Communication about scheduling stays on the platform channel rather than drifting to a personal number.

Then check the teaching claims against the syllabus rather than the subject. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE Physics should be able to say which paper the student sits for practical assessment, Paper 5 or Paper 6, and what changes between Core and Extended. A tutor who says they teach Mathematics should know whether your child sits the non-calculator paper as Paper 1 or Paper 2. These are not trick questions. Anyone teaching the syllabus answers them immediately.

Finally, ask for a short written note after each session: what was covered, what was set, what to watch. Three lines is enough, and its absence after a month tells you something.
items: Verified before shortlisting: identity, claimed qualifications, stated teaching experience.
Register a standing weekly entry with the society office or guard.
Lessons at a table in a shared room, door open, an adult at home.
Ask which practical paper and which tier the student is entered for.
Expect three written lines after each session: covered, set, watch.
Keep payment and scheduling on the agreed channel, not on a personal number.

contentBlocks.heading: What a tutor beside your child sees that a screen cannot
contentBlocks.body:
Sit next to a Grade 10 student for one hour and you learn things no report contains. You see how long they sit before writing anything. You see whether they read the question twice or once. You see the eraser used four times on a diagram that was never going to fit. You see them reach for the calculator on a paper where it will not be allowed. A tutor on a video call receives a photograph of the finished attempt, which is the evidence with the diagnosis already removed.

Here is a one-hour home session that uses that presence properly.

1. Ten minutes on the work returned since last time, read in front of the student, with two questions about why a particular step was taken.

2. Fifteen minutes of teaching aimed at the specific gap that reading exposed, not at the topic in general.

3. Twenty minutes of the student working alone while the tutor watches the pen and says nothing, which is the hardest part of the job and the most useful.

4. Ten minutes marking that work together against the mark scheme, out loud, with the student holding the pen.

5. Five minutes setting the next piece and writing down the one habit to practise this week.

Notice what dominates. The student writes for more than half the hour, and the tutor teaches for a quarter of it. A session where the tutor talks for forty-five minutes feels productive to a parent walking past and teaches very little.

The silent watching in step three is where home tuition earns its cost. That is when a tutor sees the student skip the substitution line, round too early, or freeze for two minutes without saying so. And it is the exact behaviour that will happen in the examination hall.
items: Presence reveals hesitation, skipped steps and abandoned questions in real time.
A one-hour session: review, targeted teaching, silent work, joint marking, setting.
The student should be writing for more than half the hour.
Silent watching while the student works is the most valuable part.
A photograph of finished work has the diagnosis already removed.

contentBlocks.heading: How long before IGCSE home tuition shows in the marks?
contentBlocks.body:
Expect habits to change in four to six weeks and marks to move at the next set of timed papers, which is usually the school mock. That gap frustrates families, and it is worth understanding rather than fighting. A student who has spent a year not showing working does not change in two sessions, and the change shows up in the paper before it shows up in the grade, because the grade is also affected by topics not yet retaught.

What you should see early is different. By the third or fourth week, the tutor should be able to describe your child's weakness in one specific sentence, something like: strong on setting up equations, loses marks by rounding before the final step. That sentence is worth more than a cheerful progress report. If after a month the tutor can only tell you that the student is improving, press for specifics.

The honest limits deserve the same space. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a Core entry cannot reach beyond grade C however good the teaching is, so tier is a conversation with the school rather than something tutoring can solve alone. Starting in the final weeks before the series narrows what is possible to exam technique and a few high-yield topics; that is still worth doing, but call it what it is. A student who does no work between sessions will not improve regardless of who is sitting at the table.

There are also students for whom home tuition is the wrong tool entirely. If a child is coping academically but anxious, more tutoring often makes it worse. Talk to the school first.

And if the fit is wrong, say so in the first month. Asking for a different tutor is normal and is not a complaint.
items: Weeks one to three: a precise description of what is going wrong.
Weeks four to six: working shown, questions attempted before asking for help.
Marks usually move at the next mock, not before it.
A Core entry cannot exceed grade C, whatever the tutoring does.
Anxiety with adequate marks is a school conversation, not a tutoring one.
Ask for a different match inside the first month if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a home tutor for IGCSE in India: the first session
contentBlocks.body:
Get four things ready before an IGCSE home tutor in India arrives, and the first session will do a term's worth of diagnosis.

First, the paperwork. The last school report, the most recent marked script or mock paper, and the list of subjects with syllabus codes and tiers. Marked work matters more than the report, because a report tells you the grade and a script tells you the reason.

Second, the space. A table with a chair on each side, decent light, a plug point, and the television off. A dining table works perfectly well. What does not work is a sofa, a bed, or a room where a younger sibling is watching something.

Third, the equipment the student will actually use in the examination: their own pen, pencil, ruler, the calculator they are permitted, and squared or graph paper if the subject needs it. Tutoring for a written examination should be done with the tools of a written examination.

Fourth, the practical arrangements: gate entry registered, the slot agreed for the term rather than week by week, and a clear rule about what happens if a session is missed by either side.

Then send your query or book a free consultation. Tell IB Gram the board, the syllabus codes, the tier if it is settled, the grade, your locality and the two evenings you can genuinely keep. Verified profiles within reach of your address are shortlisted, a trial is arranged so the student can judge the tutor before you commit, and lessons run at home, online or hybrid. If the match is wrong, ask for another one.
items: Have the last report and, more importantly, a recent marked script ready.
Set up a table, two chairs, good light and no television.
Use the student's own examination pen, ruler and permitted calculator.
Register gate entry and fix the slot for the term, not weekly.
Send board, syllabus codes, tier, grade, locality and two workable evenings.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor see that an online tutor misses for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: IGCSE home tutors in India see the process rather than the product, and that is the whole difference. A tutor at the table watches how long the student sits before writing, whether the question was read twice, whether steps are skipped, how the diagram is drawn and where the pen stops. Online, the tutor usually receives a photograph of a completed attempt, which is evidence with the diagnosis already removed. At Grade 9 and Grade 10 most lost marks come from process, which is why presence matters more here than it does for older students.

faqs.question: How far will an IGCSE home tutor travel in a city like Mumbai or Bengaluru?
faqs.answer: Far less than families hope, and that is realistic rather than unhelpful. Tutors hold a workable radius, usually their own locality and the ones adjoining it, because evening traffic between Powai and Thane, or between Whitefield and Jayanagar, can stretch a short trip badly. A tutor who agrees to an impossible commute in week one starts cancelling by week six. Name your locality in the query so the shortlist contains people who can genuinely keep the slot.

faqs.question: What time should the home session be for a Grade 10 student?
faqs.answer: Usually six thirty or seven in the evening on a school day, rather than immediately after the student gets home. A child who reaches home at five is not ready to think at five fifteen, and the session becomes a slow start followed by a rushed finish. Two shorter weekly sessions generally beat one long weekend sitting, because retention is better and because a single weekend slot is the first thing that gets cancelled when something else comes up.

faqs.question: How does the tutor get into our apartment society?
faqs.answer: Register a standing weekly entry with the society office or the main gate, naming the day and the time, so nothing is improvised on a Tuesday evening. Most societies in Mumbai, Gurugram, Hyderabad and Bengaluru handle this routinely once asked. Agree which entrance the tutor uses and keep the slot consistent, because an irregular pattern is what causes problems at the gate. For an independent house, simply agree who is responsible for opening the door.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the practical paper?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it depends which paper your school has chosen. Cambridge sciences assess practical work through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school decides. A tutor at home can prepare technique, tables, graphs, sources of error and the written conventions those papers reward, which is most of Paper 6. What no home tutor can provide is laboratory equipment, so a student sitting Paper 5 still depends on school practical sessions.

faqs.question: My child understands the topic but keeps losing marks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always working that is not written down. A student who solves a multi-step question in their head and writes only the final answer has staked everything on the arithmetic, so a single slip costs the whole question rather than one line. Showing the rearrangement and substitution keeps credit for the method. This habit is easiest to break with someone sitting beside the student refusing to accept an unwritten step, which takes a fortnight of irritation and then holds.

faqs.question: When is online genuinely better than a tutor at home?
faqs.answer: When the syllabus is scarce locally, when the work is short and frequent, or when travel makes a reliable slot impossible. If your child takes a subject almost nobody in your city teaches, the real choice is between a distant specialist and nobody, and distance loses that argument easily. Online is also better for a twenty-minute review of a returned paper midweek, which is practical on a call and unreasonable as a home visit across the city.

faqs.question: Which board is my child on, and why does it matter for choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Check the syllabus code on their own materials: Cambridge subjects carry codes such as 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0455 and 0500, while Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. It matters because the papers and the grading differ. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G with some 9 to 1 versions under different codes, Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1, and the exam series fall in different months. A tutor strong on one board is not automatically strong on the other.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we reasonably tutor at once?
faqs.answer: Two is a sensible ceiling for most Grade 10 students, and one is often enough. Each subject adds a weekly slot, homework set by the tutor on top of school homework, and another adult with an opinion about how to study. Students who are tutored in four subjects usually end up doing less independent practice, which is the thing that actually moves marks. If it feels as though four subjects need tutoring, talk to the school about the workload first.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of rain or traffic?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before you start, because heavy monsoon evenings in Mumbai and Chennai will cancel a home visit at some point in the year. The arrangement that works best is that a session which cannot happen in person moves online that evening rather than disappearing from the week. Also agree the notice period on both sides and what happens if the student is unwell. Settling this in advance avoids a negotiation in the middle of a bad evening.

faqs.question: Should we start in Grade 9 or wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 if the problem is habits, Grade 10 if the problem is content. Grade 9 is the cheaper year to fix how a student works, because there is time and nothing is yet urgent, and the habits built there are what carry through the mocks. Waiting until Grade 10 is still perfectly workable for a specific weakness, but a student arriving in the final months has time only for exam technique and a few high-yield topics, which is a narrower job.

faqs.question: What if we do not like the tutor after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Say so at the four-week mark and ask for a different match. The signs of a poor fit are visible early: the student is silent through the session, the tutor talks for most of the hour, or nothing set is ever marked and returned. Tell IB Gram specifically what did not work, because that makes the second match better. Changing tutors is an ordinary part of the process, and it is far less costly than waiting until the mock results arrive.

h1: IGCSE Home Tuition in India Across Grade 9 and Grade 10
heroTitle: A Two-Year Home Tuition Plan Across India
heroSubtitle: Grade 9 and Grade 10 are not two similar years with one harder than the other. They do different jobs. This page sets out what a home tutor should build in the first year, how the second tightens month by month, and where past papers belong in that sequence.
introSummary: IGCSE home tuition in India is best planned as one two-year arrangement rather than a series of monthly decisions, because the examination series at the end of Grade 10 fixes every deadline behind it. Grade 9 is the build: reading load, written method, the habit of finishing a question properly, and enough diagnostic evidence to settle Core or Extended tiering before it is decided for you. Grade 10 is the tightening: syllabus completion by a sensible date, coursework handed in on the school's timetable, and past papers used seriously rather than early. Families entering the February/March series compress all of it. What follows is the plan, worked backwards from the series, with the pressure points named.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you set up IGCSE home tuition in India for two years?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE home tuition in India starts with three facts, fixed before you look at a single tutor profile. Which board the school follows, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, because the series dates differ. Which series the school enters candidates for, since the school decides that and a student cannot choose independently. And which subjects are already confirmed for Grade 10. Everything else in the plan hangs off those three answers.

Then the process itself is short. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, and shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. If the match turns out wrong, you can ask for a different one.

For a two-year arrangement, ask one extra question at the demo stage that families usually skip. Ask the tutor to describe what they intend to have finished by the end of Grade 9. A tutor who answers with a syllabus percentage has misunderstood the year. A tutor who answers with skills, and names two, has done this before.

The frequency question resolves itself once the years are separated. One session a week per subject through Grade 9 is usually enough, and often more than enough for a student who is coping. Grade 10 moves to one or two, with the second session existing to mark written work rather than to teach new content. Booking three sessions a week in Grade 9 is the most common way families spend money early and have nothing left in reserve when the year that matters arrives.
items: 1. Confirm the board, the series the school enters, and the Grade 10 subject list
2. Send a query or book a free consultation with the school calendar attached
3. Take a demo and ask what the tutor expects to finish by the end of Grade 9
4. Agree a weekly slot for Grade 9 and a review point at the end of the year
5. Move to two sessions in Grade 10, with the second used for marking written work

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 and Grade 10: what each year of home tuition must achieve
contentBlocks.body:
Grade 9 IGCSE home tuition in India has one real purpose, and it is not covering content. It is building the working habits that Grade 10 will consume: laying out a calculation so a marker can follow it, reading a long question twice, writing a definition in the form the syllabus expects, and finishing what was started. A student who arrives in Grade 10 with those habits can absorb a heavy syllabus. A student who arrives without them will spend the year being corrected on the same four things.

The second Grade 9 job is evidence. Cambridge runs Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, Core topping out at grade C and Extended reaching A*, and the tier decision should rest on a year of marked work rather than on a hopeful conversation in April. Home tuition is well placed to collect that evidence, because the tutor sees every attempt, including the ones the school never marks.

Grade 10 tightens in three stages. The first term finishes the remaining content and starts short timed work. The middle of the year is where coursework and school mocks land together, and where most plans break. The final stretch before the series is past papers, full papers under time, marked against the published markscheme rather than against the tutor's judgement.

And the honest warning about Grade 9. Some students genuinely do not need paid tuition in that year, particularly strong ones who read widely and are coping with the reading load. For them, a short diagnostic block of six or eight sessions, timed for the end of the year, is better value than a weekly slot that runs for twelve months out of habit.
items: Grade 9 builds method and reading stamina, not syllabus coverage
A year of marked work is the right basis for a Core or Extended decision
Grade 10 term one finishes content and starts short timed questions
Mid Grade 10 stacks coursework deadlines against the school mocks
Some Grade 9 students need a diagnostic block rather than a weekly slot

contentBlocks.heading: Core, Extended and the syllabus codes that shape the plan
contentBlocks.body:
Codes matter here more than subject names, because two students in the same class can sit different papers. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 all behave differently across two years, and the tutor should be planning each one separately rather than treating them as one workload.

Tiering drives the mathematics and science plan. Where a subject offers Core and Extended, Core reaches grade C at most and Extended reaches A*, so the decision closes or keeps open what Class 11 looks like. Some Cambridge syllabuses also exist in 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout, so check which grading scale your child's subject actually uses before you interpret a mock result. A B in one system is not a B in the other.

English is where families most often plan the wrong course. Cambridge First Language English 0500 has a reading paper followed by directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio instead. English as a Second Language comes as 0510 and 0511, both with reading, writing and listening, where 0511 counts speaking into the grade and 0510 reports it separately. Literature in English is 0475. Pearson Edexcel offers English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). A tutor preparing a 0500 candidate as though the portfolio route applies, when the school has entered the written paper, has wasted a term.

So the two-year plan is really six small plans running in parallel. Ask the tutor for the code, the papers and the coursework position for each subject at the start, in writing. It takes them ten minutes and it saves an argument in Grade 10.
items: Ask for the syllabus code of every subject before planning anything
Core reaches grade C at most; Extended reaches A* in Cambridge subjects
Some Cambridge syllabuses run 9 to 1 versions under different codes
English 0500, 0510, 0511 and 0475 are genuinely different courses
Edexcel equivalents include 4EA1, 4EB1 and 4ES1 for English

contentBlocks.heading: Two-year home tuition plans across India, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE home tuition in India lives or dies on whether the weekly slot survives two years, and that is a local question. In Delhi NCR, families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad find that a Grade 9 slot booked for a quiet evening in July becomes impossible in December once school activities restart. Fix the slot around the difficult term, not the easy one. IGCSE home tuition in Delhi usually settles on a weekend anchor session plus one weekday evening.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has the same problem with less road. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are close enough that a tutor can hold three or four households in one evening, which is good for reliability and bad for flexibility: you inherit their route. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar families usually do better booking a tutor who lives on their own side. IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai is often decided by which side of a bridge everybody sleeps on.

Bengaluru spreads wider. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala, Indiranagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each have local supply, but a tutor crossing the city in the evening will quietly start arriving late by October. Chennai concentrates in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Alwarpet, Velachery and Perungudi.

In Gujarat, Ahmedabad neighbourhoods such as Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway corridor have reasonable supply, and Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot thin out quickly for specific syllabus codes. IGCSE home tuition in Ahmedabad often works as a hybrid week, with a local tutor for mathematics and an online specialist for a subject nobody nearby teaches. Hyderabad and Pune sit in a similar position for the less common codes.
items: Delhi NCR: fix the weekly slot around December, not around July
Mumbai: a tutor holding several homes in one evening gives you their route
Bengaluru: cross-city evening travel erodes punctuality by the second term
Chennai: supply clusters in Adyar, OMR, Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar
Ahmedabad, Surat and Vadodara: hybrid weeks cover the rarer syllabus codes

contentBlocks.heading: School deadlines and coursework inside the two-year plan in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School appear here only as context for the calendar that families at international schools in India work around.

The series is the anchor. Cambridge runs February/March, May/June and October/November series, with February/March offered only in India, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May/June. The school decides which one your child is entered for. Once you know it, every internal deadline can be placed behind it, and the plan stops being a guess.

Coursework is the part that breaks two-year plans, because it does not announce itself. Where a subject carries a coursework component, the school sets its own submission dates, and those dates usually fall while the rest of the syllabus is still being taught. A home tutor who learns about a portfolio deadline the week before it is due will drop teaching to rescue it, and that lost fortnight comes out of revision later. Ask the school for the coursework calendar in Grade 9 and give it to the tutor then.

Mocks are the second pressure point. Schools set their own mock dates, and a mock sits in the plan as a diagnostic rather than a target. Mark the paper properly afterwards, question by question, and let the result redirect the next six weeks. A mock that produces a number and no analysis has been wasted, which is a surprisingly common outcome.
items: Cambridge series: February/March, May/June and October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
The school chooses the series; a student cannot choose it independently
Ask for the coursework submission calendar during Grade 9, not Grade 10
Treat every mock as a diagnostic and mark it question by question

contentBlocks.heading: Should the weekly session be at home, online or hybrid?
contentBlocks.body:
Over two years of IGCSE home tuition in India the answer usually changes, and planning for that beats arguing about it twice. Here is the trade-off in one place. A home tutor sits beside the student and sees the working, the crossings-out and the point where concentration goes, which matters most in Grade 9 when habits are being formed. Online gives access to a tutor who knows a specific syllabus code, and it protects the slot from traffic and weather, which matters most in Grade 10 when losing a week is expensive. A hybrid week runs both: home classes for the teaching, an online session for marked practice and doubt-solving.

The common two-year shape looks like this. Grade 9 mostly at home, because the work being done is behavioural. Grade 10 increasingly hybrid, then heavily online in the weeks before the series, when nobody wants to spend an evening hour in a car. Families in Bengaluru and Delhi NCR arrive at that pattern by themselves, usually around the first mock.

There are exceptions in both directions. A student who works well alone can sit entirely online from Grade 9 and be fine. A student who needs somebody in the room to start at all should stay with home tuition right through the series, even at the cost of a less specialised tutor.

What does not work is switching format mid-subject with a new person each time. Keep the same tutor and change the medium. Continuity across two years is the single largest advantage a home arrangement has over a batch, and swapping tutors every term throws it away for nothing.
items: Grade 9 favours home classes, because the work is behavioural
Grade 10 favours hybrid, then online in the weeks before the series
Online reaches a tutor who knows your child's exact syllabus code
A student who cannot start alone should keep home tuition throughout
Change the medium across two years, but keep the same tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Checking an IGCSE tutor before you commit to two years
contentBlocks.body:
A two-year arrangement deserves more checking than a term does, because the cost of discovering a problem in Grade 10 is a lost year of preparation rather than a wasted month. IB Gram checks identity and the qualifications listed on a profile before it goes live, and shortlists only profiles that have been through that. Your own checking then has a narrower job: is this the right person for these subjects, across two years, for this child.

Three questions do most of the work. Which syllabus code have you taught most recently, and in which series? What does your Grade 9 plan look like, in skills rather than chapters? And how do you mark written work, with what turnaround? A tutor who cannot answer the first without hedging has probably taught a general mathematics course rather than 0580, and there is a real difference in what the papers ask for.

Then watch the demo for one specific thing. Does the tutor ask to see the student's own written work before proposing anything? Someone who arrives with a ready-made two-year plan has a plan for a category of student, not for yours.

The practical checks matter for home visits and are easy to forget. Agree the arrival time and what happens when the tutor is delayed. Tell your society or building office that a tutor will be a regular visitor so that gate entry does not become a weekly negotiation. Decide where the session happens: a table, decent light, and a door that can stay open. And agree at the start how a missed session is made up, because across two years there will be several.
items: Ask which syllabus code they taught most recently and in which series
Ask for the Grade 9 plan in skills rather than in chapters covered
Watch whether the tutor asks to see the student's written work first
Register a regular visitor with the society office to smooth gate entry
Agree the make-up rule for missed sessions before the first one happens

contentBlocks.heading: When should past papers start, and why does starting earlier backfire?
contentBlocks.body:
Past papers should start when the student can attempt most of a paper without looking anything up, which for most subjects means the middle of Grade 10 rather than the beginning of it. Before that point a past paper is not practice. It is a demonstration of what has not been taught yet, and it teaches the student that the paper is frightening.

The damage is specific and worth understanding. A student who meets full papers too early learns to skip, because skipping is the only way to survive a paper covering content from a term that has not happened. That habit is very hard to remove later, and it shows up in the series as blank space on questions the student could actually have answered. The second harm is to the supply of papers themselves. There are only so many recent papers, and using them all in October leaves nothing genuine for February.

So sequence it. Topic questions from past papers while a topic is fresh, from Grade 9 onwards, which is entirely different from doing whole papers. Then short sections under time once a subject is roughly two thirds covered. Then whole papers, in order, once the syllabus is finished, marked against the published markscheme with the marks written on. Then the most recent papers held back for the final six weeks.

Marking is where most of the value sits, not in the attempt. A paper the student marks themselves against the markscheme, with the tutor arguing about three disputed marks afterwards, teaches more than a paper handed over and returned with a score. That argument is the lesson. It is also the moment a student stops treating the markscheme as arbitrary and starts writing for it, which is the single change that moves grades in the last months.
items: Topic questions from Grade 9 onwards, as each topic is finished
Timed sections once a subject is roughly two thirds covered
Whole papers only after the syllabus is complete
The most recent papers held back for the final six weeks
Let the student mark against the markscheme and argue three disputed marks

contentBlocks.heading: What real progress looks like across two years in India
contentBlocks.body:
In Grade 9 the honest measure is not marks. It is whether the student's written work has started to look like somebody else could follow it, and whether they finish questions instead of abandoning them halfway. Expect that within six to eight weeks of starting. If the notebook still shows the same four-line answers at the end of the first term, the arrangement is not working, whatever the tutor reports.

In Grade 10 you can be more demanding. By the first mock you should see the pattern of lost marks change: fewer method errors, fewer questions missed for time, fewer answers that address a different command word than the one printed. Grades themselves move unevenly because each mock tests more of the syllabus than the last one did, so a flat score can hide real improvement. Read the question-by-question breakdown rather than the total.

The limits deserve stating. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and two years of tuition does not make a Core-tier candidate into an A* candidate by arithmetic. Starting in the last two months before the series limits the work to technique and triage. And a student who does nothing between sessions will not improve at any frequency, which is a conversation to have with the student rather than a problem to solve with more hours.

There is also a risk peculiar to long arrangements. Comfort. After eighteen months a tutor and student can settle into a pleasant routine where the hard topics never come up because both parties find them unpleasant. Ask once a term which topic the student is still avoiding. If nobody can name one, somebody is not looking.
items: Grade 9: work that another person can follow, and questions finished
Grade 10: the pattern of lost marks changes before the totals do
Read the mock breakdown by question rather than the overall score
Ask each term which topic the student is still avoiding
No tutor can guarantee a grade across two years or across two months

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IGCSE home tuition in India from Grade 9
contentBlocks.body:
The best moment to begin IGCSE home tuition in India is early in Grade 9, when there is room to build slowly, and the second best is immediately, whenever you are reading this. Before sending a query, collect four things: the board and series the school uses, the subject list with syllabus codes if you have them, the most recent marked work in the weakest subject, and the school calendar including any published coursework dates.

For a February/March entry, compress everything by roughly a term and say so in the first conversation. That series exists specifically for India and lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Class 11 admissions and for entry to the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels in the same academic year. It also means the syllabus has to be finished earlier, mocks land sooner, and the past-paper stretch is shorter. A plan built for May/June and then shifted in January is not a plan.

The first session should produce something you can hold: a rough term map, a named first target, and one piece of written work set. If it produces only a friendly conversation, ask for the map before the second session.

After that, review at three points rather than continuously. End of Grade 9, after the first Grade 10 mock, and eight weeks before the series. At each review ask the same two questions: what has actually changed in the written work, and what is the plan for the next stretch. Three good reviews across two years will do more than worrying about it every fortnight.
items: Collect the board, series, syllabus codes and the school calendar first
Say at the outset if the entry is the February/March series
Expect a term map and one piece of set work from the first session
Review at three points: end of Grade 9, first mock, and eight weeks out
Ask at each review what has changed in the written work itself

faqs.question: When should IGCSE home tuition start, Grade 9 or Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 9, if the student has weak written method or is struggling with the reading load, and Grade 10 if they are coping comfortably. Starting in Grade 9 buys time to build habits slowly, which is the cheapest way to improve a Grade 10 result. Starting in Grade 10 works too, but the same tutor then has to teach content and repair method simultaneously, and something usually gets squeezed out of the plan.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a two-year plan need?
faqs.answer: One session per subject per week through Grade 9, and one or two in Grade 10. The second Grade 10 session should exist to mark written work rather than to teach new content, which is a distinction worth stating to the tutor explicitly. Three sessions a week in Grade 9 is the most common overspend. It exhausts the student, exhausts the budget, and leaves nothing in reserve for the year that actually decides the grades.

faqs.question: When should my daughter start doing full past papers?
faqs.answer: Once the syllabus for that subject is finished, which for most subjects means the middle of Grade 10 or later. Topic questions from past papers can begin in Grade 9 as each topic is completed, and that is a different exercise. Doing whole papers too early teaches skipping, because half the content has not been taught. It also burns through recent papers that would have been far more useful in the final weeks.

faqs.question: Our school enters students for the February/March series. How does the plan change?
faqs.answer: Everything moves roughly a term earlier, and the past-paper stretch gets shorter. That series exists specifically for India so that Grade 10 results arrive in time for Class 11 admissions and for entry to the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels in the same year. Tell the tutor at the first conversation rather than in December. The syllabus has to be complete sooner, mocks land sooner, and coursework deadlines compress accordingly.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with coursework without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, by discussing the student's own draft against the published criteria and writing none of it. That is the boundary, and a good tutor states it before you ask. What they can do is question a weak plan, point at a criterion the draft ignores, and insist on a redraft. What they cannot do is supply sentences, choose the content, or work on the file themselves. If a tutor offers more than that, treat it as a warning.

faqs.question: The tutor travels from Andheri and is late every week during the monsoon. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Move that session online for the monsoon months and keep the tutor. This is the standard fix across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, and it works equally well in Bengaluru and Kolkata. Losing twenty minutes of a session every week for three months is a real cost, and changing a competent tutor over it is a bigger one. Agree the switch in advance with a date, rather than deciding it in the rain each week.

faqs.question: Should the same tutor take all the subjects?
faqs.answer: Rarely. One tutor can usually handle the sciences together, or mathematics alongside one science, but the English syllabuses are a different skill and are better handled separately. Spreading six subjects across one person produces shallow preparation in all of them. Two tutors, each covering their real strengths, is the usual sensible arrangement, with one of them treated as the person who holds the overall calendar.

faqs.question: What if the tier is wrong and we only find out in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the school immediately, because the school makes the entry decision and there are deadlines attached. Bring evidence rather than opinion: marked scripts across several months, mock papers, and a written note from the tutor about which topics are secure. This is precisely why a two-year plan collects evidence in Grade 9. A conversation backed by a folder of marked work goes very differently from one backed by a feeling.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor at all if the school is good and my son is doing well?
faqs.answer: Probably not for a full weekly year, and there is no honest reason to pretend otherwise. A student coping well in Grade 9 often benefits more from a short diagnostic block of six or eight sessions late in the year, aimed at identifying weak spots before Grade 10 begins. Reserve the weekly arrangement for a subject where marked work shows a real pattern of lost marks rather than an occasional bad test.

faqs.question: We live in Gandhinagar and cannot find a tutor for one subject. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Run a hybrid week: a local tutor at home for the subjects that are available nearby, and an online specialist for the one that is not. This pattern is common across Gujarat, including Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, and in smaller cities generally. It keeps the benefits of somebody in the room for most of the load while reaching a tutor who actually knows the syllabus code you need for the rest.

faqs.question: How do we make up sessions missed during festivals and school trips?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before the first session, because across two years you will lose several weeks to festivals, trips, illness and examinations. The workable arrangement is a fixed number of make-up sessions carried forward each term, with anything unused expiring, and notice periods on both sides. Vague goodwill breaks down by the second year. A written rule, agreed in the first week, prevents an awkward conversation at exactly the wrong moment.

comparison.heading: Which format holds a two-year IGCSE plan together across India?
comparison.intro: Over two years the question is not which format teaches better on a given Tuesday, but which one survives a school calendar. One-to-one at home holds a reluctant student to the work. One-to-one online holds the slot when roads and weather do not cooperate. A small group adds discussion and costs less per student. A large batch is the cheapest structure available.
