h1: IGCSE Private Tutors in India for Tiering and Diagnosis
heroTitle: One-to-One IGCSE Tutoring in India for Tier Decisions
heroSubtitle: Core or Extended. Foundation or Higher. These are the choices that quietly set a ceiling on a Grade 10 result, and they are almost always made on impressions rather than on marked evidence. One-to-one teaching is the only format that can gather that evidence properly.
introSummary: IGCSE private tutors in India earn their fee on one thing above all others: settling a tier decision from real marked evidence, usually in home tuition sessions where the tutor can read the student's own script line by line. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A splits into Foundation and Higher. Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*, so the entry decision sets a ceiling before the student writes a word in the exam hall. Schools generally make the call, families often disagree with it, and both sides usually argue from a general sense of how the child is doing. This page is about replacing that with paper evidence, and about knowing when the decision can still be changed.

contentBlocks.heading: Matching an IGCSE Private Tutor in India to a Tier Decision
contentBlocks.body:
Most families looking for IGCSE private tutors in India start with a subject and a grade, and most want home tuition twice a week. The useful enquiry arrives as a question: should this student sit Extended in Mathematics, and what would tell us? That framing changes the shortlist, because the tutor you need is one who works from mark schemes rather than from textbooks.

At the free consultation we ask which board and syllabus the school actually enters, which is more slippery than parents expect. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run different series and grade differently, some Cambridge syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under separate codes, and the school decides the entry rather than the family. Then we ask which grade the student is in, whether any past-paper work has been marked, what the school has said about tier, and when the next internal assessment point falls. Locality and free evenings come next, because a Grade 10 student in Dwarka or Kondapur has a narrower week than their parents believe.

Shortlisting then filters on something specific: has the tutor taught this syllabus code at this tier, and can they say what changes between the tiers in the papers themselves. Profiles are verified before they go live. Availability is always subject to level, locality and schedule, and specialists in the less common subjects book out earliest in the year.

Ask for the demo to be built around a marked script rather than a topic. Give the tutor a past-paper attempt the student has already made, and ask them to talk through where the marks stopped and what that implies about tier. You will learn more in that hour than in a term of general sessions. If the tutor is not right, ask for a different match, and describe what was missing so the next shortlist is sharper.
items: Ask which board, syllabus code and tier the school actually enters
Bring a marked past-paper attempt rather than a report card comment
Filter tutors on syllabus code and tier taught, not subject alone
Use the trial hour on that script, not on a topic introduction
Confirm the slot, since availability depends on level and locality
Say what was missing if you ask for a different match

contentBlocks.heading: Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher: What Each Ceiling Means
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the arithmetic of the decision, because it is blunter than most families realise. In many Cambridge IGCSE subjects the syllabus is tiered: Core candidates sit one pair of papers and can reach grade C at best, while Extended candidates sit a harder pair and can reach A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, works on the same principle with Foundation and Higher tiers, two calculator papers per tier, and grades reported on the 9 to 1 scale. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses exist in 9 to 1 versions under different codes.

In Cambridge Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. That is not a small step up in difficulty. The Extended papers assume algebraic fluency that Core does not, and a student pushed into them without it will lose marks across every topic rather than in one place.

The Cambridge sciences examined from 2023 follow a parallel structure. Multiple choice is Paper 1 at Core or Paper 2 at Extended, theory is Paper 3 at Core or Paper 4 at Extended, and the practical element is assessed through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, with the school choosing which. The weighting is multiple choice 30 per cent, theory 50 per cent and practical 20 per cent. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

So the honest question is never which tier sounds better. It is whether the student can hold the harder paper for its full length without collapsing, and what the Core ceiling would cost them in Class 11 admission or in moving on to the Diploma Programme or A Levels.
items: Cambridge Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*
0580 Core: Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 calculator, from 2025
0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 calculator
Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is Foundation or Higher, two calculator papers each
Cambridge sciences: multiple choice 30 per cent, theory 50, practical 20
Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with practical inside the papers

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE Subjects Turn on the Tier You Enter?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is where the decision bites hardest and where one-to-one evidence gathering is most valuable. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 the difference between the tiers shows up first in algebra and in the non-calculator paper, so a tutor gathering evidence will set Paper 2 style questions under timed conditions rather than asking the student how confident they feel. The sciences, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, split along explanation quality: Extended theory papers reward answers that carry a mechanism, while Core rewards correct recall. A student who knows the content and cannot explain it is often placed at Core when the real fix is writing practice.

Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 behave differently again, since the pressure there is writing volume and structure under time rather than tier. If your child is strong in these and weak in the tiered subjects, you are looking at a subject-specific problem rather than a general one, and you should buy tuition accordingly.

Additional Mathematics 0606 is a separate decision entirely and deserves its own conversation. It has no tiers, two written papers with a calculator allowed, and grades A* to E. The content is substantial: functions, quadratic functions, factors of polynomials, equations, inequalities and graphs, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation and integration. It is usually taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or A Level Mathematics. Pearson Edexcel's nearest equivalent is International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics, 4PM1.

Do not treat 0606 as proof of ambition. A student struggling to hold 0580 Extended should not be carrying 0606 as well, and dropping it is a reasonable decision that costs far less than a poor grade in both.
items: 0580 tier evidence comes from timed Paper 2 style algebra, not from confidence
0625, 0620 and 0610 Extended theory papers reward mechanism, not recall
0455 and 0500 pressure is writing volume and structure under time
0606 has no tiers, two calculator papers, and is graded A* to E
0606 suits students heading for Mathematics AA HL or A Level Mathematics
Edexcel's nearest equivalent to 0606 is Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1

contentBlocks.heading: One-to-One IGCSE Supply Across India, Region by Region
contentBlocks.body:
The tier question is national; the supply of IGCSE private tutors in India who can answer it is not, and home classes depend on that supply living close enough to travel. In Delhi NCR the deepest pools sit in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri, with strong availability in Gurugram along Golf Course Road and in Noida including Sector 128. Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad have fewer syllabus specialists, and a private IGCSE tutor in Delhi who lives on the wrong side of the city will not hold a twice-weekly evening slot through a full Grade 10 year.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region concentrates around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, with Powai served unevenly and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar operating as their own markets. An IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai will usually quote a shorter travel radius than a parent hopes for, and the honest reply is to book a tutor inside your cluster or to run the subject online.

Bengaluru splits between Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City in the east and south, and Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road elsewhere. Hyderabad is unusually convenient for this, with Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District, Kokapet, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad all within a workable band for an IGCSE private tutor in Hyderabad.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR is the real constraint. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula share a small pool; Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have local mathematics and science teachers but few who have taught a named Cambridge code at Extended. Families there, and families in Chennai, Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad looking for a specific syllabus, should expect to run at least one subject online rather than settle for a generalist on the strength of proximity.
items: South Delhi, Gurugram and Noida hold the deepest NCR supply for named codes
Mumbai tutors quote short travel radii; book inside your own cluster
Hyderabad's western corridor and Secunderabad sit within one workable band
Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula share one small pool of syllabus specialists
In Jaipur, Lucknow or Kanpur, expect to run at least one subject online
Proximity is a poor reason to accept a tutor who has not taught the code

contentBlocks.heading: When Schools in India Fix the Tier, and When They Revisit It
contentBlocks.body:
Entry decisions belong to the school. A student cannot choose a series or a tier independently, and the school submits the entry, so every conversation a family has about tier is ultimately a conversation with the school. Knowing that changes how you should prepare for it.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, Greenwood High International School, Chirec International School and Mercedes-Benz International School describe the same sequence of conversations wherever they are.

The timing follows the series. Cambridge series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and then May and June. Schools usually form a provisional view on tier during Grade 9 or early Grade 10 and confirm it before the entry deadline for their chosen series, which sits months ahead of the papers themselves. The practical implication is simple: evidence gathered in the first half of Grade 10 can still change an entry, and evidence gathered after the deadline cannot.

So ask the subject teacher three things early, in writing if possible. What tier are you currently planning to enter this student for? What would need to be true for that to change? And when is your deadline for deciding? A school that answers those clearly is easy to work with. A school that will not commit to a date is worth escalating to the coordinator, politely, in Grade 9 rather than in the term before the entry closes.
items: The school submits the entry; a student cannot choose a tier independently
Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June
Entries are confirmed months before the papers, so evidence must arrive early
Ask the teacher for the tier, the conditions to change it, and the decision date

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid for One-to-One IGCSE Work?
contentBlocks.body:
For the diagnostic stage, home tuition has a specific advantage that is easy to explain. Tier evidence lives in handwritten working: the line the student skipped, the rearrangement done in their head, the diagram half drawn and abandoned. A tutor sitting beside a Grade 10 student sees all of that as it happens, including the twenty seconds of hesitation that never shows up on a marked script. Home classes also let the tutor look at the folder, the notes and the state of the desk, which tell their own story about whether the problem is content or organisation.

Online is equal, and sometimes better, once the evidence is in and the work turns to practice. Marking a past paper on screen, reading a mark scheme line by line, timing a section under supervision on camera: these travel perfectly well. Online also solves the scarcity problem, and for a family in Ludhiana or Dehradun needing a specific syllabus code, an online specialist is not a compromise but the only real option.

The honest weakness of online is exactly the thing tier decisions depend on. Unless the tutor insists on a second camera on the page, a document camera or a graphics tablet, the student's working is invisible and the tutor is judging finished answers. Ask about this before the trial, not after.

Hybrid is what most families end up running, and it is a sensible design rather than a fallback. Home sessions during the diagnostic weeks and before mocks, online sessions for the routine practice in between. One subject at home and another online is common too, particularly when Mathematics needs the paper and Economics does not.
items: Home tuition shows handwritten working, hesitation and the state of the folder
Online suits marking, mark-scheme reading and timed practice equally well
Without a page camera or tablet, an online tutor judges finished answers only
Scarce syllabus codes outside the metros are realistically an online option
Hybrid: home for diagnosis and mock preparation, online for routine practice

contentBlocks.heading: Testing a Tutor's Syllabus Knowledge Before You Book
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor who has taught Mathematics for years has not necessarily taught 0580, and the gap shows only under specific questioning. Three questions separate the two, and you can ask all of them in the first ten minutes.

Which papers does a Core candidate sit in this syllabus, and which does an Extended candidate sit? Which of them is non-calculator? What would you look for in a script before recommending Extended? A tutor who has genuinely worked the syllabus answers without hesitation and usually adds detail you did not ask for. A tutor who redirects to their experience or their results is answering a different question.

Platform verification covers a different layer. Profiles are checked before they go live for identity, for the qualifications claimed, and for the subjects and levels the tutor states they teach. That removes the obvious risks, but no verification process can tell you whether this person reads mark schemes well, and that is the skill the tier decision rests on.

Then check the ordinary operational things, because they decide whether an arrangement survives a year. Whether the same tutor teaches every session or a colleague substitutes. What happens to a session missed because of school mocks or a wedding. Whether you will see written feedback and how often. Whether the tutor is willing to talk to the school's subject teacher if you ask, which is more useful than families realise during a tier disagreement. And confirm the slot is genuinely held for the term rather than reallocated at the start of the examination season.
items: Ask which papers each tier sits and which paper is non-calculator
Ask what they would look for in a script before recommending Extended
Verification covers identity, claimed qualifications, and subjects and levels taught
Check whether the same tutor teaches every session or a colleague substitutes
Agree how missed sessions and mock weeks are handled before the term starts
A tutor willing to speak to the subject teacher helps during a disagreement

contentBlocks.heading: What Evidence Actually Decides Core or Extended?
contentBlocks.body:
Impressions decide most tier calls in practice, and impressions are unreliable in both directions. This is the one job IGCSE private tutors in India are genuinely better placed to do than anybody else, because a home tutor watching a student write is looking at the raw material of the decision. A confident student who talks well in class gets pushed up. A quiet student who writes carefully gets held down. Neither assessment looked at a script under timed conditions, which is the only condition the examination will apply.

Real evidence has four parts. First, performance on tier-appropriate past-paper questions under time, not on classwork. Second, the pattern of marks lost: a student losing method marks across many topics has a fluency problem that Extended will punish everywhere, while a student losing marks in two identifiable topics has something teachable. Third, stamina, which is measured by comparing the first third of a paper with the last third. Fourth, the trajectory across Grade 9, since a student improving steadily is a different case from one who plateaued a year ago.

Gathering this is exactly what one-to-one is for, and it is why the first three sessions should be structured rather than general. A batch cannot do it. A recorded course cannot do it. Even a very good school teacher may not have time to do it for thirty students individually.

Who decides in the end? The school enters the candidate, so the school decides. But a family arriving with a marked script, a timed attempt and a written note of which topics lost marks is a very different conversation from a family expressing disappointment. If the school and the family still disagree, ask what evidence would change the school's view, produce that evidence, and give it to them early enough to matter. And take the disagreement seriously in both directions: a school holding a student at Core is sometimes right, and a grade C achieved calmly is a better outcome than a failed attempt at A*.
items: 1. Session one: a timed tier-appropriate past-paper section, attempted cold.
2. Session two: mark it together against the mark scheme, line by line.
3. Session three: retest two weak topics and compare the first and last thirds.
4. Write one page: topics lost, method marks lost, stamina, Grade 9 trajectory.
5. Take that page to the subject teacher before the entry deadline.
6. Ask what further evidence would change the school's current view.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tier Decision Gets Revisited in India Without Panic
contentBlocks.body:
A tier decision is provisional until the school submits the entry, and that is the fact families most often miss when they book IGCSE private tutors in India in a rush. There is a window, it is usually in the first half of Grade 10, and inside it a well-evidenced case can move a student either way. Outside it, the conversation changes from entry to preparation, and pretending otherwise wastes a term.

Judge tuition on evidence rather than on comfort. Six weeks in, you should see whether the pattern of lost marks has changed on a comparable paper, not whether the student feels better about the subject. Keep the first marked attempt. Ask for a second timed attempt at the same standard around week six and compare them side by side. If the same method marks are going in the same places, the plan needs changing, not extending.

Be equally willing to move down. A student who is drowning in Extended, losing marks everywhere and sleeping badly, is not being served by ambition. Moving to Core, or dropping Additional Mathematics 0606 while keeping 0580 Extended, is a legitimate decision that protects the rest of the subjects. Families rarely regret it; they regret leaving it until after the entry closed.

The honest limits are worth stating plainly. No tutor can guarantee a grade or a tier outcome, six weeks before an entry deadline is not enough time to rebuild two years of algebra, and a student who does not attempt work between sessions will not improve at any frequency. What one-to-one home tuition can reliably do is produce clear evidence, quickly, about what is actually wrong. That is worth buying even if the answer turns out to be that no tutoring is needed.
items: The decision is provisional until the school submits the entry
Compare two timed attempts at the same standard six weeks apart
If the same method marks fall in the same places, change the plan
Moving down a tier, or dropping 0606, is a legitimate protective decision
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and six weeks cannot rebuild two years

contentBlocks.heading: Starting Private Home Tuition in India for Grades 9 and 10
contentBlocks.body:
Bring four things to the first conversation and the diagnosis starts immediately. The syllabus code the school enters, taken from the school rather than guessed. One marked past-paper attempt or a returned test with the marks visible. What the subject teacher has said about tier, in their words. And two evenings that are genuinely free once school, travel and any existing classes are accounted for.

Book one subject to begin with. If two subjects look weak, there is a good chance one cause sits underneath both, and Mathematics fluency underlies more science marks than most families expect. Running the diagnosis in one subject first also keeps the student's week intact, which matters in Grade 10 more than in any year before it.

The first session should be an assessment, not a lesson. A timed section attempted cold, marked together afterwards, with the tutor naming where the marks stopped and why. Ask for a short written note after it: topics lost, method marks lost, and a view on tier with the reasoning attached. That note is what you take to the school.

After that the shape is ordinary. Sessions run at home, online or hybrid depending on your city and the subject. A demo or trial can be arranged before you commit, availability depends on level, locality and schedule, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Review properly at six weeks against a comparable paper, and be willing to conclude that the tier was right all along and the tuition can stop.
items: Bring the syllabus code from the school, not from a search result
Bring one marked attempt with the marks and comments still visible
Start with one subject; Mathematics fluency underlies many science marks
Ask for a written note on tier with the reasoning attached
Sessions run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability
Review at six weeks against a comparable paper, then decide to continue or stop

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: The ceiling and the papers. In many Cambridge IGCSE subjects, Core candidates sit one pair of papers and can reach grade C at best, while Extended candidates sit harder papers and can reach A*. In Mathematics 0580 from the 2025 examinations, Core means Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, and Extended means Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiers instead, with two calculator papers per tier and grades reported on the 9 to 1 scale.

faqs.question: Who actually decides which tier my child sits?
faqs.answer: The school does, because the school submits the entry and a student cannot choose a series or tier independently. That does not make the family powerless. A parent who arrives with a timed past-paper attempt, a marked script and a written note of which topics and method marks were lost is having a different conversation from one expressing disappointment. Ask the subject teacher what evidence would change their view, produce it before the entry deadline, and accept that the school is sometimes right to hold a student at Core.

faqs.question: When is it too late to change the tier?
faqs.answer: Once the school has submitted the entry for its chosen series, the tier is set for that series. Cambridge series run in February and March, in May and June, and in October and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June, with entry deadlines months ahead of the papers. Practically, evidence gathered in the first half of Grade 10 can still move an entry. After the deadline the useful conversation shifts from which tier to how to prepare for the one entered.

faqs.question: How do private tutors gather evidence for a tier decision?
faqs.answer: By setting tier-appropriate past-paper questions under timed conditions and then marking them with the student against the mark scheme. Four things come out of that: which topics lose marks, whether method marks are falling across many topics or a few, whether performance drops between the first third and the last third of a paper, and how the pattern compares with Grade 9. Classwork does not show any of this, because classwork is untimed and often supported. Ask for the findings in writing so they can be taken to the school.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student is heading and how secure 0580 Extended already is. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 has no tiers, two written papers with a calculator allowed, and grades A* to E, covering functions, polynomials, logarithmic and exponential functions, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, series, vectors, differentiation and integration. It suits students heading for IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or A Level Mathematics. A student already struggling with 0580 Extended should usually not carry it as well.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor reach us on weekday evenings in Gurugram or Thane?
faqs.answer: Inside a cluster, usually yes; across a city, rarely for long. A tutor living along Golf Course Road will hold a Gurugram slot twice a week, and one crossing from South Delhi at peak hour generally will not sustain it past a month. The same applies between Thane and the western suburbs of Mumbai. Ask where the tutor starts their evening from rather than where they live, and treat a long commute as the main risk to the arrangement rather than as the tutor's problem.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during private tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: Someone responsible should be at home, and it does not have to be in the room. For a Grade 9 or 10 student, sitting in tends to make them quieter and less willing to admit confusion, which is the opposite of what a diagnostic session needs. Stay within earshot in the next room, keep the lesson in a shared space rather than a bedroom, and ask for a two-minute summary at the door. Agree in advance who is told about a missed or rescheduled session.

faqs.question: What if the school says Core and we think Extended?
faqs.answer: Treat it as an evidence problem rather than a dispute. Ask the subject teacher precisely what makes them recommend Core, and what performance would change that. Then produce it: a timed Extended-style section attempted cold, marked against the scheme, with the pattern of lost marks written up. Take it in early, well before the entry deadline, and ask for a review rather than a reversal. If the evidence supports the school, accept it, because a settled grade C is a better outcome for a student than a collapsed attempt at Extended.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE private tutor in Bangalore or Hyderabad know the specific syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Some do and many do not, and the only way to find out is to ask directly. Bengaluru and Hyderabad both have reasonable pools, concentrated around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar and Koramangala in one city and Gachibowli, Madhapur, Kondapur and Jubilee Hills in the other. Ask which papers each tier sits, which is non-calculator, and how the practical component is assessed in the sciences. A tutor who has taught the code answers immediately. Proximity alone is a poor reason to book anybody.

faqs.question: How long should the diagnosis take before we commit to a term?
faqs.answer: Three sessions is usually enough to know what you are dealing with, and six weeks is the right point to judge whether the teaching is working. Sessions one to three should produce a timed attempt, a joint marking session and a retest of two weak topics. At six weeks, set a second comparable timed paper and lay the two side by side. If the same method marks are lost in the same places, change the plan or the tutor rather than adding hours to an approach that has not moved anything.

faqs.question: Is online one-to-one as good as a tutor in the room for this?
faqs.answer: For practice and mark-scheme work, yes; for the initial diagnosis, only with the right setup. Tier evidence lives in handwritten working, so the tutor must see the page as the student writes on it, through a second camera, a document camera or a graphics tablet. Ask how the trial will make the working visible before you book. Where a syllabus code has no local specialist, as in Chandigarh, Jaipur or Dehradun, an online tutor who insists on seeing the page beats a nearby generalist who has never taught it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Mathematics and a science together?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it can be an efficient choice in Grade 10. Algebraic fluency underlies a large share of the marks lost in Physics 0625 and in the quantitative parts of Chemistry 0620, so a tutor who sees both subjects spots that the science problem is a mathematics problem. The limit is depth: explanation-heavy Biology 0610 work or First Language English 0500 usually needs a different specialist. Book one subject first, confirm the diagnosis, then extend only if the same weakness is showing in both.

Stay within earshot in the next room, keep the lesson in a shared space rather than a bedroom, and ask for a two-minute summary at the door. Agree in advance who is told about a missed or rescheduled session.

mainEntity.name: What if the school says Core and we think Extended?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat it as an evidence problem rather than a dispute. Ask the subject teacher precisely what makes them recommend Core, and what performance would change that. Then produce it: a timed Extended-style section attempted cold, marked against the scheme, with the pattern of lost marks written up. Take it in early, well before the entry deadline, and ask for a review rather than a reversal. If the evidence supports the school, accept it, because a settled grade C is a better outcome for a student than a collapsed attempt at Extended.

mainEntity.name: Does an IGCSE private tutor in Bangalore or Hyderabad know the specific syllabus code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some do and many do not, and the only way to find out is to ask directly. Bengaluru and Hyderabad both have reasonable pools, concentrated around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar and Koramangala in one city and Gachibowli, Madhapur, Kondapur and Jubilee Hills in the other. Ask which papers each tier sits, which is non-calculator, and how the practical component is assessed in the sciences. A tutor who has taught the code answers immediately. Proximity alone is a poor reason to book anybody.

mainEntity.name: How long should the diagnosis take before we commit to a term?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three sessions is usually enough to know what you are dealing with, and six weeks is the right point to judge whether the teaching is working. Sessions one to three should produce a timed attempt, a joint marking session and a retest of two weak topics. At six weeks, set a second comparable timed paper and lay the two side by side. If the same method marks are lost in the same places, change the plan or the tutor rather than adding hours to an approach that has not moved anything.

mainEntity.name: Is online one-to-one as good as a tutor in the room for this?

acceptedAnswer.text: For practice and mark-scheme work, yes; for the initial diagnosis, only with the right setup. Tier evidence lives in handwritten working, so the tutor must see the page as the student writes on it, through a second camera, a document camera or a graphics tablet. Ask how the trial will make the working visible before you book. Where a syllabus code has no local specialist, as in Chandigarh, Jaipur or Dehradun, an online tutor who insists on seeing the page beats a nearby generalist who has never taught it.

mainEntity.name: Can one tutor cover Mathematics and a science together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, and it can be an efficient choice in Grade 10. Algebraic fluency underlies a large share of the marks lost in Physics 0625 and in the quantitative parts of Chemistry 0620, so a tutor who sees both subjects spots that the science problem is a mathematics problem. The limit is depth: explanation-heavy Biology 0610 work or First Language English 0500 usually needs a different specialist. Book one subject first, confirm the diagnosis, then extend only if the same weakness is showing in both.

We will ask about board, subject, grade, school calendar, locality and schedule, then shortlist verified tutors who have taught that code. A demo can be arranged before you commit, sessions run at home, online or hybrid, and a different match is always available.

h1: IGCSE Private Tuition in India: Holding a Plan for Two Years
heroTitle: A Two-Year IGCSE Tuition Plan for India
heroSubtitle: Grade 9 and Grade 10 are one course, not two school years, and tuition bought a term at a time rarely behaves that way. This page covers how many subjects a student can sustain, what a checkpoint review at the end of each term measures, what to do with the long breaks, and how to change tutor without losing ground.
introSummary: IGCSE private tuition in India is best agreed as a two-year arrangement rather than bought term by term, and for most families it runs as home tuition on fixed weeknights. The course sits across Grades 9 and 10 and ends in an exam series the school chooses, so a plan that ignores the second year is a plan that will be rewritten in a panic. Three questions decide everything: how many subjects the student can carry, what each term is supposed to prove, and what happens during the long breaks. This page answers all three, sets out a written agreement worth signing, and gives a handover you can hold a departing tutor to.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram set up a two-year IGCSE arrangement in India?
contentBlocks.body:
By starting from the exam series and working backwards, because that date sets everything else. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks which grade the student is in, which syllabuses and tiers the school has entered him for, which series the school uses, where you live and which evenings are genuinely free. Only then does a shortlist appear.

That sequence is not bureaucracy. A Grade 9 student whose school enters candidates in the February/March series has a shorter runway than the calendar suggests, and a tutor planning a leisurely first year will run out of time in a way nobody notices until the mocks. A Grade 10 student joining in October has a different problem entirely, and needs an arrangement built around triage rather than coverage.

Shortlisting filters on the syllabus code first. A tutor who teaches Mathematics is not automatically a tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier, and the difference shows up in the third month, not the first. IB Gram puts forward tutors whose profiles are verified and who teach the named syllabus at the level required, subject to availability in your locality and slot. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match.

The last step is the one families skip. Before the first session, write down the weekly shape, the review dates, the notice period on both sides, and what happens over the summer and Diwali breaks. Two years is long enough for memory to fail and for reasonable people to remember a conversation differently. A single page settles it, and a tutor who resists writing one has told you something useful.
items: 1. Confirm the exam series the school enters and the syllabus codes on the timetable.
2. Say which grade, which tier, and how many subjects you are considering.
3. Meet verified tutors who teach that named syllabus at that tier.
4. Run a trial, then agree the weekly shape, review dates and notice period in writing.
5. Fix what happens over the long breaks before the first break arrives.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel: which series your plan is actually built around
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means either Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and it is usually followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Which of those comes next should be on the table in Grade 9, because it changes which subjects deserve tuition.

The series matter more than most parents realise. Cambridge runs series in February/March, which exists only in India, in May/June and in October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and in May/June. Schools decide which series they enter students for, and a student cannot pick a series independently of the school, so the first thing any tuition plan needs is a confirmed answer from the school office rather than an assumption.

The February/March series exists specifically so that Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for IB Diploma or A Level entry in the same academic year. A family on that series is working to a deadline several months earlier than a family on May/June, and a two-year plan built on the wrong assumption loses an entire term of preparation.

Grading differs too. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, and the ceiling is real: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*. That single fact should be discussed at the start of Grade 9 and revisited at each checkpoint, because a tier decision made quietly in Grade 9 can close a door the family did not know existed. For university recognition, the Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and current requirements should be checked with the university or board concerned rather than assumed.
items: Cambridge series run in February/March, May/June and October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June
February/March exists only in India, so Grade 10 results reach Class 11 admissions in time
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1
Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the tier decision has a ceiling
The school decides the series; confirm it in writing before planning two years of tuition

contentBlocks.heading: How many IGCSE subjects can one student be tutored in at once?
contentBlocks.body:
Two, for most students, and three only for a short stretch with a specific reason. Beyond that the arithmetic stops working: every tutored subject brings its own homework, and a student with four tuition sessions a week has no unsupervised time left in which to become independently good at anything.

The usual pairing is one mathematical subject and one written one, because they fail differently and the work does not compete. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier is fixed by practice volume and by shown working; marks are lost silently in method, and the remedy is quantity of questions with someone checking the layout. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 is fixed by drafting and by reading, and the remedy is slow. Running both is sustainable. Running 0580 alongside Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 is not, because all three want the same evening energy and the same practice hours.

The sciences deserve a separate note. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 look like three problems and are often one: a student who cannot write an explanation to a mark scheme will underperform in all three, and tutoring one of them properly frequently lifts the others. Start with the weakest, teach the writing, and review before adding a second. Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 sits closer to English than to the sciences in what it demands, which surprises families every year.

So the honest sequence is to tutor fewer subjects for longer rather than more subjects briefly. If four subjects genuinely need help, that is usually a signal about workload, sleep or study method rather than four separate content gaps, and it should be discussed with the school before four tutors are hired. A student being tutored in four subjects in Grade 10 is a student with no evenings.
items: Two subjects is the sustainable ceiling for most students; three only briefly and for a reason
Pair one mathematical subject with one written one, because they fail in different ways
0580 Extended is fixed by practice volume and shown working, not by explanation
0625, 0620 and 0610 often share one problem: writing an explanation to a mark scheme
0455 Economics behaves more like 0500 English than like a science subject
Four subjects needing help usually signals workload or method, not four content gaps

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE private tuition in India: holding a slot for two years
contentBlocks.body:
A two-year booking asks something of geography that a three-month booking does not. The question is not whether a tutor can reach you in October, but whether he will still want to in the following June.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region that usually means hiring within a cluster. A tutor working Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill can hold four households in a week for two years. The same person taking on Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi or Kharghar as a single outlying booking tends to convert it to online by the second monsoon, which is fine if you planned for it and disruptive if you did not. IGCSE private tuition in Mumbai is more stable when the family accepts a hybrid week at the start.

Bengaluru is the clearest case in the country of distance defeating good intentions. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road sit far enough from Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Hebbal and Yelahanka that IGCSE private tuition in Bangalore is frequently arranged online from the first week, and nobody regrets it. Pune is friendlier: Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Kharadi, Aundh, Baner, Balewadi and Wakad are workable for home visits, though Hinjewadi traffic on a weekday evening can stretch a short trip badly, so IGCSE private tuition in Pune often runs on weekend mornings instead.

Gujarat and eastern India change the supply picture rather than the travel picture. In Ahmedabad across Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, local tutors for 0580 and the sciences are findable while 0500 and 0455 often are not, so IGCSE private tuition in Ahmedabad regularly runs as a mixed arrangement. In Kolkata around Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, and further out in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna, a parent searching for IGCSE private tuition near me may find nobody teaching the named syllabus at all. IGCSE private tuition in Kolkata, IGCSE private tuition in Delhi around Gurugram and South Delhi, IGCSE private tuition in Hyderabad around Gachibowli, and IGCSE private tuition in Chennai around Adyar all sit somewhere between those two situations.
items: Hire within a cluster the tutor already serves, or plan a hybrid week from the start
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Electronic City bookings usually work better online
Pune: Hinjewadi evening traffic pushes many arrangements to weekend mornings
Ahmedabad, Surat and Vadodara: local supply for 0580 and sciences, thinner for 0500
Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna: often no local tutor for a named syllabus
A long term IGCSE tutor with a short commute outlasts a better one across the city

contentBlocks.heading: School terms in India and the checkpoint review that follows each one
contentBlocks.body:
Schools in India run their own term structures, and the school decides which exam series its candidates sit, so IGCSE private tuition in India has to be pinned to the school's own calendar rather than to a generic one. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School all work around internal assessments, school mocks and coursework deadlines that cluster near term ends. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

At the end of each term, hold a checkpoint. It takes twenty minutes and it is the difference between an arrangement that is working and an arrangement that merely continues. A checkpoint measures four things, in this order: what the school's own marks say, what the tutor's marked work says, whether the two agree, and what the student himself thinks has changed.

Disagreement between the first two is the most useful signal in the whole process. A student scoring well in tuition and badly at school is usually being supported too closely in sessions. A student scoring well at school and badly on the tutor's harder past-paper questions has a ceiling that will appear at the real series. Neither is a disaster in Grade 9. Both are serious if they are still true in the second term of Grade 10.

The checkpoint should also revisit the tier, where the syllabus has one. Core and Extended is not a permanent decision, and a student who has moved on in Grade 9 deserves the conversation again rather than inheriting a judgement made when he was thirteen. The school has the final say, and your evidence from marked work is what makes that conversation useful rather than emotional.
items: Hold a twenty-minute checkpoint at the end of every term, with a date fixed in advance
Compare the school's marks against the tutor's marked work and look for disagreement
Scoring well in tuition and badly at school usually means too much support in sessions
Revisit Core against Extended at each checkpoint; the school has the final say
Write down one change for next term and one thing to stop doing

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or a hybrid week across two years?
contentBlocks.body:
Over two years, reliability beats almost everything else, and that reframes the usual comparison.

Home tuition is the strongest format for Grade 9 and for anyone whose marks are being lost on paper rather than in understanding. A tutor sitting beside the student sees the working he did not write down, the diagram drawn too small to label, the question abandoned after one line, and the handwriting that will cost method marks under time pressure. None of that is visible on a screen at normal quality. Home classes also enforce a start time in a way an online link does not.

Online tuition wins on continuity and on reach. A Tuesday evening slot that has never depended on traffic is a slot still standing in month twenty, and for a syllabus nobody teaches in your city it is the only option there is. For 0500 English drafting and for 0455 Economics essays, online works very nearly as well as a home visit, because the work is read rather than watched. For 0580 method marks and for 0625 diagrams, something is genuinely lost.

A hybrid week is the arrangement most two-year families end up with, and choosing it deliberately is better than drifting into it. One home session a week for the subject where paper matters, one online session for the subject where it matters less, and an agreement that a home session becomes an online session rather than a cancellation when the evening goes wrong. Stated plainly: home tuition gives the most information about how the student writes, online gives the most dependable timetable, and hybrid buys both in exchange for a schedule that has to be written down.
items: Home tuition catches method marks lost in unwritten working and undersized diagrams
Online sessions hold a weeknight slot through monsoon weeks and exam weeks
0500 and 0455 transfer well online; 0580 and 0625 lose something real
Hybrid: agree that a difficult evening converts a home session to online, not to a cancellation
Over two years, a slot that never moves is worth more than a marginally better tutor

contentBlocks.heading: What to agree in writing before the first home tuition session
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram covers identity, qualifications and claimed teaching experience, recorded against the syllabuses and levels a tutor says he teaches, before a profile goes live. That handles who the person is. What it cannot handle is what the two of you have agreed, and over two years that is where most disputes actually come from.

Put six things on one page. The weekly slot and its length. What happens to a session missed by the family and a session missed by the tutor, which should not be the same rule. The notice period on both sides, which protects the tutor as much as you. What the tutor does during school breaks. How work is set and returned between sessions. And a review date each term with everyone's name against it.

Then add the boundary. Coursework and school-assessed work must remain the student's own, and a tutor may teach the skill, discuss a plan and explain the mark scheme without writing, editing or contributing content. Say it in the agreement so nobody has to raise it awkwardly in March. Ask the school for its own written position too, because schools differ in what they expect families to declare.

There are ordinary safeguarding basics for a regular visitor as well. Sessions happen in a shared room rather than behind a closed door. An adult is at home. Messages about schedule and progress go to a parent and not only to a fifteen-year-old's phone. None of this implies distrust of anybody. It simply means that in month eighteen, when everyone is tired and the series is close, the rules were settled long ago by people who were calm.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed experience are checked before a profile goes live
Put the slot, missed-session rules, notice period and review dates on one page
Set different rules for a session missed by the family and one missed by the tutor
State the coursework boundary in writing: teach the skill, never contribute content
Keep sessions in a shared room with an adult at home, and copy a parent on messages

contentBlocks.heading: What a two-year private tuition plan in India contains
contentBlocks.body:
A plan is not a timetable. A timetable says Tuesday at seven. A plan says what the arrangement is supposed to have achieved by a named date, which means it can be wrong, which is the entire value of writing one.

The first year carries the build. Grade 9 should establish the things that are almost impossible to install in Grade 10: a note format that survives a term, the habit of attempting a question before asking about it, familiarity with how a mark scheme awards credit, and enough past-paper exposure to remove the novelty. It should be the lighter year in hours. Families routinely invert this, running nothing in Grade 9 and four subjects in Grade 10, and it is the single most common structural mistake in IGCSE private tuition in India.

The second year tightens around evidence. By the first term of Grade 10 the tutor should be working from marked papers rather than from the syllabus, and sessions should shift from teaching topics to closing named gaps. Past papers move from occasional to weekly. Timed conditions start well before the school mocks, not after them, because the first timed paper always goes badly and it is better for that to happen in November than in February.

The last phase is narrow. Six to eight weeks before the series, a plan should be dropping content rather than adding it: the tutor picks the question types that still cost marks, and everything else stops. Students resist this because dropping a topic feels like giving up. It is the opposite, and a tutor who cannot make that argument convincingly will let a student revise what he already knows because it feels pleasant.

Write the plan in one page, three phases, with a date and a test for each. Revisit it at every checkpoint. Most plans need one real revision across two years; a plan that has never been revised is a plan nobody is reading.
items: Grade 9 is the lighter year: note format, mark scheme literacy, first past papers
Grade 10 term one: work from marked papers, not from the syllabus list
Start timed conditions before the school mocks, so the first bad one happens early
Final six to eight weeks: drop content deliberately and work only on costly question types
One page, three phases, a date and a test for each, revisited at every checkpoint

contentBlocks.heading: Long school breaks in India: rest, repair or nothing at all
contentBlocks.body:
The long summer break and the Diwali break are the two windows in the Indian school year where tuition can do something it cannot do in term time, and also the two windows where families most often waste money.

The useful version is repair, and it is narrow by design. Pick one thing the student did badly in the term that just ended, work on it in short sessions two or three times a week for two or three weeks, and then stop. A Grade 9 summer spent rebuilding algebra for 0580, or the habit of writing a full explanation for 0625, pays for itself in the following term. A summer spent covering next year's syllabus in advance almost never does, because the school will teach it again and the student will sit through it twice with less attention the second time.

The wasteful version is a full timetable maintained through a holiday because stopping feels risky, and a good deal of IGCSE private tuition in India runs through April and May for exactly that reason. Students come back to Grade 10 already tired, and the arrangement has spent its goodwill before the year that needs it. Rest is a legitimate plan. So is nothing.

And watch for the signs that tuition should be reduced rather than increased. The student stops attempting hard questions between sessions and saves them for the tutor. His marks in tuition are better than his marks at school. He cannot say what he would do differently if the sessions stopped. Or he is simply never free, and the family has confused activity with progress. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and an arrangement that keeps growing every term while nobody can name what it has fixed should be questioned rather than extended. The reduction should be planned: weekly to fortnightly, with the gap week used deliberately as a test of whether anything was lost.
items: Use a break for one repair, in short sessions over two or three weeks, then stop
Teaching next year's syllabus in advance usually wastes the break and the attention
Rest is a legitimate plan for a break, and a tutor should be able to say so
Warning sign: marks in tuition are consistently better than marks at school
Reduce from weekly to fortnightly and treat the gap week as a deliberate test

contentBlocks.heading: How do you change tutor mid-course without losing the thread?
contentBlocks.body:
Deliberately, and with a written handover, because the cost of changing badly is three or four sessions of rediscovery and a student who has to sit through a second diagnosis of his own weaknesses. That experience does more damage to confidence than the original problem did.

Run the change like this:

1. Say plainly, at a checkpoint rather than by message, that the arrangement is ending, and give the agreed notice.
2. Ask the outgoing tutor for a handover note before the final session: topics covered, current tier, weak question types, the note and practice systems in use, and what he would do next.
3. Collect the physical material in one place, including marked past papers, because the new tutor's fastest route into the student is the old tutor's marking.
4. Brief the incoming tutor before the first session, and give him the handover note rather than your own summary of it.
5. Tell the new tutor not to rediagnose from scratch. Ask him to test the handover instead, which takes one session rather than four.

Do this and a change mid-course costs about a fortnight. Skip it and it costs a term, which in Grade 10 you do not have.

To start, send a query or book a free consultation with the grade, the syllabus codes and the series the school uses. IB Gram asks about level, location and schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who teach those syllabuses, subject to availability. Arrange a trial before committing, agree the written page, and set the first checkpoint date before the first session happens.
items: End the arrangement at a checkpoint, with the agreed notice, not by message
Ask for a handover note: coverage, tier, weak question types, systems, next steps
Keep all marked past papers together; they are the fastest brief for a new tutor
Ask the incoming tutor to test the handover rather than diagnose from scratch
Done properly a change costs a fortnight; done badly it costs a term

faqs.question: Should we start private tuition in Grade 9 or wait for Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Start lighter in Grade 9 rather than heavier in Grade 10, if the budget allows only one. Grade 9 is where a note format, mark scheme literacy and the habit of attempting questions before asking can actually be installed, and none of those can be built in the final six months. A single weekly session in the weakest subject through Grade 9 usually does more than three sessions a week in Grade 10. If the student is already comfortable, wait, and set a checkpoint at the end of each term to reconsider.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at the same time?
faqs.answer: Two for most students, and three only for a defined short period with a reason you can state. Every tutored subject generates homework, so four sessions a week leaves no unsupervised time, and unsupervised time is where independence is built. Pair a mathematical subject with a written one so the work does not compete for the same evening energy. If four subjects look weak at once, treat that as a workload or study-method problem and raise it with the school before hiring anybody else.

faqs.question: What exactly should a checkpoint review at the end of term measure?
faqs.answer: Four things, in order: the school's own marks, the tutor's marked work, whether those two agree, and what the student says has changed. Disagreement is the useful part. Better marks in tuition than at school usually mean the student is being supported too closely in sessions. Better marks at school than on the tutor's harder past papers means a ceiling that will appear at the series. Finish by writing one change for next term and one thing to stop, and set the next checkpoint date.

faqs.question: Is it worth keeping home tuition running through the summer break?
faqs.answer: Only in a narrow, repair-shaped form. Pick one weakness from the term that just ended, work on it two or three times a week for two or three weeks, and then stop entirely. Covering next year's syllabus in advance is usually wasted, because the school teaches it again and the student attends less carefully the second time. A full timetable maintained through a break leaves the student tired at the start of Grade 10, which is precisely the year the energy was being saved for.

faqs.question: Our home tuition tutor is moving out of Pune mid-course. How do we not lose ground?
faqs.answer: Ask for a written handover before his last session and make it a condition, even at short notice. It should list topics covered, the current tier, the weak question types, the systems in use and what he would do next. Keep the marked past papers together, because a new tutor reads more from those than from any summary. Then ask the incoming tutor to test the handover in one session rather than diagnose from the beginning. Families in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad also often switch the same tutor to online rather than replace him.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor help with coursework and school-assessed work?
faqs.answer: Only inside the boundary your school sets, and it is narrower than many families assume. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, discuss a plan, ask questions about a draft and explain how the mark scheme awards credit. A tutor may not write, edit or contribute content to anything submitted. Put that sentence in the written agreement at the start so nobody has to raise it awkwardly later, and ask the school for its own written position, because schools differ in what they require families to declare.

faqs.question: How do we know whether to reduce tuition rather than add more?

mainEntity.name: Should we start private tuition in Grade 9 or wait for Grade 10?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start lighter in Grade 9 rather than heavier in Grade 10, if the budget allows only one. Grade 9 is where a note format, mark scheme literacy and the habit of attempting questions before asking can actually be installed, and none of those can be built in the final six months. A single weekly session in the weakest subject through Grade 9 usually does more than three sessions a week in Grade 10. If the student is already comfortable, wait, and set a checkpoint at the end of each term to reconsider.

mainEntity.name: How many subjects should we tutor at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two for most students, and three only for a defined short period with a reason you can state. Every tutored subject generates homework, so four sessions a week leaves no unsupervised time, and unsupervised time is where independence is built. Pair a mathematical subject with a written one so the work does not compete for the same evening energy. If four subjects look weak at once, treat that as a workload or study-method problem and raise it with the school before hiring anybody else.

mainEntity.name: What exactly should a checkpoint review at the end of term measure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four things, in order: the school's own marks, the tutor's marked work, whether those two agree, and what the student says has changed. Disagreement is the useful part. Better marks in tuition than at school usually mean the student is being supported too closely in sessions. Better marks at school than on the tutor's harder past papers means a ceiling that will appear at the series. Finish by writing one change for next term and one thing to stop, and set the next checkpoint date.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth keeping home tuition running through the summer break?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only in a narrow, repair-shaped form. Pick one weakness from the term that just ended, work on it two or three times a week for two or three weeks, and then stop entirely. Covering next year's syllabus in advance is usually wasted, because the school teaches it again and the student attends less carefully the second time. A full timetable maintained through a break leaves the student tired at the start of Grade 10, which is precisely the year the energy was being saved for.

mainEntity.name: Our home tuition tutor is moving out of Pune mid-course. How do we not lose ground?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for a written handover before his last session and make it a condition, even at short notice. It should list topics covered, the current tier, the weak question types, the systems in use and what he would do next. Keep the marked past papers together, because a new tutor reads more from those than from any summary. Then ask the incoming tutor to test the handover in one session rather than diagnose from the beginning. Families in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad also often switch the same tutor to online rather than replace him.

mainEntity.name: Can a private tutor help with coursework and school-assessed work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only inside the boundary your school sets, and it is narrower than many families assume. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, discuss a plan, ask questions about a draft and explain how the mark scheme awards credit. A tutor may not write, edit or contribute content to anything submitted.
