heroTitle: IGCSE Online Tutors Across India, by Syllabus Code
heroSubtitle: Two students in the same Grade 10 can be sitting different syllabuses, different tiers and different exam series. A tutor who does not ask which is guessing. This page covers finding the right one online, testing them properly in a trial, and knowing when a screen is the wrong answer.
introSummary: IGCSE online tutors in India are worth the search for one narrow reason: the syllabus your child is entered for may have almost no local teachers, and somebody who has actually taught Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 is unlikely to live within driving distance of your house. IGCSE here means Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually across Grades 9 and 10, and the two award grades on different scales. So the first job is not finding a tutor. It is knowing your syllabus code, your tier and your exam series, then testing a candidate against all three in a trial lesson. A home tutor may still be the better answer, and this page says when.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match an online IGCSE tutor in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks which board the school has entered your child for, which syllabus and code, which tier, which exam series is being targeted, then the school calendar, your location and the hours you can realistically keep, and shortlists verified tutor profiles against that description. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything.

The code is what makes the shortlist useful. A parent writes to say their child needs help with Maths in Grade 10, which could mean 0580 at Core tier, 0580 at Extended tier, 0580 Extended alongside 0606, or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent with an entirely different paper structure. Those are four different tutors. The same applies in the sciences and in Economics, where the Cambridge and Edexcel papers are assembled differently even though the subject name on the report card is identical.

For a remote arrangement your address changes what is possible rather than what is available. A family in Mangaluru or Jabalpur is not restricted by a travel radius, only by the hours everyone can keep on a school night. Say which evenings genuinely survive school, sport and sleep, and say which ones only look free on paper, because the slot that gets abandoned in week three is usually the one nobody wanted.

Then you test the match rather than trusting it. Ask the tutor to open a past paper from a recent series and mark one of your child's answers aloud against the mark scheme. Watch whether the student is writing or watching. Ask what they will set for the coming week and how they will check it. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match, subject to tutor availability.
items: Give the board, the syllabus code and the tier in your first message
Name the exam series the school is entering, not just the year
Say which evenings survive school and sleep, and which only look free
Use the trial to watch a real answer marked against the mark scheme
Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, subject to availability

contentBlocks.heading: Core or Extended, Cambridge or Edexcel: settle this before booking
contentBlocks.body:
Before you hire anybody, write down four things: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series. Everything else in the arrangement follows from those, and a family that cannot state all four is not ready to judge a tutor yet. The school can confirm every one of them in a single email.

IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and what follows it varies: the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move across to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. That next step should shape which subjects get tutoring hours now, because a student heading for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level needs a different Grade 10 than one heading for ISC commerce.

Grading is where families get caught. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout. A tutor talking confidently about a grade 8 for a child sitting an A* to G syllabus has not read the entry. Tiers matter just as much. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. A student quietly entered for Core cannot reach an A no matter how many hours are bought, so tier is a conversation with the school before it is a conversation with a tutor.

Series dates then set the whole plan. Cambridge runs February and March, a series offered only in India, plus May and June and October and November. Pearson Edexcel runs January and May and June. Ask which one your child is entered for, because a February entry compresses everything.
items: Write down four things: board, syllabus code, tier and exam series
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE uses 9 to 1
Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*
Cambridge series: February and March, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel series: January, and May and June
The February and March series is offered only in India, and it compresses the year

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE syllabuses are hardest to find a tutor for locally?
contentBlocks.body:
The common subjects are not the problem. Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610 and First Language English 0500 have enough teachers in most large Indian cities that a family can usually find somebody within reach. The scarcity sits in Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450, and it gets worse the further you go from the metros.

Additional Mathematics 0606 is the clearest case. It has no tiers, two written papers with a calculator allowed, and is graded A* to E. The content runs through functions, quadratic functions, factors of polynomials, equations, inequalities and graphs, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation and integration. Students take it alongside 0580 Extended when they are heading for IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or for A Level Mathematics. The Pearson Edexcel equivalent is International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1. A general Class 10 mathematics tutor who has never seen 0606 will teach the calculus adequately and miss what the papers reward.

Computer Science 0478, examined from 2023, splits into Paper 1 on computer systems, covering data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, the internet and its uses, automated and emerging technologies, and Paper 2 on algorithms, programming and logic, covering algorithm design and problem-solving, pseudocode, programming, databases and SQL, and Boolean logic. The pre-release material was removed, and practice now runs in a language such as Python, Java or Visual Basic. Edexcel pairs a written paper with an on-screen practical programming paper in Python under code 4CP0. Very few tutors outside the metros have taught either.
items: 0606 has no tiers, two written papers with a calculator, graded A* to E
0606 is usually taken with 0580 Extended by students heading for AA HL
Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 is the nearest equivalent to 0606
0478 Paper 1 is computer systems, Paper 2 is algorithms, programming and logic
0478 practice uses Python, Java or Visual Basic; the pre-release was removed
Edexcel 4CP0 adds an on-screen practical programming paper in Python

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE online tutors in India: where the syllabus gap bites hardest
contentBlocks.body:
Local supply follows the subject, not the city, and that is why IGCSE online tutors in India are hired as often from a metro flat as from a small town. Even in a metro, a family can find four capable 0580 tutors and nobody who has taught 0606, which is why searches for an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai or an IGCSE online tutor in Delhi are usually about one stubborn subject rather than about the whole timetable. Outside the metros the same search is about the timetable.

Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai typically find strong CBSE and state-board tutors quickly and nobody who has read a Cambridge mark scheme. The same pattern runs through central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa, where a search for an online IGCSE tutor near me returns coaching centres built for entrance examinations. Typing IGCSE 0606 online tutor is a far more productive search than typing the name of your city.

In Kolkata and eastern India the split is sharp. Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore hold some genuine supply, so an IGCSE online tutor in Kolkata is often hired for Computer Science or Business Studies alone. In Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna there may be nobody at all for those codes. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula manage between them, while families in Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur are mostly hiring remotely by necessity.

Gujarat generates heavy demand against thin staffing. Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway corridor, along with Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, produce steady searches for an IGCSE online tutor in Ahmedabad, and the subject behind most of them is a science at Extended tier or Additional Mathematics. Compare an IGCSE online tutor in Hyderabad, an IGCSE online tutor in Chennai or an IGCSE online tutor in Pune, where a family in Gachibowli, Adyar or Baner can often find a local option and chooses remote teaching for the hour rather than for the access. In Powai and Whitefield the common pattern is one local tutor and one online Cambridge IGCSE tutor for the awkward code.
items: Even in a metro, 0606 and 0478 can be unstaffed while 0580 is easy
Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Madurai: strong general tutors, few Cambridge markers
Indore, Bhopal, Jabalpur, Raipur: remote teaching by necessity, not preference
Kolkata holds supply; Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna often do not
Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot: heavy demand, mostly for sciences and 0606
Search the syllabus code rather than the city name

contentBlocks.heading: Exam series and school deadlines in India, planned backwards
contentBlocks.body:
Plan from the series backwards, because the series is the only fixed point. A Cambridge candidate entered for the February and March series, which is offered only in India, has a materially shorter Grade 10 than one entered for May and June, and a student sitting October and November has a different shape again. Pearson Edexcel candidates work to January or to May and June. Ask the school which entry has been made before you buy a single hour.

The school controls more of this than parents expect. It decides tier entries, it makes the coursework and practical arrangements, it sets mock examinations, and it holds internal deadlines that fall well before anything the board publishes. Your tutor cannot see any of that. Send the school diary in the first week and ask for a term plan written against those dates rather than against a generic run of topics.

There is also the question of what comes next, which quietly shapes Grade 10. A student moving into the IB Diploma Programme needs different groundwork from one moving to Cambridge International AS and A Levels, and a student switching to CBSE or ISC in Class 11 faces a change of marking culture that is worth preparing for while the pressure is still low. Say which direction you are heading when you enquire.

One point about schools themselves. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. A tutor may have taught students from schools you recognise, which tells you about the rhythm they are used to and nothing more. Every entry, tier and deadline should be confirmed with your child's own coordinator.
items: Ask the school which series your child is entered for, in writing
The school sets tier entries, practical arrangements and internal deadlines
Internal deadlines fall well before the published board dates
Say whether Class 11 means the IB Diploma, A Levels, CBSE or ISC
Send the school diary to the tutor during the first week

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid: what the screen gains and what it loses
contentBlocks.body:
A screen gains you the right syllabus and loses you the room. That is the trade in one line. Home tuition wins where the problem is habit, attention or apparatus, remote teaching wins where the problem is a code nobody nearby has taught, and hybrid covers the common case where a household has both problems at once.

Take practical work, which is where families get vague advice. Some science candidates are entered for a practical examination and others for an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which route applies is a question for the school rather than an assumption for a tutor. The honest position is this: the write-up, the variables, the tables, the graph work and the evaluation questions can be taught extremely well on a screen, because they are paper skills. Handling apparatus cannot. If your child is entered for a practical examination and struggles with the bench itself, a home tutor with equipment on the table, or the school's own laboratory time, will do more than any remote session.

Home classes also carry information a video call does not. The tutor sees the phone, the notes, the half-finished past paper and the moment attention goes. For a Grade 9 student whose real difficulty is starting work rather than understanding it, a home tutor twice a week beats a distant specialist comfortably.

Hybrid is what most families outside the metros settle on. A local tutor at the desk for routine work and the common subjects, plus IGCSE online tutors in India for the one or two codes nobody local has taught. Run it for a month, look at the marked work, and drop whichever half is not paying for its hour.
items: Write-ups, tables, graphs and evaluation questions teach well on a screen
Handling apparatus does not; the school laboratory or a home tutor covers that
Ask the school whether the entry is practical or alternative-to-practical
Home tuition wins when the problem is starting work, not understanding it
Hybrid: a local home tutor for the common codes, remote for the scarce ones

contentBlocks.heading: How do you verify an IGCSE tutor you will never meet?
contentBlocks.body:
Verify three separate things: who the person is, whether they have taught this exact syllabus, and what happens when something goes wrong. Distance does not change the list, it only raises the cost of skipping it, because there is no gate and no reception desk where a problem can be raised in person. Families hiring IGCSE online tutors in India skip the third item most often, and it is the one that hurts in February.

On IB Gram, tutor profiles are verified before they go live, which covers identity and claimed teaching background. It does not mean anybody has watched every lesson, and no honest platform claims otherwise. Treat verification as a filter that removes the implausible, the trial as your evidence, and the first month as the actual test.

The syllabus questions are the ones a generalist cannot fake. Which series have you prepared students for? Have you taught 0580 at Extended tier, and separately 0606? For Economics 0455, how do you prepare a student for the data questions in Paper 2, and how does that differ from the Edexcel arrangement? For Business Studies, which of the six areas do students lose most marks in, and why? A tutor who has done the work answers with examples and with the language of the mark scheme. A tutor who has not answers with adjectives about passion.

Then the practical safeguards, which matter more when nobody visits your house. Keep the sessions in a shared room rather than a bedroom, with the door open. Agree whether lessons are recorded and who keeps the recording. Keep scheduling and payment inside the platform rather than drifting into private messages. Ask for a short written note after each session, and read it. Anything that starts moving off the platform and out of sight should be treated as a warning sign rather than a convenience.
items: Ask which series and which tier the tutor has actually prepared students for
Ask a code-specific question and listen for mark scheme language
Keep sessions in a shared room with the door open
Agree whether lessons are recorded and who keeps the recording
Keep scheduling and payment on the platform, not in private messages

contentBlocks.heading: What to test in an online IGCSE trial lesson in India
contentBlocks.body:
A trial is not a sample lesson. It is an interview in which the tutor happens to teach, and forty minutes used well will tell you more than any profile. Go in with five tests and a marked script, and do not let the session become a friendly conversation about how your child is finding Grade 10.

Test one. Before anything else, ask the tutor to say back the board, the syllabus code and the tier. A tutor who has taught the course will ask you for these in the first two minutes without being prompted, and one who does not ask has told you something already. Test two. Share a question your child recently got wrong and ask the tutor to mark it aloud against the mark scheme, saying where each mark was won or lost. Watch whether they can point at the specific mark rather than talking about the topic in general.

Test three. Ask them to explain the difference between two command words in that subject, and to show it on the same question. Describe against explain, state against calculate, identify against analyse. This is where most marks quietly disappear for students who know the content perfectly well. Test four. Watch who holds the pen. If the tutor spends thirty of the forty minutes talking and annotating while your child watches, that pattern will repeat every week and the student will learn to nod.

Test five, and this is the one families forget. Ask what they will set for the coming week, how long it should take, and how they will check it at the start of the next session. A tutor who has no answer is planning to fill hours. A tutor who names a specific task, a time and a checking method is planning to teach.
items: Make the tutor state the board, the code and the tier back to you
Watch them mark a real wrong answer aloud against the mark scheme
Ask them to separate two command words on the same question
Count the minutes your child spends writing rather than watching
Ask what they will set for the week and how it gets checked

contentBlocks.heading: Which students should not be taught IGCSE online?
contentBlocks.body:
Three kinds of student, in my experience of sitting with families through this. The student who cannot start work without an adult in the room. The student whose difficulty is emotional rather than academic. And the young student who has not yet built the habit of sitting at a desk for a fixed hour. For all three, IGCSE online tutors in India will be a worse buy than a patient local tutor, and it is worth saying that before anybody pays for a term.

The first case is the most common and the most misdiagnosed. A Grade 9 student who understands the material and still hands in nothing does not have a content problem. Adding a specialist on a screen gives them another hour of being taught and no more hours of working. A home tutor sitting beside them while they attempt questions solves the actual problem, and it usually solves it in weeks.

The second case needs care rather than tuition. A student in real distress about school does not need a sixth adult with opinions about their performance. Talk to the school first.

For everybody else, judge the arrangement on evidence and give it about six weeks. Look for process changes early: notes organised by topic and paper, past papers attempted under time, drafts started before the night before. By week six there should be a marked piece where the school's comment matches what the tutor predicted. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a Core entry limits the ceiling whatever anyone promises, and starting in the final months narrows what is realistically left to technique. Honest tutors say all of this at the start.
items: A student who cannot start work needs presence, not another explanation
Distress about school is a conversation with the school, not a tuition problem
Very young students rarely hold attention on a screen for a full hour
Weeks two to four: organised notes and papers attempted under time
Week six: a marked piece where school and tutor agree on the diagnosis
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a Core entry caps what is possible

contentBlocks.heading: Before the first online lesson in India: a checklist
contentBlocks.body:
Most first lessons are wasted on questions that could have been answered by email. Send the information first and the tutor arrives knowing what to do, which buys back an hour you have already paid for and sets the tone for everything after it.

Gather the four facts from the school, a recent marked script with the teacher's comments intact, the term's deadline calendar, and a plain statement of what you want to be different in six weeks. That last one is the item families skip, and it is the one that makes the arrangement reviewable. Wanting better grades is not a target. Wanting the student to attempt full past papers under time without abandoning the last question is a target.

Then deal with the setup before the lesson rather than during it. A quiet room with a door, a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, a stable connection and paper on the desk. In the sciences and in mathematics a cheap graphics tablet changes the session completely, because the student can show working instead of describing it. Test the shared whiteboard once before the first lesson so nobody spends the opening ten minutes on settings.

When you are ready, send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, tier, level, the school calendar, your location and your schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who match, subject to availability. Take the trial, run your five tests, and ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. That request is routine, and making it in week two is much easier than making it in the middle of the series.
items: 1. Get the board, syllabus code, tier and exam series from the school.
2. Collect a recent marked script and the term deadline calendar.
3. Write one specific thing you want to be different in six weeks.
4. Set up a quiet room, a proper device and a stable connection.
5. Test the shared whiteboard and, for sciences, a graphics tablet.
6. Take a trial, run your tests, then commit or ask for another match.

faqs.question: Why should I search by syllabus code instead of by city?
faqs.answer: Because the code is what determines whether a tutor can help, and the city only determines who is nearby. A search for an IGCSE tutor in your city returns everybody who teaches Grade 10 anything. A search naming 0606, 0478 or 4PM1 returns the much smaller group who have taught those papers and know what the mark schemes reward. Once you are hiring remotely, the geography stops mattering and the code becomes the only useful filter.

faqs.question: What is Additional Mathematics 0606 and does my child need it?
faqs.answer: It is a separate Cambridge IGCSE syllabus with no tiers, two written papers with a calculator allowed, graded A* to E, covering functions, polynomials, logarithms, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, series, vectors, differentiation and integration. Students usually take it alongside 0580 Extended when they are heading for IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or A Level Mathematics. If your child is heading elsewhere, it is optional, and the school is the right place to confirm.

faqs.question: Can practical science really be taught over a video call?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is worth being precise about which part. The paper skills transfer completely: planning variables, recording results in a table, drawing and reading graphs, spotting anomalies and answering evaluation questions. Handling apparatus does not transfer. Ask the school whether your child is entered for a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper. If it is the former and the bench itself is the weakness, use the school laboratory or a home tutor with equipment rather than paying for remote sessions.

faqs.question: How do I judge an online tutor in a single trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Run five tests rather than listening to a pitch. Ask them to state the board, code and tier back to you. Ask them to mark a wrong answer aloud against the mark scheme. Ask them to separate two command words on the same question. Count how many minutes your child spends writing. Ask what they will set for the week and how they will check it. A tutor who handles all five has taught the syllabus before, whatever the profile says.

faqs.question: Is an online tutor cheaper than a home tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually lower per hour for a comparable tutor, because nobody is funding travel time, though that is not the main reason to choose one. The real difference is access: remote teaching reaches the person who has taught your child's exact syllabus, which in Raipur or Mangaluru may be nobody local at any price. Weigh the hour rate against what a wasted term of generic tuition costs, and against the value of somebody who can read the mark scheme fluently.

faqs.question: We are in Guwahati and nobody local has taught Cambridge. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Split the job in two. Hire locally for routine and habit, which any capable tutor can support, and hire remotely for the syllabus itself. This pattern works across Bhubaneswar, Ranchi, Patna and much of eastern India. Give the local tutor the school diary so the two are not pulling in different directions, and make the remote specialist responsible for past papers and mark scheme work. It is usually cheaper than sending a student to a metro for weekend classes.

faqs.question: Would a home tutor still be useful alongside an online specialist?
faqs.answer: For many families, yes. The specialist handles the syllabus content and exam technique; the home tutor holds the routine, checks that the set work was attempted, and notices when a student is avoiding a subject rather than struggling with it. Grade 9 students benefit from this more than Grade 10 students, because the habit is still forming. Review it after a month and keep whichever half is producing visible change in the marked work.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Edexcel need different tutors?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, meaningfully yes. The content overlaps a great deal, but the paper structures, the command word conventions and the mark schemes differ, and preparation is mostly about those. Economics is a clear example: Cambridge 0455 uses a multiple choice paper and a structured data paper, while the Edexcel equivalent splits microeconomics and macroeconomics across two papers. A tutor fluent in one and guessing at the other will teach the subject and miss the examination.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: One or two, and rarely more. Every tutored hour is an hour taken from independent practice, which is where most of the improvement in an IGCSE grade actually comes from. If four subjects look weak, treat the weakest one properly for six weeks and reassess with the marked evidence in front of you. Families who book five subjects in September are usually cancelling three of them by December, having spent the term attending rather than working.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops during a lesson?
faqs.answer: Whatever you agreed in writing before the first lesson, which is why the question belongs in week one. Common arrangements are a rescheduled remainder, a credited part-session, or extra minutes added to the next lesson. Decide who calls whom, so neither side spends five minutes waiting. Connection drops and power cuts are a normal part of the year in many Indian towns, and any tutor who has taught here will have a routine answer ready.

faqs.question: Is online tuition safe for a Grade 9 student?
faqs.answer: It can be, with three simple rules that cost nothing. Keep sessions in a shared room with the door open rather than in a bedroom. Keep scheduling, messages and payment inside the platform instead of drifting to private numbers. Agree whether lessons are recorded and who holds the recordings. A tutor who resists any of these has given you your answer. Verification checks identity and background before a profile goes live, but your household rules do the daily work.

faqs.question: When should we start, and how long before we see something?
faqs.answer: Start in Grade 9 if the subject is genuinely hard, and start immediately if the school has flagged a tier decision. Expect process changes in weeks two to four: papers attempted under time, notes organised by paper rather than by date, fewer questions abandoned halfway. Expect marked evidence by about week six. If nothing in the folder has changed by then, the problem is the match or the diagnosis, and more hours will not repair either of them.

h1: IGCSE Online Tuition in India: Past Papers Marked Live on Screen
heroTitle: Inside an online IGCSE lesson taught across India
heroSubtitle: A past paper on a shared screen, the mark scheme open beside it, and the student writing while the tutor watches the clock. This page describes what should actually happen in an online IGCSE session minute by minute, how a handwritten script reaches the tutor, and what to do when the format goes wrong.
introSummary: IGCSE online tuition in India works or fails on one thing: whether the student is producing written work during the lesson while the tutor reads it, or merely watching someone explain. The technology is not the interesting part. What matters is the past paper annotated live, the mark scheme read line by line against the student's own answer, and timed practice done on camera so somebody sees how the last ten minutes are spent. This page sets out the mechanics in detail. It also covers scanning a handwritten script, the four ways online lessons commonly break, and where home tuition or a hybrid arrangement is the better call.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram set up IGCSE online tuition in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Setting up IGCSE online tuition in India starts with a short call that is mostly about evidence. We ask which board, which syllabus code, which tier, and which exam series the school has entered the student for, because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE run different papers on different calendars and a tutor who knows one may not know the other. Then we ask for two marked papers, ideally including one the student did badly on, because the pattern of lost marks decides who is a good match far better than a description does.

After that come the practical questions that specifically affect online lessons. Which room the student will sit in and whether anyone else uses it. Whether the connection holds during the hours you want. Whether the student can photograph or scan handwritten work and send it, since a great deal of IGCSE practice is done on paper and has to reach the tutor somehow. And which evenings genuinely survive school, travel and everything else, because an online slot is easier to book than to keep.

A shortlist follows, drawn from verified profiles matched to that syllabus and tier. Availability depends on subject, tier and the hour you want. A demo session can be arranged before the family commits, and with online lessons the demo is doing double duty: it tests the tutor and it tests the arrangement. Watch whether the student is asked to write within the first fifteen minutes.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. That is routine. What we would rather avoid is a family persisting for two months with a tutor who lectures well to a camera while the student quietly stops attempting anything.
items: Say the board, syllabus code, tier and the exam series the school entered
Send two marked papers, including one that went badly
Confirm the room, the connection and who else uses that space
Check the student can photograph or scan handwritten work and send it
Use the demo to test the arrangement, not only the tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge, Edexcel and the Core or Extended decision
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means one of two qualifications, and a tutor working online needs to know which one is on the student's timetable before the first lesson, not during it. Cambridge IGCSE comes from Cambridge International Education. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is a separate qualification with its own papers and its own calendar. Both usually run as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and students go on to the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or across to CBSE or ISC in Class 11.

The calendars diverge, and the difference matters for planning online sessions. Cambridge series run in February and March, which is a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. A family whose school uses the February and March series is working to a schedule several months ahead of one entered for May and June, and a tutor who assumes the wrong series plans the wrong revision.

Grading differs too. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and this is the single most consequential decision a Grade 9 family makes: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*.

Online lessons are unusually good for the tiering conversation, because both tiers' past papers can be put on screen side by side in the same session. A student who has never seen an Extended paper cannot judge whether it is within reach. Twenty minutes looking at both, with the mark scheme open, settles more than a term of speculation.
items: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate qualifications
Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*
Compare both tiers' past papers on screen before the school locks the entry

contentBlocks.heading: Reading a mark scheme on screen: a worked example from 0620
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the method with a real syllabus attached. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620, Extended tier, and a Paper 4 theory question the student scored two out of five on. In a classroom this comes back with a number circled. In a good online session it gets taken apart.

The tutor shares the paper, then opens the mark scheme in a second pane. The student reads the question aloud. Then the student reads the first mark scheme line aloud and is asked a single question: does your answer contain that. Not is it similar, does it contain it. Almost always the student finds their sentence says the right chemistry in words the mark scheme does not accept, or gives the observation without the explanation. Three lines of mark scheme later the student has diagnosed their own script, which is worth more than being told.

The structure of the Cambridge sciences makes this repeatable. Since the syllabuses examined from 2023, Core candidates sit Paper 1 multiple choice and Extended candidates sit Paper 2 multiple choice, both tiers sit a theory paper as Paper 3 or Paper 4, and the practical element comes through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school chooses. Multiple choice carries 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. So a student losing marks on Paper 6 and a student losing them on Paper 4 need entirely different lessons, and the weighting tells you which one to fix first.

The same routine transfers across subjects. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, puts Core candidates on Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, and Extended candidates on Paper 2 without and Paper 4 with. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers per tier. Physics 0625, Biology 0610, Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 each reward the same on-screen dissection.
items: Share the paper in one pane and the mark scheme in another, always
Ask does your answer contain this line, not is it similar
Cambridge science weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%
Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical, chosen by the school
0580 from 2025: Core sits Papers 1 and 3, Extended sits Papers 2 and 4
Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is Foundation or Higher, two calculator papers each

contentBlocks.heading: Who online tuition actually serves across India
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE online tuition in India is often sold as a convenience. For most of the families who genuinely need it, it is not a convenience at all; it is the only way to reach a tutor who knows the syllabus code on their child's timetable.

Start with the places where local supply is thin. Across central and western India, families in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa can usually find a competent Mathematics or English tutor locally and almost never one who has taught Extended tier 0620 or 0625 to the current papers. The same is true across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, and across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai. For these families online tuition removes the constraint entirely.

Then there are the metro families who choose online for a different reason: the evening. In Bengaluru, a student in Yelahanka, Hebbal, Electronic City, Jayanagar or Kanakapura Road whose best-matched tutor works out of Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala or Indiranagar is choosing between a screen and a tutor who arrives late and leaves early. In Hyderabad the split runs between the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet belt and everywhere else, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad each on their own clock. Families in Mumbai, Pune and Delhi make the same calculation.

There is a third group worth naming: students who move mid-course. A transfer from Chennai to Ahmedabad in the middle of Grade 10 used to mean losing a tutor. Online means it does not. The same applies to a family spending three months abroad, or a student whose parent is posted elsewhere. Continuity through Grade 9 and Grade 10 is worth a great deal, because the tutor who watched the Grade 9 mistakes is the one who can stop them repeating.
items: Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Goa: local supply rarely covers Extended tier sciences
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun families reach specialists no other way
Kochi, Coimbatore and Visakhapatnam: online is the realistic option, not the fallback
Bengaluru and Hyderabad families choose online to avoid a compressed evening lesson
A mid-course move between cities no longer means losing the tutor

contentBlocks.heading: School terms, mock weeks and exam series in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools appear here only as context for the calendar an IGCSE family in India is working inside.

The first thing to establish is which series the school has entered. Cambridge offers a February and March series only in India, alongside May and June and October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May and June. Schools do not all choose the same thing, and siblings at different schools can be on different clocks. Everything else in a tuition plan hangs off that date.

Work backwards from it. Grade 9 is the year to build, and it is systematically underused in India because nothing appears to be at stake. The student who spends Grade 9 learning to write to a mark scheme arrives in Grade 10 needing revision rather than repair. Grade 10 then divides into a long teaching stretch, a mock period set by the school, and a final run of timed papers. Online sessions suit that final run particularly well, because a tutor can supervise a timed paper on camera without anyone travelling anywhere during the most congested weeks of the year.

Parents at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School describe similar pressures: coursework and practical assessment arriving alongside mocks, a tier decision made earlier than expected, and a school calendar that does not leave much room once December arrives. Booking online help in August is a much easier conversation than booking it in January.
items: Establish the exam series first; everything in the plan hangs off that date
Cambridge February and March series is offered only in India
Grade 9 is for building the mark-scheme habit, not for waiting
Grade 10 splits into teaching, the school's mocks, and timed papers
Online supervision of timed papers works best in the most congested weeks

contentBlocks.heading: Where does a home tutor still beat an online lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
In three situations, clearly, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest on a page about online tuition.

The first is the student who will not start. If a Grade 9 student opens a laptop, joins the call and then spends the hour agreeing with everything, an online lesson has very limited defences. A home tutor sees the notebook, the phone, the untouched textbook and the body language, and can simply sit there until work happens. Home tuition is a behavioural intervention as much as an academic one, and some students need that more than they need a better subject specialist.

The second is heavy paper work in Mathematics. A student who needs someone watching each line of algebra as it is written, catching an error at the moment it happens, gets that faster in person. It can be done online with a document camera pointed at the page, and plenty of tutors do exactly that, but it takes deliberate setup and the family has to be willing to run it.

The third is the household without a workable space. Online lessons need a quiet room, a door and a reliable connection at the same hour each week. Where that does not exist, home classes shift the logistics onto the tutor instead of the family.

Hybrid is the arrangement that resolves most of this. One home session a week for supervised writing and whatever needs to be watched on paper, plus one or two online sessions for marking, mark scheme work and doubt-solving. It is also the most durable pattern across a full year, because the online half survives monsoon weeks, mock weeks and the evenings when nothing in the city moves. Stated plainly: home tuition buys attention, online buys expertise and reliability, and hybrid buys both at the cost of running a schedule.
items: Home tuition wins for the student who will not start work alone
Line-by-line algebra is faster in person unless a document camera is set up
Without a quiet room and a door, home classes shift the burden to the tutor
Hybrid: one home session for writing, online sessions for marking and doubts
The online half of a hybrid plan survives monsoon and mock weeks

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before booking an online IGCSE tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for the syllabus code, not the subject. A tutor who teaches IGCSE Chemistry should say 0620 without hesitation, know which tier your child sits, and know whether the school has chosen Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the practical element. Anyone who talks about IGCSE Chemistry as a single generic thing has not taught it recently. This one question does more filtering than any credential check.

Then ask a mechanics question, because this is online tuition and the mechanics are the service. How will they see the student's handwritten working. What software do they annotate in. Will the session be recorded and shared, and if so, where does the recording live. Do they send a written note after each session. A tutor who has taught online seriously has fluent answers, because they have solved these problems already. A tutor improvising will describe intentions rather than habits.

On our side, identity, qualifications and the syllabuses and tiers a tutor claims to teach are verified before a profile goes live. That establishes who someone is and what they have taught. It cannot tell you whether a particular fifteen-year-old will engage with them through a screen, which is what the demo session is for, and why asking for a different match is a normal request.

Treat some claims with real caution. Be wary of anyone advertising a guaranteed grade or a promised improvement from online classes. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a screen does not change that. Be equally wary of any provider implying an official relationship with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; those bodies approve schools as examination centres, not tuition services.
items: Ask for the syllabus code and the tier before anything else
Ask how handwritten working reaches the tutor, and in which software
Ask whether sessions are recorded, and where the recording is stored
Identity, qualifications and claimed syllabuses are verified before a profile goes live
Be wary of a guaranteed grade attached to any online package

contentBlocks.heading: The running order of an online IGCSE lesson in India
contentBlocks.body:
A well-run session of IGCSE online tuition in India has a fixed shape, and the shape exists because a screen punishes drift far more than a room does. In person, a wandering ten minutes is recoverable. Online, it is the lesson.

It opens with the previous week's written work already in the tutor's hands. That is the part families most often skip, and it is what separates a session that starts productively from one that spends its first quarter catching up. The student photographs or scans their attempt the night before and sends it. Good lighting, the whole page in frame, one image per page, nothing clever required.

Then the marking, which is the heart of it. Paper in one pane, mark scheme in the other, and the student reading each mark scheme line against their own sentence. Then a short piece of reteaching, aimed only at whatever the marking exposed. Then timed practice with the camera on and the tutor silent, which is the part students dislike and which changes results the most, because most IGCSE marks are lost to timing and structure rather than to not knowing the content. A tutor watching a student sit in silence for four minutes before starting a question has learned something no explanation would have revealed.

The session ends with the tutor annotating the shared document, the annotated file going to the student, and one specific task set for the week. Small enough to finish.

And the handwriting problem, which every Indian family asks about: the student writes on paper as they will in the exam, photographs it, and the tutor annotates the image on screen and sends it back. Nobody needs a tablet. A phone camera and reasonable light are enough.
items: 1. Last week's written attempt is photographed and sent before the lesson
2. Paper in one pane, mark scheme in the other, student reads both aloud
3. The student checks each mark scheme line against their own sentence
4. Short reteaching aimed only at what the marking exposed
5. Timed practice on camera in silence, with the tutor watching how it starts
6. Annotated file sent back, plus one small written task for the week

contentBlocks.heading: What goes wrong in online lessons, and how do you fix it?
contentBlocks.body:
Four failures account for nearly everything that goes wrong with IGCSE online tuition in India, and each has a fix that costs nothing.

The first is the silent nodder. The student agrees with everything, asks nothing, and produces no work in the lesson. The fix is structural rather than motivational: insist that at least a third of each session is the student writing while the tutor reads. If a tutor resists that, the format is not the problem.

The second is paper that never arrives. A student who does not send their written attempt turns every session into a live-teaching hour, and the marking, the only part that reliably moves grades, quietly disappears. The fix is a standing deadline the night before and a tutor who declines to proceed without it once.

The third is the room. A lesson taken in a shared living space, with a phone propped against a jug and a sibling in the background, will not hold a fifteen-year-old's attention for an hour. The fix is a door and a table, and it is worth more than any change of tutor.

The fourth is drift over the term. Sessions that began with timed practice become conversations by week eight, because talking is comfortable for everyone involved. The fix is a monthly check: ask your child what they wrote during the last lesson. If the honest answer is nothing, say so to the tutor.

As for progress, be realistic. In four weeks you should see the student naming why marks were lost rather than saying the paper was hard. Grades move over a term, and no tutor can guarantee a grade. If after six to eight weeks the written work has not changed in shape, change something: the mode, the schedule or the match.
items: Silent nodder: require a third of every session to be student writing
Missing paper: set a standing deadline the night before, and enforce it once
Wrong room: a door and a table beat any change of tutor
Term drift: ask monthly what your child actually wrote in the last lesson
Four weeks: the student names the lost marks; grades take a term

contentBlocks.heading: Setting up the desk, the camera and the scanner before lesson one
contentBlocks.body:
Half an hour of setup before the first session saves a term of friction, and none of it needs buying anything expensive.

Start with the surface and the sound. A table the student can write on with the laptop raised slightly, so the camera shows a face rather than a ceiling. A headset, because laptop speakers and a microphone in the same room produce the echo that makes students stop talking. A door that closes. A chair that is not a bed.

Then the paper pipeline. Decide now how written work travels: a phone camera, a free scanning app, one image per page, sent to the same place every time. Agree the deadline with the tutor in the first session rather than the fourth. Keep a folder, physical or digital, of every marked attempt, because by February that folder is the revision plan.

Then the practice materials. Past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports come through the school or the board's official channels, and it is worth asking the school which series and which tier your child is entered for before the first lesson so nobody practises the wrong papers.

A parent in the house but not in the room is the right balance for most Grade 9 and Grade 10 students. Close enough that the door being shut means something, far enough that the student speaks freely.

When you are ready, send a query or book a free consultation. Tell us the board, the syllabus codes, the tier and the exam series, and send two marked papers. We shortlist tutors whose verified profiles match, arrange a demo session before you commit, and change the match if the fit is wrong. Lessons can run online, at home or as a hybrid of both, and fees depend on subject, tier and schedule.
items: Raise the laptop, use a headset, and close a door before lesson one
Agree the paper pipeline and the sending deadline in the first session
Keep every marked attempt in one folder; it becomes the revision plan
Confirm the series and tier with the school so nobody practises wrong papers
A parent in the house, not in the room, suits most Grade 9 and 10 students

faqs.question: How does the tutor see my child's handwritten work in an online lesson?
faqs.answer: The student writes on paper, photographs it, and sends the image before or during the session. The tutor then annotates that image on a shared screen and sends it back. One photograph per page, taken in decent light with the whole page in frame, is all that is required, and a free scanning app makes it neater. Nobody needs a graphics tablet or a stylus. The habit matters more than the equipment, so agree a standing deadline with the tutor in the first week.

faqs.question: Can timed practice really be supervised through a screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the things online tuition does best. The student sits the paper with the camera on and the tutor watches without speaking, which reveals things a marked script never does: a four-minute stall before starting, time lost re-reading the same question, or the last section rushed. Because the tutor does not have to travel, supervising a full timed paper costs far less of everyone's evening than it would at home. Most IGCSE marks are lost to timing and structure rather than to missing content.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE online tuition worth it in Bengaluru, where local tutors exist?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the reason is the evening rather than the supply. A student in Yelahanka, Hebbal, Electronic City or Kanakapura Road whose best-matched tutor is based around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road or Koramangala is effectively choosing between a screen and a compressed lesson delivered by someone who arrived late. The same applies across Hyderabad between the Gachibowli belt and Secunderabad. If a good local tutor teaches the exact syllabus code and tier and lives close, take them. Otherwise online usually wins.

faqs.question: My son is in Indore and needs Extended tier Chemistry. Can you help?
faqs.answer: This is the clearest case for online tuition in the whole set. Across central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa, local supply covers general subjects reasonably and rarely covers Extended tier 0620 to the current papers, including whether the school has chosen Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the practical element. Online removes the geography entirely, and the marking half of the method runs at least as well on a shared screen as it does at a table.

faqs.question: Would a home tutor be better for my daughter than online lessons?
faqs.answer: If she will not start work unless someone is present, yes. Home tuition is partly a behavioural intervention: the tutor sees the untouched textbook, the phone face-up and the evening as it actually is, which no camera reliably shows. If she works when asked but needs a specialist in a particular syllabus, online is better. If both are true, a hybrid arrangement of one home session a week plus one or two online sessions solves it, and it is the most durable pattern across a full Grade 10 year.

faqs.question: How long should an online IGCSE session be?
faqs.answer: Sixty to ninety minutes for most Grade 9 and Grade 10 students, and shorter is usually better than longer. Attention on a screen runs out sooner than it does across a table, so two sessions of an hour generally produce more than one session of two hours. A timed paper is the exception: if the aim is to sit a full past paper under supervision, book the time the paper actually needs rather than cutting it short, because a rushed ending teaches the wrong habit.

faqs.question: What software and equipment do we actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. A laptop with a working camera, a headset to stop the echo that makes students go quiet, a stable connection at the same hour each week, and a phone camera for scanning written work. Most tutors annotate in a shared document or a simple whiteboard tool and will tell you which in the first session. A second screen or a printed copy of the paper helps a great deal, because it stops the student switching windows between the question and the tutor.

faqs.question: How do we know the student is not just nodding along?
faqs.answer: Ask what they wrote. Not what they learned, what they wrote. In a well-run session at least a third of the time is the student producing work while the tutor reads it, and if the honest answer after a lesson is that they wrote nothing, the format has drifted into a lecture. Ask monthly rather than weekly, so it does not become an interrogation. Then raise it with the tutor directly, because most will restructure the session immediately once asked.

faqs.question: Can online tuition help with the practical papers?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it depends which paper the school has chosen. Cambridge schools enter candidates either for Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Paper 6 is written and can be prepared thoroughly online, since it is about interpreting apparatus, readings, tables and sources of error on paper. Paper 5 involves actual practical work, so online help is limited to method, recording, analysis and the written elements around it. Confirm with the school which one applies before planning.

faqs.question: Which exam series should we plan the tuition around?
faqs.answer: Whichever one the school has entered your child for, and you should confirm it rather than assume. Cambridge runs a February and March series offered only in India, plus May and June and October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May and June. Families are sometimes several months out on their planning because they assumed the common series applied. Everything else, including when to start and when to move to timed papers, follows from that date.

faqs.question: Our connection drops sometimes. Is that a dealbreaker?
faqs.answer: No, though it needs a plan agreed in advance rather than improvised mid-lesson. Sensible arrangements include a phone hotspot as a fallback, a rule that the tutor waits five minutes before rescheduling, and audio-only continuation when video fails but voice holds. Keep the shared document open so work continues even if the call breaks. If the connection fails repeatedly at the same hour each week, move the slot before changing anything else, because the hour is usually the problem.

faqs.question: Should we start in Grade 9 or wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 9, if the aim is anything beyond damage control. Grade 9 looks low-stakes because no examination sits at the end of it, which is exactly why it gets wasted. A student who spends that year learning to write to a mark scheme arrives in Grade 10 needing revision rather than repair, and the tier decision between Core and Extended is made on real evidence instead of guesswork. Starting in Grade 10 still works, but the plan becomes triage rather than building.

A large batch buys pace and price, and gives up individual marking almost entirely.
