h1: IGCSE Tuition in India: Reading the Evidence Before You Start
heroTitle: Decide on IGCSE Tuition in India From Evidence
heroSubtitle: Before you hire anyone, read one marked paper properly. Lost marks tell you whether the problem is content, technique or timing, and the three need completely different help. Some of them need no tuition at all, just a different conversation with the school.
introSummary: IGCSE tuition in India is worth starting only once you know what is actually going wrong, and a marked past paper will tell you that in twenty minutes. Most families decide from a report grade and an anxious feeling, then buy home tuition twice a week for a subject where the student already knows the content and simply runs out of time in Paper 4. This page is a diagnosis, not a sales pitch. It covers how to read a marked script, how to separate a content gap from an exam-technique gap from a timing problem, what belongs with the school first, and the situations where the honest answer is that your child does not need a tutor this year.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you decide whether IGCSE tuition in India is the right next step?
contentBlocks.body:
Work through the evidence in a fixed order, and commit to IGCSE tuition in India only if the last step still says yes. The order matters, because each step rules out a cheaper and faster fix than the one after it.

Start with one recent marked script, ideally a full paper rather than a class test. Sit with it for twenty minutes without your child present, and mark up three categories in different colours: questions where the topic was clearly not known, questions where the topic was known and the marks went missing anyway, and questions left blank or half finished at the end. Those three piles are your diagnosis. A paper dominated by the first pile is a content problem. A paper dominated by the second is technique. A paper with a strong start and a collapsing final page is timing, and timing is often the cheapest of the three to fix.

Then talk to the subject teacher before you talk to a tutor. Ask which topics the class has covered, whether the student asks questions, whether homework arrives complete, and what the teacher would do first. Teachers usually answer this well and are rarely asked. Sometimes they will tell you the student sat the wrong tier for that paper, which changes everything.

Only after those two steps should you decide about paying anyone. And when you do, scope it to the pile that dominated the script rather than to the subject as a whole.
items: 1. Read one full marked paper alone, sorting lost marks into content, technique and timing
2. Ask the subject teacher what they would fix first, before hiring anybody
3. Check the tier and the paper combination the student is actually entered for
4. Scope the help to the dominant pile, not to the whole subject
5. Set a review date four to six weeks out, and write down what should change

contentBlocks.heading: Core or Extended, Cambridge or Edexcel: what the tier says
contentBlocks.body:
Before diagnosing anything, be certain which qualification and tier the student is entered for, because a surprising number of families are not.

IGCSE in India means either Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. The examination calendars differ. Cambridge series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. Grading differs too: Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1.

Tiering is where diagnosis most often goes wrong. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers. Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*. A student capped at C who is being tutored towards an A is being tutored towards something the entry does not allow, and nobody enjoys discovering that in February. Equally, a student struggling badly on Extended papers may be better served by a conversation about tier than by two more hours a week.

So check three things on paper, not from memory: the board, the syllabus code, and the tier. Your child's teacher or examinations officer can confirm all three. Everything else in this page assumes you have.
items: Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1
Core tiers top out at grade C, while Extended tiers reach A*
Confirm board, syllabus code and tier in writing before deciding anything

contentBlocks.heading: What lost marks look like in 0580, 0625 and 0500
contentBlocks.body:
Every subject loses marks in its own characteristic way, and recognising the pattern is most of the diagnosis.

In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, the paper split does the work for you. From the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers per tier. If the non-calculator paper is much weaker, the issue is arithmetic fluency and mental method, which is drillable and does not need an expensive teacher. If the calculator paper collapses in its second half, that is timing. If long multi-step questions lose method marks throughout, that is technique, and it is the most common finding of all.

The sciences give you an even clearer signal, because the assessment is split by skill. For Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses examined from 2023, there is a multiple-choice paper, Paper 1 at Core or Paper 2 at Extended, worth 30%; a theory paper, Paper 3 at Core or Paper 4 at Extended, worth 50%; and practical assessment worth 20% through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, depending on what the school chooses. A student strong on multiple choice and weak on theory in Physics 0625 or Chemistry 0620 has a writing and explanation problem, not a knowledge problem. Weakness concentrated in Paper 6 usually means unfamiliarity with apparatus, variables and graph work rather than missing content. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

Biology 0610 tends to lose marks on command words and precision. Economics 0455 loses them on evaluation and diagram labelling. First Language English 0500 loses them on structure and on running out of time in the longer response. Look at which of these your child's script shows before assuming the subject itself is the problem.
items: Mathematics 0580: a weak non-calculator paper points to fluency, not to understanding
Sciences from 2023: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20% of the grade
Strong multiple choice with weak theory in 0625 or 0620 is an explanation problem
Weak Paper 6 work usually means unfamiliar apparatus and variables, not missing content
Biology 0610: command words; Economics 0455: evaluation; English 0500: structure and timing

contentBlocks.heading: Where IGCSE support is easy to find in India, and where it is not
contentBlocks.body:
Supply shapes what a family can realistically choose after a diagnosis, and it is very uneven across the country. Knowing your local position before you start saves a month of disappointment.

Delhi NCR has the deepest pool for the common subjects. Families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka, or across Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Golf Course Road, will usually find several tutors for 0580 or 0620 quickly. Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are thinner but workable. IGCSE tuition in Delhi is easiest to arrange in the common sciences and hardest for Edexcel-specific subjects, since most local teaching experience is Cambridge.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is similar in depth and different in geometry. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri and Powai have their own pools, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill another, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are better served locally than from the island city. IGCSE tuition in Mumbai for 0500 First Language English is easy to find; a specialist in a minority subject is not.

Bengaluru spreads across Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road, and each belt behaves independently on a weekday. Pune splits between Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Aundh and Wakad on the other, so IGCSE tuition in Pune usually means finding someone on your side of the river. Chennai runs along Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam in the older part of the city, and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar elsewhere. IGCSE tuition in Chennai for the sciences is available, while Economics 0455 specialists are scarcer. Elsewhere, including Kolkata and Ahmedabad, the pool thins quickly outside the common subjects and online becomes the practical route rather than a compromise.
items: Delhi NCR: deepest pool for 0580 and the sciences, thinner for Edexcel syllabuses
Mumbai: island-city pools and the Navi Mumbai and Thane side rarely serve each other
Bengaluru: each belt from Whitefield to Kanakapura Road behaves independently midweek
Pune: expect to find someone on your side of the river, not across it
Chennai: sciences are findable along Adyar and OMR, Economics specialists less so
Outside the metros, online is the practical route for anything beyond common subjects

contentBlocks.heading: What to ask the school in India before hiring anyone
contentBlocks.body:
The school has information no tutor can supply, it costs nothing, and most parents skip straight past it. Ask for a short meeting with the subject teacher, not with the coordinator, and go in with specific questions.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the International Baccalaureate. Anything a school tells you about entries, tiers and deadlines overrides what you read here.

Four questions do most of the work. Which topics has the class actually covered so far, as against the scheme of work? Does the student ask questions in class, or go quiet? Does homework arrive complete and on time? And what would you fix first if this were your child? That last question is the one teachers answer most usefully and are asked least often.

There are also administrative matters worth confirming in the same conversation. Which series is the student entered for, given that Cambridge runs a February and March series in India alongside May and June and October and November. Which tier. Whether the school runs Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the sciences, because preparation differs. Whether there are school-set mock weeks you should plan around.

The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, which means Grade 9 begins with a long, unpressured stretch that most families waste and Grade 10 arrives faster than expected. Autumn of Grade 10 is when the calendar tightens: mocks, coursework where a syllabus has it, and the beginning of serious past-paper work. If you are going to start tuition at all, starting it before that squeeze is worth far more than starting during it.
items: Ask the subject teacher, not the coordinator, and ask what they would fix first
Confirm the entry series, the tier, and whether the school runs Paper 5 or Paper 6
Find out which topics the class has genuinely covered against the scheme of work
The school year runs roughly April to March, so Grade 9 offers the unpressured stretch
Starting before the Grade 10 autumn squeeze is worth more than starting during it

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or a batch: matching delivery to the diagnosis
contentBlocks.body:
Once you know which of the three problems you have, the delivery almost chooses itself. This is the step families usually take first and should take last.

A content gap needs teaching, and teaching travels. If whole topics are missing in Chemistry 0620, the priority is a teacher who explains well, and whether they sit at your table or appear on a screen matters much less than their subject depth. Online widens the pool sharply here, and for a family outside the big metros it may be the only way to reach someone who has taught the syllabus rather than merely the subject.

A technique gap is where home tuition earns its fee. Method marks lost mid-solution, working never written down, command words read carelessly, diagrams thrown together: these are visible only while the student writes, and a tutor beside them interrupts at the right second. Home classes also suit a student who needs supervision more than instruction.

A timing problem needs supervised practice under the clock, and that can be done anywhere. A batch at a coaching centre often does this well and cheaply, because everyone sits the same paper at the same time and the pressure feels real. The trade-off is that nobody diagnoses your child individually.

Hybrid is the arrangement many Grade 10 households settle on: one home visit each week for written work, and one shorter online session for doubt-solving or a timed paper. It keeps a good tutor who lives far away and keeps the week intact through monsoon in Mumbai or a heavy traffic spell in Bengaluru. Choose by diagnosis, and revisit the choice when the diagnosis changes.
items: Content gap: choose subject depth, and accept online if that is where depth lives
Technique gap: home tuition, because the errors happen while the pen is moving
Timing problem: supervised timed papers, which a batch often delivers cheaply
Hybrid: a weekly home visit plus one online session keeps a distant tutor usable
Revisit the delivery when the diagnosis changes, usually after the first mock

contentBlocks.heading: Is this tutor right for the problem you actually have?
contentBlocks.body:
Match the tutor to the diagnosis, not to the subject name. A brilliant teacher of content is not automatically the right person for a student who knows the content and loses marks through careless setting out.

IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified: identity, the qualifications claimed, the syllabuses and levels taught, and the subjects they will be matched for. That establishes who the person is and what they have done, which is the starting point and not the finish. The rest you check in the trial session.

Bring the marked script to that session. Ask the tutor to read it in front of you and say what they see. A strong tutor will name the pattern within a few minutes, distinguish a content gap from a technique one, and ask which tier and series the student is entered for. A weak one will talk about covering the syllabus from the beginning. That single exercise tells you more than any credential.

Ask also what they will not do. An honest tutor will say that coursework and controlled assessment must be the student's own work, that they cannot promise a grade, and that a particular problem needs the school rather than them. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anybody offering one before reading a single script has told you their method.

For younger students working at home, keep the practical safeguards in place: an open-door room, an adult somewhere in the flat, and an identity check on the first visit. These are ordinary professional arrangements and no reasonable tutor objects to them.
items: Bring the marked script to the trial and ask the tutor to read it aloud
Listen for a named pattern within minutes, not an offer to restart the syllabus
A good tutor asks which tier and which examination series before planning
Verified profiles cover identity, qualifications, syllabuses taught and subjects matched
Any promise of a grade made before reading a script is a warning sign

contentBlocks.heading: Content gap, technique gap or timing problem?
contentBlocks.body:
Content, technique and timing account for nearly every disappointing result, and for nearly every request for IGCSE tuition in India, they look identical on a report card, and they need entirely different responses. Telling them apart is the whole skill.

A content gap means the student genuinely does not know the material. On the script it looks like blank starts, a definition attempted in vague words, or a topic answered from general reasoning rather than from taught knowledge. Ask the student to explain the topic aloud and the gap becomes obvious in about a minute. This is the case where teaching is required, and where a good tutor is worth the money, because the school has moved on and the class will not go back.

A technique gap looks completely different. The student knows the material and says so, often with some irritation. The marks disappear in the margins: method not shown in 0580, units missing, a command word like describe answered as though it said explain, an Economics diagram drawn without axis labels, a conclusion that restates rather than evaluates. The knowledge is intact and the mark scheme is not being addressed. This is fixable relatively quickly, and it is the most common diagnosis of the three.

A timing problem announces itself on the last page. Strong answers up to question 6, then compression, then a blank. Or a student who spends fifteen minutes on a four-mark question because they refuse to move on. Timing is a behaviour, and it responds to supervised practice under the clock rather than to more teaching. It also responds, occasionally, to nothing more than being told explicitly to leave a question and come back.

One caution. All three can be masked by a fourth thing: a student who has decided they are bad at the subject. No tuition fixes that in the first fortnight, and pushing harder usually makes it worse.
items: Content gap: blank starts, vague definitions, answers built from general reasoning
Technique gap: right knowledge, missing method, misread command words, unlabelled diagrams
Timing problem: a strong first half and a compressed or blank final page
Ask the student to explain the topic aloud; a content gap shows itself in a minute
A student who has decided they are bad at the subject needs a different conversation

contentBlocks.heading: How long should home tuition in India run before you judge it?
contentBlocks.body:
Give IGCSE tuition in India four to six sessions, then review against what you wrote down at the start. If you did not write anything down at the start, that is the first thing to fix, because a vague sense that things are better is not a basis for spending another six months.

What should have changed depends on your diagnosis. For a content gap, the student should be able to explain the previously missing topic without prompting, and should attempt questions on it rather than skipping them. For a technique gap, the script should look different: working written out, units present, command words underlined, diagrams labelled. For a timing problem, the last page should be attempted, even imperfectly. Marks move later than behaviour does, and a student who finishes the paper at a lower accuracy is usually on a better path than one who is accurate and unfinished.

Now the uncomfortable part. Over-tutoring is genuinely common in Grade 10, and it costs more than money. A student in four tuitions has no unstructured study time, and unstructured study time is when learning consolidates. They stop attempting anything alone because someone will explain it on Thursday. They sleep less. Grades sometimes dip. If your child is being tutored in four subjects and still struggling, adding a fifth is not the answer.

And there are cases where no tuition is right at all. A student a grade below where they want to be, who works steadily and asks questions in class, usually needs past papers and a deadline rather than a tutor. So does a student whose only real issue is that they have never sat a full paper under timed conditions. Those are free fixes. Try them first.
items: Write down what should change before the first session, then review after four to six
Behaviour changes first: working shown, units present, the final page attempted
Four simultaneous tuitions removes the unstructured study time learning depends on
A steady student one grade short usually needs timed papers, not a tutor
If nothing has changed in six sessions, change the tutor or change the diagnosis

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IGCSE tuition in India: what to bring to the first session
contentBlocks.body:
If the evidence says hire, then buy IGCSE tuition in India precisely rather than enthusiastically. A well-scoped start is worth more than an enthusiastic one.

Have three documents ready: the most recent full marked script, the latest report, and a note of the board, syllabus code and tier. Add the school's mock dates and the examination series the student is entered for. That handful of pages lets a tutor plan a term in the first twenty minutes instead of spending three sessions working out where the student is.

Say what you want changed, in behaviour terms. Not a target grade. Something like: finishes Paper 4 with ten minutes to spare, or writes out method in every multi-step question, or can explain electrolysis without notes. Targets like these can be checked in six weeks by anybody, including your child, and they keep the arrangement honest.

Then decide delivery from the diagnosis rather than from habit. Home tuition for technique and supervision, online for reach and scarce subjects, a batch for timed practice, hybrid when the household needs both. Say which you prefer and whether you are flexible, because flexibility widens the shortlist considerably.

IB Gram asks about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shares a shortlist of verified tutors matched to that scope. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on the subject, the tier and the slot, and the weeks before a series are the hardest time to start anything.
items: Bring a full marked script, the latest report, and the board, code and tier in writing
Add mock dates and the examination series the student is actually entered for
State the change you want as a behaviour, not as a target grade
Pick delivery from the diagnosis: home classes, online, a batch, or hybrid
Say where you are flexible, since it widens the shortlist immediately
Ask early; the weeks just before a series are the hardest time to start

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child actually needs IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Read one full marked paper before you decide anything. Sort the lost marks into three piles: topics not known, topics known but marks missed anyway, and questions left unfinished. A paper full of the first pile means teaching is needed. The second means technique, which is faster to fix. The third means timing, which often needs supervised practice rather than a tutor at all. Then ask the subject teacher what they would fix first. Many families discover that the honest answer is past papers and a deadline.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a content gap and a technique gap?
faqs.answer: A content gap means the student cannot explain the topic; a technique gap means they can explain it and still lose the marks. On a script, a content gap shows as blank starts and vague definitions, while a technique gap shows as missing method in 0580, absent units, a command word misread, or an unlabelled Economics diagram. The quickest test is to ask your child to explain the topic aloud. If the explanation is fluent and the script is still poor, you have a technique problem, and that usually resolves faster.

faqs.question: Should I speak to the school before hiring a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be your first move rather than your last. Ask the subject teacher which topics the class has genuinely covered, whether your child asks questions, whether homework arrives complete, and what they would fix first. Confirm the examination series, the tier, and whether the school runs Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the sciences. These conversations cost nothing, take twenty minutes, and quite often remove the need to hire anyone. Teachers are rarely asked directly and usually answer well.

faqs.question: Is home tuition better than online for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the diagnosis. Home tuition is the stronger choice for a technique problem, because errors in setting out only appear while the student is writing, and for a student who needs supervision more than explanation. Online is stronger for a content gap, since it widens the pool to teachers who have actually taught your syllabus and tier. Many Grade 10 families in Bengaluru and Pune end up hybrid: one home visit each week plus a shorter online session for doubt-solving or a timed paper.

faqs.question: My child scored well in Grade 9 and dropped in Grade 10. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because Grade 10 assesses differently rather than because the student got worse. Papers get longer, questions combine topics, command words become stricter, and the calculator and non-calculator split in Mathematics 0580 exposes fluency gaps that class tests never touched. A drop of this kind is most often a technique and timing issue. Read the script before assuming otherwise, and check the tier, because a student sitting Extended papers for the first time will see marks fall even with unchanged understanding.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we take tuition in at once?
faqs.answer: Ideally one, occasionally two, and very rarely more. A Grade 10 student in four tuitions has no unstructured study time left, and unstructured study time is when learning consolidates. Students in that position often stop attempting work alone, because someone will explain it later in the week, and their sleep suffers. If everything looks weak at once, the problem is bigger than any single subject and belongs in a conversation with the school. Adding another tutor to a full timetable rarely helps.

faqs.question: How long before we can tell whether tuition is working?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions, judged against something written down before the first one. Look for behaviour rather than marks: method written out, units present, command words underlined, the final page attempted. Marks follow behaviour by a term, not a fortnight. If nothing has changed in six sessions, either the diagnosis was wrong or the tutor is not the right match for it, and both are worth saying out loud rather than waiting for the next report to decide for you.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework or controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Only within the rules, and the rules are strict. Coursework must be the student's own work, so a tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what the criteria ask for, and question the reasoning. They may not write, rewrite or edit the submission. Your school will explain exactly what supervision and authentication its syllabuses require, and any honest tutor will refer you there rather than offering more. If a tutor offers to produce the work, that offer puts the entry itself at risk.

faqs.question: We live in Thane and cannot find a 0455 tutor nearby. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Widen to online rather than settle for a generalist. Economics 0455 has a thinner pool than the sciences in most Indian cities, and this comes up regularly in Thane, Navi Mumbai, Greater Noida and parts of Chennai beyond Old Mahabalipuram Road. A specialist teaching the actual syllabus on a screen will usually outperform a nearby teacher who knows economics in general. If supervision is also needed, arrange one home visit a month and keep the weekly teaching online.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the final term before the exams?
faqs.answer: It is not too late, but it changes what tuition can honestly do. With a few weeks left, the work shifts from teaching content to protecting marks: timed papers, the highest-yield topics, and a deliberate decision about what to abandon. A student weak in five topics with four weeks left cannot fix five. A good tutor will name the two worth saving and say plainly that the others are being sacrificed. Expect that conversation, and be sceptical of anyone who promises otherwise.

faqs.question: Does a higher tier automatically mean a better grade?
faqs.answer: No, and the tier question deserves a proper conversation with the school. Many Cambridge subjects offer Core and Extended tiers, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. A student placed on Extended who consistently finds those papers out of reach may score better, and feel considerably better, on Core. Equally, a capable student capped at C is being limited by the entry. Ask the subject teacher which tier they recommend and why, and confirm what has actually been entered.

faqs.question: What should we prepare for the first session at home?
faqs.answer: Three documents and a quiet table. Bring the most recent full marked script, the latest report, and a written note of the board, syllabus code and tier, along with the school's mock dates. Clear a table with good light and a plug point, keep the television off, and have the textbook and notebook out before the tutor arrives. A tutor who can read a marked script in the first ten minutes will plan a better term than one who spends three sessions discovering where the student is.

h1: IGCSE Tuition Classes in India: Formats, Batches and Timetables
heroTitle: IGCSE Class Formats and Timetables Across India
heroSubtitle: One-to-one, a small batch, a past-paper clinic, a revision course before the series: four different products that all get called classes. They suit different students and they return marked work at very different speeds. This page sorts out which is which, and how each one fits around a Grade 10 timetable.
introSummary: IGCSE tuition classes in India come in four shapes: one-to-one home classes or online lessons, a small group batch, a past-paper clinic that marks timed work, and a short revision course run before a series. Each does a different job. A batch suits a student who understands the content and needs pace. A clinic suits one who knows the material and loses marks on the paper itself. One-to-one suits a problem that is specific to this student and this syllabus. The format matters far more than the provider's name, and two things decide it: how quickly written work comes back marked, and whether the timetable survives an ordinary Grade 10 school day with sport, prep and travel already in it.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a student to IGCSE tuition classes in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Format is settled before anybody is named. You send a query or book a free consultation, and the questions that follow are about the board and syllabus, the tier the school has entered the student for, the subjects, the school calendar and the hours that are actually free once a Grade 10 day has taken its share. A student doing well in Chemistry theory and badly in the alternative to practical does not need the same class as one who has not understood moles.

The second question is about evidence. Bring the last marked paper rather than a description of the problem. Marks lost on recall, marks lost on method and marks lost on reading the question look identical on a report card and need three different formats. This is the single most useful thing a parent can do before choosing anything.

Then the shortlist. Verified tutor profiles are matched against board, syllabus, subject and tier, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Ask in that session what the tutor would set in week one and when it would come back marked. Marking turnaround is the quiet difference between a class that works and one that fills an evening.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. Be specific: too fast, too slow, no written work, or a group that turned out to mix tiers. Availability of any particular format at any particular hour depends on subject, tier and schedule, and a Saturday morning batch in a small city is a harder thing to find than a weekday one-to-one online.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with board, syllabus and tier
2. Send the last marked paper, not a description of what went wrong
3. Choose the format from that evidence: one-to-one, batch, clinic or revision course
4. Take a trial session and ask when written work comes back marked
5. Fix the weekly hour against the school timetable before paying for a term

contentBlocks.heading: Core or Extended: which tier should the class teach?
contentBlocks.body:
The tier decides the class, and the school decides the tier. In India, IGCSE means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, normally taught across Grades 9 and 10 and followed by the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses having 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout.

That single fact rules out a lot of group classes. A batch containing Core and Extended candidates in the same subject is teaching two different papers at once, and one half of the room is always being underserved. Ask the question directly before enrolling: which tier is this class taught to, and what happens to a student sitting the other one.

The sciences make it concrete. For Cambridge sciences examined from 2023, Core candidates sit Paper 1 multiple choice and Paper 3 theory, Extended candidates sit Paper 2 multiple choice and Paper 4 theory, and practical work is assessed through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, with the school choosing which. Weighting runs 30 per cent multiple choice, 50 per cent theory and 20 per cent practical. Pearson Edexcel sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills examined inside the written papers.

So a class that never distinguishes Paper 5 from Paper 6 preparation is not really teaching your child's course. Ask which one the school has entered, and ask the class to say what it does differently for each.
items: Cambridge Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1
A batch mixing Core and Extended candidates underserves one half of the room
Cambridge sciences: Paper 1 or 2 multiple choice, Paper 3 or 4 theory
Practical is Paper 5 or Paper 6, and the school chooses which
Edexcel sciences are untiered, with practical skills inside the written papers

contentBlocks.heading: Subject classes at home and online, syllabus by syllabus
contentBlocks.body:
Syllabus codes are the fastest way to tell whether a class is real. Ask for the code, then ask what the class does about the parts of it that lose marks.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the subject most often taught as a batch, and it works there for a student who is fluent and slow rather than confused. Where a student is confused, a group moves past the gap and the gap widens. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 both reward a class built around question types rather than chapters, because the theory paper rewards precision of wording that no amount of reading produces on its own. Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is the volume subject: the topic list is long, so a class here should be spending its time on planned revisiting rather than on first coverage.

Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 works well in a small group, since discussion genuinely improves evaluation answers and students learn from hearing a weaker argument dismantled. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 is the opposite. Writing is personal, and a class of twelve cannot mark twelve pieces of extended writing every week with any useful detail, which is why English at IGCSE so often disappoints in a batch and improves quickly one-to-one.

Home classes have an advantage the others do not for subjects with a lot of written working. A tutor beside the student sees the method abandoned halfway, the units left off, the diagram drawn too small to label. Online works well for multiple choice drilling, for data questions, and for any subject where the work is discussion and text. Split by subject rather than picking one format for everything.
items: Ask for the syllabus code before anything else: 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0455, 0500
Mathematics 0580 suits a batch only when the student is fluent but slow
Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620 classes should be built around question types
Biology 0610 needs planned revisiting, not first coverage, from a class
First Language English 0500 rarely works in a large batch; marking cannot keep up

contentBlocks.heading: Where class formats actually exist across India
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tuition classes in India are not evenly distributed, and the gap widens sharply outside the biggest cities. In Delhi NCR the full range exists: batches and revision courses run in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon), Golf Course Road, Noida and Sector 128 Noida, while Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are thinner and mostly one-to-one. A parent looking for an IGCSE tuition class in Delhi should ask where the class physically sits before enrolling, because an advertised centre address and the actual teaching location are sometimes different.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has depth and a travel problem. An IGCSE tuition class in Mumbai held in Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli or Lower Parel means a school-night journey for a student in Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar or even Powai, and that journey is the reason batches lose students by December. Hyderabad concentrates hard: Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District have the most options, with Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills close behind, while Secunderabad and Kokapet families travel or move online. Anyone searching for an IGCSE tuition class in Hyderabad should ask about the batch size before the address.

Gujarat runs on a smaller scale. An IGCSE tuition class in Ahmedabad is usually found around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar reachable at fixed hours, and Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot supporting one-to-one far more reliably than any group.

Central and western India is where IGCSE classes near me stops returning anything useful. Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa have small IGCSE cohorts spread across few schools, so an IGCSE batch class in a specific subject at a specific tier may simply not exist. Online groups solve this properly: a small online batch can gather eight students on the same syllabus from eight different cities. The same reasoning applies to an IGCSE tuition class in Bangalore, in Chennai, in Pune and in Kolkata once you get past the mainstream subjects and into a scarce one.
items: Delhi NCR has the full range; Faridabad and Ghaziabad are mostly one-to-one
Mumbai: a batch across town is a school-night journey that ends by December
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, HITEC City and Madhapur hold most of the group options
Gujarat beyond Ahmedabad supports one-to-one far better than any batch
Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Goa: online groups gather a cohort that no city has

contentBlocks.heading: Timetabling around a Grade 10 school day in India
contentBlocks.body:
Work out the free hours before choosing the class, not afterwards. A Grade 10 student in India typically leaves the house early, returns in the late afternoon, and then has school work, an activity or two and travel already spoken for. What is left is usually two weekday evening slots and a weekend morning, and a family that books three classes into that space has built a timetable nobody can keep.

The series matters as much as the week. Cambridge exam series run in February/March, which is offered only in India, in May/June, and in October/November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The February/March series exists precisely so that Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for entry to the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels in the same academic year. Schools decide which series they enter students for, and a student cannot choose a series independently of the school, so confirm the date with the school before booking anything described as a pre-series course.

That single confirmation prevents the commonest mistake of the year. A revision course timed for May/June is useless to a student sitting February/March, and the two cohorts are often sitting in the same room in October.

For equivalence questions, the Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and families should check current requirements with the university or board concerned rather than assume. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.
items: Map the free hours first: usually two weekday evenings and a weekend morning
Cambridge series: February/March in India, May/June, and October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June
The school chooses the series; confirm the date before booking a revision course
Check equivalence requirements with the university or board, not with a class

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online groups or a hybrid Grade 10 week?
contentBlocks.body:
Home classes are the most accountable, online classes are the most available, and a hybrid week is what most Grade 10 families end up with once February approaches. Nobody plans it that way in June.

A home class cannot quietly become a shorter class. The tutor is in the room, the work is on the table, and a student cannot half-attend while a phone sits out of the camera's view. It costs travel, which shows up as a narrower choice of tutor and a rate that reflects an evening crossing a city. Online classes remove that entirely and open up small groups that no single locality could fill, which matters enormously for a scarce subject or a specific tier. What online costs is supervision: a Grade 10 student working alone in a bedroom is easier to lose than one at the dining table with a tutor beside them.

Hybrid is the useful middle for this stage. Keep one home class a week for the subject where written method needs watching, and take the rest online, including the past-paper clinic, where the work is marking and feedback rather than teaching. During the last month before a series, add short online sessions rather than extra travel.

There is one arrangement worth avoiding. Booking home classes for every subject in Grade 10 fills the week with travel that the tutor pays for and the student waits through, and by January two of those slots will have quietly moved online anyway.

Whichever way you go, write the mode against each subject in advance. A family that decides mode on the evening will be entirely online by January, without anyone having chosen that.
items: Home classes: hardest to shorten, highest accountability, narrowest choice of tutor
Online classes: widest choice, and small groups that one locality could not fill
Hybrid: one home class for written method, the rest online including the clinic
In the last month before a series, add online time rather than extra travel
Decide the mode per subject in advance or the week drifts entirely online

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before enrolling in any class?
contentBlocks.body:
Six questions, and all of them are answerable in one phone call. Which syllabus code and which tier is the class taught to? How many students are in the room, this term, not at capacity? Who marks the written work and how many days does it take to come back? Which past-paper series will be used and where do the markschemes come from? Does the same teacher take the class all year? And what happens if the student joins late or misses three weeks around a school trip?

If the answers are confident and specific, the class is probably run by somebody who has done it before. If the answer to the marking question is that work is discussed in class, you are enrolling in a lecture.

For a tutor who will teach at your house, the checks are slightly different. Identity, claimed qualifications and teaching experience are verified before a profile is shortlisted through IB Gram, and profiles are matched to board, syllabus, subject and tier. Beyond that, agree the arrival window, the rescheduling rule and gate entry at the start, and fix a single study space in the house.

One warning about language. No tutor and no class can guarantee a grade, and anything that promises a specific result, a jump of two grades or a particular percentage deserves scepticism rather than a deposit. A class that instead tells you honestly which paper the student is losing marks on, and how it plans to fix that, is giving you something far more useful.
items: Ask for the syllabus code and the tier the class is actually taught to
Ask the current number of students in the room, not the advertised capacity
Ask who marks written work and how many days it takes to return
Ask whether the same teacher takes the class for the whole year
Ask what happens if the student joins late or misses three weeks

contentBlocks.heading: Four IGCSE class formats in India, and who each one suits
contentBlocks.body:
One-to-one, run as home classes or online, is diagnosis and repair. A tutor works from this student's marked papers, finds what is actually going wrong, and rebuilds it. It suits a student whose problem is specific: a topic never understood, a method half-learned, writing that never reaches the standard the markscheme rewards. It is the most expensive hour and often the fewest hours needed.

A small batch of three or four is pace and comparison. It suits a student who broadly understands the subject and needs to move faster, to see harder questions, and to hear how somebody else answered the same thing. It fails when the group mixes tiers, when the students are at different points in the syllabus, or when the batch quietly grows to nine over a term.

A past-paper clinic is the format Indian families use least and probably need most. It is not teaching. The student sits a timed section, the work is marked against the actual markscheme, and the session is spent on why marks were lost: a command word misread, a unit dropped, an evaluation that never evaluated. A good clinic produces three things every week, and you should ask for all three: a marked script, a list of the specific errors, and the next paper to sit. If a clinic produces only a score, it is a test centre.

A pre-series revision course is compression. Two to four weeks, the whole syllabus at speed, usually in a group, timed just before a series. It suits a student who has kept up and needs consolidation. It does very little for one who has not, because there is no time to teach anything properly, and that is the honest limit nobody advertises.
items: One-to-one: diagnosis and repair for a specific, personal problem
Small batch of three or four: pace, harder questions and peer comparison
Past-paper clinic: timed section, marked against the markscheme, errors named
A clinic should produce a marked script, an error list and the next paper
Pre-series revision course: consolidation for a student who has kept up
A revision course cannot teach a syllabus that was never learned

contentBlocks.heading: Batch size and marking turnaround: what to expect in India
contentBlocks.body:
Batch size is really a marking question. A teacher with four students can mark four extended answers properly between sessions and return them with comments the student can act on. The same teacher with sixteen students cannot, so the work either goes unmarked, gets marked by somebody else, or gets discussed in class as a model answer while nobody's own script is corrected. Ask how many, and ask who marks.

A reasonable expectation for IGCSE tuition classes in India is written work returned within a week, with the errors named rather than a score written at the top. For a past-paper clinic it should be faster, because the marking is the product. For a large batch before a series, honest providers will tell you that only selected work is marked in detail, and that is fine as long as they say so.

Now the limits worth stating plainly. A class cannot make up two years of missed foundation in eight weeks. A student sitting Core cannot reach A* in that subject, because Core tops out at grade C, so the useful conversation there is about whether the school will move them to Extended and by when. A student joining a batch in January for a February/March series is joining at the point where the group is consolidating, not teaching.

And progress shows in a specific order. First the marks lost on reading the question disappear. Then method errors drop. Then content gaps close, which is slowest. If nothing has changed in the first category after six weeks, the format is wrong rather than the effort.
items: Four students is markable every week; sixteen is not, whatever is advertised
Expect written work back within a week, with errors named rather than scored
Core tops out at grade C, so the tier conversation belongs with the school
A revision course cannot replace two years of missed foundation work
Progress order: question-reading errors first, then method, then content gaps

contentBlocks.heading: A revision plan for the weeks before the series, at home
contentBlocks.body:
The last stretch is where families buy the most and gain the least, and it is where IGCSE tuition classes in India get booked all at once instead of in sequence. Here is a plan that fits around school and does not need a crash course to work. It assumes roughly eight weeks and a student who has covered the syllabus.

Run it at home wherever you can. Printed past papers, a markscheme in a separate folder, a timer, and one binder per subject beat any amount of new material bought in the final month. Home classes in this period should be short and frequent rather than long, because a tired Grade 10 student learns nothing after ninety minutes on a school night.

What IB Gram does at this point is deliberately limited. You send a query or book a free consultation. You are asked about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule. Verified tutor profiles that match are shortlisted. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Classes run at home, online or as a hybrid week, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match. Availability in the weeks before a series depends on subject, tier and schedule, and the good slots go early.

One last note for parents. In the final fortnight, reduce the tuition rather than adding to it. The marks are won by sitting papers and correcting them, and a student with three classes and no time to correct anything will walk into the hall having practised very little of what the examiner is going to ask.
items: 1. Weeks eight to six: sit one full past paper per subject, untimed, and mark it honestly
2. Weeks six to four: list the topics that lost marks, and teach only those
3. Week four: switch to timed sections, one a day, rotating across subjects
4. Week three: work through the markscheme wording for the errors that keep repeating
5. Week two: sit two full timed papers per subject under real conditions
6. Final week: correction and sleep only, with tuition reduced rather than increased

faqs.question: How big should an IGCSE batch be before it stops working?
faqs.answer: Past four or five students, written work stops being marked properly, and that is the point at which a batch becomes a lecture. The teaching can still be good. What disappears is individual correction, which is where most IGCSE marks are actually recovered. Ask how many students are enrolled this term rather than the advertised maximum, ask who marks the scripts, and ask how long marking takes. A class of twelve that returns a marked extended-writing piece every week is doing something unusual, so ask how.

faqs.question: What exactly is a past-paper clinic and what should it produce?
faqs.answer: It is a marking session rather than a teaching session. The student sits a timed section under conditions, the work is marked against the published markscheme, and the hour goes on why each mark was lost. A clinic should produce three things every week: the marked script, a written list of the specific errors, and the next paper to attempt. If all you receive is a score out of the total, it is a test centre and it will not change anything. Clinics suit students who know the content and lose marks on the paper.

faqs.question: Are home classes better than a centre batch for Grade 9 and 10?
faqs.answer: For a student with a specific gap, yes; for a student who simply needs pace and structure, often no. Home classes remove travel on a school night, make the session impossible to half-attend, and let the tutor see written method as it happens. A centre batch gives structure, a fixed routine and a much lower cost per hour, and some students work better with other students in the room. Decide by looking at a marked paper: a personal gap points home, a pacing problem points to a batch.

faqs.question: Can one class cover both Cambridge and Edexcel students?
faqs.answer: Not well, and it is worth asking before enrolling. The two systems differ in series dates, in grading, and in how practical work is assessed: Cambridge sciences use Paper 5 or Paper 6 for practical, while Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Cambridge is tiered in many subjects while Edexcel International GCSE is graded 9 to 1 throughout. A teacher can handle both in one-to-one teaching without difficulty. A group has to pick one, and a group that says it covers both is usually teaching to neither.

faqs.question: We are in Nagpur and no local batch exists for our subject. What works?
faqs.answer: A small online group is the format that solves this, and it is the reason online classes exist at all. Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik and Goa each have small IGCSE cohorts spread thinly, so a subject at a specific tier may have three interested students in the whole city. Online, a group of six on the same syllabus and tier is entirely possible. Keep one home class a week for any subject where written method needs watching, and run the rest of the week online.

faqs.question: When should we start a revision course before the series?
faqs.answer: Confirm the series first, then count back about eight weeks. Cambridge series run in February/March, which is offered only in India, May/June and October/November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Schools decide which series a student is entered for, so ask the school rather than assuming. Eight weeks gives room for one full paper per subject, a list of the topics that lost marks, and then timed practice. Starting in the last fortnight buys stress rather than marks.

faqs.question: Does a crash course work if the student has fallen badly behind?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is worth being blunt about why. A crash course compresses a syllabus for students who have already met it, so a student with two years of gaps spends the whole course watching material go past. What works better in that position is one-to-one teaching on the highest-weighted parts of the paper, plus a realistic conversation with the school about the tier. Core tops out at grade C in Cambridge subjects, and knowing which tier the student is entered for changes what the remaining weeks should target.

faqs.question: How do we fit classes around a Grade 10 school day in Mumbai or Hyderabad?
faqs.answer: Map the free hours before booking anything. Most Grade 10 students in India have two usable weekday evening slots and one weekend morning after school, activities and travel are counted. A batch in Bandra or Lower Parel is a long school-night journey from Thane or Navi Mumbai, and a centre in Gachibowli or Madhapur is a real trip from Secunderabad. Where travel eats an hour each way, take that subject online and save the home class for the one that needs a tutor in the room.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one worth it for Mathematics 0580, or is a batch enough?
faqs.answer: A batch is enough when the student understands the topics and is simply slow or careless; one-to-one is needed when a specific topic was never learned. The test is the marked paper. If marks are being lost across many topics in small amounts, that is pace and practice, which a group handles well. If a whole question type returns zero every time, a group will move past it again. Many families run 0580 in a batch and add four one-to-one sessions on the two topics that keep failing.

faqs.question: Should the same teacher take the class all year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask the question before you enrol. Continuity matters more at IGCSE than families expect, because the teacher who marked September's script is the one who knows which error has repeated four times. A class that rotates teachers loses that memory every time, and the student restarts the explanation. Where a change is unavoidable, ask for the written record of what has been covered and what keeps going wrong to be handed over. If no such record exists, that answer tells you something on its own.

faqs.question: How many subjects can realistically be taught in home classes at once?
faqs.answer: Two is comfortable, three is a stretch, and four means nothing gets corrected. Every home class or online class sets work, and work between sessions is where the improvement actually happens, so four classes a week produce four sets of tasks that a Grade 10 student with school prep cannot complete. Choose the two subjects where the marks lost are largest and most fixable, run those properly, and revisit after six weeks. Families who spread thinly across every subject usually see less movement than those who fix two and leave the rest alone.

The test is the marked paper. If marks are being lost across many topics in small amounts, that is pace and practice, which a group handles well. If a whole question type returns zero every time, a group will move past it again. Many families run 0580 in a batch and add four one-to-one sessions on the two topics that keep failing.

mainEntity.name: Should the same teacher take the class all year?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and ask the question before you enrol. Continuity matters more at IGCSE than families expect, because the teacher who marked September's script is the one who knows which error has repeated four times. A class that rotates teachers loses that memory every time, and the student restarts the explanation. Where a change is unavoidable, ask for the written record of what has been covered and what keeps going wrong to be handed over. If no such record exists, that answer tells you something on its own.

mainEntity.name: How many subjects can realistically be taught in home classes at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two is comfortable, three is a stretch, and four means nothing gets corrected. Every home class or online class sets work, and work between sessions is where the improvement actually happens, so four classes a week produce four sets of tasks that a Grade 10 student with school prep cannot complete. Choose the two subjects where the marks lost are largest and most fixable, run those properly, and revisit after six weeks. Families who spread thinly across every subject usually see less movement than those who fix two and leave the rest alone.

IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who match. A trial session can be arranged first, classes run at home, online or hybrid, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.
