h1: IGCSE Coaching in India: Where the Coaching Model Fits and Fails
heroTitle: The Batch Model Tested Against IGCSE in India
heroSubtitle: Coaching is a method, not a verdict. Repetition builds speed on a non-calculator Mathematics paper and does almost nothing for a six-mark explanation in Physics. This page separates the two, subject by subject, so you can enrol where a batch works and refuse it where it does not.
introSummary: IGCSE coaching in India is worth judging subject by subject rather than accepting or rejecting the whole model, and for several syllabuses home tuition does the job a batch cannot. Heavy repetition genuinely works on parts of Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, where a hundred similar questions build the speed a non-calculator paper demands. It fails on Physics 0625 explanation questions and on First Language English 0500 writing, because no batch can mark thirty scripts properly every week. This page sets out where the model fits, what a centre should show you before you pay, the marking numbers that decide whether a batch can teach writing at all, and the cases where a coaching class beats a private tutor outright.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Judge IGCSE Coaching in India Before Enrolling?
contentBlocks.body:
By splitting the decision by subject instead of by provider. IGCSE coaching in India is not one purchase; it is a separate judgement for every syllabus on the timetable. A family rarely needs coaching for everything, and the useful question is which one or two syllabuses would genuinely benefit from a batch and which would be damaged by one. IB Gram approaches it the same way: the query establishes the board, the syllabus codes, the tier, the school's exam series, your locality and your schedule, and only then does a shortlist make sense.

Start from evidence rather than impression. Pull the last two marked papers and sort the lost marks into three piles: marks lost because the student did not know the content, marks lost because the method was slow or careless, and marks lost because the answer did not say what the question asked for. The second pile is where drill helps. The third pile is where drill makes things worse, because repetition of a badly structured answer simply makes the habit permanent.

Then ask what the batch actually does with written work. A centre that sets past papers and returns them ticked is running attendance, not teaching. A centre that returns a script with the mark scheme wording against each lost mark is doing something a batch can genuinely do at scale. The difference is visible in a single returned paper, so ask to see one before enrolling.

Where a batch is wrong for a subject, the alternatives are a home tutor or an online one-to-one tutor, and there is no need to keep everything in one place. Plenty of families in Delhi NCR and Hyderabad run Mathematics in a batch and English at home, which is usually the correct arrangement rather than a compromise. Availability depends on the subject, the tier and the time of year, so decide the shape early in Grade 9 rather than after the first Grade 10 mock.
items: 1. Sort lost marks into content, method and question-reading before choosing anything.
2. Pick the batch only for subjects where the method pile dominates.
3. Ask to see one returned, marked script from the actual batch teacher.
4. Cover the remaining subjects with a home tutor or online one-to-one.
5. Review the split after the first Grade 10 mock, not before.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge, Edexcel, Core and Extended: What a Batch Must Track
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means either Cambridge IGCSE, offered by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a coaching batch that treats them as interchangeable will teach the wrong paper structure to half the room. The course usually runs two years across Grades 9 and 10, and is often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11.

The exam series differ, and they matter for planning. Cambridge series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, in May and June, and in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. A batch built around one calendar will be out of step with students entered for another, so ask which series the centre plans towards and whether it runs a separate group for each.

Tiering is the other thing a batch must handle honestly. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. A mixed batch containing both Core and Extended candidates is teaching two different courses in one room, and the Core students usually pay for it in confusion while the Extended students pay for it in pace.

Mathematics shows the problem most clearly. Under Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 from the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers per tier. Those are not small differences. Ask which papers the batch is preparing for, by code.
items: Cambridge or Edexcel: confirm which board the school actually enters students for
Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*, so mixed batches serve neither well
0580 Extended means Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one
Edexcel 4MA1 is Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier

contentBlocks.heading: Where Drill Works and Where It Fails, Syllabus by Syllabus
contentBlocks.body:
The whole case for IGCSE coaching in India rests on one distinction. Drill works where the skill is a procedure that must become automatic, and it fails where the skill is a judgement that must be made freshly each time. That single distinction predicts almost every good and bad outcome families report from coaching.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the strongest case for repetition, particularly for the non-calculator papers. Arithmetic fluency, index laws, surds, algebraic manipulation, factorising, solving linear and quadratic equations, working with ratio and percentage change: all of these improve with volume, and a batch can supply volume cheaply. A student who has worked through a hundred rearrangements stops thinking about rearranging and starts thinking about the problem. Physics 0625 shares some of this, because the syllabus requires students to recall and rearrange the equations, and recall responds well to repetition across motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics and space physics. Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 makes a similar demand.

Now the failures. Physics 0625 explanation questions are where drill collapses. Asking why the reading on an ammeter changes, in a way that earns every mark, requires a student to select the right physical idea, order the statements correctly and connect cause to effect in their own words. Thirty students write thirty different answers, each wrong in a different way, and a batch teacher cannot diagnose thirty different faults in a week.

English is worse still, because English at IGCSE is several distinct syllabuses. Cambridge First Language English 0500 has a reading paper and then directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio. English as a Second Language comes as 0510 and 0511, where 0511 counts speaking into the grade and 0510 reports it separately. Literature in English is 0475. Pearson Edexcel offers English Language A as 4EA1, English Language B as 4EB1 and English as a Second Language as 4ES1. Writing improves only through individual marking and redrafting. A batch cannot supply that, and home tuition or one-to-one online teaching usually can.
items: 0580 non-calculator technique, index laws and factorising: drill genuinely works
0625 equation recall and rearrangement responds well to repetition
0625 explanation questions need individual diagnosis, which a batch cannot give
0500 directed writing and composition improve only through marked redrafts
0510 and 0511 differ on speaking; confirm which the school has entered
Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 split the same way: recall drills, explanation does not

contentBlocks.heading: Coaching Supply and Home Tuition Options Across India
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE coaching in India clusters where demand is dense, and that shapes what is available to you far more than any judgement about quality. In Delhi NCR, batches are easy to find in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Gurugram along Golf Course Road and Noida around Sector 128, while families in Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad often find the nearest centre teaches CBSE with an IGCSE group attached. Chanakyapuri sits close enough to central options to have real choice. Where the nearest batch is a long evening journey, a home tutor costs less in time even when it costs more per hour.

Hyderabad has become one of the easier cities for this. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District and Kokapet sit close together, so a centre in one is reachable from several, with Secunderabad the exception. In Gujarat, families in Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev, along SG Highway, in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot will usually find general coaching and far fewer teachers who have taught a named Cambridge syllabus code to Extended tier.

Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, and across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, the honest position is that IGCSE-specific batches are scarce. What exists is often a strong CBSE centre teaching an IGCSE group on the side, which can be adequate for 0580 drill and is rarely adequate for 0500 writing. The metros tell the same story in reverse: Mumbai around Bandra and Powai, Bengaluru around Koramangala and Whitefield, Pune around Baner and Kharadi, and Chennai around Adyar and Old Mahabalipuram Road all have choice, and choice is exactly what makes the subject-by-subject split practical. Ask a centre how many years it has taught the specific syllabus code, never how long it has existed.
items: Delhi NCR: dense supply centrally, thin in Dwarka, Faridabad and Ghaziabad
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Kondapur, Kokapet and Jubilee Hills are mutually reachable
Gujarat: general coaching is available; named-syllabus Extended teaching is not
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow, Indore, Nagpur and Goa: expect CBSE centres with IGCSE groups
Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune and Chennai: enough choice to split subjects between formats
Ask how long the centre has taught that syllabus code, not how old the centre is

contentBlocks.heading: The Series Decision Schools in India Make for You
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the International Baccalaureate. Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School are named only as examples of the kind of school whose families consider coaching.

One fact reorganises the whole planning year. Schools decide which examination series their students are entered for, and a student cannot choose a series independently of the school. So the first question to any coaching centre is not about results. It is whether the batch is prepared for the series your child is actually sitting.

The February and March Cambridge series exists specifically for India, and it changes the calendar substantially. It lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for entry into the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels in the same academic year. A student entered for that series is roughly a term ahead of one entered in May and June, which means revision that starts in January is already late. A batch running a single generic timetable will not match both groups.

There is also the question of what comes after. Families weighing a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11 should know that the Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and that current requirements should be checked with the university or board concerned rather than assumed from what a neighbour did two years ago. A coaching centre is not the right source for that advice. The school's counsellor is, and the conversation belongs in Grade 9 rather than after results.
items: The school decides the series; a student cannot choose one independently
The February and March Cambridge series exists specifically for India
That series lets Grade 10 results arrive for Class 11 admissions the same year
A February entry makes January revision late, not early
Check equivalence requirements with the university or board, never by assumption

contentBlocks.heading: Batch, Home Classes or Online: Which Should Carry Which Subject?
contentBlocks.body:
Give the batch the subjects that reward volume, give home classes the subjects that need a marked script on a table, and give online the subjects nobody near you teaches properly. Most families arrive at some version of that arrangement eventually, usually after a wasted term.

A batch is the right home for 0580 practice, for equation recall in 0625 and 0620, and for the timed-paper habit that a student will not build alone. Sitting a full paper under time pressure in a room where everyone else is also writing is genuinely useful preparation, and it is cheap. A batch also supplies peer comparison, which motivates some students more than any adult can.

Home tuition is the right home for writing and for explanation. A tutor sitting beside a Grade 10 student can pick up the actual script, read the handwriting, ask why a sentence was written that way, and have the paragraph rewritten there and then. That loop takes minutes at a dining table and cannot be replicated in a batch of thirty. Home classes also let a parent see what is happening, which matters more in Grade 9 than most families expect.

Online and hybrid arrangements solve the supply problem. A student in Raipur, Ludhiana or Aurangabad taking Extended tier subjects may simply have no local teacher with the right experience, and an online one-to-one teacher in Mumbai or Bengaluru is a better answer than a nearby generalist. Hybrid, meaning a weekend home session for marking and a shorter midweek online session, works well for families splitting subjects across formats. Decide the split from your marked papers, then review it once after a full mock.
items: Batch: 0580 volume practice, equation recall, and full timed papers under pressure
Home classes: 0500 writing, 0625 explanation, and anything needing a marked redraft
Online: Extended tier subjects with no capable local teacher, whatever the city
Hybrid: a weekend home session for marking, a midweek online session for questions
Review the split once after a full mock, using the marked scripts as evidence

contentBlocks.heading: What Should a Coaching Centre Show You Before You Pay?
contentBlocks.body:
Four concrete things, and all four can be produced in a single meeting if they exist. A returned script marked by the teacher who will actually take the batch. The batch size, stated as a number rather than as the word small. The syllabus codes the group is prepared for. And the teacher's own experience with those codes, in years and at which tier.

Most of what centres advertise is unverifiable and should be treated as such. Claims about results, rankings and success rates cannot be checked by a parent and should not carry any weight in the decision. What can be checked is the teaching. Ask to sit in on one session, or ask for a trial class, and watch whether the teacher marks anything, whether students write during the session or only listen, and whether the mark scheme appears at any point.

On IB Gram's side, identity and the qualifications and teaching experience a tutor claims are verified before a profile is shortlisted, along with the subjects and levels actually taught. A centre is a different kind of arrangement, and the checking falls to you. Ask who will teach the group in practice, because the person who demonstrates is not always the person who teaches all year. Ask what happens if that teacher leaves in January.

For anything involving coursework, be careful. Cambridge First Language English 0500 can be taken with a coursework portfolio, and coursework must be the student's own work. A centre offering to produce, heavily redraft or supply model pieces for submission is putting a candidature at risk, whatever the assurances. Teaching the skill is legitimate. Producing the artefact is not, and that line should be tested explicitly before any money changes hands.
items: 1. Ask for one returned script marked by the teacher who will take the batch.
2. Ask the batch size as a number, and the syllabus codes it prepares for.
3. Ask the teacher's years of experience with those codes, at which tier.
4. Sit in on a session and watch whether students write or only listen.
5. Ask who teaches the group all year, and what happens if they leave.
6. Test the coursework boundary explicitly before paying anything.

contentBlocks.heading: Marking Turnaround: The Number That Decides a Batch in India
contentBlocks.body:
Ask one question and most of the ambiguity about a coaching centre disappears: how many written scripts does this teacher mark in detail each week, and how quickly are they returned? Everything a batch can and cannot do follows from that arithmetic, and almost no centre volunteers it.

Think about what detailed marking means for an extended-writing subject. A composition marked properly needs the teacher to read it once for effect, once for accuracy, then write comments that tell the student what to change rather than what was wrong. That is not a two-minute job. Multiply it across a full batch and then across several batches a week, and the practical ceiling becomes obvious. When the arithmetic does not work, marking degrades into ticks, a grade, and a general comment about needing more detail, which teaches nothing.

Now apply the same test to Mathematics 0580. Marking a practice paper there is faster, because the answer is right or wrong and the working shows where it failed, and a good teacher can scan thirty scripts for a common error and reteach it to the whole room. That is exactly why batches work better in Mathematics. The marking load is compatible with the format.

So the honest rule is this. Where marking can be done at scale, a batch is efficient and often better value than one-to-one. Where marking must be individual and slow, a batch will either not do it or will do it badly, and no amount of good teaching from the front compensates. Ask for the turnaround time in days, ask how many scripts, and ask to see one. A centre that answers all three precisely is worth considering. A centre that says every student gets individual attention without producing a number has told you the answer anyway.
items: Ask how many scripts the teacher marks weekly and how fast they come back
Extended writing cannot be marked at batch scale without degrading into ticks
0580 practice papers can be marked at scale, which is why batches suit them
A common error found across thirty scripts can be retaught to the whole room
Individual attention without a number attached is an adjective, not a commitment

contentBlocks.heading: Where a Batch Honestly Beats a Home Tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
A batch beats one-to-one more often than tutoring platforms admit, and the cases for IGCSE coaching in India are specific enough to name. The first is timed practice. A student who will not sit a full paper alone at home will sit one in a room where thirty others are writing, and that habit matters enormously in the months before a series. A home tutor can set a paper; only a room enforces it.

The second is pace under peer pressure. Some students work hardest when they can see where they stand among others, and they lose that entirely in a private session where the only comparison is with themselves. If your child is one of them, a batch is not a compromise; it is the correct format. The third is cost, plainly stated. A batch shares the teacher across many families and therefore costs less per hour, which for a subject that needs volume rather than diagnosis is good value rather than a lesser option.

The fourth is breadth of question exposure. In a batch, a student hears other people's mistakes, which is a cheap way to meet errors they would otherwise make themselves later. A quiet student in a good batch learns from thirty attempts a week rather than one.

And the honest limits on all of it. A batch cannot diagnose an individual weakness, cannot teach writing properly, and cannot adjust its sequence for one student. No coaching centre and no tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim attaching a number to the outcome deserves scepticism. Progress should show up in the student's own marked work within about six weeks, not in reassurance. If it does not, change the format rather than adding hours, and change one thing at a time so that you learn which part was failing.
items: Timed full papers are enforced by a room in a way no home tutor can manage
Students motivated by peer comparison genuinely do better in a batch
Shared cost makes volume practice affordable in a way one-to-one is not
Hearing thirty other mistakes a week is cheap exposure to future errors
A batch cannot diagnose one student, teach writing, or change its sequence
Expect visible change in marked work in about six weeks, or change the format

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between Coaching and One-to-One Tuition in India
contentBlocks.body:
Do the sorting exercise before you speak to anyone. Take the last two marked papers in each subject, separate the lost marks into content, method and question-reading, and write the totals down. Subjects dominated by method go to a batch. Subjects dominated by question-reading and expression go to one-to-one. Subjects dominated by missing content could go either way, and usually depend on how far behind the student actually is.

Then write down the two constraints that decide everything else: which examination series the school has entered the student for, and how many evenings a week are genuinely free once school transport and activities are counted. A plan that ignores either will not survive Grade 10.

Keep one habit running through both years. After every mock and every major test, re-sort the lost marks the same way. The proportions move, and when they move the format should move with them. A student who needed drill in Grade 9 often needs individual marking by the middle of Grade 10, and families who never re-sort keep paying for the format that solved last year's problem.

To begin, send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus codes, the tier, the school's series, your locality and your schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles have been verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, teaching can run at home, online or hybrid, and you can request a different match at any point if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on subject, tier and the time of year.
items: Sort lost marks into content, method and question-reading before enrolling anywhere
Method-heavy subjects suit a batch; expression-heavy subjects do not
Confirm the school's examination series before planning any revision timetable
Re-sort the marks after every mock and move formats when the proportions move
Book a trial before committing, and ask for a different match if the fit is wrong

faqs.question: Is IGCSE coaching in India worth it, or is one-to-one always better?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject, and answering it any other way is marketing. Coaching is genuinely good value for volume practice in Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, for equation recall in Physics 0625, and for timed full papers that a student will never sit alone at home. It is poor for First Language English 0500 writing and for explanation questions, where marks are recovered only through individual marking. Most families should split their subjects between formats rather than choosing one for everything.

faqs.question: What batch size is reasonable for an IGCSE coaching class?
faqs.answer: Ask for a number rather than accepting the word small, and then judge it against the subject. For drill-based Mathematics work, a larger group is defensible because the teaching is from the front and the marking is fast. For any subject where extended writing is assessed, the group size directly limits how much of each student's work can be read properly. If a centre will not state the number, or states one and the room looks different on the day, that is your answer about everything else.

faqs.question: Can a coaching centre prepare my child for the February and March series?
faqs.answer: Only if it runs a group built for that timetable, so ask explicitly. The February and March Cambridge series exists specifically for India and pulls the whole revision calendar forward, which means a student entered for it needs finished coverage months before a May and June candidate. Schools decide which series students are entered for, and your child cannot choose independently. A centre running one generic timetable across both groups will leave the earlier candidates short.

faqs.question: Should we use home tuition alongside a coaching batch?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it is usually cheaper than it sounds because the two cover different subjects rather than the same one twice. A common arrangement is a batch for Mathematics volume work and a home tutor for English writing or Physics explanation. What does not work is running both for the same subject, which produces contradictory methods and doubles the homework. Decide the split from marked papers, keep each subject in one format, and review after the first Grade 10 mock.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE coaching cost compared with a home tutor?
faqs.answer: Fees are not published here, but the structure is consistent. A batch is the cheapest way to buy teaching time, because one teacher is shared across many families. A home tutor is the most expensive per hour, since travel time is part of what you fund. An online one-to-one teacher usually sits between the two. What matters more than the hourly figure is whether the format can fix your child's actual problem, because cheap teaching aimed at the wrong fault costs the most.

faqs.question: Our nearest centre mainly teaches CBSE. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it depends on the subject and how the group is run. A strong CBSE mathematics teacher can often handle 0580 drill well, because the underlying technique overlaps. The risk appears in question style, command words, mark scheme wording and tiering, which are specific to the Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus. This is common in Jaipur, Lucknow, Indore, Nagpur, Raipur and Rajkot. Ask which syllabus code is taught, ask to see a marked past paper, and cover the writing subjects elsewhere.

faqs.question: Will a coaching batch help with Core versus Extended decisions?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because the decision needs individual evidence and a batch works from group evidence. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the choice shapes what a student can achieve and where they can go afterwards. The right process is to sit both tiers of past paper questions in the same topic, compare the marks and the time taken, and discuss it with the school, which enters the student. A one-to-one tutor can run that comparison in two sessions.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come after a coaching class on the same evening?
faqs.answer: It is possible and it is usually a bad idea. A Grade 10 student who has travelled to a centre, sat a batch, travelled home and then faces a home tutor at half past eight will absorb very little of the second session. If both formats are needed, separate them across different days, and protect at least two evenings a week with no scheduled teaching at all. In Mumbai, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR, where the travel itself is long, this matters even more.

faqs.question: Does a recorded course make coaching unnecessary?
faqs.answer: It replaces the explaining, not the accountability. A recorded course is always available, can be paused and repeated, and costs less than any live format, which makes it a reasonable supplement for a disciplined student revising content. What it cannot do is notice that a student has stopped, mark a composition, correct a misconception, or enforce a timed paper. Most students who buy one watch the early units and abandon the rest. Use it alongside a format that includes a person, not instead of one.

faqs.question: How quickly should we see improvement after starting coaching?
faqs.answer: Look for movement in the student's own marked work within about six weeks, and be specific about what you are measuring. If the batch was chosen for 0580 method errors, the measure is fewer careless losses on a timed paper, not the overall grade. Grades move slowly across a two-year course. No centre and no tutor can guarantee a grade, and any promise attached to a number is worth ignoring. If nothing has moved in six weeks, change format rather than adding hours.

faqs.question: Is online coaching as good as attending a centre in person?
faqs.answer: For content delivery and drill, it is close, and it opens up teachers your city may not have. For the two things a physical batch does best, timed papers under real pressure and visible peer comparison, it is weaker, because a student at home can pause, look away or quietly stop. Hybrid works well here: an online batch for teaching and practice, with occasional home sessions for marked writing. Families in Dehradun, Ludhiana, Bhopal and Goa often have no realistic alternative.

mainEntity.name: Is IGCSE coaching in India worth it, or is one-to-one always better?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends entirely on the subject, and answering it any other way is marketing. Coaching is genuinely good value for volume practice in Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, for equation recall in Physics 0625, and for timed full papers that a student will never sit alone at home. It is poor for First Language English 0500 writing and for explanation questions, where marks are recovered only through individual marking. Most families should split their subjects between formats rather than choosing one for everything.

mainEntity.name: What batch size is reasonable for an IGCSE coaching class?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for a number rather than accepting the word small, and then judge it against the subject. For drill-based Mathematics work, a larger group is defensible because the teaching is from the front and the marking is fast. For any subject where extended writing is assessed, the group size directly limits how much of each student's work can be read properly. If a centre will not state the number, or states one and the room looks different on the day, that is your answer about everything else.

mainEntity.name: Can a coaching centre prepare my child for the February and March series?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if it runs a group built for that timetable, so ask explicitly. The February and March Cambridge series exists specifically for India and pulls the whole revision calendar forward, which means a student entered for it needs finished coverage months before a May and June candidate. Schools decide which series students are entered for, and your child cannot choose independently. A centre running one generic timetable across both groups will leave the earlier candidates short.

mainEntity.name: Should we use home tuition alongside a coaching batch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frequently yes, and it is usually cheaper than it sounds because the two cover different subjects rather than the same one twice. A common arrangement is a batch for Mathematics volume work and a home tutor for English writing or Physics explanation. What does not work is running both for the same subject, which produces contradictory methods and doubles the homework. Decide the split from marked papers, keep each subject in one format, and review after the first Grade 10 mock.

mainEntity.name: How much does IGCSE coaching cost compared with a home tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees are not published here, but the structure is consistent. A batch is the cheapest way to buy teaching time, because one teacher is shared across many families. A home tutor is the most expensive per hour, since travel time is part of what you fund. An online one-to-one teacher usually sits between the two. What matters more than the hourly figure is whether the format can fix your child's actual problem, because cheap teaching aimed at the wrong fault costs the most.

mainEntity.name: Our nearest centre mainly teaches CBSE. Is that a problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, and it depends on the subject and how the group is run. A strong CBSE mathematics teacher can often handle 0580 drill well, because the underlying technique overlaps. The risk appears in question style, command words, mark scheme wording and tiering, which are specific to the Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus. This is common in Jaipur, Lucknow, Indore, Nagpur, Raipur and Rajkot. Ask which syllabus code is taught, ask to see a marked past paper, and cover the writing subjects elsewhere.

mainEntity.name: Will a coaching batch help with Core versus Extended decisions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rarely, because the decision needs individual evidence and a batch works from group evidence. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the choice shapes what a student can achieve and where they can go afterwards. The right process is to sit both tiers of past paper questions in the same topic, compare the marks and the time taken, and discuss it with the school, which enters the student. A one-to-one tutor can run that comparison in two sessions.

mainEntity.name: Can a home tutor come after a coaching class on the same evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is possible and it is usually a bad idea. A Grade 10 student who has travelled to a centre, sat a batch, travelled home and then faces a home tutor at half past eight will absorb very little of the second session. If both formats are needed, separate them across different days, and protect at least two evenings a week with no scheduled teaching at all. In Mumbai, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR, where the travel itself is long, this matters even more.

mainEntity.name: Does a recorded course make coaching unnecessary?

acceptedAnswer.text: It replaces the explaining, not the accountability. A recorded course is always available, can be paused and repeated, and costs less than any live format, which makes it a reasonable supplement for a disciplined student revising content. What it cannot do is notice that a student has stopped, mark a composition, correct a misconception, or enforce a timed paper. Most students who buy one watch the early units and abandon the rest. Use it alongside a format that includes a person, not instead of one.

heroTitle: Due Diligence Before Joining IGCSE Coaching in India
heroSubtitle: A batch is bought on a phone call and lived with for two years. Six questions, asked before anything is paid, will tell you whether this centre teaches your child's actual syllabus code, marks written work properly, and has a plan for the week your child falls behind.
introSummary: IGCSE coaching classes in India are worth considering and worth interrogating, because a batch is bought on trust while a home tutor is judged in the room. Before any money changes hands there are six things to establish: which syllabus code and tier the class actually teaches, how large the batch is and whether that is capped, who teaches it and whether that person changes, how written work is marked and returned, what happens when a student falls behind, and whether you can attend a class before enrolling. This page turns each of those into a question you can ask on the phone, along with the answer that should worry you. Ask them in that order.

contentBlocks.heading: What should you ask before joining an IGCSE coaching class in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Six questions, asked before you pay anything, tell you more than any tour of the premises. Which syllabus code and tier is this batch taught to? How many students are in it now, and is there a cap? Who teaches it, and does that person change during the course? How is written work marked, and how quickly does it come back? What happens when a child falls behind? And can we sit in on one class before enrolling?

The answers matter less than the manner of answering. A centre that knows its own batch sizes replies instantly and specifically. A centre that says small batches and moves on has just told you the cap does not exist. Ask for the numbers in the enrolment email rather than across a desk, because a verbal cap is not a cap and nobody will remember the conversation in January.

Run the same six questions past a home tutor and the difference is immediate. A private tutor answers about your child. A centre answers about the class. Both can be entirely honest, and they are answers to different questions, which is why comparing them on price alone goes wrong so often.

IB Gram sits on the one-to-one side of that comparison and says so openly. A family sends a query or books a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and the family can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Whether that beats a batch depends entirely on the six answers above.
items: 1. Which syllabus code and tier is this specific batch taught to?
2. How many students are enrolled now, and what is the cap in writing?
3. Who teaches it, and will that person change during the two years?
4. How is written work marked, and what is the turnaround in days?
5. What happens, in practice, when a student falls behind the batch?
6. Can we attend one class before paying anything at all?

contentBlocks.heading: Which board and tier is the batch actually teaching?
contentBlocks.body:
This is the question most families never ask, and it is the one that most often wastes a year. A batch advertised as IGCSE Mathematics may be taught to Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended, to 0580 Core, or to Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) at Foundation or at Higher tier. Those are four different courses sitting different papers.

The board difference is real and not cosmetic. Cambridge International Education grades most syllabuses A* to G, with 9-1 versions of some syllabuses under different codes, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1 throughout. Cambridge series run in February/March, which is offered only in India, May/June and October/November. Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. A batch pacing towards May/June is on a different timetable from a student entered for February/March, and the school decides the entry, not the family and not the centre.

Tiering is the sharper problem inside a classroom. Cambridge Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*. A batch holding both Core and Extended candidates has to teach towards one of them, and in practice it teaches to the middle, which serves neither group well. Ask outright whether Core and Extended students sit in the same room. If they do, ask what happens in the final term, when the two groups need different papers and different past papers.

The sciences add one more wrinkle. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers, while Cambridge separates practical assessment into Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. A batch built around one structure and sold to families on the other is a common mismatch and an expensive one. Get the board and the code written into the enrolment email.
items: A batch called IGCSE Maths could be 0580 Core, 0580 Extended or 4MA1
Cambridge grades A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1 throughout
Mixed Core and Extended batches drift towards the middle and serve neither
Ask what changes in the final term when the two tiers need different papers
Edexcel sciences are untiered; Cambridge splits practical into Paper 5 or Paper 6

contentBlocks.heading: Syllabus codes, papers and what a batch can realistically cover
contentBlocks.body:
Content coverage is what a batch does well. Individual paper technique is what it struggles with, and knowing where that line falls stops you expecting the wrong outcome from an honest centre.

Take Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 from the 2025 examinations. Core candidates sit Paper 1, which is non-calculator, and Paper 3 with a calculator. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4 with a calculator. A batch drills non-calculator work efficiently, because the same exercises suit the whole room. What a batch cannot easily do is watch one student's working and see where method marks are quietly being dropped, and that is exactly where most 0580 marks go missing.

The Cambridge sciences examined from 2023 split across Paper 1 or Paper 2 for multiple choice, Paper 3 or Paper 4 for theory, and Paper 5 or Paper 6 for practical, weighted at multiple choice 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. Drilling multiple choice in a batch is genuinely efficient and a good use of the format. Teaching extended response in Physics 0625 or Chemistry 0620 is much harder with a full room, because those marks turn on the precise wording of an explanation and on a diagram nobody else can see.

Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 are the two subjects where a batch can beat one-to-one outright. Hearing four answers to the same question, and watching a teacher take a weak one apart in public, teaches something a private session rarely reproduces.

So ask which subjects this centre is genuinely strong in, rather than treating enrolment as all or nothing. Plenty of families end up with a batch for two subjects and a home tutor for the one where written working is the real weakness.
items: 0580 from 2025: Core sits Papers 1 and 3, Extended sits Papers 2 and 4
Batches drill multiple choice well; explanation marks need individual attention
Cambridge science weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%
Economics 0455 and English 0500 genuinely improve with peer discussion
Enrol subject by subject rather than treating the centre as one decision

contentBlocks.heading: Coaching classes and home tuition across India: NCR, Mumbai, Gujarat, the north and the east
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE coaching classes in India are not spread evenly, so where you live changes which options are even available and how the honest comparison comes out. In Delhi NCR an IGCSE coaching class in Delhi is easy to find across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Dwarka, Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad, and so is one-to-one. The deciding factor here is usually travel: a batch that finishes at half past eight on a winter weekday in Ghaziabad costs the student an hour of study time each way, which home tuition does not.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has the deepest supply of both. An IGCSE coaching class in Mumbai runs in and around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Malabar Hill and Powai, and centres also serve Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar. Ask specifically about monsoon attendance policy, because a batch that continues while a third of the room is absent moves on regardless, and catching up is the student's problem.

Gujarat has grown quickly. An IGCSE coaching class in Ahmedabad covers Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway stretch, with Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families weighing a local batch against online one-to-one. In the east, an IGCSE coaching class in Kolkata operates around Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, while families in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna frequently find no local IGCSE tuition centre at all and go online instead.

Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, the batch on offer is often a general one with a handful of IGCSE students inside it, which is worth checking carefully before enrolling. An IGCSE coaching class in Bangalore, an IGCSE coaching class in Hyderabad, an IGCSE coaching class in Chennai and an IGCSE coaching class in Pune all exist in numbers, though the same travel arithmetic applies in each. Searching IGCSE coaching classes near me is a fine way to build a list; the six questions are how you cut it down.
items: Delhi NCR: count the travel time each way before comparing a batch with home tuition
Mumbai: ask the monsoon attendance policy, because the batch moves on regardless
Ahmedabad, Surat and Vadodara families often weigh a local batch against online
Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna: frequently no local IGCSE tuition centre at all
Smaller northern cities: check the batch is IGCSE, not a general class with IGCSE students

contentBlocks.heading: School deadlines, mocks and the series a batch is planning for in India
contentBlocks.body:
A centre plans its year around its own timetable. Your child's school plans around a different one. Where those two calendars disagree, the student absorbs the difference, which is why the series question belongs in the first phone call rather than the third month.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School each work to their own school's chosen series and internal deadlines, and no coaching centre can see those deadlines unless the family shares them.

So ask the centre directly which series its Grade 10 batch is paced for. If the school has entered your child for February/March, a batch finishing content in March is useless. Ask also when the centre runs its own tests and whether those clash with school mocks, because a fortnight of double testing helps nobody and exhausts the student.

The practical fix is simple and almost nobody does it. Take the school's internal deadline calendar and the mock dates to the enrolment meeting and ask the centre to mark where its own schedule differs. A centre that engages with that document is a centre that will notice when your child is struggling. A centre that waves it away has told you how the next two years will go.

February/March entry makes a batch finishing content in March useless
Check whether centre tests clash with the school's own mock fortnight

contentBlocks.heading: When a batch beats a home tutor, and when it does not
contentBlocks.body:
A batch wins on rhythm, on peers and on cost per teaching hour. A home tutor wins on diagnosis, on written work and on the ability to change plan in a single session. Neither statement is controversial, and the useful question is which of those your child needs this term.

Rhythm is underrated. Some students simply work better with a fixed Tuesday and Friday that somebody else has decided, and for them a batch does something no amount of one-to-one attention replaces. Peer discussion is the other real advantage, particularly in Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500, where hearing other answers is part of the learning.

Home tuition wins wherever the problem is the student's own script. Working set out so method marks survive, diagrams large enough to label, timing across a full paper, the habit of reading the command word first. A tutor at the same table sees each of these within a session. In a room of thirty, the same problems stay invisible until the mock results arrive. Home classes also flex: when a coursework deadline appears, the plan changes that week rather than next term.

Online one-to-one sits between the two and is the right answer when supply is the problem rather than method. It holds the slot through rain and travel, and it opens a national pool for a code nobody near you teaches. A small online group is a genuine middle option too, giving some peer discussion with marking that still comes back individually.

Hybrid is what most families end up building. A batch or an online group for content, a weekly home session for written work, and a review every six weeks to see whether the split is still right. Write the split down. It should change once a year, not once a fortnight.
items: A batch wins on rhythm, peer discussion and cost per teaching hour
A home tutor wins on diagnosis, written working and changing plan fast
Online one-to-one solves supply when nobody local teaches the code
A small online group gives peer discussion with individual marking
Hybrid: batch or group for content, one home session weekly for written work

contentBlocks.heading: How to verify what a coaching centre in India tells you
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every claim a centre makes can be checked in under a week, and the checking is the enrolment decision. Take the three claims families accept most readily and test each one.

The marking claim first. Centres routinely say written work is marked and returned. Ask to see a marked script from the current batch, with the student's name removed. What you are looking for is annotation against the mark scheme, not a tick and a total. Then ask the turnaround in days and write the answer in the enrolment email. A script returned three weeks later teaches nobody anything, because the student has forgotten what they were thinking.

The teacher claim second. Ask who teaches this batch, by name, and whether that person will still be teaching it next term. Teacher changes mid-course are the single most common complaint families have about centres, and the honest ones will tell you their staff turnover rather than promise continuity they cannot control. Ask also what happens if the teacher leaves in January.

The experience claim third. Ask which syllabus codes the teacher has taken through to a series, and how recently. A centre saying fifteen years of experience has not answered. A centre saying four cohorts through 0620 with the most recent in the last series has.

If you are also considering one-to-one, apply the same scepticism. On IB Gram, identity, claimed qualifications and the subjects and levels listed are verified before a profile goes live, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before a family commits. Before a first home visit, confirm identification, register the tutor at the society gate and agree who will be at home. Verification is a floor in both directions, never a verdict.
items: Ask to see an anonymised marked script from the current batch
Look for annotation against the mark scheme, not a tick and a total
Get the marking turnaround in days, written into the enrolment email
Ask the teacher's name, their recent cohorts by code, and who covers a departure
Confirm identification and gate entry before any first home visit

contentBlocks.heading: Batch size, caps and teacher continuity
contentBlocks.body:
Batch size is the number that quietly determines everything else, and it is almost never fixed. A class that begins in April with eight students can hold eighteen by September, because centres fill seats through the year and few of them publish a cap. Nothing about the advertised description changes. The marking turnaround lengthens, the teacher stops asking individual questions, and the quieter students disappear into the back row.

So ask for the cap in writing and ask what happens when it is reached. There are three honest answers. The centre splits the batch, which is good for you and expensive for them. The centre stops enrolling, which is rare. Or the centre keeps admitting students, which is the common case and which you should simply know about in advance rather than discover in November.

Teacher continuity is the second structural risk. Two years is a long time in a coaching centre's staffing, and a teacher who leaves in January of Grade 10 takes the knowledge of your child's weaknesses with them. Ask who teaches the batch, how long they have been at the centre, and what the handover looks like if they go. IGCSE coaching classes in India rarely offer a contractual answer to that, which is fair enough, but a centre that has thought about it will describe a process and a centre that has not will change the subject.

There is a third thing worth asking, and it separates serious centres from the rest. How do you know, week to week, that a particular student is falling behind? A centre with an answer runs short tests and tracks them. A centre without one finds out at the mock.
items: Batches grow through the year, so ask for the cap in writing before paying
Three honest answers at the cap: split the batch, stop enrolling, or keep admitting
Ask how long the named teacher has been at the centre and what handover looks like
A teacher leaving in January of Grade 10 takes your child's history with them
Ask how the centre spots a struggling student before the mock results

contentBlocks.heading: What happens when your child falls behind the batch?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE coaching classes in India move at the pace of a schedule rather than at the pace of your child, so falling behind is a normal event rather than a failure. What matters is whether the centre has a mechanism or a sentiment. Ask the question in those words: what is the mechanism?

Good answers sound operational. A doubt-clearing slot at a fixed time each week that the student can actually attend. Recorded or repeated sessions for missed classes. A short diagnostic test after each unit, with results shared. A named person who contacts the parent when two tests in a row go badly. Any of those is a real system.

Weak answers sound reassuring. We give individual attention. Our teachers are very approachable. The student can ask anything. None of that is a mechanism, and none of it survives a full room on a Friday evening at half past eight.

What you should expect within a term is narrow and checkable. Written work coming back annotated. Some evidence that method marks are being recovered. A student who can say what the last unit test showed. If none of those appear after a term, add a home tutor for that subject rather than more batch hours, because more of a format that is not working is rarely the answer.

And be honest about the alternative. A one-to-one tutor is not automatically better. A tutor who arrives, explains for an hour and leaves is worse than a well-run batch with proper marking. No tutor and no centre can guarantee a grade, and any promise about a specific outcome at a specific tier deserves real scepticism, whoever is making it.
items: Ask for the mechanism, not the sentiment: doubt slots, unit tests, a named contact
Individual attention is a phrase, not a system, in a room of thirty
Within a term expect annotated work and recovered method marks
If nothing changes, add one-to-one for that subject rather than more batch hours
A tutor who only explains for an hour is worse than a well-marked batch

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE coaching classes in India: the enrolment decision
contentBlocks.body:
Gather four things before you decide between IGCSE coaching classes in India and one-to-one tuition. The board and syllabus code for each subject, confirmed by the school in writing. The tier, if it has been set. The most recent marked paper, preferably one that went badly. And an honest note of how your child works, because a student who hides in a group and a student who needs a group are not the same child and should not be enrolled in the same thing.

Then do the comparison properly. Visit one class as an observer, ask the six questions, and ask for the marking turnaround in writing. In parallel, run one trial lesson one-to-one on the same marked paper. An evening of each, on the same material, settles the argument far better than a month of discussion.

If one-to-one is the answer, IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, availability is subject to the tutor's schedule and the level required, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match.

If a batch is the answer, enrol subject by subject and set a review point at the end of the first term. Many families in India end up running both, and there is nothing inconsistent about that: the batch carries content and rhythm, the home tutor carries the script. What matters is that you chose the split rather than drifted into it.
items: Gather the codes, the tier, one marked paper and an honest note on how the child works
Observe one class and run one trial lesson on the same marked paper
Get the marking turnaround in writing before paying any fee
Enrol subject by subject, with a review at the end of term one

faqs.question: What is a reasonable batch size for an IGCSE class?
faqs.answer: Small enough that the teacher marks every student's written work and still returns it within a week. That is the test, rather than a specific number, because a well-run larger group can beat a badly run small one. Ask for the current enrolment, the cap and the marking turnaround in writing. If the centre will not put a cap in the enrolment email, assume the batch will keep growing through the year, because most do.

faqs.question: How do I confirm which syllabus code a coaching class teaches?
faqs.answer: Ask for it in writing and compare it with the code your school confirmed. IGCSE Mathematics could mean Cambridge 0580 at Core or Extended, or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher, and those sit different papers. The same applies across the sciences, where Cambridge splits practical assessment into Paper 5 or Paper 6 and Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers. A centre that cannot answer precisely has answered anyway.

faqs.question: Should we use coaching classes and home tuition together?
faqs.answer: Many families in India do, and it is a sensible split rather than a contradiction. The batch carries content, rhythm and peer discussion. The home tutor carries the student's own script, where method marks, diagrams and timing are won or lost. Choose the split deliberately: usually a batch for one or two subjects and one-to-one for the subject where written working is the weakness. Review the arrangement at the end of each term.

faqs.question: What if the teacher changes in the middle of Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Ask before enrolling what the handover looks like, because it will happen to some families every year. A serious centre describes a process: written records of unit test results, a briefing between the outgoing and incoming teacher, and a parent conversation. A centre that promises it will never happen is promising something it cannot control. If the change comes at a bad moment, a short run of home tuition through the transition is the usual fix.

faqs.question: We live in Ghaziabad and the batch finishes late. Is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: Probably, if the travel is eating study time twice a week. Across Delhi NCR, a batch ending on a winter evening in Ghaziabad, Greater Noida or Faridabad can cost more in commuting and tiredness than it delivers in teaching. A home tutor removes the travel entirely, and online removes it for both sides. Compare like with like by counting the door-to-door time, not the class duration.

faqs.question: Can we attend a class before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Ask, and treat the answer as information either way. Some centres welcome an observer, some offer a trial class, and some refuse on the grounds that it disrupts the batch, which is a fair position honestly held. What you want to see is a teacher marking or discussing written work, the number of students actually present, and how many of them speak. Fifteen minutes at the back tells you a great deal.

faqs.question: Is a coaching class cheaper than one-to-one tuition?
faqs.answer: Per teaching hour, almost always, because the cost is shared across the room. Per unit of progress, that depends entirely on the student. A child who works well in a group and needs rhythm gets excellent value from a batch. A child whose marks are lost in their own working gets very little from it, however low the hourly cost. Count the outcome you need rather than the hours you buy.

faqs.question: Our school entered us for February/March. Does the batch timetable still work?
faqs.answer: Only if the centre is pacing for that series, so ask before enrolling. The February/March Cambridge series exists only in India and pulls the final revision block into winter, which means content has to finish earlier and past papers have to start sooner. A batch built around May/June will still be teaching new material when your child should be sitting timed papers. The school decides the entry, so confirm it first.

faqs.question: How quickly should marked work come back?
faqs.answer: Within a week, and ideally within a few days, because a script returned three weeks later is a script the student has forgotten writing. Ask for the turnaround in days and put it in the enrolment email. Then check it in the first month. Marking quality matters as much as speed: annotation against the mark scheme is useful, while a tick and a total teaches nothing about where the marks went.

faqs.question: Is there any IGCSE coaching in Guwahati or Ranchi, or should we look online?
faqs.answer: Local IGCSE provision in Guwahati, Ranchi, Patna and Bhubaneswar is thin, and many families there work online instead. Search by syllabus code rather than by subject, since a general class with a few IGCSE students inside it is not the same thing. If handwriting, working and timing are the weakness, pair an online specialist for content with a local home tutor who can watch the student write.

faqs.question: What should the first term of a coaching class actually deliver?
faqs.answer: A visible change in written work and some evidence the centre is tracking your child specifically. By the end of term one you should have seen annotated scripts, at least two unit test results, and a teacher who can say what your child is weakest at without checking a register. If none of that exists, the format is not working for this student, and adding more hours of the same rarely fixes it.
