h1: IGCSE Tutoring in India: Mark Schemes, Command Words, Method Marks
heroTitle: How an IGCSE Tutoring Hour Is Actually Spent in India
heroSubtitle: Most tutoring fails quietly by becoming a second school lesson: an adult explaining, a student nodding, nothing marked. This page describes the alternative in detail. Command words taught properly, a mark scheme read line by line with the student, method marks recovered, and an error log that carries the work from one week to the next.
introSummary: IGCSE tutoring in India, whether it runs as home tuition at your dining table or over a screen, should look almost nothing like a classroom hour. A school lesson teaches a topic to thirty students. A tutoring session finds out why this one student loses marks and fixes that, which usually means the tutor talks less than the parent expects and the student writes far more. The work is specific: teaching what describe, explain and calculate each demand, reading a mark scheme beside the student until the awarding of marks stops being a mystery, recovering credit for method that is currently being thrown away, and keeping a written record of recurring errors across weeks. This page sets out that method, session by session, for Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel students.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IGCSE tutoring in India start, and with what evidence?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tutoring in India should start with a marked script, not with a syllabus. You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks what the student is losing marks on rather than which topics they dislike, shortlists verified tutors against that answer, and arranges a trial before you commit. The difference between a good start and a wasted month is almost always the evidence you hand over in the first week.

The most useful documents are the ones families tend not to send. A recent marked paper with the examiner or teacher annotations still on it. A returned class test where the marks per question are visible. A report comment that says something specific, such as answers lack detail. Grades alone cannot direct a session, because two students with the same grade can be failing for opposite reasons: one knows nothing about waves, the other knows waves perfectly and writes answers that never address the command word.

From that evidence the tutor should be able to state a hypothesis in one sentence by the end of the trial. Something like: this student understands the physics and loses marks by describing where the question asks for an explanation. A hypothesis can be tested and can be wrong, which is what makes it useful. A promise to cover the syllabus cannot be either.

Then the arrangement is set: board and syllabus codes, tier, the weekly slot, and the mode. Home tuition, online or hybrid all work for this kind of teaching, though each changes how the marking is done together. Availability depends on the subject, the tier and the hours you need, and a rarer syllabus takes longer to match.
items: Send a marked script, not only a report card and a grade.
The trial should end with a specific hypothesis about lost marks.
Board, syllabus code and tier are confirmed before the first paid session.
A hypothesis that can be proved wrong beats a promise to cover everything.
Home tuition, online or hybrid: pick the one that suits joint marking.

contentBlocks.heading: Two boards, two mark schemes: Cambridge and Edexcel in India
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, normally taken across Grades 9 and 10 and followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. For tutoring, the important consequence is that the two boards ask for answers in slightly different shapes, and a tutor should know which shape your child is being marked against.

The series differ. Cambridge examinations run in February and March, a series offered only in India, in May and June, and in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. That changes the whole calendar of a tutoring plan, because the February and March candidate is doing final technique work while the May and June candidate is still building content.

Grading differs as well. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses available in 9 to 1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Tiering matters more than either: many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, where Core is capped at grade C and Extended reaches A*, and Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher.

Why does a pedagogy page care about all this? Because the mark scheme a tutor reads with the student has to be the right one. Working through an Extended scheme with a Core candidate teaches answers the student will never be asked to give, and the reverse leaves marks on the table. Bring the syllabus code to the first session. For Physics, Cambridge is 0625 and the Edexcel equivalent is 4PH1, and those two do not share a paper structure.
items: Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November.
Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June.
Cambridge grades A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1.
Core is capped at grade C; Extended reaches A*. Tutoring cannot change that.
Bring the syllabus code: Cambridge Physics 0625, Edexcel equivalent 4PH1.

contentBlocks.heading: Command words in 0580, 0625 and 0620, with one answer marked
contentBlocks.body:
Command words are the cheapest marks in the whole qualification, and the most consistently thrown away. State, describe, explain, calculate, determine, suggest and compare are not decoration at the start of a question. They tell the student what kind of sentence earns credit.

Here is a worked example of the kind a tutor should do in front of the student. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 covers thermal physics, and a question might ask the student to explain why a metal spoon feels colder than a wooden one in the same room. A common answer reads: because metal is colder than wood. Mark that honestly with the student and it earns nothing at all. It is not even a description, it is a restatement. A second attempt reads: metal conducts thermal energy away from the hand faster than wood does, so more energy leaves the hand and it feels colder. That answer contains a mechanism and a consequence, which is what explain asks for. The student has not learned any new physics between the two attempts. They have learned what the word explain was requesting.

The same discipline applies across the sciences, where Cambridge syllabuses examined from 2023 use Paper 1 multiple choice for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, Paper 3 theory for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, and practical assessment through Paper 5 or Paper 6, with weighting of multiple choice 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. Half the marks sit in theory papers, which is to say half the marks are written sentences judged against command words.

In Mathematics 0580 the equivalent skill is reading determine and show that correctly, and in 0625 it extends to recalling and rearranging the syllabus equations, which Indian students often skip because the formula came easily in class.
items: State, describe, explain, calculate and suggest each demand a different sentence.
Explain needs a mechanism and a consequence, not a restated fact.
Half of a Cambridge science grade sits in theory papers weighted at 50%.
0625 requires recalling and rearranging syllabus equations, not just using them.
Mark two attempts at the same answer together; the gap teaches the word.

contentBlocks.heading: Where IGCSE tutoring happens across India, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tutoring in India needs a table, a script and two people who can both see the mark scheme, and that is easier in some places than others. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has depth of supply and a geography that fights it. IGCSE tutoring in Mumbai works well within Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, holds together around Powai, and becomes an online question once a family is in Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane or Kharghar and the tutor is not.

IGCSE tutoring in Bangalore runs along corridors. Whitefield and Sarjapur Road form one pool, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout another, with Hebbal and Yelahanka to the north and Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road to the south. Evening traffic between corridors can stretch a short trip badly, so a Bengaluru family wanting joint marking at a table is usually matching within the corridor or going online.

IGCSE tutoring in Pune spreads across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Kharadi, Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi, and the east and west of the city behave like two separate towns on a weekday. IGCSE tutoring in Chennai concentrates in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Alwarpet and Anna Nagar, with Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Velachery and Perungudi drawing from the technology corridor.

Southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai is where the argument changes completely. In Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, the local pool for a named syllabus code may be one person or none, and a family that insists on a tutor at home may end up with a general mathematics teacher rather than someone who knows 0580 Extended. Online marking of a scanned script is a genuine substitute there. Families in Delhi NCR, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Ahmedabad face the same trade-off in milder form.
items: Mumbai: joint marking at a table works within a locality, not across the region.
Bengaluru: match inside the commute corridor or accept an online session.
Pune: east and west of the city rarely share a weekday evening tutor.
Chennai: Adyar and Anna Nagar pools differ from the OMR corridor.
Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam: the local pool for one syllabus code may be empty.
A scanned script marked online beats a nearby generalist who cannot read the scheme.

contentBlocks.heading: Why must a tutoring session not become a second school lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
Because the student already had the school lesson, and repeating it changes nothing except the family's budget. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools of this kind, among them Ecole Mondiale World School, Indus International School, Mahindra International School and The International School Bangalore, are already getting competent classroom teaching. What the classroom cannot easily do is stop and examine one student's wrong answer for eight minutes.

The failure mode is easy to recognise. The tutor arrives, opens the textbook at the chapter the school is on, explains it clearly, sets a few questions, and leaves. The parent walking past hears a confident adult teaching, which sounds like value. The student hears the same content twice and continues to lose marks in exactly the same way, because nobody has looked at how they answer.

A good tutor works from the student's output instead of from the syllabus sequence. They ask the student to attempt something first, then ask why that step was taken, then teach only the piece that was missing. They also stay aligned with the school rather than competing with it: same tier, same syllabus code, same notation. When a tutor's method contradicts the subject teacher's, the student is the one who pays, and the sensible move is to adopt the school's convention and raise the difference with the teacher.

The school calendar governs the plan. Each school sets its own mock examinations, usually some months before the series the student is entered for, and mock scripts are the best teaching material a tutor will get all year. Ask for the school's internal deadline sheet and the mock window in week one, and hand both to the tutor.
items: A second explanation of the same chapter changes nothing for the student.
Work from the student's output, not from the school's syllabus sequence.
Match the school's tier, syllabus code and notation rather than competing.
Mock scripts are the best teaching material available all year.
Get the internal deadline sheet and mock window to the tutor early.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which suits method teaching?
contentBlocks.body:
All three can carry this method, but they carry it differently, and the difference is in how the marking gets done together.

Home classes are the easiest place to teach working. The tutor watches the pen, so an unwritten step is caught as it happens rather than reconstructed afterwards, and a mark scheme can be laid flat on the table between two people. For a student whose problem is rushing, abandoning questions or writing answers too short to earn credit, home tuition is the most efficient place to start.

Online carries the mark scheme work surprisingly well, provided the tutor insists on the right habits. The student writes on paper, photographs the attempt, and both look at the same image on screen while the scheme sits beside it. What online loses is the silent observation of the four minutes before the writing starts. What it gains is reach: a tutor who genuinely knows your syllabus code may not live in your city.

Hybrid suits this method better than it suits most. The weekly home session does the sit-down work, timed practice and the joint marking that needs a table, and a short online slot midweek reviews corrections and updates the error log. That midweek slot can be twenty minutes and still be useful, which is not true of a home visit across a city.

One practical note for every mode. The student holds the pen during marking. A tutor who takes the script and annotates it while the student watches has turned an active exercise into a passive one, and the correction will not survive the week.
items: Home tuition: the unwritten step is caught as it happens, not afterwards.
Online: the student writes on paper, photographs it, and both mark on screen.
Hybrid: home session for timed work, short online slot for corrections.
Online reaches a tutor who knows your syllabus code but not your city.
In every mode the student holds the pen while the work is marked.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you tell a real IGCSE tutor in India from a confident one?
contentBlocks.body:
Confidence is easy to hire and hard to distinguish from competence, and most IGCSE tutoring in India is sold on a first conversation, so use questions with concrete answers. IB Gram verifies profiles before shortlisting, covering identity, claimed qualifications and stated teaching experience, and the questions below are what the trial session is for.

Ask which paper the student sits and why. A Physics tutor should know without hesitation that practical assessment comes through Paper 5 or Paper 6, whichever the school chose, and what changes between Core and Extended entry. A Mathematics tutor should know which of your child's papers is non-calculator. A tutor who needs to look this up in front of you has not taught the syllabus recently.

Ask to see them mark one answer. Hand over a real script, choose a four-mark question, and ask the tutor to mark it aloud against the scheme with your child. This single exercise reveals more than any conversation about experience. You will see whether they read the scheme or their own opinion, whether they can explain why a mark was withheld, and whether the student is allowed to argue back.

Ask what they do with a wrong answer. The revealing reply is a question: what did you think the question was asking? A weak reply is an immediate re-explanation of the topic.

Ask how they track recurring errors across weeks. Any serious tutor has some version of an error log, even if they call it something else, and a tutor with no system relies on memory, which fails by about session five.

Then do the ordinary safety checks for home lessons: a shared room with the door open, an adult at home, the slot fixed, and scheduling kept on the platform channel rather than a personal number.
items: Ask which papers the student sits, and which one is non-calculator.
Watch them mark one four-mark answer aloud against the real scheme.
A good tutor answers a wrong answer with a question, not an explanation.
Ask how recurring errors are tracked; memory alone fails by session five.
For home lessons: shared room, door open, an adult in the house.
Keep scheduling on the platform channel, not on a personal number.

contentBlocks.heading: Inside one hour: the running order of a tutoring session
contentBlocks.body:
The order matters more than the content, because it determines who is doing the thinking. Here is a running order that works for most IGCSE students, in any mode.

1. Retrieval, five minutes. Three questions from two weeks ago, answered cold, no notes. This is not a test. It is a check on whether last fortnight's correction actually stuck, and it decides whether the session plan survives the first five minutes.

2. The misconception hunt, ten minutes. The student attempts a question from the current topic while the tutor watches without helping. The tutor is looking for the exact point where the thinking goes wrong, which is rarely where the student thinks it is.

3. Targeted teaching, ten to fifteen minutes. Only the missing piece. Not the chapter, not a recap, not a second school lesson. If this stretches past fifteen minutes, the diagnosis in step two was too broad.

4. Independent attempt, fifteen minutes. A fresh question of the same type, written properly, timed, with the tutor silent. Silence is the instruction most tutors find hardest to follow.

5. Joint marking, ten minutes. The mark scheme comes out and the student marks their own answer aloud, line by line, with the tutor asking why each mark was or was not earned. This is where the learning is consolidated, and it is the step most often cut when the clock runs out. Protect it.

6. Error log and setting, five minutes. One line in the log, and a short piece of work set for the week.

Count the minutes. The student is working for roughly half the hour and the tutor is teaching for a quarter of it. A session that inverts those proportions is a lecture with homework attached.
items: Retrieval first: three cold questions from a fortnight ago, no notes.
Watch the student attempt before teaching anything at all.
Targeted teaching means the missing piece, not the chapter.
Fifteen minutes of timed independent work with the tutor silent.
Joint marking is the step that must never be cut for time.
Finish with one line in the error log and the week's work set.

contentBlocks.heading: What an error log shows after a term of home tuition or online work
contentBlocks.body:
An error log is a single page kept across weeks, and it is the most underrated tool in tutoring. Each entry records four things: the date, the question type, what went wrong in the student's own words, and the correction. Nothing else. Vague entries such as careless mistake are worthless; the useful entry reads like rounded to two decimal places mid-calculation, then used the rounded value.

After six to eight weeks the log stops being a record and becomes a diagnosis. Patterns appear that nobody would have seen week by week. A student discovers that almost every lost mark in Chemistry 0620 comes from unit conversion rather than chemistry, or that their Physics 0625 errors cluster in questions requiring an equation to be rearranged before substitution. That is actionable in a way that a grade never is. It also gives revision a shape in the weeks before the series, because the student revises their own errors rather than the whole syllabus again.

Progress on this method looks like a change in behaviour first. By four to six weeks the student should be reading the command word before writing, showing steps without being asked, and attempting a question before declaring it impossible. Marks usually follow at the next mock rather than the next class test. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a Core entry cannot exceed grade C whatever anyone promises.

The honest limits: a student who does nothing between sessions will not improve, method teaching cannot replace content a student never learned, and starting a few weeks before the series restricts the work to technique and the highest-yield gaps. Say all of this at the start rather than discovering it in March.

If the log is not being kept by week three, ask why. It usually means the sessions are drifting back into explanation.
items: Four fields only: date, question type, what went wrong, the correction.
Careless mistake is not an entry; rounded mid-calculation is.
After six to eight weeks the log shows patterns no report will.
Revision in the final weeks should be driven by the log, not the syllabus.
Behaviour changes in four to six weeks; marks usually move at the mock.
No error log by week three means the sessions have drifted into lecturing.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IGCSE tutoring in India, at home or online
contentBlocks.body:
Three things make the first hour of IGCSE tutoring in India productive, and none of them takes long.

Collect the evidence. A recent marked script matters more than a report, a mock paper matters more than a class test, and the syllabus codes matter more than the subject names. If the student has a returned paper with per-question marks visible, that is the single most useful document in the house.

Decide the mode honestly. If the student rushes, leaves questions half-finished or writes almost nothing down, start with home tuition, because those are habits a tutor catches from the next chair. If the syllabus is scarce where you live, or you need short frequent reviews, start online and insist that the student writes on paper and photographs it. If neither is clearly right, hybrid usually settles it within a month.

Agree what will be measured. Not a grade. Pick two behaviours, such as reading the command word before writing and showing every step of a calculation, and ask for them to be logged. You will know inside six weeks whether the arrangement is working, which is much sooner than a report card will tell you.

Then send a query or book a free consultation. Say the board, the syllabus codes, the tier if it is settled, the grade, your city and the slots you can keep. IB Gram asks about the school calendar and the schedule, shortlists verified profiles against that brief, and arranges a trial session so the student can judge the tutor before you commit. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to availability, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.
items: Bring a marked script with per-question marks, not just the report.
Rushing and unwritten working? Start with home classes.
Scarce syllabus or short reviews? Start online, on paper, photographed.
Agree two behaviours to measure instead of a target grade.
Send board, syllabus codes, tier, grade, city and workable slots.

faqs.question: What should actually happen in an IGCSE tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Roughly half the hour should be the student working and about a quarter the tutor teaching. A workable order is retrieval of older material, a watched attempt at a current question, targeted teaching of only the missing piece, timed independent work in silence, joint marking against the mark scheme with the student holding the pen, and one line added to the error log. If the tutor talks for forty-five minutes and sets homework at the end, you are paying for a second school lesson.

faqs.question: My child understands the subject but marks stay low. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually the answers do not match what the command word asked for. State, describe, explain, calculate and suggest each require a different kind of sentence, and a student who writes a fact where an explanation was wanted earns nothing, however correct the fact is. The fix is not more content. It is marking the student's own answers against the scheme until they can predict the marks themselves, which normally takes a few weeks rather than a term.

faqs.question: How does a tutor teach a mark scheme without it becoming mechanical?
faqs.answer: By making the student do the marking. A scheme read aloud by a tutor is a lecture; a scheme applied by the student to their own four-mark answer is an argument they have to win. Ask a prospective tutor to demonstrate this in the trial with a real script. You will quickly see whether they read what the scheme actually credits or simply give their own opinion, and whether they let your child push back on a withheld mark.

faqs.question: What exactly goes into an error log?
faqs.answer: Four fields and nothing more: the date, the question type, what went wrong in the student's own words, and the correction. Careless mistake is not an entry. Rounded to two decimal places mid-calculation and then used the rounded value is an entry. After six to eight weeks the log stops being a list and becomes a pattern, which is what gives final revision its shape. If no log exists by week three, the sessions have probably drifted back into explaining.

faqs.question: Does this method work in home tuition as well as online?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one adjustment each way. Home classes make watching the pen easy, so unwritten working is caught as it happens and the mark scheme lies flat on the table between two people. Online needs a rule: the student writes on paper, photographs the attempt, and both look at the image with the scheme beside it. What online loses is the silent four minutes before the writing starts, which is often where the misconception actually shows.

faqs.question: Should the tutor follow the school's order of topics?
faqs.answer: Broadly yes, and always the school's tier, syllabus code and notation. A tutor who teaches a different method for the same calculation leaves the student choosing between two adults, which helps nobody under exam pressure. Where the tutor genuinely disagrees, the sensible route is to adopt the school's convention in the session and raise the difference with the subject teacher. Sequence can deviate briefly to repair a gap from an earlier term, but not as a habit.

faqs.question: How much of this can a student do without a tutor at home or online?
faqs.answer: More than most families assume. Past papers and mark schemes are available through the school, and a disciplined student can mark their own work, keep an error log and learn the command words from the schemes themselves. What self-study cannot easily do is notice the misconception underneath a wrong answer, because the student does not know what they are not seeing. A sensible arrangement is self-marking as the routine and a tutor for the diagnosis.

faqs.question: How long before this shows up in marks?
faqs.answer: Behaviour changes in four to six weeks and marks usually move at the next mock rather than the next class test. What you should see early is the student reading the command word before writing, showing steps unprompted, and attempting a question before calling it impossible. If after six weeks none of that has changed, the sessions are not doing what this page describes. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a Core entry cannot go beyond grade C regardless of teaching.

faqs.question: We live in Coimbatore and cannot find anyone who knows our syllabus code. What now?
faqs.answer: Go online rather than accepting a general tutor nearby. In Coimbatore, Kochi, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam and similar cities, the local pool for one specific syllabus code can be very small, and a mathematics teacher who has never taught 0580 Extended will teach content competently while missing what the paper rewards. A tutor elsewhere in India who works from the right mark schemes is the better trade, and scanned scripts make joint marking entirely workable.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics, Chemistry and Biology together?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. A tutor who has taught all three at this level can work across them, particularly for command word and mark scheme technique, which transfers well between the sciences. Depth is where it breaks down: ask specific questions about the practical papers and about topics in each syllabus. If the answers thin out noticeably in one subject, split that subject off rather than accepting weaker coverage for convenience.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough?
faqs.answer: For one subject, usually yes, provided the student does the work set between sessions. This method depends on there being new evidence each week, and a student who arrives with nothing attempted turns the session into a lecture by default. Two sessions a week suit a student rebuilding a subject from a weak base or working through the final weeks before the series. More than two in one subject rarely adds anything except fatigue.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but my child does not engage?
faqs.answer: Raise it in the first month rather than the third, because engagement is a fit problem and fit problems do not resolve on their own. Listen for how much your child speaks during a session; if the answer is almost nothing across several weeks, the pairing is wrong regardless of the tutor's expertise. Tell IB Gram what specifically is not working and ask for a different match. That request is ordinary and it makes the next match better.

h1: IGCSE Tutoring Services in India and What Each One Covers
heroTitle: Every IGCSE Service, and Its Limits, in India
heroSubtitle: Subject tuition. Past-paper clinics. Coursework support. Mock preparation. Bridging from CBSE or ICSE. Subject-choice guidance. Six distinct things, often sold as one. This page separates them, says what each one includes, and says plainly where each one stops.
introSummary: IGCSE tutoring services in India cover six distinct jobs, and a family that buys the wrong one usually pays for a year of weekly home tuition when eight focused sessions would have done more. Subject tuition teaches a syllabus. A past-paper clinic teaches exam behaviour on content already learned. Coursework support discusses a draft and writes none of it. Mock preparation rebuilds timing and coverage. Bridging support carries a student arriving from CBSE, ICSE or a state board into a marking culture that works differently. Subject-choice guidance happens before Grade 9 and costs almost nothing. Each of those is described below with what it does not include, because the exclusions are where the disappointments live.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you scope which IGCSE services a family in India needs?
contentBlocks.body:
Scoping IGCSE tutoring services in India is a diagnostic exercise, and it takes about twenty minutes with the right paper in front of you. The wrong way to start is with a service name. The right way is with the student's most recent marked script, because the marks tell you which of the six jobs is actually open.

Marks lost on content the student has never securely learned point to subject tuition, usually as weekly home classes. Marks lost on content the student knows, through running out of time or answering a different command word, point to a past-paper clinic. A returned coursework draft with criterion comments points to coursework support. A mock that fell apart in the second half points to mock preparation. A student who transferred in last term and keeps writing full derivations nobody asked for points to bridging. And a Grade 8 student with a subject form due next month needs guidance, not tuition.

Once that is clear, the process is short. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability.

One caution about scoping. Most families over-buy at the start and then cannot fund the term that matters. Buy the smallest service that addresses what the script shows, review it after six weeks, and expand only if the evidence says so. A tutor who proposes a full weekly year in all six subjects after looking at one bad test has not scoped anything.
items: 1. Put the most recent marked script on the table before naming any service
2. Classify the lost marks: content, timing, command word, coursework or transfer
3. Send a query describing the pattern rather than requesting a package
4. Take a demo and ask the tutor which service they think fits, and why
5. Review after six weeks and widen the scope only if the scripts support it

contentBlocks.heading: Subject choice before Grade 9, Core and Extended tiers in India
contentBlocks.body:
The cheapest service on this page is a single conversation held a year before anybody needs a tutor. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually two years across Grades 9 and 10, and it is often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. What the student picks in Grade 8 quietly decides which of those stay open.

Tiering is the part families understand last. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, with Core topping out at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout. So a grade on a report card means nothing until you know which scale and which tier produced it. Guidance here consists of asking the school which tier the child is currently being taught towards and what evidence that rests on.

Additional Mathematics is the clearest worked example. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 has no tiers, two written papers with a calculator allowed, and is graded A* to E. Its content runs through functions, quadratic functions, factors of polynomials, equations, inequalities and graphs, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation and integration. It is usually taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for IB Mathematics AA Higher Level or A Level Mathematics, and Pearson Edexcel's nearest equivalent is International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1.

Guidance stops where the school's decision begins. A tutor can explain what a choice closes off. The school decides entries, and no service can change that.
items: Ask which tier the school is currently teaching your child towards
Core reaches grade C at most; Extended reaches A* in Cambridge subjects
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel grades 9 to 1
0606 has no tiers, two calculator papers, and is graded A* to E
0606 usually accompanies 0580 Extended for students heading to AA Higher Level

contentBlocks.heading: Subject tuition by syllabus code, and the past-paper clinic
contentBlocks.body:
Subject tuition is the service most people mean by tutoring, and it is defined by a syllabus code rather than a subject name. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 each carry their own paper structure, and a tutor who teaches to the subject in general will miss what the specific papers reward. Ask for the code on the first call. A tutor who does not know it yet should find out before the demo, and a tutor who thinks it does not matter is telling you something.

English deserves separate attention because the codes diverge completely. First Language English 0500 sets a reading paper followed by directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio in its place. English as a Second Language runs as 0510 and 0511, each with reading, writing and listening, where 0511 counts speaking into the grade and 0510 reports speaking separately. Literature in English is 0475. Edexcel offers English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). Those are six different courses, not one subject with variants.

What subject tuition does not include is exam behaviour. A student can understand every topic in 0620 and still lose a grade to pacing, to answering a six-mark question in two lines, or to a diagram that is never labelled. That is a past-paper clinic, which is a different service with a different rhythm: short blocks, whole questions under time, immediate marking against the published markscheme, and an argument about the marks afterwards.

The clinic only works once content is secure. Running one over a half-learned syllabus produces panic and burns through recent papers that would have been far more useful later.
items: Subject tuition is scoped by syllabus code, never by subject name alone
0500, 0510, 0511 and 0475 are separate courses with separate demands
A past-paper clinic treats exam behaviour, not gaps in content
Clinics need secure content first, or they simply frighten the student
Immediate marking against the published markscheme is what makes a clinic work

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE tutoring services in India reach your city
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tutoring services in India are uneven by service rather than by subject, which surprises families who assume a large city means everything is on offer. Subject tuition exists almost everywhere there are international schools. Coursework support and bridging are scarcer, because they need somebody who has actually handled a portfolio or moved students between boards.

Delhi NCR has the deepest supply of all six services. South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128 Noida, and Greater Noida hold most of it, while Dwarka, Faridabad and Ghaziabad families usually reach the same people online. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are well covered, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are better served by a local tutor for weekly work with online specialists for the rest, since evening crossings can consume the session.

Bengaluru carries strong subject supply across Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Indiranagar, Koramangala, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road, though a tutor rarely crosses the city twice a week by choice. Hyderabad concentrates around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Kokapet and Secunderabad, with mock preparation blocks easier to arrange than long weekly commitments.

Across Kolkata and eastern India the picture changes. Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore have workable local supply for the common codes, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna often have nobody for a particular one. IGCSE tutoring services in India reach those cities chiefly online, and the sensible pattern is a local tutor at home for mathematics and the sciences plus an online specialist for whatever the city lacks. Chennai and Pune sit between the two extremes, with good coverage of common subjects and thin coverage of the rest.
items: Subject tuition is widely available; coursework and bridging support are not
Delhi NCR: deepest coverage, centred on South Delhi, Gurugram and Noida
Mumbai: local tutors for weekly work, online specialists across the bridges
Hyderabad: short mock-preparation blocks are easier to book than weekly slots
Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna: online fills the gaps in local supply

contentBlocks.heading: Mock preparation and what changes in the final term in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School appear only as context for the calendar families at international schools in India work around.

The series fixes the final term. Cambridge series run in February/March, which is offered only in India, and in May/June and October/November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The school decides which series a student is entered for. Mock examinations sit some weeks before, on dates each school sets for itself, and they are the last full diagnostic anybody gets.

Mock preparation as a service is narrow and time-boxed, usually four to eight sessions. It covers coverage checking against the syllabus, one full paper per subject under proper conditions, a marked analysis of where the time went, and a short fix list. What it does not cover is teaching a topic from scratch. If the coverage check finds a whole unit missing, that is subject tuition again, and pretending otherwise inside a mock block just produces a hurried summary the student cannot use.

The final term changes the shape of everything. New content stops. Sessions shorten and become more frequent where possible. Marking turnaround matters more than teaching quality, because a script returned five days later has stopped being useful. And the last two weeks should get lighter rather than heavier, which families find counter-intuitive and students find obvious.
items: Cambridge series: February/March, May/June and October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
Mock preparation runs four to eight sessions, not a whole term
A missing unit found in a coverage check is subject tuition, not mock prep
In the final fortnight, reduce the load rather than adding to it

contentBlocks.heading: Should each service run at home, online or as a hybrid week?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tutoring services in India suit different formats, and treating them all alike is how families end up unhappy with a tutor who was fine. Stated directly: subject tuition and bridging work best as home classes, because both depend on somebody watching a student write and intervening early. Past-paper clinics and mock preparation work at least as well online, because their value is in fast marking and a saved record, and a screen delivers both. Coursework support is better online for an odd reason: the shared screen leaves visible evidence of exactly what was discussed, which protects everybody.

So the sensible arrangement for most families is a hybrid week rather than a single choice. A home tutor once or twice a week for teaching, and an online session for marked practice, particularly in the months when traffic or monsoon rain makes an evening visit unreliable. Households in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region drift towards this pattern anyway, usually after the second cancelled session.

Subject-choice guidance needs no format at all. One conversation, on a call, with the school's subject form in front of you.

The one rule worth holding to is continuity of person. Change the medium as often as the year demands, but avoid splitting a single subject between a home tutor and a separate online tutor. Two adults teaching one syllabus will contradict each other on method, and a fifteen-year-old resolves that contradiction by ignoring both. If more than one tutor is genuinely needed, split by subject and never by format.
items: Subject tuition and bridging: home classes, where the tutor watches the writing
Past-paper clinics and mock preparation: online works as well or better
Coursework support: a shared screen leaves a record of what was discussed
Subject-choice guidance needs one call, not a weekly format at all
Split tutors by subject if you must, never by format within one subject

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before you book, and what you must check
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram checks identity and the qualifications a tutor lists before a profile becomes visible, and shortlists only profiles that have been through that. That removes a category of problem entirely, and it leaves a different category untouched: whether this person can deliver the particular service you are buying. Those are separate questions and they need separate checks.

Check the service, not the person's general competence. For subject tuition, ask which code and which series they last prepared candidates for. For a past-paper clinic, ask how quickly a script comes back marked and whether the marks are written on the paper or summarised. For coursework support, ask them to describe the boundary before you raise it; a tutor who states the limit unprompted is the one you want. For bridging, ask what they usually find hardest for a student arriving from CBSE.

Then make the demo do real work. Hand over a marked script and ask the candidate to explain where the marks went. Twenty minutes of that is worth more than any amount of discussion about approach, and it tells you immediately whether they read markschemes or only textbooks.

For anything delivered at home, settle the logistics in the same conversation. Arrival time and what happens when the tutor is delayed. Gate entry, since many societies in Gurugram, Powai and Gachibowli require a regular visitor to be registered. Where the session will happen, with a table, decent light and a door left open. And the rule for a missed session, agreed in writing, before the first one is missed rather than after.
items: Verification covers identity and listed qualifications, not service fit
Ask which syllabus code and series the tutor last prepared candidates for
Ask how fast a marked script comes back, and in what form
A good tutor states the coursework boundary before you raise it
Register the tutor with your society office to avoid weekly gate friction

contentBlocks.heading: What does each IGCSE service include, and what does it exclude?
contentBlocks.body:
Subject tuition, the first of the IGCSE tutoring services in India, includes teaching a named syllabus code, setting written work and marking it, and covering topics the school has rushed or skipped. Most of it runs as weekly home tuition. It excludes fixing exam behaviour on content already known, and it excludes managing a coursework portfolio.

A past-paper clinic includes whole questions and whole papers under time, immediate marking against the published markscheme, and a running list of the errors that keep repeating. It excludes teaching unlearned content, and it should not begin before a syllabus is substantially complete.

Coursework support includes reading the student's own draft against the assessment criteria, questioning a weak plan, pointing at a criterion the draft has ignored, and insisting on a redraft. It excludes, exactly and without qualification, writing any part of the work, supplying sentences to be copied, choosing the content on the student's behalf, editing the file directly, or handling the submission. The work must be the candidate's own and the school authenticates it. A tutor who offers anything from the second list is a risk to the student's entry, not a shortcut.

Mock preparation includes coverage checks, one timed paper per subject, an analysis of where the time went, and a short fix list. It excludes new teaching, which is a different service with a different timescale.

Bridging includes translating a familiar way of studying into the one the new board rewards, and it usually runs six to twelve sessions rather than a year. It excludes catching up on two years of a different curriculum in a term.

Subject-choice guidance includes explaining what a tier or a combination closes off later. It excludes making the decision, which belongs to the family and the school.
items: Subject tuition: teaches a code; does not fix exam behaviour
Past-paper clinic: timed practice and marking; does not teach new content
Coursework support: discusses a draft; writes, edits and submits nothing
Mock preparation: coverage, timing and a fix list; no new teaching
Bridging: six to twelve sessions; not a rerun of two years of another board

contentBlocks.heading: Bridging from CBSE or ICSE: what changes, and how fast
contentBlocks.body:
Students move into IGCSE from CBSE, ICSE and state boards constantly, and back out again, and the difficulties are consistent enough to name in advance. Marking is criterion-referenced or driven by command terms rather than a fixed answer key. Coursework and internal assessment carry real weight. Wider reading and independent research are assumed. And there is less reward for a memorised derivation, which is the change students find hardest because it removes a skill they have spent years perfecting.

What that looks like in practice is a strong student suddenly scoring modestly. A girl arriving from ICSE in Salt Lake writes technically flawless physics and loses marks because the question asked her to explain and she described. That is not a knowledge problem and no amount of subject tuition fixes it quickly.

So expect the first four to six weeks to feel worse rather than better. The visible change comes next: answers shaped to the command word, working laid out for a marker, and a willingness to write an argument rather than a fact. By eight to ten weeks the marks usually start to follow. If nothing has changed in the written work by then, the service is wrong, not the student.

Two honest limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and bridging cannot compress two years of an unfamiliar syllabus into a term, so a mid-Grade 10 transfer is genuinely harder than a Grade 9 one. On equivalence for Indian university admission, the Association of Indian Universities issues it, requirements differ by university and by course, and families should confirm with the institution itself rather than rely on general advice from anybody, including a tutor.
items: Command terms replace the fixed answer key a CBSE student is used to
Coursework and internal assessment carry weight that memorising cannot cover
Expect four to six weeks before anything in the written work improves
A mid-Grade 10 transfer is materially harder than a Grade 9 one
Confirm university equivalence with the institution, not with a tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing IGCSE tutoring services in India for home or online lessons
contentBlocks.body:
Bring three things to the first conversation about home tuition or online sessions and it will be useful rather than general. The most recent marked script in the weakest subject. The syllabus codes, if the school has published them. And the calendar: mock dates, coursework submission dates, and the series the school enters candidates for.

Then ask for one service, not a package. Say which pattern of lost marks you are trying to change and let the tutor propose the smallest thing that addresses it. If the answer is a weekly slot in every subject for a year, ask what evidence supports that, and listen carefully to the answer. Over-buying at the start is the most common mistake families make, and it is the reason there is no money left for a mock block in January when it would have mattered most.

The rest is straightforward. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match and say specifically what went wrong.

One closing point that will save you a term. Write down, at the start, what would count as this service having worked. Six weeks later, check the scripts against that sentence. Families who do this change course early. Families who do not tend to discover in the final term that they bought the wrong thing in July.
items: Bring the marked script, the syllabus codes and the school calendar
Ask for one service that matches the pattern, not a full package
Write down at the start what would count as the service having worked
Check the marked scripts against that sentence after six weeks
Sessions run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with IGCSE coursework, and what is forbidden?
faqs.answer: A tutor may read the student's own draft against the assessment criteria, question the plan, point out a criterion the draft ignores and require a redraft. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply sentences to be copied, choose the content, edit the file directly or handle submission. The work must be the candidate's own and the school authenticates it. Any offer beyond discussion puts the entry itself at risk, not just the grade.

faqs.question: How do I know whether we need subject tuition or a past-paper clinic?
faqs.answer: Look at where the marks were lost rather than at the total. If the student could not attempt the question because the content was never secure, that is subject tuition. If they knew the material and lost marks to timing, to answering a different command word, or to an unlabelled diagram, that is a past-paper clinic. Most families guess wrongly in the same direction, buying tuition when the problem is behaviour under time pressure.

faqs.question: My son joined from CBSE in Grade 9. How long does bridging take?
faqs.answer: Usually six to twelve sessions, with the first four to six weeks feeling worse rather than better. The hard part is unlearning: a CBSE student is used to a fixed answer key and rewarded for memorised derivations, and IGCSE rewards answers shaped to a command term with working a marker can follow. Once that lands, progress is quick. A mid-Grade 10 transfer is a harder case and needs a frank conversation about what is realistic.

faqs.question: Can home tuition cover all six subjects with one tutor?
faqs.answer: Rarely well. One tutor can usually hold the sciences together, or mathematics with one science, but English is a separate skill and should be treated as one. Spreading six subjects across a single person produces shallow preparation everywhere. The usual arrangement is two tutors split by subject, with one of them nominated to hold the overall calendar so that coursework deadlines and mocks do not surprise anybody.

faqs.question: When should we book mock preparation?
faqs.answer: Roughly four to eight weeks before the school's mock examinations, and as a block with a defined end rather than an open commitment. The block should include a coverage check against the syllabus, one full paper per subject under proper conditions, an analysis of where the time actually went, and a short fix list. If the coverage check finds a whole unit missing, stop and treat that as subject tuition instead of rushing a summary.

faqs.question: Are these services available in smaller cities, or only in the metros?
faqs.answer: Subject tuition is available almost anywhere there are international schools, and the specialised services are not. Families in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna often have local tutors for mathematics and the sciences but nobody for a specific code or for coursework support. The workable pattern is a local tutor at home for the bulk of the week plus an online specialist for whatever the city does not contain.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor or an online tutor better for past-paper practice?
faqs.answer: Online is usually at least as good and sometimes better, which surprises people. What makes a clinic work is fast marking against the published markscheme and a saved record of repeated errors, and a shared screen delivers both cleanly. A home tutor's advantage is watching the student write, which matters more for teaching than for timed practice. Many families run home classes for teaching and online sessions for papers.

faqs.question: The school has not told us the syllabus codes. Does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal, and the school will tell you if you ask the coordinator directly. Two students in the same class can sit different papers, tiers differ in what grade they can reach, and English in particular splits into several genuinely different courses. Booking a tutor without the codes means agreeing a plan that may be aimed at the wrong papers, which nobody discovers until a mock goes badly.

faqs.question: How much notice do we need to cancel or change a service?
faqs.answer: Agree it in writing in the first week, because the awkward conversation always arrives at the worst moment. A workable arrangement is notice on both sides, a fixed number of make-up sessions carried forward each term with anything unused expiring, and a clear rule for sessions cancelled by the tutor. Availability for a replacement depends on level and schedule, so leaving a change until mock season narrows the options considerably.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us which subjects our daughter should take?
faqs.answer: A tutor can explain what each choice closes off later and no more than that. Additional Mathematics 0606 alongside 0580 Extended keeps IB Mathematics AA Higher Level and A Level Mathematics comfortably in reach, for instance, while a Core-tier entry caps the grade at C. Those are facts worth knowing. The decision belongs to the family and the school, and the school controls entries regardless of what any tutor recommends.

faqs.question: We are being offered a full year of weekly sessions in every subject. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common and it is usually more than a family needs. Start with the smallest service the marked scripts justify, review after six weeks, and widen only if the evidence supports it. Buying everything in July regularly leaves nothing for a mock block in January, which is when a focused intervention does the most good. Ask any provider proposing a full package what specific evidence led them there.

h1: IGCSE Tutor Agency in India: How They Work and What to Ask
heroTitle: How an IGCSE Tutor Agency in India Works
heroSubtitle: An agency sits between you and the person who teaches your child, and that position is either worth paying for or it is not. What decides it is screening, replacement and who answers the phone in March. Here is how to tell the difference before you commit.
introSummary: An IGCSE tutor agency in India is a business that sources, screens and places tutors, most often for home tuition, and takes responsibility for the match rather than simply publishing a list. That last clause is the whole distinction, and plenty of services blur it. Some agencies genuinely check that a tutor has taught Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended level; others forward a phone number and step back. The difference only becomes visible when something goes wrong, usually when a tutor disappears six weeks before an entry deadline. This page explains how screening against a named syllabus code actually works, how agencies compare with marketplaces and freelancers, what your contract really covers, and the questions to put to anybody before you hand over a term's schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Query Becomes a Shortlist at an IGCSE Tutor Agency in India
contentBlocks.body:
Your first exchange with any IGCSE tutor agency in India tells you most of what you need to know. A serious agency asks questions before it offers names. A listings service offers names first.

What IB Gram does is deliberately narrow, and worth stating plainly so you can hold us to it. Parents send a query or book a free consultation. We ask about the board, the syllabus the school enters, the level and tier, the grade the student is in, the school calendar, your locality and the schedule that is genuinely workable. We shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified and whose subjects and levels match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match. That is the whole service, and nothing beyond it is promised.

Notice what is missing from that list. No claim about how many tutors exist, no promise about grades, no assertion that the tutors are the best available anywhere. Any agency that leads with those is selling reassurance rather than a match, and reassurance is the cheapest thing in this industry to manufacture.

The shortlist itself should be small and explained. Three names with a sentence each about why they fit your syllabus and your locality is more useful than twenty profiles to sift. Ask why each person is on the list. If the answer is that they teach Mathematics and live nearby, the screening was done on category rather than on syllabus, and you are effectively doing the selection yourself. Availability is always conditional on level, locality and schedule, and a good agency says so rather than implying that anyone can be arranged for any evening.
items: A serious agency asks about syllabus, tier and calendar before offering names
Three explained names beat twenty unexplained profiles
Ask why each shortlisted tutor is on your list specifically
Screening on subject and postcode alone is not screening
Availability stays conditional on level, locality and schedule

contentBlocks.heading: Screening a Tutor Against a Named Syllabus Code
contentBlocks.body:
When an IGCSE tutor agency in India says it screens tutors, ask what it screens against. Screening that means anything is screening against a code, not a subject. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually taken across Grades 9 and 10 and followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. The two boards examine differently and grade differently. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under separate codes, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale.

A tutor who says they teach IGCSE Mathematics has told you almost nothing. A tutor who says they have taught 0580 Extended, and can tell you which papers that tier sits, has told you a great deal. The same applies to the tiering itself: many Cambridge subjects split into Core, which tops out at grade C, and Extended, which reaches A*. An agency that cannot say which tier a tutor has actually taught has not screened for the thing that matters most in Grade 10.

So ask the agency how they establish it. Reasonable answers involve a subject conversation with someone who knows the syllabus, a request for evidence of the tutor's teaching history, and a check of the qualifications claimed. Unreasonable answers involve a self-declared checkbox on a signup form.

Then ask what happens to a tutor who claims more than they can deliver. A functioning agency has a route for that: the family reports it, the tutor is reviewed, the profile changes or comes down. On this platform, profiles are verified before they go live, covering identity, the qualifications claimed and the subjects and levels a tutor states they teach. What no verification can establish in advance is teaching quality, which is exactly why a trial session exists and why you should use it on a real past paper.
items: Screen on the code, not the subject: 0580 Extended, not IGCSE Mathematics
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel grades 9 to 1
Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A* in many Cambridge subjects
Ask how the agency establishes the syllabus history it claims to have checked
Profiles are verified for identity, claimed qualifications and subjects taught
No screening establishes teaching quality, which is what the trial is for

contentBlocks.heading: Which Subjects Expose an Agency That Is Only a List?
contentBlocks.body:
The common subjects hide weak screening. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology have enough capable teachers in the big cities that a poorly run service will still find someone adequate, and the family never learns how little checking happened.

The exposure comes elsewhere. Ask for a tutor in Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 in a city outside the top four and watch what arrives: sometimes a genuine specialist, sometimes a commerce graduate who has never seen the syllabus. Ask for First Language English 0500 and the difference matters even more, because English is several different qualifications wearing one word, and a tutor used to a literature course will teach the wrong skills for a directed writing task. Additional Mathematics 0606 is the cleanest test of all. It is a distinct syllabus with no tiers, two calculator papers and grades A* to E, and a tutor who has not taught it will usually say so within two questions.

The sciences carry their own trap. Cambridge sciences examined from 2023 assess practical skills through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school chooses which. A tutor who does not know which one your school enters cannot prepare your child for 20 per cent of the marks. Edexcel International GCSE sciences handle this differently, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers and no tiering at all.

So use a scarce subject as your screening question even if you are hiring for a common one. Ask the agency what they would do if you needed 0606 or 0455 in your city next week. An honest answer might be that it would take a fortnight and would probably be online. A confident answer promising someone tomorrow, in any subject, anywhere, is the answer of a list rather than an agency.
items: Common subjects hide weak screening; scarce ones reveal it immediately
English at IGCSE is several syllabuses, not one, and tutors confuse them
0606 has no tiers, two calculator papers and grades A* to E
Cambridge practical marks come via Paper 5 or Paper 6, chosen by the school
Edexcel sciences are untiered with practical skills inside the written papers
Ask how a scarce subject would be sourced, even when hiring for a common one

contentBlocks.heading: Where Agencies Have Real Tutors Across India, and Where They Do Not
contentBlocks.body:
Coverage claims are the most common exaggeration in this business. A service can list every city in the country and hold genuine home tutors in four of them.

Delhi NCR is where most agencies have real depth, across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Gurugram along Golf Course Road, and Noida including Sector 128. Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are thinner than the marketing suggests, and a home tutor allocated from across the region will be reliable for a month and then not. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the same pattern repeats between Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill on one side and Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar on the other. An IGCSE tutor agency in Mumbai worth using will tell you which cluster a tutor actually lives in.

Bengaluru holds reasonable supply across Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road, and home classes work well inside each of those. Gujarat concentrates in Ahmedabad around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar sharing the same pool, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot usually mean online for a named syllabus code. Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune sit somewhere between the two extremes.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR is where the claim gets tested hardest. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula share a modest pool. Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have capable teachers, few of whom have taught a named Cambridge code. The right question to any agency is not whether they cover your city. It is how many tutors they currently have teaching your syllabus within reach of your address, and what they would offer instead if the answer is none.
items: A national coverage claim usually means genuine depth in four cities
Ask which cluster a tutor lives in, not which city they are listed under
Ahmedabad shares supply with Gandhinagar; Surat and Rajkot mean online
Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula share one modest pool of specialists
Ask what the agency offers if nobody teaches your code within reach

contentBlocks.heading: Exam Series, Entry Deadlines and the Agency Calendar in India
contentBlocks.body:
Agency behaviour changes with the calendar, and knowing the calendar is how you avoid being placed with whoever happens to be free.

Cambridge series run in February and March, a series that exists specifically for India, then in May and June, then in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. The February and March series matters here because it lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for entry to the Diploma Programme or A Levels in the same academic year. Schools decide which series they enter students for, and a student cannot choose a series independently of the school.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as B. D. Somani International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Sreenidhi International School and Singapore International School plan around the same deadlines whichever city they live in.

The practical effect on hiring is this: demand concentrates in the months before a series, good tutors are committed by then, and agencies under pressure start placing people who are available rather than people who fit. Book earlier than feels necessary. If you are starting in the term before a series, expect a narrower shortlist, ask directly whether the tutor offered is the best fit or the first free, and be more willing to take an online specialist rather than a local generalist.

One more calendar point that families forget. The Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and requirements change, so check current rules with the university or board concerned rather than accepting a general assurance from anybody selling tuition.
