contentBlocks.heading: Does an Agency Really Offer Home, Online and Hybrid?
contentBlocks.body:
Most say all three. Fewer can actually staff all three, and the gap shows up in the shortlist rather than in the brochure.

Home tuition is the hardest to supply honestly, because it is limited by geography in a way the other two are not. A genuine home tutor offer means people who live near you and will travel twice a week for a full term. Ask how many of the tutors offered for your syllabus are within a workable distance of your address, and treat a vague answer as a no. Home sessions are worth the constraint for Grade 9 and 10 work, since the tutor sees handwritten working, the state of the folder and how the student behaves when stuck.

Online removes the geography problem entirely, and for a scarce syllabus code it is usually the better answer rather than the lesser one. It also gives an agency somewhere to hide: if every shortlist you receive is online regardless of what you asked for, the local supply does not exist. That is useful information, and a straight agency will tell you directly instead.

Hybrid is the arrangement most families settle into. A home visit for the paper-based work and the diagnostic weeks, online sessions for routine practice, and a shift towards online in the weeks around mocks when schedules break. Ask whether the same tutor covers both modes, because switching person when the mode changes defeats the point. Ask, too, what happens when a home visit is missed because of traffic or illness: whether it converts to an online session that week, or simply disappears.
items: Ask how many shortlisted tutors live within travelling distance of you
All-online shortlists for a local request mean local supply does not exist
Home classes suit Grade 9 and 10 because handwritten working is visible
Hybrid works best when the same tutor covers both modes
Agree whether a missed home visit converts to an online session that week

contentBlocks.heading: What Verification Should Mean Before a Profile Goes Live
contentBlocks.body:
The word verified is used loosely, so make the agency define it. There are four separate things it could mean and a service may do one of them and imply all four.

Identity is the first: that the person is who the profile says. Qualifications claimed is the second: that a stated degree or teaching credential exists rather than being asserted. Teaching history is the third and the most valuable for IGCSE: that this tutor has actually taught this syllabus at this tier rather than a superficially similar course. Conduct and references are the fourth, and the hardest for anybody to do thoroughly.

On this platform, profiles are checked before they go live for identity, for the qualifications claimed, and for the subjects and levels the tutor states they teach. That is what verification covers, and it is worth saying what it does not cover: it is not an assessment of how well someone teaches, and no responsible service should claim otherwise.

Which is why your own checks matter as much. In the trial, hand over a past paper the student has attempted and ask the tutor to mark a question aloud against the scheme. Ask what a Core candidate sits and what an Extended candidate sits in that subject. Ask who teaches if they are unwell. For a home tutor visiting a Grade 9 or 10 student, settle the practical safeguards too: a responsible adult at home, lessons in a shared room rather than a bedroom, and scheduling messages sent to the parent rather than to the student. None of this is unusual to ask. An agency that treats these questions as an inconvenience has answered a bigger question for you.
items: Make the agency define verified: identity, qualifications, teaching history, conduct
Teaching history against a named code is the most valuable check for IGCSE
Verification is not an assessment of teaching quality, and cannot be
In the trial, ask the tutor to mark one question aloud against the scheme
For home visits, agree the adult at home, the room and the message rules

contentBlocks.heading: Agency, Marketplace or Freelance: Which Should You Use?
contentBlocks.body:
An IGCSE tutor agency in India, a marketplace and a freelance tutor fail in different ways, and choosing well means picking the failure you can live with.

A freelance tutor found through a school parent group is the oldest route and often the best teaching. You deal with one person, the arrangement is simple, and there is no margin between you and them. The risk is entirely concentrated: if that person moves city, falls ill or takes a full-time job in January, you have nothing. There is no replacement, no record of what was covered, and you restart the search in the worst month of the year. For a Grade 9 student this is survivable. For Grade 10 before a series it is expensive.

A marketplace gives you volume and visible profiles, and the selection work sits with you. That suits a confident parent who knows the syllabus and can interview well. It suits nobody who is hiring for the first time, because the platform is not making a judgment on your behalf and the profiles all read similarly. Most marketplaces also leave the payment relationship directly with the tutor, so a dispute is yours to handle.

An agency takes a margin and, in exchange, should take on the screening and the replacement. Your working relationship is with the agency even though the teaching comes from an individual, which is why the contract question matters: ask who you are actually contracting with, who you pay, and who is responsible if the tutor stops attending. A serious agency answers those in one sentence each. If an agency takes the margin and still leaves you to resolve a disappearance in March, you have paid for nothing.

Judge accordingly. Freelance for simplicity and cost. Marketplace for choice and control. Agency for continuity, screening and someone accountable when it breaks.
items: Freelance: best simplicity and cost, with no cover if the person leaves
Marketplace: widest choice, with the selection work left entirely to you
Agency: pays for screening, continuity and a route to replacement
Ask who you contract with, who you pay, and who answers when it breaks
A margin taken without replacement responsibility buys you nothing

contentBlocks.heading: What Happens When a Tutor Leaves Mid-Course in India
contentBlocks.body:
Every IGCSE tutor agency in India handles this differently, and it is the scenario to plan for, because it is common and because it always arrives at the wrong time. Tutors change jobs, relocate, or take on school posts in the same months your child is preparing for a series.

Ask three questions before you start rather than after. How quickly would a replacement be shortlisted? Does the new tutor receive any record of what has been covered, or does the family reconstruct it? Is there any cost to switching? The answers vary widely and they are rarely printed anywhere.

Then protect yourself independently of the answers. Keep your own one-page record: topics covered by date, papers attempted, and the marks lost each time. It takes two minutes after each session and it turns a handover from a month of drift into one conversation. Ask the tutor to write two lines after every session rather than a long report nobody reads. If a replacement becomes necessary near an entry deadline, that page is the difference between a new tutor starting where the last one stopped and starting again.

Be realistic about what a replacement can do. A tutor arriving eight weeks before papers is doing damage control and targeted practice, not rebuilding foundations, and any service suggesting otherwise is overselling. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and continuity is worth more in the final stretch than a marginally better teacher. If your current tutor is adequate and available through the series, keeping them is usually the right call even when a stronger name appears in February.

And if a fit is genuinely wrong, say so early. Asking for a different match in September costs a week. Asking in January costs a great deal more.
items: Ask the replacement turnaround, the handover process and any switching cost
Keep a one-page record: topics, dates, papers attempted, marks lost
Two written lines after each session beat a long report nobody reads
A tutor arriving eight weeks before papers does damage control, not foundations
Continuity usually beats a marginally better name close to a series

contentBlocks.heading: Questions to Ask Before You Sign Up for Home Tuition
contentBlocks.body:
Run the list below on any service you are considering, including this one. It takes ten minutes on a call and it separates a screening operation from a directory faster than any amount of website reading.

Then look at the claims themselves, because the warning signs are consistent. A stated number of tutors on the books, which nobody can audit. Promised grades or promised improvements, which no honest tutor offers. Ratings and success stories with no way to check them. Claims to be the leading or the top service in the country. A fee quoted before anyone has asked which syllabus your child sits. Pressure to pay for a term before a trial. Any suggestion that a tutor can write, redraft or substantially shape work your child submits, which crosses an academic integrity line no family should go near.

What good looks like is duller. Questions before names. A small explained shortlist. A trial before commitment. Plain language about what is not known. Willingness to say that a subject is not covered in your area and that online would be better.

To start here: send a query or book a free consultation with the syllabus code, the grade, the school's series and two evenings that are genuinely free. We shortlist verified tutors who match, arrange a demo before you commit, run lessons at home, online or hybrid, and change the match if it is wrong. Availability depends on level, locality and schedule, and we would rather say that plainly than promise a tutor for tomorrow.
items: 1. Which of your tutors has taught my child's syllabus code at this tier?
2. How do you verify that, and what exactly does verified cover?
3. Who do I contract with, who do I pay, and who is accountable?
4. What happens if the tutor leaves six weeks before the series?
5. Can I have a trial on a past paper before committing to a term?
6. How many tutors for this subject live within reach of my address?

faqs.question: What does a tutor agency actually do that I cannot do myself?
faqs.answer: Three things, and only three are worth paying for. It sources tutors you would not find through a school parent group, particularly for scarce syllabuses. It screens them against a named code rather than a subject label. And it replaces one when an arrangement breaks, which is the part families value only once it happens. Everything else, including the initial conversation and the trial, you could arrange yourself. If a service does not do those three things, you are paying a margin for a phone number.

faqs.question: How should an agency screen a tutor for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580?
faqs.answer: By establishing which tier they have taught and testing that they know the papers. A tutor who has genuinely taught 0580 Extended can say, without pausing, that Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, from the 2025 examinations. Screening should also check the qualifications claimed and the teaching history asserted. Ask the agency to describe the check in specific terms rather than repeating the word verified.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor leaves close to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Ask before you start, because the answers differ sharply. A functioning agency shortlists a replacement on request, passes on a record of what has been covered, and does not charge you for the switch. Protect yourself anyway by keeping a one-page log of topics, dates, papers attempted and marks lost. Be realistic about the incoming tutor's scope: arriving weeks before papers means targeted practice and damage control rather than rebuilding foundations, and no tutor can guarantee a grade in that window.

faqs.question: Is an agency better than hiring a freelance tutor directly?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends on the year. A freelance tutor found through a trusted parent group is simpler, costs less for the same hour, and often teaches very well. The weakness is concentration of risk: no cover if that person relocates or takes a job. An agency charges a margin and should absorb the screening and the replacement in return. For Grade 9 the freelance route is usually fine. For Grade 10 in the months before a series, continuity is worth more than the saving.

faqs.question: Can an agency really provide home tuition in my locality?
faqs.answer: Ask how many tutors for your syllabus currently live within travelling distance of your address, and treat a vague answer as a no. Coverage claims are the most exaggerated thing in this business, and a service can list every Indian city while holding genuine home tutors in four of them. If every shortlist you receive is online after you asked for home classes, the local supply does not exist. That is worth knowing, because an online specialist often beats a nearby generalist for a named code anyway.

faqs.question: Who is responsible if something goes wrong during a home session?
faqs.answer: Establish this in the first conversation rather than after an incident. Ask who you are contracting with, who you pay, who to contact about a problem, and what happens to a session missed on either side. Then set the household arrangements yourself: a responsible adult at home for every session, lessons in a shared room rather than a bedroom, and all scheduling messages coming to the parent rather than directly to the student. Any agency that finds these questions awkward has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What are the warning signs in an agency's marketing?
faqs.answer: A stated number of tutors on the books, which nobody outside the company can check. Promised grades or promised percentage improvements. Ratings and success stories you cannot verify. Claims to be the leading service in the country. A fee quoted before anyone asks which syllabus your child sits. Pressure to pay for a full term before a trial session. And the serious one: any hint that a tutor will write or substantially rework coursework a student submits, which crosses an academic integrity line and puts the entry itself at risk.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book for the February and March series?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because demand concentrates in the months before any series and good tutors commit their evenings first. Cambridge runs a February and March series specifically for India, alongside May and June and October and November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. Schools decide which series a student enters. If you are starting in the term immediately before papers, expect a narrower shortlist and ask directly whether the tutor offered is the best fit or simply the first available.

faqs.question: Does an agency in Delhi or Ahmedabad hold tutors for scarce subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the honest answer is city-specific. Delhi NCR has real depth across South Delhi, Gurugram and Noida, thinning towards Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. Ahmedabad concentrates around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway and shares tutors with Gandhinagar, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot usually mean online for a named code. Ask what the agency would do if nobody teaches your syllabus within reach, and prefer the service that says it would be online in a fortnight over one promising someone tomorrow.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a term upfront?
faqs.answer: Not before a trial, and not before you know the replacement policy. A demo or trial session can be arranged with a serious service precisely so that both sides can judge the fit, and paying a term ahead removes your only real leverage if the match is wrong. Ask instead how billing works, what notice either side gives, what happens to a missed session, and whether the slot is held through the examination season. A service confident in its matching does not need money in advance to prove it.

faqs.question: Can we use an agency for one subject and a school teacher for another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and plenty of families do, though check your school's policy on teachers tutoring their own students before arranging the second part. Splitting has a practical advantage: the outside tutor gives an independent read on tier and progress, which is useful precisely because it does not come from the school. Keep the subjects separate rather than having two people work on the same one, and keep your own log of what each is covering so that neither ends up repeating the other's work.

faqs.answer: Parents send a query or book a free consultation. We ask about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule. We shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified and who match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match. Availability depends on level, locality and schedule. We do not promise grades, quote a fee before understanding the requirement, or claim to be the best service in the country.

h1: IGCSE Tutor Service in India: What Happens After You Book
heroTitle: Service Levels for IGCSE Families in India
heroSubtitle: Most tutoring goes wrong in the operations rather than in the teaching: a reply that never comes, a tutor who cannot be replaced, a month with no report. This page sets out what should happen after you book, what parents should be told, and how to escalate when something is not working.
introSummary: An IGCSE tutor service in India is judged after the booking, not before it, and the part families most often run home tuition into trouble over is administrative rather than academic. How quickly is a query answered. What happens when the fit is wrong in week three. Who reschedules the Thursday session when mocks move. What are you told each month, and by whom. Where do you go when a polite request has been ignored twice. This page answers each of those in the order they arise, describes a monthly report worth reading, gives a numbered escalation path, and lists the promises any honest service will decline to make.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a booking run from first query to first session in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Five things, and a well-run IGCSE tutor service in India makes all five visible rather than hiding them behind a wall of silence. You send a query or book a free consultation. Somebody asks about the grade, the syllabus codes, the tier, the school's exam series, your locality and the evenings that work. A shortlist of verified tutors follows. A demo or trial session is arranged. You confirm, or you ask to see somebody else.

How long that takes depends on what you have asked for, and an honest answer says so rather than quoting a fixed number. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 in a well-supplied locality moves quickly. Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 at a specific weeknight time in a smaller city may take considerably longer, and for some combinations the honest answer is that a home visit cannot be arranged at all and an online tutor is the realistic route. A service that promises the same turnaround for every request has not looked at the request.

What you should expect in the meantime is contact rather than a result. Silence during a search is the commonest complaint families have, and it is entirely avoidable: an update saying the search is continuing and why is worth more than an unexplained pause. Ask at the start how you will be kept informed and through which channel, because a message thread with one named person works far better than a general number.

Before the first session, three details should be confirmed in writing: the slot and its length, the address or the meeting link, and what the tutor will bring or expect. Small things, and the first session goes badly surprisingly often because nobody confirmed that the student needed his own past papers printed.
items: 1. Send the query with grade, syllabus codes, tier and the school's exam series.
2. Answer the scheduling questions honestly, including the evenings that do not work.
3. Receive a shortlist of verified tutors, with availability stated conditionally.
4. Run a demo or trial session before committing to a weekly arrangement.
5. Confirm slot, venue or link, and materials in writing before session one.

contentBlocks.heading: Series dates, tiers and the operational calendar they create
contentBlocks.body:
Operations follow the examination calendar, so a service that does not know which series your school uses cannot schedule sensibly. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and it is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11.

Cambridge series run in February/March, May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The February/March series exists specifically for India, so that Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for IB Diploma or A Level entry in the same academic year. Schools decide which series they enter students for, and a student cannot choose a series independently of the school. That single fact decides when demand peaks, when tutors are hardest to replace, and when a reschedule request will be difficult to honour.

Tiers change the operational picture too. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, and the ceiling differs: Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. A tier change agreed with the school mid-year is an operational event, not just an academic one, because the tutor's material, the practice papers and sometimes the tutor himself have to change. Tell the service the day the school confirms it.

Grading conventions vary as well. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Reports that quote a grade should say which scale they mean. And for anyone planning ahead, the Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, with current requirements to be checked with the university or board concerned rather than assumed.
items: Cambridge series: February/March, May/June and October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
February/March is an India-only series and creates the year's busiest replacement period
Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*, so a tier change is an operational event
Reports quoting a grade should say whether the scale is A*-G or 9-1

contentBlocks.heading: Who covers 0580 or 0500 when your tutor is unavailable?
contentBlocks.body:
Somebody should, and the answer must exist before you need it rather than being improvised on a Tuesday afternoon. Illness, travel and family emergencies happen to tutors as much as to anyone, and the difference between a well-run arrangement and a poor one is whether the week is recovered or simply lost.

There are three workable answers and you should know which one applies to you. The session moves to another evening in the same week, which is the best outcome and depends entirely on your own schedule having slack in it. The session converts to online with the same tutor, which works for Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 and Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 with almost nothing lost, and works less well for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 where paper working and diagrams matter. Or the session is credited and skipped, which is honest and occasionally the right call in a light week.

What should not happen is an unannounced substitute. A different tutor arriving with no briefing wastes the hour and unsettles the student, and for Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 or Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610, where the thread of a topic runs across several weeks, it can cost more than the missed session would have. If a substitute is genuinely needed for a longer absence, ask for the handover note first and treat it as a temporary arrangement with a review date.

So ask, in the first conversation, three operational questions. What happens if the tutor cannot attend. What happens if we cannot attend. And how many sessions can be carried forward before they lapse. Sensible services answer all three without hesitating, because they have been asked before.
items: Agree the missed-session rule for both sides before the first week, not after the first miss
0500 and 0455 convert to online with little lost; 0580 and 0625 lose method and diagrams
Refuse unannounced substitutes, and ask for a handover note for any longer absence
Ask how many sessions can be carried forward before they lapse
A credited, skipped week in a light term is an honest outcome, not a failure

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE tutor service in India: response times differ by city
contentBlocks.body:
Operational promises mean different things in different places, and a service that quotes one turnaround for the whole country is quoting a marketing figure. Supply is the variable, and supply is geographic.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, an IGCSE tutor service in Mumbai covering Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill has depth, and replacing a tutor mid-term is usually possible without dropping to online. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are thinner for home visits, so a replacement there frequently arrives as an online tutor and the family should be told that plainly rather than discovering it at the trial. Chennai behaves similarly: an IGCSE tutor service in Chennai around Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam replaces quickly, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar take longer and monsoon weeks make weekday evenings unreliable.

Pune sits in the middle. Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Kharadi, Aundh, Baner, Balewadi and Wakad all have some local supply, though an IGCSE tutor service in Pune arranging anything across Hinjewadi on a weekday evening should be asked how the tutor plans to get there before the slot is agreed.

Central and western India and the south beyond the two big metros are where expectations need resetting. In Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, and in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, a named syllabus at a specific tier may have no local tutor at all. A parent searching for an IGCSE tutor service near me in those cities is usually better served by asking for online from the outset than by waiting weeks for a home visit that will not materialise. An IGCSE tutor service in Delhi across South Delhi and Gurugram, an IGCSE tutor service in Bangalore, an IGCSE tutor service in Hyderabad, an IGCSE tutor service in Kolkata and an IGCSE tutor service in Ahmedabad all fall between the two extremes, with depth in some subjects and none in others.
items: Mumbai and Chennai central localities replace a tutor fastest; outer suburbs go online
Pune: ask how a tutor will cross Hinjewadi before agreeing a weekday evening slot
Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Goa: expect online rather than a home visit for named syllabuses
Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam and Madurai: online supply is the realistic first answer
Any service quoting one turnaround for the whole country is quoting a marketing figure
Ask for the honest local answer before you wait three weeks for a home tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Rescheduling around school mocks and the exam series in India
contentBlocks.body:
School calendars are the main source of disruption in any tutoring arrangement, and they are predictable, which means the disruption is manageable if somebody bothers. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School all hit the same pattern: internal assessments and mocks land together, and the weeks around them need a different timetable rather than the usual one. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Give the service the school calendar at the start, including mock dates as soon as they are published. That one act removes most rescheduling conflicts before they happen, because the tutor plans around them instead of reacting. During a mock week the useful arrangement is usually fewer, shorter sessions rather than the normal load, since the student's evenings are already spent.

After mocks, the timetable should change again. Marked scripts arrive, and the next four to six weeks are worth more than any earlier period in the year because for the first time there is real evidence. A service that does not ask to see the mock scripts is not operating well, whatever the tutor's teaching is like.

In the final weeks before the series, sessions often need to move at short notice around the school's own revision programme and the examination timetable itself. Agree the rule for that period specifically. Many families switch to shorter, more frequent sessions, accept that some will be online, and give the tutor permission to reschedule directly with the student's calendar rather than through two adults.
items: Hand over the school calendar and mock dates at the start, not when a clash appears
During mock weeks run fewer, shorter sessions rather than the usual weekly load
The four to six weeks after mock results are the highest-value period of the year
A service that never asks to see mock scripts is not operating well
Agree a separate short-notice rescheduling rule for the weeks before the series

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits, online sessions, or a hybrid fallback?
contentBlocks.body:
Treat this as an operational decision as much as a teaching one, because the mode determines how often a session survives contact with a Tuesday.

Home tuition delivers the most information and carries the most operational risk. A tutor travelling across a metro in the evening will lose some sessions to traffic, weather and the ordinary chaos of Indian cities, and no arrangement can promise otherwise. What a well-run service can do is set the rule in advance: a tutor who cannot reach you converts the session to online from wherever he is, and a session cancelled with reasonable notice is rescheduled rather than lost. Home classes also need a settled study space and, for a Grade 9 or Grade 10 student, an adult somewhere in the flat.

Online tuition is the operationally robust option. Nothing depends on travel, short-notice rescheduling is far easier, and a replacement tutor can start within days rather than weeks because the search is no longer limited to your locality. The cost is what the tutor cannot see: the working not written down, the diagram drawn too small, the phone under the desk.

A hybrid week is the sensible default for most families and should be chosen rather than discovered. Set one home session for the subject where paper matters and one online session for the subject where it matters less, and write down that difficult evenings convert rather than cancel. Stated plainly: home visits give the best diagnosis and the least reliable calendar, online gives the most reliable calendar and the least diagnosis, and hybrid keeps the useful parts of each at the price of a schedule everyone has to actually read.
items: Set the conversion rule in advance: a blocked evening becomes an online session
Home tuition needs a settled study space and an adult somewhere in the flat
Online replacements can usually start sooner, because the search is not limited by locality
Hybrid should be chosen deliberately at the start rather than drifted into by March
No arrangement can promise that every home visit will happen on time

contentBlocks.heading: What is checked before a tutor reaches your home
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile goes live on IB Gram, identity, qualifications and claimed teaching experience are checked, and the syllabuses and levels a tutor says he teaches are recorded against what he can show. For an IGCSE booking that means the named syllabus matters: teaching Mathematics is not the same claim as teaching Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier, and the profile should distinguish them.

Say plainly what verification does not cover. Nobody has observed every lesson. Nobody can predict whether this tutor will suit this student, or whether he will still be reliable in month nine. Those are discovered, which is why a trial exists and why the replacement process matters more than the vetting process for most families.

There are checks you should run yourself in the first week. Confirm the tutor's name and contact match what you were sent. Agree that scheduling and progress messages copy a parent rather than going only to the student. Keep sessions in a shared room with the door open, which is the norm for home tuition and should not need negotiating. And ask the tutor directly which syllabus code and which tier he is teaching towards, then check that against the school's own paperwork.

One more check is worth making at the end of the first month, and almost nobody makes it. Ask the tutor what he would do if he thought the arrangement should stop. The answer separates somebody running a professional service from somebody protecting a weekly slot.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed teaching experience are checked before a profile goes live
Profiles should name the syllabus code and tier, not just the subject
Confirm the tutor's identity in week one and copy a parent on all scheduling messages
Keep home tuition sessions in a shared room with the door open, as standard practice
Ask what the tutor would do if he thought the arrangement should end

contentBlocks.heading: Service levels: what a tutoring service should commit to
contentBlocks.body:
An IGCSE tutor service in India is a set of operational commitments wrapped around a teaching relationship, and the commitments are what you are paying the service for rather than the individual. There are six worth insisting on, and each one should be answerable in a sentence.

First, a named point of contact. Not a general number, not a rotating inbox: one person who knows your case. This single item removes more frustration than everything else combined, because most complaints in this industry are really complaints about having to explain the situation again.

Second, an honest matching answer. If no tutor for Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 exists in your locality at the time you want, the useful response is that fact, offered quickly, with online as an alternative. A slow search dressed up as a careful one costs the family weeks.

Third, a replacement route. If the fit is wrong, you should be able to ask for a different match without justifying yourself at length, and without the conversation becoming personal. Fit failures are ordinary. In Grade 10 they are also urgent, and a service should treat them that way.

Fourth, records. What was covered each session, in one line, kept somewhere both sides can see. It costs the tutor two minutes and it is the only thing that makes a handover possible later.

Fifth, a monthly report to parents, which the next section covers in detail.

And sixth, an escalation path that does not run through the person you are complaining about. Every service needs one, and very few publish it. Ask for it before you need it, because the moment you need it is the moment nobody is answering.
items: A named point of contact who knows the case, not a general number
An honest matching answer quickly, including the answer that nobody is available locally
A replacement route you can use without a long justification
One line of written record per session, visible to both sides
A monthly report to parents, and an escalation path that bypasses the tutor

contentBlocks.heading: What should parents be told every month in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Four things, briefly, in writing, and without the family having to ask: what was covered, what the marked work showed, what the student is doing between sessions, and what changes next month. Half a page is plenty. A monthly report that runs to three pages of encouragement is a report nobody reads and nobody can act on.

What was covered should be specific enough to check against the school's scheme of work. Topics and question types, not simply the subject name. What the marked work showed is the part that matters most, and it should include at least one honest negative, because a month in which nothing went wrong did not happen. Between-session work should say what was set and what was actually returned, since the gap between those two is often the real story.

And the plan for next month should be short and falsifiable. Something a parent can check in four weeks without any expertise at all.

When something goes wrong and the ordinary conversation has not fixed it, escalate in this order:

1. Raise it directly with the tutor, once, specifically, and in writing rather than in passing at the door.
2. If nothing changes within two sessions, raise it with your named contact at the service and ask for a dated response.
3. Ask for a different match, and ask for the handover note as part of that request.
4. If the issue is conduct rather than fit, say so explicitly and ask for it to be recorded, not resolved informally.

And hold on to the limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade. A service that describes a specific outcome, or a particular improvement, is making a claim nobody can keep, and the honest version is a plan, a review date and the freedom to change your mind.
items: Monthly, in writing: coverage, what marked work showed, work between sessions, next month
Coverage should name topics and question types, not just the subject
Every honest monthly report contains at least one negative
Escalate in writing to the tutor first, then to your named contact with a dated response
Conduct issues should be recorded rather than resolved informally

contentBlocks.heading: The promises an honest service in India refuses to make
contentBlocks.body:
There are five, and hearing any of them should slow a family down rather than reassure it.

A specific grade, or a promised improvement of any particular size. Nobody can promise the outcome of an examination sat by somebody else, and the promise tells you the service is selling to anxiety. A better answer is a plan, a review, and an honest description of what is realistic given how many weeks remain.

Immediate availability for everything. Some combinations of syllabus, tier, locality and time slot simply have no local tutor, and the honest response is to say so and offer online. A service that says yes to every request will say yes to yours and then go quiet.

That a tutor will never change. People move cities, take jobs and have families. What can be promised is a handover note and a replacement process, which is worth far more than an assurance that will be broken eventually.

That coursework will be handled. It will not, and it should not be. A tutor may teach the skill, discuss a plan and explain how marks are awarded, and may not write, edit or contribute content to submitted work. Any service offering more than that is offering a risk to the student's entry, not a service.

And that results will be attributed to them. Teaching contributes. Schools teach most of the course. Students do the work.

To begin, send a query or book a free consultation with the grade, the syllabus codes, the tier and the school's series. IB Gram asks about level, location and schedule, then shortlists verified tutors, subject to availability. Arrange a trial before committing, and ask for your named contact and the escalation path in that first conversation rather than in a difficult month.
items: No specific grade, score or percentage improvement can honestly be promised
No service can promise instant availability for every syllabus, tier and slot
No tutor can be promised permanently; a handover process is worth more than the promise
Coursework support stops at teaching the skill and explaining the mark scheme
Ask for your named contact and the escalation path in the first conversation

faqs.question: How quickly should a query be answered and a tutor found?
faqs.answer: The reply should be quick and the match should be honest rather than fast. For a common request such as Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 in a well-supplied locality, a shortlist usually follows soon. For a specific syllabus at a specific weeknight time in a smaller city, it can take considerably longer, and sometimes the honest answer is that no local home tutor exists and online is the route. What should never happen is silence: ask at the start who will update you and through which channel.

faqs.question: What do we do if the tutor is good but the fit is wrong?
faqs.answer: Say so early and without building a case. Fit failures are ordinary, and a tutor who is excellent with one student can be wrong for another for reasons neither party controls. Ask for a different match, request a handover note as part of the change, and expect the conversation to be handled by someone other than the tutor. In Grade 10 treat it as urgent rather than polite, because a term spent being patient is a term you will not get back.

faqs.question: What should a monthly report to parents actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four things on half a page: what was covered, what the marked work showed, what the student was set between sessions and what he returned, and what changes next month. Coverage should name topics and question types rather than just the subject. There should be at least one honest negative, because a month with nothing wrong in it did not happen. The plan for next month should be short enough for a parent to check in four weeks without any subject expertise.

faqs.question: Can home tuition sessions be rescheduled during mock week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should be. During mocks the student's evenings are already committed, so fewer and shorter sessions work better than the normal weekly load, and some families pause for the week entirely. Give the service the mock dates as soon as the school publishes them, because a reschedule planned a month ahead is easy and one requested on the day is not. After mocks, the marked scripts arrive and the following four to six weeks are the most valuable of the year.

faqs.question: Our home tuition tutor keeps arriving late in Thane. What is the escalation path?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly with the tutor once, in writing and specifically, naming the dates. If nothing changes within two sessions, raise it with your named contact at the service and ask for a dated response rather than sympathy. If it still continues, ask for a different match or for the arrangement to convert to online, which removes the cause entirely. Chronic lateness across Thane, Navi Mumbai and Kharghar usually means the travel distance was never realistic, so a hybrid week is often the real fix.

faqs.question: What happens when the tutor is ill or travelling?
faqs.answer: One of three things, agreed in advance: the session moves within the same week, it converts to online with the same tutor, or it is credited and skipped. Which one suits you depends on how much slack your week has. What should not happen is an unannounced substitute arriving with no briefing, because for subjects such as Chemistry 0620 or Biology 0610, where a topic runs across several weeks, that wastes the hour. For longer absences, ask for a handover note and a review date.

faqs.question: We are in Coimbatore and nobody teaches 0455 here. What can a service realistically offer?
faqs.answer: Online, quickly, rather than a home visit eventually. Supply for named syllabuses thins sharply across Coimbatore, Kochi, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam and Madurai, and waiting for a local Economics tutor who may not exist costs a family weeks it could have spent teaching. A service worth using says this in the first conversation rather than the fourth. Economics transfers well online because the assessed work is written, so relatively little is lost by comparison with a subject where paper working matters.

faqs.question: Should the service speak to our school directly?
faqs.answer: No, and be wary of one that offers to. The relationship with the school belongs to the family, and an outside tutor contacting a coordinator or subject teacher unprompted creates awkwardness that lands on the student. What a service can do is help you prepare for the conversation: which question to ask about tier, what to bring to a parent meeting, and how to describe a difficulty precisely. Ask the school for its own written position on private tuition and coursework support.

faqs.question: How much notice do we need to give to stop?
faqs.answer: Whatever you agreed at the start, which is why agreeing it matters. A notice period of a couple of weeks is common and protects both sides: the tutor has planned his term around your slot, and you should not be locked in longer than that. Give notice at a review point rather than by message where you can, ask for a handover note whether or not a new tutor is coming, and settle anything outstanding. Ending well costs nothing and keeps the option open.

faqs.question: Is it reasonable to ask for session-by-session records?
faqs.answer: Entirely, and one line per session is enough. Date, topic, question types, and what was set. It costs the tutor two minutes, it lets you see coverage against the school's scheme of work, and it is the single thing that makes a later handover fast rather than painful. Ask for it in the first week rather than in month six, because records nobody kept cannot be reconstructed. If a service declines this, that answer is itself informative.

faqs.question: What promises should make us suspicious?
faqs.answer: Any specific grade or promised improvement, instant availability for every syllabus and slot, an assurance that the tutor will never change, and an offer to handle coursework. Each of those is either impossible or improper. The honest versions are a plan with a review date, a truthful answer about local supply, a handover process, and support that stops at teaching the skill and explaining how marks are awarded. A service that says no to something in the first conversation is usually the more reliable one.

faqs.question: Does a booking near the exam series work differently?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the operational rules should change with it. In the final weeks sessions need to move at short notice around the school's revision programme and the examination timetable, so agree a separate short-notice rule for that period. Many families shift to shorter, more frequent sessions, accept that some will be online, and let the tutor coordinate directly with the student's own calendar. Expect the content to narrow too, dropping topics deliberately rather than adding them.

comparison.heading: Who answers when something goes wrong: four tutoring routes in India
comparison.intro: These four routes teach in much the same way and differ sharply in what happens on a bad week. Judge them on one question rather than on their descriptions: if the arrangement stops working in the middle of Grade 10, who picks up the phone, and what can they actually do about it? Convenience and cost matter, but recoverability is what families remember.

h1: IGCSE Tutor Finder: Search, Shortlist and Trial in India
heroTitle: Finding an IGCSE Tutor in India, Properly
heroSubtitle: Searching is easy and shortlisting is hard. Most families meet three plausible tutors, pick the friendliest, and discover in November that nobody read the syllabus. This page is a method: where to look, which questions expose a generalist, how to run a trial, and how to choose between two candidates.
introSummary: An IGCSE tutor finder in India is really a filter, and the job is to narrow a long list of people offering home tuition and online lessons down to two you can test properly. Most searches fail at the same point: a general Class 10 tutor says yes to Cambridge IGCSE work, the family cannot tell the difference, and a term goes by before the marked papers say otherwise. The fix is unglamorous. Learn your four facts, ask the syllabus questions a generalist cannot answer, read profiles for evidence rather than adjectives, run a structured trial, then choose between two candidates on what actually happened in those trials rather than on who was warmest.

contentBlocks.heading: How does an IGCSE tutor finder in India build your shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
By asking narrow questions before it names anybody. You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks for the board, the syllabus and its code, the tier, the exam series, the school calendar, your locality and the hours you can keep, and then shortlists verified tutor profiles that match. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits.

The narrowness is the point. A directory that answers the question you typed will return everybody who teaches Grade 10 anything, and you will spend a fortnight interviewing people who were never going to fit. A filter that answers the question you should have typed returns two or three names, each of whom has taught your child's paper. Fewer names is a better outcome than more names, which is the opposite of how most search results are sold.

Locality then decides the format rather than the quality. If you are in Powai, Thane, Whitefield or Kondapur, a home tutor is usually reachable on a weekday evening and home tuition is the sensible default. If you are in Mysuru or Vijayawada, the honest answer may be that nobody nearby has taught the syllabus, and the shortlist will be online. Say which evenings genuinely survive school and sleep, because the slot decides who can take you.

Then the family does the testing. Run the trial, watch what the tutor does with a marked script, and keep notes you can compare afterwards. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match, subject to tutor availability. Asking in week two is ordinary. Asking in the week before a mock is not.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with the board and code named.
2. Give the tier, the exam series and the school's deadline calendar.
3. State your locality and the evenings that genuinely work.
4. Review a shortlist of verified profiles rather than a full directory.
5. Trial two of them, then choose, or ask for a different match.

contentBlocks.heading: Boards, tiers and series: the four facts a search starts from
contentBlocks.body:
Do not begin a search without four facts in writing: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the exam series. A tutor cannot be judged without them, and the school will supply all four in one reply. Families who skip this step are the ones who later discover that the hours were bought against the wrong paper.

IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, offered by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It usually runs across Grades 9 and 10, and it leads in three quite different directions: the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a switch to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Where a student is going should influence which subjects get hours now, because the Grade 10 that prepares a student for Mathematics at Higher Level is not the Grade 10 that prepares one for ISC.

Grades differ by board, and this catches people out constantly. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses available in 9 to 1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. A tutor who talks about a grade 7 without checking which scale applies has not looked at the entry.

Tiers are the part that quietly sets the ceiling. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. If the school has entered your child for Core, no amount of tutoring produces an A, and the useful conversation is with the school about moving tier, not with a tutor about hours. Series dates finish the picture. Cambridge runs February and March, a series offered only in India, plus May and June and October and November, while Edexcel runs January and May and June.
items: Get four facts in writing: board, syllabus code, tier, exam series
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE uses 9 to 1
Core tops out at grade C; only Extended reaches A*
Cambridge series: February and March, May and June, October and November
Edexcel series: January, and May and June
Where Class 11 leads should shape which subjects get hours now

contentBlocks.heading: Which syllabus-code questions expose a general tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
Four questions, and they take under five minutes. A tutor who has taught the syllabus answers all four without pausing. A general Class 10 tutor who has agreed to take on IGCSE work will manage one or two and start talking about experience instead, which is the answer you were looking for.

Question one, for Mathematics 0580. Which papers does an Extended candidate sit? From the 2025 examinations, Extended candidates sit Paper 2, which is non-calculator, and Paper 4, which is with a calculator; Core candidates sit Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, with a calculator. A tutor who does not know that a non-calculator paper exists has been teaching something else. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 the structure is different again: tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers in each tier.

Question two, for the sciences. Is my child sitting Paper 5 or Paper 6? Cambridge sciences examined from 2023 assess practical work either through Paper 5, a practical test, or through Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school chooses. The weighting is worth knowing before you buy hours: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

Question three, for English. Which English is it? First Language English 0500 has a reading paper and then directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio. English as a Second Language is 0510 or 0511, and the difference matters: 0511 counts speaking into the grade while 0510 reports speaking separately. Literature in English is 0475. Edexcel offers English Language A 4EA1, English Language B 4EB1 and English as a Second Language 4ES1. Question four is simply the tier, and what its ceiling is.
items: 0580 Extended sits Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 with a calculator
0580 Core sits Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 with a calculator
Edexcel 4MA1 is Foundation or Higher, two calculator papers per tier
Cambridge sciences: Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical
Science weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%
0511 counts speaking into the grade; 0510 reports it separately

contentBlocks.heading: Searching for an IGCSE tutor in India: what each city gives you
contentBlocks.body:
Supply is uneven in a way that no search box tells you, so adjust your expectations to your map before you start. In Delhi NCR the pool is deep and the distances are the problem. A family in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri can usually find a home tutor within a workable drive, while one in Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad is negotiating with the evening itself. Traffic between Noida and the southern parts of the city can stretch a short trip badly, and Golf Course Road and Sector 128 Noida families run into the same arithmetic from the other direction.

Across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, an IGCSE tutor finder in Mumbai has to account for the fact that Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli and Lower Parel are one market and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are effectively another. A Powai family will often find two good candidates locally and no specialist for an unusual code. In Bengaluru the same split runs east to west: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City hold plenty of demand, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each have their own pockets of supply. An IGCSE tutor finder in Bangalore that ignores which side of the city the tutor lives on is not doing its job.

Hyderabad is the tightest cluster of the four. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet sit close enough that an IGCSE tutor finder in Hyderabad can genuinely offer home visits, while Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad involve a separate journey. An IGCSE tutor finder in Chennai or an IGCSE tutor finder in Pune follows similar logic on a different map.

Southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai is the honest exception. In Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, searching how to find an IGCSE tutor locally usually returns general tutors and entrance-exam centres. There the search should start online and stay there for the syllabus itself, with a local home tutor kept for routine work. Typing IGCSE tutor finder near me in Vijayawada and typing it in Bandra are two different activities with the same words.
items: Delhi NCR: deep supply, long evenings; Dwarka and Ghaziabad pay in travel
Mumbai: Bandra to Worli is one market, Thane and Kharghar another
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are a different pool from Jayanagar
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kondapur sit close enough for home visits
Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Madurai: start the search online, not locally

contentBlocks.heading: School timetables in India, and when to start looking for a home tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Start the search at one of three moments: early in Grade 9 when a subject is already hard, immediately after the school raises a tier decision, or the week a mock result shows a gap that revision alone will not close. The worst moment is six weeks before the series, when everybody is looking and the good tutors are full.

The school controls more of the timetable than families realise. It makes the entries, it decides tiers, it chooses whether a science candidate sits a practical test or the alternative to practical paper, and it sets internal deadlines and mocks that fall well ahead of anything published by a board. A tutor cannot see any of it. Send the school diary in the first week and ask for the term plan to be written against those dates, not against a generic topic list.

In practice this shapes the weekly slot too. Schools in India run long days, and by the time a Grade 10 student reaches a seven o'clock session they have already been working for ten hours. Two shorter sessions usually beat one long one, and a Saturday morning slot is often the most productive hour of the week, though it is also the first to disappear from a good tutor's calendar.

One necessary note. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. A tutor may have taught students from schools whose names you recognise, which says something about the pace they are used to and nothing about any relationship. Confirm entries, tiers and deadlines with your child's own coordinator rather than with anybody selling hours.
items: Start in Grade 9, after a tier decision, or after a revealing mock
Avoid starting six weeks before the series, when good tutors are full
The school sets entries, tiers, practical routes and internal deadlines
Two shorter sessions usually beat one long evening session
Saturday mornings are productive and disappear from calendars first

contentBlocks.heading: A home tutor, an online specialist, or a centre nearby?
contentBlocks.body:
Pick the format from the problem, not from the brochure. If the student understands the content and will not start work, you need a person in the room, so home tuition wins. If the student works hard and the syllabus is unusual, you need the right teacher more than a nearby one, so online wins. If the student needs structure and company more than diagnosis, a neighbourhood centre can be reasonable value.

Home classes give a tutor information nothing else does. They see the desk, the phone, the notebook that stops three weeks ago, and the exact minute attention goes. For Grade 9 students, whose real difficulty is usually habit rather than content, that visibility matters more than syllabus depth. The price is travel: a home tutor can only take so many evening slots in a city where crossing town costs an hour, and the good ones fill those slots early.

Online widens the pool from your locality to the country. Past papers can be annotated live, a scanned script can be marked while the student watches, and a session can run the night before a mock without anybody leaving the house. What is lost is the room, which matters most for younger students and for anybody who needs supervision rather than explanation.

Hybrid is the arrangement most families reach in the end, and it is worth reaching sooner. Keep a local home tutor for the routine subjects and the habit of sitting down, and add an online specialist for the one syllabus nobody nearby has taught. Review both after a month against the marked work. Drop whichever half is not changing anything, and do not keep a tutor out of politeness.
items: Home tuition wins when the problem is starting work, not understanding it
Online wins when the syllabus is unusual and the student already works
A neighbourhood centre buys structure and company, not diagnosis
Hybrid: a home tutor for routine subjects, online for the scarce code
Review both halves after a month and drop what is not working

contentBlocks.heading: Reading an IGCSE tutor profile in India: signal against noise
contentBlocks.body:
Read every profile twice: once for what it claims, once for what it can prove. The difference between the two is the whole skill. Signal is specific and checkable. Noise is warm, general and could describe anybody teaching anything.

Signal looks like this. Named syllabus codes rather than subject names. Tiers, so 0580 Extended rather than Maths. The series they have prepared students for. A sentence about what they do in a first session. A statement of what they do not teach, which is the single most reassuring line a profile can contain, because a tutor who declines Business Studies is telling the truth about Physics. Anything that describes method in enough detail to be wrong is worth reading twice.

Noise looks like this. All boards, all subjects, all grades. Years of experience with no mention of which cohorts or which papers. Result-oriented, dedicated, passionate. Long lists of qualifications that never touch the syllabus in question. Claims about ranks and outcomes that no parent can check. Star ratings deserve caution too, since a small number of them tells you very little and they are easy to accumulate from the wrong kind of lesson.

Verification on IB Gram means identity and claimed teaching background are checked before a profile goes live. It is a filter, not a promise about teaching quality, and no honest platform will tell you otherwise. What it buys you is a shorter list of plausible people. Everything after that is your trial, your notes and your judgement of what happened in front of you.
items: Signal: named codes, tiers, series taught and what the tutor declines
Noise: all boards and all subjects, with no paper ever named
A profile that describes method specifically enough to be wrong is useful
Verification covers identity and background, not lesson quality
Treat a handful of star ratings as close to no information

contentBlocks.heading: Where families search in India, and what each source is good at
contentBlocks.body:
Five sources, and each is good at one thing and bad at another. Any IGCSE tutor finder in India, whether it is a platform, a neighbour or a search box, is only as good as the source behind it, so knowing which is which saves a month.

Other parents are the most trusted source and the narrowest. A recommendation from the class group carries real information, because somebody watched this tutor work for a term. It also carries a hidden mismatch: the tutor was right for that child's problem, which may be nothing like yours, and a tutor who rescued a student in First Language English is not automatically useful for 0580 Extended. Take the name, then run your own questions on it anyway.

The school is the second source, and it is delicate. Some schools keep a list, some prohibit their own staff from tutoring their own students, and most will at least tell you what the gap is if you ask the subject teacher directly. Ask for the diagnosis rather than the name; that is the part only the school has.

Classifieds and marketplace listings give you volume and nothing else. No verification, no filtering, and a response rate that will fill your phone for a week. They are worth using only if you already know your four facts and can screen hard on the first message. Local tuition centres are the fourth source: easy to find, easy to visit, honest about their timetable, and rarely able to tell you much about one student's specific paper.

A platform is the fifth, and its actual value is narrow but real: profiles are verified before they go live, the shortlist is matched to what you described rather than to what you typed, a trial can be arranged before you commit, and you can ask for a different match without an awkward conversation. None of that replaces your own trial. It just means you spend your trials on plausible people.
items: Other parents: high trust, tiny sample, possibly the wrong problem
The school: ask for the diagnosis rather than for a name
Classifieds: volume with no verification, only useful if you screen hard
Local centres: easy to visit, weak on one student's specific paper
A platform: verified profiles, a matched shortlist, and a trial before you commit

contentBlocks.heading: Two tutors, two trials: how do you choose between them?
contentBlocks.body:
Score both on the same five things within a day of the trials, while you still remember the detail. Who asked for the marked script before the session rather than during it. Who named a paper. Who spent more of the hour listening than talking. Who left a specific task with a way of checking it. And whose plan for the next month you could repeat to somebody else without looking at your notes.

Do not choose on warmth, and do not choose on the fee alone. Warmth is pleasant and it correlates with nothing, and the cheaper tutor who teaches the wrong paper is the most expensive option on the list. If both candidates score well, prefer the one whose diagnosis matched what the school has been saying, because agreement between two people who have not spoken is the closest thing to evidence you will get at this stage.

The honest limits belong here too. No tutor can guarantee a grade. A Core entry caps what is available whatever anybody promises. A student who does not work between sessions will not improve, and a second tutor will not fix the first tutor's unfinished homework. Starting very late narrows the work to technique, which helps, but less than starting earlier would have.

And if neither candidate is right, say so and start again rather than settling. Widen the search to online, since the pool from Kochi to Delhi NCR is larger than the pool within a ten-minute drive. Reduce the number of subjects so you are hiring for one clear problem. Ask for a different match, and expect an IGCSE tutor finder in India to run that second round without making it awkward. Occasionally the right answer is no tutor at all for a term, with the school's support hours used properly instead, and an honest platform should be willing to tell you that.
items: Score both trials the same day, on the same five questions
Prefer the diagnosis that agrees with what the school has said
Warmth correlates with nothing; the wrong paper costs the most
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a Core entry caps the ceiling
If neither fits, widen to online, cut subjects, or ask for another match

contentBlocks.heading: Your first home session in India: a script for the trial
contentBlocks.body:
Prepare three things and the trial runs itself: a recent marked script with the teacher's comments left on it, the four facts from the school, and one sentence describing what you want to be different in six weeks. Send all of it before the session so nobody spends the first fifteen minutes on introductions.

The session itself has a shape worth insisting on. Diagnosis first, teaching second, plan third. A tutor who opens by teaching a topic has skipped the only part of the hour you cannot replace, because anybody can explain quadratics and very few people can tell you why this student is losing marks on them.

Sit within earshot for the first session, not in the room. You are listening for three things: whether your child is talking, whether the tutor is asking questions or answering them, and whether the last ten minutes produce a plan rather than a summary. Home classes make this easy, and an online trial gives you the same information if you leave the door open.

An IGCSE tutor finder in India can hand you plausible names; only the trial tells you which of them teaches. Afterwards, write your notes down before you discuss it with anybody. Then decide. When you are ready to start, send a query or book a free consultation, and IB Gram will ask about board, syllabus, tier, level, the school calendar, your locality and your schedule before shortlisting verified tutors who match, subject to availability. Take the trial, use the script, and ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.
items: 1. Send the marked script and the four facts before the session.
2. Ask the tutor to name the papers and tier back to you.
3. Watch them work through one wrong answer with the student.
4. Time how long your child talks compared with the tutor.
5. Ask for one task for the week and how it will be checked.
6. Write your notes the same day, then compare the two trials.

faqs.question: Where should I actually start looking for an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Start with the school, but ask for the diagnosis rather than a name. The subject teacher can tell you whether the problem is content, technique or work rate, and that single sentence shapes everything after it. Then collect names from the class group and from a platform where profiles are verified, and screen every name with the same syllabus questions. Two well-screened candidates beat eight names on a list, and the screening takes less time than one wasted month.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a tutor has genuinely taught Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions and listen for hesitation. Which papers does an Extended candidate sit in 0580? Is my child entered for the practical test or the alternative to practical? Which English syllabus is this, and does speaking count into the grade? What is the ceiling on a Core entry? Somebody who has taught the course answers all four immediately and often corrects your phrasing. Somebody who has not will redirect towards years of experience and a general confidence about results.

faqs.question: What should I ask before the first home session?
faqs.answer: Ask for the tutor's plan for the hour, and send them the marked script in advance. A prepared tutor will tell you they intend to diagnose rather than teach, and will ask you what the school has said. Also settle the practical details before anyone travels: the start time, what happens if a session is missed, whether you will get a short written note afterwards, and where in the house the session will run. Ten minutes of email saves the first session.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in our neighbourhood good enough?
faqs.answer: For some students, yes, and it is worth saying so plainly. A centre buys structure, a fixed timetable and the company of other students working, which suits a child who needs pace more than diagnosis. What it rarely buys is attention to one student's paper. Ask which codes and tiers the batch is pitched at, how mixed the room is, and who teaches it in February rather than in August. If the answers are vague, the batch is not built around your child's entry.

faqs.question: How many tutors should we trial before deciding?
faqs.answer: Two is usually right, and three is the maximum worth the disruption. One trial gives you nothing to compare against, so a mediocre tutor looks fine. Four turns the search into the project, and meanwhile nobody is teaching your child. Run two trials in the same week, score them on identical questions the same day, and choose. If both fail, that is useful information too, and the next pair should be drawn from a different source.

faqs.question: Should we take a home tutor who lives across the city, or an online specialist?
faqs.answer: If the two are equally matched on the syllabus, take the online specialist, because a long commute quietly kills arrangements by about week eight. Tutors who cross a city in evening traffic arrive tired, cancel more often, and eventually ask to change the slot. If the distant home tutor is clearly better on the actual paper, take them and fix the schedule so the travel happens once a week rather than twice, or run one session at home and one online.

faqs.question: What does a verified profile actually guarantee?
faqs.answer: It confirms identity and checks claimed teaching background before the profile goes live, and that is the whole of it. Verification does not mean anybody has observed the teaching, and a platform that suggests otherwise is overselling. Treat it as a filter that removes the implausible so your time goes to real candidates. The evidence you rely on comes from the trial you run and from the first month of marked work, not from a badge on a listing.

faqs.question: The school has entered my child for Core. Can a tutor get an A?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor who says otherwise has not read the entry. Core tops out at grade C in the Cambridge subjects that are tiered, so the ceiling is set before tuition begins. The conversation you need is with the school about whether a move to Extended is realistic and by when, and a good tutor will help you build the evidence for that conversation rather than take your money against an impossible target. Ask for that evidence in writing.

faqs.question: None of the shortlisted tutors felt right. What do we do now?
faqs.answer: Say so and start a second round rather than settling on the least bad option. Change one variable at a time: widen from local home tuition to online, or reduce from three subjects to the single one that matters most, or shift the slot to a Saturday morning where better tutors have availability. Ask the platform for a different match and explain precisely what was missing. A vague complaint produces a vague second shortlist.

faqs.question: Should I tell the tutor what the school has said about my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, all of it, including the uncomfortable parts. A tutor who knows the student misses deadlines, avoids a particular topic or freezes in timed conditions can plan for it in week one instead of discovering it in week six. Families often soften the report to protect the child, and it costs a month. Send the actual comments, the actual marks and the actual teacher's phrasing, then let the tutor tell you whether they agree with the diagnosis.

faqs.question: How quickly should a new tutor produce something visible?
faqs.answer: Expect visible process change in two to four weeks and marked evidence by around week six. Early signs are papers attempted under time, notes organised by paper rather than by date, and a student who can say what a question is asking before starting it. If the folder looks identical after six weeks, the problem is the match or the diagnosis, and buying more hours repairs neither. Raise it then, in writing, rather than waiting for the next report.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors in the middle of Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better than persisting with an arrangement that is not working, though the timing matters. Changing early in a term costs a fortnight of settling in and is usually worth it. Changing in the weeks immediately before a series rarely is, because a new tutor spends the little remaining time learning the student. If you are close to the exams, keep the tutor and change what the sessions do instead: past papers under time, marked and discussed.
