Verification does not mean anybody has observed the teaching, and a platform that suggests otherwise is overselling. Treat it as a filter that removes the implausible so your time goes to real candidates. The evidence you rely on comes from the trial you run and from the first month of marked work, not from a badge on a listing.

mainEntity.name: The school has entered my child for Core. Can a tutor get an A?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and any tutor who says otherwise has not read the entry. Core tops out at grade C in the Cambridge subjects that are tiered, so the ceiling is set before tuition begins. The conversation you need is with the school about whether a move to Extended is realistic and by when, and a good tutor will help you build the evidence for that conversation rather than take your money against an impossible target. Ask for that evidence in writing.

mainEntity.name: None of the shortlisted tutors felt right. What do we do now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so and start a second round rather than settling on the least bad option. Change one variable at a time: widen from local home tuition to online, or reduce from three subjects to the single one that matters most, or shift the slot to a Saturday morning where better tutors have availability. Ask the platform for a different match and explain precisely what was missing. A vague complaint produces a vague second shortlist.

mainEntity.name: Should I tell the tutor what the school has said about my child?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, all of it, including the uncomfortable parts. A tutor who knows the student misses deadlines, avoids a particular topic or freezes in timed conditions can plan for it in week one instead of discovering it in week six. Families often soften the report to protect the child, and it costs a month. Send the actual comments, the actual marks and the actual teacher's phrasing, then let the tutor tell you whether they agree with the diagnosis.

mainEntity.name: How quickly should a new tutor produce something visible?

acceptedAnswer.text: Expect visible process change in two to four weeks and marked evidence by around week six. Early signs are papers attempted under time, notes organised by paper rather than by date, and a student who can say what a question is asking before starting it. If the folder looks identical after six weeks, the problem is the match or the diagnosis, and buying more hours repairs neither. Raise it then, in writing, rather than waiting for the next report.

mainEntity.name: Can we change tutors in the middle of Grade 10?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is better than persisting with an arrangement that is not working, though the timing matters. Changing early in a term costs a fortnight of settling in and is usually worth it. Changing in the weeks immediately before a series rarely is, because a new tutor spends the little remaining time learning the student. If you are close to the exams, keep the tutor and change what the sessions do instead: past papers under time, marked and discussed.

finalCta: Send a query or book a free consultation with your four facts ready: board, syllabus code, tier and exam series. IB Gram will ask about the school calendar, your locality and the hours you can keep, then shortlist verified tutors who match, subject to availability. Run two trials using the script above, compare them the same day, and ask for a different match if neither fits.

h1: IGCSE Tutor Platform in India: Verification, Profiles, Matching
heroTitle: How an IGCSE tutor platform in India should work
heroSubtitle: A platform is a filter with a process attached. This page explains exactly what is checked before a tutor profile goes live, what an IGCSE profile should state about syllabuses and tiers, how a match is made from first query to first lesson, and the checks a platform cannot make for you.
introSummary: An IGCSE tutor platform in India is only worth using if it removes work you would otherwise have to do badly yourself: confirming who a home tutor actually is, whether they have taught the syllabus code on your child's timetable, and whether the tier matches. That is the whole proposition, and it is worth being precise about its edges. This page sets out what verification covers before a profile goes live, what it cannot establish, what a good Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel profile should show, how matching runs end to end, how safeguarding differs between a home visit and an online lesson, and the three checks every family should still run themselves.

contentBlocks.heading: How matching runs end to end on an IGCSE tutor platform in India
contentBlocks.body:
Matching on an IGCSE tutor platform in India is worth describing step by step, because most families have only ever seen the output of it. You send a query or book a free consultation. We ask what the student is studying, in specifics rather than in subjects: which board, which syllabus code, which tier, which exam series the school has entered, and where the marks are being lost. Then location down to the locality, the lesson mode you want, and the evenings that genuinely survive school and travel.

That request is matched against profiles which have already been verified. The filter is narrower than families expect, which is the point. A profile that says Chemistry is not a match for a student sitting Extended tier 0620 unless the profile says so. A shortlist comes back, typically small, with the reasoning attached rather than hidden: why these people, and what each one is stronger at.

You then do the part no platform can do. Read the profiles, speak to one or two, and take a demo session. If the fit is wrong afterwards, ask for a different match. Nobody needs to justify that at length, and a platform that makes it awkward has the incentive backwards.

What makes this different from a classifieds listing is not the technology. It is that the same party is accountable at the start and at the sixth week. A listings site introduces you and disappears. A platform that arranged the match is the place you go when a home tutor stops turning up, when a syllabus turns out to be wrong, or when the student needs a different kind of teacher entirely. Availability throughout depends on subject, tier, level and schedule, and we would rather say a ring is empty than fill it with someone unsuitable.
items: 1. Send a query with board, syllabus code, tier and the school's exam series
2. Add your locality, the lesson mode you want and the workable evenings
3. We filter verified profiles against that exact syllabus and tier
4. A short shortlist comes back with the reasoning for each name attached
5. Take a demo session, then confirm, or ask for a different match

contentBlocks.heading: What a profile must state about Cambridge, Edexcel, Core and Extended
contentBlocks.body:
A useful IGCSE profile is specific in four places, and a profile vague in any of them is telling you something.

First, which qualification. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. They are separate qualifications with separate papers, and a tutor who has taught one is not automatically able to teach the other. A profile saying only IGCSE has skipped the first question a family should ask.

Second, the tier. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and the difference is not academic detail: Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. A tutor who has only prepared Core candidates is not the right match for a student whose school has entered them for Extended, however good they are. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is tiered Foundation or Higher instead, and the sciences there are untiered.

Third, the grading the tutor has actually worked with. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses available in 9 to 1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout. These are small differences with large practical consequences when a tutor is explaining to a Grade 10 student what a realistic target looks like.

Fourth, the exam series. Cambridge runs February and March, a series offered only in India, plus May and June and October and November. Edexcel runs January and May and June. A tutor who has only taught towards May and June will plan the wrong revision schedule for a February entry. Most of this belongs on the profile itself. All of it should be confirmed in the demo, because a profile is a claim and a conversation is a test.
items: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate qualifications
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*, and profiles should say which
Edexcel Mathematics A is tiered Foundation or Higher; its sciences are untiered
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE uses 9 to 1
Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
A profile is a claim; the demo session is where it gets tested

contentBlocks.heading: Syllabus codes on a profile, from 0580 to 0500
contentBlocks.body:
Codes are the most useful thing on an IGCSE profile and the thing most listings leave off. A tutor who writes Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Extended tier, has told you more in eight words than a paragraph of general description does.

Take the sciences, where the structure makes the point. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, in the syllabuses examined from 2023, put Core candidates on Paper 1 multiple choice and Extended candidates on Paper 2 multiple choice, with theory as Paper 3 for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, and the practical element through either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. The weighting is multiple choice 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. So a profile that mentions Paper 6 preparation is telling a family with a Paper 6 school something concrete, and a tutor who does not know which paper your school uses has not asked the question yet.

Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, separates the calculator and non-calculator papers by tier: Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without and Paper 4 with. The Pearson equivalent, International GCSE Mathematics A with code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher and has two calculator papers per tier. Those are not interchangeable teaching jobs.

Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 are the two most often described loosely. Economics looks like something any commerce background covers until the data response and the structured questions arrive. First Language English is regularly confused with the second language and the literature syllabuses, and the confusion usually surfaces in the first lesson rather than in the profile. Ask for codes. Every time.
items: A profile naming 0580 Extended says more than a paragraph of description
Cambridge sciences: Paper 1 or 2 multiple choice, Paper 3 or 4 theory
Practical comes through Paper 5 or Paper 6, whichever the school chose
Weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%
0580 from 2025: Core sits Papers 1 and 3, Extended sits Papers 2 and 4
Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers

contentBlocks.heading: How does a platform handle home tutor supply across India?
contentBlocks.body:
An IGCSE tutor platform in India should be honest about where supply is thin, which is the opposite of how most listings behave. A directory looks equally full everywhere because it lists everyone who registered. A platform that matches has to admit when a locality has nobody suitable, and that admission is the useful part of the service.

In Bengaluru the supply map is sharply drawn. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala and Indiranagar carry real depth for a home tutor teaching common syllabus codes. Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road often do not, and a tutor agreeing to cross the city on a weekday evening in September is agreeing to something that rarely lasts to January. Hyderabad divides similarly between the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet belt, with Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills adjacent, and Secunderabad a genuinely separate market. Pune is easier, because Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar sit close together, as do Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi.

Across Kolkata and eastern India the picture changes again. Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore have some supply for home classes; Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna have very little, and a family there is usually choosing between an online specialist and nobody. In Gujarat, a home tutor will often cross Ahmedabad between Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and Gandhinagar, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families should expect a thinner local list. Families in Mumbai and Delhi NCR run into the same pattern in their own geography.

What a platform should do with that is straightforward. Say which ring your match came from. Flag when a home visit involves a journey that will not survive the year. Offer the hybrid alternative before the arrangement fails rather than after. A match that quietly collapses in week seven is worse than a match never made, because the student has lost the term as well as the tutor.
items: A directory looks full everywhere; a matching service has to admit thin areas
Bengaluru: depth in the Whitefield and Koramangala belt, much less further out
Hyderabad: the Gachibowli to Kokapet belt behaves as one local market
Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati and Patna: often online or nobody
Ahmedabad crosses easily; Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot lists are thinner
A flagged long journey beats a home match that collapses in week seven

contentBlocks.heading: What the school knows that no platform in India can
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools appear here because a platform's information stops exactly where the school's begins, and families should know which questions to take where.

The school holds the entry. It decides the tier your child is entered at, which exam series they sit, and whether the science practical element is assessed through Paper 5 or Paper 6. No platform can see any of that, and no tutor should be guessing. Three questions to the coordinator before you book anything will save a month of misdirected preparation.

The school also holds the internal evidence. Class test patterns, the teacher's read on whether a student is coasting or struggling, and whether a poor mock reflects a genuine gap or a bad fortnight. A tutor can reconstruct some of that from marked scripts, and that reconstruction is always second-hand. Where a school offers a conversation, take it before hiring rather than after.

There is one more thing worth being blunt about. Parents at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School often hear a tutor recommended informally by other parents. That recommendation carries real information about reliability and manner. It carries almost none about whether that person has taught your child's syllabus code at your child's tier, because the recommending parent usually does not know their own child's code either. Both sources are useful. Neither replaces the other.
items: The school decides the tier, the exam series and the practical paper
Ask the coordinator those three questions before booking any tuition
Class test patterns and teacher judgement never reach a platform
A parent recommendation is evidence about manner, not about syllabus fit
Take school questions to the school and matching questions to the platform

contentBlocks.heading: Safeguarding home visits, online lessons and hybrid arrangements
contentBlocks.body:
The three modes carry different risks, and the sensible precautions differ accordingly. None of this is dramatic. It is the ordinary care any family would apply to any adult working with their child.

For home tuition, the basics are physical and simple. Lessons happen in a common area or a room with the door open rather than behind a closed bedroom door. An adult is in the house, which is not the same as being in the room. The tutor's identity is confirmed on the first visit against what the profile said, and society or building gate entry is arranged in the family's name rather than left informal. If a substitute ever arrives, no lesson happens until you have been told in advance and agreed.

For online lessons, the equivalents are digital. Sessions run on the agreed platform rather than drifting to a personal messaging app. Contact with the student stays inside channels a parent can see, and homework goes through the same route. The lesson happens in a shared part of the house with the door open, not in a bedroom with headphones on. If sessions are recorded, agree beforehand who keeps the recording and for how long.

Hybrid needs both sets of habits, and it is the mode where families most often get casual, because the online half feels informal after the home half has established trust. Keep the same rules for both.

On the platform's side, identity and the qualifications and syllabuses a tutor claims are checked before a profile goes live, and a reported concern is acted on rather than filed. What no verification can do is supervise a lesson. That part is the family's, and the arrangements above make it easy rather than intrusive.
items: Home classes happen in a common area or with the door open, adult in the house
Confirm identity on the first home visit against what the profile stated
No substitute tutor teaches without prior notice and your agreement
Online lessons stay on the agreed platform, not a personal messaging app
Agree in advance who keeps any recording, and for how long

contentBlocks.heading: What does verification actually cover, and what does it miss?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on an IGCSE tutor platform in India is a floor, not a verdict, and any provider describing it as more than that is overselling. Here is the honest boundary.

What is checked before a profile goes live: the tutor's identity, the qualifications the profile claims, and the specific boards, syllabuses, tiers and levels the tutor states they teach. A profile that claims Extended tier 0620 has to stand behind that claim. The point of the check is to remove the category of problem that wastes a family's month, which is discovering in week three that the tutor has never seen the paper your child will sit.

What verification cannot establish, and this list matters more: whether a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old will work well together; whether someone who taught brilliantly last year is distracted this year; whether a tutor who is excellent with a motivated student can handle a discouraged one; and whether the person will still find your locality convenient in January. Those are behavioural and situational, and no document check reaches them.

That gap is why the demo session exists and why asking for a different match is treated as routine. It is also why we do not publish claims that cannot be substantiated. Be wary of any platform advertising a guaranteed grade, a promised improvement or a published success rate. No tutor can guarantee a grade. Be equally wary of language implying an official relationship with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; those bodies approve schools as examination centres, not tutoring businesses.

One practical suggestion. Ask the platform directly what its verification does and does not include, and see whether the answer is specific. A vague answer to that question is more informative than a confident one.
items: Checked: identity, claimed qualifications, and the syllabuses and tiers claimed
Not checked: rapport, current motivation, and whether the journey stays convenient
The demo session is where fit is decided, not the profile
Asking for a different match should be routine, never awkward
Ask what verification excludes; a vague answer tells you a lot

contentBlocks.heading: Platform, classifieds site or a name from the parent group in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Three routes: an IGCSE tutor platform in India, a classifieds listing, or a name passed along in the school parent group. Most families try all three at once, which is why the comparison is worth making carefully.

A classifieds site is a noticeboard. Anyone can post, claims are unchecked, and the volume of responses feels like choice while actually being work transferred to you. You become the person confirming identity, testing syllabus knowledge and chasing a replacement when someone disappears. For a common subject in a dense locality this can work, and plenty of good tutors advertise that way. The cost is your time and the risk that you check less thoroughly than you think you are checking.

An informal referral through the school parent group is the opposite: very high confidence, very low coverage. The person comes with a real account of reliability and manner from someone you know. What that account almost never contains is whether they have taught your child's syllabus code at your child's tier, because the recommending parent rarely knows their own child's code. Referrals also concentrate: the three names everyone repeats are full by the start of the academic year.

A platform sits between them. It does the verification a classifieds site does not and provides the coverage a referral cannot, and in exchange it costs more than dealing with a freelancer directly and knows less about the person than a friend does. The honest summary is that a platform is worth using when you need a specific syllabus match, when you want someone accountable after week six, or when your locality does not produce a good name by itself. For a Grade 9 student needing general Mathematics support in a neighbourhood full of teachers, a referral may genuinely serve you better, and we would rather say that than pretend otherwise.
items: Classifieds: widest listing, no checks, and all the work lands on you
Referral: strong on reliability, silent on syllabus code and tier
The three names a parent group repeats are usually full by April
A platform adds verification and coverage, and costs more than a direct freelancer
For common subjects in dense localities, a referral can be the better route

contentBlocks.heading: What can a platform not see about your child?
contentBlocks.body:
Almost everything that decides whether tuition works, which is worth saying plainly on a page selling the service.

A platform sees a request. It does not see that the student has decided they are bad at Chemistry and has quietly stopped attempting questions. It does not see that a household has two adults with different views about how much pressure is appropriate. It does not see that the real problem is sleep, or a friendship that has gone wrong, or a school relationship that broke down in Grade 9 and has never been repaired. Those things determine outcomes more often than the tutor's subject knowledge does, and a marked script only hints at them.

So the family's own checks remain the important ones. After four weeks, ask the student to explain what they now do differently in a paper. If the answer is nothing, the sessions are not landing, regardless of how pleasant they are. Ask to see something they have written and had marked. Ask the tutor what they would stop doing; a good one always has an answer.

Be realistic about timing. Grades move over a term, not a month, and no tutor can guarantee a grade. A tier decision between Core and Extended is made on evidence over a year, not on a hope. And if a student is being tutored in three subjects at once while also managing coursework, the tuition itself has become part of the load. Dropping one is often the intervention that helps most.

The last check is the simplest. Is your child less anxious about the subject than they were six weeks ago? That is not a soft measure. It is the one that predicts whether they will keep working when nobody is watching.
items: A platform sees a request, never the household or the history behind it
Four weeks: the student should be able to say what they now do differently
Ask to see one piece of written work that has been marked
Grades move over a term; tier decisions rest on a year of evidence
Less anxiety about the subject after six weeks is a real indicator

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a first home session through an IGCSE tutor platform in India
contentBlocks.body:
Bring four things and the first session does real work instead of introductions.

The syllabus details, confirmed with the school: board, code, tier, exam series, and whether the science practical element is Paper 5 or Paper 6. Two marked papers, including one that went badly, because the pattern of lost marks is the best diagnostic document you own. The term calendar with mock weeks and coursework deadlines marked. And one written sentence saying what you actually want, which is worth doing because households frequently discover they disagree while saying it out loud.

Then the room. Home classes need a table the student can spread a past paper across, a working light, and a door that closes. An adult in the house, not in the room. If any part of the arrangement will run online, set up the headset and the scanning routine at the same time rather than treating it as a separate task later.

Expect the first session to be diagnostic rather than instructional. Expect the tutor to watch the student attempt something in the first fifteen minutes. Expect a short written plan afterwards naming what will be worked on and in what order.

When you are ready, send a query or book a free consultation. We ask about board, syllabus, tier, exam series, school calendar, locality and schedule, shortlist tutors whose verified profiles match those needs, and arrange a demo session before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid of the two. Fees depend on subject, tier, experience and whether the tutor travels, and we set out the structure before any lesson is booked. If the fit turns out wrong, ask for a different match.
items: Confirm board, code, tier, series and practical paper with the school first
Bring two marked papers, the term calendar and one sentence of intent
Set up the table, the light and the door before the first home session
Expect a diagnostic first lesson and a short written plan afterwards
Home, online or hybrid: say which you want when you send the query

faqs.question: What exactly does verifying a tutor profile mean?
faqs.answer: It means three specific things are established before the profile goes live: the tutor's identity, the qualifications the profile claims, and the boards, syllabuses, tiers and levels they state they teach. It is a floor rather than a judgement of teaching quality. Verification cannot establish rapport with your child, current motivation, or whether someone who taught well last year is stretched this year. Ask any platform what its verification excludes as well as what it includes, because the specificity of that answer is itself informative.

faqs.question: Why use a platform instead of a name from our school parent group?
faqs.answer: Use both, for different purposes. A referral gives you a genuine account of reliability and manner from someone you trust, which is valuable and hard to obtain otherwise. What it rarely tells you is whether that person has taught your child's syllabus code at your child's tier, because the recommending parent usually does not know their own child's code. A platform adds that filter plus coverage when your locality has no obvious name. For a common subject in a dense area, a good referral may serve you perfectly well.

faqs.question: What should a home tutor's profile tell me before the first visit?
faqs.answer: Board, syllabus codes with tiers, exam series taught towards, the modes offered, and the localities they genuinely cover. For a home tutor the last of those matters as much as the first, because a tutor listing an entire metro is describing an ambition rather than a schedule. In Bengaluru, a profile saying Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and HSR Layout is more useful than one saying Bengaluru. Treat everything on the profile as a claim to be tested in the demo session rather than as settled fact.

faqs.question: Is a platform safer than hiring directly for home classes?
faqs.answer: On identity and syllabus claims, yes, because those are checked before a profile goes live rather than left to the family. On supervision, no platform can help, and that part stays with you. Keep home lessons in a common area or with the door open, have an adult in the house without sitting in the room, confirm identity on the first visit, and insist that no substitute teaches without prior notice and your agreement. Those habits are simple and they matter more than any verification.

faqs.question: How does the platform handle online lessons differently?
faqs.answer: The safeguarding shifts from physical to digital. Sessions should run on the agreed platform rather than migrating to a personal messaging app, contact with the student should stay in channels a parent can see, and the lesson should happen in a shared part of the house rather than a bedroom with the door shut. If sessions are recorded, agree in advance who keeps the recording and for how long. Families running a hybrid arrangement should apply both sets of habits, because the online half tends to get casual once trust is established.

faqs.question: We are in Ahmedabad. How wide is the tutor list there?
faqs.answer: Reasonable within Ahmedabad itself and thinner outside it. A home tutor will often cross between Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and Gandhinagar without difficulty, which makes central Ahmedabad a workable local market for common syllabus codes. Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families should expect a shorter list and should consider online for anything at Extended tier. We would rather tell you the local list is thin than stretch someone into a journey that stops being sustainable by December.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not a good fit after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, and try to name the problem precisely, because it changes who we send next. A tutor who knows the syllabus but cannot hold the student's attention needs a different replacement from one the student likes but who is vague about mark schemes. Three or four weeks is long enough to judge fit and communication. It is not long enough to judge results, so separate those two before deciding. The request does not need to be framed as a complaint.

faqs.question: Can a platform tell us which tier our child should sit?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who says otherwise is guessing. The school decides and enters the candidate, and the tier decision should rest on a year of evidence rather than on one mock or one opinion. What a tutor can do is give you a grounded read: sit the student with both a Core and an Extended past paper, mark both against the mark schemes, and see what the gap actually looks like. Take that evidence to the coordinator. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the decision is worth real care.

faqs.question: Do you work with tutors in Pune and Kolkata?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the usual difference between dense and thin areas. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar form one workable cluster and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi another, so home matches are realistic in both. Across Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore carry some supply, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna are largely online markets. Availability always depends on the subject, the tier and the hour you need.

faqs.question: Does a platform cost more than finding a tutor ourselves?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the difference buys verification, matching against the exact syllabus and tier, and somebody accountable in week six rather than only in week one. Whether that is worth paying for depends on your situation. If you already know a good tutor who teaches your child's code, dealing with them directly will be cheaper and perfectly sensible. If you are searching cold, or need a tier or syllabus that is scarce nearby, the filter usually saves more time than it costs. There is no fixed figure; fees depend on subject, tier and schedule.

faqs.question: Are you connected to Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no official relationship to Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the International Baccalaureate, and no relationship with any school. Those bodies approve schools as examination centres; they do not approve tutoring services. If you see a provider implying otherwise, treat it as a warning about everything else they claim. Past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports reach families through their school or the board's own official channels.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a shortlist?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on what you need than on how fast anyone works. A common subject at a common tier in a dense locality is usually quick. Extended tier sciences, a specific practical paper, a rare combination or a weekday evening in a thinly supplied area take longer, and sometimes the honest answer is that nothing local fits and online is the better route. We would rather return a short accurate list than a long one padded with people who do not teach the syllabus your child sits.

mainEntity.name: What exactly does verifying a tutor profile mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: It means three specific things are established before the profile goes live: the tutor's identity, the qualifications the profile claims, and the boards, syllabuses, tiers and levels they state they teach. It is a floor rather than a judgement of teaching quality. Verification cannot establish rapport with your child, current motivation, or whether someone who taught well last year is stretched this year. Ask any platform what its verification excludes as well as what it includes, because the specificity of that answer is itself informative.

mainEntity.name: Why use a platform instead of a name from our school parent group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use both, for different purposes. A referral gives you a genuine account of reliability and manner from someone you trust, which is valuable and hard to obtain otherwise. What it rarely tells you is whether that person has taught your child's syllabus code at your child's tier, because the recommending parent usually does not know their own child's code. A platform adds that filter plus coverage when your locality has no obvious name. For a common subject in a dense area, a good referral may serve you perfectly well.

mainEntity.name: What should a home tutor's profile tell me before the first visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Board, syllabus codes with tiers, exam series taught towards, the modes offered, and the localities they genuinely cover. For a home tutor the last of those matters as much as the first, because a tutor listing an entire metro is describing an ambition rather than a schedule. In Bengaluru, a profile saying Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and HSR Layout is more useful than one saying Bengaluru. Treat everything on the profile as a claim to be tested in the demo session rather than as settled fact.

mainEntity.name: Is a platform safer than hiring directly for home classes?

acceptedAnswer.text: On identity and syllabus claims, yes, because those are checked before a profile goes live rather than left to the family. On supervision, no platform can help, and that part stays with you. Keep home lessons in a common area or with the door open, have an adult in the house without sitting in the room, confirm identity on the first visit, and insist that no substitute teaches without prior notice and your agreement. Those habits are simple and they matter more than any verification.

mainEntity.name: How does the platform handle online lessons differently?

acceptedAnswer.text: The safeguarding shifts from physical to digital. Sessions should run on the agreed platform rather than migrating to a personal messaging app, contact with the student should stay in channels a parent can see, and the lesson should happen in a shared part of the house rather than a bedroom with the door shut. If sessions are recorded, agree in advance who keeps the recording and for how long. Families running a hybrid arrangement should apply both sets of habits, because the online half tends to get casual once trust is established.

mainEntity.name: We are in Ahmedabad. How wide is the tutor list there?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reasonable within Ahmedabad itself and thinner outside it. A home tutor will often cross between Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and Gandhinagar without difficulty, which makes central Ahmedabad a workable local market for common syllabus codes. Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families should expect a shorter list and should consider online for anything at Extended tier. We would rather tell you the local list is thin than stretch someone into a journey that stops being sustainable by December.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the tutor is not a good fit after a few weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for a different match, and try to name the problem precisely, because it changes who we send next. A tutor who knows the syllabus but cannot hold the student's attention needs a different replacement from one the student likes but who is vague about mark schemes. Three or four weeks is long enough to judge fit and communication. It is not long enough to judge results, so separate those two before deciding. The request does not need to be framed as a complaint.

mainEntity.name: Can a platform tell us which tier our child should sit?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and anyone who says otherwise is guessing. The school decides and enters the candidate, and the tier decision should rest on a year of evidence rather than on one mock or one opinion. What a tutor can do is give you a grounded read: sit the student with both a Core and an Extended past paper, mark both against the mark schemes, and see what the gap actually looks like. Take that evidence to the coordinator. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the decision is worth real care.

h1: IGCSE Teachers in India: Reading Qualifications and Claims
heroTitle: Reading What IGCSE Teachers in India Claim
heroSubtitle: Cambridge training, examiner experience, fifteen years in a classroom, a doctorate in physics. Each of these means something specific and none of them means the same thing. This page explains what each claim certifies, where it stops, and how to check it without an awkward conversation.
introSummary: IGCSE teachers in India advertise credentials that sound similar and are not, and a parent arranging home tuition has no obvious way to tell a strong claim from a decorative one. A subject degree is not teaching skill. Examining experience tells you about mark schemes and nothing about patience. Years in a classroom are worth a great deal, provided they were spent on the syllabus your child is actually sitting. What follows is a plain reading of each claim, the questions that test it politely, and the situations where the most qualified person available is the wrong choice for your child.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram check what IGCSE teachers in India claim?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification here means confirming that a profile describes the person accurately. Identity, the qualifications claimed, the syllabuses and levels taught, and the subjects a teacher will be matched for. It is a check on the description, not a prediction of how your child will do, and we would rather say that plainly than dress it up.

So a profile that reads Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620, Extended tier, seven years is matched for exactly that. It is not matched for Physics because the teacher took a science degree, and it is not matched for Cambridge International AS Level work because the subject name overlaps. Families are often surprised by how much difference that makes, and it is the single most useful thing a matching platform can do.

When you send a query we ask which board, which syllabus code, which tier and which examination series, because those four things narrow the field faster than any adjective. A teacher who has taught 0580 Extended through several series is a different proposition from one who has taught school mathematics well for a decade without meeting a Cambridge paper.

What remains is your judgement, and the trial session is where you exercise it. A profile can tell you what somebody has done. Only a lesson tells you whether they can explain the thing your child cannot do. Availability depends on subject, tier and slot, and the most sought-after teachers are booked earliest in the term.
items: Profiles are verified for identity, claimed qualifications, syllabuses, tiers and subjects
A teacher is matched for the exact syllabus taught, not for the subject in general
Tell us board, syllabus code, tier and series; those four narrow the field fastest
Verification describes the person accurately; it predicts nothing about results
The trial session is where your own judgement does the work a profile cannot

contentBlocks.heading: Which credentials matter for Core, Extended and each board
contentBlocks.body:
Before weighing anybody's experience, be precise about what your child is sitting, because a credential is only meaningful against a specific entry.

IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually taught across Grades 9 and 10 and followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. The calendars differ: Cambridge runs a February and March series offered only in India, plus May and June and October and November, while Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and in May and June. Grading differs too, with Cambridge grading most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses having 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE graded 9 to 1.

Tier changes what experience is relevant. Many Cambridge subjects offer Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. A teacher whose recent work has been with Core candidates knows a different set of problems from one who routinely pushes Extended students through the harder end of Paper 4. Neither is better. They are different jobs, and the right question is which one your child needs.

Board experience is rarely transferable in the way people assume. A teacher fluent in Cambridge papers meeting an Edexcel entry for the first time will be competent, not fluent, and the difference shows in small things: the structure of the papers, the calculator rules, the way practical skills are assessed. Ask directly which board they have taught most recently, and in which series.
items: Cambridge runs February and March in India, May and June, and October and November
Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and in May and June, graded 9 to 1
Core is capped at grade C and Extended reaches A*, which are different teaching jobs
Recent Core experience and recent Extended experience are not interchangeable
Ask which board and which series the teacher has taught most recently

contentBlocks.heading: Syllabus experience: 0580 is not the same as knowing mathematics
contentBlocks.body:
A subject degree proves that somebody learned the subject. It does not prove they can teach a fifteen-year-old to pick up method marks in a specific paper, and the gap between those two things is where most disappointing arrangements live.

Take a worked example. A candidate with a master's degree in physics is asked to help a Grade 10 student with Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625. The student is strong on the multiple-choice paper, which carries 30% of the grade, and loses heavily on the theory paper, which carries 50%, with practical assessment through Paper 5 or Paper 6 making up the remaining 20% depending on what the school runs. The graduate explains physics beautifully, at a level well above what the syllabus asks, and the student's theory marks do not move. Why? Because the problem was never understanding. It was writing an answer that says what the mark scheme wants in the number of lines available. A teacher who has marked that paper repeatedly fixes this in three sessions. A physicist who has not may never see it.

The same applies elsewhere. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits Extended candidates across Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, from the 2025 examinations, while Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers per tier. Knowing that structure and knowing where each paper punishes a student is syllabus experience. Knowing mathematics is something else.

So ask what they have taught, not what they have studied. Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 each reward different habits, and a teacher who names those habits without prompting is showing you their experience more convincingly than any certificate.
items: A subject degree proves study, not the ability to teach a specific paper
Sciences from 2023: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20% of the grade
Mathematics 0580 Extended splits across a non-calculator and a calculator paper
Ask what they have taught recently, not what they studied years ago
A teacher who names each syllabus's habits unprompted is showing real experience

contentBlocks.heading: Where experienced IGCSE teachers in India are concentrated
contentBlocks.body:
Experience follows the schools, and the schools are not evenly spread. That single fact explains most of what a family finds when they start looking.

Delhi NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region hold the deepest pools. An IGCSE teacher in Delhi with years of Cambridge classroom work is findable across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Golf Course Road, with Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad thinner but real. An IGCSE teacher in Mumbai is concentrated around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, while Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar have smaller local pools that are perfectly adequate for the common subjects.

Bengaluru spreads its experience across Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road. An IGCSE teacher in Bangalore is rarely hard to find for 0580 or 0620, though Economics 0455 thins out. Chennai runs along Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam in the older districts, and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar in the newer ones, so an IGCSE teacher in Chennai is usually found on the corridor rather than across the city. Pune and Hyderabad sit somewhere between these two patterns.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR is where the argument for online becomes overwhelming. In Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, there are excellent teachers and there are not many of them, and the chance that the one nearby has taught your child's exact syllabus and tier is low. Families in these cities who insist on a local home tutor often end up with a capable teacher who is learning the paper alongside the student. Reaching further, on a screen, is usually the better trade.
items: Delhi NCR and Mumbai hold the deepest pools of classroom-experienced teachers
Bengaluru is strong for 0580 and 0620, thinner for Economics 0455
Chennai experience clusters by corridor, from Adyar to Old Mahabalipuram Road
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun have good teachers in small numbers
Outside the metros, reaching further on a screen usually beats settling nearby

contentBlocks.heading: Why a serving school teacher in India is sometimes the wrong choice
contentBlocks.body:
A teacher from your child's own school looks like the obvious answer. They know the class, the scheme of work and the student, and they are often excellent. There are still three reasons to think carefully before arranging it.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the International Baccalaureate. Many schools have their own policies on staff taking private tuition with their own students, and those policies override anything suggested here.

The first reason is the conflict itself. A teacher who marks the student's classwork and also takes payment from the family is in an uncomfortable position, whatever their integrity, and the student notices. The second is that you lose a second opinion. When the classroom explanation has not worked, the useful thing is often a different explanation, and the person most likely to repeat the first one is the person who gave it. The third is practical: a serving teacher's term is already full, and the home classes most likely to be cancelled in a busy week are the paid ones.

A teacher from a different school avoids all three, keeps the second opinion, and can speak frankly about what the school is and is not doing. That is usually the better arrangement.

The school still matters, though, and you should use it. Your child's examinations officer or subject teacher can confirm the board, syllabus code, tier and series in writing, and they will tell you whether the sciences are being assessed through Paper 5 or Paper 6. Take that to the teacher you hire. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and a teacher joining in the unpressured Grade 9 stretch has time that one joining mid-Grade 10 simply does not.
items: Your own school's teacher marks the classwork and takes the fee, which is awkward
A second explanation is the point; the first explainer is least likely to give one
Paid sessions are the ones a busy serving teacher cancels first
Ask the school to confirm board, code, tier, series and Paper 5 or Paper 6 in writing
Check the school's own policy on staff tutoring their current students

contentBlocks.heading: Does a home tutor need different skills from an online teacher?
contentBlocks.body:
Yes, and the difference is bigger than most families expect. A teacher who is superb in a living room can be flat on a screen, and the reverse is just as common, so treat the mode as part of the credential rather than as a detail to settle afterwards.

A home tutor works by observation. They watch the pen, notice the pause before a student commits to an answer, and read the room well enough to know when to stop explaining. They also manage a household: a sibling wandering through, a doorbell, a student who has come straight from school and needs five minutes. Those are real skills and they do not appear on any certificate. Home teachers who have done years of visits usually have them.

An online teacher works by structure. Screen shared, paper on view, a clear plan for ninety minutes, and enough discipline to make the student write rather than watch. The best of them use a document camera or a graphics tablet so the working is visible, and they set up the session so silence is productive rather than awkward. A teacher who has only ever taught face to face may need a term to build that, and you will be paying for the learning curve.

Hybrid needs both, which is why it suits experienced teachers and defeats inexperienced ones. A weekly home visit for the written work plus a shorter online session midweek is an excellent pattern, and it is the arrangement that lets a family in Kharghar or Dehradun keep a teacher they rate who lives somewhere else entirely.

When you interview, ask which mode they have taught most in, and how many of their current students they see on a screen. The answer is more informative than it sounds.
items: Home tuition rewards observation: the pen, the pause, the moment to stop explaining
Online teaching rewards structure, a shared screen and productive silence
A document camera or graphics tablet is a practical sign of online experience
Hybrid suits experienced teachers and exposes inexperienced ones quickly
Ask how many of their current students they teach on a screen right now

contentBlocks.heading: How to verify a credential claim in India without giving offence
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every teacher expects to be asked and very few parents actually do. The trick is to ask about specifics rather than about honesty, because a specific question is a professional conversation while a general one sounds like an accusation.

Cambridge professional development is the claim that most often goes unexamined. Training courses of this kind certify that a teacher attended and completed a course about teaching a syllabus. That is genuinely useful, and it is worth confirming which course, in which year, and for which syllabus, because a course taken for one subject says little about another and a course taken long ago may predate the syllabus your child is sitting. It certifies training. It does not certify results, and it is not a licence of any kind.

Examiner experience is the claim with the sharpest edges. A teacher who has marked scripts to a mark scheme knows where marks are awarded, how examiners read a borderline answer, and which shortcuts cost nothing. That is real value, particularly for a technique problem. What it does not give is any knowledge of a future paper, any ability to predict grade boundaries, or any influence whatsoever over your child's result. Examining work is confidential, so a teacher who hints at inside knowledge is telling you something important about their judgement, and not the thing they intended.

The third claim, years in a classroom, is the easiest to check and the least often tested. Ask which schools, which years, which board, and which grades. Then ask a question only a classroom teacher can answer well: what do most students get wrong in this topic, and why? A person who has taught thirty children through it will answer in seconds and with irritation, because the mistake annoys them. Somebody describing a career they did not have will answer in generalities. None of this is hostile. You are asking IGCSE teachers in India to talk about their work, which most of them enjoy, and the ones who bristle at a polite factual question have answered a different question for you entirely.
items: 1. Ask which syllabus code and tier they taught most recently, and in which series
2. Ask which course their training was, in which year, and for which subject
3. Ask what examining work involved and what it does not tell them
4. Show a marked script and ask what they see in it before any teaching begins
5. Ask what they will not take on, then check the answer against the trial session

contentBlocks.heading: Teacher or tutor: what is the actual difference?
contentBlocks.body:
A teacher delivers a course to a class over a year. A tutor solves one student's specific problem in the time available. IGCSE teachers in India use both words interchangeably, and the jobs are not the same, which is why some brilliant teachers make indifferent tutors and some unqualified-looking tutors are exactly right.

Classroom teaching is about coverage, pacing and managing thirty different rates of progress at once. It builds an instinct for what a whole cohort finds hard, a working knowledge of the scheme of work, and the ability to explain a topic in several ways because the first way failed for nine students. Those are valuable things to buy, particularly for a content gap, and they are the reason years in a classroom matter.

Tutoring is diagnostic work. One student, one script, one question: what is actually going wrong here, and what is the fastest route to fixing it? That requires a willingness to abandon a plan, to spend a whole session on setting out rather than on content, and to say that the student does not need you next week. Some career teachers find this uncomfortable because it looks like not teaching.

The practical consequence is simple. For missing content, weight classroom experience heavily. For a technique or timing problem, weight diagnostic instinct heavily, and test it by handing over a marked script and watching what they do with it. For a young or anxious student, weight patience above both, because no amount of syllabus knowledge survives a child who has stopped trying.

And the honest limit that applies to every title on this page: no teacher, however qualified, can guarantee a grade.
items: Teaching is coverage and pacing; tutoring is diagnosis and triage for one student
Weight classroom years heavily when whole topics are genuinely missing
Weight diagnostic instinct heavily when the marks vanish despite understanding
For a young or anxious student, patience outranks every credential on the profile
Test diagnosis by handing over a marked script and watching what happens next

contentBlocks.heading: What a strong teacher changes, and what no credential can promise
contentBlocks.body:
Credentials predict a floor, not a ceiling, and that is the right way to read what IGCSE teachers in India put on a profile. An experienced, syllabus-specific teacher is unlikely to waste your term, which is worth a great deal. What happens after that depends on the student, and no qualification changes it.

Within four to six sessions, a well-matched teacher should have produced visible changes in the work rather than in the atmosphere. The student attempts questions they used to leave. Method appears on the page in 0580. Command words are read properly before the answer starts. Practical write-ups name variables instead of describing them loosely. These are the things to look for, and they are all checkable by a parent who does not know the subject.

What no credential delivers is equally worth naming. It does not make a student work between sessions. It does not recover a year of missed foundations in six weeks, though a good teacher will say which topics are worth saving and which are being abandoned, and will say it out loud. It does not entitle anyone to write or edit coursework, which must be the student's own work. It does not predict grade boundaries. And no teacher can guarantee a grade, whatever they have marked or trained in.

One more caution about impressive backgrounds. A very senior teacher can be the wrong choice for a struggling student, because their instinct is to raise the level of discussion when the student needs the opposite. If your child leaves sessions feeling stupid, the credential is not the problem and the match is. Ask for a different one; it is a normal request.
items: Credentials raise the floor of what you will get, not the ceiling of what is possible
Check after four to six sessions: attempts, method shown, command words read properly
No qualification permits writing or editing a student's coursework
A very senior teacher can be wrong for a struggling student, and often is
If your child leaves sessions feeling stupid, change the match rather than the effort

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing between home classes and online teachers in India
contentBlocks.body:
Decide the mode before you start comparing IGCSE teachers in India, because the shortlist changes completely depending on your answer.

Choose home classes when the student needs to be watched while working, when they are young or easily distracted, or when the diagnosis is technique rather than content. Choose online when the syllabus is less commonly taught where you live, when the specific tier matters, or when your locality simply does not hold a teacher with the right experience. Choose hybrid when both are true, which is frequently the case in Grade 10.

Then send us the four things that make a shortlist precise: the board and syllabus code, the tier, the examination series, and what the most recent marked script showed. Add your locality and the evenings that work. If you are flexible about mode, say so, because that single line widens the field more than anything else you can tell us.

When you meet the teacher, spend the trial testing the match rather than admiring the background. Hand over the script. Ask what they see. Ask which syllabus they taught last and in which series. Ask what they will refuse to do. A teacher who answers all four cleanly has told you more than a page of qualifications.

IB Gram asks about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shares a shortlist of verified tutors whose profiles match. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on subject, tier and slot, and experienced teachers fill their weekday evenings first.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge professional development actually certify?
faqs.answer: It certifies that a teacher attended and completed a course about teaching a syllabus, which is genuinely useful and is not a licence. Ask three follow-ups: which course, in which year, and for which subject. A course taken for one subject tells you little about another, and one taken several years ago may predate the syllabus version your child is sitting. Training says something about how seriously a teacher takes their craft. It says nothing about results, and any teacher presenting it as a results claim is overselling it.

faqs.question: Is an examiner automatically a better tutor?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, though examining experience is valuable for a specific kind of problem. A teacher who has marked scripts against a mark scheme knows precisely where marks are awarded and how a borderline answer is read, which is exactly what a student losing marks despite understanding the content needs. What examining does not provide is knowledge of a future paper, any ability to predict grade boundaries, or influence over a result. Examining work is confidential, so treat any hint of inside knowledge as a serious warning rather than a selling point.

faqs.question: Does a subject degree matter more than teaching experience?
faqs.answer: For most Grade 9 and 10 problems, no, and the gap is often the opposite of what parents expect. A degree proves somebody learned the subject at a level far above the syllabus. Teaching a fifteen-year-old to write an answer the mark scheme rewards is a different skill, learned by marking that paper repeatedly. A physics graduate may explain beautifully and never notice that the student's theory answers are too long and too vague. Ask what they have taught recently, not what they studied.

faqs.question: How do I check a credential politely?
faqs.answer: Ask about specifics rather than about honesty, because specific questions are ordinary professional conversation. Which syllabus code and tier did you teach most recently, and in which series? Which course was your training, and in which year? What did your examining work involve, and what does it not tell you? Then hand over a marked script and ask what they see. Nobody experienced takes offence at these, and the quality of the answers will tell you more than any document.

faqs.question: Should we hire a teacher from our child's own school for home tuition?
faqs.answer: Usually not, even when they are excellent, and for three reasons rather than one. They mark the classwork and take the fee, which is awkward for everyone including the student. You lose the second explanation, which is often the whole point of hiring anyone. And paid home classes are the first thing a busy serving teacher cancels during a heavy school week. A teacher from a different school keeps the second opinion and can speak frankly. Also check your school's own policy, since many restrict the arrangement.

faqs.question: How many years of experience should we look for?
faqs.answer: Ask how many series of the specific syllabus rather than how many years in teaching. A teacher who has taken students through Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 across several examination series knows the paper's rhythms in a way a fifteen-year generalist may not. Years matter most for a content gap, where breadth of explanation helps. For technique and timing problems, recent syllabus-specific work matters more. And for a young or anxious student, both are outranked by patience.

faqs.question: Are online teachers less qualified than home teachers?
faqs.answer: No, and in smaller cities the opposite is usually true. Experience concentrates where the schools are, so a family in Dehradun, Jaipur or Ludhiana looking only for a nearby home tutor is choosing from a much smaller pool than one willing to work on a screen. What differs is the skill set: home teaching rewards observation and household management, online teaching rewards structure and a well-set-up screen. Ask how many of their current students they teach online, and look for a document camera or graphics tablet.

faqs.question: What should I ask in a trial session?
faqs.answer: Hand over a recent marked script and ask what they see, before any teaching starts. A strong teacher will name a pattern within a few minutes, distinguish a content gap from a technique one, and ask which tier and series the student is entered for. A weaker one will offer to restart the syllabus from the beginning. Then ask what they will not take on. A teacher who volunteers the coursework boundary and says plainly that no grade can be guaranteed is showing you their standards.

faqs.question: Can a teacher help with coursework or controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Only inside the rules, and no credential changes them. Coursework must be the student's own work, so a teacher may teach the underlying skill, explain what the criteria require, and question the reasoning behind a paragraph. They may not write, rewrite or edit the submission. Your school will explain the supervision and authentication its syllabuses require, and an honest teacher will point you there. Anyone offering to produce the work is risking your child's entry, whatever their qualifications say.

faqs.question: Is a teacher in Mumbai or Delhi better than one in a smaller city?
faqs.answer: Not better, but more likely to have taught your exact syllabus, which is what actually matters. Experience follows the schools, so Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai simply hold more teachers who have taken students through several Cambridge series. In Chandigarh, Mohali, Lucknow or Kanpur there are excellent teachers in smaller numbers, and the odds of finding one for a specific tier nearby are lower. That is an argument for widening the search online, not for doubting anyone's ability.

faqs.question: What if the teacher is clearly qualified but my child is not learning?
faqs.answer: Change the match, and do it without treating it as a failure on anyone's part. Credentials predict a floor rather than a ceiling, and a very senior teacher can be the wrong fit for a struggling student because their instinct is to raise the level when the student needs the opposite. Say specifically what is not working: explanations go over their head, homework is not attempted, the student is quiet throughout. That detail makes the next match better, and asking for one is entirely ordinary.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see a difference?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions, measured in the work rather than in the mood. Look for method appearing on the page in 0580, command words being read before the answer begins, practical write-ups naming variables properly, and questions being attempted rather than skipped. Marks follow behaviour by about a term. If nothing in the written work has changed after six sessions, either the diagnosis was wrong or the match is, and both deserve an honest conversation rather than another month of waiting.
