faqs.question: Which IGCSE syllabuses are hardest to find a teacher for in India?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 are the two families struggle with most, followed by Business Studies 0450 and the English as a Second Language codes. All four are offered by fewer schools than the mainstream subjects, so fewer teachers build real experience of them. The Edexcel equivalents, including Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 and Computer Science 4CP0, are scarcer still. Search by the code rather than the subject name and the shortlist becomes honest immediately.

faqs.question: How can I check a teacher really knows 0478 before booking?
faqs.answer: Ask what students most commonly lose marks on in Paper 2 and listen for specifics. A teacher who has marked pseudocode talks about undeclared variables, loops that run one iteration short and answers that describe rather than implement. Ask which programming language they teach in and whether it matches the school's choice of Python, Java or Visual Basic. Then ask for a trial with live coding, where your child types and the teacher watches.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for a coursework subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm limit that distance does not change. A teacher may explain a technique, question the student's decisions, read the assessment criteria with them and ask what is missing. A teacher may not write, rewrite or edit anything submitted, and for programming tasks that includes supplying code the student pastes in. Ask any candidate how they handle a draft before hiring. An offer to tidy the work up is a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: We live in Raipur and nobody teaches 0606 locally. What is the plan?
faqs.answer: Widen the city while keeping the code, which is the order that protects the syllabus match. Across Raipur, Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Jabalpur this is the normal situation rather than bad luck. Enquire by code, ask for a trial on a calculus past paper question, and consider a small online group with families in other cities facing the same gap. If handwritten working is also a weakness, add a local home tutor for occasional timed writing.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist better than a distant specialist?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream code, often yes. For 0606 or 0478, almost never. A local teacher learning the syllabus alongside your child is a term behind from the start, and the paper structure is where the marks are decided. The sensible compromise is hybrid: the specialist online for content and paper technique, a local home tutor once a fortnight whose only job is watching the student write under time pressure.

faqs.question: How long should an online session be for a Grade 9 student?
faqs.answer: Shorter than you think, and shorter than an equivalent session at home. Screen attention after a full school day fades quickly, so two sessions of about fifty minutes usually achieve more than one long block. Grade 10 students can hold longer when the work is timed practice, because doing a paper is easier to sustain than being taught. Agree the pattern at the start and revisit it after the first month.

faqs.question: What equipment does the student actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than most advertisements suggest. A stable connection, a device with a working camera, a notebook and a way to photograph written work will cover most subjects. A graphics tablet helps in Mathematics and a second camera pointed at the page helps a great deal for 0606, but neither is essential. For 0478 the student needs the same programming environment the school uses, installed and working before the first lesson rather than during it.

faqs.question: Can one online teacher handle both 0580 and 0606?
faqs.answer: Some can, and it is worth asking, because the two run together for many students heading towards Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Do not assume it. 0580 Extended and 0606 have different content and different demands, and a teacher strong in one may simply not have taught the other. Ask which cohorts they have taken through each code separately, and run the trial on a 0606 question rather than a 0580 one.

faqs.question: What happens when the connection fails in the middle of a lesson?
faqs.answer: Agree the answer before it happens, because it will happen during the monsoon and during power cuts. The usual arrangement is a short wait, then a phone call to decide whether to continue or reschedule, with the session made up rather than lost. Families in Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna often keep a mobile hotspot ready for exactly this. Put the policy in writing with the teacher in the first week.

faqs.question: Our school teaches Edexcel. Does an online Cambridge teacher still help?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the gap is bigger than the content suggests. Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science 4CP0 includes an on-screen practical programming paper, and Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 is structured differently from Cambridge 0606. A strong teacher can adapt, but only if they read the syllabus and two past papers first. Ask directly whether they have taught the Edexcel code and in which series, and treat a vague answer as a no.

faqs.question: Is 0510 the same as 0511 when hiring an English teacher?
faqs.answer: No, and mixing them up is the most common hiring mistake in this subject. Both assess reading and writing plus listening, but 0511 counts speaking into the final grade while 0510 reports speaking separately. That single difference changes how much lesson time should go on spoken practice. Confirm the code with the school in writing, and confirm again that the teacher you shortlist has taught that specific version recently.

h1: IGCSE Tutor Near Me: Local Supply Across Indian Cities
heroTitle: How Far Is Near for an IGCSE Tutor in India?
heroSubtitle: Near-me searches assume the right tutor is a few kilometres away. For a named Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus code, that is true in parts of six cities and untrue almost everywhere else. This page treats distance as a supply problem and shows how to widen the search without losing what proximity buys.
introSummary: Searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in India usually means one thing: you want a home tutor who can reach your address on a weekday evening without the journey wrecking the slot. That is a reasonable thing to want, and in South Delhi, Bandra, Indiranagar, Gachibowli, Adyar or Baner it is often achievable for a common subject. The difficulty appears the moment the subject becomes specific. Supply for IGCSE is not spread evenly across the country or across the syllabus: Mathematics 0580 has depth almost everywhere there are international schools, while a named science or language code can have one qualified person in a whole city. This page maps that supply, weighs a nearby generalist against a distant specialist, and gives you an order for widening the search.

contentBlocks.heading: What happens when you search for an IGCSE tutor near me in India?
contentBlocks.body:
A search engine answers a near-me query with whoever has the strongest local listing, which is a measure of marketing rather than of teaching. A matching process answers it differently: it starts at your address, widens in defined steps, and stops at the first step that produces someone who genuinely teaches your syllabus code at your child's tier. Those two answers frequently point at different people.

The widening order below is the one worth following, and the logic is that each step trades a little proximity for a lot of subject fit. Most families skip straight from step one to giving up, or from step one to accepting whoever is nearest. Both are expensive mistakes.

What you supply at the start decides how quickly this resolves. Give the locality rather than the city, the board, the syllabus codes, the tier where it is settled, the grade, and the two evenings you can genuinely keep. Say explicitly whether online is acceptable, because that single answer changes the size of the pool by an order of magnitude and there is no point in hiding it until week three.

IB Gram then shortlists verified profiles against that brief and arranges a trial session before you commit. Availability depends on the subject, the tier and the hours you need, and a rare syllabus in a smaller city will simply take longer. If the first match is wrong, ask for another in the first month rather than the third.
items: 1. Your own locality first: a tutor who can hold a weekday evening slot.
2. Adjoining localities on the same side of the city, at a later slot.
3. The wider metropolitan region, realistically for weekends only.
4. Your city online, keeping the option of occasional home sessions.
5. Anywhere in India online, which is where scarce syllabus codes live.
6. Stop at the first step that yields a genuine syllabus-code specialist.

contentBlocks.heading: Which syllabus code is your child on, and who nearby teaches it?
contentBlocks.body:
Answer the code question before the distance question, because the code determines how large your search has to be. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, normally taken across Grades 9 and 10 before the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11.

The codes are printed on the student's own materials. Cambridge subjects carry codes such as Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500. Pearson Edexcel codes look different: Mathematics A is 4MA1, and the Physics equivalent is 4PH1. Take a photograph of the front of a past paper the school has given your child and you have settled it in a minute.

Tier is the second half of the same question. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*, and Edexcel Mathematics A is tiered Foundation or Higher. A tutor who teaches Core confidently and Extended vaguely is a poor match for an Extended candidate however close they live, and the gap is not always obvious in a first conversation.

Exam series matter for the calendar of the search. Cambridge runs series in February and March, offered only in India, in May and June, and in October and November, while Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and in May and June. A family whose child sits the February and March series has less room to keep searching than one aiming at May and June, which is a practical argument for widening early rather than holding out for someone down the road.
items: Photograph a past paper front page: the code settles the board question.
Core caps at grade C; Extended reaches A*. Confirm the entry first.
A confident Core tutor can still be a weak Extended match.
February and March candidates have less time to keep searching locally.

contentBlocks.heading: Supply by subject across India: 0580 is everywhere, 0500 is not
contentBlocks.body:
Local supply is not one number. It differs sharply by subject, and knowing the shape of it saves weeks.

Mathematics 0580 is the deepest pool in the country by a wide margin. Wherever there are international schools there are people who teach it, and a family in most large cities can reasonably expect a home tutor within a workable radius. Even here there is a catch: from the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 with a calculator, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 with a calculator, and a tutor who has only prepared students for the calculator papers is half a tutor for the non-calculator one.

The sciences are thinner and thin unevenly. Cambridge syllabuses examined from 2023 assess through Paper 1 or Paper 2 multiple choice, Paper 3 or Paper 4 theory, and practical work through Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school chose, with weighting of multiple choice 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. A tutor who has never prepared a student for Paper 6 will teach the content and miss a fifth of the marks. Physics 0625 is the hardest of the three to staff locally in smaller cities, partly because students must recall and rearrange the syllabus equations rather than being given them.

Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 are where near-me searches most often fail outright. Both are commonly taught by whoever is available rather than by a subject specialist, and in a city with one or two international schools the genuine 0455 pool can be empty. Edexcel students face a narrower pool again, since untiered Edexcel sciences with practical skills assessed inside the written papers are simply less familiar to most Indian tutors than the Cambridge structure.
items: 0580 has the deepest local pool; ask about the non-calculator paper anyway.
Sciences thin unevenly; Physics 0625 is hardest to staff in smaller cities.
Practical is 20% of a Cambridge science grade, via Paper 5 or Paper 6.
0455 Economics and 0500 First Language English are the common near-me failures.
Edexcel codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1 narrow the local pool further.

contentBlocks.heading: How near is near? Local supply across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Anyone typing IGCSE tutor near me in India is really asking about supply, and supply follows international schools, which cluster. The honest map of the country is a set of islands rather than a sheet. In Delhi NCR the pools are real but separated: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri form one, Gurugram with Golf Course Road another, and Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Dwarka each draw on their own. A tutor in Gurugram will rarely cross to Ghaziabad for a Tuesday evening, and evening traffic across NCR can stretch a short trip badly.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region works the same way around the harbour. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit in one practical radius, Powai in another, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar realistically need someone on their own side. Bengaluru divides by corridor: Whitefield with Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar with Koramangala and HSR Layout, Hebbal with Yelahanka, and Electronic City with Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road. Hyderabad concentrates in Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad drawing from a smaller set. Chennai holds pools in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Alwarpet and Anna Nagar, with Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Velachery and Perungudi separate. Pune splits east and west across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Kharadi on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi on the other.

Beyond the six, near-me gets harder fast. In Gujarat, Ahmedabad holds a workable pool across Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and out to Gandhinagar, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot are thinner. Kolkata and eastern India is similar: Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat have supply, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna often do not. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula manage, while Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur depend on the subject. In southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai usually have one school and no pool. Central and western India, meaning Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, is the same story.
items: Delhi NCR: Gurugram, Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are separate pools, not one.
Mumbai and Bengaluru: match within the harbour side or the commute corridor.
Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune each split into two practical zones.
Gujarat: Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar hold supply; Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot less so.
Kolkata has a pool; Guwahati, Ranchi, Patna and Bhubaneswar usually do not.
Kochi, Indore, Nagpur, Jaipur and Coimbatore: one school, and rarely a pool.

contentBlocks.heading: Term dates, mocks and why a home tutor nearby matters in Grade 10
contentBlocks.body:
Proximity is worth most in the months when the timetable is tightest, which is the second half of Grade 10. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools of this kind, among them Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Stonehill International School, Oakridge International School and Good Shepherd International School, run into the same crunch: school mocks, coursework deadlines and the final series arriving within a few months of each other.

Here is why distance starts to matter then. A tutor ten minutes away can hold a fixed weekday evening slot for months, can move a session by a day when the school announces something at short notice, and can add an extra hour in the week before a mock without redesigning their own day. A tutor an hour away across evening traffic can do none of those things reliably, and the arrangement usually degrades into cancellations exactly when it is needed most.

The school calendar is what makes this concrete, and each school sets its own mock examination dates, usually some months before the series the student is entered for. A February and March Cambridge candidate therefore hits the crunch earlier in the academic year than a May and June candidate. Get the internal deadline sheet and the mock window from the school early and give both to the tutor, because a plan built without them is a plan built blind.

Seasonal disruption argues the same way. A heavy monsoon evening in Mumbai or Chennai, a festival week around Diwali, Pujo, Onam or Ganesh Chaturthi, or a stretch of examination leave will all cost sessions. A nearby tutor absorbs those; a distant one loses them. Agree in advance that a lost home visit moves online rather than disappearing from the week.
items: Proximity pays off most in the crunch months of Grade 10.
A nearby tutor can add an hour before a mock without redesigning their day.
Each school sets its own mock dates ahead of the entered series.
February and March candidates hit the crunch earlier in the year.
Agree that a monsoon or festival cancellation moves online, not away.

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits, online or hybrid once the search widens in India
contentBlocks.body:
Widening the search is really a decision about mode, so it helps to be clear about what each mode is good at before you trade anything away.

A home visit buys presence and reliability. The tutor sees the working as it is written, the family sees the session happening, and a fixed slot in your own locality survives a school year better than anything else. That is the thing you are protecting when you search for someone nearby, and it is a genuine thing rather than a preference.

Online buys subject fit. It puts the whole country in the pool, which is the only way some families will ever reach a tutor who has actually taught their syllabus code at their tier. It also allows short, frequent contact: a twenty-minute review of a returned paper midweek is easy on a call and impossible as a cross-city visit.

Hybrid is the honest middle and is underused in India. One home session a week with a nearby tutor for sit-down work and timed practice, plus a shorter online session with a specialist for the parts of the syllabus the local tutor is weaker on. Some families run this as two tutors deliberately, one local generalist and one distant specialist, and for a scarce subject it can be the best available arrangement even though it sounds complicated on paper.

One thing to settle before you commit. If you go online because nobody nearby teaches the code, insist that the student writes on paper and photographs the work. Otherwise the session drifts into talking, and the handwriting and timed practice that Grade 10 depends on quietly stop happening.
items: Home classes buy presence and a slot that survives the school year.
Online buys subject fit, which is what a scarce syllabus code needs.
Hybrid: a nearby tutor for sit-down work, a distant specialist for depth.
Two tutors, one local and one specialist, is a legitimate arrangement.
Online only works for Grade 10 if the student still writes on paper.

contentBlocks.heading: Checking that a tutor really teaches your syllabus code
contentBlocks.body:
Near-me searches produce confident local answers, so this check matters more here than anywhere else on the site. IB Gram verifies profiles before shortlisting, covering identity, claimed qualifications and stated teaching experience. What it cannot verify is whether a tutor who says IGCSE Mathematics has ever taught 0580 Extended specifically, and that is the question a family has to ask.

Four questions do most of the work, and they are not trick questions. Which papers does my child sit for this subject, and which of them is non-calculator? For a science, which practical paper has the school entered them for, Paper 5 or Paper 6, and how does your teaching differ between the two? What changes in your approach between Core and Extended, or between Foundation and Higher on Edexcel? And which past paper series do you work from, and how do you get the mark schemes?

A tutor who teaches the code answers these immediately, in plain language, and usually adds something you did not ask. A tutor who teaches the subject in general pauses, generalises, or tells you that the boards are all much the same. They are not, and someone who says so is telling you what they do not know.

Then ask for one marked answer during the trial. Hand over a real script, pick a four-mark question, and watch them mark it with your child against the scheme. This takes ten minutes and settles more than a long conversation about credentials.

For a home visit, add the ordinary arrangements: register a standing weekly gate entry with the society, teach in a shared room with the door open, keep an adult at home, and keep scheduling on the platform channel rather than a personal number.
items: Ask which papers, and which one is non-calculator, for this exact code.
Ask whether the school entered Paper 5 or Paper 6 and what changes.
Ask what differs between Core and Extended in their teaching.
Ask which past paper series and mark schemes they actually use.
Watch them mark one four-mark answer with your child in the trial.
For home lessons: standing gate entry, shared room, an adult at home.

contentBlocks.heading: A nearby generalist or a distant specialist: which costs more marks?
contentBlocks.body:
This is the real decision hiding inside every search for an IGCSE tutor near me in India, and the answer is not the same for every family, so weigh it rather than guessing.

The nearby generalist wins when the problem is behaviour. A student who does not start work without someone present, who rushes, who leaves questions half-finished or who writes almost nothing down is losing marks to habits, and habits are fixed by a person at the table twice a week. A competent local tutor who knows the subject broadly will fix those faster than a distant expert who sees a photograph of the finished answer. Reliability compounds too: a nearby tutor keeps the slot, and a slot kept for eight months beats a better tutor seen irregularly.

The distant specialist wins when the problem is the syllabus. If your child is an Extended candidate whose marks fall specifically in the theory paper, or who cannot handle the practical paper the school entered them for, or who is taking a code almost nobody local has taught, then subject depth is the binding constraint. A general tutor will teach content the student mostly has and miss the thing the paper actually rewards. In that situation insisting on nearby buys a comfortable arrangement and costs marks.

So test it with one question. Is my child losing marks because of how they work, or because of what the paper asks for? Look at a marked script for the answer. Unfinished questions, no working, careless arithmetic and blank diagrams point to the local tutor. Complete, neat answers that still score badly point to the specialist.

And for a household that genuinely needs both, the two-tutor hybrid is not extravagant. It is the arrangement the evidence points at.
items: Unfinished questions and missing working: a nearby tutor fixes this faster.
Neat, complete answers scoring badly: the paper is the problem, not the habits.
A kept weekly slot for eight months beats a better tutor seen irregularly.
For a scarce code, insisting on nearby buys comfort and costs marks.
Read a marked script before deciding; it answers the question in minutes.

contentBlocks.heading: When insisting on a home tutor nearby costs the student marks
contentBlocks.body:
Some honest limits, because a page about finding an IGCSE tutor near me in India that only sells proximity is not much use.

The first limit is arithmetic. A tutor who spends longer travelling to you than teaching prices that time somehow, either in the rate or by taking fewer students, and the arrangement is fragile because the first bad traffic evening breaks it. If the only nearby candidate is one long journey away, you have not really found a local tutor. You have found a distant one who has agreed to travel, and those arrangements rarely survive a full school year.

The second limit is fit. Accepting the nearest available person for a subject they teach only occasionally is the most common near-me mistake, and it is expensive in a quiet way: the sessions are pleasant, the student likes the tutor, and the marks do not move because nobody is teaching what the paper rewards. Give it six weeks and look at a marked script, not at the atmosphere.

The third is timing. Searching locally for two months before widening costs a term, and in a February and March series that term is most of the runway. Widen early. You can always narrow again.

What progress should look like, once the right tutor is in place: a specific description of the weakness inside three weeks, changed working habits by four to six weeks, and marks moving at the next mock rather than the next class test. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a Core entry cannot exceed grade C whatever anyone claims, and a student who does no work between sessions will not improve regardless of who sits beside them.

If the match is wrong, say so in the first month and ask for a different one. That is a normal request, not a complaint.
items: A tutor travelling longer than they teach is not a stable arrangement.
The nearest available person for an occasional subject is the classic mistake.
Judge at six weeks on a marked script, not on how the sessions feel.
Searching locally for two months before widening can cost a whole term.
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and Core cannot exceed grade C.
Ask for a different match inside the first month if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: Widening the search for an IGCSE tutor near me in India
contentBlocks.body:
Do this in one sitting and you will know within a week whether a local match exists.

Write down the facts first: board, syllabus codes, tier where it is settled, grade, the series the school has entered your child for, your locality by name rather than your city, and the two evenings you can genuinely keep. Add one line about what a marked script shows, such as loses marks on the theory paper despite knowing the content. That line is what turns a near-me query into a brief.

Then decide your widening limit in advance, before anyone is charming you. How far will you actually let a tutor travel, and what happens at each step if nobody appears? Families who settle this early make better decisions than families who improvise it under time pressure in Grade 10.

Be explicit about online. Saying that you would prefer home tuition but will accept online for a scarce code is far more useful than saying nothing, because it lets the search run both paths at once instead of sequentially.

Then send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, shortlists verified profiles that match, and arranges a trial session before you commit to anything. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to availability at your subject and hours. Use the trial to watch one answer marked against the scheme, ask your child afterwards whether anything became clearer, and if the answer is no, ask for a different match.
items: Write the brief: board, codes, tier, grade, series, locality, two evenings.
Add one line from a marked script about where marks are actually lost.
Decide your travel limit before you start talking to anyone.
Say plainly that online is acceptable for a scarce code; it doubles the pool.
Use the trial to watch one answer marked, then ask your child privately.

faqs.question: How far will an IGCSE tutor actually travel for a home session?
faqs.answer: Usually their own locality and the ones adjoining it, on the same side of the city. Tutors hold a radius because travel time is unpaid teaching time, and someone spending longer travelling than teaching either prices it into the rate or quietly starts cancelling. Evening traffic between Powai and Thane, Whitefield and Jayanagar, or Gurugram and Ghaziabad can stretch a short trip badly. Name your locality rather than your city and the shortlist becomes far more realistic.

faqs.answer: Widen to online rather than accepting a general tutor nearby, especially if a marked script shows complete answers scoring badly. In Kochi, Coimbatore, Indore, Nagpur, Guwahati and similar cities the local pool for one specific code can genuinely be empty, and the real choice is between a distant specialist and nobody. Insist that the student keeps writing on paper and photographing the work, so the handwriting and timed practice that Grade 10 depends on continue.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist better than a distant specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends on what a marked script shows. Unfinished questions, missing working, careless arithmetic and blank diagrams are habit problems, and a competent local tutor at your table twice a week fixes those faster than anyone at a distance. Neat, complete answers that still score badly are a syllabus problem, and there a specialist who knows your code and tier is worth the distance. Read the script before deciding; it takes ten minutes and settles the argument.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor really teaches my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask four specific questions. Which papers does my child sit, and which is non-calculator? For a science, is the school entered for Paper 5 or Paper 6, and what changes between them? What differs in your teaching between Core and Extended? Which past paper series and mark schemes do you use? Someone who teaches the code answers immediately and adds detail. Someone who teaches the subject in general will tell you the boards are much the same, which they are not.

faqs.question: Can we keep a home tutor and add an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a scarce subject it is often the best available arrangement. One nearby tutor holds the weekly home session for sit-down practice, timed questions and working shown on paper, while a specialist elsewhere in India takes a shorter online slot for the parts of the syllabus the local tutor is weaker on. Agree which topics belong to whom, and make sure both use the school's tier and notation so your child is not caught between two methods.

faqs.question: Why is supply so much thinner outside the six big metros?
faqs.answer: Because the supply behind every search for an IGCSE tutor near me in India follows international schools, and those cluster. Delhi NCR, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune have enough schools to sustain a pool of experienced tutors per subject. A city with one or two international schools has a handful of teachers and almost no independent pool, so a named code may have nobody at all. That is not a reflection on the city. It is arithmetic, and online is the straightforward answer to it.

faqs.question: How long should I search locally before widening?
faqs.answer: A couple of weeks, not a couple of months. Searching locally through most of a term is the expensive version of this mistake, and it hurts most for a February and March Cambridge candidate whose runway is shorter than a May and June candidate's. Run both paths at once instead: say at the query stage that you prefer a tutor at home but will accept online for a scarce code, and the search covers both rather than working through them in sequence.

faqs.question: Is a neighbourhood tuition centre a reasonable near-me answer?
faqs.answer: For some students, genuinely yes. A centre gives routine, peers to compare against and the lowest cost per hour of any taught option, and a student who needs structure more than diagnosis can do well there. The limits are equally clear: feedback is pitched at the batch, individual coursework rarely gets attention, and the centre teaches whichever board it has most students for. Ask which syllabus code is actually being taught in that batch before enrolling.

faqs.question: Does proximity matter more in Grade 9 or Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 10, by some distance. In Grade 9 there is room in the week and a slightly awkward slot survives. In the second half of Grade 10, with school mocks, coursework deadlines and the final series close together, you need a tutor who can hold a fixed evening, move a session at short notice and add an hour before a mock. A long commute makes all three unreliable exactly when the schedule has no slack left.

faqs.question: What happens on a heavy monsoon evening or during a festival week?
faqs.answer: Agree in advance that a session which cannot happen in person moves online that evening rather than vanishing from the week. Monsoon evenings in Mumbai and Chennai will cancel home visits at some point, and Diwali, Pujo, Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi each take days out of the calendar depending on the city. A nearby tutor absorbs most of this. A distant one does not, which is one more argument for settling the rule before the term rather than during it.

faqs.question: How quickly can a match be found in my locality?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the tier and the hours, and there is no useful average. Mathematics in a metro locality at a weekend slot resolves quickly. A specific science code at a fixed weekday evening in a smaller city may not resolve at all locally. Availability is always subject to who is genuinely free at the hours you named, so the fastest way to speed it up is to offer a second acceptable slot rather than to push for a faster answer.

faqs.question: What if the local tutor we chose is pleasant but nothing is improving?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked script at the six-week point rather than judging the atmosphere. Pleasant sessions with no movement usually mean the tutor is teaching content the student already has while missing what the paper rewards. Ask them to describe your child's weakness in one specific sentence; if they cannot, that is your answer. Tell IB Gram what is not working and ask for a different match. Doing it at six weeks rather than six months is the whole point.

A city with one or two international schools has a handful of teachers and almost no independent pool, so a named code may have nobody at all. That is not a reflection on the city. It is arithmetic, and online is the straightforward answer to it.

mainEntity.name: How long should I search locally before widening?

acceptedAnswer.text: A couple of weeks, not a couple of months. Searching locally through most of a term is the expensive version of this mistake, and it hurts most for a February and March Cambridge candidate whose runway is shorter than a May and June candidate's. Run both paths at once instead: say at the query stage that you prefer a tutor at home but will accept online for a scarce code, and the search covers both rather than working through them in sequence.

mainEntity.name: Is a neighbourhood tuition centre a reasonable near-me answer?

acceptedAnswer.text: For some students, genuinely yes. A centre gives routine, peers to compare against and the lowest cost per hour of any taught option, and a student who needs structure more than diagnosis can do well there. The limits are equally clear: feedback is pitched at the batch, individual coursework rarely gets attention, and the centre teaches whichever board it has most students for. Ask which syllabus code is actually being taught in that batch before enrolling.

mainEntity.name: Does proximity matter more in Grade 9 or Grade 10?

acceptedAnswer.text: Grade 10, by some distance. In Grade 9 there is room in the week and a slightly awkward slot survives. In the second half of Grade 10, with school mocks, coursework deadlines and the final series close together, you need a tutor who can hold a fixed evening, move a session at short notice and add an hour before a mock. A long commute makes all three unreliable exactly when the schedule has no slack left.

mainEntity.name: What happens on a heavy monsoon evening or during a festival week?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree in advance that a session which cannot happen in person moves online that evening rather than vanishing from the week. Monsoon evenings in Mumbai and Chennai will cancel home visits at some point, and Diwali, Pujo, Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi each take days out of the calendar depending on the city. A nearby tutor absorbs most of this. A distant one does not, which is one more argument for settling the rule before the term rather than during it.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can a match be found in my locality?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the subject, the tier and the hours, and there is no useful average. Mathematics in a metro locality at a weekend slot resolves quickly. A specific science code at a fixed weekday evening in a smaller city may not resolve at all locally. Availability is always subject to who is genuinely free at the hours you named, so the fastest way to speed it up is to offer a second acceptable slot rather than to push for a faster answer.

mainEntity.name: What if the local tutor we chose is pleasant but nothing is improving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at a marked script at the six-week point rather than judging the atmosphere. Pleasant sessions with no movement usually mean the tutor is teaching content the student already has while missing what the paper rewards. Ask them to describe your child's weakness in one specific sentence; if they cannot, that is your answer. Tell IB Gram what is not working and ask for a different match. Doing it at six weeks rather than six months is the whole point.

IB Gram asks about the school calendar and schedule, shortlists verified profiles that match, and arranges a trial before you commit. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and you can ask for a different match at any point.

heroTitle: How Near Is Near Enough in India?
heroSubtitle: A tutor fifteen minutes away and a tutor across the city teach the same syllabus. They do not keep the same Tuesday. This page is about distance: the evening slot, the monsoon, the society gate, the missed session, and when a distant tutor is still the right answer.
introSummary: Searching for an IGCSE home tutor near me in India is really a search for a weekday evening that survives a whole Grade 10 year. Proximity does not make a tutor better. It makes them reliable, which in the final year is close to the same thing. A tutor who lives twenty minutes away arrives at seven, every week, through rain and roadworks. A tutor who crosses the city arrives at half past seven in October and stops coming in January. This page sets out what near means in each metro, how to handle a cancelled session, when to run a hybrid week instead, and when the honest answer is to search outward and take the better tutor online.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram find a home tutor near you in India?
contentBlocks.body:
A search for an IGCSE home tutor near me in India goes into the brief as a radius and a set of times, not as a pin. Say the locality, say which evenings are genuinely free, and say the latest hour a session can start on a school night. Those three things filter a shortlist faster than any subject requirement, because a tutor who cannot make eight o'clock in Kharadi on a Wednesday is not a candidate however good they are.

The rest is straightforward. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match.

One instruction is worth giving explicitly at the start: ask where the tutor is travelling from, and what else they teach on that evening. A tutor who has a session ending at seven in Koramangala and yours starting at seven thirty in Whitefield is promising something the road will not allow. Better to know in week one than to discover it in week nine.

And set the fallback at the same time. Agree now what happens when the tutor cannot reach you: the session moves online, or it moves to a named day, or it is made up at the weekend. Families who settle this before the first session almost never argue about it. Families who leave it open argue about it in November.
items: 1. Give the locality, the free evenings and the latest possible start time
2. Ask each shortlisted tutor where they travel from and what precedes your slot
3. Take a demo at home and time the tutor's actual arrival, not the promise
4. Agree the online fallback and the make-up rule before the first session
5. Review after a month, counting late arrivals rather than remembering them

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 and Grade 10 ask different things of a nearby tutor
contentBlocks.body:
In Grade 9 distance is an inconvenience. In Grade 10 it is a risk. That is the whole argument, and it is worth understanding before you compromise in either direction.

IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually two years across Grades 9 and 10, and often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. The first of those two years has slack in it. A session lost in September of Grade 9 can be made up in October and nothing breaks. The second year has almost none, because past-paper work has to be sequenced and a fortnight lost in January cannot be recovered in February.

So the sensible pattern is to accept more travel in Grade 9 and less in Grade 10. A specialist who travels from the other side of Hyderabad is a reasonable choice for a Grade 9 student building method. The same arrangement for a Grade 10 student in the term before the series is a slow-motion problem, and the family usually sees it coming and hopes anyway.

There is a second difference that has nothing to do with roads. A Grade 9 student can absorb a session that starts late and runs short. A Grade 10 student sitting down at eight fifteen after a full school day and an hour of school homework will give you forty useful minutes at best. Lateness costs more in the second year because the student has less left to give, which is the part families underestimate when they compare two tutors on paper.
items: Grade 9 has slack: a lost session can genuinely be made up later
Grade 10 sequences past papers, so a lost fortnight is not recoverable
Accept more travel in the first year, less in the second
A late start costs more in Grade 10, when the student is already spent
Judge a tutor on arrival time over a month, not on the first week

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE subjects justify looking beyond your locality
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject is worth a compromise on distance, and knowing which are is how families avoid both mistakes at once.

Mathematics 0580 and the three sciences, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, are taught by enough people in most large Indian cities that a competent nearby tutor is usually available. For these, take the local person. The gain from a marginally stronger tutor across town is smaller than the loss from two cancelled sessions a month, and a nearby tutor can also drop in for an extra hour before a test, which a distant one never will.

The calculation changes for the less common codes. Additional Mathematics, Economics 0455, and the specific English syllabuses each thin out quickly outside the main clusters. English in particular is not one subject: First Language English 0500 sets a reading paper and then directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio; English as a Second Language runs as 0510 and 0511, with 0511 counting speaking into the grade and 0510 reporting it separately; Literature in English is 0475; and Pearson Edexcel offers 4EA1, 4EB1 and 4ES1. A tutor who is excellent at 0500 may be the wrong person for 4ES1, and in a smaller locality there may be nobody who has taught the right one.

Coursework-bearing subjects are the other case for widening the search, because experience with a portfolio is rarer than experience with a syllabus.

So split the list before you start looking. Local for the big four. Prepared to travel, or prepared to go online, for everything else. That single decision resolves most of the arguments families have with themselves about distance.

A nearby tutor can add an hour before a test; a distant one cannot

contentBlocks.heading: What near really means across India, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
Near is a time rather than a distance, and for an IGCSE home tutor near me in India that time differs in every city. In Delhi NCR, a tutor living in South Delhi can hold Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri comfortably and will struggle with Dwarka on a weekday evening. Gurugram (Gurgaon) works as its own zone, with Golf Course Road tutors rarely crossing to Faridabad or Ghaziabad. Noida, Sector 128 Noida and Greater Noida form a third. Families often search across the whole of Delhi NCR and then wonder why the shortlist will not commit to a fixed hour.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is more forgiving within a zone and less forgiving across one. Bandra, Juhu and Andheri sit together. Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit together. Powai is its own island in practice. And Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar should be treated as separate cities for this purpose, because a crossing at the wrong hour can eat the session and the tutor's patience with it.

Bengaluru is the clearest case of all. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and HSR Layout form an eastern belt; Indiranagar and Koramangala a central one; Hebbal and Yelahanka a northern one; Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road a southern one; and Electronic City stands apart. A tutor promising to move between belts at seven in the evening is optimistic.

Hyderabad splits between the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet corridor and the older city around Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad. Pune divides similarly: Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Viman Nagar on one side, Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi on the other, with Kharadi pulled between them. Chennai behaves the same way along Old Mahabalipuram Road. In every one of these cities, the practical test is identical. Ask the tutor which localities they already teach in on that day.

contentBlocks.heading: School timings, mocks and the evening slot in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School and Singapore International School appear only as context for the kind of calendar families at international schools in India deal with.

The school day sets the earliest possible slot and the series sets how long the arrangement has to survive. Cambridge series run in February/March, offered only in India, and in May/June and October/November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The school decides which series a student sits. For a February/March entry, the crucial months are exactly the ones with the shortest evenings and the heaviest school schedule, which makes proximity matter more, not less.

Then there is the bus. A student who leaves school at three and reaches home at half past four in Thane or Greater Noida has a different evening from a classmate who walks home in ten minutes, even though both attend the same school. Build the slot around the arrival, not around the bell.

Mocks reshape the week for two or three weeks each year, and the sensible response is to plan for it rather than cancel. A nearby tutor can shift to a morning slot during a mock fortnight or add a short session the evening before a paper. A tutor travelling an hour each way will not, and should not be asked to. That flexibility is most of what proximity actually buys you across a school year.

Cambridge series: February/March, May/June and October/November
Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
A February/March entry puts peak pressure in the shortest evenings
A nearby tutor can move to a morning slot during mock fortnight

contentBlocks.heading: Keeping a distant tutor: the hybrid week explained
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison stated plainly. A tutor who comes to the house watches the student write and can react in the moment, which no camera fully replaces. An online tutor is never late, never rained off, and can be the best person for the syllabus rather than the best person within six kilometres. A hybrid week takes one of each: the tutor comes once at the weekend, when traffic is lighter and the session can run long, and teaches online midweek for marked practice and doubt-solving.

The hybrid week exists precisely to solve the problem this page is about. You found someone good and they live too far to come three times. Rather than rejecting them or accepting three unreliable visits, take one reliable visit and two reliable calls. The student gets the same person throughout, which matters more than the medium, and the household stops rearranging its evening around a road.

When does full home tuition remain the right answer? When the student will not start work unless an adult is sitting there. When the subject involves a lot of diagram and apparatus work. And when the student is young enough that a screen loses them.

When is full online better? When the code is rare, when the family moves house or city, when the monsoon reliably takes out a month of evenings, and when the honest local options are weaker than the distant one.

The one arrangement to avoid is two different tutors for the same subject, one at home and one online. They will teach different methods within a month and the student will trust neither. Keep the person, change the medium.
items: Hybrid: one weekend visit plus two midweek online sessions with the same tutor
Full home tuition suits a student who will not begin work unaided
Full online suits rare codes, frequent moves and monsoon-heavy months
A weekend visit can run longer, since the road is quieter
Never split one subject between a home tutor and a separate online tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a nearby home tutor, and getting through the society gate
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram checks identity and the qualifications a tutor lists before a profile becomes visible, and shortlists only profiles that have been through that. For a tutor coming into your house every week, that is the floor rather than the ceiling, and three practical checks belong on top of it.

First, the demo at home. Watch the arrival as carefully as the teaching. Did they arrive on time, did they know how to reach the building, did they text when delayed. A tutor who handles the first visit well usually handles the fortieth one well too.

Second, the gate. Most gated societies and apartment complexes in Gurugram, Powai, Gachibowli, Balewadi and New Town require visitors to be registered, and a tutor left arguing with security at the gate loses ten minutes and a good deal of goodwill. Register them as a regular visitor in the first week. Give the security desk the name, the day and the time. Where an app is used, add the tutor to the frequent visitor list rather than approving each entry from upstairs.

Third, the room. A table with room for two papers, decent light, a plug point, and a door that stays open. Not a bedroom. Not the dining table with the television on behind it. And an adult in the house, which is ordinary practice for a minor and something no reasonable tutor objects to.

The last thing to settle is the missed session, which is the commonest source of friction in a home arrangement and the easiest to prevent with one short conversation before it happens.
items: 1. Message within thirty minutes of the slot if either side cannot make it
2. Convert the session to online rather than cancelling, wherever possible
3. If it must be cancelled, name the make-up date in the same message
4. Cap carried-forward make-up sessions per term and let unused ones lapse
5. Review the count each term, and change tutors if the pattern continues

contentBlocks.heading: Why does proximity protect a weekday evening slot in Grade 10?
contentBlocks.body:
Because a nearby home tutor's cost of coming is small, and a distant one's cost of coming grows all year. That is the whole mechanism, and it explains behaviour that families otherwise read as unreliability or rudeness.

A tutor who lives fifteen minutes away spends perhaps thirty minutes travelling for a ninety-minute session. A tutor crossing a metro at half past six spends ninety minutes travelling for the same ninety minutes of teaching, which means your session costs them three hours of their evening. In July, when the schedule is light and the roads are tolerable, they will do it happily. By October the same trip has become the worst booking in their week, and it is the one that gets moved when anything else comes up. Nobody is behaving badly. The arithmetic simply changed.

Monsoon rain makes the same point faster. A road that is passable in April becomes a forty-minute standstill in July across much of Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru, and the tutor who was ten minutes late starts being thirty minutes late. A short trip stays short in the rain. A long one does not.

There is a second, quieter benefit. Proximity makes the small extra possible: an unplanned hour the evening before a Chemistry test, a swap from Tuesday to Wednesday because the school moved an event, a fifteen-minute overrun to finish a question. None of these are in any agreement. All of them happen when a tutor lives nearby and almost never when they do not.

So when you are choosing between a slightly better tutor far away and a good one close by for Grade 10, you are not really choosing between two levels of teaching. You are choosing between thirty-eight sessions and perhaps twenty-eight.
items: A distant session can cost a tutor three hours for ninety minutes of teaching
That arithmetic worsens through the year and quietly moves your slot
Monsoon rain lengthens a long trip far more than a short one
Proximity makes the unplanned extra hour before a test possible
The real comparison is thirty-eight sessions against twenty-eight

contentBlocks.heading: When nobody nearby fits, how far should you search?
contentBlocks.body:
When no IGCSE home tutor near me in India turns out to fit, search outward in a defined order rather than lowering the standard by degrees, which is what most families do without noticing.

Start with your own locality and a competent tutor, even if they are not the strongest candidate. Then widen to the adjacent belt, accepting a later start. Then consider a weekend-only home arrangement with a better tutor further away. Then a hybrid week. Then fully online with the best available specialist anywhere in the country. Work down that list in order and stop at the first option that actually holds a weekly hour, because a good plan that survives is worth more than an excellent plan that collapses in December.

What you should not do is keep a nearby tutor who is the wrong fit simply because they are convenient. Convenience is worth a lot and it is not worth everything. If after six weeks the marked work has not changed, the sessions have drifted into conversation, or your child has stopped asking questions, ask for a different match and say exactly what went wrong.

The honest limits apply here as everywhere. No tutor can guarantee a grade, near or far. Proximity improves attendance, not teaching. A student who does no work between sessions will not improve at any distance. And starting in the last weeks before the series narrows everything to technique and triage, whoever is sitting across the table.

One more thing that does not appear in any brochure. If you are choosing between two acceptable tutors, pick the one your child speaks to more easily. Across a two-year arrangement, that matters more than either the distance or the certificates.
items: Widen in order: locality, adjacent belt, weekend visit, hybrid, then online
Stop at the first option that will actually hold a weekly hour
Convenience is worth a lot, and it is not worth a wrong fit
Six weeks with no change in the written work means change the match
Between two acceptable tutors, pick the one your child talks to

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an IGCSE home tutor near me in India
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send anything about home tuition, write down four lines. The locality and the nearest landmark. The evenings that are genuinely free, after school activities and the bus. The latest hour a session can begin on a school night. And the subjects, with syllabus codes if you have them.

Those four lines do more work than a paragraph about what you are looking for, because they let a shortlist be filtered on the constraint that actually breaks arrangements. Most home tuition fails on the calendar, not on the teaching.

The process itself is short. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. If the match is wrong, ask for a different one.

Use the demo to settle the practical questions while everybody is in the room. Where the tutor travels from. What happens when the roads fail. Whether the society gate needs a registration, and who will arrange it. Which day is the fallback. And where in the house the sessions will happen. Five minutes on all of that at the first visit prevents most of what goes wrong later, and a tutor who answers those questions crisply has clearly done this before.

Anyone searching for an IGCSE home tutor near me in India is really asking for a Tuesday that holds. Set the arrangement up so that it does.
items: Write down the locality, free evenings, latest start time and subjects
Ask at the demo where the tutor travels from and what precedes your slot
Arrange the society gate registration in the first week
Agree the bad-weather fallback day before you need it

faqs.question: How far away is too far for a home tutor?
faqs.answer: Judge it in evening minutes rather than kilometres, and treat about half an hour each way as the practical ceiling for a weekday session. Beyond that the tutor is spending three hours of an evening on a ninety-minute lesson, and that booking becomes the first thing to move when their schedule tightens. Weekend visits can stretch further, because roads are quieter and the session can run longer to justify the trip.

faqs.question: Our tutor travels from Hinjewadi to Koregaon Park and is always late. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Move that session to the weekend and run midweek online with the same person. This crossing, and its equivalents in Bengaluru and Delhi NCR, is one of the most common causes of a failing arrangement, and it is almost never the tutor's fault. Changing tutors over it usually costs you more than it saves. Changing the format costs nothing and keeps the relationship the student has already built.

faqs.question: What happens when a home session is missed because of rain or traffic?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because it will happen several times in a Grade 10 year. The workable arrangement is a message within thirty minutes of the slot, conversion to an online session wherever possible rather than a cancellation, a named make-up date in the same message if it must be cancelled, and a cap on how many make-ups carry forward each term. Written down in week one, this never becomes an argument.

faqs.question: Our society requires visitor approval every time. How do other families handle it?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor as a frequent or regular visitor with the security desk in the first week, giving the name, the day and the time. Most complexes in Gurugram, Powai, Gachibowli, Balewadi and New Town have this facility, and many now run it through an app. It removes a weekly ten-minute delay and the friction that comes with it. Do it before the second session rather than after the fifth.

faqs.question: Is a nearby average tutor better than a distant excellent one?
faqs.answer: For Grade 10, usually yes, provided the nearby one is genuinely competent. The comparison is not between two standards of teaching; it is between roughly thirty-eight sessions and roughly twenty-eight, and the difference in attendance outweighs a modest difference in quality. For Grade 9, where the year has slack, and for a rare syllabus code where local supply is genuinely poor, the distant specialist is the better choice.

faqs.question: What if there is no IGCSE tutor at all in our part of the city?
faqs.answer: Widen the search in a set order rather than lowering the standard step by step. Try the adjacent locality with a later start time, then a weekend-only home visit from someone further away, then a hybrid week, then fully online. Stop at the first option that will hold a weekly hour reliably. Many families in Greater Noida, Thane and outer Bengaluru end up at the hybrid step and are perfectly well served there.

faqs.question: Should the parent be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the house, which is ordinary practice where the student is a minor and something no reasonable tutor objects to. That does not mean sitting in the room. Hovering changes how a teenager behaves and usually makes them quieter, not more attentive. Keep the session in a shared space with the door open, stay within earshot, and ask the tutor for a short summary at the end rather than watching.

faqs.question: Where in the house should sessions happen?
faqs.answer: At a table with room for two sets of papers, good light, a plug point nearby and a door that stays open. Not a bedroom, and not the dining table with a television running behind it. For science subjects, leave space for a laptop alongside the papers, since diagrams and simulations get used more than families expect. The setup sounds trivial and it makes a real difference to how much gets written in ninety minutes.

faqs.question: Can a nearby tutor add an extra session before a test?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and this is one of the real advantages of proximity that never appears in any agreement. A tutor who lives fifteen minutes away can drop in for an hour the evening before a Chemistry test; a tutor crossing the city cannot and should not be asked. Availability still depends on their schedule, so ask early rather than the same afternoon, and do not build a term plan around it.

faqs.question: How does the February/March series change what we need from a tutor?

mainEntity.name: How far away is too far for a home tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Judge it in evening minutes rather than kilometres, and treat about half an hour each way as the practical ceiling for a weekday session. Beyond that the tutor is spending three hours of an evening on a ninety-minute lesson, and that booking becomes the first thing to move when their schedule tightens. Weekend visits can stretch further, because roads are quieter and the session can run longer to justify the trip.

mainEntity.name: Our tutor travels from Hinjewadi to Koregaon Park and is always late. What should we do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Move that session to the weekend and run midweek online with the same person. This crossing, and its equivalents in Bengaluru and Delhi NCR, is one of the most common causes of a failing arrangement, and it is almost never the tutor's fault. Changing tutors over it usually costs you more than it saves. Changing the format costs nothing and keeps the relationship the student has already built.

mainEntity.name: What happens when a home session is missed because of rain or traffic?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree the rule before it happens, because it will happen several times in a Grade 10 year. The workable arrangement is a message within thirty minutes of the slot, conversion to an online session wherever possible rather than a cancellation, a named make-up date in the same message if it must be cancelled, and a cap on how many make-ups carry forward each term. Written down in week one, this never becomes an argument.

mainEntity.name: Our society requires visitor approval every time. How do other families handle it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Register the tutor as a frequent or regular visitor with the security desk in the first week, giving the name, the day and the time. Most complexes in Gurugram, Powai, Gachibowli, Balewadi and New Town have this facility, and many now run it through an app. It removes a weekly ten-minute delay and the friction that comes with it. Do it before the second session rather than after the fifth.

mainEntity.name: Is a nearby average tutor better than a distant excellent one?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Grade 10, usually yes, provided the nearby one is genuinely competent. The comparison is not between two standards of teaching; it is between roughly thirty-eight sessions and roughly twenty-eight, and the difference in attendance outweighs a modest difference in quality. For Grade 9, where the year has slack, and for a rare syllabus code where local supply is genuinely poor, the distant specialist is the better choice.

mainEntity.name: What if there is no IGCSE tutor at all in our part of the city?

acceptedAnswer.text: Widen the search in a set order rather than lowering the standard step by step. Try the adjacent locality with a later start time, then a weekend-only home visit from someone further away, then a hybrid week, then fully online. Stop at the first option that will hold a weekly hour reliably. Many families in Greater Noida, Thane and outer Bengaluru end up at the hybrid step and are perfectly well served there.

mainEntity.name: Should the parent be at home during a home tuition session?

acceptedAnswer.text: An adult should be in the house, which is ordinary practice where the student is a minor and something no reasonable tutor objects to. That does not mean sitting in the room. Hovering changes how a teenager behaves and usually makes them quieter, not more attentive. Keep the session in a shared space with the door open, stay within earshot, and ask the tutor for a short summary at the end rather than watching.

mainEntity.name: Where in the house should sessions happen?

acceptedAnswer.text: At a table with room for two sets of papers, good light, a plug point nearby and a door that stays open. Not a bedroom, and not the dining table with a television running behind it. For science subjects, leave space for a laptop alongside the papers, since diagrams and simulations get used more than families expect. The setup sounds trivial and it makes a real difference to how much gets written in ninety minutes.

mainEntity.name: Can a nearby tutor add an extra session before a test?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, and this is one of the real advantages of proximity that never appears in any agreement. A tutor who lives fifteen minutes away can drop in for an hour the evening before a Chemistry test; a tutor crossing the city cannot and should not be asked. Availability still depends on their schedule, so ask early rather than the same afternoon, and do not build a term plan around it.

heroTitle: Where a Nearby IGCSE Tutor Beats a Better One
heroSubtitle: Distance is not one question, it is six, one for each subject your child takes. Handwritten algebra needs a person beside the page. A discussion of exam technique does not. Decide subject by subject and the near-me problem mostly dissolves.
introSummary: A parent typing IGCSE private tutor near me in India is really asking two questions at once: can I find someone good, and do they need to be in the room? For some syllabuses the answer is yes, and home tuition is worth a compromise on the tutor. For others a screen costs nothing and the wider search wins easily. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 lives in handwritten working. Physics 0625 lives in diagrams and in equations recalled and rearranged. First Language English 0500 lives in drafting. Each of those behaves differently over a video call. This page sets out where presence genuinely matters, where it does not, what a thin local pool costs you in choice, and how to trial a nearby tutor and a distant one on equal terms before deciding.

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a Near Me Search Into a Real Shortlist in India
contentBlocks.body:
A search for an IGCSE private tutor near me in India returns whoever has bought the top result, which is why the shortlist has to be rebuilt from your side. Start by writing down three things: your address, the subjects, and for each subject whether the student's difficulty is in producing written work or in understanding content. That third column decides almost everything.

At the consultation we ask which board and syllabus code the school enters, the grade, the tier where one applies, your locality and which evenings survive after school and travel. Then we ask the question most services skip: which subject matters most this term? Families in Velachery or Wakad often want four subjects covered and have room for two. Deciding which two is the useful part of the conversation.

The shortlist that comes back is usually mixed on purpose. A home tutor from inside your own cluster for the subject that needs paper, and an online specialist for the subject where nobody nearby has taught the code. Parents sometimes resist that, expecting one arrangement for everything, and it is worth resisting the resistance. Profiles are verified before they go live, and availability depends on level, locality and schedule.

Then trial both, properly, before choosing. Not a friendly introductory chat with each, but the same task given to both: a past-paper question the student has already attempted, marked aloud against the scheme. The difference between the two tutors will be obvious within twenty minutes, and it will not be the difference you expected. If neither fits, ask for a different match and say which part fell short, because that sentence does more for the next shortlist than a general no.

Decide which two subjects matter this term rather than covering four badly

contentBlocks.heading: Tier Changes the Answer: Core, Extended, Foundation, Higher
contentBlocks.body:
Before deciding how far a tutor can be, settle which papers your child is sitting, because the tier changes what the tutoring has to do.

Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the two are different courses in practice rather than two versions of the same one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, splits into Foundation and Higher instead, with two calculator papers per tier. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under separate codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale.

Why this bears on distance: a Core candidate is usually working on accuracy, method and confidence, which needs close supervision of the page and benefits most from someone in the room. An Extended candidate near the top of the range is usually working on the hardest questions in the paper, where the conversation is about strategy and where an outstanding tutor two thousand kilometres away is worth more than an adequate one nearby. The same logic applies between Foundation and Higher in the Edexcel route.

The tier also changes the urgency. In Cambridge Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. A student moving up to Extended in Grade 10 has a specific gap to close under time pressure, and for those weeks a local home tutor who can come twice a week is often more valuable than a better tutor available once. Frequency beats brilliance when a deadline is fixed.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE Subjects Need a Tutor in the Room?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics 0580 is the strongest case for presence, and the reason is mechanical rather than sentimental. Marks in the non-calculator papers are lost in the working: a sign dropped in line three, a rearrangement done mentally and wrongly, a page where the student stopped writing because they were stuck and never showed why. A tutor beside the page sees the error as it forms and can stop the pen. On screen, unless the page is on camera, the tutor sees a finished answer and has to reverse-engineer the mistake.

Physics 0625 is the second. The syllabus covers motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics and space physics, and students must recall and rearrange the equations in the syllabus rather than read them off a sheet. Much of the marking rests on diagrams: ray diagrams, circuit diagrams, force arrows drawn to the right point of application. Drawing alongside a student and correcting the pencil is genuinely different from describing a correction. The Edexcel equivalent, 4PH1, behaves the same way.

First Language English 0500 is the third, and the most surprising to parents. The syllabus is a reading paper and then directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio. Drafting is a physical process: crossing out, rewriting the opening, moving a paragraph. Sitting beside a student while they rework two sentences teaches more than an hour of discussion. Note that English at IGCSE is several syllabuses, not one, including English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511, where 0511 counts speaking into the grade while 0510 reports it separately, and Literature in English 0475. Edexcel offers English Language A 4EA1, English Language B 4EB1 and English as a Second Language 4ES1. Check which your child sits before hiring anyone at all.

0625 requires recalling and rearranging syllabus equations, not reading them off

contentBlocks.heading: How Small Your Local Pool Really Is, Across India
contentBlocks.body:
Anyone typing IGCSE private tutor near me in India overestimates local supply, because a listing counts tutors by subject rather than tutors who have taught the code. Strip out everyone who has not, and the pool within a reasonable radius is often two or three people, sometimes none.

Delhi NCR illustrates it well. South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri have genuine depth, as does Gurugram along Golf Course Road and Noida including Sector 128. Move to Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad and the same subject returns a much shorter list. A tutor willing to cross from one of the strong areas will do it for a term and then renegotiate, which families experience as unreliability and is really distance.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is a set of islands. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill trade tutors among themselves; Powai is served unevenly; Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are effectively their own market with their own smaller pool. Chennai concentrates in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar, thinning along Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) towards Perungudi and out to Velachery. Pune divides between Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Aundh on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Wakad, Hinjewadi and Kharadi on the other.

Gujarat is the clearest example of the trade-off. Ahmedabad holds a workable pool around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close enough to share it, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot have very few tutors for a named Cambridge code. A family in Rajkot choosing strictly on proximity is choosing from almost nobody, and that is not a compromise worth making for a subject that travels well. The honest version of a near-me search is: who is genuinely close, who is genuinely good, and does this subject care.
