contentBlocks.heading: School Timings, Traffic and the Weekday Evening in India
contentBlocks.body:
The real constraint on a nearby tutor is not kilometres, it is the shape of a Grade 10 evening. School finishes, travel happens, the student eats, and what remains is a window that closes early because they have to be up at six. Any arrangement that assumes otherwise fails in week five.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Greenwood High International School and Chirec International School describe the same evening whichever city they are in.

Traffic is the second constraint and it is asymmetric. A tutor coming towards you in the peak direction loses far more time than one travelling against it, which is why two tutors the same distance away can have completely different reliability. Monsoon weeks make it worse, and in Mumbai and Chennai a few days each year simply remove the possibility of a home visit. Agree in advance that those sessions convert to online rather than vanish.

Then there is the calendar. Cambridge series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. School mocks land weeks before whichever series your child is entered for, and in those weeks the timetable becomes unpredictable: a session moved twice is normal. A local tutor absorbs that more easily than a distant one for home sessions, and an online tutor absorbs it best of all, because a cancelled slot can be replaced at short notice without anybody travelling.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Deciding Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
Run this as a grid rather than a single choice. For each subject, ask whether the marks are lost on paper or in understanding, and whether a tutor who has taught the code exists within travelling distance. Two questions, four outcomes, and the arrangement falls out of it.

Marks lost on paper with a local specialist available: book home classes. This is the standard case for 0580 and for 0625 diagram work, and the twice-weekly rhythm of a nearby home tutor is worth more than a marginally stronger teacher on a screen.

Marks lost on paper with nobody local: book online, but insist on the setup. A second camera on the page, a document camera or a graphics tablet, and a tutor who asks the student to think aloud while writing. Without that the online lesson becomes a discussion of finished answers, which is precisely the wrong medicine. Ask for it in the trial and judge whether the tutor has done it before.

Understanding rather than production, whether local supply exists or not: online is equal, and often better because the choice is wider. Theory recall, mark-scheme reading, exam technique, Economics 0455 essay planning and most Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 revision work fall here.

Hybrid is the natural end state for a household with two or three subjects running. One subject at home with a nearby tutor, another online with a specialist, and a shift towards online in the fortnight around mocks. Families in Ahmedabad, Thane or Perungudi tend to arrive at this within a term anyway. Deciding it deliberately at the start saves two months of trying to make one arrangement serve everything.

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a Nearby Tutor and a Distant One to the Same Standard
contentBlocks.body:
The phrase IGCSE private tutor near me in India carries a hidden bias: proximity relaxes judgment. A tutor who lives two streets away and comes recommended by a neighbour gets hired on a conversation, while a tutor in another city is interrogated about syllabus codes. Apply the harder standard to both.

The subject questions are identical whoever is asking. Which papers does each tier sit in this syllabus, and which are non-calculator? What do you look for in a marked script before recommending a tier change? How do you teach equation rearrangement to a student who has memorised the formulas but cannot use them? A tutor who has worked the code answers immediately, from either end of the country.

Platform verification covers identity, the qualifications a tutor claims and the subjects and levels they state they teach, checked before the profile goes live. It does not measure teaching, which is why the trial exists. For a distant tutor, add one question to the trial: show me how you will see my child's working. If the answer is vague, the distance is a real cost rather than a neutral one.

For the local tutor, add the household checks instead, and do not skip them because the person feels familiar. A responsible adult at home during every session. Lessons in a shared space rather than a bedroom. Scheduling messages to the parent, not to the student. Clear handling of a session missed because the tutor is unwell or stuck in traffic. These are ordinary arrangements, and a tutor who bristles at them is telling you something worth hearing before a term begins rather than after.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does Near Enough Mean for Home Classes in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Near is not a distance, it is a reliability threshold. A tutor is near enough if they can arrive twice a week, at the same time, for a whole term, without the arrangement becoming a negotiation. In practice that means inside your own cluster rather than inside your own city, and parents who search for an IGCSE private tutor near me in India are usually surprised by how small that radius turns out to be.

What proximity actually buys is worth naming precisely, because it is easy to overvalue. It buys the tutor's eyes on the page while the student writes. It buys the folder, the notes and the desk, which tell you whether the problem is understanding or organisation. It buys a two-minute conversation at the door that no message thread replicates. And it buys frequency, which matters more than most families expect in the months before a series.

What it costs is choice. Restricting a search to a four-kilometre radius in Surat or Perungudi may leave nobody who has taught your syllabus code, and a general Mathematics teacher who has never seen 0580 Extended is not a substitute for a specialist on a screen. The trade only makes sense while a real specialist remains inside the radius.

So set the rule by subject. If the subject lives on paper and someone qualified is genuinely close, take the local tutor even if a better one exists elsewhere. If the subject is about understanding, or if nobody local has taught the code, take the distant specialist and stop apologising for the screen. And if the honest answer is both, run one subject each way. That is not a compromise; it is the arrangement most families in Indian cities end up with once they stop treating near as a single decision.

contentBlocks.heading: Is a Nearby Tutor Worth More Than a Better One?
contentBlocks.body:
Sometimes, and the conditions are specific enough to state. Proximity wins when the subject depends on written production, when the student needs frequency more than depth, when they are young enough or disorganised enough that being observed changes their behaviour, and when a qualified person is actually available close by. Take away any one of those and the argument weakens.

Proximity loses when the local option has not taught the syllabus. This is the mistake that costs families a term: hiring a nearby graduate for Physics who does not know that 0625 requires recalling and rearranging equations, and discovering it in February. A tutor's convenience is not a qualification, and a friendly neighbour with a science degree is still a stranger to the mark scheme.

Judge either choice on the same evidence at six weeks. Set a comparable past-paper section, marked the same way as the first one, and lay the two attempts side by side. Look at where the marks moved and where they did not. If the same method marks are falling in the same places, the format is not the problem and neither is the distance; the plan is.

The limits apply equally to both. No tutor can guarantee a grade. Nobody rebuilds two years of algebra in the six weeks before a series. A student who does not attempt work between sessions will not improve whether the tutor sits beside them or appears on a screen. And a tutor changed three times in a year does more harm than a merely adequate one kept steady, which is the strongest practical argument for choosing an arrangement you can actually sustain through to the exam series.

contentBlocks.heading: Trialling a Local and a Distant Tutor Fairly
contentBlocks.body:
Most families searching for an IGCSE private tutor near me in India never actually compare. They try the nearby tutor, it is fine, and the question of whether a specialist would have been better goes unanswered for two years. Running both trials in the same week costs one extra evening and settles it.

Prepare one thing before either session: a past-paper question your child has already attempted and had marked, with the marks and comments visible. The same question goes to both tutors. Do not tell either what the other said.

What you are judging is narrow. Does the tutor find the actual error rather than re-teaching the topic? Do they name the mark scheme point where the marks stopped? Does your child talk during the session or only listen? And for the distant tutor specifically, could they see the working, or were they guessing from a typed answer?

Afterwards, ask your child which session they would rather repeat, and take the answer seriously without treating it as final. A fifteen-year-old's preference for whichever tutor was less demanding is information, not instruction.

To begin: send a query or book a free consultation with the syllabus code, the grade, your locality and two evenings that are genuinely free. We shortlist verified tutors, usually a local option and an online one so the comparison is real, and a demo can be arranged before you commit. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, availability depends on level, locality and schedule, and you can ask for a different match at any stage.

2. Book a trial with a local tutor and an online specialist in the same week.

4. Judge whether each found the real error and named the mark scheme point.
5. Ask the distant tutor to show how they saw the handwritten working.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the clearest, because errors form in the working and a tutor beside the page can stop the pen mid-line. Physics 0625 is next, since the syllabus requires recalling and rearranging equations and much of the marking rests on diagrams drawn correctly. First Language English 0500 is third, because drafting is physical: crossing out, rewriting an opening, moving a paragraph. Revision and theory work travel perfectly well online.

faqs.question: Which subjects are genuinely fine online?
faqs.answer: Anything where the work is understanding, recall and exam technique rather than handwritten production. Reading a mark scheme line by line, planning an Economics 0455 answer, revising Chemistry 0620 or Biology 0610 theory, drilling command words, and timing a section under supervision all work as well on screen as in person. For these, restricting your search to a few kilometres costs you choice and buys you nothing. Judge the tutor on whether they have taught the code, not on how far away they live.

faqs.question: How small is the local pool for a named syllabus, really?
faqs.answer: Smaller than a search result suggests, because most listings count tutors by subject rather than by code. Strip out everyone who has not actually taught, say, 0580 Extended, and a four-kilometre radius in Surat, Perungudi or Greater Noida can leave nobody. Strong pockets exist: South Delhi, Gurugram along Golf Course Road, Bandra and Juhu, Adyar and Nungambakkam, Koregaon Park and Aundh, Satellite and Bodakdev in Ahmedabad. Outside them, plan on at least one subject running online.

faqs.question: How do I trial a nearby tutor and a distant one fairly?
faqs.answer: Give both the same task in the same week and tell neither what the other said. Use a past-paper question your child has already attempted and had marked, with the comments visible, and ask each tutor to work through where the marks stopped. Judge four things: whether they found the actual error rather than re-teaching the topic, whether they named the mark scheme point, whether your child spoke during the session, and whether the distant tutor could genuinely see the handwritten working.

faqs.question: Can we use a home tutor for one subject and an online tutor for another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most households it is the sensible design rather than a fallback. Run the paper-heavy subject at home, typically Mathematics or Physics, with a tutor from inside your own cluster who can come twice a week. Run the understanding-heavy subject online with whoever has genuinely taught that code, wherever they live. Keep the same tutor per subject rather than swapping formats mid-term, and keep a single log of topics covered so neither tutor repeats the other's work.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travel to Thane, Velachery or Wakad on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Usually only if they already live in that cluster. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar operate as their own market rather than as suburbs of the western line, and the same is true of Velachery and Perungudi relative to central Chennai, or Wakad and Hinjewadi relative to Koregaon Park. A tutor who agrees to cross the city will typically manage it for a term and then renegotiate. Ask where the tutor starts their evening from before you accept a slot.

faqs.question: Is a nearby tutor worth choosing over a better one further away?
faqs.answer: When four conditions hold together, yes. The subject depends on written production, the student needs frequency more than depth, being observed changes how they work, and a genuinely qualified person is available close by. Remove any one and the case weakens. The common mistake is hiring a nearby graduate who has never taught the syllabus, then discovering in February that they did not know 0625 requires equations to be recalled and rearranged. Convenience is not a qualification.

faqs.question: What should an online tutor do to see my child's working?
faqs.answer: Insist on one of three arrangements before the trial: a second camera pointed at the page, a document camera, or a graphics tablet the student writes on. The tutor should also ask your child to think aloud while writing rather than present a finished answer. If a tutor has done this before, they will describe their setup without hesitation. If the answer is vague, the lesson will become a discussion of completed work, which is the wrong treatment for a handwriting-based problem.

faqs.question: Does the tier change how close the tutor needs to be?
faqs.answer: It does, more than parents expect. A Core candidate, or a Foundation candidate on the Edexcel route, is usually working on accuracy, method and confidence, which benefits from close supervision of the page and from twice-weekly contact, so a nearby home tutor is worth a compromise. A strong Extended or Higher candidate is working on the hardest questions in the paper, where the conversation is strategic. For them, an outstanding specialist in another city is worth far more than an adequate one down the road.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once?
faqs.answer: Two is usually the ceiling in Grade 10, and one is often enough. Each arrangement takes an evening, travel time and homework between sessions, and a student carrying four external classes has no time left to practise independently, which is where improvement actually comes from. Pick the subject with the nearest deadline and the clearest evidence of a gap. If two subjects are weak, check first whether one cause sits under both, since algebraic fluency explains a surprising share of lost Physics marks.

faqs.question: What happens to home sessions during monsoon or mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before the term starts rather than improvising. In Mumbai and Chennai a few days each year remove the possibility of a home visit entirely, and in mock weeks the school timetable moves sessions at short notice. The workable arrangement is that any session prevented by weather, traffic or a school clash converts to an online session that same week rather than being cancelled. Put it in the first conversation, alongside how a tutor's own illness is handled.

faqs.question: How soon should we decide between local and online?
faqs.answer: Within the first three sessions, and definitely before the term before the exam series. Cambridge runs series in February and March, in May and June and in October and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June, with mocks landing weeks before whichever one applies. Changing format close to papers costs continuity at the worst moment. Trial both early in Grade 9 or the first half of Grade 10, decide per subject, then hold the arrangement steady.

h1: IGCSE Tuition Near Me: Choosing a Venue in Your Own Locality
heroTitle: Where IGCSE Lessons Should Happen Near You
heroSubtitle: Five venues are available to most families: your own home, the tutor's home, a neighbourhood centre, a library or cafe, and online. They differ on travel, on supervision and on the study hours a commute quietly removes from a Grade 10 week. This page compares them and helps you pick for your own locality.
introSummary: A search for IGCSE tuition near me in India usually returns three or four options within a few kilometres, and they are not interchangeable. Home tuition at your own table, the tutor's flat two societies away, a centre on the main road, a library corner, or a screen. The right answer depends less on teaching quality than on distance, on who is supervising, and on how many study hours the journey costs each week. A Grade 10 student has a fixed number of usable evening hours, and a commute spends them before the lesson starts. This page compares all five venues honestly and shows how the answer shifts between a metro suburb and a smaller city.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram find tuition near you across India?
contentBlocks.body:
By treating your locality as a constraint rather than a preference, and by telling you early when the constraint cannot be met. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks which grade the student is in, the syllabus codes and tier, the school's exam series, your locality and pin code, and the evenings that are genuinely free. Location and time are asked together, because a tutor who is nearby but only free on Sunday mornings is not actually near you in any useful sense.

What comes back is a shortlist of verified tutors with the venue stated. Some will travel to you. Some teach from their own home and expect the student to come. Some are online only. Availability is always conditional on locality and slot, and the honest position for a few syllabus and tier combinations is that nobody within a sensible distance teaches them at all.

That last answer is the one worth valuing. A family that spends three weeks waiting for a nearby Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 tutor has spent three weeks it could have spent being taught online. Ask for the local supply picture in the first conversation, subject by subject, and make the venue decision with that information rather than against it.

Then run a trial before committing, and run it at the venue you actually intend to use. A trial at your home tells you very little about whether your son will get to the tutor's flat in Kondapur on a Wednesday. If the fit or the venue turns out to be wrong, you can ask for a different match rather than persevere with a journey nobody enjoys.
items: 1. Give your locality and pin code along with the evenings that are genuinely free.
2. Ask for the local supply picture per syllabus, including the answer that nobody is nearby.
3. Review a shortlist of verified tutors with the venue stated for each.
4. Run the trial at the venue you actually intend to use every week.
5. Change the venue, or the match, before the arrangement settles into a habit.

contentBlocks.heading: Why does the venue question get urgent in Grade 10?
contentBlocks.body:
Because the calendar tightens and the evenings do not get longer. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Grade 9 has slack in it. Grade 10 does not.

The series matters here. Cambridge series run in February/March, May/June and October/November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The February/March series exists specifically for India, so that Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for IB Diploma or A Level entry in the same academic year. Schools decide which series they enter students for, and a student cannot choose one independently. A family on February/March reaches the pressure point months earlier, which means a venue that costs an hour of travel each way stops being affordable much sooner.

Tiering sharpens it further. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. A student working towards Extended needs practice volume, and practice volume needs unbroken time at a desk. Every hour spent travelling to a centre is an hour not spent on a past paper.

So the venue calculation changes between the two years. In Grade 9, a centre or a tutor's home is often perfectly reasonable, and the routine of going somewhere can help a thirteen-year-old take the work seriously. By the second term of Grade 10, with mocks in view, most families should be minimising movement. That usually means home tuition or online, and it is worth planning the switch rather than making it in a panic.
items: Cambridge series: February/March, May/June and October/November; Edexcel: January and May/June
February/March is an India-only series, so that year's pressure point arrives earlier
Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*, and Extended needs practice volume
Grade 9 tolerates travel; Grade 10 usually should not
Plan the switch from a travelling venue to home tuition rather than making it in a panic

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE subjects lose the most when the venue is wrong?
contentBlocks.body:
The ones where the tutor needs to watch a pencil move. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the clearest case: marks are lost in working that was thought and never written, in a line skipped because it seemed obvious, in a layout that a marker cannot follow. A tutor sitting beside the student catches that in the moment. A tutor on a screen sees the answer and has to reconstruct the rest, and a tutor at a centre with six other students does not see it at all.

Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 behaves similarly because of diagrams and units. A ray diagram drawn too small to label, a circuit sketched without the component the question needed, an answer given without units, are all things somebody physically present corrects on the spot. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 sit in the middle: the definitions and the explanation writing transfer to a screen well, while labelled diagrams do not.

At the other end, Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 and Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 travel almost perfectly. Both are assessed through writing that is read rather than watched, so a tutor in another city with the draft open on a shared screen loses very little. For these two subjects, a distant specialist online beats a nearby generalist almost every time, and families who insist on proximity for them are paying a real price in teaching quality for no practical gain.

That gives a rough rule for a mixed week. Keep the subject where paper matters at home, wherever the best local option is. Send the written subjects online, however far away the tutor lives. Very few families run all their tuition in one venue once they have thought about it this way.
items: 0580 Mathematics loses the most on a screen: unwritten working and unreadable layout
0625 Physics needs someone watching diagrams, labels and missing units
0620 and 0610 transfer partly: explanation writing yes, labelled diagrams no
0500 and 0455 transfer almost fully, because the work is read rather than watched
A mixed week is normal: paper subjects nearby, written subjects online

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE tuition near me in India: what near means in your city
contentBlocks.body:
Near is a time, not a distance, and the two diverge wildly across Indian metros. A search for IGCSE tuition near me in India from Bandra and the same search from Whitefield produce results that look similar and behave completely differently.

In Delhi NCR, near is realistic inside a pocket and fictional across one. South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri form one workable cluster; Golf Course Road and central Gurugram (Gurgaon) form another; Noida, Sector 128 Noida and Greater Noida form a third. Crossing between them on a weekday evening can stretch a short trip badly, and families in Dwarka, Faridabad and Ghaziabad discover this in week three rather than week one. Someone searching for IGCSE tuition near me in Delhi should ask which side of the city the tutor starts from before agreeing a seven o'clock slot.

Mumbai compresses everything. IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai works well inside Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, where two kilometres is genuinely two kilometres for most of the evening. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are separate markets, and a tutor crossing into them is making a promise the monsoon will break. Bengaluru is the most extreme case in the country: IGCSE tuition near me in Bangalore means something entirely different in Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout or Jayanagar than it does in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City, Hebbal, Yelahanka or along Kanakapura Road, and the honest answer for the outer ring is usually online.

Hyderabad is the friendliest of the big cities. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Kokapet and the Financial District sit close enough that IGCSE tuition near me in Hyderabad often means a genuine ten-minute journey, with Secunderabad the exception. Chennai splits between the older localities, Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar, where IGCSE tuition near me in Chennai behaves like a neighbourhood service, and the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery corridor, where it does not. Pune is workable across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Kharadi, Aundh, Baner, Balewadi and Wakad, though anything involving Hinjewadi at six in the evening should be questioned, so IGCSE tuition near me in Pune frequently ends up on weekend mornings.
items: Near is a time, not a distance, and the two diverge most in Bengaluru and Delhi NCR
Delhi NCR splits into pockets: crossing between them on a weekday evening rarely works
Mumbai: the island city and the western suburbs are workable; Thane and Kharghar are separate
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Kondapur and Jubilee Hills are genuinely near each other
Chennai: Adyar and Alwarpet behave locally; the OMR corridor does not
Pune: ask about Hinjewadi before agreeing any weekday evening slot

contentBlocks.heading: School timings in India and the hours a commute quietly eats
contentBlocks.body:
Work the arithmetic once and the venue question usually answers itself. A Grade 10 student at a school such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Aditya Birla World Academy, B. D. Somani International School, Greenwood High International School, Canadian International School Bangalore, Chirec International School, Sreenidhi International School, Mercedes-Benz International School or Singapore International School typically leaves home early, travels, sits a full school day, travels back, and arrives with a fixed and fairly small number of usable evening hours before sleep. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Into that window you are placing a lesson. If the lesson happens at home, the cost is the lesson. If it happens somewhere else, the cost is the lesson plus two journeys plus the waiting and settling at each end, and the journeys are the part that cannot be shortened by working harder. Two lessons a week at a centre across the locality can remove a substantial share of the week's independent study time, and independent study is where IGCSE marks are actually made.

There is a second cost that families underestimate. A student who has travelled arrives tired and leaves tired, and the work he does after getting home at nine is not the same quality as the work he would have done at seven. Homework then slides to the weekend, the weekend fills, and by the middle of Grade 10 the whole schedule is running late.

School calendars make it worse at exactly the wrong moment. Internal assessments and mocks cluster, and in those weeks a travelling venue is the first thing families cancel. If your venue is the thing that gets dropped whenever the term gets busy, it was the wrong venue. Home tuition and online sessions survive busy weeks because nothing about them depends on the roads.
items: Count the journey, the waiting and the settling, not just the lesson hour
Two travelling lessons a week can remove a large share of independent study time
A tired student after a commute does lower-quality work than the same student at home
Whatever gets cancelled first in a busy week was the wrong venue
Home tuition and online sessions survive mock weeks; travelling arrangements often do not

contentBlocks.heading: Your home, the tutor's home, a centre, or online?
contentBlocks.body:
Each venue buys something and costs something, and the sensible approach is to name both rather than to pick on instinct.

Your own home costs the most per hour, because the tutor's travel is inside the price, and it buys the most supervision and the least lost time. Home tuition also gives the tutor information nobody else gets: the desk, the noise, the phone, the folder that has not been opened. For a Grade 10 student in the second term, home classes are usually the strongest option available, and for a student who is disorganised rather than weak they are worth paying extra for.

The tutor's own home is cheaper and shifts the travel onto the student. It can work well, particularly where the tutor lives close and teaches in a room set aside for it. It also puts a fifteen-year-old in somebody else's house without a parent present, which deserves the checks in the next section rather than an assumption.

A neighbourhood centre buys structure and a working environment, and costs individual attention. For a student who cannot study at home because the flat is small or busy, a centre can be exactly right. Ask about batch size, who teaches each week, and whether the centre teaches your named syllabus or a blended course.

A library or a cafe is the weakest of the five. It is fine occasionally, and unreliable as a weekly arrangement: noise, no board, no wall socket, and nothing kept between sessions.

Online costs the physical information and buys everything else. No travel, a slot that holds through the monsoon, and access to a tutor who teaches the exact syllabus and tier. A hybrid week combines them properly: one home session for the subject where paper matters, one online session for the subject where it does not, with the rule that a difficult evening converts a home visit to online rather than cancelling it.
items: Your home: most supervision, least lost time, highest price per hour
The tutor's home: cheaper, shifts travel to the student, needs explicit checks
A centre: structure and environment, at the cost of individual attention
A library or cafe: acceptable occasionally, unreliable as a weekly venue
Online plus one weekly home visit is the hybrid most Grade 10 families settle on

contentBlocks.heading: Sending a Grade 10 student to a tutor's home: what to check
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile goes live on IB Gram, identity, qualifications and claimed teaching experience are checked, and the syllabuses and levels a tutor says he teaches are recorded. That is the platform's part. When your child is the one travelling, there is a second set of checks that belongs to you, and they are ordinary rather than suspicious.

Visit once before the arrangement starts. See the room. Lessons should happen in a shared or open room rather than a bedroom, with somebody else in the house during the session. Note who else is there, and note whether other students come and go, because a tutor running back-to-back sessions has a very different setup from one teaching a single student in a family flat.

Settle the practical rules in the same visit. Fixed start and end times, so your child is not waiting outside for fifteen minutes. A clear route and a fixed mode of travel, agreed rather than improvised. A message when he arrives and when he leaves, which most fifteen-year-olds accept without complaint if it is framed as logistics rather than surveillance. And scheduling and progress messages copied to a parent, not sent only to the student.

Then ask the syllabus questions you would ask anyway. Which code, which tier, how work is marked and returned. A tutor teaching in his own home should still be working to Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended or whichever syllabus your school has entered, and not to a generalised Grade 10 course assembled from several boards.

If any part of this feels awkward to raise, that is a reason to raise it rather than to skip it. Professional tutors expect these questions and most have answers ready.

Fix start and end times, the travel route, and arrival and departure messages

contentBlocks.heading: Five venues for IGCSE tuition, compared on travel, safety and lost time
contentBlocks.body:
Most families typing IGCSE tuition near me in India are really asking a question with three parts: how far, how safe, and how much of the evening does it cost. Taking the five venues against those three tests produces a clearer answer than any general advice about teaching quality.

On travel, the ranking is obvious and worth stating anyway. Online costs nothing. Your home costs nothing to the student and shifts the burden to the tutor, which is reflected in the price. The tutor's home costs two journeys. A centre costs two journeys and usually a fixed timetable you cannot move. A library or cafe costs two journeys to a place with none of the equipment.

On safety and supervision, your own home is strongest, with a parent in the flat and a shared room. Online is next, provided the session happens in a common area rather than behind a bedroom door, and provided somebody occasionally walks past. A centre is generally well supervised during the class and least supervised on the journey, particularly after dark. The tutor's home needs the specific checks set out above. A cafe offers nothing at all.

On lost study time, the differences are larger than families expect. Two travelling sessions a week, each with a journey at both ends and waiting time in between, can cost a substantial part of a Grade 10 student's usable weekday study hours across a term. Nothing about the teaching makes that back.

Which leaves a simple conclusion that most families reach eventually and would benefit from reaching sooner. Travel for something you cannot get any other way. Do not travel for convenience, for habit, or because the centre is on the way home. And if the nearest good option for a subject is genuinely far, take it online rather than taking a worse one nearby.
items: Three tests decide a venue: distance in time, supervision, and study hours lost
Online and your own home cost the student no travel at all
A centre is well supervised in class and least supervised on the journey after dark
Two travelling sessions a week cost a real share of a Grade 10 study week
Travel only for something unavailable another way, never out of habit

contentBlocks.heading: When no venue near you in India works, and online wins
contentBlocks.body:
Outside the six big metro clusters the venue question often answers itself, and families spend months refusing to accept the answer. In Ahmedabad across Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, local tutors exist for Mathematics and the sciences and thin out sharply for Economics and First Language English. The same pattern repeats in Kolkata and eastern India across Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, and more sharply in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR shows it too. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula have some supply; Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have little for named international syllabuses, and what looks like a nearby option is frequently a CBSE tutor teaching a Grade 10 course under a different label. The southern cities beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, meaning Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, and the central and western cities of Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, are in the same position.

In all of these places, a search for IGCSE tuition near me in India returns results that are near but not right. The honest comparison is not between a nearby tutor and a distant one; it is between a nearby generalist and a specialist who actually teaches your syllabus at your tier. For 0500 and 0455 that comparison is not close. For 0580 and 0625 it is genuinely finely balanced, and the best arrangement is often a local tutor for the paper-heavy work with an online specialist for the rest.

Be realistic about what changing venue can do. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and moving a lesson from a centre to your dining table does not by itself fix a content gap. What it does is give back study hours and let somebody watch the student work. And if the honest answer is that your child does not need tuition at all, a good tutor will say so at the trial rather than book the slot.

Chandigarh has some supply; Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun and Kanpur have little
Kochi, Coimbatore, Indore, Nagpur and Goa: a nearby generalist is often the only local option

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing a venue in India: a step-by-step for your locality
contentBlocks.body:
Do this once, properly, and you will not revisit it for a year.

1. Write down the student's actual free evening hours on each weekday, after school, travel and any activity, and be honest about the finishing times rather than the timetabled ones.
2. For each subject you are considering, decide whether it is a paper subject where somebody should watch the working, such as 0580 and 0625, or a written subject that reads well on a screen, such as 0500 and 0455.
3. Ask what exists within a genuinely short journey at the times you have, by syllabus and tier rather than by subject name, and treat nobody being available as useful information.
4. Price the journey, not the lesson: two trips, the waiting, and the tiredness afterwards.
5. Choose home tuition or online for anything in Grade 10 term two onwards, and allow a centre or the tutor's home only where the environment at home genuinely does not work.

A venue chosen this way tends to survive the year, which is the only test that matters. Venues chosen on convenience get cancelled in the first busy fortnight.

To start, send a query or book a free consultation with your locality, the grade, the syllabus codes and the evenings that work. IB Gram asks about level, location and schedule, then shortlists verified tutors with the venue stated for each, subject to availability. Arrange a trial at the venue you intend to use, and ask for a different match if either the tutor or the journey turns out to be wrong.
items: Write down real free evening hours per weekday before looking at any tutor
Split subjects into paper subjects and written subjects before choosing a venue
Ask what exists nearby by syllabus code and tier, not by subject name
Price two journeys, the waiting and the tiredness, not only the lesson
From Grade 10 term two, default to home tuition or online unless home genuinely fails

faqs.question: How far is too far for a weekday IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: Measure it in evening minutes rather than kilometres, and set the limit before you start looking. As a working rule, if the round trip plus waiting takes longer than the lesson itself, the venue is costing more than it delivers. In Bengaluru and Delhi NCR that threshold is crossed within a few kilometres on a weekday evening, while in Hyderabad or Ahmedabad the same distance may be genuinely quick. Time the journey once at the actual hour you would travel, not on a Sunday afternoon.

faqs.question: Is it safe to send a Grade 10 student to the tutor's home?
faqs.answer: It can be, with checks you should make openly rather than quietly. Visit once before starting and see the room. Insist that lessons happen in a shared or open room with another adult in the house. Agree fixed start and end times so nobody waits outside, agree the travel route, and ask for a message on arrival and departure. Make sure scheduling and progress messages copy a parent. Professional tutors expect all of this, and hesitation about any of it is itself an answer.

faqs.question: Is a nearby tuition centre better than a distant online tutor?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject and on why the student is struggling. A centre gives structure, company and a working environment, which genuinely helps a student who cannot study at home. An online specialist gives exact syllabus and tier fit, which matters more for Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 than for anything else. For Mathematics 0580 the answer is closer, because somebody should be watching the working. Many families use both, one subject each, and that is a sensible outcome rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: Does home tuition cost more, and is the difference worth it?
faqs.answer: Yes, it usually costs more per hour, because the tutor's travel time is inside the fee. Whether it is worth it depends on what you are short of. If your evenings are tight and your child loses study hours to commuting, home tuition often pays for itself in returned time. If the home is small, noisy or shared and the student genuinely cannot concentrate there, the extra money buys you nothing and a centre may work better. Price the journey alongside the lesson before deciding.

faqs.question: We live in Whitefield and the good tutors are in Indiranagar. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Take them online rather than asking anyone to make that journey twice a week. Bengaluru is the clearest case in the country where near on a map and near in an evening are different things, and an arrangement built on crossing the city will quietly collapse within a term. Keep one local option for the subject where paper working matters most, if a decent one exists in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road or along Electronic City, and run everything else online with whoever teaches your syllabus best.

faqs.question: Can home lessons still work if our flat is small and busy?
faqs.answer: Often yes, with one change: pick the quietest hour rather than the most convenient one. A dining table with the television off works better than most bedroom desks, and many families in Powai, Thane and Kharghar run home tuition earlier or later than they first intended for exactly this reason. If the flat truly cannot be quiet, a nearby centre or the tutor's home becomes the sensible choice, and that is a practical decision rather than a failure of any kind.

faqs.question: What about a library or a cafe as a meeting point?
faqs.answer: Occasionally fine, and poor as a weekly arrangement. There is no board, no reliable power socket, no way to leave materials between sessions, and usually enough background noise to make a ninety-minute session tiring. Cafes also make timed practice almost impossible, which matters increasingly through Grade 10. Use one to meet a tutor for the first time if you prefer neutral ground, then move to a proper venue once the arrangement is settled. Do not build a two-year plan around a table you do not control.

faqs.question: How much study time does a commute actually cost?
faqs.answer: More than the clock suggests, because the journey is only part of it. Count the trip out, the waiting at each end, the trip back, and the drop in quality of whatever work happens afterwards. Two travelling sessions a week remove a real share of a Grade 10 student's usable weekday hours across a term, and independent practice is where IGCSE marks are made. Run that calculation on paper once. It changes most families' venue decision immediately and permanently.

faqs.question: Nothing near us in Jaipur teaches the Cambridge syllabus. What now?
faqs.answer: Move online and stop searching locally, because waiting costs more than travelling would. Outside the six large metro clusters, and across Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur in particular, what appears to be a nearby international tutor is frequently a CBSE tutor teaching a relabelled Grade 10 course. Ask any local candidate directly which syllabus code and tier he teaches, and check the answer against your school's paperwork. An online tutor who teaches your exact syllabus is the better hire.

faqs.question: Should the venue change between Grade 9 and Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Usually, and planning the change is better than being forced into it. Grade 9 has enough slack that a centre or a tutor's home is reasonable, and for a younger student the routine of going somewhere can help him take the work seriously. From the second term of Grade 10, with mocks in view and past papers taking over, most families should be minimising movement. Decide the switch date at the end of a term rather than during a bad week.

faqs.question: Can one venue serve two children in the same family?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and back-to-back sessions at home are usually simpler than moving two students to a centre on different days. Where the children are in different grades, expect two separate sessions rather than a shared one, since the content diverges quickly. In shorter-distance cities such as Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune, two consecutive home visits on one evening work well. Across Mumbai or Delhi NCR, one at home and one online is the arrangement that actually holds through a full year.

faqs.question: How do we test a venue before committing to it?
faqs.answer: Run the trial at the venue you intend to use every week, not at whichever place is easiest to arrange once. If the plan is the tutor's home, travel there at the real hour on a real weekday. If the plan is a centre, sit through a session rather than a sample class. If the plan is online, test the connection at the time the lesson would run, when the whole building is also online. A trial at the wrong venue tells you about the tutor and nothing about the arrangement.

h1: IB and IGCSE Tutors in India for the Whole School Journey
heroTitle: IB and IGCSE Tutoring Across India
heroSubtitle: Plenty of Indian households run two boards at once: one child in Grade 9 sitting Cambridge papers, another in DP2 counting points towards 45. The two systems overlap more than families expect and diverge exactly where it costs marks. This page is about covering both without doubling the week.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE tutors in India are hired mostly by two kinds of family: the household running two children on different boards, and the student who has just finished Grade 10 and walked into DP1 expecting the same rules to apply. One home tutor can sometimes serve both, and holding one home tuition slot two evenings a week is far easier than holding four. But the systems reward different things. IGCSE asks a student to answer a question precisely against a mark scheme; the Diploma Programme asks them to produce and defend their own work against criteria. Knowing where the overlap is real and where it is imaginary is what stops a household hiring four tutors when it needed two.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match one tutor to two boards in India?
contentBlocks.body:
By treating it as two requests in one enquiry rather than as one vague request. You send a query or book a free consultation, and IB Gram asks separately about each child: the board, the programme, the subject and level or tier, the exam series, the school calendar, then your locality and the hours the household can realistically hold. The shortlist comes back as verified profiles matched to both descriptions, with a demo or trial arranged before anything is committed.

The useful question is where the two requests actually meet. A Grade 9 child doing Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier and a DP1 sibling on Mathematics Applications and Interpretation are closer than they look, because the underlying algebra is shared and the difference sits in what each examination rewards. A Grade 10 child on First Language English 0500 and a DP2 sibling writing an Extended Essay are not close at all, whatever the subject label suggests.

Locality then decides whether one person can serve both children in one visit. In Bandra, Whitefield, Gachibowli or Koregaon Park a tutor can often take two back-to-back home sessions in the same evening, which is the cheapest hour you will ever buy in travel terms. In Greater Noida, Kharghar or Kanakapura Road the travel may mean one child gets the home slot and the other goes online.

Then the household tests it. Watch both trials, ideally in the same week, and compare what each tutor did with a marked script rather than how the conversation felt. If one child's fit is wrong, ask for a different match for that child only. Splitting a shortlist is normal and it is easier than persisting with one person stretched across two boards they do not both know.

Say whether you want one tutor for both or two specialists
Name the evenings the whole household can hold, not just one child's
Ask whether back-to-back home sessions are possible in your locality
Trial both children in the same week, then compare notes once

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE and the IB Diploma: what they share and where they part
contentBlocks.body:
They share a culture and disagree about assessment. Both expect reading beyond the textbook, both use command words that carry precise meanings, both punish an answer that is correct but not the answer asked for, and neither rewards a memorised derivation the way board examinations in India often do. That shared culture is why one good tutor can sometimes work across both, and why a switching student recognises the terrain even when the rules change.

The structures are different animals. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually across Grades 9 and 10. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some in 9 to 1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. Cambridge series run in February and March, May and June, and October and November; Edexcel runs January and May and June.

The Diploma Programme is a single two-year award rather than a set of separate subjects. A student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, which carries 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level at 150 hours, each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together add up to 3 points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, and Creativity, Activity, Service must be completed.

The divergence that matters is arithmetic. At IGCSE each subject stands alone, so a weak subject costs one grade. In the DP the points combine, so a weak Higher Level subject drags the total and the core can rescue or sink it. That is why tutoring priorities differ between two children in the same house.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject: what changes between IGCSE and the DP?
contentBlocks.body:
Less than students fear in content, and much more than they expect in what is being marked. The step is not a step up in difficulty so much as a change in what counts as a good answer, and it catches capable Grade 10 students in their first DP1 term.

Mathematics is the cleanest case. A student leaving Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier has the algebra for either Diploma route, and one who has also done Additional Mathematics arrives with a real head start. What changes is the framing: Analysis and Approaches leans on algebraic reasoning and proof, while Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling and statistics with technology in constant use, and neither rewards the reliable, method-following work that carried a student through Grade 10. A tutor who has taught 0580 and AI can usually hold both children in one household. A tutor who has only taught 0580 will teach DP mathematics as harder Grade 10, which is the most common failure here.

Physics shows the second change. IGCSE Physics 0625 rewards a correct calculation and a clear definition. IB Physics asks the same student to design, evaluate and write up their own investigation, and the marks sit in the reasoning rather than in the answer. The practical write-up skills built at IGCSE transfer well. The independence does not come automatically, and it is the part worth tutoring early.

English is the sharpest break. First Language English 0500 is a reading paper and then directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio, and a student can prepare by practising forms. IB English requires sustained argument about texts with no answer key at all. Economics adds a third pattern, where the IB internal assessment asks for the student's own selection and analysis of material rather than a structured data response.

Additional Mathematics at IGCSE is a genuine head start for Higher Level
IGCSE rewards the right answer; the DP rewards defensible reasoning
0625 practical write-up skills transfer; the independence has to be taught
0500 can be prepared by form practice; IB English cannot
The IB internal assessment uses material the student selected themselves

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE tutors in India: finding one who covers both
contentBlocks.body:
IB and IGCSE tutors in India who genuinely hold both systems are rarer than single-board tutors everywhere, and the only difference between cities is how much rarer. In Delhi NCR the pool is the deepest in the country, so a household in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri or on Golf Course Road can often find one person for two children. Dwarka, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and Sector 128 Noida pay for the same person in travel time, and evening traffic across the region can stretch a short trip badly, which is why back-to-back sessions matter so much there.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves as two markets. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill hold enough supply that an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai can usually be found for one subject pair, while Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar families often end up with one tutor at home and one online. Powai sits between the two and behaves like whichever side the tutor lives on. In Bengaluru the same pattern runs along the east, from Whitefield and Sarjapur Road through Electronic City, with Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each holding their own pockets.

Hyderabad is the easiest metro for a two-child household, because Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Kokapet and the Financial District sit close together, though Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad are a separate journey. In Chennai the demand runs through Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery and along Old Mahabalipuram Road and Perungudi, and in Pune through Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad. An IB and IGCSE tutor in Chennai or an IB and IGCSE tutor in Pune is usually reachable for one child at home and available online for the other.

Beyond the metros, dual-board supply thins fast and hybrid becomes the normal answer. In Gujarat, Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev, the SG Highway corridor, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot generate real demand against few genuine dual-board teachers. Kolkata and eastern India splits between Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore, which hold some supply, and Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna, which hold very little. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, and across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, and in central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa, most households run one local tutor for routine work and one online specialist for the harder board.
items: Delhi NCR has the deepest dual-board pool and the longest evening journeys
Mumbai splits: Bandra to Worli is one market, Thane and Kharghar another
Hyderabad suits two-child households; Gachibowli to Kondapur is a short hop
Chennai and Pune: usually one child at home, one online, in the same evening
Ahmedabad, Surat, Kolkata, Chandigarh, Kochi, Indore: hybrid is the normal answer

contentBlocks.heading: Two exam calendars in one house: the school year in India
contentBlocks.body:
Write both calendars on one page before you buy a single hour. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March. IB examination sessions run in May and November, schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, and results are released in early July. Cambridge series run in February and March, May and June, and October and November, while Pearson Edexcel runs January and May and June.

The February and March Cambridge series exists specifically for India, and it changes a household's planning more than anything else on this page. It lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Class 11 admissions here and for Diploma Programme or A Level entry in the same academic year. Schools decide which series a student is entered for; a student cannot choose independently. So ask the school, in writing, which series each child is in before you assume the two calendars are months apart. Quite often they are weeks apart.

That produces the pinch point most families meet exactly once and never forget: a Grade 10 child sitting papers in February and March while a DP2 sibling is deep in internal assessment deadlines and mock examinations, with both sets of school deadlines falling earlier than the published board dates. The only workable response is to decide in advance whose deadlines win in that window, and to front-load the other child's work into the previous term.

One necessary note before school names come up. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. A tutor may have taught students from schools you recognise, which tells you about the pace they are used to and nothing else. Confirm entries, series and deadlines with each child's coordinator.
items: 1. Write both children's series and internal deadlines on one page.
2. Ask each school, in writing, which series that child is entered for.
3. Mark the weeks where the two calendars collide, usually February.
4. Decide in advance whose deadlines take priority in that window.
5. Front-load the other child's work into the previous term.
6. Review the page each term, because school dates move.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when two children need different boards
contentBlocks.body:
For a two-child household the format question is really a scheduling question. One home tutor doing back-to-back sessions is the most efficient arrangement that exists, because you pay travel once and the house only has to be quiet for one block of the evening. That is the main practical reason families look for IB and IGCSE tutors in India rather than for two separate people. It only works if that person genuinely knows both boards, which is the condition families waive when they are tired.

Home tuition also solves a problem specific to households with two students: supervision. A parent cannot sit with both children every evening, and a tutor in the house raises the working temperature for the sibling who is not in the session. That effect is real and nobody advertises it. The cost is the usual one. A home tutor can hold only so many evening slots, and in a large city the travel narrows the pool of people who can reach you at seven o'clock at all.

Online widens the pool to the country, which matters more here than on a single-board page, because you are searching for a rarer person. For the DP core in particular, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay support, the specialist is frequently in another city. A session can also run in a gap that a travelling tutor could never fill, such as forty minutes before dinner on a Wednesday.

Hybrid is what most two-board households settle into. One home tutor, twice a week, covering the Grade 9 or Grade 10 child and the routine subjects for both. One online specialist for the Higher Level subject or the core. Review the whole arrangement once a term against marked work from both children, and be willing to drop the half that has stopped producing anything.
items: Back-to-back home sessions pay for travel once and quieten the house once
A tutor in the house lifts the working temperature for the other child too
Online reaches the rarer dual-board or core specialist in another city
Short online slots fill gaps a travelling tutor could never take
Review both children's marked work once a term, then cut what is idle

contentBlocks.heading: When can one tutor genuinely cover both boards?
contentBlocks.body:
When the subject is cumulative and the tutor has taught both syllabuses to completion. Mathematics is the clearest yes: somebody who has taken students through 0580 Extended and through a Diploma mathematics course can hold both children, because the content stacks and they know what each examination wants. Physics and Chemistry are usually yes at the lower Diploma levels. English and the Diploma core are usually no.

The test is not whether they say yes. Everybody says yes. Ask them to describe the difference between what earns marks in a Grade 10 answer and what earns marks in a Diploma answer on the same topic, and listen for whether they talk about criteria and command terms or simply about difficulty. Ask which parts of IGCSE preparation actively mislead a DP1 student, because a tutor who has watched the transition will name two or three immediately.

Then verify the ordinary things. On IB Gram, profiles are verified before they go live, which covers identity and claimed teaching background rather than lesson quality, and no honest platform claims more than that. Ask which series and sessions they have prepared students for. Ask what they will not teach, because a tutor who declines the Extended Essay while taking Mathematics is being straight with you.

And set the integrity line early, since it differs between your two children. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. A teacher may give feedback on one draft, and nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit a submission. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB. A tutor who is casual about that with the older child should not be in the house with the younger one either.
items: Mathematics and lower-level sciences: one tutor can often cover both boards
English, TOK and the Extended Essay: usually a separate specialist
Ask what earns marks differently on the same topic in each board
Ask which IGCSE habits actively mislead a DP1 student
Feedback on one draft only; nobody writes or edits a submission
Verification covers identity and background, not lesson quality

contentBlocks.heading: The household with two boards, and how to plan it in India
contentBlocks.body:
Start from the household rather than from the child who is shouting loudest. Two children on different boards means two calendars, two sets of school expectations, one set of evenings and usually one quiet room. The families who manage this well make three decisions early and then stop renegotiating them every week, and only then do they go looking for IB and IGCSE tutors in India.

Decision one is priority. In any given term, one child's work matters more, and pretending otherwise produces an arrangement where both get half of everything. A DP2 student in the months before May outranks a Grade 9 student almost always. A Grade 10 student in the February and March series outranks a DP1 sibling in the same weeks. Say it out loud, revisit it each term, and tell both children the reasoning, because the sibling who is deprioritised handles it better when it is a stated plan rather than a pattern they notice.

Decision two is the shape of the week. Two evenings with a tutor in the house, back to back, beats four scattered evenings for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching: the house settles once, the parent is free the other nights, and neither child gets used to being interrupted. Protect one evening a week with no tuition for anybody.

Decision three is what each child's tuition is for. The younger child on IGCSE usually needs habit and technique. The older child in the Diploma Programme usually needs feedback on their own work and help with planning. Those are different jobs, and asking one tutor to do both for both children is where households overspend. A student moving in from CBSE, ICSE or a state board needs a fourth thing again: time to adjust to criterion-referenced and command-term marking, coursework that carries real weight, and wider reading in place of memorised derivations.
items: Decide each term which child's calendar takes priority, and say so
Two back-to-back evenings beat four scattered ones for the whole house
Keep one evening each week free of tuition for everybody
Younger child: habit and technique. Older child: feedback and planning
A student switching from CBSE or ICSE needs adjustment time, not more hours

contentBlocks.heading: What can home tuition fix across two boards, and what can it not?
contentBlocks.body:
It can fix technique, pace and the gap between what a student knows and what they write down. It cannot fix a subject choice made two years ago, a tier entry the school has already made, or a student who will not work between sessions. Being honest about that division saves a household a great deal of money and a certain amount of arguing.

Subject choices at IGCSE shape Diploma options later, and this is the part families discover too late. A student who drops a science at Grade 9, or who sits Core tier in mathematics, arrives at the Diploma with fewer realistic Higher Level routes, because the school will look at what has been demonstrated. Tutoring in Grade 9 that protects an option is worth more than tutoring in DP1 that tries to recover one. If your younger child is choosing subjects this year, spend an hour on that decision before spending twenty on tuition.

Progress looks similar on both boards and should be judged the same way. In weeks two to four, expect process changes: papers attempted under time, notes organised by paper or by criterion, drafts started earlier. By week six, expect a marked piece where the school's comment and the tutor's prediction agree. If the folder looks unchanged after six weeks, the match or the diagnosis is wrong and more hours will not repair either.

The limits are worth stating plainly to both children. No tutor can guarantee a grade. A Core entry caps what is available at IGCSE. In the Diploma the points combine, so recovering a Higher Level subject late in DP2 is harder than protecting it in DP1. And a household that is already stretched sometimes needs fewer commitments rather than another one.
items: Home tuition fixes technique and pace, not a subject choice made in Grade 9
IGCSE choices and tiers narrow which Higher Level routes stay open
An hour spent on subject choice beats twenty spent recovering one
Weeks two to four: papers under time, notes organised, drafts started earlier
No tutor can guarantee a grade, on either board
Sometimes the right answer is fewer commitments, not another tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started in India: one enquiry, two children, one home slot
contentBlocks.body:
Send one enquiry covering both children rather than two separate ones, because the scheduling constraint is shared and a shortlist built without it will fall apart in week two. Include for each child the board, the programme or syllabus with its code, the level or tier, the exam series, and one sentence on what the school has actually said. Most enquiries about IB and IGCSE tutors in India arrive with only half of that, and the shortlist suffers for it.

Add the household facts next: your locality, the two evenings that genuinely work, whether back-to-back sessions at home are possible, and whether you would accept one child online if that buys a better tutor for the other. Families who state that last point up front get a much better shortlist, because it doubles the number of workable combinations.

When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule for each child, then shortlists verified tutors who match, subject to availability. Ask for a demo for each child. Run them in the same week so you are comparing like with like rather than comparing a fresh impression against a fading one.

The first home session should be diagnosis for both children, not teaching. Expect the tutor to ask for marked work, to watch each student attempt something, and to finish with a plan naming what each child will do before the next session. If one child's fit is wrong, ask for a different match for that child alone. Splitting the arrangement is normal, and it is much easier in week two than in February.
items: Send one enquiry for both children, with each child described separately
State whether back-to-back home sessions are possible at your address
Say whether one child could go online if it buys a better match
Run both demos in the same week and compare them once
Ask for a different match for one child alone if that is what is needed

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach both IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: In cumulative subjects, often yes, and in others rarely. Mathematics is the strongest case: somebody who has taken students through 0580 Extended and through a Diploma mathematics course understands how the two connect. Physics and Chemistry work at the lower Diploma levels. English, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay usually need a separate person, because what earns marks is entirely different. Test the claim by asking how a good answer differs between the two boards on the same topic.

faqs.question: How hard is the jump from Grade 10 into DP1?
faqs.answer: The content jump is smaller than families fear and the assessment jump is larger. A capable IGCSE student already has the algebra, the write-up skills and the habit of reading a question carefully. What is new is independence: coursework that the student designs and defends, marking against criteria rather than a fixed answer key, and reading beyond the set text. Most students who struggle in the first DP1 term are not short of content; they are still answering as though there is one right answer.

faqs.question: Should we book the same home tutor for both of our children?
faqs.answer: Only if that person genuinely knows both boards; otherwise book two and stagger the evenings. The efficiency of one tutor doing back-to-back home sessions is real, and it is the single best scheduling arrangement for a two-child household. But it is not worth buying at the price of a tutor guessing at one child's syllabus. Test both children separately in the same week and decide on the evidence rather than on the convenience.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject choices affect Diploma options later?
faqs.answer: Mathematics tier and the sciences matter most. A student entered for Core mathematics, or one who drops a science at Grade 9, narrows which Higher Level routes a school will support later, because schools place students on demonstrated evidence. Additional Mathematics is a real advantage for anyone heading towards Higher Level mathematics. If your younger child is choosing subjects now, spend time on that decision with the school before spending money on tuition afterwards.

faqs.question: Our two children have exams weeks apart. How do we schedule tuition?
faqs.answer: Decide before the term which calendar takes priority, and tell both children. Cambridge candidates in the February and March series and a DP2 sibling heading for May will collide, and pretending they will not produces an arrangement where both get half attention. Front-load the lower-priority child's work into the previous term, keep back-to-back home sessions so the house settles once, and protect one evening a week with no tuition for anybody.

faqs.question: Why does the February and March Cambridge series matter so much here?
faqs.answer: Because it exists specifically for India and it changes when results arrive. It lets Grade 10 results come through in time for Class 11 admissions here and for Diploma Programme or A Level entry in the same academic year. Schools decide which series a student is entered for, and a student cannot choose independently. Ask each child's school in writing which series they are in, because families frequently assume a May entry and plan the whole year around the wrong date.

faqs.question: We are moving from CBSE to an international board. What should we expect?
faqs.answer: Expect the marking culture to change more than the content. Students moving in from CBSE, ICSE and state boards meet criterion-referenced or command-term marking instead of a fixed answer key, coursework and internal assessment that carry real weight, wider reading and independent research, and less emphasis on memorised derivations. Give the student a term to adjust before judging their results, and use tutoring for the transition itself rather than for content they already know.

faqs.question: Will Indian universities accept these qualifications?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, with a step families should not skip. Equivalence for Indian university admission is issued by the Association of Indian Universities, and requirements differ by university and by course. So confirm current requirements directly with the institution concerned rather than relying on general advice, including advice from a tutor. Do this in Grade 11 rather than in the final term, because a document requirement discovered late is a genuinely stressful problem to solve quickly.

faqs.question: Is online tuition a fair substitute when no dual-board home tutor is nearby?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for the older child and less often for the younger one. A Diploma student works well with a specialist on a screen, particularly for Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay or a thinly taught Higher Level subject. A Grade 9 student who needs supervision rather than explanation does better with somebody in the room. The common answer for households in Indore, Kochi or Guwahati is one local tutor at home and one online specialist for the harder board.

faqs.question: How much can a tutor help with internal assessment and coursework?
faqs.answer: They can teach the skill and question the reasoning, and that is where the line sits. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. A teacher may give feedback on one draft, and nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit the submission. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB. Any tutor casual about this with your older child should not be teaching your younger one either.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor across two children?
faqs.answer: Two or three in total, not two or three each. Every tutored hour removes time from independent work, and in a household with two students it also removes attention from the parent who is coordinating everything. Treat the most consequential subject for each child and reassess after six weeks with the marked evidence in front of you. Families who book five or six subjects in a single term usually cancel half of them and lose the term to logistics.

faqs.question: When should we start, and how soon will we see something?
faqs.answer: Start in Grade 9 for a subject that is already hard, and at the start of DP1 for the transition itself, rather than waiting for a bad report. Expect process changes in two to four weeks and marked evidence by about week six, on either board. If nothing in the folder has changed by then for one of the children, change that arrangement and leave the other alone. Changing both at once means you learn nothing about either.
