h1: IB and IGCSE Home Tutors in India for Two Children at Once
heroTitle: One Home Visit, Two Boards, Across India
heroSubtitle: Your daughter is in Grade 10 on Cambridge IGCSE. Your son has just started DP1. This page is about the arrangement most such households want: one tutor, one trip up to your flat, two sessions back to back, and an honest account of when that plan quietly stops working.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE home tutors in India are hired most often by households running two boards at once: one child in Grade 9 or 10 on Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, another in the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP). The question is rarely whether such a tutor exists. It is whether one home visit can serve both children in the same evening without either being short-changed. Sometimes it can. A two-hour home tuition slot, split cleanly, holds up when the subjects sit close together and both children are steady. It falls apart when one of them is in trouble. What follows is how to tell those two situations apart before you book, and what the tutor has to be able to do.

contentBlocks.heading: How does one home visit get matched to two children in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a single query describing both children, and it is treated as one scheduling problem rather than two separate hires. The intake questions come first: which board each child follows, which subjects and syllabus codes, which grade or DP year, what the school calendar looks like this term, your locality, and the evenings that are genuinely free.

That last answer decides more than parents expect. A family in Powai with a Grade 10 student and a DP1 student often has three usable weekday evenings once school transport, sport and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments are taken out. So the shortlist is built against those three evenings rather than an ideal timetable. Profiles that are verified and that cover both boards are put forward first. Where no single person fits, you should be told that plainly instead of being sold a compromise, and IB and IGCSE home tutors in India who claim both boards without evidence are the commonest thing to screen out.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. For a two-child booking, insist the trial covers both children on the same evening. That is the only honest test of the arrangement. A tutor who is fluent with your DP1 son and visibly out of depth on IGCSE Physics 0625 will show it inside the first ninety minutes, and you will have learned something no profile could tell you.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. Nothing about a first shortlist is binding. There is no prize for persisting with someone who suits one child and not the other, and the longer you wait the harder the switch becomes for the child who is already behind.
items: 1. Send one query naming both children, their boards, grades and subjects
2. Answer intake questions on school calendar, locality and free weekday evenings
3. Receive verified profiles screened for genuine teaching on both boards
4. Run one trial evening that teaches both children back to back
5. Confirm the slot, or ask for a different match without justifying yourself

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 10 IGCSE and DP1 under the same roof
contentBlocks.body:
The two qualifications in your house are built differently, and a parent who understands that stops comparing the wrong numbers. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. Cambridge exam series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, and again in May and June and in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered into Core and Extended: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*.

The Diploma Programme is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four sit at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to 3 points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions. CAS must also be completed. Exam sessions run in May and November, and schools here almost always enter candidates in May, which suits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July.

Between them sits the Middle Years Programme (MYP), five years across eight subject groups, every subject marked against four criteria scored 0 to 8. If your younger child is in MYP rather than IGCSE, the same household logic applies, but the marking language the tutor must speak changes again.
items: Cambridge IGCSE: two years, Grades 9 and 10, tiered Core or Extended
Cambridge series in February and March, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series in January and in May and June
Diploma Programme: six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, graded 1 to 7
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45
DP candidates in India are overwhelmingly entered for the May session

contentBlocks.heading: Which subjects can one tutor honestly carry across both boards?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics, Physics and English are the three pairings where one person can usually teach both children well. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended shares a great deal of machinery with DP Mathematics Applications and Interpretation (AI) and, more distantly, with Analysis and Approaches (AA). A tutor who is strong on algebraic fluency at 0580 will be useful to a DP1 student who is still dropping method marks in AA problem sets.

Physics is similar but narrower. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 rewards equation recall and rearrangement, while DP Physics from the 2025 assessment structure asks for Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data-based questions and Paper 2 extended response, plus a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade and marked on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation at 6 marks each. A tutor who teaches only numerical drill will get the Grade 10 child through and leave the DP child stranded on explanation questions.

English splits the other way. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 and DP English A both reward close reading, so the skill transfers, but the assessments look nothing like each other and a tutor must be able to move between a mark scheme and a criterion descriptor without blurring the two.

Economics is where the pairing usually breaks. IB Economics is a Diploma subject with four units and a portfolio of three commentaries of up to 800 words each, and there is no IGCSE equivalent sitting neatly underneath it. If your DP child takes Economics and your Grade 10 child takes Business or Accounting, accept that these are separate hires. One tutor covering four subjects across two boards in two hours a week is a fantasy that costs a term to disprove.
items: 0580 Extended into Mathematics AA or AI: the strongest single-tutor pairing
0625 Physics into DP Physics: fine for content, weaker on explanation marks
0500 First Language English into English A: skill transfers, assessments do not
IB Economics has no IGCSE twin, so plan it as a separate subject hire
Ask which syllabus codes and which DP subject guides the tutor has taught

contentBlocks.heading: Where dual-board families sit across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi NCR produces the most of these requests, and the geography inside it matters. A family in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri can usually hold a fixed weekday slot because tutor supply is dense nearby. Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are a different matter: evening traffic on the expressways can stretch a short trip badly, and a tutor who commits to 6.30pm in Dwarka after a session in Noida will be late more weeks than not.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit close enough that an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai can string two households together. Powai is its own pocket. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar usually need a tutor who already lives there, because crossing the city on a weekday evening eats the session.

Bengaluru splits along the same lines. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Bangalore working Whitefield or Sarjapur Road rarely takes a Jayanagar or Kanakapura Road booking in the same week, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Electronic City each behave like separate towns after 5pm.

Hyderabad is kinder. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet sit tightly together, so an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Hyderabad can often serve two families in one evening, while Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad need their own planning. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar form one cluster and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi another. Requests from Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad for IB and IGCSE home tutors in India follow the same rule: name your locality first, and let the shortlist follow from it.

Mumbai: Bandra to Lower Parel chains well, Thane and Kharghar usually need a local tutor
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road behave as a separate city after 5pm
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kokapet sit close enough for back-to-back visits
Pune: Koregaon Park and Kharadi form one cluster, Baner and Hinjewadi another
Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad requests work the same way: locality before subject

contentBlocks.heading: Two exam calendars colliding in one Indian school year
contentBlocks.body:
The hardest part of running two boards at home is not the teaching. It is the calendar. An IGCSE child entered for the February and March Cambridge series is revising hard in December and January, exactly when a DP1 sibling is in the middle of first-year internal assessment work and heading towards a March or April round of school assessments. If the IGCSE child is entered for May and June instead, both children peak together, and the household has one brutal quarter rather than two awkward ones.

International schools in India mostly run an academic year from roughly April to March, with a long summer break and a shorter winter break. Parent-teacher meetings, mock examinations and coursework deadlines are set school by school, so two children at the same school can still have completely different pressure weeks. Families searching from around schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School, Pathways World School or Mahindra International School all describe the same squeeze. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

What this means practically is that a home tutor working with two children must be told both calendars in the first week, and must be allowed to shift the balance between the children as the term moves. Some weeks the Grade 10 child needs ninety minutes and the DP1 child thirty. Six weeks later that reverses.

Ask the school's coordinator for the mock dates and the internal deadline list early. A tutor planning against guesses will plan badly, and by the time it shows in a report, a term has gone.
items: Get both children's mock and coursework dates from the school in writing
A February and March IGCSE entry creates a December crunch for the household
A May entry for both children compresses the pressure into one quarter
Let the tutor rebalance time between the two children as deadlines move
School holidays are the only slack in the year, so protect part of them

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when two children share one evening
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the default for this arrangement for an unglamorous reason: one trip serves two children, and the tutor sees the actual conditions the work happens in. A home tutor notices that the Grade 10 child is writing on a wobbly table with the television audible, and that the DP1 child has commandeered the only quiet room. That observation is worth as much as the teaching some weeks.

Online tutoring wins on supply. If your DP child needs HL Chemistry and your Grade 10 child needs Additional Mathematics 0606, no one within reach of your locality may teach both, and two online specialists will beat one convenient generalist every time. Online also survives monsoon weeks, exam-season travel and a tutor who changes cities.

Hybrid is what most two-child households settle into after a term. The pattern that holds best is a weekly home session where both children are taught back to back, plus a short online session for whichever child is closer to a deadline. The tutor keeps the relationship and the room presence, and the family stops losing a whole week when traffic or illness kills the visit.

The honest trade-off: home lessons cost travel time, which limits how many slots any tutor can hold and makes weekday evenings scarce; online lessons cost presence, which matters most for a younger child and for anything involving handwritten working. Hybrid costs a little of both and is the most administratively fiddly to run. Pick on the basis of which child is more fragile, not on which is cheaper to arrange.
items: Home visits: one trip, two children, and the tutor sees the real study conditions
Online: far wider supply for rare syllabus codes and HL subjects
Hybrid: one home evening plus a short online session before a deadline
Handwritten working and diagrams are the clearest argument for home classes
A household with two study spaces can run two online lessons at once; most cannot

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a dual-board tutor enters your home?
contentBlocks.body:
Check three things: identity, subject evidence on both boards, and references from a household that ran a similar arrangement. Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they go live, which covers identity and claimed qualifications. What a platform cannot see is whether someone who has taught IGCSE Mathematics for years has ever marked against a DP criterion, and that is exactly where IB and IGCSE home tutors in India are most often oversold.

So test it yourself. Ask which syllabus codes the tutor has taught and in which years. Ask what the command term evaluate demands in a DP answer, and how that differs from explain in a Cambridge mark scheme. Ask them to describe, without notes, the structure of the DP internal assessment in your child's subject. A person who knows will answer in specifics and will also tell you what they do not teach.

The home visit brings its own checks. Agree who else is at home during sessions, where the lessons happen, and whether a door stays open. Keep lessons in a shared part of the flat rather than a bedroom. Tell your building or society office that a tutor will be visiting on fixed evenings so gate entry does not become a weekly argument. Note the arrival and finish times for the first month and see whether they hold.

And ask about integrity directly. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft of an internal assessment. It does not allow a tutor or a parent to write, rewrite or edit the student's submission. A tutor who is vague on that point is a risk to your DP child's diploma, whatever they do for your Grade 10 child.
items: Ask for syllabus codes and DP subject guides taught, with years and schools
Test one command term from each board in conversation, not on paper
Agree the room, the open door and who is at home during sessions
Register the tutor's fixed evenings with your society or building gate
Confirm the tutor's position on internal assessment drafts before the first lesson

contentBlocks.heading: What actually changes when a tutor switches boards mid-evening
contentBlocks.body:
An hour of Cambridge IGCSE teaching and an hour of Diploma Programme teaching are not the same hour done twice. They ask different things of the person doing them, and the switch between them is the skill you are really paying for.

IGCSE teaching at Grade 10 is mostly about precision against a mark scheme. There is a right answer, there are method marks, and much of the work is making a capable student stop losing marks they already earned: showing working, writing units, using the command word the question actually used. The tutor's instinct is to correct fast and drill the corrected version until it sticks.

DP teaching pulls in the opposite direction. The student has to justify, evaluate and sustain an argument, and the tutor's job is to keep asking why until the student's own reasoning holds. Correcting fast here is a mistake. A DP student who is handed the answer learns to wait for it, and that habit shows up in a mock script in DP2 when nobody is there to hand it over.

So the tutor who does this well changes register deliberately between the two sessions, usually with a break between them. Watch for it during the trial. If the DP hour sounds like the IGCSE hour with harder content, the tutor has one mode and your older child is being taught as though they were still in Grade 10.

There is one more thing that only shows up in a shared visit. Siblings compete. A child who hears the tutor visibly enjoying the other one's subject will draw conclusions. Ask the tutor how they handle that, and if the answer is that it has never come up, they have not done this before.
items: IGCSE hour: precision, method marks, command words, fast correction
DP hour: justification, evaluation, and deliberately slower questioning
A break between the two sessions is what makes the switch possible
Watch the trial for one register used twice rather than two registers
Sibling comparison is real: ask how the tutor keeps the two hours separate

contentBlocks.heading: When two separate tutors beat one shared visit in India
contentBlocks.body:
Two tutors is the better answer more often than families expect, and it is worth saying plainly before you spend a term proving it. The shared visit works when both children are broadly on track and want sharpening. It stops working the moment one of them is genuinely behind, because a child in difficulty absorbs whatever time is in the room, and the other child silently becomes the one who gets the leftover twenty minutes.

The second case is subject distance. If the pairing is 0580 Mathematics and DP English A, you are not hiring a dual-board tutor, you are hiring two people and hoping one body contains them. The third case is temperament. Some children will not work in front of a sibling, and no amount of scheduling fixes that.

As for progress, be realistic about what you should see and when. In the first two or three weeks a good tutor is mostly diagnosing, and the visible output is a clearer picture of what is wrong rather than better marks. By around six weeks you should see specific changes: working shown in full on a Grade 10 script, a DP paragraph that answers the command term rather than circling it. If nothing has moved by then and the tutor cannot tell you precisely what they are working on, that is your signal.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a promised improvement in points is a claim to walk away from, as is any claim to be first in the country. Availability of IB and IGCSE home tutors in India is always subject to who is actually free in your locality at the hour you need, and that is a real constraint rather than a sales line.
items: One child in real difficulty will absorb the whole shared session
Distant subject pairings mean two hires, whatever the profile says
Some children simply will not work in front of a sibling
Expect diagnosis in weeks one to three, specific change by around week six
Availability depends on level, locality and schedule, and it changes each term

contentBlocks.heading: Booking back-to-back home sessions in India: the first fortnight
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send the query, spend twenty minutes gathering evidence. For the IGCSE child: the most recent marked script or report, the syllabus codes from the school, the tier they are entered for where the subject is tiered, and the exam series the school has entered them into. For the DP child: the subject list with HL and SL marked, the latest report with its 1 to 7 grades, any internal assessment deadlines already issued, and the mock dates if the school has published them.

Then write down the evenings that are genuinely free. Not the evenings that could be freed if everything went well. The real ones.

In the first week, the trial evening happens with both children. In the second week, the tutor should come back with a plan that says what each child is working on, in what order, and how the two hours will be split for the next month. If that plan does not arrive, ask for it before the third session rather than after the first month's fees.

The arrangement is not permanent. Families change the balance at every school holiday, drop one child's sessions when a board series finishes, and add an online hour when a deadline lands. IB and IGCSE home tutors in India work best when the household treats the slot as something reviewed every term, not something signed for a year. And if the match is wrong, say so early. That is a normal request, not a complaint.
items: Collect marked scripts, syllabus codes, HL and SL choices and report grades first
Write down the evenings that are actually free, not the aspirational ones
Week one is the shared trial; week two should produce a written plan
Review the split between the two children at every school holiday
Ask for a different match early rather than waiting out a bad term

faqs.question: Can one home tutor really teach both my IGCSE and DP children in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the subjects are close and both children are broadly on track. The pairing that works most reliably is Mathematics, followed by Physics, because the content sits on a single ladder. Ask for a trial evening that teaches both children back to back before you commit to anything longer, and watch whether the tutor changes register between the two hours. If the Diploma Programme hour sounds like the Grade 10 hour with harder questions, one of your children is being short-changed and you should plan for two tutors instead.

faqs.question: Does a shared session, with both children taught together, ever work?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and it is worth being blunt about it. The boards assess differently, the children are at different stages, and the one who is further behind will take the room. There is one exception: a short shared block on a skill both children need, such as reading a question's command word carefully or setting out working legibly. Even then, keep it to part of the evening and teach the two syllabuses separately. Families who try a fully shared hour usually abandon it within a month.

faqs.question: What if my two children go to different schools in different parts of the city?
faqs.answer: They still share an address in the evening, so the home visit is unaffected. What changes is the calendar. Two schools mean two sets of mock dates, two coursework deadline lists and two holiday patterns, and the tutor needs both in the first week. In Delhi NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region this is common, with one child in a school near Gurugram and another closer to South Delhi. Give the tutor written dates rather than verbal ones, and update them when the school revises.

faqs.question: How does the tutor manage weekday evening traffic in a city like Bengaluru?
faqs.answer: By not crossing the city. A tutor who lives or already teaches in Whitefield or Sarjapur Road will hold a 6.30pm slot there reliably, and the same person attempting Jayanagar afterwards will not. Evening traffic between the eastern and southern parts of Bengaluru can stretch a short trip considerably, so build the shortlist around tutors already working in your cluster. Where no one in your cluster teaches both boards, a hybrid week, one home evening plus one online session, usually beats a tutor who is late every second week.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home while the tutor is teaching?
faqs.answer: Someone responsible should be in the flat, particularly for a younger child, but not in the room watching. Keep sessions in a shared space such as a study or dining area rather than a bedroom, with the door open. Sitting in changes how a student behaves: they stop admitting what they do not understand, which is the single most useful thing that happens in a good session. Check in at the start and the end, ask the tutor for a two-minute summary, and leave the middle alone.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session is missed because of illness or a school event?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens rather than after. The usual arrangement is that a session cancelled with reasonable notice is rescheduled, often as an online session later in the week, and a session cancelled at the door is not. With two children this matters more, because one missed evening costs both of them. Many families keep one weekend morning as the standing catch-up slot during exam terms. Put whatever you agree in a message so there is no argument in a difficult week.

faqs.question: My Grade 10 child is entered for the February and March series. Does that break the shared slot?
faqs.answer: It reshapes it rather than breaking it. From about November, the IGCSE child needs the larger share of each evening because their series arrives first, and the DP1 child can usually absorb a lighter term if their internal assessment deadlines allow. Once the Cambridge series finishes, the balance should swing hard the other way. Tell the tutor about the February and March entry at the intake stage, because a tutor planning for a May series will pace the whole year wrongly.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor genuinely knows both boards rather than claiming to?
faqs.answer: Ask for specifics that cannot be bluffed. Which syllabus codes have they taught, in which years, and for which exam series? What does the Diploma Programme internal assessment in your child's subject consist of, described without notes? What is the difference between how explain is marked in a Cambridge mark scheme and how evaluate is marked against a DP criterion? Verified profiles cover identity and qualifications. Whether someone has actually marked against both systems is the part you test in conversation and in the trial.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring good enough for the Grade 10 child if the DP child gets the home slot?
faqs.answer: It can be, with one caveat. Grade 10 work involves a great deal of handwritten working, diagrams and timed practice on paper, and a tutor who cannot see the page as it is written misses the errors that cost method marks. If the Grade 10 child goes online, insist on a document camera or a phone stand pointed at the page, and on scripts being photographed and sent before each session. Without that, the online hour becomes a discussion rather than a correction.

faqs.question: How much notice do I need to give to start, and will a tutor commit to a full year?
faqs.answer: Matching a single-board request is usually quicker than matching a household that needs both boards in one visit, so allow more time and expect a shorter shortlist. Availability depends on the subjects, the level and the evenings you need, and it varies by locality: Gachibowli and Powai are easier to staff than Greater Noida or Kharghar. As for commitment, treat it as a term at a time. Reviewing the arrangement at each school holiday serves the family better than a year-long agreement.

faqs.question: When should we give up on one tutor and hire two?
faqs.answer: When one child is consistently getting the shorter half of the evening, when the tutor's plan for one of them has stopped being specific, or when the subject pairing was always too distant to hold. Give it around six weeks, which is long enough for diagnosis and for early change to appear. If the marked work shows no difference and the tutor cannot name what they are working on this month, hire separately. Splitting early costs less than a wasted term for the child who was quietly dropped.

Grade 10 work involves a great deal of handwritten working, diagrams and timed practice on paper, and a tutor who cannot see the page as it is written misses the errors that cost method marks. If the Grade 10 child goes online, insist on a document camera or a phone stand pointed at the page, and on scripts being photographed and sent before each session. Without that, the online hour becomes a discussion rather than a correction.

mainEntity.name: How much notice do I need to give to start, and will a tutor commit to a full year?

acceptedAnswer.text: Matching a single-board request is usually quicker than matching a household that needs both boards in one visit, so allow more time and expect a shorter shortlist. Availability depends on the subjects, the level and the evenings you need, and it varies by locality: Gachibowli and Powai are easier to staff than Greater Noida or Kharghar. As for commitment, treat it as a term at a time. Reviewing the arrangement at each school holiday serves the family better than a year-long agreement.

mainEntity.name: When should we give up on one tutor and hire two?

acceptedAnswer.text: When one child is consistently getting the shorter half of the evening, when the tutor's plan for one of them has stopped being specific, or when the subject pairing was always too distant to hold. Give it around six weeks, which is long enough for diagnosis and for early change to appear. If the marked work shows no difference and the tutor cannot name what they are working on this month, hire separately. Splitting early costs less than a wasted term for the child who was quietly dropped.

finalCta: Send one query covering both children: their boards, grades, subjects and syllabus codes, your locality and the evenings that are genuinely free. You can also book a free consultation instead. You will be asked about the school calendar and both exam series, then sent verified profiles that match. A trial evening teaching both children can be arranged before you commit, and if the fit is wrong for either child, ask for a different match.

heroTitle: Grade 10 into DP1: Home Tuition Across India
heroSubtitle: One school year decides more than any other in this system. Grade 10 finishes, results arrive, Diploma subjects get chosen, and a long summer sits in the middle of it. This page follows that year phase by phase and says what a tutor at home should be doing in each.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE home tuition in India is at its most useful across one specific stretch: the last two terms of Grade 10, the results, the subject-selection conversation, and the summer before Diploma Programme year one. A home tutor working through that year is doing four jobs in sequence, not one job repeated. Finishing the Cambridge IGCSE course well. Reading the marked evidence honestly enough to inform Higher Level choices. Holding the summer open so that it builds something. Then landing the first weeks of DP1 without the usual shock. This page sets out each phase, what should change in the weekly sessions, and what tends to go wrong when the summer is treated as a holiday and nothing else.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB and IGCSE home tuition in India get matched to the transition year?
contentBlocks.body:
By asking which phase of the year you are already in. A request sent in September of Grade 10 and a request sent in June after results arrive are two different jobs, and the shortlist should not look the same. So the first questions are about timing: which exam series the school has entered the student for, how many terms remain, and whether Diploma Programme (DP) subjects have been chosen yet.

You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram then asks about the board, the syllabus codes on the school's list, the exam series, your locality and the two or three weekday slots your family can genuinely protect. Those answers matter more than they sound. A Cambridge February/March candidate in Bengaluru is working to a different clock from a May/June candidate in Chennai on the same syllabus, and a tutor who has only ever taught the May/June rhythm will plan the wrong term. Locality decides availability in the same blunt way. A tutor living near Sarjapur Road can hold a seven o'clock weekday slot in HSR Layout most weeks, and will struggle to hold that same slot in Yelahanka once the evening traffic sets in.

Then you read the shortlisted profiles, which are verified before they go live, and meet one or two. A trial session can be arranged before the family commits. In this particular year, the thing worth watching in a trial is whether the tutor mentions next year at all. A tutor who treats the Grade 10 series as the finish line will teach to the finish line and leave the harder work of DP1 to somebody else.

If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match and give one concrete reason rather than a general complaint. Availability at any given hour depends on subject, level and schedule, so a Sunday morning slot in South Delhi may take longer to fill than a Tuesday evening one in Dwarka.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, naming the school's exam series
2. Answer the matching questions: syllabus codes, terms remaining, locality, protected weekday slots
3. Read the verified shortlist and pick one or two tutors to meet
4. Take a trial session and ask what DP1 will demand of this student
5. Agree a phase plan that says what changes the week results arrive

contentBlocks.heading: From Cambridge IGCSE tiers into Diploma Higher Level: the structural jump
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Either way it is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. Cambridge series run in February/March, May/June and October/November, and the February/March series exists specifically for India. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9-1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme is built on an entirely different frame. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours each, the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points, so the maximum is 45, and 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well.

So the jump is not a jump in difficulty alone. It is a change in what the qualification is counting. A tiered Extended paper rewards accuracy inside a fixed ceiling. A DP grade is assembled from external papers plus internally assessed coursework, and the core sits on top of all of it. A student who has spent two years optimising for one shape meets a different shape in July.

Schools decide which series a student is entered for, and a student cannot choose a series independently of the school. The Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and families should check current requirements with the university or board concerned rather than assume. Home tuition through this year should make that structural difference visible early, not in the third week of DP1.
items: Cambridge series: February/March, May/June, October/November; Edexcel: January and May/June
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A* on tiered Cambridge syllabuses
Six DP subjects, three or four at HL with 240 recommended hours each
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points; 45 is the maximum
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions

contentBlocks.heading: 0580 Extended, 0625 and 0500: what DP1 asks of each
contentBlocks.body:
Take Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 first, because it carries the heaviest consequence. A student finishing Extended has met algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and a first pass at calculus. DP Mathematics then splits into two separate subjects, each available at HL and SL. Analysis and Approaches (AA) is algebraic and proof-heavy. Applications and Interpretation (AI) is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often steered towards AA, but the right choice depends on the degree and the student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement.

Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 into DP Physics is a different kind of step. The IGCSE paper rewards a correct number. DP Physics keeps the numbers and adds sustained written explanation, where command terms set the depth an answer needs. A student who has been drilled to produce answers quickly, and who has never had to justify a claim in three sentences, loses marks in DP1 that have nothing to do with the physics.

Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 into English A is the quietest trap. The IGCSE writing tasks are shorter and the reading passages are chosen for accessibility. DP English A asks for analysis of unseen material and comparison across studied works, and the marks come from the quality of the argument rather than from correctness. Strong 0500 candidates sometimes drop hardest here, because nothing about their Grade 10 experience warned them.

This is the concrete work for IB and IGCSE home tuition in India during the final Grade 10 term. Finish the syllabus properly. Then, in the same sessions, start showing the student what their own answer would need in order to survive a DP marker. A tutor holding both syllabuses can do that in the same hour. A tutor holding one cannot.
items: 0580 Extended feeds Mathematics AA or AI; the coordinator makes the final placement
AA is algebraic and proof-heavy; AI is modelling and statistics with technology throughout
0625 into DP Physics adds sustained explanation to the numerical work

contentBlocks.heading: Where the Grade 10 to DP1 handover happens across India
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi NCR spreads the problem out. Families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri usually have a reachable pool of tutors on a weekday evening. Dwarka, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are harder to serve at six o'clock, and Greater Noida is harder still. Gurugram (Gurgaon) sits somewhere in the middle: a tutor already on Golf Course Road can take a second household nearby, while a tutor crossing from Noida or Sector 128 Noida on a Wednesday is at the mercy of one stretch of road. Requests for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Delhi therefore stand or fall on how tightly the slots are drawn.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is a set of separate markets that happen to share a name. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill hold dense supply. Powai is well served but awkward to reach from the western suburbs on a weekday. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar and Thane are their own pools, and a family searching for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai from Kharghar should expect a local tutor or an online one rather than somebody travelling from Bandra.

Bengaluru divides along the same lines. Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar are workable in the evening. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road each need a tutor who already lives in that belt. Chennai is gentler: Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are close together, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar want somebody local.

In Gujarat, Ahmedabad concentrates supply around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar reachable. Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot thin out quickly, and IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ahmedabad is easier to arrange than the same request from Rajkot. The pattern repeats for Hyderabad around Gachibowli, for Pune around Koregaon Park, and for Kolkata around Salt Lake.

Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar and Thane are their own pools, not extensions of Bandra

contentBlocks.heading: The transition-year calendar Indian families are actually working to
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and international schools here bend that year around two separate examination calendars. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this site, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. What follows is the general shape families deal with, not any one school's timetable.

A Grade 10 cohort entered for the Cambridge February/March series sits papers while the rest of the school is still in ordinary term. That series exists so that results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for DP or A Level entry in the same academic year. Which means the pressure lands earlier than parents expect, and the tutoring plan for December and January has to be built backwards from February rather than from May.

Then comes the gap. Papers finish, school effectively ends for that cohort, and a long stretch opens before DP1 teaching begins. Some schools run a bridging programme; many do not, and the ones that do rarely run it for every subject. Results arrive, subject placements are confirmed or argued over, and the DP1 timetable starts.

From there the clock belongs to the IB. DP exam sessions run in May and November, schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, and May results are released in early July. So a student starting DP1 in the middle of the calendar year has two years to the session that matters. The first of those years is the one where good habits are cheap to build and expensive to skip. Home tuition across the transition should be planned against that whole span, not against the next unit test, and the plan should be written down where the family can see it.
items: The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March at most international schools
February/March is a Cambridge series offered only in India, for Class 11 admissions
Schools decide the series; a student cannot choose one independently of the school
DP sessions run in May and November; Indian schools overwhelmingly enter May
May results are released in early July, two years after DP1 begins

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid through the results summer in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition wins during the Grade 10 term and loses some of its edge during the summer. That is the short answer, and it is worth understanding why before you fix a pattern for the whole year.

In the final Grade 10 months the work is handwritten, timed and full of small silent errors. A home tutor sitting beside the student sees a method mark thrown away, a diagram drawn too small to label, a unit dropped on line three. None of that is reliably visible over a video call, because the student either holds the page up after the fact or photographs it later. Home classes also survive the ordinary chaos of an Indian evening better than people expect: the tutor arrives, the phone goes on the table, and ninety minutes actually happen.

The summer inverts several of those advantages. Families travel. Grandparents in another city get a visit. The student who was in Powai in April is in Coimbatore in June. An online tutor keeps the thread through all of that, and the bridging work between IGCSE and DP1 is mostly reading, planning and discussion rather than timed paper practice, which online handles well. This is also the point where a family in a smaller city can reach a subject specialist they will never find locally.

Hybrid is the honest answer for most households buying IB and IGCSE home tuition in India across this particular year. Home sessions while school is running and papers are being written. Online through the summer and through any travel. Then home again from the first weeks of DP1, when the student is tired and a person in the room is worth more than a better tutor on a screen. Agree the switch dates in advance, in writing, so nobody has to renegotiate them in the middle of June.
items: Home sessions catch handwritten method marks that a camera never shows
Online keeps the plan alive through summer travel and a change of city
Hybrid weeks suit the transition: home in term, online across the break
A family outside the metros reaches a dual-syllabus specialist only online
Fix the switch dates in writing before the Grade 10 papers finish

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor who claims to teach both Cambridge IGCSE and the DP?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with what the platform does, then do the part only you can do. Anybody offering IB and IGCSE home tuition in India is making two claims at once, and the second one is rarely tested. Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they go live, which covers identity and the qualifications and teaching experience a tutor puts forward. That is a floor. It is not a judgement about whether this particular person can carry a student from 0580 Extended into Mathematics AA HL, because almost nobody can verify that from documents alone.

So test the dual claim directly, and test it with specifics rather than with a general question. Ask which syllabus codes they have taught in the last two years and in which series. Ask what changes in their teaching between a Cambridge Extended candidate in January and the same student in August as a DP1 student. A tutor who genuinely works across both will answer in concrete terms: different marking language, different length of written answer, coursework appearing where none existed before. A tutor who does not will answer with adjectives.

The second test is about honesty on placement. Ask what they would do if the student's marked papers pointed away from the HL combination the family has already decided on. The right answer involves showing you the evidence and sending you to the DP coordinator, not agreeing with you.

Then the checks that belong to the household. Meet the tutor before the first home session, not after. Keep the first few home classes in a room where somebody else walks past. Ask for the written term plan and read it. Notice whether work set in one session is actually looked at in the next, because that single habit separates a tutor with a plan from a tutor with an hour to fill. If something feels off, say so early and ask for a different match.
items: Ask which syllabus codes were taught in the last two years, and in which series
Ask what changes in their teaching between January Extended and August DP1
Ask what they would do if marked evidence contradicted the family's HL plan
Meet before the first home session and keep early sessions in a shared room
Check that work set last week is actually reviewed this week

contentBlocks.heading: The long summer between Grade 10 and DP1, used properly
contentBlocks.body:
This is the part of the year almost nobody plans, and it is the part that decides how DP1 feels in September. Papers are finished. Results may not have arrived. School has stopped. And somewhere between six and ten weeks of unstructured time sits in front of a sixteen-year-old who has just come off an examination series and is entitled to be tired.

The wasted version is familiar. Nothing happens for the first three weeks, which is reasonable. Nothing happens for the next five either. Results arrive, subjects get confirmed in a hurry, and the student walks into DP1 having read nothing, written nothing and forgotten the algebra they were fluent in during February. The first internal assessment conversation lands in October and the student is still catching up on content.

The useful version is smaller than parents imagine, and it is the version IB and IGCSE home tuition in India should be sold as. Two sessions a week, not five. One mathematics strand kept warm, because algebraic fluency decays faster than anything else and Mathematics AA punishes that decay immediately. One long reading habit for English A, which costs nothing and pays for two years. One conversation about what an internal assessment actually is, so the word is not new in October. And genuine rest, protected on purpose rather than by accident.

The third piece is the subject decision itself, and it should be made on evidence rather than on ambition. Marked Grade 10 papers are the best evidence a family will ever have, and they are usually read once and filed. A tutor who reads them properly can tell you where the student was fluent, where they were merely accurate, and where they were guessing. That is the input for HL choices. It is not the final word, because the school's coordinator makes the placement, but it changes the conversation from a preference into an argument with evidence behind it.
items: Two sessions a week through the break is enough; five is a way to burn out
Keep one mathematics strand warm, because algebraic fluency decays fastest
Build a reading habit for English A before DP1 rather than during it
Read the marked Grade 10 papers properly before confirming HL choices
Protect rest deliberately; an exhausted DP1 student loses the whole first term

contentBlocks.heading: What honest progress looks like through this year in India
contentBlocks.body:
Progress from IB and IGCSE home tuition in India does not look like a rising score in this year, because for several months there is no score to rise. So judge it differently in each phase, and be suspicious of anybody who offers you a single number.

During the final Grade 10 term, the signal is error type. In four to six weeks of home tuition you should see the same mistakes stop repeating. Working shown where it was previously skipped. Units written. Diagrams labelled. A student who can say why a mark was lost rather than only that it was lost. If a tutor has been coming for two months and cannot show you a list of the errors they are tracking, that is worth asking about.

Across the summer the signal is different again. It is whether the student picks the work up without being chased. That sounds soft. It is the single best predictor of how DP1 goes, because the Diploma runs on self-directed work and no tutor can supply that from outside.

In the first DP1 term the honest signal is comprehension speed. Is the student following the lesson in real time, or reconstructing it afterwards at home? A tutor should be able to tell you which, and should tell you plainly if the HL combination is proving too heavy while there is still time to raise it with the coordinator.

The limits, stated plainly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, in either system. Starting in January of Grade 10 narrows what is achievable in that series, though it does nothing to the DP1 preparation, which is the larger prize. And some students in this year need fewer commitments rather than more hours. If a household is running three tuition subjects through a summer that was meant to be recovery, the plan is wrong.
items: In term: repeated errors stop repeating, and the student can say why
Across the summer: work is picked up without being chased
In DP1: the student follows lessons live instead of rebuilding them at home
Ask to see the error list your tutor is tracking after six weeks
No tutor can guarantee a grade; a late start narrows the Grade 10 series only

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in India before DP1 begins
contentBlocks.body:
Getting this right takes one honest hour of preparation from the family, and most of it is gathering paper.

Bring the student's last two marked scripts in each subject you are worried about, including the ones that went badly, because those carry the most information. Bring the school's subject list with syllabus codes on it, and the exam series the school has entered the student for. Bring the shortlist of DP subjects if one exists, with the HL choices marked as provisional. Then write down, honestly, the two or three weekday evenings your household can protect. Not the ones you would like to protect. The ones that will still be free in November when a school event lands on a Thursday.

The first session should not be teaching. It should be a diagnosis: the tutor reading those scripts with the student present, asking them to explain two or three answers, and separating a content gap from an exam-technique gap from a timing problem. Those three need entirely different work, and treating one as another wastes a term. Expect to come out of that first hour with a short written plan covering the rest of Grade 10 and a sentence about what changes after results.

After that the rhythm is simple. Weekly home classes while school is running. A review conversation every few weeks with you in the room for ten minutes. A deliberate reset when results arrive. And a second diagnosis in the first month of DP1, because the student who walks into the Diploma is not quite the student who walked out of Grade 10, and the plan should be rewritten rather than extended.
items: Bring the last two marked scripts per subject, especially the weak ones
Bring the syllabus codes and the exam series the school has entered
Name two or three weekday evenings that will still be free in November
Expect the first session to diagnose rather than teach
Rewrite the plan in the first month of DP1 instead of extending the old one

faqs.question: When should IB and IGCSE home tuition in India start if my child is entering DP1 next year?
faqs.answer: Ideally in the term before the Grade 10 series, because that is when the marked evidence you need for subject selection is being produced. Starting then gives a tutor two jobs at once: finishing the IGCSE course properly, and reading the student's scripts closely enough to say something useful about Higher Level choices. Starting after results is still worthwhile, but you lose the diagnostic value of watching the student work under pressure, and you compress the bridging work into a shorter summer.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor really teach both the IGCSE course and DP1 content?
faqs.answer: Some can, in a narrow band of subjects, and many cannot. Mathematics is the most common genuine overlap, because 0580 Extended content sits directly underneath early Mathematics AA and AI work. Sciences are plausible. English is harder, since English A demands a different kind of writing altogether. Ask for the syllabus codes and DP levels taught in the last two years rather than accepting a general claim, and be willing to use two tutors if the honest answer is that one person cannot cover both well.

faqs.question: My child's results were good. Do they still need help before DP1?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for a reason that surprises parents. Strong IGCSE performance is built on accuracy inside a bounded syllabus, and the Diploma rewards something else: sustained written explanation, independent research and coursework produced to criteria. A student who coasted on speed and recall can find DP1 genuinely hard while a slower, more analytical classmate settles quickly. The useful work here is not remedial. It is a short bridging programme so the first internal assessment is not the first encounter with the demand.

faqs.question: How many home sessions a week make sense during the summer break?
faqs.answer: Two is the usual sensible ceiling, and one is often enough. The summer between Grade 10 and DP1 has to do two contradictory things: recover a tired student and build a bridge. Five sessions a week does the second and destroys the first. Two sessions, one for mathematics fluency and one for reading and writing, leave the rest of the break genuinely free. If a family is running three or four tuition subjects through the break, the plan usually needs cutting rather than adding.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Kharghar or Greater Noida on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends almost entirely on where the tutor already lives. Supply in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and Delhi NCR is not evenly spread. Tutors cluster near the areas with the most international schools, so Bandra, Powai, South Delhi and Gurugram are easier to serve than Kharghar, Faridabad or Greater Noida at six in the evening. The practical answer for outlying areas is usually a local tutor at home for the term, with an online specialist for a subject nobody nearby teaches.

faqs.question: How do we choose between Mathematics AA and AI?
faqs.answer: Start from the degree, then check the evidence, then hand it to the coordinator. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. Students aiming at engineering or economics are often steered towards AA, but the right choice depends on the specific degree and the specific student. A tutor who has read the marked 0580 papers can tell you where the student was fluent rather than merely correct. The school's DP coordinator makes the final placement.

faqs.question: What does the February/March series change for our planning?
faqs.answer: It moves everything earlier. The February/March Cambridge series exists specifically for India, and it lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for Diploma or A Level entry in the same academic year. A tuition plan for a February/March candidate has to be built backwards from February, which means past-paper work starts in November rather than March. It also means the gap before DP1 is longer, which is an advantage if it is used and a liability if it is not.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on home classes during this year?
faqs.answer: For the first session or two, yes, and after that only for the review conversation. A sixteen-year-old about to start the Diploma needs to practise asking a question without a parent answering for them. Stay in the house, keep the door open, walk past occasionally. Then take ten minutes every few weeks to hear what is actually being worked on. Constant presence during the lesson tends to make students quieter, and a quiet student in a one-to-one session is not getting value from it.

faqs.question: What happens if we lose a month to travel or illness?
faqs.answer: Say so early and rebuild the plan rather than trying to catch up by doubling sessions. A missed month in the final Grade 10 term is serious and usually means narrowing the work to the topics with the most marks attached. A missed month in the summer is much less serious, and in most cases the honest advice is to let it go and restart in the first weeks of DP1. Availability of your original tutor after a long gap depends on level and schedule, so tell them as soon as you know.

faqs.question: Is online tuition enough for the bridging work between the two courses?
faqs.answer: For most of it, yes, and that is unusual to say on a home tuition page. Bridging work is reading, discussion, planning and concept-building rather than timed handwritten practice, and all of that transfers to a screen without much loss. Online also solves the summer travel problem and reaches specialists in other cities. Where online is weaker is exactly where Grade 10 revision lives: watching a student's working appear on paper in real time. So most families end up hybrid across this year.

faqs.question: How do we know the tutor is not just doing the coursework for our child?
faqs.answer: Ask to see what the student produced between sessions, in their own handwriting or their own document history. Every internal assessment in the Diploma is the student's own work, and the school submits it and runs similarity checking. A tutor may teach a skill, question reasoning and point at a criterion. mainEntity.name: When should IB and IGCSE home tuition in India start if my child is entering DP1 next year?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ideally in the term before the Grade 10 series, because that is when the marked evidence you need for subject selection is being produced. Starting then gives a tutor two jobs at once: finishing the IGCSE course properly, and reading the student's scripts closely enough to say something useful about Higher Level choices. Starting after results is still worthwhile, but you lose the diagnostic value of watching the student work under pressure, and you compress the bridging work into a shorter summer.

mainEntity.name: Can one home tutor really teach both the IGCSE course and DP1 content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some can, in a narrow band of subjects, and many cannot. Mathematics is the most common genuine overlap, because 0580 Extended content sits directly underneath early Mathematics AA and AI work. Sciences are plausible. English is harder, since English A demands a different kind of writing altogether. Ask for the syllabus codes and DP levels taught in the last two years rather than accepting a general claim, and be willing to use two tutors if the honest answer is that one person cannot cover both well.

mainEntity.name: My child's results were good. Do they still need help before DP1?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, and for a reason that surprises parents. Strong IGCSE performance is built on accuracy inside a bounded syllabus, and the Diploma rewards something else: sustained written explanation, independent research and coursework produced to criteria. A student who coasted on speed and recall can find DP1 genuinely hard while a slower, more analytical classmate settles quickly. The useful work here is not remedial. It is a short bridging programme so the first internal assessment is not the first encounter with the demand.

mainEntity.name: How many home sessions a week make sense during the summer break?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two is the usual sensible ceiling, and one is often enough. The summer between Grade 10 and DP1 has to do two contradictory things: recover a tired student and build a bridge. Five sessions a week does the second and destroys the first. Two sessions, one for mathematics fluency and one for reading and writing, leave the rest of the break genuinely free. If a family is running three or four tuition subjects through the break, the plan usually needs cutting rather than adding.

mainEntity.name: Will a tutor travel to Kharghar or Greater Noida on a weekday evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, and it depends almost entirely on where the tutor already lives. Supply in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and Delhi NCR is not evenly spread. Tutors cluster near the areas with the most international schools, so Bandra, Powai, South Delhi and Gurugram are easier to serve than Kharghar, Faridabad or Greater Noida at six in the evening. The practical answer for outlying areas is usually a local tutor at home for the term, with an online specialist for a subject nobody nearby teaches.

mainEntity.name: How do we choose between Mathematics AA and AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start from the degree, then check the evidence, then hand it to the coordinator. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. Students aiming at engineering or economics are often steered towards AA, but the right choice depends on the specific degree and the specific student. A tutor who has read the marked 0580 papers can tell you where the student was fluent rather than merely correct. The school's DP coordinator makes the final placement.

mainEntity.name: What does the February/March series change for our planning?

acceptedAnswer.text: It moves everything earlier. The February/March Cambridge series exists specifically for India, and it lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for Diploma or A Level entry in the same academic year. A tuition plan for a February/March candidate has to be built backwards from February, which means past-paper work starts in November rather than March. It also means the gap before DP1 is longer, which is an advantage if it is used and a liability if it is not.
