h1: IB and IGCSE Private Tutors Who Know Both Mark Schemes
heroTitle: Both Mark Schemes, One Private Tutor in India
heroSubtitle: A Cambridge mark scheme and an IB criterion descriptor reward different things on the page. A tutor who has only ever taught one of them will quietly coach your child into the wrong habits. This page is about finding the tutor in India who genuinely holds both, and about testing that claim before you commit.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE private tutors in India are the small number of home tutors who can read a Cambridge mark scheme and an International Baccalaureate (IB) criterion descriptor in the same hour, then tell a student which of the two they are currently writing for. Most tutors cannot. Someone trained on International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) papers drills command words and method marks. Someone trained in the Diploma Programme (DP) teaches command terms and criterion strands. Put the first in front of a DP1 student and you get tidy answers that stall at four out of seven. Put the second in front of a Grade 10 candidate and you get discussion where the mark scheme wanted a stated equation. This page explains the gap and how home tuition closes it.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist a dual-board private tutor in India?
contentBlocks.body:
By asking you which board each child is on, which syllabus codes and which levels, and then only shortlisting tutors whose verified profiles show both systems rather than one system and a claim about the other. A parent sends a query or books a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs, and arranges a demo or trial session before the family commits.

The dual-board question makes that intake longer than usual. A family in Powai with a Grade 10 daughter on Cambridge IGCSE and a DP1 son needs different answers than a family with one student who finished IGCSE in May and starts the Diploma Programme in the same building in July. The first family may be better served by two specialists on back-to-back slots. The second is exactly the case where one tutor who holds both is worth waiting for.

So the shortlist is deliberately short. IB and IGCSE private tutors in India are a narrow pool by definition. Tutors who have taught 0580 Extended and IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in the same academic year are not common in any one locality, and pretending otherwise would waste your evenings on trials that go nowhere. Where the local pool has nobody credible, the honest answer is an online specialist, or a hybrid week, and the consultation will say so rather than sending you a weaker nearby name.

Lessons then run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability. If the fit is wrong after the trial, you can ask for a different match. Nothing beyond that is promised, because nothing beyond that is in anyone's control.
items: 1. Send the board, grade, syllabus code and level for every child in the house
2. IB Gram asks what the last marked script or criterion sheet actually said
3. Verified profiles showing both systems are shortlisted, not profiles claiming both
4. A trial session is arranged, with a marked piece of the student's own work
5. You confirm, change the match, or are told the honest answer is two tutors

contentBlocks.heading: Core and Extended against HL and SL: two decisions India gets muddled
contentBlocks.body:
Parents hear tiering and level as the same word, and they are not. Cambridge tiering is a decision about which paper a student sits. Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects run Core and Extended tiers, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. Choosing Core is choosing a ceiling in exchange for a paper the student can finish. It is an assessment decision, usually taken with the subject teacher, usually reversible up to a point in Grade 10.

Higher Level and Standard Level in the Diploma Programme are a different animal. Three or four of the six subjects are taken at Higher Level, with 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level with 150 hours. There is no ceiling on the Standard Level grade: both levels are graded 1-7. What changes is content, depth and the shape of the papers. A Standard Level 7 and a Higher Level 5 are not the same thing to a university, but neither is a capped grade.

The muddle costs real points. A family that treats Extended as the equivalent of Higher Level will push a child onto three Higher Level subjects because they coped with Extended papers, and a private tutor is then asked to rescue a choice that was wrong in February. A family that treats Core as a safe option because Standard Level felt safe has closed doors before Grade 10 ends.

A tutor who holds both systems will lay the two decisions side by side, with the student's own marked work in front of them, and say which one is actually on the table this term.
items: Cambridge Core caps at grade C; Extended reaches A* on the same subject
Diploma Programme HL runs 240 recommended hours, SL 150, both graded 1-7
Tiering decides which paper is sat; level decides how much content is taught
Extended competence does not automatically predict a comfortable Higher Level
Standard Level has no grade ceiling, which Core does, and families confuse this

contentBlocks.heading: What is the real difference between a command word and a command term?
contentBlocks.body:
A command word belongs to a Cambridge question and points at a mark scheme with numbered marking points. A command term belongs to an IB question and points at a criterion descriptor written in levels. Both tell the student how deep to go. Only one of them is scored by ticking discrete points, and that single difference changes how an answer should be built.

Take Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625. An explanation question with four marks has four things the examiner is looking for, and a student who writes three of them in beautiful prose scores three. Method marks in Mathematics 0580 work the same way: shown working earns marks even where the final figure is wrong. Sciences examined from 2023 run Paper 1 or Paper 2 multiple choice, Paper 3 or Paper 4 theory, and practical assessment through Paper 5 or Paper 6, with multiple choice at 30 per cent, theory at 50 and practical at 20. That weighting rewards precision and coverage.

Now take DP sciences, first assessed 2025. Paper 1 splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions; Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response work. The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent and is marked on four criteria of six marks each, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, with a maximum of 3,000 words. Nobody ticks four points in an Evaluation criterion. The examiner decides which level the whole piece sits in.

So the habit that earns marks at IGCSE, write every listed point and stop, produces a flat DP answer that never reaches the top band. The reverse habit loses easy marks in Grade 10.
items: 0580 rewards shown working; a wrong answer with correct method still scores
0625 explanation questions have countable marking points, not a quality band
0500 First Language English trains the writing that DP English A then reshapes
DP scientific investigation: four criteria of six marks, 3,000 words maximum
DP Paper 1B data questions look like nothing on a Cambridge theory paper

contentBlocks.heading: Where do dual-board private tutors actually live in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Close to the schools that run both curricula, which means a handful of pockets in each metro and very thin supply outside them. IB and IGCSE private tutors in India sit where that overlap sits, and nowhere else. This matters more for a two-board request than for anything else, because you are looking for an intersection of two small pools rather than a sample from one large one.

In Delhi NCR, families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri usually have the shortest travel for a home visit, while Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad face a weekday evening crossing that can stretch a short trip badly. A parent searching for an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Delhi should decide early whether the tutor travels or the student does. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the split runs between Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill on one side and Powai, Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar on the other; an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who lives in the suburbs rarely holds a 6 pm island-city slot in monsoon.

Bengaluru, often still written as Bangalore, concentrates supply around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, with Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road thinner. Hyderabad clusters in Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur and Kondapur, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Secunderabad and Kokapet within reach.

Beyond Delhi NCR, northern India is a different problem. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula have some depth. Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur often have none for this combination, and an honest search there widens to online within a week.
items: Delhi NCR: shortest home visits in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri
Mumbai: suburbs to island city on a weekday evening rarely works twice a week
Bengaluru and Hyderabad: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Gachibowli and Kondapur dominate
Chennai and Pune families usually find one board locally and the other online
Chandigarh, Jaipur and Lucknow: a dual-board search widens to online quickly

contentBlocks.heading: One school year in India, two exam calendars to survive
contentBlocks.body:
A household running both boards is running two clocks. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; what follows is the general pattern families at international schools here describe, not a statement about any particular school.

Cambridge exam series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May or June series. The IB Diploma Programme has May and November sessions, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July.

Put those together and one house can have a Grade 10 student sitting a February or March Cambridge series while a DP2 sibling is in the last stretch before May. Mocks for both land earlier still, at dates each school sets for itself. The February or March entry is the one families underestimate, because it pulls the whole Grade 10 revision block forward by a full term while the Diploma Programme student is still working through internal assessment deadlines.

There is also the transition year. A student finishes IGCSE, waits for results, picks six Diploma Programme subjects from six groups, and starts DP1 in a new assessment culture in the same month. The summer between is the single most useful window a dual-board tutor gets, and most families do not think to use it until September, when the first criterion-marked task comes back lower than anyone expected.
items: Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May or June
IB May session dominates in India; results are released in early July
School mock dates are set by each school and land months before the series
The IGCSE-to-DP1 summer is the most useful and least used window in the year

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when a student sits between two mark schemes?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition wins where handwriting, working and diagrams carry marks, online wins where the tutor's dual-board depth is rarer than convenience, and a hybrid week is what most two-board households actually settle on. That is the short answer. The reasoning is worth a paragraph each.

A home tutor sits beside the script. In Cambridge Mathematics 0580, method marks are lost silently: the student knows the method, does it in their head, writes the answer, and the examiner has nothing to reward. You see that on paper across a desk in ten minutes. You often miss it on a shared screen for a month. The same is true of a rushed 0625 circuit diagram or a Grade 10 student who cannot finish a paper in the time allowed because they draft in their head. Home classes catch physical habits.

Online wins the supply argument. The tutor who has marked both Cambridge theory papers and DP extended-response answers may live in another city, and insisting on proximity means accepting someone who really only knows one of your two systems. For Diploma Programme discussion work, essay planning and internal assessment conversations inside academic integrity rules, a screen costs you very little.

Hybrid is the honest compromise. One home session a week for written work, one online session for the reading-and-reasoning side, and an extra online slot in the fortnight before mocks. It also survives monsoon, traffic and a tutor who moves house, which a pure home arrangement in Mumbai or Bengaluru often does not.
items: Home tuition catches silent method-mark losses that a screen hides for weeks
Online reaches the dual-board specialist your locality does not contain
Hybrid: paper-based work at home, reasoning and planning work online
Monsoon and evening traffic break pure home schedules in Mumbai and Bengaluru
A young MYP or Grade 9 student usually needs the home session more than a DP2 student

contentBlocks.heading: How do you test whether a tutor really knows both systems?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for two things in the same trial: a Cambridge mark scheme read aloud against the student's own answer, and an IB criterion descriptor applied to a second piece. A tutor who knows both will handle the switch without changing vocabulary mid-sentence. A tutor who knows one will describe the other in generalities and move the conversation back to content.

Verification is where IB and IGCSE private tutors in India are separated from tutors who have read about the second board. IB Gram checks identity and qualifications, and confirms which boards, syllabuses and levels a tutor has actually taught before a profile is verified and shown to a family. That is a documentary check. It cannot tell you whether this particular tutor will teach your particular child well, so the trial is not a formality and should not be treated as one.

Bring evidence to it. A marked Grade 10 script with the examiner's annotations, or a returned Diploma Programme task with the criterion levels circled, gives the tutor something real to work on and gives you something to judge. If they talk about the paper without looking at the marks, that tells you a great deal in five minutes.

The questions that separate a genuine dual-board private tutor from a confident generalist are specific rather than clever. Which tier is this student entered for, and who decides. Which command term is doing the work in this Diploma Programme question. What does the mark scheme give for this line of working. Where would this answer sit in the criterion, and what single change moves it a band. You are listening for whether the answers come from the documents or from memory of teaching something adjacent.
items: Ask them to mark one Cambridge answer and one IB criterion task in the same trial
Listen for tier and level being kept apart, not used as synonyms
Bring a marked script; a tutor who ignores the annotations is guessing
Ask which syllabus codes and which DP subjects they have taught, not studied
Check identity and qualifications yourself; verification is a floor, not a verdict

contentBlocks.heading: Diagnosing a student caught between two marking cultures
contentBlocks.body:
Most students who need a dual-board tutor are not weak. They are fluent in one grammar of answering and are being marked in another. The diagnosis is about finding which habits transferred, which ones are now costing marks, and which ones were never there at all.

The habits that transfer are worth naming, because families assume everything must be rebuilt. Precision with units and significant figures transfers straight from 0625 into Diploma Programme sciences. Shown working from 0580 transfers into Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and stays useful. The reading stamina and paragraph control built in First Language English 0500 is most of what English A asks for in Paper 1. A student who did those well starts DP1 ahead.

The habits that must be unlearned are narrower and more stubborn. Writing to a fixed number of marking points. Treating every question as a retrieval task. Answering discuss as though it said describe. Stopping when the content is out rather than when the criterion is satisfied. And in the other direction, a Diploma Programme student helping a younger sibling will add evaluation to a Cambridge four-mark question and run out of time.

A three-session diagnosis looks like this.

1. Session one: the student answers one timed question on each board, unaided, and the tutor marks both in front of them against the actual documents.

2. Session two: the two markings are compared line by line, and the student says out loud what each system wanted, in their own words.

3. Session three: the student rewrites both answers and predicts their own marks before the tutor gives any, which is where the real gap shows.
items: Transfers well: units, significant figures, shown working, paragraph control
Must go: writing to a mark count instead of to a criterion descriptor
Must go: treating discuss and describe as interchangeable command words
Watch for a DP student over-answering a Cambridge four-mark question
Self-prediction of marks is the fastest test of whether the culture has landed

contentBlocks.heading: What should dual-board home tuition change by the second month?
contentBlocks.body:
By the end of six to eight weeks you should be able to see a change in how the student talks about marks, not only in the marks. That is the honest measure, and it is checkable. Ask them why they lost two marks on a question. A student who says the topic was hard has not moved. A student who says the mark scheme wanted the equation stated and they went straight to substitution has moved a great deal.

On paper, the signals differ by board. At Cambridge, look for fewer silent method losses, fuller working, and questions attempted rather than left blank because time ran out. In the Diploma Programme, look for one criterion strand rising rather than an overall grade jumping, because criterion-marked work moves unevenly and a whole grade rarely shifts in a term.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any home tutor who offers a promised improvement in exchange for a term of fees is telling you something about their marketing rather than their teaching. Be equally careful with a claim to be first in the country. Grades depend on the student's work between sessions, the school's teaching, the papers that actually appear, and how the student is on the day.

There are also limits worth stating plainly. Home tuition cannot fix a subject chosen against the student's interests and strengths. It cannot replace attendance. Two boards in one household means a real time cost for the family, and there are weeks in a February series or a May session where the right decision is to pause tuition rather than add it.
items: Six to eight weeks is a fair first review, not two weeks and not a full term
Cambridge signal: fuller working, fewer blank questions, better time control
Diploma Programme signal: one criterion strand rising, not the whole grade
Ask the student to explain a lost mark; the answer shows whether it landed
Pause rather than add tuition in the fortnight a series or session begins

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in India with two boards in one house
contentBlocks.body:
Before you book anything, spend twenty minutes gathering evidence, because a dual-board request is easy to describe badly and expensive to describe badly. IB and IGCSE private tutors in India will ask for this material at the first conversation anyway. What the tutor needs is not a general worry. It is the board, the grade, the syllabus code, the tier or level, and one piece of marked work per child.

For the Cambridge student, find the most recent marked paper with the examiner's or teacher's annotations on it, and the school's statement of which tier they are entered for. For the Diploma Programme student, find a returned task with criterion levels, the subject and level for all six subjects, and the school's mock dates. If a report comment says the student needs to develop analysis, bring the report too. That sentence means something specific and a good tutor will ask what task it referred to.

Then say what your week can actually hold. Two children, two boards and four sessions a week is a lot of house to run on a weekday evening, and it is better to start with two sessions that survive than four that collapse by Diwali.

The first session itself is diagnostic, not a lesson in the usual sense. Expect the tutor to watch the student work rather than talk at them, to ask what the last marked script meant, and to leave with a short plan naming the first thing to fix. A demo or trial can be arranged before you commit, and if the match is wrong you can ask for a different one.
items: Gather one marked script per child, with annotations, before the consultation
State board, grade, syllabus code and tier or level for each student
Bring the school's mock dates and the entry series for the Cambridge child
Start with the number of home classes the household can hold in a bad week
Expect the first session to diagnose and end with one named thing to fix

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach both IGCSE and IB Diploma properly?
faqs.answer: Some can, and fewer than claim to. The overlap is real in Mathematics and the sciences, where content genuinely carries forward from 0580 and 0625 into Analysis and Approaches and Diploma Programme Physics. What does not carry forward is the marking culture, and that is where most tutors are only half equipped. Test it in the trial by asking for one Cambridge answer marked against a mark scheme and one IB task marked against a criterion descriptor, in the same session, on the student's own work.

faqs.question: My son finished IGCSE in May and starts DP1 in July. What should home tuition do in between?
faqs.answer: Use the gap for the assessment culture, not for content. Two or three home sessions a fortnight across that summer are usually enough to teach command terms properly, to write one criterion-marked piece and mark it together, and to read a Diploma Programme subject guide with the student so the vocabulary is familiar before term begins. Content pre-teaching is mostly wasted, because the school will cover it anyway. What is not wasted is arriving in DP1 already knowing what evaluate is asking for.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travelling to our home in Gurugram hold a weekday evening slot all year?
faqs.answer: Only if they live close enough that the trip is not the deciding factor. A home tutor coming from within Gurugram, along Golf Course Road or a neighbouring sector, will usually hold a 6.30 pm slot through the year. Someone crossing from South Delhi or Noida at that hour will start cancelling by the second month, whatever they promise in September. Ask where the tutor is travelling from before you agree the slot, and consider making one of the two weekly sessions online from the start.

faqs.question: Do we need two separate tutors for two children on different boards?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is worth saying so plainly. One tutor across both boards makes sense when the subject is the same, the two students can take back-to-back slots, and the tutor has genuinely taught both syllabuses. It stops making sense when the subjects differ, when both children need the same evening hour, or when the dual-board claim turns out to be one board plus confidence. Two specialists on alternate days is frequently the cheaper mistake to avoid.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a command word and a command term in practice?
faqs.answer: A command word in a Cambridge question points you at a mark scheme with countable marking points, so explain with four marks wants four identifiable things. A command term in an IB question points at a criterion descriptor written in bands, so evaluate wants a quality of reasoning that no tick list captures. Students who move from one to the other keep the old instinct and lose marks either by under-writing a Diploma Programme answer or over-writing a Cambridge one.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Somebody responsible should be in the flat, and not in the room. For a Grade 9 or Grade 10 student, an adult at home is a reasonable safeguarding baseline and also keeps the session from drifting. Sitting in changes what the student is willing to admit they do not understand, which is the most valuable thing a private tutor can get out of them. The compromise most families reach is an open door, a visible study space and a short conversation with the tutor at the end.

faqs.question: How do we know whether our child should take Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: From marked evidence rather than from confidence. A tutor gathers two or three past papers sat under time at Extended level, marks them against the real mark scheme, and looks at whether the student is losing marks on the harder questions or on carelessness across the whole paper. The school makes the entry decision and the subject teacher holds the strongest view, so a private tutor's job is to give the family evidence for that conversation rather than a competing verdict.

faqs.question: Is online tuition good enough for Mathematics, where working matters?
faqs.answer: It can be, with one piece of equipment and one habit. The equipment is a document camera or a phone stand pointed at the page, so the tutor watches the working appear rather than seeing a finished photograph. The habit is that the student writes as they would in the exam, not in a chat box. Without those two things, online Mathematics quietly becomes a conversation about methods, and the method marks keep going missing on the real paper.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in Chennai and nobody nearby teaches both boards. What now?
faqs.answer: Widen the search rather than lower the standard. Families in Adyar, Besant Nagar or along Old Mahabalipuram Road often find a strong single-board tutor locally for home classes and take the second board online from Mumbai, Bengaluru or Delhi NCR. That hybrid split is usually better than one nearby generalist covering both weakly. The same pattern works in Pune around Koregaon Park, Baner and Kharadi, and in Ahmedabad around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session is missed because of traffic or illness?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because it will happen. The workable arrangement is that a session cancelled by the tutor is rescheduled or moved online within the same week, and a session cancelled by the family with reasonable notice is rescheduled where the tutor's timetable allows. Monsoon weeks in Mumbai and long weekends around Diwali break more sessions than anything else. Writing down how many reschedules are realistic per term prevents the awkward conversation in December.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. Should we change tutor?
faqs.answer: Not yet, but ask a sharper question. One month is roughly six sessions, which is enough to change how a student explains a lost mark and not enough to move a criterion level or a paper grade. Ask the tutor what specifically they are working on, what evidence they are tracking, and what they expect to look different by week eight. A tutor who cannot answer that is not planning. At that point, asking IB Gram for a different match is reasonable.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to the exam boards or to any school?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. It has no connection to the International Baccalaureate, to Cambridge International Education or to Pearson Edexcel, and no relationship with any school mentioned on this page. Schools are named only as local context for the calendar pressures families here describe. All entry decisions, tier and level choices, internal assessment deadlines and mock dates come from your own school, and the coordinator or subject teacher is the person to confirm them with.

comparison.heading: How do the four ways of tutoring two boards compare in India?
comparison.intro: One-to-one at home suits the child whose marks are lost on paper, in working and diagrams. One-to-one online suits the household that needs genuine dual-board depth more than convenience. A small online group works when two or three students share a syllabus and a tier. A large batch is the cheapest per hour and sometimes the right call for drilling a single Cambridge topic. The trade-off that decides it is usually whether anyone needs to see the student's handwriting.

h1: IB and IGCSE Private Tuition Held Across Four School Years
heroTitle: Four School Years, One Tuition Plan in India
heroSubtitle: Most families hire a tutor term by term and never step back to look at the whole span. This page treats Grade 9 to DP2 as one arrangement: where home tuition should be heaviest, where it should deliberately thin out, which subjects to release early, and how a termly review keeps the plan honest.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE private tuition in India works best when it is planned as one four-year arrangement rather than four separate rescues, with home tuition rising and falling deliberately as the student moves from Grade 9 through Grade 10, DP1 and DP2. The load should not be flat. Grade 9 usually needs light support that builds habits; Grade 10 tightens ahead of the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel series; DP1 is the year most families underbuy; DP2 should get narrower and sharper, not broader. A plan written down at the start and reviewed at the end of every term tells you when to add a subject, when to cut hours, and when a tutor has finished the job and should be released.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a four-year tuition plan get matched to one student in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the span, not with this term's problem. When a family asks about IB and IGCSE private tuition in India for a student somewhere between Grade 9 and DP2, the first questions are about the whole ladder: which board the school follows now, whether the International General Certificate of Secondary Education course is Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, which exam series the school enters candidates for, and which subjects are likely to be carried into the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP). A Grade 9 student who has just moved across from a CBSE school sits at a different point from a DP1 student whose first Internal Assessment (IA) draft has come back marked. Both can be planned for. They should not be planned for the same way.

Then the practical questions, which decide whether the plan survives contact with a real week. Where you live, because a weekday evening home tutor in Powai is a different proposition from one in Rajarhat. What the school week already holds, including Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments once the Diploma Programme starts. How many subjects the household can realistically sustain at once, which is almost always fewer than the number a worried parent first names. And the shape of the spend across four years rather than one term, because an arrangement that is comfortable in Grade 9 and impossible in DP2 was never a plan.

IB Gram then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against the boards, syllabuses and levels you named, subject to tutor availability in your locality. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match. What does not happen is a four-year sale. The commitment is made one stage at a time, with a review already diarised for the end of the term, and the long plan written as a document that either survives that review or gets changed in front of you.
items: 1. Send the current report card, the board, and the year group the student is in today
2. Name the exam series the school enters: Cambridge February/March, May/June, or the IB May session
3. Say which subjects are likely to continue into DP1, and at roughly which level
4. Agree the tuition load for this stage only, never for all four years at once
5. Run a demo session, then confirm one weekly slot the household can actually hold
6. Diarise the first termly review before the first lesson is taught

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 to DP2: what the four-year ladder actually contains
contentBlocks.body:
The ladder carries two qualifications and they are marked in completely different ways, which is why a single plan has to be written rather than assumed. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. Cambridge exam series run in February/March, a series offered only in India, then May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*.

After Grade 10 the common routes are the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. For families reading this page the route is usually the DP: two more years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to three further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. CAS must also be completed. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter the May session, and May results are released in early July.

Read the two structures together and the load curve writes itself. Grade 9 ends in no external examination, so tuition should be light and aimed at habits. Grade 10 carries the first real series, so it rises. DP1 is where IB and IGCSE private tuition in India is most often underbought, because the final papers feel distant while the internal assessments are already being set. DP2 should narrow: fewer subjects under tuition, more timed past papers, and hours concentrated on the two or three subjects that are still moving.
items: Grade 9: light load, no external series at the end of the year
Grade 10: the heaviest IGCSE term is the one before the entered series
DP1: coursework starts early while exams still feel far away
DP2: fewer subjects under tuition, more timed papers, mocks several months before May
A February/March Cambridge entry pulls the whole Grade 10 curve forward by months

contentBlocks.heading: Which subjects deserve four years of tuition, and which deserve one term?
contentBlocks.body:
Very few subjects deserve four unbroken years. Mathematics is the usual exception, and the reason is structural rather than sentimental. A student on Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended who goes on to IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is building one continuous edifice, and an algebra gap tolerated in Grade 9 reappears in DP1 calculus wearing different clothes. That subject can justify a long, low-intensity arrangement: one session a week for most of the span, lifting before the series and before DP2 mocks, and rarely more than that. The alternative route, Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, changes the emphasis but not the argument.

Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 into IB Physics follows a different pattern, and treating it like mathematics wastes money. The IGCSE work rewards equation recall, rearrangement and clean units. The Diploma work rewards explanation written to a command term: define and describe are cheap, while explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent carry the marks students lose. Most physicists need two concentrated blocks rather than four years: one in Grade 10 ahead of the entered series, one in DP1 as the scientific investigation and the longer written responses arrive. Between those blocks a competent student should be left alone to work.

Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 is usually the shortest intervention on the whole ladder. A student who reads widely may need six weeks of work on structuring a response and nothing further until the DP English course changes the demand. IB Economics is a one-and-a-half-year subject by definition, begun fresh in DP1, so no part of it belongs in a Grade 9 plan. Writing that sentence down early is what stops a family paying for four years of a subject that has existed for eighteen months.
items: Mathematics 0580 Extended into Analysis and Approaches: the one genuine long-arc subject
Physics 0625 into IB Physics: two blocks, Grade 10 series and DP1 investigation
First Language English 0500: short, sharp interventions rather than a standing weekly slot
IB Economics: starts in DP1, so it cannot appear in a Grade 9 budget
Any subject dropped after Grade 10 leaves its tuition hours free for DP1

contentBlocks.heading: Where a four-year arrangement survives across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
A four-year plan is really a four-year logistics problem, and geography decides how much of it can be taught at home. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the honest answer varies by address. A tutor living around Bandra, Juhu or Andheri can hold a weekday evening slot in those pockets for years. Crossing between Worli or Lower Parel and Powai in evening traffic is a different matter, and families in Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi or Kharghar often find that the tutor who is willing in Grade 9 quietly becomes unreliable by DP2. Parents searching for IB and IGCSE private tuition in Mumbai should test the commute in the first month, not the third year.

Bengaluru has the same problem in a different street layout. Whitefield and Sarjapur Road families draw from a deep local pool, while Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road can be thin for a specific HL subject; Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout sit in between. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Kharadi travel comfortably together, while Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi form a second cluster that a tutor rarely crosses twice a week. Requests for IB and IGCSE private tuition in Pune usually work best when the tutor is inside one of those two clusters.

Gujarat and the east run on a smaller supply. In Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway corridor hold most of the demand, with Gandhinagar reachable and Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot usually better served by a hybrid week. Families asking about IB and IGCSE private tuition in Ahmedabad should assume the DP2 specialist may be online. The same holds in Kolkata and eastern India, where Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore have real local options while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna lean on remote teaching. Across Delhi NCR, Hyderabad and Chennai the pattern repeats: dense supply near the big school clusters, thinner beyond them.
items: Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri and Powai hold slots; Thane and Kharghar strain
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are deep, Yelahanka and Electronic City are thin
Pune: Koregaon Park and Kharadi form one cluster, Baner and Hinjewadi another
Gujarat: Bodakdev, Satellite and Gandhinagar for home visits, Surat and Rajkot hybrid
Kolkata and eastern India: Salt Lake, Ballygunge and Alipore local, Guwahati and Patna online
Delhi NCR, Hyderabad and Chennai supply clusters tightly around the international schools

contentBlocks.heading: The four school calendars in India a single plan has to absorb
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, which is why the IB May session fits it so neatly and why the Cambridge February/March series, offered only in India, sits awkwardly in the middle of a school year. A four-year plan has to absorb four of these cycles in a row, and each one has a different pressure point. Grade 9 has almost none, which is exactly why it is the cheapest year in which to fix a habit. Grade 10 has one: the entered series, whether that is February/March, May/June or October/November for Cambridge, or January or May/June for Pearson Edexcel. DP1 has coursework deadlines the school sets internally. DP2 has mocks, whose dates each school fixes for itself, usually several months before May.

International schools in India also set their own internal deadlines for drafts, and those deadlines are what actually govern a student's term. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School, Chirec International School, Mahindra International School and Jamnabai Narsee School all describe the same rhythm: a quiet start, a crowded November and February, and a final term that feels like it belongs to someone else. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

So the plan should be written against dates, not against months in the abstract. Ask the school for the mock window, the coursework submission dates and the entry deadlines at the start of each year, and put them in the same document as the tuition plan. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show how marks are actually awarded. May results are released in early July, which is the one date that closes the whole four-year span and the only one no school in India can move.
items: Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, which the IB May session matches
Cambridge February/March series is offered only in India and shifts Grade 10 forward
Each school fixes its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May
Coursework and draft deadlines are set internally and dominate DP1 terms
May results arrive in early July, closing the four-year span

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition in Grade 9, hybrid in DP2: how the mode should shift
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in one paragraph. A home tutor sits beside the student and sees the working, the crossed-out line, the diagram drawn too small, and the handwriting that collapses under time pressure; the cost is travel, and travel is what makes a slot fragile in the fourth year. An online tutor reaches the specialist your locality does not contain and never cancels for rain, but cannot see what the student is doing with their pen unless the student shows it. A hybrid week takes one session at home and one online, which is the arrangement most four-year plans end up at, because it buys presence where presence matters and reach where reach matters.

Mapped onto the span, the shift is usually the same. Grade 9 is the year for home classes: a fourteen-year-old learning to keep an error log needs somebody in the room, and the tutor learns how the household actually works. Grade 10 keeps home tuition through the series, because timed written practice under observation is worth more than any screen share. DP1 often begins to tilt, as HL subjects narrow the supply of tutors who can teach them and the good one turns out to live in another city. By DP2 a hybrid week is common: home sessions for the subject where written technique is the problem, online for the specialist.

There are exceptions worth naming. A student who is genuinely disorganised does badly online in every year, whatever the subject. A student in Bhubaneswar or Guwahati taking a rare HL subject has no realistic home option and should go online from the start rather than accept a local generalist. And a family that moves house mid-DP, which happens often enough in India, will find that an online tutor survives the move while a home tutor does not. Decide the mode per subject per year, and revisit it at every review.
items: Grade 9: home classes, because habits are built in the room and not on a screen
Grade 10: keep home tuition through the series for observed timed writing
DP1: expect one subject to move online as HL supply narrows
DP2: a hybrid week, home for written technique and online for the specialist
Any year: a disorganised student needs presence more than the syllabus needs a specialist

contentBlocks.heading: What should you verify at the start, and again before DP1 begins?
contentBlocks.body:
Verify twice, because the job changes. At the start of Grade 9 you are checking that the tutor genuinely teaches the named syllabus rather than school mathematics in general: ask which board, which syllabus code, which tier they usually enter students at, and how Core differs from Extended in the subject they are about to teach. Ask them to talk you through a marked script. A tutor who can explain where method marks were lost in a piece of 0580 Extended working, in plain words, is telling you more than any list of qualifications. IB Gram checks profiles before they go live and matches on board, syllabus and level, but the family should still run this conversation themselves.

The second check comes before DP1, and most families skip it. The person who was excellent with a Grade 10 student may have no Diploma Programme experience at all, and the gap between the two is real: criterion descriptors instead of mark schemes, command terms instead of command words, and an Internal Assessment whose boundaries on outside help are far stricter than anything at IGCSE. Ask directly whether they have taught at HL, what the difference in demand is between HL and SL in their subject, and where exactly they stop when a student brings an IA draft to a session.

Then there is what no verification can cover. A platform cannot see whether your child will talk to this particular adult, whether the tutor will still be in your city in two years, or whether the chemistry that works at fourteen still works at seventeen. So build the check into the plan rather than treating it as a one-off: a short conversation at every termly review about whether this tutor is still the right person for the next stage, asked while nothing is going wrong.
items: Ask for board, syllabus code and tier before the first lesson, every time
Have the tutor walk you through a marked script and the method marks lost
Re-verify before DP1: HL experience is a separate question from IGCSE experience
Ask where the tutor stops on an Internal Assessment draft, in their own words
Repeat one short suitability question at every termly review, not only in a crisis

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE private tuition in India as one four-year plan
contentBlocks.body:
A four-year plan is a single document that says, for each of Grades 9 and 10 and DP1 and DP2, which subjects are under tuition, how many hours a week, in which mode, and what has to be true at the end of that year for the arrangement to continue. That is the whole idea. Families who think in terms of IB and IGCSE private tuition in India as a rolling monthly service end up with the load only ever going up, because adding a subject is an easy decision and removing one never gets made at all.

The load should be a curve, not a line. Grade 9 is low: one subject, perhaps two, aimed at study habits, note-taking, and the first encounter with a mark scheme. Grade 10 is the first genuine peak, concentrated in the term before the entered series, and it should fall away the moment those papers are written. The long gap between the Grade 10 series and DP1 is deliberate empty space, and a family that fills it with tuition out of anxiety has spent the student's only real rest in four years. DP1 is the year that quietly matters most, because subject choices harden, the Extended Essay and IA work begins, and habits set here are what DP2 runs on. DP2 is the second peak, and it should be the narrowest: two or three subjects, timed papers, and mock results driving the last decisions.

Which years matter least is the harder claim. Grade 9 matters enormously for habits and very little for content, so paying for heavy subject coverage there is usually waste. The first term of DP1 is often over-tutored while students are still finding the level, and the last six weeks of DP2 are frequently over-tutored too, when what the student actually needs is quiet time with past papers and sleep.
items: One document covering four years, reviewed termly, rewritten whenever the evidence changes
Load rises in Grade 10, falls after the series, rises again through DP1 into DP2
DP1 is the year most families underbuy and DP2 the year they overbuy
The gap after the Grade 10 series is rest, not a selling opportunity
Grade 9 buys habits cheaply; buying content there rarely repays itself

contentBlocks.heading: When should home tuition hours fall, and when should they stop entirely?
contentBlocks.body:
Four unbroken years with the same weekly tutor is the failure mode nobody plans for and many families reach. The warning signs are specific. The student waits for the session before attempting homework. They can do a question with the tutor present and not without. They describe a topic in the tutor's phrasing rather than their own. They have stopped asking the school teacher anything. None of that means the tutor is bad; a tutor who explains beautifully every week can create exactly this. It means the arrangement has outlived its purpose and the hours should come down.

Cutting hours is a decision, not a drift. Halve the frequency for a term and see what happens to the marks, which is the only honest test available. If the work holds, halve it again. If it falls back within a fortnight, the gap was real and the hours return, but now you know what you are paying for. Stopping a subject entirely is the version of this that families find hardest, and the criteria are worth writing down in advance: the student is self-correcting, they are hitting the target band on unseen timed work, and they can explain their own errors before anyone points them out. When all three hold for two consecutive assessments, stop. A tutor who tells you to stop is worth keeping for the next subject.

What progress looks like is modest and slow. Expect the first change in how the student approaches a question rather than in the grade, usually within a few weeks. Expect the grade to move over a term, sometimes two. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anybody who offers one over four years should be treated with real scepticism. Home tuition also cannot fix a bad subject combination, a sleep problem, or a school placement that was wrong from the start.
items: 1. Week one of term: agree the two or three outcomes this term must produce, in writing
2. Mid-term: compare one piece of marked school work against those outcomes
3. End of term: tutor, parent and student review what moved and what did not
4. Same meeting: decide to raise, hold, halve or stop the hours for each subject
5. Before the next term starts: update the four-year document with the decision

contentBlocks.heading: Writing down a four-year plan before the first home session in India
contentBlocks.body:
Bring three things to the first conversation and the plan almost writes itself. The most recent report card, with criterion comments or grades exactly as the school issued them. A piece of marked work, ideally a script with the marker's annotations rather than a clean printout. And the school calendar for the year, including the mock window and coursework deadlines if the school has published them. Those three documents tell a tutor more in ten minutes than an hour of description.

The first session should not be teaching. It should be diagnosis: what the student can already do unaided, where the working breaks down, and whether the problem is content, technique or timing. A tutor who starts lecturing from minute one has skipped the only part of the process that makes the next four years cheaper. Expect the first session to end with a written note of what will be worked on for the next six weeks, and expect that note to be short.

Then agree the shape. One stage at a time, a fixed weekly slot the household can genuinely hold, a mode chosen per subject, and a review date already in the diary. Send a query or book a free consultation, name the board, the syllabus, the level, your locality and the schedule you can hold, and IB Gram will shortlist verified profiles that match, subject to availability. A demo or trial session can be arranged first. If the match is wrong, ask for a different one, and do it early rather than three terms later when the plan has quietly bent itself around the wrong person.
items: Bring the report card, one marked script, and the school's published calendar
Keep the first session diagnostic: no teaching until the problem is named
Agree one stage of the plan, not four years, and write the review date down
Choose the mode per subject: home, online, or a hybrid week
Ask for a different match early if the fit is wrong, subject to availability

faqs.question: Should we book tuition for all four years at once?
faqs.answer: No, and an arrangement that asks you to is worth questioning. Book one stage at a time, with the four-year plan written down as an intention rather than a contract. The student in Grade 9 and the student in DP2 are different people with different subjects, and the tutor who suits one may not suit the other. What should be fixed for four years is the review habit, not the booking. Agree the hours for this term, diarise the review, and decide again with evidence in hand.

faqs.question: Which of the four years matters most?
faqs.answer: DP1, in most cases, and it is the year families most often underbuy. Subject choices harden, the Extended Essay and the first Internal Assessments begin, and the working habits formed there are what DP2 runs on. Grade 10 feels more urgent because the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel series is visible, and it does need a concentrated push before the entered series. But a strong Grade 10 followed by a drifting DP1 is a far more common story than the other way around.

faqs.question: How do we stop our child depending on a tutor for four straight years?
faqs.answer: Build the exit into the plan from the first session rather than hoping it happens. Ask the tutor at the start what the student should be able to do unaided by the end of each term, and test that with unseen timed work the tutor has not prepared. Cut the frequency deliberately once a term and watch what happens. Dependence shows up as a student who waits for the session before attempting homework, or who explains a topic only in the tutor's own phrasing.

faqs.question: What does a termly review actually involve?
faqs.answer: A short meeting with the tutor, the parent and the student, held at the end of term against outcomes agreed at the start of it. You look at one or two pieces of marked school work, compare them with what was promised, and then make a single decision per subject: raise the hours, hold them, halve them, or stop. The decision goes into the four-year document with a date. Reviews that produce no decision are conversations, and conversations do not change a load curve.

faqs.question: Can the same home tutor stay with us from Grade 9 to DP2?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is genuinely valuable when it works, because that person holds four years of error logs and knows which topic failed in Grade 9. But it is not the default you should plan for. Higher Level teaching is a different skill from IGCSE teaching, and a tutor who is excellent with a Grade 10 student may have no Diploma Programme experience. Re-verify before DP1 begins, ask about HL specifically, and treat continuity as a benefit rather than an obligation.

faqs.question: How many subjects should be under tuition in each year?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. One or two in Grade 9 is usually right, since the year is about habits rather than content coverage. Grade 10 may justify two or three in the term before the entered series, falling back afterwards. DP1 is typically two, chosen from the Higher Level subjects. DP2 should be the narrowest of all, often two subjects and sometimes one, with the remaining time given to timed past papers the student does alone.

faqs.question: We are in Whitefield in Bengaluru and evening traffic is heavy. Does a home tutor work across four years?
faqs.answer: Usually yes in Whitefield and along Sarjapur Road, because the local pool is deep enough that a tutor can live within a short run of you. The risk is not the first year but the fourth, when a tutor who was crossing the city willingly in Grade 9 starts rescheduling in DP2. Test the commute early, keep the slot in one consistent window, and plan for at least one subject to move online by DP1. A hybrid week is the usual settlement.

faqs.question: When should we stop tuition in a subject completely?
faqs.answer: When three things hold together for two consecutive assessments: the student self-corrects without prompting, they hit the target band on unseen timed work, and they can explain their own errors before anyone points them out. Stop then, even if the term has time left on it. You can always restart before mocks. A tutor who raises the subject of stopping before you do is usually the one worth calling back for the next subject on the ladder.

faqs.question: What happens to the plan over the long summer and the Diwali break?
faqs.answer: Treat the gap after the Grade 10 series as genuine rest, because it is the only real break in four years. For other holidays, a short block works better than a thinned-out weekly slot: a few concentrated sessions on one topic, then nothing. Families in Koregaon Park and Kalyani Nagar often find tutors more available in holidays and book more than the student needs. Decide the holiday load at the termly review, before the anxiety of an empty week sets in.

faqs.question: Our child is already in DP1. Is it too late to plan the whole span?
faqs.answer: It is late for Grades 9 and 10, which are gone, but not for the part that remains. Write the plan backwards from May of DP2 instead: mock dates, coursework deadlines, the subjects still moving, and the ones that should be released. Starting late narrows what is possible, and honest planning means naming that. Two years planned properly beats four years of unplanned weekly sessions, and the termly review works exactly the same way from here.

faqs.question: Does a long plan mean a better final result?
faqs.answer: It means fewer wasted hours and better decisions, which is a different claim. No tutor or platform can promise a particular diploma score, and any four-year offer that implies one deserves scepticism. What a written plan reliably changes is the pattern where families pay for a subject nobody has reviewed in two years, or discover in DP2 that a gap from Grade 9 was never closed. Progress shows first in how a question is approached, then in the marks, usually over a term.

h1: IB and IGCSE Online Tutors Reaching Every Indian City
heroTitle: One Online Tutor Pool for Both Boards in India
heroSubtitle: Plenty of families in India run two boards at once: one child in Cambridge IGCSE Grade 10, another in the second year of the Diploma Programme. Online lessons let both reach the same checked pool of teachers instead of whoever happens to live within driving distance of your gate.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE online tutors in India are worth searching for when your locality cannot staff both boards at once. A family with a Grade 9 child on Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 and an older child on Diploma Programme Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is looking for two fairly rare specialists, and few neighbourhoods hold both. Online lessons pool supply nationally, so the search stops being about who lives nearby and starts being about who actually teaches the syllabus. This page covers the combinations that are hardest to staff locally, how one tutor can teach two children in different cities, what the arrangement quietly costs you, and how to judge a dual-board tutor inside a single trial lesson.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a two-board request become one online shortlist in India?
contentBlocks.body:
You send one query naming both children, both boards and both weekly timetables, and the shortlist is built backwards from whichever child is harder to staff. That is almost always the one sitting a named syllabus code with few local teachers. The easier request bends around the harder one, because a good Additional Mathematics 0606 teacher is scarcer than a good Grade 8 mathematics teacher, and scheduling the scarce person first is the only way the week works.

The questions asked at the start are dull and necessary. Which board: Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel for the younger child, and which programme for the older one. Which level: Core or Extended at IGCSE, Higher Level or Standard Level in the Diploma Programme. Which exam series the school has entered the student for. What the school day looks like, including the bus, and what else is already in the evening. Where you are, because even an online arrangement is governed by your local clock and your local power supply.

What comes back is a shortlist of verified tutor profiles matched to those facts, not a directory dump. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong after it. Availability is always subject to the tutor's own schedule, and the scarcer the combination, the fewer slots there are to choose between.

Families searching for IB and IGCSE online tutors in India usually want one arrangement rather than two, and that is how the shortlist is put together.

One caution before you send anything. If you ask for both children to be taught at the same hour to save your evening, you narrow the pool sharply. Stagger them by an hour and the shortlist usually widens.
items: 1. Send one query covering both children, both boards, both school timetables
2. Name the exam series each child has been entered for
3. Staff the scarcer syllabus first, then fit the second child around it
4. Run a trial lesson per child before any ongoing arrangement begins
5. Review the pairing after a month and change either match if needed

contentBlocks.heading: Two boards under one household: IGCSE, MYP and the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means either Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. What follows it varies: the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move across to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Cambridge exam series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June.

The Diploma Programme runs across two years, DP1 and DP2. A student takes six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL), with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to three further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Primary Years Programme (PYP) sit below the DP in IB schools, and plenty of Indian families have one child in the MYP and another already in DP1. That is a gentler pairing than IGCSE plus DP, because the criteria language carries across.

Grading scales differ, which trips parents up constantly. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. The DP grades 1 to 7. A 6 and an A are not the same currency, and no tutor should let you compare them as though they were.
items: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are two boards, not one
February and March is a Cambridge series offered only in India
DP: six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, 240 hours each
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to three points toward 45
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A* on Cambridge tiered papers
CAS is a completion requirement, not a graded subject

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB and IGCSE subject combinations are hardest to staff locally?
contentBlocks.body:
The hardest single combination to staff from one locality is Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 alongside Diploma Programme Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Both are taught by the same kind of person, and there are not many of them in any one suburb. 0606 has no tiers, two written papers with a calculator allowed, and is graded A* to E. Its content runs through functions, quadratic functions, factors of polynomials, equations, inequalities and graphs, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation and integration.

It is usually taken alongside 0580 Extended by a student heading for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL or A Level Mathematics. Pearson Edexcel's nearest equivalent is International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, and a teacher who knows 0606 cold does not automatically know 4PM1's paper structure.

DP Mathematics splits into two subjects, each available at HL and SL. Analysis and Approaches (AA) is algebraic and proof-heavy. Applications and Interpretation (AI) is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often advised towards AA, but the right choice depends on the degree and the student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement. A tutor who tells you which one to pick without reading a single piece of the student's written work is guessing.

Other thin combinations show up again and again: IGCSE Physics 0625 with DP Physics HL, and IGCSE First Language English 0500 with DP Economics, where the second child needs a reader and a writer rather than a calculator. Online is how these get covered at all outside the largest metros.

Edexcel's nearest equivalent to 0606 is Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
AA is proof-heavy; AI is modelling and statistics with technology throughout
IGCSE Physics 0625 paired with DP Physics HL is a thin local market
First Language English 0500 with DP Economics needs a writing specialist

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB and IGCSE online tutors in India reach that local pools cannot
contentBlocks.body:
Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai together hold a real number of international-school families, and almost none of them can find an Additional Mathematics 0606 teacher and a DP Physics HL teacher within the same postcode. This is the clearest case for pooling. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Chennai or an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Bangalore is reachable from all of southern India the moment the lesson stops requiring a car.

Central and western India runs the same way. Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad have families whose nearest realistic alternative is a weekly drive that eats the evening. In Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat have somewhat more local supply, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna have far less, so an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kolkata often ends up teaching a child in Guwahati on the same evening.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR follows the same shape. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula are reasonably served; Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur are patchier by subject. In Gujarat, Ahmedabad neighbourhoods such as Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway corridor have options, while Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot thin out quickly once you name a syllabus code.

The metros are not immune. A family in Whitefield or Sarjapur Road, in Powai or Thane, in Gachibowli or Kondapur, in Koregaon Park or Baner, still faces weekday evening traffic that can stretch a short trip badly. Online does not fix traffic. It removes it from the lesson.
