contentBlocks.heading: School calendars in India when two children sit different boards
contentBlocks.body:
Running two boards means running two calendars in one house, and they do not line up. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, which is why schools here overwhelmingly enter DP candidates for the May session rather than November. May results are released in early July. The younger child on Cambridge IGCSE may be entered for the February and March series, a series offered only in India, or for May and June, or for October and November, and the school decides. If your child is on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE instead, the series are January and May and June.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named by a family, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Nothing on this page describes what any particular school teaches.

What this means practically is that the crunch weeks arrive at different times for your two children, and one of them will always be in a quiet phase while the other is drowning. Use it. Move hours between the two children deliberately at the start of each term instead of holding both at a fixed weekly count all year.

The mock season is the pressure point families underestimate. International schools in India tend to run internal mocks well before the live series, and coursework deadlines land in the same weeks. A DP2 student is finishing internal assessment drafts while a Grade 10 student is sitting mocks, and both want the same Tuesday evening. Decide in advance which child gets the contested slot, rather than rescheduling in a panic on the day.
items: Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, so May is the usual DP session
May DP results are released in early July
Cambridge series: February and March, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January, and May and June
Internal mocks and coursework deadlines cluster before the live series
Rebalance hours between the two children each term, not each week

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid when two boards pull in different directions
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition and online tuition are not rivals so much as different answers to different constraints. A home tutor sitting beside a student sees the rough working, the crossed-out line, the moment attention goes. That is worth a great deal for a younger child or a student who avoids starting. Online buys reach: the person who genuinely teaches 0606 and Mathematics AA HL, wherever they live.

Most households who hire IB and IGCSE online tutors in India end up hybrid without planning it. The Grade 9 child keeps a weekly home tutor for habit and supervision, because at that age presence in the room does more than expertise. The DP2 child goes online to a subject specialist, because at that stage expertise does more than presence. If the specialist happens to live in your city, a monthly home visit before each mock round is a reasonable compromise and worth asking about.

There are cases where online is simply the wrong call. A student who will not open a document unless someone is watching. A child with no quiet corner, where home classes at least create a boundary the household respects. A subject where the tutor needs to see hand-drawn construction lines as they happen and the family has no document camera or tablet.

And there is the household equipment problem nobody mentions on a sales call. Two children online at the same hour on one connection, in one flat, with one decent pair of headphones between them, goes badly. Stagger the slots. Put the second child in a different room. Check the upload speed, not just the download speed, because a frozen tutor is a wasted hour.
items: Home tutoring wins on supervision, starting work, and reading body language
Online wins on reach: the right syllabus specialist regardless of city
Hybrid: home classes for the younger child, online specialist for the DP student
Two simultaneous online lessons on one connection is a predictable failure
Ask whether an online tutor will do occasional home visits before mocks

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor who claims to teach both boards?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for the syllabus codes and the exact levels the tutor has taught, then ask what they last taught and when. A tutor who says 0580, 0606 and Mathematics AA HL should be able to tell you, without pausing, that 0606 has no tiers and is graded A* to E while 0580 is tiered with Core capped at C. If that distinction is fuzzy, the claim to teach both boards is thin.

Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they are shown to you, and identity, qualifications and stated teaching experience are part of that. Verification tells you a person is who they say they are and has taught what they claim. It cannot tell you whether your particular child will work with them. That is what a trial is for, and a two-board family should run one trial per child rather than assuming the second will go like the first.

Some checks are yours alone. Ask to see a piece of feedback the tutor has written on a student's work with the name removed. Ask what they do when a student's answer is right but the method will not survive a harder question. Ask how they mark: against the mark scheme's command words, or against their own sense of a good answer.

On academic integrity, one rule settles most arguments. Coursework and internal assessment must be the student's own work, and a tutor may teach the skills, discuss the approach and comment on drafts within the school's rules, but may not write, redraft or supply any part of the submission. A tutor who offers to do more than that is a reason to stop the conversation.
items: Ask for syllabus codes, levels and the most recent year each was taught
Test one board-specific detail live: tiers, grading scale, paper structure
Request anonymised written feedback on a real student script
Run one trial per child; do not assume the second will match the first
Confirm the tutor's limits on coursework and internal assessment before booking

contentBlocks.heading: What pooled supply actually changes for a family in India
contentBlocks.body:
Pooling is the whole argument for IB and IGCSE online tutors in India, and it is worth stating plainly. When lessons have to happen in your drawing room, the set of tutors you can hire is the set who will drive to your address on a weekday evening. When lessons happen online, that set becomes everyone in the country who teaches the syllabus and is free at that hour. For a common request the difference barely matters. For 0606 plus Mathematics AA HL it is the difference between a choice and no choice.

There is a second effect that families notice only later. A wider pool means you can be fussy about the thing that actually matters to you rather than the thing that is available. If your child needs someone patient rather than someone brilliant, you can hold out for patient. If your DP2 student needs someone who marks harshly and fast, you can ask for that specifically.

One tutor teaching two children in different cities is the case that surprises people most. An older sibling in a university hostel in Manipal and a younger one at home in Ahmedabad can share the same teacher across two different boards, back to back, on the same evening. The tutor carries the family context between the two lessons, which no two separate tutors ever do.

Pooling has a ceiling, though. It widens choice; it does not create expertise where none exists. Very rare subject and level pairings stay hard to fill in any pool, and the honest answer in those cases is a shorter shortlist and a longer wait.
items: Local hiring is limited to who will travel to your address
Online hiring is limited only by syllabus knowledge and the clock
A wider pool lets you choose on temperament, not just availability
One tutor can hold both children's context across two cities
Rare level and subject pairings remain scarce even nationally

contentBlocks.heading: What is lost when both children go online in India
contentBlocks.body:
Something real is given up when a household moves to IB and IGCSE online tutors in India for both children, and a page that pretends otherwise is not worth reading. The first loss is incidental supervision. A home tutor who arrives at six o'clock forces the desk to be cleared and the phone to be put down. An online lesson does not, and a student who is skilled at looking attentive can coast for weeks before anyone notices.

The second loss is peripheral vision. A tutor in the room sees the diagram drawn wrongly before the student says a word, sees the eraser used four times on the same line, sees the older sibling's argument still sitting in the air. On screen you get what the camera is pointed at, which is usually a face rather than a page. Insist that written work is held up to the camera or photographed and sent, every session, or the loss compounds.

The third is the hardest to fix: two children online in the same household is genuinely more household management than two home tutors arriving on different days. You become the scheduler, the technical support and the person who checks whether anyone actually did the work.

On progress, be patient and be specific. Ask for one measurable change by the end of the first month, named in advance: a paper section done in the real time allowed, a criterion that stops losing marks, an unfamiliar question attempted rather than skipped. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any promised improvement stated as a number should make you suspicious rather than reassured. What you can reasonably expect is that the student's written work gets more organised and that fewer marks go missing to method.
items: Incidental supervision disappears; a screen does not clear the desk
The tutor sees a face, not the page, unless work is shown every session
Two online children means the parent becomes scheduler and technical support
Set one named, checkable change to review at the end of month one
Treat any promised numeric improvement as a warning sign, not a selling point

contentBlocks.heading: Setting up dual-board online tuition in India: the first fortnight
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first session, gather four things for each child. The current report or subject feedback, in the school's own words. A recent piece of marked written work, ideally one the student did badly on. The syllabus code and level, confirmed with the school if you are unsure. The exam series the school has entered them for. That last one is worth a message to the coordinator, because families guess it wrong often.

The first lesson for each child should be diagnostic rather than impressive. Expect the tutor to give a short piece of work and watch the student do it, rather than lecture for an hour. By the end, you should be told something you did not already know: not that your child needs to practise more, but that the loss is concentrated in a particular paper section, or a particular command word, or in the gap between knowing the method and writing it down in a form that earns marks.

In week two, set the rhythm. Fixed slots, staggered so the two children are never online together. A shared folder where scanned work and feedback live, so nothing depends on anybody's memory. One short written note per child per month, sent to you.

Then leave it alone for four weeks before judging. If after a month the picture has not moved, say so directly and ask for a different match. Changing a tutor early costs a week; keeping the wrong one out of politeness costs a term.
items: Collect report, marked work, syllabus code and exam series per child
Ask for a diagnostic first lesson, not a demonstration lecture
Stagger the two slots so no two lessons share one connection
Keep scanned work and tutor feedback in one shared folder
Review at four weeks, and ask for a different match if nothing moved

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach both IGCSE and IB Diploma subjects well?
faqs.answer: Some can, in a narrow band. A mathematics specialist who teaches Additional Mathematics 0606 and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is teaching adjacent content, and that pairing is common and credible. A claim to teach IGCSE Chemistry, DP Economics and MYP English equally well is not. Ask for the syllabus codes and levels taught in the last two years, and ask one board-specific question live. Broad claims that collapse under a specific question are the clearest warning you will get.

faqs.question: How many more tutors can we actually reach by going online?
faqs.answer: There is no honest number to quote, and anyone quoting one is guessing. What can be said is structural: hiring locally limits you to people willing to travel to your address at a fixed weekday hour, while hiring online limits you only to people who know the syllabus and are free at that hour. For a common request the two pools overlap heavily. For 0606, DP Physics Higher Level or First Language English 0500, the online pool is the only one that reliably contains anybody.

faqs.question: Which IB and IGCSE combinations should we assume are hard to find locally?
faqs.answer: Assume difficulty whenever both children need a specialist in the same narrow area. Additional Mathematics 0606 with Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL is the classic case. IGCSE Physics 0625 with DP Physics HL is another. First Language English 0500 with DP Economics is harder than it looks, because the second child needs a reader and essay marker rather than a problem-solver. Outside the biggest metros, assume all three of those pairings require a national search and plan the timetable accordingly.

faqs.question: Do online lessons work as well for a Grade 9 student as for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and it is worth saying so before you pay for anything. A DP2 student has a deadline in view, knows what they are weak at, and will work between sessions. A Grade 9 student often needs someone in the room to make the session start at all. If both children must be taught, the common pattern is home tuition for the younger child and an online specialist for the older one, with the arrangement reviewed once mocks have been sat.

faqs.question: We live in Coimbatore. Is there any local option at all, or is online the only route?
faqs.answer: Local options exist for mainstream subjects, and you should check them first, because a home tutor who can reach you has advantages no screen matches. Where Coimbatore, Mysuru, Kochi, Visakhapatnam and similar cities run short is in named syllabus codes at the top levels. If your search has already failed twice for the same subject and level, that is the signal to stop searching locally and pool nationally instead.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach our two children living in different cities?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more useful things this arrangement allows. An older sibling in a hostel and a younger one at home can be taught back to back on the same evening by one person, across two different boards. The tutor carries the family context between the two lessons, which two unconnected tutors never do. Slots depend on the tutor's availability, and back-to-back scheduling is easier to secure if you are flexible about which evening.

faqs.question: What does verification actually cover before we see a profile?
faqs.answer: Identity, qualifications and stated teaching experience are checked before a profile is shown to you. That establishes the person is who they claim and has taught what they claim. It does not establish that they suit your child, that they mark to the standard you want, or that they will be patient with a student who is behind. Those are trial-lesson questions, and with two children on two boards you should run one trial for each rather than generalising from the first.

faqs.question: How should we judge a dual-board tutor inside a single trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Give them a piece of your child's marked work from a real assessment and watch what happens. A strong tutor will ask the student to redo one question aloud, will identify where the marks left the answer rather than where the answer was wrong, and will name the paper section or command word involved. A weak one will explain the topic again from the beginning. Also watch whether the tutor asks about the exam series and level before teaching anything.

faqs.question: What if our internet or power supply is unreliable during the lesson?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, not after. A workable arrangement is that a session dropping in the first ten minutes is rescheduled, while a session that drops later is completed by a written summary and continued next time. Ask the tutor to send scanned annotated work after each session so nothing depends on the call surviving. If outages are frequent in your area, a hybrid week with periodic home classes is the more honest solution.

faqs.question: Should we still consider home tuition for one child while the other is online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that split is the most common sensible outcome for two-board families. Home tuition gives the younger child supervision and a fixed boundary in the week, which is worth more at Grade 9 than raw subject expertise. The online tutor gives the older child a specialist the neighbourhood does not contain. Cost, travel and your own evening all sit differently for each child, so treat the two decisions separately rather than picking one mode for the household.

faqs.question: How long should we wait before deciding an online arrangement is not working?
faqs.answer: Four weeks is fair for IB and IGCSE online tutors in India, with a named checkable change agreed at the start. Choose something specific: a paper section completed in the real time allowed, an unfamiliar question attempted rather than skipped, a criterion that stops bleeding marks. If none of that has moved after a month, say so plainly and ask for a different match. Changing tutors early costs a week of continuity, while staying with a poor fit out of politeness costs the term.

faqs.question: Does using online tutors for both children mean less contact with what they are doing?
faqs.answer: It can, unless you design against it. Two home tutors arriving on different evenings generate conversation whether you want it or not. Two online sessions can run for a month with nobody in the house knowing what was covered. Fix it cheaply: one shared folder holding scanned work per child, a short written note from each tutor once a month, and the rule that written work is shown to the camera in every session.

comparison.heading: How do online tutors compare with home tuition, a batch or a course in India?
comparison.intro: Four ways to buy teaching, and the choice usually turns on one thing: how scarce your syllabus and level are. If a good local teacher exists for both children, a home tutor is hard to beat for supervision. If one child needs a rare combination, online reach wins. A centre batch suits a student who works better with peers watching, and a recorded course suits a disciplined reviser topping up.

heroTitle: Two Exam Calendars, One Household, Online Across India
heroSubtitle: One child sits the Cambridge series, the other the IB May session. Mock periods land weeks apart, both children want the same desk, and the broadband is shared. This page sets out how lessons for two boards fit into one week, and when to move a child offline instead.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE online tuition in India is what most two-board households settle on, because it is the only arrangement that lets two children learn in the same hour without two tutors arriving at the door. The scheduling problem is real. Cambridge series run in February/March, May/June and October/November, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June, and schools in India almost all enter Diploma Programme candidates for the May session. So one child's mock fortnight can sit on top of the other's coursework deadline. This page lays the two calendars side by side, works through devices, bandwidth and study space in a single flat, and gives you a weekly pattern a family can actually hold. Home tuition and hybrid weeks are covered too, with the trade-offs stated plainly.

contentBlocks.heading: How does one enquiry in India produce two lesson timetables?
contentBlocks.body:
Send one enquiry for the household, not one per child. That single message should carry both calendars, because the shortlist changes completely depending on which weeks are already spoken for. IB Gram asks for board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. With two children on different boards, the schedule question does most of the work.

What matters first is the dated skeleton of your year: the series your Grade 10 child is entered for, the Diploma Programme (DP) mock window the school has fixed for DP2, and any coursework deadline already on the noticeboard. Schools decide which series they enter students for, and they set their own mock dates, so this information comes from the school rather than from a platform. Once those dates sit on one sheet, the clash weeks become visible, and they are usually fewer than parents fear. Three or four fortnights in the year carry real pressure. The rest of the year is ordinary.

Matching then runs against that sheet rather than against a blank free-slot grid. A tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended well but only on Tuesday evenings is no use if that hour already belongs to your DP1 child's Physics session. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and with two children it helps to run both trials in the same week, so you can compare how each tutor answers a rescheduling request rather than only how each one teaches.

IB and IGCSE online tuition in India is easier to match than a home visit for exactly this reason: an online tutor spends no time travelling, so the hours either side of fixed school timings stay usable. Availability is still subject to tutor availability and depends on level and schedule. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match.
items: 1. Send both children's boards, levels and school dates in one enquiry
2. Mark the clash weeks: mock windows, coursework deadlines, exam series dates
3. Shortlist tutors against those weeks, not against an empty timetable
4. Run both trial sessions in the same week and compare rescheduling answers
5. Fix the two weekly slots, then review after the first mock period

contentBlocks.heading: Two exam calendars side by side: February/March, May/June and the IB May session
contentBlocks.body:
Put both calendars on one page before you book anything. Cambridge exam series run in February/March, May/June and October/November, and the February/March series is offered only in India. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) has sessions in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July.

Now read what that means inside one house. If your Grade 10 child is entered for February/March, their exam block lands before the DP2 child's May papers, which is the friendlier arrangement: the younger child finishes and the house goes quiet just as the older one enters the final stretch. The February/March series exists specifically for India and lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Class 11 admissions and for DP or A Level entry in the same academic year. If the Grade 10 child is entered for May/June instead, the two exam blocks overlap almost completely, and every evening in April and May has to be rationed. A student cannot choose a series independently of the school, so ask the coordinator early.

The Diploma side brings structure the IGCSE side does not have. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours each and the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Those hours are already timetabled at school. Anything private sits on top of them.

So the honest planning question is not how many hours of IB and IGCSE online tuition in India a family should buy. It is which weeks have room at all, and which weeks you should deliberately leave empty.
items: Cambridge series: February/March (offered only in India), May/June, October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
IB Diploma sessions: May and November; schools in India almost all use May
DP results released in early July, once the Indian school year has turned
Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*

contentBlocks.heading: Which subjects should own the scarce evening slots in a two-calendar week?
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject deserves a weekday evening, and in a two-calendar house you cannot pretend otherwise. Rank subjects by how much of the grade sits in a timed written paper, and by how far the student currently is from where the school expects them to be.

On the Cambridge side, Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, and the tier sets the ceiling: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. A student entered for Extended but working at Core pace usually needs short, frequent sessions rather than one long weekly block, because the loss is in method and shown working rather than in understanding. Physics 0625 rewards equation recall and explanation written in the right order, which is drilled in small doses. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 needs drafting time between sessions more than it needs contact hours, which makes it the first subject to move to a fortnightly rhythm when the week tightens.

On the Diploma side, IB Mathematics AA and AI are different courses rather than harder and easier versions of one course, and a Higher Level choice carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level. IB Physics and IB Economics both ask for extended written answers governed by command terms: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent. A student who can do the calculation and still loses marks is usually answering a different command term from the one printed on the paper.

Here is the scheduling consequence. Diploma written work expands to fill whatever time it is given, so it should hold the fixed weekday slots. IGCSE past-paper practice compresses well and can be moved around. When both children need the same hour, the subject with a dated external paper closest in the calendar takes it, and the other moves to the weekend or drops for a fortnight.
items: Mathematics 0580: the Core ceiling is grade C, Extended reaches A*
Physics 0625: equation recall and ordered explanation, not numerical drill alone
First Language English 0500: drafting between sessions beats extra contact hours
IB Mathematics AA and AI are separate courses, taken at HL or SL
Command terms set the depth: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent

contentBlocks.heading: Bandwidth, back-up and the evening slot: two-calendar households across India
contentBlocks.body:
Where you live changes the answer more than parents expect, and it changes it through the evening rather than through the syllabus.

In Bengaluru, families in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City often already run one child online, simply because weekday evening traffic between those areas and the rest of the city can stretch a short trip badly. HSR Layout, Koramangala, Indiranagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each have their own version of the same problem. In Hyderabad, the corridor through Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet empties late, while Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad sit differently again. Chennai splits between Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) and Perungudi on one side and Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar and Velachery on the other. IB and IGCSE online tuition in Chennai is frequently chosen for the second child alone, because one home visit an evening is manageable and two are not.

Beyond the metros the argument is about supply rather than traffic. In Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, and across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa, a family running two boards at once will rarely find local specialists for both. Online tuition is not a compromise there. It is the only way to reach an HL subject specialist and a 0625 specialist in the same week.

The metros still matter for comparison. IB and IGCSE online tuition in Bangalore, in Hyderabad, in Pune around Koregaon Park, Baner, Hinjewadi and Kharadi, in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region around Powai, Bandra and Thane, and in Delhi NCR around Noida, Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Dwarka all meet the same shared-desk problem once two children are studying at once. Traffic only decides whether home tuition is still on the table at all.
items: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City: evening traffic decides the format
Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur and Kokapet: a corridor that empties late
Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Adyar and Anna Nagar: two very different commutes
Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore, Nagpur and Goa: supply, not traffic
Powai, Bandra, Noida, Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Koregaon Park: shared desks either way

contentBlocks.heading: When do the two mock periods collide on a school calendar in India?
contentBlocks.body:
School calendars are the fixed points. Everything you arrange privately has to bend around them.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. Grade 10 mocks are set separately, and generally timed against whichever series the school has entered the cohort for. Two departments, two decisions, and no obligation on either to check the other. So in plenty of houses the DP2 mock fortnight and the Grade 10 mock fortnight land within days of each other, or overlap in the middle. Parents describe the same fortnight every year: two sets of past papers on the dining table, two laptops, and a printer that runs out of ink at the worst possible moment.

Families at international schools in India name the same places when they write in, among them Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Chirec International School, Mahindra International School, Greenwood High International School and Mercedes-Benz International School. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Those names appear because parents use them, and for no other reason.

What you can ask the school for is short, and worth asking in writing: the series each child is entered for, the mock dates for both year groups, and the internal deadlines for coursework and Internal Assessment (IA) drafts. Ask in the first month of the academic year rather than in January. Once those dates exist on one sheet, a tutor can plan backwards from them, and you can see which fortnights should carry no tuition at all. The Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and admission requirements are worth confirming with the university or board concerned rather than assuming them.
items: Ask for both year groups' mock dates in the first month of term
Schools set DP2 mock dates, usually several months before the May session
Grade 10 mocks are timed against the series the school has entered
Internal Assessment and coursework deadlines belong on the same single sheet
Confirm equivalence and admission requirements with the university or board concerned

contentBlocks.heading: One home, two screens: when to move a child offline to save the week
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in one paragraph. A home tutor in the room sees handwriting, sees working crossed out, and catches a student quietly guessing, which is worth most for Grade 9 and Grade 10 written method. An online tutor costs nothing in travel, can be a specialist from another city, and frees the hours either side of school, which is worth most when the week is tight. A hybrid week takes one home visit for the subject that needs a person present and runs everything else on screen. The trade-off is plain: presence buys detection, online buys schedule and reach, and hybrid buys some of each at the cost of two routines to remember.

In a two-calendar household the arithmetic shifts again, because the binding constraint is not the child. It is the house. One flat with two live lessons in the same hour means two quiet corners, two devices, two headsets, and enough upstream bandwidth for two video streams with screen sharing. Most home broadband in the metros handles that. Most dining tables do not.

So the honest answer is that IB and IGCSE online tuition in India works best when only one lesson is live at a time. Stagger the two by an hour wherever the school timetable allows it. Where it does not, move one child offline: a home tutor for the Grade 10 student in the living room while the DP2 student takes Physics online in the bedroom removes the bandwidth clash entirely, and gives the younger child the person-in-the-room advantage they generally need more.

Move a child offline when the subject is handwriting-heavy, when the student drifts on screen, or when the shared study space cannot hold two lessons. Keep them online when the tutor you want lives in another city, when the only free slot is early or late, and when an exam block is close enough that travel disruption is a risk not worth carrying.
items: Two live lessons need two rooms, two devices and two sets of headphones
Stagger the start times by an hour before spending anything on equipment
Move handwriting-heavy IGCSE subjects offline first if the week collapses
Hybrid: one home visit a week, with everything else taught on screen
Keep online where the specialist you need lives in another city

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a tutor who has to hold a shifting, shared schedule
contentBlocks.body:
Verification for this kind of arrangement has two halves, and only one of them belongs to a platform.

IB Gram checks a tutor's profile before it goes live: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the boards, syllabuses and levels the tutor says they teach. A profile that says IB and IGCSE should name syllabus codes and levels, because 0580 Extended and Mathematics AA at Higher Level are not one skill in two costumes. Shortlisting then uses what you have told us about board, level, school calendar, location and schedule. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and you can ask for a different match if the fit turns out to be wrong.

The half nobody can do for you is the scheduling half. A tutor can be genuinely strong and still be wrong for a household that has to move a slot three times a term. Test it directly during the trial. Ask what happens when a mock week is announced late. Ask whether a Tuesday session can shift to a Saturday morning in exam term, and how much notice that needs. Ask how work is handed over if the tutor is unavailable in the week before a paper. Vague answers here cost a family more than a flat first lesson does.

Check the practical things yourself as well. Whether the tutor annotates a scanned script rather than only talking over it. Whether a photograph of handwritten working is acceptable between sessions. Whether their own connection is stable at the hour you actually want, which is not the hour they demonstrated at. And whether they will send two short notes a month rather than one long one, because with two children you need to compare rather than admire. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anyone offering one has told you something useful about themselves.
items: Profiles are checked for identity, qualifications and the syllabuses actually taught
Ask in the trial how a late-announced mock week would be handled
Confirm the tutor can annotate a scanned or photographed handwritten script
Agree how much notice a schedule change needs, in both directions
Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, rather than waiting

contentBlocks.heading: Whose deadline wins when two children clash in India?
contentBlocks.body:
This is the question families actually ring about, and it deserves a rule rather than a negotiation every Sunday evening.

The rule worth adopting is dated externality. When two demands collide, the one closest to a fixed external date the family cannot move takes the slot. An external written paper sat in a series beats a school mock. A school mock beats a coursework deadline the teacher has already said can slip a few days. A coursework deadline beats ordinary weekly tuition. Apply it coldly and the arguments mostly stop, because the rule is visible on a sheet rather than arbitrated by whoever is most upset at the time.

There are two sensible exceptions. The first is a Diploma Internal Assessment or Extended Essay draft with a hard school deadline, because a missed draft slot loses supervision time rather than practice time, and supervision is not repeatable. The second is a student genuinely at risk against the Diploma's failing conditions, where 24 points is the minimum for the diploma and the core contributes up to 3 of the 45 available. Risk of losing an award outranks improving a grade that is already safe.

What the rule must never become is a permanent hierarchy in which the older child always wins. Across a year, a Grade 10 child entered for February/March takes priority in December and January, and the DP2 child takes it in March and April. Write that down in advance and show both of them. Children accept a rule they can see coming far better than a decision made at eight in the evening by a tired parent.

One more thing. If applying the rule means one child gets no tuition for a fortnight, that is usually the right answer rather than a failure. A fortnight without a session costs less than two rushed sessions in a house where nobody can concentrate.
items: Dated externality: the nearest fixed external date takes the contested slot
An external series paper beats a mock, which beats a movable deadline
Exception: a hard Internal Assessment or Extended Essay draft deadline
Exception: a Diploma student at risk against the 24-point minimum
Write the priority order down in advance and show both children

contentBlocks.heading: What a month of IB and IGCSE online tuition in India should change
contentBlocks.body:
Set expectations by the calendar rather than by the week.

After a month of IB and IGCSE online tuition in India, the thing that should have changed is not the marks. It is whether the week holds. Ask three questions at the four-week point. Did the sessions happen at the times agreed. Did work set between sessions get done. Did the shared study space cause a row more than once. If those three answers are good, the arrangement is working even when no score has moved yet. If sessions kept slipping, the timetable is wrong, and no amount of teaching quality repairs a timetable.

Subject progress runs on a slower clock. On the Cambridge side, the first honest evidence usually comes from a full past paper sat under timed conditions after six to eight weeks and marked against the markscheme rather than by impression. On the Diploma side, criterion feedback on a piece of written work, or a mock script read beside the previous one, is the readable signal, and the school's mock cycle decides when that arrives. Between those points you are watching process, not outcome.

The limits are worth saying plainly. A tutor cannot change a predicted grade, because the school forms it. A tutor cannot move a series date, extend a coursework deadline, or sit beside a student in an examination hall. Starting in the final term narrows what is possible to exam technique and triage, which is real but modest. And two children in tuition at once is harder to sustain than one, so if the household is fraying, dropping a subject is a better decision than shortening sleep.

If two mock cycles pass and nothing has moved for one child, change something structural rather than adding another hour to an already full week.
items: Four weeks: judge whether the timetable held, not whether marks moved
Six to eight weeks: one full timed past paper, marked to the markscheme
The school's mock cycle decides when Diploma evidence becomes readable
A tutor cannot change a predicted grade or move a series date
If the household is fraying, drop a subject before shortening sleep

contentBlocks.heading: Setting up two online lessons in one home in India: the first fortnight
contentBlocks.body:
Two weeks is enough to set this up properly, and setting it up properly saves the rest of the year.

Before you write in, gather four things for each child: the board and the syllabus or level, the series or session they are entered for, the school's mock dates if published, and the last piece of marked work with the teacher's comments still on it. The marked work matters more than the report card, because it shows a tutor what the loss actually looks like. Then add one household item: a sketch of the week showing school timings, travel, any coaching or activities already committed, and the hours the study space is genuinely free.

From there the sequence is short. Parents send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability.

The first session with each tutor should not be a lesson. It should be a diagnosis: a short piece of work done live, a look at the marked script you sent, and an agreement about what the next four sessions will cover. Ask each tutor to put that plan in two or three lines you can read in a minute.

IB and IGCSE online tuition in India works best when the week is decided before the term starts and revisited only at the mock cycles. Set the two slots, set the priority rule, and leave the clash fortnights empty on purpose. If a match is not working after a fair trial, ask for a different one rather than waiting for the term to end.
items: Gather board, level, series, mock dates and one marked script per child
Sketch the week: school timings, travel, activities and free study hours
Book both children's trials in the same week, then compare the answers
Treat the first session as a diagnosis rather than as a lesson
Leave the clash fortnights deliberately empty when you set the timetable

faqs.question: Can two children take online lessons in the same hour in one flat?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but only in separate rooms and with headphones on. The bandwidth demand of two live video lessons with screen sharing is manageable on most home broadband in Indian metros; the real constraint is sound. Two people talking through a doorway spoils both sessions, and the younger child is the one who loses more. If you have only one usable study space, stagger the start times by an hour, or move one child to a home tutor so that only one lesson is ever on screen.

faqs.question: My Grade 10 child's mock week falls on my DP2 child's Internal Assessment deadline. Which one gets the tutor?
faqs.answer: The Internal Assessment deadline, in most cases. A school mock can be sat with less preparation and its result is mainly diagnostic, while a missed draft deadline costs supervision time the student cannot get back and feeds work that goes forward to the final award. Check one thing first: whether that mock is being used to help form a predicted grade, since a predicted grade is set by the school and matters in applications. If it is, split the fortnight and give each child two short sessions rather than one long one.

faqs.question: Does the February/March Cambridge series make the year easier or harder to schedule?
faqs.answer: Easier, in a household that also has a Diploma candidate. The February/March series is offered only in India and lets Grade 10 results arrive in time for Class 11 admissions and for Diploma Programme or A Level entry in the same academic year. It also finishes before the IB May session, so the Grade 10 child is done while the DP2 child is still in final revision. If the school enters your child for May/June instead, the two exam blocks overlap almost entirely and the spring becomes the hardest stretch of the year.

faqs.question: How much internet do two simultaneous online lessons actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than most families assume, though the upload speed matters more than the download. A live lesson with a shared screen and a visible student is a two-way video call; two of those run comfortably on a typical fibre connection and struggle on a shared mobile hotspot. Test it once at the hour you plan to use, with both children connected at the same time, rather than at eleven in the morning when the line is quiet. Keep mobile data as a back-up on one phone through the mock fortnights and the exam series.

faqs.question: We live in Whitefield and weekday traffic is brutal. Should we move both children online?
faqs.answer: Move the child whose subjects lose least from a screen, not both automatically. Evening traffic between Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and the rest of Bengaluru can stretch a short trip badly, which is why so many families there already run at least one lesson online. But a Grade 10 student losing method marks in Mathematics 0580 Extended often gains from a home tutor watching the working go down on paper. A hybrid week, with one home visit and the rest online, is the settlement most households in that part of the city reach.

faqs.question: Would home tuition for one child be better than putting a second child on a screen?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Splitting the format solves the space, device and bandwidth problem in a single move: one child takes a home tutor in the living room while the other takes an online lesson in a bedroom. Home tuition also suits handwriting-heavy work and younger students who drift on screen. The cost is travel time and a slot that is harder to move at short notice, because a tutor who has already crossed the city cannot reschedule as easily as one who simply opens a laptop.

faqs.question: What should happen to the timetable during the DP2 mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Thin it deliberately. Schools set their own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, so the fortnight is known well in advance. Inside that window the Diploma student needs fast marking turnaround and short targeted sessions rather than new teaching, and the Grade 10 child is generally better served by pausing for two weeks than by squeezing sessions in around the noise. Agree that pause with both tutors when you first book, not in the week itself when everyone is already stretched.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both children, across both boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, in closely related subjects, and it is worth asking. A tutor who genuinely teaches Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended and IB Mathematics AA can run back-to-back sessions online, which saves a scheduling slot and gives one person the whole household's picture. But a dual-board claim needs testing. Ask how a markscheme differs from a criterion descriptor, and what changes in the way an answer is structured. Two specialists usually beat one generalist stretched thin across four different papers.

faqs.question: How do we handle a session missed during a clash week?
faqs.answer: Decide the rule before it happens. Agree with each tutor whether a missed session is rescheduled within the same week, carried to the next one, or simply dropped, and agree how much notice each side owes the other. In exam term, carrying sessions forward tends to create a pile-up exactly when the student has least room, so dropping is often the kinder choice. Write this into the arrangement at the start, along with what happens when the tutor is the one who is unavailable.

faqs.question: My Grade 9 child drifts during online lessons. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Partly. Shorter sessions, a camera that stays on, work produced live rather than described, and a parent within earshot rather than in the room all help. Ask the tutor to close each session by setting one piece of work that must be photographed and sent before the next one. If the drift continues after a month, the format is wrong for that child at that age, and a home tutor or a hybrid week is the sensible change rather than a stricter rule about the screen.

faqs.question: We are in Kochi and there are no local tutors for either board. Is online the only option?
faqs.answer: Realistically yes, and that is not a downgrade. Outside the metros, in Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore or Nagpur, a household running one Cambridge candidate and one Diploma candidate will rarely find local specialists for both subjects at the levels needed. Online reaches a Higher Level specialist in another city in the same week a Physics 0625 tutor teaches your Grade 10 child. The trade-off is that nobody is watching the handwriting, so send scanned work every week and expect the tutor to mark it.

acceptedAnswer.text: Thin it deliberately. Schools set their own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, so the fortnight is known well in advance. Inside that window the Diploma student needs fast marking turnaround and short targeted sessions rather than new teaching, and the Grade 10 child is generally better served by pausing for two weeks than by squeezing sessions in around the noise. Agree that pause with both tutors when you first book, not in the week itself when everyone is already stretched.

mainEntity.name: Can one tutor teach both children, across both boards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, in closely related subjects, and it is worth asking. A tutor who genuinely teaches Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended and IB Mathematics AA can run back-to-back sessions online, which saves a scheduling slot and gives one person the whole household's picture. But a dual-board claim needs testing. Ask how a markscheme differs from a criterion descriptor, and what changes in the way an answer is structured. Two specialists usually beat one generalist stretched thin across four different papers.

mainEntity.name: How do we handle a session missed during a clash week?

acceptedAnswer.text: Decide the rule before it happens. Agree with each tutor whether a missed session is rescheduled within the same week, carried to the next one, or simply dropped, and agree how much notice each side owes the other. In exam term, carrying sessions forward tends to create a pile-up exactly when the student has least room, so dropping is often the kinder choice. Write this into the arrangement at the start, along with what happens when the tutor is the one who is unavailable.

mainEntity.name: My Grade 9 child drifts during online lessons. Is that fixable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partly. Shorter sessions, a camera that stays on, work produced live rather than described, and a parent within earshot rather than in the room all help. Ask the tutor to close each session by setting one piece of work that must be photographed and sent before the next one. If the drift continues after a month, the format is wrong for that child at that age, and a home tutor or a hybrid week is the sensible change rather than a stricter rule about the screen.

mainEntity.name: We are in Kochi and there are no local tutors for either board. Is online the only option?

acceptedAnswer.text: Realistically yes, and that is not a downgrade. Outside the metros, in Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore or Nagpur, a household running one Cambridge candidate and one Diploma candidate will rarely find local specialists for both subjects at the levels needed. Online reaches a Higher Level specialist in another city in the same week a Physics 0625 tutor teaches your Grade 10 child. The trade-off is that nobody is watching the handwriting, so send scanned work every week and expect the tutor to mark it.

finalCta: Send one query for the household, with both children's boards, levels and school dates in it, or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who fit the weeks you actually have free. A trial session can be arranged before you commit, and lessons run at home, online or hybrid.
