h1: IB and IGCSE Tuition in India: What Changes Between the Boards
heroTitle: Two Boards, Two Different Jobs in India
heroSubtitle: Cambridge IGCSE and the IB Diploma Programme reward different work, so the tuition that carried a student through Grade 10 often stalls in DP1. This page sets out the gaps subject by subject in Mathematics, the sciences and English, and what a tutor should change first.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE tuition in India is really two jobs, and a home tutor who teaches both should be able to say out loud where the two syllabuses part company. At Cambridge IGCSE the reward goes to accurate, fast, well-rehearsed method on predictable question types. In the Diploma Programme the same student is asked to design an investigation, justify a modelling choice, and write to criteria that name the thinking, not the answer. The content overlap is real, so a strong Grade 10 student is rarely lost. The habit gap is the problem. This page compares Mathematics 0580 into Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Physics 0625 into the Diploma sciences, and First Language English 0500 into English A, then sets out a bridging plan for the transition summer.

contentBlocks.heading: From a Grade 10 report card to a matched tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
A brief that says "needs help with Maths" produces a general Maths tutor, and a general Maths tutor is exactly what fails a board transition. The brief that works names the syllabus code, the tier, the school's exam series and the Diploma Programme (DP) subjects the student has been placed into. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended and DP Mathematics Applications and Interpretation (AI) at Standard Level (SL) are not the same subject with a different label, and the person teaching them needs to have taught both.

So start with paper evidence. A marked script tells a tutor more in ten minutes than a term of report comments: whether marks went on method, on recall, on rearrangement, or on reading the command word. Send the last two marked papers, the school report, and the subject list for DP1 if the school has issued it.

What happens next is deliberately plain. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus codes, the levels, the school calendar, your location and the weekly schedule you can actually hold. It shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, subject to tutor availability, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match rather than waiting out a term.

Families arranging IB and IGCSE tuition in India often have two children on two boards, or one child crossing between them in the same year. Say that at the start. It changes which tutor is worth shortlisting, because a single visit that covers a Grade 9 Cambridge student and a DP1 sibling only works if one person genuinely holds both assessment systems.
items: 1. Send two marked scripts and the report, not just the grade average
2. Name the syllabus code: 0580, 0625, 0500 or the Edexcel equivalent
3. State the DP subjects and levels the school has confirmed for DP1
4. Take a demo on a topic the student is stuck on this week
5. Fix the weekly slot, the mode, and how feedback reaches you

contentBlocks.heading: Core, Extended, SL and HL: the four labels that set tuition in India
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It usually runs as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. After it, students go into the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or across to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G, with 9-1 versions of some syllabuses under different codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1.

The tier matters more than parents expect. Many Cambridge subjects are split into Core and Extended. Core tops out at grade C. Extended reaches A*. A student sitting Core Mathematics cannot reach an A* however well the papers go, and a student pushed into Extended too early loses marks on questions the Core paper would never have asked. That decision should be made on evidence from real past-paper attempts, not on ambition, and the school makes the final call.

Exam series are the other structural fact. Cambridge runs February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May/June. A February/March entry compresses Grade 10 revision into a shorter run-up and pushes the transition summer earlier.

On the IB side the labels change meaning. Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) are not tiers of difficulty in the Cambridge sense; they are different volumes of the same subject, with HL adding Additional Higher Level (AHL) content on top of a shared core. Tuition planned around the wrong label wastes the first month. Ask the tutor which tier and level the student is registered for before the first session, and ask what changes in their teaching because of it.
items: Core caps at grade C; Extended reaches A* on many Cambridge syllabuses
Cambridge series: February/March in India, May/June, October/November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
HL adds Additional Higher Level content to a core shared with SL
Tier and level placement is the school's decision, made on evidence

contentBlocks.heading: 0580, 0625 and 0500: what actually changes in the Diploma Programme?
contentBlocks.body:
Three changes do most of the damage. Mathematics adds justification to accuracy. The sciences add a graded investigation the student designs alone. English adds unseen analysis under time, against a mark scheme that rewards argument rather than neatness. Everything below is those three, in detail.

Mathematics first. Cambridge 0580 Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4 with a calculator; Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers per tier. DP Mathematics then splits into two subjects, each offered at HL and SL. Analysis and Approaches (AA) is algebraic and proof-heavy. Applications and Interpretation (AI) is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology used throughout. Students aiming at engineering or economics degrees are often steered towards AA, but the right choice depends on the degree and the student, and the DP coordinator makes the final placement. A 0580 student who scored on procedure and never wrote a line of reasoning will feel AA proof questions as a wall.

Sciences next. Cambridge Physics 0625 covers motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics and space physics, and it requires students to recall and rearrange the syllabus equations. Pearson Edexcel's equivalent is 4PH1. The DP sciences, first assessed in 2025, set Paper 1 in two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based, with Paper 2 carrying short-answer and extended-response questions. Then there is the internal assessment (IA), a scientific investigation worth 20% of the subject, marked on four criteria of six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, within a 3,000-word maximum.

English last, and it is the change families see coming least.
items: 0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator, Paper 4 calculator; Core sits 1 and 3
4MA1 is Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers in each tier
DP sciences IA: 20%, four criteria of six marks, 3,000 words maximum
0625 requires recall and rearrangement of the syllabus equations
AA is proof-led; AI is modelling and statistics with technology throughout

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition across India: what each metro changes about the weekly slot
contentBlocks.body:
Geography decides the timetable more often than teaching preference does. In Delhi NCR a tutor living in South Delhi can reach Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri for an early evening slot, but a Dwarka or Faridabad family asking the same tutor for a weekday visit is asking them to cross the city twice in peak traffic. Gurugram families on Golf Course Road, and Noida families in Sector 128 or Greater Noida, usually get a steadier arrangement by booking a tutor who already teaches inside the same corridor. Ghaziabad sits far enough out that online becomes the sensible default for a scarce subject.

Mumbai splits the same way. A Bandra, Juhu or Andheri household is inside a dense supply pocket, and IB and IGCSE tuition in Mumbai is easy to arrange there for mainstream subjects. Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are workable. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are a different calculation: the trip in evening traffic can stretch a short distance into a long one, and a tutor who agrees to it in June quietly starts cancelling by October.

Bengaluru is the clearest case for hybrid. A Whitefield or Sarjapur Road family and a tutor based in Jayanagar or Kanakapura Road are on opposite sides of the evening crawl, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Electronic City each have their own supply. Searches for IB and IGCSE tuition in Bangalore rise every August, which is exactly when the good weekday slots go.

Chennai families in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Alwarpet, Anna Nagar and Velachery usually manage home visits comfortably, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) and Perungudi stretch a tutor's radius. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Kharadi form one cluster and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi another; crossing between them on a weekday is the thing that breaks a schedule. Families in Hyderabad, Kolkata and Ahmedabad often find the specialist for one syllabus simply is not local, and pool supply nationally by going online for that subject alone.
items: Delhi NCR: Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri are easy; Ghaziabad rarely is
Mumbai: Bandra, Juhu, Powai are dense; Kharghar and Thane stretch a radius
Bengaluru: book inside your corridor, not across Whitefield to Jayanagar
Chennai: Adyar and Anna Nagar work; OMR and Perungudi need an early slot
Pune: Kharadi and Hinjewadi are one weekday trip too far from each other
Hyderabad, Kolkata and Ahmedabad: go online for the scarce syllabus only

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar that shapes IB and IGCSE tuition in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School, Mahindra International School, Chirec International School and Ecole Mondiale World School are named only because families searching this page recognise them.

The calendar pressure is predictable, which is what makes it manageable. Grade 10 begins under the shadow of whichever series the school has entered: a February/March Cambridge entry means mock exams land soon after the winter break and the real papers follow almost immediately, while a May/June cohort gets a longer revision run and a shorter summer afterwards. The transition summer between Grade 10 and DP1 is the single most useful window in the whole five-year stretch, and it is the one most families spend recovering.

Then DP1 starts, and the load arrives in a different shape. Coursework does not queue politely: the science investigation, the first Mathematics exploration draft and the early English oral preparation all sit in the same terms as ordinary teaching. Schools set internal deadlines well before any external one, and those internal dates are the ones a tutor must plan around.

What families should ask their own school, early, is straightforward: which exam series has the cohort been entered for, which tier in each Cambridge subject, and what the internal coursework deadlines are for DP1. A tutor cannot get those answers for you and should not guess them. Bring them to the first session and the planning stops being generic. Without them, even good home tutoring drifts into whatever topic feels urgent that week, which is how a term disappears.
items: Ask the coordinator which exam series the cohort has been entered for
Internal coursework deadlines fall well before any external deadline
A February/March entry pulls mocks forward into the winter term
The Grade 10 to DP1 summer is the cheapest time to close a gap
DP1 coursework overlaps ordinary teaching rather than following it

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when a student is crossing boards in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition wins on attention and accountability, online wins on supply, and hybrid wins for most families crossing boards. That is the short answer. The longer one depends on which of the three problems you are solving.

Home tuition is the right default when the student needs to be watched working. Rearranging an equation, setting out a proof, showing working that earns method marks: these are visible habits, and a tutor sitting beside a student catches the shortcut being taken before it hardens. Home lessons also hold a rhythm that online sessions lose, because the slot is physically blocked out and nobody quietly attends with the camera off. The cost is travel, which is why a home tutor's radius is the honest limit on who you can book.

Online tuition wins where supply is thin. A tutor who has taught both 0580 Extended and Mathematics AA HL, or both 0625 and DP Physics, may not live within reach of your locality at all. Online also suits paper review well: a marked script on screen, annotated live, with the mark scheme open alongside. It suits a nervous younger student less, and it suits an easily distracted one badly.

Hybrid is what most transition-year families settle into. One home session a week for the subject that needs supervision, one online session for the scarce specialism, and a short online check before a coursework deadline. It also survives the school year better: when exam season or a family trip disrupts the routine, the online half continues while the home visit pauses. Decide it deliberately rather than by drift, and review it once a term.
items: Home lessons: best for working habits, method marks and accountability
Online: best for scarce dual-board specialists and live paper annotation
Hybrid: one home visit plus one online session is the common settlement
Younger or distractible students usually need the home session to lead
Review the mix once a term rather than letting travel decide it

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a tutor teaches on both boards?
contentBlocks.body:
Check three things: what the tutor has actually taught, how recently, and whether they can talk about assessment criteria without prompting. Everything else is secondary. A tutor who has taught Cambridge for years and has only read about the Diploma Programme will be confident and wrong in exactly the places that cost marks.

On the platform side, IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the boards and syllabuses they say they have taught. That check is a filter, not a substitute for your own conversation. Verification confirms that someone has taught DP Chemistry; it cannot tell you whether they are the right person for your specific, stubborn, half-confident Grade 10 student.

So run your own five minutes. Ask which paper a named topic appears in. Ask what the four assessment criteria for the science investigation are called, and what a weak Evaluation section usually looks like. Ask how they would teach a student to rearrange a 0625 equation who has always looked the rearrangement up. Ask what they would do differently for AA against AI. The answers separate the specialist from the generalist quickly, and they cost you nothing.

Then watch the demo for one thing: does the tutor diagnose or does the tutor lecture? A good first session includes a question the student cannot answer, and the tutor treating that as useful information rather than an embarrassment. Be wary of anyone who offers a promised improvement in a fixed number of weeks, or describes themselves as first in the country. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the ones who talk that way are usually selling the thing they cannot deliver.
items: Verified profiles cover identity, qualifications claimed, boards taught
Ask which paper a named topic sits in, and why
Ask for the four science IA criteria by name, unprompted
A good demo finds a gap; a weak one performs a lesson
Treat promised improvements in fixed weeks as a warning sign

contentBlocks.heading: What a student who coasted at IGCSE meets in DP1
contentBlocks.body:
Some students get through Grade 10 on memory and speed. They learn the question types, they work fast, they do not often have to explain themselves, and they finish with good grades and no study system. Those are the students who struggle most in DP1, and it usually shows in October rather than June.

The first thing that changes is that answers stop being the point. In DP Mathematics, particularly Analysis and Approaches, credit attaches to the argument: the line that says why this substitution is allowed, the justification of a domain, the structure of a proof. A student trained to reach the number quickly writes the number and loses the rest. In the sciences, Paper 1B is data-based and Paper 2 asks for extended response, so the ability to read a graph nobody has explained in class and write a paragraph about what it implies becomes a graded skill rather than a nice extra.

The second thing is that work arrives without a due-date rhythm. The scientific investigation is designed by the student. Nobody hands out the research question. A student used to being given the task waits, politely, for weeks. This is where good IB and IGCSE tuition in India earns its place: not by teaching content the school is already teaching, but by making the student produce a draft early enough that the criteria can still be applied to it.

The third is written volume under time. English A Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen passages, one at SL and two at HL, and Paper 2 is a comparative essay on two studied works. The Individual Oral runs 15 minutes, a 10-minute analysis linked to a global issue followed by five minutes of questions, and HL students also write an HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. A 0500 student who wrote well to a familiar brief now has to think on an unseen text, out loud, on the record. That is a practice problem, and it responds well to home tuition where the same passage can be attempted twice in one sitting.
items: Method marks give way to justification, especially in Mathematics AA
Paper 1B is data-based; unexplained graphs become a graded skill
The scientific investigation starts with the student's own question
English A Paper 1 is unseen analysis; Paper 2 compares two studied works
The Individual Oral is 15 minutes: 10 of analysis, five of questions
The HL essay runs 1,200 to 1,500 words on a studied text

contentBlocks.heading: What honest progress looks like in a transition year in India
contentBlocks.body:
In the first month, expect diagnosis rather than improvement. A tutor who has done the job properly can tell you by the fourth session which topics are genuinely missing, which are present but slow, and which look like content problems and are really reading-the-question problems. If nobody can tell you that after a month, change something.

By the end of the first term, the visible changes are process changes: working shown without being asked, a plan for a draft instead of a panic before a deadline, a student who can say what a command word wants. Marks often move later than habits do, and sometimes they dip first, because a student being asked to justify their reasoning writes more slowly before they write better.

There are limits worth naming. Starting in the final weeks before a Cambridge series narrows what tuition can do to targeted paper technique on the topics most likely to pay. Tuition in four subjects at once usually helps none of them, because the total weekly hours stop leaving time to do the practice that tuition sets. A student who does not do work between sessions gets the value of one session, repeated. And some students do not need a tutor at all: if the gap is confidence after one bad paper, a conversation with the subject teacher is often the whole fix.

Say the honest thing about outcomes too. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any number attached to a promise about results is a sales device. What good IB and IGCSE tuition in India can reasonably offer is a clear picture of where the student is, a plan the family can see, and steady evidence that the plan is being followed.
items: Month one should produce a diagnosis you can read, not a grade jump
Habits change before marks; scores sometimes dip while reasoning grows
Four subjects tutored at once usually helps none of them properly
Between-session work is what makes the next session worth booking
Sometimes the honest answer is that no tutor is needed yet

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE tuition in India: the first two sessions
contentBlocks.body:
Prepare three things before the first session of IB and IGCSE tuition in India and it will not be wasted. The last two marked papers, with the marks the student lost still visible. The school report, including subject teacher comments rather than only grades. And the subject and level list for DP1 if it exists, or the tier the school has placed the student in for each Cambridge subject.

Session one should be mostly the tutor listening and testing. Expect them to work through a question the student got wrong and ask why each step was taken, because that is how a habit shows itself. Expect at least one thing the student cannot do that everybody assumed they could. Expect a short summary afterwards, in writing, that you can actually understand.

Session two is where the plan appears: which topics, in what order, against which deadline, and what the student does in the days between. For a transition family, that plan should name the summer explicitly. Finish the Cambridge syllabus properly, then spend part of the break on the three bridging skills rather than on next year's content.

If the fit is wrong, say so early. You can ask for a different match, and a tutor who is excellent for a confident DP2 student can be the wrong person for a hesitant Grade 9 one. Availability depends on level, subject and schedule, and the scarce combinations go first, so a family that starts asking in April has more choice than one that starts in the second week of the school year. Send the query with the syllabus codes in it, and the shortlist you get back will be worth reading.
items: Bring two marked scripts, the report and the DP1 subject list
Session one is diagnosis: expect questions, not a polished lecture
Session two should produce a written plan with dates you recognise
Ask for a different match early if the fit is visibly wrong
Scarce dual-board combinations fill first; asking in April buys choice

faqs.question: Is IGCSE good preparation for the IB Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Yes for content, less so for habits. A student who has done Cambridge IGCSE Extended Mathematics, a science and First Language English arrives in DP1 with most of the knowledge the first term assumes. What the two years did not build is the habit of justifying an answer, designing an investigation from scratch, and writing about an unseen text under time. That is why the useful bridging work is skill work rather than content revision, and why the transition summer matters more than an extra month of Grade 10 content coverage.

faqs.question: Should my child take Mathematics AA or AI after 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree the student is aiming at and on evidence from their own work, not on which subject sounds harder. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics are often advised towards AA, but the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement. Ask the tutor to set one AA-style proof question and one AI-style modelling question, and let the two attempts inform the conversation with the school.

faqs.question: How much does IB and IGCSE tuition in India cost?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by subject, level, city and whether the tutor travels, so no honest page can print a figure. What you can compare is structure. One-to-one costs more per hour than a batch and buys the whole hour. A home tutor's travel is built into the rate in practice. Scarce combinations, such as a tutor who teaches both 0625 and DP Physics, cost more than a widely taught one. Ask for the rate per session, the session length, and the notice period for cancellation before you commit.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travel to our locality on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes inside their own corridor, and rarely across a metro at peak hour. A tutor based in Bandra will hold a weekday slot in Juhu or Andheri comfortably; the same tutor agreeing to Thane or Kharghar usually starts rescheduling by the second month. In Bengaluru the Whitefield and Sarjapur Road side and the Jayanagar side behave like two different cities in the evening. Ask where the tutor lives before you ask whether they can come, and consider an earlier slot or a hybrid mix.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer between Grade 10 and DP1?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. First, close the Mathematics reasoning gap: a fortnight of writing out full justified solutions rather than answers. Second, read one scientific investigation's criteria and plan a small experiment end to end, so the shape of the internal assessment is familiar before school sets one. Third, practise unseen textual analysis twice a week on short passages. That is enough. Racing ahead into DP1 content is the least useful way to spend the break, and it usually wears the student out before the year starts.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be in the house and visible at the start and end, especially for the first few weeks and for younger students. That is a reasonable safeguarding practice and it also keeps the session honest on both sides. Set up the study space in a common area rather than a bedroom, with a table, decent light and no television in earshot. Ask the tutor for a short written note after each session so you know what was covered without sitting through the hour.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really handle both a Grade 9 IGCSE child and a DP1 sibling?
faqs.answer: Some can, and they are genuinely scarce. The two jobs need different mark schemes, different pacing and different feedback language, and a tutor who is strong on Cambridge past-paper technique is not automatically strong on criterion-based DP marking. mainEntity.name: Is IGCSE good preparation for the IB Diploma Programme?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes for content, less so for habits. A student who has done Cambridge IGCSE Extended Mathematics, a science and First Language English arrives in DP1 with most of the knowledge the first term assumes. What the two years did not build is the habit of justifying an answer, designing an investigation from scratch, and writing about an unseen text under time. That is why the useful bridging work is skill work rather than content revision, and why the transition summer matters more than an extra month of Grade 10 content coverage.

mainEntity.name: Should my child take Mathematics AA or AI after 0580 Extended?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the degree the student is aiming at and on evidence from their own work, not on which subject sounds harder. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics are often advised towards AA, but the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement. Ask the tutor to set one AA-style proof question and one AI-style modelling question, and let the two attempts inform the conversation with the school.

mainEntity.name: How much does IB and IGCSE tuition in India cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees vary by subject, level, city and whether the tutor travels, so no honest page can print a figure. What you can compare is structure. One-to-one costs more per hour than a batch and buys the whole hour. A home tutor's travel is built into the rate in practice. Scarce combinations, such as a tutor who teaches both 0625 and DP Physics, cost more than a widely taught one. Ask for the rate per session, the session length, and the notice period for cancellation before you commit.

mainEntity.name: Will a home tutor travel to our locality on a weekday evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes inside their own corridor, and rarely across a metro at peak hour. A tutor based in Bandra will hold a weekday slot in Juhu or Andheri comfortably; the same tutor agreeing to Thane or Kharghar usually starts rescheduling by the second month. In Bengaluru the Whitefield and Sarjapur Road side and the Jayanagar side behave like two different cities in the evening. Ask where the tutor lives before you ask whether they can come, and consider an earlier slot or a hybrid mix.

mainEntity.name: What should we do in the summer between Grade 10 and DP1?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three things, in this order. First, close the Mathematics reasoning gap: a fortnight of writing out full justified solutions rather than answers. Second, read one scientific investigation's criteria and plan a small experiment end to end, so the shape of the internal assessment is familiar before school sets one. Third, practise unseen textual analysis twice a week on short passages. That is enough. Racing ahead into DP1 content is the least useful way to spend the break, and it usually wears the student out before the year starts.

mainEntity.name: Does a parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for the whole session, but be in the house and visible at the start and end, especially for the first few weeks and for younger students. That is a reasonable safeguarding practice and it also keeps the session honest on both sides. Set up the study space in a common area rather than a bedroom, with a table, decent light and no television in earshot. Ask the tutor for a short written note after each session so you know what was covered without sitting through the hour.

Each wins something real. The school teacher knows the internal deadlines and sets the predicted grade; a batch costs less per hour and gives peer discussion; past papers cost nothing but time. The deciding question is whether the student's problem is content, habit, or simply unpractised.

h1: IB and IGCSE Tutoring: One Method Across Two Assessment Systems
heroTitle: One Method, Two Assessment Systems, Across India
heroSubtitle: The International Baccalaureate and IGCSE ask different things of the same student. A mark scheme rewards a complete, precise answer under time. A criterion descriptor rewards a documented process. A good tutor teaches both without confusing them, and knows the week in the year when the two approaches have to separate.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE tutoring in India works best when a home tutor teaches the shared skill first and the board-specific habit second. Reading the command word properly, showing working a marker can follow, revising from your own errors instead of from fresh notes: that part carries across both systems. Then the method has to fork. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reward an answer built against a mark scheme, timed and complete. The International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (MYP) and Diploma Programme (DP) reward work built against criterion descriptors, which ask what the student did and how honestly they recorded it. A tutor who treats the two systems as one will drill a Diploma student who needed planning taught, or leave a Grade 10 student exploring when the paper wanted speed.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram turn a two-board request into a shortlist in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Every request for IB and IGCSE tutoring in India starts the same way. You send a query, or book a free consultation, and the first questions are deliberately boring. Which board, which syllabus code, which level. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier is not the same request as Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL), and a tutor who is strong at one may be ordinary at the other. IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school calendar, your location and the weekly schedule you can actually protect, and then shortlists tutors whose profiles have been verified against those needs.

The two-board request is the one families get wrong most often, usually by understating it. A parent writes in asking for maths help for a Grade 10 child, and three questions later it turns out there is also a DP1 sibling who needs Economics, and the family would prefer one tutor in the house on one evening rather than two people on two evenings. That is a different shortlist. So say it at the start.

What comes back is a set of profiles, not a single name. You look at them, you ask for a demo or trial session, and you decide. If the fit is wrong after that session, or after six weeks, you ask for a different match. Nobody expects you to justify it at length. Availability is always conditional on who is free in your part of the city at the hour you want, which is why the location question matters as much as the syllabus one.

Home tuition is the default here. A verified tutor travels to your flat or house and teaches at the student's own desk, with the school's books and the student's own marked scripts in reach. Online and hybrid are both offered, and for some requests they are the better call, but the starting assumption is a home tutor.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, naming both boards and both levels
2. IB Gram asks about syllabus codes, level, school calendar, locality and weekly schedule
3. A shortlist of verified tutor profiles matched to those needs comes back to you
4. Arrange a demo or trial session before the family commits to anything at all
5. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability in your area
6. Ask for a different match at any point if the fit is wrong

contentBlocks.heading: Core and Extended tiers, MYP criteria, HL and SL: what the method sits on
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and it is usually followed by the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses exist in 9-1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1 throughout.

The IB side has three shapes a tutor may meet. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) has no external examination. The MYP runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, with every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or MYP 4. MYP eAssessment is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so there is no single national MYP examination anywhere in India.

The Diploma Programme is two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level (SL) with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to three points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed.

Those structures are why a single tutoring style cannot be lifted from one board and dropped on the other. Tier decisions, criterion counts and teaching hours all pull the weekly plan in different directions.
items: Cambridge Core tier caps at grade C; Extended tier reaches A* on the same syllabus
MYP: four criteria A-D, each out of 8, a total out of 32
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL with 240 recommended teaching hours
TOK and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points, maximum 45
MYP eAssessment is optional and decided school by school, not nationally in India

contentBlocks.heading: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625 and English 0500 beside their IB counterparts
contentBlocks.body:
Take Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. Both want algebra that does not collapse under pressure. The difference shows in what the paper asks for beyond the answer. A 0580 Extended candidate who shows a clear line of working and a correct final value has done the job. An IB Mathematics student at HL is also going to be assessed on an exploration, where the mathematics has to be chosen, justified and reflected on, and where a perfect calculation attached to a question nobody asked earns very little.

Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and IB Physics sit the same way. In 0625 a student learns to recognise the standard experiment, the standard graph and the standard source of error. In IB Physics the same student has to design an investigation of their own and defend the choices. Tutors who came up through one board tend to teach its instinct. So a Physics tutor trained on 0625 will often over-prepare a DP student for recall and under-prepare them for the explanation that carries the marks.

First Language English 0500 is the clearest case of all. The 0500 candidate is reading unseen passages and writing to a mark scheme under time, with a directed writing task that has a fixed audience and purpose. The MYP student writing for Criterion C and Criterion D is being judged on producing text and on using language, which is a different instruction even when the essay looks similar on the page.

IB Economics rounds this out. The commentary work rewards a student who can connect a real event to a diagram and admit the limits of the model. A tutor who only ever taught definitions and diagrams for a written paper will struggle to teach that, and it is worth asking a candidate tutor directly which of the two they have taught more recently.
items: Mathematics 0580 Extended rewards clean working; an IB exploration rewards justified choices
Physics 0625 trains standard experiments; IB Physics asks the student to design one
First Language English 0500 is unseen reading and directed writing against a mark scheme
IB Economics commentaries reward connecting a real event to a diagram honestly
Ask a tutor which board they taught most recently, and in which subject

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB and IGCSE tutoring in India happens, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the method question becomes a geography question fast. A tutor living in Bandra or Juhu can hold a weekday evening slot in Worli, Lower Parel or Malabar Hill without much drama. Ask the same person to reach Powai or Andheri at seven in the evening and the traffic decides, not the calendar. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar and Thane are effectively their own market: families there usually do better with a tutor based on that side of the water, and often accept a slightly later slot in exchange for someone who is reliably on time. IB and IGCSE tutoring in Mumbai splits along those lines more than along any syllabus line.

Bengaluru is the city where a good tutor and a willing family can still fail on distance alone. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City sit a long way from Indiranagar, Koramangala and Jayanagar, and the evening crawl between them can stretch a short trip badly. HSR Layout is a useful middle ground. Hebbal and Yelahanka work best with a tutor from the north of the city. Kanakapura Road families often end up on a hybrid week by choice.

Pune is kinder. Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Viman Nagar form one cluster; Baner, Balewadi, Aundh and Wakad another; Hinjewadi and Kharadi each have their own rhythm around office traffic. Delhi NCR spreads further: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri are one pocket, Gurugram along Golf Course Road another, and Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad each need a tutor who lives on that side.

Hyderabad runs on Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills. In Chennai, Adyar, Besant Nagar and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) are the usual requests. Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Coimbatore, Thiruvananthapuram, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai frequently have no local tutor for a specific syllabus code, and online becomes the honest answer. The same is true across Kolkata and eastern India, where Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat have options and Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna often do not.
items: Mumbai: Bandra, Juhu, Worli and Powai are separate evening markets, not one city
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road to Indiranagar is an evening trip worth avoiding
Pune clusters as Koregaon Park and Kalyani Nagar, then Baner, Balewadi and Aundh
Delhi NCR: Gurugram, Noida, Greater Noida and Faridabad each need a locally based tutor
Kochi, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati and Patna often have no local tutor for a given code

contentBlocks.heading: Two exam calendars inside one school year in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. School names below are context only.

The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and that is the frame every family here plans inside. The IB Diploma Programme examination sessions run in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, with results released in early July. Cambridge examination series run in February and March, which is a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June.

Put those together and a household with a Grade 10 child and a DP2 child can be facing two live exam runs inside the same term, with two different sets of internal deadlines feeding them. The Cambridge February and March series in particular catches families out, because it sits in the part of the year when the school is also closing out coursework and running mocks. Parents at international schools across India describe the same squeeze: reports, parent meetings, a Personal Project deadline in MYP 5, and a draft due for a Diploma subject, all inside three weeks.

This is the practical argument for booking home classes early in the year rather than in the panic window. Slots in the good evening hours, roughly five to eight on weekdays, get taken first in every city. A family that starts home tuition in June or July is choosing from a wider set of tutors than one that starts in December.

Also worth saying plainly: not every squeeze is a tutoring problem. Sometimes the answer is dropping one commitment for a term, and a decent counsellor will tell you that before selling you hours.
items: Indian academic year runs roughly April to March; DP schools here mostly sit the May session
Cambridge runs a February and March series offered only in India, plus June and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June
May DP results are released in early July, which sets the summer planning window
Evening slots between five and eight fill first in every Indian city

contentBlocks.heading: Do home classes, online or hybrid carry this method better in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Home classes carry the method best when the work is physical: marked scripts spread on a table, a maths page the tutor can watch being written in real time, a Physics diagram redrawn three times. For a Grade 9 or Grade 10 student building exam stamina, a home tutor sitting beside the desk catches the habit that a screen hides, which is the student quietly skipping the working and going straight to an answer. That single habit costs more marks across 0580 and 0625 than any gap in content.

Online carries the method better when the constraint is supply rather than attention. A DP2 student in Coimbatore who needs IB Economics is not going to find that person locally, and a strong online tutor beats a nearby generalist every time. Online also wins in the last fortnight before an exam series, when nobody wants to lose ninety minutes to Bengaluru traffic in each direction. Screen sharing a scanned script and annotating it live is genuinely good now.

Hybrid is the arrangement most households buying IB and IGCSE tutoring in India settle into. One home session a week for the subject that needs a person in the room, one online session for review, marking and quick doubt-solving. It also survives the weeks when a tutor is travelling or a child is unwell, which is the real reason continuity holds.

The trade-off stated plainly: home tuition gives the most attention and the least flexibility, online gives the widest choice of tutor and the weakest grip on a distracted student, and hybrid gives most of both at the cost of a slightly more complicated week. Families in Powai, Whitefield and Gachibowli tend to land on hybrid for exactly that reason.
items: Home tuition catches the skipped-working habit that a screen reliably hides
Online widens the tutor pool for a rare syllabus code outside the metros
Hybrid holds continuity through travel weeks, illness and exam-season traffic
One home session plus one online review session suits most two-board households
Before an exam series, moving temporarily online saves two traffic-heavy trips a week

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor can read both a mark scheme and a criterion?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask them to do it in front of you. Hand over one marked script from your child's school, a recent one with the teacher's comments still on it, and ask the tutor to say what the marks were actually given for. A tutor who genuinely works across both systems will talk about the specific instruction on the page. On a Cambridge paper they will point at the command word and the mark allocation. On an MYP task they will name the criterion and the strand inside it, and say which band the work is sitting in and what would move it up.

What IB Gram checks before a profile is shortlisted: identity, the qualifications and teaching background the tutor claims, and the boards and levels they say they can teach. That verification is real, and it is also not a substitute for your own judgement in the trial session. The two do different jobs.

What you should check yourself, in order. Whether the tutor has taught your exact syllabus code recently, not just the subject. Whether they can explain a grade boundary without hand-waving. Whether they ask about the school's internal deadlines rather than only the external exam date. Whether they are comfortable saying they do not know something. And whether your child talks more in the second half of the trial session than the first, which is usually the most reliable signal in the whole hour.

Be wary of anyone who offers a promised improvement in a fixed number of weeks, or describes themselves as first in the country. Nobody can honestly say that. A tutor who instead tells you the first month will be spent on gaps from last year is being straight with you, even though it is a less comfortable sales pitch.
items: Give the tutor a marked school script and ask what the marks were given for
IB Gram verifies identity, qualifications and the boards and levels a tutor claims
Ask whether they taught your exact syllabus code recently, not just the subject
A tutor comfortable saying 'I don't know' is usually the safer choice
Treat a promised improvement in a fixed number of weeks as a warning sign

contentBlocks.heading: The shared method, and the exact point where it has to fork
contentBlocks.body:
Everything useful in IB and IGCSE tutoring in India, on either board, comes down to three things. The student learns to read the instruction before answering. The student learns to make their thinking visible on paper. And the student learns to revise from their own wrong answers rather than from a clean set of notes, because a clean set of notes tells you nothing about where you actually fail. That is the shared method, and it is worth about as much in Grade 9 as it is in DP2.

Here is where it forks, named exactly. On IGCSE, the target is a mark scheme: a fixed list of creditable points, written by someone who will never meet your child, applied under time pressure. Preparation is therefore convergent. You find the standard question types, you learn what each command word is buying, you practise until the answer arrives fast and complete, and you mark your own work against the scheme rather than against your feeling about it.

On the IB side, the target is a criterion descriptor: a band of qualities, judged holistically against a body of work, often including work the student designed themselves. Preparation is divergent. You spend time choosing a good question, you document decisions as you make them, you reflect on what did not work, and you reread your own paragraph against the descriptor asking whether the evidence for that band is visible on the page.

Drilling a criterion-assessed task produces a generic piece of work that ticks nothing. Exploring a mark-scheme paper produces a thoughtful, unfinished script. Both fail for the same underlying reason: the student was trained against the wrong target. A tutor working across both boards has to be able to switch instruction mid-week, and to tell the student out loud which mode they are in today. Saying it out loud matters more than it sounds.
items: Shared: read the instruction, show the thinking, revise from your own errors
IGCSE preparation is convergent, aimed at a fixed and creditable list of points
IB preparation is divergent, aimed at a band of qualities judged across a body of work
Drilling a criterion task yields generic work; exploring a timed paper yields unfinished work
Name the mode at the start of each session so the student knows the target

contentBlocks.heading: What home tuition changes in a term across India, and what it does not
contentBlocks.body:
In the first three or four weeks, expect the visible change to be small and procedural. The student starts writing working out. The student starts attempting the question that used to be skipped. Marked scripts come back with fewer blank spaces. That is the honest shape of early progress, and a parent who was promised a jump in grades inside a month was sold something that nobody can deliver.

By the end of a term, roughly eight to twelve weeks of steady weekly home lessons, you should be able to see a specific, nameable change. On a Cambridge Extended paper, the long structured questions at the back that used to be left blank are being attempted. In MYP, a criterion that sat stubbornly in a lower band has moved, and the student can tell you why. If neither of those is true after a term, the problem is the match, the frequency or the diagnosis, and it is time to change one of them rather than add hours.

What tutoring does not fix. It does not fix a student who is not sleeping. It does not fix six subjects that were all chosen for the wrong reasons. It does not fix an integrity problem, and no tutor should touch one: every IB internal assessment is the student's own work, a teacher may give feedback on one draft, and nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit the submission. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than the school alone.

And sometimes the right answer is fewer hours, not more IB and IGCSE tutoring in India. A DP1 student in Salt Lake with three tutors and no free evening is not short of teaching. That student is short of time to think, and the counsellor who says so is doing the family more good than the one who adds a fourth subject.
items: Weeks one to four: working gets written down, skipped questions get attempted
By the end of a term: a named criterion moves, or back-page questions stop being blank
No tutor may write, rewrite or edit an internal assessment; the student submits their own work
Teacher feedback on one draft is allowed; a tutor teaches the skill and questions the reasoning
If nothing has moved after a term, change the match or the diagnosis, not the hour count

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE tutoring in India: what to gather this week
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send an enquiry about IB and IGCSE tutoring in India, spend twenty minutes collecting four things. The exact syllabus codes and levels for every subject you want covered, taken from the school's own subject list rather than memory. The last two marked scripts or task sheets, with the teacher's comments intact. The school's internal deadline calendar for the term, which is usually more useful than the external exam date. And the two or three weekday evening windows your family can genuinely protect, allowing for traffic in your part of the city.

That last one is where most plans quietly fail. A slot at six-thirty in Andheri or Whitefield sounds fine in July and becomes impossible in September once activities restart. Pick the window you can still keep in a bad week.

The first session should not be a lesson. It should be a diagnosis: the tutor reads the marked scripts, asks the student to attempt two or three questions unaided, watches how the student works rather than what they know, and comes out with a short list of what is actually wrong. Content gaps, writing problems and timing problems look identical from a report card and need completely different treatment. A tutor who starts teaching Chapter 1 in minute five has not diagnosed anything.

After that, agree the shape out loud. How many sessions a week, which subject gets the home visit and which gets the online slot, what the tutor will send you after each session, and when you will both review whether it is working. Six weeks is a fair review point. If it is not working then, say so early. Asking for a different match is a normal request, not a complaint, and the whole arrangement is built to allow it.
items: Collect exact syllabus codes and levels from the school's subject list, not from memory
Bring the last two marked scripts with the teacher's comments still on them
Note the school's internal deadlines, which usually matter more than the exam date
Choose evening windows you can keep in a bad week, not an ideal one
Treat the first session as a diagnosis, and set a six-week review date

faqs.question: Can one tutor genuinely teach both IB and IGCSE well?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only if they can name the difference in how the two are marked. Plenty of tutors have taught both and teach them identically, which is the actual risk. In the trial session, ask the tutor to explain how they would prepare a student for a Cambridge structured question and then for an MYP criterion task. If the two answers sound the same, keep looking. A tutor who says they drill one and coach planning for the other is describing the real distinction.

faqs.question: What actually changes between a mark scheme and a criterion descriptor?
faqs.answer: A mark scheme is a fixed list of creditable points applied to one answer under time. A criterion descriptor is a band of qualities judged across a body of work, often work the student designed themselves. In MYP each subject has four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, totalling 32 before grade boundaries convert it to a 1-7. Practically, one rewards speed and completeness, the other rewards documented reasoning and honest reflection on what went wrong.

faqs.question: My child finishes IGCSE this year and starts the Diploma next. When should the tutoring change?
faqs.answer: Change the method after the final Cambridge or Edexcel paper, not before. Right up to the last exam the target is the mark scheme, and switching early costs marks the student has already earned. The useful window is the gap between the exam series and the start of DP1, when a tutor can introduce what Higher Level actually demands, how 240 recommended teaching hours are spread, and what an exploration or investigation will ask. Two or three sessions in that window save months later.

faqs.question: Will a tutor who only drills past papers harm my child in MYP?
faqs.answer: It can, quietly. Drilling produces a student who answers quickly and writes generically, and generic work sits in the middle bands of a criterion no matter how fast it was produced. The MYP student needs to show a process: the choices made, the evidence gathered, the reflection on what did not work. Ask any prospective tutor to look at one of your child's returned criterion tasks and say which band it is in and what would move it. That answer tells you everything.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment or with coursework?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, and point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit any part of the submission, and neither can a parent. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The school submits it and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than by the school alone. Any tutor who offers more than this should be declined.

faqs.question: How do home tuition slots work on weekday evenings in Mumbai or Pune?
faqs.answer: Most families want five to eight in the evening, which is also when traffic is worst, so the practical answer depends on where the tutor lives. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region a tutor based in Bandra or Juhu can usually hold a Worli or Lower Parel slot; Powai, Thane and Navi Mumbai generally need someone from that side. Pune is easier, with Koregaon Park and Kalyani Nagar forming one cluster and Baner, Balewadi and Aundh another. Book early in the academic year for the better windows.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home session?
faqs.answer: Somebody responsible should be in the flat, particularly for younger students, but sitting inside the room usually makes things worse. Students self-censor when a parent is listening, and the tutor then cannot see where the confusion really is. A reasonable arrangement is a door left open, a study space in a common area rather than a bedroom, and a short conversation with the tutor at the end of each home visit. That gives you oversight without shutting the student up.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for this kind of method teaching?
faqs.answer: It works well for review, marking and doubt-solving, and less well for building a physical habit. Watching a student write their working out in real time is easier across a table than across a screen. What online does better than anything else is supply: a family in Coimbatore or Bhubaneswar looking for a specific syllabus code will often find nobody locally, and a strong online tutor beats a nearby generalist. Many households run a hybrid week for exactly this reason.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for a written diagnosis before you change anything. A month is enough to see procedural change, such as working being shown and back-page questions being attempted, but not enough to move a grade. If even the procedural change is absent, the likely causes are a wrong diagnosis, too few sessions, or a personality mismatch. Asking for a different match is a normal request and is built into how the platform works. Adding a second subject at that point rarely helps.

faqs.question: How is IB and IGCSE tutoring in India usually priced?
faqs.answer: Fees are charged by the session and vary with the level, the subject and the city, so Higher Level Physics costs more per hour than Grade 9 support, and metro rates differ from smaller cities. Home tuition costs more than online for the same tutor, because travel time is real time. Nobody can quote you a sensible figure without knowing the board, the level and your locality, and a platform that quotes one before asking is guessing. Ask for the structure, then compare like with like.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and cannot find a local IB tutor. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Online, usually, and it is a reasonable outcome rather than a compromise. Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru and Visakhapatnam frequently find nobody locally for a particular Diploma subject, and the same holds in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati and Ranchi. Where a local tutor exists for the more common subjects, a hybrid week works: home lessons for the subject that needs a person in the room, online for the rare one. Availability depends on who is free at your hour.

faqs.question: What should the very first session cover?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, not a lesson. The tutor should read two recent marked scripts, ask the student to attempt a few questions unaided, and watch how the student works rather than test what they know. Content gaps, writing problems and timing problems look identical on a report card and need entirely different treatment. By the end the tutor should be able to tell you which of the three you are dealing with, and what the next four weeks will target. Teaching Chapter 1 from minute five is a bad sign.

The school teacher suits a student who is broadly fine and needs to ask better questions. A coaching batch suits a confident student who wants volume and pace. Self-study with past papers suits a disciplined Grade 10 candidate. The trade-off that decides it is usually attention against cost.

h1: IB and IGCSE Tuition Classes for Mixed-Board Groups
heroTitle: Mixed-Board Tuition Classes Across India
heroSubtitle: A class that holds Grade 10 Cambridge candidates and DP1 students together is either the cheapest good decision a family makes or an hour paid for twice and used once. The difference is composition: who is in the room, what each student is actually working on, and whether the tutor planned one lesson or two.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE tuition classes in India are sold as one product, and they are not one product. A small home tuition group of three Grade 10 Cambridge candidates working through Mathematics 0580 Extended is a different animal from a room where two IGCSE students sit beside a DP1 student. The overlap between the two systems is real in a few places and imaginary in most. This page is about composition: which students can genuinely share an hour, how a bridging class between Grade 10 and DP1 should be built and paced, what a mixed revision class can deliver in the weeks before papers, and the batch size past which a group stops being a class and becomes a queue. Read it before you pay for a seat.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram compose a mixed-board class in India?
contentBlocks.body:
By asking who else is in the room before agreeing there should be a room at all. A parent enquiring about IB and IGCSE tuition classes in India usually opens with a question about fees and slots, and the honest reply is a set of questions back: which board, which grade, which syllabus code or subject group, and what exactly is going wrong. Two Grade 9 Cambridge students on Mathematics 0580 Extended can share a tutor comfortably. A Grade 9 student and a DP2 student cannot, whatever the subject on the label.

So composition happens before the timetable. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level or tier, the school calendar the student sits inside, location and the evenings the household can genuinely hold week after week. Where a group makes sense, families with matching descriptions can be offered the same verified tutor in the same slot. Where it does not, the shortlist is for one-to-one home tuition instead, and the family is told why rather than being sold a seat that happens to be empty. Availability is always subject to who is free in that locality at that hour.

Verification runs on the tutor, not on the group. Profiles are checked before they go live, and you can see which boards and which syllabuses a tutor claims to teach. A demo or trial session can be arranged before anyone commits, and a demo matters more for a group than for one-to-one, because it is the only way to watch whether the tutor can hold two levels of question in one hour without losing either student. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid.

If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, ask for a different match. That is a normal request, not a complaint, and it is far cheaper than a term spent in the wrong room.

2. Say whether you want one-to-one or will consider a small group
3. IB Gram shortlists verified tutors holding that exact board and level
4. Take a demo and watch the tutor handle two levels in one hour
5. Confirm the slot, or ask for a different match if the fit is wrong
6. Review the composition again after the first reporting cycle

contentBlocks.heading: Where Cambridge IGCSE and the IB Diploma genuinely overlap in one class
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with what each qualification actually is, because a shared class only works where the structures line up. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Both are usually two-year courses across Grades 9 and 10. Cambridge exam series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, then October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) is a different shape entirely. Two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to three further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. Exam sessions run in May and November, schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, and May results are released in early July.

So where can a mixed group sit? Content overlaps early and narrowly. A Grade 10 Extended student and a DP1 Standard Level student can share an algebra hour without either being short-changed. Assessment overlaps nowhere. One student is being marked against a mark scheme, the other against criteria, and a tutor who teaches both the same way is teaching one of them badly.

The transition summer between Grade 10 and DP1 is the one case where mixing is the entire point. A bridging course should run in four blocks, in this order:
1. Close the IGCSE content that DP1 quietly assumes, subject by subject, from the student's own marked papers.
2. Introduce criteria properly: read one real criterion aloud and mark a short piece of work against it.
3. Build DP1 habits: research question shape, referencing discipline, and a first look at TOK vocabulary.
4. Rehearse the opening weeks of DP1 content so that term one feels like revision rather than a shock.
items: Cambridge series: February and March, May and June, October and November
Edexcel International GCSE series: January, then May and June
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A* on tiered Cambridge syllabuses
DP: six subjects, three or four HL at 240 hours, SL at 150
TOK and the EE add up to three points towards a maximum of 45
Bridging works in the transition summer; DP2 and Grade 9 never mix well

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject: which mixed groups work, and which waste the hour
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is the subject where mixing succeeds most often, and even there it succeeds only at the edges. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, puts Core candidates on Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, and Extended candidates on Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier. DP Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA), which is algebraic and proof-heavy, and Applications and Interpretation (AI), which leans on modelling, statistics and technology throughout. An Extended student practising non-calculator algebra and an AA Standard Level student practising the same manipulation are doing genuinely the same work for forty minutes. After that they part company, because one is heading for a mark scheme and the other for an unfamiliar-context question.

Physics mixes badly. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 rewards equation recall and clean rearrangement; DP Physics rewards an argued explanation and a designed investigation. Put both in one room and the IGCSE student sits through discussion they cannot use while the DP student redoes substitution they mastered two years ago. If the family wants both covered, book the same tutor for two consecutive slots rather than one shared slot.

English is the quiet trap. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 trains directed writing and summary against a mark scheme. DP English asks for sustained analysis of how a writer builds meaning. The vocabulary of the two courses sounds similar enough that parents assume one class covers both. It does not.

IB Economics sits somewhere in between. Definitions, diagrams and the discipline of labelling axes transfer cleanly from a Grade 10 commerce background, and a mixed hour on diagram technique is honest value. The internal assessment portfolio is not group work, and should never be taught as though it were.
items: 0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 calculator, from the 2025 exams
Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1): Foundation or Higher, two calculator papers per tier
DP Mathematics AA is proof-heavy; AI is modelling and statistics with technology
0625 Physics and DP Physics rarely reward the same hour of teaching
0500 First Language English and DP English A share vocabulary, not method
Diagram technique in Economics transfers; the IA portfolio never does

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE tuition classes in India: where a mixed group can actually meet
contentBlocks.body:
A group needs a venue, and in Indian cities the venue decides the group. In Delhi NCR, a class drawn from South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri can meet at one family's flat because the distances inside that ring are short. Pull in a fourth student from Dwarka, Faridabad or Ghaziabad and weekday evening traffic will cost that child the first twenty minutes of every session. Gurugram (Gurgaon) groups work best when every family lives off the same stretch of Golf Course Road; Noida groups hold together around Sector 128 Noida, and a student from Greater Noida is usually better served online.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is a set of islands for this purpose. A home tuition group in Bandra, Juhu or Andheri is realistic. Powai and Worli each work internally. Lower Parel and Malabar Hill families can sometimes join a South Mumbai group. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar should be treated as separate catchments, not suburbs of the same class, and a parent searching for an IB and IGCSE tuition class in Mumbai should ask which specific locality the group meets in before anything else.

Hyderabad is friendlier. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District sit close enough that a group of three from different societies is genuinely workable, and Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills form a second natural cluster. Secunderabad and Kokapet families usually need their own group or an online seat. Families looking for an IB and IGCSE tuition class in Hyderabad often find the group forms faster than a one-to-one slot does.

Gujarat runs differently again. In Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway corridor can share a tutor, and Gandhinagar families can often join an early-evening slot. Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot rarely have enough students on the same board and grade in one locality, so an online group is the realistic form of an IB and IGCSE tuition class in Ahmedabad's smaller neighbouring cities. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, the same is true of Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula, which can pool between them, while Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur almost always pool online. Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata families ask the same question in the same words, and the answer is the same: a mixed board tuition class is worth joining only if the other seats are filled by students your child's work actually resembles.

contentBlocks.heading: Two exam calendars in one classroom: the school year in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and that single fact deforms every group timetable. The IB May session sits at the end of it, which is why schools here enter candidates for May almost without exception and why DP2 students vanish from group classes in February. Cambridge families face a different squeeze: the February and March series exists only in India, so a Grade 10 candidate entered for it is sitting real papers while the DP1 student beside them is still in ordinary term time. A class that ignores this will spend February teaching content to one student and past papers to another.

School mocks compound it. Most international schools in India run internal mocks in the weeks before the external series, and a mixed group will hit two mock periods that do not align. The honest answer is to plan the group's year backwards from both dates at enrolment, and to write into the arrangement that the group splits into separate slots for the four to six weeks around each series. Families who agree that in advance avoid the argument later.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. School names appear here only as context for the calendar pressures families describe.

Expectations differ too. International schools in India generally set coursework deadlines that cluster in DP1 term three, and they expect parents to track them. A tutor running home classes for a mixed group should know those deadlines, but should never be the person managing them. That is the school's coordinator, and a family that outsources the calendar to a tutor loses the one person with authority to change it.

February and March Cambridge series is offered only in India

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online groups or hybrid for a mixed-board batch
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition for a group means one tutor, one living room and two or three families who have agreed to share it. It is the strongest format for younger students and for anyone whose attention wanders on a screen, because the tutor can see a page, a posture and a half-written line at the same time. It is also the most fragile. One family moves house, one child falls ill, and the group is a one-to-one session that two families are paying for. Agree in advance what happens when a seat empties.

Online groups solve supply. A student in Kanpur or Rajkot who needs a mixed-board tutor will usually find nobody within a reasonable travel radius, and an online group pools students from Pune, Chennai and Dehradun into one workable class. The trade-off is real: screen-shared past papers work well, but the tutor cannot glance sideways at three notebooks, and a quiet student stays quiet for longer than they would in a room.

Hybrid is the format most mixed groups end up in, and it is a sound choice rather than a compromise. Run the teaching hour online, where materials and annotation are easy, and keep one home visit a fortnight for the work that needs a person in the room: a diagnostic, a timed paper under real conditions, a reset when the group has drifted. Families in Thane, Greater Noida and Secunderabad often settle here because a weekly home visit is not sustainable but a fortnightly one is.

Most families weighing IB and IGCSE tuition classes in India end up choosing between these three, so here is the comparison stated plainly. Home classes buy presence and lose reach. Online buys reach and loses presence. Hybrid buys most of both and costs a little more planning from the parent, because someone has to hold two different kinds of week in their head.
items: Home classes: best for younger students and for groups that need close supervision
Online groups: the only realistic format outside the metro clusters
Hybrid: weekly online teaching plus a fortnightly home visit for timed work
