contentBlocks.heading: How should you check a tutor who runs a mixed IGCSE and IB class?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask three questions and listen to the specifics rather than the confidence. First: which syllabus codes and which subject groups do you teach, by name? A tutor who genuinely runs mixed groups will say 0580 Extended and Mathematics AA Standard Level in the same breath and will tell you which parts of each they would teach together. A tutor who answers "IB and IGCSE maths" has told you nothing. Second: how do you mark? The answer should describe a mark scheme for one student and criteria for the other, in different words. Third: what do you do in the four weeks before the February series? A real answer involves splitting the group.

IB Gram checks a tutor's identity and claimed teaching background before a profile goes live, and the profile shows the boards, programmes and levels the tutor teaches. Verification is not an endorsement of every claim a tutor makes about their results, and no platform can verify a promised improvement, so treat any such promise with caution wherever you see it.

There is a check only you can run. Sit in on the demo, or at least the last ten minutes of it. Watch whether the tutor asks each student a different question. A tutor teaching a mixed group well looks slightly inefficient: they set one student working while they talk to the other, then swap. A tutor who lectures the whole hour at one level is running a batch, not a class, and one of the children in that room is being carried along for nothing.

Ask for the tutor's plan for the first four sessions in writing. It does not need to be long. It needs to name what each student will do.
items: Ask for syllabus codes and subject groups by name, not board names
Ask how marking differs between a mark scheme and criteria
Ask what happens to the group in the four weeks before a series
Sit in on the demo and watch whether each student is asked something different
Request a written plan for the first four sessions before confirming
Treat any promised improvement as a reason for more scrutiny, not less

contentBlocks.heading: What can a mixed IB and IGCSE revision class honestly deliver in India?
contentBlocks.body:
A mixed revision class can deliver three things well and should not be asked for a fourth. It can teach exam behaviour that is board-neutral: reading a question stem twice, allocating minutes to marks, showing method so that a marker can follow it, and checking units. It can run a timed paper under conditions, because sitting silently for ninety minutes is the same skill on every syllabus. And it can build the habit of self-marking, where a student marks their own script before the tutor does and learns where they flatter themselves.

What it cannot deliver is content repair. If a Grade 10 student has not understood moles and a DP1 student has not understood bonding, one hour cannot fix either while the other watches. Content repair is one-to-one work, and a family that buys IB and IGCSE tuition classes in India hoping for it will be disappointed in week three, usually quietly, and usually after paying for a term.

The sharpest use of a mixed revision class is the six-week run into a series, with one condition: the students must be at similar distance from their target, not on similar syllabuses. Two students who both lose marks by rushing benefit from the same hour even if one is sitting 0625 and the other DP Physics. Two students on the identical syllabus, one aiming to pass and one aiming for the top band, share nothing useful.

That is the composition rule in one line. Group by the problem, not by the board.

So when a class is advertised as covering both systems, the question to ask is not whether the tutor knows both. It is which problem the hour is built around, and whether your child has that problem.
items: Delivers well: timing, method presentation, question reading, self-marking
Delivers well: a full timed paper sat under real conditions
Cannot deliver: content repair for two different gaps in one hour
Group by the shared problem, not by the shared board label
Six weeks before a series is the sharpest window for a revision group
Same syllabus but different target bands is a worse match than it looks

contentBlocks.heading: Batch size, level spread and the point where a mixed class quietly fails
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every complaint about IB and IGCSE tuition classes in India traces back to one of two numbers: how many students are in the room, and how far apart they are. Two students is a pair, three is a class, four is the practical ceiling for a mixed-board group, and above that a tutor is delivering a lecture with occasional eye contact. This is not a rule about attention spans. It is arithmetic: in a sixty-minute hour, four students on two boards leave roughly twelve minutes of individual attention each once you subtract setup and the shared explanation, and twelve minutes is not enough to diagnose anything.

Level spread matters more than size. A group where every student is within about one grade band of the others can be taught as one group with differentiated questions. Stretch that to three bands and the tutor must run two lessons in parallel, which is real work and should be priced and staffed as such. Ask directly what the spread in the group is. A tutor who does not know is not tracking it.

Progress in a mixed group shows up later than parents expect and in a different place. In the first three or four weeks you should see the student's written method get tidier and their timing improve on practice questions. Grades usually move after the following school assessment, not before, and sometimes they do not move at all in the first term because the student was already being carried by memory and is now doing the harder thing properly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, in a group or one-to-one, and a class advertised as a claim to be first in the country is telling you about its marketing rather than its teaching.

There is also an honest case for stopping. If two of the three students have caught up and the third has not, the group has done its job and the third child needs a different arrangement. Say so early. Groups that outlive their composition waste more money than they ever saved.
items: Four students is the practical ceiling for a mixed-board group
Keep the level spread inside roughly one grade band where possible
Expect tidier method and better timing before any grade movement
Ask the tutor what the spread in the group currently is
Stop the group when only one student still needs it
No tutor can guarantee a grade in any format

contentBlocks.heading: Starting a bridging class or home tuition group in India: what to prepare
contentBlocks.body:
Bring evidence to the first conversation and the composition question answers itself. The single most useful document is a marked script: a recent test, a returned paper, an internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments. A tutor reading two marked scripts can tell you in ten minutes whether those two students belong in the same hour. A tutor working from a parent's description of the problem is guessing, however experienced.

Second, bring the calendar. School term dates, the mock window, the exam series each student is entered for, and the evenings your household can hold without renegotiating every week. A group built around an evening that only works in theory collapses by week four.

The first session of a bridging class should not teach anything new. It should establish where each student actually is: a short diagnostic on the assumed content, a look at how they set out working, and a conversation about what they think is hard. Expect the tutor to change the plan after it. A plan that survives the first session unaltered was not a plan.

For bridging classes IGCSE to IB specifically, the transition summer is the window, and it closes when DP1 begins. Once term starts, the bridging content competes with new teaching and loses. Families in Bengaluru, Pune, Chennai and across Delhi NCR who start this in the weeks after the Grade 10 papers finish get a calmer DP1 than families who wait for the first report card. If the summer has already gone, the work still helps, but it now belongs in a one-to-one home tuition slot rather than a group, because each student's gaps will have diverged.
items: Bring a recent marked script for every student joining the group
Bring term dates, the mock window and the exam series each student sits
Name two evenings the household can hold for a full term
Expect the first bridging session to diagnose rather than teach
Start bridging in the transition summer, before DP1 teaching begins

faqs.question: Can one class genuinely hold IGCSE and IB students at the same time?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only under conditions worth stating plainly. It works when the students share a problem rather than a board: both rushing, both losing method marks, both weak at reading a question stem. It works in early algebra, where a Grade 10 Extended student and a DP1 Standard Level student cover the same ground. It fails whenever the hour has to repair different content gaps, because one student then sits through teaching they cannot use. Ask the tutor which specific topics they plan to teach jointly and which they will split.

faqs.question: What exactly is a bridging class, and when should it run?
faqs.answer: A bridging class closes the gap between finishing Grade 10 and starting DP1, and the transition summer is the window. It has four jobs: finishing the IGCSE content that DP1 assumes, introducing criterion-based marking, building referencing and research-question habits, and previewing the first weeks of DP1 content. Once DP1 teaching begins, bridging work competes with new material and loses. If the summer has passed, the same content still helps, but it now belongs in an individual slot because the students' gaps will have separated.

faqs.question: How many students should a mixed-board batch have?
faqs.answer: Four is the practical ceiling and three is better. In a sixty-minute session, four students across two boards leaves each child roughly twelve minutes of individual attention once setup and shared explanation are subtracted, and twelve minutes is not long enough to diagnose a real problem. Level spread matters even more than headcount: keep the group within about one grade band. Ask the tutor what the current spread is. If they cannot tell you, they are not tracking it, which is itself the answer.

faqs.question: Does a home tuition group cost less than one-to-one home classes?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, because the tutor's time and travel are shared between families. Whether it costs less overall depends on fit. A group that suits your child is the better value of the two. A group that does not suit them is an hour bought at a discount and used at a loss, and families often keep paying for a term before admitting it. Fees depend on level, subject, schedule and locality, so ask for the structure in writing before the first session rather than after.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our home in Powai for a group of two families?
faqs.answer: Often, subject to availability, and the two families being close to each other matters more than either being close to the tutor. Within the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, a group drawn from Powai alone is straightforward. A group split between Powai and Thane usually is not, because one family is asking the tutor to absorb a weekday evening commute that will eat into the session. If the second family lives across the city, an online group or a hybrid arrangement is the honest alternative.

faqs.question: What can a mixed revision class deliver in the last six weeks before papers?
faqs.answer: Exam behaviour, and that is worth a great deal. Timing against marks, reading a question stem properly, setting out method so a marker can follow it, checking units, and sitting a full paper in silence under conditions. Self-marking is the other real gain: a student who marks their own script before the tutor does learns quickly where they have been flattering themselves. What six weeks cannot deliver is content repair for two different gaps at once. If that is what your child needs, book individual sessions instead.

faqs.question: There is no IB group near us in Gachibowli. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Widen the catchment before widening the format. Within Hyderabad, students from Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District can realistically form one group, and families often find a group assembles faster than a suitable one-to-one slot does. If that still does not produce three students on a matching description, an online group pooling students from several cities is the next step, and a hybrid pattern with one home visit a fortnight keeps the in-person element that younger students need.

faqs.question: Can a group class help with internal assessment or coursework?
faqs.answer: Only at the level of general technique, and this boundary matters. A tutor can explain what a criterion means, show how a published criterion is worded, and discuss the shape of a good research question with a group. A tutor cannot work on a specific student's draft in front of others, and should not. Internal assessment is individual work that the school authenticates, so anything closer than general technique belongs in a one-to-one session with a clear record of what was advised and what the student wrote.

faqs.question: We are in Chandigarh and there are no local mixed-board classes. Is online the answer?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with one caveat about age. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula can sometimes pool enough students between them for a local group, and that is worth checking first. Beyond that cluster, an online group is the realistic option, and it works well for Grade 10 and DP students who can sustain attention on a screen. For a younger child, consider a hybrid pattern instead: online teaching with a periodic home visit for supervised written work.

faqs.question: What if my child turns out to be the weakest student in the group?
faqs.answer: Raise it in week two rather than week eight. A well-composed group keeps every student inside roughly one grade band, so a child who is visibly behind the others is evidence that the composition was wrong, not that the child is failing. The fix is usually a move to individual sessions for a few weeks to close the specific gap, then a return to a group if one still fits. Ask for a different match if the tutor does not agree to reassess.

faqs.question: How do we tell a genuine bridging class from a repackaged Class 11 batch?
faqs.answer: Ask what the first session does. A genuine bridging class begins with a diagnostic on the content DP1 assumes and changes its plan afterwards. A repackaged batch begins teaching Class 11 chapters on day one and calls it a head start. Ask which criteria the course introduces and in what week. Ask whether students are grouped by subject or by grade. A course that cannot answer those questions is selling a timetable rather than a transition.

faqs.question: When should we move the group back to one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: When the group's shared problem has stopped being shared. That shows up in three ways: one student needs topics the others have finished, the tutor starts running two parallel lessons in the same hour, or progress stalls for one child while the others move. Any of those is a signal, not a failure. A group that outlives its composition wastes more money than it originally saved, so review the arrangement at the end of each term rather than drifting into the next one.

comparison.intro: Four formats, and the choice is usually settled by one trade-off rather than by fees. One-to-one at home buys diagnosis and presence. One-to-one online buys reach and easy rescheduling. A small online group buys peer comparison at a lower cost per hour. A large classroom batch buys the lowest cost per hour and a fixed, disciplined timetable, and gives up individual attention to get there.

heroTitle: How Rare Dual-Board Tutors Are Across India
heroSubtitle: Most tutors teach one board well and pick up the second later. That is why a search for someone local who genuinely holds both Cambridge IGCSE and the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme returns so little. This page explains how thin that pool is, which board pairings are realistically findable nearby, and what to do when none of them is.
introSummary: Searching for an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India usually means you want one verified home tutor, close enough to visit on a weekday evening, who can teach both boards. That person exists, but they are scarce in any single locality, and scarcer still in the subject you actually need. IB Gram takes the query, asks which boards, syllabus codes and levels are involved, and builds a shortlist from verified profiles, at home, online or hybrid. Sometimes that shortlist has one name on it. More often it has two: a specialist for each board. Below is how to tell which of those two answers is right for your child, and how to test a dual-board claim before you commit to anything.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a dual-board request in India turn into two shortlists?
contentBlocks.body:
A search for an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India is not one request. It is two, and treating it as one is how families end up with a tutor who is fluent on one board and improvising on the other. When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks which board each child is on, which syllabus codes appear on the school's subject list, which level, what the school calendar looks like this term, where you live and which evenings are free. The location question is not a formality on this search. A home tutor who can reach Powai on a Tuesday cannot usually reach Thane the same evening, and saying so early saves everyone a fortnight.

What happens next is a deliberate split. The requirement is broken into its parts, one per board and subject, and each part is matched separately against verified profiles. Where the same name comes back for both parts, that name is worth a long look, because it is uncommon. Where it does not, you are shown two people instead of one, and told plainly which of them would be travelling to you and which would be teaching online.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and on this search the trial matters more than usual, because a dual-board claim is easy to write on a profile and hard to hold up for ninety minutes. If the fit is wrong, you can ask for a different match. Availability is always subject to the tutor's own schedule, level and travel radius.

The search itself runs outward, in a fixed order, and most families find their answer somewhere in the middle of it.
items: 1. Start in your own locality, naming both boards and every syllabus code.
2. Widen to the neighbouring suburb a tutor can reach on a school night.
3. Widen to the whole metro, but only for a weekend session.
4. Split the request: one specialist per board, with the mode left open.
5. Keep the commoner board local and take the scarcer one online.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and Cambridge IGCSE: which pairs one tutor can hold
contentBlocks.body:
Set the two systems side by side before you judge anyone's claim. IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. It is usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and it is followed by the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), by Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or by a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1.

The DP is a different shape entirely. Six subjects from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well.

Below the DP the IB also runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and the Middle Years Programme (MYP), and this is where the pairing question gets real. A tutor who teaches Grade 10 Cambridge IGCSE and DP1 in the same subject is holding two versions of one body of knowledge. That is a reasonable ask. A tutor asked to cover PYP inquiry work for a younger child and HL content for an older one in the same evening is being asked to do two unrelated jobs, and the second one usually suffers.

So read a profile that lists every programme as a record of what the person has seen, not a list of what they teach at depth.
items: Cambridge IGCSE Grade 10 with DP1 in one subject: a realistic pair
MYP 5 with Cambridge IGCSE: same age group, different assessment language
PYP alongside any Diploma Programme subject: two unrelated jobs, rarely one person
Core tier IGCSE with Higher Level DP: a wide stretch for anyone
Edexcel International GCSE with Cambridge IGCSE: closer than either is to the DP

contentBlocks.heading: Which subject pairs across IGCSE and the DP are realistically findable nearby?
contentBlocks.body:
Three pairs come up again and again, and they are the ones you can realistically find within reach of your home: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 with IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) or Applications and Interpretation (AI), Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 with IB Physics, and Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 with IB English. Outside those three, the local pool thins very fast indeed.

Physics shows why the pairing is hard. Cambridge IGCSE sciences examined from 2023 run Paper 1 multiple choice for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, then Paper 3 theory for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, and practical assessment through either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school chooses. The weighting is 30% multiple choice, 50% theory and 20% practical. DP sciences, first assessed in 2025, look nothing like that: Paper 1 splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response work, and the internal assessment (IA) is a scientific investigation worth 20%, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, inside a 3,000 word maximum. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. HL and SL share that structure, with HL adding Additional Higher Level (AHL) content. A tutor who moves between the two without hesitating is telling you something real.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers. If one child sits Edexcel and the other sits the DP, the pairing changes again, because there is no separate practical paper to prepare for.

IB Economics is the honest counter-example. Most Indian schools offer nothing at Grade 9 and 10 that feeds straight into it, so a dual-board Economics tutor within travelling distance is not something to hold out for. Take that subject online and stop searching your locality for it.
items: 0580 Extended into Mathematics AA: the pair most often held by one person
0625 Extended into DP Physics: ask them to describe Paper 1B
0500 into IB English: strong on one board, uneven on the other
Edexcel International GCSE sciences: no separate practical paper in the plan
IB Economics: no feeder IGCSE course, so search online from the start

contentBlocks.heading: Dual-board scarcity across India, locality by locality
contentBlocks.body:
Dual-board supply follows the international schools, and those cluster. In Delhi NCR that means South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri on one side, with Gurugram (Gurgaon), Golf Course Road, Dwarka, Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad spread across the other. A parent hunting an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Delhi is really asking about one half of the capital region, not all of it.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves the same way. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli and Lower Parel sit close enough to share a tutor, while Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are separate evenings altogether. An IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Mumbai who lives in Andheri will hold a Bandra slot all year and quietly drop a Kharghar one. Bengaluru splits along corridors instead: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala, Indiranagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar, Kanakapura Road. An IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Bangalore is a question about which corridor you are on, because evening traffic between Whitefield and Jayanagar can stretch a short trip into an unusable one.

Hyderabad concentrates along Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills and Kokapet, so an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Hyderabad is often reachable across that whole western belt. Chennai runs through Adyar, Besant Nagar, Anna Nagar, Velachery and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), and an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Chennai working on OMR is drawn from a different pool than one in Anna Nagar. Pune sits either side of the river: Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Kharadi on one bank, Baner, Balewadi and Hinjewadi on the other, which makes an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Pune a crossing question as much as a subject one.

Beyond the six metros the pool narrows sharply. Ahmedabad, with Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and Gandhinagar alongside it, holds some local supply, so an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Ahmedabad is findable while the same search in Surat, Vadodara or Rajkot is not. Across Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge and Alipore carry nearly all of what exists, which is why families in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna should plan for online from the start. Northern India beyond Delhi NCR, meaning Chandigarh, Mohali, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun, southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, meaning Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru and Visakhapatnam, and central and western India, meaning Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik and Goa, all carry single-board tutors in fair numbers and dual-board ones only by chance. The phrasing families type varies: a local IB IGCSE tutor, an IB IGCSE tutor nearby, a dual board tutor near me, a both boards tutor India search. The supply sitting behind every one of them is the same. An IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India is, in practice, a question about which pocket of which city you happen to live in.
items: Delhi NCR splits into a South Delhi pool and a Gurugram (Gurgaon) one
Powai, Thane and Kharghar are separate evenings, not one Mumbai search
Whitefield and Sarjapur Road hold more dual-board supply than Kanakapura Road
Gachibowli, Kondapur and Kokapet usually sit inside one reachable belt
Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Indore and Nagpur: plan for online from the start

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar in India behind a dual-board home tuition slot
contentBlocks.body:
The two calendars do not line up, and that is the practical reason a single tutor gets squeezed. Cambridge exam series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, then again in May and June and in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. The IB Diploma Programme examines in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which suits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July.

Put a Grade 10 child on a February and March Cambridge series and a DP2 sibling on the May session in the same household, and January becomes the pinch point. One child is in final revision while the other is still finishing coursework and heading into mocks. A tutor holding both is being asked to carry two peak loads a few weeks apart, from the same diary. Two tutors simply do not have that problem, and for some households that is the whole argument.

Schools stack their own pressure on top. Mock windows, internal deadlines for the IA and the EE, subject-selection meetings for Grade 10 students moving into DP1, and report cycles that land at different times for different year groups. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Stonehill International School, Chirec International School, Mahindra International School and Pathways World School will recognise the pattern, even though every school runs its own version of it. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Ask the coordinator which series each child is actually entered for before you book anything. A home tutor engaged for a May plan when the school has entered a February and March series costs you a term you cannot get back.
items: Cambridge series: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January, then May and June
IB Diploma Programme: May and November, with India overwhelmingly entering May
May Diploma Programme results are released in early July
Confirm the entered series with the coordinator before booking a home tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits, online lessons and the hybrid split for two boards
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in plain terms. A home tutor gives you the one thing a screen cannot: they see the working your child actually writes, the diagram drawn in a hurry, the question skipped in silence. An online tutor gives you reach, which on a dual-board search is precisely the commodity in short supply. A hybrid week gives you both and costs you a simple routine, because two people, or one person working in two modes, means two sets of expectations for the household to hold.

Most families who search for an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India end up on the hybrid answer, and it comes with a simple rule. Keep the board with local supply at home, and take the scarce one online. For a lot of households that means Cambridge IGCSE taught in person, where handwritten method marks and rushed diagrams are easiest to catch, and the Diploma Programme subject taught online, where the pool of tutors is national rather than local.

There are exceptions worth naming out loud. A DP student drafting the scientific investigation gains from someone in the room reading it against Research design and Evaluation with them, page by page. A Grade 9 student who is disorganised rather than weak needs presence more than expertise, so the home lessons should go to that child even though the subject is the easier one. And a flat with one usable study table and two lessons at the same hour cannot run both online, whatever the supply map says.

Online is not the consolation prize here. It is how a family in Guwahati or Indore reaches the same specialist a family in Bandra can book in person.
items: Home tutor: catches handwritten working, silent skips and rushed diagrams
Online tutor: a national pool, which is what scarcity actually needs
Hybrid week: commoner board taught in person, scarcer board online
One study table and two lessons: settle the timing before booking
Home sessions still lose when the only local option is the weaker teacher

contentBlocks.heading: How do you test a dual-board claim in a single trial lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
Hand the tutor one marked script and ask them to mark it twice: once the way a Cambridge examiner would, against a mark scheme, and once the way a DP teacher would, against a criterion descriptor. A tutor who genuinely holds both will change vocabulary, change what they hunt for, and explain why. One who does not will mark it the same way twice and call the second reading a summary.

Then ask four questions with checkable answers. Which paper carries the practical for your child's Cambridge science, Paper 5 or Paper 6, and what is the difference between them. What is the DP scientific investigation worth, and what are its four criteria. What does the Core tier top out at, and what can Extended reach. How many points can TOK and the Extended Essay contribute between them. None of these are trick questions. A person who teaches both boards answers without pausing. A person who has taught one and read about the other pauses, and the pause is the information you came for.

Verification on IB Gram's side covers what a platform can see before a profile goes live: identity, the qualifications and teaching experience the tutor states, and the subjects and levels claimed on the profile. It cannot see whether that person is any good with your particular child at nine o'clock on a Thursday after a long school day. That part is yours, and the trial is where you find it out.

Watch for one pattern in particular. A profile listing both boards, every programme from PYP to DP, and a dozen subjects is usually describing availability rather than depth. Ask which two of those they have taught all the way to an exam series in the last two years, and listen to how specific the answer gets.
items: Ask for one script marked against a mark scheme, then against a criterion
Paper 5 or Paper 6: which practical route does the school actually use?
Scientific investigation: worth 20%, four criteria, a 3,000 word maximum
Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*
Ask which boards and subjects they taught to a series recently
Check identity and stated experience yourself, before any home visit

contentBlocks.heading: How rare is a genuine IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Rare enough that you should plan for not finding one. Start with the arithmetic of supply. Every locality has a pool of tutors. A fraction of that pool teaches international boards at all, rather than CBSE or ICSE. A fraction of that fraction teaches your subject. A smaller fraction again has taught both Cambridge IGCSE and the Diploma Programme through to a real exam series, not merely read the syllabus documents. Then apply your travel radius, your one free weekday evening and the level you need. Every filter cuts the pool, and the dual-board filter cuts it hardest of all.

There is a second reason the search disappoints. "IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India" is a phrase with steady demand behind it, and profiles get written to meet demand. A tutor who teaches 0580 confidently and has helped a couple of DP students with revision will list both boards, honestly enough in their own mind. The claim is not a lie. It is simply not the same thing as depth on both, and a parent reading the profile cannot tell the two apart.

So the useful question is not whether somebody nearby says they teach both. It is whether the pairing you need is one of the findable ones, and whether the board you care about more this year is the board they are strong on. A student who is comfortable on the IGCSE side and about to start DP1 needs the DP strength. A convenient tutor whose real ground is 0580 will feel helpful for a term and then stall, and the stall will look like the student's fault.

One more thing, said plainly. Scarcity is not a reason to settle, and it is not a reason to panic either. It is a reason to search in order and to stop at the first honest answer, even when that answer turns out to be two people rather than one.
items: Board, subject, level, evening, radius: five filters applied in that order
Dual-board depth is the filter that removes the most names
A board listed on a profile is availability, not exam-series experience
Decide which board matters more this year, then weight the search
Stopping at the first honest answer beats waiting for a perfect one

contentBlocks.heading: When convenience is quietly costing the stronger student in India
contentBlocks.body:
One tutor, one slot, one payment, one person to talk to. The convenience is real, and for plenty of households it is the right trade. It stops being the right trade at a specific point: when the more ambitious of the two students is the one whose board the tutor is weaker on.

Picture a household in Koregaon Park. The Grade 10 child is struggling with 0580 Extended and needs steady, patient work on method and shown working. The DP2 child is aiming high in Physics HL and needs somebody who can argue about a Paper 2 extended-response answer and read a scientific investigation draft against Research design and Evaluation. A single tutor who is strong on the IGCSE side will lift the younger child and hold the older one level. Nobody complains, because nothing visibly goes wrong. The cost is invisible, which is exactly why families keep paying it.

What progress should look like is worth setting down before you start. After four to six weeks of regular sessions you should see the student attempting question types they used to leave blank, reading a command word or a command term more precisely, and getting marked work back with fewer repeats of the same error. After a full term, the error log should have changed shape rather than shortened. If the only change is that homework now gets finished, the fit is wrong, and you can ask for a different match.

The limits are worth saying too. No tutor can guarantee a grade. Home tuition cannot replace attendance, school feedback or the coordinator's advice. And a DP student already at capacity with CAS commitments and stacked IA deadlines will not improve because a third evening has been booked. Sometimes the honest recommendation is fewer hours, not more.
items: Convenience wins when both students sit at similar levels of risk
Convenience loses when the ambitious student gets the weaker board
Four to six weeks: expect attempted questions and sharper command-term reading
One term: expect the error log to change shape, not disappear
Adding an evening to a full DP week usually subtracts rather than adds

contentBlocks.heading: Starting the search for a dual-board home tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
Prepare four things before you send anything. The board and syllabus code for every subject in question, copied from the school's subject list rather than from memory. The exam series each child is entered for. Two evenings a week that are genuinely free after school, activities and travel. And one piece of real evidence per child: a marked script, a report carrying criterion comments, or a returned IA draft.

Then send the query, or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists verified profiles against each part of the requirement. Say in your first message that you will consider two tutors rather than insisting on one. A shortlist for an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India comes back faster and stronger when the matching is not hunting for a single rare profile.

The first session should not be teaching. It should be diagnosis: the tutor reading the evidence you supplied, watching the student attempt one question unaided, and coming back with what they believe the actual problem is and how many sessions a week it needs. A tutor who starts lecturing three minutes into a trial has told you how the next six months will go.

After the trial, decide on one question only. Has anyone on this shortlist shown, rather than stated, that they can work on both boards at the depth your children need? If yes, book the home slot. If not, put the scarcer board online and keep the local board in person. Availability, as always, depends on level, subject and schedule.
items: Bring syllabus codes from the school's subject list, not from memory
Confirm which exam series each child has been entered for
Name two genuinely free weekday evenings before asking for a home visit
Supply one marked script or criterion report per child
Say you will consider two tutors, not one, in the first message

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches both IB and IGCSE actually available near me, or am I searching for something rare?
faqs.answer: Rare, and the sensible planning assumption is that you will not find one inside your own locality. Local supply follows the international schools, so a family in Gachibowli or Bandra has a better chance than one in Vadodara or Ranchi. Fix the subject and the level and the pool narrows again, because a dual-board claim at Grade 10 is far commoner than dual-board depth at Higher Level. Search your locality first, widen once, and if two honest specialists appear before one dual-board tutor does, take the two.

faqs.question: How do I test a dual-board claim in a trial lesson without embarrassing the tutor?
faqs.answer: Hand over one marked script and ask for two readings of it: one against a Cambridge mark scheme, one against a Diploma Programme criterion descriptor. It is an ordinary teaching request, not an interrogation, and good tutors enjoy it. Then ask which paper carries the practical for your child's Cambridge science, what the scientific investigation is worth, and what the Core tier tops out at. Someone who teaches both boards answers plainly. Someone who has taught one and read about the other hedges, and the hedge is your answer.

faqs.question: Should I hire one tutor for both boards, or two specialists?
faqs.answer: Two specialists, if the board that matters more to you this year is the board a single tutor would be weaker on. One tutor, if both children sit at similar levels of risk and the convenience of one slot and one conversation is what keeps the routine alive in a busy household. Write down whose result matters most over the next twelve months before you compare any profiles. That one line settles the question faster than reading ten profiles will.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor really travel to Whitefield or Sarjapur Road on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes if they already live on that corridor, and often no if they do not. Evening traffic across Bengaluru can stretch a short trip badly, so tutors protect their own radius whether or not they say so at the start. A home tutor based in Jayanagar will quietly stop taking a Whitefield slot by the second month, usually with a run of reschedulings first. Ask where the tutor is travelling from before you agree a time, and prefer someone whose home sessions already run in your part of the city.

faqs.question: Nobody near me in Kochi or Coimbatore teaches both boards. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Stop searching locally for the scarcer board and take it online, while keeping the other board in person if a local tutor for it exists. Smaller cities across southern India, along with Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Indore and Nagpur, carry single-board tutors in reasonable numbers and dual-board ones only by accident. Treat the hybrid week as the plan rather than the compromise. It is how a family outside the metro clusters reaches subject depth that no amount of further local searching would have produced.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor teach my Grade 10 and DP1 children in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and back-to-back home sessions are the most common way dual-board households actually run. Two things decide whether it works. First, whether the tutor can genuinely switch assessment language between a Cambridge mark scheme and an IB criterion, which the trial should establish. Second, whether your evening has room for two full sessions after school, travel and activities. Watch the second one carefully. A tutor arriving at seven for two long sessions finishes very late, and the younger child usually gets the tired half of the visit.

faqs.question: What does an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the board, the subject, the level and whether the tutor travels to you, so no single figure is meaningful and nobody should quote one before the requirement is clear. Higher Level Diploma Programme work and scarce board pairings sit at the upper end of whatever the local range is. A tutor travelling to your address prices that travel into the slot. Two specialists are not automatically dearer than one dual-board tutor either, because families usually buy fewer sessions of each.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for the board my local tutor is weaker on?
faqs.answer: It works well for content, argument and paper technique, and less well for catching sloppy handwritten working as it happens. For a Diploma Programme subject, where much of the value sits in discussing an extended-response answer or a scientific investigation draft against its criteria, online is close to equivalent. For Grade 9 and Grade 10 written method, agree in advance how scripts reach the tutor, and insist the student works on paper and photographs it rather than typing answers into a chat window.

faqs.question: We have had a dual-board tutor for a month and nothing has changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask for the evidence before you change anything. A month of weekly sessions should show the student attempting question types they used to skip and handling command words and command terms more precisely, even where the marks have not moved yet. If the tutor cannot point to anything that specific, ask for a different match rather than for more hours. If they can, give it a few more weeks, because marks tend to lag understanding by most of a term.

faqs.question: If we can only keep one home tutor, which board should it be?
faqs.answer: Keep the board where being in the room earns the most, which is usually the IGCSE side. Method marks lost in handwritten working, a diagram drawn too fast, a question abandoned halfway down the page: those are the things a tutor sitting beside a Grade 9 or Grade 10 student catches immediately and a camera does not. Diploma Programme work is more discussion than paper, so it survives a screen better. Reverse the rule if the DP student is the one in real trouble.

faqs.question: Our tutor is not working out and the February and March series is close. Can we change now?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a bad fit costs the most precisely when a series is near, so do not wait it out. Ask for a different match, send the same evidence again, and be specific about what did not work rather than saying it was not clicking. Expect the replacement to spend a first session on diagnosis rather than content, which is not wasted time. If the series is only weeks away, narrow the brief to past papers and marked feedback on the papers actually being sat.

First, whether the tutor can genuinely switch assessment language between a Cambridge mark scheme and an IB criterion, which the trial should establish. Second, whether your evening has room for two full sessions after school, travel and activities. Watch the second one carefully. A tutor arriving at seven for two long sessions finishes very late, and the younger child usually gets the tired half of the visit.

mainEntity.name: What does an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in India cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees depend on the board, the subject, the level and whether the tutor travels to you, so no single figure is meaningful and nobody should quote one before the requirement is clear. Higher Level Diploma Programme work and scarce board pairings sit at the upper end of whatever the local range is. A tutor travelling to your address prices that travel into the slot. Two specialists are not automatically dearer than one dual-board tutor either, because families usually buy fewer sessions of each.

mainEntity.name: Does online tuition really work for the board my local tutor is weaker on?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works well for content, argument and paper technique, and less well for catching sloppy handwritten working as it happens. For a Diploma Programme subject, where much of the value sits in discussing an extended-response answer or a scientific investigation draft against its criteria, online is close to equivalent. For Grade 9 and Grade 10 written method, agree in advance how scripts reach the tutor, and insist the student works on paper and photographs it rather than typing answers into a chat window.

mainEntity.name: We have had a dual-board tutor for a month and nothing has changed. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for the evidence before you change anything. A month of weekly sessions should show the student attempting question types they used to skip and handling command words and command terms more precisely, even where the marks have not moved yet. If the tutor cannot point to anything that specific, ask for a different match rather than for more hours. If they can, give it a few more weeks, because marks tend to lag understanding by most of a term.

mainEntity.name: If we can only keep one home tutor, which board should it be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep the board where being in the room earns the most, which is usually the IGCSE side. Method marks lost in handwritten working, a diagram drawn too fast, a question abandoned halfway down the page: those are the things a tutor sitting beside a Grade 9 or Grade 10 student catches immediately and a camera does not. Diploma Programme work is more discussion than paper, so it survives a screen better. Reverse the rule if the DP student is the one in real trouble.

mainEntity.name: Our tutor is not working out and the February and March series is close. Can we change now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and a bad fit costs the most precisely when a series is near, so do not wait it out. Ask for a different match, send the same evidence again, and be specific about what did not work rather than saying it was not clicking. Expect the replacement to spend a first session on diagnosis rather than content, which is not wasted time. If the series is only weeks away, narrow the brief to past papers and marked feedback on the papers actually being sat.

finalCta: Send one query with both children's boards, syllabus codes and entered exam series, and say which evenings are genuinely free. IB Gram asks the follow-up questions, shortlists verified profiles against each board, and arranges a demo or trial session before you commit to anything. Lessons run at home, online, or as a hybrid week split between the two. If the match is wrong after the trial, ask for a different one.
