h1: IBDP Tutors in India for the Two-Year Diploma Programme
heroTitle: Understanding the Diploma Before You Hire in India
heroSubtitle: The Diploma Programme is one qualification made of six subjects, two core courses and a set of conditions that can sink an otherwise good score. Before you hire anyone, it helps to know exactly which part of that structure your child is struggling with, and which parts a tutor cannot touch at all.
introSummary: IBDP tutors in India are usually hired subject by subject, but the diploma is not marked subject by subject, and that mismatch is where families waste the most money. A DP student sits six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, and adds up to three more points from the core. Home tuition in one weak subject may change very little if the real problem sits in the core or in a failing condition nobody explained. This page sets out the structure of the qualification in plain terms, maps where tutoring helps across DP1 and DP2, and shows how to read a school report and a predicted grade before you decide anything.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a Diploma Programme request in India become a shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
It starts with the subject and level, not the school. You send a query or book a free consultation, and the first questions are which DP year the student is in, which six subjects they take, which of those are Higher Level (HL) and which Standard Level (SL), what the last report said, and what the school has already flagged. Location and the evenings you can protect come next, because a two-hour HL session is hard to place on a weekday.

The reason for asking about all six subjects, when you only want a tutor for one, is that the diploma is a single award. A student scraping through HL Chemistry while quietly failing to submit Theory of Knowledge (TOK) work has a bigger problem than chemistry. IBDP tutors in India who ask only about the subject they will teach are giving up the one piece of context that changes the plan.

From there you receive profiles that are verified and that match the subject, the level and your schedule. A demo or trial can be arranged before you commit, and for DP work the trial should use the student's own material: a returned mock script, a marked internal assessment draft, a paper the student got wrong. Not a generic topic lesson.

Lessons run at home, online or in a hybrid pattern, and the mode is decided by supply and by the student rather than by preference. If the shortlist is wrong, ask for a different match. In DP2 especially, a mismatched tutor costs weeks the calendar does not have.
items: 1. Send the full six-subject list with HL and SL marked, plus the DP year
2. Add the latest report, predicted grades if issued, and any coordinator concerns
3. Name the evenings you can hold and whether home visits are practical
4. Review verified profiles matched on subject, level and schedule
5. Run a trial built on the student's own marked work, then confirm or re-match

contentBlocks.heading: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, and a core that decides the rest
contentBlocks.body:
The International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP) runs for two years, DP1 and DP2. A candidate takes six subjects from six groups. Three or four are studied at Higher Level, with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the remainder at Standard Level, with 150 hours each. Every subject is graded 1 to 7, which gives a maximum of 42 subject points.

The core adds the rest. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay (EE) are graded A to E and combine, through a matrix, for up to 3 further points. That is where 45 comes from. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) carries no points but must be completed. The diploma minimum is 24 points, subject to the IB's failing conditions, and those conditions are the part parents rarely hear about until late: an E grade in either TOK or the EE is itself a failing condition, whatever the subject total says.

Exam sessions run in May and November. Schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March, and May results are released in early July.

The practical consequence of 240 hours against 150 is not prestige, it is pace. An HL class covers Additional Higher Level content on top of everything the SL class does, in the same school week. A student carrying four HLs has chosen roughly a third more taught content than a student carrying three, and in DP2 that difference is felt every single week. This is the most common reason a family ends up looking for IBDP tutors in India in the first term of DP1.
items: Six subjects from six groups, graded 1 to 7, for a maximum of 42 points
Higher Level: 240 recommended hours; Standard Level: 150 hours
TOK and the Extended Essay combine for up to 3 points, taking the maximum to 45
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions
An E in TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition on its own
May and November sessions exist; Indian schools almost always enter May

contentBlocks.heading: Which DP subjects need IBDP tutors in India, and at what point?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics and the sciences generate the most requests, and they generate them at predictable moments. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level produces a wave of queries about eight weeks into DP1, when the gap between a strong Grade 10 record and HL proof work first becomes visible. Mathematics Applications and Interpretation produces fewer early requests and more late ones, usually around the exploration.

The sciences follow a different curve. Under the assessment structure first examined in 2025, Paper 1 splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, and Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. The internal assessment is the scientific investigation, worth a fifth of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, with a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. HL and SL share that assessment structure, and HL adds Additional Higher Level content.

So science requests cluster twice: once when extended response marking disappoints a student trained on numerical answers, and once when the investigation is due.

Economics, English A and the humanities behave differently again. Their difficulty is written expression under a command term, and a tutor helps most in DP1, when habits are still forming, rather than in the panic of DP2. The subject that most often needs help and least often gets it is the one the student chose because it looked easy. Ask which subject the student avoids doing homework in. That is usually the answer, whatever the report says.
items: Mathematics AA HL: requests peak about two months into DP1
Sciences: two peaks, extended response marking and the scientific investigation
The investigation carries four criteria of 6 marks and a 3,000-word maximum
Humanities and English A: help pays off in DP1, not in the DP2 panic
The avoided-homework subject is often the real problem, not the low grade

contentBlocks.heading: Where Diploma Programme teaching capacity sits across India
contentBlocks.body:
DP specialists cluster where the schools are, and the map is uneven. Delhi NCR holds the deepest pool: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka in the city, then Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. An IBDP tutor in Delhi can often keep two weekday slots close together; the same tutor asked to reach Faridabad on a Wednesday evening usually cannot.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves as several markets. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Malabar Hill and Powai are workable for an IBDP tutor in Mumbai holding evening slots, while Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar realistically need someone based there. Bengaluru splits east and south: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road, with an IBDP tutor in Bangalore rarely crossing between clusters after 5pm. Hyderabad is more compact, with Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District, Kokapet, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad. Chennai spreads along Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Alwarpet and Perungudi. Pune covers Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad.

Beyond the metros the picture thins quickly. In Gujarat, an IBDP tutor in Ahmedabad may serve Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway and Gandhinagar, with Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot usually online. Kolkata and eastern India, from Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat out to Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna, has real but shallow local supply at HL. The same is true of northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur; of southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai; and of central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad. In those cities the honest answer is that IBDP tutors in India are found online for HL subjects and locally for SL support.
items: Delhi NCR and Mumbai hold the deepest Higher Level pools
Bengaluru and Chennai supply is real but splits sharply by cluster after 5pm
Hyderabad's western corridor is the easiest metro for back-to-back home visits
Gujarat, Kolkata and eastern India carry SL locally and HL online
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Kochi, Coimbatore, Indore and Nagpur: expect an online HL tutor
Ask where a tutor lives before you ask what evening they are free

contentBlocks.heading: What the DP2 year looks like against a school calendar in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and the DP2 year is the tightest twelve months most students will have faced. Teaching of new content typically continues into the winter. Internal assessment deadlines in several subjects land between roughly October and January, set by the school rather than by the IB. Mock examinations are scheduled by each school, usually several months before May. Then teaching stops, study leave begins, and the May session arrives.

What that produces is a pile-up. A student can have a science investigation, an Economics commentary, an English assignment and the Extended Essay final version competing for the same three weeks, while the school is still covering Additional Higher Level content and mocks are being marked. Families searching from around schools such as Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School or Good Shepherd International School describe an almost identical November. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Home tuition planned against this calendar looks different from home tuition planned against a syllabus. In DP1 the work is building method and getting ahead of the internal assessments. In the first half of DP2 it is deadline triage and mock preparation. After mock results, it is targeted repair on specific papers.

Get the school's internal deadline list and mock dates in writing at the start of DP2. Without them, a tutor is guessing, and a guessed plan in DP2 is a plan that arrives a month late.
items: Ask the coordinator for internal deadlines and mock dates at the start of DP2
October to January is where most internal assessment deadlines stack up
Mocks sit several months before May and are set school by school
DP1 builds method; DP2 triages deadlines, then repairs what mocks exposed
May results arrive in early July, after the school year has already closed

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid across the two diploma years
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition suits DP1 best. The student is still building working habits, and a tutor in the room sees what a screen hides: the notes that were never made, the textbook still shrink-wrapped, the phone face-up on the table. Home classes also survive a bad broadband week, which matters in a household where someone else is on a call every evening.

Online wins on supply, and at Higher Level that is often decisive. A student taking HL Chemistry in Kochi, HL Economics in Raipur or HL Physics in Guwahati may have nobody within reach who has taught that subject guide, and a good online tutor beats a local generalist by a wide margin. Online also handles DP2 well, when sessions get shorter and more frequent and a fifty-minute slot before a deadline is worth more than a fixed two-hour visit.

Hybrid is the pattern most DP families arrive at by the middle of DP1. One home session a week for the long work, sustained problem sets, past paper conditions, a draft talked through, and one shorter online session for review or a specific question. It keeps presence without spending an entire evening on travel every time.

The trade-off stated plainly: home lessons buy attention and observation at the cost of travel time and scarcity, online lessons buy subject depth and flexibility at the cost of everything the tutor cannot see, and hybrid buys most of both at the cost of more scheduling work for you. For a DP2 student in a small city with a rare HL subject, online is not the compromise, it is the right answer.
items: DP1 favours home sessions: habits, notes and observation matter most then
Higher Level scarcity outside metros makes online the realistic option
DP2 favours shorter, more frequent sessions, which online delivers cheaply
Hybrid: one long home visit plus one short online review each week
Whatever the mode, insist on work being sent before the session, not during it

contentBlocks.heading: What should you verify before a DP tutor enters your home?
contentBlocks.body:
Verify three layers: who they are, what they have actually taught, and where they draw the line on internal assessment. Identity and claimed qualifications are checked before a profile goes live. The rest is your job, and it takes one conversation.

On teaching, ask which DP subject guide they work from and when it was last updated, because subject guides change and a tutor working from a retired guide will teach content that is no longer assessed. Ask how many DP2 cohorts they have taken through to a May session. Ask what they think the commonest reason is that students lose marks in extended response in their subject. A person who has taught the course answers that instantly and specifically.

On integrity, be direct. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft; it does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit a submission. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. The school submits the work and runs similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone. A tutor who offers to tidy up a draft is offering to put your child's diploma at risk.

For home visits, settle the practical things in week one: which room, who is at home, gate and society entry, and what happens when a session is missed. Those conversations are much easier before the first lesson than after the third.
items: Ask which DP subject guide they teach from and when it was issued
Ask how many DP2 groups they have taken through to a May session
Confirm in words that they will not edit or rewrite an internal assessment
Agree the room, the open door and who is at home for a home visit
Register the tutor's fixed evenings with the building or society gate

contentBlocks.heading: Where the 45 points actually come from, and where they leak
contentBlocks.body:
A parent who can hold the arithmetic in their head makes better decisions than one who cannot, so here it is. Six subjects, each 1 to 7, gives 42. TOK and the Extended Essay together give up to 3. That is 45. The diploma is awarded at 24, subject to the failing conditions.

Points leak in three predictable places. The first is a single subject that was chosen badly and has been at a 3 since the first report; no amount of tutoring in DP2 rebuilds two years of foundations, and the honest conversation is about whether the level can be changed while there is still time. The second is the core. TOK has two assessments: an exhibition of three objects linked to one of 35 prescribed prompts, up to 950 words, internally assessed and worth a third of the grade, and an essay on one of six prescribed titles, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed and worth two thirds. The Extended Essay is an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of work, supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded along the way. Students treat both as side projects, and then discover the failing conditions.

The third leak is internal assessment work submitted late or thin. Internal assessments carry serious weight in most subjects and are marked before any examination is written. A student who loses marks there has to make them up under exam conditions, which is the hardest possible way to do it.

Note that the EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so never work from criterion mark allocations you found online. Follow the version your DP coordinator issues, and tell your tutor to do the same.
items: 42 subject points plus up to 3 from the core equals a maximum of 45
TOK: exhibition of three objects at 950 words, essay at 1,600 words
The Extended Essay is up to 4,000 words and around 40 hours of work
A subject stuck at a low grade since DP1 is a level decision, not a tuition one
Follow the Extended Essay guidance your coordinator issues, not an older version

contentBlocks.heading: Reading a DP report and a predicted grade without panicking
contentBlocks.body:
A DP report is not a percentage, and reading it as one leads families to hire in the wrong month. Subject grades are 1 to 7 and are usually the teacher's best current estimate against IB grade boundaries, which move between sessions. A 5 in DP1 term one and a 5 in DP2 term one mean quite different things, because the second is measured against far more content.

The predicted grade is a separate thing again. The school forms it, the school submits it, and no tutor can change it. What a tutor can do is change the evidence the school is looking at: better mock scripts, a stronger internal assessment, work that arrives on time. That is a slow lever, and it works only if there is enough time left for new evidence to accumulate.

On progress, expect the first two or three weeks to produce diagnosis rather than marks. By around six weeks you should see something concrete: a mock question type that used to be skipped now attempted, working set out so method marks survive, a draft that responds to a criterion instead of describing the topic. If nothing has changed and the tutor cannot name this month's focus, change tutor.

And be wary of what is promised. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a promised improvement in points is a claim to walk away from, and so is a claim to be first in the country. Availability of IBDP tutors in India depends on the subject, the level and the hour you need, and at HL in a smaller city it can be genuinely limited.
items: Subject grades are 1 to 7 against moving boundaries, not percentages
The school forms and submits predicted grades; a tutor cannot alter them
A tutor changes the evidence, which takes time to accumulate
Weeks one to three are diagnosis; expect specific change by around week six
Treat any promised point gain as a reason to look elsewhere

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in India for DP1 or DP2
contentBlocks.body:
Gather four things before you send anything. The six-subject list with HL and SL marked. The most recent report, with the 1 to 7 grades and the teacher comments, not just the grades. Any internal assessment deadlines and mock dates the school has issued. And a clear statement of which evenings are actually free, allowing for CAS and school commitments.

Then name the problem as precisely as you can. Not "Physics is weak" but "loses most of the extended response marks and has not started the investigation". A specific problem produces a specific shortlist; a vague one produces a general tutor.

The first session should use the student's own material. A returned mock paper, a marked draft, a set of questions they got wrong. By the end of it you should have an answer to one question: what exactly is this student losing marks for? If the tutor cannot say, the trial has told you something useful anyway.

After that, review monthly in DP1 and fortnightly in DP2. Sessions should get shorter and sharper as May approaches, not longer. A DP2 student sitting through three-hour evening sessions in March is a student who is not sleeping, and tired students lose more marks than untutored ones. Home tuition should reduce the load on the week, not add to it.

One last thing that families forget until it bites. Tell the tutor early if the student is also preparing for university entrance tests or a portfolio, because those deadlines sit outside the school calendar and nobody at school is tracking them. A home tutor planning a DP2 revision block around May will plan it wrongly if an entrance examination lands in January. And if your child is in DP1 now, book the review conversation for the end of the school year before the year gets away from you; that is the point where dropping a subject to Standard Level, or stopping tuition altogether, is still an easy decision rather than a fraught one.
items: Bring the six-subject list, the latest report, deadlines and free evenings
State the problem as a specific loss of marks, not as a weak subject
Use the student's own marked work in the first session
Review monthly in DP1 and fortnightly through DP2
Sessions should shorten as May approaches; protect sleep over extra hours

faqs.question: My child takes six subjects. How many can we realistically tutor at once?
faqs.answer: One properly, two at a stretch, three almost never. A DP student already has around thirty taught periods a week plus internal assessment work, CAS and the core, and adding three tutored subjects turns the week into something no teenager sustains through DP2. If three subjects genuinely look weak, the problem is usually not three separate content gaps but one shared cause: time, organisation or a subject choice that was wrong from the start. Fix the cause and the number of tutors needed usually drops to one.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Higher Level and Standard Level in practice?
faqs.answer: Higher Level is 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra hours carry Additional Higher Level content on top of everything the SL course covers. Week to week that means more new material, longer problems and, in the sciences, extra examination content rather than a different investigation. It is not simply harder marking of the same course. A student carrying four HLs has chosen roughly a third more content than one carrying three, which is why four HLs is the single most common cause of a difficult DP1.

faqs.question: Can a tutor change my child's predicted grade?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor who suggests otherwise should be ruled out immediately. The school forms the predicted grade and the school submits it. What a tutor can change is the evidence the school sees: a stronger mock script, an internal assessment handed in on time and properly addressing the criteria, classwork that shows the student can now do what they could not in November. That is a slow mechanism, and it needs enough time left for new evidence to build before predictions are finalised.

faqs.question: Is home tuition worth it when we live far from the tutor, say in Thane or Greater Noida?
faqs.answer: Often not on a weekday. Evening traffic between the outer suburbs and the central pockets of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region or Delhi NCR can stretch a short trip badly, and a tutor who arrives late and leaves early is charging for time nobody teaches in. Two better options exist: find a tutor already living in your area, even if their subject match is slightly weaker, or run a hybrid week with one weekend home session and shorter online sessions midweek. Both usually beat a distant weekday home visit.

faqs.question: When in DP1 should we start, and is it too late in DP2?
faqs.answer: Starting in the second term of DP1 is the most useful moment: the first reports have arrived, the student knows what the course feels like, and there is enough time left for method to change. It is not too late in DP2, but the work changes shape. From roughly January the goal stops being new learning and becomes recovering marks on paper types the mocks exposed. Starting after mock results with a clear script to work from is far more effective than starting vaguely in September.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do about the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Less than families hope, and deliberately so. The Extended Essay is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with recorded reflection sessions, and it must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach research question design, argument structure and the discipline of reading a criterion. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit any of it. The same applies to the TOK exhibition and essay. Since an E in either is a failing condition, the useful help here is usually about starting early rather than about polishing prose.

faqs.question: Should a parent stay in the room during home sessions?
faqs.answer: Be in the flat, not in the room. DP students in particular stop admitting confusion when a parent is listening, and admitting confusion is most of what a good session is for. Keep lessons in a shared space such as a study or dining area with the door open rather than in a bedroom. Ask the tutor for a short summary at the end of each session and a written note monthly. That gives you more real information than sitting through two hours ever will.

faqs.question: How do we find a tutor for a Higher Level subject in a city like Kochi or Indore?
faqs.answer: Assume online and be pleasantly surprised if not. DP teaching capacity sits where IB schools cluster, so Kochi, Coimbatore, Indore, Nagpur, Bhubaneswar and Chandigarh often have someone who can support SL work but nobody who has taught a specific HL subject guide. An online specialist from another city solves this properly. Where the student also needs supervision and structure, a local tutor for study habits combined with an online HL specialist for subject depth works better than compromising on either.

faqs.question: The school says everything is fine but the grades are 4s. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask a more specific question before hiring anyone. Request the mark breakdown behind the grade, the criteria or paper sections where marks were lost, and what the teacher thinks the cause is. A 4 built on weak extended response needs different help from a 4 built on missing content or on work handed in late. Many schools will also arrange subject support before you pay for anything outside. If the answer after that conversation is still vague, take a marked script to a trial session and ask a subject specialist the same question.

faqs.question: How long should a DP session be, and how often?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes to two hours once a week suits DP1, where sustained work on problem sets and drafts matters. DP2 usually works better with two shorter sessions, because the student needs feedback loops rather than long teaching blocks. Avoid three-hour evening sessions entirely; concentration does not survive them and sleep matters more to a DP2 student's marks than an extra hour of past papers. Adjust around mocks and deadlines rather than keeping a fixed pattern all year.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so and ask for a different match. It is a normal request and it costs nothing to make. Before you do, check the diagnosis is not the problem: ask the tutor what specifically they are working on this month and what evidence they expect to see change. A clear answer that is taking time is different from no answer at all. If it is the second, replace them, and do it quickly. In DP2 a wasted month is a month the calendar never returns.

mainEntity.name: My child takes six subjects. How many can we realistically tutor at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: One properly, two at a stretch, three almost never. A DP student already has around thirty taught periods a week plus internal assessment work, CAS and the core, and adding three tutored subjects turns the week into something no teenager sustains through DP2. If three subjects genuinely look weak, the problem is usually not three separate content gaps but one shared cause: time, organisation or a subject choice that was wrong from the start. Fix the cause and the number of tutors needed usually drops to one.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Higher Level and Standard Level in practice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Higher Level is 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra hours carry Additional Higher Level content on top of everything the SL course covers. Week to week that means more new material, longer problems and, in the sciences, extra examination content rather than a different investigation. It is not simply harder marking of the same course. A student carrying four HLs has chosen roughly a third more content than one carrying three, which is why four HLs is the single most common cause of a difficult DP1.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor change my child's predicted grade?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and any tutor who suggests otherwise should be ruled out immediately. The school forms the predicted grade and the school submits it. What a tutor can change is the evidence the school sees: a stronger mock script, an internal assessment handed in on time and properly addressing the criteria, classwork that shows the student can now do what they could not in November. That is a slow mechanism, and it needs enough time left for new evidence to build before predictions are finalised.

mainEntity.name: Is home tuition worth it when we live far from the tutor, say in Thane or Greater Noida?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often not on a weekday. Evening traffic between the outer suburbs and the central pockets of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region or Delhi NCR can stretch a short trip badly, and a tutor who arrives late and leaves early is charging for time nobody teaches in. Two better options exist: find a tutor already living in your area, even if their subject match is slightly weaker, or run a hybrid week with one weekend home session and shorter online sessions midweek. Both usually beat a distant weekday home visit.

mainEntity.name: When in DP1 should we start, and is it too late in DP2?

acceptedAnswer.text: Starting in the second term of DP1 is the most useful moment: the first reports have arrived, the student knows what the course feels like, and there is enough time left for method to change. It is not too late in DP2, but the work changes shape. From roughly January the goal stops being new learning and becomes recovering marks on paper types the mocks exposed. Starting after mock results with a clear script to work from is far more effective than starting vaguely in September.

mainEntity.name: What can a tutor do about the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Less than families hope, and deliberately so. The Extended Essay is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with recorded reflection sessions, and it must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach research question design, argument structure and the discipline of reading a criterion. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit any of it. The same applies to the TOK exhibition and essay. Since an E in either is a failing condition, the useful help here is usually about starting early rather than about polishing prose.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent stay in the room during home sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Be in the flat, not in the room. DP students in particular stop admitting confusion when a parent is listening, and admitting confusion is most of what a good session is for. Keep lessons in a shared space such as a study or dining area with the door open rather than in a bedroom. Ask the tutor for a short summary at the end of each session and a written note monthly. That gives you more real information than sitting through two hours ever will.

comparison.heading: How do the four ways of getting DP help compare in India?
comparison.intro: A DP student can be taught one to one at home, one to one online, in a coaching batch, or through a recorded course they work alone. Each buys something real. The home tutor buys attention and observation, online buys access to subject specialists, a batch buys volume of practice at a lower cost per hour, and a recorded course buys availability at two in the morning before a mock. The deciding question is whether the student's problem is content or behaviour.

h1: IBDP Home Tutors in India for DP1 and DP2 Workloads
heroTitle: Home Tutors Who Fit a Real DP Week in India
heroSubtitle: A Diploma student is usually not short of teaching. They are short of hours. This page is about the arithmetic of the DP week first, and only then about the tutor: what a home session should look like when the student already has coursework due, service commitments and a mock cycle closing in.
introSummary: IBDP home tutors in India work inside a week that is already full before they arrive, and the good ones plan around that rather than ignoring it. A Diploma Programme student carries six subjects, three or four of them at Higher Level, internal assessment drafts across most of those subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, all running at once. Adding two home sessions to that week without removing anything is how students stop sleeping. So the useful question is not how many hours of home tuition to buy. It is which hour of the existing week the tutor replaces, what gets dropped to make room, and when the tuition itself should be cut back.

contentBlocks.heading: How are IBDP home tutors in India matched to an already full week?
contentBlocks.body:
By starting from the calendar rather than from the subject. Before any tutor is shortlisted, the questions are about what the student is already carrying: which subjects at which level, which internal assessment drafts are due and when, what the service commitment actually costs in hours each week, and when the school has set its DP2 mock examinations. Only after that does the conversation move to who teaches Chemistry Higher Level.

You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the programme year, the six subjects and their levels, the school's deadline calendar, your locality and the slots your household can hold. That last question is harder for a Diploma family than for any other. A DP2 student home at half past four with a rehearsal on Tuesday, a service project on Saturday morning and a draft due on Friday has perhaps two protectable evenings, and pretending otherwise produces a timetable that collapses in week three.

The shortlist comes from verified profiles, and in DP the level detail matters more than the subject name. Somebody who teaches Standard Level Economics well may not be the right person for the Higher Level policy work. Say the level out loud when you ask.

Then the trial. A demo session can be arranged before the family commits, and there is one thing worth watching above all others in a DP trial. Does the tutor ask to see the school's deadline list? A tutor who plans a session without knowing that a 3,000-word report is due in eleven days is going to teach the wrong thing at the wrong time. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match and name the reason.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with the six subjects and levels listed
2. Hand over the school's deadline calendar and the mock dates before matching begins
3. Count the hours already taken by service commitments and rehearsals honestly
4. Read the verified shortlist, checking level taught rather than subject name
5. Run a trial and watch whether the tutor asks to see the deadline list

contentBlocks.heading: Six subjects, three Higher Levels and a core: what actually fills DP1 and DP2
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) is a two-year course across DP1 and DP2. Six subjects are taken from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Every subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the International Baccalaureate's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed alongside all of it.

Write those hours out and the week stops being abstract. Three HL subjects at 240 recommended hours each, three SL subjects at 150, plus a core that carries its own teaching and its own deadlines. Schools fit that into two years of timetable, and the student fits the rest into evenings and weekends.

CAS is where families consistently underestimate the cost. It is not assessed with a grade, so it reads as optional on a report and it is not. Service projects need planning, travel and reflection, and the travel in particular is expensive in a city where a Saturday morning commitment eats half the day.

This is the context IBDP home tutors in India have to work inside. A home tutor arriving with a plan built for a student with free evenings is planning for somebody who does not exist. The realistic shape is one or two subjects tutored at once, one session each per week in DP1, with the option to move a single HL subject to two sessions during the mock season and then back down again afterwards.
items: Three or four HL subjects at 240 recommended hours; the rest SL at 150
Each subject graded 1 to 7; TOK and the EE add up to 3 points
45 is the maximum score; 24 is the diploma minimum, subject to failing conditions
CAS carries no grade and still costs real hours every single week
One or two tutored subjects at a time is the realistic ceiling in DP2

contentBlocks.heading: Where the internal assessments land, and why they stack
contentBlocks.body:
Internal assessment is the reason a Diploma week suddenly breaks in the second half of DP1. Each subject sets its own coursework, schools set their own internal deadlines, and nobody coordinates across the six.

In the sciences, first assessed in 2025, the internal assessment is the scientific investigation. It is worth 20% of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, with a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. The written papers sit alongside it: Paper 1 has two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, and Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response work. HL and SL share that assessment structure, with HL adding Additional Higher Level content.

Mathematics runs its own version. The exploration is the same task for Analysis and Approaches and for Applications and Interpretation at both levels: 20% of the final grade, 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 on five criteria. A Presentation carries 4 marks, B Mathematical communication 4, C Personal engagement 3, D Reflection 3, and E Use of mathematics 6. HL work is judged against a higher standard on criterion E. The teacher may comment on one draft, and the work must be the student's own.

Now stack them. A student with two sciences and mathematics is writing three substantial pieces of coursework, plus TOK and the Extended Essay, in overlapping months. A home tutor who understands that sequencing will spend three weeks on research design before data collection rather than on syllabus content, because that is what is actually due. A tutor who only teaches content will teach content while the deadline passes.
items: The science investigation is 20%, four criteria of 6 marks, maximum 3,000 words
Group investigation of up to three students, but an individual written report each
Paper 1A is multiple choice, 1B data-based; Paper 2 adds extended response
The mathematics exploration is 20%, 12 to 20 pages, 20 marks on five criteria
Criterion E carries 6 marks and is judged to a higher standard at HL

contentBlocks.heading: Finding a weekday evening slot for a DP student across India
contentBlocks.body:
A Diploma session is often ninety minutes or two hours rather than one, and that single fact changes the geography for IBDP home tutors in India. A tutor will cross a city for a two-hour HL booking that they would never cross it for a forty-minute one. So DP supply behaves differently from junior-school supply in every metro.

In Delhi NCR, South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri hold the densest pool, and Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road is close behind. Noida and Sector 128 Noida are workable for a tutor already on that side. Dwarka, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida are genuinely harder after five o'clock, and families there tend to end up hybrid. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the pattern repeats: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Malabar Hill and Powai are reachable, while Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar and Thane need a tutor who already lives locally.

Bengaluru punishes optimism about distance. Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar work well together. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road each behave as separate markets on a weekday evening. Hyderabad is easier than most: Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District and Kokapet sit close enough that a tutor can hold two households in an evening, though Secunderabad is a longer run.

Pune spreads along its own corridors. Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Viman Nagar form one pocket; Baner, Balewadi, Aundh and Wakad another; Hinjewadi and Kharadi sit at the ends. A request for an IBDP home tutor in Pune from Hinjewadi and the same request from Koregaon Park are not equally easy to fill. Chennai and Ahmedabad follow the same rule.
items: A two-hour HL booking pulls a tutor further than a short session ever will
South Delhi and Golf Course Road hold supply; Greater Noida and Faridabad do not
Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar need a tutor who already lives locally
Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kondapur sit close enough for two evening households
Hinjewadi and Kharadi are the hard ends of the Pune corridor after five

contentBlocks.heading: Mock cycles and the Diploma calendar schools in India run to
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this site, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. The calendar described here is the general shape families at international schools deal with, not any particular school's timetable.

DP examination sessions run in May and November. Schools in India almost all enter candidates for May, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March, and November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. That is the fixed frame, and everything else a school does is arranged inside it.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. Mocks are the single most useful event in the two years for a home tutor, and they are routinely wasted. The marks come back, the family looks at the numbers, and the scripts go into a bag. What matters is not the mark. It is which command terms the student mishandled. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a student who writes an explanation where an evaluation was asked for will lose the same marks in May unless somebody sits with them and shows them the pattern.

Around the mocks the tuition plan should visibly change. Before them, content and coursework. During the mock fortnight, almost nothing, because a tutor adding sessions in that week is taking away revision time. After them, four to six weeks of targeted work drawn directly from the scripts. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the International Baccalaureate's official channels, and they show exactly how marks are awarded.
items: DP sessions run in May and November; Indian schools overwhelmingly enter May
May results are released in early July, after two years of DP teaching
Each school fixes its own DP2 mock dates, usually months before May
Mock scripts matter more than mock marks; read the command terms missed
Cut sessions during the mock fortnight rather than adding them

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when the DP week is already full in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition costs the student nothing in travel, and for a Diploma student that is the whole argument. Everything else is a trade.

A tutor who travels to you converts a commute into study time. A DP2 student who would otherwise spend part of an evening getting to a centre and back keeps those hours, and in a week where sleep is already being borrowed against, that is not a small saving. Home sessions also show the tutor something a screen hides: the desk, the pile of unfinished drafts, whether the student is working in a room with a television on. A good home tutor uses that information. Several times a year the right recommendation is to change the room, not the teaching.

Online buys a different thing, which is choice. Higher Level subjects with small cohorts are thinly taught in most Indian cities, and a family in Kochi, Nagpur or Guwahati may have no local option at all for HL Economics or HL Physics. Online also survives a week that has gone wrong. A session at seven in the morning before school, or a rescheduled half-hour on a Sunday, is possible online and impractical for somebody who has to travel.

Hybrid is what most Diploma households settle on by the middle of DP1, and it is a sensible landing point rather than a compromise. One home session a week for the subject where written working and drafts need to be seen on paper. One online session for the subject where the best available tutor lives in another city. Then, in the eight weeks before the May session, a shift towards online for its flexibility, because by then what the student needs most is the ability to move a slot without losing it.
items: A home visit converts a commute into revision time the student keeps
A home tutor sees the desk, the drafts pile and the noise in the room
Online reaches HL specialists that a smaller Indian city simply does not have
Online survives a broken week: early mornings and rescheduled half-hours
Most DP households land on hybrid by the middle of DP1

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before an IBDP home tutor takes a DP2 slot?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification does two jobs, and only one of them belongs to the platform. Profiles are verified before they go live, which covers identity and the qualifications and teaching experience the tutor puts forward. That is the floor. The rest is a judgement about DP depth, and you are better placed to make it than any document check.

Ask three questions and listen to the shape of the answers. First, which subjects at which level have they taught in the last two years, and for which session. A tutor who has taught SL for three years and is about to take an HL student should say so rather than blur it. Second, how do they work with internal assessment, and where exactly do they stop? The correct answer names a boundary: teach the skill, question the reasoning, point at a criterion, never write or edit the submission. Third, what would they do in the fortnight before mocks? A tutor who says they would add extra sessions has misunderstood the job.

Then the household's own checks, which matter more for a DP student than for a younger one. Meet the tutor before the first home session. Agree where in the flat lessons will happen, and keep the door open. Ask for the term plan in writing and check that it names the school's deadlines rather than only topics.

One warning sign is worth stating plainly. Any offer that involves a promised improvement of a fixed number of points should be treated with real scepticism. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and in the Diploma the score depends on external papers marked elsewhere, coursework the student writes themselves, and a core the tutor does not control.
items: Ask which subjects at which level were taught in the last two years
Ask where the tutor stops on internal assessment, and expect a named boundary
Ask what they would do in the fortnight before mocks; fewer hours is correct
Require a written term plan that names school deadlines, not just topics
Treat any promised number of extra points with real scepticism

contentBlocks.heading: A week at capacity: what home tuition should subtract, not add
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the week a Diploma student in DP2 often actually has. School until mid-afternoon. Travel home. Two subjects of homework that are genuinely non-negotiable because they feed a graded task. A draft in progress. A service commitment that takes a weekend morning and some planning during the week. Somewhere in there, the Extended Essay, which needs long uninterrupted blocks and gets fragments instead.

Into that, a family adds two tuition subjects at two sessions each. Four sessions, plus the work the tutors set between them. The student now has less unstructured study time than before the tutoring started, and unstructured study time is where consolidation happens. This is the most common way a well-intentioned tuition plan makes a Diploma student worse.

The subtraction principle is simple to state and hard to follow. Every hour of tuition added should replace an hour of something else, and the tutor should say what. Usually it replaces unfocused revision, which is the right trade. Sometimes it should replace a second tuition subject. Occasionally the honest recommendation is to stop tutoring one subject entirely so the student can finish an internal assessment that is worth 20% of a grade.

When should a tuition subject be cut? When the student is turning up to sessions without having done the work between them, which almost always means there is no room rather than no will. When two subjects are being tutored and both are drifting. When an internal assessment deadline is inside three weeks and the tutored subject is not the one with the deadline. And in the fortnight before mocks, when the most valuable thing anybody can give a Diploma student is an empty evening. A tutor who never recommends cutting anything is selling hours, not teaching.
items: Every tuition hour added should replace a named hour of something else
Four sessions a week can leave less consolidation time than none at all
Cut a subject when work between sessions stops being done at all
Cut back when a 20% internal assessment is due in another subject
An empty evening before mocks is worth more than an extra session

contentBlocks.heading: Honest progress for a Diploma student in India, term by term
contentBlocks.body:
Judge the first two months on behaviour rather than on marks, because in DP1 there often are no marks worth reading yet. The things to watch are whether the student is arriving at sessions with specific questions, whether work set is being attempted, and whether the tutor can name two concepts that have moved.

By the end of DP1, a reasonable expectation is that internal assessment work is genuinely under way rather than being talked about, that the student can explain what each command term requires, and that a mock or end-of-year paper shows fewer answers of the wrong type. Not necessarily a higher mark. Fewer answers where the student wrote what they knew instead of what was asked.

In DP2 the honest measure is mock-to-final trajectory, and it has to be read carefully. Mocks are set by the school and are not calibrated against the May session, so a mock mark is a diagnostic instrument and not a prediction. What a tutor should be able to show you after a mock is a list: this topic, this command term, this timing problem, this many marks each.

The limits deserve stating. No tutor can guarantee a grade. The predicted grade is formed by the school and a tutor cannot change it, though better work in front of the subject teacher can inform it. Starting tuition in the January of DP2 narrows what is realistic, particularly for coursework that is already submitted. And there are students whose problem is not teaching at all. A DP student sleeping five hours a night does not need IBDP home tutors in India. They need two commitments removed, and a decent tutor will say so in the first month rather than the sixth.
items: First two months: specific questions, work attempted, two concepts named as moved
End of DP1: coursework under way, and fewer answers of the wrong type
A mock mark is a diagnostic, not a prediction of the May result
The school forms the predicted grade; a tutor can inform it but not change it
A student sleeping five hours needs fewer commitments, not more sessions

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IBDP home tutors in India before the coursework season
contentBlocks.body:
The preparation that makes the first session useful takes about an hour and mostly involves finding paper.

Gather the six subjects with levels written next to them, the school's deadline list for internal assessments, the mock dates if they have been published, and the last marked script in each subject you are worried about. Then do the harder piece. Write out the student's actual week, hour by hour, including travel, the service commitment, any rehearsal or training, and the time they currently go to sleep. Most families find one or two hours they thought existed and do not.

The first session should be a diagnosis rather than a lesson. The tutor reads the scripts with the student present, asks them to talk through two answers, and separates three things that look identical on a report: a content gap, a command-term problem, and a timing problem. Each needs different work. A content gap needs teaching. A command-term problem needs marking practice against the actual markscheme. A timing problem needs supervised timed writing and nothing else. Treating the third as the first wastes a term, and in DP2 there are not many terms left.

After that, the rhythm should be visible and written down. One session a week per tutored subject as the default. A review conversation every few weeks, ten minutes, with you in the room. A deliberate reduction in the mock fortnight. Then a rebuilt plan after mock scripts come back, targeted at the specific marks the scripts show were lost. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, and say why in one sentence.
items: Bring the six subjects with levels, the deadline list and the mock dates
Write out the student's real week, including travel and sleep, before booking
Expect the first hour to separate content, command-term and timing problems
Default to one session a week per subject and justify anything more
Rebuild the plan from the mock scripts, not from the mock marks

faqs.question: How many home sessions a week can a Diploma student actually sustain?
faqs.answer: Two a week in total across all subjects is a sensible default in DP1, and three is usually the ceiling in DP2 even for a student who is coping well. The limiting factor is not the lesson but the work set between lessons, which doubles the real cost of every session. Families who book four or five sessions a week almost always find that homework stops being done, and at that point the tuition is displacing the consolidation it was meant to support.

faqs.question: Should we add tuition before the DP2 mock examinations?
faqs.answer: Before them, yes, if there is a genuine content gap. During the mock fortnight itself, no. Each school sets its own mock dates several months before the May session, and in that fortnight the most valuable thing a student can have is unstructured revision time in their own room. A tutor who proposes extra sessions in mock week is adding load at the worst possible moment. Restart afterwards, with a plan built from the scripts rather than the marks.

faqs.question: How much time does CAS really take, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: More than the report suggests, and no, not directly. Creativity, Activity, Service must be completed for the diploma, carries no grade, and therefore disappears from a family's mental accounting while still consuming weekend mornings, travel and reflection writing. A tutor should account for it when planning the week, ask when the commitment falls, and avoid scheduling a demanding session immediately after it. What a tutor must not do is produce reflections or organise the student's activities for them.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with the internal assessment, or is that not allowed?
faqs.answer: They can help, within a boundary that is clearly drawn. Every internal assessment is the student's own work. The International Baccalaureate's policy allows a teacher to comment on one draft, and it does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit a submission. So a tutor may teach research design, explain what a criterion is asking for, question a weak conclusion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph. The words on the page must stay the student's. Schools submit the work and run similarity checking.

faqs.question: My child has three Higher Level subjects and is drowning. What should change?
faqs.answer: Start by counting hours rather than by hiring anyone. Three Higher Levels at 240 recommended hours each, alongside three Standard Levels, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the service requirement, is a full load by design. If the student is consistently short of sleep, the first conversation is with the Diploma coordinator about whether one subject should move to Standard Level while that is still possible. Tuition helps a student who is behind in one subject. It does not help a student whose week does not fit.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Kharghar, Greater Noida or Hinjewadi in the evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes for a two-hour Higher Level booking, and often no for anything shorter. Diploma sessions tend to be longer than junior ones, which widens the distance a tutor will accept, but supply still clusters near the areas with the most international schools. Families in Kharghar, Thane, Greater Noida, Faridabad or Hinjewadi should expect either a local tutor or a hybrid arrangement. Availability at any particular hour depends on subject, level and schedule.

faqs.question: What is the right session length for a DP subject?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes suits most Higher Level work and an hour suits most Standard Level work, with two-hour sessions reserved for coursework blocks. The reason is the nature of the task. An extended-response answer takes twenty minutes to write and another twenty to mark properly with the student, so a sixty-minute slot rarely gets through a full cycle at Higher Level. For younger students shorter is better, but a Diploma student can hold a long session if it has a clear structure.

faqs.question: How do we handle two children on different programmes in the same home?
faqs.answer: Stagger rather than overlap, and protect the study space. A Diploma student needs a quiet room and long blocks, which is difficult if a younger sibling is having a lesson at the kitchen table at the same hour. Where a single tutor covers both, back-to-back home sessions in one visit work well and cut the travel cost for everyone. Where two tutors are involved, put them on different evenings unless the flat genuinely has two usable rooms.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so and ask for a different match, with one concrete reason. Useful reasons sound like this: no work is being set between sessions, the student is not talking during the lesson, the plan ignores the school's deadlines, or the level of the material is below what Higher Level requires. Vague dissatisfaction produces a similar replacement. A specific sentence changes the next shortlist. A trial session with the new tutor can be arranged before the family commits again.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for Diploma subjects, or is home better?
faqs.answer: Both work, and they are good at different things. Online reaches specialists in other Indian cities for thinly taught Higher Level subjects, survives a week that has gone wrong, and handles coursework discussion well through a shared screen. Home sessions save travel, show the tutor the student's actual working conditions, and suit written subjects where paper matters. Most Diploma families in India end up hybrid: one subject at home, one online, with a shift towards online in the weeks before May.

faqs.question: When should we stop tutoring altogether?
faqs.answer: When the student is consistently doing the work between sessions without prompting and asking sharper questions than the tutor has time to answer. That combination means the dependence has flipped the right way. Other honest stopping points exist too: when an internal assessment in another subject needs the hours more, when the student is not sleeping, and when the family is running three tuition subjects in DP2 and the marks are not moving in any of them.
