h1: IBDP Home Tuition in India Planned Around the Mock Cycle
heroTitle: A Two-Year DP Calendar, Taught at Home in India
heroSubtitle: The Diploma Programme is not a syllabus you cover at whatever pace suits. It is a fixed run of terms, internal deadlines, mocks and one exam session, and every sensible tuition plan is built backwards from that. This page lays the calendar out and says what tuition should be doing in each phase.
introSummary: IBDP home tuition in India works best when it is planned backwards from the May session rather than forwards from the day you hire someone. Schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, the academic year runs roughly April to March, and results are released in early July. That fixes everything else: where the DP2 mocks land, when past papers stop being premature, and how long the final revision block can honestly be. A home tutor who arrives without that map will teach whatever topic the student is worried about this week, which feels productive and leaves the same gaps in March. This page sets out the two years term by term, what mocks are actually for, and what changes once their results come back.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a DP home tutor to your mock dates in India?
contentBlocks.body:
By asking for the school's calendar before asking anything about the subject. IBDP home tuition in India is a scheduling problem as much as a teaching one. A parent sends a query or books a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, shortlists tutors whose verified profiles match, and arranges a demo or trial before the family commits. For a Diploma Programme request, the calendar questions carry most of the weight.

The reason is scheduling, not paperwork. A tutor who already holds three DP2 students in Powai through January and February cannot take a fourth two-hour Higher Level slot in the same window, however good the match looks in September. Knowing the mock dates and the subject load at the start avoids a tutor who is available now and unavailable exactly when you need them.

The intake also asks which stage you are in, because the tuition looks completely different across the two years.

1. DP1, first two terms: build the habits and fill the gaps left by the previous board, with no past-paper work at all.

2. DP1 end and the long break: internal assessment groundwork, and the one honest chance to strengthen a weak Higher Level subject before the workload arrives.

3. DP2, first term: full-paper technique begins, timed sections rather than whole papers, and command terms taught explicitly.

4. DP2, after mocks: the plan is rebuilt from the mock scripts, and tuition narrows to the two or three subjects where a point is actually available.

Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.
items: Send the six subjects with levels, plus the school's mock window, at the first message
Say which term the student is in; DP1 term two and DP2 term two need different tutors
Verified profiles are shortlisted against the subject and the level, not the subject alone
A trial is arranged, ideally around a marked piece of the student's own work
Availability through January and February is confirmed before the slot is agreed

contentBlocks.heading: DP1 and DP2: what each term of the two years has to finish
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme is a two-year course of six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together add up to 3 points, so 45 is the maximum, and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service has to be completed as well.

Spread across an Indian school year starting in April, that produces four working terms and two breaks. DP1 term one is for the transition: a student arriving from Cambridge IGCSE, the Middle Years Programme, CBSE or ICSE is learning a new assessment vocabulary, and tuition that races into content misses the actual problem. DP1 term two is where Higher Level subjects start to separate from Standard Level ones in difficulty, and where a bad subject choice becomes visible.

The long break between DP1 and DP2 is the highest-value window in the whole two years, and the least used. Internal assessment drafting, a weak Higher Level topic revisited without timetable pressure, and reading ahead into the first DP2 unit all fit there comfortably.

DP2 term one carries the heaviest load in the programme: internal assessment deadlines in several subjects stack, Extended Essay work is due, Creativity, Activity, Service has to keep running, and mocks are visible on the horizon. DP2 term two is mocks, the rebuild after them, and the final revision block. Home tuition that has not planned for that stack will simply be cancelled during it.
items: Six subjects from six groups; three or four at Higher Level, the rest Standard Level
Higher Level runs 240 recommended teaching hours, Standard Level 150
Subjects graded 1-7; Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions
The break between DP1 and DP2 is the most useful unbooked time in the course

contentBlocks.heading: Past papers in the DP: when should each subject start them?
contentBlocks.body:
Late in DP1 at the earliest, and properly only in DP2. Starting earlier backfires for a specific reason: a past paper tests content the student has not been taught yet, so most of what comes back is noise. The student concludes they are bad at the subject, the tutor spends the session teaching the unseen topic anyway, and a limited stock of real papers has been burned for no diagnostic value.

Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they are finite. Treat them as measuring instruments rather than practice material. In DP1, the right unit of practice is a single question or a section, taken from a topic just taught, marked against the markscheme in front of the student. That teaches the same technique without consuming a whole paper.

Command terms are the other half. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a student who answers discuss at the depth of describe will lose marks in every subject at once. A home tutor should be naming the command term in the question out loud every session from DP1 term two onwards, not saving it for a revision workshop in February.

Sciences are worth a specific note. Under the structure first assessed in 2025, Paper 1 splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, while Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response work. The internal assessment, a scientific investigation worth 20 per cent, is marked on four criteria of six marks each and runs to a maximum of 3,000 words. Paper 1B rewards a skill that no amount of content revision produces on its own.
items: DP1: single questions and sections from taught topics, marked with the markscheme open
DP2: whole papers under time, spaced so there are unseen papers left in March
Subject reports tell you what candidates got wrong; read them with the student
Command terms named aloud in every session, not taught once as a list
Paper 1B data questions need separate practice from content revision

contentBlocks.heading: IBDP home tuition in India: which cities hold evening slots in exam term
contentBlocks.body:
Every city holds them in August. The question is which ones still hold them in January, when a DP2 student has mocks, an internal assessment deadline and a tutor who has to cross the city at 7 pm. Distance is what breaks Diploma Programme schedules, and it breaks them at the worst possible moment.

In Delhi NCR, a tutor living in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri can usually reach another South Delhi address without the trip deciding the session. Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are each viable within themselves and difficult across. Families searching for IBDP home tuition in Delhi in DP2 should look inside their own sub-city first. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is starker still: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill form one practical zone, and Powai, Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar another. IBDP home tuition in Mumbai across that line in monsoon usually converts to online by July whether the family planned it or not.

Bengaluru concentrates Diploma Programme teaching near Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, with Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road further out; IBDP home tuition in Bangalore is really a question about which corridor you live on. Chennai works along Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Alwarpet and Perungudi.

Gujarat is a thinner market. Ahmedabad has some depth around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar reachable, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families usually build a hybrid week from the start rather than discovering the need in December.
items: Delhi NCR: book inside your own sub-city for DP2, not across the NCR
Mumbai: island city and the eastern suburbs are separate markets after 6 pm
Bengaluru and Chennai: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Adyar and Old Mahabalipuram Road
Hyderabad around Gachibowli and Pune around Baner both hold evening slots reasonably
Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot: plan the hybrid week in April, not January

contentBlocks.heading: Mock dates, the May session and the school year in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. What follows describes the general pattern families at international schools here live with, not the arrangements of any particular school.

Exam sessions run in May and November. Schools in India almost all enter candidates for May, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March; November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and those dates are the single most important thing a family can tell a tutor at the first conversation.

Mocks are not a prediction and should not be read as one. They exist to put a student through full papers under time before it matters, to give teachers evidence, and to expose the difference between knowing a topic and answering a question on it. A mock result that is lower than the school report is the normal outcome, not a crisis, because most students have never sat the whole paper in one sitting until then.

What the mock does change is where tuition goes next. Read the scripts, not the grades. A student losing marks across every subject in the last twenty minutes has a timing problem, and that is one fix applied six times. A student losing marks only on extended-response questions has a writing problem. A student who was simply not taught a unit has a content problem, and that one belongs back with the school.

May results are released in early July, which is when the next set of conversations begins.
items: May and November sessions exist; schools in India overwhelmingly use May
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May
Mocks are evidence, not predictions; a dip is the normal first result
Read mock scripts for the pattern of loss, not the grade on the front
Results are released in early July, after which the school route applies

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid through the last six months before May?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition for anything written by hand under time, online for anything that is really a conversation, and hybrid for almost everyone in DP2. Most IBDP home tuition in India ends up as some version of the third. That is the practical answer, and the reasons are about the calendar rather than about teaching quality.

A home tutor sees the physical conditions of the exam being rehearsed. Whether the student writes fast enough, whether they plan an extended response or start writing immediately, whether their diagrams are legible, whether they run out of time on Paper 2 because Paper 1 rattled them. Those are visible across a desk and easy to miss on a screen. Home classes also mean the student loses no study time to travel, which in DP2 term two is worth more than it sounds.

Online earns its place on supply and on resilience. A Higher Level subject with few local teachers is often only available online, and an online session survives a monsoon evening in Mumbai, a flooded underpass in Bengaluru and a tutor whose own timetable shifted. During the mock fortnight, an online half-hour to go through one question is possible when a full home visit is not.

Hybrid is what most DP2 households end up running: one home session a week for timed written work, one online session for marking, planning and internal assessment discussion inside academic integrity rules, and short online check-ins in the weeks either side of mocks. Set it up in DP1 rather than converting under pressure in January, because a tutor the student already trusts online is worth far more than a new one.
items: Home: timed written papers, handwriting speed, planning habits, diagram quality
Online: marking a script together, discussing a draft, reaching a rare Higher Level tutor
Hybrid: one home session, one online session, short online check-ins near mocks
Online sessions survive monsoon, traffic and a shifted school timetable
Build the hybrid pattern in DP1; switching under pressure in January rarely works

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a tutor joins the DP revision plan?
contentBlocks.body:
Three things: that they have taught this subject at this level, that they know where the school's mock sits in the year, and that they understand the line they must not cross on internal assessment. Everything else is secondary, and a tutor who is vague on any of the three will cost you a term.

IB Gram verifies identity and qualifications and confirms which programmes, subjects and levels a tutor has actually taught before a profile is shown to a family. That is a documentary check and it is worth having. It cannot tell you whether this person will work well with your particular student in February, which is what the trial session is for.

The integrity question deserves a direct conversation rather than an assumption. Every internal assessment is the student's own work. A teacher may give feedback on one draft. Nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit the submission. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than by the school alone. A tutor who offers to tidy up a draft is offering the family a risk, not a service.

The remaining checks are yours to make. Ask which papers the tutor has marked and how recently. Ask what they will do in the first three sessions. Ask what they expect to have finished before the mock window opens, and write the answer down, because that is the thing you will review in January.
items: Confirm the subject and the level taught, not just the subject
Ask where they think the school's mock window sits and what they will do before it
Internal assessment: skills and questioning only, never writing or editing the work
Ask what the first three sessions will cover and what evidence they will track
Verification is a floor; the trial session is where the actual judgement happens

contentBlocks.heading: Planning backwards from May: the block that decides the last ten weeks
contentBlocks.body:
Work from the exam and move backwards. That is the whole method, and it changes what a tutor does in October as much as what they do in March. A plan that runs forwards will always be behind, because there is more Diploma Programme content than there are weeks, and something has to be chosen deliberately rather than abandoned by accident.

Start with the papers themselves. For each of the six subjects, write down which papers are sat and roughly how long they are. Then mark the school's mock window. Then mark the internal assessment deadlines the school has set. What is left between those markers is the real teaching time, and it is usually about half of what parents assume.

The final revision block is built like this.

1. Ten weeks out, list every topic across all six subjects as secure, shaky or untaught, using the mock scripts as evidence rather than the student's feeling.

2. Eight weeks out, spend tuition time only on shaky topics in the two or three subjects where a point is realistically available, and hand the secure topics back to self-study.

3. Five weeks out, switch from topics to whole papers under exam time, one per subject per fortnight, marked with the markscheme open.

4. Two weeks out, stop teaching new content entirely and rehearse only timing, command terms and the order in which the student will attack each paper.

The hardest part is step two. Spreading tuition thinly across all six subjects feels fair and produces the smallest gain, because a subject sitting at a comfortable level rarely moves in ten weeks while a shaky one often does.
items: Write the paper list, the mock window and the internal assessment deadlines first
Ten weeks out: classify every topic as secure, shaky or untaught from mock evidence
Eight weeks out: tuition goes only where a point is realistically available
Five weeks out: whole papers under time, marked with the markscheme open
Two weeks out: no new content, only timing, command terms and paper order

contentBlocks.heading: What should change in the plan after mock results arrive in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Almost everything, and that is the point of having mocks at all. IBDP home tuition in India should look different in February from how it looked in October. A plan that survives the mock results unchanged was not a plan, it was a timetable. The rebuild is the most valuable week of work a home tutor does in the whole two years.

Start by separating the three kinds of loss. Content the student never learned goes back to the school first, because a tutor filling a unit the class was not taught is expensive and duplicated. Technique losses, where the content was known and the answer did not earn the marks, are exactly what tuition is for. Timing losses are usually a single fixable habit, such as writing full sentences in a question that wanted a value, or planning an extended response for far too long.

Then reallocate. If a student is comfortable in three subjects and shaky in three, the honest reallocation moves hours away from the comfortable ones even where those are the subjects the student enjoys and the tutor is strongest in. This is where families most often overrule the evidence.

No tutor can guarantee a grade or a point total, and a home tutor selling a promised improvement in exchange for a block booking after mocks is selling the family's anxiety back to them. Treat a claim to be first in the country the same way. What honest tuition can offer is better use of the weeks that remain.

There is also a case for less. A student already carrying six subjects, Creativity, Activity, Service, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge may need sleep and fewer commitments more than another two hours a week, and a good tutor will say so out loud.
items: Separate content loss, technique loss and timing loss before changing anything
Content the class never covered goes back to the subject teacher first
Move hours towards shaky subjects even when the student prefers the strong ones
Six to eight weeks is a fair review point; two weeks tells you nothing
Sometimes the right advice after mocks is fewer hours, not more

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IBDP home tuition in India before the calendar closes in
contentBlocks.body:
The useful time to arrange IBDP home tuition in India is early in DP1 or during the break before DP2, not in the week after mock results. By then the good subject tutors in your locality are holding full evening timetables, and you are choosing from whoever is left rather than from whoever fits.

Before the consultation, gather four things. The six subjects with their levels. The school's mock window and any internal assessment deadlines already issued. The most recent marked piece of work in each subject you are worried about, with the teacher's comments on it. And an honest note of what the week already contains, including Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, travel and the hour the student actually gets home.

That last item matters more than parents expect. A plan built for a student who is home at 4 pm collapses for a student who is home at 6.30 pm three days a week, and it is better to book two sessions that will survive DP2 than four that will be cancelled through January.

The first session should be diagnostic. Expect the tutor to look at marked work, ask the student to attempt one question while they watch, and finish with a short written plan naming what the first month will cover and how it connects to the mock window. A demo or trial can be arranged before you commit, lessons run at home, online or hybrid subject to availability, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. After results in early July, anything about re-marks, retakes or carried-forward internal assessment marks goes to your DP coordinator, who is the only person who can confirm eligibility and deadlines.
items: Arrange it in DP1 or over the break, not in the week after mock results
Bring six subjects with levels, mock dates and issued internal assessment deadlines
Bring one recent marked piece per worrying subject, teacher comments included
State the hour the student is actually home, including travel and activities
Anything about re-marks or retakes after July goes to the DP coordinator first

faqs.question: When should we start IBDP home tuition, DP1 or DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, if there is any real doubt about a subject. Starting in DP1 gives a tutor time to fix habits rather than patch content, and it means the student already trusts the person when DP2 term two arrives. Starting in DP2 is common and still worth doing, but the work becomes triage: choosing the two or three subjects where a point is available and accepting that the others will sit where they are. The worst start is the week after mock results, when good tutors are already fully booked.

faqs.question: How many home sessions a week does a DP student need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. One session a week per subject you are genuinely worried about, with real work in between, beats three sessions a week that leave no time to practise. A DP2 student carrying six subjects, Creativity, Activity, Service, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge has very little spare evening time, and tuition that fills all of it stops the independent work that actually moves grades. Two subjects at one session each is a common and sustainable starting point.

faqs.question: Our tutor travels from Thane to Bandra. Will that hold through DP2?
faqs.answer: Honestly, probably not through January and February. A crossing like that on a weekday evening is fine in a light term and starts producing late arrivals and cancellations exactly when the mock cycle makes every session matter. Two fixes work. Move one of the two weekly sessions online from the start, so the pattern is already normal when weather or traffic intervenes. Or look again within your own zone, where a slightly less experienced tutor who arrives reliably is often the better outcome.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Someone responsible in the flat, yes; in the room, no. For a seventeen-year-old, an adult present is a sensible baseline and keeps the session from drifting, while sitting in changes what the student will admit they do not understand. The more useful parental role is at the end: five minutes with the tutor on what was covered and what the student should do before the next session. Ask for that routinely rather than only when you are worried.

faqs.question: What are mocks actually for, and should we panic at a low result?
faqs.answer: Mocks exist to put a student through full papers under time before it counts, and to give teachers evidence. A drop against school report grades is the usual first outcome, because most students have never sat a whole paper in one sitting until then. What matters is the pattern inside the scripts. Marks lost in the last twenty minutes across every subject is a timing problem with one fix. Marks lost only on extended responses is a writing problem. Neither is a prediction.

faqs.question: When should past papers start?
faqs.answer: Single questions from taught topics late in DP1, and whole papers under time from DP2 term one. Starting whole papers earlier wastes them, because the paper tests content the student has not yet been taught and the result measures the timetable rather than the student. Papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels and are a finite resource. Keep several unseen ones for March, when a genuinely unfamiliar paper is the only honest rehearsal left.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that should be stated before the first session. Every internal assessment is the student's own work. A teacher may give feedback on one draft; nobody, tutor or parent, may write, rewrite or edit the submission. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. The school submits the work and runs similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than the school alone.

faqs.question: We live in Surat and there is no DP tutor nearby. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Build a hybrid week deliberately rather than waiting for the local search to fail. Families in Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot usually find one subject covered locally at home and take the rest online from Ahmedabad, Mumbai or Bengaluru. Set that up in DP1 so the student is already comfortable working on a screen before DP2, and buy the small amount of equipment that makes online Mathematics and sciences work properly: a stand or document camera pointed at the page, and a second device for the markscheme.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session is missed during the mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in advance, because the mock fortnight is exactly when sessions get missed. The workable arrangement is that anything cancelled by the tutor moves online within the same week, and anything cancelled by the family with notice is rescheduled where the timetable allows. It is also reasonable to plan a lighter fortnight around mocks deliberately, with two short online check-ins instead of two full home sessions, so nothing has to be cancelled at all.

faqs.question: Results come out in early July. What should we do in that week?
faqs.answer: Very little on the first day, and then one conversation with the DP coordinator. May results are released in early July. If a grade looks wrong, the coordinator can explain an enquiry upon results, which has a short deadline, and can confirm whether a later session is possible and what carries forward. Internal assessment marks are usually carried forward to a retake, so tuition afterwards targets the externally assessed papers. Deadlines, eligibility and costs all come from the coordinator, not from a tutor.

faqs.question: Is tuition worth it if the student is already scoring well?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes the honest answer is no. A student comfortably placed across all six subjects, sleeping properly and managing their own revision does not need a tutor, and adding one can crowd out the independent practice that got them there. The cases where it is worth it are narrow: one Higher Level subject sitting a band below the rest, a specific paper type that keeps costing marks, or a student who is scoring well and cannot finish a paper in time.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to the IB or to any school?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no connection to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and no relationship with any school mentioned here. Schools are named only as context for the calendar pressures families in India describe. Mock dates, internal assessment deadlines, session entry, predicted grades and anything to do with results come from your own school and your DP coordinator, and those are the people to confirm every date with.

comparison.heading: How do the tuition formats compare across a DP year in India?
comparison.intro: A home visit suits the student who needs written papers watched and a week that does not lose an hour to travel. An online tutor suits a rare Higher Level subject or a household where evening traffic decides everything. A small online group suits two or three students on the same subject and level revising together. A batch is cheapest per hour and can drill a single topic well. The deciding question is usually whether anyone needs to watch the student write under time.

rows.label: Attention per student
cells: Complete, and the tutor also sees the desk, the noise and the state of the student
Complete within the frame of the camera and the shared screen
Shared across three or four, which keeps everyone answering out loud
Low; the pace follows the middle of the room rather than your child

cells: Planned around this student's three or four Higher Level subjects specifically
Same planning, with access to Higher Level teachers your city may not have
Only works when the group shares the subject and the level exactly
One pace for a mixed group; Higher Level depth is usually the casualty

rows.label: Timed paper practice
cells: Strongest: the tutor watches pace, planning time and handwriting under pressure
Workable with a camera on the page, though easier for the student to drift
Papers are set but rarely watched per student while being written
Practice is set and returned; the writing itself is not observed

cells: The tutor travels, so DP2 study time is not lost to the commute
Nobody travels, which is why it holds through monsoon and exam term
Nobody travels, but the slot is fixed by the group rather than by you
The student travels at the busiest hour, often twice a week

h1: IBDP Private Tutors for Higher Level Subjects and Predicted Grades
heroTitle: Higher Level Tuition and Predicted Grades in India
heroSubtitle: Two things bring most Diploma families to one-to-one help: a Higher Level subject that has pulled away from the student, and a predicted grade that arrived lower than expected. This page is about both. Higher Level carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and that difference is usually where the trouble sits.
introSummary: IBDP private tutors in India are usually hired for one of two reasons: a Higher Level subject has moved beyond what the student can follow in class, or a predicted grade has come back below what a university offer needs. Most families start with home tuition, a tutor at the dining table on a weekday evening once school and CAS commitments are done. Higher Level is not Standard Level with more homework. It is 240 recommended teaching hours against 150, and the extra content is examined alongside everything else. A predicted grade, meanwhile, is formed by the school, not by you and not by a tutor. What a tutor can change is the evidence the school is looking at.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist an HL tutor in India for one weak subject?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the subject and the level, not the programme. A request that says "DP help" produces a broad shortlist and a slow start. A request that says "Physics HL, DP2, Paper 2 extended response, mocks in January" produces a short one. When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school calendar, your location and the schedule you can actually hold. Those six answers do most of the filtering.

Level is the filter families skip. A tutor who is comfortable with Chemistry at Standard Level may be genuinely out of depth in the Additional Higher Level content, and the gap only surfaces in the fourth session, when the student brings a question the tutor cannot take apart on the spot. So the shortlist for a Higher Level subject is built from people who have taught that subject at that level, and the trial tests exactly that.

IBDP private tutors in India are matched on availability as much as on subject. A Higher Level session that runs ninety minutes or two hours needs a slot that survives a full Diploma week. If the student has Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) on two evenings and an internal assessment draft due, a Saturday morning block is more honest than an eight o'clock Tuesday that will be cancelled twice a month. Profiles are verified before they go live, a demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and if the fit is wrong you can ask for a different match.

One more thing families rarely think to include. Send the predicted grade if one has been issued, and say what it was based on. A tutor who knows which evidence the school is weighing works differently from one who is guessing.
items: 1. Send the subject, the level, the year group and your locality in one message.
2. Add the current grade, the predicted grade if issued, and the mock dates.
3. IB Gram shortlists verified profiles that have taught that subject at Higher Level.
4. Run a trial session on a topic the student has already failed once.
5. Agree the weekly slot around CAS, IA deadlines and school timings before paying.

contentBlocks.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what the extra ninety hours contain
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four are taken at Higher Level (HL) and the rest at Standard Level (SL). The International Baccalaureate (IB) sets 240 recommended teaching hours for an HL subject against 150 for an SL one. Ninety hours of difference, per subject, inside the same two years.

Those ninety hours are Additional Higher Level (AHL) content. In the DP sciences the assessment structure is shared: HL and SL sit the same shape of paper and complete the same scientific investigation. The extra is content, and it is examined alongside everything else rather than in a separate paper of its own. That is why a Higher Level student who falls behind does not fall behind evenly. They fall behind on the AHL topics specifically, while the common core still looks respectable in a class test.

Now the harder case. A student picks three HLs in DP1 for reasons that made sense at the time: a parent's expectation, a degree they thought they wanted, friends in the same set. By the second term of DP1 one of the three is clearly not working, and the other two are being starved to keep it alive. Three options exist. Keep all three and accept a lower grade in one. Move the failing subject to Standard Level, if the school's timetable and the IB's deadlines allow it. Or change subject entirely, which depends on what the school can timetable. Only the DP coordinator can say which is open, and until when.

Dropping an HL to SL is the right advice more often than pride allows. It is right when one Higher Level grade is dragging two other subjects down with it, when the degree the student is heading towards does not require that subject at HL, and when enough of DP1 or early DP2 remains for the change to settle. It is usually wrong late in DP2, wrong when the university course explicitly asks for that subject at Higher Level, and wrong when the real problem is a study-habit issue that would follow the student into SL anyway.
items: HL: 240 recommended teaching hours per subject, against 150 hours at SL
Three or four subjects at HL; the remainder taken at Standard Level
The extra hours are Additional Higher Level content, examined alongside the core
Sciences: HL and SL share the paper structure and the scientific investigation
Before dropping to SL, get the university's level requirement in writing
Only the DP coordinator can confirm whether a level change is still possible

contentBlocks.heading: Where the Additional Higher Level content actually bites, subject by subject
contentBlocks.body:
In the DP sciences, AHL material is usually met late in DP1 or early in DP2, by which point the student has built a habit of study on the common core. The habit is the problem. A topic that was answerable in three lines starts demanding a full extended response in Paper 2, and the student keeps writing three lines. Tutors see this constantly in IB Physics and IB Chemistry: the arithmetic is fine, the explanation is thin, and the command term was "explain" or "evaluate" rather than "calculate". Paper 1 splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, and a student can hold a decent 1A score while 1B and Paper 2 quietly decide the grade. IB Biology carries a different load again: there is more to hold, and extended responses reward the student who organises an answer before writing it.

Mathematics is its own decision. DP Mathematics comes as two subjects, Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each available at HL and SL. AA is algebraic and proof-heavy. AI is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often steered towards AA, but the right choice depends on the degree and on the student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement. A student strong at procedure and weak at proof will feel AA HL in a way AA SL never showed them. IB Economics and IB English A also run at both levels; ask the subject teacher what the Higher Level components are there.

One part of the Diploma does not change with level at all, and it is worth knowing. The scientific investigation is the same internal assessment for HL and SL students: 20% of the subject grade, marked on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation at six marks each, with a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. So an HL student can bank the same twenty per cent as an SL classmate, on identical criteria. When the AHL content is going badly, that is often where the cheapest marks are sitting.
items: AHL content stacks on the common core, usually late in DP1
Paper 1 has 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions
Paper 2 extended responses punish three-line answers trained on the common core
Mathematics AA is algebraic and proof-heavy; AI is modelling and statistics-heavy
The scientific investigation is identical at HL and SL: 20% of the grade
Four criteria at six marks each, maximum 3,000 words, individual report

contentBlocks.heading: IBDP private tutors in India: where Higher Level specialists actually sit
contentBlocks.body:
IBDP private tutors in India are not spread evenly, and Higher Level supply thins by subject rather than by city. A family searching for an IBDP private tutor in Delhi will find people for Mathematics and Economics within a short radius of South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri or Golf Course Road in Gurugram (Gurgaon). The same family searching for HL Chemistry with real AHL depth may end up looking at Dwarka, Noida, Sector 128 Noida or Greater Noida, and weekday evening traffic between Ghaziabad or Faridabad and the far side of Delhi NCR can stretch a short trip into an unusable one.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the pattern repeats along the rail and road lines. A tutor living in Andheri or Powai can hold a weekday slot in Juhu or Bandra; the same person crossing to Worli, Lower Parel or Malabar Hill in the evening is a different proposition. Families in Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar often run a hybrid week for this reason, and a search for an IBDP private tutor in Mumbai frequently ends with one home session and one online session rather than two of either.

Bengaluru splits the same way. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City sit far enough from Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Jayanagar that a parent looking for an IBDP private tutor in Bangalore should decide early whether proximity or Higher Level depth wins. In Hyderabad, Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District form one cluster, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad on the far side of the evening peak. An IBDP private tutor in Hyderabad who lives in Kokapet suits a family there and suits a family in Secunderabad badly.

Beyond the metros, northern India beyond Delhi NCR is where the Higher Level problem is sharpest. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula have an international school population without the tutor density to match it, and Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar and Ludhiana have less again. An IBDP private tutor in Chennai, in Pune, in Kolkata or in Ahmedabad is easier to find for a common Higher Level subject than for a rare one. For those families, a private IBDP tutor near me is the wrong search. The right one is an IBDP HL private tutor who teaches online, wherever they happen to live.

contentBlocks.heading: Mock dates, predicted grades and the school calendar in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and IB schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May session. November exists and is used by a small minority of schools and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. That calendar is the frame for everything on this page: a Higher Level problem noticed in DP1 has room to be fixed, and the same problem noticed after the DP2 mocks has very little.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. Mocks are where the Higher Level gap becomes visible to everyone at once, because the paper is long, the AHL content is in it, and nothing can be looked up. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore each work to their own internal deadlines, and those dates are what a tutor should be told first. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

What the calendar means in practice is that the useful conversation with the school happens before the mock, not after it. Ask the subject teacher what the student is currently working at in Higher Level terms and what would have to change to move a band. Ask the DP coordinator when predictions are finalised at your school, because schools differ and no tutoring page can tell you that date. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, so ask what will be released and when.

And plan the home tuition slot around the school's own revision timetable rather than against it. A DP2 student sitting in a home session three evenings a week during an exam term is not revising. They are attending.
items: Indian academic year runs roughly April to March; May is the standard session
November is used by a small minority of schools and by retake candidates
May results are released in early July
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May
Ask the DP coordinator when your school finalises predicted grades

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a two-hour Higher Level session in India?
contentBlocks.body:
For a Higher Level subject, home tuition wins on the things that are hard to see through a screen: the student's working on paper, the moment they stop and look away, the past-paper question they quietly skipped. Online wins on choice of tutor. Hybrid is what most DP2 families in India eventually settle on, and it is not a compromise so much as a sensible reading of the week.

Take the three honestly. A home tutor in the room can watch a student attempt a Paper 2 extended response under time and intervene at the sentence where the reasoning breaks, not ten minutes later when the answer is finished and the error has hardened. That is worth a great deal in a subject where AHL content is being applied rather than recalled. But a home tutor is drawn from whoever can reach your locality on a weekday evening, and for a rare Higher Level subject that pool can be very small.

Online reverses the trade. A specialist who has taught the subject at Higher Level for years may live in another city entirely, and for a family in Dehradun or Ludhiana that is the difference between a real option and none. The cost is real too: annotation on a shared screen is slower than a pencil on the student's own page, and a tired DP2 student at nine in the evening holds attention better in a room than on a call.

Hybrid takes one of each. One home session a week for the work that needs paper and presence, one online session for the second subject or for a specialist you could not otherwise reach. It also survives the monsoon, an exam term and a tutor's own travel in a way that two home sessions do not. IBDP private tutors in India increasingly work this way by default, and it is reasonable to ask for it from the start.
items: Home classes: presence, paper, and the tutor sees the actual working
Online: reach a genuine Higher Level specialist living in another city
Hybrid: one home session weekly plus one online, common among DP2 families
Home visits lose most often to traffic, monsoon and exam-term timetables
Online loses to late-evening fatigue and slower live annotation

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a Higher Level home tutor takes the subject on?
contentBlocks.body:
Check that they have taught the subject at Higher Level, not merely the subject. Ask which AHL topics they have taught most recently and to whom. Ask how they would mark one extended response against its command term. Somebody who answers those three in specifics has taught Higher Level; somebody who answers in generalities has taught Standard Level and read the Higher Level guide.

IBDP private tutors in India listed on IB Gram have their profiles verified before they go live, and that covers identity together with the qualifications and teaching experience a tutor claims. What verification cannot do is tell you whether this person will hold a sixteen-year-old's attention for two hours on a Thursday. That is what the trial is for, and a trial should run on a topic the student has already failed, not on a fresh one where everything still looks fine.

There is one check specific to predicted grades that families almost never make. Ask the tutor directly what they believe they can and cannot influence about a prediction. The honest answer is that they cannot influence it at all and can only change the work the school sees. Anyone who suggests otherwise, or who offers to speak to the school on your behalf about a grade, has told you something useful about how they work.

Ask about materials too. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels and show how marks are awarded, and a tutor should be working from those rather than from a private question bank of unknown origin. Then check the practical side: gate entry at your society, whether the person is comfortable holding a weekday evening slot through an exam term, and exactly what happens to a missed home session.
items: Ask which AHL topics they taught most recently, and at which level
Ask them to mark one extended response against its command term
Run the trial on a topic the student has already failed once
Materials should come through the school or the IB's official channels
Ask what they claim they can influence about a predicted grade

contentBlocks.heading: How is a predicted grade formed in India, and who decides it?
contentBlocks.body:
A predicted grade is the school's judgement of the grade a student is likely to achieve in the May session, expressed on the same 1 to 7 scale as the final grade. It is formed by the subject teacher and submitted by the school through the DP coordinator. It is not formed by a tutor, not negotiated by a parent, and not something IB Gram or any other platform takes any part in.

What goes into it varies by school, which is exactly why the only reliable source on your child's prediction is your child's school. In most cases the teacher is weighing evidence you can also see: classwork, unit tests, the DP2 mock script, drafts of the internal assessment, and how the student handles command terms under timed conditions. Command terms matter here more than families expect. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth of answer, and a student who writes past the term is read as not yet secure at Higher Level. If you do not know which evidence your school weighs most, ask the coordinator.

Here is the part families misread. A low prediction in a Higher Level subject is usually not a judgement about intelligence or effort. It is a statement that the most recent Higher-Level-standard evidence does not support a higher number. The mock script is a document sitting in a file, and it says what it says.

So the useful question is never whether the prediction can be raised. It is what the next piece of evidence would have to look like, and whether there is time for that piece to exist before the school closes its list. Sometimes there is not, and then the honest answer is that this year's prediction is what it is. The work from that point is for May, where the grade is decided by external papers and the internal assessment.
items: The subject teacher forms the prediction; the school submits it
It uses the same 1 to 7 scale as the final subject grade
Evidence usually includes classwork, unit tests, mock scripts and IA drafts
No tutor and no platform takes any part in forming it
Ask your DP coordinator which evidence your school weighs most heavily

contentBlocks.heading: What can a tutor change about a prediction, and what cannot be changed?
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor cannot change a predicted grade. They can change the work a prediction is made from, and only where there is time for new work to exist before the school decides. That is the whole honest answer, and any claim beyond it is worth scrutinising.

What shifts first is not the grade. It is the shape of the student's answers. Within three or four sessions a decent Higher Level tutor should have the student distinguishing what "explain" asks for from what "evaluate" or "to what extent" asks for, and writing to the command term instead of around it. Marks follow that, but with a lag, and the lag runs longer at Higher Level than at Standard Level because the AHL content still has to be learned underneath the technique.

Set a review point at six to eight weeks, and judge it against evidence rather than feeling. A marked past-paper question at the start, the same standard of question at the end, both marked against the official markscheme. If nothing has moved and the student is genuinely doing the work between sessions, change something: the tutor, the mode, or the number of subjects being tutored at once. A DP2 student in home tuition for four subjects is not receiving four subjects' worth of help. They are receiving four interruptions.

And the limits, plainly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, at Higher Level or anywhere else. A student starting in February of DP2 with three weak HLs has a narrower set of outcomes than one starting in DP1, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. Tutoring also cannot fix sleep, a week with no free evenings, or a subject the student actively dislikes at Higher Level depth. Sometimes the right advice is fewer commitments rather than more hours.
items: 1. Week one: mark one full past-paper question together against the official markscheme.
2. Weeks two to four: rebuild the two AHL topics the mock showed as weakest.
3. Weeks five to seven: one timed extended response weekly, marked to the command term.
4. Week eight: sit a full paper under exam conditions and compare against week one.
5. Weeks nine to twelve: rotate remaining weak topics and hand marking to the student.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting Higher Level home tuition in India: what to send first
contentBlocks.body:
Send four things and you will get a usable shortlist on the first pass: the subject and the level, the school and its DP2 mock dates, the current grade along with the predicted grade if one has been issued, and the two or three evening slots you can genuinely hold. Add your locality, so that the home tuition option is a real one rather than a theoretical one.

Then the consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school calendar, your location and the schedule, shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match those needs, and arranges a demo or trial session before the family commits. Families approaching IBDP private tutors in India during a DP2 exam term should expect a rare Higher Level subject to take longer to place than a common one, and availability always depends on the tutor's own schedule and the level you need.

The first session should not be teaching. It should be diagnosis. A good Higher Level tutor will ask the student to attempt one past-paper question cold, will read the mock script if you have it, and will come out of that hour naming two or three specific topics rather than proposing to revise the syllabus. Bring the marked mock, the internal assessment feedback if any exists, and the most recent report.

One honest note before you book anything. If the student's real problem is carrying three Higher Level subjects, CAS and an internal assessment deadline in the same fortnight, adding home classes this month may be the wrong move. Fix the week first. Then bring in a tutor, with something specific for that person to do.
items: Send subject, level, current grade, predicted grade and your locality
Include the school's DP2 mock dates and any internal assessment deadlines
Name two or three weekday evening slots the family can genuinely hold
Bring the marked mock script and the latest report to the first session
Ask for a trial before committing, and for a different match if fit is wrong

faqs.question: Can a private tutor get my child's predicted grade changed?
faqs.answer: No. A predicted grade is formed by the subject teacher and submitted by the school through the DP coordinator, and a tutor sits entirely outside that process. What a tutor can do is change the work the school is looking at, which only helps if a piece of assessed work is still to come before predictions are finalised. Ask your coordinator when that point falls at your school, because it varies. After it, the target is the May session itself rather than the prediction.

faqs.question: What actually makes Higher Level harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Content volume and the depth of reasoning expected, rather than difficulty in the abstract. The IB sets 240 recommended teaching hours for a Higher Level subject against 150 at Standard Level, and that extra time is filled with Additional Higher Level content. In the DP sciences the paper structure is shared across both levels, so a Higher Level paper can look familiar while drawing on a much larger pool and asking for longer chains of reasoning in the Paper 2 extended responses.

faqs.question: My child chose three HLs and one is failing. What are the options?
faqs.answer: There are three, and the school controls all of them. Keep the subject at Higher Level and accept a lower grade there while protecting the other two. Move it to Standard Level, if the timetable and the IB's deadlines still allow it. Or change the subject entirely, which is the rarest outcome and depends on what the school can timetable. Book a conversation with the DP coordinator before speaking to anyone else, including a tutor, because only the coordinator knows which door is still open.

faqs.question: Is it too late to drop an HL to SL during DP2?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the only person who can answer is your school's DP coordinator, since the school submits any change and the IB sets the deadlines. As a rough rule, a level change made early in DP1 settles easily, one made in the first term of DP2 is difficult but sometimes possible, and one attempted close to the May session usually is not. If the change is closed, protect the other five subjects and target the externally assessed papers in the failing one.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travelling to Powai or Bandra hold a weekday evening slot in exam term?
faqs.answer: Usually only if they already live close by. Evening traffic in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region can stretch a short trip badly, and a tutor crossing from Andheri to Worli twice a week during an exam term will start rescheduling. The arrangement families in Powai, Bandra and Thane tend to land on is a hybrid week: one home session at a time the tutor can reliably reach you, and one online session for work that does not need paper and presence.

faqs.question: How many weeks does it take to close a Higher Level gap?
faqs.answer: Plan for a term and judge it at six to eight weeks. The shape of the student's answers should change first, usually within three or four sessions, as they begin writing to the command term rather than around it. Marks move later, because the Additional Higher Level content underneath still has to be learned. If a marked past-paper question at week eight looks like the one from week one, and the student has done the work between sessions, change something.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during a Higher Level session?
faqs.answer: In the house yes, in the room no. A sixteen-year-old working on an Additional Higher Level topic will perform for an audience rather than admit confusion, and admitting confusion is the entire point of the hour. Set the session at a table with good light and no television, be available for a two-minute conversation at the end, and read the tutor's notes. For a much younger student the answer is different, but not for DP2.

faqs.question: Do I need a Higher Level specialist, or will a good SL tutor do?
faqs.answer: For the common core, a strong Standard Level tutor is often fine. For the Additional Higher Level content they usually are not, and the gap shows up several sessions in, when the student brings a question the tutor cannot take apart on the spot. Ask any candidate which AHL topics they have taught most recently and to whom. Specific answers mean they have taught Higher Level. General ones mean they have read the guide.

faqs.question: We live in Chandigarh and nobody nearby teaches HL Physics. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Search online rather than nearby. Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun have international school populations without matching tutor density, and for a rare Higher Level subject the local pool may be empty rather than merely small. An online specialist in another city beats a nearby generalist who has only taught the subject at Standard Level. If you want presence too, keep one local home session for a subject the local pool can genuinely cover.

faqs.question: How is an IBDP private tutor's fee usually structured?
faqs.answer: By the hour, by the level and by the mode, with no single rate across the country. A Higher Level subject typically sits above the same subject at Standard Level because of preparation and marking time, a home visit prices in the tutor's travel, and an online session with the same person usually does not. Exam-term slots are scarcer than DP1 slots. Ask for the structure in writing before the trial, including what happens to a session cancelled at short notice.

faqs.question: The DP2 mock went badly. Should we start home tuition now or wait for the results meeting?
faqs.answer: Start now, with the mock script in hand. That marked script is the single most useful document a tutor can read, because it shows which Additional Higher Level topics failed, whether the loss was content or command term, and whether the student simply ran out of time. Waiting costs weeks you do not have before May. Bring the script, the markscheme if the school released it, and the subject teacher's written comments to the first home session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the scientific investigation without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits the IB sets and your school enforces. The internal assessment in the DP sciences is worth 20% and is marked on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, six marks each, inside a 3,000 word maximum. A tutor may teach what each criterion asks for, discuss a draft the student has already written, and ask hard questions about the data. A tutor may not design the investigation, write text, or edit the submission.

comparison.heading: Which format actually suits a Higher Level subject in India?
comparison.intro: Four formats, one question: how much of the hour goes on your child's specific Higher Level gap? One-to-one at home spends all of it and costs the most per hour. A small online group spends part of it and gives the student other people's questions, which is genuinely useful in a discussion-heavy subject. A large batch spends almost none of it, but covers content cheaply and suits a student who simply missed a term of school.
