h1: IBDP Online Tuition: Working on an IA Draft Over a Screen
heroTitle: Working on a DP Internal Assessment Online in India
heroSubtitle: A DP student in Hyderabad shares a maths exploration on screen. The tutor reads criterion C aloud, asks which sentence shows personal engagement, and waits. Nothing is typed into that document by anyone except the student. That is the shape of an online Diploma Programme session run properly.
introSummary: IBDP online tuition in India is a one-to-one Diploma Programme session run over a video call and a shared screen, and for most DP2 families it exists because of internal assessment. The work sits in a document. The tutor reads it against the published criteria, question by question, and the student makes every change. The International Baccalaureate (IB) allows a teacher to comment on one draft of an internal assessment (IA); it allows nobody, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit what the student submits. So the session is built around teaching, questioning and marking rather than fixing. This page sets out the running order of such a lesson, how a past paper is marked live, what the school's similarity checking will see, and the note you should receive afterwards.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IBDP online tuition in India start from one IA draft?
contentBlocks.body:
It starts with the draft. You send a query or book a free consultation, say which internal assessment the student is stuck on, and IB Gram asks the questions that decide the match: subject and level, the school's internal deadline, the criteria the teacher has already flagged, your city, and the slots the student can genuinely keep each week.

Most DP2 requests arrive in one of three shapes. A mathematics exploration sitting at eleven pages that reads like a textbook chapter. A scientific investigation with plenty of data and an evaluation worth almost nothing. A Theory of Knowledge (TOK) exhibition with three objects and no honest link to the prompt. Saying which one you have changes the shortlist, because a tutor fluent in the five exploration criteria is not automatically the right person for a Physics investigation.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. For IBDP online tuition in India that trial should use the student's own draft rather than a sample, because what you are testing is method, not subject knowledge. Watch what the tutor does in the first ten minutes. One who starts rewriting a paragraph has told you everything you need. One who highlights criterion D, asks the student what reflection means in this subject, and then stays quiet while the student thinks, is showing you the thing you are actually paying for.

IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose stated experience matches the subject, the level and the deadline you named. Lessons run online, at home or hybrid, subject to tutor availability, and the family can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Ask for that change early rather than at the end of a term. A DP2 student has a fixed number of weeks before the May session, and four wasted sessions in November are four sessions nobody can recover in March.
items: 1. Send the query with subject, level, school deadline and the IA type.
2. A consultation call confirms the criteria flagged and the weekly slots.
3. IB Gram shortlists verified tutors matching that subject, level and timeline.
4. A trial session runs on the student's real draft, not a sample.
5. Sessions begin online, at home or hybrid, with a written note each time.

contentBlocks.heading: DP1 and DP2 on screen: which internal assessments land when
contentBlocks.body:
The IB Diploma Programme (DP) runs two years, DP1 and DP2. A student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. TOK and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed alongside all of it.

Exam sessions run in May and November. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which fits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March, and May results are released in early July. Work backwards from that and the shape of the two years is plain enough. DP1 is where habits and the content base get built. DP2 is where internal assessment, mock cycles and final revision all try to occupy the same months.

IBDP online tuition in India behaves differently across those two years. In DP1 a screen session is usually about content and technique: a topic taught properly, a set of questions attempted and marked, an error log started. In DP2 the same hour is almost always about a piece of assessed work sitting in a shared document, or a past paper being marked while the student watches. The hour is the same length. What the student brings to it is not.

Internal deadlines are set by the school and not by the IB, so confirm every date with the DP coordinator rather than trusting a parent forum. The pattern families in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai describe is consistent: first drafts requested late in DP1 or early in DP2, feedback returned once, final versions due while mocks are running. A tutor who knows that pattern plans the term around it instead of reacting to it in February.
items: Six subjects from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level
HL carries 240 recommended teaching hours, SL 150, across DP1 and DP2
Subjects graded 1 to 7; TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions
May session for most Indian schools, with results released in early July

contentBlocks.heading: What does a maths exploration look like in a shared-screen session?
contentBlocks.body:
It looks like the criteria on one half of the screen and the student's document on the other. The mathematics exploration is the same task for Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) at both levels: 20% of the final grade, 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 on five criteria, and the work must be the student's own.

Those criteria are A Presentation (4 marks), B Mathematical communication (4), C Personal engagement (3), D Reflection (3) and E Use of mathematics (6). HL work is judged against a higher standard on criterion E, which is where most HL explorations quietly lose ground. A session on criterion B is not really a session about mathematics. It is about whether every symbol has been defined, whether notation stays consistent from page four to page fourteen, and whether a reader who is not the student's own teacher could follow the argument at all.

The DP sciences, first assessed in 2025, share a structure worth knowing before you book anything. Paper 1 has two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions; Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. The internal assessment is the scientific investigation, worth 20%, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, with a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. HL and SL share the assessment structure, and HL adds Additional Higher Level (AHL) content.

So a Chemistry investigation session and an English A session look nothing alike on screen. For the investigation the tutor is usually parked on Evaluation, asking what the student would change and why, and refusing to supply the answer. For Economics or English A the screen holds one paragraph and one command term, and the work is reading each against the other. The subject decides the tool. The rule about who holds the cursor never changes.
items: Five exploration criteria: presentation, communication, engagement, reflection, use of mathematics
The exploration is 20% of the grade, 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20
Criterion E carries 6 marks and is judged harder at Higher Level
Scientific investigation: four criteria of 6 marks, maximum 3,000 words
Science Paper 1 splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions
Group investigation allowed up to three students, but every report is individual

contentBlocks.heading: Where IBDP online tuition in India removes the evening commute
contentBlocks.body:
Bengaluru is the clearest case. A DP2 student in Whitefield or on Sarjapur Road whose best Mathematics AA HL option teaches out of Jayanagar is looking at a weekday evening spent crossing the city, and evening traffic on that route can stretch a short trip badly. The same pair meet online at seven instead, with the exploration already open. Families in Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Electronic City describe the identical trade.

In Hyderabad the pattern repeats around office hours. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District empty out slowly on weekday evenings, and a tutor travelling from Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills or Secunderabad into Kokapet for a two-hour HL session spends more time in a car than in the lesson. IBDP online tuition in Hyderabad mostly exists for that reason and not for any preference about screens. Chennai families in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery and along Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) say much the same, with Perungudi and Alwarpet adding their own evening squeeze.

Outside those cities the argument changes from convenience to availability. Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, a family in Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Thiruvananthapuram, Visakhapatnam or Madurai may find no local DP Physics HL teacher at all, and the same holds across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa and Nashik. Online is not the convenient option there. It is the only option, which is why requests for IBDP online tuition in India arrive as often from Vijayawada or Aurangabad as from a metro suburb.

The metros still dominate the enquiry list. Parents look for IBDP online tuition in Mumbai from Bandra and Powai, IBDP online tuition in Delhi from Noida, IBDP online tuition in Pune from Koregaon Park, and IBDP online tuition in Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad through the rest of the year. What differs is not the lesson. It is what the family gives up by choosing it: in a metro, an evening; outside one, nothing, because there was no local alternative to give up.
items: A Whitefield student reaches a Jayanagar tutor at seven without crossing Bengaluru
Gachibowli and Kokapet families avoid a two-hour round trip for one lesson
Chennai: Adyar, Velachery and OMR households share the same evening squeeze
Kochi, Coimbatore and Visakhapatnam often have no local HL subject teacher
Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Raipur choose online for supply, not convenience

contentBlocks.heading: School deadlines in India that decide when the IA draft is ready
contentBlocks.body:
Schools set the internal calendar, and the internal calendar is what actually governs an IA. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore appear only because Indian families recognise the kind of calendar an international school runs.

That calendar has predictable pressure points. A research question approved. A first draft submitted. One round of written feedback. A final version. The IB's position is that a teacher may comment on one draft, and schools build their deadlines around that single round, which is why a student who misses the draft deadline loses the only formal feedback they were entitled to. Mock examinations usually land in the same window, and CAS commitments are rarely far behind.

Then there is the predicted grade. Schools form it from the evidence they hold, and no tutor can change it by asking. What a tutor can do is make the next piece of work better, which changes the evidence. A tutor who offers to get a prediction raised is describing something outside their control, and you should read the offer as a warning. Parents in Delhi NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region raise this constantly in DP2, usually in January, usually after the draft round has already closed.

Ask the DP coordinator three things in writing at the start of DP2: the internal deadline for each subject's IA, whether draft feedback will be written or verbal, and the date the school submits work for similarity checking. Those three dates set the tuition plan. Everything else, including how many sessions a week are worth booking, follows from them. Write them somewhere the student can see them.
items: Get each subject's internal IA deadline from the coordinator in writing
Confirm whether the school's draft feedback is written or given verbally
Mock examinations and final IA versions usually collide in the same weeks
Predicted grades come from school evidence; no tutor can negotiate them
The May session suits the Indian school year; results follow in early July

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid for a DP student in India drafting an IA?
contentBlocks.body:
Take the three honestly. A home tutor sitting beside a DP student sees what a camera does not: the page pushed away, the calculator reached for far too early, the working written down and then scratched out. For a student who avoids starting, that physical presence is worth more than any software. A home tuition slot also survives a bad network evening, and the tutor meets the household, which tells them more about the student's week than a call ever will.

Online wins on a different axis. The draft already lives on a screen, and so does the tutor's annotation of it, which means IBDP online tuition in India fits IA work more naturally than it fits, say, a hand-drawn geometry lesson. Version history stays visible. A marked past paper can be back with the student the same night. And the specialist who teaches Mathematics AA HL properly may live in another city, which is the whole reason a family in Coimbatore or Nashik ends up online in the first place.

Hybrid is what most DP2 families settle into without ever planning it. Home sessions at the weekend for the long working stretches, online sessions midweek for draft review and quick marking. The trade-off is coordination: two modes mean two sets of materials, and a tutor who does not keep one shared folder will lose track of which version of the exploration is current. Agree the folder before the first lesson, not in March.

Where online genuinely loses: a student who needs someone in the room to stay on task, a subject where handwritten working matters and the student will not photograph it, and a household where the only quiet room is also the family room at eight in the evening. Home classes solve the first. The second is fixable in one conversation, because the student can photograph the page or the tutor can work from a document camera. Nothing solves the third except moving the slot earlier.
items: Home tutoring suits a student who will not start without someone present
Online suits IA drafting: the document and the criteria share one screen
Hybrid: weekend home sessions for depth, midweek online ones for drafts
One shared folder for every version, whichever mode the week uses
Online fails where the only quiet room is the family room at eight

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check an online DP tutor before the IA season?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for three things and judge the answers yourself. Which DP subjects and levels they have actually taught, not studied. What their position is on editing a student's internal assessment. And what you, the parent, receive after each session. A tutor who answers the second question vaguely should not be handed a DP2 draft.

IB Gram verifies profiles before they go live: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the subjects and levels the tutor says they teach. That is a floor, not a judgement about whether this person suits your child. Verification cannot see whether a tutor explains criterion C well, or whether they will hold a boundary at eleven at night when a deadline is two days away and an anxious parent is asking for one small fix. Ask the platform what was checked and what was not, and treat any refusal to answer as information.

So run your own checks in the trial. Give the tutor a real paragraph from the student's draft and ask what they would say to the student about it. The useful answer names a criterion and asks a question. The unhelpful answer is a rewritten paragraph pasted into the chat window. Ask how they would mark a Paper 2 extended-response answer with the student watching, and whether the student or the tutor holds the pen. Watch the silence after your question too, because a tutor who rushes to fill it will do the same to a thinking student.

Then check the operational details, because those decide whether the arrangement survives February. Ask whether sessions are recorded and who keeps the recording. Ask what happens to a missed slot. Ask how a marked script is shared: a photograph buried in a chat thread is not a record you can read three weeks later. A home tutor faces the same questions, but online makes the answers easier to verify, because almost everything leaves a file behind.
items: Ask which DP subjects and levels the tutor has taught, not studied
Ask their exact position on editing a student's internal assessment
Test the trial with a real paragraph and listen for a named criterion
Confirm recording, storage and who can see the session afterwards
Agree how marked scripts are shared and stored, not photographed into chat

contentBlocks.heading: The running order of an online DP lesson, minute by minute
contentBlocks.body:
A good online DP session has a shape, and the shape shows itself in the first two minutes. It opens with the student saying what changed since last time, not with the tutor talking. It closes with the student writing the next action in their own words. Between those two points the hour usually splits into a marking block and a drafting block.

The marking block is where a past paper gets done live. The student's attempt is on screen, the mark scheme sits beside it, and the tutor works through question by question, asking what the examiner was looking for before saying anything about the answer itself. For a science Paper 1B data-based question that means reading the stimulus aloud and identifying what the data actually shows. For a Paper 2 extended-response answer it means counting the marks available and checking whether the answer contains that many distinct points. Marking live is slower than marking privately and returning a score. It is also the only version where the student learns the mark scheme instead of merely receiving it.

The drafting block is the IA. Criteria on one side, draft on the other, cursor under the student's control. The tutor reads a paragraph, names the criterion it is meant to serve, and asks the student to read it again against the descriptor. Often the student fixes it without being told anything at all. When they cannot, the tutor teaches the underlying skill using a different example and then returns to the draft. Nobody types in that document except the student, and the version history shows exactly that.

Ninety minutes is long for a screen. Split it: forty minutes marking, a genuine break away from the desk, forty minutes drafting, five minutes to write the next action. A DP2 student who has been in school since morning will fade in the last quarter of any session, which is why the writing down happens before the fade rather than after it.
items: 1. First five minutes: the student says what changed since the last session.
2. Next forty minutes: a past paper marked live, question by question.
3. A real break away from the desk, camera off, roughly five minutes.
4. Next forty minutes: the IA draft read against one criterion at a time.
5. Last five minutes: the student writes the next action in their own words.

contentBlocks.heading: What similarity checking sees, and the line a tutor holds
contentBlocks.body:
Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft; it does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit the student's submission. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone.

Stated as examples, because the abstract version helps nobody. A tutor may teach the statistical test the investigation needs, question why a conclusion does not follow from the graph, point at criterion D and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it, mark a past paper, or explain what the command term evaluate actually demands. A tutor may not draft a research question and hand it over, write the evaluation section, rewrite a paragraph as an example and let it stay in the document, or fix the language of a submission line by line. The first list is teaching. The second is somebody else's work under the student's name.

Similarity checking compares a submission against published sources and against other submitted work. It does not know who was on a video call. What it does expose, and what a teacher who has read the student all year notices immediately, is a sudden change of register: an introduction written in a sixteen-year-old's voice followed by an evaluation written in nobody's voice. Teachers raise that mismatch far more often than software does.

On progress, be patient and specific. Expect a visible change in one criterion within three or four sessions, not a transformed grade in a month. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any tutor who offers one is telling you they do not understand how criteria are moderated. If nothing has shifted after six sessions, change something: the tutor, the mode, or the number of subjects being tutored at once. A home tutor is sometimes the right change, rather than more online hours.
items: A tutor may question reasoning, teach a skill, and mark practice work
A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of the submission
Similarity checking reads text, but the subject teacher reads the register
Expect one criterion to move in three or four sessions, not a grade
No tutor can guarantee a grade; treat any such offer as a warning

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IBDP online tuition in India with a draft and a past paper
contentBlocks.body:
Have two files ready before the first session: the current version of the internal assessment, and one recent marked past paper or test script. That is enough. A tutor can plan a term from those two documents far faster than from any amount of description, because one shows what the student writes and the other shows what they do under time pressure.

Practical setup takes about ten minutes. A laptop rather than a phone, because the student needs the criteria and the draft side by side. Headphones. A quiet slot the household agrees to respect. If the subject involves handwritten working, a phone camera and a shared folder are enough to start; a graphics tablet helps but is not a requirement. Agree where marked scripts will live, and keep every version of the IA in one place with dates in the file names.

After each session you should receive a short written note, and you should ask for one if it does not arrive. It needs four things: what was covered, which criterion or paper section was worked on, what the student is doing before the next session, and one honest line about how the hour went. Not a grade prediction. Not a paragraph of encouragement. A parent who reads four of those notes in a row can tell whether anything is moving, which is more reliable than asking a tired seventeen-year-old how tuition is going.

Then keep the arrangement under review. Two subjects tutored at once is normal in DP2. Four usually means the timetable needs fixing before the teaching does. If the student is sleeping badly, cutting a session is a better decision than adding one, and a good tutor will say so first. Availability depends on level and schedule, so give two possible slots rather than one when you write in.
items: Bring the current IA version and one recent marked past paper
A laptop, not a phone: criteria and draft must sit side by side
One dated folder for every IA version and every marked script
Expect a written note after each session, covering four specific things
Ask for a different tutor early if the fit is clearly wrong

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with an IBDP internal assessment at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the skill the assessment needs, question the reasoning, mark practice work, and point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. What no tutor may do is write, rewrite or edit the submission. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to comment on one draft; it does not extend that permission to anyone outside the school. Everything genuinely useful happens on the teaching side of that line.

faqs.question: My child's tutor offered to polish the IA before submission. Is that allowed?
faqs.answer: No, and the offer tells you something about the tutor. Polishing a submission line by line is editing, which the IB does not permit from a tutor or from a parent. The honest version looks different: the tutor names the criterion a weak paragraph is failing, explains what the descriptor asks for, and the student rewrites it themselves. If the writing genuinely needs work, that is a skill to teach across several sessions, not a service to buy in the final week before a deadline.

faqs.question: What will the school's similarity checking actually pick up?
faqs.answer: It compares the submitted work against published sources and against other submitted work, so copied text and reused material surface quickly. It does not know who was on a video call. The stronger detector is the subject teacher, who has read the student's writing all year and notices when one section arrives in a completely different register. That mismatch is usually what starts a conversation, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than by the school on its own.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark a past paper live over a screen?
faqs.answer: The student's attempt is shared on screen and the tutor works through it question by question, asking what the examiner wanted before commenting on the answer. For a science Paper 1B data-based question that means reading the stimulus and saying what the data shows. For a Paper 2 extended response it means counting the marks available and checking that the answer contains that many distinct points. It is slower than returning a score by email, and considerably more useful.

faqs.question: We are in Chennai and the right Economics HL tutor is in Delhi. Does online really work?
faqs.answer: For DP2 subject work, usually yes. A student in Adyar or Anna Nagar working with a tutor in Delhi NCR loses physical presence and gains a specialist who has actually taught the level. Ask for a trial on the student's own material before committing, and watch whether the tutor holds attention for a full session over a screen. If the student drifts badly in that trial, a local home tutor with slightly less subject depth may still be the better arrangement.

faqs.question: There are no IB tutors in Kochi. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Online is the realistic answer, and it is why families across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai rely on it. Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam and Madurai rarely have a local DP Physics HL or Mathematics AA HL teacher free in the evenings. The same applies across central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur and Nashik. Online tuition there is not a compromise on a home visit, because there was no home visit available to compare it against.

faqs.question: What should I receive as a parent after each online session?
faqs.answer: A short written note, and you should ask for one if it does not arrive. It should say what was covered, which criterion or paper section was worked on, what the student is doing before the next session, and one honest line about how the hour went. Four of those notes read together will tell you whether anything is moving. A grade prediction is not part of it, and neither is a paragraph of reassurance written to keep you calm.

faqs.question: Is home tuition better than online tuition for IA work?
faqs.answer: Not usually, though it is better for some students. IA work lives in a document, so a screen is where the criteria and the draft naturally sit side by side. Home tuition wins where the student will not begin without someone in the room, or where handwritten working matters and the student will not photograph it. Plenty of DP2 families in Bengaluru and Pune end up hybrid: home sessions at the weekend for long work, online midweek for draft review.

faqs.question: How long and how often should online DP sessions be?
faqs.answer: Most DP students manage one session a week per subject, of sixty to ninety minutes, and ninety only if it is split with a real break. A screen session at the end of an Indian school day competes with homework, CAS and sleep. Two subjects tutored at once is common in DP2; four is usually a sign that something else needs fixing, most often the timetable rather than the teaching. Frequency depends on level and schedule.

faqs.question: What equipment does the student actually need?
faqs.answer: A laptop, headphones and a stable connection cover most of it. A phone will not do for IA sessions, because the criteria and the draft need to be visible together. If the subject involves handwritten working, a phone camera and a shared folder are enough to get scripts to the tutor; a graphics tablet is a convenience rather than a requirement. Agree the folder and how files will be named in the first session, before versions start multiplying.

faqs.question: Mock results were poor in DP2. Is it too late to start online tuition?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to narrow. With the May session ahead, target the papers where marks are cheapest to recover instead of attempting full syllabus coverage. Read what the mock script shows: unfinished papers point at timing, lost explanation marks point at technique, and blank topics point at content. Internal assessment deadlines may already have passed, in which case tuition belongs entirely on the externally assessed papers. Confirm every remaining date with the DP coordinator.

faqs.question: How is IBDP online tuition in India usually priced?
faqs.answer: By the hour, and it varies with level, subject and how experienced the tutor is, so treat any single figure you read online with suspicion. Higher Level sessions and scarce subjects generally sit above Standard Level ones. An online slot usually costs less than an equivalent home tuition slot, because nobody is paying for travel time. Ask what a trial costs, what notice is needed to cancel a session, and whether unused sessions carry over.

The deciding question in DP2 is simple: does the student need attention on one document, or coverage of a syllabus?

h1: IBDP Tuition in India: Reading Criterion Feedback Before You Start
heroTitle: Reading DP Evidence Before You Book Tuition in India
heroSubtitle: Most parents arrive with a worry and a report card. Start instead with the four things a Diploma Programme school has already told you: criterion comments, a predicted grade, a returned internal assessment draft and a marked mock script. Read those properly and the hiring decision usually makes itself.
introSummary: IBDP tuition in India is worth starting only when the evidence from school says a tutor can fix something, and a home tutor sitting beside the student is the usual first form it takes. That evidence is specific: the criterion comments on an internal assessment draft, the predicted grade the school has formed, the marked mock script, and the pattern of marks lost across Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2. Those four sources answer different questions. One shows a content gap, one shows a writing problem, one shows a timing problem, and the fourth tells you how the school currently reads your child. This page is about reading them before you spend anything, because tuition for IB Diploma students is often the second-best answer.

contentBlocks.heading: From a marked script to a shortlist: how IBDP tuition in India starts
contentBlocks.body:
A useful shortlist starts from a sentence with evidence in it. "My son needs help in Physics" produces a general Physics tutor. "My son is in DP2, takes Physics at Higher Level, lost most of his marks on the extended response questions in Paper 2 of the school mock while Paper 1A was fine, and his scientific investigation came back with a low Evaluation score" produces someone who has marked that kind of work before. The second request is no harder to write. It only asks that you read the papers already sitting in the house.

So the first step is yours. Gather the marked mock script, the internal assessment draft with the teacher's criterion comments, the latest report with its predicted grades, and one honest week of the student's timetable. Then send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school's mock and deadline calendar, your location and the slots that are genuinely free. From that it shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose subjects and levels match, subject to tutor availability in your area.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Treat it as a diagnostic appointment rather than a sales call. Hand the tutor the criterion feedback and ask what they would work on in the first three sessions, and why. A tutor who answers with a general revision plan has not read the evidence. A tutor who says the Data analysis marks are already strong and the loss is in the Conclusion has.

Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. And if the trial ends with the tutor saying the student needs two sessions on one skill rather than a standing weekly slot, that is a result worth paying attention to.
items: 1. Send the mock script, IA draft and report, not a general worry.
2. IB Gram asks about subject, level, mock dates, location and free slots.
3. A shortlist of verified profiles matched to that evidence, subject to availability.
4. A demo or trial where the tutor reads the criterion feedback with you.
5. Home, online or hybrid lessons, with a different match if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: DP1 or DP2: which year's evidence are you actually reading?
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme runs over two years, DP1 and DP2. A student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level, which carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well. Schools here almost all enter candidates for the May session, which sits inside an academic year running roughly April to March, and results are released in early July.

The question of whether IBDP tuition in India is needed in DP1 is not the same question asked in DP2, because the evidence means different things. A DP1 term grade is a snapshot of a course that is nowhere near finished. Higher Level content arrives at a different rate from Standard Level content, and those extra ninety hours have to land somewhere, so a dip in an HL subject in the first two terms is often pacing rather than capability. Wait a unit. Look at whether the same topic type fails twice.

A DP2 mock is a different animal. It is a rehearsal of the real paper, written under something close to real conditions, and it is one of the main things a school uses when it forms a predicted grade. A weak DP2 mock is worth acting on quickly, because the calendar between mocks and May is short and every other subject wants the same hours.

The practical difference is this. In DP1 you are deciding whether a habit needs correcting. In DP2 you are deciding where a limited number of remaining hours should go, and that is a harder decision made under more pressure.
items: Six subjects from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level
Higher Level runs to 240 recommended teaching hours, Standard Level to 150
Each subject graded 1 to 7; TOK and the EE add up to 3 points
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions
May session for almost every school here, with results in early July

contentBlocks.heading: What a low criterion score tells you in Physics, Maths AA and English A
contentBlocks.body:
Criterion feedback is the most misread document a DP parent holds. It is not a mark out of a hundred in disguise. Each criterion measures a separate skill, and the pattern across them is the diagnosis.

Take the sciences. The internal assessment is the scientific investigation, worth 20% of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, inside a 3,000 word maximum. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. A student who scores well on Data analysis and poorly on Research design can handle numbers but did not plan the experiment properly, and that is one long conversation about variables and method, not twelve weeks of subject tuition. Reverse it and the diagnosis reverses: strong design, weak analysis, and there is real technique to teach. Low Conclusion and Evaluation with everything else solid is almost always a writing problem. The student did the science and then failed to say what the result meant against the hypothesis, or to name the limitations honestly.

Mathematics behaves the same way. The exploration is the same task for Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) at both levels: 20% of the grade, 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 on five criteria. A Presentation and B Mathematical communication carry 4 marks each, C Personal engagement and D Reflection 3 each, and E Use of mathematics 6, with HL work judged against a higher standard on E. A high E with a low B means the mathematics is sound and the writing around it is not. That is an editing skill and it moves quickly.

In English A, read the teacher's comments for verbs. Command terms set the depth an answer needs, and describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent are not interchangeable. A student who describes where the question said evaluate will lose marks in every subject on the timetable, not only in one.
items: Scientific investigation: four criteria of 6 marks, 20% of the subject grade
Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion, Evaluation, inside a 3,000 word maximum
Mathematics exploration: 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 on five criteria
Criterion E, Use of mathematics, carries 6 marks and a higher HL standard
Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data-based, Paper 2 extended response
Command terms set depth: describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent

contentBlocks.heading: Where a DP diagnosis gets harder to act on across India
contentBlocks.body:
Reading the evidence is the same everywhere. Acting on it is not, because the tutor who can read a Higher Level Chemistry investigation is not evenly spread across the country. Families search for IBDP tuition in India from Delhi NCR, from a tower in Worli and from smaller cities where the nearest DP school is a long drive away, and the honest answer differs by place.

In Delhi NCR the pool is deep and the geography is punishing. A family in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri usually has options within a reasonable radius. Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad sit further out, and a tutor coming from Golf Course Road in Gurugram (Gurgaon) to Sector 128 Noida in the evening is crossing the worst hour of the day. Searches for IBDP tuition in Delhi and across the Noida belt often end in a hybrid week for exactly that reason. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is split by the same problem. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are dense enough to support home visits; Powai, Thane, Vashi, Navi Mumbai and Kharghar are a different calculation, and parents looking for IBDP tuition in Mumbai from those pockets should test an online trial before assuming a weekday evening slot will hold through DP2.

Bengaluru spreads in every direction. Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar are workable; Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road each sit on their own traffic problem, so IBDP tuition in Bangalore is usually planned around which side of the city the tutor lives on. In Chennai, Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are comparatively easy, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar stretch the evening commute. Pune divides between Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Viman Nagar on one side and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad, Kharadi and Hinjewadi on the other, and IBDP tuition in Pune tends to follow that line.

For IBDP tuition in Hyderabad the Gachibowli corridor holds most of the demand. Families asking about IBDP tuition in Kolkata or IBDP tuition in Ahmedabad often find that the subject, not the postcode, decides the answer. If nobody within reach has marked a scientific investigation before, widen the search online rather than settling for a general tutor who happens to be nearby.
items: Delhi NCR: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Dwarka, Noida and Greater Noida
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Juhu, Powai, Thane, Vashi and Kharghar
Bengaluru: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Hebbal and Electronic City
Chennai: Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) and Anna Nagar
Pune: Koregaon Park, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi and Wakad
Outside these clusters, an online trial widens the shortlist faster than waiting

contentBlocks.heading: What should the DP coordinator fix before you pay for tuition in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Before spending anything on IBDP tuition in India, spend an hour with the school. Most of the evidence you need is held there, and some of what worries you is free to fix. Parents whose children attend schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School and Mahindra International School ask the same questions every year, and a subject teacher is usually willing to answer them. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Ask for the markscheme alongside the returned script, not instead of it. A mock paper without its markscheme gives you a number; with it, you can see whether the marks were lost on recall, on method, or on the last two extended response questions where a student who ran out of time simply stops writing. Ask which papers and which pieces of work the predicted grade was formed from, because a prediction built on one bad fortnight reads very differently from one built on four terms. Ask when the DP2 mock examinations fall, since each school sets its own dates, usually several months before the May session.

Ask about the internal assessment timetable too. The school's deadline is almost always earlier than the one the student believes, and for the mathematics exploration the teacher can comment on one draft. That single comment is valuable, and some students waste it by submitting a half-finished attempt to meet a date.

Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show how marks are awarded rather than how a parent feels they should have been. A coordinator who agrees to a fortnightly check on one subject may solve the whole thing without outside help. But if that conversation produces nothing concrete, you at least now know precisely what you would be hiring for.
items: Ask which papers and which work the predicted grade was formed from
Request the markscheme alongside the returned mock script, not instead of it
Mock dates are set by each school, usually months before the May session
Subject reports and past papers come through the school or IB official channels
Confirm the internal assessment deadline the school is actually working to

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which one shows you the problem?
contentBlocks.body:
The three modes are not equally good at diagnosis, which matters more than usual on a page about deciding. Pick the one that can expose the thing you suspect.

A home tutor is the strongest choice when the suspected fault is invisible on a finished page. Working written on paper, a diagram redrawn three times, a student who reaches for the calculator before reading the question, the hour at which the desk is actually occupied: a home tutor sees all of it, and none of it survives into the answer you were shown. Timing problems in particular are easiest to catch with someone in the room and a clock on the table. Home classes also remove the travel the student would otherwise lose, which on a DP2 week is not a small thing. The cost is the tutor's own travel. Evening traffic across a large metro can shorten a home session before it begins, and a missed slot during the mock fortnight is hard to replace.

Online is the stronger choice for reach and for reading written work closely. A Higher Level subject with few local teachers becomes reachable from anywhere, and a shared screen holding a script and a markscheme side by side is a good place to work through criterion feedback line by line. What online loses is everything happening off camera. A student can look attentive and be somewhere else entirely.

Hybrid is where most diagnosing families end up. One home session a fortnight for the things that need a person in the room, shorter online reviews in between for marking and follow-up. Start with home tuition if you cannot yet name the problem. Move weight online once you can, and keep one home session in the month so nobody loses sight of how the student actually works when left alone.
items: A home tutor sees the working on paper, not only the final answer
Online sessions reach a Higher Level specialist living in another city
Hybrid: one home session a fortnight, shorter online reviews in between
Timed practice is easier to police with someone in the room
Heavy evening traffic can shorten a home session before it begins

contentBlocks.heading: Which tutor can actually read the feedback you are holding?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification answers two different questions, and families usually ask only the first. The platform's job is to check who the tutor is: identity, claimed qualifications, and the subjects and levels they actually teach, before a profile goes live. Your job is to check whether this particular person can read the particular document in your hand.

That second check takes one trial session. Put the marked mock script or the returned investigation in front of them and ask three things. Which criterion would you target first, and why that one. What would the next four sessions look like, concretely. And what will you not do. The last question matters most in the Diploma Programme, because internal assessment work must be the student's own. A tutor who offers to tidy up an exploration or rewrite a conclusion is offering something that can put the student's diploma at risk, and that offer should end the conversation there.

Listen for specifics. Someone who has marked scientific investigations will talk about Evaluation in terms of limitations and realistic improvements rather than in terms of neatness. Someone who has taught the exploration will know that criterion E is where Higher Level work is held to a higher standard, and will say so without being prompted. Someone who has taught neither will talk about experience in general and about building the student's confidence.

Do the ordinary checks as well, because no platform sees everything. Meet the tutor before the first home session, agree who is in the house while lessons run, and keep the first commitment short. A month is long enough to tell whether the diagnosis was right, and short enough that being wrong costs the family very little.
items: Identity, qualifications and the subjects and levels each tutor actually teaches
Ask the tutor to mark one of your child's paragraphs against the descriptor
Ask what they will not do, including writing any part of the IA
Check they know which criteria the school has already commented on
Meet before the first home visit and keep the first commitment short

contentBlocks.heading: Does your DP child need IBDP tuition in India at all?
contentBlocks.body:
IBDP tuition in India earns its place when a named problem exists, a tutor can move it, and the student has the hours to spare. Miss any one of those three and the money buys stress.

Start with the predicted grade, read honestly. The school forms it from its own evidence and its own professional judgement. It is not a promise, not a verdict, and not something a tutor can change by asking. It can be informed by better work arriving before the school settles its view, which is a slower and less certain thing than most parents are told. If the prediction is a point below what you hoped, the useful question is not how to raise the number. It is which piece of work the school is reading when it writes that number down.

Then separate the three problems, because they look identical on a report and need completely different responses. A content gap shows as consistent failure on one topic type across several assessments while everything else holds. A writing problem shows as correct thinking that loses marks anyway: right answer, wrong command term, missing justification, a conclusion that restates the result instead of evaluating it. A timing problem shows as strong early questions and thin or blank later ones, or an internal assessment handed in at a rush with the Evaluation section visibly shorter than the rest. Content gaps respond well to tuition. Writing problems respond to tuition only when the tutor marks against criteria instead of explaining the content again. Timing problems often respond to nothing but supervised practice and a shorter week.

And sometimes the honest answer is fewer commitments. A student carrying three Higher Levels, CAS activities on two evenings, an Extended Essay that has not been started and a weekend obligation has no room for another appointment. Removing one thing may do more than adding one. Say that out loud before you hire anybody.
items: Step 1: Read the criterion comments and note which criterion is lowest.
Step 2: Separate the content gap, the writing problem and the timing problem.
Step 3: Ask the subject teacher what they would fix first.
Step 4: Count the committed hours in a real week, including CAS and travel.
Step 5: Remove a commitment before adding one, if the week is already full.
Step 6: Only then hire, and only for the specific problem you named.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging DP home classes by the next mock, not by the next session
contentBlocks.body:
Give IBDP tuition in India one full assessment cycle before you judge it. In practice that means six to eight weeks, or whatever period ends with a school assessment in that subject, whichever comes later. Anything shorter and you are reading noise. Anything much longer and you have stopped evaluating altogether.

What should move first is not the grade. Grades on criterion-marked work move slowly, because the same descriptors are applied by the same teacher to work of gradually improving quality. What should move first is the shape of the student's answers. An evaluation paragraph that names a specific limitation instead of saying the experiment could be improved. A mathematics exploration paragraph that explains why a method was chosen. A Paper 2 answer that responds to the command term it was actually given. Ask the tutor, at week four, what evidence they have that anything has changed, and expect a piece of the student's own work as the answer rather than an impression.

The second signal is the error log. If the same mistake keeps arriving in week six that arrived in week one, either the diagnosis was wrong or the work between sessions is not happening. Both are fixable, and both need saying rather than waiting out.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any promise of a particular score should make you cautious rather than relieved. What honest home tuition offers is a clearer picture of what is wrong and steady work on it. There is also an end point, which nobody mentions often enough. When the student can do alone what the tutor was doing alongside them, the sessions should reduce and then stop. Dependence is a real cost in DP2, because the examination hall contains exactly one person.
items: Judge against the next assessment cycle, not against the next session
Early movement shows in structure and command term use, before grades shift
An error log that stops repeating the same mistake is real progress
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a promise of one is a warning sign
Stop when the student can do alone what the tutor did alongside them

contentBlocks.heading: Bringing the evidence to a first DP home session in India
contentBlocks.body:
The first session is worth preparing for, because it is the only one where the tutor knows nothing and has to find out everything. Twenty minutes of gathering beforehand changes what that hour can do.

Put four things on the table. The marked mock script, with the markscheme if the school released it. The internal assessment draft with the teacher's criterion comments still on it, unedited. The latest report, including the predicted grades. And one honest week of the timetable, with school hours, CAS, travel and the evenings that are genuinely free. That last document is the one families are most tempted to improve, and the one that most often explains the problem on its own.

A good first session then looks like this. The tutor reads the evidence in front of the student rather than about them. They pick one criterion or one question type and work through it out loud, so you can watch the gap being found instead of described. They set one piece of work for the coming week, small enough that it will actually be done. And they say what they think the problem is, in a sentence you could repeat to the subject teacher without translating it.

What happens afterwards is your decision, and it should stay a small one at first. Agree a short initial run, agree a review date, and agree who reports what to whom. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match; that is a normal request and not a complaint. And if the first session ends with the tutor telling you the student needs a fortnight of supervised timed practice rather than a standing weekly commitment, take the advice. It is the most useful thing a tutor can say and the least profitable one.
items: Bring the marked mock script and, where available, the markscheme
Bring the IA draft with the teacher's criterion comments still on it
Bring one honest week of the timetable, including CAS and travel
Name the single problem you want solved in the first month
Agree a review date and who reports what to whom

faqs.question: Does my DP child need tuition, or is this just a hard term?
faqs.answer: Usually a hard term, and the evidence will tell you which. Look for repetition rather than a single low result: the same topic type failing across two or three assessments, or the same criterion flagged twice by the teacher, points to a real gap. One poor paper in a fortnight that also held a deadline, an illness or a CAS trip does not. Give a single bad result one more assessment cycle before acting, unless it lands in DP2, where the calendar is short enough that waiting costs more than starting.

faqs.question: What does a low score on one internal assessment criterion actually mean?
faqs.answer: It names the skill that failed, which is far more useful than a total. In the sciences, the investigation is marked on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation at 6 marks each. A low Research design with strong Data analysis means the planning failed, not the science. A low Conclusion and Evaluation with the rest intact is a writing problem. In the mathematics exploration, a high criterion E with a low criterion B means the mathematics is right and the communication around it is not. Fix the named skill, not the whole subject.

faqs.question: The predicted grade came back lower than we expected. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Ask the school which work it was formed from, before doing anything else. A prediction is the school's professional judgement built on its own evidence, and knowing whether it rests on one mock or on four terms of work changes what is worth doing next. No tutor can change a prediction directly. Better work arriving before the school settles its view can inform it, which is slower and less certain than parents are often led to believe. Treat the number as information about how the school reads your child, then work on the underlying piece.

faqs.question: How do I tell a timing problem from a content gap on a mock script?
faqs.answer: Read the script in order and watch where the marks stop. A timing problem leaves strong early answers and thin, rushed or blank later ones, often in Paper 2 where the extended response questions sit at the end. A content gap is scattered instead: the student loses marks on one topic wherever it appears, early or late, and gains them comfortably elsewhere. If the last two questions are empty and everything before them is solid, more subject teaching will not help. Supervised timed practice will, and it costs less.

faqs.question: Should the first diagnostic sessions be at home or online?
faqs.answer: At home, if you cannot yet name the problem. A home tutor sees the rough working, the hesitation, the calculator reached for too early and the state of the desk, and none of that appears in the finished answer you were shown. Once the problem is named and it is clearly a content gap, online is efficient and widens the choice of tutor considerably. Many families settle on a hybrid week: one home session a fortnight, with shorter online reviews in between for marking and follow-up.

faqs.question: Can the diagnosis be done online if we are in Whitefield or Gachibowli and no tutor lives nearby?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one adjustment. Ask for the student's written work to be photographed and sent before the session, rough working included, so the tutor is reading paper rather than a clean typed version. On camera, ask for one question to be attempted live rather than discussed afterwards. Families across Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City and the Gachibowli corridor commonly work this way, because a specialist for a particular Higher Level subject may simply not exist within travelling distance of the house.

faqs.question: What should we have ready at home before the first session?
faqs.answer: Four documents and a quiet table. The marked mock script with its markscheme if the school released it, the internal assessment draft with the teacher's criterion comments left exactly as they were written, the latest report including predicted grades, and one honest week of the timetable showing school hours, CAS, travel and genuinely free evenings. Resist tidying any of it. The unedited draft and the real timetable are the two documents that most often explain the problem, and both lose their value once improved.

faqs.question: How long should we give it before deciding tuition is not working?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks, or until the next school assessment in that subject, whichever falls later. Criterion-marked grades move slowly, so judge the shape of the work first: an evaluation paragraph that names a specific limitation, an answer that matches its command term, a method choice that is explained rather than assumed. At week four, ask the tutor what evidence exists that anything has changed, and expect a piece of your child's own work in reply rather than a general impression of progress.

faqs.question: My child has three Higher Levels, CAS and an Extended Essay that has not started. Should we add tuition?
faqs.answer: Probably not yet, and possibly not at all. A week already at capacity cannot absorb another appointment, and adding one usually costs sleep, which shows up as exactly the timing problems you are trying to solve. Map the real hours first, travel and CAS included. If something has to give, decide what comes off the list before deciding what goes on it. If tuition is still needed after that, take it in one subject rather than three, and review the arrangement after a month.

faqs.question: Is searching for IBDP tuition near me the right approach, or does the subject decide?
faqs.answer: The subject decides more often than the postcode does. For a widely taught Standard Level subject, a nearby home tutor is usually both available and better, because physical presence adds something real. For a Higher Level subject that few people teach, insisting on proximity means choosing a generalist over someone who has actually marked that kind of work. Search locally first, give it a fortnight, then widen online rather than settling. A good distant tutor beats a convenient wrong one in the Diploma Programme.

faqs.question: Should we simply wait for the next mock before starting anything?
faqs.answer: It depends on which year the student is in. In DP1 waiting is often right, because a course that is a third finished produces unreliable evidence and a second data point costs you very little. In DP2 the calendar argues the other way: mock dates are set months before the May session, results arrive in early July, and the weeks in between are already spoken for. In DP2, act on the evidence you have and treat the next mock as the review point rather than the starting gun.

A one-to-one home tutor sees how the student works; an online tutor reaches a subject specialist you cannot find locally; a batch gives peer comparison at a lower cost per hour; a recorded course closes a clean content gap cheaply. The deciding trade-off is whether your problem is visible in finished written work, or only in how that work gets made.
