h1: IBDP Tutor Near Me: Where DP Specialists Actually Are
heroTitle: Where DP Teaching Capacity Sits Across India
heroSubtitle: Diploma Programme teaching is concentrated where IB schools are. This page explains what that means if you live in Powai, in Kochi, or somewhere with no international school at all: how far a home tutor will travel for a Higher Level session, and when a distant specialist online is simply the better answer.
introSummary: Searching for an IBDP tutor near me in India returns whoever is closest, not whoever teaches your subject, and for the Diploma Programme those are rarely the same person. Home tuition still works well in the pockets of every metro where IB schools cluster, because that is where DP teachers live. Outside those pockets the local pool thins fast, and it thins by subject before it thins by programme. A family in Whitefield has options a family in Jabalpur does not. So the useful question is not who is nearest. It is which of your six subjects genuinely needs someone in the room, which can be taught well from another city, and how wide your search has to go before it stops being a search and becomes a decision.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a DP subject request in India become a shortlist by distance?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the six subjects and their levels, not with your pin code. A request that reads Higher Level Chemistry, Standard Level Mathematics Applications and Interpretation, DP2, mocks in January is something a coordinator can act on. A request that reads my son needs a Diploma Programme tutor close by is not, because it describes a radius rather than a need, and a radius cannot be taught.

When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks for the board and programme, each subject with Higher or Standard Level marked, the school's mock dates, your locality and the evenings that are genuinely free once activities and CAS commitments are counted. Location is one filter among several, and it is deliberately applied last. The search runs subject first: everyone who teaches Higher Level Physics for the Diploma Programme, then everyone who can reach Kondapur on a weekday evening, rather than the other way round. Reverse that order and you get a shortlist of people who live nearby and have never taught a DP class in their lives.

What comes back is a set of verified profiles with the levels each person actually teaches named rather than implied. If two of them are a short ride from you and a third teaches online from another city, trial both kinds before you decide anything. A demo or trial session can be arranged first, and a family that watches the same Higher Level question handled by a nearby generalist and by a distant specialist usually stops arguing about distance inside a week.

If the fit turns out wrong, ask for a different match. That is an ordinary request and it is far better made in the first fortnight than in the February of DP2. Availability depends on subject, level and schedule, so an unusual Higher Level combination takes longer to fill than a Standard Level one, and a family that says so early gets a better answer.
items: 1. List all six DP subjects with Higher or Standard Level marked clearly.
2. Add the school's mock window and the May session year.
3. Name your locality and the two evenings that are genuinely free.
4. Ask for a nearby tutor and a distant specialist together.
5. Trial both on the same Higher Level question and compare.
6. Decide subject by subject, not once for the whole timetable.

contentBlocks.heading: DP1, DP2 and the point where a nearby generalist stops being enough
contentBlocks.body:
The International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP) runs over two years, DP1 and DP2. A student takes six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL), which carries 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Every subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the award of the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well.

That structure is the whole reason local supply behaves the way it does. A strong Class 12 science or mathematics teacher can often hold an SL course for a term, because the content overlaps with what is taught widely in Indian schools and the depth is manageable. The 240-hour HL courses are different. The extra hours are not simply more of the same material, and the assessment rewards a kind of answer that a teacher who has never marked against IB command terms does not naturally produce. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each demand a different depth, and a student who writes a good explanation where the paper asked for an evaluation loses marks without understanding why.

So the honest line is drawn at level, not at programme. Across most Indian cities you can find somebody within a reasonable distance who will do useful work with an SL subject. Finding somebody nearby who has taught three HL cohorts through to a May session is a narrower search, and in many places it fails. That failure is not a reflection on your locality. It is arithmetic: the number of people who have taught a given HL subject is small, and they live near the schools that employ them.
items: Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level
HL carries 240 recommended hours, SL 150, each graded 1-7
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points, maximum 45
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the failing conditions
CAS must be completed alongside the six subjects and the core

contentBlocks.heading: Which DP subjects are worth travelling for, and which are not?
contentBlocks.body:
Travel for a Higher Level subject where the local teaching is scarce and the marking is unforgiving, and do not travel for a Standard Level subject your child is already passing. In practice that means Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level Physics and Higher Level Chemistry justify a longer trip or a distant specialist online, while Standard Level Economics and most English A work does not.

Mathematics is the clearest case. DP Mathematics exists as two subjects, each available at HL and SL: Analysis and Approaches (AA), which is algebraic and proof-heavy, and Applications and Interpretation (AI), which is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often steered towards AA, though the right choice depends on the degree and the student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement. AA HL is the single hardest thing to staff locally in most Indian cities, because proof technique is not something a tutor picks up from a textbook the week before. AI HL is staffed even more thinly, since fewer teachers have run it and the technology-led approach is unfamiliar to many.

The sciences split differently. Physics and Chemistry at HL reward a tutor who has watched students lose marks on explanation rather than calculation, which is the standard failure mode for a student trained on numerical drill. Biology at HL is heavy on writing, and a student who can already write reasonable prose often needs less specialist help than the same student in Physics. Economics rewards a tutor who reads command terms properly, and English A rewards close reading and argument, both of which travel well over a screen. Sit down with the six subjects and mark each one travel or do not travel. The list is usually shorter than parents expect.
items: Mathematics AA HL: proof-heavy, algebraic, the hardest subject to staff locally
Mathematics AI HL: modelling and statistics with technology used throughout
Physics and Chemistry HL: explanation marks, not calculation, decide the grade
Biology HL: a writing subject as much as a memory subject
Economics and English A: command terms and argument, both fine on screen

contentBlocks.heading: Mapping DP supply across India: the clusters, the edges and the gaps
contentBlocks.body:
Diploma Programme teachers live where Diploma Programme schools are, and those schools sit in a fairly small number of pockets. In Delhi NCR the pockets are South Delhi and Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri, Dwarka, Golf Course Road in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Sector 128 Noida and, more thinly, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. A parent in Chanakyapuri searching for an IBDP tutor near me in Delhi has a real local pool. A parent in Faridabad searching the same phrase is already looking at a cross-city trip on a weekday evening, which is why so many NCR families end up running a hybrid week.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves the same way. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel, Malabar Hill and Powai hold most of the capacity; Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar hold much less of it, and the harbour and the rail line make an evening crossing unpredictable. A search for an IBDP tutor near me in Mumbai from Thane and the same search from Bandra are not the same search at all. Bengaluru is spread wider: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar, Kanakapura Road and Electronic City each have their own evening traffic problem, and a tutor in Jayanagar will think twice about Whitefield. Hyderabad concentrates around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District, Kokapet, Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills, with Secunderabad a longer haul. Chennai runs along Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Perungudi and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR). Pune clusters in Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Kharadi, Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi.

Beyond the six metros the picture changes in kind, not just in degree. In Gujarat, Ahmedabad holds most of it around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close by and Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot much thinner. In Kolkata and eastern India the capacity sits in Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna have very little. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula form one small pool, and Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have single-figure options in any one HL subject. In southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai are the same story. Central and western India, meaning Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Nashik, Aurangabad and Goa, is where a purely local search usually ends without a match.
items: NCR capacity: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Golf Course Road, Sector 128 Noida
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, then Thane and Kharghar
Bengaluru and Hyderabad: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Gachibowli, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills
Chennai, Pune and Ahmedabad: Adyar, OMR, Koregaon Park, Baner, Bodakdev
Thin pools: Salt Lake, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Kochi, Coimbatore, Indore, Nagpur
A local IBDP tutor is a locality question, never a city question

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar in India that decides how far a DP tutor will travel
contentBlocks.body:
IB schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May session; November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. That single fact sets the rhythm of the whole market. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, mock examinations are set by each school several months before May, and May results are released in early July. Every DP tutor in the country is working to the same clock, which means their diaries fill in the same weeks.

The practical effect on distance is direct. Between roughly September and the mock window, a tutor who already has DP2 students will not add a slot that costs an hour of travel each way, because that hour has to come out of a different family's session. In April and May of DP1, the same tutor will happily take it. So a family in Kharadi or Yelahanka that starts looking in DP1 can often keep a good tutor who lives twenty minutes away, while the same family starting in the October of DP2 is choosing between whoever is left within a very short radius and a specialist online. Anyone typing IBDP tutor near me in India in September is searching a smaller map than the same family would have found in April, and the map has nothing to do with where they live. Timing widens or narrows it more than geography does.

Names like Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore come up constantly in these conversations, and every one of them sets its own internal deadlines. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Ask your school for its mock dates and its internal coursework deadlines before you contact anybody, because those dates decide which half of the year you are hiring into, and that in turn decides how far anyone will drive for you.
items: Schools in India overwhelmingly enter the May session, not November
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March
Each school fixes its own DP2 mock dates, months before May
May results are released in early July, which sets the retake question
Tutor diaries tighten from September, and travel is the first thing cut

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a two-hour Higher Level session?
contentBlocks.body:
For a two-hour Higher Level session the plain comparison is this. Home tuition is best when the student needs supervision as much as teaching, because a tutor in the room sees the page, the hesitation and the phone. Online is best when the specific person who knows your HL subject lives somewhere else, and it costs you nothing in teaching quality if the tutor knows how to annotate a paper on screen. Hybrid, meaning one home session and one online session a week, is what most DP families in big metros settle on, and it exists because travel is the expensive part.

Work through the arithmetic honestly. A home tutor crossing Bengaluru from Hebbal to Sarjapur Road in evening traffic is spending a substantial part of the evening in a car, and that time is paid for somewhere, either in fees, in a shorter session, or in a tutor who arrives tired. That is a real cost, and for Standard Level work it is usually not worth paying. For a DP2 student who will not start a past paper without somebody sitting there, it is worth paying, because the alternative is a session that does not happen.

Online has its own failure mode. A Higher Level Mathematics session where the tutor cannot see the student's working as it is written is a wasted hour, and the fix is mechanical rather than mysterious: a graphics tablet, a second camera pointed at the page, or the student photographing the sheet at each stage. Ask about it at the trial.

Hybrid is the compromise that keeps a good but distant person. The home visit takes the week's hard teaching and the check on habits; the online session takes the follow-up, the marked paper and the quick doubt-solving. Families in Navi Mumbai, Greater Noida and Wakad use this pattern constantly, because it converts a tutor who could never come twice a week into one who comes once.
items: Home tuition wins on supervision, habits and seeing the written working
Online wins on reach, and loses nothing if the setup is right
Hybrid keeps a distant specialist by halving the travel weeks
Ask at the trial how the tutor will see handwritten working online
Standard Level work rarely justifies an hour of a tutor's travel

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a distant HL specialist as closely as a home tutor down the road
contentBlocks.body:
Proximity feels like evidence and is not. A tutor who lives in your building has been checked by nobody, and a tutor three cities away can be checked thoroughly. Before a profile goes live on IB Gram, identity and the qualifications claimed are checked, and the subjects and levels a person says they teach are recorded against their name rather than left vague. A platform can verify documents and history. It cannot verify chemistry between a particular teenager and a particular adult, and it cannot promise a grade, because no tutor can.

So run the same four checks on both candidates. Ask which Higher Level subjects they have taught through to a May session, and how many cohorts. Ask how they get past papers, markschemes and subject reports, which come through the school or the IB's official channels and show exactly how marks are awarded; a tutor who cannot answer that has been teaching from a textbook. Ask them to mark one of your child's real answers in front of you and explain the command term the question used. And ask what they will not do, because the correct answer includes writing any part of an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay.

For a home tutor there is a second layer that has nothing to do with teaching. Society and apartment gate entry, a fixed arrival time, a room with a door that stays open, and an adult in the house. These are not insults to a professional. They are ordinary and any serious home tutor expects them.

For a distant online tutor, check what you can see rather than what you are told. Turn the camera on. Watch a full session once. Ask the school's DP coordinator whether the approach matches what the department expects, because a tutor teaching against the grain of the school costs a student more than no tutor at all.
items: Ask which HL subjects they have taught through to a May session
Ask where past papers, markschemes and subject reports actually come from
Have them mark one real answer and name the command term
Confirm the line on Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work
For home visits: gate entry, fixed timing, open door, adult present

contentBlocks.heading: What does an IBDP tutor near me in India search actually return?
contentBlocks.body:
It returns proximity, and proximity is the one variable the Diploma Programme cares about least. A search for an IBDP tutor near me in India ranks people by where they are, which would be sensible if DP teaching were evenly spread. It is not. Diploma teaching capacity is a by-product of Diploma schools, so it follows them into a handful of localities per city and stops. Between those localities there are large parts of every metro, and most of the country, where the nearest person who has genuinely taught Higher Level Chemistry is not nearby by any definition.

That is why a near me search feels thin in a way that a Class 10 board tutor search never does. There is nothing wrong with your area. There is simply a small population of people who have run an HL course, and they took jobs near the schools that offer it.

The sensible response is to widen the search in a fixed order rather than all at once, subject by subject, stopping at the first level that produces a real specialist. Doing it for one subject at a time matters, because your Standard Level Economics answer and your Higher Level Mathematics answer will almost certainly be found at different distances.

When the widening stops, you have a decision rather than a search, and it is a decision you can defend to yourself. A family in Ballygunge might end with a local person for Economics and an online specialist in another city for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL. A family in Powai might keep everything local. A family in Bhopal might go online for everything and use the saved travel time for supervised past-paper practice at the kitchen table. All three are correct answers to the same question.
items: 1. Your own locality, for any subject at Standard Level first.
2. Neighbouring localities within a short weekday-evening ride of home.
3. The whole metro, accepting one home visit a week rather than two.
4. Any city in India, online, for the scarce Higher Level subject.
5. Stop at the first step that produces a genuine HL specialist.

contentBlocks.heading: What a widened search costs a DP student, and what it buys
contentBlocks.body:
Be clear about the trade. Choosing an IBDP tutor near me in India on distance alone buys reliability: the session happens, the tutor is not stuck somewhere, the student cannot claim the internet failed. Choosing a distant specialist buys subject depth and costs you the physical presence. Neither is free, and a family that pretends otherwise ends up disappointed in the wrong direction.

What should change, and roughly when. In the first two or three sessions a good tutor should be able to tell you what is actually wrong, and the answer should be specific: the student knows the content but writes descriptions where evaluations are asked for, or the algebra is fine and the proof technique is absent. By six to eight weeks you should see it in marked work rather than in the tutor's opinion. Over a term, the change shows up in mock performance and in how the student talks about the subject. If none of that has happened by the second month, the match is wrong and asking for a different tutor is the correct move, not a failure of nerve.

The honest limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and nobody outside the school forms the predicted grade. A tutor cannot manufacture the 240 hours of an HL course in a February. A tutor cannot fix a subject choice that was wrong at selection, though a good one can make the best of it. And for a DP2 student already at capacity with CAS, coursework deadlines and mocks, adding a third weekly session often makes things worse, because the student stops sleeping and starts arriving unprepared.

Sometimes the right answer is fewer sessions in fewer subjects, taught by somebody further away who is genuinely good.
items: Two or three sessions: a specific diagnosis, not a general impression
Six to eight weeks: the change visible in marked work, not opinion
One term: mock performance and the way the student discusses the subject
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the school forms the predicted grade
For a full DP2 week, fewer sessions taught better usually beats more

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a first DP home session in India, near or far
contentBlocks.body:
Gather four things before you write to anyone, and the whole process gets shorter. Your child's six subjects with the level of each. The school's mock dates and the next internal deadline. Two photographs of recently marked work, ideally one good answer and one that lost marks. And the two evenings in the week that are actually free, checked against activities rather than assumed.

Then send the query or book a free consultation. IB Gram will ask about the board, the syllabus, the levels, the school calendar, your locality and your schedule, and will come back with verified profiles matched against those needs rather than against your pin code alone. Ask deliberately for a mix: at least one person who can reach you for home classes and at least one specialist elsewhere who would teach online. Seeing both is how families searching for an IBDP tutor near me in India stop guessing about whether distance matters for their particular subject.

A trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything. Use it properly. Give the tutor one real past-paper question in the subject you are worried about, sit within earshot for the first ten minutes, and listen for whether the tutor explains the command term or simply supplies the answer. That difference is the whole job.

After the trial, decide subject by subject. Keep the nearby home tutor where presence and supervision are what the student needs, and take the distant specialist online where the Higher Level content is what the student needs. If the fit is wrong later, ask for a different match. Starting in DP1 gives you the widest map; starting in DP2 narrows it, but it does not close it.
items: Six subjects and levels, written down before the first message
Mock dates and the next internal deadline from the school
Photographs of one strong answer and one that lost marks
Two evenings that are genuinely free once activities are counted
Ask for one nearby tutor and one distant specialist to trial

faqs.question: How far will a DP tutor actually travel for a two-hour Higher Level session?
faqs.answer: Far enough to be worth their evening, and no further. In practice a tutor with a full DP2 list will take a trip within their own part of the city and refuse one that crosses it, because an hour each way costs them a whole second session. Between Andheri and Powai, usually yes. Between Hebbal and Electronic City in evening traffic, usually no. A DP1 slot in April is easier to place than a DP2 slot in October, and a two-hour session travels better than a one-hour session because the travel is amortised over more teaching.

faqs.question: There is no IBDP tutor nearby in my city at all. What should I do first?
faqs.answer: Speak to your school's DP coordinator before you hire anybody. Ask what the subject department already offers in the way of clinics, past-paper sessions and consultation time, because that is free, aligned with how the class is being taught, and often the fastest fix. If the gap is real after that conversation, widen the search by one subject rather than by the whole timetable, and expect the answer in scarce Higher Level subjects to be an online specialist in another city.

faqs.question: Should I choose a nearby home tutor or a better Higher Level specialist in another city?
faqs.answer: Decide by what is actually wrong, not by distance. If the student knows the material but will not sit down and practise, a nearby home tutor who arrives at a fixed time is worth more than a better teacher on a screen. If the student works hard and is still losing marks at Higher Level, the specialist wins, and it is not close. The tie-breaker is the trial: give both the same past-paper question and watch which one explains the command term instead of supplying the answer.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor who teaches Class 12 Physics handle DP Higher Level Physics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes for the content, rarely for the assessment. The overlap in material is real, and a strong school teacher can be genuinely useful on the physics itself. What usually goes missing is the marking culture: IB command terms set the depth an answer needs, and a student trained on numerical drill writes a correct calculation where an explanation was asked for and loses the marks. Ask any candidate to mark one of your child's real answers and name the command term the question used before you commit.

faqs.question: Which DP subjects are hardest to find a tutor for locally in India?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at Higher Level, in both of its forms, and then the Higher Level sciences. Analysis and Approaches HL is proof-heavy and algebraic, and the number of people who can teach proof technique properly is small everywhere outside the metro clusters. Applications and Interpretation HL is staffed even more thinly because fewer teachers have run it. Standard Level Economics, English A and Biology are far easier to cover locally, which is exactly why they are the wrong subjects to spend your travel budget on.

faqs.question: We live in Nagpur. Is a local Diploma Programme tutor realistic, or should we go online?
faqs.answer: Assume online for Higher Level subjects and check locally for Standard Level ones. Central and western India, including Nagpur, Indore, Bhopal, Raipur and Nashik, has very few people who have taught a DP cohort through to a May session, and the ones who exist are usually already attached to a school. The same applies in Coimbatore, Jaipur, Guwahati and Bhubaneswar. This is not a disadvantage any more. It simply means the shortlist is national instead of local.

faqs.question: Does a weekday evening home session work for a DP2 student in Delhi NCR traffic?
faqs.answer: It works if the tutor is close and the slot is fixed, and it fails quietly if either is missing. A tutor coming from South Delhi to Sector 128 Noida on a weekday evening will be late often enough to erode the session, and a DP2 student cannot afford twenty minutes of every lesson. Families in Dwarka, Ghaziabad and Faridabad commonly solve this by taking the home session at the weekend and the midweek one online, which keeps the tutor and removes the traffic.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses a home session in the weeks before mocks?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as you can and agree a replacement slot in the same week rather than rolling it forward. Mock preparation is sequenced, so a session skipped in the run-up is not the same as a session skipped in DP1, and pushing it into the next week compresses the revision block at the end. If the tutor travels a long way, an online replacement session is usually easier to arrange than a second home visit, and it is better than losing the week.

faqs.question: Is Mathematics AA or AI easier to find near me?
faqs.answer: AA is easier to find than AI, and both are harder than anything else on the timetable. Analysis and Approaches has been taught by more people, so a local pool in Bandra, Gachibowli or Koregaon Park will usually contain somebody. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout, and fewer teachers have carried a cohort through it. Remember that the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement between the two, so confirm the subject before you start searching for anybody.

faqs.question: How do I judge an online DP tutor I will never meet in person?
faqs.answer: Judge the lesson, not the profile. Sit in on a full trial with the camera on, and check three things: whether the tutor can see your child's handwritten working as it is produced, whether they mark against the command term rather than against a memory of the right answer, and whether they can say where past papers, markschemes and subject reports come from. Then ask what they will not do, and listen for a clear line on Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work.

faqs.question: Is it too late in DP2 to start looking for a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is late, not too late, but the map shrinks. By the October of DP2 most experienced DP tutors have filled their weekday slots, and travel is the first thing they stop offering, so a nearby generalist and a distant specialist online become the two realistic choices. Narrow the request to one or two subjects, be exact about the mock dates, and accept a weekend or an online slot. May results come out in early July, and the retake route exists if the year genuinely runs out.

comparison.heading: Four ways to reach a Diploma Programme tutor in India, compared
comparison.intro: A tutor who travels to you is worth most when supervision is the problem. An online specialist anywhere in India is worth most when the subject is scarce. A neighbourhood centre suits a student who needs structure and company more than personalisation. And a specialist in another city, online, is often the only real option for a Higher Level subject nobody near you has taught.

h1: IB MYP Tutors in India for Criterion-Based Assessment
heroTitle: Criterion-Based MYP Tutoring Across India
heroSubtitle: Your child's MYP report does not carry percentages. It carries four criterion scores, each out of 8, and a subject grade from 1 to 7 that the IB's grade boundaries produce from the total out of 32. Tutors matched here teach to those descriptors, at home, online or hybrid.
introSummary: IB MYP tutors in India work on something most parents were never taught to read: a criterion score. Families who want a home tutor sitting beside the student usually arrive holding a report with four letters on it, A, B, C and D, each carrying a number out of 8, and no percentage anywhere. That report is not vague. It is precise about different things than a marks statement is. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, and every subject in it is assessed against those same four criteria. A tutor who cannot explain what Criterion B asks for is not an MYP tutor, whatever else they know.

contentBlocks.heading: Criterion-based assessment explained: four criteria, 32 marks, one grade
contentBlocks.body:
Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A, B, C and D. Each criterion is scored from 0 to 8. Add the four and the maximum is 32. That total is then converted, through IB grade boundaries, into the subject grade from 1 to 7 that you see on the report. Two steps, not one. A parent who reads the 32 as though it were a percentage is reading a number that was never built to work that way.

This is where most of the confusion starts. A 5 out of 8 looks, to an eye trained on percentage marks, like a bare pass, and parents react accordingly. It is not a bare pass. Each criterion score is awarded against a descriptor, which is a written account of what work at that level actually does. A 5 means the work showed what a 5 describes and did not yet show what a 6 describes. The useful question is therefore never how to collect more marks. It is which specific thing the next descriptor names, and whether the student has ever been taught to do it.

There is a second misreading, quieter and more expensive. Two students can reach the same criterion total, and therefore the same subject grade, from completely different profiles. One is strong on Criterion A and weak on B and C. The other is even across all four. The report shows one number for both, and the teaching each needs has almost nothing in common. A parent looking only at the 1 to 7 will not see this, and neither will a tutor who was told only the grade.

The descriptors themselves, and the boundaries applied to the total, sit with your school. Ask the MYP coordinator for both before you hire anybody.
items: Four criteria, A to D, each scored from 0 to 8, in every MYP subject
A criterion total out of 32, converted by IB grade boundaries to a grade from 1 to 7
The 32 is not a percentage and does not behave like one
Identical subject grades can hide opposite criterion profiles and opposite teaching needs
The descriptor, not the textbook chapter, states what the next score requires

contentBlocks.heading: How do we match IB MYP tutors in India to a stuck criterion?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the criterion, not the subject. When a family writes in, the first thing asked is which criterion keeps coming back low and in which subject, because that one detail changes who should teach the student. A low Criterion A in Sciences and a low Criterion C in the same subject are different problems with different fixes, and a shortlist built without that information is guesswork dressed up as a service.

The rest is ordinary and deliberately dull. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about the board, the subject and the criteria used in it, the MYP year, the school calendar, your locality and the slots that genuinely exist in your week once school transport and activities are counted. From that, IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything, and if the fit turns out to be wrong you can ask for a different match. IB MYP tutors in India are matched against the criterion in front of you rather than a general claim to know the programme.

One instruction is worth giving early. Ask for the trial to be spent marking your child's own work against a descriptor rather than teaching a fresh topic. You learn more from forty minutes of that than from a month of polished lessons, because you get to watch whether the tutor can name the gap or only fill it. Lessons then run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability in your area, and the first plan should say which criterion it is aimed at.
items: 1. Send the report page and name the criterion that keeps coming back low.
2. A short consultation covers subject, MYP year, school calendar, locality and workable slots.
3. You receive a shortlist of tutors whose profiles are verified for that subject.
4. Run a demo and watch the tutor mark one piece against the descriptor.
5. Home classes, online or hybrid lessons begin, subject to tutor availability.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP 1 to 5 in India: where the criteria actually bite
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme runs for five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, covering roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. What changes over those years is the content. What does not change is the assessment shape: four criteria per subject, each out of 8, a total out of 32, and grade boundaries turning that into a grade from 1 to 7. A student who never learned to investigate patterns in MYP 2 meets the same criterion in MYP 5 with far harder mathematics attached to it.

Two pieces of work sit outside the ordinary unit cycle. The Community Project comes in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5. Both eat time in a year that is already full, and both are the student's own work. Ask the coordinator in writing what outside help is permitted before a tutor touches either, and treat that answer as the boundary. A good tutor will ask questions about the project and decline to supply content for it.

MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, which covers on-screen examinations along with ePortfolios, is optional. Each school decides whether to offer it, and there is no single national MYP examination in India. So a family in Bengaluru and a family in Ahmedabad can both be in MYP 5 and be planning for quite different final years. Confirm which applies at your school before you buy a year of IB MYP tuition aimed at an examination that may not be happening.

Load should not be flat across the five years. MYP 1 to 3 is where habits are cheap to build. MYP 4 and 5 is where choices start closing doors, and where IB MYP tutors in India are usually called in late.
items: Five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, eight subject groups
The same four criteria apply in every year while the content grows harder
Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, Personal Project in MYP 5, both time-heavy
MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides whether to offer it
There is no single national MYP examination in India, so plans must be school-specific

contentBlocks.heading: MYP Mathematics criteria A to D, and what a tutor does with each
contentBlocks.body:
MYP Mathematics is the clearest place to see criterion teaching, because the four criteria are named plainly: A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, and D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Each is scored from 0 to 8. A student can be genuinely good at mathematics and still score unevenly across those four, and the pattern of the unevenness is the diagnosis.

Take the most common one. A student solves every equation set in class, so Criterion A looks healthy. Criterion B sits low, term after term. That usually means the student has never been taught to generalise: to take three worked cases, notice what stays constant, write a rule, test it, and say why it holds. Nobody teaches that by doing more sums. A tutor working on B gives the student patterns with no method attached and makes them describe what they see before any algebra appears. Criterion C is different again, and often mistaken for untidiness. Communicating is about whether the reasoning can be followed: notation used correctly, steps in an order, a diagram labelled, a conclusion that answers the question asked. Criterion D asks the student to take a real situation, choose a model, use it, and then say honestly where the model stops being true.

Schools often split MYP 4 and 5 mathematics into standard and extended mathematics. Extended covers additional topics that prepare a student for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA), so this is a decision with consequences beyond the current report card. It should be made on evidence from criterion scores, not on ambition alone.

The other subject groups work the same way with different criterion titles. Sciences, Language and literature and Individuals and societies all carry four criteria out of 8. Get the exact titles from your school's subject guide.
items: Criterion A: Knowing and understanding, scored 0 to 8, the part most drill already covers
Criterion B: Investigating patterns, where generalising a rule is the taught skill
Criterion C: Communicating, judged on notation, order, labelling and a stated conclusion
Criterion D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts, including the limits of the model
Standard against extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5, with extended leading towards DP Mathematics AA

contentBlocks.heading: Where home tutors for MYP criteria work across India
contentBlocks.body:
Supply for criterion-literate MYP teaching follows the international schools, and those cluster. In Delhi NCR a home tutor may hold slots across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri, or on the Gurugram (Gurgaon) side around Golf Course Road, while Dwarka, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad each sit far enough out that one tutor rarely covers two of them on a weekday. An IB MYP tutor in Mumbai typically works a corridor rather than a city: Bandra, Juhu and Andheri as one, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill as another, with Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar effectively separate markets once evening traffic sets in.

Bengaluru splits the same way. A tutor living near Whitefield or Sarjapur Road will take Indiranagar, Koramangala or HSR Layout at a push, and will quietly avoid Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar or Kanakapura Road in the same week. An IB MYP tutor in Hyderabad usually anchors around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur and Kondapur, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Kokapet and Secunderabad added by preference. An IB MYP tutor in Chennai works Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet or Nungambakkam, or the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) belt through Perungudi and Velachery, but seldom both. An IB MYP tutor in Pune covers Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar, or the Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi side.

Beyond the metros the map thins. An IB MYP tutor in Ahmedabad may serve Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway stretch across Gujarat, with Gandhinagar, Vadodara, Surat and Rajkot usually online. In Kolkata the same holds for Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, and across eastern India Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna are mostly online territory.
items: Delhi NCR home tuition works as corridors, not as one city-wide radius
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli and Thane rarely share a tutor
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune each have two or three practical tutoring belts
Gujarat: Ahmedabad, Bodakdev and Gandhinagar at home, Surat and Vadodara usually online
Northern India beyond Delhi NCR, including Chandigarh, Mohali, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun, depends on reach

contentBlocks.heading: The MYP school calendar in India and what it does to a term plan
contentBlocks.body:
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and MYP reporting follows the school's own units rather than a national timetable. A criterion is reported when the unit that assessed it finishes. That is why a parent can spend six weeks waiting for a number to move and see nothing: the criterion in question simply was not assessed again in that window. Ask the subject teacher which criteria the next unit will carry, and plan tuition against that answer.

Families at international schools in India, including names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore, deal with broadly similar pressure points: interim reports, parent-teacher meetings, project deadlines and a long summer break in the middle of it all. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

The pressure points that matter for MYP tutoring are predictable. Project deadlines, the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5, land on top of ordinary unit assessment rather than instead of it. Diwali and the long summer break both break the rhythm of weekly home classes, and both are good moments to work on a criterion without a deadline attached, which is when Criterion B work actually goes best.

One caution about parent-teacher meetings. Go in with the criterion, not the grade. The question that gets a useful answer is not why the grade dropped, it is what the descriptor at the next level asks for in this subject and what the teacher would want to see in the next piece of work.
items: The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, and MYP reporting follows school units
A criterion score only moves when a unit assessing that criterion is marked
Project deadlines stack on top of unit assessment, not in place of it
Long breaks suit criterion work that needs thinking time rather than revision
At a parent-teacher meeting, ask about descriptors and next steps, not about the grade

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for MYP criterion work in India?
contentBlocks.body:
For criterion work the honest answer is that mode matters less than most pages pretend, with one real exception. Criterion C, Communicating, is largely about what the student puts on paper: notation, order, labelling, the visible chain of reasoning. A home tutor sitting beside the student watches that happen live, catches the step skipped in the head, and can point at the exact line where a reader would lose the thread. That is harder on a screen, though a document camera or a photographed page closes most of the gap.

Online wins on reach, and reach is the binding constraint for MYP criteria help outside the big metros. A family in Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Thiruvananthapuram, Mangaluru or Madurai, or in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik, Raipur, Jabalpur, Aurangabad or Goa, may have no locally available tutor who has ever marked against an MYP descriptor. A generalist nearby is not a substitute for that. The same applies in northern India beyond Delhi NCR, where Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Amritsar, Ludhiana, Kanpur and Dehradun all have families in this position.

Hybrid is the arrangement most working families end up with and few plan for. One home session a week, usually at the weekend when a tutor can actually reach Powai or Whitefield without losing an hour to traffic, plus one shorter online session midweek for marking and follow-up. It keeps the paper-and-pen work in the room and keeps the feedback loop tight.

And there is a case against home tuition worth saying plainly. If the only tutor who genuinely understands Criterion B in your child's subject lives in another city, a weaker home tutor nearby is the wrong choice. Take the online specialist.
items: Home tuition is strongest for Criterion C, where handwritten working and layout are the evidence
Online tuition is strongest for reach when no local tutor has marked to MYP descriptors
Hybrid: one weekend home session plus a shorter midweek online review of marked work
A nearby generalist rarely beats a distant tutor who can read a criterion descriptor
Whichever mode you choose, ask for written criterion feedback after each piece of marked work

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check that a tutor can really read a criterion descriptor?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask them to do it, once, in front of you. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose stated subject, level and board match what the family asked for, and that removes the obvious risks. It cannot tell you whether this particular person thinks in criteria, and that is the thing your child's report actually depends on. So the family's own check matters, and it takes one session.

Hand the tutor a piece of your child's marked work and the descriptor the school used. Watch what happens. A criterion-literate tutor reads the descriptor first, then the work, and says something specific: this paragraph states the pattern but never tests it, so it cannot reach the next level on Criterion B. A syllabus tutor reads the work first and starts correcting mistakes. Both look competent for ten minutes. Only one of them will move the score.

Three questions separate them quickly. Ask which four criteria apply in this subject at this school and what each is called. Ask what they would do differently for a student sitting at 4 on Criterion B compared with a student sitting at 4 on Criterion C, because the answer should be two different lessons. Ask how they would know, three weeks in, whether the work was landing, given that the school may not assess that criterion again for a while.

The rest is ordinary diligence and it is yours to do. Confirm identity at the door for home visits, keep sessions in a part of the house where someone passes through, and keep a record of what was covered. Politeness and verification are not in conflict.
items: IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified for the subject, level and board claimed
Your own test: give the tutor one marked script and the descriptor, then watch the order they read them in
Ask for the four criterion titles used in that subject at your school
Ask how a 4 on Criterion B is taught differently from a 4 on Criterion C
For home visits, confirm identity, keep the study space semi-public, and log what was covered

contentBlocks.heading: Why does a criterion score move slowly, and when should you worry?
contentBlocks.body:
Because the score is a report of an event, not a measure of effort. A criterion only produces a new number when the school next assesses that criterion, and that can be a full unit away. Families who start home tuition in week one and check the portal in week four are looking for evidence that has not been generated yet. This is the single most common reason a parent concludes that tutoring is not working when it is.

So watch the leading signals instead. The student can say, unprompted, what the descriptor at the next level asks for. Rough work starts showing a tested rule rather than three answers. A conclusion appears at the end of a Criterion D task naming where the model breaks. Drafts come back shorter and better organised. None of these are numbers, and all of them arrive before the number does.

Now the limits, stated plainly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any offer to do so on a criterion-marked programme should be treated with real scepticism, because the tutor does not mark the work. Some low criterion scores are not subject problems at all: a child whose Criterion C is weak across every subject usually has a writing and organisation problem, and that is one piece of work with a tutor, not a year of subject tuition. Sometimes the right answer is fewer commitments rather than more, particularly in MYP 5 when a Personal Project is running. And sometimes the coordinator or subject teacher should be asked to intervene first, at no cost, before any IB MYP tutors in India are contacted at all.

If nothing has shifted after two assessed units, change something. Usually the tutor's approach. Occasionally the tutor.
items: A criterion score changes only when a unit assessing that criterion is marked
Leading signals: the student can state what the next descriptor asks for
Rough work shows a rule being tested, not three unconnected answers
No tutor can guarantee a grade on a programme where the school does the marking
Weak Criterion C in every subject is a writing problem, not four subject problems

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home classes with an MYP criterion tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
Bring five things to the first conversation and the first month goes faster. The most recent report showing criterion scores by subject. Two pieces of marked work, ideally one strong and one weak, because the contrast is where the diagnosis lives. The descriptor sheet or subject guide, if your school shares it. The school calendar with unit assessment and project dates on it. And an honest weekly timetable including sport, music and travel, so the slot booked is one the family can keep in month three, not just in week one.

The first session should not be a lesson. It should be an assessment of a different kind: the tutor reads the marked work against the descriptor, asks the student to explain their own reasoning aloud, and comes out of it naming one criterion to work on and what the first four weeks will look like. If the tutor finishes that session having taught a topic and said nothing about criteria, you have the wrong tutor, and asking for a different match at that point costs you nothing but a week.

After that, the rhythm is steady and unglamorous. Weekly home classes or online sessions, work set between them, and a short written note to you after each marked piece saying which criterion it targeted and what changed. Ask for that note in writing from the start. It is the only record that survives a change of tutor.

Parents send a query or book a free consultation to begin. IB Gram asks about the subject, the criteria, the MYP year, your locality and your schedule, and comes back with IB MYP tutors in India whose profiles match, subject to availability in your area.
items: Bring the latest report with criterion scores for every subject
Bring two marked pieces, one strong and one weak, for contrast
Bring the descriptor sheet or subject guide if the school shares it
Bring the school calendar with unit assessments and project deadlines marked
Expect the first session to diagnose a criterion rather than teach a topic

faqs.question: What do the four letters on my child's MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: They are the four assessment criteria, A to D, that every MYP subject is marked against, each scored from 0 to 8. The four add to a total out of 32, and IB grade boundaries convert that total into the subject grade from 1 to 7 beside them. The letters are not sections of a paper or topics. They are different kinds of thinking, which is why a student can be strong on one and weak on another.

faqs.question: My daughter scored 5 out of 8 on Criterion B. Is that bad?
faqs.answer: No, and the instinct to read it as a percentage is what makes it feel bad. A criterion score is awarded against a descriptor, a written account of what work at that level does, so a 5 means the work showed what a 5 describes and not yet what a 6 describes. It is a position on a ladder, not a fraction. Read the descriptor one level up and find the single thing her work did not do.

faqs.question: How does a total out of 32 become a grade from 1 to 7?
faqs.answer: Through IB grade boundaries, which are applied to the criterion total rather than to any percentage. The four criterion scores are added, giving a figure out of 32, and that figure falls into a band producing the final subject grade from 1 to 7. Your MYP coordinator can show you the boundaries used for that reporting period. Two consequences follow: small movements in one criterion may not change the grade, and the same grade can come from very different profiles.

faqs.question: Is MYP eAssessment compulsory at the end of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: No. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, which covers on-screen examinations along with ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is also no single national MYP examination in India, so what MYP 5 looks like genuinely varies between schools in the same city. Ask your coordinator directly, in writing, before committing to a year of tutoring built around an examination. If your school does not offer eAssessment, planning should be built around unit assessment and the Personal Project instead.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor reach our flat in Powai on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends far more on where the tutor lives than on distance. Across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, tutors work corridors rather than the whole city, so a tutor based around Powai or Andheri may hold a weekday evening slot there while refusing one in Thane or Navi Mumbai the same week. The same pattern holds in Bengaluru between Whitefield and Jayanagar. If evening traffic makes a weekday home visit fragile, a weekend home session with a midweek online review usually holds better.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in the room during home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: For an MYP-age student, be nearby rather than in the room. Home classes work best in a part of the house where someone passes through, which handles safeguarding without turning the session into a performance. Sitting in tends to make a thirteen-year-old answer to you instead of to the tutor, and criterion work depends on the student being willing to be wrong out loud. Ask instead for a short written note after each marked piece saying which criterion it targeted and what changed.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and cannot find an MYP tutor nearby. What now?
faqs.answer: Go online, and do not settle for a nearby generalist as a compromise. Outside the metros, in Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore, Nagpur, Jaipur or Dehradun, the binding constraint is not distance but whether anybody locally has marked work against an MYP descriptor. A tutor who knows the content but not the criteria will improve answers without moving scores. A document camera or photographed pages covers most of what a home visit would add.

faqs.question: How long before a stuck criterion actually improves?
faqs.answer: Longer than most parents expect, because the number only changes when the school next assesses that criterion, which can be a full unit away. Judge the first month on leading signals: the student can state what the next descriptor asks for, rough work shows a rule being tested, conclusions name the limits of a model. If two assessed units pass with none of that, change the approach, and if the approach does not change, change the tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project or the Community Project?
faqs.answer: Only within the boundary your school sets, and you should get that boundary in writing before any session touches the project. The Personal Project comes in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and both are the student's own work. A tutor can legitimately ask questions, push on the quality of the thinking, and help the student plan their time. Supplying content, drafting sections or editing the write-up is a different thing entirely, and a good tutor will refuse it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between standard and extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5?
faqs.answer: Schools often split MYP 4 and 5 mathematics into standard and extended, with extended covering additional topics that prepare a student for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. The decision shapes what is realistic at Diploma Programme level, not just the current report. Base it on criterion evidence rather than ambition: a student scoring well on Criterion A but poorly on Criterion B is not yet doing the investigative work extended mathematics demands.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring just early Diploma Programme preparation?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way wastes the MYP years. The Diploma Programme grades each subject from 1 to 7 through examinations and internal assessment, while the MYP marks four criteria out of 8 in every subject across five years. What transfers is the habit: a student who can read a descriptor, find the gap and rewrite accordingly arrives in DP1 already able to use a mark scheme. Drilling DP content in MYP 3 does not produce that.

The same pattern holds in Bengaluru between Whitefield and Jayanagar. If evening traffic makes a weekday home visit fragile, a weekend home session with a midweek online review usually holds better.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent sit in the room during home tuition sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an MYP-age student, be nearby rather than in the room. Home classes work best in a part of the house where someone passes through, which handles safeguarding without turning the session into a performance. Sitting in tends to make a thirteen-year-old answer to you instead of to the tutor, and criterion work depends on the student being willing to be wrong out loud. Ask instead for a short written note after each marked piece saying which criterion it targeted and what changed.

mainEntity.name: We live in Kochi and cannot find an MYP tutor nearby. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go online, and do not settle for a nearby generalist as a compromise. Outside the metros, in Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Indore, Nagpur, Jaipur or Dehradun, the binding constraint is not distance but whether anybody locally has marked work against an MYP descriptor. A tutor who knows the content but not the criteria will improve answers without moving scores. A document camera or photographed pages covers most of what a home visit would add.

mainEntity.name: How long before a stuck criterion actually improves?

acceptedAnswer.text: Longer than most parents expect, because the number only changes when the school next assesses that criterion, which can be a full unit away. Judge the first month on leading signals: the student can state what the next descriptor asks for, rough work shows a rule being tested, conclusions name the limits of a model. If two assessed units pass with none of that, change the approach, and if the approach does not change, change the tutor.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project or the Community Project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only within the boundary your school sets, and you should get that boundary in writing before any session touches the project. The Personal Project comes in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and both are the student's own work. A tutor can legitimately ask questions, push on the quality of the thinking, and help the student plan their time. Supplying content, drafting sections or editing the write-up is a different thing entirely, and a good tutor will refuse it.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between standard and extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Schools often split MYP 4 and 5 mathematics into standard and extended, with extended covering additional topics that prepare a student for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. The decision shapes what is realistic at Diploma Programme level, not just the current report. Base it on criterion evidence rather than ambition: a student scoring well on Criterion A but poorly on Criterion B is not yet doing the investigative work extended mathematics demands.

mainEntity.name: Is MYP tutoring just early Diploma Programme preparation?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and treating it that way wastes the MYP years. The Diploma Programme grades each subject from 1 to 7 through examinations and internal assessment, while the MYP marks four criteria out of 8 in every subject across five years. What transfers is the habit: a student who can read a descriptor, find the gap and rewrite accordingly arrives in DP1 already able to use a mark scheme. Drilling DP content in MYP 3 does not produce that.

heroSubtitle: The last two Middle Years Programme years are where a student quietly decides how hard the Diploma Programme is going to feel. Home tuition in MYP 4 and MYP 5 works on the extended mathematics decision, the Personal Project, and the writing and planning habits that DP1 simply assumes a student already has.
introSummary: IB MYP home tutors in India teach the Middle Years Programme at your own dining table, and in MYP 4 and MYP 5 that home tuition has one job: make DP1 survivable. These are the years when schools split mathematics into standard and extended, when the Personal Project lands in MYP 5, and when a student's criterion scores start predicting something. The MYP runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. There is no single national MYP examination in India, so nobody outside the school is going to tell you where your child stands. A home tutor working weekly is often the first person who does.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a MYP 4 or MYP 5 request in India become a home tutor shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the school's own evidence. Not your impression of how the term went, but the criterion breakdown: which of A, B, C and D your child scores well on, and which one keeps coming back low. A student sitting at 7 out of 8 on Knowing and understanding and 3 on Investigating patterns has a very specific problem, and it is not that they are bad at mathematics. Send that, plus the school's MYP 5 deadline calendar if you have one, and the two or three units that went badly.

What happens next is deliberately boring. IB Gram asks about the board, the subject, the year group, whether the school streams mathematics into standard and extended, the school calendar, your locality and the evenings that are genuinely free after school and activities. It then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches that description rather than the general idea of an IB tutor. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything, and if the fit is wrong after two or three sessions you can ask for a different match without an argument.

The MYP 4 and MYP 5 detail matters more than families expect. A tutor who has taught only Diploma Programme classes will often teach a fifteen-year-old as though the criteria did not exist, and a tutor whose experience stops at MYP 3 may not see the extended mathematics decision coming at all. Say which of the two you need, in the first message.

Be honest in the brief about time as well. If the Personal Project is due this term and your child's week is already full, a tutor who arrives planning to add two hours of homework will make the term worse rather than better.
items: 1. Send the criterion breakdown from the last report, not a summary of it
2. Name the year precisely: MYP 4 or MYP 5, and the subject
3. Say whether the school streams standard and extended mathematics, and which stream your child is in
4. Give two workable weekday evenings and your locality, so travel is realistic
5. Book a trial session, then review the fit after three home sessions

contentBlocks.heading: MYP 4 and MYP 5: the two years that set how hard the Diploma Programme feels
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8. Those four add up to a total out of 32, and the school converts that total into a final grade from 1 to 7 using IB grade boundaries. No percentages anywhere. A parent reading an MYP report looking for marks out of 100 will misread the entire document.

Two of the five years carry projects. The Community Project comes in MYP 3 or MYP 4, and the Personal Project comes in MYP 5. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, which is on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides for itself whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination here, which is exactly why MYP 4 and MYP 5 feel low-stakes to a fifteen-year-old, and why DP1 lands so hard on students who spent them coasting.

What sits on the other side is a two-year Diploma Programme, DP1 and DP2: six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four taken at Higher Level (HL) with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Every subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 more points, so the maximum is 45 and 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed alongside all of it.

Families who book IB MYP home tutors in India for these two years are usually buying a runway rather than a rescue. Diploma examinations run in May and November, and schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which fits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July. Work backwards from that and MYP 5 stops looking distant.

Four criteria per subject, A to D, each scored out of 8
A criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1-7 grade at IB boundaries
Community Project in MYP 3 or MYP 4; Personal Project in MYP 5
MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and each school decides

contentBlocks.heading: Standard or extended mathematics in MYP 4 and MYP 5, and what each one closes off
contentBlocks.body:
MYP Mathematics is assessed on four criteria: A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, and D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each scored out of 8. Schools commonly split MYP 4 and MYP 5 mathematics into standard and extended. Extended covers additional topics, and those additional topics are what prepare a student for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches.

So a decision a school often asks a fourteen-year-old to make in one short conversation has a consequence two years out. DP Mathematics comes as two subjects, each available at HL and SL. Analysis and Approaches (AA) is algebraic and proof-heavy. Applications and Interpretation (AI) is built on modelling and statistics, with technology used throughout. Students heading towards engineering or economics degrees are often advised towards AA, although the right choice depends on the degree and on the student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement.

A home tutor's job in MYP 4 is to gather evidence for that decision rather than campaign for one side of it. Can the student hold an algebraic argument over four or five lines without losing a sign? Do they enjoy the pattern-finding work in criterion B, or do they only ever want the formula? Standard mathematics taken by a student who would have coped with extended can close off an AA route that a degree later asks for. Extended pushed on a student already struggling with criterion C produces two miserable years and a worse MYP grade.

The same logic runs through the other subjects. IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology reward students who can explain a mechanism, not only calculate a number, and that habit is slow to build. IB Economics rewards precise definitions. IB English A rewards students who read beyond the set texts. A home tutor who works only on this fortnight's unit test is not preparing anyone for DP1, whatever the unit test scores look like.

Extended mathematics covers additional topics that lead towards DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches

contentBlocks.heading: IB MYP home tutors in India: what MYP 4 and MYP 5 look like region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Coverage matters here because the mathematics stream decision and the Personal Project happen in the same months everywhere, so evening slots get scarce at the same time. In Delhi NCR that means South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka on one side, and Gurugram (Gurgaon), Golf Course Road, Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad on the other. An IB MYP home tutor in Delhi who lives in Noida and teaches in Gurugram will not hold a six o'clock Tuesday slot through a whole term. Evening traffic across that crossing can stretch a short trip badly.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the pattern is vertical rather than horizontal. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit close together on a map and far apart in practice, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are a separate commute entirely. An IB MYP home tutor in Mumbai usually works one corridor. Ask which one before you ask anything else.

Bengaluru splits the same way: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City in one direction, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road in another, Hebbal and Yelahanka to the north. An IB MYP home tutor in Bangalore living in Jayanagar will offer you a Saturday morning for Whitefield, not a Wednesday evening. In Hyderabad the international school families cluster around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Kokapet and Secunderabad, and an IB MYP home tutor in Hyderabad covering Gachibowli and Kondapur can often hold two evenings a week. Pune runs along Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad, and an IB MYP home tutor in Pune based in Kharadi reaches Viman Nagar easily and Hinjewadi rarely.

Outside those clusters the supply of IB MYP home tutors in India thins quickly. An IB MYP home tutor in Chennai, in Kolkata or in Ahmedabad exists, but the pool for one subject at MYP 5 is small, and a search for an MYP home tutor near me may return nobody who has taught criterion B in extended mathematics. That is the point at which MYP home tuition across India stops being a local question.

contentBlocks.heading: The MYP 5 school year in India: Personal Project deadlines and DP subject selection
contentBlocks.body:
The school calendar does most of the deciding. An Indian academic year running roughly April to March puts the MYP 5 Personal Project deadlines, the DP subject selection forms and the final MYP reports inside the same handful of months, and those are also the months when families travel for the winter break. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore each run their own calendar, and no two of them are identical. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

What international schools in India generally expect of an MYP 5 student is more than the student expects of themselves. Criterion-assessed tasks across eight subject groups, unit deadlines that do not move, a Personal Project supervisor to meet, and a subject selection decision the DP coordinator will ask the family to confirm. A student who has floated through MYP 3 on ability alone meets all of that in one year.

Ask the school three things early, and ask them in writing. Which term the Personal Project report is due. Whether the school offers MYP eAssessment and, if so, in which subjects. And when the DP subject selection conversation happens, because the standard against extended mathematics decision is usually settled before that meeting rather than during it.

Home tuition should be planned around those dates rather than around a fixed weekly habit that ignores them. A home tutor who does not ask for the school calendar in the first session will collide with it by the third. If the school reports at the end of each term, that report is the natural review point for the home tutor arrangement too.
