Ask whether the school offers MYP eAssessment, and in which subjects
Ask when DP subject selection is confirmed with the coordinator
The school reporting cycle is the natural review point for home tuition
Winter travel and Personal Project deadlines often land in the same weeks

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid for MYP 4 and MYP 5 in India?
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor sits beside a fifteen-year-old and sees what a screen hides: a diagram drawn too small, working abandoned halfway down the page, a phone face-down but alive. At MYP 4 and MYP 5, when a student is old enough to be left alone and not yet disciplined enough to deserve it, that presence is worth more than it will be in DP2. Home sessions also show the tutor the actual study space, which is quite often the real problem.

Online tutoring wins on supply. If your child needs extended mathematics taught by someone who has walked students into AA HL, and nobody within a sensible drive has done that, an online specialist in another city is the better teacher, and the better teacher beats the closer one at this stage. Online works less well for a student who needs supervision more than instruction, and at fourteen a good many of them do.

Hybrid is what most families using IB MYP home tutors in India settle into by the second term: one home visit a week for the long written session and the Personal Project check-in, plus one shorter online session midweek for a specific criterion or a piece of returned feedback. It protects the slot when traffic, monsoon or a school event kills the visit, and it keeps the rhythm when the tutor travels.

The honest limit is this. A hybrid week only works if the two sessions have separate jobs. Two near-identical sessions in two different formats confuse a fourteen-year-old and waste an hour a week. Decide which session owns the written work and which owns the questioning, write it down, and tell the student which is which so they arrive prepared for the right one.
items: Home sessions catch abandoned working, cramped diagrams and a phone kept nearby
Online reaches an extended mathematics specialist your own locality may not have
Hybrid: one home visit for long written work, one short online criterion session
Give each session in a hybrid week a different job, in writing
Monsoon and school events break single-format weeks more often than families expect

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor who says they teach MYP 4 and MYP 5 criteria?
contentBlocks.body:
A verified profile is a floor, not a verdict. IB Gram checks a profile before it goes live: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the programmes and subjects the tutor says they teach. What no platform can see is whether this particular person will hold the attention of your particular fifteen-year-old at seven on a Wednesday evening. You find that out in the trial, and only in the trial.

Three questions separate an MYP 5 tutor from a general tutor. First, ask them to name the four MYP mathematics criteria and then say which one your child's report shows as weak. Second, ask what extended mathematics covers that standard does not, and why that matters for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. Third, ask what they will refuse to do on the Personal Project. A tutor who answers the third question quickly and firmly is the one to book.

Then do your own checks, because they are yours to do and nobody else will. Meet the tutor at the first home visit rather than handling it by message. Keep home lessons in a shared part of the house with the door open. Ask for a plan for the term in writing after session three rather than before, so it is built on what the tutor has seen rather than on your description of the problem. And ask the school's MYP coordinator whether they notice any change by the next reporting cycle.

Be wary of anyone who promises a grade jump, quotes a success rate, or offers to look over the Personal Project report before submission. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and no honest tutor goes near that document.
items: Profiles are checked for identity, qualifications claimed and programmes actually taught
Ask the tutor to name the four MYP mathematics criteria without prompting
Ask what they will refuse to do on the Personal Project
Keep home lessons in a shared room with the door open
Ask for a term plan after session three, built on evidence

contentBlocks.heading: What should MYP 4 and MYP 5 home tuition in India actually build?
contentBlocks.body:
Four things, and none of them is next week's unit test: writing that argues rather than asserts, mathematical working a stranger can follow, the habit of reading a criterion descriptor before starting a task, and the ability to carry one piece of work across three weeks without being chased. Those four are what DP1 assumes a student already has on day one.

Take the writing first. The Diploma Programme asks for extended prose in almost every group, and the students who struggle are rarely the ones who do not know the content. They are the ones who write three sentences where the criterion asked for an argument. An MYP 5 home tutor should be marking the student's own paragraph against the descriptor in front of them, out loud, most weeks. Not correcting it quietly and handing it back clean. Marking it, saying why, then making them rewrite one paragraph.

Second, working. Criterion C is Communicating, and it is the criterion students trained on speed and final answers lose most often. The fix is unglamorous: the tutor declines to accept an answer without the lines that produced it, for a whole term, until the student stops resenting it and starts doing it unprompted.

Third, planning, which the Personal Project in MYP 5 tests for real. It is the student's own work from start to finish, and a tutor's role is to ask questions about the plan, teach research and referencing as general skills, and then get out of the way. What a good home tutor does here is protect the calendar: a short fortnightly check that the process journal is being kept, that the goal has not quietly tripled in size, and that nobody is planning to write the report in the last four days. Most Personal Projects are not lost to ability. They are lost to a month that turned out to have no spare evenings in it. And fourth, independence: if a student still needs IB MYP home tutors in India to tell them what to revise once DP1 starts, the MYP 5 tuition did not work.
items: Writing that argues against a descriptor, not three asserted sentences
Working a stranger can follow, which is criterion C Communicating
Reading the criterion descriptor before starting, on every single task
Carrying one piece of work across three weeks without being chased
A fortnightly check that the process journal is genuinely being kept

contentBlocks.heading: Progress across MYP 4 and MYP 5, and when MYP tutoring should stop
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the MYP is slower to see than progress on an exam course, because the thing being measured is a criterion score out of 8 and it moves in whole points. A student stuck on 3 for Investigating patterns does not reach 6 in a month. A realistic first target is one criterion moving one point by the next reporting cycle, with the home tutor able to show you the specific piece of work where it happened and explain what changed in it.

So give a home tuition arrangement a term rather than a fortnight. What you should see inside the first month is different in kind: the student explaining in their own words what a criterion is asking for, homework being started earlier in the week, fewer arguments about it at home. Those are the leading signs. The grade is the lagging one.

Now the part most pages leave out. MYP tutoring should stop when the student can do those four things without help, when the reason you started has actually been fixed, or when the tutoring has quietly become a reason not to ask the class teacher. Three unbroken years of tuition from MYP 3 into DP1 produces a student who is excellent at being taught and not yet able to work alone, which is a worse position to enter the Diploma Programme in than a gap or two. A tutor who never raises stopping is not doing the whole job.

And there is the case where the answer is no tutor at all. One bad unit, a term disrupted by illness, a teacher change mid-year: these look like subject problems and usually are not. Talk to the MYP coordinator first. If the school's own answer fixes it, you have saved a year of evenings and your child has kept them.
items: One criterion moving one point by the next reporting cycle is realistic
Leading signs: earlier starts, fewer arguments, the student explaining the criterion
Stop when the student can plan and revise without being told to
Unbroken tuition from MYP 3 into DP1 builds dependence, not independence
Talk to the MYP coordinator before hiring anyone at all

contentBlocks.heading: Starting MYP 4 or MYP 5 home tuition in India before the Personal Project lands
contentBlocks.body:
Gather three documents before you send anything. The most recent report with the criterion breakdown for each subject. The school's term calendar with the Personal Project deadlines marked on it. And one piece of your child's own recent work that you thought was weak. That third document tells a tutor more than the other two put together, because it shows the error rather than describing it.

Then decide the constraint honestly. Which two evenings are genuinely free after school, sport and travel? Availability is subject to tutor availability and depends on the level and the schedule you need, and a slot that only exists on paper collapses by week three. If Tuesday and Friday are the truth, say Tuesday and Friday, and say what time the student actually gets home.

The first session with IB MYP home tutors in India should not be a lesson. It should be a diagnosis: the tutor reading that weak piece of work with the student, asking why each step was taken, and finishing with two or three sentences about what they believe is actually wrong. If you are handed a syllabus plan instead, that tutor has not looked at your child yet.

After that the shape is simple enough to hold for a year. One weekly home session with a written focus agreed in advance. Work set between sessions that takes less time than the session itself. And a review conversation at the end of each term in which somebody is allowed to say that this has done its job and can now stop.
items: Bring the latest report with the criterion breakdown for every subject
Bring the term calendar with Personal Project deadlines marked on it
Bring one recent piece of work you thought was weak
Name two evenings that are genuinely free, not theoretically free
Expect a diagnosis in session one, not a syllabus plan

faqs.question: Does a student really need a tutor in MYP 4, or can this wait until DP1?
faqs.answer: Waiting until DP1 means starting the hardest two years with the gaps still in place. MYP 4 is the cheapest year to fix working, writing and planning, because nothing is riding on it yet and a student is still allowed to be slow at something. But a tutor is not automatically the answer. If the report shows one weak criterion in one subject and the class teacher has a plan for it, follow the school's plan for a term and book a home tutor only if nothing moves.

faqs.question: Should we choose standard or extended mathematics in MYP 4?
faqs.answer: Decide on evidence rather than ambition. Extended covers additional topics that prepare a student for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, so choosing standard can close off an AA route that an engineering or economics degree may later expect. Look at the criterion scores. A student holding criterion B Investigating patterns and criterion C Communicating at a solid level usually copes with extended. A student scoring well only on Knowing and understanding often does not. The school's DP coordinator makes the final placement, so raise it with them early.

faqs.question: How much time does the Personal Project in MYP 5 actually take?
faqs.answer: More than the timetable suggests, and the time goes into places students do not expect. The Personal Project comes in MYP 5, and what eats the term is not the product but the process journal, the supervisor meetings and the written report. Students underestimate the report every single year. Spread across the months the school allows, it is manageable in short regular sittings. Compressed into a final fortnight, it collides with unit deadlines and DP subject selection at once.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, but inside a narrow boundary. A home tutor may ask questions about the goal, teach research and referencing as general skills, discuss how a process journal is kept, and help the student build a realistic schedule. What a tutor must not do is choose the topic, draft any part of the report, edit the student's text or supply content for it. The Personal Project is the student's own work and the school supervisor oversees it. A tutor offering to review the report before submission should be declined.

faqs.question: Will an IB MYP home tutor travel to Whitefield in Bengaluru or Gachibowli in Hyderabad on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, provided the tutor already lives on that side of the city. Home visits in Bengaluru and Hyderabad are decided by corridor rather than by distance on a map. A tutor in Koramangala may cover HSR Layout and Sarjapur Road comfortably and treat Whitefield as a weekend trip, while in Hyderabad a tutor around Kondapur will hold Gachibowli and Madhapur slots easily. Evening traffic on the longer crossings can stretch a short trip badly, so offer two possible evenings rather than one.

faqs.question: One criterion score dropped this term. Is that a real problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not on its own. Criterion scores move in whole points out of 8, and a single drop after a hard unit, a missed week or an unfamiliar task type is ordinary. What matters is the pattern across subjects and across terms. The same criterion sitting low in mathematics, in the sciences and in English A, term after term, is a skill problem rather than a content problem, and that is worth a tutor. One low score in one unit is worth a conversation with the subject teacher instead.

faqs.question: How many home sessions a week does an MYP 5 student need?
faqs.answer: For most students one a week per subject is enough, and two subjects at once is the practical ceiling in MYP 5. The Personal Project and the school's own deadlines already fill the week, and home sessions that set more work than a student can finish make the term worse rather than better. A workable shape is one longer home session for the main subject plus a short online session midweek for feedback. Review the load at the end of each term instead of drifting into more.

faqs.question: Does MYP eAssessment change what we should prepare for?
faqs.answer: Only if your school offers it. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, it is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it, so the first step is asking your coordinator rather than assuming either way. Where a school does offer it, preparation looks more like timed examination practice. Where it does not, and with no single national MYP examination in India, everything rests on internally assessed criterion work spread across the whole year.

faqs.question: When should MYP tutoring stop?
faqs.answer: When the reason you started has been fixed, or when the student can plan and revise without being told to. A tutor should be the one raising this, not you. The warning sign is a student who is comfortable, scoring reasonably, and quietly unable to begin a piece of work until the tutor arrives on Tuesday. Stopping at the end of MYP 5, with a light check-in during the long break before DP1 begins, is a common and sensible point. Dependence carried into DP1 is harder to unwind than a gap.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring enough for MYP 4, or should lessons be at home?
faqs.answer: At MYP 4 a home tutor usually has the edge, because a fourteen-year-old's attention and written working are both easier to manage in the room than through a screen. Online becomes the better choice in one common case: when the subject specialist you need, particularly for extended mathematics, is not available anywhere near you. A hybrid week takes most of both, with one home visit for long written work and one short online session for feedback. Judge the format after three sessions, not after one.

faqs.question: We are moving from Pune to Delhi NCR mid-year. What happens to the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Plan the handover around the school calendar rather than around the moving date. If the tutor in Pune has been working across Koregaon Park or Baner for a term, the cheapest option is often to keep that person online until the term ends and find a home tutor in Delhi NCR from the next one, so the Personal Project work and the term's criterion evidence are not disrupted twice over. Ask the departing tutor for a written handover of what was fixed and what was not.

h1: IB MYP Home Tuition and the Limits Around the Personal Project
heroTitle: MYP Home Tuition in India, With Project Lines Drawn
heroSubtitle: Your child is in the Middle Years Programme, a project is due, and nobody has told you where a tutor must stop. This page sets out the weekly plan a home tutor builds from criterion feedback, and the exact limits on the Personal Project and the Community Project.
introSummary: IB MYP home tuition in India is a weekly arrangement in which a verified tutor teaches an International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) student at home, planning each session from the criterion feedback the school has already written. The MYP runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. Those criterion scores are where a home tutor should start. The harder part is the boundary: the Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 must remain the student's own work, and a tutor who forgets that puts the student at risk. This page states that line precisely.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a project deadline in India turn into a matched MYP home tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks what the school has actually said about the work, and a shortlist of verified tutor profiles comes back for you to trial. The first question is almost never which subject. It is which criterion the school keeps marking down, and whether a project deadline is sitting in the middle of it.

So the intake conversation is specific. Which board and programme, which MYP year, which subject group, which criterion letters appear in the last report, and what the school calendar looks like for the coming term. Where you live matters too, because a home tutor who has to cross a metro at seven in the evening will cancel more often than one who lives two streets away. If the Personal Project or the Community Project is already under way, say so at the start. That changes the kind of tutor who fits, not just the timetable.

A tutor who is right for project season is not always the strongest subject specialist available. They need to be comfortable teaching a research skill and then putting their pen down. They need to know what a supervising teacher at school is for, and to work with that teacher's instructions rather than around them. Ask about it in the trial. A tutor who offers to polish a project report has told you everything you need in one sentence.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, subject to tutor availability. Use it properly. Bring the last marked task with the criterion grid still attached, and watch whether the tutor reads the descriptors or skips straight to content. If the fit is wrong after a few weeks, you can ask for a different match. Changing early costs a fortnight. Changing during project submission in MYP 5 costs a good deal more.
items: 1. Send the last report with the criterion scores, not just subject grades.
2. Name the MYP year, the subject group and any project deadline already fixed.
3. Give your locality, school timings and the evenings that are genuinely free.
4. Review shortlisted profiles, then run a trial session on a real marked task.
5. Agree in writing what the tutor will not touch on project work.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP 1 to MYP 5, and where the two projects land in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, for students roughly aged eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. The Community Project falls in MYP 3 or MYP 4, depending on how your school has structured it. The Personal Project falls in MYP 5. Those two points in the programme are what this page is built around, because they are where outside help most often goes wrong.

Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D. Each is scored 0 to 8, so the criterion total for a subject comes out of 32, and that total converts to a final grade from 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. A parent who grew up with percentage marks reads a 5 out of 8 as a near failure, which it is not. The conversion is not arithmetic you can do at the dinner table, and a tutor who pretends otherwise is guessing at something the IB decides.

MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, meaning on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional. Each school decides whether to offer it, and there is no single national MYP examination in India. Two families living in the same locality in Powai can therefore be working towards genuinely different MYP 5 years. Ask your school's MYP coordinator which route your child is on before you plan a single session, because it changes what the final year contains and how much room the project has.

What a home tutor does inside all this is narrower than most parents expect. They cannot change a criterion score. They can teach the skill the descriptor asks for, watch the student attempt it, and hand the marking back to the school. In MYP 3 and MYP 4 that work is mostly habit building and repair. In MYP 5 it runs alongside a project the tutor must not touch, which is the harder arrangement of the two to hold steadily.
items: MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, eight subject groups
Four criteria per subject, A to D, each scored 0 to 8
Criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade
Community Project in MYP 3 or MYP 4, depending on the school
Personal Project in MYP 5, supervised by a teacher at school
MYP eAssessment is optional; each school decides whether to offer it

contentBlocks.heading: Building a week from criterion feedback, criterion by criterion
contentBlocks.body:
Criterion feedback is the most underused document in an Indian family's house. It arrives with the report, gets read as a number, and goes into a drawer. A home tutor should start there instead. If the same criterion letter is low in sciences and in individuals and societies, the problem is not two subjects at once. It is one skill showing up twice, and chapter revision will not move it.

So the plan is written per criterion, not per chapter. Take a student whose subject grades look acceptable but whose scores on one criterion keep landing low across three subjects. What moves that is repeated practice at the specific thing the descriptor names, using the student's own last task as the worked example, with the tutor asking questions rather than supplying sentences. The student rewrites; the tutor reads the descriptor aloud and asks whether the rewrite meets it.

Here is a weekly routine an MYP student can actually hold alongside school, activities and a project.

1. One ninety-minute home session on the subject where the criterion evidence is weakest.

2. Two short stretches of the student's own, about thirty minutes each, redoing one past task against its descriptor.

3. One fixed hour for project work, during the Community Project or in MYP 5, with no tutor present and no tutor messages.

4. One short review at the weekend where the student explains to you what changed and why.

That is the whole week. Anything heavier and the project is what gets squeezed, which defeats the purpose of hiring anyone.

Across the eight subject groups the emphasis differs. In language and literature the criterion work is largely about organising an argument. In mathematics it is about showing a pattern and justifying it rather than reaching an answer quickly. In design it is the process record that carries marks. A tutor who teaches all three the same way is teaching content, not criteria.
items: Read the criterion letters across subjects before choosing which subject to tutor
Use the student's own marked task as material, never a fresh worksheet
Practise the skill the descriptor names, then hand marking back to school
Keep an error log of criterion comments that repeat term after term
Protect one untouched hour a week for the student's own project work

contentBlocks.heading: IB MYP home tuition in India: what each region changes about project weeks
contentBlocks.body:
IB MYP home tuition in India runs on weekday evenings, and the evening is a different problem in every city. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region a tutor travelling from Bandra or Lower Parel towards Powai after six is at the mercy of one road. Families in Andheri, Juhu, Worli and Malabar Hill usually find someone within a few kilometres. In Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar the pool is thinner, and a search for IB MYP home tuition in Mumbai often ends with a tutor who serves one corridor only.

Bengaluru has the same shape with different roads. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and HSR Layout hold their own supply, and Indiranagar, Koramangala and Jayanagar are easier again. Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road sit far enough out that a tutor's travel decides the slot more than the subject does. Parents typing IB MYP home tuition in Bangalore are really asking whether anyone will cross that city twice a week in term time. Chennai splits between Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam on one side and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery and Anna Nagar on the other, which is why IB MYP home tuition in Chennai gets answered corridor by corridor.

In Gujarat the international school families cluster in Ahmedabad, around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close enough to share tutors on some evenings. Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot have fewer MYP-experienced teachers, so IB MYP home tuition in Ahmedabad is easier to arrange than the same request from Rajkot. Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai frequently find no local MYP specialist at all, and a hybrid week is the honest answer rather than a compromise.

The same pattern repeats elsewhere. Delhi NCR and Hyderabad have deep pools in some pockets and almost none in others, and Pune families usually manage a weekday visit within their own quadrant. Searches for IB MYP home tuition in Delhi, IB MYP home tuition in Hyderabad, IB MYP home tuition in Pune and IB MYP home tuition in Kolkata all run into one question. Evening traffic between a suburb and the nearest international school can stretch a short trip badly, and a tutor late twice over stops being a weekly fixture.
items: Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Powai and Thane are three separate travel problems
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road hold supply; Electronic City often does not
Chennai: the Adyar side and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) are answered separately
Gujarat: Ahmedabad, Satellite and Bodakdev are served; Rajkot and Surat far less
Southern India: Kochi, Coimbatore and Visakhapatnam usually need a hybrid week

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar in India that both MYP projects are pinned to
contentBlocks.body:
International schools in India mostly run a year that opens around April or June and closes around March or May, with a long summer break and a shorter Diwali break, and MYP project milestones are set against that shape. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, so confirm your own dates with your school's MYP coordinator rather than with a tutor.

The Personal Project does not arrive as one deadline. It arrives as a chain of them: a proposal, a goal, meetings logged with the supervisor, a process journal checked at intervals, then the product and the report. Schools spread these across MYP 5, and the crunch usually lands mid-term when ordinary subject assessments are also due. A family that marks only the final submission date in the calendar gets surprised twice, once at the proposal and once when the journal is first inspected.

What the supervising teacher at school is responsible for is specific, and parents are rarely told it plainly. That teacher meets the student at set points, records those meetings, checks the process journal, gives feedback on one draft, confirms the work is the student's own and submits it. They are the person who signs off authenticity. A home tutor is not part of that chain and cannot be added to it. If a tutor's advice contradicts the supervisor's instruction, the supervisor wins, every time, without discussion.

So the home tuition plan bends around school dates instead of competing with them. Before a milestone, sessions get shorter and subject work gets lighter. After a report arrives, the plan is rewritten from the new criterion comments rather than continued out of habit. In the fortnight before a long break a tutor should be setting work the student can do alone, because a family travelling for three weeks will not hold a weekly slot. None of this is possible unless you have asked the school for its milestone dates in writing.
items: Ask the MYP coordinator for project milestone dates in writing, early
Mark proposal, journal checks and submission separately, not just the final date
Expect project crunch to collide with ordinary subject assessment in the same term
Plan lighter home sessions in the fortnight before any milestone
Rewrite the plan each time a report with criterion comments arrives

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when the work must stay the student's own?
contentBlocks.body:
Home suits the ordinary subject work and the habit building, online suits the specialist your city does not have, and hybrid suits most MYP 5 families, because project weeks need fewer visits and shorter check-ins. The integrity rules are identical in all three. What changes between them is how easy those rules are to hold on a tired Tuesday.

In a home session the tutor can see the process journal lying open on the table, which is useful and risky in equal measure. Useful, because the tutor can point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. Risky, because a tutor sitting beside a tired fourteen-year-old at nine at night is one sentence away from dictating. A parent in the next room is a reasonable safeguard and not a sign of distrust, and any tutor worth keeping will say the same.

Online lessons make that line easier to police, which surprises people. The student keeps the document on their own device, the tutor sees a shared screen and cannot reach the keyboard. For families in Coimbatore or Vijayawada, online is often the only route to an MYP-experienced teacher at all, and it carries discussion, questioning and criterion reading perfectly well. It carries less well for a younger MYP student who drifts after forty minutes with nobody in the room.

A hybrid week is where most MYP families settle: one home session for the subject that needs a person present, one online session for the subject whose specialist lives in another city, and project hours with neither. Ask a prospective tutor how they would run a week like that. If the answer is that they would simply add hours as the deadline approaches, keep looking at other profiles.
items: Home sessions: best for habit building and a student who drifts alone
Online sessions: the route to a specialist your own city lacks
Hybrid weeks: one home visit, one online session, project hours with neither
Keep the document on the student's device in every mode, including at home
Extra hours near a deadline is a warning sign, not a plan

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a tutor goes near a project in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Check identity, MYP teaching experience, and the answer to one integrity question, in that order. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against identity and qualification documents and against the programmes and subjects they claim to teach. That is the platform's part of the work. The integrity question is yours to ask, and no verification process can ask it on your behalf.

The question itself is short. My child is in MYP 5, the Personal Project report is due in three weeks, what would you do in our sessions? A tutor who offers to help structure the report, tighten the writing or check the reflections has failed the question. A tutor who says they would teach the referencing or research skill in the abstract, ask what the supervisor has already advised, and otherwise stay out of the report has passed it.

Then check the ordinary things, which parents skip because they feel rude. Has this tutor taught the MYP specifically, or only a board where content coverage is the entire job? Can they explain what a criterion total out of 32 does and does not tell you about a student? Will they put in writing that they will not write, rewrite or edit any submitted work? Are they comfortable with a parent being in the house during sessions? Four answers tell you more than a page of listed qualifications.

And check what only you can see. A verified profile confirms documents and claims; it cannot confirm how a person behaves at ten at night when a deadline is close and a student is upset. Sit in on a session occasionally. Read the process journal yourself, without commenting on the content. Keep the arrangement written down, project boundary included, and the awkward conversation never has to be had at all.
items: Confirm identity documents and the exact programmes the profile claims to teach
Ask the MYP 5 integrity question and listen to the whole answer
Get the project boundary written into the arrangement before the first session
Check the tutor has taught criterion-marked work, not only content syllabuses
Agree that a parent may be present in the house during sessions

contentBlocks.heading: The Personal Project boundary, stated exactly
contentBlocks.body:
Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft. It does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit the student's submission. That is the whole rule, and it governs the Personal Project and the Community Project exactly as it governs a science task or a language essay.

Here is what a tutor may do. They may teach the underlying skill: how to narrow a research question until it is answerable, how to keep a process journal that records decisions as they happen, how to reference a source properly, how to read a criterion descriptor and see what it is actually asking for. They may question the reasoning: why this goal, what evidence supports that claim, what would a reader fail to follow here. They may point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. They may discuss the project as they would discuss any idea.

Here is what must remain entirely the student's own. The choice of goal. The research and the reading behind it. Every sentence of the report. The product itself. The reflections, which exist to record what the student thought, not what a tutor thought on their behalf. A tutor who suggests a better goal has taken the decision away; a tutor who rewrites a paragraph as an example has written that paragraph. The line is not about intention or generosity. It is about whose words are submitted under the student's name.

The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone. That is worth understanding well before a panicked week in MYP 5. IB MYP home tuition in India is bought to make a student more capable on their own, and a report the student did not write teaches nothing while putting the rest of their year at risk. When in doubt, the instruction to a tutor is four words long: discuss it, touch nothing.
items: May do: teach research questions, referencing, journal keeping and criterion reading
May do: question reasoning and ask the student to reread their own work
Must not: write, rewrite or edit any part of the submission
Must not: choose the goal, the product or the reflections for the student
The school submits the work and runs similarity checking before it goes

contentBlocks.heading: How can a parent tell legitimate support from too much?
contentBlocks.body:
Read one page of the report aloud and ask your child to explain it without the document in front of them. If they can, the work is theirs. If the vocabulary is not theirs, if the structure is smoother than anything they have written before, or if they cannot say why a paragraph sits where it sits, something has gone wrong and it is better found now than after submission.

Other signals are quieter. The process journal is thin while the report is polished. The student discusses the project only during the tutor's session and never otherwise. Sessions close to the deadline get longer and the student emerges with more finished than the hours can explain. A tutor who asks for editing access to the document is asking for the wrong thing, whatever reason is offered.

What honest progress looks like over a term is slower and much less dramatic. The same criterion comments start repeating less often. The student can name what a descriptor is asking before attempting the task rather than after being marked. A supervisor meeting goes better because the student walks in with something of their own to say. Nobody can promise a result, and no tutor can guarantee a grade, since grade boundaries are set by the IB and a total out of 32 moves for reasons no tutor controls.

Be honest about the limits as well. IB MYP home tuition in India cannot fix a student who is over-committed, and adding a second tutor in MYP 5 is usually the wrong response to a project that has slipped. Sometimes the right answer is fewer activities and a frank conversation with the coordinator. Sometimes it is no tuition at all for a term. A tutor who says that out loud has earned more of your trust than one who quietly books the extra hours.
items: Ask the student to explain a page of their report without reading it
Compare the roughness of the process journal with the polish of the report
Watch for sessions that grow longer as a deadline gets closer
Expect repeated criterion comments to thin out over a term, not vanish
Fewer commitments sometimes beats more home tuition during MYP 5

contentBlocks.heading: Starting MYP home tuition in India: what to gather this week
contentBlocks.body:
Send four things and the first session stops being a getting-to-know-you hour. The last report with the criterion scores still attached. One marked task carrying the school's own comments. The project milestone dates from the coordinator. Your honest weekday evening availability, including the evenings already given to sport, music or travel time.

From there the sequence is ordinary. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs, subject to availability. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and if the match turns out wrong you can ask for a different tutor without starting the whole search again.

The first session should not open with teaching. It should open with the tutor reading the marked task in front of the student and asking what the criterion comment meant. Most students cannot answer that, and the size of the gap is the plan. By the end of the hour you should have one criterion named as the term's focus, the weekly shape agreed, and the project boundary said out loud with the student sitting there.

Say it in front of the child deliberately. The Personal Project is yours, the tutor will ask you questions about it, and the tutor will not write any of it. A thirteen or fifteen-year-old who hears that stated calmly at the start of an arrangement rarely tests it later in the year. And you will have removed the one conversation that becomes almost impossible once a deadline is three days away and everyone is tired.
items: The last report, with criterion scores and comments, not just grades
One marked task the school has annotated, in any subject group
Project milestone dates confirmed by the MYP coordinator in writing
Weekday evenings that are genuinely free after school and activities
A written note of what the tutor will not touch on project work

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with the MYP Personal Project at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only with the skills around it and never with the work itself. A tutor may teach how to narrow a research question, how to keep a process journal, how to reference sources and how to read a criterion descriptor. They may question the student's reasoning and ask them to reread their own paragraph against a criterion. They may not choose the goal, write or rewrite any sentence, or edit the report. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work, and the school confirms that before submitting it.

faqs.question: What support is legitimate on the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4?
faqs.answer: The same boundary applies, with one practical difference: the Community Project is often done in a group, so the student is also managing other people. A tutor can legitimately teach planning, time management, how to record a meeting and how to reflect honestly on what went wrong. They can ask what the group agreed and whether the evidence supports the claim being made. They cannot design the service action, write the reflection or produce the presentation. If a tutor offers to build the slides for your child, decline politely and say why.

faqs.question: What is the supervising teacher at school actually responsible for?
faqs.answer: The supervisor meets the student at set points, records those meetings, checks the process journal, gives feedback on one draft, confirms the work is the student's own and submits it. That teacher owns the process, not the tutor. If a tutor's advice contradicts an instruction from the supervisor, follow the supervisor without arguing about it. Ask the MYP coordinator early who the supervisor is and how often they meet, because families often discover the meeting schedule only after a milestone has quietly passed.

faqs.question: My child scored 5 out of 8 on a criterion. Is that bad?
faqs.answer: No, and reading it as a percentage is the commonest mistake parents make with the MYP. Each of the four criteria is scored 0 to 8. The four add to a total out of 32, and that total converts to a final grade from 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries set by the IB. A 5 is not a share of anything. What matters is which criterion sits consistently lower than the others across subjects, because that repeating pattern is what a tutor can genuinely work on.

faqs.question: How many home tuition sessions a week does an MYP student need?
faqs.answer: Usually one or two, and fewer during a project term rather than more. One ninety-minute session on the weakest criterion, plus short independent practice the student does alone, is enough for most MYP 3 and MYP 4 students. In MYP 5 the sensible move is often to reduce rather than add, because the Personal Project needs protected hours with nobody else in them. Families who stack three or four sessions a week through project term usually find the project is what gets squeezed out.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Whitefield or Sarjapur Road on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, subject to tutor availability, because that side of Bengaluru has a reasonable pool of MYP-experienced teachers. The honest constraint is travel rather than willingness. A tutor already working in Whitefield can usually hold a seven o'clock slot; one crossing from Jayanagar or Yelahanka in evening traffic will cancel more often than either of you would like. Ask candidates where their other students live before agreeing a time, and keep a hybrid option for the weeks when the road wins.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and cannot find an MYP tutor nearby. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Online one-to-one, almost always, and at MYP level it works better than families expect. Smaller cities such as Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru and Visakhapatnam have few MYP-trained teachers, so insisting on a local visit usually means accepting someone who teaches a different board entirely. A tutor working online can be matched on subject group and MYP experience instead of postcode. For a younger MYP student, keep sessions shorter and have a parent in the room for the first few weeks.

faqs.question: How do I know if my child's project help has crossed the line?
faqs.answer: Ask them to explain one page of their report without looking at it. A student who wrote the page can tell you what the paragraph is doing and why it sits there. Other signals: a thin process journal beside a polished report, vocabulary that is not theirs, or sessions that lengthen as the deadline nears while the student's own working hours shrink. If you are unsure, show the supervisor and ask directly. Raising it early is far easier than answering it afterwards.

faqs.question: Does the school check the Personal Project for originality?
faqs.answer: Yes. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than by the school alone. That is why the boundary matters more than it feels like it should during a busy week. A report that a tutor tightened is not a small favour; it makes the student's own declaration of authenticity untrue. Teach the student to keep the journal honestly from the first week and the question never has to arise.

faqs.question: Our school offers MYP eAssessment in MYP 5. Should tuition change?
faqs.answer: Somewhat, yes. MYP eAssessment is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so first confirm with your coordinator that your child is actually sitting it. Where a school does offer it, MYP 5 carries on-screen examinations and ePortfolios alongside the Personal Project, which makes protected project hours harder to defend. The plan usually becomes fewer subjects tutored, more independent practice, and one clear decision about which criterion is worth the term's attention.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session is missed during project deadline week?
faqs.answer: Agree the answer before it happens rather than afterwards. Most families settle on a short online replacement instead of a rescheduled visit, because deadline week is exactly when a two-hour block cannot be found. Write down how much notice each side gives, whether a missed session is made up or forgiven, and who calls whom. A missed session in an ordinary week is trivial. A missed session in the fortnight before a Personal Project milestone is the one you will remember.

h1: IB MYP Private Tutors for a Criterion Score That Will Not Move
heroTitle: One criterion, diagnosed and moved, across India
heroSubtitle: Your child understands the topic and still scores 3 on Criterion B. That gap is a skill problem, not a knowledge problem, and it has its own fix. This page sets out how a one-to-one tutor finds the stuck criterion, what changes in each session, and how progress across India is checked.
introSummary: IB MYP private tutors in India are most useful when one criterion refuses to move while the others are fine, and most home tuition of this kind starts with a marked task rather than a syllabus. In the International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP), every subject is assessed against four criteria (A to D), each scored 0 to 8, and the total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A child can know the content well and still lose marks in Criterion C Communicating because the reasoning is never written down. A home tutor working one-to-one can see that in a single session. A batch teacher usually cannot, because the batch is marked on answers.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a stuck MYP criterion in India become a shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with evidence, not a subject name. When a family asks IB Gram for IB MYP private tutors in India, the first question is not which subject is weak but which criterion is weak, and what the last three marked tasks actually said. A parent who sends a photograph of one marked task with the criterion descriptors attached will get a far better match than a parent who writes that mathematics is a problem.

That evidence changes the shortlist. A child losing marks on Criterion B Investigating patterns needs someone who can teach a student to generalise a rule and justify it. A child losing marks on Criterion C Communicating needs someone who will make them write, then mark the writing in front of them. These are different teaching skills, and plenty of capable subject tutors have only one of them.

IB Gram asks about the board, the subject, the MYP year, the school calendar, your locality and the slots your evenings can actually hold. Then it shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches the criterion you named. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and that trial is better spent on the stuck criterion than on a general revision of the topic. If the fit is wrong afterwards, ask for a different match. Home tuition arranged this way should never feel locked.

One caution. If your child's levels are low across A, B, C and D in every subject, the problem is probably not a criterion at all. It is workload, sleep, or a gap that goes back a year, and a tutor for one subject will not touch it. Say so in the enquiry, because the honest answer may be fewer commitments rather than another weekly session.
items: 1. Send the last three marked tasks with their criterion descriptors attached.
2. Name the criterion that is stuck, not just the subject.
3. Give the MYP year, school timings and two workable evening slots.
4. Take a trial session spent entirely on that one criterion.
5. Review after four sessions against a fresh task, not a feeling.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP 1 to 5 in India: the year a criterion usually gets stuck
contentBlocks.body:
The MYP runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Criterion levels exist from the start, but most families only begin reading them properly around MYP 3, when tasks get long enough for a weak criterion to show a consistent pattern rather than a bad week.

MYP 3 and MYP 4 are where the stuck criterion usually declares itself. Up to that point a quick, confident student can carry a subject on Criterion A Knowing and understanding alone, because the tasks are short and the answer is the marked object. From MYP 4 the tasks lengthen, an investigation asks for a generalisation and a justification, and a student who has never had to explain anything begins scoring 7 on one criterion and 3 on another in the same report. That split is the signal worth acting on.

MYP 5 adds two pressures at once. The Personal Project comes in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and both take real hours out of the week. Schools also often split MYP 4 and MYP 5 mathematics into standard and extended, where extended covers additional topics that prepare a student for Diploma Programme (DP) Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. A child sitting on the boundary of that decision with a weak Criterion B is in a genuinely difficult position, because extended asks for more of exactly the thing they cannot yet do.

MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, the on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination in India. So ask your coordinator which route your school follows before you plan a single session around it.
items: MYP 1 to 3: criterion levels exist but the patterns are still noisy
MYP 4: task length grows and a weak criterion becomes visible
MYP 4 to 5: standard or extended mathematics, informed by Criterion B
MYP 5: the Personal Project takes weekly hours out of subject study
MYP eAssessment is optional; confirm with your coordinator, not a parent forum

contentBlocks.heading: Criterion A is fine and Criterion B is not: four score patterns read properly
contentBlocks.body:
MYP Mathematics is the clearest place to see this, because its four criteria are named plainly: A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, and D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each scored 0 to 8. Four patterns come up again and again, and each one means something different.

High A, low B. The student executes a method accurately and quickly, then freezes when asked to find a pattern, describe the rule in general terms and justify why it holds. This is common among students who arrived from a procedure-heavy background where accuracy was the whole game. It is not a mathematics weakness. Nobody has ever asked them to generalise.

High A and B, low C. The student sees the structure, solves the problem in their head, and writes three lines where the task needed a labelled diagram, consistent notation, a stated variable and reasoning between steps. Criterion C is not marked on neat handwriting. It is marked on whether a reader can follow the argument without guessing. A student with strong content knowledge scores badly here precisely because the thinking felt obvious, so they left it out.

High A, B and C, low D. The student is fluent inside mathematics and lost the moment a question wraps it in a real context, asks them to choose a model, then asks whether that model was reasonable. The last part defeats most of them. They build the model and never comment on its limitations.

Flat and low everywhere. This is not a criterion problem. It is a content gap, a workload problem or a collapse in confidence, and it needs the subject teacher and the coordinator before any tutor.
items: High A, low B: accurate method, no habit of generalising a rule
High A and B, low C: reasoning happens silently and never reaches the page
Low D only: fluent in the mathematics, unable to judge a model's limits
Flat low levels: usually content or workload, not a single criterion
Rising A with static C across two terms: more revision is not the fix

contentBlocks.heading: IB MYP private tutors in India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Where you live changes which mode is realistic, not whether criterion work is possible. Supply for IB MYP private tutors in India is uneven, so the map matters. In Delhi NCR, families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka have the deepest local pool, and an IB MYP private tutor in Delhi can often hold a fixed weekday evening home class. Cross Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Golf Course Road into Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad and the arithmetic changes. Evening traffic on those corridors can stretch a short trip badly, so a tutor on the same side of the city is worth more than a marginally stronger one who is not.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has the same shape. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit close enough that an IB MYP private tutor in Mumbai can take two home classes in one evening. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are a different question, and many families there run one home class at the weekend and keep the midweek session online.

In Hyderabad, Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Secunderabad and Kokapet are well served, and an IB MYP private tutor in Hyderabad travels within that western arc rather than across the city. Pune behaves similarly around Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad, where an IB MYP private tutor in Pune can hold an after-school slot.

Beyond those clusters the search widens. An IB MYP private tutor in Bangalore or Bengaluru, in Chennai, in Kolkata or in Ahmedabad is findable. In Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, criterion teaching is scarce, and online is the honest answer. Searching for a private MYP tutor near me there tends to return board tutors rather than a MYP criteria tutor, and the two are not the same job.

Powai to Thane: a weekend home class, midweek online, one tutor throughout
Gachibowli and Kondapur: tutors travel within the arc, rarely across it
Koregaon Park and Kharadi: after-school slots before the evening traffic builds
Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun: online is usually the honest recommendation

contentBlocks.heading: What does a school report in India actually tell you about a criterion?
contentBlocks.body:
It tells you less than you expect, and more than most parents read. An MYP report gives a level from 0 to 8 for each of A to D, often with a comment against each. The number is not a percentage and does not behave like one. A 5 on a demanding task is a different achievement from a 5 on a gentle one, and the total out of 32 becomes a 1 to 7 grade only after IB grade boundaries are applied. Parents used to marks out of 100 misread a 4 as a failure. It is not one.

The comment matters more than the number, so look for the verb. If the comment against Criterion C says the student should justify each step or define variables before using them, that is a specific, teachable instruction. If it says only that the student should communicate more clearly, ask the teacher what a level 6 response to that exact task would have contained. Most teachers at international schools in India answer that question when it is asked politely, and the answer beats a term of general tuition.

Calendars matter too. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore each run their own reporting cycles, and criterion tasks cluster before them. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Practically, the useful moment to start home tuition is just after a report, not just before the next big task. You then have fresh evidence and a clear run of weeks in which to change something.
items: A criterion level from 0 to 8 is not a percentage
Read the verb in the comment: justify, define, label, generalise
Ask what a level 6 response to that exact task contained
Criterion tasks cluster before reporting cycles at international schools here
Start just after a report, while the evidence is still fresh

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid for criterion work in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Criterion work has one requirement the mode must respect: the tutor has to see the page while it is being written, not afterwards. That is the whole argument, and everything else follows from it.

Home tuition wins on Criterion C. A tutor sitting beside a student watches the notation go wrong in real time, catches the variable that was never defined, and stops them mid-line to ask what a reader would think there. For a thirteen-year-old whose Criterion C level has not moved in two terms, that presence is hard to replace, which is why most families who ask IB Gram for IB MYP private tutors in India begin with home classes. The costs are travel, a fixed slot the tutor must protect, and a smaller local pool.

Online wins on reach and, often, on Criterion B. Investigation work happens on a shared screen anyway, with a spreadsheet or graphing tool open, and a specialist in another city can teach generalisation as well online as in your drawing room, provided the student writes on paper and photographs it between steps. Online also removes the evening travel problem, which counts for more in Greater Noida and Thane than anywhere else.

Hybrid is where most families settle after a term: one home class a week for the sit-beside written work, and one online session for investigation practice and marked feedback on a task done in between. It keeps a good tutor who lives far away and still gives the student one lesson where somebody watches the pen move.

The honest limit is domestic. A home class can be worse than online when the only available space is a shared room with a television on. Judge the room, not the idea.
items: Home classes: strongest for Criterion C, notation and written reasoning
Online: strongest for reach, investigation work and shared-screen graphing tools
Hybrid: one home class weekly, one online, a marked task in between
Online removes the Greater Noida and Thane evening travel problem entirely
A noisy shared room beats nothing at home, but only just

contentBlocks.heading: Checking that a home tutor can actually mark against a criterion
contentBlocks.body:
Subject knowledge is the easy thing to verify and the least useful. Almost any competent graduate can do MYP 4 mathematics. Far fewer can hold a criterion descriptor in one hand and a student's script in the other and say, honestly, this is a 4, and here is the sentence that would have made it a 6.

IB Gram checks identity, qualifications and teaching experience before a profile goes live, and each profile states which programmes and levels the tutor actually teaches. That is a floor, not a verdict. The checks that decide this particular hire are yours to run.

In the trial, hand the tutor a marked task your child has already done and ask three things. Which criterion is costing the most marks here. What precisely is missing from this response. What would you have the student do differently next time. A tutor who answers with generalities about practice and revision is a subject tutor rather than a MYP criteria tutor. A tutor who asks to see the criterion descriptors the school used is showing the right instinct.

Ask as well whether they have taught the MYP, not only the Diploma Programme. The two are marked differently, and a strong DP tutor who has never worked from criterion descriptors will teach content well and leave Criterion C where it was. For a one to one MYP tutor, that experience matters more than years in the job.

For a home tutor, add the ordinary safeguards. Photo identification at the society gate, sessions in a room with the door open, a parent somewhere in the flat, and a written agreement covering timings and cancellation. None of that is distrust. It is what any serious tutor expects.
items: Ask which criterion is costing marks on a task already marked
A tutor who requests the school's criterion descriptors is a good sign
Confirm MYP experience specifically, not only Diploma Programme teaching
Photo identification at the society gate for every home visit
A written agreement on timings, cancellation and how feedback reaches you

contentBlocks.heading: A worked example: moving one MYP criterion over a single term
contentBlocks.body:
Take the shape of a case that recurs. A MYP 4 student in Powai scores 7 and then 6 on Criterion A across two mathematics tasks, and 3 on Criterion C both times. The school comment says the working is unclear. The parent reads that as untidiness and buys new notebooks. It is not untidiness.

Session one is diagnostic and nothing else. The tutor gives back a task the student has already done and watches them redo it unaided, saying nothing. The student solves it correctly in four lines. The tutor then asks the student to read those four lines aloud as though they were a stranger. The student cannot say what one of the letters stands for. That is the finding, and it took one session.

Session two changes one rule and leaves everything else alone. Every variable is defined in words before it is used, and every line opens with a connective saying why it follows. The mathematics is not retaught. The student resents this for roughly twenty minutes, then produces a response twice as long as usual and insists it is a waste of time.

Sessions three to six apply the same rule to harder tasks, with the tutor marking each response against the school's own Criterion C descriptors in front of the student, out loud, before handing it back. Around session five the student starts defining variables without being told. That is the moment worth paying for.

By the end of the term, the Criterion C level on a comparable task moves from 3 to 5 or 6. Criterion A does not change, because it was never the problem. No tutor can promise that timeline for a particular child, and a criterion stuck behind a content gap takes longer. But the shape holds: find the missing habit, install one rule, apply it under marking until it runs on its own.
items: Session one: the student redoes a marked task while the tutor watches
Session two: one rule installed, every variable defined before it is used
Sessions three to six: the same rule against harder tasks, marked aloud
Criterion A stays flat throughout, because it was never the weakness
Resistance in the first two sessions is normal and not a warning sign

contentBlocks.heading: How do you know the criterion has genuinely moved?
contentBlocks.body:
A rising level is not proof. Criterion levels are awarded on tasks, and tasks vary in difficulty, so a move from 4 to 6 on an easier unit tells you very little. Four checks separate real movement from a soft task.

Compare like with like first. Ask whether the new task demanded the same strands of that criterion as the old one, because a Criterion B task that supplies the pattern is not the same as one that asks the student to find it. Next, look for the behaviour appearing without prompting. The habit has moved when your child defines variables, labels axes or states a limitation in a piece of work the tutor never saw. Then ask the school, since a subject teacher will usually say plainly whether the change shows in class work as well as in submitted tasks. Last, watch the other criteria. Real movement on C often nudges D up slightly, because clearer writing exposes clearer thinking, and one criterion leaping while everything else freezes is worth questioning.

There is a harder truth inside this. Parents who engage IB MYP private tutors in India for a single criterion are buying diagnosis, a rule and honest marking. The tutor cannot make the student apply that rule in a school assessment with nobody watching. Transfer belongs entirely to the student, and it is the part that fails most often. A student who performs the habit beautifully in a session and abandons it in the assessment has not moved the criterion. They have learned to please the tutor.

So set the expectation with your child early, not only with the tutor. Two terms is a fair horizon for a criterion stuck on habit. Longer, if the content underneath is thin as well.
items: Compare tasks demanding the same criterion strands, not any two tasks
The habit appears in work the tutor never saw
The subject teacher sees the change in ordinary class work too
One criterion jumping while the rest freeze is worth questioning
Transfer to unsupervised school tasks belongs to the student alone

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in India for one criterion, not six subjects
contentBlocks.body:
Keep the first commitment small. One subject, one criterion, one session a week, reviewed after four sessions against a fresh marked task. Families who begin home tuition in three subjects because the report looked bad usually finish the term with a tired child and no clear evidence about any of it.

Before sending an enquiry, gather three things. The last two or three marked tasks with their criterion levels and comments. The school's criterion descriptors for that subject, if the teacher will share them. And an honest note of which two evening slots your week can hold every week, not only in a good one. Families looking for IB MYP private tutors in India who send that much get a shortlist that fits. Families who send a subject name get a generic one.

What follows is straightforward. You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, subject, MYP year, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who have taught the criterion worrying you. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, subject to tutor availability. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid. If the match is wrong, ask for a different one.

The first session should not be a lesson. It should be the diagnostic described above, with your child redoing an old task while the tutor watches. Tell the tutor that is what you want, and tell your child too, so nobody arrives expecting a chapter.

And if the tutor says after three sessions that the real problem is workload, or a gap going back to MYP 2, listen. That answer is worth more than a term of tuition booked out of worry.
items: One subject, one criterion, one weekly session to begin with
Send marked tasks and criterion descriptors, not just a subject name
Name two evening slots your week holds in a bad week
Ask for the first session to be diagnostic rather than taught
Review after four sessions against a fresh marked task

faqs.question: My child gets 7 on Criterion A and 3 on Criterion B. What is actually wrong?
faqs.answer: Nothing is wrong with their mathematics; the missing skill is generalisation. Criterion A rewards knowing a method and applying it correctly, which your child clearly can do. Criterion B Investigating patterns asks for something else: find a pattern, describe the general rule in symbols or words, test it, and justify why it holds. Students who came through a procedure-heavy primary education are rarely asked to do any of that, so they meet it for the first time in MYP 3 or MYP 4. It is a teachable habit, usually over a term, and retaught content will not touch it.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor work on one criterion only, or does the whole subject need reteaching?
faqs.answer: One criterion is usually the right scope, and a good home tutor will insist on it. If Criterion A levels are healthy, the content is already in place, and reteaching it wastes the session and bores the student. The work instead stays narrow: a rule about how responses are written or investigated, applied to tasks the student can already solve, marked aloud against the school's descriptors until the habit holds without prompting. Reteaching content is only justified when every criterion is low together, which points to a gap rather than a habit.

faqs.question: How long should it take to move a criterion?
faqs.answer: A criterion stuck on habit rather than knowledge usually shows movement within a term of weekly sessions, and settles over two. No tutor can promise a particular level by a particular date, and anyone who does is selling something. The variables are how entrenched the habit is, how often the school sets tasks against that criterion, and whether the student applies the rule when nobody is watching. If nothing has changed after six or seven sessions on a criterion that should be habit-driven, the diagnosis was probably wrong and should be revisited rather than repeated.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor coming to Powai or Bandra on a weekday evening actually fit around MYP timings?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided you name the slot rather than asking what is available. Most MYP students in Bandra, Juhu, Powai and Andheri finish school and an activity by early evening, which leaves a narrow window that fills quickly. A home tutor living in the same cluster can hold that window week after week. One crossing the city from Thane or Navi Mumbai during peak evening traffic will eventually start arriving late, and a criterion session that begins twenty minutes short is not worth much. Ask where the tutor lives before you ask anything else.

faqs.question: Should we be preparing for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Only if your school offers it, and that is a question for the MYP coordinator rather than an assumption. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 consists of on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, it is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination in India, so a tutor promising exam preparation for the MYP without first asking what your school does is not paying attention. If your school does offer it, the criterion habits described on this page matter more rather than less, because that work is still assessed against criteria.

faqs.question: How are fees usually structured for a private MYP tutor?
faqs.answer: By the hour or by a monthly block of sessions, and the structure matters more than the headline figure. A home class costs more than online with the same tutor, because travel is priced into the slot, and a longer commitment is sometimes quoted differently from a rolling arrangement. Ask three questions before agreeing anything: what happens to a session the family cancels, what happens to one the tutor cancels, and whether marking work between sessions is included or charged separately. Criterion work generates marking, so that last point is not a small detail.

faqs.question: My child is choosing between standard and extended mathematics in MYP 4. Does a weak criterion decide it?
faqs.answer: It should inform the decision without settling it. Schools often split MYP 4 and MYP 5 mathematics into standard and extended, and extended covers additional topics that prepare a student for Diploma Programme Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. A student with a weak Criterion B will find extended harder, because extended asks for more investigation and justification, not simply more topics. But if Analysis and Approaches is the intention later, the better answer may be to take extended and fix Criterion B deliberately this year. Your school's mathematics teacher holds the evidence, so ask them first.

faqs.question: We are in Chandigarh and cannot find an MYP tutor locally. Does online really work for a fourteen-year-old?
faqs.answer: Yes, on two conditions. The student must write on paper during the session and show the page rather than typing answers into a chat box, because the criterion being fixed usually lives in written reasoning. And an adult should be in the flat, though not in the room, for the first few weeks, since attention at fourteen drifts faster online than in person. Families in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun run this arrangement routinely, because criterion teaching is scarce outside the big metros and a nearby generalist is not a substitute.

faqs.question: The criterion level went up but the task looked easier. How do I tell the difference?
faqs.answer: Compare what the two tasks demanded, not the two numbers. Ask the teacher whether both assessed the same strands of that criterion, and whether the newer one supplied any structure the older one did not. Then look for the behaviour in work the tutor never touched: a defined variable in a class exercise, a labelled diagram on a homework sheet nobody marked. That unprompted appearance is the real evidence. A level that rises only on tutored tasks and falls back on school tasks means the habit has not transferred yet.

faqs.question: What does the student have to do that the tutor cannot do for them?
faqs.answer: Apply the habit in an assessment with nobody watching. The tutor can find the stuck criterion, install a specific rule, and mark work honestly against the descriptors. Transfer belongs to the student alone, and it is where this work most often stalls. In practice that means writing the extra two lines in a timed class task when it feels unnecessary, rereading their own response as a stranger before submitting it, and telling the tutor honestly when they did not do it. A student who performs the habit only in sessions has learned to please the tutor.

faqs.question: Is a shared drawing room good enough for a home class, or do we need a separate study space?
faqs.answer: A shared room works if two things are true: the television is off, and nobody walks through repeatedly. Criterion work needs the student to write and think aloud, and both collapse under interruption. A dining table in a quiet corner beats a beautiful desk in a busy passage. In smaller flats across Indian cities this is a real constraint, and the honest fix is usually timing rather than furniture, so pick the hour when the household is quietest. If no such hour exists, an online session with the student in a closed room may serve better than a home visit.

comparison.heading: One-to-one, a small group or a batch: what moves a criterion in India?
comparison.intro: Every format teaches mathematics. They differ in whether anyone watches the student write. A criterion like Communicating is marked on the page, so the format that lets a teacher interrupt mid-line is worth more than the one with the best notes. A batch costs less per hour, and a small group gives the peer discussion that sharpens an explanation. Choose on which criterion is stuck, then on logistics.
