heroTitle: Online MYP Support Across India, Phase by Phase
heroSubtitle: Your child is twelve, the school has placed them in a Language Acquisition phase you do not fully understand, and the nearest tutor who knows the Middle Years Programme lives in another city. This page is about what online tutoring can and cannot do at that age, said plainly.
introSummary: IB MYP online tutors in India teach Middle Years Programme students, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, one to one over video, usually because the right specialist does not live within driving distance of the family. The most common request at this stage is language: a student who speaks English adequately but keeps losing marks against the Language Acquisition criteria, and a parent who searched for an ESL tutor because nobody mentioned that the International Baccalaureate (IB) has no subject by that name. Online lessons work well here. They also fail in specific, predictable ways at this age, and both halves of that are set out below, together with session length, the supervision an online lesson genuinely needs at home, and the point at which a home tutor is the better answer.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a request for MYP language help in India turn into a shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks which MYP year your child is in, which phase the school has placed them in for Language Acquisition, what the most recent criterion feedback actually said, where you are and which evening slots the household can hold. A shortlist of verified tutor profiles matching those answers comes back, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything.

Those questions are not a form for the sake of a form. A tutor who has taught phase 2 writing to twelve-year-olds is doing a different job from one who has prepared a phase 5 student for the move into Diploma Programme (DP) English B, and a family that cannot start before eight in the evening on weekdays rules out a large part of the available pool before subject even enters the conversation. Say the awkward parts out loud at this stage. If your child sulks through school language lessons, that belongs in the query.

Bring the report, not a summary of it. MYP reports carry criterion letters and short comments rather than percentages, and the comments are where the diagnosis sits. A parent telling us the child got a 4 in Language Acquisition gives a tutor very little to work with. A parent forwarding the line about organising ideas across a sustained piece of writing has effectively given the tutor a first lesson plan.

The trial matters more at this age than at any other. You are not only testing subject knowledge; you are testing whether a stranger on a screen can get a reluctant thirteen-year-old to talk for forty minutes. Sit within earshot for that first one. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match, and say specifically what was wrong, because a vague report of not clicking is not actionable and a report that the tutor talked at her for the whole hour is.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, naming the MYP year and phase
2. Share the last report's criterion comments, not just the criterion grades
3. Give your real weekday and weekend slots before discussing subject depth
4. Receive a shortlist of verified profiles matched to phase, subject and schedule
5. Run a trial session and watch how the tutor handles silence and stalling
6. Confirm, or ask for a different match, naming what specifically did not work

contentBlocks.heading: MYP 1 to 5: what an online tutor can hold at eleven, and at fifteen
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. That structure, and not a percentage, is what an online tutor has to teach towards.

The gap between an MYP 1 student and an MYP 5 student is wider than most parents expect, and it changes what a screen can carry. At eleven, a child is still learning how to be taught: how to say that they do not understand without embarrassment, how to sit with a hard question for two minutes instead of guessing. Online lessons at that age have to be short, heavily structured and visibly active, with the student writing or speaking every few minutes. At fifteen, with the Personal Project running and DP subject selection approaching, a student can sustain a longer session and can be left to draft while the tutor watches the shared document.

Two projects sit inside the programme and both change the tutoring conversation. The Community Project comes in MYP 3 or 4, the Personal Project in MYP 5. These are the student's own work. A tutor may ask questions about a plan, teach a research or writing skill in general, and help a student read the criteria they are being marked against. A tutor may not supply the content, the structure or the reflection. Online makes that boundary easier to cross carelessly, because a shared screen invites a helpful adult to start typing.

MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, which combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination in India. So ask your coordinator directly whether your child's cohort will sit eAssessment, because a tutoring plan for a cohort that will is not the same plan as one for a cohort that will not.
items: MYP 1 to 5, eight subject groups, four criteria per subject scored 0 to 8
Criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade via IB grade boundaries
Community Project in MYP 3 or 4; Personal Project in MYP 5, entirely the student's own
MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and decided school by school
No single national MYP examination exists in India, so school evidence is what you have

contentBlocks.heading: Language Acquisition phases 1 to 6, and what a tutor works on inside each
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the thing almost every parent gets wrong. The IB has no subject called ESL. What your child is taking is Language Acquisition, taught in the MYP in phases 1 to 6, and the school places the student in a phase rather than a year group. A child can sit in MYP 3 and work in phase 2. That is not a failure. It is how the course is built, and the first thing to ask the language department is which phase your child is in and what would move them to the next one.

In the early phases, tutoring is mostly about production under low pressure: getting a student to speak in full sentences, to write more than four lines without stopping, to build the vocabulary a school subject actually needs rather than a general word list. In the middle phases, the work shifts to organisation and register. Students who can make themselves understood begin losing marks for structure, for repeating the same connective, for writing a text that ignores its intended audience. In the later phases it becomes analytical: reading an unfamiliar text and inferring rather than decoding, and writing at length with a controlled argument.

Whichever phase your child sits in, the work should happen inside their own writing, every session. A tutor should be marking the student's paragraph against the criterion descriptor in front of them, on screen, not handing back a corrected version. Correction teaches the tutor. Annotation teaches the student.

Where this leads matters, because parents plan for it late. In the DP, students whose first language is not English take English B at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL), or, for genuine beginners, English ab initio, which is SL only. English B is built around five themes: Identities, Experiences, Human ingenuity, Social organization and Sharing the planet. It is assessed by Paper 1, a writing task covering productive skills, Paper 2, listening and reading for receptive skills, and the individual oral, with two literary works added at HL. The phase your child leaves MYP 5 in shapes which of those doors is realistically open, and IB MYP online tutors in India spend a good deal of MYP 4 and 5 quietly building towards that decision. The same logic governs the other subjects families ask about, from IB Mathematics AA and AI through Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A.
items: There is no IB subject called ESL; the MYP course is Language Acquisition, phases 1 to 6
Phase placement is decided by the school, not by the student's year group
Early phases: sentence-level production, subject vocabulary, speaking without freezing
Middle phases: organisation, register, connectives, writing for a stated audience
Later phases: inference from unfamiliar texts and sustained written argument
DP route ahead: English B at SL or HL, or English ab initio at SL only

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB MYP online tutors in India reach when the specialist lives elsewhere
contentBlocks.body:
Language Acquisition teaching for the MYP sits where the international schools are, and those cluster hard. Families in Delhi NCR, in Powai and Andheri, in Bengaluru around Whitefield, in Gachibowli in Hyderabad, in Adyar in Chennai and in Koregaon Park in Pune can usually find somebody locally who has taught the phases. Outside those clusters the pool thins quickly, which is the plain reason most searches for IB MYP online tutors in India start somewhere else entirely.

Take southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai. A family in Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam, Madurai or Thiruvananthapuram may have a good school within reach and still find that nobody within an hour's drive has taught MYP Language Acquisition to a phase 3 student. In central and western India, the same holds for Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik, Raipur and Goa. The honest answer there is not that a local generalist will do; it is that an online tutor who knows the criteria is worth more to your child than a nearby tutor who will teach grammar drills.

In Kolkata and eastern India the picture varies within a single city. Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat households often have options, while families in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi or Patna are usually looking at a screen from the start. Evening traffic between the eastern suburbs and the older parts of the city can stretch what looks like a short trip, so even where a home tutor exists, a six o'clock start is fragile on a weekday. That is why parents there who began by searching for an IB MYP online tutor in Kolkata rarely go back to a home visit.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR follows the same logic. Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula have reasonable supply; Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur much less. In Gujarat, families in Ahmedabad around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, frequently ask for an IB MYP online tutor in Ahmedabad and end up matched with someone in another state, which is fine for language work and less obviously fine for a subject that needs a shared sheet of paper. The same requests arrive as searches for an IB MYP online tutor in Mumbai, in Delhi, in Bangalore, in Hyderabad, in Chennai and in Pune, and the answer differs mostly by how much local choice the family already has.
items: Metro clusters with local supply: Delhi NCR, Powai and Andheri, Whitefield, Gachibowli, Adyar
Southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai: Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Visakhapatnam, Madurai
Central and western India: Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik, Raipur, Jabalpur and Goa
Kolkata and eastern India: Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Patna
Northern India beyond Delhi NCR: Chandigarh, Mohali, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Kanpur
Gujarat: Ahmedabad's Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, plus Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara

contentBlocks.heading: The MYP year in India: criterion reports, projects and the term that tightens
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named anywhere on this site, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. What follows is about the calendar pressures families at international schools in India deal with in general, because those pressures decide when online tutoring helps and when it merely adds an evening commitment.

Most international schools in India run a year that opens around late July or August and closes in the following May or June, with a long break in the middle and shorter breaks around the autumn festivals. Criterion feedback arrives in waves rather than once a term, attached to specific assessed tasks. This is the single biggest source of parental confusion. You will get a 5 for criterion C on one task and a 3 on the next, and neither is a trend. Wait for two or three data points on the same criterion before you conclude anything about your child.

The pressure points are predictable. For MYP 3 and 4 students, the Community Project eats weekends in a way nobody warns families about. For MYP 5, the Personal Project and, where the school offers it, eAssessment preparation land in the same stretch as DP subject selection conversations. Language Acquisition students feel that last one most sharply, because the phase they are working in is part of what determines which DP language route the school will recommend.

So plan tutoring against the calendar rather than against panic. The useful windows are the weeks just after the first substantial criterion feedback arrives, and the stretch before the Personal Project's main drafting period. The useless window is the fortnight before a deadline, when a tutor can only watch a student produce something rushed. And in the long mid-year break, a lighter online rhythm, one session a week rather than two, holds a language better than stopping entirely and restarting cold in August.
items: School years commonly open in late July or August and close the following May or June
Criterion feedback arrives task by task, so read trends across two or three tasks
Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 quietly consumes weekends for several weeks
MYP 5 stacks the Personal Project against DP subject selection conversations
A lighter weekly online session across the long break beats stopping and restarting

contentBlocks.heading: Screen, room or both: picking a mode for a twelve-year-old in India
contentBlocks.body:
For a younger secondary student the short version is this: a home tutor in the room holds attention better, an online tutor gives you access to someone who actually knows the phases, and a hybrid week is the compromise most families with an eleven to fourteen year old end up choosing. None of the three is right in general. The right one depends on your child's temperament and on what exists within reach of your locality, which is why most parents comparing IB MYP online tutors in India are really comparing two constraints at once.

Home tuition wins on presence. A tutor sitting beside a twelve-year-old sees the pencil stop, sees the eyes drift to the door, sees the page where the handwriting degrades because the student gave up halfway through a paragraph. None of that is reliably visible over video. Home sessions also ask less of you, because supervision is built in. The cost is choice: in most of India outside the metro clusters, the set of home tutors who have genuinely taught MYP Language Acquisition is small, and sometimes empty.

Online wins on match quality, on travel and on continuity. Nobody cancels because of rain in Nagpur or a blocked road near Salt Lake, sessions start on time at seven in the evening on a Tuesday, and a student can work with a tutor who has taught their exact phase. It costs attention. A thirteen-year-old with a laptop, a second tab and no adult in the house will drift, and any tutor who tells you otherwise has not taught that age group online.

Hybrid means a real split, not a vague promise: one home session a week for the work that needs paper and a person, one online session for the specialist teaching. Families in Ahmedabad and Chandigarh use this shape often, pairing a local home tutor for study habits with an online language specialist. It costs more coordination, and the two tutors have to actually speak to each other, which somebody in the family has to arrange and keep arranging.
items: Home tutoring: best attention for a younger student, smallest pool outside metro clusters
Online: best match quality and reliability, weakest on holding an eleven-year-old's focus
Hybrid: one home session for paper work, one online session for specialist teaching
Online removes travel loss but transfers supervision work to a parent at home
Whichever mode you pick, keep the same tutor across a term rather than rotating

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor your child only ever meets on a screen?
contentBlocks.body:
You check three things: identity, that the person teaching is the person on the profile; experience, that they have taught the MYP phases and criteria rather than general English; and conduct, that the lesson is held in a way you can see. IB Gram verifies profiles before they go live. There are also checks a platform cannot do for you, which you must run yourself in the trial and across the first fortnight.

Ask the questions a general tutor cannot answer. Which criterion do students most often get stuck on in the phase my child is in, and what does the work to move it look like? What is the difference between marking a student's writing and annotating it against a descriptor? Where exactly is the line on the Personal Project? A tutor who has done this work answers those in concrete terms within a minute. A tutor who has not will talk about confidence and fundamentals.

For a younger student, add safeguarding to the list and treat it as non-negotiable. Lessons should run in a shared family space with the door open, not in a bedroom. The account should be the parent's, not the child's. Camera on for both sides. No lesson communication through a channel you cannot see, which means no private chats and no direct messaging between tutor and child outside the platform.

Then check the ordinary things, because they are the ones that break. Does the tutor have a second device or a phone hotspot when the connection drops? Can they annotate on screen, or will they spend the lesson describing corrections out loud? Will they send a short written note after each session saying what was covered and what the student should do before the next one? For an eleven or twelve-year-old that note is the only reliable record you will get, because asking the child how the lesson went produces a single word.
items: Profiles are verified before they go live; the trial is where you check the teaching
Ask which criterion students get stuck on in your child's phase, and why
Shared family space, door open, camera on, parent's account, no private channels
Confirm a backup connection and on-screen annotation before you commit
Require a short written note after every session; a child's word for it is not a report

contentBlocks.heading: How do you keep an eleven to fourteen year old genuinely engaged online?
contentBlocks.body:
Honestly? Partly by design, and partly by accepting that you will not manage it every time. A younger secondary student cannot hold a screen the way a Diploma student can, which is the first thing good IB MYP online tutors in India adjust for. An online MYP session has to be built in short blocks with the student producing something every few minutes, and it has to be shorter overall than the ninety minutes a DP lesson runs. Forty-five minutes is usually the working ceiling at eleven or twelve. Sixty at fourteen, with a break in it.

A session that works at this age has a shape. It opens with two or three minutes on what the student did since last time, then a short piece of the student's own work on the shared screen with the tutor annotating against a criterion, then a task the student does live while the tutor stays quiet, then a five-minute break away from the desk, then a second short block, then a two-line summary the student writes themselves. The passive stretch, tutor talking while the child watches, should never run more than about eight minutes in one go.

Now the supervision, which is the part nobody puts on a tutoring page. An online MYP lesson at this age needs an adult in the house and within earshot, not in the room. You are not monitoring the teaching. You are there so the laptop does not quietly become a second browser tab, so a dropped connection gets fixed in thirty seconds instead of eight minutes, and so the session actually starts at the agreed time. Sit at the dining table with your own work. Once a student is fifteen and self-starting, step back. Before that, presence in the house is part of what makes the session work at all.

The setup does real work too. A laptop rather than a phone, a plain wall behind the student, headphones, and paper and a pen on the desk, because a student who never writes by hand in a language lesson is being trained for the wrong task. Notifications off on the device, and the phone in another room. Small things, and they are the difference between a lesson and an hour of watching somebody teach.
items: Forty-five minutes is the practical ceiling at eleven or twelve; sixty at fourteen with a break
Never more than about eight minutes of tutor talk before the student produces something
A five-minute break away from the desk, mid-session, is not lost time
An adult within earshot and in the house, not sitting in the room
Laptop not phone, headphones, pen and paper on the desk, notifications off

contentBlocks.heading: When should a younger student not be tutored online at all?
contentBlocks.body:
There are four situations where the answer is no. A student who cannot yet read comfortably in English should be taught in person, because early reading needs somebody watching the eyes and the mouth. A student with a diagnosed attention or processing difficulty usually needs the room, unless the school's learning support team advises otherwise. A household with no quiet space and no adult at home during the slot should not start online. And a child who is already in school for a full day, in coaching after that and an activity on top does not need another screen; they need something taken out of the week.

Beyond those, there is a softer case for stopping. If, after six or seven weeks, your child is still not talking in the lesson, still needs you to launch the call, and still cannot tell you in their own words what the last session was about, online is not landing. Change the mode before you change the tutor. A home tutor for a term often fixes what looked like a tutoring problem and was really a medium problem.

What should progress look like when it is working? In the first month, small process changes: the student opens the laptop without being asked twice, produces a paragraph rather than three lines, starts using the criterion language when talking about their own work. By the second or third month, changes in the work itself: fewer comments about organisation on returned tasks, a criterion that had been sitting at the same number for two terms finally moving. Criterion scores are noisy, so read the comments alongside them rather than tracking the number alone.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anybody describing a specific score improvement for a criterion-marked programme is describing something they do not control. Availability is subject to tutor schedules and depends on level, phase and the slot you need. What is reasonable to expect is a clear plan, honest notes after each session, and a tutor who will tell you when your child should stop being tutored.
items: No online tutoring if the student cannot yet read English comfortably
Learning support advice comes first where attention or processing difficulties are diagnosed
No quiet space and no adult at home during the slot means online will not hold
An already overloaded week needs something removed, not an added session
Month one brings process changes; months two and three show in the marked work
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and availability depends on phase, level and schedule

contentBlocks.heading: Starting online MYP tuition in India: what the first two weeks look like
contentBlocks.body:
Before you book anything, gather three things: the last two reports with the criterion comments visible, a piece of your child's recent written work in the language subject, and an honest list of the evening slots your household can hold without a fight. That third one causes more arrangements to collapse than subject mismatch ever does. A slot that requires the family to eat dinner at half past nine will not survive past week four.

Tell your child what is happening, and let them hear the reason. At eleven to fourteen, a student who thinks tutoring is a punishment for a bad report behaves accordingly in the first session. A student who has been told that the school says their ideas are good but the writing is not organised yet, and that somebody is going to help with exactly that, walks in differently. Use the school's own words rather than your own worry.

The first session should not teach much. A good tutor spends it finding out where the student actually is: reading something aloud, writing a short piece live, talking about what they find hardest. Expect the tutor to ask your child questions you already know the answer to. That is the tutor building a baseline, and it is why the first session can feel light. By the end of the second, you should have a written plan naming the criterion being targeted first and what will be different in the work by the end of the term.

After that the rhythm settles. One or two sessions a week depending on the phase and the MYP year, a short note after each, a short conversation with you every three or four weeks, and a review at the end of the term against that written plan. If the match is wrong at any point, ask for a different tutor. Changing at week three costs your child almost nothing. Changing in MYP 5 in February costs a great deal, and that asymmetry is the whole argument for taking the trial seriously.
items: Bring two recent reports with criterion comments and one piece of the child's own writing
Agree the weekly slot against the household's real evenings, not the ideal ones
Explain the reason to the student in the school's own words before the first session
Expect a diagnostic first session and a written plan by the end of the second
Review against that plan each term; change the tutor early if the fit is wrong

faqs.question: Is my child's ESL class the same as MYP Language Acquisition?
faqs.answer: Yes in practice, and no in name: the IB has no subject called ESL, and what your child is taking is Language Acquisition. Parents search for ESL because that is the label used in many other systems, and schools sometimes use it informally too. In the MYP the course runs in phases 1 to 6, and the school places a student in a phase rather than by year group. Ask the language department which phase your child is in, and ask what specifically would move them to the next one.

faqs.question: How long should an online MYP session be for a twelve-year-old?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes, with a short break in the middle, is the practical ceiling at eleven or twelve. By fourteen a student can usually hold sixty minutes if the session is broken into blocks and they are producing work rather than listening. Ninety minutes, which is normal for a Diploma Programme lesson, does not translate to this age group online. Two shorter sessions a week beat one long one, because the recall gap is smaller and neither session asks for more attention than the student has to give.

faqs.question: Do I need to sit in the room during an online lesson, or is being at home enough?
faqs.answer: Being in the house and within earshot is enough; sitting in the room is usually not needed. Your job is not to supervise the teaching. It is to make sure the session starts on time, that a dropped connection is fixed quickly, and that the laptop does not become a second browser tab. Sit at the dining table with your own work. Once a student is around fifteen and starting sessions themselves, step back further. For a younger child, an adult at home during the lesson is part of what makes it work.

faqs.question: My son is thirteen and hates being on a screen after school. Is online pointless for him?
faqs.answer: Not pointless, but you should change the shape of the session rather than push harder. A thirteen-year-old who resists online tutoring is usually reacting to passive teaching: an adult talking while he watches. Ask for a session where he is writing, speaking or annotating every few minutes, with the tutor quiet for stretches. Move the slot away from immediately after school. If six or seven weeks of that changes nothing, a home tutor for a term is the sensible next step to try.

faqs.question: We live in Kochi and there is no MYP language specialist here. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Online is the realistic answer, and it is a genuinely good one for language work. Southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, including Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru and Madurai, has far fewer tutors who have taught the MYP phases than the metro clusters do. A local generalist teaching grammar drills will not move a criterion. An online tutor who has taught your child's phase can. Where a local home tutor exists for general study habits, a hybrid week combining both often works better than either alone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project or the Community Project?
faqs.answer: Only within clear limits, and those limits are stricter than most families assume. The Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 are the student's own work. A tutor may help the student read and understand the criteria, ask questions about a plan, and teach a general research or writing skill. A tutor may not supply content, structure, wording or reflection. Online makes the line easier to cross carelessly, so agree it explicitly before any project work begins.

faqs.question: How do I read an MYP report when there are no percentages on it?
faqs.answer: Read the comments first and the criterion numbers second. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, and the total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A single criterion score reflects one task, so it moves around a good deal. Look for the same criterion staying low across two or three tasks, and read what the teacher wrote about why. That comment is what a tutor can actually work on.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor in Ahmedabad better than an online tutor from another state?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the local tutor has taught the MYP phases, and most have not. Families in Ahmedabad around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and in Gandhinagar, Surat and Vadodara, often choose between a nearby tutor with general experience and a distant one with the right specialism. For Language Acquisition the specialism matters more than the presence. For a younger or easily distracted student, presence matters more. A hybrid week gets you both, at the cost of more coordination each week.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so, specifically, and ask for a different match. Describing what went wrong matters more than the fact that it did: a report that the tutor spoke for the whole hour while your daughter never said a word produces a much better second match than a vague sense that it did not click. Changing a tutor in the first few weeks costs your child almost nothing. Changing one in MYP 5 during the Personal Project period costs a great deal, which is why the trial deserves your attention.

faqs.question: Will my child sit an MYP examination at the end of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and only your school can tell you. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios, it is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination in India. Ask your coordinator directly whether your child's cohort will sit eAssessment, because the tutoring plan differs: a cohort sitting on-screen examinations needs timed practice, while one that is not should spend that time on criterion work instead.

faqs.question: How does MYP Language Acquisition connect to the Diploma Programme later?
faqs.answer: The phase your child leaves MYP 5 in shapes which DP language route the school recommends. Students whose first language is not English take English B at Standard Level or Higher Level, or, for genuine beginners, English ab initio, which is Standard Level only. English B is built around five themes, Identities, Experiences, Human ingenuity, Social organization and Sharing the planet, and is assessed by Paper 1 for productive skills, Paper 2 for listening and reading, and the individual oral, with two literary works added at Higher Level.

Families in Ahmedabad around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and in Gandhinagar, Surat and Vadodara, often choose between a nearby tutor with general experience and a distant one with the right specialism. For Language Acquisition the specialism matters more than the presence. For a younger or easily distracted student, presence matters more. A hybrid week gets you both, at the cost of more coordination each week.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so, specifically, and ask for a different match. Describing what went wrong matters more than the fact that it did: a report that the tutor spoke for the whole hour while your daughter never said a word produces a much better second match than a vague sense that it did not click. Changing a tutor in the first few weeks costs your child almost nothing. Changing one in MYP 5 during the Personal Project period costs a great deal, which is why the trial deserves your attention.

mainEntity.name: Will my child sit an MYP examination at the end of MYP 5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly, and only your school can tell you. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios, it is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination in India. Ask your coordinator directly whether your child's cohort will sit eAssessment, because the tutoring plan differs: a cohort sitting on-screen examinations needs timed practice, while one that is not should spend that time on criterion work instead.

mainEntity.name: How does MYP Language Acquisition connect to the Diploma Programme later?

acceptedAnswer.text: The phase your child leaves MYP 5 in shapes which DP language route the school recommends. Students whose first language is not English take English B at Standard Level or Higher Level, or, for genuine beginners, English ab initio, which is Standard Level only. English B is built around five themes, Identities, Experiences, Human ingenuity, Social organization and Sharing the planet, and is assessed by Paper 1 for productive skills, Paper 2 for listening and reading, and the individual oral, with two literary works added at Higher Level.

You will be asked about the school calendar, your location and the schedule, then sent verified tutor profiles that match. A trial session can be arranged before you commit, and you can ask for a different tutor if the fit turns out wrong.

heroTitle: Reading an MYP Report Before Hiring Anyone in India
heroSubtitle: An MYP grade of 4 tells you almost nothing on its own. This page shows you how to read the four criterion scores sitting behind it, what to ask the coordinator first, which MYP years tuition genuinely helps, and when the right decision is to wait a term.
introSummary: IB MYP tuition in India is worth starting only when the report shows a pattern, and most families book home tuition before they have looked properly. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) assesses every subject against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. Those four add to a total out of 32, and the school applies International Baccalaureate (IB) grade boundaries to turn that total into a 1 to 7 grade. One low criterion in one reporting cycle is a hard unit. The same low criterion twice, or across several subjects, is a gap. This page is about telling those apart before you hire an MYP home tutor, what to ask the coordinator first, the years where tuition pays off, and what over-tutoring a thirteen-year-old costs later.

contentBlocks.heading: From a criterion report to a shortlist: how IB MYP tuition in India starts
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents reach us with a number rather than a problem. My daughter got a 4 in Individuals and Societies. That 4 is the end of a calculation, not the beginning of one. Behind it sit four criterion scores out of 8 each, a total out of 32, and a set of IB grade boundaries the school applies. Two students can both hold a 4 in the same subject and need completely different help, or no paid help at all.

So the first conversation is about evidence, not availability. When you send a query about IB MYP tuition in India, IB Gram asks which MYP year the student is in, which subject groups are slipping, which criteria are low and which are perfectly fine, what the subject teacher has written in the comment box, what the school calendar holds for the next term, where you live and which evenings are genuinely free. None of that is filler. A student weak on criterion D in Sciences needs a different tutor from one weak on criterion A in the same class, and a family in Kharadi with two activity evenings needs a different schedule from one in Vasant Kunj.

Only then do we shortlist. Profiles are verified before they go live, and matching works on the criterion and the year, not on the subject name alone. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything, and if the fit turns out wrong you can ask for a different match. Availability depends on level, locality and schedule.

And sometimes the honest outcome of that conversation is that you do not need a tutor this term. We will say so. A parent who books six weeks of home tuition to fix a unit the whole class found hard has bought nothing except a tired child and a fortnight of arguments about Thursday evenings.
items: 1. Collect the last two reports with all four criterion scores visible
2. Separate the criteria scoring well from the one that keeps dropping
3. Ask the subject teacher whether the whole class found that unit hard
4. Email the MYP coordinator before you contact any tutor at all
5. Agree one checkable target with your child, in their own words
6. Only then send a query, naming the criterion and the year

contentBlocks.heading: Which MYP years does tuition in India actually pay off in?
contentBlocks.body:
MYP 4 and MYP 5, in most cases. The Middle Years Programme runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. In MYP 1 to MYP 3 a low criterion score is usually a maturity or habit problem, and both improve on their own more often than anxious parents expect. By MYP 4 the work has real depth, the Personal Project is close, and the Diploma Programme (DP) is near enough that a gap left alone starts to cost something measurable.

That is the general pattern, not a rule. Three situations justify help earlier. A student who has just moved from a CBSE or ICSE school into an MYP classroom and cannot work out what is being asked of them. A student with a language gap that is dragging down every subject rather than one. And a student whose confidence has collapsed far enough that they have stopped attempting work in order to avoid failing at it.

The projects change the timing question. The Community Project comes in MYP 3 or MYP 4, and the Personal Project in MYP 5. Both are the student's own work and a tutor's role around them is narrow. IB MYP tuition in India should not be timed to begin in the week a project deadline lands, because that is exactly when the temptation to help too much is strongest for everybody in the house.

MYP 5 may also involve eAssessment, which means on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios. It is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. There is no single national MYP examination in India, so your own school's reporting is the only evidence you have to work from. Ask which route your school follows before you plan a single session around it.
items: MYP 1 to MYP 3: read the pattern, fix habits, usually wait
MYP 4: the year a quiet gap begins to cost something
MYP 5: Personal Project year, so protect time rather than adding hours
A board switch into the MYP justifies short, early support at any year
Confirm whether your school offers MYP 5 eAssessment before planning around it

contentBlocks.heading: What the four criteria in each MYP subject are really telling you
contentBlocks.body:
Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. The four add to a total out of 32, and the school converts that total into a 1 to 7 grade using IB grade boundaries. Your report should print all four. If it prints only the final grade, ask for the criterion breakdown, because the grade on its own hides everything that would tell you what to do.

Read the profile, not the total. A student sitting at 6, 6, 3 and 4 has a different problem from one sitting at 4, 4, 4 and 4. The first is strong somewhere and collapsing somewhere specific, which is usually teachable. The second is thin everywhere, which is more often about workload, attention or academic language than about the subject, and a subject tutor will not touch it.

Then read across the eight subject groups. Write the four numbers for each subject on one sheet of paper. If the same letter is low in three subjects, open those three descriptors side by side: they will not say the same thing, because criteria differ by subject, but they often point at one underlying skill your child has not been taught to do. If one subject is low on all four criteria while the rest are healthy, that is the subject to look at and the only one.

Check the descriptors themselves. The school prints a short descriptor for the band your child landed in, and the band above it is printed too. Read that one. It states exactly what the next level of work requires, and often the distance is a single habit rather than a term of teaching. Parents who do this sheet-of-paper exercise arrive at a tutor conversation with a question instead of a worry.
items: Ask for criterion scores, not a grade, if the report shows only one
Write all four numbers for all eight subject groups on one sheet
A spiky profile is teachable; a flat low profile is usually not subject-specific
Read the band descriptor above the one your child was given
The same letter means different things in different MYP subjects

contentBlocks.heading: Across India, what MYP tuition near me actually returns
contentBlocks.body:
MYP tuition near me is the search, and the honest answer changes with your postcode. In Delhi NCR, families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri sit close to a reasonable pool, while Dwarka, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad thin out quickly. Gurugram (Gurgaon) around Golf Course Road and Noida near Sector 128 hold more MYP-capable tutors than the outer sectors, but weekday evening traffic between Gurugram and South Delhi can stretch what looks like a short trip, so a six o'clock home session across that line is optimistic in term time.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the geography is the constraint. IB MYP tuition in Mumbai is easiest to arrange in Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill. Powai works as its own pocket. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar and Thane families usually do better with a hybrid week than with a tutor crossing the city twice in an evening.

IB MYP tuition in Bangalore concentrates around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, with Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road harder to serve in the evening peak. In Chennai, Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Alwarpet and Anna Nagar are straightforward, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery depend entirely on which direction the tutor is already travelling. IB MYP tuition in Pune runs smoothly in Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar, Kharadi, Aundh and Baner; Hinjewadi, Balewadi and Wakad families should ask about the return trip before fixing a slot.

Beyond those clusters, IB MYP tuition in Hyderabad, in Kolkata and in Ahmedabad is real but narrower, and IB MYP tuition in Delhi is not the same market as IB MYP tuition in Chennai. Where the local pool is thin, online reaches the tutor who matches the criterion.

Powai, Thane and Kharghar often work better hybrid than as home visits
Whitefield and Sarjapur Road have depth; Yelahanka and Hebbal have less
OMR and Velachery slots depend on the direction the tutor travels
Hyderabad, Kolkata and Ahmedabad have real but narrower MYP supply

contentBlocks.heading: What to ask the MYP coordinator before hiring anyone in India
contentBlocks.body:
Ask the coordinator first. It costs nothing, it is faster than finding a tutor, and in a fair number of cases it ends the matter. At international schools in India the MYP coordinator can see criterion data across every subject your child takes, which is a view neither you nor any tutor will ever have.

Five questions are worth sending by email, in writing, so you still have the answers in three months. Is this criterion score below what the class typically produces on this unit, or in line with it? Has the same criterion been low in previous reporting cycles? Is there support already available inside school, such as a subject clinic, a learning support referral or a structured study period? What will the next unit demand that this one did not? And, if we did hire a private tutor, what would you want that tutor to work on?

That last question changes everything that follows. A coordinator who answers it has handed you a target, and a target is the difference between useful IB MYP tuition in India and a vague weekly hour that nobody can evaluate.

The calendar matters as much as the answers. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March. Reports arrive at the end of each reporting cycle, unit assessments and project deadlines cluster together, and the long summer and Diwali breaks are when a genuine gap can be closed without competing with school work. Starting home classes in the week a Community Project draft is due helps nobody.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this site, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. School names appear as context for families and nothing more.
items: Ask in writing, so the answers survive three months of term
Request comparison with the class, not just your child's raw score
Ask what in-school support exists before paying for anything outside
Ask the coordinator what a tutor should work on specifically
Long summer and Diwali breaks suit gap-closing better than a busy term

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a thirteen-year-old?
contentBlocks.body:
For an MYP student, home tuition usually wins on attention and honesty, and online wins on choice of tutor. A thirteen-year-old is harder to hold on a screen than a DP student and much easier to read in a room. If a suitable tutor is reachable near you, and the criterion is low because your child is not attempting the work rather than not understanding it, choose home tuition.

A home tutor sees what a camera does not: the phone lying face down on the table, the half-finished task pushed under a textbook, the notebook with no dates in it since August. For criteria that depend on process rather than recall, that visibility is the whole value.

Online earns its place when the gap is narrow and specialist, when the family lives in Kharghar, Yelahanka or Greater Noida and the drive destroys the slot, or when the better tutor simply lives in another city. Online MYP sessions work better short and frequent than long and weekly, with a parent within earshot for the first few weeks, because attention at this age is not yet self-managed.

Hybrid is where most MYP families end up, and it is not a compromise. One home session a week for the work that needs watching, one shorter online session for review and doubt-solving. In a heavy traffic week the home visit converts to online instead of being lost, and monsoon does the same thing to a Mumbai or Chennai evening.

The trade-off, plainly. Home tuition buys attention and accountability at the cost of travel time and a smaller local pool. Online buys the right tutor and reliable timing at the cost of everything the tutor cannot see. Hybrid keeps most of both and asks the family to hold two routines instead of one.
items: Choose home tuition when the problem is effort rather than understanding
Choose online when the gap is narrow and the specialist lives elsewhere
Hybrid keeps a distant tutor without losing every traffic-hit evening
Keep online MYP sessions shorter than you would for a DP student
A parent within earshot helps online at eleven to fourteen, not at seventeen

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check an MYP home tutor fits this particular criterion?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask them to explain the criterion you are worried about, in their own words, before they teach anything. An MYP home tutor who has genuinely taught the programme will describe what the band descriptors ask for and how four scores out of 8 become a 1 to 7. A tutor who has only taught CBSE or ICSE will talk about chapters, portions and marks. The difference shows inside two minutes.

IB Gram verifies profiles before they go live: identity, claimed qualifications and teaching experience, and the programmes and year groups a tutor says they can cover. A verified profile is a floor, not a verdict. Three checks stay with you.

Watch the trial session with the door open. You are not marking the tutor's subject knowledge. You are watching whether your child talks. An MYP student who answers in single words for forty minutes will not improve, however strong the teaching.

Ask what the first four sessions will cover, and expect an answer that names the criterion rather than the chapter. Then ask what they will do if the score has not moved by the next reporting cycle. A tutor who has thought about failure has thought seriously about the work.

Ask directly about the Personal Project and the Community Project. The right answer is that they will discuss, question and teach skills, and will not draft, edit or supply content. A tutor offering more than that is a risk to your child's record, not a shortcut around it.

For home classes, settle the practical things before the first visit: which room, who else is in the house, gate and visitor entry in your society, and what happens when a session is missed. These sound trivial until an evening is lost at the gate.
items: Ask the tutor to explain your child's weak criterion before any teaching
A verified profile is a floor; the trial session is the real test
Watch whether your child speaks, not whether the tutor sounds impressive
Expect a named criterion in the first four-session plan
Agree project boundaries out loud: discuss and question, never draft or edit
Settle room, gate entry and missed-session rules before the first home visit

contentBlocks.heading: Does my MYP child need tuition, or a closer look at the report?
contentBlocks.body:
Most of the time, a closer look. Here is the test that separates the two. A hard unit produces one low criterion, in one subject, in one reporting cycle, and the teacher's comment says something close to the class found this demanding. A genuine gap produces the same low criterion twice in a row, or the same letter low across several subjects, and the teacher's comment names a behaviour rather than a topic.

Four things look like a subject problem and are not. A student who is short of sleep because the week has no empty space left in it. A student who cannot find anything, whose notebooks are unordered and whose deadlines arrive as surprises. A student new to academic writing in English, where every subject reads as weak because the writing is weak. And a student who has quietly decided they are bad at the subject and stopped trying, so the belief is never tested. Not one of those four is fixed by an extra hour of the same subject, and three of them get worse when you add one.

There is a fifth case that genuinely is a subject gap. Something specific was missed, very often during a move between schools, cities or boards, and everything built on top of it wobbles. That responds quickly to one-to-one work, sometimes within a handful of sessions, and it is the clearest reason to hire.

So the useful question is not does my MYP child need tuition. It is this: what exactly would tuition fix, and how would we both know in six weeks? If you cannot answer both halves, you are not ready to hire anyone. Tuition for MYP students bought without an answer to those questions tends to quietly run for a year.
items: One low criterion, one subject, one cycle: usually a hard unit
The same criterion low twice: treat it as a real gap
Sleep, organisation, academic English and lost confidence all mimic subject weakness
A gap from a school or board move responds fastest to one-to-one work
If you cannot say what six weeks should change, do not hire yet

contentBlocks.heading: Over-tutoring at thirteen, and what it costs in DP1
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the MYP is slow to reach a report and quick to reach the work. Expect a change in how your child talks about the subject within three or four sessions, a change in the quality of submitted work within six to eight weeks, and a change in the criterion score only at the next reporting cycle. Judging IB MYP tuition in India by the grade alone means waiting an entire cycle to learn something the notebook would have told you in a fortnight.

Now the harder part, which nobody selling tuition wants to write down. A thirteen-year-old with a tutor for every subject has no unstructured time left, and unstructured time is where the MYP actually does its work. The programme asks students to investigate, plan their own approach and reflect on it afterwards. A student whose every difficulty is dissolved by an adult within the hour never practises the one skill the Diploma Programme demands relentlessly two years later.

The bill arrives in DP1. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours each and the rest at Standard Level at 150, internal assessments, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) on top. A student who learned at thirteen that somebody else does the starting cannot carry that. It shows up as a capable sixteen-year-old sitting frozen in front of an open-ended task.

Honest limits, then. No tutor can guarantee a grade. Some criteria move slowly because they depend on maturity rather than instruction. A student who does not want a tutor will waste the tutor's time and yours. Two subjects at a time is a sensible ceiling for an MYP student, and one is very often better.
items: Talk changes in weeks, work changes in months, the score changes at the cycle
Protect unstructured time: the MYP is assessed on independent thinking
Two tutored subjects is a ceiling at this age, one is often enough
A student who does not want tuition will not benefit from it
Plan an exit from the start, not an open-ended weekly commitment

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB MYP tuition in India, or deciding to wait a term
contentBlocks.body:
Prepare three things before the first session and it will be worth twice as much. The last two reports with all four criterion scores visible rather than only the grades. The most recent piece of marked work in the subject, with the teacher's annotations still on it. And the coordinator's written reply, if you sent that email.

The first session should not be a lesson. A good MYP home tutor spends it working out what the student can already do: reading the marked work, asking the student to explain their own answer aloud, and finding the exact point where the thinking stops. By the end there should be a named target, said in the student's hearing, and an agreed way of checking it that does not depend on the next report card.

Fix the review date at the start rather than the end. Six weeks, with the report and the notebook side by side on the table. If nothing has shifted and the tutor cannot explain why, change the tutor or stop altogether. Neither is a disaster; drifting for a year is.

Keep the possibility of stopping open in front of your child. An MYP student who knows that home tuition ends when the gap closes behaves differently from one who assumes it is now permanent. Say it out loud in the first week and mean it.

If you decide to wait, that is a decision rather than a failure to act. Write down the criterion you are watching, tell the subject teacher you are watching it, and look again at the next reporting cycle. Plenty of families who ask about IB MYP tuition in India in October find in January that the unit changed and there was never a gap.
items: Bring the last two reports, one marked script and the coordinator's reply
Expect diagnosis in the first session, not a lesson from page one
Set the six-week review date before the first session happens
Tell your child openly that tuition ends when the gap closes
Waiting a term is a decision: write down what you are watching

faqs.question: Does my MYP child need tuition at all?
faqs.answer: Probably not yet, unless the same criterion has been low across two reporting cycles or across several subjects. One weak score in one cycle is far more often a hard unit than a gap. Read the four criterion scores, compare them across the eight subject groups, and ask the subject teacher how the class as a whole handled that unit. If the answer is that most of the class struggled, wait for the next unit and watch.

faqs.question: What does a criterion score of 4 out of 8 actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means the work sat in the middle band of that criterion's descriptor for that task, and nothing more. It is not a percentage and it does not convert to one. The four criterion scores add to a total out of 32, and the school applies IB grade boundaries to produce the 1 to 7 grade. Read the descriptor your school printed for that band, then read the band above it to see what the next level of work requires.

faqs.question: How do I tell a hard unit from a genuine gap?
faqs.answer: Look for repetition and for spread. A hard unit shows up once, in one subject, in one reporting cycle, usually with a teacher comment about the demands of the task. A genuine gap shows up twice in the same criterion, or as the same letter dropping in three different subjects at the same time. Repetition tells you the student cannot do something; a single dip usually tells you the task was hard for everybody in the room.

faqs.question: What should I ask the MYP coordinator before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Ask five things in writing. Whether the score is below or in line with what the class produced on that unit. Whether the same criterion was low in earlier cycles. What support already exists inside school. What the next unit will demand. And what the coordinator would want a private tutor to work on. That last answer gives you a target, and a tutor working towards a named target can be evaluated in six weeks rather than six months.

faqs.question: Which MYP year is the right time to start?
faqs.answer: MYP 4 and MYP 5 are where tuition most often justifies itself, because the work deepens and the Diploma Programme is close. Earlier help is justified in three situations: a recent move into the MYP from a CBSE or ICSE school, an academic language gap affecting every subject, or a collapse in confidence severe enough that the student has stopped attempting work. Outside those, MYP 1 to MYP 3 problems usually respond to habits rather than paid sessions.

faqs.question: Can an MYP home tutor come on weekday evenings in Bengaluru or Pune?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, subject to tutor availability and to the direction of travel. In Bengaluru, slots around Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are easier to hold than Yelahanka or Electronic City in the evening peak. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Aundh are straightforward, while Hinjewadi and Wakad depend on the return journey. Tell us your two best evenings and your locality, and we will shortlist accordingly.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during an MYP home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the house, and no, not in the room after the first session or two. A child of eleven to fourteen behaves differently with a parent sitting alongside, and the tutor loses the chance to see how the student works unaided. Stay within earshot, keep the door open, and read the notebook afterwards rather than supervising during. If the student needs you present to stay on task, that itself is useful diagnostic information.

faqs.question: How much does IB MYP tuition in India cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the subject, the MYP year, the tutor's experience and whether sessions run at your home, online or in a hybrid pattern. Home visits carry travel time and are priced accordingly, online is usually lower for the same tutor, and a batch is lower per hour than either. Ask for the fee structure in writing before the trial, including what happens with cancellations, and compare the total termly commitment rather than the hourly figure.

faqs.question: My child already has several classes. Should we add one more?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. Two tutored subjects at a time is a sensible ceiling for an MYP student, and one is often better. The programme is assessed on investigation, planning and reflection, and every one of those needs unscheduled time to develop. If the week is already full, the useful move is to remove something rather than add. Drop the weakest-value commitment first and see what the next reporting cycle shows.

faqs.question: We live in Kolkata and cannot find an MYP tutor nearby. What now?

faqs.question: How long before we know whether MYP tuition classes are working?
faqs.answer: Three to four sessions for a change in how your child talks about the subject, six to eight weeks for a visible change in submitted work, and a full reporting cycle before the criterion score moves. mainEntity.name: Does my MYP child need tuition at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: Probably not yet, unless the same criterion has been low across two reporting cycles or across several subjects. One weak score in one cycle is far more often a hard unit than a gap. Read the four criterion scores, compare them across the eight subject groups, and ask the subject teacher how the class as a whole handled that unit. If the answer is that most of the class struggled, wait for the next unit and watch.

mainEntity.name: What does a criterion score of 4 out of 8 actually mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: It means the work sat in the middle band of that criterion's descriptor for that task, and nothing more. It is not a percentage and it does not convert to one. The four criterion scores add to a total out of 32, and the school applies IB grade boundaries to produce the 1 to 7 grade. Read the descriptor your school printed for that band, then read the band above it to see what the next level of work requires.

mainEntity.name: How do I tell a hard unit from a genuine gap?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for repetition and for spread. A hard unit shows up once, in one subject, in one reporting cycle, usually with a teacher comment about the demands of the task. A genuine gap shows up twice in the same criterion, or as the same letter dropping in three different subjects at the same time. Repetition tells you the student cannot do something; a single dip usually tells you the task was hard for everybody in the room.

mainEntity.name: What should I ask the MYP coordinator before hiring anyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask five things in writing. Whether the score is below or in line with what the class produced on that unit. Whether the same criterion was low in earlier cycles. What support already exists inside school. What the next unit will demand. And what the coordinator would want a private tutor to work on. That last answer gives you a target, and a tutor working towards a named target can be evaluated in six weeks rather than six months.

mainEntity.name: Which MYP year is the right time to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: MYP 4 and MYP 5 are where tuition most often justifies itself, because the work deepens and the Diploma Programme is close. Earlier help is justified in three situations: a recent move into the MYP from a CBSE or ICSE school, an academic language gap affecting every subject, or a collapse in confidence severe enough that the student has stopped attempting work. Outside those, MYP 1 to MYP 3 problems usually respond to habits rather than paid sessions.

mainEntity.name: Can an MYP home tutor come on weekday evenings in Bengaluru or Pune?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually yes, subject to tutor availability and to the direction of travel. In Bengaluru, slots around Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are easier to hold than Yelahanka or Electronic City in the evening peak. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Aundh are straightforward, while Hinjewadi and Wakad depend on the return journey. Tell us your two best evenings and your locality, and we will shortlist accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent be at home during an MYP home tuition session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in the house, and no, not in the room after the first session or two. A child of eleven to fourteen behaves differently with a parent sitting alongside, and the tutor loses the chance to see how the student works unaided. Stay within earshot, keep the door open, and read the notebook afterwards rather than supervising during. If the student needs you present to stay on task, that itself is useful diagnostic information.

mainEntity.name: How much does IB MYP tuition in India cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees depend on the subject, the MYP year, the tutor's experience and whether sessions run at your home, online or in a hybrid pattern. Home visits carry travel time and are priced accordingly, online is usually lower for the same tutor, and a batch is lower per hour than either. Ask for the fee structure in writing before the trial, including what happens with cancellations, and compare the total termly commitment rather than the hourly figure.

mainEntity.name: My child already has several classes. Should we add one more?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost certainly not. Two tutored subjects at a time is a sensible ceiling for an MYP student, and one is often better. The programme is assessed on investigation, planning and reflection, and every one of those needs unscheduled time to develop. If the week is already full, the useful move is to remove something rather than add. Drop the weakest-value commitment first and see what the next reporting cycle shows.
