h1: IB PYP Tutors in India: What a Tutor Does With No Exams
heroTitle: What PYP Tutoring Means in India
heroSubtitle: The Primary Years Programme sets no external examinations and publishes no grades, so a parent shopping for a tutor has nothing to point at. This page explains what a PYP home tutor can honestly work on, what belongs to the school, and the cases where hiring nobody is the better decision.
introSummary: IB PYP tutors in India work with children aged three to twelve in a programme that has no external examinations and no published grades, so a good home tutor builds reading, number sense, curiosity and communication rather than drilling anyone for a paper. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) organises learning around six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, with the ten attributes of the International Baccalaureate (IB) learner profile running through all of it, and it ends with the PYP exhibition in the final year. That structure changes what you should ask for. A parent who wants a weekly home tuition slot for a seven-year-old needs a tutor who can sit beside the child, follow the current unit of inquiry, and stop when the child has had enough. Many families, honestly, need no tutor at all.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a PYP child in India when there is nothing to revise?
contentBlocks.body:
It starts from the child rather than the syllabus, because the Primary Years Programme hands you no syllabus to work from. IB Gram asks the age and year group, which unit of inquiry the class is currently on, what exactly you have noticed at home, your locality and society gate arrangements, and the one hour in the week that is genuinely free. It then shortlists tutors whose verified profiles match those needs.

That first conversation is deliberately slow, and it should be. A parent who says a child is weak in maths usually means one of four quite different things. The child cannot yet hold number bonds. Or the child cannot read the word problem. Or the child freezes when asked to explain a method out loud. Or the child is simply slower than a class that moves fast, which is not a problem at all. Those four need different people and different work. A tutor who is excellent with a nine-year-old stuck on place value can be the wrong choice for a five-year-old still settling into English as the language of instruction.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything. Ask for the trial at the time you actually want the weekly slot rather than at a convenient Sunday morning, because a tired child at seven in the evening is the real test of whether a tutor can hold a young learner. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability in your part of the city. If the fit is wrong after the trial, ask for a different match. With a small child that is far better done in week one than in week six.

One more signal worth watching during matching. The tutor should want to know what the school is already doing before proposing anything at all. If the first thing offered is a worksheet pack, the tutor has a product rather than a plan.
items: 1. Send the child's age, year group and the current unit of inquiry
2. Describe what you have noticed at home in plain words, not labels
3. Confirm locality, society gate rules and the weekday slot you can hold
4. Take a trial session at the real time, with the child rested
5. Review after six to eight weeks and decide whether to continue or stop

contentBlocks.heading: Six transdisciplinary themes, ten learner profile attributes, one exhibition
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme runs from age three to age twelve, and its structure is short enough to state in a paragraph. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet. The IB spells that fifth theme with a z, and schools keep the spelling exactly as written.

Each theme means something plain. Who we are covers identity, health, relationships and what it means to belong to a family or a class. Where we are in place and time covers homes, journeys, history and how a place changes. How we express ourselves covers stories, art, music and the many ways a child gets an idea across. How the world works covers the physical and natural world and what people do with what they find in it. How we organize ourselves covers the systems people build, from a classroom duty rota to a neighbourhood market. Sharing the planet covers finite resources, other living things and fairness between people who want the same things.

Those themes are taught through units of inquiry rather than chapters. A unit runs for several weeks, pulls in reading, writing, number work, science and social studies as the inquiry needs them, and finishes with children showing what they now understand. Running through all of it are the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, which the school will use as everyday vocabulary and which a parent can quietly use as a checklist at home. In the final year of the programme, students complete the PYP exhibition, an extended piece of inquiry the class works towards over an extended period.

And here is the part that unsettles Indian parents most. There are no external examinations in the PYP and no published PYP grades. Nothing is ranked, nothing arrives as a percentage. If you have come from a CBSE or ICSE primary where a unit test lands every few weeks, the quiet feels like information being withheld. It is not. It is the design. Marks that look familiar arrive later, in the Middle Years Programme (MYP), where every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored zero to eight, with the criterion total out of thirty-two converted through grade boundaries into a final grade on a one to seven scale.
items: Six themes, taught through units of inquiry rather than textbook chapters
Ten learner profile attributes, used by the school as shared everyday language
The PYP exhibition comes in the final year of the programme
No external examinations and no published PYP grades at any stage
Criterion marking, A to D and zero to eight, begins later in the MYP

contentBlocks.heading: What does a PYP tutor actually teach when there are no exams?
contentBlocks.body:
Four things, mostly: reading, number sense, curiosity and communication. A tutor doing this job properly is not covering a syllabus and not drilling past papers, because neither exists at this stage. The work is to make a child fluent enough in reading and number that the class inquiry stops being blocked by mechanics. IB PYP tutors in India are asked most often for English and mathematics, and both requests usually turn out to be about fluency rather than content.

Reading comes first because everything else sits on it. A tutor should separate decoding from comprehension, because they fail differently. A child who stumbles over unfamiliar words needs short, daily reading aloud from a book slightly easier than the one that is frustrating him. A child who reads a page fluently and then cannot say what happened needs to be stopped mid-page and asked what she thinks is coming next. Vocabulary from the current unit belongs in these sessions: if the class is working inside Sharing the planet, the words about water, waste and habitat should be read, used and argued about, not written out ten times.

Number sense is the second pillar, and it is not arithmetic speed. A child who can execute long multiplication but cannot say whether the answer is roughly sensible has procedures without understanding. Good early work uses counters, money, a measuring jug and a kitchen scale. Part-whole relationships, number bonds, place value and estimation before any algorithm. A tutor who reaches for a speed drill in the first fortnight has misread the programme entirely.

Curiosity and communication are the two that parents undervalue and the PYP takes seriously. Curiosity is trainable: a tutor can teach a child to turn a vague wondering into a question that can actually be investigated, which is the exact skill the exhibition will later demand. Communication means explaining a method out loud, presenting a finding to an adult who asks follow-up questions, and writing three sentences that say what the child meant rather than what sounded impressive. For a child who has moved into an IB school from another board or another country, the language of instruction is its own piece of work and should be named as such.
items: Decoding and comprehension treated as separate problems with separate fixes
Number bonds, place value and estimation before any written algorithm
Vocabulary drawn from the current unit of inquiry, used rather than copied
Turning a vague wondering into a question a child can investigate
Explaining a method aloud, then writing what was actually meant
Language of instruction support for a child new to an IB school

contentBlocks.heading: IB PYP tutors in India: where home lessons for a young child are practical
contentBlocks.body:
Supply follows the schools, and the schools cluster. In Delhi NCR that means South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri, and then the newer belts: Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, Noida including Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. A family looking for an IB PYP tutor in Delhi will usually find someone within a sensible radius. A family in Greater Noida or Ghaziabad may find the nearest primary-experienced tutor sits on the far side of an evening commute, and for a forty-five minute lesson with a seven-year-old that is a poor trade for everyone, the tutor included.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the demand sits in Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill, with Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar behind them. An IB PYP tutor in Mumbai who lives in Powai will hold a Powai slot week after week and will quietly start cancelling a Worli one. Pune behaves similarly across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad, except that an IB PYP tutor in Pune crossing towards Hinjewadi on a weekday evening is fighting traffic that can stretch a short trip badly. Early-evening slots for small children are the first casualty.

The southern metros are the deepest market. In Bengaluru, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each have their own supply, and an IB PYP tutor in Bangalore will usually define a radius of a few kilometres rather than a city. Hyderabad concentrates around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Kokapet and Secunderabad, so an IB PYP tutor in Hyderabad can often reach two or three families in one evening. In Chennai, Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Alwarpet and Velachery are comfortable for a home visit, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) and Perungudi stretch a tutor's evening; an IB PYP tutor in Chennai on the OMR corridor will usually want two sessions in the same building to make the trip work.

Beyond the six metros the answer changes shape. In Gujarat, an IB PYP tutor in Ahmedabad will cover Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway stretch, with Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot thinner. In Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat have real options, so an IB PYP tutor in Kolkata is findable, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna usually mean an online or hybrid arrangement. The same holds across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, where Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun have some supply and Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur very little; across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, where Kochi, Coimbatore, Thiruvananthapuram, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai vary street by street; and across central and western India, where Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik and Goa are workable and Raipur, Jabalpur and Aurangabad rarely are. In every one of those places, a searching parent typing PYP tutor near me should widen to online before accepting a tutor with no experience of young children.
items: Delhi NCR: Vasant Kunj and Golf Course Road hold slots better than Ghaziabad
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: a Powai tutor holds Powai; Thane and Kharghar need their own
Bengaluru and Hyderabad: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Gachibowli and Kondapur have real depth
Chennai: Adyar and Besant Nagar are easy; the OMR corridor needs two sessions
Gujarat and the east: Bodakdev and Salt Lake yes, Rajkot and Ranchi usually online
Smaller cities: Dehradun, Nashik and Visakhapatnam are where hybrid weeks earn their keep

contentBlocks.heading: The PYP school year in India: reports without grades, and exhibition season
contentBlocks.body:
Families at international schools in India deal with a calendar that looks nothing like the CBSE or ICSE year their cousins follow, and with reporting that refuses to give them a rank. Parents often arrive at a tutoring conversation with a school name they heard in a building WhatsApp group: Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School, The International School Bangalore. Nothing is said here about what any of those schools teaches or where it sits. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

What matters for tutoring is the rhythm, and the rhythm is set by your own school, so confirm dates with the class teacher rather than with a neighbour. Term breaks, the Diwali gap, a winter holiday and a long summer all interrupt a young child's habits more than they interrupt a teenager's. A six-year-old who has read nothing for five weeks comes back genuinely rusty. This is the single strongest argument for light, short tuition across a break rather than an intensive burst at the end of it.

Reports at this stage describe what a child can do and what the class has inquired into. They do not rank. An Indian parent used to a marks column will read three paragraphs of careful description and feel that nothing was said. Read it again with a pencil. Underline every verb: explains, attempts, listens, revises, collaborates. Those verbs are the report. If two of them worry you, that is the sentence to take to the class teacher, and then to the PYP coordinator if the teacher's answer does not satisfy you.

Exhibition season in the final year of the programme is when tutoring requests spike, and it is the moment to be most careful. The exhibition is the child's work and the class's work. A tutor may help a child sharpen a research question, find a readable source, practise speaking aloud, and manage time across weeks. A tutor may not write, script, design or rehearse the child into someone else's project. Ask your school what outside support it considers acceptable, and follow that answer rather than this page.
items: Confirm your own school's term dates before planning any weekly slot
Long breaks cost a young child habits, not syllabus coverage
Read the written report by underlining its verbs, then ask about two
The class teacher comes first; the PYP coordinator comes next
Exhibition support means questions and time management, never writing the work

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid for a child under twelve?
contentBlocks.body:
Home, in most cases at this age. A young child learns from a person in the room who can point at the page, move a counter, notice a yawn and change the activity before attention collapses. Online lessons ask the child to supply the attention that a tutor's physical presence would otherwise supply, and at primary age that is a great deal to ask. Home classes also let a tutor see the actual conditions: the table, the noise, the television, the older sibling doing homework three feet away.

Online earns its place in specific situations rather than as a default. A family in Bhubaneswar, Dehradun or Nashik may have no primary-experienced tutor within reach at all, and a competent online teacher beats a nearby generalist who has never taught a seven-year-old. Older PYP children, in the last year or two of the programme, cope with a screen far better than a five-year-old does. Sessions should be short, an adult should be within earshot, and the camera should spend as much time pointed at the child's page as at the child's face. Set against that, a child already on screens for parts of the school day does not need more of them.

Hybrid is the compromise most Indian metro families actually end up with, and it is a reasonable one. One home session a week where the real teaching happens, plus a short online check-in mid-week to keep reading or number work ticking. In Gurugram, Thane or on the OMR stretch in Chennai, a hybrid week is often the only way to keep a tutor who is genuinely good with small children but does not live ten minutes away. It also survives monsoon weeks, exam-season traffic and the evening a society gate decides visitors need fresh approval.

Stated plainly, so you can weigh it in one line: a home tutor gives a primary child the most attention and the least friction and costs the most travel time; an online tutor gives you reach and reliability and costs the child's attention; a hybrid week buys back some of each and needs an adult at home for the online half to work at all.
items: Home classes suit the youngest children and reveal the real study conditions
Online suits older PYP children, short sessions and cities with no local supply
Hybrid keeps a good tutor who lives too far for a weekday visit
An adult within earshot is not optional for an online primary lesson
Point the camera at the page, not only at the child's face

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a PYP tutor when no grade will ever prove them right
contentBlocks.body:
With no examination result waiting at the end, verification has to happen before the tutoring rather than after it. IB Gram checks identity and the claims a tutor makes on a profile about the programmes and age groups they have taught, and a profile is verified before a family sees it. What no platform can see is how a particular adult behaves with your particular child in your drawing room on a Wednesday evening. That part is yours.

The most useful check is the cheapest. During the trial, watch whether the tutor asks about the current unit of inquiry, asks what the child likes reading, and speaks to the child rather than about the child. A tutor who conducts the whole trial facing the parent has told you something. So has one who corrects every error the moment it appears; a young child needs a few seconds of silence to catch a mistake herself, and a tutor who cannot tolerate that silence will teach dependence instead of thinking.

Experience needs to be read carefully too. A great deal of advertised IB experience means Diploma Programme teaching, which is a different job from sitting with an eight-year-old. Ask directly which age groups the tutor has taught and for how long, ask what a session with a six-year-old looks like minute by minute, and ask for a reference from a family with a child of similar age. Politeness costs nothing and these are fair questions.

Safeguarding is the part parents skip because it feels awkward. Do not skip it. Home sessions belong in a common room with the door open, not in a bedroom. An adult should be in the house. Messages and photographs go to the parent's phone, never to the child's. Visitor entry through the society gate should be logged in the normal way rather than waved through as a family friend. If anything about a tutor's manner with your child makes you uneasy, you do not owe an explanation. Ask for a different match.
items: Watch whether the tutor addresses the child or performs for the parent
Ask which age groups, specifically; IB experience often means Diploma teaching
Request a reference from a family with a child of similar age
Common room, door open, an adult in the house, every session
Messages and photographs to the parent's phone, not the child's

contentBlocks.heading: Why most PYP children in India need no tutor at all
contentBlocks.body:
Most children in the Primary Years Programme do not need a paid tutor, and hiring one because two neighbours have is the commonest mistake families make at this stage. The programme is built to move with the child. There is no external examination bearing down, no published grade to defend, and no syllabus race to fall behind in. A child who is slower at reading in Class 2 than the loudest child in the building is very often just a child who will read fluently in Class 3.

Before you hire anyone, three conversations and three habits are worth more than a term of paid sessions. Ask the class teacher what she sees, in specifics, and what she would like you to do at home. If that answer is thin, ask the PYP coordinator. Ask whether the school already runs support inside the school day, because many do and many parents never find out. Then, at home: read aloud together for twenty unhurried minutes, cook and shop with the child doing the weighing and the change, and leave enough unscheduled time that the child gets bored. Boredom is where curiosity is manufactured, and curiosity is half of what this programme is trying to build.

There are real exceptions, and they are specific rather than vague. A child who has moved mid-year from another board or another country and is meeting English as the language of instruction for the first time. A child returning after a long illness or absence. A child whose difficulty has already been identified by a qualified professional, where a tutor works alongside that plan and is never a substitute for it. A child in the final year whose reading is weak enough that exhibition work is genuinely out of reach. Those four are worth paying for.

Watch the total load as carefully as the tutoring itself. School, a tutor twice a week, a sport, a music class and a coding club leave a nine-year-old with no hour that belongs to her. A tutor who never once suggests reducing hours is not looking after your child's interest, and IB PYP tutors in India who work honestly with this age group will tell you to stop well before you were planning to.
items: Ask the class teacher for specifics before you ask anyone for a quote
Find out what support the school already runs inside the school day
Twenty unhurried minutes of reading aloud beats an hour of worksheets
Hire for a named reason: a move, an absence, a diagnosis, the exhibition
Count the whole week's commitments, not just the tuition hours

contentBlocks.heading: Progress without marks: what should change in a term of PYP tuition
contentBlocks.body:
No number is coming, so agree with the tutor in the first week on what you will look at instead. Good markers are ordinary and observable. The child picks up a book without being told. A page is read without stalling on three words a line. The child explains how an answer was reached, unprompted, including the wrong turns. A question about the current unit comes up at dinner. Three written sentences say what the child actually meant. Six to eight weeks is a fair first window for IB PYP tutors in India to show something on that list, and a fair point at which to stop if nothing has moved.

Be honest with yourself about what tutoring cannot do here. No tutor can guarantee anything at this age, and any promise about outcomes for a seven-year-old should be treated with real scepticism. A tutor cannot change what a school report says, cannot speed up the maturity that makes some of this click, and cannot substitute for sleep. Progress at primary age is lumpy rather than linear: a fortnight where nothing appears to happen, then a week where the child suddenly reads a chapter book. Judging a tutor on a flat fortnight is unfair to both of them.

The risk that deserves more attention than it gets is dependence. A child who will not begin homework until the tutor arrives has learned something, and it is not mathematics. A good tutor plans reduction from the start: fewer prompts inside the session, then shorter sessions, then a fortnightly rhythm, then an ending. Ask in the first month what the exit looks like. A tutor who has no answer is planning to be there indefinitely.

Set a review conversation every few weeks and keep it short. Three questions do the job. What has changed that you can point to. What is still stuck and why. What should we do differently for the next four weeks. Write the answers down, because in eight weeks you will not remember what was said in week two, and the written trail is the only record this programme will ever give you.
items: Agree observable markers in week one, before any money changes hands
Six to eight weeks is a fair first window, then a real decision
Expect lumpy progress: flat fortnights followed by sudden jumps
Ask what the exit plan looks like within the first month
Keep a short written record of every review conversation

contentBlocks.heading: Starting PYP home tuition in India: a numbered plan for one term
contentBlocks.body:
Four things make the first conversation useful: the most recent school report, the title of the unit of inquiry the class is working on now, a short written list of what you have actually noticed at home, and the weekday slot your household can genuinely protect. Add a note about the room the lessons will use and who will be at home during them. Send that and a matching conversation takes minutes instead of a week.

A sensible first term of home tuition for a PYP child looks like this:

1. Weeks one and two: the tutor observes and diagnoses, reads with the child, watches how number work is done, and proposes two or three specific goals in writing.
2. Weeks three to five: short, focused sessions on those goals only, with a five-minute task set between sessions that a parent supervises but does not teach.
3. Weeks six to eight: the first review conversation, evidence of what has changed, and an honest decision about continuing, changing tutor, or stopping.
4. Weeks nine to twelve: consolidation, a deliberate reduction in prompting inside the session, and a plan for the school break that is light rather than intensive.

The first session itself should be gentle and short. The tutor meets the child, finds out what the child is interested in, reads something together, does a little number work with objects rather than a worksheet, and ends before the child is tired. No assessment, no diagnostic test, no homework pack. A parent watching will sometimes feel that too little happened. That is usually the sign of someone who knows this age group.

After that, the arrangement is yours to steer. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Ask to move to a hybrid week if travel is killing the slot. Ask to reduce from two home sessions to one when the child is coping, which is a request a good tutor will welcome rather than resist.
items: Send the report, the current unit title, your notes and the slot
Weeks one and two are for diagnosis and two or three written goals
Between-session tasks stay at five minutes and stay parent-supervised
The first session ends before the child is tired, deliberately
Reduce hours as soon as the child copes, not when the term ends

faqs.question: What does a PYP tutor actually do if there are no examinations?
faqs.answer: A PYP tutor builds the foundations the inquiry rests on: reading fluency and comprehension, number sense, the habit of asking a question that can be investigated, and the ability to explain thinking out loud. Because the Primary Years Programme has no external examinations and no published grades, there is no paper to prepare for and no drill that makes sense. IB PYP tutors in India who insist on tests and worksheet packs at this stage have simply imported a coaching model from a different system.

faqs.question: Does my child even need a tutor in the PYP?
faqs.answer: Probably not. Most primary children do not need paid tutoring, and the usual triggers are parental anxiety and comparison with a neighbour rather than anything the school has said. Speak to the class teacher first and ask for specifics, then the PYP coordinator if the answer is vague. Genuine reasons to hire include a mid-year move into a new language of instruction, a long absence, a difficulty already identified by a qualified professional, or weak reading in the exhibition year.

faqs.question: How long should a home tuition session be for a PYP child?
faqs.answer: Shorter than you expect, and shorter than most tutors will offer. For the youngest children, work in short bursts with movement between them, and finish before attention collapses rather than after. Older children in the last years of the programme can hold a longer stretch, though still less than a teenager. A good home tutor will end a session early when the child is spent and say so honestly, rather than filling the booked hour with colouring and calling it teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the PYP exhibition?
faqs.answer: Within limits, yes. A tutor can help a child turn a broad interest into a researchable question, find sources the child can actually read, practise presenting to someone who asks follow-up questions, and plan the work across the available weeks. A tutor must not write, script, design or produce any part of it, because the exhibition is the child's own work. Ask your school directly what outside support it considers acceptable, and treat that answer as the rule.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during the lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, an adult should be in the house for every home session with a primary-age child, and that is a safeguarding baseline rather than a preference. Sessions belong in a common room with the door open. Being in the house does not mean sitting in the room correcting the child, which undermines the tutor and makes children perform rather than think. Stay within earshot, keep out of the teaching, and ask your questions after the tutor has packed up.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor in Bengaluru or Hyderabad come for one short early-evening slot?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the travel makes sense. Tutors working in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Gachibowli or Kondapur frequently teach two or three families in the same evening, so a short session fits neatly between others. A single short slot across the city is harder, and a tutor who accepts one may start cancelling within a month. If you are in Yelahanka or Secunderabad and the good tutors are elsewhere, a hybrid week usually holds better than a long commute.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring realistic for a seven-year-old?
faqs.answer: It is possible but rarely the first choice at that age. A seven-year-old has to supply the concentration that a tutor's physical presence would otherwise supply, and most cannot sustain it for long. If online is the only option because no experienced primary tutor lives nearby, keep sessions short, have an adult within earshot throughout, and make sure the camera spends time on the child's page. Children in the last years of the programme manage a screen considerably better.

faqs.question: What are the six transdisciplinary themes, and do I need to know them?
faqs.answer: They are Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet, and learning is organised around them through units of inquiry. You do not need to master them, but knowing which one your child's class is currently working on is the single most useful thing you can tell a tutor. It turns generic reading practice into reading that supports what the child is doing this month.

faqs.question: We are moving from CBSE into an IB school in Pune. What should tutoring focus on?
faqs.answer: On language of instruction and on the shift from being told to being asked. A child arriving in Koregaon Park or Baner from a CBSE primary usually copes with the number work and struggles with open-ended questions, group discussion and writing in their own words. Focus the first term there rather than on content. Expect a settling period of a few months, keep the tuition light, and review with the class teacher before extending it into a second term.

faqs.question: How are fees worked out for IB PYP tuition, and what drives them up?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on session length, the tutor's experience with primary-age children, how far they travel, the city, and how many sessions a week you book. Home visits carry travel time, so they cost more than the same tutor teaching online. A PYP child needs fewer hours than a Diploma student, so a sensible arrangement here should be lighter than what families budget for older siblings. Ask for the rate, the session length and the cancellation terms in writing before the trial.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Say so early and ask for a different match. With young children, a mismatch of manner matters more than a mismatch of subject knowledge, and it shows up within two or three sessions: the child goes quiet, invents reasons to leave the table, or the tutor talks over her. That is information, not failure. Explain what you observed, ask for someone with a different style, and start the six to eight week window again with the new person.

h1: IB PYP Home Tutors in India for Short, Focused Sessions
heroTitle: Short PYP Sessions at Home Across India
heroSubtitle: A tutor for a six or nine year old is not a smaller version of a Diploma tutor. The work is thirty to forty-five minutes long, it moves, it happens at your dining table, and it ends before the child is tired. This page is about how those sessions are built.
introSummary: IB PYP home tutors in India work in short blocks, because a primary-age child cannot hold a long one, and a good home tutor designs the session around that limit rather than fighting it. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, so nothing here is about drilling for a paper. What a session has to do instead is hold attention, keep the child physically comfortable, and end with something finished. That means a cleared dining or kitchen table, a timer the child can see, two or three changes of activity inside forty-five minutes, and a parent close enough to hear but not seated at the child's elbow. The rest of this page sets out how that is built, city by city.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you brief IB PYP home tutors in India about a young child?
contentBlocks.body:
Tell them the child's age in years and months, the time the child reaches home from school, and what the child is like after six in the evening. Those three facts shape a primary session more than any subject request does. A brief that says only that the child needs help with maths gives a tutor nothing at all to plan around.

When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks about the programme, the school calendar, your location and the schedule you want. For a PYP child, add the domestic detail that actually decides whether a session works. Whether there is a younger sibling at home on weekday evenings. Whether the child still naps on some days. Whether school work is already finished before the tutor arrives, or the tutor is expected to sit through it. Where in the flat the child normally works, and whether that place is free at the hour you are asking for. A tutor who knows that dinner is at half past seven will plan a forty-minute session that closes at quarter past, rather than one that runs into a hungry child.

IB Gram then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience sits with primary-age learners rather than with Diploma students. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, subject to tutor availability. Use the trial to watch what no profile can show you. Does the tutor come down to the child's eye level. Does the tutor speak to the child, or over the child's head to you. Does the tutor notice the exact moment attention goes, and change the task instead of repeating the instruction more loudly. Parents looking for IB PYP home tutors in India often judge a trial on how much the child learned in an hour. At this age, the better test is whether the child was willing to sit down again the next week.

And if the fit is wrong, ask for a different match early. With a young child, three uncomfortable sessions cost far more than a change of tutor does.
items: 1. Send the child's age in years and months, not only the class.
2. Say when school ends, when dinner happens and when bedtime is.
3. Name your locality and the society gate rules a visitor must follow.
4. Describe where the child works: dining table, floor mat or bedroom desk.
5. Book a trial, then watch the first ten minutes rather than the last.

contentBlocks.heading: Six transdisciplinary themes, and what forty-five minutes can honestly hold
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from age 3 to age 12. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet. Children meet these as units of inquiry, alongside the ten attributes of the IB learner profile. In the final year of the programme, students complete the PYP exhibition. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades.

A unit of inquiry runs in class for weeks. One home session cannot carry a unit, and a tutor who tries to re-teach the whole thing will fill the table with paper and lose the child by the twentieth minute. What fits in forty-five minutes is one strand. If the class is working under How the world works and the child is stuck on writing down what they observed, the session is about writing one clear observation sentence, twice, and reading it back. The theme stays in the background as context. The skill underneath is the work.

Age changes the shape more than the theme does. With a child of four or five, a session is closer to twenty-five minutes and is mostly spoken, physical and playful, with a pencil in hand only briefly. At six to eight, thirty to forty-five minutes works if it is cut into pieces. From nine upward, a child can hold a longer middle section and begin to plan their own work, which is what the exhibition year eventually asks of them.

The learner profile is more useful in a home session than parents expect. A tutor who says, out loud, that the child was a risk-taker for trying a hard word, or reflective for spotting their own error, is using the school's own vocabulary. The child hears the same words at school the next morning. That is worth more than a sticker.
items: Six transdisciplinary themes taught through units of inquiry, not through separate subject periods
Ten learner profile attributes used as plain session language, not as decoration
The PYP exhibition falls in the final year of the programme
No external examinations and no published PYP grades to prepare for
One strand of a unit per session, never the whole unit at once

contentBlocks.heading: Which parts of a unit of inquiry survive a short session at the table?
contentBlocks.body:
Three things survive: reading aloud with someone listening properly, number sense handled with objects the child can move, and the child's own inquiry question turned into a sentence they can say. Everything else the school owns and teaches better than a visiting tutor can. A home tutor who stays inside those three is useful. One who tries to run a parallel syllabus is not, because the PYP has no syllabus to run in parallel.

A worked example. A child in Class 3 decodes fluently and sounds like a strong reader, but cannot tell you what happened in the page she just read. A useful session does not begin with a comprehension worksheet. The tutor reads two paragraphs with her, closes the book, and asks her to retell it while holding up a finger for each event. She gets three. They reopen the book, find the two she missed, and she retells it again standing up, walking the sequence across the room. Then she writes one sentence. The whole sequence is about twelve minutes and it moves twice.

That movement is the point, and it is not a break bolted on to the end. Play and physical work belong inside the structure. Number bonds sorted into two hoops on the floor. A number line taped along the corridor that the child jumps along while counting in threes. Coins and bottle caps for place value instead of a column of digits. Building the shape before drawing it. A child who has been sitting in a classroom since morning will give you better attention standing than seated, and a tutor who understands that gets more done in thirty minutes than a worksheet session gets in an hour.

What does not belong at this age: timed drills, marking in red, a stack of printed sheets sent home as extra work, and any attempt to teach next year's content early. Handwriting, spacing and presentation are fair game, and are often the quickest visible win in a primary home tuition arrangement.
items: Reading aloud, then retelling from memory before any written comprehension work
Number sense with counters, coins and a floor number line, not columns
One written sentence done well beats a page of half-finished answers
Handwriting, spacing and presentation: the fastest visible change at this age
The child's own inquiry question, rehearsed out loud until it is clear

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB PYP home tutors in India can realistically reach by six in the evening
contentBlocks.body:
For a primary child the clock matters more than the kilometre count. A tutor who arrives at a quarter to eight meets a child with nothing left. So the local question is not how far a tutor will travel, but who can be at your table while the child is still awake and pleasant.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, that usually means someone in or beside your own suburb. A family in Bandra or Juhu has a different evening from one in Powai or Thane, and a tutor crossing from Andheri to Navi Mumbai or Kharghar at peak hour is making a promise the road may not keep. Evening traffic between Worli, Lower Parel and the western suburbs can stretch a short trip badly. A parent searching for an IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai does better with a short list near Vashi or Malabar Hill than a long one across the city.

Bengaluru is the same problem in another shape. Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are their own worlds on a weekday, and an IB PYP home tutor in Bangalore living in Indiranagar or Koramangala may not reach HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka or Electronic City in time. Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road families often find supply closer than they expect. Pune is kinder: Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Viman Nagar sit close together, Baner, Balewadi, Wakad and Hinjewadi form a second cluster, and Kharadi and Aundh a third. An IB PYP home tutor in Pune inside your cluster will hold a five o'clock slot far better than one crossing town.

In Hyderabad, the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District and Kokapet belt is dense enough that an IB PYP home tutor in Hyderabad can reach two families in one evening, while Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad are separate runs. Across Gujarat, Ahmedabad families in Satellite, Bodakdev and along SG Highway have local options, Gandhinagar sits close, and Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot are thinner, which is where a hybrid week starts to make sense. contentBlocks.heading: The primary school day in India that decides your session time
contentBlocks.body:
Work backwards from the school bus, not from the tutor's diary. A primary child at an international school in a large Indian city is often out of the house early, spends a long stretch on the bus in both directions, and then has an activity on two or three afternoons. By the time the bag is down and something has been eaten, it can be five or half past five. That leaves one usable window, and it is narrow.

Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Stonehill International School, Pathways World School and The International School Bangalore all work around versions of the same evening. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Nothing on this page describes what any particular school teaches or where it sits.

The year has its own pressure points, and they are different from the ones secondary parents talk about. There is no external examination season in the PYP. Instead there are conference weeks where the child often leads the conversation about their own work, portfolio evenings, unit celebrations, sports days and, in the final year of the programme, the exhibition, which takes over a child's term in a way parents rarely anticipate. A long summer break and a shorter festival break both interrupt any weekly rhythm you build, and a young child loses fluency over a break faster than an older one does.

Before you hire anyone, ask the class teacher two questions and write the answers down. What exactly is the child finding hard, in the teacher's own words. And what is the teacher already doing about it in class. A class teacher who says the child is quiet in group work is describing something a home tutor can genuinely help with. A teacher who says the child is fine and the worry is yours is also giving you useful information, and it is worth hearing before a tutor enters the house.
items: Work backwards from bus arrival and dinner, not from the tutor's free hour
Two or three afternoons a week are usually already taken by activities
Conference weeks, portfolio evenings and the exhibition shape the year, not exams
Long breaks cost a young child fluency faster than they cost an older student
Ask the class teacher what is hard and what is already being done

contentBlocks.heading: Home sessions, online or hybrid for a child aged six to eleven?
contentBlocks.body:
For most children under nine, home sessions work and unsupported online sessions do not. A tutor in the room can move a child's hand to correct a pencil grip, push a counter across the table, notice a squint, and read the two seconds of body language that say the child has stopped following. None of that reaches through a screen for a six-year-old, and an adult ends up sitting beside the child running the call, which defeats the purpose.

Online earns its place later and in narrower slots. A child of ten or eleven who can already work independently for a stretch will manage a short online session, particularly for talking work: reading aloud, retelling, rehearsing a presentation, discussing an inquiry question. Online also solves a supply problem honestly. If you are in Rajkot, Vadodara or a smaller city where no primary IB home tutor is available at all, a good online teacher beats a weak local one. And online survives a monsoon evening, a fever, or a week when the family is travelling, which a home visit does not.

Hybrid is what most PYP families settle into once they stop treating the choice as permanent. One home visit a week that does the hard, physical, pencil-and-paper work, plus one short online check-in of fifteen or twenty minutes later in the week to hear the child read or to look at a piece of writing. The home lesson carries the teaching. The online slot carries the habit. It costs the family less travel dependence and gives the tutor two contacts with the child instead of one.

The trade-off stated plainly: home tuition buys attention and physical correction at the price of traffic, cancellations and a fixed travel radius; online buys reach and reliability at the price of everything that happens below the shoulders; hybrid buys most of both and asks a parent to run the device once a week. Under nine, weight it heavily towards home classes. Over ten, the balance genuinely opens up, which is why most IB PYP home tutors in India will ask the child's age before they discuss mode at all.
items: Under nine: home sessions, because correction at this age is physical
Ten and above: short online slots work well for reading and talking tasks
Hybrid week: one home visit for teaching, one brief online check for habit
Online rescues a fever week, a monsoon evening or a family trip
An adult must set up and stay near the device for any online primary lesson

contentBlocks.heading: Safeguarding basics when a tutor visits a young child at home in India
contentBlocks.body:
Four things, every time, and none of them are negotiable because the child is small. Government photo identity seen and matched to the person at your door on the first visit. A profile that has been verified before it went live, with the tutor's teaching background checked rather than only claimed. The session held in a shared room with the door open, never a bedroom with the door shut. And an adult in the flat for the whole of it, with the tutor told plainly that this is the arrangement.

Then the things a platform cannot see and you must handle yourself. Tell building security or the society office who is coming and on which evenings, so gate entry is routine and nobody is standing in the lobby with a child waiting upstairs. Keep all communication in one channel you can read; there is no reason for a tutor and a seven-year-old to be messaging privately. No photographs or videos of the child without your explicit say-so, and none posted anywhere. No lifts in a tutor's car. If a session needs to be rescheduled, it is rescheduled with you, not agreed with the child at the door.

The harder skill is being nearby without hovering, and most parents get this wrong in the first fortnight. Being in earshot is the safeguarding requirement. Sitting at the child's elbow is not, and it changes the child's behaviour immediately: they start checking your face after every answer instead of thinking. Take the next chair, or the far end of the same room, with something of your own to do. Do not supply the answer when the child pauses. Do not correct the child's spelling from across the room. A tutor needs to see the child get something wrong, because that is the whole diagnostic.

Give the child two sentences of their own: that they may say they want a break, and that they may stop and come to you at any moment for any reason. A child who knows both will tell you if something feels off. Watch for a child who was willing and is suddenly not, and act on it rather than explaining it away.
items: Photo identity checked at the door on the first visit, matched to the profile
Shared room, door open, an adult in the flat throughout the session
One communication channel with the parent; no private messaging with the child
No photographs of the child and no lifts in the tutor's car
Sit in earshot with your own work, and let wrong answers happen

contentBlocks.heading: A forty-five minute PYP session, minute by minute
contentBlocks.body:
Forty-five minutes is about the ceiling for a child of seven or eight, and it only holds if it is cut into pieces before the tutor walks in. Here is a shape that works, and that any competent tutor should be able to describe to you in one line before the first session.

1. Minutes 0 to 5. Arrival and settling. The table is already clear. The child says one thing about the school day, and the tutor writes the three things they will do on a sheet the child can see and tick off.

2. Minutes 5 to 20. The hardest task first, while attention is at its strongest. New number work, or the piece of writing the child has been avoiding. This is the only part of the session that should feel like effort.

3. Minutes 20 to 25. Movement, built in rather than begged for. The child stands, fetches something from another room, acts out a sequence, jumps a number line or sorts cards on the floor. No screen and no snack, because both are hard to come back from.

4. Minutes 25 to 38. The second task, lighter and more spoken. Reading aloud, retelling, a conversation about the child's inquiry question, a game that hides practice inside it.

5. Minutes 38 to 45. Finishing. One thing is completed, named out loud and shown to a parent. The tutor says what happens next week. The child packs the box themselves.

Shift the numbers for the child in front of you. At five, the whole thing is closer to twenty-five or thirty minutes with two movement points. At ten or eleven, the middle block can stretch and the child can be asked to choose the order. What should not move is the ending. A session that runs over by ten minutes because the work was not finished teaches a young child that sitting down with a tutor means an evening with no clear edge, and that is how willingness is lost.
items: Hardest task early: attention is a budget that is spent, not renewed
A visible three-item plan the child ticks off as the session runs
One movement point in a thirty-minute session, two in forty-five
Finish something every time, name it, and show it to a parent
Stop on the minute, even when the work is incomplete

contentBlocks.heading: How long can a young child actually focus, and what changes by age?
contentBlocks.body:
Roughly: a child of four or five gives an adult-directed task a few minutes before needing to move; at six or seven it is closer to ten or twelve minutes; at eight or nine, around fifteen; and by ten to twelve a child can hold twenty or a little more with one break. These are working figures a tutor plans around, not measurements, and your child may sit well outside them on either side, or on either side of them from one evening to the next.

What that means in practice is that the session length you are paying for is not the attention you are getting. Forty-five minutes of home tuition is three usable blocks with joins between them. A tutor who plans one continuous forty-five-minute task is planning thirty-five minutes of drift. And a tired child at seven in the evening is a younger child than the same child at four in the afternoon on a Saturday.

Progress at this age does not show up as a number, because there are no published PYP grades to watch. Look instead at willingness, which usually moves first, within two or three weeks: the child stops negotiating about the session. Then look at volume and independence over six to eight weeks: a longer piece of writing, a child who rereads their own sentence without being told, a child who reaches for the counters unprompted. Ask the tutor for two lines after each session and keep them, because the change is slow enough that you will not see it without notes.

And the limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and in the PYP there is not even a grade to point at. A home tutor cannot fix a child who is sleeping badly, a week with an activity on every afternoon, an uncorrected vision or hearing problem, or a language gap that needs school-level support. If a child is doing well at school and the worry is yours rather than the teacher's, an honest tutor will say so and suggest waiting. The better IB PYP home tutors in India say it early, and they lose a booking by saying it. Take it seriously when you hear it.
items: Attention is a budget: it is spent through the session and does not refill
The same child at 4 pm is not the same child at 7 pm
Willingness shifts in two or three weeks; written volume takes six to eight
Two written lines from the tutor after each session, kept and reread monthly
Sleep, activity overload and eyesight are checked before tuition hours are added

contentBlocks.heading: Setting up the dining table in India before the first PYP session
contentBlocks.body:
Clear it completely. Not pushed to one side: cleared, because a child of seven will find the one interesting object left on the table within ninety seconds. Then check the chair, which almost nobody does. The child's elbows should rest at about table height and their feet should be flat, on the floor or on a footstool, a low stool or a stack of old directories. A child whose legs are swinging in mid-air will fidget for the whole session, and everyone will blame the child's concentration.

Light from the side rather than from behind, so the writing hand does not cast a shadow across the page. Seat the child facing a wall or a window, not the television and not the doorway everyone walks through. Keep everything the session needs in one box that lives in one place: the school reading book, the maths notebook, sharpened pencils, an eraser, blank paper, a small whiteboard and marker, a timer with a face the child can read, and a glass of water. Hunting for a sharpener costs four minutes of a forty-five minute session and breaks the thread.

The household matters as much as the furniture. Television off, not muted. Phones out of the room, including yours. Younger siblings occupied somewhere else, which is the single hardest thing to arrange and the most worth arranging. If the doorbell tends to go at that hour, tell whoever answers it not to bring anybody through the room.

Most IB PYP home tutors in India will ask you to have all of this ready before they arrive, and the ones who do not ask should still find it waiting. The first session should not be a teaching session. Expect the tutor to read with the child, play something numerical, ask what the child thinks they are good at and what they find hard, and watch how the child holds a pencil. Expect it to finish a few minutes early on purpose. What you should get afterwards is a short, plain description of what the tutor saw and what they propose to start with, and a date for the next one.
items: Table cleared completely; feet flat on the floor or on a footstool
Light from the side so the writing hand casts no shadow
One box: reading book, notebook, pencils, blank paper, whiteboard, timer, water
Television off, phones out of the room, younger siblings occupied elsewhere
First session diagnoses and ends early; expect two plain lines afterwards

faqs.question: How long should a home tuition session be for a six-year-old?
faqs.answer: Thirty minutes, or forty-five at the very most, and cut into two or three blocks with movement between them. A six-year-old who has been at school since morning has very little sustained attention left by evening, and a longer booking does not buy more learning; it buys drift. If you feel the child needs more contact time, two short home sessions in a week beat one long one. Ask the tutor how they intend to divide the time before you agree the slot.

faqs.question: Should I sit in the room while the home tutor works with my child?
faqs.answer: Stay within earshot, not at the child's elbow. Being in the same room with the door open is the safeguarding arrangement, and for a young child it is the right one. But sitting alongside changes what the child does: they look at your face after every answer instead of thinking, and they stop risking a wrong one. Take the far chair with something of your own to do, do not supply answers during pauses, and let the tutor see the mistakes. The mistakes are the diagnostic.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Class 4 and reads well behind her classmates. Is that a tutoring problem?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but ask the class teacher first and ask specifically. Reading behind peers can mean decoding, fluency, comprehension, vocabulary, or simply less reading at home, and each needs a different response. Get the teacher's own description of what breaks down, in writing if you can. If the school is already running support, a tutor should work alongside it rather than start something parallel. And have her eyesight and hearing checked before adding hours, because that is a common and easily missed cause.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a PYP child, or is a home visit necessary?
faqs.answer: Below about nine, a home visit is usually necessary; above ten, online genuinely works for the right tasks. A younger child needs physical correction, objects to move and an adult who can see their hands, and none of that travels through a screen well. From ten or eleven, short online slots suit reading aloud, retelling and talking about an inquiry question. A hybrid week, one home session plus one brief online check, is what most families end up preferring.

faqs.question: We live in a two-bedroom flat in Andheri. Where should the session actually happen?
faqs.answer: The dining table, almost always, with the television off and the younger child occupied somewhere else. A bedroom with the door shut is not appropriate for a visiting tutor and a young child, and a bedroom desk is usually too cluttered with the child's own things to hold attention. In a compact flat in Andheri, Powai or Thane, the dining table is the only surface with proper light and a chair at the right height. Clear it completely before the tutor arrives.

faqs.question: How do I find a PYP home tutor near me in Whitefield or Sarjapur Road?
faqs.answer: Send your locality, the exact evening hour you need and your child's age, and ask to be shortlisted only from tutors who can reach you before that hour. In Bengaluru this matters more than anywhere: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road are far enough from Indiranagar or Hebbal on a weekday that a tutor who agrees to the slot in principle may not hold it in practice. Ask a shortlisted tutor where they live and what else they teach that evening.

faqs.question: What should a tutor do when my child simply refuses to sit down?
faqs.answer: Start the session standing up and get the child working before the chair is ever mentioned. A skilled primary tutor will begin with something physical, a card sort on the floor or a counting game, and move to the table once the child is already engaged. Refusal is usually about the transition, not the work. What a tutor should not do is bargain, threaten to tell you, or hold a standoff. If refusal repeats every week, the slot is probably too late in the evening.

faqs.question: Is play during a paid session a waste of the slot?
faqs.answer: No, provided the play is the teaching rather than a reward bolted on afterwards. Counters sorted into groups are multiplication. A number line jumped along the corridor is counting in threes. Acting out the order of events in a story is comprehension. What would waste the slot is free play with no learning purpose, or a game used to fill time because the tutor has run out of plan. Ask the tutor to tell you what each game is teaching.

faqs.question: What safeguarding checks should I do before a tutor visits my young child at home?
faqs.answer: Match photo identity to the person at your door on the first visit, keep the session in a shared room with the door open, and have an adult in the flat throughout. Tell building security who is coming and on which evenings. Keep all messages in one channel you can read, with no private contact between the tutor and the child. No photographs of the child, and no lifts in anyone's car. Tell your child they may stop and come to you at any time.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a primary-age child actually need?
faqs.answer: One or two, and for most children one is enough. A PYP child is at school all day and already doing the substantive work there; tuition adds a focused half hour on one specific difficulty. Three or four sessions a week for a nine-year-old is usually a sign that the wrong problem is being solved, or that a scheduling or sleep issue is being treated as an academic one. Start with one, review after six weeks, and add only if there is a clear reason.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor misses a weekday evening slot because of Pune traffic?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because with a young child it will happen. A reasonable arrangement is that the tutor tells you as early as they can, the session is either shifted within the same week or converted to a shorter online slot that evening, and a repeated pattern is a matching problem rather than a traffic problem. If a tutor coming from Hinjewadi to Koregaon Park is late twice a month, ask for a match closer to your cluster.

faqs.question: My child is in the PYP exhibition year. Can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help with the skills around it and must not touch the work itself. The exhibition falls in the final year of the programme and is the child's own inquiry, so a tutor who drafts, edits or scripts any part of it has taken it away from them. What is legitimate: helping the child narrow a question, rehearsing how they will explain it aloud, teaching them to plan a week, and calming the panic. Confirm the boundary with the school's coordinator.

comparison.heading: How do the four ways of getting PYP help in India compare for a young child?
comparison.intro: A tutor at your table suits a child under nine, because correction at that age is physical and immediate. An online tutor suits a child who can already work alone, or a family with no local option. A neighbourhood centre suits a family who wants company and a lower hourly cost. A distant specialist suits a specific difficulty nobody nearby handles. Travel and the hour of the evening usually decide it.

An online tutor anywhere in India

cells: Your own table, chair height and lighting, fixed once and reused
Your table again, but the tutor cannot see or correct the setup
A desk built for the purpose, often better than a home dining table

cells: Easy: floor work, number lines in the corridor, objects to sort
