h1: IB PYP Home Tuition for Reading, Number Sense and Routine
heroTitle: What PYP Home Tuition Should Build in India
heroSubtitle: Your child has no marks to chase and no exam date to work back from. That makes primary tutoring easy to get wrong. This page sets out the four things worth building at this age, the evening routine that holds them, and how home tuition fits a primary week without extending it.
introSummary: IB PYP home tuition in India should build four things: reading fluency and comprehension, number sense that comes before procedures, handwriting and presentation a child is not ashamed of, and a daily routine the household can actually keep. It should not try to cover a syllabus, because the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) does not have one to cover. Learning for ages three to twelve is organised around six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, with no external examinations and no published PYP grades. So a good home tutor works on the foundations underneath the inquiry, in short sessions, and then gets out of the way. The rest of this page is what those foundations look like in practice, region by region, evening by evening.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a request for IB PYP home tuition in India turn into a foundations plan?
contentBlocks.body:
A request for IB PYP home tuition in India rarely arrives as a subject request. It arrives as a worry. He reads the words but cannot tell you what happened. She is still counting on fingers in Grade 3. His notebook is a mess and the class teacher has mentioned it twice now. None of that maps onto a subject, so the matching conversation has to start somewhere else: with what the child can already do, unaided, on an ordinary Tuesday.

1. You send a query or book a free consultation, and describe the worry in the words you would use with a friend rather than in school language.
2. IB Gram asks about the child's age and year group, the school calendar, the unit of inquiry the class is currently working through, your locality, and the two or three evening slots that genuinely exist in your week.
3. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who have taught primary-age children, not only Diploma Programme (DP) students.
4. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and in that session the tutor should spend more time watching than teaching.
5. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. With a young child, fit outranks credentials.

The trial is the part worth protecting. A tutor who arrives with a worksheet pack has already decided what is wrong before meeting the child. A tutor who asks your child to read aloud from a book picked at random, then asks two questions about that page, has real evidence inside twenty minutes. The plan should be built from that evidence and written down somewhere you can see it.

Availability stays conditional, and honestly so at primary level. Fewer tutors want an early-evening slot with a seven-year-old than want a DP Physics slot, because the work is harder to do well and looks less impressive on a profile. Ask what else the tutor teaches.
items: The worry in your own words, before anyone translates it into subjects
Age, year group and the unit of inquiry the class is working on now
Two or three evening slots that exist in reality, not on paper
A trial in which the tutor mostly watches and listens
Written evidence from that trial, not a ready-made starting plan

contentBlocks.heading: Why syllabus coverage is the wrong frame for the PYP
contentBlocks.body:
The PYP runs from ages three to twelve and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet. A class works through units of inquiry inside those themes. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, and in the final year of the programme the student completes the PYP exhibition.

So there is nothing to cover. A parent who asks a tutor to finish the chapters before the unit ends is asking for something the programme does not contain. The unit will close whether or not a set of pages has been worked through, and the next one will open on a different theme with different material. A tutor who promises coverage is selling a board-exam service with an IB label stuck on the front.

What does carry from one unit to the next is capability. A child who reads fluently gets through the unit text faster and has attention left over for the thinking. A child with genuine number sense can handle the measuring and data work inside How the world works without the arithmetic swallowing the inquiry. A child who writes legibly at speed gets the idea onto the page before it evaporates. None of those three expires when a unit ends, which is precisely why they are what home tuition at this stage should build.

The ten attributes of the IB learner profile point the same way. Inquirer, thinker, communicator and the rest describe dispositions rather than content, and no tutor can coach a disposition directly. But a child who reads and reasons without struggling has room to be curious. A child who is still drowning in decoding does not, however willing they are.
items: Six transdisciplinary themes, worked through as units of inquiry, not chapters
No external examinations and no published PYP grades at any stage
The PYP exhibition falls in the final year of the programme
Ten learner profile attributes describe dispositions, not content to be taught
Capability carries across units; coverage of one unit does not

contentBlocks.heading: What does good reading practice actually look like at home?
contentBlocks.body:
Good reading practice at home is short, daily and out loud. Ten to fifteen minutes with a book the child can mostly manage, read aloud to an adult who is genuinely listening rather than half watching something else. Fluency is not speed. It is reading in phrases instead of word by word, pausing at full stops, and letting the voice fall at the end of a sentence. A child who reads a page correctly in a flat monotone is decoding rather than reading, and comprehension will trail behind until that changes.

Comprehension work is where most primary tuition goes wrong. Asking what happened in the story tests memory. Better questions ask for evidence: which word tells you the character was frightened, what do you think happens next and what in the text makes you say so, read me the line that proves it. Two or three such questions per page is plenty. Twenty is an interrogation. Over a term the child begins pointing at the evidence before being asked, and that is the actual goal.

The second half of the work is unglamorous. Handwriting and presentation still matter, and not for neatness. A child who forms letters slowly spends working memory on the pen rather than on the sentence, so what reaches the page is shorter and simpler than the thinking behind it. Presentation matters because PYP work is meant to be communicated and shown, and by the time the exhibition arrives in the final year, work that cannot be read cannot be shown. Five minutes of letter formation at the start of a home session, then not mentioned again for the rest of the hour, is usually enough.

Parents sometimes ask whether to start early on the subjects listed further up the school, such as IB Mathematics AA and AI, IB Physics, IB Chemistry, IB Biology, IB Economics or IB English A. Those belong to the Diploma Programme and are many years away. Reading, number and the pen are what pay for themselves now.
items: Fluency is phrasing and expression, not words read per minute
Comprehension questions should ask for evidence from the page itself
Five minutes of letter formation, then left alone for the hour
A messy notebook often means a slow pen rather than carelessness
Reading volume matters more than book difficulty at primary age

contentBlocks.heading: PYP home tuition across India: what each region does to your evening
contentBlocks.body:
A primary child's lesson has to sit between school pick-up and bedtime, and that window is far narrower than a teenager's. In Delhi NCR, a tutor living in Dwarka who teaches in Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri can usually hold a five o'clock slot; the same tutor asked to reach Sector 128 Noida or Greater Noida on a weekday evening will start arriving late, and a late start with a seven-year-old is a wasted hour. Families in Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, and in Faridabad and Ghaziabad, generally do better with a competent tutor from the same sector than with a stronger one from across the river.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region divides the same way. IB PYP home tuition in Mumbai works inside pockets: Bandra, Juhu and Andheri; Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill; Powai largely on its own. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are better served by tutors who already live there. Chennai spreads north to south, so Adyar, Besant Nagar and Alwarpet form one workable cluster, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery another, with Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar nearer the centre.

Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai the supply thins noticeably. Kochi, Coimbatore and Thiruvananthapuram usually have primary tutors. Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai often do not have one who knows the PYP at all, and that is where a hybrid week earns its place. In Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town and Rajarhat sit close enough to share a tutor, while Ballygunge and Alipore form their own pocket; IB PYP home tuition in Kolkata is practical there and much harder in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna.

The metro clusters concentrate predictably. IB PYP home tuition in Bangalore gathers around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar and HSR Layout. IB PYP home tuition in Hyderabad follows Gachibowli, Madhapur, Kondapur and Jubilee Hills. IB PYP home tuition in Pune sits in Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner and Kharadi. IB PYP home tuition in Ahmedabad is mostly Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and IB PYP home tuition in Delhi follows the South Delhi and Dwarka clusters above.
items: Delhi NCR: a same-sector tutor usually beats a better one across the river
Powai, Bandra and Thane each work best with tutors living there
Adyar and Besant Nagar cluster separately from Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR)
Salt Lake, New Town and Rajarhat can share a tutor; Ballygunge cannot
Searching PYP home tuition near me is sensible at this age, not lazy
Primary years home tuition thins out fast outside the six metro clusters

contentBlocks.heading: The primary school year in India, and where a tutor fits
contentBlocks.body:
International schools in India do not all start their year in the same month, and holiday dates move about. Your own school's calendar is the only one that matters, so ask the PYP coordinator for it in writing at the start of the year and plan around that. What is common across them is the shape of the pressure points, and for a primary child those pressure points are never examinations. They are the student-led or three-way conference, the portfolio going home, the unit celebration, and in the final year, the exhibition.

Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore are named here only because Indian families recognise them. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

What the calendar does to home tuition is simple enough. Term time is when the evening is already full, so sessions should be short and few. The long break is when a genuine reading habit can be built, because nothing else is competing for that fifteen minutes and a child will tolerate a book they would resist on a school night. Families who do it the other way round, cramming tuition into a busy term and stopping entirely in the holidays, end up with the worst of both.

Before hiring anyone, put one question to the class teacher: is my child behind, or am I anxious? A primary teacher sees a whole class every week and knows the range that age actually covers. If the answer is that the child is fine, the honest next step is no tuition and a book at bedtime. If the answer is specific, write down exactly what the teacher said and hand it to the tutor.
items: Ask the class teacher first: genuinely behind, or a parent's anxiety?
Conferences, portfolios and unit celebrations are the pressure points, not examinations
Term time calls for fewer sessions; long breaks suit habit building
Your own school's calendar dates are the only ones worth planning around
IB Gram is independent of every school named on this page

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid for a child of seven or eight?
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the plain comparison. One-to-one home tuition is the best fit for a PYP child, because reading aloud, handwriting and spoken number work all want an adult in the room who can see the page and the pen at the same time. One-to-one online is the second choice and becomes genuinely good from around ages nine to eleven, once a child can hold a conversation through a screen without an adult managing it for them. A hybrid week, one home session plus a shorter online check-in, is often the most practical of the three in the larger Indian cities, because it keeps the face-to-face work and removes one commute.

Online has one real advantage at this age, and it is not convenience. It is reach. A family in Mysuru or Ranchi with no primary tutor within a sensible distance can work with someone based in Bengaluru or Salt Lake. The cost is supervision. For a child under about seven, expect to sit beside them for the whole online session, which means the family pays with an hour of its own time as well as the fee.

Home tuition has limits too, and they are worth naming. A tutor caught in weekday evening traffic arrives tired, and by then the child is already past their best hour of the day. In Andheri, or out along Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), a tutor who left on time can still reach the door after the slot has begun. If that happens twice in a month, move that session online rather than pushing bedtime later and later.

A small online group class has its place. Reading discussion works in a group, because hearing how another child answered is part of the learning. Handwriting does not work in a group at all, and a child who needs to be asked something directly every couple of minutes will quietly disappear in one.
items: Home suits the under-nines because the page and the pen stay visible
Online becomes genuinely workable from around ages nine to eleven
A hybrid week keeps face-to-face work and removes one commute
Online reaches families where no primary tutor lives within reach
A small online group helps reading talk, never handwriting

contentBlocks.heading: Checks that matter before a tutor enters your home in India
contentBlocks.body:
Verification by a platform and verification by a parent are two different jobs, and for a primary child the second one carries more weight. Before a profile goes live, IB Gram checks identity documents, the qualifications claimed and the teaching experience stated, and the profile shows what the tutor actually teaches and at which stages. What no platform can see from a document is whether this particular adult is any good with a seven-year-old, in that child's own house, at six in the evening.

So run your own check during the trial, and make it practical rather than conversational. Ask the tutor to show you, not tell you, how they would teach a child to work out thirty-four minus eighteen without the column method. Ask what they would do if your child simply refused to read aloud that day. Ask how many primary children they currently teach against how many DP students. A tutor whose week is entirely Diploma Programme revision will treat your eight-year-old like a small teenager, usually without meaning to.

Two things are worth insisting on for home lessons with a young child. The session happens in a shared part of the house with the door open, and an adult is somewhere in the flat. Not seated in the room necessarily, but present and reachable. Keep society or apartment gate entry registered in your own name so you always know who is coming up, and keep the same tutor week to week rather than accepting substitutes, because a young child spends the first few sessions deciding whether this adult is worth trusting.

Then check the unglamorous things. Does the tutor arrive when they said they would? Do they leave a two-line note about what was done? A tutor who cancels twice in the first month is telling you something reliable about the next six.
items: Identity, qualifications and stated experience checked before a profile goes live
Ask how many primary children the tutor currently teaches each week
Ask them to teach a subtraction without the column method, in front of you
Lessons in a shared room, door open, an adult present in the flat
Same tutor each week; decline substitutes for a young child

contentBlocks.heading: Why IB PYP home tuition in India should start with number sense, not procedures
contentBlocks.body:
Number sense is knowing what a number is worth before knowing what to do with it. A child who has it can tell you that four hundred and two is close to four hundred, that nineteen fives is about a hundred, and that an answer of twenty-four to thirty-four minus eighteen looks wrong, all without writing anything down. A child who does not have it owns a set of procedures and no way of catching a mistake, which is why the marks can look fine in Grade 2 and come apart around Grade 5.

Take thirty-four minus eighteen. Taught as a procedure, the child writes it in a column, crosses out the three, borrows a ten, and arrives at sixteen if every step went right. Taught for sense, the child counts up instead: eighteen to twenty is two, twenty to thirty-four is fourteen, so the gap is sixteen. Ask that second child to check it and they will say that sixteen and eighteen make thirty-four, because they can picture it. Both children wrote sixteen. Only one of them is still right when the numbers get uglier, and only one can spot their own error before an adult does.

The tutor's job is to keep asking the question with no procedure attached to it. Roughly how much? Is that more or less than half? Which is bigger, three quarters or two thirds, and how do you know without finding a common denominator? Show me seven eights using seven fours twice. None of that is enrichment or extra. It is the ground the procedures are supposed to stand on.

This is also why IB PYP home tuition in India should never be measured in worksheets completed. Thirty subtraction sums done correctly by a child who cannot say what subtraction means is thirty repetitions of a misunderstanding. Five questions asked out loud and answered out loud, with the child explaining the reasoning each time, does more in ten minutes.
items: Estimating before calculating is the fastest test of real number sense
Counting up beats borrowing for most two-digit subtractions
Ask for the reasoning aloud, not only the answer
Five spoken questions beat thirty written sums at this age
Procedures without sense usually hold up until roughly Grade 5

contentBlocks.heading: How will you know it is working when there are no PYP grades?
contentBlocks.body:
With no external examinations and no published PYP grades, progress has to be read from the child rather than from a report card. Fluency shifts first, usually within six to eight weeks of genuine daily reading, and you hear it before you could measure it: the voice starts carrying phrases instead of words. Number sense takes longer, a term rather than a month, and the first sign is not a correct answer but a sensible estimate offered without prompting. Handwriting improves fastest of the three and then levels off, which is normal and not a failure.

Write down three specific things in week one. Not reading better. Something you could witness: reads a page of a Grade 2 book without stopping twice; says roughly how much nineteen fives comes to without reaching for a pen; writes four legible lines in five minutes. Look at those same three in week eight. If none of them has moved, either the plan is wrong or the child needs something a tutor cannot provide, and both are worth finding out sooner.

The honest limit is that IB PYP home tuition in India cannot fix everything, and some of what parents bring to it is not a tuition problem at all. A child who cannot sit still at seven, a child whose reading has stalled despite months of daily practice, or a child who reverses letters consistently may need a proper assessment rather than more hours with a tutor. A good tutor will say that out loud, and will say it early rather than after a year of fees.

The other limit is the evening itself. Two hours of tuition stacked on top of a full school day produces a tired child, and a tired child learns very little and starts resenting the tutor who takes the last hour of their day. If the routine cannot hold, cut the tuition rather than the sleep.
items: Fluency shifts first, usually within six to eight weeks
Number sense takes a term, and shows up as better estimates
Write three observable things in week one, recheck them in week eight
Persistent letter reversal or stalled reading may need a proper assessment
If the routine cannot hold, cut the tuition, not the sleep

contentBlocks.heading: Starting PYP home tuition in India without building a second school day
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first session, prepare three things and nothing more: the book your child is currently reading, their school notebook exactly as it looks today, and one sentence describing what worries you. No stationery haul, no printed worksheet packs, no revision guides bought in advance.

The first home session should be mostly diagnostic. The tutor listens to the child read, asks two comprehension questions, sets one arithmetic question and watches how it gets answered rather than whether the answer is right, and looks at a page of existing handwriting. Twenty minutes of that tells a competent tutor more than any test would, and it tells you something too, because you can see whether your child relaxed or froze.

Then agree the routine below with the tutor, and agree who owns which part of it. The tutor owns the weekly session. You own the daily fifteen minutes. The school owns the units of inquiry. Nobody owns all three, and that division is the point: IB PYP home tuition in India works when it slots into a week the family was already living, and fails when it adds a second timetable on top of the first one.

Start with one session a week. Add a second only if the first is clearly working and the child is not flattened by it. Sessions run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and your locality, and you can ask for a different match at any point without having to justify it at length. PYP tuition at home is meant to be a small, steady thing. If it ever feels like a project, something has gone wrong with the plan rather than with the child.
items: 1. Fifteen minutes of reading aloud, same time daily, no screen in the room
2. Five minutes of number talk: one question asked aloud, answered aloud
3. School homework as set, with a hard stop when the time is up
4. Five minutes of handwriting on two days a week, not seven
5. One home session a week, two at most, in the same slot each time
6. Nothing academic after dinner, including the night before a conference

faqs.question: My child is in Grade 2 and reads slowly. Is that worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Not yet, in most cases. Slow reading in Grade 2 is common and usually responds to fifteen minutes of reading aloud every day to an adult who is actually listening. Give that eight weeks before hiring anyone. If the child is still reading word by word after that, still cannot answer a question about the page they have just read, or has started avoiding books altogether, then bring in help. The test is whether daily practice has genuinely been tried, not whether your worry is real.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor work on when the PYP has no syllabus?
faqs.answer: Four things: reading fluency and comprehension, number sense, handwriting and presentation, and the habit of doing a small amount every day. None of those belong to a single unit of inquiry, so none of them expire when the unit closes and the class moves on. A home tutor who instead asks for the unit planner and starts pre-teaching its content is copying a board-exam model onto a programme that has no external examinations and no published PYP grades to prepare for.

faqs.question: How do we stop home tuition from turning the evening into a second school day?
faqs.answer: Cap the total, in writing, before you start. One home session a week, fifteen minutes of reading daily and five minutes of number talk is enough at primary age, and school homework has to sit inside that total rather than on top of it. Set a hard stop time and hold it even when the work is unfinished. An unfinished worksheet costs nothing at this stage. A child who begins dreading the evening costs a great deal, and it takes months to undo.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is decoding or comprehension?
faqs.answer: Read the page to your child instead of having them read it, then ask exactly the same questions. If they answer well when you read and poorly when they read, the problem is decoding and the fix is fluency practice. If they answer poorly either way, it is comprehension, and the work is questions that force them back to the text for evidence. This test takes five minutes at the kitchen table and changes what a tutor should be doing from the first session.

faqs.question: My child still counts on fingers in Grade 3. Should we stop it?
faqs.answer: No, not directly. Finger counting is a symptom of missing number facts rather than the cause, and banning it removes the only working method the child has. Build the facts underneath instead: doubles, the pairs that make ten, and counting up for subtraction. Ask for estimates out loud so that speed is not the measure of success. The fingers drop away on their own once something better is available, usually over a term rather than a fortnight.

faqs.question: Does handwriting still matter when schools use laptops so much?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a reason that has nothing to do with neatness. A child who forms letters slowly spends attention on the pen rather than on the sentence, so what reaches the page comes out shorter and simpler than what is in their head. Presentation matters as well, because PYP work is meant to be communicated and shown, and by the exhibition in the final year, work nobody can read cannot be shown to anybody. Five minutes twice a week is usually enough.

faqs.question: We are in Powai and the tutor we like is in Worli. Is home tuition still practical?
faqs.answer: Probably not as a weekly arrangement. Evening traffic across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region can stretch a short trip badly, and with a young child a late start wastes the best part of the hour you are paying for. Two better options exist. Find a tutor inside Powai even if the profile reads as slightly less impressive, or run a hybrid week with one home session at a weekend time and one shorter online session midweek. The second keeps the tutor you liked.

faqs.question: Is online tuition workable for a seven-year-old, or is a home tutor the only real option?
faqs.answer: A home tutor is the better default at seven, and online becomes genuinely workable from around ages nine to eleven. Below that an adult usually has to sit beside the child for the whole session, so the family pays with an hour of its own time as well as the fee. Online is still the right call when no primary tutor is reachable locally, which happens far more often in Mysuru, Vijayawada or Guwahati than it does in a metro suburb.

faqs.question: What should PYP reading help look like over a long school holiday?
faqs.answer: Shorter and more frequent than during term. Fifteen minutes daily beats an hour twice a week, and the holiday is the only stretch of the year when nothing else competes for that fifteen minutes. Let the child choose the book even when it sits below their level, because volume matters more than difficulty for building fluency. One session a week to check comprehension and set the next fortnight's reading is usually the right amount of paid help over a break.

faqs.question: How soon should we expect to see a change?
faqs.answer: Fluency moves first, often within six to eight weeks of genuine daily reading, and you will hear it before you could measure it. Number sense takes about a term and shows up as better estimates rather than faster answers. Handwriting improves quickly and then levels off. Write down three specific, observable things in the first week and look at those same three in week eight. If none has moved, change the plan or ask whether an assessment is the more useful step.

faqs.question: Is searching for PYP home tuition near me sensible in a smaller city like Coimbatore?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more so at primary age than at any later stage, because a tired child cannot absorb a session that started late. Begin with the tightest radius you can manage and widen only if nobody nearby teaches primary years. In Coimbatore, Kochi or Bhubaneswar the local pool is small, so the honest sequence runs: look locally first, then consider a hybrid week, then go fully online with a specialist based in Bengaluru or Chennai if that is what it takes.

faqs.question: What does IB PYP home tuition in India cost, and what changes the fee?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed rate. IB PYP home tuition in India is priced by the tutor, and the fee depends on the stage, their experience, your locality and how far they have to travel to reach you. Primary sessions are usually shorter than Diploma Programme ones, which changes the total rather than the hourly basis. Online sessions and hybrid weeks usually cost less than a weekly home visit. Ask for the structure in writing before the trial, including missed sessions.

Evening traffic across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region can stretch a short trip badly, and with a young child a late start wastes the best part of the hour you are paying for. Two better options exist. Find a tutor inside Powai even if the profile reads as slightly less impressive, or run a hybrid week with one home session at a weekend time and one shorter online session midweek. The second keeps the tutor you liked.

mainEntity.name: Is online tuition workable for a seven-year-old, or is a home tutor the only real option?

acceptedAnswer.text: A home tutor is the better default at seven, and online becomes genuinely workable from around ages nine to eleven. Below that an adult usually has to sit beside the child for the whole session, so the family pays with an hour of its own time as well as the fee. Online is still the right call when no primary tutor is reachable locally, which happens far more often in Mysuru, Vijayawada or Guwahati than it does in a metro suburb.

mainEntity.name: What should PYP reading help look like over a long school holiday?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shorter and more frequent than during term. Fifteen minutes daily beats an hour twice a week, and the holiday is the only stretch of the year when nothing else competes for that fifteen minutes. Let the child choose the book even when it sits below their level, because volume matters more than difficulty for building fluency. One session a week to check comprehension and set the next fortnight's reading is usually the right amount of paid help over a break.

mainEntity.name: How soon should we expect to see a change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fluency moves first, often within six to eight weeks of genuine daily reading, and you will hear it before you could measure it. Number sense takes about a term and shows up as better estimates rather than faster answers. Handwriting improves quickly and then levels off. Write down three specific, observable things in the first week and look at those same three in week eight. If none has moved, change the plan or ask whether an assessment is the more useful step.

mainEntity.name: Is searching for PYP home tuition near me sensible in a smaller city like Coimbatore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and more so at primary age than at any later stage, because a tired child cannot absorb a session that started late. Begin with the tightest radius you can manage and widen only if nobody nearby teaches primary years. In Coimbatore, Kochi or Bhubaneswar the local pool is small, so the honest sequence runs: look locally first, then consider a hybrid week, then go fully online with a specialist based in Bengaluru or Chennai if that is what it takes.

mainEntity.name: What does IB PYP home tuition in India cost, and what changes the fee?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed rate. IB PYP home tuition in India is priced by the tutor, and the fee depends on the stage, their experience, your locality and how far they have to travel to reach you. Primary sessions are usually shorter than Diploma Programme ones, which changes the total rather than the hourly basis. Online sessions and hybrid weeks usually cost less than a weekly home visit. Ask for the structure in writing before the trial, including missed sessions.

IB Gram will ask about age, school calendar, locality and the evening slots that genuinely exist, then shortlist verified tutors who teach primary-age children. A trial can be arranged before you commit, at home, online or hybrid. If the match is wrong, ask for another.

One-to-one online sees the face and, with a little care, the page. A small group adds other children's answers, which is useful for reading talk and useless for handwriting. A large batch is the cheapest per hour and the least suited to a seven-year-old.

h1: IB PYP Private Tutors and the Risk of Over-Tutoring a Child
heroTitle: Should You Hire a PYP Tutor in India?
heroSubtitle: Most primary-age children in the Primary Years Programme do not need paid help at home. Some genuinely do. This page sets out the narrow cases where one-to-one home tuition earns its place, the signs that a child is already carrying too much, and how to stop when stopping is the right call.
introSummary: IB PYP private tutors in India are worth hiring far less often than the search volume suggests, and an honest tutor will tell you so before you book. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from ages 3 to 12, sets no external examinations and publishes no grades, so there is no score for home tuition to lift. What remains are real but narrow problems: a child who has moved mid-year into an inquiry-led classroom from a very different system, a reading or number gap the class teacher has already flagged, a language barrier, or a long absence through illness. This page is written to help you decide against hiring if that is the honest answer. If it is not, it tells you what to ask for and how to keep the hours small.

contentBlocks.heading: How Does IB Gram Shortlist a PYP Tutor in India Without Pushing You to Hire?
contentBlocks.body:
By starting from the assumption that you will not hire, and asking the questions that test it. When a family sends a query about IB PYP private tutors in India, the first thing we ask is what the class teacher has actually said, in their own words, and what the school has already tried this term. A parent who cannot answer that yet is not ready to choose anyone. A shortlist sent at that moment would be guesswork dressed up as service, and for a seven-year-old the cost of guessing is an hour of childhood every week.

If the picture is clear enough to act on, the query becomes a short intake conversation. You send a query or book a free consultation. We ask about the child's age and year group, the board and programme, the school's calendar and where the term's pressure points fall, your locality, and the hours that are genuinely free once school, travel and existing activities have been counted. Location weighs more at this age than at any other. A young child cannot absorb a long evening trip across a metro and should not be asked to.

Then we shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches what you described, subject to availability. You can ask for a demo or trial session before committing to anything, and for a primary-age child that trial should happen with a parent within earshot. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match rather than persevering out of politeness.

One more thing about intake. We ask for the total weekly load before we ask about subjects. A child already doing a full school day, a sport, a music class and a language class on weekday evenings has no room for another appointment, whatever a reading assessment says.
items: 1. Write down what the class teacher said, in their exact words.
2. Ask the school what support it has already tried this term.
3. Send a query or book a free consultation with those notes ready.
4. Answer the intake questions: age, programme, school calendar, locality, free hours.
5. Read verified profiles, then arrange one trial session with a parent nearby.
6. Decide afterwards, including the option of not hiring anyone at all.

contentBlocks.heading: The PYP Has No Exams in India, So What Would a Tutor Even Target?
contentBlocks.body:
Something you write down yourself, because the programme will not hand you a number. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12, sets no external examinations and publishes no grades. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet. Children meet these as units of inquiry, and the ten attributes of the IB learner profile describe the dispositions the programme is trying to build. None of that converts into a percentage you can chase.

In the final PYP year students complete the exhibition, a piece of collaborative inquiry the child is meant to own. This is the point where outside help most often goes wrong. A tutor may discuss the topic, ask questions that sharpen it and teach a skill the child then applies. A tutor must not research, draft, structure or rehearse the work into something the child could not have produced. If a tutor offers to help your child 'prepare' the exhibition, ask exactly what they mean, and be prepared to walk away from the answer.

Measurable targets arrive later. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project comes in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP 5 eAssessment is optional, with each school deciding whether to offer it.

So a parent who wants a number has to wait several years for one. Pulling MYP-style pressure down into primary is the single most common way over-tutoring starts in Indian households.
items: Six transdisciplinary themes, taught as units of inquiry, not as a syllabus
Ten learner profile attributes describe dispositions, not marks to be raised
The PYP exhibition in the final year must remain the child's own work
Criterion grades begin in the MYP: four criteria, 0 to 8, totalling 32
Write one observable goal by hand before you approach any tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Reading, Number Sense and the Subjects That Can Wait
contentBlocks.body:
The honest list of what one-to-one can work on at primary level is short: reading, writing, number sense and spoken communication. That is roughly it. Everything else a young child needs, including curiosity and the habit of asking a second question, grows better in a classroom full of other children than in a paid hour at the dining table.

Precision matters inside that short list, because the four look alike and need different work. A child who reads aloud fluently but cannot tell you what happened in the paragraph has a comprehension problem, not a decoding problem, and drilling phonics will waste both of you. A child who can complete column subtraction correctly but cannot say whether 402 minus 198 lands nearer 200 or 300 has a number sense gap sitting underneath a working procedure. A child whose sentences collapse on paper but flow in conversation usually needs sequencing and handwriting stamina, not more vocabulary. Ask any candidate to tell you which of these they think your child has, and why, from the evidence you have given them. A tutor who cannot separate them in a trial will not separate them in March either.

The subjects families ask about most are the ones that can wait longest. IB Mathematics AA and AI, IB Physics, IB Chemistry, IB Biology, IB Economics and IB English A all belong to the Diploma Programme, which is many years away from a nine-year-old. Pre-teaching Diploma content in primary buys nothing and costs the child the unstructured time that builds the reading habit those subjects will later demand.

One genuine exception is language. Where a family speaks little English at home and the child is new to an English-medium inquiry classroom, short, regular, spoken work does measurable good. Keep the mother tongue going in parallel. Dropping it to make room for tuition is a bad trade.
items: Comprehension and decoding are different problems needing different weekly work
Number sense sits under procedure: estimation, place value, and what an answer means
Handwriting stamina and sequencing explain many collapsed written pieces
Diploma subjects such as Mathematics AA and AI can safely wait years
Spoken English work helps where the home language differs, without dropping the mother tongue

contentBlocks.heading: Where PYP Home Tuition Is Practical Across India, and Where It Is Overkill
contentBlocks.body:
Geography decides more of this than parents expect, because the question is never only whether a tutor is good. It is whether an eight-year-old has any usable evening left. In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, a child travelling from Bandra, Juhu or Worli to school and back in weekday traffic arrives home tired, and a home tutor arriving soon afterwards competes with dinner and sleep. In Powai, Andheri and Lower Parel the tutor pool is deeper and travel is shorter, so a short session can work. Out in Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar, families searching for an IB PYP private tutor in Mumbai often find the realistic answer is a tutor who lives in the same node, or a short online session on the two days that stay free.

Bengaluru shows the same pattern more sharply. The distance between Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City is a real constraint on any weekday visit, while a family in Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar or on Kanakapura Road can usually find someone within a few minutes' drive. Searches for an IB PYP private tutor in Bangalore should be read as searches for a neighbour who teaches, not for the most impressive profile in the city. The same is true in Hyderabad, where Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, the Financial District, Kokapet and Secunderabad each have their own supply, and where a parent typing private PYP tutor near me is asking a sensible question.

Pune families in Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar, Aundh and Wakad face short distances and heavy peak-hour movement, so an IB PYP private tutor in Pune is usually found within the same corridor. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, local primary-level supply is thinner and PYP private tuition in India often becomes hybrid by necessity. Requests for an IB PYP private tutor in Delhi, an IB PYP private tutor in Chennai, an IB PYP private tutor in Hyderabad, an IB PYP private tutor in Kolkata or an IB PYP private tutor in Ahmedabad follow the same rule: the nearer the tutor, the smaller the disruption to the child.

Bengaluru: Whitefield to Sarjapur Road on a weekday evening rules out most visits
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kondapur hold enough local supply for short sessions
Pune: Koregaon Park, Baner and Kharadi work best with a tutor in the same corridor
Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun: thinner primary supply, so hybrid weeks make sense
In every city, a nearer tutor beats a more impressive distant one at this age

contentBlocks.heading: The Primary School Year in India and the Months Parents Panic
contentBlocks.body:
Worry runs on a calendar, and it helps to recognise your own position on it. The first parent-teacher meeting of the year is when most PYP tuition decisions get made, usually within forty-eight hours of hearing a comment the parent did not expect. A teacher says a child is quiet in discussions, or still finding written reflection hard, and by the weekend the family is collecting tutor numbers from a building WhatsApp group. Nothing about that comment required a hire. It required a follow-up question to the teacher, which almost nobody asks in the meeting itself because the queue is moving.

The second pressure point is the long summer break, when families decide to 'use the time'. A structured hour every day of a primary child's holiday is the clearest case of over-tutoring we see, and it tends to arrive with the best intentions. The third is the exhibition year, where the visible output makes parents nervous on their child's behalf. The fourth is a mid-year move, which in Indian international schools happens more often than people assume, because parents relocate for work between Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and children change systems in the middle of a unit of inquiry.

Families ask us about schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We cannot tell you what any individual school runs or expects, and any tutor who claims inside knowledge of a school's practice is overselling.

What is common across international primary classrooms in India is a report written in comments rather than marks. Read the comments twice before you act on them. Then ask the teacher which single thing they would change if they could.
items: The first parent-teacher meeting drives most hiring decisions, often within two days
The long summer break is where holiday over-scheduling usually begins
A mid-year move between cities disrupts a unit of inquiry, not a syllabus
Reports come as comments, not marks; read them twice before acting
Ask the teacher for the one change they would make, and start there

contentBlocks.heading: Home Classes, Online or Hybrid: What Suits a Child Under Twelve?
contentBlocks.body:
For most primary children, home classes work best, online works in short bursts from roughly age nine, and a hybrid week is the quiet way to cut total hours without cutting support. That is the whole comparison in one sentence, and the reasoning matters more than the verdict.

A home tutor sitting beside a young child sees what a screen cannot: the pencil grip, the pause before a word, the eyes drifting to the window at minute eighteen, the quiet guess made to end the question. Physical objects still do heavy lifting at this age, and counters, number lines and a real book on the table are hard to replicate remotely. Home lessons also mean no travel for the child, which is the single biggest argument for them in Indian cities. A home tutor absorbs the traffic instead of the eight-year-old.

Online earns its place in three situations. The child is in the upper PYP years and can hold attention on a screen with an adult in the room. The family lives where local primary supply is thin, as it often is in Dehradun, Kanpur or Ludhiana. Or the specific need is spoken language practice, which travels well over a call. Below roughly age nine, online sessions need so much parental supervision that the parent is effectively teaching, and if that is the case you should ask why you are paying for the middle layer.

A hybrid week is often the honest compromise: one home visit for the work that needs a person in the room, one short online check-in for practice, and nothing else. It also makes stopping easier, because dropping the online half is a smaller decision than ending the arrangement. Whichever mode you choose, the quality of the tutor's questioning matters more than the medium, and no mode makes a tutor worth having if the child did not need one.
items: Home classes suit younger PYP children: no travel, physical materials, visible body language
Online suits upper primary, thin local supply, or spoken language practice
A hybrid week trims total hours while keeping one person in the room
Below roughly age nine, online needs so much supervision the parent teaches anyway
Screen fatigue is real when the school day already involves devices

contentBlocks.heading: What to Check Before a Home Tutor Sits With Your Seven-Year-Old in India
contentBlocks.body:
Check identity, check experience with this age group specifically, and then check the things no platform can see for you. Verification on IB Gram means a profile is reviewed before it goes live: identity documents, claimed teaching experience and references, and the subjects and stages the tutor says they can teach. That is a floor, not a finished answer, and any service that presents vetting as the end of your responsibility is telling you something about itself.

What you check yourself falls into two parts. The first is safeguarding, and it is not negotiable for a primary-age child. Home sessions happen in a shared room with the door open, not behind a closed bedroom door. An adult is in the flat throughout, even if not in the room. The tutor does not take the child anywhere, does not message the child directly, and does not use the child's phone or account. Society gate entry and visitor records should run normally rather than being waived because it is inconvenient. None of this implies suspicion of a particular person. It is simply how sessions with young children should be arranged everywhere.

The second part is fit, which matters more at seven than at seventeen. Ask the tutor what they do when a child refuses to start. Ask how long they expect a session to hold attention, and listen for whether the answer is honest or flattering. Watch the trial from the next room and notice whether the tutor waits after asking a question. Then ask the child afterwards, in a neutral way, what they did. A child who cannot tell you anything about the hour has been talked at.

One more check, the one parents skip: ask what would make the tutor recommend ending the arrangement. A tutor who has no answer has never considered it.
items: Profiles are reviewed for identity, references and the stages actually taught
Shared room, open door, an adult in the flat, gate entry as normal
No direct messaging to the child and no taking the child anywhere
In the trial, watch whether the tutor waits after asking a question
Ask what would make this tutor recommend stopping, and judge the answer

contentBlocks.heading: When Do IB PYP Private Tutors in India Genuinely Help?
contentBlocks.body:
In four or five recognisable situations, and not many others. IB PYP private tutors in India help most clearly when a child has moved mid-year from a very different system into an inquiry-led classroom and is fluent in procedures but lost in open-ended tasks. They help when the class teacher has already identified a specific reading or number gap, has tried in-class support, and has told you plainly that short, regular reinforcement at home would speed things up. They help when English is not the language of the household and the child is behind in speaking rather than in thinking. They help after a long absence through illness, where the child is capable and simply missed weeks. And they help, sometimes, where a learning difference has been identified and the family wants a tutor who works alongside the school's plan rather than inventing a parallel one.

Notice what those cases share. Somebody outside the family, who sees the child in a classroom every day, has described a concrete difficulty. The goal can be written in one sentence. And there is an end point that both of you can recognise.

Now the situations that feel identical to worried parents and are not. A report comment saying the child could contribute more in discussions is a personality observation, and hiring a one to one PYP tutor for it usually produces a child who performs confidence in one room and stays quiet in the other. A cousin's percentage marks in another board are not a benchmark, because the PYP publishes no grades to compare them against. A parent's own anxiety about the Diploma Programme, nine years away, is real but should not be paid for by a nine-year-old's evenings. Wanting a head start is the weakest reason of all.

And there is a fifth non-reason worth naming: everyone else in the building has a tutor. That is the one families find hardest to argue with, and the one that deserves the least weight.
items: A mid-year move from a very different system into inquiry-led learning
A specific gap the class teacher has named after trying in-class support
A household language gap showing up in speaking rather than thinking
Recovery after a long illness, where the child is capable but missed weeks
Not a reason: a quiet-in-discussion comment, a cousin's marks, or a head start

contentBlocks.heading: The Warning Signs of Over-Tutoring, and the Review That Asks You to Stop
contentBlocks.body:
The clearest warning sign is a child who has no unscheduled afternoon in the week. Count it honestly: school hours, travel, homework, sport, music, language class, and then the tutor. If there is no block of time in which a primary child may be bored, the load is too heavy regardless of how well each activity is going. Other signs come in order. Stomach aches on tuition days. A child who asks how many more sessions are left. Work produced for the tutor that is visibly better than work produced alone, which usually means the tutor is doing the thinking. Reluctance to read for pleasure, the first thing to disappear when reading becomes a task. And a household where the tutor knows most about the child's learning, which means the school conversation has gone quiet.

Keep hours honest with a cap you set before you start, not after. For a PYP child, we would not advise more than two paid sessions a week, of thirty to forty-five minutes each, in one area at a time. Below age seven, one short session a week is usually the ceiling. Write the cap down and tell the tutor what it is, because a cap that only lives in your head drifts upward one week at a time.

Then run a review every six weeks, out loud, with the tutor present for the last part:

1. Say in one sentence what you hired for, without adding anything new.
2. Ask the class teacher whether they can see a difference in the classroom.
3. Ask the child what they would do with a free Wednesday evening.
4. Choose one of three things: stop, continue unchanged for one more block, or change tutor.

Stopping is the default option on that list, not the failure option. Among IB PYP private tutors in India working through this platform, raising it first is part of the job once the goal has been met or the child is clearly carrying too much. A tutor who has never suggested ending sessions tells you something. Progress here looks like a child reading something nobody asked them to read, or explaining their own method unprompted. Nobody can promise that by a date.
items: No unscheduled afternoon in the week is the strongest signal to cut back
A cap set in advance: two short sessions weekly, one area at a time
Under age seven, one short weekly session is usually the sensible ceiling
Review every six weeks and treat stopping as the default outcome
A tutor who never suggests stopping has not been watching the child
Real progress shows as unprompted reading and self-explained method

contentBlocks.heading: Before You Book: What to Ask the School First in India
contentBlocks.body:
The school is free, sees your child every day and has already formed a view. Ask there first. Request a short meeting with the class teacher rather than raising it in the parent-teacher queue, and bring one question: what is the specific difficulty, described in terms of what the child does, not what the child is. Then ask what the school will do about it in class over the next few weeks, whether any in-school reading or language support exists, and whether the PYP coordinator should be part of the conversation. Ask how you will both know in six weeks whether it has worked. Most families who do this properly find they do not need to hire anyone, because a teacher who has been asked a precise question usually acts on it.

If you have done that and the difficulty is still there, then a tutor is a reasonable next step. Prepare three things before the first session: the teacher's description in their own words, a sample of the child's recent work done without help, and your cap on hours. Tell the tutor the cap in the first conversation. A tutor who argues you up from it has answered your most important question for free.

The first session should be mostly listening and watching. Expect the tutor to read with the child, set one or two small tasks, and talk to you for a few minutes at the end about what they noticed rather than what they plan to sell. A short written note after each session is more useful than a monthly report at this age, because primary children change quickly.

Families who come to IB Gram looking for IB PYP private tutors in India are welcome to use the consultation purely to test whether they need one. That is a legitimate use of it, and a personal tutor for PYP work is only worth arranging once the school route has genuinely been tried.
items: Ask the class teacher for the difficulty described as behaviour, not as character
Ask what the school will change in class over the next six weeks
Bring the teacher's words, unaided sample work, and your hours cap
Expect a short note after each session rather than a monthly summary
Use a free consultation to test whether you need a tutor at all

faqs.question: Does my PYP child actually need a private tutor?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and that is the most useful sentence on this page. The Primary Years Programme publishes no grades and sets no external examinations, so there is no score to raise and no deadline pressing on a nine-year-old. Tuition earns its place when somebody who sees your child in class every day has named a specific difficulty and the school has already tried something. If your reason is a vague feeling, a comparison with another child, or worry about the Diploma Programme years away, start with a conversation at school instead of a booking.

faqs.question: What should I ask the class teacher and the PYP coordinator before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions, in this order. What exactly is the difficulty, described as something the child does rather than something the child is? What has the school already tried in class this term? What will the school do about it over the next six weeks? And how will we both know whether it has worked? Ask for a short meeting rather than raising it in the parent-teacher queue, where the line is moving and nobody can think. Many families find that a precise question to a teacher solves the problem without any hiring at all.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of private tuition are too many for a child of eight?
faqs.answer: For a child of eight, more than two short paid sessions a week is usually too many. We would suggest a cap of two sessions of thirty to forty-five minutes, in one area at a time, and below age seven a single short weekly session. Set that cap before you start and tell the tutor what it is. Caps that exist only in a parent's head drift upward by one session at a time, usually after a report or a sibling comparison, and nobody notices until the child has no free afternoon left.

faqs.question: What are the warning signs that my child is doing too much?
faqs.answer: The clearest sign is a week with no unscheduled afternoon in it. After that, watch for stomach aches or delays on tuition days, a child asking how many sessions remain, reading for pleasure quietly disappearing, and work produced with the tutor that is visibly better than work produced alone. That last one usually means the tutor is doing the thinking. One more signal is structural: if the tutor has become the adult who knows most about your child's learning, the conversation with the school has gone quiet and should be restarted.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than online lessons for a child under ten?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for children under about nine or ten. A home tutor in the room sees the pencil grip, the pause before a word and the quiet guess made to end a question, and can put physical counters, number lines or a real book on the table. Online below that age tends to need so much parental supervision that the parent ends up teaching while paying someone else to watch. From roughly age nine, short online sessions work well, particularly for spoken language practice or where local supply is thin.

faqs.question: How long should a PYP home tuition arrangement run before we review it?
faqs.answer: Six weeks, then a real review rather than a polite one. Say in one sentence what you hired for, ask the class teacher whether anything has changed in the classroom, ask your child what they would do with a free evening, and then choose between stopping, continuing unchanged for one more block, or changing tutor. Treat stopping as the default rather than the failure option. Primary children change quickly, and an arrangement that made sense in August can be pure habit by November if nobody checks.

faqs.question: Our daughter moved from a CBSE school into the PYP in Gachibowli mid-year. Is that a reason to hire?
faqs.answer: It is one of the few genuine reasons, though often for a shorter period than families expect. A child arriving from a procedure-heavy system into inquiry-led learning is frequently strong at computation and lost in open tasks, and a few weeks of one-to-one work on explaining reasoning, planning a piece of writing and asking questions can settle it. Set an end point at the start. In Hyderabad, families in Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kondapur generally find someone close enough for short weekday sessions, which keeps the disruption small.

faqs.question: Should a tutor ever tell us to stop paying for sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a good one will say it first. A tutor working with a primary child should raise the question the moment the original goal has been met, or when the child is visibly carrying too much across the week. That duty is part of the job at this age, not a courtesy. If a tutor has never once suggested reducing frequency or ending the arrangement, ask them directly what would make them recommend it. An answer that does not exist tells you the person has been teaching the timetable rather than watching the child.

faqs.question: Is private tuition a sensible spend at primary level at all?
faqs.answer: Only against a named problem, and it is worth being clear-eyed about the economics. Fees at this level are quoted per session and vary by city, by the tutor's experience and by how far they travel, so ask about the basis rather than the number: what a session includes, what happens if you pause for a school break, and how notice works. Then ask what the same money and the same hours would do if spent on books, an unhurried evening or a weekend activity the child chose. Sometimes that is the better answer.

faqs.question: We live in Whitefield and the school run eats the evening. Does that change the home or online decision?
faqs.answer: It changes it a great deal. If the daily commute already takes a large part of the evening, adding a tutor who also travels across Bengaluru simply moves the problem. Look for a home tutor living within your own area, so the visit does not depend on a long crossing from Indiranagar or Koramangala at peak hour, or run a hybrid week with one short online session. The same reasoning applies between Bandra and Powai, or across Pune from Hinjewadi to Kharadi. Nearer usually beats better at primary level.

faqs.question: My child is in the PYP exhibition year. Can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: Only in ways that leave the work entirely the child's own. In the final PYP year students complete the exhibition, which is meant to be their inquiry, their questions and their conclusions. A tutor may discuss the topic, ask questions that sharpen a line of thinking, and teach a skill such as note-taking or structuring a talk, which the child then applies alone. A tutor who offers to research it, draft it or rehearse it into a polished performance is offering something you should refuse, and the school would refuse it too.

faqs.question: What if we stop and the worry comes back?
faqs.answer: Then you restart, which is much easier than never having stopped. Keep the tutor's details, tell them honestly why you are pausing, and agree that you may return after a term. Most families who stop find the worry was carried by the arrangement itself rather than by the child, and it fades within a few weeks. If it does not, you now have better evidence than you had the first time: you know what changed while the sessions ran, what held afterwards, and what the school observed in between.

acceptedAnswer.text: Probably not, and that is the most useful sentence on this page. Ask for a short meeting rather than raising it in the parent-teacher queue, where the line is moving and nobody can think. Many families find that a precise question to a teacher solves the problem without any hiring at all.

A small online group sits between them and does one thing the others cannot, which is give a young child someone to think out loud with.
