h1: IB PYP Online Tutors in India: Age Limits and Screen Reality
heroTitle: Online PYP Tutoring in India, Assessed Honestly
heroSubtitle: Online tutoring suits some primary children and fails others, and age decides it more often than subject or tutor does. This page sets out the ages a screen can hold, the ages it cannot, the supervision every lesson needs, and the point at which you should insist on a person in the room.
introSummary: IB PYP online tutors in India teach primary children over video, usually in short one-to-one sessions built around reading, number sense and the unit of inquiry the child is already doing at school. Whether that works depends almost entirely on the child's age. Below about seven, a screen rarely holds a child long enough to teach anything, and an adult ends up teaching the lesson while the tutor watches. Between seven and nine it can work in short bursts with someone sitting alongside. From roughly nine to eleven, most children can use a video lesson properly. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from ages 3 to 12, so no single answer covers the whole programme. Read the age sections before you book, and be willing to choose a home tutor instead.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a request for IB PYP online tutors in India start with the child's age?
contentBlocks.body:
It starts with the age, not the subject. Before a single profile is shortlisted, IB Gram asks how old the child is, which year of the Primary Years Programme (PYP) they are in, what the class teacher has actually said, and which adult will be in the house during lessons. Those four answers decide whether online is sensible at all, and for a younger child the honest reply is often that it is not.

Most requests for IB PYP online tutors in India arrive with a worry attached rather than a subject. The child reads slowly. The child cries over maths homework. The child has moved from a CBSE school and the inquiry work makes no sense to anyone at home. A parent in Jaipur described a nine-year-old who could decode words fluently but could not answer a single question about what she had just read. That is a real problem, and it is one a screen can work on. A five-year-old who cannot yet form letters is a different problem, and a video call is the wrong tool for it.

The practical questions come next, because they decide more than people expect. Which device, and is it on a table or on a bed? Is there a corner of the flat where the child can sit without a younger sibling climbing on them? Who can stay within earshot for the whole session, every week, not only the first one? A family that cannot answer the last question should not book an online slot for a primary child.

After that, shortlisting. Profiles that are verified and match the age and the request are sent across, a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and lessons run at home, online or hybrid depending on what suits. Availability is subject to tutor schedules and the slot you can hold on a weekday evening. If the fit is wrong after a few sessions, ask for a different match. And if the trial shows a child who simply will not work with a screen, say so and switch to a home tutor.
items: 1. Send the child's age, PYP year group and what the class teacher has said.
2. Answer the practical questions: device, room, connection and which adult stays nearby.
3. Read a shortlist of verified profiles matched to that age, not only the subject.
4. Run a trial of twenty to thirty minutes and watch how the child responds.
5. Agree a short weekly slot, or agree that a home tutor is better.
6. Review after four to six weeks and change the tutor or the mode.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP ages 3 to 12 online: which years a screen can hold
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet. Children work through units of inquiry rather than chapters, the ten attributes of the IB learner profile run across everything, and in the final year students complete the PYP exhibition. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades.

That structure matters for the screen question because there is no syllabus to march through. A tutor cannot fall back on covering the next chapter, which is the thing online delivery does most easily. What a PYP tutor works on instead is reading, number sense, curiosity and the ability to explain a thought out loud. Those are conversational and observational, and observation is exactly what a camera degrades.

Across the nursery and early primary years, ages three to six, a video lesson rarely holds. The child looks at their own face, at the mouse, at a sibling walking past. Anything the tutor asks for has to be fetched, opened or explained again by an adult, and within ten minutes that adult is teaching the lesson while the tutor watches. By seven or eight, short sessions become possible, but only with someone sitting alongside and a timer that ends the lesson at twenty-five minutes rather than when the content runs out.

From roughly nine upwards the picture changes. A ten-year-old can open a document, type an answer, scroll back to something the tutor marked last week and say out loud that they are lost. In the exhibition year, online support is genuinely useful: shaping a research question, narrowing a topic, structuring a presentation and rehearsing it are all conversations, and conversations travel well over video. The exhibition must remain the student's own work, so a tutor's job there is to question, not to write.
items: Ages 3 to 6: online rarely works; the adult ends up teaching the lesson.
Ages 7 to 8: workable in twenty-five minute bursts with an adult sitting alongside.
Ages 9 to 11: most children can hold a video lesson and work on screen.
Exhibition year: research, narrowing a topic and rehearsing all travel well over video.
Six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, not a syllabus to be covered.
No external examinations and no published PYP grades, so progress is judged differently.

contentBlocks.heading: What can a PYP tutor actually teach a seven-year-old through a screen?
contentBlocks.body:
Less than most parents assume. Through a screen a seven-year-old can be taught reading aloud, comprehension, spelling patterns and some number work. What cannot be taught is anything that needs a hand beside theirs: pencil grip, letter formation, laying out a subtraction, cutting and folding a shape. Those need a person in the room.

Reading is the strongest case for online work at this age. The tutor hears every hesitation, every substituted word, every guess made from the first letter, and can stop the child mid-sentence in a way a parent listening from the kitchen cannot. Comprehension follows the same logic. A shared text on screen, a question, a pause long enough to be slightly uncomfortable, and then a better question. None of that needs physical materials, and a good tutor can run it for twenty minutes without the child noticing the time.

Number sense sits halfway. Counters, a number line, coins and a measuring tape do most of the teaching in early primary maths, and a tutor cannot place them on your table. What works is an agreement: the tutor sends a short list on the morning of the lesson, and an adult sets those objects out before the child sits down. What does not work is a tutor sharing a bright animated screen and calling it handling quantity. If the child is still counting on fingers to add within twenty, that gap usually closes faster at the kitchen table with a home tutor.

It helps to be clear about what this stage is for. IB Mathematics AA and AI, IB Physics, IB Chemistry, IB Biology, IB Economics and IB English A are years away, and nothing in the PYP is preparation for them in the usual sense. The foundation a primary tutor builds is narrower and more durable: fluent reading, a feel for quantity, handwriting that does not hurt, and the habit of explaining why an answer is what it is.
items: Reading aloud works well online: the tutor hears every hesitation and substitution.
Comprehension talk works: questions about a shared text need no physical materials.
Handwriting and pencil grip do not work on screen; they need a hand alongside.
Number sense needs objects on the table, set out by an adult beforehand.
Spelling patterns, word families and vocabulary transfer to a screen without much loss.
Later subjects such as IB Mathematics AA and AI are years away; foundations come first.

contentBlocks.heading: Where in India a screen beats a commute for a primary child
contentBlocks.body:
IB PYP online tutors in India are worth most where the local pool of primary specialists is thin, and that is a real map rather than a slogan. In southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai often find that the tutors advertising locally are set up for board exam coaching for older students. A parent looking for an IB PYP online tutor in Chennai usually has choices within a few kilometres of Adyar or Anna Nagar. A parent in Madurai may have none in the city at all.

The same pattern runs through central and western India. Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad all have international school families and very few primary inquiry specialists, so online widens the pool sharply. In Kolkata and eastern India, a family in Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore or Rajarhat can usually find someone willing to come to the flat, while families in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi or Patna often cannot. An IB PYP online tutor in Kolkata is a convenience. In Guwahati it may be the only option there is.

In Gujarat, Ahmedabad has clusters of international school families around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close enough for a tutor to travel on a good evening, while Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot are thinner. Families asking for an IB PYP online tutor in Ahmedabad are usually choosing between a nearby generalist and a distant primary specialist. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR the same question repeats in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur.

Inside the big metros the argument flips for young children. If you are in Delhi NCR, in Powai or Bandra, in Bengaluru, in Hyderabad around Gachibowli, or in Pune, a home tutor can usually reach you, and for a child under nine that is almost always the better call. Searches for an IB PYP online tutor in Mumbai or an IB PYP online tutor in Bangalore are common anyway, and parents in Delhi, Hyderabad and Pune ask exactly the same thing. Online earns its place in a metro mainly when evening traffic between the tutor's area and yours makes a weekday visit unreliable, or when the specialist you want lives in another city.
items: Kochi, Coimbatore, Mysuru and Madurai: few primary inquiry specialists advertising locally.
Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna: online is often the only realistic option.
Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway: a nearby generalist against a distant specialist.
Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Goa and Nashik: school families, thin primary supply.
Chandigarh, Mohali, Jaipur, Lucknow and Dehradun: the same thin-supply question repeats.
Delhi NCR, Powai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune: a home tutor can usually reach you.

contentBlocks.heading: School screen hours in India, and what is left for an evening session
contentBlocks.body:
The school year for primary children in India usually runs from April or June through to March or May depending on the school, with a long summer break, a shorter break around Diwali and a winter break. Reports go home two or three times a year, and parent teacher conferences sit near the end of each term. There are no external examinations and no published PYP grades, so those conversations, and the written comments on a report, are the only formal evidence a parent gets.

Screens are already part of that day. Primary classrooms at international schools in India use interactive boards, tablets or laptops are timetabled into several lessons a week, homework and reading logs are often posted to a portal, and the child may watch something on a device during a long bus ride. By the time a nine-year-old is home at half past four, the eyes have done a full day's work. Adding an evening of PYP online classes in India on top of all that is a real cost rather than a neutral choice, and it is the strongest single argument for a home tutor for younger children.

Expectations also differ from what many Indian parents grew up with. There is no rank, no percentage and no exam to revise for. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School and Pathways World School meet the same pattern, and the first instinct is often to hire someone to produce marks that do not exist. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Timing matters more than families expect. The weeks after a report goes home are when most enquiries arrive, and they are a sensible moment to start, because the teacher's comments give a tutor something specific to work on. The weeks before the exhibition in the final PYP year are another. The worst time to begin is the fortnight before a long break, when four sessions are followed by a month of nothing and the child comes back having lost the thread.
items: Reports two or three times a year; conferences near the end of each term.
No rank, no percentage and no exam to revise for in the PYP.
Interactive boards and timetabled device periods already fill part of the school day.
Start soon after a report, not in the fortnight before a long break.
The exhibition year is the one stretch where online support clearly earns its place.

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid for a child of eight in India?
contentBlocks.body:
For a child of eight the ranking is usually home first, hybrid second, online third, and that order reverses as the child gets older. A home tutor sits beside the child and sees the pencil, the posture and the exact second attention goes. An online tutor sees a framed head and whatever the camera happens to be pointed at. A hybrid week, one home session plus one short online session, keeps a good tutor when they cannot travel twice.

Home tuition is the default for the youngest children for an unglamorous reason: a person in the room can redirect a wandering child without saying a word. A home tutor also sees the working as it is produced, which is where primary maths errors live, not in the answer. The cost is travel. Evening traffic in most Indian cities can stretch a short trip badly, and a tutor who arrives late twice in a month is a tutor who will quietly give up the slot.

An online PYP tutor earns their place on reach and reliability. The specialist who has taught early reading for years may live in another city, and no amount of local searching will produce them. Online lessons also survive the monsoon, an unwell tutor and an exam week at the tutor's own school. What they cost is the physical channel: the tutor cannot hand the child a pencil, cannot point at the page, and cannot easily tell the difference between a child thinking and a child lost.

Hybrid is the compromise worth arranging more often than families do. One weekly home visit for the physical work, handwriting, layout and manipulatives, then one shorter midweek online session for reading aloud and a check on the week's homework. The child gets a person in the room where it matters and the tutor does not have to cross the city twice. For most families with a child between eight and eleven, that shape holds together across a full school year better than either extreme does.
items: Home tutor: sees the pencil, the posture and the second attention slips away.
Online tutor: reach and reliability, paid for by losing the physical channel.
Hybrid: one home visit for physical work, one short online session midweek.
Under nine, home first; from nine to eleven, online becomes a fair choice.
A tutor who arrives late twice a month will quietly give up the slot.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor your young child meets only on a screen?
contentBlocks.body:
You check two different things, and only one of them is the platform's job. Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they are shortlisted, which covers identity and the qualifications and experience a tutor claims. What verification cannot cover is the part you care about most with a young child: whether this adult is any good with eight-year-olds. So there are checks the platform runs, and checks only you can run.

Ask for primary experience specifically, and ask what it consisted of. A tutor who has taught Diploma Programme (DP) Physics for years is not a PYP tutor, and a confident answer about criteria tells you nothing about whether they can hold a child's attention for twenty minutes. Better questions: what does a first session with a nine-year-old look like, how do you end a session that has gone badly, and what do you do when a child says nothing for two minutes?

Then the safeguarding rules, which matter more online than at home because you are not in the room by default. Cameras on at both ends for the whole session. The lesson happens in a shared family space, not a bedroom with a closed door. No private messaging, calls or social media contact between tutor and child outside the platform, ever, and homework and feedback come to the parent. Ask whether sessions are recorded, who holds the recording and for how long, and decline if the answer is vague.

Watch the trial with your own eyes rather than reading a report about it afterwards. Does the tutor speak to the child or about the child? Do they wait after a question, or fill the silence themselves? Does your child look at the tutor's face or at their own thumbnail in the corner? An online tutor for young children who cannot get a first smile in ten minutes is unlikely to get one in week six. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match, and do it early rather than after a whole term.
items: Cameras on at both ends, for the whole session, in both directions.
Lessons in a shared family space, never a bedroom with the door shut.
No private messaging or calls between tutor and child outside the platform.
Ask what a first session with a nine-year-old actually looks like.
Ask who holds any recording and for how long; vagueness is itself an answer.

contentBlocks.heading: Ages nine to eleven: what changes for online PYP tutoring in India
contentBlocks.body:
Somewhere between nine and eleven most children cross a line that makes online tutoring workable. They read to learn rather than learning to read. They can hold attention for half an hour without an adult resetting them. They can operate a document, a scroll bar and a mute button. And they can say out loud that they do not understand.

That last one is the real threshold. What IB PYP online tutors in India can do at nine or ten and cannot do at six is rely on the child to report their own confusion. A six-year-old who is lost goes quiet, or agrees with everything, or starts talking about a dog. In the room, a tutor reads that in a second from the shoulders and the pencil. On a screen, the same child looks like a child who is listening carefully. The lesson continues, the tutor is pleased, and nothing has been learned.

Below that line the failure is predictable. The adult in the room becomes the teacher, repeating every instruction and fetching every object, and the family is paying a tutor to supervise a parent. Attention drains into the interface rather than the work. And the physical part of primary learning, forming letters, laying out columns, handling counters, does not cross a connection at all. This is why a page about online tutoring should be willing to talk a parent out of it. For a six-year-old who cannot yet write a neat lowercase a, book a home tutor or wait a year.

Screen time deserves a harder look than it usually gets, and the argument is not that screens are bad. It is about stacking. A child who has had a smartboard lesson, a timetabled device period, a bus ride with a tablet and a homework portal to check has already spent much of the day looking at a lit rectangle. A forty-minute evening video lesson lands on top of that, in the hour when a primary child should be outdoors or reading on paper. If you are choosing between a home tutor and PYP online tuition for a child under ten and everything else is equal, the screen count breaks the tie.
items: Reading to learn, not learning to read: the clearest single sign of readiness.
Can say plainly that they do not understand, without being prompted first.
Holds attention about thirty minutes without an adult resetting them halfway.
Opens a document, scrolls and types without narrating every click aloud.
Count the day's existing screen hours before adding an evening video lesson.

contentBlocks.heading: When to refuse online outright and insist on a person in the room
contentBlocks.body:
There are cases where the right advice is to refuse online outright, and IB PYP online tutors in India who are worth hiring will say so before they take the booking. Refuse it if the child is under about seven. Refuse it if the presenting problem is handwriting, pencil grip, letter formation or the physical layout of written maths. Refuse it if no adult can be within earshot for every session.

Refuse it too if the only device is a phone, if the child would have to sit in a bedroom with the door shut, or if the household cannot find a twenty-five minute window that is not already noisy. And refuse it if the child is genuinely distressed by the camera. Some children are. Pushing through that teaches a young child that being tutored is something unpleasant, which is a more expensive problem than the one you started with.

Where online does go ahead, judge it on evidence rather than mood, which is harder in a programme with no external examinations and no published PYP grades. Six weeks is a fair window. By then a child working on reading should stop at fewer words on an unseen page, reread less, and answer a question about what happened without going back to hunt for it. A child working on number should start a task without an adult restarting them. A child working on inquiry should mention their unit at the dinner table unprompted.

If none of that has shifted in six weeks, change something: the tutor, the time of day, the length of the session, or the mode. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and in the PYP there is no grade to guarantee, so anyone selling an outcome is selling something they cannot deliver. The honest ceiling is this. Online tutoring can build reading fluency, number confidence and the habit of explaining. It cannot replace a person beside a young child, and it cannot fix a problem the school has not yet been asked about.
items: Refuse online below about seven; the adult in the room ends up teaching.
Refuse it when the problem is handwriting, grip or letter formation.
Refuse it when no adult can be within earshot for every single session.
Six weeks is a fair window to see reading or number confidence shift.
Without grades, judge fluency, independence and unprompted talk about the unit.

contentBlocks.heading: Before the first online PYP session in India: the room, the adult, the timer
contentBlocks.body:
Booking IB PYP online tutors in India takes about ten minutes of preparation and it is worth doing properly. Send the child's age and PYP year, one or two sentences of what the class teacher said, the worry in your own words, and the two or three evening windows you can genuinely hold each week. Say which device you have and where in the house it will sit.

Then set the room up before the first session rather than during it. A table, not a bed and not a sofa. The device at the child's eye level so the tutor sees a face rather than a ceiling fan. Paper and a pencil in shot, tilted so the tutor can see the page when asked. Headphones if there are siblings around. A glass of water within reach, because a child who leaves the chair at minute twelve often does not come back. And a timer, set by you, so the session ends on time rather than when the material runs out.

An adult stays within earshot. Not hovering behind the chair, not answering for the child, just close enough to hear the tone of the lesson and to step in if the connection or the child falls over. For the first two or three sessions, sit where you can see the screen. After that most parents can move to the next room and leave the door open.

The first session will not teach much, and it should not try to. A good tutor spends it finding out what the child can already do: listening to them read something unseen, watching them attempt a few questions, asking what they are working on in their current unit of inquiry. You should get a short note afterwards saying what was found and what the next few weeks will work on. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and if the match is wrong you can ask for a different one.
items: A table, not a bed; the device set at the child's eye level.
Paper and pencil in shot, tilted so the tutor can see the page.
A timer set by the parent, so the session ends on time.
An adult within earshot, close enough to hear the tone of the lesson.
A short written note after each session saying what the tutor found.

faqs.question: Is my six-year-old too young for an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly, yes. At six, a video lesson usually turns into an adult in the room repeating every instruction while the tutor watches, and the physical work a six-year-old needs, letter formation, pencil grip, handling counters, does not cross a connection. If the worry is real, a home tutor is the better spend, and very often the class teacher can address it first. Revisit the online question in two or three years, when the child can report their own confusion.

faqs.question: At what age does online PYP tutoring genuinely start to work?
faqs.answer: Around nine, and reliably by ten or eleven for most children. The change is not reading ability alone. It is that the child can hold attention for half an hour, operate a document without narrating every click, and tell the tutor plainly that they are lost. A child who does all three will get real value from a screen. A child who does none of them will not, whatever their age, and no tutor can compensate for that gap from another city.

faqs.question: How long should an online session with a primary child be?
faqs.answer: Twenty to thirty minutes for a seven or eight-year-old, and thirty to forty-five minutes for a nine to eleven-year-old. Set a timer and stop at it, even mid-task, because a lesson that runs until the content is finished teaches a child that sessions never end. Two short sessions a week almost always beat one long one at this age. An hour with a primary child on a screen is rarely an hour of actual work.

faqs.question: My child is already on screens all day at school. Does an evening online lesson make that worse?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is a fair reason to choose a home tutor instead. Primary classrooms use interactive boards, device periods are timetabled, homework often sits on a portal, and a long bus ride adds more. An evening video lesson stacks on top of all of it, in the hour a young child should be outdoors or reading on paper. If home and online are otherwise equal for your child, the screen count should decide it.

faqs.question: Do I have to sit with my child for the whole online lesson?
faqs.answer: You need to be within earshot every time, and in the room for the first two or three sessions. After that most parents can move next door and leave the door open. Being present is not about distrust. A primary child will lose the connection, drop the headphones or wander off, and somebody has to notice within a minute. What you should not do is answer for the child or repeat the tutor's questions in your own words.

faqs.question: We are in Coimbatore and nobody nearby teaches primary inquiry. Is online the answer?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the child is nine or older. In Coimbatore, Kochi, Madurai or Visakhapatnam the tutors advertising locally are usually set up for older students and board exam coaching, so going online widens the pool to people who have actually taught early reading. For a younger child, a capable local teacher who comes to the house still beats a distant specialist on a screen. Age decides this more than distance does.

faqs.question: Would a home tutor be better than an online tutor for a PYP child in Pune?
faqs.answer: In Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad or Delhi NCR a home tutor is usually the better choice for a child under nine, because local supply is reasonable and a person in the room does more at that age. Online becomes sensible when the specialist you want lives elsewhere, or when evening traffic between Hinjewadi or Kharadi and your area makes a weekday visit unreliable. A hybrid week, one visit plus one short call, often settles the argument.

faqs.question: How do I judge an online PYP tutor in a single trial session?
faqs.answer: Watch the child, not the tutor. Does the tutor talk to your child or about them? Do they leave silence after a question instead of filling it themselves? Does your child look at the tutor or at their own thumbnail? A good trial ends with the tutor telling you something specific they noticed, not a pitch. If there is no warmth in twenty minutes, there will not be any in week six either.

faqs.question: There are no grades in the PYP. How will I know online tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Judge fluency, independence and talk. Within about six weeks a child working on reading should stop at fewer words on an unseen page and answer a question about it without rereading. A child working on number should begin a task without being restarted. A child working on inquiry should mention their unit unprompted. The class teacher noticing a change is the strongest signal of all. If nothing shifts, change the tutor, the time or the mode.

faqs.question: My child cries or hides from the camera. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Stop, and do not push through it. Some primary children find being watched on video genuinely uncomfortable, and forcing the sessions teaches them that tutoring is unpleasant. Try one session with the camera off and audio only, or with you visible in frame beside them. If neither helps, switch to a tutor in the room. This is one of the clearest cases where online is the wrong tool and refusing it is the right call.

faqs.question: How do we keep a young child safe during an online lesson at home?
faqs.answer: Keep the lesson in a shared family space rather than a bedroom, with cameras on at both ends and the door left open. There should be no private messaging, calls or social media contact between tutor and child outside the platform, and all homework and feedback should come to you. Ask whether sessions are recorded, who keeps the recording and for how long. A tutor who is vague about any of this is telling you something.

h1: IB PYP Tuition in India: Usually the Answer Is Not Yet
heroTitle: Deciding About PYP Tuition in India
heroSubtitle: Most primary children in an IB school do not need paid tuition. Some genuinely do. This page sets out which situations call for a home tutor, what your child's class teacher and PYP coordinator should be asked to do first, and how to act on a worry without hiring anybody at all.
introSummary: IB PYP tuition in India is worth paying for in a small number of situations, and home tuition is the usual format when it is, but for most primary-age children the honest answer is not yet. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from ages three to twelve, sets no external examinations and publishes no grades, so there is no mark to rescue and no paper to drill. That changes what a decision to hire a home tutor is even based on. What follows is the set of worries that genuinely justify paying someone, the ones a conversation at school will settle faster and for nothing, a numbered sequence to work through before any money changes hands, and the case for waiting one full term before you decide.

contentBlocks.heading: What does IB Gram do with a PYP enquiry from India that may not need a tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
It asks questions until the worry has a shape, and then says whether a tutor is the right answer to it. Parents send a query or book a free consultation. What follows is a conversation about your child's year group, the school and board, what the class teacher has actually said, what you have seen at home over the past few months, what else the week already contains, where you live and which evenings are genuinely free.

For a Grade 10 student sitting a series in five months, those questions produce a shortlist quickly. For a seven-year-old they quite often produce a different conclusion. Nothing is wrong that a term and one honest conversation with the school will not settle, and home tuition would only add a second working day to a child who already has one.

The reason is the programme itself. The PYP organises learning around six transdisciplinary themes taught through units of inquiry, alongside the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, and there are no published PYP grades to read. So a request for IB PYP tuition in India cannot be tested against a mark the way a Diploma Programme (DP) request can. It has to be tested against a described behaviour: the child has stopped reading for pleasure, cries at homework three nights out of five, or joined mid-year from another system and cannot follow how the class works.

Where a tutor is warranted, IB Gram shortlists profiles that have been verified and that fit the child's age, the area of the worry, your locality and your free slots. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. Availability depends on level and schedule. And where a tutor is not warranted, you should expect to be told so, because a platform that agrees with every anxious parent is of no use to anyone.
items: 1. Send a query describing the worry as an observable behaviour, not as a grade
2. Answer questions on year group, school, board, locality, free evenings and existing activities
3. Hear a straight view on whether the school should be asked to act first
4. Receive verified profiles matched to the child's age and the worry, if warranted
5. Arrange a demo or trial session before agreeing to any weekly arrangement
6. Review after a few weeks, ask for a different match, or stop altogether

contentBlocks.heading: Ages three to twelve: which PYP years a worry is worth acting on
contentBlocks.body:
The PYP covers ages three to twelve, which is far too wide a band to treat as one decision. A worry about a four-year-old and a worry about an eleven-year-old in the exhibition year are different problems with different answers, and the hiring logic that fits one is wrong for the other.

Below about six, paid tuition is almost never the right move. What looks like a gap at that age is usually a difference of a few months in development, and children who look behind in the nursery and reception years routinely level out without anybody paying for anything. The exception is a suspected specific difficulty, which needs a proper assessment arranged through the school rather than a subject tutor working around it. A home tutor cannot diagnose, and should not try.

Between six and nine, most enquiries arrive. Reading and early number start to diverge visibly within a class, and a parent can see it at the dining table every evening. This is the band where the school's own intervention should come first and usually does: reading groups, a support teacher, a changed seating plan, a fortnight of targeted work. Ask what already exists before you buy a parallel version of it.

Between nine and twelve the useful work shifts towards independence, reading stamina and organising oneself, because that is what the next programme will demand. Students complete the PYP exhibition in the final year, and the exhibition must be the child's own work. A tutor who produces it has damaged the child and broken the school's rules in the same hour. If your child moves on to the Middle Years Programme (MYP) next, where every subject is assessed against four criteria (A to D) each scored 0 to 8 and the total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade, the preparation that matters now is the habit of finding out unaided, not content coverage.
items: Ages three to six: read together daily; paid tuition is almost never warranted
Ages six to nine: most enquiries arrive here, and most are answered by the school
Ages nine to twelve: independence and reading stamina matter more than covering content
Exhibition year: the work must be the child's own, whoever else is in the room
Any age: a suspected learning difficulty needs assessment, not a subject tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Is it a real subject gap, or simply where your child is at eight?
contentBlocks.body:
Three tests separate the two, and you can apply all three this week without paying anyone. Does the difficulty persist across months rather than a bad fortnight? Does it show up in more than one setting, at school and at home? And has the class teacher raised it independently, before you brought it up? A difficulty that fails all three tests is almost always ordinary variation at primary age.

Reading is where most worries start. A child of seven who still sounds out words is not in trouble. The same child at nine, still sounding out the same words, reading nothing voluntarily and avoiding books at home, is a different signal and worth acting on. With mathematics, counting on fingers at seven is normal and often sensible. A child who has practised number bonds for a year and still cannot say what six and four make without counting has a gap that will widen, because everything later is built on it.

Written English deserves a separate note in Indian classrooms. Plenty of children work in English at school and in Marathi, Tamil, Hindi or Gujarati at home, and their written English lags for a stretch. That is an exposure question, answered by reading volume and conversation, and paying for weekly grammar drills rarely touches it.

Then there are the subjects that should not be tutored at this stage at all. Science, social studies and the units of inquiry teach a child to ask and find out; coaching a nine-year-old through a unit produces a polished poster and a child who has learned that adults supply the answers. Note too that the subject specialisms families recognise, IB Mathematics AA and AI, IB Physics, IB Chemistry, IB Biology, IB Economics and IB English A, all belong to the Diploma Programme. None of them exists in the PYP. A tutor who sells that expertise for a nine-year-old has misread the programme, and that alone should end the conversation.
items: Persistence: the same difficulty visible across several months, not one difficult fortnight
Breadth: it appears at school and at home, not only in one room
Agreement: the class teacher raised it first, without being prompted by you
Language: lagging written English where another language is spoken at home is usually exposure
Warning sign: anyone offering Mathematics AA or Physics expertise to a nine-year-old

contentBlocks.heading: IB PYP tuition in India, region by region: where the decision actually changes
contentBlocks.body:
Where you live changes the answer more than most parents expect, because it changes what is realistically available and what an evening can hold. Across Delhi NCR, from South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka to Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, and out to Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad, families searching IB PYP tuition in Delhi usually have real choice at primary level. The constraint is not supply, it is the evening. A tutor crossing from Noida to South Delhi for a short primary slot will keep it for a month and then start rescheduling. Hire inside your own sector or suburb.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the same rule bites harder. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are close on a map and far apart at half past five, and Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are a separate travel world again. A family in Thane searching PYP tuition near me and a family in Worli doing the same are asking different questions. For a child of seven, the tutor who lives fifteen minutes away and arrives calm beats the better-credentialled one who arrives late and leaves early.

Bengaluru has depth: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road all have primary-experienced tutors, so IB PYP tuition in Bangalore is rarely a supply problem. Count the school run first, though, because a Whitefield child already spends a long stretch of the day in a bus. In Hyderabad the pool sits around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and the Financial District, and in Pune around Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Baner, Balewadi, Hinjewadi, Kharadi, Viman Nagar and Aundh, so IB PYP tuition in Hyderabad and IB PYP tuition in Pune both work well inside those pockets.

Chennai families in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Alwarpet and Perungudi find that IB PYP tuition in Chennai is workable, though OMR traffic decides the slot rather than the tutor. Across central and western India, in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad, the pool of tutors who have actually worked in a PYP classroom is thin, and so is it for families searching IB PYP tuition in Kolkata or IB PYP tuition in Ahmedabad. That thinness is where the waiting argument is strongest. Do not hire the only person available simply because they are the only person available.
items: Delhi NCR: hire within your own sector; cross-city evening slots quietly collapse by week five
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: a Powai tutor for a Powai child; the creek decides more than distance does
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road families should count the school bus before adding anything
Hyderabad and Pune: Gachibowli and Koregaon Park pools are strong, but shallow at primary level
Chennai and central India: thin local supply makes waiting or online the two honest options

contentBlocks.heading: The PYP school year in India, and the months that manufacture a panic
contentBlocks.body:
Most international schools here run an April to March year, though some follow an August start, so check yours before planning anything around a term. Whichever it is, the worry arrives on a predictable schedule: a few weeks after the first report of the year, and again in the weeks before the final reporting round. Those two windows produce the great majority of searches for IB PYP tuition in India, and a fair number of them are calendar effects rather than learning problems.

The report is the trigger. A PYP report comes back as descriptive comments about the units covered and the learner profile attributes, with no percentage and no rank. A parent who grew up with CBSE or ICSE mark sheets reads two pages of careful prose and genuinely cannot tell whether their child is fine. That uncertainty feels exactly like bad news. It usually is not. Before acting on it, read the report twice and underline only the sentences that describe something your child does or does not do, ignoring the ones that describe the unit.

Then use the conference properly. Parent-teacher and student-led conferences are short, and most of the time goes on pleasantries. Walk in with one question written down: compared with what you would expect of a child this age, where is she, and what one thing should we work on at home this term? A teacher who has forty other conversations that week will answer a specific question far better than an open one.

Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore ask versions of this every year. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Naming a school says nothing about which programme it runs or where it is.
items: First report of the year: comments, not percentages; read it twice before reacting at all
Conferences: arrive with one written question about your own child, not about the unit
The long summer: the cheapest intervention available is reading daily, for pleasure
Exhibition season: school deadlines rise, and outside help must stay off the work itself
Mid-year arrival: give one complete term before judging the child or the school

contentBlocks.heading: If you do hire: home classes, online or hybrid for a primary child?
contentBlocks.body:
The plain version, and it holds across the country. For a child under about nine, a home tutor in the room beats an online tutor on a screen, because a young child leaks information through posture, pencil grip and the half-second pause before an answer, and a camera loses most of it. For a child of ten or eleven who can already work alone for twenty minutes, online becomes genuinely viable and widens the choice of tutor far beyond your own locality. Hybrid sits between the two and works when the home visit is the anchor and the online slot is the top-up, not the reverse.

Home classes buy presence. The tutor sees the guess, the copying, the point at which attention goes, and can change what happens next without asking. They cost travel, which means the realistic pool is whoever can reach you before the child is tired, and in a heavy-traffic evening that pool is smaller than the search results suggest.

Online buys reach. For a family in Indore, Nashik or Raipur where nobody nearby has taught inside a PYP classroom, a short online session with someone who has is a better bet than a local tutor running photocopied worksheets. The price is supervision. A six or seven-year-old will not hold a screen alone, so an adult sits beside them for the whole session, and if nobody in the house can do that on a Tuesday evening, online is not actually available to you.

Hybrid is the compromise most families land on when the tutor they want lives across the city: one home session a week, plus a short online check-in midweek to keep the reading or the practice honest. It is also the sensible shape during monsoon weeks, when a home visit in Mumbai or Chennai can fall through with no notice at all.
items: Home tuition: strongest under nine, because the tutor sees hesitation a camera never catches
Online: viable from around ten, and the only real option where local primary supply is thin
Hybrid: one home session weekly plus a short online check-in between visits
Under six: neither mode; read with the child yourself and speak to the school
Any mode: keep sessions short and stop before the child is visibly tired

contentBlocks.heading: What to verify before a home tutor sits with your PYP child in India
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles have been verified before they reach you, and that verification is a floor rather than a verdict. It establishes that the person is who they say they are and has the background their profile claims. It cannot establish that they will be good with your particular seven-year-old, because nothing except a trial session can establish that.

So do your own checking, and do it in the first meeting rather than in month three. Sit in on the trial and watch the child, not the tutor. A good primary tutor gets a quiet child talking within ten minutes, asks far more than they explain, and leaves the child slightly pleased with themselves. A weak one talks for forty minutes while the child nods. You will know which you are watching without any special expertise.

Ask the credential question plainly. Someone who has taught primary children will mention units of inquiry and the learner profile without prompting, describe what a six-year-old can and cannot sit through, and ask you about sleep and screen time before asking about marks. Someone whose experience is Diploma Programme Chemistry will talk about syllabus, coverage and papers. Neither is dishonest, but only one of them is right for your child. Ask directly how many primary-age children they have taught one to one, and what they would do in the first session.

Safeguarding is the part parents skip because it feels rude. Do not skip it. Home sessions belong in a visible room with the door open and an adult somewhere in the flat. There should be no private messaging between tutor and child, no lifts, no sessions moved to the tutor's own house without you. Ask how they will tell you when the child has understood something rather than simply copied it, and listen for a concrete answer.
items: Sit through the trial and watch your child's face rather than the tutor's technique
Ask what the first session will contain before agreeing to book it
Keep home sessions in a visible room with the door open
No private messaging between tutor and child; every arrangement goes through you
Ask how the tutor tells understanding apart from a correct copied answer

contentBlocks.heading: When does a PYP child in India genuinely need tuition?
contentBlocks.body:
In four situations, broadly. A child who has moved into an IB school from CBSE, ICSE, a state board or another country and is lost in the method rather than the content. A child with a persistent reading or number difficulty that the school has already named and is already working on. A child who has missed a long stretch of school through illness or a family move. And a child whose confidence has collapsed to the point of refusing to try. Outside those four, IB PYP tuition in India is usually premature.

The board switch deserves the most patience. Students move into the IB from CBSE, ICSE and state boards, and back out again, and the differences they meet are real: criterion-referenced or command-term marking instead of a fixed answer key, coursework that carries genuine weight, wider reading and independent research, and much less emphasis on memorised derivations. A primary child does not meet criteria yet, but they meet the shape of it. A nine-year-old who has spent four years being told exactly what to memorise can look weak for a whole term purely because nobody has ever asked them a question with no single right answer. That is disorientation, not a gap, and it resolves. Give it a term before you spend anything.

Equally, be clear about what does not justify hiring. Being in the middle of the class. One unit that went badly. A teacher your child does not warm to. A cousin in another school who has three tutors' worth of evening classes. A worry that arrived in the same week as the report and has no history behind it.

And weigh the other side of the ledger, which parents rarely do. Every hour of tuition is an hour not spent reading for pleasure, playing, or being bored, and boredom at eight is not wasted time. The real risk with primary tuition is not the money. It is a child who learns at eight that school is a thing you need paid help to survive.
items: 1. Write the worry down as one observable behaviour, dated, in plain words
2. Email the class teacher and ask whether they see the same thing
3. Ask what the school is already doing, and what it will do next term
4. Ask the PYP coordinator what in-school support exists before any outside help
5. Change one thing at home: nightly reading, earlier bedtime, or fewer activities
6. Wait one full term, re-read your note, and decide again

contentBlocks.heading: What waiting one term actually costs in India, and what it usually saves
contentBlocks.body:
The fear underneath most primary enquiries is that a small gap now becomes a crisis at sixteen. Occasionally it does. Mostly it does not, because primary learning is not a ladder where a missed rung is permanent, and because the school is already working on the thing you have noticed.

What waiting costs is one term. What it buys is evidence. A worry still present in March, in the same words you wrote down in July, is a real worry and you can act on it with confidence. A worry that has quietly gone, as most do, is exactly why waiting exists. Write the note, date it, put it away, and take it out again at the end of the term. That single habit saves more families money and more children evenings than any advice about choosing tutors.

If you do hire, set the review terms before the first paid session, because there are no grades to point at later. Agree three observable signs: she reads a page without stopping, he attempts a problem before asking for help, she brings a book to you unprompted. Review at six to eight weeks. Not at six months, and not at the end of the year, by which time you will have paid for a habit rather than a result. If nothing has shifted at eight weeks, the answer is a different match or no tutor at all, and stopping is a perfectly respectable outcome.

Be honest about the limits too. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and in a programme with no published grades there is nothing to guarantee in the first place. A home tutor cannot replace an assessment the school has recommended, cannot compensate for a class that is not being taught well, and cannot make a tired child learn at half past seven in the evening after a long bus ride home.
items: Agree three observable signs of progress before the first paid session begins
Review at six to eight weeks, never at the end of the school year
A worry still present after a term, in identical words, is a genuine worry
Stopping is a legitimate result, and a good tutor will say so first
No tutor substitutes for an assessment the school has recommended

contentBlocks.heading: Acting on a worry about PYP tuition in India without hiring anyone
contentBlocks.body:
Almost all of the first step costs nothing and can be done this week. Write one paragraph describing what you see, with a date on it, using behaviour rather than judgement: not weak at maths, but cannot recall number bonds to ten without counting, still, in December. Email that paragraph to the class teacher and ask two questions. Do you see the same thing in class, and what is the school already doing about it?

The reply tells you most of what you need. A teacher who has not noticed anything and can describe your child's work in detail is usually telling you the truth. A teacher who says they have been watching it since August and has already put support in place has given you a plan you do not have to pay for. A vague reply is itself information, and that is the point at which the PYP coordinator is the right person to ask, because the coordinator can say what support exists in the school and who provides it.

Then change one thing at home and leave everything else alone. Reading together every night, an earlier bedtime, or dropping one weekday activity will each do more for a tired eight-year-old than an extra class. Give it a term.

If you still want to talk it through after that, book a free consultation and say plainly that you are not sure you need anyone. Bring the report, the teacher's reply and the week as it actually runs. IB Gram will ask about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, and if home tuition is warranted you will see verified profiles and can arrange a trial before committing to anything weekly.
items: Bring the latest report and any written comment from the class teacher
Bring the week as it stands, including every activity and the travel each involves
Bring the one behaviour that worries you, described without the word weak
Expect questions about board, locality, schedule and what the school has already done
Expect a trial session before any weekly home tuition is agreed

faqs.question: My child's PYP report has no grades. How do I know whether there is a problem at all?
faqs.answer: You judge it from described behaviour, not from a mark, because there is none to judge. Read the report twice and underline only the sentences that describe what your child does or does not do, ignoring those that describe the unit. Then ask the class teacher one direct question: compared with other children this age, where is she, and what should we work on at home? Vague reassurance is not an answer, and a specific question usually gets a specific reply.

faqs.question: What exactly should I ask the class teacher before I look for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask three things, in writing, so the teacher has time to think. First, do you see at school what we are seeing at home, described in one concrete sentence. Second, what is the school already doing about it, and since when. Third, what one thing should we do at home this term. Those answers will either give you a plan that costs nothing, or tell you the school has not noticed something real, which is itself the signal you were looking for.

faqs.question: What can the PYP coordinator do that a paid tutor cannot?
faqs.answer: The coordinator can change what happens for six hours a day, which no tutor can touch. They can arrange in-school support, ask a specialist teacher to observe, move a child into a different reading group, recommend a formal assessment, and hold the class teacher to a plan across the term. Go to the coordinator when the class teacher's reply has been vague, when the same issue has run across two teachers, or when you want to know what support the school provides before you buy a parallel version of it.

faqs.question: We have just moved from Dubai and my son has joined an IB school in Chennai. Should we arrange home tuition straight away?
faqs.answer: No, wait a term unless the school asks otherwise. A child who has changed country, school, friends and often language is dealing with all of that before any academic question. What looks like a learning gap in the first two months is usually disorientation, and it resolves without intervention in most cases. Use the term to set up a settled evening routine and to talk to the class teacher twice. If the same difficulty is still there in identical words at the end of it, a home tutor in Adyar or Nungambakkam becomes a reasonable next step.

faqs.question: Is there anything useful I can do about a worry without hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually more effective than tuition at this age. Read with your child every night, including books well below their level, since fluency comes from volume rather than difficulty. Talk about what you read instead of testing it. Drop one weekday activity to buy back an hour. Move bedtime earlier by twenty minutes and see what changes in a fortnight. Then write down what you observe, dated. Most primary worries respond to one of those four changes long before they need a paid tutor.

faqs.question: How long should we wait before deciding, and what are we waiting for?
faqs.answer: One full term, and you are waiting for evidence that the worry is durable. Write a dated paragraph now describing exactly what you see, put it away, and read it again at the end of term. If the same sentences still apply, you have a real difficulty worth paying to address and you can brief a tutor precisely. If they no longer apply, you have saved a term of evenings and money. Waiting is not passivity here; it is the only way to tell a pattern from a bad month.

faqs.question: Everyone in my daughter's class in Bandra seems to have a tutor. Are we putting her at a disadvantage?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, and the premise is usually wrong anyway. Parents report tuition selectively, so the classroom always sounds more tutored than it is. More importantly, extra hours at primary level do not compound the way parents assume. A child who reads widely, sleeps enough and has time to be bored tends to arrive at the Middle Years Programme in better shape than one who has spent four years in scheduled evening classes. Judge by your own child's reading and confidence, not by the school gate conversation.

faqs.question: Should we get a home tutor now so that the Middle Years Programme is easier later?
faqs.answer: That is rarely a good reason on its own. The MYP asks for independent work, sustained reading and organising oneself, and none of those is built by adding another adult who supervises. If you want to prepare your child for MYP, protect independent reading time, let them struggle for ten minutes before helping, and make them responsible for their own bag and deadlines. Home tuition helps later if there is a specific gap to close now. Bought as insurance against a programme two years away, it mostly builds dependence.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor make sense if the real problem is that our evenings are chaotic?
faqs.answer: No, and hiring one will usually make a chaotic evening worse. If homework is happening at nine at night between a dance class and dinner, the difficulty is the timetable, not the child's understanding. Fix the week first: drop one activity, move the homework slot earlier, and put screens away during it. Many families in Gurugram, Powai and Whitefield find the worry disappears within a month of doing only that. If it survives a calmer routine, then a home tutor has something real to work on.

faqs.question: The school has suggested an assessment for a possible learning difficulty. Do we need a tutor as well?
faqs.answer: Do the assessment first and decide afterwards. An assessment tells you what is actually happening, and the right support may be a specialist rather than a general tutor, which is a different person with different training. Hiring a subject tutor in the meantime can mask the pattern the assessment is looking for, and it delays the thing that will actually help. Ask the PYP coordinator what the school will put in place once the report arrives, and treat outside help as something you add to that plan, not instead of it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me whether my child needs a tutor, or is that a conflict of interest?
faqs.answer: It is a conflict, and you should weigh their answer accordingly. Anyone who tells you that every primary child benefits from extra classes is selling, not advising. A tutor worth hiring will ask what the school has said, will suggest you speak to the class teacher first, and will name the point at which sessions should stop. Ask the question directly at the trial: under what circumstances would you tell us to stop paying you? A person who has no answer to that has told you a great deal.

comparison.heading: Before you commit: how do four PYP options compare in India?
comparison.intro: None of these is the right first move if you have not yet spoken to the class teacher. Once you have, the choice turns on your child's age and how thin the local pool is. A home tutor suits younger children, online widens the pool, a batch costs less per hour and gives a child peers to work beside, and a recorded course asks nothing of your calendar. Read the rows for what each one does badly.

rows.label: Attention for a young child
cells: Undivided, with an adult beside the child who sees hesitation and guessing as it happens
Undivided, but held through a screen, which is hard work below about nine
Shared; a quiet child can hide, though some children work better alongside peers
None at all; nobody notices when a misunderstanding sets in

rows.label: Fit with the PYP
cells: Can follow the current unit of inquiry and the child's own reading level
The same, provided the tutor has taught primary and not only Diploma Programme subjects
Usually a fixed worksheet sequence unrelated to what the class is inquiring into
Generic primary content, rarely mapped to the Primary Years Programme in any way

rows.label: Travel and evening time
cells: The tutor travels, so your pool is whoever can reach you before the child tires
Nobody travels, which matters on a weekday in Whitefield, Thane or on OMR
The child travels, often in traffic, after an already long school day
No travel; the child works whenever the household has a quiet ten minutes

rows.label: Scheduling flexibility
cells: Good, but a rescheduled slot is hard to replace in the same week
Very good; a missed slot can often be moved to the next morning
Fixed batch timings that the family works around, not the reverse
Complete; it waits for you through exam weeks, illness and travel

rows.label: Feedback to you
cells: In person at the door each week, which is the most candid form of it
Usually a written note or a short call after the session
Periodic and general, since the teacher is describing a group
None, unless the platform reports what was watched and completed

rows.label: Trial before committing
cells: A demo or trial session at home, with you in the room watching
A trial call, easy to arrange and easy to walk away from
Often a demo class, though the batch you join later may differ
Free preview lessons, and nothing to cancel if you stop

rows.label: Cost structure
cells: Highest per hour, and the tutor's travel time is part of what you pay for
Lower per hour than a home visit, since nobody is travelling anywhere
Lowest per hour of any taught option, because the cost is shared
A one-off or subscription cost with no per-session charge at all

rows.label: Who it suits best
