h1: IB Diploma Tutors in India and the Award as a Whole
heroTitle: Reading the Whole Diploma Score in India
heroSubtitle: Most families hire subject by subject. The diploma is marked as one award: six grades out of 42, up to three points from the core, and a set of failing conditions that can undo a decent total. This page works through the arithmetic before it recommends anyone.
introSummary: IB Diploma tutors in India are usually hired one subject at a time, which is why home tuition often starts in the wrong place. The diploma is a single award. Six subjects carry grades of 1 to 7, giving 42; Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to 3 more, so 45 is the ceiling and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the International Baccalaureate's failing conditions. Once you see the total that way, the question changes. Not which subject is weakest, but where the next point is cheapest to buy with the hours a Diploma Programme (DP) student actually has. That is the question this page answers, and it is the one a good home tutor should ask in the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a points-first query in India reach the right IB Diploma tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
A points-first query is answered by working out which point is reachable before anyone is shortlisted. You send the six subjects with their levels, the most recent grades, the TOK and EE letters if the school has issued them, and the total the student is aiming at. Only then does a tutor name get attached to the request.

The sequence runs like this.
1. You send a query or book a free consultation, listing all six subjects, Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL) against each, and the latest reported grade.
2. IB Gram asks about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, and adds two questions this page cares about: where the core stands, and which total the family has in mind.
3. The request is read as arithmetic. A student on 33 who wants 38 needs five points, and those five have to be named before a tutor is chosen.
4. Profiles matching the named subjects are shortlisted, verified, and put in front of you with what each tutor actually teaches at HL and SL.
5. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and the trial is asked to test the specific gap rather than the subject in general.

Most families arrive naming one subject. Physics, usually, or Mathematics. Sometimes that subject is genuinely where the total is leaking. Often it is not, and the cheaper point sits in a Standard Level subject nobody is worried about, or in a TOK exhibition that has been left until the last term.

Where the shortlist runs thin, availability stays conditional on level and schedule, and the answer may be an online tutor rather than a local one. IB Diploma tutors in India are not evenly spread, and a two-hour HL slot on a weekday evening is a real constraint. If the fit is wrong after a few sessions, you can ask for a different match without restarting the whole plan.
items: Send all six subjects with HL or SL marked, not only the weak one
Include the latest TOK and EE letters if the school has issued them
Name the target total, so the gap can be counted in points
Ask what the trial session will test before you agree to it
Availability depends on level, locality and the evening slot you need

contentBlocks.heading: The 45 points, itemised: where every single one is earned
contentBlocks.body:
Forty-five points come from two places and nowhere else. Six subjects are each graded 1 to 7, which is 42 at the ceiling. TOK and the EE are each graded A to E and combine for up to 3 further points. That is the whole sum. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must be completed, but it carries no points at all, which surprises families every year.

Three or four of the six subjects are taken at Higher Level, with 240 recommended teaching hours each; the rest are Standard Level at 150 hours. The hours matter for planning because they tell you where the school is already spending time. An HL subject has ninety more hours of school teaching behind it than an SL subject sitting in the same student's timetable.

So the arithmetic of a total is blunt. A student holding 5, 5, 6, 4, 6 and 5 has 31 from subjects. Add 2 from the core and the total is 33. Moving that student to 38 means finding five points somewhere, and there are only seven places to look: six subject grades and one combined core score.

This is where the whole-award view earns its keep. A parent watching one subject sees a 4 and books tuition for it. A tutor reading the full profile sees that the 4 sits in an HL subject where the next boundary is a long way off, while two SL subjects are sitting near the top of their band and a TOK exhibition has not been started.

IB Diploma tutors in India who work this way begin with the grade sheet rather than with the complaint. The teaching still happens subject by subject once the plan is set. But the order in which subjects are picked up, and the hours each is given, comes out of the arithmetic instead of out of whichever paper went badly last.
items: Six subject grades of 1 to 7 give a maximum of 42 points
TOK and the Extended Essay combine for up to 3 points, giving 45
CAS must be completed but contributes no points to the total
Higher Level carries 240 recommended hours, Standard Level 150
Only seven scores exist: six subjects and one combined core figure

contentBlocks.heading: Six grades out of 42: which subject point is cheapest to gain?
contentBlocks.body:
The cheapest point usually sits in a subject the student is close to passing out of, not in the subject they find hardest. A 4 that is two marks under a boundary is cheaper than a 6 that needs a different quality of answer to become a 7. Cheapness is distance to the next boundary divided by the hours that distance would take.

Work it component by component. In IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology, a student trained on numerical drill often loses marks on the command terms rather than on the content: explain, discuss and to what extent all ask for something that define and describe do not. Those marks come back reasonably quickly with a tutor who marks the student's own answer in front of them. In IB Mathematics AA and AI the pattern is different. A missing technique costs the same marks in every paper until it is fixed, so the work is slower and the gain is more durable.

IB Economics and IB English A behave differently again. Written subjects reward structure, and structure is teachable inside a few sessions in a way that content knowledge is not. A student who writes everything they know, in the order they thought of it, is usually losing marks that a plan would recover.

Then look at internal assessment. Every subject carries coursework marked inside the school against published criteria, and a draft that has been read against those criteria before submission tends to score closer to the student's real level. A tutor may teach the skill, question the argument and point at a criterion. The writing stays the student's own, and the school's own policy on drafts is the one that governs.

Ranking the seven scores by cost, honestly, is the most useful hour of IB diploma tuition a DP1 family will buy. It is also the hour most often skipped.
items: Rank each subject by distance to the next boundary, not by difficulty
Command terms: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent
Written subjects often gain faster from structure than from more content
A criterion-checked internal assessment draft scores nearer the real level
A slow technical fix in Mathematics AA pays in every paper afterwards

contentBlocks.heading: IB Diploma tutors in India: the six-subject load, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
Where you live decides how much of the six-subject load can be carried at home. In Delhi NCR, a family in Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri can usually hold two or three home sessions a week inside South Delhi, and Dwarka works if the tutor is already on that side. A student in Sector 128 Noida or Greater Noida whose tutor sits in Gurugram (Gurgaon) near Golf Course Road is buying evening traffic with every visit, and the run between Faridabad or Ghaziabad and the centre can stretch what looks like a short trip. An IB Diploma tutor in Delhi will often hold one locality well and refuse another outright.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the split is sharper. An IB Diploma tutor in Mumbai living in Bandra, Juhu or Andheri may take Worli and Lower Parel on the same evening, while Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are effectively separate markets after six. Malabar Hill families often end up hybrid for the same reason.

Bengaluru families ask for an IB Diploma tutor in Bangalore and mean Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Indiranagar or Koramangala; Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road each sit far enough apart that one tutor rarely covers two. Hyderabad concentrates around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Kokapet and Secunderabad asking for an IB Diploma tutor in Hyderabad more often than supply comfortably answers. In Chennai, an IB Diploma tutor in Chennai working Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet or Nungambakkam will think twice about Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi, Velachery or Anna Nagar on a weekday. Pune spreads the same way: an IB Diploma tutor in Pune in Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar or Viman Nagar is a different proposition from Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad, Kharadi or Hinjewadi.

Outside the metros the arithmetic changes. In Gujarat, an IB Diploma tutor in Ahmedabad may cover Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway but not Gandhinagar, and Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot families usually go online. An IB Diploma tutor in Kolkata covering Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore or Rajarhat is easier to find than anything in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi or Patna. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have thin Diploma Programme supply. The same holds across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, and across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad. A search for an IB diploma tutor near me returns a short list in those places, and the honest answer is a hybrid week built around one specialist.
items: Delhi NCR: South Delhi and Dwarka hold slots; Ghaziabad rarely does
Mumbai: Bandra to Powai after six in the evening is a different city
Bengaluru and Hyderabad: Whitefield and Gachibowli concentrate DP supply
Chennai and Pune: OMR and Hinjewadi push families towards a hybrid week
Smaller cities: Indore, Kochi and Guwahati usually start online

contentBlocks.heading: What the May session timetable does to a DP2 year in India
contentBlocks.body:
Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, and that single fact sets the shape of a DP2 year. The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, so DP2 begins in April, the examinations arrive in May of the following year, and results are released in early July. November exists, but it is used by a small minority of schools and by retake candidates.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore deal with broadly similar pressure points, whatever the differences between them.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. Mocks are the last full rehearsal, and they are also the point at which the points arithmetic stops being theoretical. Before mocks, a family is guessing at a total. After mocks, the gap is measurable and the hours left are countable, which is why a plan written in DP1 should always be rewritten once mock scripts come back.

The core keeps its own calendar and it rarely lines up neatly with the subject one. The EE runs across both years with reflection sessions recorded along the way, and the TOK exhibition and essay land in terms where subject deadlines are already heavy. Students who lose points in the core usually lose them to collisions in the timetable rather than to any inability.

So plan backwards. Ask the DP coordinator for the mock window, the internal deadlines for the EE and TOK, and the school's own policy on drafts, then put those dates on one page before booking anything. Home tuition booked against that page does entirely different work from home tuition booked against a bad report.
items: Schools in India mostly enter the May session; November is a minority route
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, so DP2 starts in April
May results are released in early July, months after the last paper
Each school fixes its own DP2 mock dates, usually months ahead of May
Ask the coordinator for the EE and TOK internal deadlines in writing

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for the whole-diploma view in India?
contentBlocks.body:
For a whole-diploma plan, home tuition suits the subject that needs a person watching the work happen, online suits the core and the scarce specialism, and hybrid suits almost every family by DP2. The trade-off is plain. A home tutor sees the student's real conditions; an online tutor is chosen from the whole country.

Home classes put someone beside the student while a derivation is written out or a paragraph is planned. That matters where marks are lost silently, in working that is never shown and diagrams that are rushed. It matters again for a student who will not open a book without company in the room. The cost is travel, and travel in an Indian metro on a weekday evening is paid in the student's hours as well as the tutor's.

Online lessons cost nothing in travel and reach a specialist who lives in another city. For TOK and the EE this is usually the better call, because a conversation about an argument works as well on a shared screen as across a table, and because the people who teach those parts of the diploma well are not evenly distributed. Online also survives monsoon evenings and examination-term chaos in a way that home visits do not.

Hybrid is the arrangement most DP2 families reach, and it is a design rather than a compromise. One home session a week for the subject that needs supervision, one or two online sessions for the core or a second subject, and the marking done between sessions instead of inside them. A household in Powai or Whitefield can hold that week. Two home visits across the same city usually cannot.

Home tutoring is worse than online when the right person lives three hours away, when the study space at home is shared with a younger sibling, or when the week is already too full to lose an hour to a doorbell. Say that early, and the plan survives the year.
items: Home tuition: strongest where working, diagrams and shown method go wrong
Online: strongest for TOK, the Extended Essay and scarce Higher Level subjects
Hybrid: one home session plus online contact, the usual DP2 shape
Travel is paid in the student's hours, not only in the tutor's
A shared study space at home can make online the sounder choice

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a home tutor takes on a points plan?
contentBlocks.body:
Check that the person advising on all seven scores has actually taught more than one of them, and that the profile in front of you names subjects and levels rather than boards. A tutor who teaches HL Physics well is not automatically the person to rank where a point is cheapest across six subjects and a core.

IB Gram checks tutor profiles before they are shown: identity, the qualifications claimed, and the subjects and levels each tutor says they teach. Verification is a floor, not a verdict. It tells you the claim has been looked at. It does not tell you whether this person suits your child, and no platform can see that from a profile.

So run your own checks, politely and early. Ask which subjects the tutor has taught at Higher Level and for how long. Ask what they would do with a grade sheet showing a 4 in one HL subject and 6s elsewhere, then listen for whether the answer is about the 4 or about the whole total. Ask what they will not help with, because a tutor who has no boundary around the EE and the internal assessments has not read the rules. And ask what the school's coordinator should be doing that a tutor should not.

For a home tutor there is a second layer, because somebody is entering your flat every week. Agree the entry arrangement with your society gate, keep sessions in a space a parent can pass through, and fix in advance what happens when a session is missed on either side.

Claims about examiner or moderator work are worth asking about rather than assuming. Experience of how marks are awarded is genuinely useful, particularly for command terms. It is not a shortcut to a grade, and anyone presenting it as one has told you something about how they sell.
items: Profiles should name subjects and levels taught, not only the board
Ask how the tutor would read a full grade sheet, not one subject
Ask what the tutor will not help with on the EE and coursework
Agree society gate entry and missed-session rules before week one
Treat examiner experience as useful context, never as a shortcut

contentBlocks.heading: Chasing points against learning the subject: the honest difference
contentBlocks.body:
There is a real difference between the two, and pretending otherwise is dishonest in both directions. Chasing points means reading boundaries, drilling the question types that recur, and spending hours where the marks sit. Learning the subject means understanding it well enough that the marks follow. Most of the time these overlap comfortably. Where they part company is worth naming precisely.

They part company in three places. The first is the last ten weeks before May, when learning a topic properly is no longer available and pattern work genuinely scores better. The second is a subject the student will never touch again, where a competent 5 bought with technique is a reasonable purchase and a deep 6 is not worth the term it would cost. The third is the subject the student is going to read at university, where a technique-only 6 leaves them opening a first-year course with nothing underneath it.

The honest position is that the two years contain a fixed number of study hours, and the family is allocating them rather than creating them. A student taking IB Physics into an engineering degree should not be drilled past their understanding in it. A student taking it because Group 4 required something should not be given a term of conceptual teaching they will never use again.

Say the goal out loud, because the goal changes the method. A family wanting IB 45 points help is asking for something very specific and very expensive in hours: no cheap points left anywhere, the core secured early, and every subject held near the top of its band. A family that needs 32 for a course offer is asking a different question, and the answer there usually involves fewer sessions rather than more.

IB Diploma tutors in India who ask what the points are for, before asking what is going wrong, tend to produce plans a household can actually hold. And a plan nobody can hold produces no points at all.
items: Name the target first: 45 and 32 call for genuinely different plans
Technique work pays best in the final weeks before the May session
Deep teaching pays best in the subject continuing at university
A fixed number of study hours is being allocated, never created
Fewer sessions is sometimes the honest recommendation

contentBlocks.heading: Failing conditions: the rules that sink a good total in India
contentBlocks.body:
A student can reach 24 points and still not receive the diploma. Twenty-four is the minimum, but it is a minimum subject to the International Baccalaureate's failing conditions, and those conditions are set by the IB rather than by any tutor or platform. Two of them matter enough to name here. An E in TOK or in the Extended Essay is a failing condition. CAS must be completed.

That first one catches families every year, and it catches good students. A candidate with strong subject grades who treated TOK as the thing to do after everything else, and who never rewrote the essay draft after feedback, can arrive in July with a total that looks respectable and no diploma behind it. The core is worth up to three points, which sounds small until it is the thing standing between a student and the award itself.

Ask your DP coordinator for the current list of failing conditions in writing, and ask in DP1 rather than in the last term. The rules are not secret and the coordinator will have them to hand. Nobody should be working from a tutor's memory of them, and that includes the tutor.

What honest progress looks like is slower than most families expect. Six to eight weeks of consistent work usually shows up as better scripts before it shows up as a better grade, because a grade is a boundary and boundaries move in steps. Ask for evidence in marked work rather than in reassurance. If two months of home tuition have produced no change in a marked script, something in the diagnosis is wrong, and the plan should change instead of continuing.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any total remains a prediction until results arrive in early July. What tutoring can do is make sure that no point is lost to something avoidable.
items: 24 points is the diploma minimum, and still subject to failing conditions
An E in TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition
CAS must be completed, though it carries no points of its own
Get the current failing-conditions list from the DP coordinator in writing
Expect better scripts before better grades; boundaries move in steps

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in India with the points arithmetic on paper
contentBlocks.body:
Bring one page. The six subjects with HL or SL marked against each, the most recent grade for every one of them, the TOK and EE letters if the school has issued them, the mock window, and the total the student is aiming at. That page is the whole brief, and it takes about fifteen minutes to write.

Send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram will ask about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified and whose subjects and levels match what is on your page. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything. Availability depends on level, locality and the slot you need, so a weekday evening in a far suburb may take longer to fill than a Saturday morning in the same city.

The first session should not be teaching. It should be reading: the grade sheet, one recent marked script, and the calendar. By the end of it you should have the seven scores ranked by how cheaply each could move, an agreed order of work, and an honest statement about which of them will not move much at all.

Then the ordinary work starts, subject by subject, at home or online or inside the hybrid week most DP2 households settle into. Review it every few weeks against marked evidence rather than against how the sessions felt. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match; that is a normal request and not a complaint.

And if the arithmetic says the student does not need six subject tutors, or any at all, a good adviser will tell you that as well.
items: Write one page: six subjects, levels, latest grades, core letters, target total
Add the mock window and any EE or TOK internal deadlines
Book a free consultation; a trial can be arranged before you commit
Expect the first session to read evidence rather than to teach
Review every few weeks against marked work, not against how it felt

faqs.question: How are the 45 IB Diploma points actually made up?
faqs.answer: Forty-two points come from six subjects graded 1 to 7, and up to three more come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together. That is the entire sum. Creativity, Activity, Service must be completed but adds nothing to the total. So a student has seven scores in play rather than six, and the combined core score is the one families most often forget when they work out how far they are from a target.

faqs.question: Is 24 points enough to be awarded the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four is the minimum, but reaching 24 does not by itself award the diploma. The total must also satisfy the International Baccalaureate's failing conditions, so a candidate can meet the points and still miss the award. An E in Theory of Knowledge or in the Extended Essay is one such condition, and Creativity, Activity, Service must be completed. Ask your DP coordinator for the current list in writing rather than relying on anybody's memory of it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really tell us where a point is cheapest to gain?
faqs.answer: A good one can give you a ranking, not a promise. It is built from the grade sheet, recent marked scripts and the mock window: how far each score sits from the next boundary, how many hours that distance would take, and whether the subject rewards technique or understanding. The ranking is a working hypothesis and it changes after mocks. Treat anyone who produces one without looking at marked work with real caution.

faqs.question: Our school has predicted an E in TOK. What does that do to the diploma?
faqs.answer: An E in Theory of Knowledge is a failing condition, so it puts the award itself at risk however strong the six subject grades are. Treat it as urgent rather than as a three-point problem. The TOK exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 prompts at up to 950 words and is internally assessed; the essay answers one of six prescribed titles at up to 1,600 words and is externally assessed. Speak to the coordinator this week.

faqs.question: Can an IB Diploma home tutor come to our flat in Powai on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, subject to tutor availability and to how far the tutor lives from you. Powai, Bandra and Andheri each have local supply, but a tutor crossing the Mumbai Metropolitan Region after six in the evening is buying a long trip with every visit, and that tends to show up as cancelled sessions by November. Ask any candidate where they live before you ask when they are free. A hybrid week often holds better.

faqs.question: Should we book home tuition for all six subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Six simultaneous arrangements leave the student no hours to work alone, and independent work is where most of the consolidation actually happens. Start with the two scores the ranking says are cheapest to move, hold them for six to eight weeks, then review against marked work. Home classes for a third subject can be added if the week still has room in it. A DP2 student usually has less room than the family thinks.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram help with the Extended Essay, and where is the line drawn?
faqs.answer: Support covers the thinking and the skills, never the writing. A tutor can help shape a research question, discuss whether an argument holds together, explain what the criteria ask for, and question a claim the student has made. The essay runs to 4,000 words over roughly 40 hours and is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded. That supervisor and the school's policy govern what outside help is permitted.

faqs.question: We live in Indore. Is an IB diploma tutor near me realistic, or should we go online?
faqs.answer: In Indore, as in Bhopal, Nagpur, Kochi or Guwahati, local Diploma Programme supply is thin, and a search for a nearby specialist often returns nothing at all for Higher Level subjects. Online is usually the honest answer, and it is not a downgrade for core work or for a scarce subject. Where a local tutor exists for one subject, a hybrid week works well: that person at home, the specialist online, one plan between them.

faqs.question: How much does IB diploma tuition cost, and what drives the difference?
faqs.answer: Fees are quoted per session and depend on level, subject, locality and whether the tutor travels to you. Higher Level work and core support usually sit above Standard Level subject tuition, and a home visit carries the tutor's travel inside the rate. Frequency matters more than most families expect, since two sessions a week doubles the monthly figure. Ask for the rate, the session length and the cancellation terms in writing before the first lesson.

faqs.question: What should we do if home sessions show no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so directly, and ask to see the evidence rather than a reassurance. A month is short for a grade to move, but it is long enough for marked scripts to look different. If they do not, the diagnosis is probably wrong: the problem may be timing, or writing, or a topic from two years back, rather than the one being taught each week. Change the plan, or ask for a different match. Both are normal requests.

faqs.question: Is aiming for 45 points a sensible goal for our child?
faqs.answer: For most students it is the wrong target, and chasing it costs more than it returns. Forty-five requires every one of the six subjects at the top of its band and full marks from the core, with no weak component anywhere in the profile. If the offers your child needs sit in the thirties, plan for those and keep the spare hours for sleep and for CAS. Ambition is useful. An arithmetic nobody can hold is not.

A tutor can help shape a research question, discuss whether an argument holds together, explain what the criteria ask for, and question a claim the student has made. The essay runs to 4,000 words over roughly 40 hours and is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded. That supervisor and the school's policy govern what outside help is permitted.

mainEntity.name: We live in Indore. Is an IB diploma tutor near me realistic, or should we go online?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Indore, as in Bhopal, Nagpur, Kochi or Guwahati, local Diploma Programme supply is thin, and a search for a nearby specialist often returns nothing at all for Higher Level subjects. Online is usually the honest answer, and it is not a downgrade for core work or for a scarce subject. Where a local tutor exists for one subject, a hybrid week works well: that person at home, the specialist online, one plan between them.

mainEntity.name: How much does IB diploma tuition cost, and what drives the difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees are quoted per session and depend on level, subject, locality and whether the tutor travels to you. Higher Level work and core support usually sit above Standard Level subject tuition, and a home visit carries the tutor's travel inside the rate. Frequency matters more than most families expect, since two sessions a week doubles the monthly figure. Ask for the rate, the session length and the cancellation terms in writing before the first lesson.

mainEntity.name: What should we do if home sessions show no progress after a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so directly, and ask to see the evidence rather than a reassurance. A month is short for a grade to move, but it is long enough for marked scripts to look different. If they do not, the diagnosis is probably wrong: the problem may be timing, or writing, or a topic from two years back, rather than the one being taught each week. Change the plan, or ask for a different match. Both are normal requests.

mainEntity.name: Is aiming for 45 points a sensible goal for our child?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most students it is the wrong target, and chasing it costs more than it returns. Forty-five requires every one of the six subjects at the top of its band and full marks from the core, with no weak component anywhere in the profile. If the offers your child needs sit in the thirties, plan for those and keep the spare hours for sleep and for CAS. Ambition is useful. An arithmetic nobody can hold is not.

comparison.intro: Four arrangements are on the table for a family thinking in points rather than in subjects. A home tutor sees the student's conditions; an online tutor is chosen from the whole country; a batch is cheaper per hour and gives peer discussion; a recorded course is available at two in the morning. The deciding trade-off is whether your plan needs someone watching one student's work, or simply needs the content covered.

heroTitle: The Home a Diploma Student Studies In, Across India
heroSubtitle: Most advice about the Diploma Programme talks about syllabus and timetables. This page is about the room. Where the desk goes in a two-bedroom flat, what a younger sibling does at seven in the evening, how a household holds a week through DP2, and what a tutor sitting in that room can actually see.
introSummary: IB Diploma home tutors in India teach in the place the student actually works, which is usually a bedroom shared with a sibling, a dining table that has to be cleared by seven, or a corner of a living room with the television two metres away. That physical setting decides more about the final two years than most families expect. A home tutor who walks in every week sees the real conditions: the chair that is too low, the light falling behind the writing hand, the phone face-down but still buzzing. This page covers the domestic side of the Diploma Programme (DP): setting up a study space in an ordinary Indian flat, managing noise and siblings, building a week the whole household can hold through DP2, and why sleep belongs in the conversation.

contentBlocks.heading: How do we match IB Diploma home tutors in India to the room they will teach in?
contentBlocks.body:
We ask where the lesson will physically happen before we ask anything else. Which room. Who else is in it at seven in the evening. Whether the door closes. What the table is like, and whether a second child needs that same table at the same hour. Only after that do we talk about subjects and levels.

That order surprises some parents. It exists because a match that ignores the room fails quietly. A tutor booked for a Wednesday slot in Powai discovers that Wednesday is the evening the physiotherapist comes for the grandmother, and the only quiet room is taken. A family in Gachibowli books eight o'clock and the student is already fading by half past. These are not scheduling details. They are the difference between a session that moves a criterion and a session that fills an hour.

So the consultation runs through the household before it runs through the syllabus. You tell us the board, the six subjects, which three or four are Higher Level (HL), the school's mock window and your locality. You also tell us what the evening really looks like: dinner time, the sibling's own tuition, the parent who reaches home at nine, the society gate rules that make a visitor sign in and wait. We then shortlist tutors whose verified profiles match both halves of that picture, subject and setting, and you can arrange a demo session before the family commits to anything.

If the room turns out to be unworkable, we say so rather than sending someone into it. Sometimes the honest answer is a hybrid week: the tutor comes on Saturday morning when the flat is quiet and a younger sibling is at football, and the midweek session runs online from whichever corner is free. Availability is always subject to who is actually free in your locality at the hour you need, and we would rather tell you that at the start than after two wasted weeks.
items: 1. Tell us the six subjects, the Higher Level choices and the school's mock window
2. Describe the room honestly: table, chair, door, light, and who else uses it
3. Give two or three evening slots the whole household can genuinely hold
4. Review a shortlist of verified profiles matched to subject, level and locality
5. Run a demo session in the actual room, not in a neutral space
6. Confirm the weekly slot, or ask for a different match without justifying it twice

contentBlocks.heading: Two years, one flat: what DP1 and DP2 ask of a household in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme runs two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four are taken at Higher Level, for which 240 teaching hours are recommended; the rest are Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to three further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the award of the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed alongside all of it.

Read those numbers as a household load rather than a course outline. Three Higher Level subjects at 240 hours each is the school's teaching time, and homework sits on top of it. The desk in your flat is going to be occupied on most evenings for two years, by one person, who needs it undisturbed. Nobody plans for that when the DP is chosen in Grade 10.

DP1 and DP2 feel different at home, and it helps to name the difference early. DP1 is wide and fairly forgiving: six new subjects, TOK starting, CAS beginning, the EE research question still being circled. The student still comes to dinner and still argues about the remote. DP2 narrows and hardens. Internal assessment deadlines land in clusters, the EE goes to final draft, the school's mock examinations arrive several months before May, and the same student now wants the table from seven until eleven and is short with anyone who opens the door.

Households that hold DP2 well have usually decided three things in advance: which room belongs to the student in the evening, what the rest of the family does instead of using it, and which two evenings are protected from everything, including tuition. A DP home tutor who understands that is planning around a real week. One who does not will keep proposing a Thursday slot that the family will keep cancelling.
items: Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, the rest Standard Level
240 recommended hours per HL subject, 150 per SL subject, before any homework
Grades 1 to 7 per subject, plus up to three core points, 45 maximum and 24 minimum
DP1 is wide and survivable; DP2 concentrates deadlines and shortens tempers
Decide early which room is the student's in the evening, and what everyone else does

contentBlocks.heading: Which of the six subjects actually needs the desk, and for how long?
contentBlocks.body:
The sciences and Mathematics need the most desk surface, English A needs the least surface but the longest unbroken quiet, and Economics needs a working printer more than it needs space. That is the practical division most DP households arrive at by the middle of DP1, usually after a few arguments about who gets the dining table.

Take the sciences, first assessed in 2025. Paper 1 comes in two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, and Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. The internal assessment (IA) is the scientific investigation, worth 20 per cent of the subject grade, marked on four criteria of six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, inside a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each writes an individual report. HL and SL share the assessment structure, with Additional Higher Level (AHL) content added at HL. A student drafting that report at home needs the laptop, the raw data, a printed copy of the criteria and space to spread graphs side by side. A narrow dining table will not hold all four at once, and the student ends up working on the floor.

Mathematics, whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, punishes a cramped surface more than any other subject. Working runs down a page and across to a second. A student squeezing algebra into a margin makes sign errors that have nothing to do with understanding. A home tutor sitting beside that student sees the error at the moment it is written, which is a different experience from reading a photograph of it two days later.

English A and TOK are the quiet subjects. They need forty uninterrupted minutes more than they need a big table, and forty uninterrupted minutes in an Indian flat at eight in the evening is genuinely hard to find. Economics and the other Group 3 subjects sit in between: commentaries and portfolio work that mostly need the printer to be working and the previous draft to be findable. Command terms matter across all of them, because define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth, and a student who reads them casually loses marks they understood perfectly well.
items: Sciences: Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data-based, Paper 2 extended response
Scientific investigation: four criteria of six marks, 20 per cent, 3,000 words maximum
Mathematics needs page width; cramped working produces sign errors, not real gaps
English A and TOK need forty quiet minutes far more than they need desk area
Command terms set the depth: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent

contentBlocks.heading: Study corners across India: what each city does to a home lesson
contentBlocks.body:
An IB Diploma home tutor in Mumbai, an IB Diploma home tutor in Delhi and an IB Diploma home tutor in Bangalore are solving the same subject problem in three quite different rooms. Space, noise and the shape of the evening change from city to city, and the sensible answer about where a lesson sits changes with them.

In Delhi NCR the study space is often the most generous of any metro and travel is the constraint. A family in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj or Chanakyapuri usually has a room that closes properly. A tutor crossing from Dwarka to Golf Course Road in Gurugram (Gurgaon), or from Sector 128 Noida out to Faridabad, spends exactly the part of the evening the student needs. Greater Noida and Ghaziabad households often settle on one long weekend home visit plus a shorter midweek session online. Winter brings its own quiet problem: in a Delhi flat in January the warmest room is frequently the one with the television in it.

Mumbai Metropolitan Region is the opposite trade. Flats in Bandra, Juhu, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill are compact, and the study corner is often in a bedroom or a passage. Powai and Andheri families sometimes have a little more room and the same interruption problem. Across Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar, a tutor who lives locally holds a weekday evening slot far more reliably than one travelling in from the island city, and any IB Diploma home tutor in India working through July should have an agreed online fallback for the monsoon.

Bengaluru households in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala and Indiranagar tend to run late work schedules, so the flat is often empty until nine and then suddenly full. Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road families face long crosstown evenings that make a nearby tutor worth more than a marginally better distant one. In Hyderabad, an IB Diploma home tutor in Hyderabad working in Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur or the Financial District is usually teaching in a newer, quieter apartment, while Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad homes are older and more porous to street noise. Kokapet is still building, and late construction noise is a real reason some families move the midweek session online.

Pune follows its own pattern. Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar and Viman Nagar are close enough to most international schools that a home tutor can arrive soon after the student does. Baner, Balewadi, Aundh and Wakad are workable in either direction, while a tutor travelling to Hinjewadi or Kharadi at six in the evening may reach a student who has already lost the best hour of their day. An IB Diploma home tutor in Pune will often propose a later start for that reason. Outside these clusters, an IB Diploma home tutor in Chennai, an IB Diploma home tutor in Kolkata working around Salt Lake, or an IB Diploma home tutor in Ahmedabad near Bodakdev, is drawing on a thinner local pool, and diploma home tuition there frequently becomes a hybrid arrangement by necessity rather than by preference.
items: Delhi NCR: larger rooms, longer evening travel, and a January heating problem
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: compact flats, bedroom study corners, monsoon fallbacks
Bengaluru: late-filling homes in Whitefield and Sarjapur Road, long crosstown evenings
Hyderabad: quieter new apartments in Gachibowli and Kokapet, noisier older Banjara Hills
Pune: Koregaon Park and Viman Nagar are close in, Hinjewadi and Kharadi cost the best hour
Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad: thinner local pools, so hybrid weeks are common

contentBlocks.heading: The school year in India, read off the kitchen calendar
contentBlocks.body:
IB schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May examination session. November is used by a small minority and by retake candidates. May fits the Indian academic year, which runs roughly April to March, and May results are released in early July. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Those dates matter at home because they collide with everything else a household does. The DP2 mock fortnight tends to land in the same stretch as winter weddings and visiting relatives. The long October and November festival period arrives while internal assessment drafts are due. Guests sleep in the room the student studies in. A grandparent's visit is not negotiable, and nor should it be, but it should be on a calendar the tutor can see.

The practical move is a single shared calendar in the kitchen or on a phone, carrying four things: school mock dates, IA and EE deadlines as the school issues them, family events that will take over a room, and the tutoring slots. Most families discover the clash only when it happens. Written down in September, the same clash is a fifteen-minute conversation about moving two sessions.

Schools also expect a good deal of independent work, and the expectation rises sharply in DP2. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show how marks are awarded. If your child is not using them by the start of DP2, that is a conversation for the subject teacher and the DP coordinator first, before any decision about home tuition. A tutor can build the habit, but the school is the source of the material and of the predicted grade, and neither of those is something an outside tutor controls.
items: Schools in India overwhelmingly enter the May session; November is the minority and retake route
The academic year runs roughly April to March; May results are released in early July
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May
Put mocks, IA deadlines, family events and tuition slots on one visible calendar
Past papers and markschemes come through the school or the IB's official channels

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid when the study space is the real problem?
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in one paragraph. A home tutor comes to your flat and teaches in the conditions the student actually works in, which is the only way anyone outside the family sees those conditions. An online tutor gives you reach, so a rare Higher Level subject taught by nobody in your locality becomes available, and no evening is lost to travel. A hybrid week takes one home session and one online session, and for most DP2 households in India it is the arrangement that survives contact with reality.

What a home tutor sees that an online tutor never will is worth being specific about. Posture and fatigue, because a student slumped by the twentieth minute is not lazy, they are short of sleep. The chair, which in many flats is a dining chair at the wrong height for a laptop. The light, which for a right-handed student writing at a table with the window on their right falls behind the hand and makes them tilt. The phone, face-down on the table and vibrating. The sibling who opens the door four times in an hour. The printer that has been out of ink since August, which is why no past paper has been attempted on paper. None of that reaches a camera pointed at a face.

Online wins on different ground, and the honest cases are clear. If the only quiet hour in your home is ten at night, a tutor who does not have to travel can take it. If the flat is genuinely unworkable and the student concentrates better in a library or at a relative's house, online follows them there. If the subject is thinly taught in your city, an online specialist beats a nearby generalist, and it is not close.

The hybrid week is the compromise most families end up at. The weekend home session is the one where paper is marked in front of the student and the working conditions get checked. The midweek online session handles follow-up, a marked question or two, and a short accountability conversation. IB Diploma home tutors in India who work this way tend to keep the home visit for whatever genuinely needs the room, and send everything else down the wire.
items: Home visit: the tutor sees posture, light, chair, noise and the actual working surface
Online: reach for scarce HL subjects, no travel, and a late slot that a commute would kill
Hybrid: weekend home session for marking on paper, midweek online for follow-up
Choose online without guilt if the only quiet hour in the flat is after ten at night
Choose home if the student's written working, not their understanding, is where marks go

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check about someone who sits in your home every week?
contentBlocks.body:
Check identity, subject depth at the level your child is taking, and the household rules you will apply to every visitor, in that order. A tutor who teaches in your home is a person in your private space for a couple of hours a week across two years, so the checks are not only about teaching.

On our side, a profile is verified before it goes live: identity documents, the qualifications claimed, and the subjects and levels the tutor says they teach. Where a tutor claims IB-specific experience, that claim is part of what is checked rather than something taken on trust. What we cannot see is whether the person will suit your particular child, which is why a demo session exists and why you can ask for a different match without building a case for it.

On your side, there are checks no platform can do for you. Ask for photo identity at the first visit and note it, the way you would for any professional entering the flat. Register the tutor at the society gate rather than waving them through, so there is a record of arrival and departure. Keep the door of the study room open, or use a room that is visible from the rest of the house. Have an adult or a household staff member present in the flat during sessions, particularly in the first several weeks. Agree at the start that lessons are not recorded or photographed without your knowledge, and that your child's work, drafts and school feedback are not shared with anyone else.

Subject checks are separate and just as important. Ask the tutor to talk through how the scientific investigation criteria are actually applied, or what a command term like evaluate demands that explain does not. Ask what they will not do: a tutor who offers to write or heavily edit an IA or the Extended Essay is describing academic misconduct, and that is the clearest disqualifying answer you will ever get.
items: Verified before listing: identity documents, qualifications claimed, subjects and levels taught
Ask for photo identity on the first visit and register the tutor at the society gate
Keep the study room door open, or use a room visible from the rest of the flat
Have an adult or household staff member in the flat, especially in the first few weeks
Agree no recording or photographs, and no sharing of your child's drafts or feedback
A tutor offering to write or heavily edit an IA or the EE has disqualified themselves

contentBlocks.heading: A study space that works in a two-bedroom flat: the concrete version
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the surface. The student needs a table that holds an open past paper, a markscheme beside it, a calculator and a notebook, all visible at once. That is roughly the width of two A4 sheets side by side with room for the hand to move, and most dining tables manage it while most bedroom study tables do not. If the choice is a proper study table too small to hold a paper and a markscheme together, or the dining table cleared by a quarter to seven, take the dining table. Students who cannot see the markscheme next to their own answer stop comparing the two, and comparing the two is most of what improves a mark.

Then the chair, where more damage is done than anywhere else. A dining chair at a dining table is usually fine. A dining chair pulled up to a low centre table in the living room is not, and a student on a bed with a laptop is writing nothing at all. Feet flat, elbows a little above the table, screen at eye level if a laptop is involved, which usually means a few books under it. Then the light. A right-handed student should have the window or the lamp on their left, otherwise their own hand shades the line they are writing. A fair share of the complaints about untidy handwriting and careless slips in a DP2 mock come back to a student working in the shadow of their own wrist.

Now the things around the table. One socket within reach, because a laptop dying mid-session costs ten minutes. A shelf or a single box file per subject, not a shared pile, so an IA draft can be found in seconds. A small whiteboard, or even a sheet of chart paper on the wall, because a tutor explaining a derivation needs somewhere to write that is not the student's own page. A wall clock the student can see without turning, which matters more than it sounds once timed practice starts. And a fixed place for the phone that is outside the room, because face-down on the table still works as an interruption.

Last, what the space is not. It is not the room the television lives in, unless the television is genuinely off for the whole evening and everyone accepts that. It is not the bed. It is not a corner that has to be assembled from scratch each evening, because a ten-minute setup cost turns into a reason not to start. A home tutor who comes in every week can tell you which of these has quietly broken, and that is the sort of thing which never shows up in a progress report.
items: Table wide enough for an open past paper and its markscheme side by side
Chair at dining height, feet flat, laptop raised to eye level on a couple of books
Light from the left for a right-handed student, so the writing hand casts no shadow
One box file per subject, a socket in reach, a visible clock, phone parked outside the room
A small whiteboard or chart paper for the tutor's working, kept off the student's page
Never the bed, and never a corner that has to be rebuilt from scratch every evening

contentBlocks.heading: Sleep, and why a Diploma tutor in India should raise it
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor who never mentions sleep is missing the largest single variable in DP2 performance, and they are usually the last adult outside the family with a clear view of it. The student will not tell the school they were up until two. They will tell a tutor they see alone every week, or the tutor will simply notice: the twentieth-minute slump, the arithmetic that was fine last month, the same explanation needed twice.

The arithmetic of a DP2 evening is unforgiving. School until three or four, travel, CAS or a sport, dinner, then a session from eight to ten, then an IA draft. A ten o'clock finish followed by two hours of independent work puts the student in bed at one and up at six, and five hours of sleep does not hold six subjects. This is the point where tutoring can make things worse instead of better, and an honest tutor will say so. Sometimes the right recommendation is to drop from two sessions a week to one, or move a session to Saturday morning, or stop entirely for a fortnight around a mock.

What progress should look like is slower and less dramatic than most families hope. Over the first month, expect the tutor to find the actual problem rather than fix it, and expect that diagnosis to be uncomfortable. By the end of a term, expect specific improvements you can point to: a criterion the student used to lose marks on, timing on Paper 2, working that a marker can follow without guessing. Across DP1 into DP2, expect the student to need the tutor less rather than more. A student still leaning on a tutor in the last term before May has been taught dependence, not method.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any arrangement that suggests otherwise should be treated with real scepticism. The predicted grade belongs to the school and is formed from the school's own evidence. Good IB Diploma home tutors in India improve the work that evidence is drawn from, and that is where their influence honestly ends.
items: A tutor who never asks about sleep is missing the biggest DP2 variable in the house
Five hours of sleep does not hold six subjects; the fix is fewer commitments, not more
Month one is diagnosis, not repair, and the diagnosis is often uncomfortable
By term end, expect named improvements: a criterion, Paper 2 timing, followable working
Dependence is failure: a DP2 student should need the tutor less as May approaches

contentBlocks.heading: Before DP2 begins: a numbered home setup for the final year
contentBlocks.body:
The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the last cheap opportunity to fix the physical side, and it takes an afternoon. Once the internal assessment cluster arrives, nobody is going to rearrange furniture. Families who do this in the break spend the rest of the year arguing about content rather than about who has the table.

What you prepare before the first session is short. The student's last report and any criterion feedback. One marked script, ideally a mock, because a marked script tells a tutor more in five minutes than a conversation tells them in an hour. The school's mock dates and IA deadlines if they have been issued. A list of the six subjects with levels marked. And a straight answer about the evenings: which two are already gone, and which hour is genuinely free.

The first session itself should not be a lesson. Expect the tutor to look at the marked script with the student, ask them to redo one question while they watch, and then say what they saw. Expect them to look at the room, because they should. Expect a plan naming the next three or four weeks in terms of specific work, not a promise about a grade. If none of that happens in the first session, that is useful information about the tutor.

To start, send us a query or book a free consultation. We will ask about the board, the subjects and levels, the school calendar, your locality and your schedule, then shortlist verified tutors who fit. A demo session can be arranged before you commit, lessons can run at home, online or hybrid, and if the match is wrong you can ask for a different one. Booking IB Diploma home tutors in India is easiest in the break, before a tutor's weekday evening slots have been taken for the year.
items: 1. Choose the room and the surface, and agree who gives it up in the evening
2. Fix the chair, raise the laptop, and move the light to the student's left
3. Set up one box file per subject and get the printer working before August
4. Put mock dates, IA deadlines and family events on one calendar everyone sees
5. Agree the phone's parking place outside the room, and a fixed session start time
6. Book the tutoring slots around the two evenings the household refuses to give up

faqs.question: Where in the house should a DP home tuition session actually happen?
faqs.answer: Wherever there is a table wide enough for an open past paper and its markscheme side by side, and a door that can be shut. In most Indian flats that is the dining table rather than the bedroom study table, which is usually too narrow. Avoid the living room if the television is on, and avoid the bed entirely. If the only workable surface is the dining table, agree that it is cleared by a quarter to seven, so the session starts on time instead of ten minutes late every week.

faqs.question: Our two children share a bedroom. Can home tuition still work there?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not in that bedroom. The realistic arrangement is that the session moves to the dining or living area and the younger sibling takes the bedroom for that hour, with the swap fixed on the same evenings each week so nobody renegotiates it. Rotating rooms works badly, because the setup cost eats the first ten minutes. If both children are being tutored, back-to-back slots with one tutor, or staggered evenings, usually cause less friction than running two sessions at once inside one flat.

faqs.question: Who should be at home when the tutor comes, and where should they sit?
faqs.answer: An adult or a household staff member should be in the flat, and not in the room. Being present in the house is a sensible safeguarding baseline, especially in the first several weeks. Sitting inside the session is different and usually unhelpful, because a sixteen-year-old will not admit confusion in front of a parent, and the tutor then loses the honest answers that make diagnosis possible. Keep the door open or use a visible room, ask for the last five minutes as a summary, and otherwise stay out of it.

faqs.question: My child studies until two in the morning. Should the tutor raise it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a good one will raise it without being asked. Five hours of sleep does not hold six subjects, and a tutor sees the consequences before anyone else: the slump twenty minutes in, arithmetic errors that were not there last month, the same explanation needed twice. Expect the recommendation to be subtraction rather than addition, which may mean one session a week instead of two, or a pause around the mock fortnight. A tutor who responds to exhaustion by adding hours has understood nothing.

faqs.question: We live in a compact flat in Bandra with no spare room. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Work with the hour rather than the room. Pick the evening hour when the flat is emptiest, usually before the working parents return, and protect it. Use the dining table with the television off, headphones for the student if a sibling is around, and a fixed parking place for phones outside the room. Many families across Bandra, Juhu and Lower Parel run the weekend session at home when there is space and time, then take the midweek session online from whichever corner is quiet. That pattern is normal here, not a failure.

faqs.question: How many evenings a week should a Diploma student give to tutoring?
faqs.answer: For most DP students, one or two subjects tutored once a week each is the ceiling that still leaves room for the student's own work. Three or more tuition evenings in DP2 usually means the student is being taught instead of practising, and practice is what moves a grade in a criterion-marked programme. Two evenings should also stay completely free of tuition, school work permitting. If the plan keeps needing a third and a fourth evening, the problem is the number of commitments rather than the amount of teaching.

faqs.question: Is the dining table good enough, or do we need a proper study desk?
faqs.answer: The dining table is usually better, because width matters far more than the label on the furniture. A student needs to see their own answer and the markscheme at the same time, and a narrow study desk forces them to stack the two and stop comparing them. Buy a better chair before you buy a better table. Raise the laptop on a couple of books so the screen sits at eye level, put the light on the left for a right-handed student, and the setup is essentially done.

faqs.question: Construction noise near our building in Kokapet runs late. Does online help?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, because headphones and a close microphone cut noise for both the student and the tutor in a way an open room cannot. Families in Kokapet, Gachibowli and parts of Kondapur often find the online midweek session easier for exactly this reason. But noise that makes concentration impossible also makes independent study impossible, and that is the bigger problem. If the only quiet stretch is early morning, consider moving the student's own work there and keeping the session for a later, noisier hour when a tutor's presence carries the attention.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor notice that an online tutor cannot?
faqs.answer: Posture, light, noise, clutter and fatigue. A home tutor sees a chair at the wrong height, a writing hand casting a shadow across the line, a printer out of ink since August so no paper has been attempted on paper, a sibling opening the door four times an hour, and a phone face-down and buzzing. They also see how the student sets up and packs away, which says a great deal about how the other six evenings of the week are going. A camera pointed at a face shows none of it.

faqs.question: Our DP2 child has stopped eating with the family. Should we worry?
faqs.answer: It is common in the months before May, and it is worth addressing rather than accepting. The meal is often the only point in the day when someone would notice how the student is really doing, so losing it removes the household's early warning system. A reasonable compromise is one fixed meal together on most days, kept short and free of questions about deadlines. If the student is skipping meals to buy study hours, that is a signal to cut commitments, and a tutor who sees them weekly should be asked what they are observing.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us and ask for a different match. You do not need to build an argument for it, and a month is a reasonable point to judge, because the first few weeks are mostly diagnosis. Useful things to say: the student is not talking during sessions, the work set is not being marked, the tutor keeps re-teaching rather than letting the student practise, or the slot keeps moving. We shortlist again against the same subject, level, locality and schedule, and a demo session can be arranged before you switch.

h1: IB Diploma Online Tutors in India for the Core and Rare Subjects
heroTitle: Core and Rare Subject Tutors Online Across India
heroSubtitle: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the subjects your city has almost no teacher for, taught one to one over video. This page explains what online core support can legitimately do, where the line sits, and why your school supervisor still holds the final word on the essay.
introSummary: Families look for IB Diploma online tutors in India when the part of the diploma that needs help is the part their city does not staff: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE), or a subject with one teacher in the whole school. The core carries up to 3 of the 45 points, and an E grade in either TOK or the EE is a failing condition, so it is not a soft extra. Online is usually the only way to reach a teacher who has actually marked this work. Home tuition and hybrid weeks still suit subject teaching, and we say where. What follows sets out the two TOK assessments separately, the EE with the school supervisor's role protected, and the exact boundary a tutor must not cross.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a Theory of Knowledge request in India reach a teacher?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with what you actually have. Most families write in with one line: the TOK essay is due, or the exhibition commentary came back carrying a comment nobody at home can decode. That is enough to begin. The shortlist gets much better, though, if you send specifics: whether it is the exhibition or the essay, which of the six prescribed titles the student is drawn to, what the school's internal deadline is, and what the supervisor or TOK teacher has already said about the work so far.

IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs. For core work the match is narrower than for subject tuition. A strong Physics tutor is not automatically someone who can sit with a student and interrogate a knowledge claim about the natural sciences, and a fluent essayist is not automatically someone who has read the current assessment instrument. Families searching for an online TOK and EE tutor usually want one person who can do both. That person exists. They are simply not common, and they are rarely in your neighbourhood.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and for core work that trial belongs on the student's own material rather than on a tour of the areas of knowledge. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. Timing is subject to tutor availability and to the hour you want, which for a DP2 student in Coimbatore or Jabalpur usually means late evening, after school, activities and travel are finished.

One caution before you start. If the school has not yet given the feedback the student is entitled to, get that first. A tutor working ahead of the school's own process produces a student arguing two different plans at once, and in DP2 that costs more time than it saves.
items: 1. Send the exact task: exhibition, TOK essay, or the Extended Essay.
2. Name the deadline your school set, not the IB session date.
3. Say what the supervisor or TOK teacher has already told the student.
4. Take a trial built around the student's own draft or object choice.
5. Ask for a different match if the first session feels generic.

contentBlocks.heading: Three core points, one failing condition: the diploma arithmetic in India
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four of them are taken at Higher Level (HL), which carries 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level (SL) at 150 hours. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, which gives 42. The last three points come from Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together, so the maximum is 45. Twenty-four points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed, and it takes weekday hours without adding a point.

Read that arithmetic again, because parents in India usually read it wrong. The core is not a rounding error. TOK and the EE are each graded A to E, the two grades combine on a matrix worth up to 3 points, and an E in either one is a failing condition on its own. A student sitting comfortably in the high thirties can still lose the diploma through the core. That is the strongest argument for treating core support as seriously as a final paper in a Higher Level subject.

The calendar makes it harder. Exam sessions run in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which fits the Indian academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July. So the core deadlines fall inside the same DP2 winter when mock examinations, internal assessments in every subject and university applications all land together. Nobody plans it that way. It simply happens, year after year.

Naming the structure this precisely tells you where an hour of tutoring is worth most. For a student already scoring 6s, another subject hour moves very little. A clean TOK essay and a finished EE can move the core grade, and the core grade moves the total.

HL carries 240 recommended hours, SL 150, each graded 1 to 7
TOK and the EE combine for up to 3 points; 45 is the maximum
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions
An E grade in TOK or the EE is a failing condition by itself
May session for most schools in India, with results released in early July

contentBlocks.heading: Which diploma subjects are thinly taught, and who teaches them online?
contentBlocks.body:
The thinly taught subjects are whichever ones your school runs with a single teacher, plus the core, which many schools hand to whoever has a free period. Mathematics AA and AI, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A are usually well staffed in Indian cities. TOK is not, and an EE in anything unusual is not either.

That matters because the EE is written in one DP subject or as an interdisciplinary essay. A student who wants to research a question in a subject their school teaches to only a handful of candidates is asking a supervisor to stretch. The supervisor still supervises, and should. But the subject-specific reading behind the question, the conventions of evidence in that discipline, and the difference between a descriptive survey and an argued essay are exactly what an outside teacher can work on without touching a word of the writing.

TOK is thin for a different reason. It is nobody's degree subject. The course runs across the core theme, knowledge and the knower, two of five optional themes, and five areas of knowledge: history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts. A teacher confident in three of those areas can still leave a class stranded in the other two, and the prescribed title a student picks may sit squarely in the weak one.

So families look for IB Diploma online tutors in India for a very specific reason: the person who can do this work is rarely in the same postcode. An online IB diploma tutor who has taught the exhibition repeatedly is worth more than a local generalist who has read the guide once. Ask what a tutor has actually taught, not what they could teach. And ask which area of knowledge they would decline, because anyone claiming equal strength across all five is telling you something useful about themselves.

Five areas of knowledge: history, human sciences, natural sciences, mathematics, the arts
The EE is written in one DP subject or as an interdisciplinary essay
Ask a tutor which area of knowledge they would decline to teach
Usually well staffed locally: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, English A

contentBlocks.heading: Where in India the core is taught by nobody within driving distance
contentBlocks.body:
Core teaching capacity sits where the IB schools are, and even there it runs thin. A family in Powai, Bandra or Andheri can usually find somebody; the same request from Kochi, Coimbatore or Madurai often returns nothing local at all.

Take southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai first. Thiruvananthapuram, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada each have families running the full diploma with no TOK specialist within reach. Central and western India looks the same: Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik, Raipur, Jabalpur, Aurangabad and Goa. Evening traffic between a suburb and the nearest international school in these cities can stretch a short trip badly, and a weekly two-hour essay session lost to travel is a session not spent on the essay.

Kolkata and eastern India behaves differently again. Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore sit close enough together for a home tutor to travel, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna have no such option for core work. Searches for an IB Diploma online tutor in Kolkata come mostly from those first five localities, and the answer is often a teacher in another state.

Northern India beyond Delhi NCR covers Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur. In Gujarat, requests cluster in Ahmedabad around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, and then in Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot.

The metros are not exempt. An IB Diploma online tutor in Delhi is often the practical answer for a student in Gurugram (Gurgaon) or Noida whose evenings are already gone. An IB Diploma online tutor in Bangalore serves Whitefield and Sarjapur Road for the same reason. An IB Diploma online tutor in Hyderabad, an IB Diploma online tutor in Chennai and an IB Diploma online tutor in Ahmedabad follow the pattern from Gachibowli, Adyar and Bodakdev, while an IB Diploma online tutor in Mumbai and an IB Diploma online tutor in Pune work with Worli and Baner. IB Diploma online tutors in India exist as a category because the alternative is no teacher.

Central and western India: Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik, Raipur, Goa
Kolkata and eastern India: Salt Lake, Ballygunge, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Patna
Northern India beyond Delhi NCR: Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Kanpur
Gujarat: Ahmedabad, Satellite, Bodakdev, SG Highway, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara
