contentBlocks.heading: The core calendar in India: exhibition, reflections and the May session
contentBlocks.body:
Ask your DP coordinator for the school's own core calendar in writing, and plan around that rather than around the IB session dates. Schools in India set internal deadlines for the TOK exhibition, the TOK essay and each EE reflection session, and those internal dates are what actually govern a student's term.

The shape is fairly consistent. The exhibition usually belongs to DP1, when the student is still working out what a knowledge question even is. The EE research question is settled in DP1 as well, with the first reflection session recorded, and the bulk of the 4,000 words written across the long summer break and the first DP2 term. The TOK essay, answering one of six prescribed titles released for each exam session, arrives in DP2 alongside mocks and internal assessments in every subject. Since schools here enter candidates for the May session, that pile-up lands in the same two or three months.

Families name the same schools when they call: Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We say nothing about what any school teaches or how it runs its core.

What we will say is that expectations differ sharply between schools on how much scaffolding the core receives. Some run timetabled TOK lessons every week and a supervisor who meets the student monthly. Others run a handful of sessions and expect the student to manage. You can find out which kind you are dealing with in one conversation with the coordinator, and that conversation should happen before you hire anybody.

Diwali and the long summer break are the two windows where core work genuinely fits. Use them.
items: Ask the coordinator for the school's written internal core deadlines
The exhibition usually sits in DP1; the TOK essay lands in DP2
EE reflection sessions are recorded along the way, not at the end
The May session concentrates core deadlines into the busiest DP2 term
Summer and Diwali breaks are the realistic windows for EE drafting

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home or hybrid for core work in India?
contentBlocks.body:
For the core, online usually wins, and the reason is supply rather than teaching quality. A home tutor who can teach the TOK exhibition well is rare outside a few metro pockets, so choosing home tuition for the core often means choosing a weaker teacher. For ordinary subject work the calculation flips, and a home tutor is frequently the better call.

Here is the plain comparison. A home tutor sits beside the student, sees the half-written paragraph, notices the stalling and the avoidance, and holds a weekday evening slot reliably because the travel is short. An online tutor reaches you from anywhere, which for the core is the entire point, and can share a screen, open the prescribed titles, and annotate the student's own paragraph live. A hybrid week takes both: home sessions for the subject the student is struggling with, online sessions with the core specialist who lives in another city.

Hybrid is what most DP2 families in India end up running, and it is the honest answer rather than a fudge. A Mathematics home tutor on Tuesday in Baner, a TOK teacher on Saturday morning from wherever they happen to be, and nothing else in the week.

The trade-offs are real. Online core sessions fail when the student joins with nothing open, because discussing a knowledge question in the abstract is pleasant and useless. They also fail on a phone. Home sessions fail when the tutor is competent at the subject and out of their depth on the criteria, which a family often cannot see for a full term. And a hybrid week fails when the two tutors contradict each other about the same essay, so tell each one what the other is doing.

IB Diploma online tutors in India cannot read a room the way somebody sitting across the table can. Accept that and compensate: camera on, document shared, and the student doing the talking.
items: Online: the only route to a core specialist in most Indian cities
Home: better for subject teaching where local supply is genuinely good
Hybrid: subject sessions at home, core sessions online, agreed between both tutors
Online core sessions need a shared document open from the first minute
A phone screen is not enough for reading a 1,600-word essay

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a TOK or Extended Essay tutor you never meet?
contentBlocks.body:
Check three things, in this order: what they have taught, what they will refuse to do, and what they say about your school's supervisor. A tutor who answers the third question by explaining that the supervisor leads and they support is worth more than one with a longer list of qualifications.

IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified against the details they claim, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Verification covers identity and stated experience. It cannot tell you whether this particular person will be good with your particular child on a Thursday night in Ranchi, and no platform can. That part stays with you.

So run the trial on real material. Put the student's chosen object, or the draft research question, on the shared screen and watch what the tutor does with it. A good one asks the student why they chose it and then stays quiet while the student flounders for a minute. A poor one starts proposing better objects within four minutes, which is the same instinct that later becomes rewriting the essay.

Ask directly what the tutor will not do. The answer should be unambiguous: they will not write, rewrite or edit the submission, and they will not produce a model answer to the student's own prescribed title. If the reply is vague, or worse, reassuring, stop there. You are being sold the thing that gets a candidate reported.

Finally, ask which version of the EE guide they work from. The guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so a tutor quoting criterion mark allocations from memory may be quoting something that no longer applies. The correct answer is that they follow whichever version your DP coordinator issues, and that they would like to see it. IB Diploma online tutors in India who say that are reading the right documents.
items: Verified profiles cover identity and stated experience, not classroom chemistry
Run the trial on the student's own object, draft or research question
Ask what the tutor refuses to do, and listen hard for vagueness
Check which EE guide version they use, updated for first assessment in 2027
Watch whether they let the student struggle before stepping in

contentBlocks.heading: The integrity line on TOK and the Extended Essay, stated exactly
contentBlocks.body:
Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft. It does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit the student's submission. That is the whole boundary, and for the core it bites harder than it does for ordinary subject tuition, because the core is almost entirely written work produced away from a classroom, at a desk at home, over months.

What a tutor may legitimately do is teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. Those are not consolation prizes. Teaching a student to tell a knowledge question from a topic, or to see that their second body paragraph asserts where it should argue, moves the grade more than any amount of quiet editing, and the skill survives into the next task.

The exhibition and the essay need the line drawn differently. For the exhibition, the student links three objects to one of the 35 IA prompts in up to 950 words, internally assessed, worth one third of the TOK grade. The objects must be the student's own choice, and choosing them for a student is the most common quiet breach. A tutor may ask why an object matters, what it shows about how knowledge is produced, and whether the link to the prompt is genuine. A tutor may not hand over a list.

For the essay: one of six prescribed titles, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed, two thirds of the grade. The title is set by the IB and must be answered as written. A tutor may teach a student how to unpack a title into the question it is actually asking, and may not supply the argument that answers it.

The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not the school alone. Families underestimate that last part. The consequence does not stay inside the building.
items: Feedback on one draft is allowed; writing, rewriting or editing is not
Exhibition: three objects, one of 35 IA prompts, up to 950 words
Essay: one of six prescribed titles, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed
The exhibition is internally assessed and worth one third of the TOK grade
The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking
Malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone

contentBlocks.heading: Why your school supervisor outranks any tutor you hire
contentBlocks.body:
The Extended Essay is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, and that is not an administrative detail. The supervisor records the reflection sessions, knows the school's internal deadlines, and is accountable inside a process a private tutor sits entirely outside. So when the supervisor and the tutor disagree, the supervisor wins. Tell your tutor that on day one and watch the reaction, because the reaction tells you a great deal.

The EE itself is an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of work, written in one DP subject or as an interdisciplinary essay, graded A to E, and combined with TOK for up to 3 points. Forty hours spread across more than a year is not much per week, which is precisely why it slides. A tutor's most useful contribution is often not subject expertise at all. It is holding the student to a schedule the supervisor has already set.

Do not let an outside tutor rewrite the research question the supervisor approved. If the tutor genuinely believes the question is unworkable, the student should take that argument back to the supervisor in their own words, and the supervisor decides. This is also the honest reason to be careful with EE criteria: the guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so follow the version your DP coordinator issues rather than any printout a tutor brings to a session.

Progress on core work looks slower than progress in a subject. Expect the first three or four sessions to produce very little visible text, because they should be spent on the question and the structure. By the second month the student should be able to explain their own argument out loud without reading it off the screen. If after two months they still cannot say what their essay claims, something is wrong, and it may be that the tutor is doing the thinking.

No tutor can guarantee a grade on the core, and anyone who talks about the 3 points as though they were purchasable is describing a different transaction altogether.
items: The EE is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school
Up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of work, graded A to E
Reflection sessions are recorded by the supervisor, not by an outside tutor
Follow the EE guide version your DP coordinator issues, not a tutor's printout
If supervisor and tutor disagree, the supervisor's instruction stands

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with IB Diploma online tutors in India: bring the prompt and the draft
contentBlocks.body:
Bring three things to the first session and the hour will not be wasted: the task itself, whatever the school has already said about it, and the student. Not a summary of the student's problem written by a parent. The student.

For TOK exhibition work, that means the current object choices and the IA prompt the student is considering out of the 35. For the essay, the six prescribed titles for the session, with the student's shortlist and the reason behind it. For the EE, the research question as the supervisor last saw it, the reflection notes, and an honest word count of what actually exists. A blank document is a legitimate starting point. A document a parent has tidied up is not.

The first session should end with a plan the student can repeat back without prompting. Typically that is a next chunk of writing with a deadline earlier than the school's own, one specific skill to practise, and one question to take to the supervisor. If the tutor closes by emailing a corrected version of the student's paragraph, raise it immediately, because that is the line and it has just been crossed.

Practical matters. Sessions for a DP2 student usually sit late on weekdays or on weekend mornings, subject to tutor availability and to the student's CAS and mock timetable. Ninety minutes suits core work better than an hour, since unpacking a title takes time before anything gets written. Online diploma classes in India run on the same evening pattern whether the tutor is in Chandigarh or Kochi. And IB diploma online tuition for the core is better booked as a block that ends at a deadline than as an open-ended weekly habit.

If the fit is wrong after two sessions, ask for a different match. That is quicker than hoping it improves, and in DP2 there is no spare term to lose.
items: Bring the object choices or the shortlisted prescribed title to session one
Bring the research question exactly as the supervisor last approved it
Ninety minutes suits core work better than a sixty-minute slot
Book core support as a block ending at a deadline, not open-ended
Ask for a different match after two sessions if the fit is wrong

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the TOK exhibition without choosing the objects?
faqs.answer: Yes, and choosing the objects is precisely what they must not do. The exhibition links three objects to one of the 35 IA prompts in up to 950 words, and the choice is part of what is assessed. A tutor can ask why an object matters to the student, whether the link to the prompt is real or decorative, and what the object shows about how knowledge is produced. If a tutor arrives at the first session with a list of suggested objects, that is the wrong tutor.

faqs.question: Is it allowed for a tutor to read my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Reading and discussing a draft is allowed; editing it is not. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft, and it does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit the student's submission. In practice a tutor may point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it, or question whether a claim is supported by the evidence given. The corrected paragraph emailed back is the version that crosses the line.

faqs.question: Our school released the TOK essay titles late. Can online sessions catch up?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because the essay runs to 1,600 words rather than 4,000, and much of the work is thinking rather than typing. Six prescribed titles are released for each exam session, and the first useful session is spent unpacking the chosen title into the question it is really asking. Two or three focused sessions plus the student's own drafting can produce a real essay. What cannot be compressed is the reading behind the examples, so pick a title where the student already has material.

faqs.question: There is no TOK teacher anywhere near us in Bhubaneswar. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Look online, and look outside your own state. Core teaching capacity in India clusters where the IB schools are, so Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna rarely have a local specialist, and neither do Jabalpur, Raipur or Mysuru. An online session with somebody who has taught the exhibition many times beats a local generalist who has not. Speak to your DP coordinator first, though, because the school's own TOK teacher costs nothing and is the person marking the exhibition.

faqs.question: How many sessions does core support usually take?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect for TOK, and more than they expect for the Extended Essay. The TOK essay often needs a handful of sessions around drafting, and the exhibition needs two or three if the objects are already well chosen. The EE runs to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of student work spread over more than a year, so support there works better as a short block at each stage: question, outline, first draft, final tightening. Open-ended weekly sessions tend to create dependence.

faqs.question: What does an online core session actually look like?
faqs.answer: A shared document, the student's own text on screen, and the student doing most of the talking. A typical ninety minutes opens with whatever has been written since last time, moves to one criterion or one weak paragraph, and ends with a specific writing task due before the school's internal deadline. There is no lecture. If the tutor talks for forty minutes about the areas of knowledge while the student listens politely, the session is not doing the work you are paying for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what each Extended Essay criterion is worth?
faqs.answer: They can tell you which version of the guide they are reading, and that is the answer you actually want. The EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so mark allocations quoted from memory or from an old printout may not apply to your child's session. Ask your DP coordinator which version the school is working to and use that document for everything. A tutor who insists on numbers without checking the school's version is working from something out of date.

faqs.question: Would home tuition be better than online for the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Only if a genuinely capable EE teacher lives close enough to visit, which for most families in India is the sticking point. A home tutor sees the blank page and the avoidance, which matters on a task that slides for months. An online tutor is usually the stronger teacher for the core, simply because the pool is national rather than local. Many families run a hybrid week: home sessions for a subject, online sessions for the core. That is a sensible arrangement, not a compromise.

faqs.question: What if a tutor's advice contradicts our school supervisor?
faqs.answer: The supervisor wins, every time. The Extended Essay is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, that teacher records the reflection sessions, and the school submits the work. A private tutor sits outside all of it. If the tutor believes the research question is unworkable, the student should take that argument to the supervisor in their own words and let the supervisor decide. A tutor who encourages a student to quietly ignore the supervisor is a risk rather than an asset.

faqs.question: Our child is scoring in the high thirties. Is the core worth tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: It is often the cheapest place left to gain. Subject grades at that level move slowly, while TOK and the Extended Essay together carry up to 3 points on an A to E matrix, and the work is finite and written rather than examined under timed conditions. There is also a downside to protect: an E in either one is a failing condition, whatever the subject grades look like. So the honest reason to tutor the core is not ambition. The diploma itself can turn on it.

faqs.question: We are in Koregaon Park and want weekday evening slots. Is that workable online?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and evening slots are what most DP2 families ask for. Online removes the tutor's travel, so a session in Koregaon Park, Baner or Kharadi can start at the time it says rather than after traffic has finished with everybody. Availability still depends on the tutor's other bookings and on the student's CAS and mock timetable, so book a recurring slot early, before the DP2 deadline season. Weekend mornings suit ninety-minute core sessions better than a tired weekday hour.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the student to explain their own argument out loud, without reading from the screen. On core work that is the real test, because early sessions legitimately produce little visible text while the question and the structure are being settled. If the student can say what their essay claims and why, progress is happening. If they cannot, and yet polished paragraphs keep appearing, the tutor may be doing the thinking. Raise it directly, and ask for a different match if the answer is unconvincing.

h1: IB Diploma Private Tutors for the Core: TOK, EE and CAS
heroTitle: One-to-one core support for DP students across India
heroSubtitle: The diploma core is where schools in India support students least evenly. TOK has two assessments and a word limit on each, the Extended Essay runs on a two-year timeline, and CAS quietly takes weeknights. A home tutor can teach all three without ever touching the student's own writing.
introSummary: IB Diploma private tutors in India are one-to-one teachers who take on the parts of the DP a school covers unevenly: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Most families book home tuition for a subject and then discover the core is what is actually slipping. TOK carries two assessments with different word limits and different weightings. The EE is a 4,000-word independent research essay supervised by a teacher at your child's own school. CAS is not graded, yet it still claims hours from a week that is already full. This page explains what each element demands, what a private tutor may legitimately do with each, and where the line falls.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you find an IB Diploma private tutor in India for TOK, the EE and CAS?
contentBlocks.body:
You tell IB Gram which core element is actually the problem, which DP subject the Extended Essay sits in, and when the school's next internal deadline falls. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose verified profiles match that combination, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to weekly home sessions. IB Diploma private tutors in India are shortlisted against the core element, not just against a subject name.

A parent who writes in about Physics wants a Physics teacher. A parent who writes in about the core may want three unrelated things. The TOK essay needs someone who can argue about knowledge in the natural sciences and in history without turning the session into a philosophy seminar. The Extended Essay needs someone who knows the research conventions of the subject the essay is written in, whether that is Economics or English A. CAS needs no teaching at all. It needs a plan for a week that has run out of evenings.

So the consultation asks narrower questions than usual. Which prescribed title has your child chosen, or is the choice still open? Has the exhibition been drafted, and has the school given feedback on it yet? Which subject is the EE written in, and who is the supervisor? How many reflection sessions have been held? What has the DP coordinator said in writing about internal deadlines? The answers change which tutor is right, and sometimes they change the answer to whether a tutor is needed at all.

Availability depends on the element, the level and your schedule, and core specialists are thinner on the ground than subject tutors in most Indian cities. If the first match is wrong, say so early. The family can ask for a different tutor, and it is far better to change in DP1 than three weeks before an internal deadline in DP2.
items: 1. Send a query naming the core element, the EE subject and the school's next deadline.
2. Book a free consultation covering board, level, school calendar, locality and weekly schedule.
3. Receive a shortlist of verified tutor profiles matched to that core element.
4. Run a demo or trial session before committing to any weekly arrangement.
5. Agree a term plan with the tutor, written against the school's own dates.
6. Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, without waiting.

contentBlocks.heading: Three points, two grades and one failing condition: where the core sits
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) runs over two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four of those are taken at Higher Level (HL), with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at Standard Level (SL), with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, which accounts for 42 points. The last three come from the core.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and the two grades combine to award up to 3 points. That is the whole of the core's contribution to the maximum of 45. It sounds small next to 42, and families treat it that way until they read the failing conditions. An E in either TOK or the EE is a failing condition on its own. A student can hold a comfortable subject total and still not be awarded the diploma.

Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) carries no points and no grade. It must still be completed. A student who has not completed CAS has not completed the diploma, whatever the subject grades say. This is the part parents find hardest to accept, because there is no mark to watch and no line on a report card that moves week by week.

Twenty-four points is the minimum for the award of the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Exam sessions run in May and November, and schools here overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which fits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July. Every core deadline a school sets is working backwards from that one date, which is why the school's calendar, and not the tutor's, decides the plan.
items: Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, 240 hours each
Standard Level subjects carry 150 recommended teaching hours; every subject is graded 1 to 7
TOK and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and combine for up to 3 points
An E in either TOK or the EE is a failing condition, whatever the subject totals say
CAS carries no points and no grade, and must still be completed for the diploma
Twenty-four points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions

contentBlocks.heading: The TOK exhibition, the TOK essay and a 4,000-word EE: the numbers that matter
contentBlocks.body:
TOK has two assessments, and they are not alike. The exhibition asks the student to choose three objects and link them to one of 35 IA prompts, written up in no more than 950 words. It is internally assessed by the school and is worth one third of the TOK grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for each exam session, runs to a maximum of 1,600 words, is externally assessed, and carries the remaining two thirds.

The course behind those two pieces has a shape worth knowing before you hire anyone. There is the core theme, knowledge and the knower. There are two optional themes chosen from five. And there are five areas of knowledge: history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics, and the arts. A tutor who cannot move between at least three of those areas with real examples will struggle with the essay, because the essay is judged on how the student handles knowledge across them rather than on what they know about any one.

The Extended Essay is a different animal. It is an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words, expected to take roughly 40 hours, written in one DP subject or as an interdisciplinary essay, and graded A to E. It is supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded along the way.

One warning about marking. The EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so nobody outside your school should be quoting criterion mark allocations at you, a tutor least of all. Ask the DP coordinator which version of the guide your child is working to, get the answer in writing, and make the tutor work from that document rather than from whatever they remember from an earlier cohort.

The exhibition is internally assessed and carries one third of the TOK grade
TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles per session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed
Five areas of knowledge: history, human sciences, natural sciences, mathematics and the arts
Extended Essay: up to 4,000 words, roughly 40 hours of work, graded A to E
Ask your coordinator which EE guide applies; it changed for first assessment in 2027

contentBlocks.heading: IB Diploma private tutors in India: core help from Powai to Whitefield
contentBlocks.body:
IB Diploma private tutors in India cluster where the DP schools are, and core specialists cluster harder still. In Delhi NCR that means South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri, with a second pool around Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Golf Course Road, a third across Noida, Sector 128 Noida and Greater Noida, and thinner supply in Dwarka, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. Families at the edges often settle on two home visits a week and one online session, because evening traffic on the ring roads can stretch a short trip into a long one.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the pattern repeats along the western suburbs. A request for an IB Diploma private tutor in Mumbai usually means Bandra, Juhu, Andheri or Powai, sometimes Worli, Lower Parel or Malabar Hill. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Kharghar and Thane are a separate problem, because the tutor who suits your child may live across a bridge, and a weekday evening slot over that distance is fragile in the monsoon.

Bengaluru families searching for an IB Diploma private tutor in Bangalore are usually in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Koramangala or Indiranagar, with Hebbal, Yelahanka, Jayanagar, Kanakapura Road and Electronic City further out. Chennai requests come from Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Alwarpet, Anna Nagar and Velachery, and along Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) through Perungudi. An IB Diploma private tutor in Chennai who already lives in Adyar will hold an early evening slot in Besant Nagar far more reliably than one travelling out along OMR.

Beyond the metros the arithmetic changes. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, a local TOK specialist may simply not exist, and online stops being a compromise. The same holds for families searching for an IB Diploma private tutor in Hyderabad, Pune, Kolkata or Ahmedabad when the request is TOK rather than Mathematics.
items: Delhi NCR: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Dwarka, Gurugram (Gurgaon), Noida and Greater Noida
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai and Kharghar
Bengaluru: Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Electronic City
Chennai: Adyar, Besant Nagar, Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR)
Northern India beyond Delhi NCR: Chandigarh, Mohali, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun and Kanpur
A private IB diploma tutor for TOK is scarcer than a subject tutor in every city

contentBlocks.heading: Why core support at school varies in India, and what lands back at home
contentBlocks.body:
Core support at school varies more than any other part of the DP. Some schools timetable TOK weekly across both years, run Extended Essay workshops in DP1, and appoint supervisors early. Others fold TOK into a general studies period, leave supervisor allocation until the summer between DP1 and DP2, and treat CAS as a portal the student is meant to fill in alone. Both kinds of school exist in the same city, sometimes on the same road.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore are named only because families ask about the calendar pressures students at international schools in India live with.

Those pressures are predictable. The May session drives everything, so DP2 mocks usually land in the middle of the school year, the EE final submission comes earlier than families expect, and the TOK essay upload sits close behind it. Internal deadlines are set ahead of the IB's, deliberately, to leave the school room to check and submit. A home tutor who does not have those dates on paper is planning against the wrong calendar, however good they are.

So ask the school first, and ask in writing. What is the school's internal deadline for the EE, and for the TOK exhibition and the TOK essay? How many reflection sessions are scheduled, and when? What does the supervisor expect to see at each one? Which CAS evidence is still outstanding? Bring that single document to the first home session and let the tutor plan around it.
items: Ask for the school's internal EE deadline in writing, not the IB's published date
Confirm how many reflection sessions are scheduled and what each one expects
Check when the TOK exhibition draft is due and who gives feedback on it
Find out which CAS evidence is still outstanding on the school's own portal
Bring all of it to the first session so the plan matches the school calendar

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which suits TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition suits the Extended Essay best, online suits the TOK essay best, and a hybrid week suits most DP2 students. That is the short version. The reasoning matters more than the rule, because the three core elements make different demands on the room.

The EE is long, messy and paper-heavy. A home tutor sitting beside the student can look at a printed draft, a pile of sources and a half-built bibliography at the same time, and can see the working conditions the student actually has: the desk, the noise, the phone face-up beside the laptop. Home sessions also survive the DP2 slump better than anything else, because a student cannot quietly fail to turn up to their own dining table.

TOK is different. The essay is argument, and argument travels well over a screen. A shared document with the prescribed title on one side and the student's paragraph on the other works as well online as in a room. This matters because TOK specialists are scarce outside the metros, and an online tutor in Bengaluru can take a student in Dehradun on a Tuesday evening without either of them losing an hour to traffic.

CAS needs neither, strictly. It needs a fortnightly conversation about the week ahead, which is why it usually rides along at the end of an existing home session rather than becoming a booking of its own. A hybrid week is the honest answer for most families: one home session for the EE, one online session for TOK, and CAS handled in the last ten minutes of whichever comes first. IB Diploma private tutors in India work across all three modes, and the mix should change as DP2 tightens.
items: Extended Essay: home sessions win, because drafts, sources and notes spread across a table
TOK essay: online works as well as home, and widens the pool of specialists
CAS: a short fortnightly check-in, usually attached to the end of an existing session
Hybrid weeks suit DP2, when mock periods make a fixed slot hard to hold
Online is no downgrade for TOK; often it is the only route to a specialist

contentBlocks.heading: Before a core tutor enters your home in India: what is checked, and what you check
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is shortlisted, IB Gram checks the profile: identity, the qualifications claimed, the programmes and subjects the tutor says they teach, and the level they teach at. Profiles are verified before they reach a family. That is where a platform's knowledge ends and yours begins, and for the core the gap is wider than for an ordinary subject.

A verified profile can tell you that someone has taught DP Economics. It cannot tell you whether they have ever read a TOK exhibition commentary, or whether they know that the exhibition is internally assessed and the essay is not. So ask directly. Which prescribed titles have you worked with? Can you name the five areas of knowledge without looking them up? What do you do with a student whose three objects all sit in the same area of knowledge?

For the Extended Essay, the useful questions are about process rather than content. Ask what the tutor does when a student brings a draft to a session. The honest answer involves reading it, asking questions about it, and handing it back unmarked. Ask what happens if the school supervisor has said something the tutor disagrees with. The honest answer is that the supervisor wins, and a tutor who hesitates over that question has told you enough.

Then do the things a platform cannot do for you. Meet the tutor once before the first full home session. Keep lessons in a shared part of the house rather than a bedroom. Agree in writing what happens when a session is missed on either side. And watch how your child talks about the tutor after three weeks, which will tell you more than any profile ever will.
items: Identity, qualifications and the programmes and subjects claimed are verified before shortlisting
Ask which prescribed titles and IA prompts the tutor has actually worked with
Ask what the tutor does when handed an Extended Essay draft to read
Meet the tutor once before the first full home session in your house
Keep home sessions in a shared room and agree missed-session terms in writing

contentBlocks.heading: Where does a private tutor stop on the exhibition, the EE and CAS?
contentBlocks.body:
Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft. It does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit what the student submits. That single rule governs what IB Diploma private tutors in India may do with all three core elements, and it bites differently in each.

On the TOK exhibition, a tutor may teach what an IA prompt is asking, may discuss what makes an object specific rather than generic, and may ask why a chosen object belongs to that prompt at all. A tutor may not choose the objects and may not write the commentary. The practical test is simple. If the student cannot explain a sentence of their own commentary without reading it aloud first, that sentence should not be in the file.

On the TOK essay, a tutor may unpack a prescribed title, teach how a knowledge question is built, and supply worked examples from the natural sciences or history so the student can see what a usable example looks like. A tutor may not supply the examples that go into the essay, and may not redraft a paragraph. Pointing at a criterion and asking the student to reread their own paragraph against it is teaching. Rewriting the paragraph is not.

On the Extended Essay the line is sharpest, because the EE is where outside help most often crosses it. The supervisor is a teacher at the student's own school, the reflection sessions are recorded, and the school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking. A tutor sits outside all of that. They may teach how to narrow a research question, how to evaluate a source, how to reference properly, and how an argument holds over 4,000 words. They may not write, edit or restructure it. CAS is simpler still: a tutor cannot do CAS and cannot write reflections. Malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone, and the consequences land on the student.
items: A teacher may give feedback on one draft; nobody may write or edit the submission
Tutors may teach the skill, question the reasoning and point at a criterion
On the exhibition: discuss what makes an object specific, never choose the objects
On the EE: teach research question design and referencing, never redraft the text
CAS reflections must be the student's own; a tutor can only help plan the hours
Schools run similarity checking, and the IB handles malpractice findings, not the school alone

contentBlocks.heading: When should core progress show, and what does a term-by-term plan look like?
contentBlocks.body:
Give the core a term, not a month. A TOK essay improves when a student's thinking improves, and that is slower than a subject grade moving. What you should see inside four to six weeks is different in kind: a sharper research question, a student who can say what their prescribed title is actually asking, and drafts that arrive before the school's deadline rather than on the evening of it.

Now the honest limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and on the core that is doubly true, because the exhibition is marked by the school and the essay by an external examiner nobody will ever meet. A tutor also cannot make CAS happen. If your child has not started CAS in DP1, hiring someone in DP2 is a late and expensive way to find that out.

There are cases where the right answer is no tuition. A student whose EE is on schedule and whose TOK essay draft has come back with workable supervisor feedback does not need a core tutor. They need to do the reading. Adding a weekly session there takes an evening away from the six subjects where 42 of the 45 points sit, and good IB Diploma private tutors in India will say so rather than take the booking.

Where a tutor genuinely earns the slot is the student who has stalled. The EE with no research question by March of DP1. The exhibition draft that keeps being postponed. The student who argues well over dinner and writes nothing on the page. Those are fixable, and they are fixed faster by one person watching the whole core than by three teachers each watching a third of it.
items: 1. DP1 term one: settle the EE subject and sketch two or three candidate research questions.
2. DP1 term two: hold the first reflection session, read widely, and narrow to one question.
3. DP1 term three: complete most of the EE research and start choosing exhibition objects.
4. Summer between DP1 and DP2: draft the EE fully and clear outstanding CAS strands.
5. DP2 term one: submit the exhibition and choose from the session's six prescribed titles.
6. DP2 term two: finish the TOK essay, close CAS, and hand everything in early.

contentBlocks.heading: Your first home session on the core in India: what to have ready
contentBlocks.body:
Bring paper. The first home session on the core works best when the tutor can see the actual documents: the school's deadline sheet, the EE research question as it currently stands, any supervisor feedback in writing, the exhibition draft if one exists, and a screenshot of the CAS portal showing what is still outstanding.

The session itself should not really be teaching. An hour spent reading what exists, asking the student to explain their own research question out loud, and working out which of the three core elements is genuinely behind is worth more than an hour on knowledge questions. Expect the tutor to finish that session with a plan written against the school's dates, not a generic two-year schedule copied from the last family.

Parents should be in the house and not in the room, for a DP student. A seventeen-year-old talks differently when a parent is listening, and the core depends on the student saying plainly what they do not understand. Ask for a short summary after each session instead, and read it.

To start, send a query or book a free consultation. Say which core element is the problem, name your locality, and say which evenings are actually free once school, activities and CAS commitments are accounted for. IB Gram will ask about board, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then come back with verified profiles that match, and a demo session can be arranged before you commit to anything. Availability depends on the element, the EE subject and your schedule, and it is tightest for TOK outside the big metros.
items: The school's deadline sheet for the EE, the TOK exhibition and the TOK essay
The current EE research question, however rough, and the supervisor's last written feedback
The exhibition draft and the three objects, if the student has chosen them
A screenshot of the CAS portal showing which strands are still outstanding
Two evening slots that survive school, CAS commitments and traffic in your locality

faqs.question: Can a private tutor help my child write the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is telling you something important about themselves. The Extended Essay must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach how to narrow a research question, how to judge whether a source is usable, how to reference consistently, and how an argument holds together over 4,000 words. They may read a draft and ask questions about it. They may not write a sentence of it, restructure it or edit it. Your school submits the essay and runs it through similarity checking.

faqs.question: Who supervises the Extended Essay, and can we appoint someone outside the school?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is a teacher at your child's own school, and that cannot be outsourced. Reflection sessions are held with that supervisor and recorded along the way, which forms part of the assessment record rather than an administrative formality. A private tutor works alongside that relationship and never in place of it. If the tutor's advice and the supervisor's instructions differ, the supervisor's instruction is the one the student follows, every time. The school knows which version of the guide applies and is accountable for what is submitted.

faqs.question: Is TOK worth paying for when the whole core is only 3 points?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because the real risk is the failing condition rather than the points. TOK and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E and combine for up to 3 points towards a maximum of 45. An E in either is a failing condition on its own, so a student sitting on a comfortable subject total can still miss the diploma. Judge it on where your child currently stands. If the TOK essay draft is coming back workable, spend that evening on the six subjects instead.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come to our flat in Bandra or Powai on a weekday evening for TOK?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, subject to tutor availability and your exact locality. Weekday evening slots across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region are the most requested and the first to go, so a family in Bandra, Juhu, Andheri or Powai should ask early in DP1 rather than partway through DP2. Distance decides reliability more than anything else does. A tutor living inside the same cluster of suburbs will hold an evening slot far better through the monsoon than one crossing from Thane or Navi Mumbai twice a week.

faqs.question: What does a home session on the Extended Essay actually cover?
faqs.answer: Reading, questioning and planning, in that order. The tutor reads what exists, asks the student to explain the research question out loud without notes, and finds the point where the argument stops being the student's own. Then the two of them plan the next fortnight against the school's deadline sheet. A good home session usually ends with the student holding a short list of things to read and one section to write, and with the tutor holding nothing at all.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Diploma private tutor in India cost for the core?
faqs.answer: It depends on the element, the level and your city, and no honest answer is a single figure. One-to-one core tuition at home costs more per hour than an online session, because travel time is being paid for as well as teaching. TOK and the Extended Essay usually cost more than a routine subject hour, because far fewer tutors teach them at all. A small online group class shares the cost. Ask for the rate in writing before the demo session, and ask what a missed session costs.

faqs.question: Our daughter is behind on CAS. Can a tutor fix that?
faqs.answer: Not directly. CAS carries no grade and no points, and it must still be completed for the diploma to be awarded, which means the student has to do it herself. A tutor can help in one narrow way: by sitting down with the school's portal, working out which strands are genuinely outstanding, and building those into a week that already holds six subjects and an Extended Essay. Creativity, Activity and Service are her own commitments, and the reflections must be hers.

faqs.question: We live in Chandigarh and nobody here teaches TOK. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Online, and for TOK that is not a second-best choice. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, a local TOK specialist is often unavailable at any price. The TOK essay is argument on a page, which transfers to a screen better than almost any other DP work. Keep the Extended Essay with a local tutor if you have one, run TOK online, and treat that hybrid week as the normal arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and the school supervisor give different advice?
faqs.answer: The supervisor wins, without discussion. The school holds the current guide, sets the internal deadlines, records the reflection sessions and submits the work. A tutor sits outside all of that and is working from whatever you have shown them. The EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so a tutor quoting criterion mark allocations from memory may be quoting a version that no longer applies to your child. Ask your DP coordinator which guide is in force and make the tutor work from it.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in the room during a home session on the core?
faqs.answer: For a DP student, no. Be in the house, not in the room. The core depends on a seventeen-year-old admitting what they do not understand about their own argument, and that conversation changes the moment a parent is listening to it. Keep sessions in a shared part of the house rather than a bedroom, which settles the safeguarding question without sitting in. Ask the tutor for three lines afterwards: what was covered, what the student will do next, and what is worrying them.

faqs.question: Our DP2 son has mocks and an EE deadline in the same fortnight. What should give?
faqs.answer: The EE deadline is fixed and the mocks are not, so plan around the deadline first. Schools in India set internal deadlines ahead of the IB's precisely to leave room to check and submit, which makes the school's date the real one. Tell the tutor about the clash at the start of term and not in the week itself. In practice that fortnight usually holds if the essay was drafted over the summer between DP1 and DP2, and it rarely holds if it was not.

faqs.question: When should core tuition start, DP1 or DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, if the choice is yours. The Extended Essay is roughly 40 hours of work spread over a two-year timeline, and almost every family who books core help in DP2 is paying to recover ground rather than to build it. Starting in DP1 also spreads the CAS strands across two years instead of cramming them into one. If you are already in DP2, begin with a single diagnostic session rather than a weekly booking, and decide from what that session finds.

comparison.heading: How does one-to-one core tuition at home compare with the alternatives in India?
comparison.intro: The core is not a syllabus you can cover in a batch, because the exhibition, the essay and the EE are each one student's own piece of work. Group formats still earn their place: TOK improves in discussion, and a batch usually costs less per hour. The trade-off is simple. A group gives your child other people's ideas; one-to-one gives your child time on their own argument.

Works as a short fortnightly call, provided the student brings the portal open.
Rarely covered, since CAS is personal and the evidence differs for every student.
Not covered. CAS is not a taught subject and no batch can complete it.

cells: Highest per hour, since one tutor's full attention and travel time are both being paid for.
Lower than home, because no travel is priced in and the pool of tutors is larger.
Shared across the group, so lower per student for the same hour of teaching.
Lowest per hour, which is its main argument and sometimes a sufficient one.

cells: Strong. One person holds the whole core history, from research question to final submission.
Strong, and unaffected by a family moving between cities mid-programme.
