h1: IB Diploma Tuition, Retakes and an Enquiry Upon Results
heroTitle: After IB Diploma Results: Retake Support Across India
heroSubtitle: Results arrive in early July, and the questions that follow have short fuses. This page explains an enquiry upon results, how a November retake is registered through a school, what your child would sit again, and how home tuition, online lessons or a hybrid week should be planned around it.
introSummary: IB Diploma tuition in India after results is a different job from tuition during the two teaching years, and home tuition for a retake candidate has to be built backwards from a November session rather than a May one. May results are released in early July. Within days a family has to work out three separate things: whether to ask the school about an enquiry upon results, which is a re-mark; whether a retake in a later session is worth registering for; and whether the honest answer is to accept the result and move on. Those are three decisions, not one, and they run on different clocks. This page takes them in order, says plainly which answers only your Diploma Programme (DP) coordinator can give, and describes what tutoring should and should not try to fix.

contentBlocks.heading: From July results to a retake plan: how IB Diploma tuition in India starts
contentBlocks.body:
A query that arrives in July reads differently from one that arrives in September. The student has a result. There is a transcript with grades on it, a total, and in some cases a failing condition that sank an otherwise reasonable set of sixes. So the first conversation is not about a syllabus. It is about which of the three routes the family is actually on: a re-mark, a retake, or neither.

IB Gram is an independent platform, and the International Baccalaureate (IB) sets the rules that decide two of those three routes. What the platform can do is narrow the teaching problem. When you send a query or book a free consultation, you will be asked for the subjects and levels, the grades that came back, which papers the marks fell on if you know, whether the school has been contacted about an enquiry upon results, the city and locality you are in, and the days and hours a student who is no longer in school every morning can actually work.

Those answers change the shortlist a great deal. IB Diploma tuition in India at this stage is a shortlist built on papers rather than on a syllabus. A candidate targeting one Higher Level (HL) subject needs one specialist. A candidate rebuilding four subjects for a November session needs a schedule before she needs a tutor. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match those needs, subject to tutor availability, and a demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits. Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week. If the fit is wrong after a few sessions, ask for a different match rather than waiting the term out.

One caution at the start. Nobody here can tell you whether your child is eligible to register, when the deadline falls, or what it costs. Those three belong to the DP coordinator, and a shortlist built before those answers arrive is a shortlist built on a guess.
items: 1. Send the July results, subject by subject, with levels and any failing condition noted.
2. Ask the DP coordinator about an enquiry upon results before the short deadline passes.
3. Confirm with the coordinator whether registration for a later session is open to your child.
4. Tell IB Gram the target session, the subjects, your locality and the weekly hours available.
5. Run a trial session on a past paper from the subject that fell furthest.
6. Fix the weekly shape: home tuition, online or hybrid, and review it after a month.

contentBlocks.heading: What carries forward to a November session, and what must be sat again
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme is two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects taken from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level (SL) with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the ceiling and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed.

A retake does not reopen all of that. Internal assessment marks are usually carried forward, which is the single most useful sentence on this page, because it means the internally assessed work already marked and moderated is not produced a second time. The retake mainly targets the externally assessed papers.

That changes the arithmetic of what tutoring is for. If a student lost a grade because the internal assessment was weak, a retake cannot recover it, and that is worth knowing before anyone pays for lessons. If the student lost the grade on Paper 2, the retake is aimed at exactly the thing tuition can move. Read the two cases differently, because they lead to opposite decisions.

The core needs its own thought. The TOK exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 prompts, runs to 950 words, is internally assessed and carries one third of the TOK grade. The TOK essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for each exam session, runs to 1,600 words and is externally assessed for the other two thirds, which means a November candidate faces a different set of titles from the ones sat in May. TOK and EE grades run A to E, an E in either is a failing condition, and whether either component carries into a new session is a question for the DP coordinator and nobody else.
items: Internal assessment marks are usually carried forward; the coordinator confirms this for your child.
Externally assessed papers are what a later session actually puts in front of the student.
A weak internal assessment is not repaired by sitting the written papers again.
TOK essay titles are released per session, so a November candidate answers different ones.
Twenty-four points is the diploma minimum, subject to the failing conditions the IB sets.

contentBlocks.heading: Which papers does a retake actually put your child back in front of?
contentBlocks.body:
The externally assessed papers of the subjects you re-register, and nothing else. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, English A: in each case the written papers come round again, while the internally assessed work already submitted usually stays where it is. So the plan is narrow, and it should look like this.

1. Pull the returned mark breakdown for every subject being retaken and mark where the loss sat, paper by paper.

2. Work only on externally assessed components for the first month, using past papers, markschemes and subject reports obtained through the school or the IB's official channels.

3. Drill the command terms that carried the lost marks. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each demand a different depth, and a student who answers all six the same way loses marks in every subject at once.

4. From the second month, sit full papers to time, one subject a week, and mark them against the markscheme with the tutor in the room.

5. In the final stretch before the session, stop teaching content and work only on the three or four question types that still cost marks.

The subject detail matters here. A Mathematics candidate who lost marks through method rather than concept needs timed writing, not re-teaching. A Physics candidate who can calculate but cannot explain is losing marks on command terms, and that is a teachable, fixable gap. An English A candidate retaking Paper 1 is practising guided analysis on unseen material, so no amount of re-reading the set texts will help. And an Economics candidate who underperformed on the written papers is in a very different position from one whose portfolio was the problem.
items: Mathematics AA and AI: the written papers return, the internally assessed exploration usually does not.
Physics, Chemistry and Biology: written papers return; internally assessed practical work normally carries forward.
Economics and English A: externally assessed papers only, set on the new session's material.
Command terms set the depth: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent.
Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or official IB channels.

contentBlocks.heading: Studying for a November retake from any part of India
contentBlocks.body:
A retake term has one advantage over a school year: the student is not in class from eight in the morning. That frees daytime hours, and it changes where home tuition is practical.

In Delhi NCR, a tutor who would never cross from Noida to Gurugram (Gurgaon) for a seven o'clock slot will often take a two-hour afternoon session, because the road empties in the middle of the day. Families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka usually have the widest choice of subject specialists. Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad are thinner, and evening traffic on the expressways can stretch a short trip badly, so an afternoon home visit or a hybrid week tends to hold better there.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region splits the same way. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit inside a workable radius for most tutors. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar do not, and a family searching for IB Diploma tuition in Mumbai from Kharghar will usually get a stronger tutor online than a nearer one who arrives tired.

Bengaluru is the clearest case of all. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road are far from Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Jayanagar in practice, whatever the map suggests. In Hyderabad, Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Kokapet and the Financial District cluster neatly, while Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad are a separate run for a tutor to make.

Beyond the metros, families in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai search for IB Diploma tuition near me and find nobody teaching a retake subject at Higher Level. That is not a failure of the search. It is supply. IB Diploma tuition in India for a November session is, for a great many families outside the six metro clusters, an online arrangement with a hybrid month before the papers.
items: Delhi NCR: afternoon home sessions beat evening ones once school no longer sets the clock.
Searches for IB Diploma tuition in Delhi and in Hyderabad thin out by locality, not by city.
IB Diploma tuition in Bangalore: Whitefield and Jayanagar are two entirely different supply pools.
IB Diploma tuition in Chennai, Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad often resolves to an online specialist.
Kochi, Coimbatore and Visakhapatnam: expect a hybrid month rather than weekly home visits.

contentBlocks.heading: Why a retake in India is registered through a school, not by the family
contentBlocks.body:
A candidate cannot register herself. Registration for a later session goes through a school, normally the one the candidate sat the exams with, and most often the target is the following November. That single fact reorganises the whole summer, because it means the first call is not to a tutor. It is to the DP coordinator at the school your child has just left.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools appear here as context for the calendar that families in India live inside, nothing more.

That calendar is worth spelling out. IB schools in India almost all enter candidates for the May session, which fits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March. November is used by a small minority of schools and by retake candidates. So a retake student is out of step with everyone around her. Her former classmates are deep in university admissions in the autumn while she is still preparing papers, and the school's own DP2 mock cycle, which each school sets for itself several months before May, is not built for her at all.

Names such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore come up constantly in these conversations, from the Mumbai Metropolitan Region to Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai. What matters is not the name on the transcript. It is whether that school's coordinator is willing and able to register a candidate who has already left the roll. Ask early, ask directly, and ask in writing so that the reply exists somewhere other than in memory.
items: Registration for a later session runs through a school, normally the one the candidate sat with.
Email the former school's DP coordinator rather than phoning, and keep the reply.
Indian IB schools enter almost everyone in May; November carries the minority and the retakes.
A retake candidate sits outside the school's DP2 mock cycle and must build her own.
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, which is why May dominates here.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a retake term in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition for the subject that needs a person in the room, online for the specialist you cannot reach locally, and hybrid for most retake candidates, because a retake term is long enough that the right answer changes inside it. That is the short version. The longer one depends on how many subjects are being sat again.

A single-subject retake usually works at home. One tutor, two sessions a week, the same table, papers marked in front of the student. A home tutor also sees what a screen hides: the student who has stopped getting dressed before lunch, the room that has quietly become a bedroom again, the phone face-up beside the question paper. In a retake term, with no school timetable holding the day together, that observation is worth nearly as much as the teaching.

A three or four subject rebuild rarely stays at home. Finding three verified specialists who will each travel to Powai or Sarjapur Road on fixed weekday afternoons is hard, and IB Diploma tuition in India at that scale is normally two subjects taught at home and the rest online.

The hybrid pattern that works best in a retake term is not a fixed weekly split. It is online teaching through the content months, then home sessions for the last stretch, when papers are being sat to time and somebody needs to watch the student write. Online lessons hold the schedule when a tutor is unwell or the monsoon closes a road in Bengaluru or the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Home classes hold the student's attention when motivation goes, which in a retake term it usually does, somewhere around the second month.
items: One subject, one tutor: home tuition is usually the simplest arrangement to hold together.
Three or four subjects: expect online lessons for the scarce Higher Level specialists.
Hybrid works best as online content months, then home sessions for timed papers.
Online lessons survive monsoon roads and tutor illness; a home visit often does not.
A home tutor sees the student's real working conditions, which a screen never shows.

contentBlocks.heading: What to check in a retake tutor before home classes start
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram covers identity, qualifications and teaching background, and profiles are verified before a tutor is shortlisted. That is the platform's half of the work. The family's half is narrower and more specific for a retake than for ordinary tuition, because the tutor is being hired for one task with a fixed date at the end of it.

Ask three things. Has this tutor taught the subject at the level being retaken, rather than a neighbouring level. Has he worked with a candidate sitting a November session rather than a May one, which has a different run-up and a very different feel. And can he mark a past paper against the markscheme in front of you at the trial, out loud, explaining where each mark went and why. The third question separates a subject expert from an examiner-minded teacher, and for a retake you want the second kind.

Then the ordinary checks, which do not stop mattering because the student is older. If the tutor is coming into your home, note the identity document, tell your society or building office the name in advance, and hold the sessions in a room with the door left open rather than a bedroom. In Gurugram (Gurgaon), Bandra or Banjara Hills, gate entry for a regular visitor is usually arranged once with the association office rather than argued at the gate every week.

And check what the tutor will not claim. No tutor can guarantee a grade in a retake session, and a tutor who says otherwise has told you something useful about himself. The honest answer to what a retake can achieve is a range and a set of conditions.
items: Confirm the tutor has taught the exact subject and level your child is retaking.
Ask for one past paper marked live against the markscheme during the trial session.
Check the identity document yourself and register the tutor at the society gate once.
Hold home sessions in a shared room with the door open, never in a bedroom.
Treat any promise about a certain points jump as a reason to look elsewhere.

contentBlocks.heading: What is an enquiry upon results, and who asks for one?
contentBlocks.body:
An enquiry upon results is a re-mark: a formal request, made through the school rather than by the family, to have a candidate's externally assessed work looked at again. The school submits it. The parent asks the school. There is a deadline shortly after results come out, and it is short, which is the whole reason this page exists.

Results are released in early July. The temptation is to spend a week being upset and then act. That week is often the entire window, and by the time a family has finished comparing the transcript against the predicted grades, the decision has made itself.

So treat it as a two-day job. Look at each subject where the grade is lower than everything the student produced all year and lower than the school's own expectation. A grade two below a consistent pattern is a far stronger case than a grade one below a hopeful one. Then email the DP coordinator with the subjects, the reason for each, and a direct question about the deadline, the eligibility and the cost. The coordinator will have done this before, many times.

Understand what a re-mark is not. It is not an appeal about how hard a paper was, and it is not a second opinion on internally assessed work. Whether a grade can move in either direction, and what happens to the rest of the diploma if it does, is something the coordinator will explain before anything is submitted. Some families run both tracks at once: they ask about an enquiry and begin planning a November retake in the same week, on the assumption that the re-mark will change nothing. That is the cautious order, and usually the correct one.
items: An enquiry upon results is a re-mark, submitted by the school, not by a parent.
The deadline falls shortly after results and is short; the coordinator knows the date.
Build the case from subjects that fell well below a consistent year of work.
Ask about eligibility, the deadline and the cost in one written email to the coordinator.
Plan the November retake in parallel, assuming the re-mark changes nothing at all.

contentBlocks.heading: Retake or move on: which decision fits your child in India?
contentBlocks.body:
There is a version of this decision that nobody sells, and it is the right one for a fair number of families: do not retake. A university place already accepted, a course that does not need the missing point, a student who is flattened after two years of Creativity, Activity, Service commitments and internal assessment deadlines stacked on each other. In those cases a retake buys a better number on a certificate that nobody will ask about again.

The cases for retaking are narrower and much clearer. The diploma itself was missed and a place depends on it. A course requires a specific subject grade the student did not reach. Or the gap is one or two points and sits on a paper the student demonstrably underperformed on, which the mark breakdown will show.

Progress in a retake term also looks different from progress during DP2. No criterion feedback arrives from a teacher and there is no mock cycle to measure against, so you build your own. A full paper under timed conditions every two or three weeks, marked against the markscheme, with the score written down where both of you can see it. If the score has not moved after three of those, the arrangement is not working, and the honest response is to change the tutor or change the plan rather than quietly continue.

Be straight about the limits too. IB Diploma tuition in India cannot recover marks lost on internally assessed work that carries forward. It cannot make a student who has mentally moved on start caring again. And it cannot compress a subject that was never properly learned into eight weeks, which is a real thing tutors are asked to attempt every July.
items: Retake when a place depends on the diploma or on one named subject grade.
Move on when the missing point changes nothing that has already been accepted.
Measure progress with a timed paper every two or three weeks, marked and recorded.
Three flat scores in a row means change the plan, not simply add hours.
No tutor can recover marks lost on internally assessed work that carries forward.

contentBlocks.heading: Preparing for a first home session after results in India
contentBlocks.body:
Bring paper to the first session. Not a description of what went wrong, but the documents: the results transcript, any mark breakdown the school has released, the last two mock scripts if they still exist, and the subject reports if the school shared them. A first home session that starts from real scripts is worth three that start from a conversation.

The session itself should do one thing: establish where the marks actually went. A good tutor will take one past paper in the weakest subject, have the student sit a section of it in front of him, and mark it aloud. By the end you should be holding a list of question types rather than a list of topics, because a retake plan built on topics covers everything and fixes nothing.

Set the shape of the term at that first meeting. How many sessions a week per subject, which days, what happens between sessions, and what the student does alone. A retake candidate with no school day has more hours and less structure than she has ever had, and the structure has to come from somewhere. Two home sessions a week with nothing in between is worse than one session with four hours of set work attached to it.

Agree a review point before you start. A month is sensible. At that review, look at the timed scores and decide whether the tutor, the mode or the plan needs to change. Availability for any particular tutor depends on level and schedule, so if a change is needed, ask early rather than at the end of the term when the session is close.
items: Bring the transcript, the mark breakdown, the last mock scripts and any subject reports.
Expect the first session to produce a list of question types, not a list of topics.
Agree sessions per week, the days, and the work done between them, in writing.
Set a one-month review against timed paper scores before the first lesson happens.
Ask for a different match early if the fit is wrong; do not wait it out.

faqs.question: My child missed the diploma by two points. Is a retake the right call?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if a university place genuinely depends on the diploma rather than on individual grades. Two points is a realistic gap to close when the loss sits on externally assessed papers, because those are exactly what a later session puts back in front of the candidate. It is a poor bet when the points went on internally assessed work, which is usually carried forward and cannot be improved by sitting the papers again. Ask the school for the mark breakdown before deciding anything, and ask the DP coordinator whether registration is open to your child at all.

faqs.question: How do we request an enquiry upon results, and how long do we have?
faqs.answer: You do not request it directly. The school submits it, and the parent asks the school, so the first step is an email to the DP coordinator naming the subjects and the reason for each. The window after results is short, which is why this should be a two-day job rather than a two-week one. The coordinator will confirm the deadline, whether your child is eligible and what it costs, and those three answers come from her office, not from a tutor or a website. Plan the retake in parallel, assuming the re-mark changes nothing.

faqs.question: Does a retake mean sitting the internal assessment again?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Internal assessment marks are normally carried forward into the later session, so a retake mainly targets the externally assessed papers, and the coursework already submitted and moderated stays as it is. That is good news for a student whose written papers went badly, and bad news for one whose internal assessment dragged the grade down, because a retake cannot repair that. The Theory of Knowledge exhibition is internally assessed while the essay is not, so the core needs its own conversation. Only the DP coordinator can confirm exactly what carries for your child.

faqs.question: Can we start home tuition before the school confirms registration?
faqs.answer: You can, and for one or two subjects it is often sensible, because the content work is the same either way and July is not a month to waste. Keep it small until the coordinator replies. A single weekly home session in the weakest subject costs little in time and builds the diagnostic picture you will need anyway. What you should not do is commit to three or four subjects of home tuition for a full term before anyone has confirmed that your child can register for the session you are aiming at.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a retake candidate need at home each week?
faqs.answer: For one subject, usually two home sessions a week with substantial work set between them. For three or four subjects, the honest answer is that home lessons alone will not fit the week, and most families run two subjects at home and the rest online. The number matters less than the ratio. A retake candidate has no school day, so the hours worked alone should outweigh the hours with a tutor by a wide margin, and the sessions exist mainly to set, mark and correct that independent work.

faqs.question: We are in Kochi and nobody here teaches Higher Level Chemistry. What now?
faqs.answer: Go online for that subject and stop searching locally, because the supply genuinely is not there. Higher Level specialists cluster where the IB schools cluster, which in practice means Delhi NCR, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune. Families in Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam and Mysuru routinely find the right teacher two cities away. If travel is possible, a hybrid arrangement works well: online teaching through the content months, then a short block of home sessions in the weeks when full papers are being sat to time.

faqs.question: Is the November session harder than May?
faqs.answer: There is no basis for saying one session is harder than the other, and a tutor who tells you otherwise is guessing. What genuinely differs is the run-up. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, so a November candidate prepares without a cohort, without the school's mock cycle and often without classmates to compare work against. The Theory of Knowledge essay titles are released for each session, so a November candidate answers a different set from the one sat in May. Build your own checkpoints, because the school calendar will not supply them.

faqs.question: What does IB re-mark help from a tutor actually look like?
faqs.answer: Very little, and that is the honest answer. A re-mark is submitted by the school, assessed by the IB and decided without any input from a private tutor. What a tutor can reasonably do is read the mark breakdown with you and say whether the pattern looks odd for the standard of work he has seen, which is useful context for the email you send the coordinator. Anyone advertising influence over the outcome of an enquiry upon results is selling something that does not exist.

faqs.question: The tutor comes home on weekday afternoons. Does a parent need to be at home?
faqs.answer: Someone responsible should be in the flat, though not in the room. For a seventeen or eighteen year old the requirement is lighter than for a younger child, but a home session should still run in a shared room with the door open rather than a bedroom. Arrange gate entry once with your society or building office in Gurugram, Powai or Banjara Hills rather than negotiating it weekly at the gate. And if nobody can be present on a given afternoon, move that session online rather than cancelling it.

faqs.question: Our child already holds a university place. Should we retake anyway?
faqs.answer: Usually not. If the offer has been accepted and the course does not require the missing point or the missing subject grade, a retake spends a term of a young adult's life improving a number nobody will ask about again. The exceptions are real, though: a deferred place conditional on the diploma, a course with a named subject requirement, or a plan to apply elsewhere next year. Confirm the position with the university in writing before deciding, and treat what an agent or a tutor thinks as secondary.

faqs.question: How do we know after a month whether the retake tuition is working?
faqs.answer: By the timed scores, not by how the sessions feel. Agree before the first lesson that the student will sit a full externally assessed paper under timed conditions every two or three weeks, marked against the markscheme, with the score written down. After a month you will be holding two or three data points. If they have not moved, change something: the tutor, the mode or the plan. Continuing an arrangement that produced no movement in a short retake term is the most common mistake families make.

acceptedAnswer.text: For one subject, usually two home sessions a week with substantial work set between them. For three or four subjects, the honest answer is that home lessons alone will not fit the week, and most families run two subjects at home and the rest online. The number matters less than the ratio. A retake candidate has no school day, so the hours worked alone should outweigh the hours with a tutor by a wide margin, and the sessions exist mainly to set, mark and correct that independent work.

mainEntity.name: We are in Kochi and nobody here teaches Higher Level Chemistry. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go online for that subject and stop searching locally, because the supply genuinely is not there. Higher Level specialists cluster where the IB schools cluster, which in practice means Delhi NCR, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune. Families in Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam and Mysuru routinely find the right teacher two cities away. If travel is possible, a hybrid arrangement works well: online teaching through the content months, then a short block of home sessions in the weeks when full papers are being sat to time.

mainEntity.name: Is the November session harder than May?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no basis for saying one session is harder than the other, and a tutor who tells you otherwise is guessing. What genuinely differs is the run-up. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, so a November candidate prepares without a cohort, without the school's mock cycle and often without classmates to compare work against. The Theory of Knowledge essay titles are released for each session, so a November candidate answers a different set from the one sat in May. Build your own checkpoints, because the school calendar will not supply them.

mainEntity.name: What does IB re-mark help from a tutor actually look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Very little, and that is the honest answer. A re-mark is submitted by the school, assessed by the IB and decided without any input from a private tutor. What a tutor can reasonably do is read the mark breakdown with you and say whether the pattern looks odd for the standard of work he has seen, which is useful context for the email you send the coordinator. Anyone advertising influence over the outcome of an enquiry upon results is selling something that does not exist.

mainEntity.name: The tutor comes home on weekday afternoons. Does a parent need to be at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Someone responsible should be in the flat, though not in the room. For a seventeen or eighteen year old the requirement is lighter than for a younger child, but a home session should still run in a shared room with the door open rather than a bedroom. Arrange gate entry once with your society or building office in Gurugram, Powai or Banjara Hills rather than negotiating it weekly at the gate. And if nobody can be present on a given afternoon, move that session online rather than cancelling it.

mainEntity.name: Our child already holds a university place. Should we retake anyway?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. If the offer has been accepted and the course does not require the missing point or the missing subject grade, a retake spends a term of a young adult's life improving a number nobody will ask about again. The exceptions are real, though: a deferred place conditional on the diploma, a course with a named subject requirement, or a plan to apply elsewhere next year. Confirm the position with the university in writing before deciding, and treat what an agent or a tutor thinks as secondary.

mainEntity.name: How do we know after a month whether the retake tuition is working?

acceptedAnswer.text: By the timed scores, not by how the sessions feel. Agree before the first lesson that the student will sit a full externally assessed paper under timed conditions every two or three weeks, marked against the markscheme, with the score written down. After a month you will be holding two or three data points. If they have not moved, change something: the tutor, the mode or the plan. Continuing an arrangement that produced no movement in a short retake term is the most common mistake families make.

h1: IB Maths Tutors in India for Analysis and Approaches and Applications
heroTitle: Choosing an IB maths tutor in India
heroSubtitle: Two different mathematics courses sit behind the same subject name, and the one your child is placed in changes what tutoring has to do. This page covers Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation, at Higher Level and Standard Level, the exploration, and how home tuition is arranged across Indian cities.
introSummary: IB Maths tutors in India teach two different Diploma Programme (DP) courses, not one. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) is algebraic and proof-heavy; Mathematics Applications and Interpretation (AI) is modelling and statistics-heavy, with technology used throughout. Each runs at Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), so a family arranging home tuition is really choosing between four courses. Get that wrong and the first month goes to waste. The mathematics exploration, the same internal assessment (IA) task in all four, carries 20% of the final grade and is marked out of 20 on five criteria. A home tutor worth keeping teaches the course and the exploration together rather than one after the other, and says plainly when a student is sitting in the wrong course.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram shortlists an AA or AI maths tutor in India
contentBlocks.body:
Tell us the course, not the subject. "We need a maths tutor" is the most common request we receive and the least useful. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation SL are different teaching jobs, and a tutor who is strong in one can be merely adequate in the other. So the first thing we ask is which of the four Diploma Programme (DP) mathematics courses the school has placed the student in, whether that placement is settled, and what the student's last two pieces of marked work actually looked like.

After that the questions get practical. Is the student in DP1 or DP2? Has the exploration been started, chosen, or not yet mentioned in class? Which school calendar are you working to, and when do mocks land? Where do you live, how does evening traffic run between that locality and the areas where DP teachers tend to live, and is a weekday evening home session realistic, or would two online slots hold better? A parent in Powai and a parent in Yelahanka get different answers to that last question, and both answers change again during the monsoon.

Then we shortlist. Profiles are verified before they go live, and we match on the specific course rather than on the word "maths". You can book a free consultation first if you would rather talk it through than write it out. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits to anything, and the trial is worth designing: hand the tutor one marked script and one exploration idea, then watch what they do with both. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match. That is a normal request rather than a complaint, and it is far cheaper in DP1 than in the term before the papers.
items: 1. Send the course: AA or AI, HL or SL, DP1 or DP2.
2. Add the last marked script and any exploration idea so far.
3. Tell us your locality, evening slot and whether home lessons are practical.
4. Review a shortlist of verified profiles matched to that exact course.
5. Run a trial session, then confirm, change the match or stop.

contentBlocks.heading: HL and SL in DP Mathematics: hours, and what the step up costs
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme runs over two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four of those are taken at Higher Level, which carries 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level, which carries 150. Every subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to 3 further points, which puts the maximum at 45, and 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well, and it eats real hours in a DP week.

Hold those two numbers next to each other: 240 against 150. The gap is ninety recommended teaching hours over two years, and it is not spread thinly across the course. It is extra content, taken faster, examined against a higher standard. Families who treat Higher Level as Standard Level with a little more discover the difference somewhere in the second term of DP1, usually in the middle of an algebra or calculus block, and usually in the same fortnight as three other internal assessments.

This is where IB Maths tutors in India spend a large part of their time. Not teaching new material, but repairing an HL start that went too fast. A student who is coping at SL pace and sinking at HL pace is not a weak mathematician. They are in the wrong course for their timetable. The honest conversation is about whether the HL is needed for the degrees on the list, whether dropping to SL frees the hours two other Higher Levels are quietly demanding, and what the school's deadline for a level change actually is. That deadline is set by the school, so ask the DP coordinator early rather than in DP2. Home tuition can buy a student time inside an HL course. It cannot create the ninety hours.
items: Higher Level: 240 recommended teaching hours; Standard Level: 150 hours
Each DP subject is graded 1 to 7, and the diploma maximum is 45
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points between them
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions
A level change has a school deadline: ask the DP coordinator, not us
CAS hours are real hours; count them before adding a second HL tutor

contentBlocks.heading: The exploration: 20% of the grade, 12-20 pages, five criteria
contentBlocks.body:
The mathematics exploration is the same task in all four courses. Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level or Higher Level, the student writes one piece of 12 to 20 pages, it carries 20% of the final grade, and it is marked out of 20 against five criteria: A Presentation, worth 4; B Mathematical communication, worth 4; C Personal engagement, worth 3; D Reflection, worth 3; and E Use of mathematics, worth 6. HL work is judged against a higher standard on criterion E. The teacher can comment on one draft, and the work must be the student's own.

Read those weightings again, because most students write as though only criterion E existed. Presentation and mathematical communication are worth 8 marks between them, more than use of mathematics on its own. A student who does genuinely ambitious mathematics and presents it as a wall of unlabelled working, with symbols introduced without definition and no thread running from the question to the conclusion, loses in A and B what was gained in E. Reflection costs marks too, because "this was interesting" is not reflection. Reflection is what the student did when the first method failed.

Criterion C, personal engagement, is where topic choice pays off. A topic borrowed from a list because it looked mathematically impressive gives a student nothing to be engaged about. A topic that comes out of something they actually do, a sport, a daily train route, a game, a family business, a musical instrument, gives them reasons to make choices and then discuss those choices honestly.

At Higher Level the bar on criterion E moves. A competent exploration that would read well at SL can read thin at HL, and the fix is rarely more pages. It is a question with somewhere to go: a model that can be tested and refined, a proof that needs a real argument, a data set that behaves awkwardly enough to be worth interrogating.
items: 1. Six to eight weeks out, list three topics from things the student actually does.
2. Turn each one into a question with mathematics that can be pushed further.
3. Check the level: does criterion E have room to breathe at HL or SL?
4. Gather the data or set up the model before writing a single page.
5. Write the full draft, then submit the one draft the teacher may comment on.
6. Rework against all five criteria, check notation and page count, then submit.

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB Maths tutors in India actually are, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
IB Maths tutors in India cluster where the DP schools cluster, and the map is lumpy. In Delhi NCR the pool spreads across South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and Dwarka, and separately across Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road and into Noida, Sector 128 Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad. Those are two travel problems, not one. A tutor living in Noida will often hold a weekday evening slot in Sector 128 Noida and think twice about Dwarka on the same evening, so a family looking for an IB Maths tutor in Delhi should ask where the tutor is starting from, not only where they are willing to go.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region splits the same way. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill form one cluster; Powai sits awkwardly between clusters; Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar form another. An IB Maths tutor in Mumbai who lives in Andheri is a realistic weekday home tutor for Juhu and a monsoon gamble for Kharghar. In Bengaluru the logic runs along the traffic axes: Whitefield and Sarjapur Road, then Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout, then Hebbal and Yelahanka to the north and Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road to the south. Families searching for an IB Maths tutor in Bangalore usually find it is crossing the city on a weekday evening, not the distance itself, that kills a home session.

Hyderabad concentrates around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad on the other side of a long evening drive. Chennai runs from Adyar, Besant Nagar and Alwarpet down Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) through Perungudi, with Nungambakkam, Anna Nagar and Velachery each their own calculation. Pune spreads across Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Kharadi on one side, Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi on the other.

Beyond the metro clusters the arithmetic changes. In Gujarat, Ahmedabad holds most of the supply around Satellite, Bodakdev and SG Highway, with Gandhinagar close by and Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot needing a different plan. In Kolkata and eastern India, Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat have some capacity, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna rarely do at Higher Level. Across northern India beyond Delhi NCR, in Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur, AA HL is an online-first search. The same holds across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai, and across central and western India in Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad.

An IB Maths tutor in Chennai on Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) may not reach Anna Nagar by seven
An IB Maths tutor in Kolkata around Salt Lake or New Town covers Rajarhat more easily than Alipore
An IB Maths tutor in Ahmedabad near Bodakdev or SG Highway can usually reach Gandhinagar

contentBlocks.heading: The May session and the maths calendar families in India plan around
contentBlocks.body:
Exam sessions run in May and November. Schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which fits an Indian academic year running roughly April to March, and May results are released in early July. Everything else in a DP mathematics plan hangs off those dates.

Work backwards from them. If the papers are in May, the exploration has to be finished and submitted well before them, because no student can revise calculus properly while still rewriting criterion B. Mocks land earlier still, and mocks are the last honest evidence a family gets before the real thing. The practical consequence is that the useful window for rebuilding a broken foundation in AA HL is DP1 and the first half of DP2. Not March.

International schools in India, among them Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore, each run their own internal deadlines for drafts, mocks and reports, and those deadlines differ from one another. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Ask your own school for its dates and hand them to the tutor in the first week.

Two calendar pressures catch families out. The first is the long gap between one school year ending and the next starting, when a DP1 student either loses the thread entirely or quietly closes a gap with a light weekly home session. The second is the run of internal assessment deadlines that stack in DP2: mathematics, two sciences, an essay, all inside the same few weeks. A home tutor who knows those dates plans around them. A tutor who does not will schedule two hours of past papers on the evening before a physics draft is due, and the student will sit through it and learn nothing.
items: May session for most candidates in India, with results released in early July
November is the other session; confirm with the DP coordinator which one applies
The Indian academic year runs roughly April to March, so DP1 starts mid-calendar
Give the tutor your school's draft, mock and report dates in week one
DP2 internal assessment deadlines stack; plan maths around them, not through them

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which mode suits an AA HL student?
contentBlocks.body:
For most Analysis and Approaches HL students, home tuition is the better default and online is the better fallback, with hybrid the honest answer in a large metro. The reason is physical. Higher Level algebra and calculus are judged on written working, and a tutor sitting beside a student sees a line go wrong in real time, before it becomes six lines of confident nonsense.

That advantage is real, and it is not unlimited. A home tutor who spends ninety minutes in evening traffic to teach for ninety minutes will eventually start moving the slot, and a slot that keeps moving in DP2 is worse than a reliable screen. Online lessons remove travel completely, which is why they hold better in the weeks around mocks, and they reach specialists who are simply not in your city. A family in Dehradun or Vijayawada looking for AI HL will find the choice is not home against online. It is online against nothing.

Online has its own costs. A student can nod convincingly at a screen for forty minutes without writing anything down. The fix is mechanical: the student works on paper, the paper reaches the tutor by camera or photograph, and the tutor marks it where the student can watch. A graphics tablet on the tutor's side matters more for mathematics than for most subjects, because here the teaching is the working.

Hybrid is what many families in Bengaluru, Pune and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region end up doing without ever deciding to. One home session a week, in person, for the heavy teaching and the exploration conversation. One shorter online session midweek for marking, doubt-solving and holding the student to a deadline. It survives traffic, exam weeks and a tutor's own timetable better than two home visits do, and it keeps the in-person contact that written mathematics needs. Choose it deliberately rather than drifting into it after three cancellations.
items: Home lessons: working seen live, errors caught on the line where they happen
Online lessons: no travel, and a far wider choice of AA and AI specialists
Hybrid: one home session weekly plus a shorter online marking slot
Online only works when the student writes on paper and the tutor marks it
In heavy traffic, a reliable online slot beats a home visit that keeps moving

contentBlocks.heading: What should you check before a maths home tutor starts?
contentBlocks.body:
Check three things: which of the four courses the tutor has actually taught and for how long, what they do with a marked script placed in front of them, and what they say about the exploration. Everything else is secondary. Profiles on IB Gram are verified before they go live, which covers identity and claimed experience, but verification is not the same as fit, and fit is yours to judge.

The course question is the one families skip. "I teach IB maths" should be met with "which course, at which level, and in which year". A tutor who has taught Applications and Interpretation SL for years may be excellent and still be learning AA HL on your child's time. Ask them to describe the difference between the two in their own words. A serious answer names the algebraic, proof-heavy character of AA against the modelling, statistics and constant technology use of AI within about a minute.

The script test beats any credential. Give the tutor one marked piece of the student's work and ask what went wrong. A good IB Maths tutor in India will separate a content gap from a notation habit from a misread question, and say which one is costing marks, rather than offering to reteach the whole topic from the beginning.

The exploration question sorts out the rest. Ask what they would do if the student arrived with a draft. The answer you want is that they would ask the student to read their own paragraph against a criterion and explain why it earns the mark, and that the one permitted draft comment comes from the teacher rather than from them. Any tutor who offers to write, rewrite or tidy up a submission is describing something the IB's academic integrity policy does not allow. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone.
items: Ask which of the four courses they teach, at what level, and when
Give them a marked script and ask what specifically went wrong
Ask how they would handle an exploration draft the student brings along
Confirm they know your school's deadlines before the first home session
Check the slot they can hold all year, not only this month

contentBlocks.heading: AA or AI: how should a family in India actually decide?
contentBlocks.body:
Decide from the degree and from the student, in that order, and treat reputation as noise. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often advised towards Analysis and Approaches, and that advice is frequently right. But it is advice rather than a rule, the correct choice depends on the specific degree and the specific student, and the school's DP coordinator makes the final placement.

Start with the degree list. Universities publish their own subject requirements, and some are explicit about which mathematics course and which level they expect. Read the actual pages for the actual courses your child is considering, in India and abroad, rather than relying on what a cousin was told four years ago. If every course on the list accepts either subject, the decision is free and should be made on the student.

Then look at the student, using evidence instead of instinct. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. It is not the easy option. It is a different subject. A student who enjoys data, context and building something that answers a real question often produces better work in AI than a grinding, unhappy pass in AA. A student who likes structure, argument and proof finds AA far more satisfying than an AI course full of interpretation.

The failure mode is well known in Indian schools. A student takes AA HL because the family believes it looks stronger, carries it for eighteen months at the cost of two other subjects, and finishes with a diploma total lower than AI HL plus two rested subjects would have produced. The points arithmetic is unforgiving. Every subject is graded 1 to 7, and losing a point in three subjects to protect one is a poor trade. Ask the coordinator what evidence they used for the placement, and ask what the deadline for changing it is.
items: Check each university course page for its stated mathematics requirement
AA is algebraic and proof-heavy; AI is modelling, statistics and technology throughout
AI is a different subject, not a lighter version of AA
The DP coordinator makes the final placement; ask what evidence was used
Count the cost to the other five subjects before defending an HL choice

contentBlocks.heading: What progress in IB maths should look like in India, term by term
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in mathematics is visible earlier than in most subjects, which is useful, and it does not look like a grade moving. In the first month the thing to watch is the error log: whether the same mistake keeps returning. A student who made six algebraic slips in one script and makes two in the next has improved, even if both scripts carry the same mark. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a promise about a specific number of points should be treated with real scepticism.

By the end of the first term you should see three changes. Working that a marker can follow without guessing. A student who attempts the later parts of a question instead of stopping at the first obstacle. And an exploration that exists in some form rather than as an intention. If none of those has shifted after a term of weekly home tuition, the problem is not effort, and the conversation needs to change.

Sometimes the honest answer is a level change. The HL students who should move to SL are not the ones who find the course hard, because Higher Level is meant to be hard. They are the ones whose other subjects are being eaten, who work long hours on mathematics and still cannot finish a paper, and whose marked work shows a foundation that was never solid. The evidence to gather is two mock scripts, the teacher's written comments, and an honest count of hours per week per subject. Take that to the DP coordinator, and do it in DP1 or early DP2, because a school's deadline for changing level is fixed and does not care about your reasons.

And sometimes the answer is fewer commitments rather than more tuition. IB Maths tutors in India meet plenty of students who do not need another two hours a week. They need sleep, a CAS load that is not running away from them, and one subject less to worry about.
items: Month one: the same error stops repeating, even if the mark holds steady
Term one: working a marker can follow without guessing the method
Term one: the student attempts later parts instead of stopping
Term one: an exploration topic exists on paper, not as an intention
No honest tutor promises a number; ask what evidence they will show you

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a first home session for maths in India
contentBlocks.body:
Prepare four things and the first session stops being an introduction and starts being work. The last marked script, with the teacher's comments still on it. The school's calendar of drafts, mocks and reports. A written note of which course the student is in and whether anyone at home is still arguing about it. And the exploration, in whatever state it is: a topic, three bad ideas, or nothing at all, which is also information.

Send a query or book a free consultation. We ask about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school calendar, your location and the schedule you can actually hold, then shortlist verified tutors who match those needs. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, subject to tutor availability, and lessons run at home, online or hybrid depending on what your week and your locality allow.

The first home session should not be a lecture. A tutor worth keeping spends the first part of it reading the student's own work and asking questions about it, sets one clear target for the next four weeks, and tells you at the end what they think is actually wrong. If the tutor spends that session teaching a topic from the front without looking at a single piece of the student's writing, notice it.

Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong. It is a normal request. A tutor who is excellent with an AI SL student building a statistics exploration may not be the right person for an AA HL student stuck on proof by induction, and neither of them has done anything wrong. Get this right in DP1 and the second year becomes a matter of practice and pacing rather than repair.
items: Bring the last marked script with the teacher's comments left intact
Bring the school's dates for drafts, mocks and reports
Say which course the student is in, and whether it is disputed
Say where you are and which evening slot you can hold all year
Ask for a trial before committing, subject to tutor availability

faqs.question: Should my child take Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Decide from the degree requirements first, then from the student's actual mathematical strengths. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-heavy with technology used throughout. Students heading for engineering or economics degrees are often steered towards AA, and that is often correct, but the right choice depends on the specific degree and the specific student. Read the university course pages yourself rather than trusting hearsay. The school's DP coordinator makes the final placement, so ask what evidence they used to make it.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with the mathematics exploration without breaking the IB's rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the underlying mathematics, question the reasoning, point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit the submission. The teacher, not the tutor, is the person who may comment on one draft. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB rather than the school alone. Any tutor offering to polish a draft is offering something you should refuse.

faqs.question: My child is in AA HL and struggling. When should we move to SL?
faqs.answer: Move when the evidence shows the Higher Level is costing the other subjects, and move early. Gather two mock scripts, the teacher's written comments and an honest count of weekly hours per subject, then take all of it to the DP coordinator. Difficulty on its own is not the signal, because HL carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at SL and is meant to be demanding. The signal is a foundation that never became solid plus two other subjects sliding. The school sets the deadline for a level change, so ask for that date now.

faqs.question: How much does an IB maths tutor in India cost?
faqs.answer: Fees vary, and no honest page can print a single figure. IB Maths tutors in India set rates by course, level, experience and whether the lesson is at home or online. Expect Higher Level to sit above Standard Level, and expect a home visit to carry the tutor's travel time in some form. Weekly frequency changes the monthly total far more than the hourly rate does. Ask for the fee structure in writing before the trial, ask what a missed session costs, and ask whether anything changes in the run-up to the May session.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Powai or Thane for weekday evening home classes?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the answer depends on where the tutor starts from rather than on the distance itself. Within the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, a tutor living in Andheri or Juhu can usually hold a weekday evening home session in Bandra or Powai; Thane and Kharghar are a different trip, and the monsoon makes it harder again. Ask which localities the tutor already teaches in on weekday evenings. Society and apartment gate entry needs arranging in advance, and a first home visit goes more smoothly if the guard already has the name.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor who has taught AI, or will an AA tutor manage?
faqs.answer: Prefer a tutor who has taught the course your child is actually in. The two courses overlap, and a strong mathematician can cross over, but Applications and Interpretation uses technology throughout and leans on modelling and statistics in ways an AA specialist may handle competently rather than fluently. Ask what AI teaching they have done, at which level, and in which year. If the only available specialist for AI HL lives in another city, an online IB Maths AI tutor usually beats a local AA tutor learning the course as they go.

faqs.question: What should a home session look like in the weeks before mocks?
faqs.answer: It should look like marking, not teaching. By that stage new content is rarely the problem, so the session is best spent on the student's own written attempts: a timed question done before the tutor arrives, marked in front of them, with each lost mark named precisely. Keep one short slot for the exploration if it is still open. Cut any session that recovers a topic the student already half-knows. And protect sleep in that fortnight, because a tired student gains nothing from a ninety-minute home lesson at ten at night.

faqs.question: Is online maths tutoring as good as having the tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For most students it comes close, and for some it is better, but it needs a different discipline. Written working is what mathematics is marked on, so an online lesson only works when the student writes on paper and the tutor can see and mark that paper live, by camera or photograph. A graphics tablet on the tutor's side helps a great deal. Online removes travel, which protects the slot during exam weeks, and it opens up specialists in other cities. Hybrid, one home session plus one online, suits many families best.

faqs.question: Nobody in Kochi or Coimbatore seems to teach AI HL. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Go online, and stop treating that as a compromise. Across southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, and equally in Indore, Bhopal, Guwahati or Jaipur, Higher Level mathematics specialists are scarce because DP teaching capacity gathers around the schools in the larger metros. The realistic choice in Kochi, Coimbatore or Visakhapatnam is an online specialist against a local generalist, and for AI HL the specialist usually wins. Some families run a local home tutor for routine practice and an online specialist for the harder teaching and the exploration.

faqs.question: What calculator and technology should the student be using?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because the permitted technology is set by the subject guide and by the school's own policy, and the teacher will confirm what applies. What matters for tuition is that the student uses whatever they will use in the exam room from the start of DP1, not from March of DP2. Applications and Interpretation uses technology throughout, so fluency with it is part of the course rather than an extra. Marks go missing through rounding too early, unlabelled graphs, and answers written down without the method that produced them.

faqs.question: There has been no improvement after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Say so directly, and say it to the tutor first. One month is enough to see an error log shorten even when the grade has not moved, so if nothing at all has changed, ask the tutor what they think is wrong and what they would do differently over the next four weeks. If the answer is more of the same, ask for a different match. That is a normal request and not a complaint. Occasionally the honest finding is that the student is in the wrong course, which belongs with the DP coordinator.

faqs.question: When is it too late to start maths tuition before the May session?
faqs.answer: It is rarely too late to help, but what help means changes sharply with timing. Started in DP1, tuition can rebuild a foundation properly. Started after mocks in DP2, it can only sharpen technique, protect the marks the student already knows how to earn, and make sure the exploration is not still open. Exam sessions run in May and November, most schools in India enter candidates for May, and results are released in early July. Inside the final term, be specific about which papers and which topics you want covered.

The trade-off that decides it is simple: how much of the problem is specific to this student, and how much is just practice not yet done?

h1: IB Physics Tutors in India for HL, SL and the Investigation
heroTitle: Physics at HL and SL, taught across India
heroSubtitle: Paper 1A rewards speed. Paper 1B rewards reading a graph properly. Paper 2 rewards an explanation that holds together from first line to last. Most students arrive strong on the first and thin on the third, and the scientific investigation sits underneath all of it carrying a fifth of the subject grade.
introSummary: IB Physics tutors in India are usually hired for one reason: the numbers are right and the marks are still missing. Most families begin with home tuition, a verified tutor at the dining table two evenings a week, because a Physics answer is written by hand and marked on paper. Under the science assessment first examined in 2025, Paper 1 comes in two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based; Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions; and the scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade. Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) sit on the same assessment structure, with Additional Higher Level content on top for HL. This page sets out what each component asks for, where explanation marks go missing, and how to plan the investigation from question to report.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a Physics request in India become a shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with evidence, not with availability. The first conversation is about which level the student sits, HL or SL, and which part of the course is actually failing. A student who loses marks in Paper 1A has a content problem or a timing problem. A student who writes three lines where an extended-response question wanted a chain of reasoning has a writing problem, and no amount of extra derivation practice will touch it. If you have the last marked script, share it. Two minutes with a real answer tells a tutor more than twenty minutes of description does.

The second half of the conversation is logistics. Your locality, because a home tutor has to reach you after school hours on a weekday. Your school's calendar, because a DP2 student three weeks from mocks needs different sessions from a DP1 student in October who has not yet chosen an investigation question. The rest of the week matters too: five other subjects, Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments, and whatever the student does on a Saturday. IB Gram then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches the level and the component you named, subject to tutor availability.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Spend it on one real question rather than a tour of the syllabus. Hand the tutor the last extended-response answer the student wrote, and watch. A tutor who reads it back, stops at the exact sentence where the reasoning jumps, and asks the student what is carrying the argument at that point is doing the job. A tutor who turns to the whiteboard and re-derives a formula the student already knows is filling an hour.

And if the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, ask for a different match. Nobody is offended. The tutor who suits a quiet student needing slow questioning is often the wrong tutor for one who wants to be pushed hard through past papers, and that mismatch shows early.
items: 1. Send the level, the weakest component, and the last marked Physics script.
2. A free consultation covers level, school calendar, locality and the weekly schedule.
3. IB Gram shortlists verified profiles matched to Physics at HL or SL.
4. Run a demo session on one real extended-response answer, not a syllabus tour.
5. Confirm a weekly slot at home, online or hybrid, or request a different match.

contentBlocks.heading: Physics HL against Physics SL: 240 hours, 150 hours and the AHL content
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) runs over two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects drawn from six groups. Three or four are taken at Higher Level (HL), which carries 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level (SL), at 150 hours. Every subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together contribute up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum, and 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the International Baccalaureate's failing conditions. CAS must also be completed.

Physics sits inside that structure as one of the six. The point that matters for tutoring is that HL and SL share the assessment structure. Same papers, same scientific investigation, same four criteria. What HL adds is Additional Higher Level (AHL) content, and the extra recommended hours to cover it. The difference is not that HL questions are a different species. There is simply more syllabus standing behind them, and less room to be slow.

This changes how tutoring hours should be spent. A student struggling at HL rarely needs the AHL content taught again from the beginning. More often the core is shaky and the AHL material built on top of it has nothing to stand on. A tutor who spends the first two sessions testing core topics, then moves to the AHL work, usually finds the real gap fast. Reteaching AHL content over a weak core is the most common way a term of Physics tuition gets wasted.

The level decision itself belongs to the student, the subject teacher and the DP coordinator. A tutor can inform it by showing what the student's work looks like under timed conditions and by being honest about how much ground is left before May. Moving from HL to SL is not a failure. Carrying three Higher Levels that all demand long written answers is a scheduling problem far more often than an ability one.
items: HL carries 240 recommended teaching hours; SL carries 150 hours
HL and SL share papers, criteria and the scientific investigation
AHL content is the HL addition, not a different paper format
Each subject is graded 1 to 7; TOK and the EE add up to 3 points
24 points is the diploma minimum, subject to the IB's failing conditions

contentBlocks.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: what each Physics component asks for
contentBlocks.body:
Under the science assessment first examined in 2025, Paper 1 comes in two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice. Paper 1B is data-based. They reward different habits, and students who prepare for one often walk into the other unready. Paper 1A punishes hesitation: a question you cannot place inside a minute is a question to mark and come back to. Paper 1B punishes careless reading of a table or a graph, which means units, scales, uncertainties, and the difference between a gradient and a value read straight off an axis.

Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions. The short-answer part is where most students in India are comfortable, because it resembles the work they have done since Class 9. The extended-response part is where the marks go missing. It asks for a sustained piece of reasoning, written out, with every step visible and every step doing work. A correct final statement with nothing underneath it earns very little.

Then the scientific investigation, which is the internal assessment (IA). It is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade and is marked on four criteria of 6 marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. The report has a maximum of 3,000 words. Students may investigate in groups of up to three, but each student writes an individual report. A fifth of the grade is worth a boundary to most candidates, and it is the only component where the student controls the conditions.

Families comparing IB Physics tutors in India often ask which component to work on first. The honest answer is whichever one the last marked script points at. If Paper 1A is fine and extended response is thin, the syllabus is not the problem and more content teaching will not help. If the investigation is still unstarted in February of DP2, that is the emergency, whatever the paper marks say.
items: Paper 1A: multiple choice, where hesitation costs more than ignorance
Paper 1B: data-based questions on tables, graphs, gradients and uncertainty
Paper 2: short-answer questions plus extended response that must hold together
Scientific investigation: 20 per cent, four criteria of 6 marks each
Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion, Evaluation; maximum 3,000 words

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB Physics home tutors work across India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
In Delhi NCR the practical question is which side of the region you sit on. A home tutor living in South Delhi or Vasant Kunj can hold a weekday evening slot in Chanakyapuri or Dwarka without much difficulty. The same tutor crossing to Sector 128 Noida or Greater Noida on a Tuesday evening is a different proposition, because evening traffic between Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Noida can stretch a short trip badly. Families in Faridabad and Ghaziabad often find the local pool of DP Physics specialists thin, so a search for an IB Physics tutor in Delhi widens across the region or moves online.

Across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the distances look small and behave large. Bandra, Juhu, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit close together on a map, and a tutor based in Andheri or Powai can usually serve several of them in a week. Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar are a separate travel problem after six in the evening, and a parent looking for an IB Physics tutor in Mumbai from Thane should expect a shorter list than one looking from Bandra. A hybrid week often settles it: one home session at the weekend, one online session midweek.

Bengaluru splits the same way. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City are their own worlds on a weekday evening, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout and Jayanagar can be covered from one base, and Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road each carry their own supply problem. A family asking for an IB Physics tutor in Bangalore from Whitefield is really asking who lives close enough to arrive by seven. In Hyderabad the DP pool clusters around Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and the Financial District, with Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills well covered and Secunderabad and Kokapet harder; a good IB Physics tutor in Hyderabad will name the localities they reach before discussing anything else.

Chennai runs along its own lines. Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are close-knit; Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery depend heavily on when the lesson starts, and Anna Nagar is a separate trip again. An IB Physics tutor in Chennai plans a week around two of those clusters, not five. Outside these regions the pattern repeats with less depth: an IB Physics tutor in Pune, an IB Physics tutor in Kolkata or an IB Physics tutor in Ahmedabad exists, but the pool is smaller and HL specialists are fewer, which is why a search for an IB Physics tutor near me so often ends with a strong online tutor from another city. IB Physics tutors in India are not evenly distributed, and pretending otherwise costs a family a month.
