h1: IB English Tutors in India for English A and English B
heroTitle: English A and English B tutoring across India
heroSubtitle: Two different subjects sit behind the words IB English. English A is Studies in Language and Literature; English B is Language Acquisition. This page explains both, the papers and orals inside each, and how home tuition, online lessons or a hybrid week are arranged for families across India.
introSummary: IB English tutors in India teach two separate subjects, and most families book home tuition before they are certain which one their child is actually taking. English A sits in Studies in Language and Literature, either Language and Literature or Literature. English B sits in Language Acquisition at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL), with English ab initio (SL only) kept for genuine beginners. The assessments differ completely: guided textual analysis of unseen passages in one, a listening and reading paper in the other. A home tutor who has taught only one route will slow the other down. Ask any tutor which route they have taught, which papers they have marked, and how they prepare the 15-minute Individual Oral before you agree to a weekly slot.

contentBlocks.heading: How do we match an English A or English B student with an IB English tutor in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Everything starts with one question that families often cannot answer on the phone: is the student registered for English A or English B? The Diploma Programme (DP) treats them as different subjects from different groups, so a wrong assumption wastes the first month. We ask you to check the subject name on the school's registration slip or with the DP coordinator, and to say whether the level is Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL).

Then we ask for evidence rather than opinions. A marked Paper 1 response, a returned Paper 2 essay with the criterion comments still attached, a recording or the teacher's notes from a practice Individual Oral: any one of these tells a tutor more than a description of the problem ever will. Parents in Bengaluru and Chennai often send a photo of a marked script, which is enough to begin. If nothing has been marked yet because it is early in DP1, we ask what the student is currently reading and how the learner portfolio is being kept.

With the route, the level and one piece of marked work, the shortlist becomes narrow and honest. We look for IB English tutors in India who have taught that route, not English in general, and who can talk about the guiding question on Paper 1 without being prompted. You get profiles, not a single name, and you speak to the tutor before anything is booked.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, subject to tutor availability. Most families use it to watch the tutor take one unseen passage apart with the student. Lessons then run at home, online or hybrid, depending on where you live and how the school week falls. If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, ask for a different match. A tutor who suits a quiet Literature student is often the wrong person for a nervous English B speaker.
items: 1. Confirm the subject: English A Language and Literature, English A Literature, or English B
2. Confirm the level, SL or HL, and whether the HL essay applies
3. Send one marked script or criterion comment sheet from the school
4. Receive a shortlist of tutors who have taught that exact route
5. Run a trial on one unseen passage, then decide
6. Fix the weekly slot: home, online or hybrid, and review after a month

contentBlocks.heading: English A against English B, and why families in India pick wrong
contentBlocks.body:
Studies in Language and Literature is the group English A belongs to, and a student takes either English A: Language and Literature or English A: Literature. Language Acquisition is a different group, and that is where English B (SL or HL) sits, with English ab initio offered at SL only for genuine beginners. Both routes are graded 1 to 7, both count towards the 24 points a candidate needs for the diploma, and both fill a slot in the six subjects from six groups that make up the Diploma Programme. They are not two difficulty settings of one subject.

Here is where families go wrong. A student who speaks English fluently at school and at home is placed in English B because the family believes Language Acquisition is the safer route to a 7, or because an older cousin did it. Sometimes the opposite happens: a child who joined an international school in Grade 9 after years in a regional-language medium is pushed into English A Literature because English B sounds like an admission of weakness. Both choices cost the student. A fluent speaker in English B spends two years on receptive tasks well below their ceiling and can still drop marks because the paper rewards a register they never practise. A student placed too high in English A meets two unseen passages at Higher Level with no scaffolding, and loses ground in every other subject while trying to keep up.

The consequence lands late, which is the real problem. Registration is confirmed by the school and changing route in DP2 is rarely practical, so this conversation belongs in the term before the DP starts. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) the equivalent is Language Acquisition, taught in phases 1 to 6, and the phase a student reaches in MYP 5 is the best single indicator of which DP route fits. The IB has no subject called ESL. Parents search for that term constantly, and what they mean is English B or, occasionally, ab initio.
items: English A: Language and Literature, or English A: Literature, at SL and HL
English B at SL or HL; English ab initio at SL only
Five English B themes: Identities, Experiences, Human ingenuity, Social organization, Sharing the planet
MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases 1 to 6 before the DP
The IB has no subject called ESL, whatever the search results suggest
HL English B students also study two literary works

contentBlocks.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2, the Individual Oral and the HL essay, component by component
contentBlocks.body:
Paper 1 is a guided textual analysis of unseen passages: one passage at SL, two at HL, written on material the student has never met before. The guiding question printed with each passage is not the essay title. It points at one feature of the text, and its job is to give a way in, not to fence the answer off. Students who treat it as a question to be answered in the first paragraph and then abandoned produce strong openings and weak bodies.

Paper 2 is a comparative essay on two works studied during the course, written without the texts in the room. The real demand is not memory of plot. It is holding one argument across two works so that each text earns its place, which means the student must have planned pairings long before the exam and must know which of their works speak to which kind of question.

The Individual Oral runs for 15 minutes: a 10-minute analysis linking an extract to a global issue, then 5 minutes of questions. A preparation plan that works:

1. Choose the global issue first, narrow enough to be argued for ten minutes.

2. Pick one literary extract and one non-literary extract that genuinely carry that issue.

3. Draft ten bullet points rather than a script, then time a read-through aloud.

4. Rehearse the 5 minutes of questions with someone willing to interrupt.

HL students in English A also write the HL essay, 1,200 to 1,500 words on a work or text studied. The learner portfolio is required of every student and is not directly assessed, which is exactly why it gets neglected. It is also where the Individual Oral and the HL essay ideas come from, so a term of empty portfolio entries shows up as a thin oral in DP2. English B is assessed on a different shape: Paper 1 is a writing task testing productive skills, Paper 2 covers listening and reading as receptive skills, and there is an individual oral.
items: Paper 1: one unseen passage at SL, two at HL, with guiding questions
Paper 2: comparative essay on two studied works, texts not available
Individual Oral: 10 minutes of analysis, then 5 minutes of questions
HL essay: 1,200 to 1,500 words on one studied work or text
Learner portfolio: required, not directly assessed, and the source of oral ideas
English B: writing task, listening and reading paper, individual oral

contentBlocks.heading: Where home tuition for IB English works across India, city by city
contentBlocks.body:
IB English tutors in India cluster where the international schools are, and the map is uneven. Delhi NCR holds the largest pool of English A teachers in the country, and it is also one of the hardest places to hold a fixed evening slot. A tutor living in South Delhi or Vasant Kunj will take a weekday booking in Chanakyapuri without much thought, and will hesitate over the same slot in Sector 128 Noida or Faridabad, because evening traffic on that stretch can stretch a short trip into something that eats the lesson. Families in Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, in Dwarka, in Greater Noida and in Ghaziabad usually do better with a tutor drawn from their own side of the city, or with a hybrid week.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the constraint is the bridge and the rail corridor rather than raw distance. An IB English tutor in Mumbai who lives in Bandra or Juhu can serve Andheri and Worli comfortably; asking the same person to reach Vashi, Kharghar or Thane on a weekday evening invites cancellations. Powai, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill families tend to get the steadiest home tuition because the pool sits close. Navi Mumbai works best with a local tutor or with online lessons.

Bengaluru is a supply story with a traffic problem laid over it. An IB English tutor in Bangalore who lives in Indiranagar or Koramangala may be excellent and still unable to reach Whitefield or Sarjapur Road for an evening class. HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka, Electronic City and Kanakapura Road each carry their own small pools. In Chennai, an IB English tutor in Chennai working out of Adyar, Besant Nagar or Alwarpet covers Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar easily, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery are better served by someone already on that corridor.

In Kolkata and eastern India the pool is thinner. Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore do have English A teachers, and an IB English tutor in Kolkata will usually travel within that ring. Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna are where online lessons stop being a compromise and become the only way to reach a teacher who has actually taught English B HL. The same holds for an IB English tutor in Hyderabad, in Pune or in Ahmedabad when the family needs the Literature route rather than Language and Literature: the local pool may hold one or two suitable people, and a hybrid week of one home visit and one online session is the usual answer.
items: South Delhi, Vasant Kunj, Dwarka, Noida, Gurugram (Gurgaon), Faridabad and Ghaziabad
Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Thane, Navi Mumbai and Kharghar
Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, HSR Layout, Yelahanka and Electronic City in Bengaluru
Adyar, Besant Nagar, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) and Anna Nagar in Chennai
Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge and Alipore, plus Bhubaneswar, Guwahati and Patna
Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad: thin Literature pools, so hybrid weeks work better

contentBlocks.heading: What the school calendar does to English deadlines in India
contentBlocks.body:
Exam sessions run in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session. That fits the Indian academic year, which runs roughly April to March, and it sets every deadline a DP English student meets. May results are released in early July. Work backwards from there and the two years take a shape: DP1 ends with the first serious Paper 1 practice, DP2 opens with the Individual Oral recording window and the HL essay, mocks land in the middle of the year, and the final weeks go to Paper 2 revision on works read eighteen months earlier.

International schools set internal deadlines well ahead of the IB's own, because teachers need time to mark, standardise and upload. Families are regularly caught by this. The Individual Oral is not an exam-week event; it is recorded during ordinary teaching weeks, often while the student is also finishing a science internal assessment (IA) and a mathematics exploration. A home tutor who books English sessions without asking what else is due that fortnight ends up teaching a tired student who has already written three drafts that week.

Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore are names families recognise, and they appear here only as context for the kind of calendar pressure that exists. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate (IB), Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

One practical habit helps more than any study plan. Ask the school for the English department's term calendar at the start of DP1, put the oral window and the HL essay deadline on the same sheet as the mock dates, and give a copy to the tutor. Most of the panic that reaches us in November is a deadline nobody wrote down.
items: May session for almost all schools in India; results in early July
The academic year runs roughly April to March, so DP1 starts mid-year
The Individual Oral is recorded in teaching weeks, not exam weeks
HL essay deadlines usually sit close to other subject IA deadlines
Ask for the English department term calendar at the start of DP1

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for IB English: which suits the Individual Oral?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition, online lessons and a hybrid week each do something different for IB English, and the Individual Oral is what separates them. Home classes put a tutor in the room while the student speaks for ten minutes without a script, and the tutor can see the hands, the eyes leaving the page, the exact moment the argument runs out. That is hard to read through a screen. For a student who freezes in the oral, a home tutor is often worth more than a better-qualified online one.

Online lessons win on text work. A Paper 1 passage shared on screen and annotated live in two colours while the student watches beats two people leaning over one printed sheet. Mark schemes and criterion descriptors sit open alongside. For English B listening practice, online is the natural format because the audio is already on the device. Online also solves supply: the tutor who has genuinely taught English A Literature at HL may live in another city altogether.

Hybrid is what most DP families in India settle on, and not by accident. One home session a week for the oral and for essay planning, one online session for unseen passages and marked work, keeps travel down and the schedule intact through monsoon, exam weeks and the weeks when three deadlines collide. When a family in Whitefield or Kharghar tells us the tutor keeps cancelling, hybrid is usually the fix rather than a new tutor.

The trade-off in one line: home tuition buys presence and oral confidence, online buys choice of tutor and better text annotation, and hybrid buys most of both at the cost of a slightly less settled routine. Cost structure differs too, because travel time is real time, and a tutor crossing a metro twice a week prices that in. Most IB English tutors in India will work in all three modes, so the question is which one your week can actually hold.
items: Home tuition: best for the Individual Oral and for a nervous speaker
Online: better annotation of unseen passages, and far more tutor choice
Hybrid: one home visit plus one online session in most weeks
English B listening work is easier online than at the dining table
Travel time is real time and shows up in the cost structure

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check that a tutor has actually taught English A?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram means profile checks before a profile goes live: identity, claimed qualifications, and the boards, programmes and subjects the tutor says they have taught. For English that last part matters more than in most subjects, because English A and English B are different jobs, and one line saying IB English on a profile hides which of them the tutor really knows.

So ask directly, and ask about components rather than credentials. What does the guiding question on Paper 1 do, and what should a student do with it? How do you help a student pick two works that pair well for Paper 2? Walk me through the last Individual Oral you prepared a student for: what was the global issue, and which extracts did they use? A tutor who has taught the route answers all three in specifics within a minute. A tutor who has taught general English literature on another board will talk about themes and essay structure and never mention a criterion.

For English B the equivalent questions are about the five themes and the receptive paper. Which theme do your students find hardest to write about, and why? How do you train listening when the student only ever hears one accent? What changes at HL, where two literary works are also studied?

There are checks only you can do, and they feel awkward the first time. Meet the tutor, or see them on video, before a home visit is arranged. Ask for the first two sessions to be treated as a trial. Keep home classes in a room where a family member passes through. Ask how work will be returned and when you will hear anything at all. If a tutor claims examiner experience, ask which component and which session, and treat a vague answer as an answer. No platform can watch a tutor teach every week, which is why the family's own judgement after three sessions is the check that matters most.
items: Identity and claimed qualifications checked before a profile goes live
Ask which route: English A Literature, Language and Literature, or English B
Ask about one specific Individual Oral they prepared, issue and extracts
Treat the first two sessions as a trial, then decide
Keep home sessions in a room the household passes through
Examiner claims: ask which component and which exam session

contentBlocks.heading: What an IB English tutor in India does that a general English tutor cannot
contentBlocks.body:
An IB English tutor in India is doing something narrower than teaching English well. The difference shows in marking. A general tutor reads a student's Paper 2 essay and says the argument needs more evidence. A DP English specialist reads the same essay against the criterion the examiner will use, points at the sentence where the comparison collapsed into two separate summaries, and rewrites that one sentence with the student to show what the criterion is asking for. The first response is true. The second changes the next essay.

The second difference is the unseen passage. Most English teaching in the country, on any board, runs on studied texts: read the chapter, learn the themes, answer on the chapter. Paper 1 removes the text the student prepared and hands them one they have never seen, with a guiding question attached. Teaching that is a separate skill, built by working through many passages at speed and by training the student to write a thesis about a text they met four minutes ago. A tutor who has only taught studied texts cannot fake it.

Third, and least visible, is the oral. English A and English B both end in a spoken assessment, and very few classrooms rehearse a student for ten minutes of continuous analysis with a teacher listening. A tutor who prepares orals knows the failure mode is not nerves. It is a global issue chosen too broadly, so the student runs out of argument at minute six and starts retelling the extract.

And there is a limit worth stating early. Good IB English tutors in India cannot raise a predicted grade by talking to the school, cannot write any part of the HL essay, and cannot manufacture the reading a student did not do in DP1. What they can do is make the reading that remains count for considerably more.
items: Marks the student's own essay against the criterion, in front of them
Drills unseen passages at speed, which studied-text teaching never builds
Rehearses ten minutes of continuous oral analysis, then the questions
Teaches command terms and the register each component rewards
Cannot write the HL essay or change a predicted grade

contentBlocks.heading: What progress in English A and English B looks like, term by term
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in English is slower to see than in mathematics, and parents used to marks out of 100 find the first two months unconvincing. Set the expectation properly. In the first three or four sessions the change is in the student's talk, not their grade: they begin naming what a text is doing rather than what it says. By six to eight weeks a marked Paper 1 response should carry a thesis in the opening paragraph instead of description. Criterion scores usually move after that, not before.

For English B the curve has a different shape. Productive skills respond faster, because a writing task has a structure that can be taught, and the receptive paper improves last, since listening and reading gains come from volume and volume takes months. A student who moves from a 4 to a 5 on writing within a term may hold flat on the receptive paper for longer than that, and it is not a sign the home tuition is failing.

Here are the limits, stated plainly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim otherwise is a reason to walk away. A tutor cannot change a predicted grade, which the school forms from its own evidence. Starting in January of DP2 narrows what is possible to exam technique and Paper 2 planning, because the works have been read and the oral is done. And some students do not need a tutor at all: if the school's feedback says the writing is strong and the problem is submitting late, that is a study-habits conversation rather than a reason for weekly English classes.

Review the arrangement every four to six weeks with one question. What can the student do in writing now that they could not do last month? If neither you nor the tutor can answer it, change something. Sometimes that is the tutor. More often it is the focus of the sessions.
items: Weeks one to four: the way the student talks about texts changes first
Weeks six to eight: a thesis appears in Paper 1 openings
English B writing improves before listening and reading do
Review every four to six weeks against one written question
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and predicted grades stay with the school

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home classes for IB English in India: what to prepare
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started takes one short conversation and three documents. Send a query or book a free consultation, and be ready to say which route the student is on, the level, the school, the locality and the two or three evening slots that actually work in your week. If you do not know the route, say so. The coordinator can confirm it, and it is better to wait two days than to book the wrong tutor.

The three things worth having to hand: the most recently marked piece of English work with the teacher's comments, the list of works being studied this year, and the school's English term calendar if you have it. Families who send those get a shorter shortlist and a faster start. Without them the first session becomes a diagnosis, which is fine, but it costs a week.

The first session itself should not be a lecture. Expect the tutor to take one unseen passage, work through it out loud with the student, ask the student to write for fifteen minutes, and then read that writing against a criterion while the student watches. For English B the equivalent is a short writing task under one of the five themes, marked in front of them. By the end of that session you should have a plan for the next six weeks, in writing, with the school's deadlines already on it.

Then fix the practical things. Where in the flat the lesson happens, who lets the tutor in at the society gate, what happens when a session is missed, and how you will hear about progress. Home classes run better when those are agreed in week one rather than argued about in week five. A trial can be arranged before you commit, subject to tutor availability.
items: Have the last marked English script and the teacher's comments ready
Know the route, the level, and whether the HL essay applies
List the works being studied this year before the first session
Agree the study space, gate entry and missed-session rule in week one
Ask for a six-week written plan at the end of session one

faqs.question: Is IB English A the same as IB English B?
faqs.answer: No. English A is Studies in Language and Literature, taken as either Language and Literature or Literature, and it assumes the student already works comfortably in English. English B is Language Acquisition, offered at Standard Level and Higher Level for students still building the language, with English ab initio at SL kept for genuine beginners. The papers, the orals and the skills being marked differ in each. Choosing between them is a registration decision made with the school, not something a tutor decides for you.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come to Bandra or Powai for IB English on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region has a reasonable English A pool around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Powai and Worli. The honest caveat is the corridor. Someone living on the western side will hold an early evening slot in Andheri far more reliably than the same slot in Vashi, Kharghar or Thane, where a weekday crossing can stretch badly. If you are in Navi Mumbai, look for a tutor already living there, or plan a hybrid week instead. Availability always depends on level and schedule.

faqs.question: Our school put our daughter in English B but she speaks English at home. Should we push for English A?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the DP coordinator before registration is confirmed, and bring evidence rather than an opinion. The useful evidence is her MYP Language Acquisition phase, her most recent written work and the English teacher's comments. Fluency in conversation is not the same as the analytical writing English A demands, so schools are sometimes right to be cautious. But a genuinely fluent student left in English B spends two years below her ceiling, and the route becomes very hard to change once DP2 begins.

faqs.question: What does IB individual oral help actually involve?
faqs.answer: Four things, in order: choosing a global issue narrow enough to argue for ten minutes, selecting one literary and one non-literary extract that genuinely carry that issue, building ten bullet points rather than a script, and rehearsing the five minutes of questions with someone who will interrupt. Most students prepare the ten-minute analysis and ignore the questions, which is where the assessment usually goes soft. A tutor who has prepared orals before will make the student speak from the first session, not the last.

faqs.question: Does the IB offer an ESL subject?
faqs.answer: No. The IB has no subject called ESL, though families search for the term constantly and some tutors advertise it anyway. What parents usually mean is English B, which sits in Language Acquisition at Standard Level or Higher Level, or English ab initio at SL for genuine beginners. In the Middle Years Programme the equivalent is Language Acquisition, taught in phases 1 to 6. If a profile says ESL and nothing else, ask which of these the tutor has actually taught, and for how long.

faqs.question: What should a home tuition session for English A look like?
faqs.answer: It should involve the student writing, not the tutor talking. A good ninety minutes might run like this: fifteen minutes on an unseen passage read aloud and annotated together, twenty-five minutes of the student writing an opening under time, then the tutor marking that opening against the criterion while the student watches and asks questions. The rest goes to the works being studied for Paper 2, or to portfolio entries. If home classes are mostly the tutor explaining themes, the student is not improving.

faqs.question: How is the fee for an IB English tutor in India worked out?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the level, the tutor's experience with the specific route, how many sessions a week you book and whether the tutor travels to you. We do not publish figures, because a single number would mislead across cities and levels. What you can compare fairly is the structure: whether marking between sessions is included, whether the rate changes for HL, what happens to the fee when a session is missed, and whether any commitment runs beyond the month you are in.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the HL essay without breaking academic integrity rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may discuss which studied work suits an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words, question whether the line of inquiry is arguable, teach the student how to structure an extended argument, and read a finished draft to say where the reasoning thins. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit sentences in the submission, supply the argument, or hand over paragraphs. The school supervises the essay, and the student's own words are the entire point of it.

faqs.question: We are in Salt Lake and cannot find an IB English tutor near me. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Widen the search in two steps rather than lowering the bar. Across Salt Lake, New Town, Rajarhat, Ballygunge and Alipore there are English A teachers, so first ask for anyone in that ring who can hold a fixed evening slot. If the student needs English B HL or the Literature route specifically, accept that Kolkata and eastern India has a thin pool, and go online for the subject expertise while keeping one home visit a fortnight for oral rehearsal. The same applies in Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring good enough for English B listening practice?
faqs.answer: For listening it is better than the alternative. The audio is already on the device, the tutor can pause, replay and annotate a transcript on a shared screen, and the student answers under conditions close to the paper itself. What online does less well is the individual oral, where the tutor loses the small physical signals that show a student is losing the thread. Most families settle on hybrid: online for the receptive paper and written tasks, a home visit for speaking.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month of classes. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence before changing anything. Request the student's marked work from the last four sessions and look for one specific change: is there a thesis in the opening paragraph of a Paper 1 response where there used to be description? If there is none, the problem is usually focus rather than the person. Say plainly what you want the next month to produce, in writing. If nothing shifts after that conversation, ask for a different match. That request is normal.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home during a home session, and should a parent sit in?
faqs.answer: Someone from the household should be around, but sitting inside the room for the whole session is usually counterproductive with a DP student. Keep the lesson in a room a family member passes through, leave the door open, and stay reachable. Teenagers rehearsing an oral in front of a parent tend to perform rather than think. A short conversation with the tutor at the end of the session, with the student present, will tell you more than an hour of watching.

comparison.heading: How do the four ways of supporting DP English in India compare?
comparison.intro: Four ways an Indian family supports DP English, and each is genuinely better at something. The school teacher knows the student's works and forms the predicted grade. A coaching batch gives peer discussion, which the oral benefits from. Past papers cost nothing and are always available. One-to-one earns its place only where individual evidence is needed: an oral rehearsed properly, an essay marked against a criterion in front of the student.

h1: IB TOK Tutors in India for the Exhibition and the Essay
heroTitle: TOK in India: three objects, then 1,600 words
heroSubtitle: Theory of Knowledge is graded twice: an exhibition of three objects in DP1 and a prescribed title essay in DP2. Together they carry up to three diploma points with the Extended Essay. This page explains both assessments, the five areas of knowledge behind them, and where a tutor must stop.
introSummary: IB TOK tutors in India teach Theory of Knowledge (TOK) as a subject with two graded pieces, and most families book home tuition for it in the term the exhibition is set. The exhibition asks for three objects linked to one of 35 Internal Assessment (IA) prompts, runs to 950 words, is marked inside the school, and carries one third of the TOK grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for each exam session, runs to 1,600 words, is marked outside the school, and carries the other two thirds. Together with the Extended Essay (EE), TOK contributes up to three points towards the 45 available in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP). An E in either is a failing condition.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a prescribed title brief become a TOK tutor match in India?
contentBlocks.body:
It becomes a match when the enquiry names the assessment, the stage and the deadline. A message saying a child needs TOK help produces a generic shortlist. A message saying the exhibition commentary is due in six weeks, that the child is in DP1, and that the school has already circulated the 35 IA prompts produces tutors who have taught that exact piece before.

So send the specifics. IB Gram asks about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school calendar, your location and the schedule your week can actually hold. For Theory of Knowledge, three extras change the shortlist more than anything else: which exam session the child sits, whether the exhibition or the essay is the live problem, and which two of the five optional themes the school selected. Add the student's six DP subjects if you have them, because a student taking two group 4 sciences will reach for the natural sciences in every paragraph and needs someone who can push them somewhere else.

IB Gram then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches what you described. A demo or trial session can be arranged before the family commits, and for this subject that trial is best spent on one real object or one real prescribed title rather than on a tour of the course. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability. If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, ask for a different match.

One honest limit. Prescribed titles are released for each exam session, and until the school hands them over there is no essay to work on. Families who ask for IB TOK tutors in India in September of DP2 sometimes expect essay drafting from the first session. What a tutor can do before the titles land is teach the five areas of knowledge properly, which is the work that makes the eventual essay possible.
items: 1. Name the assessment: exhibition objects, exhibition commentary, or the prescribed title essay.
2. Give the exam session, the DP year and the school's internal deadline.
3. Say which two optional themes the school chose, if the coordinator has confirmed them.
4. Share the last piece of written TOK feedback the teacher gave, in full.
5. Book a trial on one real object or one real title, not an overview.

contentBlocks.heading: Where TOK sits in the Diploma Programme core across India
contentBlocks.body:
TOK is not a seventh subject, and it does not carry a 1 to 7 grade. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects taken from six groups. Three or four of those sit at Higher Level (HL), with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at Standard Level (SL), with 150. Those six subjects are graded 1 to 7, which accounts for 42 of the 45 points available. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) are graded A to E, and the two of them together contribute up to three further points. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed, and it carries no points at all.

Twenty-four points is the minimum for the award of the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. One of those conditions is an E in TOK or in the EE. That single line is what brings most parents to a page like this late in DP2. A student can sit six creditable papers and still miss the diploma because the TOK essay was never seriously attempted, and no amount of subject tuition repairs it afterwards.

The calendar follows from the session. Exam sessions run in May and November, and schools in India overwhelmingly enter candidates for May, which fits an academic year running roughly April to March. May results are released in early July. In practice that puts the exhibition inside DP1 for most schools here and the essay inside DP2, with the school's internal essay deadline sitting well ahead of the May papers. Ask your DP coordinator for both internal dates in writing at the start of DP1.

So the tutoring load for this part of the core is lumpy rather than steady. Many families take a short run of home tuition around the exhibition, stop, and restart when the prescribed titles arrive. Paying for a weekly slot across two full years is usually money better spent on a subject.
items: Six subjects from six groups, three or four at HL with 240 hours
TOK and the EE are graded A to E, never on the 1 to 7 scale
Up to three core points on top of 42 subject points, giving 45
An E in TOK or the EE is a failing condition for the diploma
May session for almost all schools here, with results in early July

contentBlocks.heading: Which TOK assessment carries more weight, the exhibition or the essay?
contentBlocks.body:
The essay, by two to one. The exhibition carries one third of the TOK grade and the essay carries two thirds, so the essay is where the grade is decided. But the exhibition is finished first, its mark is settled while the essay is still unwritten, and a poor exhibition leaves the essay having to do all the work. Treat them as one grade collected in two instalments.

The exhibition asks the student to choose three objects and link them to one of 35 IA prompts published for the course. The written commentary runs to 950 words, which is short enough that every sentence has to earn its place, and it is internally assessed. Most of the difficulty is not in the writing. It is in the choice of objects, because an object that does not open the prompt cannot be rescued by good prose. A student who picks something generic and then spends 300 words explaining why it is interesting has already lost the paragraph.

The essay is a different exercise. Six prescribed titles are released for each exam session, the student answers one of them, the limit is 1,600 words, and it is externally assessed. The title is answered as it is set, not as the student wishes it had been set. That is the most common failure of all: a student reads a title about the natural sciences and mathematics, then writes the general essay on truth they had already planned in their head.

A tutor's work across the two pieces is the same skill taught twice. Turning a first-order subject question into a knowledge question. Holding two areas of knowledge in view instead of one. Finding a counterclaim that is genuinely uncomfortable rather than a straw man. IB TOK tutors in India who can do that with a real object on the table are worth far more than a tutor who lectures on the course.
items: 1. Read the 35 IA prompts and shortlist three that genuinely interest the student.
2. Fix one prompt first, then hunt objects; never choose the objects first.
3. Test each candidate object by asking what it shows about knowledge itself.
4. Keep three objects that pull in different directions, not three that agree.
5. Draft roughly 300 words per object, then cut the whole thing to 950.
6. Check every paragraph answers the prompt, not the object's backstory.

contentBlocks.heading: IB TOK home tutors in Gurugram, Powai, Whitefield and Gachibowli
contentBlocks.body:
Distance matters less for this subject than for a lab science, but it still decides whether a weekday evening slot survives the term. In Delhi NCR, families in South Delhi, Vasant Kunj and Chanakyapuri usually have the shortest hop to someone who knows the course; from Dwarka, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida the pool thins quickly, and evening traffic coming back from Gurugram (Gurgaon) or Golf Course Road can stretch a short trip into an unpredictable one. A parent in Sector 128 Noida asking for an IB TOK tutor in Delhi is often better served by someone based in Noida itself. Search the locality, not the city.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the same pattern repeats with water in the way. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri, Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill sit within reach of each other on a good evening. Powai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar do not, and a family in Kharghar looking for an IB TOK tutor in Mumbai should expect the honest answer to be online for the essay, with home visits only if a suitable person lives close.

Bengaluru splits along the same lines. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Electronic City are each their own city by seven in the evening, while Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Hebbal, Yelahanka and Kanakapura Road each have separate supply. A search for an IB TOK tutor in Bangalore that ignores which side of town you live on will waste a fortnight.

Hyderabad and Pune are kinder. An IB TOK tutor in Hyderabad reaching Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, Financial District or Kokapet can often hold a second slot in Jubilee Hills or Banjara Hills the same week, though Secunderabad is its own run. In Pune, Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Viman Nagar and Kharadi form one cluster while Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi form another, so an IB TOK tutor in Pune will usually pick a side. Beyond these, an IB TOK tutor in Chennai, an IB TOK tutor in Kolkata or an IB TOK tutor in Ahmedabad is a thinner search, and TOK exhibition help delivered online is the realistic route. IB TOK tutors in India for a course this specialised are not spread evenly, and typing TOK tutor near me into a search box will not change that.
items: Delhi NCR: Vasant Kunj and South Delhi hold evening slots better than Faridabad
Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Powai, Thane and Kharghar usually mean online for the essay
Bengaluru: Whitefield and Electronic City are separate pools after seven o'clock
Hyderabad: Gachibowli, Madhapur and Kondapur can share one person's evening
Pune: Koregaon Park and Baner are two clusters, not one catchment

contentBlocks.heading: The TOK calendar in India: exhibition term, essay term, May session
contentBlocks.body:
International schools here run this part of the core on their own internal calendar, and that calendar is the thing to get hold of early. Two dates matter: the school's deadline for the exhibition commentary, and its deadline for the final essay. Neither is the IB's own deadline. Both are set so the school has room to mark, check internally and upload, which means the real date a student works to is usually weeks earlier than the student assumes.

Families who write to us have children at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Pathways World School, Stonehill International School, Indus International School, Oakridge International School, Mahindra International School, Good Shepherd International School and The International School Bangalore. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Those names are context for parents, nothing more.

What varies most between schools is how much timetabled teaching a student actually gets. Some run a protected weekly period across both years with a teacher who has taught the course for a decade. Some fold it into a general studies slot that is the first thing sacrificed when a mock cycle arrives. Some rotate subject teachers through it, so a student meets four different voices in a year and never learns one method. Ask at a parent meeting how the course is staffed. The answer tells you more than any brochure.

Then there is the pile-up. In DP2 the essay deadline tends to land in the same stretch as internal assessment deadlines across several subjects, CAS sign-off and mock examinations, with the May session waiting behind all of it. A student who leaves the essay until that window is writing 1,600 words at the worst possible moment. Home tuition booked in the quiet part of DP1 costs a family far less stress than a rescue in the noisy part of DP2.
items: Ask for the exhibition and essay deadlines in writing during DP1
Check whether the course has a protected weekly period or shares a slot
Ask who teaches it and whether that teacher changes during the year
Expect the essay deadline to collide with IA deadlines and mock examinations
School deadlines sit weeks ahead of anything the IB itself requires

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid for TOK: which suits the exhibition commentary?
contentBlocks.body:
All three work, and the choice turns on one thing: whether the student needs to be talked into thinking or talked out of drifting. A home tutor sits at the table, can see the notebook, and can stop a student mid-sentence when a claim goes unexamined. That physical presence is worth most during the exhibition, when three objects have to be handled, photographed and argued over, and somebody has to say no to the first idea.

Online is stronger than most parents expect for the essay. A 1,600-word argument lives on a screen anyway. A shared document, a tutor reading the student's own paragraph back to them and asking which sentence carries the counterclaim, an outline marked up live: none of that needs the tutor in the room. Online also solves supply. A family in Kharghar, Yelahanka or Greater Noida can reach a theory of knowledge tutor who would never make the drive, and for a course taught by relatively few people in India that reach is the whole argument.

Hybrid is where most DP families settle. One home session a fortnight for the harder conversations, short online sessions in between to check a draft has moved. It also survives the school year here better: monsoon weeks, mock weeks and the long summer break all break a fixed schedule, and the online leg keeps the thread.

Now the trade-offs, stated plainly. Home tuition is the most expensive use of a tutor's evening because of travel, and it is the first thing traffic destroys. Online loses the small signals, the pause before an answer, the page pushed quietly away, that tell a tutor a student has not understood. Hybrid asks the household to hold two different rhythms, and some households never manage it. For this subject, IB TOK tutors in India usually suggest home sessions for the exhibition and online for essay drafting, and you should reverse that only if the student writes better with somebody physically beside them.
items: Home tuition suits the exhibition: objects on the table, first ideas refused
Online suits essay drafting, because the argument already lives on a screen
Hybrid keeps continuity through monsoon weeks, mock cycles and the summer break
Online widens supply far beyond the few people teaching the course locally
Home visits cost the most travel time and collapse first in traffic

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a tutor really knows all five areas of knowledge?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram verifies the profiles of the tutors it shortlists, and you should still run your own check, because a claim to teach this course is easy to make and hard to see through. Ask three questions in the trial. First, what is the difference between a subject question and a knowledge question? Anyone who cannot answer that cleanly in a minute has not taught the course. Second, which of the five areas of knowledge do they find hardest to teach, and why? Everybody finds one hard, and a tutor who says none is bluffing. Third, how would they handle a student who writes about the natural sciences in every single paragraph?

Then ask about the boundary, and listen for whether they raise it before you do. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The IB's academic integrity policy allows a teacher to give feedback on one draft; it does not allow anyone, tutor or parent, to write, rewrite or edit the student's submission. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, question the reasoning, and point at a criterion and ask the student to reread their own paragraph against it. That is the whole permitted range. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone.

Someone who offers to tidy up the commentary, or who returns a version with sentences rewritten, is putting the diploma at risk and should be declined on the spot. This is stricter than ordinary subject tuition, and it is worth saying to your child as well, because the pressure to accept a rewritten paragraph is very real at eleven at night.

Check the practical things too. Ask which exam sessions they have taught through, whether they have worked on the exhibition as well as the essay, and what they do when a student's chosen title turns out to be the wrong one. IB TOK tutors in India who have been through a full cycle answer that last question immediately.
items: Ask them to separate a knowledge question from an ordinary subject question
Ask which of the five areas of knowledge they teach least well
Listen for the integrity boundary offered before you have raised it
Decline anyone who offers to edit, tidy or rewrite the submission
Ask which exam sessions they have taught the course through

contentBlocks.heading: What IB TOK tutors in India actually teach, hour by hour
contentBlocks.body:
The course has three parts, and anyone who only teaches essay technique is teaching a third of it. First is the core theme, knowledge and the knower, which every student takes. It asks what the student's own position does to what they can know: their schooling, their languages, their community, the things they have never had reason to doubt. Students here often find this the easiest part to talk about and the hardest to write about, because the honest personal example feels too small to put into an essay.

Second are the optional themes. Schools choose two of five, and those two shape the examples a whole cohort reaches for. Ask your coordinator which two, then check that a prospective tutor is comfortable in both. A student who has spent a term on one theme will drag it into the essay whether it fits the title or not.

Third are the five areas of knowledge: history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts. All five are studied. This is where most of the essay marks are won and lost, because a prescribed title names areas of knowledge and the student has to compare them honestly. The common pattern in schools here is a cohort strong on the natural sciences and mathematics, comfortable enough in history, and nearly silent on the arts and the human sciences. Half the value of a good tutor is forcing the second half of that list into a student's working vocabulary.

An hour with a decent tutor does not look like a lecture. It looks like this: read the title aloud, say what it is actually asking, name two areas of knowledge that pull against each other, produce one real example in each, then attack your own example. Repeat until the student stops needing the prompt. IB TOK tutors in India who work this way produce students who can write the essay without help, which is the only kind of help that is permitted.
items: Core theme: knowledge and the knower, studied by every DP student
Two optional themes out of five, chosen by the school rather than the student
Five areas: history, human sciences, natural sciences, mathematics and the arts
Most essay marks turn on comparing two areas of knowledge honestly
Sessions run on real examples the student produces, not on lecture notes

contentBlocks.heading: What progress on a TOK essay draft looks like in India, month by month
contentBlocks.body:
Progress here is visible in the quality of a student's questions long before it is visible in any mark. Within the first two or three sessions you should hear the vocabulary change at the dinner table: not better grades, but a child saying that a claim depends on how the evidence was gathered. If nothing like that has happened after a month, something is wrong with the match, and you should say so rather than wait.

On the essay itself the sequence is slow, and it should be. Understanding the title takes longer than parents expect, often two sessions on its own. Then an outline that names the areas of knowledge and the claims. Then a full draft. Then the one round of teacher feedback the school permits, and a revision the student makes alone. A tutor can work either side of that feedback and must not touch the document itself.

Be careful about what you are measuring. The school forms the predicted grade and a tutor cannot change it. No tutor can guarantee a grade, in this subject or any other, and anyone promising a particular letter for the essay should be treated with real scepticism. The honest measure is whether the student can explain their own argument to you, out loud, without reading it off the page.

There are limits worth naming before you book anything. Starting six weeks before a DP2 essay deadline buys damage control, not a strong essay. A student who has drifted through eighteen months of lessons has a genuine hole and will need the five areas of knowledge built almost from scratch. And if a child is already carrying six subjects, stacked IA deadlines and CAS, adding another weekly commitment can make the whole term worse. Sometimes the advice IB TOK tutors in India should give is to drop something else first.
items: Sessions one to three: the student's questions sharpen before any mark moves
Two whole sessions can go on understanding the prescribed title alone
Outline, full draft, then the school's single permitted round of feedback
The school sets the predicted grade and a tutor cannot move it
Six weeks before a deadline buys damage control, not a strong essay

contentBlocks.heading: Starting TOK home tuition in India before the prescribed titles land
contentBlocks.body:
The best time to start is the term before you need to. For most schools here that means a short run of home tuition in DP1 around the exhibition, and a second run early in DP2 as soon as the prescribed titles are handed out. Starting much earlier is usually unnecessary. Starting later is the reason most of these enquiries arrive in the first place.

Prepare four things before the first session. The 35 IA prompts, or the prescribed titles if the school has released them. Whatever else the school has issued: the assessment instructions, the internal deadline, any exemplar shared in class. The last written comment the teacher made on your child's work. And the student's six DP subjects, because a tutor will build examples out of what the student already knows well.

The first session should not be a lecture on the course. A good one opens with the student explaining, in their own words, what the exhibition prompt or the essay title is asking. It usually goes badly, and that is the point: the gap between what a title says and what a student thinks it says is the whole job. By the end of that hour there should be one written knowledge question, two areas of knowledge named, and one example in each that the student produced themselves.

Send the enquiry with the exam session, the DP year, your locality and two evening slots that genuinely work for the household. IB Gram will ask about the board, the syllabus, the level, the school calendar, your location and the schedule, then shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified. Ask for a trial before you commit. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different match, and do it early rather than at the deadline.
items: Bring the 35 IA prompts, or the released prescribed titles, to session one
Bring the school's internal deadline and the teacher's last written comment
Book the DP1 run around the exhibition rather than after it closes
Expect the first session to expose a misread title, quite deliberately
Offer two evening slots the household can hold for a whole term

faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers should be declined. Every IB internal assessment is the student's own work. The school submits the work and runs it through similarity checking, and malpractice findings are handled by the IB, not by the school alone.

faqs.question: How many home tuition sessions does the TOK exhibition usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, provided they start early. A short run of home tuition in DP1 is normally enough for the exhibition: one session to settle the prompt, one or two on testing candidate objects, one on structuring the 950 words, and one after the student has drafted alone. The essay in DP2 needs more, because understanding a prescribed title takes longer than writing about it. The actual number depends on the student and on tutor availability, so treat any fixed package sold in advance with suspicion.

faqs.question: Our evenings in Bandra and Andheri are already full. When do home sessions for TOK fit?
faqs.answer: Late weekday evenings and weekend mornings, in practice. This is one of the easier DP commitments to schedule, because it needs no laboratory and no two-hour block; a focused hour works. Families across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region often put the home session on a Saturday morning before the day fills up, and keep a short midweek online check-in for drafts. If your locality is Powai, Thane or Navi Mumbai, expect the home leg to be harder to hold and plan the hybrid pattern from the beginning rather than after it fails.

faqs.question: What actually happens if my child gets an E in TOK?
faqs.answer: An E in TOK is a failing condition for the diploma, which means it can cost the award even when the six subject grades are perfectly good. TOK and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and together contribute up to three points towards the maximum of 45, with 24 points the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. This is why the essay is worth protecting in DP2 rather than sacrificing to an IA deadline. Your DP coordinator can confirm exactly how the conditions apply to your child.

faqs.question: Is the exhibition or the essay worth more of the TOK grade?
faqs.answer: The essay, at two thirds of the grade against the exhibition's one third. The exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 IA prompts, runs to 950 words and is internally assessed. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for each exam session, runs to 1,600 words and is externally assessed. Both matter. But the exhibition finishes first and its mark is settled while the essay is still being written, so a weak exhibition puts far more pressure on the essay than the other way round.

faqs.question: Nobody in Gachibowli seems to teach this course. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Widen the search online, and do it early rather than after a month of asking neighbours. Relatively few people teach Theory of Knowledge in any single locality, and Hyderabad is no exception, so a family in Gachibowli, Kondapur or the Financial District may find the nearest suitable person lives in another city altogether. Searching TOK tutor near me tends to return general DP subject tutors instead. Ask instead for somebody who has taken students through both the exhibition and the essay, wherever they are based, and run the sessions online.

faqs.question: How should a student choose between the six prescribed titles?
faqs.answer: By sketching a rough outline for two of them before committing to either. Six prescribed titles are released for each exam session and the student answers one. The instinct is to pick the title that sounds most interesting, which is usually the one with the least available material behind it. A better test is whether the student can name two areas of knowledge that genuinely pull against each other inside that title, and produce one real example in each. If that takes more than twenty minutes, try a different title.

faqs.question: Does online TOK tutoring work as well as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For the essay, yes, and sometimes better. A 1,600-word argument lives in a document anyway, and a shared screen is a natural place to question a claim line by line. For the exhibition, sessions in the room have the edge, because three physical objects are easier to argue about across a table. Online also reaches people who could never travel to Yelahanka, Greater Noida or Kharghar on a weekday evening. What you lose is the small signals: a pause, a shrug, a page pushed quietly away.

faqs.question: The school has not told us which two optional themes they chose. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough to ask. The course covers the core theme, knowledge and the knower, plus two of five optional themes chosen by the school, plus five areas of knowledge. The two optional themes shape the examples a whole cohort has already practised, so a tutor who knows them can build on the student's existing material instead of starting again. Email the DP coordinator and ask for the two themes and the internal deadlines in the same message. Both answers are useful, and neither is confidential.

faqs.question: Can TOK support on its own lift the three core points?
faqs.answer: Not on its own, because those points come from TOK and the Extended Essay together. The two are graded A to E and combine for up to three points, so a better TOK grade helps only in combination with the EE grade. The EE is a separate piece of work: an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of effort, supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded along the way. The EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so follow the version your DP coordinator issues.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student in Pune start TOK support?
faqs.answer: In the term the exhibition is set, neither much before nor after. For a family in Koregaon Park, Baner or Kharadi that usually means a short run of sessions once the school has circulated the IA prompts, then a pause, then a restart in DP2 when the prescribed titles arrive. Starting in the first weeks of DP1 spends money on a course the student has barely met. Starting after the internal deadline is announced leaves no room to change objects when the first three do not work.

comparison.heading: How do TOK tutors in India compare with school lessons, a batch and self-study?
comparison.intro: Four ways a family here gets this course taught, and each is genuinely better at something. The school teacher is the only person who may give the single permitted feedback on a draft. A batch gives a student other people's knowledge questions to argue with, which the course rewards. Self-study costs nothing and builds the independence the essay is marked on. One-to-one buys attention on this student's own argument. The trade-off that decides it is usually time rather than quality.
