introSummary: IGCSE Maths tutors in India teach three named courses, most often as home tuition at the family's own dining table: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1. Each is tiered or structured differently, and each is examined on its own papers. From the 2025 exams, a Core candidate for 0580 sits Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one; an Extended candidate sits Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Edexcel 4MA1 runs Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers in either tier. Most of what a good Maths tutor does is narrower than parents expect: recovering method marks, fixing non-calculator arithmetic, and keeping an error log that says exactly what to revise next.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match an IGCSE Maths tutor in India to 0580, 0606 or 4MA1?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the code, not the subject name. A message saying a Grade 10 child needs Maths help produces a general shortlist. A message saying 0580 Extended, entered for the May/June series, losing marks on Paper 2, produces a useful one. IGCSE Maths tutors in India teach to a named syllabus, and Cambridge 0580, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 are three separate jobs with three separate mark schemes.

When you send a query or book a free consultation for home tuition, IB Gram asks for the board, the tier the school has entered the student for, the exam series, your locality, and the evenings that are genuinely free once school and other coaching are accounted for. Those answers decide the shortlist. Only profiles that have been verified and that match the code and tier go on it, which is why the first question back to you is usually about the syllabus rather than about grades.

Ask for a trial before committing. For Maths, the trial that tells you something is not a lecture on a topic the student already knows. Hand the tutor a marked school test and ask them to work through two questions the student got wrong, out loud, and then explain why the marks went. A tutor who reaches for the mark scheme and talks about method marks is teaching the subject as it is actually assessed. A tutor who reworks the sum correctly and moves on is not.

Availability depends on level, locality and schedule. A student in Kharghar or on Kanakapura Road may find the local pool thin for 0606 in particular, because far fewer teachers carry that syllabus than carry 0580. If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, say so and ask for a different match rather than waiting for the term to end.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation naming the syllabus code and tier.
2. IB Gram asks about board, level, school calendar, locality and free evenings.
3. You get a shortlist of verified profiles matched to 0580, 0606 or 4MA1.
4. A demo or trial session is arranged before the family commits to anything.
5. Home classes, online or a hybrid week; ask for a different match if needed.

contentBlocks.heading: Core, Extended, Foundation, Higher: which Maths tier is your child entered for in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Tier is the first decision and it is not the student's to make alone. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, the school enters a candidate for either Core or Extended. Core tops out at grade C. Extended reaches A*. That one fact settles more arguments in Indian households than anything else about the syllabus, because a student aiming at IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level (AA HL) or A Level Mathematics cannot afford a Core entry, whatever this term's test scores say.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) frames the same decision differently. A candidate sits Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers in either tier, and Edexcel International GCSE grades on the 9-1 scale rather than A* to G. So a family moving a child between a Cambridge school in Pune and an Edexcel school in Ahmedabad is not simply changing textbooks. The grade scale, the tier names and the calculator rules all change at once, and a term can be lost to that confusion.

Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 sits outside all of it. There are no tiers. It is examined by two written papers with a calculator allowed in both, and it is graded A* to E. It is usually taken alongside 0580 Extended rather than instead of it, by students heading for IB Mathematics AA HL or A Level Mathematics. Pearson Edexcel's nearest equivalent is International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1).

So who should take 0606? A student who finishes 0580 Extended past papers with time to spare and asks why a method works, not only how. A student scraping through Extended should not be carrying a second Maths syllabus as well. Two Maths courses in Grade 10 is a real load, and the honest advice is often to drop the idea and arrive in the Diploma Programme (DP) with a clean, confident Extended grade instead.
items: 0580 Core: Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 calculator, with a grade C ceiling
0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 calculator, reaching grade A*
Edexcel 4MA1: Foundation or Higher tier, two calculator papers, graded on 9-1
0606 Additional Mathematics: no tiers, two calculator papers, graded A* to E
Edexcel's nearest equivalent to 0606 is Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1

contentBlocks.heading: Paper 1 and Paper 2 without a calculator: the 0580 structure in detail
contentBlocks.body:
From the 2025 exams, Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 puts a non-calculator paper in front of every candidate. Core candidates sit Paper 1, which is non-calculator, and Paper 3, on which a calculator is allowed. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4 with a calculator. For students taught in Indian schools where the calculator has been in the pencil case since middle school, this is the change that hurts, and it is the most common reason a family starts looking for an IGCSE 0580 tutor somewhere around October.

What the non-calculator paper really tests is arithmetic fluency that has quietly rotted. Multiplying a decimal by a decimal. Dividing by a fraction. Simplifying a surd. Converting a recurring decimal to a fraction. Working in standard form by hand. Estimating to one significant figure before the real calculation, which is also how a student catches an absurd answer on the calculator paper. None of this is difficult content. All of it is slow and error-prone when the last unaided long multiplication happened four years ago, and the paper is timed.

Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 sets no non-calculator paper: both papers in each tier allow a calculator. That does not make the course easier. An Edexcel 4MA1 tutor in India will usually spend the recovered time on multi-step problem questions and on the accuracy of a number that has been rounded three times on its way through a calculation.

Additional Mathematics 0606 is a different animal again, and its content list is worth reading aloud to a student before they opt in: functions, quadratic functions, factors of polynomials, equations, inequalities and graphs, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, coordinate geometry of the circle, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation and integration. Calculus in Grade 10 is the part that surprises parents most.
items: Core 0580: Paper 1 without a calculator, Paper 3 with one allowed
Extended 0580: Paper 2 without a calculator, Paper 4 with one allowed
4MA1 allows a calculator in both papers, at Foundation and at Higher
Both 0606 papers allow a calculator and include differentiation and integration
Non-calculator practice belongs in every week, not the fortnight before mocks

contentBlocks.heading: Where families find IGCSE Maths home tuition in India, region by region
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE Maths tutors in India are not spread evenly, and the gap is sharper for 0606 than for 0580. In Delhi NCR the pool is deep but the geography is punishing: a tutor living in Dwarka and a student in Sector 128 Noida are on opposite sides of the city, and weekday evening traffic between South Delhi, Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Ghaziabad can stretch a short trip badly. Families in Vasant Kunj, Chanakyapuri and on Golf Course Road usually find a home tutor inside their own sector belt, while Greater Noida and Faridabad take longer to fill. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Delhi will often say yes to three localities and no to the fourth, and that is a sign of a tutor who keeps commitments.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region behaves the same way. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Mumbai based in Bandra will hold a Juhu, Worli or Malabar Hill slot comfortably and think twice about Thane on a Wednesday. Powai and Andheri tend to be self-contained. Navi Mumbai, Vashi and Kharghar are better served by tutors who already live across the creek, because a home tutor booked across the harbour on a monsoon evening is a booking that will eventually be missed.

In Bengaluru, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Indiranagar, Koramangala and HSR Layout hold their own tutors, while Yelahanka, Hebbal, Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road often work better as hybrid weeks. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Bangalore who lives on one side of the city rarely crosses it twice a week, whatever the first phone call promises. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Hyderabad usually works the Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur and Financial District corridor, with Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Kokapet close behind and Secunderabad a separate run. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Chennai covers Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet, Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar easily, while Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Perungudi and Velachery depend entirely on where the tutor already is. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Pune treats Koregaon Park, Kalyani Nagar, Kharadi and Viman Nagar as one run and Baner, Balewadi, Aundh, Hinjewadi and Wakad as another.

Outside the metros the arithmetic changes. In Gujarat, an IGCSE Maths tutor in Ahmedabad will travel within Satellite, Bodakdev and the SG Highway stretch, with Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot thinner. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Kolkata covers Salt Lake, New Town, Ballygunge, Alipore and Rajarhat, while Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi and Patna across eastern India lean on online lessons. The same holds for northern India beyond Delhi NCR, where Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Kanpur have international schools but few 0606 specialists; for southern India beyond Bengaluru and Chennai, where Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Coimbatore, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Madurai run on a mix of local home tuition and online sessions; and for central and western India, where Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Raipur, Jabalpur, Goa, Nashik and Aurangabad usually mean one good local tutor for 0580 and a distant specialist for Additional Mathematics.

Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra and Powai self-contained, Kharghar needs a tutor across the creek

contentBlocks.heading: The February/March series and what a Grade 10 Maths year looks like in India
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge exam series run in February/March, May/June and October/November, and the February/March series is offered only in India. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Which one your child sits is the school's decision, not the family's, and a student cannot enter a series independently of the school. So the first question for a Grade 10 parent is not which tutor, but which series, because a February/March entry compresses the whole plan by roughly one term.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. School names appear here only as context for the kind of calendar families are working around.

That calendar is the real constraint. International schools in India typically open the academic year around April or June, run a first mock cycle mid-year and a second closer to the series. Maths is usually the subject whose syllabus finishes last, because the later topics in 0580 Extended and almost all of 0606 land in the final terms. A tutor who starts in January against a February/March entry has weeks, not months, and should say that plainly rather than talk about a rescue. Grade 9 is the cheap year to fix algebra. Grade 10 is the expensive one.

The February/March series exists so that Grade 10 results arrive in time for Indian school admissions to Class 11 and for entry to the IB Diploma Programme or Cambridge International AS and A Levels in the same academic year. Families planning a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11 should also know that the Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence for international qualifications, and that current requirements are worth checking with the university or board concerned rather than assuming from what another family did three years ago.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May/June
The school decides the series; a student cannot enter one independently
February/March results arrive in time for Class 11, DP or A Level entry
Check equivalence with the university or board concerned, not with other parents

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a subject written out by hand?
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the comparison in one paragraph. Home tuition puts the tutor beside the student's own paper, which matters more in Maths than in almost any other IGCSE subject, because the marks live in the working and the working is handwritten. Online tuition gives access to a specialist who may be the only person within reach who has taught 0606, and it removes travel entirely. Hybrid splits the week: home lessons for the long teaching hour, an online slot for a short marked past-paper review. The trade-off is simple. Home costs travel time and is hostage to traffic and monsoon, while online costs the tutor a clear view of the page unless the student photographs the script and sends it before the session.

Most IGCSE Maths tutors in India offer all three, and the right answer changes with the student rather than with the city. A student who abandons a question halfway and hides it needs someone in the room. A student who is disciplined, writes fully and photographs their work needs a better tutor more than a nearer one.

What online genuinely fixes for Maths is the geometry of the page. A document camera, or a modest tablet with a stylus, lets the tutor annotate the student's own script line by line, and a recorded worked solution can be replayed the night before a test. What it does not fix is pace. A tutor cannot see a student quietly stop writing at minute forty.

Hybrid weeks tend to hold best in the outer suburbs: Yelahanka, Greater Noida, Kharghar, Wakad. The home lessons anchor the relationship and the online slot keeps the marking turnaround short. Agree at the start which day is which, and put it in writing, because a hybrid week that drifts becomes an online-only week nobody actually chose.
items: Home lessons: the tutor sees the working, the crossings-out and the timing
Online: reach a 0606 specialist in another city, with no travel lost
Hybrid: home lessons for teaching, an online slot for marked past papers
Online needs a stylus, tablet or document camera to annotate handwritten working
Home lessons lose to traffic and monsoon, so agree a fallback slot early

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check that a tutor has actually taught 0580 Extended?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification is two jobs, and only one of them belongs to a platform. IB Gram checks identity and qualification documents and the teaching claims on a profile before it goes live, and profiles that have not been verified do not reach a shortlist. What no platform can see from a document is whether this person can teach your child, which is exactly what the trial session exists for.

So ask the syllabus questions yourself. They take four minutes and they are hard to bluff. Which papers does an Extended candidate sit, and which of them is non-calculator? What is the grade ceiling on Core? On 4MA1, which tier has the school entered the student for, and how many calculator papers is that? For 0606, name five topics from the content list. A tutor who has taught the course answers all of these without pausing. A general Maths tutor who picked up the word IGCSE from a listings site answers the first and stalls on the rest.

Then ask for evidence of marking. Request that the tutor marks one past-paper question the student has already attempted, in writing, with the marks broken down. You are looking for a script that says where the method mark was earned and where the accuracy mark went, not a tick and a score out of six. A tutor who cannot do that in fifteen minutes will not do it across a term either.

A search for an IGCSE Maths tutor near me returns listings, advertisements and a few genuine profiles, in no useful order. Judge them on those four minutes rather than on the photograph. And check the practical things a parent should always check before home visits: who else is at home during the session, where in the flat the lesson will sit, and how a missed slot gets made up.
items: Ask which 0580 papers are non-calculator before you ask anything else
Ask for one past-paper question marked in writing, with the marks broken down
For 0606, ask the tutor to name five topics from the content list
Confirm in writing which tier the school has entered the student for
Before home visits, agree study space, supervision and how missed sessions are made up

contentBlocks.heading: Method marks: the marks 0580 candidates throw away in silence
contentBlocks.body:
Method marks are why a Maths tutor is different from a Maths video. Cambridge and Edexcel mark schemes award marks for a correct method even when the final answer is wrong, and they award accuracy marks separately. A student who writes only the answer is betting the whole question on getting it right. A student who writes the method out is insured against one slip.

Take a short example. Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + 3y = 12 and x - y = 1. The student rearranges the second equation to x = y + 1, substitutes into the first to get 2(y + 1) + 3y = 12, expands to 5y + 2 = 12, and finishes with y = 2 and x = 3. Now suppose the expansion slips and the line reads 5y + 1 = 12, giving y = 2.2 and x = 3.2. The rearrangement and the substitution are still visible on the page, so the method marks stand and only the accuracy marks go. Now suppose the same student writes nothing but y = 2.2, x = 3.2. Everything goes with it.

That is the whole lesson, and students trained on objective-type tests and quick multiple-choice practice lose marks to it in every series. They have been taught to work in their head and write the answer, because that is what speed looks like in a competitive entrance paper. IGCSE Maths rewards the opposite habit, and it rewards it on both the calculator and the non-calculator papers.

So a good tutor spends real time on presentation: one step per line, an equals sign that means equals, the formula written before numbers are substituted into it, units carried through, rounding done once at the end, the final answer underlined. It feels pedantic in September. By February it is worth marks on every paper, and it costs nothing to learn.
items: Method marks survive a wrong final answer, while a bare answer earns nothing
One step per line, and no more than one operation on that line
Write the formula first, then substitute the numbers into it
Round once, at the end, to the accuracy the question asks for
Underline the final answer so the examiner is not hunting for it

contentBlocks.heading: An error log across one term: how Maths progress shows up in India
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in Maths is measurable, which makes it easier to be honest about than most subjects. The instrument is an error log, and it should exist on paper or in one shared document from the second session onwards. Not a notebook of solved questions. A log of mistakes.

Here is the routine across a term. Every marked question the student gets wrong goes in with four columns: the paper and question number, the topic, what actually went wrong in one phrase, and the correction worked properly. The one-phrase column is the important one, and it has to be specific. The word careless is useless. Expanded the bracket without distributing the minus sign is a fixable thing. Once a fortnight the tutor sorts the log by that column and reads it back. Patterns appear quickly: a student who believes they are weak at trigonometry is often weak at rearranging a formula, and every trigonometry error turns out to be the same algebra error wearing a different hat.

By the end of a term you should be able to see three things. Which phrases have stopped appearing. Which have moved between Paper 2 and Paper 4, or between a 0580 question and a 0606 one. And which are still there every fortnight. That third group is the honest agenda for the next term. This is what IGCSE Maths tutors in India should be showing you at a review, in place of a general report that the child is improving.

And the limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anyone who offers one on a syllabus with two externally marked papers should be treated with real scepticism. Six weeks of home tuition will not turn a Core candidate into an Extended candidate at the top of the scale. What it can realistically do is stop three specific errors repeating, which on a two-paper Maths entry is usually worth more than new content.
items: Four columns: paper and question number, topic, the error in one phrase, correction
Sort the log by error phrase once a fortnight and read it back aloud
Specific phrases only, such as dropped the minus sign, never just careless
Review after six to eight weeks against the log, not against a feeling
No tutor can promise a grade on two externally marked Maths papers

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IGCSE Maths home classes in India: the first hour, minute by minute
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first session, put three things on the table: the most recent marked school test with the teacher's comments still on it, the student's own working notebook so the tutor can see the handwriting under time pressure, and a clear statement of the tier and the series the school has entered the student for. If you do not know the tier, ask the school before the first hour rather than after it. Half of a first session otherwise goes on guessing.

What the first hour should not be is a diagnostic test you paid for. A tutor can read a marked script in ten minutes and learn more from it than from an hour of fresh questions. The rest of the hour belongs to teaching.

For home classes, settle the practical things at the same time: the room, whether a sibling will be in it, the society or gate entry arrangement so the tutor is not standing outside for ten minutes of a paid hour, and what happens to a slot missed because of traffic or illness. Weekday evenings after seven fill first in every metro, so a family in Powai or Gachibowli booking in September has more choice than one booking in December.

Then the running order below, which is what a productive one-hour Maths session looks like and which should be recognisable from week two onwards. It is deliberately front-loaded with recall and back-loaded with timed work, because the two things a Grade 10 student cannot fake are whether last month's topic survived and whether the working holds up at exam pace. Ask for the error log entries after each session so you can watch the same structure repeating.
items: 1. Five minutes: three recall questions from an older topic, written out fully.
2. Ten minutes: last week's homework marked against the mark scheme, together.
3. Twenty-five minutes: new teaching, tutor works one example, student works the next.
4. Ten minutes: one timed past-paper question at exam pace, with no help.
5. Ten minutes: error log updated, and homework set from the same topic.

faqs.question: Does my child need a separate Additional Maths 0606 tutor, or can one tutor cover 0580 too?
faqs.answer: Usually one tutor can cover both, but only if they have genuinely taught 0606. The overlap is real at the algebra end and disappears completely at calculus, so ask the tutor to name five topics from the 0606 content list before you assume anything. Someone comfortable with differentiation, integration, circular measure and the coordinate geometry of the circle can run both courses in one weekly slot. Someone who hesitates should take 0580 only, and you should look for an Additional Maths 0606 tutor separately, online if no one local teaches it.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Core and Extended for Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: Decide it from marked past papers, not from a feeling about the child. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*, so the decision closes doors if it is made early and never revisited. Sit the student for a full Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 under timed conditions, mark them honestly against the mark scheme, and look at whether the lost marks are content the student has not met or method they have not practised. The school makes the entry, so bring evidence to the subject teacher rather than an opinion.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE Maths home tutor reach us on weekday evenings in Mumbai or Pune?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the tutor already lives in your belt of the city. A home tutor based in Bandra will hold a Juhu or Worli slot week after week and will struggle with Thane on the same evening. In Pune, Koregaon Park and Kalyani Nagar work as one run while Baner, Balewadi and Hinjewadi form another. Book the earliest evening slot the student can genuinely use, keep it fixed, and agree in advance what happens when monsoon traffic makes the trip impossible. All of it is subject to tutor availability and the school timetable.

faqs.question: What does one hour of IGCSE Maths home tuition actually cover?
faqs.answer: A productive hour is five minutes of recall from an older topic, ten minutes marking last week's homework against the mark scheme, twenty-five minutes of new teaching in which the tutor works one example and the student works the next, ten minutes of a timed past-paper question with no help at all, and ten minutes updating the error log and setting homework. If the whole hour is the tutor talking and the student copying, the format is wrong. The student should be writing for at least half of it.

faqs.question: My child gets the right answers in class but loses marks in tests. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the working is not on the page. Cambridge and Edexcel mark schemes award method marks separately from accuracy marks, so a student who computes in their head and writes a single line has nothing left to score when the final number is wrong. Ask to see the last marked script. If you find long stretches of blank space above short answers, that is the whole diagnosis, and it is fixable in a few weeks of disciplined presentation rather than months of new content.

faqs.question: Is the non-calculator paper really a problem for students in Indian schools?
faqs.answer: For many of them, yes. From the 2025 exams, Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without one, and students who have used a calculator since middle school find their unaided arithmetic slow rather than wrong. Fractions, surds, standard form, recurring decimals and estimation all come back. The fix is boring and reliable: a short non-calculator set every week from Grade 9 onwards, timed, with the calculator kept out of the room while it is done.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE Maths tutors in India charge, and what changes the fee?
faqs.answer: Fees are set by the individual tutor and vary with level, locality, travel and whether the session runs at home or online. A tutor carrying 0606 as well as 0580 Extended generally sits at the higher end, because far fewer teachers hold that syllabus. Home lessons carry the tutor's travel time, and online sessions usually do not. Ask for the rate per session, the session length, the cancellation terms and whether marking between sessions is included, and get all four in writing before the trial.

faqs.question: We are in Indore and nobody local teaches 0606. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Run 0580 with a local home tutor and 0606 online with a specialist. That split works well, because the 0580 work benefits most from someone watching the handwriting while the 0606 work is largely conceptual and teaches fine on a shared screen with a stylus. The same pattern suits families in Bhopal, Nagpur, Nashik, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Dehradun, Jaipur and Guwahati. Ask the online tutor how the written script reaches them each week, because a photograph sent the night before is what makes the session worth having.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel 4MA1 easier than Cambridge 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: They are different, not ranked. 4MA1 is tiered Foundation or Higher and allows a calculator in both papers of either tier, while 0580 Extended puts Paper 2 in front of the candidate with no calculator at all. Edexcel grades on the 9-1 scale and Cambridge grades 0580 from A* to G. A student weak at unaided arithmetic may find 4MA1 kinder, and a student weak at long multi-step problems may not. The school chooses the board in any case, so the comparison is mostly academic.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month of home classes. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the error log before you ask for a new tutor. A month is four sessions, which is enough to see whether the same error phrases keep appearing but not enough to move a grade. If no log exists, that is the problem and it is the tutor's to fix. If it exists and the same three phrases repeat every fortnight, the teaching is not landing, and you should ask for a different match rather than waiting out the term in hope.

faqs.question: Should we start Maths tuition in Grade 9 or wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 if the goal is 0606 or a confident Extended entry, Grade 10 if the goal is fixing something specific. IGCSE is a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and the later 0580 Extended topics plus almost all of 0606 land in the final terms, so a student who arrives in Grade 10 already shaky on algebra spends the year catching up instead of practising papers. Starting earlier also means the tier decision is made on real evidence.

introSummary: IGCSE Physics tutors in India work on one skill before any other: recalling the equations in the syllabus and rearranging them under time pressure. Most families start with home tuition, because a tutor sitting beside a Grade 10 student can see the rearrangement go wrong on paper, halfway down the working, before a wrong final answer hides it. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 covers motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Pearson Edexcel's equivalent is International GCSE Physics 4PH1. Cambridge assesses through multiple choice worth 30% of the total, theory worth 50%, and a practical component worth 20%. contentBlocks.heading: How a request for IGCSE Physics tutors in India turns into a shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Start with a query or a free consultation. IB Gram asks a short set of questions: Cambridge 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1, Core or Extended, which exam series the school has entered the student for, whether the school runs Paper 5 or Paper 6, and which topics have already gone badly. Those five answers change the shortlist more than anything else you could tell us.

The most useful thing you can send is a marked script. A Grade 10 mock paper with the teacher's ticks and crosses still on it tells a tutor in ten minutes what a phone call cannot tell them in an hour. If marks are being dropped on numerical questions, the problem is usually equation recall and rearrangement. If the numbers are right and the written answers are thin, the problem is explanation. Those are two different strengths in a tutor, and the shortlist should reflect which one you actually need.

Then we look at location and schedule. Home tuition works well where a tutor lives within a sensible evening run of your locality, and we say so honestly when it does not. IGCSE Physics tutors in India who live on the same side of a metro as their student hold a weekday slot far better than one crossing the city at peak hour. A family in Powai and a family in Kanakapura Road will get different advice about the same request. Availability is always subject to tutor availability, and a Grade 10 evening slot in the weeks before a series is the hardest one to hold.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit to anything. Ask the tutor to spend it on one past paper question rather than on introductions. And if the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, ask for a different match. That is a normal request, not a complaint.

2. Add a marked mock script or the most recent school report.
3. IB Gram shortlists verified tutors who teach 0625 or 4PH1.

contentBlocks.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6 for 0625: who decides this in India?
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge IGCSE sciences examined from 2023 have a fixed shape. Paper 1 is multiple choice for Core candidates and Paper 2 is multiple choice for Extended. Paper 3 is the Core theory paper and Paper 4 the Extended theory paper. The practical component is either Paper 5, a practical test done in a laboratory, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about practical work. The school chooses which of those two its candidates sit. Parents ring us asking to switch, and the honest answer is that the entry belongs to the school, so ask the examinations officer rather than the tutor.

The weighting settles where tuition time should go. Multiple choice carries 30% of the total, theory 50%, and the practical component 20%. A student who drills multiple choice all term and never writes a full explanation has spent most of the effort on the smaller half of the assessment.

Core and Extended are not interchangeable. Core tops out at grade C and Extended reaches A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses exist in 9-1 versions under different codes, which is worth confirming with the coordinator before you buy a revision book. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 is untiered: every candidate sits the same Paper 1 and Paper 2, practical skills are assessed inside those written papers, and grading runs 9-1.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We shortlist IGCSE Physics tutors in India against the syllabus code and the tier the school has actually entered, because a tutor who has only ever taught Extended 0625 will not automatically know what a 4PH1 mark scheme rewards, and the reverse is just as true.
items: Paper 1 multiple choice for Core; Paper 2 multiple choice for Extended
Paper 3 Core theory; Paper 4 Extended theory, the longer written paper
Paper 5 is the practical test; Paper 6 the alternative to practical
Weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical component 20%
Edexcel 4PH1 is untiered: Paper 1 and Paper 2, graded 9-1

contentBlocks.heading: Which 0625 equations must be recalled and rearranged?
contentBlocks.body:
All of them. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 gives candidates no equation sheet, so every relationship in the syllabus has to come out of the student's own memory, in the right form, and then be rearranged for whichever quantity the question asks about. That second half is where students trained on plug-in practice quietly lose marks.

Recall and rearrangement are separate skills and they need separate practice. A student can write the density relationship correctly and still fail to make volume the subject of it under exam pressure. The drill that works is short and frequent: the tutor names a quantity, the student writes the equation from memory and then rearranges it three ways, out loud, in under a minute each. Ten minutes of that at the start of a home tuition session, every week, does more than an hour of it once a term. Rotate the topics so that motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism and nuclear physics all come round.

Units and significant figures are the quiet mark-losers. A correct number with the wrong unit, or a unit that does not follow from the rearrangement, often scores nothing at all. Teach the student to carry units through the algebra rather than bolt them onto the answer at the end. On significant figures, the working rule is to match the data given in the question rather than copying whatever the calculator display shows.

Graph skills come third and carry real marks across motion, thermal physics and electricity. Plotting accurately, choosing a scale that uses the printed grid, drawing a line of best fit by judgement rather than joining dots, and reading a gradient off a large triangle are all teachable inside one session and then maintained in five minutes a week. IGCSE Physics tutors in India should be asking for that work on paper, with a pencil and a ruler, not on a screen.
items: Recall drill: name a quantity, write the equation, rearrange three ways
Carry units through the algebra instead of adding them at the end
Match significant figures to the data given, not the calculator display
Gradients read off a large triangle drawn on the printed grid
Line of best fit drawn by judgement, never dot-to-dot joining

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE Physics home tutors, locality by locality across India
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi NCR is the widest of the clusters and the hardest to cross on a weekday. A tutor living in South Delhi or Vasant Kunj can hold a six o'clock slot in Chanakyapuri without much trouble, and will think twice about Greater Noida on the same evening. Families in Dwarka, in Gurugram (Gurgaon) along Golf Course Road, in Sector 128 Noida, in Faridabad and in Ghaziabad usually do better with a tutor from their own side of the region. An IGCSE Physics tutor in Delhi who has to cross the city at peak hour will cancel more often than one who walks over.

In the Mumbai Metropolitan Region the same pattern repeats along the rail and road lines. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri and Powai form one practical catchment; Worli, Lower Parel and Malabar Hill another; Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Thane and Kharghar a third. An IGCSE Physics tutor in Mumbai who lives in Thane is a reasonable match for Kharghar and a poor one for Malabar Hill on a Tuesday evening.

Bengaluru splits east, north and south. Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Indiranagar and Koramangala make one set of runs; Hebbal and Yelahanka sit north; Electronic City, Jayanagar and Kanakapura Road are their own problem. An IGCSE Physics tutor in Bangalore will tell you honestly whether Whitefield to Jayanagar works at seven in the evening, and a good one will refuse the slot rather than take it and cancel.

Hyderabad is kinder. Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur, the Financial District and Kokapet sit close together, and Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Secunderabad are reachable from them, so an IGCSE Physics tutor in Hyderabad can often hold two evening slots. In Chennai, Adyar, Besant Nagar, Alwarpet and Nungambakkam are one cluster, while Perungudi, Velachery and the Old Mahabalipuram Road corridor are another, and Anna Nagar sits apart from both. Families searching for an IGCSE Physics tutor in Chennai on the OMR stretch usually widen to online faster than families in Adyar do. In Koregaon Park in Pune, in Salt Lake in Kolkata and in Bodakdev in Ahmedabad the local pool for 0625 Physics specifically is smaller, so an IGCSE Physics tutor in Pune, an IGCSE Physics tutor in Kolkata or an IGCSE Physics tutor in Ahmedabad is often found through a hybrid week rather than a purely local search.

Mumbai Metropolitan Region: Bandra, Andheri, Powai, Worli, Thane, Navi Mumbai

contentBlocks.heading: The Grade 10 calendar in India and when Physics revision has to start
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in India means Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and the Physics syllabus is back-loaded in most schools. Electricity and magnetism and nuclear physics tend to arrive late in Grade 10, which is exactly when the student is also trying to revise motion, forces and energy from a year earlier. Plan for that, or the last term becomes a scramble that nobody enjoys.

The exam series decide everything else. Cambridge runs a February/March series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May/June. A February/March candidate has a shorter Grade 10, so past paper work has to begin around the winter break rather than comfortably after it. International schools in India, the kind of school families have in mind when they name Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee School, Greenwood High International School, Chirec International School or Mercedes-Benz International School, run their own mock cycles, and those mock scripts are the single best piece of evidence a tutor can work from.

School expectations add their own pressure. Most schools set an internal deadline for practical work well before the series, and Grade 10 students are usually also carrying a sport, a music grade or a service commitment. A home tutor who books eight in the evening on a Wednesday and then finds the child walked in at half past seven from basketball will not hold that slot for long. Agree the realistic time, not the ideal one.

There is a second calendar question after the exams. Students go on to the IB Diploma Programme, Cambridge International AS and A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11, and each of those makes a different demand on Physics. Ask the tutor in the final term what the student should read over the long summer rather than letting the subject go cold for three months.
items: Cambridge series: February/March (offered only in India), May/June, October/November
Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June each year
Electricity, magnetism and nuclear physics often taught late in Grade 10
Mock scripts from school are the most useful evidence a tutor reads
After Grade 10: IB Diploma Programme, AS and A Levels, CBSE or ISC

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a 0625 Physics student
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the default for Physics at this level, and the reason is paper. Equation rearrangement happens in the student's own handwriting, and most of the errors are visible only while they are being made: a sign lost in a transposition, a unit dropped after a division, a triangle mnemonic used in place of algebra. A tutor sitting beside the student catches those in the moment. A tutor on a screen usually sees only the finished answer.

Online is better than home tuition in three situations, and it is worth being blunt about them. When nobody within reach teaches 0625 Physics to Extended standard, a distant specialist beats a local generalist every time. When the family lives outside the metros and the alternative is a long weekly drive, online wins on the study hours the student gets back. And when the week is already full, a forty-five minute online session at nine in the evening is possible where a home visit is not.

Hybrid is what most families settle on by the second term. One home visit a week for the paper-based work, equations, graphs and full written answers under time, plus one shorter online session for doubt-solving, going through a past paper the student has already attempted, or a quick pass over multiple choice. A hybrid week also survives monsoon disruption and traffic in a way that two home visits do not.

The trade-off, stated plainly. Home tuition gives the tutor the student's working as it forms, and costs travel time that limits how many slots exist. Online opens a much wider pool of IGCSE Physics tutors in India, and costs the tutor's direct view of the page unless the family sets up a camera over it. Hybrid buys most of both and asks the household to keep two routines running instead of one.
items: Home sessions: paper, pencil, ruler, and the tutor watching the working
Online: a document camera or phone stand pointed at the student's page
Hybrid: one home visit weekly plus a shorter online doubt-solving slot
Online suits families outside the metros seeking an Edexcel 4PH1 tutor
Scanned scripts sent before an online lesson save the first ten minutes

contentBlocks.heading: How do you check a Physics tutor really knows 0625 and 4PH1?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask three questions and listen for syllabus detail. Which practical component does the school enter for, Paper 5 or Paper 6, and how does your teaching change between the two? Which equations does 0625 expect a candidate to recall unaided? What does a three-mark explanation question in electricity look like, and how are those three marks split? A tutor who genuinely teaches the syllabus answers all three without hesitating.

IB Gram checks what can be checked before a profile goes live: identity, claimed qualifications, the syllabuses and tiers the tutor says they teach, and teaching history. What no platform can see is whether a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old will work well together in a room on a Thursday evening. That part is yours, and a trial session is how you find out.

Do your own checks as well. Watch a demo instead of reading about one. Ask the tutor to mark one of your child's past answers in front of you and explain each mark, rather than describing their approach in general terms. Ask what they intend to do in the first four weeks and what evidence they will use to decide whether it worked. Ask how they handle a topic the student has already been taught badly, because unlearning a wrong method takes longer than teaching a new one, and a tutor who has not thought about that will simply repeat the school.

Two warning signs are worth naming. A tutor who cannot say which syllabus code they are teaching is running a general physics course, which is not the same thing as 0625 or 4PH1. And a tutor who promises a specific result is telling you about their marketing rather than their teaching. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the honest ones say so before you think to ask.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed syllabus codes are checked before listing
Ask which practical paper the school enters for, and why it matters
Have the tutor mark one past answer aloud, mark by mark
Agree what four weeks should change, and how you will know
A tutor who cannot name the syllabus code teaches general physics instead

contentBlocks.heading: Explanation questions in 0625: where the marks are actually awarded
contentBlocks.body:
An explanation question does not ask what happens. It asks why, and the mark scheme pays for the steps of the reasoning, one mark per step, in an order that has to be visible on the page. A student who writes the right conclusion with no chain in front of it usually collects one mark out of three and cannot understand why.

Take a standard three-mark question. A metal block and a plastic block have been sitting in the same room, and the student is asked why the metal feels colder to the touch. The answer that scores is a chain. Metal is the better conductor of thermal energy. So thermal energy is transferred away from the hand faster. So the hand cools faster and the block feels colder. Three linked statements, three marks. What most students write, that metal is a better conductor so it feels colder, is two statements, and it takes two of the three marks every time.

The habit that fixes this is mechanical, and it is the single most useful thing IGCSE Physics tutors in India do in the first month. Count the marks. Write that many linked statements. Join them with because or so. Then read the question back and check that each statement is about physics rather than about the apparatus, because describing the equipment is not a mark.

Command words matter as much as content. State and give want a short answer with no reasoning attached to it. Explain and describe want different things, and a student who treats them as synonyms will lose marks on one of them all year. Calculate wants the working shown, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip. Suggest allows an answer that is not in the syllabus as long as the physics is sound. Practise all of these on real past papers with the mark scheme open beside the student, not read out afterwards.
items: Count the marks, then write that many linked physics statements
Join the reasoning steps with because or so, in a visible order
Describing the apparatus scores nothing; the physics has to appear
Explain, describe, state and suggest each want a different answer shape
IGCSE physics past papers help most with the mark scheme open alongside

contentBlocks.heading: Space physics, nuclear physics and the topics left until last
contentBlocks.body:
Every 0625 cohort leaves the same topics until the end. Space physics is the usual one, because it often arrives last in the school's scheme of work and feels detachable from the rest of the syllabus. Nuclear physics is the second. The parts of thermal physics that depend on particle explanations are the third. None of them are optional and all of them appear on the theory paper.

Space physics rewards late revision more reliably than most topics, which is why leaving it out entirely is a mistake in the other direction. Much of it is recall and clear description rather than long calculation, so a student who spends two focused sessions on it in the final weeks can pick up marks that the same two sessions spent on electricity would not deliver. A tutor planning backwards from the series should book those sessions deliberately rather than hoping there is time left over.

What progress should look like, honestly. In the first month, equation recall improves and you can see it in the number of numerical questions attempted rather than skipped. By the second month, explanation answers get longer and gain structure, and marks on the written paper move before the multiple choice score does. Real change across a full paper usually shows over a term rather than a fortnight, and it shows first on the paper types the tutor has been working on.

Now the limits. A tutor cannot fix a topic the school has not taught yet, and should not race ahead of the class without the family agreeing to it first. A student missing Grade 9 foundations in algebra will move slowly in Physics however good the Physics teaching is, and that gap is worth addressing directly instead of pretending it is a Physics problem. And a week carrying four tuition subjects leaves no room for the independent past paper practice that actually moves a grade.
items: Space physics rewards late revision better than electricity usually does
Nuclear physics and particle explanations are the other common late gaps
Month one: fewer numerical questions skipped. Month two: longer explanations
Weak Grade 9 algebra slows Physics progress whatever the tutor does
Four tuition subjects a week crowds out independent past paper practice

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IGCSE Physics home tuition in India: what to prepare
contentBlocks.body:
Three things make a first session useful and all of them are already in the house. The most recent marked Physics paper, with the marks still written on it. The school's scheme of work or topic list for the year, which tells the tutor what has been taught and what has not. And the student's own exercise book, because handwriting, layout and the way working is set out are part of the diagnosis.

Say what you actually want. Families often open with a target grade and end up with a tutor working on the wrong thing for a month. If the problem is that numerical answers are being guessed, say that. If it is that the student writes one line where the question wants three, say that instead. The first session should end with the tutor telling you in plain words what they found and what the next four weeks will cover.

A first home tuition session on 0625 usually runs like this. Ten minutes of rapid equation recall across two or three topics, to find out what is genuinely in memory. Twenty minutes on one past paper question, worked on paper, with the tutor watching the working form. Fifteen minutes marking that answer against the real mark scheme, with the student reading the scheme aloud. Ten minutes on whichever topic the student named as their worst. Five minutes setting the work for the week.

Lessons run at home, online or as a hybrid week, subject to tutor availability and to your locality. If the fit turns out to be wrong, ask for a different match; it costs nothing to say so early and a great deal to say so in the final term. Families in Gachibowli, Andheri, Whitefield and South Delhi all begin the same way: one query, one shortlist, one trial.
items: Bring the last marked Physics paper, its mark scheme and the exercise book
Name the specific problem, not the target grade, on the first call
First hour: recall drill, one question, marking, worst topic, homework
Ask for a different match if the fit is wrong after two sessions
Home classes, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability in your locality

faqs.question: Does my child have to memorise every equation for IGCSE Physics 0625?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 expects candidates to recall the equations in the syllabus and to rearrange them, so there is no sheet to fall back on in the exam hall. Recall alone is not enough either. A student who can write the equation but freezes when the question asks for a different subject will still lose the mark. Practise both together, in short bursts, several times a week rather than in one long session before a test.

faqs.question: How do we practise equation rearrangement at home between tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: Keep it to ten minutes and make it verbal. You name a quantity, the student writes the equation from memory, then rearranges it for each of the other quantities in turn, saying the step out loud. Rotate topics so motion, thermal physics, waves and electricity all come round within a fortnight. You do not need to know Physics to run this; you only need the answer key the tutor leaves behind, and consistency matters far more than your own subject knowledge.

faqs.question: My son gets the right answer but only scores two marks out of three. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme is paying for reasoning steps, not for the conclusion. A three-mark explanation question wants three linked physics statements in a visible order, and most students write two and assume the third is obvious. The fix is mechanical: count the marks in the bracket, write that many statements, and join them with because or so. Describing the apparatus does not count as one of them, which surprises students who have written a full paragraph.

faqs.question: Is my child sitting Paper 5 or Paper 6, and can we change it?
faqs.answer: The school chooses, and the family cannot change it. Paper 5 is the practical test, taken in a laboratory, and Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, a written paper about practical work. Ask your school's examinations officer or Physics coordinator which entry has been made, because the answer changes how a tutor spends the practical part of the preparation. Either way the practical component carries 20% of the total, with multiple choice at 30% and theory at 50%.

faqs.question: What does a one-hour IGCSE Physics home tuition session actually look like?
faqs.answer: A useful hour has five parts. Ten minutes of rapid equation recall across two or three topics. Twenty minutes on one past paper question worked on paper while the tutor watches the working. Fifteen minutes marking that answer against the real mark scheme with the student reading it. Ten minutes on whichever topic the student says is worst. Five minutes setting the week's work. Sessions that are one long explanation from the tutor feel productive and change very little.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE Physics tutors in India charge?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on level, tier, experience, the mode of lessons and your locality, so any figure quoted before those are known is guesswork. One-to-one home tuition costs more per hour than a batch, because the tutor is teaching one student and travelling to you. Online usually sits below home tuition for the same tutor since there is no travel. Ask for the per-session fee, the session length, the cancellation terms and whether materials are included, and get all four in writing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our flat in Powai or Whitefield on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it depends on where the tutor lives rather than on the locality itself. A tutor already in Powai or Andheri can hold a Powai slot reliably; one coming from Navi Mumbai on a Tuesday cannot promise the same. The same logic applies in Whitefield against Jayanagar. Society and apartment gate entry is worth sorting once, by adding the tutor to the visitor list for a standing slot, rather than at seven in the evening each week.

faqs.question: Does online Physics tuition really work for a Grade 10 student?
faqs.answer: It works when the tutor can see the page. Set a phone or a document camera over the student's notebook so the working is visible as it is written, and the main weakness of online Physics disappears. Without that the tutor sees only finished answers and misses the rearrangement error that caused them. Online is the right call when no local tutor teaches 0625 to Extended standard, and a hybrid week is often the better compromise once the term settles.

faqs.question: We are in Koregaon Park in Pune and cannot find a 0625 Physics tutor nearby. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Widen the search in two steps rather than one. First look across the city for a tutor willing to hold one weekly visit, accepting that a second weekly visit is unlikely. Then take the rest online with a specialist from anywhere in the country. Families in Salt Lake in Kolkata and Bodakdev in Ahmedabad run the same arrangement. A strong distant tutor who sees the working through a camera beats a nearby generalist who has never taught the syllabus.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 is tiered and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 is not. Cambridge Core candidates take Paper 1 and Paper 3 and can reach grade C; Extended candidates take Paper 2 and Paper 4 and can reach A*, with Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the practical component. Edexcel runs Paper 1 and Paper 2 for every candidate, assesses practical skills inside those written papers, and grades 9-1. Confirm the code on the school's entry before buying any book.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month of tuition. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence rather than a reassurance. A month should show something small and specific: fewer numerical questions skipped, or explanation answers that now run to three statements. If the tutor cannot point to anything concrete, the plan was probably never specific enough. Agree one measurable target for the next four weeks, ask for one marked past paper question a week as the record, and if nothing moves after that, ask for a different match.

faqs.question: Should we start Physics tuition in Grade 9 or wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Start in Grade 9 if the problem is method, and wait if the problem is only a hard unit. Grade 9 is the cheap year to build equation recall, unit discipline and graph skills, because the content pressure is lower and habits formed then survive Grade 10. Waiting is sensible where a student is coping and one topic went badly, since a single term of school teaching often resolves it. Ask the school's subject teacher first; that conversation costs nothing.

Grade 9 is the cheap year to build equation recall, unit discipline and graph skills, because the content pressure is lower and habits formed then survive Grade 10. Waiting is sensible where a student is coping and one topic went badly, since a single term of school teaching often resolves it. Ask the school's subject teacher first; that conversation costs nothing.
